title: fix: make lazy sync additive-only to prevent overwriting webhook data
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
`/api/auth/me` calls `syncSubscriptionFromStripe()` which fetches from Stripe API and blindly overwrites all subscription fields in DynamoDB — even fields that webhooks already wrote correctly. This creates a race condition where stale Stripe API data can overwrite fresh webhook data (e.g., `subscription_status`, `subscriptionType`, `current_period_end`).

## What this fixes (after)
`syncSubscriptionFromStripe()` is now additive-only:
1. Reads the current user record from DynamoDB first
2. Fetches subscription data from Stripe
3. For each field (`subscription_status`, `stripe_subscription_id`, `subscriptionType`, `has_payment_method`, `current_period_end`):
   - If DynamoDB value is null/undefined -> writes the Stripe value (backfill)
   - If DynamoDB value is already set -> **skips** (trusts the webhook)
4. Only writes to DB if there are actual gaps to fill
5. Returns null if nothing needed updating

Webhooks remain the source of truth. Lazy sync only backfills gaps for legacy records or missed webhooks.

## How to test
1. Create a user with `stripe_customer_id` but no `subscription_status` in DynamoDB
2. Call `GET /api/auth/me` — lazy sync should backfill all subscription fields
3. **Expected**: All null fields populated from Stripe

4. Now set `subscription_status: "past_due"` manually in DynamoDB (simulating a webhook)
5. Call `GET /api/auth/me` again — Stripe says "active" but DB says "past_due"
6. **Expected**: `subscription_status` remains "past_due" (webhook data preserved, NOT overwritten)

7. Set `subscriptionType: null` but keep other fields set
8. Call `GET /api/auth/me`
9. **Expected**: Only `subscriptionType` is filled from Stripe; other fields untouched

## Edge cases to check
- User record not found in DynamoDB (returns null, no crash)
- All subscription fields already populated (no DB write at all)

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 6 test cases in `lazySyncAdditiveOnly.test.ts` (could not run locally due to sandbox ECANCELED errors — CI will verify)
- Tests cover: null backfill, non-null preservation, partial null fill, full sync when all null, webhook data preservation

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts` — additive-only logic in `syncSubscriptionFromStripe()`
- `backend/src/__tests__/lazySyncAdditiveOnly.test.ts` — new test file (6 tests)

## What was NOT tested
- E2E with actual Stripe webhook + auth/me call sequence (requires live Stripe test mode)
- Concurrent webhook + auth/me race (would need integration test with timing control)

title: docs: parallel tool calls token consumption investigation
body:
## Summary
- Documents Apr 5 investigation of whether parallel LLM tool calls use more tokens than sequential ones
- Key finding: parallel calls share one input context (far cheaper for large N), but produce more output tokens in the single response

title: fix: preserve default variable values across scheduled chat runs
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: `prefilledWithoutRequest` checked `valuesProvidedAfterLastRun`, which became `false` after the first run (config-time values have `variableValuesUpdatedAt < lastRunTime`). This caused the scheduler to incorrectly enter the email request flow, setting `variableRequestSentAt`.
- **Cascading bug**: Once `variableRequestSentAt` was set, `hadVariableRequestFlow = true`, so variables were cleared after every subsequent run — even though the user never clicked the email link.
- **Three-layer fix** in `agentModeController.ts`:
  1. `prefilledWithoutRequest` — removed `valuesProvidedAfterLastRun` requirement. Default values set at config time are valid for all runs, not just the first.
  2. `shouldClearVariablesAfterRun` — now requires `hadVariableRequestFlow && accessTokenWasConsumed`. Variables are only cleared when the user actually submitted via the email link (token consumed). If no one clicked the email link, values persist as permanent defaults.
  3. `updateScheduledChat` — when re-saving a schedule with all values pre-filled, now also resets `variableRequestSentAt` and related email flow fields. This is the recovery path for already-broken schedules (e.g. Karthy's).

## Affected account

`karthy@goaldenhour.com` — "Karthy Linkedin Outreach Connect" schedule. After this is deployed, open the schedule in Scheduled Chats → Agent Mode → click **Update Schedule** (no changes needed). This will clear `variableRequestSentAt` and restore permanent pre-filled defaults mode.

title: fix: wire MCP OAuth routes through CORS + accept form POST bodies
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

> Pairs with customer portal PR #474 (form POST consent fix). Both must ship together for the MCP OAuth flow to actually work in a browser.

## What was wrong (before)

The MCP OAuth 2.1 backend shipped 5 weeks ago but the consent flow has been completely broken from a browser. Three distinct bugs in the same module:

1. \`setupMcpOAuth(app)\` was called BEFORE the global CORS middleware and body parsers in \`app.ts\`. The OAuth endpoints never got \`Access-Control-Allow-Origin\` headers applied. Any cross-origin request from the customer portal got blocked with a CORS error.
2. The decision endpoint only accepted JSON bodies and only read the JWT from the \`Authorization\` header. The canonical OAuth consent pattern uses a plain HTML form POST, which uses \`application/x-www-form-urlencoded\` encoding and can't set custom headers.
3. \`if (!approved)\` treated the string \`\"false\"\` as truthy because form encoding coerces everything to strings. A naive boolean check would have auto-approved denied requests.

## What this fixes (after)

- **Move \`setupMcpOAuth(app)\`** from line 88 to after the global \`express.json\` / \`express.urlencoded\` / CORS middleware. The OAuth routes now inherit both body parsers + CORS automatically.
- **Drop the per-route body parsers** (\`express.json()\` on \`/oauth/register\` and \`/oauth/authorize/decision\`, \`express.urlencoded()\` on \`/oauth/token\`) — they were only needed because the routes were registered before the global parsers.
- **New \`authFromBodyOrHeader\` middleware** on \`/oauth/authorize/decision\`: reads the JWT from \`Authorization\` header (API clients) OR \`req.body.jwt\` (browser form POSTs), then delegates to the existing \`authenticateToken\` middleware. Backwards-compatible with the header path.
- **New \`isApproved\` helper** that handles both boolean \`true\` and string \`\"true\"\` correctly. Form POSTs can't accidentally flip deny into approve.
- **Two new tests** for the form POST path: one asserting form POST with \`approved=\"true\"\` succeeds, one asserting \`approved=\"false\"\` (string) correctly denies via the access_denied path.

## How to test

### Unit tests
\`\`\`
cd backend && npx jest src/mcp/oauth/__tests__/oauthRoutes.test.ts
\`\`\`
**Expected**: 21/21 pass.

### CORS preflight (live test env)
\`\`\`
curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"HTTP %{http_code}\\nA-C-A-O: %header{Access-Control-Allow-Origin}\\n\" \\
  -X OPTIONS http://35.163.236.170:3001/oauth/authorize/decision \\
  -H \"Origin: http://35.163.236.170:5174\" \\
  -H \"Access-Control-Request-Method: POST\"
\`\`\`
**Expected before this PR**: no CORS header.
**Expected after this PR**: \`HTTP 204 + Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://35.163.236.170:5174\`.

### Full OAuth flow via curl
\`\`\`
TOKEN=\$(curl -s -X POST http://35.163.236.170:3001/api/auth/login \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{\"email\":\"test@example.com\",\"password\":\"Test123!\"}' \\
  | python3 -c \"import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['token'])\")

CLIENT=\$(curl -s -X POST http://35.163.236.170:3001/oauth/register \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{\"client_name\":\"Test\",\"redirect_uris\":[\"https://httpbin.org/get\"],\"grant_types\":[\"authorization_code\"],\"response_types\":[\"code\"],\"token_endpoint_auth_method\":\"none\",\"scope\":\"mcp:tools\"}' \\
  | python3 -c \"import json,sys;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['client_id'])\")

# Form POST simulation (browser path)
curl -i -X POST http://35.163.236.170:3001/oauth/authorize/decision \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \\
  -d \"approved=true&client_id=\$CLIENT&redirect_uri=https://httpbin.org/get&scope=mcp:tools&state=tx&code_challenge=E9Melhoa2OwvFrEMTJguCHaoeK1t8URWbuGJSstw-cM&code_challenge_method=S256&jwt=\$TOKEN\"
\`\`\`
**Expected**: \`HTTP 302 Found\` with \`Location: https://httpbin.org/get?code=<real_code>&state=tx\` and CORS headers present.

### Browser test (after both PRs merge)
1. Log in to the test env at http://35.163.236.170:5174
2. Open a fresh consent URL (use the helper script in the test plan)
3. Click Approve
4. **Expected**: browser navigates through the 302 chain to httpbin.org/get with the auth code visible in the URL params
5. **Expected**: NO CORS errors in the console, NO \"Failed to fetch\" errors

## Edge cases to check

- Form POST with \`approved=\"false\"\` (string) → must redirect with \`error=access_denied\`. Regression test added.
- JSON body path (existing API clients with Authorization header) → must still work. Existing tests still pass.
- Token endpoint refresh flow → unchanged, still works (no body parser changes that affect it).

## Test Evidence

- Backend: 21/21 pass in \`src/mcp/oauth/__tests__/oauthRoutes.test.ts\` (19 existing + 2 new)
- Live test env: full OAuth flow verified via curl, including form POST with JWT in body, token exchange with PKCE, and the deny path
- CORS preflight verified via OPTIONS request

## Files changed

- \`backend/src/app.ts\` — move \`setupMcpOAuth(app)\` call after CORS + body parsers
- \`backend/src/mcp/oauth/oauthRoutes.ts\` — remove per-route body parsers, add \`authFromBodyOrHeader\` middleware, add \`isApproved\` helper, use both on the decision endpoint
- \`backend/src/mcp/oauth/__tests__/oauthRoutes.test.ts\` — 2 new tests for form POST + string \`approved\`

## What was NOT tested

- **Live claude.ai integration** — pending PR merge + production deploy. The curl path proves the OAuth contract works exactly as claude.ai would consume it, but the actual claude.ai web UI integration is a separate verification step.
- **Refresh token flow with form POST encoding** — refresh tokens are typically used by API clients, not browser form POSTs, so the existing JSON path covers it. If a browser-only client needs to refresh via form POST in the future, this PR's changes already support it (the global urlencoded parser handles it).
- **Param-tampering attacks** — backend is the source of truth for PKCE validation; this PR doesn't change any of that logic.

## Pairs with

- **Customer portal PR #474** — switches the consent page from fetch-based POST to HTML form submission. Must ship together: this PR alone doesn't help if the frontend is still using fetch; the frontend PR alone doesn't help if the backend rejects form bodies.

3. `if (!approved)` treated the string `"false"` as truthy because form encoding coerces everything to strings. A naive boolean check would have auto-approved denied requests.

**How to test**:

1. **Sessions column → Created column**: The admin users table had a "Sessions" column that showed a `1` chip for nearly every user — not informative, and took up a column where signup date is more useful for triaging new signups. nginx/ELB are configured for 10 minutes, but `mcpFetch` killed the request at 5 minutes.

title: Fix Emma sidebar chat issues
body:
## Summary
- **Bug 1 — Session appears empty on reopen**: When localStorage entry expires (5-min TTL), the fallback API call used `limit=1` without a page filter. If the user had been on other pages since, the most recent emma-sidebar session was for a different page, making the current page's history invisible. Fixed by passing `pageIdentifier` as a query param so the server returns only sessions for that specific page.
- **Bug 2 — Emma shows error even though schedule was created**: `createScheduledChat` only auto-populated `emailNotifications` from `user.email` in the "variables present and unfilled" case. Schedules created without variables and without email ended up with an empty `emailNotifications: []`. On a later update call without email, the validation rejected it ("At least one email notification required"), forcing an extra `get_user_profile` + retry. Fixed by always falling back to `user.email` when no emails are provided (except when all variables are pre-filled, which is an intentional silent run).

title: fix: brand guidelines delete causes logos to be deleted
body:
## Summary

- **Root cause 1 (data loss):** GET, POST, and DELETE brand guidelines handlers all read the user record via `UserIdIndex` GSI (eventually consistent). If a logo was recently uploaded, the GSI could return a stale record without the logo — so writing back the updated attachments would silently remove the logo from DynamoDB. Fixed all three handlers to use `dynamodb.get({ Key: { email }, ConsistentRead: true })`.

- **Root cause 2 (org users):** POST handler was reading `existingBrandGuidelines` from the user record even for org users (who store brand guidelines at org level). Fixed by checking `user.orgId` and reading from the org record instead.

- **Root cause 3 (legacy keyless assets — Lyndi's exact scenario):** `lyndi@every.io`'s attachments were uploaded via the old file path and have no `key` field. The DELETE endpoint now accepts a `?url=` query param as fallback: when key is absent, the attachment is matched by URL in DynamoDB and the S3 key is extracted from the URL for cleanup.

## Test plan

title: fix: paginate Fathom recordings + fallback for Talked funnel stage
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
`backend/src/services/prospectMeetingService.ts` (`getFathomRecordings`) only fetched **page 1** of Fathom's `/v1/meetings` endpoint. Fathom paginates with `next_cursor` at a default page size of 10. Any customer with >10 recordings in the window silently lost everything after the first 10 — and the "Talked" funnel stage on the partner portal admin dashboard shows `0` for every channel (LinkedIn / Outbound / Paid Ads) because most past events can't find a matching recording.

Hit prod `/api/admin/funnel-metrics?period=30d` with Harsha's JWT on 2026-04-07 — confirmed `Talked: 0` across all channels with no errors.

## What this fixes (after)
1. `getFathomRecordings()` now follows `next_cursor` until exhausted or until `FATHOM_MAX_PAGES` (20 pages / 200 recordings) is hit, warning in the log if the cap is reached.
2. Each recording now captures `calendar_invitees_domains_type === 'one_or_more_external'` as a `hasExternalInvitees` flag on the `FathomRecordingMatch`.
3. `classifyMeetingStatus()` gains a fallback: if transcript speaker diarization is unavailable (common for fresh recordings where `GET /recordings/:id/transcript` returns empty), but the Fathom listing says the recording had external invitees, we classify as `talked` instead of silently falling through to `no-show`. Transcript speakers still win when available.
4. `getProspectMeetingMetrics()` logs a summary line at the end: `period=30d events=211 externalEvents=52 pastExternal=47 fathomRecordings=70 fathomExternal=22 matched=X transcriptOk=Y talked=Z noShows=W` — so next time Talked shows 0 the root cause is immediately visible in CloudWatch.

## How to test
1. Log in to the partner portal as the admin account (`ruiwangwarm@gmail.com`).
2. Go to `/admin/funnel-metrics` (or wherever the funnel dashboard lives on your test env).
3. Pick period = `30d`.
4. **Expected**: `Talked` stage for LinkedIn / Outbound / Paid Ads now shows non-zero values (exact count depends on how many prospect meetings happened in the last 30 days on Harsha's account).
5. In the backend logs on the test env, search for `[ProspectMeeting] period=`.
6. **Expected**: A single summary line per funnel request showing `fathomRecordings`, `matched`, `transcriptOk`, `talked`, `noShows` — non-zero on the matched/talked counts.

## Edge cases to check
- User with <10 recordings in the window: should behave identically to before (single page fetched, no regression).
- User whose Fathom account is disconnected: should still return empty recordings array, no error thrown.
- Fathom API 5xx mid-pagination: the try/catch around the loop swallows the error and returns whatever pages were fetched so far (non-fatal — funnel degrades gracefully).

## Test Evidence
- `npx jest src/__tests__/prospectMeetingService.test.ts` → **10 passed, 0 failed**
- `npx jest --testPathPattern='prospectMeeting|fathom'` → **67 passed, 0 failed** across 8 suites (all adjacent Fathom tests still green)
- Type check: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.jest.json` → clean
- Tested as: unit tests with mocked axios + Fathom config. Not yet run against live Fathom in test env.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/prospectMeetingService.ts` (119 +, 35 -)
- `backend/src/__tests__/prospectMeetingService.test.ts` (new, 196 lines)

## What was NOT tested
- Live Fathom API call against the test env — needs Fathom credentials on the test env box. Next step after merge: sync to test env and reload the funnel page with Harsha's account to confirm non-zero Talked.
- The previous-period comparison branch wasn't given its own test case, but it uses the same `classifyMeetingStatus` helper which is covered.
- Rate-limit / 429 handling from Fathom during pagination — relies on existing non-fatal try/catch.

title: fix: classify Google Calendar 403s + persist gmail granted_scopes
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The business funnel "Talked" stage silently showed 0 when the Google Calendar API was actually returning 403 SERVICE_DISABLED — indistinguishable from "no meetings booked". On top of that, gmail OAuth /connect only wrote `granted_scopes` on the connection record and left the legacy `BaseOAuthConfig.scopes` field empty, so scope-related debugging required hitting DynamoDB directly.

## What this fixes (after)
- `prospectMeetingService.fetchCalendarEvents` now classifies 403s into `service_disabled | scope_not_granted | insufficient_permissions | quota_exceeded | forbidden_unknown`, returns `{events, error?}`, and propagates the classification through `ProspectMeetingMetrics.calendarError`.
- `businessFunnelService.buildTalkedSources` renders that error as a human-readable `errorSource` on the Talked stage for all three channels (linkedin, outbound, paid_ads), so the frontend can show an actionable banner instead of a misleading 0.
- `gmailAuth` /connect now populates BOTH `config.scopes` and `config.granted_scopes` from the OAuth response, and `connectedAccountsDb` exports a `hasGmailCalendarScope` helper that reads either field so new and old records both work.

## How to test
No UI surfaces yet (frontend banner is a follow-up). Verify via unit tests and log inspection:

1. Run `cd backend && npx jest --testPathPattern='prospectMeeting|gmailAuth|hasGmailCalendarScope|connectedAccounts|businessFunnel'`
2. **Expected**: All tests pass (77 tests across 9 suites).
3. On test env or dev, disable the Calendar API in the GCP project and hit the funnel endpoint.
4. **Expected**: CloudWatch shows `[ProspectMeeting] Calendar fetch failed [service_disabled]: Google Calendar API is disabled in the GCP project — enable it in the Google Cloud console.` and the Talked stage's sources contain an `errorSource` with that message.
5. Re-enable Calendar API, disconnect + reconnect Gmail in the portal.
6. **Expected**: After reconnect, `AW-Users[{userId}].connected_accounts[{gmail}].config.scopes` is a populated array matching `granted_scopes` (previously it was `[]`).

## Edge cases to check
- 403 with an unrecognized `reason` field (e.g. a new Google enum) falls through to `forbidden_unknown` rather than being misclassified.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 42 passed, 0 failed (prospectMeeting + gmailAuth + hasGmailCalendarScope)
- Related suites: 35 passed, 0 failed (connectedAccounts + businessFunnel)
- TypeScript: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean

title: fix: prevent duplicate auto-engagement replies from concurrent scanner instances
body:
## Summary

- **Bug:** Auto engagement was posting two replies to the same LinkedIn comment. Root cause was a race condition: multiple Elastic Beanstalk instances each ran the scanner simultaneously, both read `hasEngaged() → false` before either had written the tracking record, then both created separate schedule records (different UUIDs) for the same comment. The existing `claimAction` guard only deduplicates the *same* schedule ID — it couldn't prevent two distinct schedules from both executing.
- **Fix:** Changed `recordEngagement(status='queued')` from a plain DynamoDB `UPDATE` to a **conditional UPDATE** — succeeds only if the item doesn't exist yet, or is a retryable failed item. The first instance to write wins and returns `true`; all others get `ConditionalCheckFailedException` and return `false`. `scheduleOneAction` skips `createSchedule` when `false`, so only one schedule is ever created per comment.
- **Dry-run verified** against dev DynamoDB: concurrent `Promise.all` of two claim attempts → exactly one succeeds.

## Test plan

- [x] 3 new unit tests: concurrent duplicate prevention (post engagement + comment reply), schedule still created when claim succeeds
- [x] All 419 test suites / 6272 tests pass
- [x] Dry-run against dev DynamoDB confirms atomic behavior

title: fix: prevent double-escaping of MCP tool results stored in S3

## Summary

- `get_chat_history` and other `mcpToolRegistry` tools wrap their output in the MCP envelope `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: '<JSON>' }] }`. Previously `JSON.stringify(result)` was used to produce the S3 payload, causing the inner JSON to be double-escaped — field names like `"sessionId"` were stored as `\"sessionId\"` in the S3 file.

title: fix(partner-portal): tier filter dropdown reads dynamically from AW-Settings
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)

The Users tab in the partner portal had a Tier filter dropdown with a hardcoded MenuItem list:

\`\`\`tsx
<MenuItem value="Managed">Managed</MenuItem>
<MenuItem value="Super Premium">Super Premium</MenuItem>
<MenuItem value="Advanced">Advanced</MenuItem>
<MenuItem value="Basic">Basic</MenuItem>
<MenuItem value="Free">Free</MenuItem>
\`\`\`

The list silently drifted as new tiers were added to \`AW-Settings.subscription_types\`. Specifically, **\`Pro\` and \`Premium\` exist as defined tiers** (with proper allowedPages / allowedSkills / token allowances) but were missing from the filter. After today's tier reconciliation moved a bunch of users to \`subscriptionType: "Pro"\`, there was no way to filter the user list for them.

## What this fixes (after)

The filter now renders MenuItems dynamically from \`availableSubscriptionTypes\` — the same state that powers the per-row edit dropdown a few hundred lines below in the same file (line 3866). \`availableSubscriptionTypes\` is loaded via \`GET /api/admin/subscription-types\` when the Users tab mounts (line 897), so this introduces no new fetches and adds no latency.

\`\`\`tsx
<MenuItem value="all">All Tiers</MenuItem>
{availableSubscriptionTypes.map((t) => (
  <MenuItem key={t} value={t}>{t}</MenuItem>
))}
<MenuItem value="none">No Tier</MenuItem>
\`\`\`

The \`"all"\` and \`"none"\` sentinel options stay (they're filter modes, not real tiers).

Result: any tier defined in \`AW-Settings.subscription_types\` automatically appears in the filter. Two dropdowns in the same file now share one source of truth.

## How to test

1. Log in to the partner portal as an admin
2. Go to the Users tab
3. Click the **Tier** filter dropdown
4. **Expected**: every tier defined in \`AW-Settings.subscription_types\` is listed (Free, Basic, Pro, Premium, Managed, Super Premium, Advanced, etc.) plus the \`All Tiers\` and \`No Tier\` sentinels at top and bottom
5. Select \`Pro\` from the filter
6. **Expected**: the user list filters to only users with \`subscriptionType: "Pro"\`
7. Open a user card and click the edit (pencil) icon next to their subscription chip
8. **Expected**: the per-row edit dropdown shows the same set of tiers as the filter dropdown — they're now consistent

\`partner-portal/src/__tests__/AdminDashboard.tierFilter.test.tsx\` (new file, 5 tests in the same isolated-component pattern as \`AdminDashboard.subscriptions.test.tsx\`):

1. Renders every tier from \`availableSubscriptionTypes\` as an option
2. Includes \`"Pro"\` even though the old hardcoded list omitted it (regression)
3. Always keeps the \`"all"\` and \`"none"\` sentinel options
4. Shows only the sentinels when \`availableSubscriptionTypes\` is empty (degraded fallback)
5. Selecting a dynamic tier fires \`onChange\` with the tier name

Local jest run was unreliable through symlinked monorepo node_modules — relying on GitHub CI as the gate. PR will not be merged until CI is green.

---

### Fix: Prioritize active subscriptions in `syncSubscriptionFromStripe` (commit `caf7e9a0`)
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: fix | **Priority**: High — **directly fixes Karthy / GoaldenHour showing as Canceled**

**What changed**: `syncSubscriptionFromStripe` was calling `stripe.subscriptions.list({ status: 'all', limit: 1 })`. Stripe returns subs in reverse-chronological order, so if a customer had a canceled sub created after their active one (e.g., an old failed checkout re-run), the canceled one came back first and overwrote their status in DynamoDB. Now fetches up to 10 subs and sorts by status priority (`active > trialing > past_due > canceled`) before picking one. Matches the logic already used in `reconcileAllStripeUsers`.

**How to test**
1. Confirm current state: partner portal → Users tab → search "Karthy" (or GoaldenHour)
2. **Expected (before deploy)**: Status shows `Canceled`
3. Deploy this PR to prod

title: fix: paginate Fathom meetings in Emma fathom_get_meetings tool
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The `fathom_get_meetings` Emma tool called the Fathom API once and read only the first page of results (default 10 items). Users asking Emma "what meetings did I have in March?" got silently truncated results — only the first 10 of potentially 70+ recordings were returned. The code comment on line 121 literally acknowledged `next_cursor` exists but never followed it.

## What this fixes (after)
The tool now follows `next_cursor` in a pagination loop (same pattern already shipped for `prospectMeetingService.ts` in commit 330e95b9). A safety cap of `FATHOM_TOOLS_MAX_PAGES = 20` (200 meetings max) prevents runaway pagination from unbounded date ranges.

## How to test
1. Connect a Fathom account with 10+ meetings
2. Go to Agent Mode (`/agent`)
3. Ask Emma: "What meetings did I have this month?"
4. **Expected**: All meetings returned, not just 10
5. Check backend logs for `[fathom_get_meetings]` — should NOT see `FATHOM_TOOLS_MAX_PAGES` warning for normal accounts

## Edge cases to check
- User with 200+ meetings in date range (should hit safety cap and log warning, not infinite loop)

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 19 passed, 0 failed (7 new pagination tests)
- Tested pagination: single-page, multi-page (3 pages), safety cap, empty response, null cursor, empty string cursor, network error

title: fix: skip slack suggest when message @mentions Emma (already handled by Emma)
body:
## Summary
- When a client @mentions Emma in Slack, Slack fires both an `app_mention` event (Emma responds directly in Slack) and a `message` event (caught by the slack-suggest handler). This caused a duplicate \"suggested reply\" email to founders even though Emma was already responding.
- Fix: lazily fetch and cache Emma's Slack bot user ID via `auth.test()`, then skip `handleSlackTriggeredSession` only when the message specifically mentions Emma (`<@BOT_USER_ID>`).
- Messages that @mention other users (e.g. @Rui) are unaffected — they still go through the suggest flow and trigger an email if triage determines the message is actionable.

title: fix: deduplicate LinkedIn posts to prevent multiple comments on same post
body:
## Root Cause

LinkedIn's `/rest/posts` API returns the same physical post under two different URN formats in a single `listPosts` response:
- `urn:li:share:X` (share URN)  
- `urn:li:ugcPost:Y` (UGC post URN)

The scanner treated each URN as a distinct post and scheduled the same engager accounts to comment on both — resulting in AI Fusion Tech and Rui Wang each appearing 2–3 times in the comments on the "What's up with AI April 13" LinkedIn post.

The existing per-(postId, engagingAccountId, actionType) dedup in the tracking table correctly prevents double-execution **for the same URN**, but had no defense against two URNs representing the same physical post.

## Fix

In `scanOwnerPostsForEngagement`, before the scheduling loop, filter `recentPosts` into `dedupedPosts` using a `Set<string>` keyed on `post.commentary || post.content`. The first URN wins; the second is logged and skipped. Posts with no parseable content are kept as-is (no false deduplication).

Also included: an earlier fix that respects the engager's own `preferredActions` setting (a like-only engager like AI Fusion was being scheduled for comments even when the owner wanted comments — now the engager's preference gates it too).

## Tests

3 new content-dedup tests:
- Same commentary, two URNs → only one schedule created
- Distinct commentary → both posts scheduled  
- No commentary field → both posts kept (no false dedup)

All 37 tests pass.

## Test plan
- [ ] Review content-dedup logic in `scanOwnerPostsForEngagement`
- [ ] Confirm 37 scanner cron tests pass
- [ ] Monitor LinkedIn posts after next scanner run for duplicate comments

## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
No way to rank 17k+ leads for outreach. Heat is implicit in \"did this person sign up / open a deal / engage recently\" but nobody aggregates those signals into a single score.

## What this fixes (after)
Pure scoring service per the CRM Unification v1 spec:

- `+25` has AW-Users record (signed up)
- `+40` has active Stripe subscription (paying or trialing)
- `+20` status in {qualified, proposal_sent, negotiating} OR open Deal at Qualified+
- `+15` engagement event <7d old
- `+10` isICP === true
- `-50` contactStatus !== 'active' (do-not-contact, unsubscribed) with a hard ceiling at 49
- Clamp 0-100

Three surfaces:
- `computeHeatScore(signals, now?)` — pure sync scorer, clock-injected for tests
- `computeForContact(contactId, { loadSignals })` — async wrapper with injected fetcher
- `recomputeBatch(contactIds, { loadSignals })` — for migrations and POC reassignment

The signal-loader is dependency-injected so this PR doesn't have to ship the AW-Leads email-index GSI query + Stripe lookup. Those wire in after A1/B1/D2 land.

   computeHeatScore({ hasUserRecord: true, hasActiveSubscription: true, isICP: true, contactStatus: 'active' })

title: feat(crm): C3 — lifecycle compute service (8-state auto-derivation)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
No single source of truth for lifecycle stage. Each UI surface had to recompute \"is this person paying / trialing / churned\" from raw Stripe status + deal rows + engagement. The 3-tab CRM landing (Inbox / Working / Paying) needs a stable enum to filter by.

## What this fixes (after)
Pure, priority-ordered classifier that returns one of 8 stages:

1. canceled subscription OR no activity >60d → `churned`
2. past_due OR health<40 OR no usage >30d (only while currently paying) → `at_risk`
3. active subscription → `paying`
4. trialing subscription → `trialing`
5. open Deal (not Won/Lost) → `in_deal`
6. AW-Users record, no deal/sub → `signed_up`
7. email only → `inbox`
8. domain-only / empty → `unknown`

Plus `applyAndUpdate(contactId, deps)` — reads signals via injected loader, computes, and on transition persists the new stage and logs a `lifecycle.changed` event. No-op when the stage is unchanged.

## How to test
1. ` cd backend && npm test -- lifecycleService`
2. **Expected**: 21 tests pass
3. REPL:
   ```js
   computeLifecycle({ subscriptionState: 'active', lastActivityAt: '<today>', email: 'a@x.com' })
   ```
4. **Expected**: `'paying'`
5. ```js
   computeLifecycle({ subscriptionState: 'past_due', currentLifecycle: 'paying', email: 'a@x.com' })
   ```
6. **Expected**: `'at_risk'`
7. Verify no-op:
   ```js
   applyAndUpdate('a@x.com', { loadSignals: () => ({ currentLifecycle: 'signed_up', hasUserRecord: true, email: 'a@x.com' }), persistLifecycle, logTransitionEvent })
   ```
8. **Expected**: `result.changed === false`, neither persist nor log called

## Edge cases to check
- at_risk rules are gated to currently-paying customers (signed_up user with past_due sub stays signed_up)
- Won/Lost deals do NOT count as open (falls through to signed_up)
- Malformed timestamps are silently ignored (no false churn)
- Future timestamps treated as unknown (clock-skew guard)
- applyAndUpdate no-op: unchanged lifecycle never touches DynamoDB or the event log

- Unit tests: 21 passed, 0 failed

- `backend/src/services/lifecycleService.ts` (new)

title: feat(crm): B1 — unified sync endpoint POST /api/crm/sync
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
CRM signals came in from half a dozen sources (signup, Stripe, lead forms, Emma chat, Fathom, manual edits) and each handler wrote directly to AW-Leads with its own ad-hoc merge logic. No single source of truth for identity resolution, no event log, no dedup on webhook replay, and score recomputes were scattered across each call site.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds the hub entry point the CRM Unification v1 epic has been waiting on: `POST /api/crm/sync`.

- **`contactSyncService.ts`** — pure dependency-injected composition layer
  - `resolveIdentity()` — normalises email to the canonical `contactId`; falls back to `nocontact:<sourceRecordId>` when no email is available
  - `mergeFields()` — source-aware precedence (Stripe wins on payment fields; `lead_form`/`fathom`/`manual` win on human-editable fields; generic sources never clobber existing values)
  - `syncContact()` — idempotent on `sourceRecordId` (short-circuits the entire recompute on replay), logs the event via `contactEventsDb`, then recomputes heat/health/lifecycle when a `loadSignals` fetcher is wired
- **Route**: `POST /api/crm/sync` on the existing CRM router (JWT-protected). 400 for missing required fields, 500 for downstream failures.

Scoring is fully DI — downstream hooks (B2 signup, B3 Stripe) supply their own `loadSignals` so this PR doesn't have to ship the AW-Leads email-index GSI lookup or Stripe join wiring.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npm test -- contactSyncService`
2. **Expected**: 26 tests pass — identity resolution, merge rules, idempotency, score recompute, validation
3. Start the backend dev server
4. `curl -X POST http://localhost:3001/api/crm/sync -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"source":"manual","sourceRecordId":"test_1","identity":{"email":"jane@acme.com"},"eventType":"contact.created","payload":{"note":"test"}}'`
5. **Expected**: 200 response with `{ contactId: 'jane@acme.com', created: true, deduplicated: false, event: {...}, scores: {...} }`
6. Replay the same curl
7. **Expected**: `{ ..., deduplicated: true, created: false, event: <the original event> }` — no new row in AW-ContactEvents
8. `curl ... -d '{"source":"manual","sourceRecordId":"test_2","identity":{},"eventType":"contact.created"}'`
9. **Expected**: 400 with message `Invalid body. Required: source, sourceRecordId, eventType, identity.`

## Edge cases to check
- Email with uppercase / whitespace normalises to lowercase contactId
- Free-email providers (gmail/yahoo/outlook/icloud/proton) don't pollute the `_identity.domain` field
- Supplied `domain` on the identity wins over the derived one
- `customFields` on the input flows through to `event.payload._customFields`
- Same email arriving from two different sources resolves to the same `contactId`
- Domain-only submission creates a provisional `nocontact:<sri>` event — a later email submission is a separate event until B1.5 merges the Lead rows

title: feat(crm): D1 — internal enrichment endpoint (AW-Users + Stripe join)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
We already know whether a lead is signed up, what plan they're on, what Stripe is charging them, and when their period ends — but none of that data lives on AW-Leads. The CRM lead-detail drawer had no way to show it without every caller hand-rolling the AW-Users + Stripe join.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds `GET /api/crm/leads/:leadId/enrichment?listId=<id>` which joins at read time — no migration, no denormalised copy.

- **`internalEnrichmentService.ts`** — pure DI service:
  - `getUserByEmail` fetcher (AW-Users lookup by lowercase email)
  - `getStripeSubscriptionForCustomer` fetcher (picks best subscription by status priority: active > trialing > past_due > canceled)
  - Stripe errors are swallowed (non-fatal) and fall back to DB-only data
- **`InternalEnrichmentCache`** — TTL-gated `Map<email, EnrichmentResult>`, 1h default, clock-injected for tests
- **Route**: owner-only (lead list must belong to the authed user). Returns empty enrichment when the lead has no email (nothing to join on).

Response shape:
```json
{
  "isUser": true,
  "signupDate": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "subscriptionType": "pro",
  "stripeStatus": "active",
  "mrr": 49,
  "currentPeriodEnd": "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z",
  "stripeCustomerId": "cus_..."
}
```

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npm test -- internalEnrichmentService`
2. **Expected**: 15 tests pass (no-user, no-Stripe, full-join, Stripe error, cache TTL, cache collision, case-insensitive)
3. Start backend, log in as `test@example.com`
4. Find a lead on a list the account owns (any list from `/crm`).
5. `curl 'http://localhost:3001/api/crm/leads/<leadId>/enrichment?listId=<listId>' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'`
6. **Expected**: 200 JSON with the shape above. If the lead's email matches an AW-Users row, `isUser: true`; if they have a Stripe sub, the stripe fields are populated.
7. Call the same endpoint with a lead email that is NOT in AW-Users
8. **Expected**: `{ "isUser": false, ... all nulls ... }`
9. Call the same endpoint for a lead that belongs to a DIFFERENT user's list
10. **Expected**: 404 `Lead list not found`

## Edge cases to check
- Lead with no email → returns empty enrichment (200, no error)
- Missing `?listId` query → 400
- User has `stripe_customer_id` but Stripe is down → DB-only data, Stripe warn logged, no 500
- Repeat call within 1h → short-circuits DB + Stripe (cache hit)

title: feat(crm): G1 — ask_crm Emma tool for free-form pipeline questions
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Emma could run structured tools (`get_leads`, `search_leads`, `get_lead_details`) but users had to frame every pipeline question as a filter expression. Strategic questions like "who should I reach out to today" or "is Jane at Acme paying us" or "which deals are about to close" had no single answer surface — Emma had to guess which tool(s) to call and hope the LLM stitched the answer together.

## What this fixes (after)
New Emma tool `ask_crm` plus a pure orchestrator service that does the stitching:

- **`askCrmService.ts`** — intent classifier + per-intent rankers:
  - `hot_leads` → non-churned, non-do-not-contact, sorted by heat desc
  - `at_risk` → lifecycle=at_risk, sorted by health asc
  - `deals_closing` → lifecycle=in_deal, sorted by dealValue desc
  - `paying_customers` → lifecycle in {paying, trialing}
  - `specific_contact` → token-substring match on name/email/company
- Falls back to the C1 heat + C3 lifecycle compute services when the Lead row doesn't yet have stored `heatScore` / `lifecycle` (non-disruptive to the existing 17k rows)
- Returns `{ intent, summary, items[], totalConsidered }` where each item has a `citationUrl` Emma can cite as `[name](/crm/lists/.../leads/...)`

- **Tool registration** in `backend/src/emma/tools.ts`:
  - Name: `ask_crm`
  - Input: `{ question, limit?, load_limit? }`
  - Iterates the user's lists lazily, capped at `load_limit` (default 500) — plenty for `founders@agentweb.pro`

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npm test -- askCrmService`
2. **Expected**: 20 tests pass (intent classifier, rankers, filters, citation URL encoding)
3. Start backend and customer portal. Log in as `test@example.com`
4. Open Emma chat, ensure CRM tools are installed (install_skills if needed)
5. Ask Emma: `Who should I reach out to today?`
6. **Expected**: Emma calls `ask_crm`, gets back a `hot_leads` answer, and narrates the top N with inline citations to `/crm/lists/...`
7. Ask: `Is <firstName> at <company> paying us?` using a real lead name/company from one of your lists
8. **Expected**: `specific_contact` intent, Emma names the person and summarises their lifecycle / subscription state

## Edge cases to check
- `"who is at risk"` — must be `at_risk` intent, not `specific_contact` (the regex order matters; this is covered by a unit test)
- Empty question → `unknown` intent, falls through to heat-ranked generic list
- Lead with stored `heatScore` takes precedence over on-the-fly compute
- `limit` is clamped to 1..25 at the tool boundary; `load_limit` defaults to 500
- Leads marked `do-not-contact` are excluded from hot_leads
- Churned leads excluded from hot_leads

## Test Evidence

title: feat(crm): B2 — signup hook + Emma session CRM signals
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
`contactSyncService` (B1) shipped as the unified entry point for CRM signals, but nothing was calling it. The two highest-volume signals — new signups and Emma chat engagement — were still invisible to the AW-ContactEvents log, so heat/health/lifecycle had nothing to score.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds two fire-and-forget hooks that feed `contactSyncService`:

- **`db.createUser`** → logs `{ source: 'signup', eventType: 'contact.created', sourceRecordId: 'user-<userId>' }`. First/last name falls back to parsed `displayName` when not provided. OAuth signups are tagged `signupSource='oauth'`, password signups `'password'`.
- **`chatbotService.createChatSession`** → logs `{ source: 'emma_session', eventType: 'engagement.emma_session', sourceRecordId: 'emma-session-<sessionId>' }`. Skipped for admin delegate access so "as a user" impersonation doesn't pollute the real user's engagement signal.

Both hooks live in a new `crmSignalHooks.ts` service so per-source payload shape and error handling are in one place. Errors are swallowed inside the hook (sync pipeline failures must never break signup or chat).

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npm test -- crmSignalHooks`
2. **Expected**: 9 tests pass (onUserSignup, onEmmaSessionStart variants)
3. Start backend dev server
4. Register a new user via `POST /api/auth/register` or OAuth
5. **Expected**: backend logs show the signup hook firing (`contactEventsDb.logEvent` with `source='signup'`). An entry appears in `Dev-AW-ContactEvents` with `contactId = <lowered-email>`, `sourceRecordId = 'user-<userId>'`.
6. Open Emma chat as a regular user
7. **Expected**: a second event with `eventType='engagement.emma_session'` on the same `contactId`.
8. Replay the same Emma session (same sessionId) — only one event in the log (dedup via contactSyncService).

## Edge cases to check
- Admin delegate sessions do NOT log an engagement event (behaves like the existing `lastActiveAt` gate).
- Missing email on createUser is impossible (schema requires it) but `onUserSignup` still no-ops gracefully if email is empty.
- Same user registering twice: second `createUser` fails the DynamoDB `ConditionExpression`, so the hook never fires.

title: feat(crm): B3 — Stripe webhook -> AW-ContactEvents sync
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Stripe billing events updated `AW-Users` and `payment-history` but never flowed into `AW-ContactEvents`. The CRM lifecycle service (C3) can't transition a contact to `paying` / `at_risk` / `churned` without seeing `payment.*` events, so churn risk and MRR-tied lifecycle were dead.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds a fire-and-forget CRM mirror inside `stripeController.handleWebhook`:

- After the primary handler runs (`handleCheckoutSessionCompleted`, `handleSubscriptionUpdated`, etc.), every event is passed to `onStripeSubscriptionEvent` → `contactSyncService.syncContact`.
- **Idempotent** on the Stripe event id (`sourceRecordId = 'stripe-<eventId>'`) so Stripe's at-least-once delivery is safe — replays short-circuit in `contactSyncService`.
- **Identity resolution**: prefers `customer_details.email` from the event; falls back to `findUserByStripeCustomerId` + user.email.
- **Event type mapping**:
  | Stripe event | Contact event type |
  |---|---|
  | `customer.subscription.created` / `checkout.session.completed` | `payment.subscribed` |
  | `customer.subscription.deleted` | `payment.canceled` |
  | `customer.subscription.updated` / `invoice.payment_*` | `payment.updated` |
- **Never blocks Stripe**: runs as `void sendStripeEventToCrm(event)`, and the hook itself swallows all errors. Webhook ack latency unaffected.

Lifecycle + health recompute is deliberately deferred to D2. Both services require a `loadSignals` fetcher bound to AW-Leads — once D2 ships that loader, `contactSyncService` will recompute uniformly for every source (not just Stripe), which is the correct architectural boundary.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npm test -- crmSignalHooks`
2. **Expected**: 15 tests pass (9 B2 + 6 new Stripe path tests)
3. Start backend dev server with Stripe CLI forwarding: `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3001/api/stripe/webhook`
4. Trigger a test event: `stripe trigger customer.subscription.updated`
5. **Expected**: backend logs show `[stripe->crm]` activity; `Dev-AW-ContactEvents` has a new row with `source='stripe'`, `eventType='payment.updated'`, `sourceRecordId='stripe-evt_<id>'`.
6. Replay the same event (`stripe events resend <evt_id>`).
7. **Expected**: no new row — `contactSyncService.findBySourceRecordId` short-circuits.
8. Trigger `stripe trigger customer.subscription.deleted`
9. **Expected**: new row with `eventType='payment.canceled'`.

## Edge cases to check
- Event with no email and no matching user → logs a warning, does not crash the webhook (returns `{ received: true }` anyway)
- Stripe's 3-day retry window → idempotent sync means multiple retries produce exactly one ContactEvent row
- `customer.subscription.deleted` followed by `customer.subscription.created` on a cheaper plan → two distinct events, both logged

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 15 passed, 0 failed (crmSignalHooks)
- Typecheck: clean on changed files

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/crmSignalHooks.ts` (+onStripeSubscriptionEvent)
- `backend/src/services/__tests__/crmSignalHooks.test.ts` (+6 Stripe tests)
- `backend/src/controllers/stripeController.ts` (wire `sendStripeEventToCrm` into webhook switch)

## What was NOT tested
- Live `stripe trigger` against the test env — no infra changes here, B1 already validated the write path
- Lifecycle/health recompute — gated on D2's signal loader, not this PR

- Backend prereq: #1140 (B1 sync endpoint) — merged

- Fix: route passes `req.user.isAdmin` (already correctly set by auth middleware from the server-minted `_svc` token) to the service, bypassing the redundant DB lookup

The full auth chain was working correctly — `mcpFetch` mints a `_svc` JWT with `isAdmin: true` when `isDelegatedAccess` is true, and `auth.ts` middleware correctly trusts `_svc` token claims. The only broken link was the service-level DB re-check.

This is not a security issue: `callerIsAdmin` comes from `req.user.isAdmin` on the server, derived from the server-minted JWT — it is not controllable by Emma or the LLM.

title: feat(crm): auto-enroll signups into founders@ AgentWeb Signups list
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Every new AgentWeb signup wrote an event to `AW-ContactEvents`, but nothing ever enrolled that signup as a **Lead** in a visible CRM list. Emma (and the founders sales loop) had no automatic view of new signups — you had to CSV-import them by hand. In parallel, `Lead` / `ContactEvent` rows had no `tenantId`, so the upcoming multi-tenant Epic would have needed a schema migration on all 17k existing leads.

## What this fixes (after)
1. **Auto-enrol**: On every platform signup (source=`signup`, eventType=`contact.created`), we create (or reuse) a system-managed list named **"AgentWeb Signups"** owned by `founders@agentweb.pro` and drop the signup in as a lead row.
2. **Multi-tenant primitive**: `tenantId` now threads through `ContactEvent`, `Lead`, and `SyncInput`. Today it's always `founders@`. When the next-sprint Epic ships, turning on tenant-scoped CRM is a one-line change — no DynamoDB migration needed.
3. **Idempotent**: Second signup with the same email is a no-op (logs, skips). Deduplicated events skip auto-enrol entirely.
4. **Scoped**: Only platform-scoped signups enrol into the founders list. Tenant-scoped signups (future) do NOT spill over.
5. **Never breaks signup**: Every error path in the auto-enrol service is swallowed and logged. Signup latency + reliability unaffected.
6. **Backfill script**: `backend/scripts/backfill-tenantId.ts` sets `tenantId` = list owner on every existing lead. Dry-run by default, `--apply` to write. NOT run in CI.

## How to test

### Unit (automated)
1. `cd backend && npm run test:run`
2. **Expected**: All 104 tests in the touched suites pass (`contactEventsDb`, `contactSyncService`, `crmSignalHooks`, `leadSchema`, new `signupAutoEnrollService`).
3. Full suite: 6087/6087 ran tests pass. 40 suites fail with pre-existing `@google-cloud/text-to-speech` import errors — unrelated to this PR (confirmed by stashing + re-running on unmodified `harsha/dev`).

### Manual (test env, once merged)
1. Register a new user via the customer portal signup page (use a fresh email, e.g. `signup-test-$(date +%s)@example.com`).
2. **Expected**: Signup completes normally (no visible latency hit, no error toast).
3. Log in as admin (`ruiwangwarm@gmail.com`), navigate to the CRM for the `founders@agentweb.pro` account.
4. **Expected**: A list named "AgentWeb Signups" exists. The new email appears as a lead with `lifecycle=signed_up`, `tenantId=be754b6c-767e-44ec-b181-4042cfe45ea9`.
5. Register a second user with the SAME email (should fail signup, but just to test idempotency, re-fire the CRM hook): no duplicate row.
6. Inspect `Dev-AW-ContactEvents` for the new event — `tenantId` is unset (platform-scoped signup = no tenantId).

### Edge cases to check
- OAuth signups (Google, LinkedIn) still enrol — `isOAuthUser` flows through the same `onUserSignup` hook.
- If the founders list doesn't exist yet on first-ever signup, the service creates it with `isSystemManaged: true` and `listType: 'customers'`.
- DynamoDB outage during auto-enrol: signup still succeeds, error is logged, event is still written to `AW-ContactEvents`.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: **104 passed, 0 failed** across the 5 touched suites.
  - `signupAutoEnrollService.test.ts`: 9 new tests (create list, reuse list, idempotency, non-signup skip, dedup skip, tenant scoping, explicit founders tenantId, missing email, error swallow).
  - `contactSyncService.test.ts`: 4 new tests (tenantId propagation + 3 auto-enroll hook tests).
- Full backend suite: 6087/6087 ran tests pass. 40 pre-existing suite failures (missing `@google-cloud/*` deps) — unrelated and present on base `harsha/dev`.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/signupAutoEnrollService.ts` (new, 167 lines)
- `backend/src/services/contactSyncService.ts` (tenantId on SyncInput, autoEnroll dep, lazy-require hook)
- `backend/src/services/contactEventsDb.ts` (tenantId on ContactEvent + LogEventInput)
- `backend/src/services/db.ts` (tenantId on createLead, isSystemManaged on createLeadList)
- `backend/src/utils/leadSchema.ts` (tenantId on LeadCrmExtensions + buildLeadCrmFields)
- `backend/src/services/__tests__/signupAutoEnrollService.test.ts` (new, 9 tests)
- `backend/src/services/__tests__/contactSyncService.test.ts` (+4 tests, jest.mock for autoEnroll)
- `backend/scripts/backfill-tenantId.ts` (new, one-shot backfill, dry-run default)

## What was NOT tested
- Live DynamoDB write against Dev-AW-* tables — only unit-tested with stubs. Watchdog will redeploy to test env post-merge; verify manually per the steps above.
- Cross-region behaviour (backfill script assumes `us-west-2` via env or default).
- Scale: the founders list will grow unbounded as signups accrue. Not a problem today; monitor.

## Related PRs
- Backend: standalone (this PR)
- Customer Portal: standalone — no UI changes, list appears in existing CRM page

## Notion task
https://www.notion.so/34309247c95181ab8f61c0c651fc1cf3

## Rollback plan
Single `git revert` on `harsha/dev`. No data-loss risk — all writes are additive (new leads, new list, new optional field). The `AgentWeb Signups` list and its leads can be left in place after revert, or deleted via the CRM UI.

## What was wrong (before)

body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The /crm Inbox tab dedupes ~5000 leads by email CLIENT-SIDE. On founders@'s 5015 leads across 23 lists, the tab fetches each list sequentially (cap 500/list) then groups by email in JavaScript. Load time: 30-90s. Reviewer flagged this on PR #535 as a known follow-up.

## What this fixes (after)
New backend endpoint `GET /api/crm/contacts` groups by lowercased email server-side and returns the exact `InboxLead` shape the frontend already expects. Fan-out across lists is parallel. Expected load on the same account: <1s.

Frontend wiring lands in a separate customer-portal PR so this can ship independently; frontend has a fallback path to the legacy per-list fetch if the endpoint isn't available.

## How to test

### Backend unit tests
1. `cd backend && npm test -- --testPathPattern="contactDedupService|crm.contacts"`
2. **Expected**: 15 new tests pass (9 service + 7 route), plus the 26 neighbour tests in `crm.contactStatus` also still green. Total 41 passed.

### Manual curl test (test env, admin-any user with sales lists)
1. Grab a JWT for `test@example.com` via `/api/auth/login`.
2. `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://<test-env>/api/crm/contacts?listType=sales&limit=50`
3. **Expected**: JSON response `{ contacts: [...], total, rawCount, listsCount, durationMs }` with `durationMs < 1500` for typical accounts. Each contact has `email` lowercased, `lists` populated with each list the email appears in, `primaryLead` set, `heatScore` 0-10.
4. Invalid listType: `curl ...?listType=bogus` -> **Expected**: 400.
5. Invalid sort: `curl ...?sort=abc` -> **Expected**: 400.
6. No auth: `curl ...` without bearer -> **Expected**: 401 (blocked by `authenticateToken` middleware).

## Edge cases to check
- User with **zero** sales lists: returns `{ contacts: [], total: 0, listsCount: 0 }`.
- User with one corrupt list that throws on getLeadsByListId: still returns a useful response with the healthy lists (the service swallows per-list errors and logs).

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 41 passed, 0 failed (new + neighbours).
- Tested as: backend-only. Frontend integration lands in paired customer-portal PR.

`remapFilesForSubPage` now accepts optional `pageMetadata` (name + description) and, when remapping `app/page.tsx` to `app/<slug>/page.tsx`, injects (or replaces) a Next.js `metadata` export that sets `title` from the page name and `description` from the prompt. Sub-pages now ship with their own `<title>`. Client components are left alone since they cannot export metadata.

2. Generate a second landing page via Emma with a clearly different name, e.g. "Black Friday Promo".
3. Wait for the Vercel build to complete and open the newly deployed sub-page (e.g. `https://<project>.vercel.app/black-friday-promo`).
4. **Expected**: the browser tab title and `<head><title>` show "Black Friday Promo" — not the root layout's original title (e.g. not the xCures/HIMSS one).
5. View page source (`view-source:`) and confirm the `<title>` tag reflects the new page's name.

cd backend
npm test -- services.v0Service.test.ts -t "remapFilesForSubPage|injectPageMetadata"
```
Expected: 14 passed.

title: fix: landing page <title> inherits stale 'xCures | HIMSS 2026' on every new page
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Every landing page Emma generated for a user rendered the same hardcoded `<title>` — e.g. `xCures® | HIMSS 2026 Digital Resource Package` — regardless of the actual page content. The stale title came from the root `app/layout.tsx` of the user's first-ever generation, and because `remapFilesForSubPage` intentionally skips `app/layout.tsx` for sub-pages (they share the root layout), the stale `<title>` leaked into every subsequent page.

## What this fixes (after)
New helper `ensurePageMetadataTitle(content, title)` injects (or rewrites) a Next.js App Router `export const metadata = { title }` on the remapped `app/<slug>/page.tsx`. Next.js resolves page-level metadata over layout metadata, so the rendered `<title>` now reflects the actual page name. Handles: existing metadata objects (rewrites the title field), typed metadata (`: Metadata`), template-literal titles, `'use client'` directives, and quote-escaping.

## How to test
1. In the customer portal, log in as a user who already has at least one generated landing page (e.g. `agentwebintegration@xcures.com` or any test account whose repo's `app/layout.tsx` has a hardcoded `<title>`).
2. Ask Emma to generate a new landing page ("create a landing page for X").
3. Wait for the generation + deploy to finish. Open the deployed URL.
4. **Expected**: browser tab shows the NEW page's title (or, worst-case, the Next.js default). It must NOT show `xCures® | HIMSS 2026 Digital Resource Package` or whatever the old layout title was.
5. View source of the deployed page.
6. **Expected**: `<title>` reflects the new page name (from `export const metadata` on the page).
7. Repeat for a user on their FIRST generation — confirm nothing about first-page behaviour regressed (first page still renders; the metadata injection is a no-op if no sub-page is created).

## Edge cases to check
- A v0-generated `page.tsx` that already contains `export const metadata = { title: "…" }` — verify the title is rewritten in place, not duplicated (covered by unit test).
- Titles containing double quotes — escaped via `\"` (covered).

## Test Evidence
- `src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts`: 63 passed, 0 failed (including 5 new metadata-injection tests on `remapFilesForSubPage` and 7 new tests on `ensurePageMetadataTitle`)
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean

- `backend/src/services/v0Service.ts` (+65, new helper + remap integration)
- `backend/src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts` (+115, 12 new tests)

## What was NOT tested
- End-to-end Playwright run against a live Emma generation — Playwright is QA's exclusive resource this cycle. The fix is unit-tested at the remap/metadata-injection boundary, which is where the bug lives.
- Did NOT attempt to also rewrite the root `app/layout.tsx` on first-page generation. Scoped fix to what the customer reported (sub-pages inheriting stale title); if v0 itself emits a bad title on first generation that's a separate issue.

title: fix: circuit breaker and dead client eviction for MCP Brave Search timeouts
body:
## Summary

- **Circuit breaker in `McpClientService`**: after 3 consecutive connection failures within a 5-min window, subsequent calls fail immediately with a clear \"service temporarily unavailable\" message instead of spawning a new npx subprocess and waiting 15s each time. Circuit auto-resets on first successful connection.
- **Dead client eviction**: when `callTool()` throws a connection-level error on a pooled client, the dead client is removed from the session pool so the next call reconnects cleanly instead of reusing a broken client.
- **Improved LLM error message in `formatToolError()`**: connection timeout errors now include a \"do NOT retry\" directive, preventing the LLM from cycling through all 5 Brave search tool variants when the service is unreachable.

**Root cause of the reported issue** (William Liu, session `01769494-4b78-484f-944c-5409925cdc33`, April 16 2026): Brave Search runs as a stdio subprocess (`npx -y @brave/brave-search-mcp-server`). When the npx spawn timed out at 15s, there was no circuit breaker, so the LLM retried all 5 variants × 15s = 75+ seconds of spinning before giving up. The vague \"Adjust the plan\" error message actively encouraged the LLM to try other variants.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test -- --testPathPattern="mcp.mcpClientService"` — 43 tests pass, including 4 new tests for circuit breaker state transitions and dead client eviction
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` — TypeScript compiles cleanly
- [ ] Manual browser tests (session `e449aca4-4ebe-47e1-831f-28e23851b7cf`):
  - `bravesearch_brave_web_search` — worked, returned results

title: fix: prevent duplicate LinkedIn comments

## Summary
- Before posting a comment, the agent now calls `getComments()` on the post and checks if the actor's URN already appears

body:
## Root cause

The previous fixes added a filter in the browser's \`unhandledrejection\` handler (\`main.tsx\`), but \`/api/errors/report\` is **unauthenticated**. Bots or scanners can POST bare payloads that completely bypass the frontend filter.

Confirmed by inspecting today's Notion oncall items (created at 05:32 and 19:04 UTC, both after the April 25 fix deployed): they contained **no \`url\`, \`stack\`, or \`userAgent\` fields** — fields that the real browser reporter always includes. This proves the requests never went through a browser.

## Fix

Added a server-side guard in \`backend/src/routes/errors.ts\` that drops \`"Failed to fetch"\` before reaching \`reportUIError\`, regardless of how the request was sent.

title: harshit/ external CRM sync - HubSpot and Attio support
body:
## Summary

This PR implements full external CRM sync support for HubSpot and Attio, enabling users to connect their AgentWeb lead lists to external CRM systems and keep records synchronized in real-time via webhooks.

### What's Included

- **CRM Adapter Pattern** (`services/adapters/`): Unified adapter interface for HubSpot and Attio, making it easy to add new CRM providers in the future
- **HubSpot Integration** (`services/hubspotService.ts`, `routes/hubspotAuth.ts`): Full OAuth flow, contact create/update/upsert, property management, and webhook subscription handling
- **Attio Integration** (`services/attioService.ts`, `routes/attioAuth.ts`): Full OAuth flow, record create/update/upsert, attribute management, and webhook event handling
- **External CRM Sync Service** (`services/externalCrmSyncService.ts`): Orchestrates bidirectional sync between AgentWeb leads and external CRM records, with per-field mapping support
- **Per-List CRM Webhook Endpoint** (`routes/crmWebhook.ts`): Dedicated webhook endpoint per lead list for receiving real-time updates from HubSpot/Attio
- **CRM Sync Routes** (`routes/crmSync.ts`): REST API for configuring CRM sync settings, field mappings, and toggling webhook sync on/off
- **Lead List Database Storage**: Migrated CRM sync configuration from settings service to lead list DynamoDB records for proper data locality
- **Provider Locking**: Prevents multiple CRM providers from being configured on a single lead list to avoid conflicts
- **Secrets Manager Integration** (`utils/secretsManager.ts`): Secure OAuth token storage for CRM provider credentials

### Key Design Decisions

- CRM sync config is stored on the lead list record (not user settings) so it travels with the list
- Each lead list gets a unique webhook URL, scoping incoming webhooks to the correct list
- Provider locking at the API level prevents accidental dual-configuration
- Field mappings are user-configurable per list, with sensible defaults for common fields

title: fix(mcp-oauth): gate dev auto-approve, drop dev-user fallback
body:
## Risk: High | Priority: High

Touches the MCP OAuth authorization endpoint. Held for CTO approval per auth/agent-infra policy.

## What was wrong (before)

`/oauth/authorize` had a "dev mode" short-circuit that skipped the customer-portal consent page whenever `NODE_ENV === 'development'`:

- Fires on **staging** (`api-stage.agentweb.pro`) and the cloud test env, not just local dev, because both run with `NODE_ENV=development`.
- The handler has no auth middleware, so `req.user` is always undefined → the code fell back to the literal string `"dev-user"` for `userId`.
- Net effect: any unauthenticated caller on staging or test env can POST `/oauth/register` (public DCR), GET `/oauth/authorize` (auto-approves), POST `/oauth/token` (exchanges the code for a real `mcp:tools` access token). The token is accepted by `/mcp/` server-side.
- The customer portal's consent page (`OAuthAuthorize.tsx`) is **dead code** in those environments — never reached.

Confirmed live today against staging and test env.

## What this fixes (after)

`backend/src/mcp/oauth/oauthRoutes.ts`:

1. Replace `NODE_ENV === 'development'` with an explicit opt-in env flag `MCP_OAUTH_SKIP_CONSENT=true`. Staging and prod don't set it, so they always redirect to the consent page.
2. Drop the `"dev-user"` fallback entirely. The shortcut now uses `getUserFromToken(req)` and requires a real authenticated user. If no user is resolved, the request falls through to the consent page (fail safe, not fail open).
3. Fix is the minimum surface — no other behavior changes.

## How to test

**Automated (new)**
`backend/src/mcp/oauth/__tests__/oauthRoutes.test.ts` adds three cases that lock the fix:
1. Flag unset, valid JWT → consent redirect, no code issued.
2. Flag set, unauthenticated → consent redirect, no code issued (regression guard for anonymous `dev-user` tokens).
3. Flag set, authenticated → 302 to `redirect_uri` with `code`, and `createAuthorizationCode` is called with the real `userId` (explicit assertion that `"dev-user"` is never passed).

Run: `cd backend && npm test -- src/mcp/oauth/__tests__/oauthRoutes.test.ts`

**Manual (against staging after deploy)**
1. `curl -X POST https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/oauth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"client_name":"probe","redirect_uris":["https://httpbin.org/get"],"scope":"mcp:tools"}'` — grab the `client_id`.
2. `curl -i "https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<id>&redirect_uri=https://httpbin.org/get&scope=mcp:tools&code_challenge=j5vsamLdKOvTbRIndFWS3mZYs2l0o7uYpMWC9oPqbEI&code_challenge_method=S256&state=s1"`
   - **Expected after fix:** 302 to `https://app.agentweb.pro/oauth/authorize?...` (customer portal consent page).
   - **Before fix:** 302 directly to `https://httpbin.org/get?code=...&state=s1` (consent bypassed).
3. Repeat against prod — should be unchanged (already redirects to consent).

## Edge cases to check

- A developer running backend locally with `MCP_OAUTH_SKIP_CONSENT=true` AND a valid Authorization header → still gets instant approval, tied to their real `userId`. (The shortcut still works for its intended use case.)
- Flag set but JWT is expired or invalid → falls through to consent page rather than 401ing, so MCP clients don't see a breaking change.

## Test Evidence

- Type-check: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (exit 0)
- Unit tests: added 3 new cases (existing 4 GET /oauth/authorize tests preserved). Running locally is blocked by a pre-existing Node 23 / jest package-config issue in the backend repo; CI will execute them.
- Manual live test: root cause reproduced against staging + test env before the fix. Prod verified already correct.

## Files changed

- `backend/src/mcp/oauth/oauthRoutes.ts` — the fix
- `backend/src/mcp/oauth/__tests__/oauthRoutes.test.ts` — regression tests

## What was NOT tested

- No end-to-end test with a real MCP client (Claude.ai, mcp-inspector). The unit tests cover the server-side contract, but a real client round-trip was not re-run post-fix.
- No load or rate-limit testing of `/oauth/register` — the public DCR endpoint remains unchanged. If spam registration is a concern, file a follow-up.
- No change to the `POST /oauth/authorize/decision` path; that flow (consent form submit) was already gated behind `authenticateToken` via `authFromBodyOrHeader` and is unchanged.

`git revert <merge-commit>` on `harsha/dev`. No DB migrations, no env schema changes — setting `MCP_OAUTH_SKIP_CONSENT=true` is opt-in and defaulting to unset matches prior prod behavior.

title: fix: Meta ad account connection fails across load-balanced instances
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause:** Meta OAuth token sessions were stored in an in-process `Map` on each backend instance. With 2 EB instances behind the load balancer, `/finalize` (which stores the session) and `/connect-ad-accounts` (which reads it) could land on different instances — causing "Invalid or expired token session" errors.
- **Fix:** Replaced the in-memory Map with a DynamoDB table (`AW-OAuthSessions`) with a 10-minute TTL. All instances now read/write from the same shared store.
- **Also:** Improved error logging in `getAdAccounts` — failures (e.g. missing `ads_management` permission) are now logged with error code and classification instead of being silently swallowed.

## Test plan

- [ ] DynamoDB round-trip (write → read → delete) confirmed working

Run `NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node src/scripts/create-tables.ts` once after deploy, or create the `AW-OAuthSessions` table in the prod AWS account manually. The table is simple: hash key `sessionId` (String), PAY_PER_REQUEST billing, TTL on the `ttl` attribute.

title: feat(onboarding): Phase 1 — persist onboarding events + derived stage
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The onboarding flow (`OnboardingV2.tsx`) emits `goal_selected` / `brand_submitted` / `data_connected` / etc. events to `localStorage` only. `POST /api/onboarding/events` returns 404 and the server has no idea where a user is in onboarding. The Lifecycle Drip epic can't segment users by stage because the stage doesn't exist server-side.

## What this fixes (after)
Phase 1 of the Lifecycle Drip epic. Makes those events persist on the User record and exposes a derived `onboardingStage` field so Emma, the admin UI, and the drip campaign engine can segment users by where they are in onboarding.

New endpoints:
- `POST /api/onboarding/events` — append `{event, ts, data?}` to the caller's event log. Validates event name, caps payload at 2KB, caps log at 50 events (FIFO drop), recomputes `onboardingStage` on every append.
- `GET /api/onboarding/events/me` — read the caller's event log + current derived stage.
- `GET /api/onboarding/users?stage=<stage>` — admin-only segmentation endpoint used by Emma and the drip UI.

Derived stage (pure function in `utils/onboardingStage.ts`, no DB dep):
`signed_up_no_start` → `goal_selected` → `brand_submitted | brand_skipped` → `data_connected` → `channel_connected` → `onboarding_completed` → `active | stale` (no activity for 30+ days).

## How to test
1. Sign in to the test env as `test1@example.com` / `Test123!`.
2. Grab the JWT from localStorage (`authToken`) and hit:
   ```
   curl -X POST http://<test-env>/api/onboarding/events \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"event": "goal_selected", "data": {"goal": "paid_ads"}}'
   ```
   **Expected**: `200 { onboardingStage: "goal_selected", eventCount: 1, recorded: {...} }`
3. Hit `GET /api/onboarding/events/me` with the same token.
   **Expected**: the event you just recorded appears in the log and `onboardingStage` is `goal_selected`.
4. POST another event: `{"event": "brand_submitted", "data": {"companyName": "Acme"}}`.
   **Expected**: `onboardingStage` flips to `brand_submitted`, `eventCount` is 2.
5. POST `{"event": "onboarding_completed"}`.
   **Expected**: `onboardingStage` is `active` (because the user just logged in, `lastActiveAt` is fresh) or `onboarding_completed` if the user has no `lastActiveAt`.
6. Log in as admin (`ruiwangwarm@gmail.com` / `12345678`) and hit:
   ```
   curl http://<test-env>/api/onboarding/users?stage=goal_selected \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>"
   ```
   **Expected**: 200 with `{ stage: "goal_selected", count: N, users: [...] }` listing every user currently at that stage.
7. Try the same endpoint as `test1@example.com`. **Expected**: `403 Forbidden`.
8. POST an invalid event: `{"event": "totally_made_up"}`. **Expected**: `400 { message: "Unknown event: totally_made_up" }`.

## Edge cases to check
- Rapid duplicate events (same user, same event name within 1s) — they should all be appended; no dedup.
- A user's `onboardingEvents` array being populated via direct DynamoDB write (simulating migration) before any POST — `GET /me` should still derive the correct stage.
- The 50-event cap: spam 60 events and confirm the first 10 get dropped FIFO.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: **38 new, 0 failed** (17 for the derivation util, 21 for the HTTP routes).
- Full backend suite: **7092 passed, 1 pre-existing failure** unrelated to this PR (`crmBackfill.test.ts` — confirmed failing on clean `harsha/dev` without my changes; belongs to the CRM Backfill sprint task).
- Tested as: mocked `userDb` (no DynamoDB writes during tests). Real end-to-end verification will happen in QA against the test env.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/utils/onboardingStage.ts` — new pure stage-derivation util
- `backend/src/utils/__tests__/onboardingStage.test.ts` — 17 tests
- `backend/src/routes/onboardingEvents.ts` — new router (3 endpoints)
- `backend/src/routes/__tests__/onboardingEvents.test.ts` — 21 tests
- `backend/src/services/db.ts` — add `onboardingEvents` + `onboardingStage` fields to the `User` interface
- `backend/src/app.ts` — mount the new router at `/api/onboarding`

## What was NOT tested
- **Real DynamoDB writes.** All tests mock `userDb`. QA will exercise the real path against the test env's `Dev-AW-Users` table.
- **High-concurrency appends.** If two devices POST two events in the same millisecond, Dynamo's read-modify-write here is last-writer-wins for the events array. Acceptable for Phase 1 (onboarding is single-device in practice); add an atomic `list_append` update expression in Phase 2 if it becomes a real problem.
- **Frontend integration.** `OnboardingV2.tsx` still writes to localStorage only. Wiring the client to also POST here is a follow-up PR (intentionally kept out of scope — task description says Phase 1 is "backend signal persistence" and the frontend tracker already exists).
- **Stale detection on users who never hit the endpoint.** `stale` only triggers for users with `onboarding_completed` in their log. Users who never completed onboarding don't get a `stale` stage even if they've been dormant for months. Phase 2 can add a cron job to re-derive stages daily.
- **GSI on `onboardingStage`.** The admin list endpoint does a full scan. Fine for today's ~5k user base; add a GSI if it gets hot.

## Related PRs
- Backend: this PR, standalone
- Customer Portal: follow-up needed to POST from `OnboardingV2.tsx` instead of just localStorage
