title: fix(onboarding): GET /icp/status uses strong-consistent base-table read
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Companion to [PR #1355](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/1355). #1355 fixed the IMMEDIATE response of POST \`/icp/regenerate-one\` to bypass the eventually-consistent \`UserIdIndex\` GSI by returning the start patch directly. But the FE polling hook continues hitting GET \`/icp/status\` afterward, which **still** queried the GSI — so the first poll after the regen could still return the stale pre-update row (\`icpStatus='ready'\` + old \`icpResult\`), causing the polling hook to terminate before the LLM finished.

Verified during the **2026-04-27 Maya verification run** ([Notion sub-task](https://www.notion.so/34e09247c951817e9aaffff6cd5bbc40)): #1355's POST response was correct (status='running'), but Maya still got stuck because the very next status poll hit a stale GSI read returning 'ready', which the FE polling hook treats as terminal.

## What this fixes (after)
GET \`/icp/status\` now reads by email (the base table's primary key) with \`ConsistentRead=true\`. No GSI propagation lag, no stale reads.

Adds new helper \`userDb.getUserByEmailConsistent(email)\` for any other route that needs a strong-consistent read after a write in the same request flow.

With this in place: after the regen POST, polling sees \`status='running'\` until the LLM persists fresh ICPs (~30-60s), then \`'ready'\` with new content — at which point the FE's content-aware useEffect (from FE PR #675) clears the regen flag and the new card renders.

## How to test
1. Sign up new test user on \`http://34.222.47.141:5174\`, walk to icpReview screen
2. Click "Regenerate this one" on any ICP card
3. Open DevTools → Network tab
4. **Expected**: \`POST /api/onboarding/icp/regenerate-one\` → 200 (status='running'), then \`GET /api/onboarding/icp/status\` polls every ~1500ms returning \`status: 'running'\` for ~30-60s
5. After ~30-60s, polling returns \`status: 'ready'\` with new icpResult
6. **Expected**: stall swaps back to a fresh ICP card with new content (was: stuck forever)

## Edge cases to check
- Initial /icp/start path (POST then poll) — also benefits from the consistent read; first poll after the start sees 'running' immediately
- Auth middleware sets req.user.email correctly for delegated tokens too — verified via existing tests

## Test Evidence
- 46 passed, 0 failed across onboardingSteps + onboardingBrandReview suites
- New test: \"uses strong-consistent base-table read, NOT the eventually-consistent GSI\". Mocks BOTH a stale getUserById and a fresh getUserByEmailConsistent; asserts the route returns the consistent value AND never touches the GSI. Verified failing on old code, passing on new code.
- \`npx tsc --noEmit\` clean

## Files changed
- \`backend/src/services/db.ts\` (+26 — new \`getUserByEmailConsistent\` method)
- \`backend/src/routes/onboardingSteps.ts\` (+24/-3 — new requireUserEmail helper, /icp/status uses it)
- \`backend/src/__tests__/onboardingSteps.test.ts\` (+32/-3 — updated 3 existing /icp/status tests + added new differential test)

## What was NOT tested
- Live test env walkthrough — recommended before merging the next mega PR. Maya verification rerun confirms the fix end-to-end.
- Other 4 GET /*/status routes (\`competitor\`, \`creative-dir\`, \`ad-image\`, \`ad-copy\`, plus brand-build) have the same bug shape. Aligning them is a follow-up — kept this PR scoped to the immediate Maya fix.

## Related PRs
- Backend: \`#1355\` already merged (POST response fix)
- Customer Portal: \`#675\` already merged (FE content-aware regen-clear)

Together: #675 + #1355 + this PR fully close the Maya regen-spinner-stuck bug. Each PR fixes a different layer of the same root cause (GSI eventual consistency).

title: revert: PR #1344 maxRetries cap (regression observed across 6 persona runs)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
PR #1344 set DynamoDB DocumentClient `maxRetries: 3` (vs SDK default 10) under the hypothesis that throttled GSI queries were burning ~10s of exponential backoff and showing up as the 9s adImage poll outliers in Tom's pre-fix baseline.

Across **6 persona runs** on 2026-04-27 post-fix (Maya, Tom×2, Sam, Riley, Jordan), ad-image/status polls now show **65-86s outliers** — 7-9x WORSE than the 9s pre-fix observation. Same shape (always 2-4 polls back-to-back at end of ad-image step), reproduced across multiple personas, not env noise.

The original retry-exhaustion hypothesis doesn't fit the data. Either the slowness was always per-attempt-slow (sync S3 / image-gen / auth-middleware double-read) and the higher retry budget masked it, or maxRetries=3 is starving a legitimately-slow case.

## What this fixes (after)
Pure revert to SDK default. Returns to known-good baseline (the 9s outliers from yesterday were still there but 7-9x smaller than today's regression).

The actual root cause of the 9s outliers is the **duplicate `getUserById` call in auth middleware → route handler** (every authed request reads the user twice via the eventually-consistent `UserIdIndex` GSI). That fix lives in [Notion task 34e09247…0867a13](https://www.notion.so/34e09247c95181cf96a5c0fb00867a13) and needs CTO review per the global auth-touching rule. Shipping that fix is the proper resolution; #1344 was a speculative shortcut that didn't pan out.

## How to test
1. Sync test env, run any onboarding flow
2. **Expected**: ad-image/status polls return ~100ms baseline, with occasional ~9s outliers (the pre-fix behavior, which is what we want back)
3. **Expected**: NOT seeing 65-86s outliers anymore

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- No tests added/changed — pure config revert. The original PR didn't add tests either (config-only).

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/db.ts` (-7/+1)
- `backend/src/config/aws.ts` (-3/+1)

## What was NOT tested
- Live test env walkthrough — recommended after merge. The next 5-persona rerun will confirm outliers shrink back to ~9s.

## Related
- PR #1344 (this reverts the config change)
- Notion task: dup-getUserById fix (proper root-cause resolution, pending CTO review)

title: feat(onboarding): backend services route errors through reportUIError → Notion oncall pipeline
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
5 onboarding services silently swallowed LLM/orchestration failures in console.error only. When ICP discovery / competitor research / creative-direction / ad-image / ad-copy generation failed mid-onboarding, the user kept seeing a stuck spinner and the team had no signal — no Notion task, no email, nothing.

The rest of the portal already has a closed-loop error pipeline (`reportUIError → createOncallItem → sendOncallAlert`) that creates a Notion oncall task + emails Rui. Onboarding wasn't plugged into it.

## What this fixes (after)
Every catch block that flips a `*Status` field to `failed` now also fires `reportUIError` with structured context (userId, error, stack, step name). The 30-min dedup prevents flooding when the same user retries.

Operations instrumented:

title: feat(onboarding): stuck/abandoned user detector + rich Notion oncall context
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
PR A (companion) routes onboarding errors INTO the existing reportUIError → Notion oncall pipeline. But two gaps remained:

1. **No detection for users who get stuck without an explicit error.** A user idling on `buildingAdImage` for 3 hours never fires anything — no error, just inactivity. We don't know they're stuck until they email us.
2. **Notion oncall task wasn't enough context to investigate.** The task body had the error message + URL, but Rui still had to query DDB by hand to see what stage the user was at, which steps were ready/failed, what events fired before the error.

## What this fixes (after)

**1. `onboardingStuckDetector` cron — runs hourly.**
Scans `userDb.getAllUsers` for users matching:
- Stage NOT in {`onboarding_completed`, `active`}
- Last event > 1h ago (configurable via `ONBOARDING_STUCK_HOURS`) → fires `reportUIError('onboarding:stuck')`
- Stage IS engaged (past `signed_up_no_start`) AND last event > 24h ago (`ONBOARDING_ABANDON_HOURS`) → fires `reportUIError('onboarding:abandoned')` (takes precedence)

The 30-min dedup in errorReporter prevents a hourly cron from flooding the same user.

**2. Rich Notion context for onboarding-tagged ops.**
When `operation.startsWith('onboarding:')`, the Notion task body now includes:
- `User Email` + signup ts
- `Onboarding Stage` (current)
- `Step Status` table — brandBuild / icp / competitor / creativeDir / adImage / adCopy with status + startedAt + completedAt + error each
- `Recent Events (last 20)` — timestamped event log
- `Investigate as User` URL — existing delegate-as-user flow

Enrichment fails open — if `userDb.getUserById` is unreachable, the base Notion task still fires with the original context. Never blocks the alert.

## How to test
1. Manually set a test user's last `onboardingEvents` entry to >1h ago + `onboardingStage='goal_selected'`. Run `runOnboardingStuckDetector()` directly.
2. **Expected**: 1 Notion oncall task fires with operation `onboarding:stuck`, body includes the user's full step status table + last 20 events.
3. Repeat for an engaged stage + 25h-old event. **Expected**: `onboarding:abandoned` (not stuck), takes priority.
4. Re-run within 30 min. **Expected**: dedup kicks in, no second Notion task.

## Edge cases to check
- Users with no events but a recent createdAt → no fire (they just signed up)
- Users where `getUserById` errors during enrichment → original Notion task fires anyway
- 5000+ users in the table → `getAllUsers(true)` filters bot-like emails; cron handles linearly. If user count grows large, swap to a `scan with FilterExpression` follow-up.

## Test Evidence
- 6/6 stuck detector classification + dispatch tests pass
- 13/13 errorReporter tests pass (10 existing + 3 new enrichment cases)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean

## Files changed
- NEW: `backend/src/cron/onboardingStuckDetector.ts` (+144)
- NEW: `backend/src/cron/__tests__/onboardingStuckDetector.test.ts` (+144)
- MODIFIED: `backend/src/utils/errorReporter.ts` (+72) — onboarding enrichment
- MODIFIED: `backend/src/__tests__/utils/errorReporter.test.ts` (+84) — 3 enrichment cases
- MODIFIED: `backend/src/server.ts` (+21) — cron registration alongside existing dripExecutor

## What was NOT tested

- `ONBOARDING_STUCK_HOURS=0.01` short-loop test on test env (set env, restart backend, observe cron tick on a stuck user)

title: fix(onboarding): mirror icpResult + competitorResult to User.marketStrategy
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
After v2 onboarding completed, the main account looked blank — Agent Mode, chatbot, and other product surfaces all read from `User.marketStrategy.icp[]` and `.competitors[]`, but the per-step onboarding services (`onboardingIcpService`, `onboardingCompetitorService`) wrote ONLY to `User.icpResult` / `User.competitorResult` and never mirrored over.

User finished onboarding seeing 5 ICPs on the review screen, then opened Agent Mode and saw zero ICPs. Same for competitors.

## Why this fix and not 'modify the brand-build prompt'
The existing `onboardingBrandBuildService.ts:100-105` comment is explicit — combining brand DNA + ICP + competitor into a single Emma session was unreliable: "Emma frequently produced a brand but failed to populate marketStrategy.icp / .competitors before exiting." The intentional split is brand-build → its own session, ICP/competitor → focused per-step LLM calls. This PR keeps that split and adds a deterministic backfill at the end of each per-step service.

## What this fixes (after)
Each service gains:
1. **A pure mapper** (`mapIcpResultToMarketStrategy`, `mapCompetitorResultToMarketStrategy`) — exported, fully unit-tested
2. **A read-merge-write helper** (`mirrorIcpsToMarketStrategy`, `mirrorCompetitorsToMarketStrategy`) — preserves existing `businessOverview` / `competitors` / `icp` when writing
3. **A call** to the helper after the readyPatch lands

Best-effort by design: errors in the mirror step are logged but do NOT roll back the readyPatch — onboarding still works, the mirror is a separate failure mode that just retries next run. The ICP mapper inverts the existing `mapMarketIcpToResult` in `onboardingBrandBuildService`.

## How to test
1. Sign up new test user, complete onboarding through icpReview + valuePropReview
2. Open Agent Mode (or any product surface that reads marketStrategy)
3. **Expected**: ICPs from onboarding visible in Agent Mode (was: empty)
4. Same for competitors after the cascade fires (`competitorReadyPatch` → mirror)
5. Refresh user record via DDB scan: `User.marketStrategy.icp[]` populated with the 5 personas, `competitors[]` populated with deduped names

## Edge cases to check
- User in an org → mirror writes to `User.marketStrategy` (per-user). Org-level marketStrategy unchanged. (`agentModeService.updateMarketStrategy` would gate on org ownership; we use direct userDb write to bypass that — onboarding output is per-user.)
- Existing marketStrategy with competitors but no icp → mirror adds icp, preserves competitors
- User disappears between readyPatch + mirror read → mirror exits silently (logged), readyPatch stands

## Test Evidence
- 36/36 onboardingIcpService tests pass (8 new for mapper + integration mirror behavior)
- 37/37 onboardingCompetitorService tests pass (5 new)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/onboardingIcpService.ts` (+91): `mapIcpResultToMarketStrategy` (exported helper) + `mirrorIcpsToMarketStrategy` (private) + 1-line wire after readyPatch
- `backend/src/services/onboardingCompetitorService.ts` (+96): same pattern, with cross-ICP competitor dedup
- `backend/src/__tests__/onboardingIcpService.test.ts` (+134): 8 new tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/onboardingCompetitorService.test.ts` (+140): 5 new tests

## What was NOT tested
- Live test env walkthrough — recommended after merge. Easy to verify: complete a fresh onboarding, then `aws dynamodb get-item ...` and confirm `marketStrategy.icp[]` is populated.

## Related

## Mega PR: harsha/dev → main (backend)

## Summary
8 PRs — 4 onboarding fixes, 1 onboarding observability foundation, 1 marketStrategy mirror, 1 attribution enrichment, 1 revert. All passed CI on harsha/dev.

## How to review
Walk the testing plan below. Comment on this PR with `fix #NNN: …` or `revert #NNN`. Anything you don't mention = approved to ship.

---

### PR #1355: icp/start + regenerate-one return start patch instead of stale GSI read
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 2

**What changed**: POST `/api/onboarding/icp/start` and `/api/onboarding/icp/regenerate-one` now respond with the just-written start patch directly, instead of round-tripping through the UserIdIndex GSI which is eventually consistent and was returning the previous (stale) state for ~1-2s.

**How to test**:
1. Already covered end-to-end by the regen-spinner-stuck fix below (#675 frontend). Verify there by triggering an ICP regen and confirming the spinner clears within ~30s.
2. **Expected**: no "ghost in progress" flicker on the review screen anymore.

**Edge case to check**: rapid double-click on Regen — second click should still work (existing dedup logic).

---

### PR #1357: GET /icp/status uses strong-consistent base-table read
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 3

**What changed**: Frontend polling against `GET /api/onboarding/icp/status` now reads the User row directly (strong-consistent) instead of via UserIdIndex GSI. Eliminates a class of "polling sees pre-update row" bugs where the UI never updated despite the backend completion.

**How to test**: same flow as #1355 — confirm regen → ICP refresh propagates to UI within one polling tick.

---

### PR #1365: revert PR #1344 (DDB retry budget cap)
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: revert | **Files**: 1

**What changed**: Reverted the `maxRetries=3` cap from #1344. Persona runs showed ad-image generation outliers JUMPED from 9s → 65-86s after #1344, because some legitimate calls genuinely need >3 retries when AWS Bedrock throttles.

**How to test**: existing benchmarks. ICP/competitor/ad-image latency p50/p95 should match pre-#1344 numbers.

**Edge case to check**: when AWS Bedrock returns 429s, the SDK now uses default 10 retries — confirm we don't see degraded latency in low-traffic windows.

**Note**: #1344 is included in this mega PR (since it's in harsha/dev) but is effectively a no-op because #1365 reverts it. Net effect on `main`: zero retry-cap change.

---

### PR #1370: backend services route errors through reportUIError → Notion oncall pipeline
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: feat | **Files**: 5

**What changed**: Every onboarding backend service (icp / competitor / creativeDir / adImage / adCopy) now calls `reportUIError({ operation: 'onboarding:<step>:llm-generation', ... })` from its catch block. The 30-min dedup window inside `reportUIError` keeps Notion from flooding when a single user hits the same failure repeatedly.

**How to test**:
1. SSH to test env, inject an LLM failure on a test user (e.g., set BEDROCK env to invalid)
2. Trigger `/api/onboarding/icp/start`
3. **Expected**: a Notion task appears in the Sprint Tasks DB tagged `Oncall + UI Error` with `operation: onboarding:icp:llm-generation`. Email also fires to ruiw@agentweb.pro.
4. Trigger again within 30 min → **Expected**: no second Notion task (deduped).

**Edge case to check**: Notion API down → `reportUIError` falls through to email-only without crashing the user request.

---

### PR #1371: stuck/abandoned user detector cron + rich Notion oncall context
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: feat | **Files**: 6 (~+464 lines, includes tests)

**What changed**: New cron `onboardingStuckDetector` runs hourly, scans users with `onboardingStage` set but not completed, and fires `reportUIError('onboarding:stuck' | 'onboarding:abandoned', ...)` for matches. Also extends `errorReporter.enrichOnboardingContext` so onboarding-tagged Notion tasks include user identity, current stage, per-step status table, last 20 onboarding events, and a delegate-as-user URL.

**How to test**:
1. On test env: set a test user's `icpStartedAt` to 10 min ago, leave `icpStatus = running`
2. Manually trigger the cron (or wait for next hourly tick)
3. **Expected**: a Notion task fires titled `UI Error: onboarding:stuck` with the user's full context (email, stage, step status table, events, delegate URL).

**Edge case to check**: a user that abandoned >24h ago should fire `onboarding:abandoned`, not `onboarding:stuck`.

---

### PR #1379: mirror icpResult + competitorResult to User.marketStrategy
**Risk**: Medium | **Type**: fix | **Files**: 3 (~+461 lines, includes tests)

**What changed**: When the per-step services finish ICP / competitor work, they now ALSO write the result into `User.marketStrategy.icp[]` / `User.marketStrategy.competitors[]`, not just `User.icpResult` / `User.competitorResult`. The rest of the product (Agent Mode, Show page, downstream consumers) reads from `marketStrategy`, so without this mirror the onboarding output was invisible to Emma / the user's main account.

**How to test**:
1. On test env: complete onboarding through ICP + competitor steps for a fresh user
2. Open Agent Mode chat → ask "what are my ICPs?"
3. **Expected**: Emma references the just-generated personas, not "no ICPs found".
4. Open the Show page → **Expected**: ICPs section populated.

**Edge case to check**: a user who had ICPs generated BEFORE this PR (legacy) — they still have only `User.icpResult`, no mirror. Backfill is out of scope; new generations going forward will mirror. Document this caveat.

---

### PR #1380: UTM attribution in Notion oncall context
**Risk**: Low | **Type**: feat | **Files**: 2 (errorReporter + test)

**What changed**: `enrichOnboardingContext` now surfaces `User.firstTouch` / `User.lastTouch` UTM dimensions, referrer, and landing URL on onboarding-tagged Notion tasks. Last-touch source only shown when it differs from first-touch.

title: feat(onboarding): OnboardingPipelineOrchestrator + User.steps schema (Eager DAG sub-task 1)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Onboarding state lives in 6 separate per-axis status fields (icpStatus, competitorStatus, creativeDirStatus, adImageStatus, adCopyStatus, brandBuildStatus) and the services cross-call each other (\`onboardingIcpService\` directly invokes \`startCompetitorStrategyForUser\`, with a \`setTimeout(2000)\` to dodge a GSI propagation race). There is no single source of truth for "what should fire next given current user inputs" — every refactor risks dropping a cascade trigger or duplicating work.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds the foundation for the Phase 2 eager DAG: a pure-logic \`OnboardingPipelineOrchestrator\` service with a declarative DAG, SHA-256 input-hash dedup, a generation counter for cancel-and-replace concurrency, and provenance precedence so user-authored data is never overwritten. \`User.steps\` is an additive optional field on the db schema. Nothing in production behaviour changes in this PR — the orchestrator is gated behind \`EAGER_ONBOARDING_PIPELINE_ENABLED\` (env) and/or \`User.useEagerPipeline\` (per-user) and is not wired to any route or service yet. Sub-task 2 will refactor the existing onboarding services to delegate to this orchestrator.

## What was wrong (before)

## What this fixes (after)

## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
PR #1371's onboarding stuck-detector cron started flooding the Notion oncall view with 100+ duplicate-title tasks per day. Four root causes: (1) `User.onboardingStage` never auto-advances backend-side, so users who finish the pipeline but close the tab stay at e.g. `brand_submitted` forever; (2) the cron has no all-steps-ready short-circuit and no test-account filter; (3) cron-fired tasks land directly in the active sprint via `Move to Current Sprint = true`; (4) every task shares the same `"UI Error: onboarding:stuck"` title so they all collapse on the board.

## What this fixes (after)
1. **Stage auto-advances** — new `markOnboardingCompletedIfTerminal(userId)` helper appends a synthetic `onboarding_completed` event and re-derives the stage when all 6 step statuses are `'ready'`. Wired into all 5 onboarding services + the brand-build hook in `agentModeService`.
2. **Detector ignores all-steps-ready users** and skips emails matching `@agenttest.com`, `@example.com`, or any localpart with `+qa`.
3. **Cron-fired tasks route to Backlog** via a new `routeToBacklog` flag on `createOncallItem` (sets `Move to Current Sprint = false`).
4. **Per-user title format**: `Onboarding stuck: {email} @ {stage} ({h.h}h)` so each user is visually distinct on the sprint board.

## How to test
1. Wait for the next hourly cron tick on prod (`onboardingStuckDetector`).
2. Go to the Notion sprint board → Backlog view filtered by tag `Oncall`.
3. **Expected**: New stuck-detector tasks appear in **Backlog**, not the Current Sprint view. Each task title is `Onboarding stuck: <email> @ <stage> (<h>h)` (no two should share a title for distinct users).
4. Cross-check: visit any user the cron flagged whose 6 step statuses are all `ready` in DynamoDB — confirm NO task fires for that user.
5. As a sanity check, fire `reportUIError` from a non-cron source (any agent-mode failure) and confirm the title still uses `UI Error: <operation>` and the task auto-promotes into the current sprint.

## Edge cases to check
- Existing legacy users with stale stages but all-steps-ready — covered by Bug 2 short-circuit (Bug 1's backfill only fires going forward when a step write happens).
- A real user with a `+qa` somewhere later in their email (e.g. `harsha+qa-batch@startup.io`) — intentional: the planner accepted these are test accounts.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: full backend suite ran — **521 suites passed, 8145 tests passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**.
- New tests:
  - `backend/src/utils/__tests__/onboardingStage.test.ts` — 11 new cases for `markOnboardingCompletedIfTerminal` (happy path, all-no-op branches, missing user, dryad-style errors, FIFO event cap, malformed userId).
  - `backend/src/utils/__tests__/errorReporter.test.ts` (new file) — 14 cases covering cron source detection, per-user title formatting, fallbacks, and dedup interaction.
  - `backend/src/cron/__tests__/onboardingStuckDetector.test.ts` — 8 new cases covering the all-steps-ready short-circuit, test-domain filter (parameterized), and missing-email fallback.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- Tested as: unit only — full live cron run will validate on next prod tick (cron is idempotent + best-effort dedup, low blast radius).

## Files changed
- `backend/src/utils/onboardingStage.ts` (helper added)
- `backend/src/utils/errorReporter.ts` (cron source routing + per-user title)
- `backend/src/services/notionService.ts` (`routeToBacklog` flag)
- `backend/src/cron/onboardingStuckDetector.ts` (steps-ready + test-domain filters)
- `backend/src/services/onboarding{Icp,Competitor,CreativeDir,AdImage,AdCopy}Service.ts` (helper invocation)
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` (helper after brand-build ready patch)
- New + extended tests as listed above

## What was NOT tested
- Live Notion-render of the per-user title format (DEV envs suppress Notion oncall creation; the property body has been verified against the existing data-source schema).
- The interaction with `mirrorOnboardingEventToLead` when the synthetic `onboarding_completed` event is appended via the helper — the helper writes directly to `userDb.updateUser`, not through `routes/onboardingEvents.ts`, so the lead-mirror is intentionally NOT triggered (matches the task's contract: "synthetic event has the right shape", does not say to mirror).

## Related PRs

- Customer Portal: standalone — no FE changes
- Builds on PR #1371

title: fix(onboarding): one daily aggregated stuck-user report instead of per-user flooding
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The hourly `onboardingStuckDetector` cron (PR #1371) fired one `reportUIError` per stuck user per tick, producing 100+ duplicate-title oncall tasks per day in the Notion sprint board. Rui flagged this on Apr 29 and again on Apr 30 (#bug-report) — the volume buried real signal and was assigned to Harsha but couldn't be addressed without a structural change. ftan's correct read: most stuck users are abandonment, not bugs — but real users *are* getting stuck, and silencing the cron entirely loses that signal.

## What this fixes (after)
Replaces the per-user fire-pattern with a **single daily aggregated report**. Real users stuck in the funnel are still surfaced — but as one Notion task per day, grouped by stage, with sample emails per stage and the oldest-stuck duration. Real-time error reporting through `reportUIError` (LLM failures, FE swallows) is unchanged; only the stuck-user observability cron is collapsed.

Concretely:
- `runOnboardingStuckDetector` now returns `DailyStuckReport`: `{ scanned, totalStuck, byStage: { [stage]: { count, sampleEmails, oldestHours } }, notionUrl }`.
- Posts ONE Notion oncall task per run via `createOncallItem`, titled `Onboarding stuck users — daily report YYYY-MM-DD`. Body lists every affected stage in order of severity (count desc, oldest-hours tiebreak), with `Stage: brand_submitted: 17 users (oldest: 28.4h) — a@x.com, b@y.com, ..., +12 more` rows.
- Skips the post entirely on a zero-stuck day (no spam Notion tasks for empty reports).
- Cron interval bumped from `1h` to `24h` in `server.ts`.
- Filters retained from PR #1397: terminal-stage skip, all-six-steps-ready short-circuit, test-domain email filter (`@agenttest.com`, `@example.com`, `+qa` localpart).

## How to test
1. Wait for the next daily cron tick on prod (24h after backend restart, or restart backend to fire ~5min later).
2. Go to Notion sprint board → search title `Onboarding stuck users — daily report`.
3. **Expected**: Exactly one task created for today, with body listing each non-empty stage and its count + sample emails + oldest-stuck hours.
4. Confirm there are no new `UI Error: onboarding:stuck` or `UI Error: onboarding:abandoned` per-user tasks created from this cron path.
5. Verify a recent stuck user (e.g. one of the existing ones in `Backlog` view tagged `Oncall`) appears in the daily report's `Stage: <their stage>` row.
6. As a sanity check, confirm a real onboarding service error (e.g. an LLM failure during `icpService`) still posts its own per-user task via `reportUIError` — that path is untouched.

## Edge cases to check
- A day where no users meet the stuck threshold — confirm NO Notion task is created (not even an empty one).
- A stage with >5 stuck users — sample is capped at 5 and the row shows `+N more`.
- A Notion API outage — detector still returns the report (`notionUrl: null`), no exception bubbles.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: full backend suite ran — **519 suites passed, 8112 tests passed, 1 unrelated flake in `admin.gtmPlans.test.ts` (passes 26/26 in isolation)**.
- New + rewritten tests in `backend/src/cron/__tests__/onboardingStuckDetector.test.ts` — 8 cases covering: zero-stuck → no Notion post, multi-stage grouping with correct counts + oldestHours, sample-cap-at-5 with `+N more` overflow, all-steps-ready short-circuit (regression), test-domain filter (regression), terminal/missing-stage skip, sub-threshold idle skip, Notion-API-failure resilience.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- Tested as: unit only (live cron tick will validate on next backend deploy/restart; failure mode is bounded — at worst the cron skips a day and the next tick recovers).

## Files changed
- `backend/src/cron/onboardingStuckDetector.ts` (rewritten — aggregator + single-task post)
- `backend/src/cron/__tests__/onboardingStuckDetector.test.ts` (rewritten to match new contract)
- `backend/src/server.ts` (cron interval `1h` → `24h`, comment updated)

## What was NOT tested
- Live Notion render of the per-stage rows in production (DEV envs suppress `createOncallItem`; the property body and bullet structure are verified against the existing `createOncallItem` schema used by every other oncall path).
- The interaction with the existing 30-min dedup in `errorReporter.ts` — no longer relevant because this path no longer calls `reportUIError`. Real per-user error paths remain unchanged.

## Related PRs
- Backend: standalone (this one)
- Customer Portal: standalone — no FE changes
- Builds on PR #1371 (original detector) and PR #1397 (filters), replacing the alerting shape from both.

N/A — operational fix per Harsha's direct ask in #bug-report (Apr 30 08:30 PT).

title: harshit/crm_list_search_tool_bug_fix
body:
## Summary

Fixes a silent data-loss bug in Emma's `search_leads` tool and extends it to search across multiple lead lists in one call.

### Bug fix — pagination cursor

When the caller's `limit` was reached partway through an underlying DynamoDB page, `search_leads` returned that page's `lastEvaluatedKey` as `next_cursor` — i.e. a key pointing past leads we had never scanned. Subsequent calls with that cursor silently skipped the unscanned tail of the page, dropping matches.

The cursor is now anchored to the last scanned `leadId`. Since `leadId` is the sort key on `AW-Leads`, `{ listId, leadId }` is a native `ExclusiveStartKey`, and the next call resumes immediately after the last lead we looked at — no skips, no duplicates.

`has_more` now reflects whether `next_cursor` is set, instead of whether the underlying DynamoDB query has more raw leads (which doesn't imply more matches).

### Feature — multi-list search

`search_leads` now accepts an optional `list_ids: string[]` (cap 5) alongside the existing single `list_id`. Each returned lead carries its `listId`/`listName` so Emma can attribute results when summarising. The cursor freezes the resolved list set so paging stays stable even if the caller's `list_ids` change between calls. Inaccessible lists in a multi-list call are silently skipped (the call still returns matches from accessible lists); single-list calls still hard-error on a missing or denied `list_id`.

Per-lead match logic is extracted into a private helper so the inner loop can be reused per list. For broad cross-CRM strategic questions ("who should I reach out to today?"), `ask_crm` remains the right tool — `search_leads` stays focused on structured field-level filtering on a known small set of lists.

### Commit structure

- `fix(emma)`: cursor anchoring (impl)
- `test(emma)`: cursor pagination tests + update legacy crmTools test
- `feat(emma)`: list_ids support (impl + tool definition)
- `test(emma)`: multi-list tests
- `docs`: release notes

title: fix(headless): fix skeleton loading state on analytics pages in headless browser
body:
## Summary

- Patches `document.visibilityState` and `document.hidden` to always report `visible` in headless Chromium — fixes frameworks that skip rendering when the page is considered hidden
- Patches `document.hasFocus()` to always return `true`
- Patches `IntersectionObserver.observe()` to immediately fire callbacks with `isIntersecting: true` — fixes pages that lazy-load content behind intersection events that never fire in headless
- Dispatches a `visibilitychange` event on `DOMContentLoaded` for one-shot listeners that run exactly once when a tab becomes visible

## Root Cause

Pages like `rankai.ai/dashboard/*/analytics` consistently render as grey skeleton placeholders in headless Chromium because:
1. Headless Chrome sets `document.visibilityState = 'hidden'`, causing frameworks (React, Vue) to skip skeleton-to-content transitions
2. `IntersectionObserver` callbacks never fire because there's no real viewport, so lazy-loaded chart/data components never hydrate
3. Data IS present in the DOM (confirmed via `document.body.innerText`) — only the visual rendering is gated on these browser signals

title: harshit/crm-enrichment-upgrade2
body:
## Summary

Major lead-enrichment overhaul. The original PR title only covered the email-verification slice (commit `ab3bc7c9`), but this branch grew to **8 feature commits / ~14,000 LOC across 70 files** spanning four broad themes:

1. **Cache layer + per-field clustering** for the existing web-search enrichment pipeline (commits `87804e59`, `e605359d`).
2. **enrich.so integration** — email verification, find-email, reverse-lookup, quotas, group-email Proposal-B (`ab3bc7c9`).
3. **Bulk enrichment surface** — list-wide find / lookup / validate jobs with provider-agnostic counts and provider-name badges (`ee00f9e9`, `c3a2d1b1`, `74e68b2d`, `c1e27d5f`).
4. **Cache-first Unipile profile/company wrappers** so repeated LinkedIn lookups across sessions don't re-hit Unipile (`72a027e9`).

The companion customer-portal PR is https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/722.

---

## Required infrastructure changes (READ BEFORE MERGING)

### New DynamoDB table — must exist in dev and prod before deploy

Run `NODE_ENV=<env> npx ts-node backend/src/scripts/create-tables.ts` (table creation is idempotent — `ResourceInUseException` is swallowed):

| Table | Hash | Range | GSI |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AW-EnrichmentRawCache` | `canonicalId` (S) | `fieldGroup` (S) | `entityKey-fieldGroup-index` (entityKey HASH, fieldGroup RANGE, projection ALL) |

Billing mode: `PAY_PER_REQUEST`. Stores raw cached payloads for **all** enrichment providers; rows are namespaced by a `cacheType` discriminator (`field_group | enrichso | unipile | unipile_company`) so a single table backs every provider.

### New AWS Secrets Manager entries — must be provisioned before deploy

| Secret | Format | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dev/AgentWeb/EnrichSo` | plain string (the API key) | `getEnrichSoApiKey()` in `secretsManager.ts` |
| `prod/AgentWeb/EnrichSo` | plain string (the API key) | same — environment-selected at runtime |

Until the secrets exist, `enrichSoServiceFactory.initEnrichSoService()` logs a warning and **falls back to LLM-based** email finder / reverse lookup. The boot path picks them up automatically once provisioned (no code change).

### Existing secrets reused (no provisioning needed)

- `dev/AgentWeb/Unipile` / `prod/AgentWeb/Unipile` — already in use by LinkedIn outreach; the new cache wrappers reuse these.
- `dev/AgentWeb/Google/Search` / `prod/AgentWeb/Google/Search` — used by the Crunchbase/web specialists for SERP queries.

### Soft schema additions (no migration required, safe with existing rows)

- `AW-LeadLists` — adds optional fields: `enrichmentFieldConfig`, `linkedinSearchTemplate`, `fieldGroups`, `ungroupedClusters`, `goldenSet`, etc.
- `AW-Leads` — adds optional `enrichmentMetadata` map (per-field provenance: `{ source, provider, confidence, enrichedAt, sourceUrl, sourceQuote, verifiedBy, rejectedAt, rejectedReason, criticVerdict }`).
- `AW-Configs` — uses `configId='system:enrichSoUsage'` for race-safe per-user daily quota counters (50/day shared lookup cap).

---

## What's in this PR (by commit)

### `87804e59` — caching layer for lead enrichment with per-group refresh
- New service `enrichmentCacheService` with TTL-aware get/set keyed by `(canonicalId, fieldGroup)`.
- New Emma tool entry, new route hooks, and the `AW-EnrichmentRawCache` table itself.
- Per-group refresh so re-enriching one field group doesn't bust the cache for others.

### `e605359d` — per-field clustering, specialists, validation, golden-set eval
- Replaces the single global `web_search_template` with **per-field-group LLM-clustered search queries** (`enrichmentClusterService`).
- **Crunchbase specialist** (`crunchbaseSpecialist.ts`): three FieldSpecialists for funding round, total funding, HQ city. Drops `site:crunchbase.com` for open-web news SERP parsing (more accurate for funding figures); shares one search across the three via in-memory dedup with 5-min TTL; precision-filters results that don't mention the company name.
- **Field alias resolution** (`enrichmentFieldAliasService`): user-typed labels like "HQ", "headquarters", "main office" all resolve to the canonical `hqCity` field. Combines a static map with an LLM fallback; returns null for unmappable labels rather than guessing.
- **Type-aware validation** (`enrichmentFieldTypes`, `enrichmentValidation`): per-field type tags (URL / email / number / enum) with format checks before the value is written.
- **`enrichmentMetadata` sidecar** on each lead with `source`, `provider`, `confidence`, `sourceUrl`, `sourceQuote`, `enrichedAt`, `enrichedJobId`, `criticVerdict`.
- **`webContentFetcher`** — SSRF-safe HTML→text extractor (5s timeout, 1MB body cap, 4KB output cap, blocks private/link-local IPs, skips known login-walled domains). Used to pull main-content snippets when SERP titles+snippets are too short.
- **Golden-set evaluation harness** (`enrichmentEval.test.ts` + `fixtures/enrichmentGoldenSet.json`) for regression-checking enrichment quality.
- **`enrichmentLogger`** — structured per-job logger.

### `ab3bc7c9` — email verification + finder + reverse lookup (the original "enrich.so" piece)
- **Routes:** `POST /lists/:listId/leads/:leadId/validate-email`, `POST /leads/lookup-by-email`, `POST /leads/find-email`.
- **`enrichSoService`** — provider client with per-endpoint TTL (validate 30d / find 90d / reverse 60d / negative 7d / error 1h), in-memory LRU on top of the DDB cache, and a namespaced cache-key scheme that prevents collisions with field-group rows.
- **`enrichSoQuota`** — race-safe per-user daily counter on `AW-Configs` (key `system:enrichSoUsage`) with 50/day shared lookup cap and a route-level abuse gate (RFC ≤254 chars, format check).
- **M4-style targeted DDB write** (`SET customFields.email_validation = :v`) so background validation never clobbers concurrent customFields edits.
- **Group email — Proposal B**: preview returns `undeliverableEmails` / `riskyEmails` arrays; send accepts a per-address `includeUndeliverableEmails: string[]` whitelist.
- **Specialists** for the existing pipeline: `enrichSoEmailFinder` and 5× `enrichSoReverseLookup` (firstName/lastName/company/title/linkedin) sharing one API call per (userId, email) via an in-flight promise dedup map.
- **Emma tool `find_or_lookup_email`** — union inputs (`email | name+company | leadId`), bulk arrays (cap 25), returns structured data, never auto-updates leads.
- `getEnrichSoApiKey()` added to `secretsManager.ts` (reads `dev/AgentWeb/EnrichSo` / `prod/AgentWeb/EnrichSo`).

### `ee00f9e9` — bulk enrichment endpoints + counts
- `GET /lists/:listId/leads/enrichment-counts` returns `{ total, withEmail, validate, find, lookup }` so the UI can render "X pending · Y already done" without a client-side scan.
- `POST /lists/:listId/leads/find-emails`, `POST /lists/:listId/leads/lookup-emails`, `POST /lists/:listId/leads/validate-emails` (bulk async background jobs; respond 202 with `{ queued, skipped, alreadyDone }`).

### `c3a2d1b1` — tag enriched fields with provider name
- Specialists now write `enrichmentMetadata[field].provider = 'enrich.so' | 'crunchbase' | …` so the UI badge can show the actual provider name (admin/QA only — see customer-portal PR for the gate).

### `74e68b2d` — preserve value on field reject; clean metadata stamps on flip
- Mark-wrong now keeps the field value visible in the UI and only stamps `enrichmentMetadata[field].rejectedReason / rejectedAt` instead of nulling the column.
- `verify` strips a prior `rejectedReason / rejectedAt`; `reject` strips a prior `verifiedBy` — flipping the verdict leaves a clean current state on disk.

### `c1e27d5f` — per-list enrich.so field config + extended profile fields
- New `enrichmentFieldConfig` per lead list (`firstName/lastName/company/title/linkedin` default ON; `summary/skills/connectionCount/location/headline/pastCompanies/education` default OFF) gates which fields the reverse-lookup specialists may write.
- Standard fields → top-level columns; extended fields → `customFields[<field>]`. Existing values are never overwritten.
- New `GET/PATCH /lists/:listId/enrichment-field-config` to read and update.
- Bulk lookup-emails and the counts endpoint both respect the config.

### `72a027e9` — cache-first Unipile profile/company wrappers
- New `unipileProfileService` and `unipileCompanyService` route LinkedIn `/users/{id}` and `/companies/{id}` through `AW-EnrichmentRawCache` (`cacheType='unipile' | 'unipile_company'`, 30-day TTL). Viewer-relative fields (`network_distance`, `is_following`, etc.) stripped before persisting.
- `agentModeService` `get-profile` / `get-company` tool calls and the received-invitations enrichment path now go through the wrappers.
- `get-profile` fetches now request `linkedin_sections=*` so the cached payload includes experience, education, skills. Connection-degree pre-flight check stays lean (no sections) since it's a viewer-relative call that wouldn't be cacheable anyway.

---

## Test plan

- [x] **Backend: 463 unit tests pass** across the affected suites (`enrichSo*`, `enrichmentField*`, `enrichmentCache*`, `enrichmentCluster*`, `enrichmentEval`, `crunchbaseSpecialist`, `webContentFetcher`, `crm.routes`, `crm.enrichSoRoutes`, `linkedInOutreachService`, `unipile*`, `enrichmentValidation`, `enrichmentGroups`, `crmEnrichmentService` + the golden-set eval).
- [x] `npx tsc` — only pre-existing errors in `remotionService` / `voiceService` (unrelated, present on `main`).
- [x] Multi-agent test orchestration on the email-finder slice (1 manager + 4 parallel testers + 1 fixer) caught a regression where `leadIds: []` validated all leads — fixed in this PR with a regression test.
- [x] Manual smoke on cloud test env: validate-email round trip, find-email format gates, lookup quota 429 enforcement, group-email per-address override flow, bulk lookup with field-config gating, Unipile cache hit/miss path.

## Pre-deploy checklist

- [ ] `prod/AgentWeb/EnrichSo` secret provisioned with the production enrich.so API key.

title: fix(scoring): include cross-window sessions and always re-fetch after sync
body:
## Summary

- **Bug 1 — `createdAt` filter removed** (`chatbotService.ts`): `getRecentSessionsPage` was filtering out sessions whose `createdAt` predated the query window even when `updatedAt` was inside it. Since `updatedAt` only advances on real message writes (not scoring), any session the DynamoDB `BETWEEN` query returns was genuinely active in the window. Sessions that started late at night and continued past midnight were being silently excluded from the 24-hour satisfaction report.

- **Bug 2 — sync re-fetch always fires** (`routes/admin.ts`): When `sync=true` and no judges are configured, `scoreSessionIfNeeded` was persisting a new score to DynamoDB but the response returned the stale in-memory object (`satisfactionScore: null`). The re-fetch was previously gated on `judges.length > 0`. Now re-fetches unconditionally so the response always reflects freshly computed scores.

## Root cause context

The daily satisfaction report (seen in the shared session) showed 0 unsatisfied sessions out of 45 — but the report runs `get_chat_history` with `sync=true`. Without the re-fetch fix, sessions scored for the first time during the sync call would appear with `satisfactionScore: null`, making them look unscored rather than potentially low-scoring. And without the `createdAt` filter fix, any session that started before midnight but was active during the 24h window would be silently dropped from the count.

## Test plan

- [x] New test: `admin.chatSessions.test.ts` — verifies `getChatSession` is called twice (hydration + re-fetch) when `sync=true` with no judges, and response includes the newly scored score
- [x] Updated test: `chatbotService.pagination.test.ts` — old "exclude sessions outside time range" test flipped to "include sessions created before window if they had messages within it"; added "sessions created just before startTime" test
- [x] All 8158 tests pass, TypeScript compiles clean

title: fix(data-analysis): fail gracefully when dataset is too large for sandbox
body:
## Summary
- Adds an upfront size guard (200K chars) on `analysis_instruction` so the LLM gets an actionable error instead of a silent Gemini failure when data is too large to embed inline
- Detects local file path and tool-response path references in `analysis_instruction` and returns a clear error explaining the sandbox is remote/isolated — this was the actual root cause of session `9d2b2c07`: the agent passed `/home/bard/tool-responses/...` paths 8 times, Gemini couldn't access them, and it simulated results instead
- Updated tool description and parameter docs to make the correct workflow explicit upfront: embed small data inline, or use `save_file` to get an S3 URL and pass it in `file_urls`
- Improved catch block to detect HTTP 413 / payload-too-large errors with the same actionable guidance

## Root cause (from real session data)
The failing session had `analysis_instruction` calls of only ~6,600 chars — the dataset size was never the issue. The agent was writing Python code that tried to open S3-offloaded tool response paths like `/home/bard/tool-responses/{sessionId}/yvsosw0l.txt`. Those paths don't exist in the remote Gemini sandbox. Because the error was generic, the agent retried the identical broken call 8 more times and eventually simulated results.

title: feat(video): add Video Production skill best-practices system prompt
body:
## Summary

- Encodes the Haven AI ad production learnings into the Video Production built-in skill as a comprehensive `systemPrompt`
- Extends `BUILT_IN_SKILLS` type in `agentModeService.ts` to carry an optional `systemPrompt`, which is now passed through `ensureBuiltInSkills()` on startup
- Adds `seed-video-production-skill.ts` to backfill dev and prod environments where the skill DB record already exists without a system prompt

## What's in the system prompt

The prompt encodes three source documents from the Haven AI production into a 10-layer pipeline:

1. **Brief** — research brand via `search_web` before writing anything
2. **Strategy & Hook** — declare one of 6 named archetypes (Data-Led, Pain Agitation, Social Proof, Time-Bound Promise, Direct Challenge, Contrarian); archetype selected by audience temperature (cold/warm/hot)
3. **125-Character Gate** — VO hook must work standalone before Meta truncation; self-qualifying copy required
4. **Script & VO Math** — per-shot word budget at 2.5 wps, emphasis beat protection, backup lines
5. **Veo Shot Prompts** — anti-UI clause, 4s/8s snap rule, brand color as mandatory lighting element in every shot
6. **Character Anchoring** — `list_characters` → `startFrame` for visual consistency across shots
7. **Overlay Specs** — mobile font minimums (108px caption, 44px toast, etc.), spring vs interpolate decision rule, stagger discipline
8. **End Card** — mandatory Remotion-only CTA frame with brand mark + offer + URL + button
9. **Multi-Aspect Reflow** — 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 notes per shot
10. **Cost & Safety** — plan first, $30 ceiling, default PAUSED in ad platforms

Plus an 8-item QA rubric and explicit anti-patterns list.

## How to backfill existing environments

```bash
# Dev
NODE_ENV=development npx ts-node src/scripts/seed-video-production-skill.ts

# Prod
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node src/scripts/seed-video-production-skill.ts
```

The seed script is idempotent — updates systemPrompt and toolNames on an existing record, creates if missing.

title: fix(sequences): reduce spam — proxy S3 images and inject unsubscribe URL at send time
body:
## Summary
- Rewrites S3 image `src` URLs through `https://api.agentweb.pro/asset/<base64url>` at send time, so image hostnames are consistent and don't mismatch the sending domain (a Resend/Gmail spam signal)
- Injects real unsubscribe URLs into every sequence email at send time — the worker was calling `substituteVariables()` but never `injectUnsubscribeUrl()`, leaving `{{unsubscribeUrl}}` as a broken placeholder in delivered emails
- Both fixes apply to the live worker send path and the test-email send path

## Summary

- Adds `local-agent-relay/` — a Python HTTP server that bridges AgentWeb/Emma to a Codex agent running on the user's local machine via ngrok

- Open a URL and extract visible text/titles/summaries
- Read data from authenticated sites the user is already logged into
- Summarize page content from any website

1. Run `codex-relay serve --secret YOUR_SECRET --cwd ~/agent-work --sandbox danger-full-access` locally

title: chore(telemetry): kill onboarding telemetry pipeline

## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Two telemetry pipelines were dumping into Notion's sprint board and on-call email:
1. `errorReporter.reportUIError` created a Notion oncall task **per UI error event** + emailed on-call. With no rate-limit beyond a 30-min dedup, every onboarding-stuck/abandoned user generated a fresh \`UI Error: onboarding:*\` task. Result: 200+ telemetry rows in the sprint board, and on-call email noise that was rarely actioned.
2. The daily \`runOnboardingStuckDetector\` cron created 1 grouped \"Onboarding stuck users — daily report\" Notion task per backend instance per day.

Net effect: sprint board choked with auto-generated junk, real tasks invisible.

## What this fixes (after)
- \`reportUIError\` now emits a single structured \`[uiError]\` \`console.error\` log line with the full enriched context. **No Notion task. No email.** Logs are sufficient for post-hoc investigation.
- Dedup (30 min by operation + normalized error), onboarding step-status enrichment, and attribution (UTM/referrer/landingUrl) enrichment are all preserved — they now show up inside the log payload instead of the Notion task body.
- The daily-summary cron's initialization is removed from \`server.ts\`. The cron implementation file (\`cron/onboardingStuckDetector.ts\`) and its unit tests are preserved — easy to re-enable if we ever want the daily roll-up back.

## How to test

2. \`npx jest src/__tests__/utils/errorReporter.test.ts\` — 19 tests pass, asserting:

title: CRM enrichment upgrade 2: Apollo waterfall, ICP find-leads, security hardening
body:
## Summary

Follow-on work to PR #1432 — extends the CRM enrichment stack with the Apollo people-enrichment waterfall, ICP-driven find-leads, and broad security/quality hardening across the find-email and Apollo paths.

## ⚠️ Pre-merge / pre-deploy: Apollo Secrets Manager entry required

Before this branch is deployed, the Apollo credentials must exist in AWS Secrets Manager — otherwise every Apollo-backed code path (`getApolloApiKey`) throws on first call and `enrichLeadsWithApolloInBackground` aborts via the `isApolloServiceReady()` gate.

**Secret names** (from `backend/src/utils/secretsManager.ts`):
- Dev / staging: `dev/AgentWeb/Apollo`
- Production: `prod/AgentWeb/Apollo`

**Required JSON shape** — whitespace-only values are rejected:
```json
{
  "apiKey": "<Apollo people-enrichment API key>"
}
```

**Create / update commands:**
```bash
# Dev / staging
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name dev/AgentWeb/Apollo \
  --secret-string "{\"apiKey\":\"<APOLLO_API_KEY>\"}"

# Production
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name prod/AgentWeb/Apollo \
  --secret-string "{\"apiKey\":\"<APOLLO_API_KEY>\"}"

# To update an existing secret use put-secret-value with --secret-id instead of create-secret.
```

**Verification after creating the secret:**
```bash
# 1. Read it back (should print valid JSON with apiKey)
aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id dev/AgentWeb/Apollo --query SecretString --output text

# 2. Hit the bulk-enrich health gate — 503 means the secret is missing / unreadable
curl -s -w "\nstatus=%{http_code}\n" -X POST \
  https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/api/crm/lists/<listId>/leads/enrich-with-apollo \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <jwt>" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
```

> **Note:** A working-tree-only debug shortcut hardcoded the API key in `backend/src/utils/secretsManager.ts` during development. That change is **not** in this PR. Rotate the key before deploy if it was ever shared in plaintext.

### Apollo + waterfall
- Apollo people-enrichment as a sibling provider to enrich.so with signal-based waterfall (linkedin → Apollo first, email → enrich.so first); new fields: employment history / tech stack / headcount growth / funding (`feat(crm): wire Apollo + CSV import wizard + email-job tracker into backend`).
- Per-field confidence in `apolloOrgEnrichment` specialists, central confidence registry, Apollo-domain handling, and `forceRefresh` plumbing.
- Cache TTL tightening: org cache 30d → 7d, Tier-3 placeholder 90d → 7d, transient-error TTL shortened with `Retry-After` honored.
- Bulk-enrich: per-(user,list) lock; quota applied to Tier-3 `runWaterfall`; quota skipped on cache hits.
- Waterfall: log Tier-3 placeholder write failures instead of swallowing; pick source label from input signal not provider; normalize linkedin URLs in `apolloDedupToken`.

### Find-leads / ICP
- Top-up loop with persisted resume cursor for `importLeadsFromSearch`; cursor wins over URL in Unipile `searchPeople`; tests cover top-up loop, dedup-driven trim, resume-cursor persistence.
- Phase 2: `/find/from-icp` route + `icpSource` attribution; ICP persona filter extractor handles more cities + multi-word industries.
- LinkedIn search location stored on `customFields.location`; auto-DNC undeliverable leads on email validation; default model defaults to `gpt-5-chat-2`.
- Skip web search when template placeholders all resolve to empty.

### Security / hardening
- IDOR fix on `find-email` route (authorize `persistTo*` target list).
- Webhook auth moved to header + constant-time compare; conditional write (`attribute_not_exists(email)`) closes TOCTOU on the placeholder write; ownership re-verified post-auth in waterfall webhook.
- New `ssrfGuard.ts` utility (RFC1918, loopback, link-local 169.254 metadata, CGNAT, ULA, multicast, broadcast, IPv4-mapped, plus forbidden hostname literals; URLs that parse but have empty hostname rejected; redirects blocked via `maxRedirects:0`).
- New `unsubscribeUrl.ts` HMAC-SHA256 over normalised `listId:leadId:email` with `JWT_SECRET`, hex prefilter and constant-time compare.
- Debug-route gating; CSV input caps (per-lead key count, customField value length, `columnMapping` size); `request_id` length + charset capped in Apollo cache-key builder.

### Reliability fixes (post-review)
Concurrency-critical fixes after the multi-agent review on this branch:
- **`fix(apollo): convert bulk-enrich writes to setLeadFields`** — `enrichLeadsWithApolloInBackground` was the one path commit `787888bf` missed. Two concurrent workers each spread `lead.customFields` (a stale snapshot) into `updateLead`, clobbering each other's `customFields`/`enrichmentMetadata` on the same list. Now uses targeted document-path SETs via `setLeadFields`.
- **`fix(crm): atomic mergeFieldNames via list_append + dedup-on-read in getLeadListById`** — replaced the read-modify-write in `mergeFieldNames` (two concurrent post-job calls on the same list could lose updates) with a single `UpdateItem` using `list_append(if_not_exists(fieldNames, :empty), :incoming)`. `getLeadListById` dedupes + sorts on read so transient duplicates under high concurrency are hidden from consumers.
- **`test(security): branch coverage for ssrfGuard + unsubscribeUrl`** — pushed both files to ~100% branches (hex-form IPv4-mapped IPv6, literal-public-IP fast path, DNS-throws / DNS-empty / no-message paths, `0.0.0.0/8`, `::` unspecified, trailing-slash baseUrl, falsy-email round-trip, defensive `timingSafeEqual` catch). Internal validators that callers already gate (e.g. `ipv4ToInt` malformed-IP returns) carry `/* istanbul ignore next */` with one-line justifications.

### Refactors / tests
- Extract `findEmailsForLeadsInBackground` to a service module.
- Lead-field updates: optional `ifNotExists` clause + populated-fields tracking; race conditions on parallel-worker enrichment writes resolved via targeted writes (`setLeadFields`) and atomic `mergeFieldNames` (see *Reliability fixes* above for the missed Apollo bulk path + RMW fix that landed in this round).
- NFKD-fold diacritics in `emailPatterns` (Müller → muller); GC stuck-running email jobs.
- Tests added for top-up loop, cursor pagination, location persistence, find-leads NaN guard, `enrichSoRoutes` drift repair, plus new tests for the `setLeadFields` Apollo-bulk path and the atomic `mergeFieldNames` semantics.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd backend && npx tsc` — TypeScript compiles clean (pre-existing unrelated errors in `voiceService.ts` / `remotionService.ts` from optional deps; not introduced here)
- [x] `cd backend && npm test` — full suite green (9,287 passing, 3 skipped) — Apollo, waterfall, find-leads, find-email runner, security, race-fix tests
- [x] CI Backend tests + coverage gate (≥95% branches) — passing on the latest push
- [ ] **Pre-deploy:** `dev/AgentWeb/Apollo` Secrets Manager entry created with `apiKey`; verified via `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value`
- [ ] **Pre-deploy (prod):** `prod/AgentWeb/Apollo` populated with `apiKey`
- [ ] Smoke find-leads from ICP on test env: returns leads, persists `customFields.location`, attributes `icpSource`
- [ ] Smoke bulk Apollo enrich on test env: per-(user,list) lock holds; quota decrements on Tier-3, not on cache hits; concurrent workers no longer clobber each other's `customFields`
- [ ] Smoke find-email with both linkedin-first and email-first signals; webhook ownership rejection on swapped IDs
- [ ] Verify auto-DNC fires for undeliverable validation results

title: fix(crm): LinkedIn outbound messages invisible + inbound duplicating on re-sync
body:
## Root Cause

Two bugs in how `update-conversation-history` / `sync-linkedin-messages` calls the Unipile API:

### Bug 1 — Inbound messages duplicating on every re-sync

The dedup key was `linkedin_msg_${msg.id}` — but `msg.id` is an **ephemeral Unipile-internal UUID that changes on every API call**. Because DynamoDB `put()` uses this as the primary key, each sync inserts brand-new rows instead of overwriting existing ones.

**Fix:** Key `eventId` on `msg.provider_id`, which is stable across calls.

### Bug 2 — Outbound (sent) messages never appearing

`getAllMessagesFromAttendee` was called **without `account_id`**. Without it, Unipile has no context for which account is "us", so `is_sender` is always `0` (received) for every message. Fangfang's manual replies were classified as inbound and silently discarded as duplicates — they never showed up as `linkedin.message.sent`.

**Fix:** Thread `account_id` through `getMessagesWithContact(attendeeId, account_id)` and pass it in the Unipile params.

## Changes

- `linkedInOutreachService.getMessagesWithContact` — new required `account_id` param, passed to `getAllMessagesFromAttendee`
- `agentModeService` `update-conversation-history` case — pass `account_id` arg + use `msg.provider_id` for eventId
- `crm.ts` `sync-linkedin-messages` endpoint — same two fixes
- Tests updated to assert `provider_id`-based eventId and `account_id` pass-through

## Data cleanup needed

The 6 existing duplicate records in prod `AW-EmailEvents` (3× Elvis "Sounds great", 3× Francesca "Thanks Fangfang") were created with the old random-key scheme and need to be deleted manually. After deletion the next sync will re-create them correctly with stable keys. title: fix(agent-mode): add search_tool_response and read_tool_response to FOUNDATION_TOOLS
body:
## Root Cause

When a tool response exceeds 10KB, agent mode uploads the full content to S3 and injects a header into the in-memory tool result:

```
[Full response stored at S3 key: ... — use search_tool_response tool to find specific fields]
```

The LLM needs `search_tool_response` and `read_tool_response` to retrieve the full content. But these tools were **not** in `FOUNDATION_TOOLS` — they were gated behind skill installation. The LLM could see the S3 reference but had no callable tool to act on it, so it summarized from the truncated 20KB preview only.

## Evidence

Confirmed in session `59ad8694` (Phoenix demo transcript):
- `read_knowledge_base_files` returned 27KB → S3 overflow triggered, 20KB preview kept
- LLM tried `search_tool_response` → error: `"Tool is not available. You must install the required skill first"`
- LLM tried `read_tool_response` → same error
- Emma then summarized from the 20KB prefix, missing the final portion of the transcript where **"call was cut short"** and **"follow-up scheduled same day"** were recorded

## Fix

Add `search_tool_response` and `read_tool_response` to `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS` so they are always available whenever the S3 overflow mechanism fires.

title: fix(crm): fix outbound LinkedIn messages invisible — use chat-based message fetch for correct is_sender
body:
## Root Cause

`getAllMessagesFromAttendee` in the Unipile Node SDK has **no `account_id` parameter** in its type definition (`GetAllMessagesFromAttendeeInput`). The `account_id` we were passing was silently ignored, so Unipile had no way to determine which side was "us" — and `is_sender` was always `0` for every message. All messages appeared as received.

By contrast, `GetAllChatsFromAttendeeInput` **does** accept `account_id`, and `getAllMessagesFromChat` fetches messages from a known conversation where `is_sender` is correctly set.

## Fix

Two-step approach in `getMessagesWithContact`:
1. Call `getAllChatsFromAttendee({ attendee_id, account_id, limit: 1 })` to find the `chat_id`
2. Call `getAllMessagesFromChat({ chat_id })` to get messages — `is_sender=1` now correctly identifies outbound messages

The public function signature (`attendeeId, account_id`) is unchanged, so both callers (`agentModeService.ts` and `crm.ts`) need no changes.

## Tests

- Added 3 new unit tests for `getMessagesWithContact` in `linkedInOutreachService.test.ts`:
  - Verifies it calls `getAllChatsFromAttendee` with `account_id` to find the chat
  - Verifies it calls `getAllMessagesFromChat` with the found `chat_id`  
  - Verifies it returns empty array when no chat found (does not call message API)
  - Verifies it filters out `is_event=1` system messages
- All 107 tests pass

title: feat(work-plan): user instructions field replaces raw prompt display
body:
## Summary

Adds a customer-facing \`userInstructions\` field to work-plan steps, capped at 500 chars, surfaced in the partner portal editor. Backend validation prevents persisting oversized values. Pairs with a customer-portal PR that swaps the display from raw prompt to user instructions.

## Why

Customer portal's \`HorizontalPlanProgress\` was rendering the step's \`description\` field directly in the expanded-step panel — but \`description\` holds the LLM's raw system prompt. End users were seeing internal prompts that overflowed the panel (which doesn't scroll). User report: "we are exposing the raw prompts ... user can't scroll (and it just looks ugly no matter how it's rendered)".

## Design

\`description\` stays untouched (backend continues using it for the LLM prompt). New \`userInstructions\` field is the only thing rendered to end users.

- Optional, max 500 chars (~5 short lines at text-sm + leading-relaxed, fits the panel)
- Validation in \`workPlanService.createWorkPlan\` + \`updateWorkPlan\` via a new private \`validateSteps()\` method
- Error format: \`step N: userInstructions exceeds 500 characters (got M)\` — 1-indexed for clarity
- Partner portal Work Plans page gets a multiline TextField with live N/500 counter (red at cap)

## How to test

1. Open partner portal → **Work Plans** → edit any plan.
2. Each step now has TWO text fields: \`description\` (LLM prompt — not shown to users) and a new multiline **User Instructions** textarea with a 0/500 counter.
3. Type past 500 chars → the counter turns red and the input hard-caps via maxLength.
4. Save with an oversized userInstructions via curl → backend returns 4xx with \`step N: userInstructions exceeds 500 characters\`.
5. Save with a valid userInstructions → persists, reloads correctly.
6. Open Agent Mode in customer portal with that plan → expand the step → see your user instructions (not the raw prompt). Empty instructions → "User instructions not yet provided for this step." (delivered by paired customer-portal PR.)

## Edge cases checked

- Empty / undefined userInstructions: passes validation, displays empty-state on customer side.
- userInstructions of wrong type (number) on the API: rejected with \`step N: userInstructions must be a string\`.
- Multi-step plan with one bad step out of three: validateSteps points to the exact step number that failed.
- Existing plans without userInstructions: still load + save correctly (no migration required).

## Test Evidence

- Backend: \`npx jest src/__tests__/workPlanService.test.ts\` — 18/18 pass (4 new for userInstructions + 14 existing)
- Backend: \`npx tsc\` — clean
- Partner portal: \`npx tsc --noEmit\` — clean

## Files changed

- \`backend/src/services/workPlanService.ts\` (+25 / -2)
- \`backend/src/__tests__/workPlanService.test.ts\` (+82 new tests)
- \`partner-portal/src/pages/WorkPlans.tsx\` (+35 / -1)

## What was NOT tested

- No backfill script for existing plans. They'll all show the empty-state placeholder until an admin fills in userInstructions per step. Easy to add later if desired.

title: fix(work-plan): wire userInstructions end-to-end (route → session → render)
body:
## Summary

Closes the gap left by agentweb#1475. The userInstructions field is now actually wired end-to-end from the partner portal save → predefined plan storage → session bootstrap → customer portal render. Multiple field whitelists were silently dropping it along the way.

## Why

After #1475 shipped, an admin saved \`userInstructions\` on a step in the partner portal's Work Plans editor and the field disappeared on reload. After fixing the route, a brand-new session against the saved plan still rendered the empty-state placeholder in \`<HorizontalPlanProgress />\`. Two more whitelists in the data path were dropping the field.

The service-level tests in workPlanService.test.ts (from #1475) all pass — they invoke the service directly and bypass these route/controller filters. Coverage gap.

## Two commits, two fixes

### 1. \`fix(work-plan-routes): pass userInstructions through admin + user route whitelists\`

\`POST /api/admin/work-plans\`, \`PUT /api/admin/work-plans/:id\`, and \`POST /api/user-work-plans\` all built \`normalizedSteps\` by explicitly picking 5 fields, dropping \`userInstructions\`. \`PUT /api/user-work-plans/:id\` was already correct (it spreads \`...steps\` directly).

New \`workPlanRoutes.userInstructions.test.ts\` covers all four endpoints end-to-end via supertest + a backwards-compat case. **4 of 5 tests fail with the bug, all 5 pass after the fix.**

### 2. \`fix(agent-mode): preserve userInstructions through session bootstrap + tools\`

Three places in the agent-mode path also stripped the field while copying steps from the predefined plan into a session's runtime workPlan:

- \`agentModeController.createSessionWithPlan\` (line 5172) — primary user path: \`POST /api/agent-mode/public/plan/:planTitle/session\`
- \`agentModeService.createWorkPlan\` — Emma's \`create_work_plan\` tool
- \`agentModeService.modifyWorkPlan\` — Emma's \`modify_work_plan\` tool (both update + add-step branches)

Plus type signature updates on \`chatbotService.updateSessionWorkPlan\` and the two agent-mode methods so future refactors can rely on the type system to catch field drops.

\`userInstructions\` now travels exactly the same rails as \`description\` and \`requiredFunctionCalls\` — copied at session bootstrap from the predefined plan, snapshotted into the session row, rendered from the session by the customer portal.

## How to test

After this lands and the staging deploy completes:

1. Partner portal → Work Plans → edit a system plan → step 1 → set "User Instructions" to e.g. \`"Emma will read your brand guidelines"\` → save.
2. Curl-verify it persists: \`curl https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/api/agent-mode/public/plans | jq '.[] | select(.title=="Landing Page Builder") | .steps[0].userInstructions'\` should return the string.
3. Customer portal → start a **brand new** chat session against that plan.
4. Expand step 1 in the plan view → see your user instructions, not the empty-state placeholder.
5. Existing sessions started before this fix will still show the empty state — their \`workPlan.steps\` rows in DynamoDB were frozen without the field. Only new sessions get it.

## Edge cases checked

- Steps without userInstructions: pass through cleanly with the field absent (covered by backwards-compat test).
- Wrong-type userInstructions on a step: rejected by the \`workPlanService.validateSteps\` validator from #1475 with \`step N: userInstructions must be a string\`.
- userInstructions over 500 chars: rejected by validator with the precise length in the error.
- Emma editing a session's plan via \`modify_work_plan\`: preserves userInstructions on both updated and newly-added steps.

## Test Evidence

- Route tests: 5/5 in \`workPlanRoutes.userInstructions.test.ts\`
- Service tests (existing, from #1475): 18/18 still green
- \`npx tsc\` clean across the backend

## Files changed

\`\`\`
backend/src/__tests__/workPlanRoutes.userInstructions.test.ts (new, +189)
backend/src/routes/adminWorkPlanRoutes.ts (+2 lines)
backend/src/routes/userWorkPlanRoutes.ts (+1 line)
backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts (+5 lines)
backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts (+5 lines, type updates)
backend/src/services/chatbotService.ts (+5 lines, type updates)
\`\`\`

## What was NOT done

- **No backfill script** for existing sessions started before this fix. Their stored workPlan.steps don't carry userInstructions; they'll continue to render the empty state. If retroactive update is desired, a one-time scan-and-patch script over \`Dev-AW-ChatSessions\` / \`AW-ChatSessions\` is straightforward — flag separately if you want it.

## Related PRs

- Pairs with the customer-portal display PRs already merged on the customer-portal repo

title: fix: website scans no longer report 429 asset errors as site failures
body:
## Summary
- Adds guidance to Emma's system prompt to correctly distinguish Cloudflare/bot-protection 429s on static assets from genuine website failures
- When a headless browser visits sites like ai2030.org, Cloudflare rate-limits CSS/JS/image asset requests with 429 while the main HTML loads fine — Emma was incorrectly reporting these sites as broken
- Emma now checks whether the main HTML document loaded (2xx) and whether page content is present before concluding a site is down

## Root Cause
Verified against ai2030.org: the main HTML returns 200 with 486KB of content and a proper page title, but 250+ asset requests (CSS, JS, fonts, images) return 429 because Cloudflare detects the headless browser and rate-limits it. Emma saw the 429s in `playwright_browser_network_requests` and reported the site as broken.

## Fix
Added a "429 Errors on Static Assets — Bot Protection, Not a Broken Site" subsection to the "Browser & Visual Verification" section of `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts` with explicit rules:
1. Don't flag a site as broken based solely on 429s for static assets
2. Check the main HTML document status — if 2xx, the site is reachable
3. Use `browser_evaluate` to confirm meaningful content loaded
4. Report 429 asset issues as "automated browser may be rate-limited by bot protection, but site appears functional for regular visitors"

## Test plan
- [ ] Manually trigger the scheduled "Website Scan - ai2030.org" chat for user xzhang@ai2030.org and verify Emma no longer reports the site as broken
- [ ] Verify a genuinely broken site (4xx/5xx on the HTML document) still gets reported correctly

title: fix(chatbot): truncate oversized non-string message content before DynamoDB write
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause (found in prod logs):** The session `cae6bac5` failed with `ValidationException: Item size has exceeded the maximum allowed size` at 15:47:52 UTC. The agent generated a large HTML report as an assistant message with array-typed content blocks, which bypassed the existing 350KB size check (that check only applied to `typeof content === 'string'`). The write failed, the error was swallowed by the try/catch, email was sent from in-memory content, but the response was never persisted to the DB.
- **Fix:** Switch from checking `message.content.length` to checking `JSON.stringify(message).length` — this catches oversized items regardless of content type. Non-string (array) content that exceeds the limit is stringified then truncated before writing.
- Updated the test for this code path to match the new behavior (array content now gets truncated instead of passing through unchanged).

## Test plan

title: fix: compose_video clip ordering - prevent incoherent shot sequences
body:
## Root Cause

When the agent generates clips individually (not via a single `durationSeconds` call), clips appear in context in generation order — not shot order. When `compose_video` was called, URLs were copied from context in generation order, causing Remotion to stitch them in the wrong narrative sequence.

**Juan's session (b1e9b7ba):** S3 (haven_s3_morning.mp4) was generated last and ended up at position 8 in the composed video instead of position 3. The final 30s Meta ad had completely incoherent shot sequencing.

## Fixes

### 1. `compose_video` tool description — strengthened ordering warnings
- Added `CRITICAL:` prefix warning in tool description that `clip_urls` order determines final playback order, and to never pass in context/generation order
- Updated `clip_urls` property description to explicitly say "sort by shot number before passing"

### 2. Haven Video Agent skill prompt (applied directly to prod DynamoDB)
- Added a `## CLIP SEQUENCING — MANDATORY PRE-COMPOSE CHECKLIST` section
- Requires the agent to build an explicit ordered manifest (S1: url, S2: url...) and verify ascending shot numbers before calling `compose_video`
- Flags the anti-pattern of scrolling through context to copy URLs

### 3. Re-composed Juan's video (delivered)
- Correct order: S1→S2→S3→S4→S5→S6→S7→S8
- New URL: https://s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/remotionlambda-useast1-rc326aiifn/renders/mvoo2pkrnm/users/a3917669-1c7d-45ed-8ef9-f454de109b6f/remotion/1778542648437_haven_30s_meta_ad_v2_corrected.mp4
