title: fix(social): stop posting LLM refusals and templated junk as engagement comments
body:
## Problem

Investigation of the **automated social-engagement comments** (the user reported being unhappy with their quality). I queried the real generated comments from `Dev-AW-SocialEngagementTracking` (60 records with `generatedText`) and traced them back to `backend/src/cron/socialEngagementExecutor.ts`. The data exposed several concrete bugs:

1. **🔴 Model refusals posted verbatim.** When post content was empty/unavailable, the LLM replied to the *prompt* and that text was posted to LinkedIn:
   - *"Please provide the text of the LinkedIn post so I can tailor the critique…"*
   - *"Please provide the post content you are referring to, and I will craft a response that aligns with Rui's analytical perspective."* (leaked the persona name)
2. **🔴 Preamble leak.** *"…here is a versatile, professional comment suitable for most enterprise AI discussions: \<actual comment\>"* — the meta-preamble was posted along with the comment.
3. **🟠 Comments asked questions** despite the prompt explicitly banning it.
4. **🟠 Severe repetition / templated voice.** Most comments opened with *"The shift toward…"* / *"Moving beyond…"* and stacked the same buzzwords (agentic workflows, data governance, operational debt, observability…), regardless of the post.
5. **🟠 Boilerplate org auto-replies** ("Thank you for sharing…", "Thank you for the kind words…").

### Root causes
- Insufficient input validation — the `!postContent` guard missed whitespace-only/thin content, which is what produced the "please provide the post" refusals.
- No output validation — refusal/preamble text was never checked before `createComment`.
- Weak model (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite`) at `temperature: 0.9` with a soft prompt → homogeneous, off-instruction output.

## Fix (`socialEngagementExecutor.ts`)
- **Model upgrade** `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` → `gemini-3.5-flash`; **temperature** `0.9` → `0.7`.
- **Hardened prompts**: ban the observed templated openers, buzzword stacking, and trailing questions; instruct the model to emit `SKIP` instead of a meta-response when it can't write a specific comment.
- **`sanitizeGeneratedComment()`** (new, exported + unit-tested): strips wrapping quotes, salvages the real comment from a colon-introduced preamble, and rejects refusal/meta/empty output.
- **Skip rather than post junk**: on generation failure or rejection, post nothing (the canned fallbacks were themselves bot-like). Like/reaction sub-actions still proceed.
- **Tighter content guards**: post content < 20 chars, or missing original comment text on replies → skip.

## Tests
- New unit tests for `sanitizeGeneratedComment` using the exact production refusal strings.
- Updated executor tests: LLM failure / refusal / thin content now assert **no** comment is posted.
- **All 156** social-engagement-related tests pass; `npx tsc` clean.

## Verification

title: fix(coding-agent): stream Opus 4.8 bearer path to fix landing-page edit timeouts
body:
## Problem

A landing-page compliance edit via `coding_agent` timed out before completing (session `ac42f498…`, reported by lyndi@every.io). Both the broad edit AND a narrow single-concern retry returned `iterations: -1` — the outer 10-minute wrapper firing, *not* the 50-iteration ceiling. The bug report's "edit was too broad" hypothesis is contradicted by the evidence.

**Root cause:** the coding-agent default model had been switched to `anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, which routes through the bearer-token Bedrock client using the **blocking `/invoke` endpoint**. Each non-streaming turn (up to 16K tokens) had to fully complete before the loop advanced, so the 10-minute budget allowed only ~2 slow Opus turns — exhausting it before the agent could read → edit → deploy.

## Changes

- **Stream the bearer path** — replaced `/invoke` with `invoke-with-response-stream`. Added `_parseEventStreamFrames` (hand-rolled `vnd.amazon.eventstream` binary frame parser, no new dependency) + `_accumulateBedrockStream` (reconstructs the exact `Anthropic.Message` the loop already consumes — `create()` contract unchanged). Wire format empirically confirmed against the live endpoint before writing the parser.
- **Coherent timeouts** — replaced the fixed 5-min per-request cap with a 2-min inter-chunk idle timeout (only true stalls abort), and raised `AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS` 10m → 20m.
- **Honest aborts** — idle-timeout aborts tagged `status: 408` + `isTimeout`, reported as "timed out" and not retried. Applied to bearer and Vertex paths.
- **Cost observability** — guarded `context.onUsage` hook (loop previously discarded `response.usage`); no behavior change when unset.

## Testing

- `codingAgentService.test.ts`: +8 tests (frame parsing whole/partial/multi, message reconstruction, empty-stream→retryable 5xx, throttle→429, 408-reported-not-retried). **61/61 pass**, `npx tsc` clean.
- Verified end-to-end in a real browser: the Opus 4.8 path completed (iters=6), deployed to a draft branch, and the preview rendered the correct change.

## Model eval (Sonnet 4.6 vs Opus 4.8)

24 real runs (4 edit tasks × 2 models × trials), correctness scored from the deployed DOM:

| Metric | Sonnet 4.6 | Opus 4.8 |
|---|---|---|
| Success rate | **12/12 (100%)** | 8/12 (67%) |
| Correct when completed | 12/12 | 8/8 |
| Latency (avg) | 51s | 79s (up to 166s) |
| Cost per edit | **$0.09** | $0.48 (5.3×) |

Opus's 4 failures were all the bearer-account stalling >120s. **Recommendation: keep the coding agent on Sonnet 4.6** (prod already is). The streaming fix still matters — it makes Opus usable when healthy and surfaces stalls honestly.

title: fix(landing-pages): resolve public URL from the attached subdomain (fixes org-member 404s)
body:
## Problem

Reported (High priority, session `a007c0c2-5474-4031-a736-521b71e980dd`): **all landing pages return 404** for member account `jpruter@every.io`, while the org owner `lyndi@every.io` sees the correct subdomain on the **same** pages.

## Root cause

This is an **org-sharing read-time enrichment bug**, not a platform outage or DNS issue. In `GET /api/landing-pages/v0/generated`, the block that backfills each page's `customDomainUrl` from `AW-CustomDomains` had two defects:

1. **Caller-scoped lookup** — it called `listDomains(callerUserId)`. An org member viewing a shared page owns no `AW-CustomDomains` rows, so enrichment was skipped entirely and the member saw the **stale** `customDomainUrl` stored on the page record.
2. **Only filled blanks** — when a page stored an old managed subdomain that was later detached from its Vercel project, that host serves a Vercel `DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND` 404 and was **never corrected**, even for the owner.

### Verified against prod data (every.io project `prj_aODtNYNBkDWHaWYJjkJxMzNA8W39`)

| Host | Source | Live |
|---|---|---|
| `everyio-day-zero-founders.agentwebforms.com` | stored on page records (stale) | **404** `DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND` |
| `everyio.agentwebforms.com` | actually attached (`AW-CustomDomains`) | **200** ✅ root + sub-pages |

`listDomains(jackie)` → `[]`; `listDomains(lyndi)` → `[everyio.agentwebforms.com]` — exactly why the member 404s and the owner doesn't. The same divergence affects the `story-with-ai-kids-books-store` project, confirming it's systemic to the pattern, not a one-off.

## Fix

`GET /generated` enrichment now treats the domain **attached to the Vercel project** (`AW-CustomDomains`) as authoritative:

- Lookups are scoped **per page owner** (gathered from each page's `userId`), not the caller — so org members resolve the same URL the owner sees.
- A stored **managed** subdomain (`*.agentwebforms.com`) that diverges from the attached one is **corrected**; a stored **verified custom domain** is left untouched.
- When a project has both a verified custom domain and a managed subdomain, the **custom domain is preferred**.

Exported `SUBDOMAIN_BASE` from `customDomainService` so the route can recognize managed subdomains.

Simulated against the live every.io records, the fix repoints the pages to `https://everyio.agentwebforms.com[/slug]`, which return **200**.

## Tests

- New cases: member sees owner-scoped enrichment; stale `*.agentwebforms.com` corrected to attached host; verified custom domain preferred and untouched; matching stored host kept as-is.
- `npx tsc` clean; **full backend suite green (11458 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed)**.

## Out of scope / follow-ups (operational — need prod access this cloud-dev role lacks)

- **Data backfill:** the fix corrects the URL at read time. Persisting the corrected `customDomainUrl`/`deployedUrl` back to `AW-LandingPages` (so other consumers — e.g. the agent engine, emails — also benefit) would need a one-off migration.
- **Two app-level 404s** on every.io: `…/every-io-day-zero-founders` and `…/every-io-seed-stage-founders` return `x-matched-path: /404` (the route files appear missing from the deployed app). This is a **separate, pre-existing** issue, not the subdomain mismatch fixed here.
- Why the subdomain detached in the first place (suspect: `removeDomain` cascade in `customDomainService.ts`) is worth a hardening follow-up so pages can't silently point at a detached host again.

title: feat: Google Ads integration
body:
## Summary

Adds a full **Google Ads integration** to AgentWeb — OAuth connection flow, a backend service wrapping the Google Ads REST API (v24), agent-mode tools, Emma tools, and subscription gating.

## What's included

**OAuth & connection** (`routes/googleAdsAuth.ts`, `config/integrations.ts`, `utils/secretsManager.ts`)
- OAuth init/callback/finalize/connect/disconnect flow
- `google_ads` PlatformType + Secrets Manager credential storage
- Correct `login-customer-id` header handling and refresh-token writes

**Service layer** (`services/googleAdsService.ts`, 818 lines)
- HTTP helper, auth, account listing
- Budget + campaign CRUD
- Ad group, keyword, and ad methods
- Assets, asset groups, Performance Max (PMax) with brand guidelines
- Reporting (`getQuickMetrics`, search) and negative keywords

**Agent & Emma tools** (`services/agentModeService.ts`, `emma/tools.ts`, `docs/agentModeSystemPrompt.ts`)
- `call_google_ads_api` + `call_google_ads_reporting_api` agent tools
- Schema synced with skill prompt
- Gemini client base-URL fix (OpenAI-compat)

**REST routes** (`routes/googleAds.ts`, registered in `app.ts`)

**Subscription gating** (`services/subscriptionService.ts`, `SubscriptionTypesTab.tsx`)

**Tests** — comprehensive coverage across service, routes, auth, tools, and secrets manager (`googleAdsService.test.ts` 818 lines, `googleAdsTools.test.ts` 516 lines, plus auth/routes/secrets tests).

**Docs** — design spec and Phase 1 implementation plan under `docs/plans/`.

## Google Cloud / Google Ads app setup (one-time)

These steps produce the `clientId`, `clientSecret`, and `developerToken` that go into the Secrets Manager secret below.

1. **Google Cloud project** — In the [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/), create or select a project for AgentWeb.
2. **Enable the Google Ads API** — *APIs & Services → Library →* search **"Google Ads API"** → **Enable**.
3. **OAuth consent screen** — *APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen.* Set user type (External), app name, and support email, then add the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords`. Add test users (or publish the app) so accounts can authorize.
4. **OAuth 2.0 Client ID + secret** — *APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID →* application type **Web application**. Add the authorized redirect URI (must match `${BACKEND_URL}/api/oauth/google-ads/callback`):
   - Dev: `http://localhost:3001/api/oauth/google-ads/callback`
   - Prod: `https://api.agentweb.pro/api/oauth/google-ads/callback`

   The created client yields the **`clientId`** and **`clientSecret`**.
5. **Developer token** — In a Google Ads **manager (MCC) account**: *Tools & Settings → Setup → API Center* → copy the **`developerToken`**. New tokens have Test-Account access only; apply for **Basic/Standard** access to call production accounts.
6. Store all three values in Secrets Manager (next section).

## Secrets Manager setup

The integration reads the Google Ads OAuth **app** credentials from AWS Secrets Manager at runtime (`getGoogleAdsCredentials` in `utils/secretsManager.ts`). Per-user OAuth access/refresh tokens are stored separately on the connected account, not here.

Create the secret in each environment **before** connecting an account:

- Dev: `dev/AgentWeb/Google/Ads`
- Prod: `prod/AgentWeb/Google/Ads`

Secret format (JSON string):

```json
{ "clientId": "...", "clientSecret": "...", "developerToken": "..." }
```

```bash
aws secretsmanager create-secret \
  --name dev/AgentWeb/Google/Ads \
  --secret-string '{"clientId":"...","clientSecret":"...","developerToken":"..."}'
# repeat with prod/AgentWeb/Google/Ads for production
```

If any of `clientId`, `clientSecret`, or `developerToken` is missing/empty, `getGoogleAdsCredentials` throws and Google Ads calls fail fast.

## Notes
- API version: Google Ads v24
- Manager-account support was removed to simplify the auth flow

title: fix(crm): HubSpot sync — pre-create non-standard props, default auto-sync ON
body:
## Summary

Fixes three related defects in the External CRM (HubSpot/Attio) sync, surfaced by a real failed push on a HubSpot lead list.

### 1. `notes` (non-standard) properties failed every push — `PROPERTY_DOESNT_EXIST`
`pushLeads` builds the contact payload from **both** `contactFieldMapping` and `customFieldMapping`, but the pre-create loop that calls `ensureContactProperty` only iterated `customFieldMapping`. Legacy configs place a non-standard property such as `notes` in `contactFieldMapping`, so it was pushed but never created → HubSpot rejected every lead carrying notes.

**Fix:** single `STANDARD_CONTACT_PROPS` source of truth; ensure any push-enabled non-standard property from **either** mapping list, de-duplicated.

### 2. New leads silently never auto-synced
A newly configured sync stored `autoSyncEnabled=false` unless the client explicitly sent `true`, while the setup UI defaults the toggle ON. A partial save (e.g. the side-effect save from Test Connection, which omits `autoSyncEnabled`) silently disabled auto-sync, so new/edited leads were never pushed.

**Fix:** default a brand-new config's `autoSyncEnabled` to `true`. Explicit `false` and existing stored values are still respected.

> Note: with the auto-sync default and the `notes` fix together, new leads (including those with notes) now actually deliver — previously they failed silently in `autoSyncLead`'s catch.

## Tests
- `externalCrmSync.service.test.ts`: non-standard property pre-creation (legacy `notes` in contactFieldMapping, standard props skipped, dedup, pull-only skipped); auto-sync default true / explicit false / partial-save preservation.
- Verified TDD: the legacy-`notes` test and the auto-sync-default test each fail on pre-fix code.

title: fix(coding-agent): confine landing-page edits to the targeted page
body:
## Problem

A user asked the coding agent (Emma's `coding_agent` sub-agent) to make **one** change — replace placeholder logos in the trust bar of a **single** landing page (page `109ff6bd-…`). Instead, the agent edited **6 files across multiple unrelated page variants** and made unrequested copy changes ("As seen in:" → "Backed by").

### Root cause

The coding agent operates on one `pageId`, but **many landing pages share a single GitHub repo**: each page is an `app/<slug>/` sub-route directory, and the root page owns the top-level `app/` files (`app/page.tsx`, `app/layout.tsx`, `components/`, …). Nothing constrained a run to its page:

1. The system prompt gave **no scope instruction**.
2. The pre-fetched `list_files` dumped the **entire repo** (every sibling page) into the agent's first message — inviting edits to other pages.
3. **No tool enforced a path boundary** — `edit_file`/`revert_file` accepted any path the model produced.

## Fix — defense in depth

Resolve each run's editable boundary (`PageScope`) from the page record + its repo siblings (the owner's other pages), then enforce it three ways in `codingAgentService.ts`:

1. **Filter** the pre-fetched file listing to the page's scope — the agent never even sees sibling files.
2. **Prompt** — append a strict scope clause naming the only directory it may touch, plus "make only the change asked for; do not relabel copy."
3. **Hard guard** (the real guarantee) — `executeTool` blocks out-of-scope `edit_file`/`revert_file` writes and returns a corrective message so the agent self-corrects. Reads stay unrestricted so it can still inspect shared code for context.

**Scope rules:** a sub-page may only edit `app/<slug>/**`; the root page may edit everything *except* sibling `app/<slug>/` dirs. Resolution is **best-effort** — if the page lookup fails, the run stays unrestricted rather than blocking all work (no behavior change for the existing path), so this is purely additive.

## Tests

- Pure helpers: `resolvePageScope`, `isPathInScope` (incl. prefix-collision `my-page` vs `my-page-2`, path normalization, sibling dedup), `filterFileListingToScope`, `buildScopeSystemClause`.
- Loop-level: out-of-scope edit is blocked with **no write** + corrective message fed back; in-scope edit goes through; listing filtered + scope clause injected into the system prompt; resolution-failure → unrestricted fallback.
- `npx tsc` clean. Full backend suite: **11,512 passed, 0 failed** (84 in `codingAgentService`, +14 new).

title: fix(landing-pages): survive transient v0 HTTP 500s during landing page generation
body:
## Problem

`generate_landing_page` was failing permanently with `HTTP 500: {"error":{"code":"500",...}}` whenever the v0 generation service returned a transient server error. The page record was created but no v0 chat was generated, so the page landed in `failed` status with `iterations=0`. Two consecutive attempts failed with distinct error IDs (`cTB9mKjrgTQzCHfFeqs7NpemR7MMsbQW`, `ts1CdfhB8odbI5zgrOHB9M9xbHyxXzdv`), pointing at a transient v0-side outage rather than a code-side request defect.

`deploy_landing_page` on the failed page returned `Landing page has no v0 chat — generate first`, confirming generation never produced a v0 chat — and there was no recovery path, so each retry orphaned a fresh failed record.

## Root cause

The v0 SDK throws `Error("HTTP <status>: <body>")` on any non-2xx response (`v0-sdk/dist/index.js:36`). `withRetry` in `v0Service.ts` only classified **network-level** failures (`fetch failed`, `ECONNREFUSED`, timeouts, socket hang-ups, etc.) as retryable — HTTP 5xx/429 were treated as fatal. So a transient v0 500 failed on the **first** attempt, and `generateFirstPage`'s catch block wrote `status:"failed"`, `iterations:0` with the raw message.

## Fix

1. **Retry transient HTTP 5xx / 408 / 429** in `withRetry`, reusing the existing exponential backoff (2s/4s/8s + jitter). HTTP 4xx client errors still fail fast (no point retrying a bad request/auth failure).
2. **Recycle failed records on retry.** `generateLandingPage` now reuses the newest prior first-page record that failed *before* a v0 chat existed (no `v0ChatId`, no `githubRepoUrl`, no `slug`) instead of minting a new UUID — so repeated retries reset that record to `generating` rather than piling up orphaned empty pages. Records that already have a `v0ChatId` (recoverable via deploy) are left untouched.

## Tests

- `v0Service.withRetry.test.ts`: retries on HTTP 500/502/503/429, fails fast on HTTP 4xx, exhausts retries on persistent 500.
- `services.v0Service.test.ts`: recycles a failed record with no v0 chat; does NOT recycle a failed record that already has a `v0ChatId`.
- `npx tsc` clean. Full v0 + landing-page suites: **255 tests passing**.

## Files
- `backend/src/services/v0Service.ts` — retry classification + record recycling
- `backend/src/__tests__/v0Service.withRetry.test.ts`, `backend/src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts` — tests
- `backend/src/docs/user-release.ts` — release note

title: fix(landing-pages): match Vercel build to pushed commit before marking deployed (404 bug)
body:
## Problem

Reported as *"1 landing page always get 404 in account demo@empathiaai.com"*. Forensics on that account's live site:

| Page | slug | DB status | Live URL |
|------|------|-----------|----------|
| Cardiology Demo (root) | — | deployed | **200** ✅ |
| PHSA re-engagement | `phsa-re-engagement` | deployed | **404** ❌ |
| infoway re-engagement | `infoway-re-engagement` | deployed | **404** ❌ |

Sub-pages live at `/{slug}` inside the site's shared GitHub repo + Vercel project. PHSA & infoway are marked `status: deployed` in DynamoDB, **but no commit for either route exists on `main`**, and Vercel has **zero production deployments** in the window they were marked deployed. They were flagged live against the *old root* build → permanent 404.

## Root cause — two code paths marked pages "deployed" against a stale build

1. **`pollVercelDeployment`** accepted the **newest** Vercel deployment (`limit=1&since=…`) as success without checking it was the build for the commit we just pushed. A stale build that predates the push (and lacks the new `app/<slug>/` route) was taken as a successful deploy.

2. **Auto-heal** (`getDeploymentStatus`, also used by the `GET /generated` list endpoint) promoted any `failed`/`deploying` page to `deployed` whenever the project's latest deployment was `READY` — again with no per-page route check. This could even *undo* fix #1 by re-healing a correctly-failed sub-page back to `deployed`.

## Fix

- **`pollVercelDeployment(projectId, token, sinceMs, expectedCommitSha?)`** — when a target commit is supplied, scan the last 10 deployments and only accept a `READY` one whose `meta.githubCommitSha` matches the commit we pushed. Both deploy paths thread the pushed SHA through (`addPageToExistingRepo` for sub-pages; `createGitHubRepoAndPush` → `createVercelProject` for first-page deploys). If the matching build never goes live, the page is marked `failed` (retryable) instead of falsely `deployed`.
- **`getDeploymentStatus`** — now probes the page's own public URL (`isLandingPageUrlLive`) and only heals to `deployed` when that URL resolves (2xx/3xx). When the project is `READY` but the page's route is not live, it returns `buildStatus: "route_not_live"` and leaves the record untouched. This closes the second path (and the list endpoint that calls it).

## Tests (TDD)

- `pollVercelDeployment`: FAIL test reproduces the bug (READY for a different/stale commit must not mark deployed → failed/timeout) + SUCCESS (ignore stale READY, accept once our commit's build is READY).
- `getDeploymentStatus`: FAIL test (project READY but sub-page URL 404s → stays failed, no DB write) + SUCCESS (URL resolves → healed).
- Verified both FAIL tests failed before their fix.
- `npx tsc` clean (`--max-old-space-size=6144`). All landing-page suites pass (212 tests): `services.v0Service`, `v0Service.withRetry`, `landingPageStaging`, `routes.landingPageGeneration`, `orgSharedLandingPages`.

## Rebased

Rebased onto latest `main` (picks up the merged v0 5xx/429 retry fix and coding-agent scope work); release-notes conflict resolved keeping all entries.

## Not covered (operational follow-up)

The empathiaai account's existing `phsa`/`infoway` records are already `deployed` but their v0-generated source was never committed to git, so they can't be repaired by code — the user must regenerate those two pages. This PR prevents *new* pages from entering that broken state and stops auto-heal from re-breaking them.

title: fix(meta): unwrap adimages response so distinct creatives get unique hashes
body:
## Problem

Reported for account `1358071355944019` (Every.io): Meta `UPLOAD_IMAGE` (`call_meta_marketing_api`, `entity_type=AD_CREATIVE`) returned **duplicate/scrambled image hashes** across visually distinct creatives (three different PNGs all returned `098be9e994ea4542532b5838a3b92910`), blocking a 12-creative lead-gen campaign.

## Root cause

Meta's `/adimages` endpoint returns the upload result **keyed by filename**:

```json
{ "images": { "<filename>": { "hash": "...", "url": "..." } } }
```

`metaService.uploadImage` returned the Facebook SDK's raw `adImage._data` — i.e. the **whole `images` map** — rather than the inner entry. `uploadMetaAdsImage` then wrapped that map and returned it to the agent with **no top-level hash**. Consequences:

1. The agent had to dig the hash out of a filename-keyed map itself; across a batch of 12 it mis-mapped hashes to the wrong creative ("scrambled"), and filename reuse/dedup collapsed distinct images onto one hash.
2. The three COPY_AD re-upload readers (`uploaded?.image_hash`) were **always `undefined`**, silently broken.
3. Tests mocked `{ _data: { hash } }` — a shape Meta never returns — so the suite stayed green while production was broken.

## Fix

- `metaService.uploadImage` now unwraps the single `images`-map entry into a flat `{ hash, url, ... }`, with a fallback to `_data` for already-flat responses.
- `uploadMetaAdsImage` surfaces top-level `image_hash`/`image_url`, and returns `success: false` with `NO_IMAGE_HASH` when Meta returns no hash (instead of a raw map). The three COPY_AD readers now resolve correctly with no further change.

## Tests

- Rewrote the two misleading mocks to Meta's real filename-keyed shape (these would fail against the old code).
- Added: distinct images → distinct hashes (no scrambling), flat-response fallback, and the `NO_IMAGE_HASH` failure path.
- `npx tsc` clean; all meta suites pass (62 + 66 tests).

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The intermittent `Invalid parameter` / no-response failures under parallel load likely stem from `FacebookAdsApi.init()` setting a **global static default API** that's re-initialized per call (`metaService.ts:75`). Hardening that singleton against concurrent token cross-talk is a larger, separate refactor — recommend tracking it separately.

title: fix(linkedin): post-accept follow-up draft now uses brand voice & message history
body:
## Problem

The LinkedIn **invite note** reads well, but the **suggested follow-up message draft** generated *after* a connection is accepted looked generic and low-quality.

## Root cause

The post-accept follow-up is generated by `generateConnectionFollowUpDraft()` in `linkedInConnectionSyncCron.ts`. It **does** fetch message/engagement history — so "does the draft consider message history?" → yes. But its other context was broken:

1. **Brand voice & market strategy were silently dropped.** The code read `brand.guidelines` and `strategy.strategy`, but `readBrandGuidelines()` / `readMarketStrategy()` return `{ exists, formattedContent }` — there is no `.guidelines` / `.strategy` field. Both conditions were always false, so the follow-up never received any brand voice or offer context. The invite note (which reads well) *does* get brand guidelines — that asymmetry was most of the quality gap.
2. **History had no direction.** The activity dump didn't distinguish messages *we sent* from ones *they sent*, so the model couldn't acknowledge a reply vs re-introduce itself.
3. **Thin prompt.** No banned-words list and no good/bad example, unlike the invite prompt.

## Fix

- Read `formattedContent` from the correct shape so brand/offer context actually reaches the prompt
- Label each engagement `You sent` / `They sent` and instruct the model to acknowledge replies
- Port the invite note's style into the follow-up prompt: lead with something specific, banned-words list, good/bad example

## Tests

Added 4 tests to `linkedInConnectionSync.notifyNewConnections.test.ts` (TDD — written failing first):
- brand voice from `formattedContent` reaches the prompt
- market strategy from `formattedContent` reaches the prompt
- brand/strategy lines omitted when neither exists
- sent vs received messages are labelled
- prompt includes banned-words list + good/bad example

All 18 tests in the suite pass; `npx tsc` clean.

title: fix(crm): backfill partial LinkedIn connection caches so already-connected leads aren't offered an invite
body:
## Problem

Lead **Ramesh Lakshminarayanan** (`rlakshminarayanan@cenlar.com`) in Jerry Shan's outreach list (`list_1775076744638_kc5hhkm9p`) showed a **Send LinkedIn Invite** button, but clicking it errored with *"already connected with this person."*

## Root cause (confirmed against live prod data)

The CRM decides whether to offer the invite from the **`AW-UnipileConnections` cache**, but the actual send does a **live Unipile `network_distance` check**. When the cache is missing a genuinely-connected lead, the two disagree → the UI offers the invite and the live send blocks it.

The list's LinkedIn account `QBdKa04gQLKTuKYEJuOLtA` (Jerry Shan) had **1,051 live connections but only 64 cached**. Ramesh (`/in/ramesh-lakshminarayanan-72657298`) was genuinely **FIRST_DEGREE** (connected 2026-04-12) but absent from the cache.

Why the cache was stranded: the earlier "empty cache → full sync" fix only backfills when the cache is **completely empty**. This account had a `__latest__` watermark set (from incremental polls), so the cron stayed on the 3-page (~60 newest) incremental path forever and **never backfilled** the ~987 older connections.

> The other two records the user mentioned — **Michael Hoare** (`mh@fluro.co.uk`) and a second Ramesh record (`/in/ramesh-lakshminarayanan-a73a9915`) — are actually **2nd-degree with live *pending* invitations** (sent 2026-05-03), which is correct/expected. Only the `-72657298` Ramesh was the genuine cache bug.

## Fix

1. **One-time backfill marker** — new `__fullsync__` sentinel row per account. `syncConnectionsForAccount` forces a full backfill until the marker is set (covering both empty *and* partial caches), then reverts to the cheap incremental poll.
2. **Self-heal** — when `checkIsNotAlreadyConnected` detects a live 1st-degree connection, it upserts that connection into the cache so the invite button disappears immediately, without waiting for the next sync.
3. **Immediate prod repair** — ran the new backfill script against `QBdKa04gQLKTuKYEJuOLtA`: cache went from **64 → 1,051** connections; Ramesh `-72657298` is now cached, so the button will no longer be offered.

## Tests

- `linkedInConnectionSync.partialCacheBackfill.test.ts` (new) — full-syncs partial caches, sets the marker, reverts to incremental, honours explicit `fullSync`.
- `linkedInConnectionSync.initialFullSync.test.ts` — updated to drive backfill off the marker.
- `linkedInOutreachService.test.ts` — self-heal on live already-connected, resilient when the cache write fails, no write for 2nd-degree.

All LinkedIn/unipile suites pass: **610 tests / 26 suites**. `npx tsc` clean.

title: fix(coding-agent): allow edits across all routes of a multi-route landing project
body:
## Problem (HIGH — reported by a customer)

A user (every.io, page \`109ff6bd-…\`) asked Emma's \`coding_agent\` to make a trivial one-block edit to a sibling route's file (\`app/every-io-series-a-scaling/_components/lead-capture-form.tsx\`). Earlier in the **same session** the agent had edited files across all three of the project's route directories. A later call then **hard-refused**: *"This session is scoped exclusively to \`app/every-io-day-zero-pre-seed-fou/\` … the system rejected the write attempt … underlying tool enforcement cannot be overridden."* Both line-edit and search/replace modes were blocked. The refusal was **inconsistent** (same file editable earlier) and **wrong** for a multi-route project.

### Root cause — PR #1739 modeled the data backwards

[PR #1739](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/1739) (merged 2026-06-02, one day before the report) added a per-route hard lockout assuming \`pageId\` ↔ a single \`app/<slug>/\` directory. But the data model is the opposite: **many \`AW-LandingPages\` records share ONE repo + Vercel project**. I confirmed this in DynamoDB for the reported project — 7 page records (1 root + 6 sub-routes) all sharing repo \`lp-every-io-day-zero-founders-438047a2\` and project \`prj_aODtNYNBkDWHaWYJjkJxMzNA8W39\`. So \`resolvePageScope\` marked the run a "sub-page" and treated every other route in the same project as an off-limits "sibling page."

The agent's file API is **already physically confined to the one repo behind its \`pageId\`**, so #1739's guard never prevented cross-*repo* edits — its only real effect was blocking legitimate cross-*route* edits **within one project**. The "intermittency" was #1739's best-effort fallback: when the page lookup failed, scope was \`undefined\` → unrestricted → edits went through; when it resolved → locked to one route.

A second latent bug: #1739 built \`siblingSlugs\` from \`getLandingPagesByOwner\` **without filtering by repo**, so an owner's pages in entirely separate repos were also treated as siblings.

## Fix — repo-wide scope (keep #1739's intent, drop the route lockout)

In \`backend/src/services/codingAgentService.ts\`:

1. **\`PageScope\`** is now the run's repo: \`{ repoUrl, routeSlugs }\` (route slugs are informational, for the prompt).
2. **\`resolvePageScope\`** groups route slugs by **shared \`githubRepoUrl\`** — fixing the cross-repo "sibling" bug.
3. **\`isPathInScope\` → \`isSafeRepoPath\`**: any in-repo path is editable; only paths that **escape the repo** (absolute or \`../\` traversal) are rejected. The \`executeTool\` write guard now applies this safety check unconditionally.
4. **File listing** is no longer filtered — the agent sees the whole repo (all routes + shared files), as it should for a multi-route project.
5. **System prompt** names all of the project's routes and **keeps #1739's soft anti-overreach guidance** ("make ONLY the specific change asked for") — without hard-locking routes.

Resolution stays best-effort (missing page → unrestricted), so this is purely additive over the existing path.

## Tests

Reworked the page-scope unit + loop tests for repo-wide semantics: \`resolvePageScope\` groups by repo (ignoring other repos), \`isSafeRepoPath\` allows own + sibling routes + shared files and rejects \`../\`/absolute escapes, \`buildScopeSystemClause\` lists routes + keeps the guidance. Loop-level: **a sibling-route edit in the same repo now goes through (regression test for the report)**, own-dir edit still works, a repo-escaping write is blocked with a corrective message, the full repo listing is shown unfiltered, and a missing page record still falls back to unrestricted editing.

- \`npx tsc\` clean. Full backend suite: **11,574 passed, 0 failed** (3 pre-existing skips).

## Manual verification (browser, against test account's multi-route site)

Drove Emma in the customer portal against \`test@example.com\`'s \`lp-taskflow-landing\` project (1 root + 6 sub-routes, one repo). Opened a session on the **About Us** page and asked it to edit a **sibling route**. The \`coding_agent\` saw the full repo listing (all sibling routes), committed \`{/* qa-scope-check */}\` to **\`app/retryfix-demo/page.tsx\`** on a staging branch (\`draft/…\`), and the Vercel build succeeded — **no scope refusal**, exactly one file touched. Verified the commit on GitHub, then cleaned up the draft branch + PR. Under #1739 this cross-route edit would have been hard-blocked.

title: fix(crm): LinkedIn acceptance notifications — restore, gate on sender, drop Slack, suppress backfill flood
body:
## Summary

Fixes the LinkedIn "invitation accepted" notification flow on three axes, **plus the root cause of a production notification flood** observed on 2026-06-03.

### 1. "Stopped sending" bug — trailing-slash URL mismatch
`notifyNewConnections` looked up leads with the connection's slash-normalized URL (`.../in/john/`), but leads store `linkedin` **without** a trailing slash. The exact `LinkedinLookupIndex` GSI match never hit → no email. **Fix:** query both slash/no-slash variants (deduped) via `findLeadsForConnectionUrl`.

### 2. Slack should not fire
`notifyLinkedInConnectionAccepted` posted to Slack whenever the owner had a `slackChannel`. **Fix:** acceptance alerts are now email-only. (Generic lead-list alerts still use Slack.)

### 3. Gate on assigned LinkedIn sender (lead-list level)
**Fix:** notify only when `list.linkedInAccountId` is set **and** equals the connection's `accountId`.

### 4. 🚨 Root cause of the notification flood — initial-backfill suppression
**Production incident (2026-06-03 16:33–16:42 UTC):** a Unipile account's first-ever sync backfilled 3,447 historical connections; `notifyNewConnections` treated each as freshly accepted and sent ~86 emails (+Slack) to one owner (`murray.newlands@gmail.com`) for a 132k-lead list with **no sender assigned**. (Not from this branch — pre-existing `main` behavior; it self-terminated once the watermark advanced.)

**Fix:** `runLinkedInConnectionSync` checks the watermark **before** syncing each account; on an empty-cache initial backfill it caches connections silently and skips **both** notification and enrollment. Combined with the sender gate, this list would have sent **zero** emails.

## Tests
- `linkedInConnectionSync.notifyNewConnections.test.ts` — slash-variant matching, variant dedup, sender-gate; mock now mirrors real trailing-slash normalization.
- `leadListAlertService.linkedInConnectionAccepted.test.ts` — asserts Slack is never called.
- `linkedInConnectionSync.initialBackfillNoNotify.test.ts` — asserts initial backfill caches silently (no notify/enroll) while a populated cache processes new connections normally.

641 tests across `linkedIn*`/`leadListAlert*` pass. `tsc` clean.

## Notes
- User release notes added for 2026-06-03.
- Investigation + incident write-up in `dev.md`.

title: fix(meta): auto-resize oversized ad images and surface real upload errors
body:
## Problem

Uploading ad images to Meta via `call_meta_marketing_api` (`entity_type=AD_CREATIVE`, `action=UPLOAD_IMAGE`) failed for images larger than Meta's accepted dimensions, returning an unhelpful generic error:

```json
{"success":false,"message":"Invalid parameter","error":"Invalid parameter"}
```

**Root cause:** source PNGs were 4096×4096. Meta's image-ad upload rejects oversized images; 2048×2048 versions uploaded fine. Reported on account `act_1358071355944019` (Every.io) — 6 of 12 creatives (all 4096px) failed identically on retry.

## Fix

**Primary — auto-resize (`backend/src/services/metaService.ts`):**
- New `resizeImageForMeta(buffer, filename)` (uses `sharp`, already a dependency).
- Downscales the longest side to ≤1936px (`fit: inside`, aspect ratio preserved, never enlarged) and keeps the encoded asset < 8MB before upload.
- PNGs stay PNG (preserves logo transparency); falls back to JPEG only if a re-encoded PNG is still over the byte cap. JPEGs drop quality progressively (90→75→60→45→30) until under the cap.
- If `sharp` is unavailable or throws, the original buffer is uploaded so the call still attempts (logged, non-fatal).
- `uploadImage` calls this up front.

**Secondary — error surfacing (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`):**
- `uploadMetaAdsImage` now reads the `structuredError` that `metaService.handleError` attaches (`code`, `error_subcode`, `error_user_msg`, …), appends the user-facing reason to `message`, and returns a `meta_error` field — so callers see Meta's actual reason instead of bare "Invalid parameter".

## Tests

- New `metaService.imageResize.test.ts` (9 tests): passthrough within limits, 4096px PNG downscale, PNG→JPEG fallback over 8MB, too-heavy-but-in-dimension re-encode, progressive JPEG quality drop, quality-floor loop exit, non-error throw, sharp-failure fallback, missing-metadata.
- Extended `agentModeService.metaAdvanced.test.ts` (+1): structured-error surfacing.
- `resizeImageForMeta` is fully branch-covered.

title: fix(scheduled-chat): auto-pause schedules whose owning user no longer exists
body:
## Problem

A scheduled chat (e.g. *"Website Scan: sentriq.io"*, schedule `079f2863-af06-4760-b324-4ec87e6df52e`) threw on every execution:

```
User not found: 23635a2a-5715-41e4-9826-71471a19f03f
```

The schedule's owning user had been deleted, but the schedule remained `active`. On each run, `runScheduledChat` → `checkTokenUsage` → `getUserTokenUsage` looked up the user and threw `User not found`, which surfaced as an unhandled error, fired an oncall alert, and left the schedule firing forever.

## Fix

Added an owner-existence guard at the top of `runScheduledChat` (`backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts`):

- Looks up the schedule owner up front.
- If the user no longer exists, **auto-pauses the schedule** (`status: 'paused'`, the same state used by the existing runCount auto-pause) so it stops firing.
- Returns a graceful `failure` run result (recorded via `addRunResult` for UI visibility) instead of throwing.
- **Test runs** (`isTest = true`) do not mutate the schedule's status.

## Tests

- `agentModeController.scheduledChat.test.ts`: new cases asserting auto-pause + graceful failure on missing user, and that test runs do not pause.
- `agentModeService.scheduledChatAdminTools.test.ts`: added a default admin `getUserById` mock so its schedules satisfy the new owner-existence guard.

title: fix(meta): creative swap on AD UPDATE actually changes the ad
body:
## Problem

Reported by Juan Burgos (juan@usehaven.ai), Priority: High. Session `b3ec70ac-50e4-4079-96f5-6e6c17329352`.

Updating an existing Meta ad's creative via `AD UPDATE` with a new `creative_id` returned `{success: true, message: 'Ad updated successfully'}`, but the old image kept showing in Ads Manager. Reproduced on ad IDs `120245416959310173` (M4) and `120245416959300173` (M7).

## Root cause

`updateMetaAdsAd` (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`) classifies params into a creative-swap path (triggered by `link_url`, `body`, `image_hash`, etc.) vs. a standard ad-level update. `creative_id` was in *neither* list, so a directly-supplied `creative_id` fell through to the standard path and was sent to Meta's `POST /{ad-id}` endpoint **unnested**, as a top-level `creative_id`.

Meta only honors the creative when it is nested as `{ creative: { creative_id } }` (the same shape `createAd` and the existing swap path already use). A top-level `creative_id` is **silently ignored** — the API returns success but the ad keeps its old creative. That exactly matches the report.

The suspected "delete and recreate the ad" workaround is **not** required — nesting the field fixes it on the same ad ID.

## Fix

- `updateMetaAdsAd` now detects a directly-supplied `creative_id` and issues it as `{ creative: { creative_id } }`, applying any other ad-level params (e.g. `status`, `name`) in a separate update. Returns `new_creative_id` in the result.
- Tool description (`emma/tools.ts`) now documents that `AD UPDATE` accepts `creative_id` to swap to a pre-built creative, and that changing an ad's image does not require delete-and-recreate.
- Release note added for 2026-06-03.

## Tests

Added two cases to `agentModeService.metaAdsCRUD.test.ts`:
- nests a directly-supplied `creative_id` (and asserts a bare top-level `creative_id` is never sent)
- applies an ad-level `status` change alongside a direct `creative_id` swap

body:
## Summary

Lets **Emma** (the in-app sidebar / customer-portal assistant) work with work plans the way Agent Mode does — both *following* an active plan and *launching* a predefined template — entirely from chat.

Two related capabilities:

### 1. Emma follows an active work plan
`chatbotService.generateChatResponse` now injects the session's active work plan into the LLM context (via the reusable `AgentModeService.buildWorkPlanContextMessages()`, extracted from `buildMarketingContext`). Previously Emma was blind to an existing plan; now she lists the steps, advances step status, and resumes across turns.

### 2. Emma can launch a predefined work plan template
- **`applyPredefinedWorkPlan()`** (agentModeService) — resolves a template by title/planId (honoring system/public/private visibility), copies its steps into `session.workPlan` as pending, auto-installs the skills the plan needs, carries welcome/autocomplete through, and applies the plan's default model when supported. Refuses to clobber an active plan unless `force=true`.
- **`list_predefined_work_plans` is now role-aware**: non-admins get the published/launchable set (system/public + their own/org private) via the public agent-mode route; admins / admin-delegated sessions keep the full management list. (Removed from `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES`.)
- New **`launch_predefined_work_plan`** Emma tool; both listing/launch tools added to `FOUNDATION_TOOLS`.

### Tool-availability plumbing (required for launched plans to run)
Emma's tool set previously ignored installed skills and plan step requirements. `generateChatResponse` now additively expands `toolsToInclude` with (a) tools from `session.associatedSkills` and (b) the active plan steps' `requiredFunctionCalls` — so a launched plan's steps (e.g. `generate_landing_page`) can actually execute.

title: fix(scoring): skip in-flight sessions with no assistant turn
body:
## Problem

A scheduled **Daily Satisfaction Score Report** run (session `a2f98bd8-d936-48ce-87db-8443f03c67a9`) terminated with no assistant output and scored **1/5 across all judges**. The bug report diagnosed this as a crash/OOM/timeout, but that was a misdiagnosis — there was no crash.

## Root cause: self-referential scoring race

The report job runs the `get_chat_history` tool with `sync=true` over a window ending at "now". The sync block in `routes/admin.ts` scores **every** session in that window via `scoreSessionIfNeeded` / `scoreSessionWithJudgeIfNeeded`.

The report's **own session** falls inside that window. Scheduled/agent runs persist the injected user prompt immediately at session creation, but the assistant response is only saved **after** the run completes (`agentModeController.ts`). So the sync pass observes the report's session as just `[system, user]` — a user prompt with no reply yet — and scores it 1/5. The only gate was `userMessages >= 1`; nothing checked that an assistant response existed.

## Fix

Add a `hasAssistantTurn()` check to both `scoreSessionIfNeeded` and `scoreSessionWithJudgeIfNeeded`: a session is only scored once the model has actually responded (text **or** a tool call).

**Distinguishing in-flight from crashed.** A turn-less session is *either* still running *or* it crashed before producing output — indistinguishable from the message shape alone (there is no status field on `ChatSession`). We use **staleness** via `updatedAt`:

| State | assistant turn? | `updatedAt` age | action |
|---|---|---|---|
| In-flight | no | within 60-min grace window | skip — scored on a later pass once it has run |
| Crashed/stalled | no | older than 60 min | score **1/5** as a failed run (deterministic, no LLM call) |

The 60-minute grace window sits comfortably above any plausible scheduled-run duration, so a slow-but-healthy run is never misread as a crash. A missing/invalid `updatedAt` is treated as failed so such a session is never skipped forever. This closes the gap where a genuine crash would otherwise be silently dropped from satisfaction reporting — and protects any *other* session mid-flight in the sync window, not just the self-referential case.

## Tests

`sessionScoring.inProgressSession.test.ts` (9 tests), using timestamps relative to `now` so the grace window is exercised deterministically:
- **in-flight (recent):** default + judge scoring skipped; empty assistant message skipped
- **stale/failed:** scored 1/5 across all dimensions for both default and judge scoring, with no LLM call but the failure persisted; missing `updatedAt` also treated as failed
- **has assistant turn:** scores normally on content (text and tool-call-only turns), regardless of age

All 11,697 backend tests pass; `npx tsc` and `npm run build` clean. (Coverage scope is `src/utils/**` only and CI runs with the threshold disabled — this `services/` change does not affect the gate.)

title: fix: materialize perform_data_analysis file_urls in code-exec sandbox + upgrade model
body:
## Problem

`perform_data_analysis` (Node-only; `agentModeService.performDataAnalysis`) sent each file from `file_urls` to Gemini's `code_execution` sandbox as an `inlineData` part with `mimeType: application/json` (for `.json`) or `text/plain` (for other types). When asked to analyze large S3-backed tool-response files (e.g. a daily token/cost report over `get_chat_history` + `list_all_clients`), the files never appeared in the sandbox filesystem. The model fell back to re-pasting the JSON inline, truncated the large payloads, and produced **inconsistent, untrustworthy totals** (the same report returned `$673.74` in one run and `$458.74` in another; category breakdowns didn't reconcile; one hardened run timed out).

## Root cause (verified empirically against the live Gemini API)

The determinant is **MIME type + model**, not inline-vs-Files-API:

| What was sent | Live API result |
|---|---|
| `application/json` | ❌ **HTTP 400** "mime type application/json is not supported for code execution" |
| `text/plain` | ⚠️ Accepted but **silently NOT written to disk** → model can't `open()` → inlines & truncates |
| `text/csv` | ✅ Materialized at `/root/input_file_<n>.csv` (`SANDBOX_INPUT_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY=/root`) |
| model `gemini-2.5-flash` (old default) | ⚠️ intermittent **HTTP 500** on valid payloads |
| model `gemini-3-pro-preview` | ❌ **HTTP 404** "no longer available" |
| model `gemini-3.5-flash` | ✅ reliable; Google's documented code-exec model |

So the earlier "inline parts never hit the filesystem" theory was wrong — `text/csv` parts *do* materialize. The bug was the JSON/text MIME types plus a flaky model default.

## Fix

- **Send every file part as `text/csv`** so it materializes on disk regardless of real content type. JSON/text content inside a `.csv`-named file reads + `json.loads()` fine; the model is told the contents may be CSV/JSON/JSONL/text.
- **Tell the model the exact on-disk filenames** (`input_file_0.csv`, `input_file_1.csv`, …) and that it MUST read them from disk as the complete dataset rather than relying on possibly-truncated inline data.
- **Default model `gemini-2.5-flash` → `gemini-3.5-flash`** (override still honored via `DATA_ANALYSIS_LLM_NAME`).

## Verification

- **Unit tests:** 8 new tests (mime forced to `text/csv` for `.json`/`.txt`, filename manifest `input_file_0/1.csv`, model default + override). Full `agentModeService` suite: **1445 passing**. `npx tsc` clean.
- **Live API e2e:** two JSON files via `file_urls` → grand total matched expected **exactly**, per-category breakdown reconciled to the total.
- **Real session in browser (dev):** copied the reported prod session (`0c7cfa43-…`, "Daily Token Usage & Cost Report — Analysis failed") to dev and re-ran. Emma confirmed: *"the analysis read the files from disk … input_file_0.csv and input_file_1.csv … No JSON was inlined. It parsed 65 sessions and 309 clients."* Single consistent **Grand Total Cost: $525.19** (vs the broken run's $673.74 / $458.74).

title: fix(mcp): enable_lead_list_public_access hits the endpoint that actually persists the flag
body:
## Summary

Fixes the bug report: `enable_lead_list_public_access` returns `API error (403): Access denied`, blocking public landing-page lead capture.

Investigation surfaced **two distinct problems** — one a real code bug, one a data/ownership issue:

### Issue A — code bug (fixed here)
The tool issued `PUT /api/crm/lists/:listId` with `{ publicAccessEnabled: true }`. That generic list-update route (`crm.ts:1311`) destructures a **fixed allow-list** of fields, and `publicAccessEnabled` is **not** in it — so the flag was silently dropped and never persisted. On a list the caller *does* own, the tool would return 200 but **no-op**.

The fix points the tool at the dedicated `PUT /api/crm/lists/:listId/public-access` route (`crm.ts:5162`) with `{ enabled: true }` — the handler that actually writes the flag.

### Issue B — the reported 403 (data, not code — no fix needed)
Confirmed against DynamoDB. List `list_1780588875317_fyxi8vves` is owned by `userId 0d53ae05-…` (`demo@opsera.com`, no orgId). The reporter (harsha, `userId 1743956381327`, a different org) is **not** the owner and shares no org, so `canAccessCrmList` correctly returns 403 — this is working-as-intended IDOR protection, even for admins. The list was created via a direct `AW-LeadLists` table write that set a different owner, exactly as the report suspected.

**Note:** the list now already has `publicAccessEnabled: true`, and the public capture endpoint (`crmPublic.ts:162`) gates only on that flag (no ownership check), so **the funnel capture step is already unblocked** regardless of Issue B. To self-serve via the tool in future, the list must be owned by (or org-shared with) the calling account.

## Changes
- `backend/src/mcp/server/apiTools.ts` — route `enable_lead_list_public_access` to `PUT /api/crm/lists/:id/public-access` with `{ enabled: true }`.
- `backend/src/__tests__/mcp.apiTools.test.ts` — 3 tests: correct endpoint/body, never the generic route, and 403 propagation.

title: fix(webhooks): auto-enroll public forward-lead captures into drip sequences
body:
## Problem

The public `forward-lead` webhook (`backend/src/routes/webhooks.ts`) saves captured leads but never enrolls them into list-bound drip sequences. Leads captured through a landing-page form were never enrolled, even when an active sequence had that list in `autoEnrollListIds` / `enrollmentTrigger.type = 'list_membership'`. The first sequence step (e.g. the "here's your PDF" email) never fired for public form leads — only manually/quick-added leads (the authenticated path) got enrolled.

**Root cause:** The authenticated path in `src/routes/crm.ts` (~L1949) calls `autoEnrollLeadInSequences(...)` inside `Promise.allSettled([...])` after `createLead`. The public path in `webhooks.ts` only ran auto-draft / auto-send / lead-list alert in its fire-and-forget block and never invoked enrollment.

## Fix

Mirror the CRM path: add an `autoEnrollLeadInSequences` helper to `webhooks.ts` (identical to the one in `crm.ts`) and call it in the `if (isNew || isUpdated)` fire-and-forget block, using the **list owner's** `userId` since the public webhook request is unauthenticated. Errors are logged and swallowed so enrollment never affects the API response.

Per-list sequence capability (`autoEnrollListIds`, `getSequencesByAutoEnrollList`, `list_membership` trigger) already worked — the only gap was the public webhook not invoking enroll.

## Tests

Added an "Auto-enroll into list-bound drip sequences" block to `webhooks.leadForwarding.test.ts`:
- enrolls a newly created public-form lead into a watching sequence
- enrolls an updated existing lead
- does not call `bulkEnroll` when no sequences watch the list
- does not enroll when the lead exists with no changes (`lead.unchanged`)
- does not fail the request when enrollment throws

All 26 tests in the suite pass (53 across all webhook suites). `npx tsc` is clean.

Reported by Harsha. Compounds with AGW-37509247 (`enable_lead_list_public_access` 403) — both block the AI Readiness lead-magnet funnel.

title: feat(meta): per-placement image asset customization (asset_feed_spec)
body:
## Problem

`call_meta_marketing_api`'s `AD_CREATIVE CREATE` only reliably supported a single image (`image_hash`/`image_url`) per creative. It could not build a creative with **placement-level asset customization** — mapping different images to different placements within one creative (e.g. a 1:1 square image for Feed and a 9:16 vertical image for Stories/Reels) via Meta's `asset_feed_spec` / `asset_customization_rules`.

When an ad set switches to manual placements that include Stories & Reels, any ad whose creative only has a feed-format (square/4:5) image throws Meta's *"invalid format / lacking 9:16 for story and reel"* error and gets auto-paused. The correct fix is to attach a vertical 9:16 asset for Stories/Reels while keeping the square image for Feed — in the same ad/creative. Previously this could only be done manually in Ads Manager (Media → Edit per placement).

## What changed

A new `placement_assets` creative type (mutually exclusive with `video_id` and `carousel_cards`):

```jsonc
placement_assets: [
  { image_hash: "<square>",   is_default: true },                 // fallback (Feed)
  { image_hash: "<vertical>", placements: ["story", "reels"] }    // 9:16 for Stories/Reels
]
```

- **`metaService.ts`** — `MetaPlacementAsset` type, a friendly placement-token → `customization_spec` map (`feed`, `story`/`stories`, `reels`, `instagram_reels`, …), `validatePlacementAssets`, and `createPlacementCustomizedCreative` which builds the `asset_feed_spec` (`images` + `adlabels`, `asset_customization_rules` with scoped/`is_default` rules, `bodies`/`titles`/`link_urls`/`ad_formats`/`call_to_action_types`) alongside `object_story_spec`.
- **`agentModeService.ts`** — `resolvePlacementAssetHashes` uploads any `image_url` assets to hashes (`asset_feed_spec.images` requires hashes), wired into both `AD_CREATIVE CREATE` and the `AD UPDATE` creative-swap path. `placement_assets` added to `CREATIVE_CONTENT_KEYS`, and the swap carries over body/title/link/CTA from the existing creative so the **same `ad_id`** is pointed at the new multi-placement creative — no UI.
- **`tools.ts`** — `placement_assets` input schema + tool-description guidance (including the "fix an existing ad" flow).

title: feat(crm): scalable 'accepted-but-not-followed-up' LinkedIn lead finder
body:
## Problem

Identifying leads that **accepted a LinkedIn invite but still need a follow-up** required calling `get_lead_details` individually for every lead, because the list-level tools (`get_leads` / `search_leads`) don't return connection status, engagement direction (inbound vs outbound), or last-engagement timing. This is an N+1 pattern that's infeasible for realistic 200–1000 lead lists — slow, token-expensive, and it blows the per-call lead caps.

## Fix

Adds a dedicated list-level tool **`get_leads_needing_followup(list_id)`** (proposed fix #3) that returns the pre-computed cohort in a **constant number of queries** instead of per-lead fan-out.

All cross-lead signal is loaded once, up front:
- `getAllConnectionsByAccount(accountId)` → who is connected + `connectedAt`
- `getEventsByEmailDomain(`linkedin-{listId}`)` → LinkedIn message direction/timestamps
- `getEventsByEmailDomain(userEmailDomain)` → email message direction/timestamps

Leads are then segmented in memory. A lead qualifies as "needs follow-up" when it is a 1st-degree connection (invite accepted) **and** the most recent message is not an outbound touch sent after `connectedAt` — i.e. we never followed up post-accept, or they replied and we owe a response (`awaitingReply: true`).

Each returned lead carries the signal fields the report asked for:
`linkedInConnectionStatus { isConnected, connectedAt, connectedAtTimestamp }`, `lastEngagementType`, `lastEngagementDirection` (inbound/outbound), `lastEngagementAt`, `awaitingReply`. The response also reports `scannedLeads` / `scannedAllLeads` so the agent knows whether the whole list was covered.

The existing `get_leads` / `search_leads` / `get_lead_details` contracts are untouched.

## Tests

New suite `agentModeService.getLeadsNeedingFollowup.test.ts` (10 cases): access checks, missing LinkedIn account, **no N+1 (asserts constant query count)**, accepted-not-contacted detection, exclusion of unconnected and already-followed-up leads, `awaitingReply` on inbound reply, limit, and graceful error handling.

- Full backend suite: **11,878 passed, 0 failed** (3 skipped)

title: fix(crm): allow org members to configure external CRM sync on shared lists
body:
## Problem

Org user `jpruter@every.io` opened a teammate's lead list (`Every Leads`, `listId=list_1775599551252_w6uvjg07x`), clicked **External CRM sync → HubSpot**, and got:

> Failed to load your sync configuration. Your saved settings are intact.

## Root cause

The external CRM sync endpoints (`backend/src/routes/crmSync.ts`) gated every operation behind an **owner-only** check:

```ts
if ((list as any).userId !== userId) return { ok: false, status: 403, error: 'Access denied' };
```

The list is owned by `lyndi@every.io`; `jpruter` is a **different member of the same org** (both `orgId=3d196bb2-…`, confirmed in prod DynamoDB). So the `GET /api/crm-sync/config/:listId/:provider` request returned **403**, which the frontend catches and renders as the generic "Failed to load your sync configuration" error.

This was inconsistent with the rest of the CRM API: `crm.ts` already shares lead lists across org members via `canAccessCrmList()`. A second, identical owner-only gate also existed in the service layer (`externalCrmSyncService.getConfig` returned `null` when `config.userId !== userId`), which would have hidden a teammate's saved config even past the route.

## Fix

Make both gates org-aware, mirroring the existing `canAccessCrmList()` pattern:

- **`routes/crmSync.ts` — `verifyListOwnership`**: grant access when the requester owns the list **or** shares an org with the owner. This covers all sync endpoints (config get/save/delete, test, push, pull, property/pipeline discovery, delete-lead).
- **`services/externalCrmSyncService.ts` — `getConfig`**: same org-aware check before returning a config.

Encrypted API keys remain usable by any org member because the AES key is derived from `JWT_SECRET` (the stored `userId` is only an embedded signature, not required for decryption), so push/pull/test work for the teammate too.

## Tests

- `crmSync.routes.test.ts`: org member can GET/PUT config on a teammate's list (200); different-org and no-org users are denied (403).

title: fix(crm-enrichment): resolve LinkedIn-only leads via Unipile getProfile in identity resolution
body:
## Problem

Leads imported into a CRM list with **only a LinkedIn URL** (no name/email/company) that Apollo can't match were being **silently dropped**. In a 68-lead benchmark run, 7 leads were skipped with no data.

Root cause (confirmed via live test-server logs): identity resolution ends with a person-completeness gate that requires a first/last name. For a LinkedIn-only lead the *only* name source there is Apollo-match-by-LinkedIn; when Apollo has no record, the gate returns `ok=false` and the lead is skipped **before the waterfall runs** — so the Unipile `getProfile(linkedin)` call (waterfall tier 3.5b) that resolves name/title/company directly from the URL never executes. Unipile itself works fine (it HIT 14/14 times whenever reached).

## Fix

Wire **Unipile `getProfile(linkedin)` into the identity resolver** as a new step (3.5): when a LinkedIn `/in/` URL is present but first/last name is still missing after Apollo, resolve name/title/company from the URL **before** the completeness gate. Mirrors `findUnipilePerson` Case A (account resolution + 429 rotation across connected accounts).

- `enrichmentIdentityResolver.ts` — new optional `findUnipileProfileByUrl` dep + step 3.5

title: fix(agent): logo regeneration on matching background for newsletter/composite output
body: ## Problem Across multiple sessions (systemic pattern, score 3), the agent could not reliably handle a logo with a solid background when placing it on a colored/gradient surface (e.g. a newsletter header). Reproducing an affected session showed the deeper issue: a transparent PNG **renders against a black/white backing in the chat preview**, so the model can't visually confirm transparency — it second-guesses correct results, and either stops to ask the user to re-export or produces a logo with a visible box on the gradient. ## Approach An earlier iteration of this PR added a programmatic background-removal pipeline (alpha analysis + flood-fill chroma-key + a `remove_logo_background` tool). In testing, the model still distrusted the (correct) "already transparent" verdict because the preview looked black-backed — so the root failure persisted. **That entire pipeline was reverted.** This PR instead fixes the behavior via the **agent system prompt** (`backend/src/docs/agentModeSystemPrompt.ts`), adding a "Logo Backgrounds" section that instructs the agent to: - **Match the logo's background to its destination** — when a logo needs to look seamless on a colored/gradient surface, regenerate it with `generate_image` using that *exact* background (same hex for solid sections; same gradient stops + direction for headers), passing the logo via `logo_image`. The logo then blends in with no visible box, sidestepping transparency entirely. - Generate **one version per surface** when the same logo appears on multiple backgrounds (e.g. gradient header + dark footer). - Prefer this over asking the user to re-export a transparent file. - For HTML/newsletter output, read the destination background straight from the CSS behind the logo's `` and reuse those exact color values. Also fixes outdated prompt guidance that told the agent to pass logos via `inputImages` (correct param is `logo_image`). ## Verification - `npx tsc` clean. - **Browser test against the reproduced session** (copied to dev, tested in customer portal, cleaned up): given a logo "with a solid box that clashes with the header," the agent generated a logo with the **exact gradient baked into its background** for the header and a white logo on solid `#1a1a2e` for the footer, then **delivered the updated HTML (`_v7.html`) without stopping for permission**. Its only question was a genuine ambiguity (header had changed from gradient to solid blue across revisions). Final message: *"The logo image has that exact same gradient baked into its background … no visible box … the logo's background and the bar's gradient are identical, so they blend invisibly."* ## Net change Two commits: the system-prompt instruction + a user release note. No production code paths or tests changed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(crm): skip leads with invalid email during HubSpot sync
body:
## Problem

Syncing a lead list to HubSpot reported an error like:

> `https://superdm.me/chessbaseindia: Property values were not valid: {"isValid":false,"message":"Email address https://superdm.me/chessbaseindia is invalid","error":"INVALID_EMAIL","name":"email"}`

(Reported for list `list_1775599551252_w6uvjg07`.)

## Root cause

In `HubspotAdapter.pushLeads`, the only guard before upserting was `if (!lead.email) continue;` — a presence check, not a format check. When a lead's `email` field actually held a non-email value (a profile/social URL), it was passed straight to HubSpot's `email` property, which HubSpot rejects with `INVALID_EMAIL`. That surfaced as a per-lead sync error.

## Fix

`backend/src/services/adapters/hubspotAdapter.ts`:
- Trim the email and reuse the existing `validateEmail` util (`src/utils/validation.ts`).
- If the value isn't a valid email, increment `errorCount` and push a clear per-lead message (`Invalid email "…" — skipped (not a valid email address)`), then `continue` — the rest of the batch still syncs.
- Whitespace-only / empty emails are treated as missing (skipped silently, as before).

## Tests

`backend/src/__tests__/hubspotAdapter.pushLeads.test.ts` (new, 5 cases):
- URL-in-email → skipped, error recorded, no upsert attempted
- malformed email (no domain) → skipped with error
- whitespace-only email → skipped, no error
- valid email → still upserted
- mixed batch → valid leads sync, invalid one is isolated

All 135 tests across the hubspot/crm suites pass; `npx tsc` clean.

## Release notes

Added a user-facing "Fixed" entry to `backend/src/docs/user-release.ts`.

title: fix(scoring): don't penalize judge for flagged brand/topic mismatch
body:
## Problem

A satisfaction-judge false-negative pattern flagged across 3 sessions (Webinar follow-up email, Sustainable Packaging LinkedIn post, Budgeting App ad analysis). When the requested content topic doesn't match the stored brand guidelines, the agent **correctly** flags the mismatch and either asks a clarifying question or proceeds with placeholders. This is the *desired* behavior — but the judge was scoring these sessions 2–3 (low `goalCompletion`), treating the flag/clarification as a failure.

The fix is **not** to change agent behavior (it's good), but to teach the judge that flagging a mismatch is correct.

## Change

Add a "Brand / topic mismatch" clause to `DEFAULT_SCORING_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in `sessionScoringService.ts`:
- Flagging a mismatch, asking one clarifying question, or proceeding with placeholders (`[Brand Name]`, `[URL]`) is expected helpful behavior, not a failure → score ≥ 4.
- A clarifying question about the mismatch is **not** counted as the user "having to repeat themselves".
- The score is only lowered when the assistant **repeatedly refuses to produce any usable output** after the user has clearly pushed back.

## Tests

Added 4 assertions to `sessionScoring.bugReported.test.ts` covering the new clause. Full suite passes (13/13). `npx tsc` clean.

title: fix(crm): sync email-less leads to HubSpot
body:
## Problem

When a lead's email field was empty, the HubSpot sync **silently skipped** it — the lead never made it into HubSpot, with no error or feedback. This is because HubSpot dedups contacts by email, and our `upsertContact` requires an email for its search-then-create-or-update flow.

User question was: *"if an email is empty, the sync cannot work for HubSpot sync — is there a way to still sync?"* The need is to **push** these leads into HubSpot.

## Fix

HubSpot's API does support email-less contacts — `hubspotService.createContact` / `updateContact` already work without an email; only `upsertContact` requires it (for the dedup search). So the fix is adapter-only in `hubspotAdapter.pushLeads`:

- **Has a valid email** → unchanged (`upsertContact`, find-or-create by email).
- **No email, but synced before** (`syncMetadata.hubspot_contact_id` present) → `updateContact(id, …)`, so we don't create a duplicate.
- **No email, never synced** → `createContact(…)` with whatever mapped fields exist (name, company, phone, custom props).
- **No email and no mappable properties at all** → still skipped (nothing to push).

Invalid (malformed) emails are still rejected with a clear per-lead error — that behavior is unchanged. This covers both bulk sync and single-lead auto-sync, since auto-sync routes through `pushLeads`.

## Tests

- `hubspotAdapter.pushLeads.test.ts` — added cases for create-when-no-id, update-by-stored-id, whitespace email, and skip-when-no-props.
- `externalCrmSync.service.test.ts` — replaced the old "skips leads without email" test with create-not-upsert coverage.
- Full backend suite passes (`npx jest`, exit 0); `npx tsc` clean.

title: fix(stripe): 'Switch to Free' 500s for schedule-managed subs (release schedule before cancel)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
"Switch to Free" (Settings → Subscription → Manage Plan → /pricing → Switch to Free) returned **500 "Failed to cancel subscription."** for any customer whose subscription was attached to a Stripe **subscription_schedule** — which is how this codebase applies sales coupons and scheduled tier changes. `/api/stripe/cancel-subscription` called `subscriptions.update({ cancel_at_period_end: true })` directly, and Stripe rejects that on schedule-managed subs: *"...updating any cancelation behavior directly is not allowed. Please update the schedule instead."*

Reported by customer **Jerry Shan (Insightful-Tech)** on 2026-06-05 ("It asks 'Cancel sub?' ... 'Failed to cancel....' A never-ending loop"). Confirmed in prod logs — schedule `sub_sched_1Tec78GS8i9KS4NKrUslkxkj` rejected 4 consecutive attempts. He applied a sales 90%-off coupon, which attached the schedule.

## What this fixes (after)
The handler now detects an attached schedule and **releases it first** (releasing preserves the subscription's current price/discount — it just detaches the schedule), then sets `cancel_at_period_end: true`. It also clears any stale cached `scheduledChange` so `/auth/me` doesn't surface a phantom pending change.

## How to test
1. As a subscriber whose sub has a coupon/scheduled change applied via a Stripe subscription_schedule, go to `/settings` → Subscription → **Manage Plan**.
2. On `/pricing`, click **Switch to Free** → **Cancel subscription**.
3. **Expected**: success message "Your subscription will cancel at the end of the current period." (no "Failed to cancel" error). Sub shows `cancel_at_period_end=true` in Stripe; the schedule is released.
4. Reload `/settings`.
5. **Expected**: "Canceling" badge + period-end date, no phantom scheduled-change notice.

## Edge cases to check
- Subscriber **without** any schedule: cancel still works unchanged (no release call).

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: **12 passed, 0 failed** (`stripeSubscription.test.ts`). 4 new cancel tests; the 2 schedule-release tests were verified **failing without the fix**.
- `npx tsc` clean.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- Schedule-managed sub → `subscriptionSchedules.release(scheduleId)` is called **before** `subscriptions.update`, returns 200 → test `releases an attached subscription_schedule before canceling`.
- Schedule expanded as object → releases `schedule.id` → test `releases an attached schedule when it is expanded to an object`.
- No schedule → `release` is **not** called → test `should NOT call subscriptionSchedules.release when the sub has no schedule`.
- Stale `scheduledChange` cleared on the user record → asserted in the release test.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/stripe.ts` — release schedule before cancel + clear scheduledChange
- `backend/src/__tests__/stripeSubscription.test.ts` — regression tests

## What was NOT tested
- No live end-to-end run against a real Stripe schedule (unit-mocked). Reactivate (`/reactivate-subscription`) has the symmetric pattern but is **not** changed here — flagging for follow-up if a schedule-attached reactivate is ever hit.

## Related PRs
- Backend: standalone
- Customer Portal: standalone (frontend already calls the endpoint correctly)

## Notion task
- None yet — happy to file one if you want it tracked.

title: feat(loops): durable learning store + cooldown read-back (loop self-awareness)
body:
Builds the two pieces that make a loop aware of its own in-flight + failed fixes — so it won't re-propose a fix it already dispatched or one that already failed.

- **DynamoLearningStore** — durable Layer-5 store (Dev-AW-LoopLearning) over the injected DynamoPort. Replaces InMemoryLearningStore, which forgot all history on each redeploy (so the loop currently has *no* persistent memory).
- **CooldownRuleSet** — wraps any policy (DSL or LLM analyst) and drops a proposal when the same rule's last shipped fix is **in flight** (shipped, not yet graded) or **graded regressed/no_change/inconclusive within the cooldown**. An `improved` fix is never suppressed.

Together with the attribution engine (#1713) this closes the learning loop: **propose → ship → grade → read-back → don't repeat.**

## Tests — 7, all green
- durable round-trip + date revival; `lastOutcomeForRule` returns the most recent graded record
- cooldown: suppresses in-flight + recent-failure; does NOT suppress improved / elapsed-cooldown / no-history

`npx jest loops` → 97 pass. tsc clean.

## NOT done (activation, slow-observable by nature)
This is the components. Turning it on live = create the Dev-AW-LoopLearning table, swap the loops' store to DynamoLearningStore, wrap their policy in CooldownRuleSet, **record ship-time in the ✅ reaction handler**, and schedule `runAttribution`. And it only observably suppresses after multiple runs across the settle window (days) — there's nothing to suppress until a fix has shipped and been graded. The unit tests are the verifiable proof of the behavior today.

title: Fix local agent relay 503 (ngrok idle timeout) with chunked heartbeats
body:
## Summary
- **Root cause:** Long browser scans buffered their entire result before sending any bytes, so ngrok's 300s idle timeout fired (`ERR_NGROK_3004` / 503) and the relay then hit `BrokenPipeError` writing into the dead socket.
- **Fix (`local-agent-relay`):** run the Codex task in a worker thread and stream a whitespace keep-alive chunk every 30s, delivering the real JSON as the final chunk. Requires `protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"` — `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` defaults to 1.0, where chunk framing leaks into the body undecoded (caught via end-to-end curl, not assumed).
- **Backend (`localAgentTools.ts`):** raise the `run_local_agent_task` timeout cap from 600s → 900s now that the connection stays alive.
- Added relay unit/integration tests for the chunked heartbeat path.
- Release note for 2026-06-07.

## Deploy status
- **Dev relay (port 8081)** and **prod relay (port 8080)** both already redeployed on the Mac mini and verified end-to-end (HTTP/1.1 200, `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, clean JSON; a 72s prod scan returned valid JSON with zero BrokenPipe).

title: fix(crm-enrichment): evaluate smart fields via LLM even without dep data
body:
## Summary

Smart-field evaluation previously **skipped the LLM entirely** when none of a field's dependencies could be enriched, on the assumption the LLM would return `null` anyway. That assumption was wrong: the LLM still receives the lead's native context (company, title, website, etc.) and can often infer the value from domain knowledge — or apply the condition's explicit `else` branch.

## Changes

- **`crmEnrichmentServiceV3.ts`** — Remove the early-return that skipped `evaluateSmartField` when no dependency data was available. The LLM is now always asked, passing through whatever dep values exist (possibly empty).
- **`enrichmentPrompts.ts`** — Update the smart-field eval system prompt so the LLM honors an explicit default/"else" outcome (e.g. "... else No") instead of returning null. It still returns null only when the data is genuinely insufficient *and* no default is specified, so we never fabricate a value.

## Tests

- Updated the smart-field test to assert the LLM is invoked (with empty dep values) when no dependency data is available, and that the LLM-decided value is written with `source: 'llm'`.
- Added `enrichmentPrompts.test.ts` covering the explicit default/else prompt behavior.
