title: feat: alert when forward-lead silently drops leads (404/403)
body:
## Risk: Low | Additive observability only

## What was wrong (before)
`POST /api/webhooks/forward-lead` correctly returns **404** (list not found) and **403** (list not public), but every landing-page client swallows the rejection and shows the visitor a success screen. A misconfigured lander silently drops **every** submission. This is exactly how the `demystifying-ai` lander lost leads for weeks (it POSTed to a list ID that didn't exist).

## What this fixes (after)
On 404/403, the handler now records the drop via `recordLeadCaptureFailure`:
- **Always** emits a structured `[lead-capture-failure]` log with a `lead_capture_failure` marker (greppable for log-based alerting), list ID, source/lander, and email *domain* only (PII minimization).
- **Optionally** posts a Slack alert naming the list ID + lander, gated on `LEAD_CAPTURE_ALERT_SLACK_CHANNEL`. **Default-off** (log-only) — no infra dependency until you set the env var.

No change to the existing status contract or the success path — purely additive.

## How to test
1. POST to `/api/webhooks/forward-lead` with a `listId` that doesn't exist → still 404, now also logs `lead_capture_failure`.
2. POST with a list where `publicAccessEnabled !== true` → still 403, now logs the failure with the owner's userId.
3. Set `LEAD_CAPTURE_ALERT_SLACK_CHANNEL=#some-channel` → the same cases also post a Slack alert.
4. A successful forward → no failure recorded.

title: fix(agentMode): make session-generation claim atomic (B2)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The `/generate` and interactive-share `/generate` endpoints in `controllers/agentModeController.ts` rejected concurrent requests for the same session with a hand-rolled `activeSessionGenerations.has(sessionId)` check followed by a *separate* `activeSessionGenerations.add(sessionId)`. The two statements were duplicated at both call sites and were only race-free because nothing `await`ed between them. That makes the single-flight guarantee fragile: any future edit inserting an `await` between the check and the set re-opens a window where two near-simultaneous `/generate` calls both pass the check and both proceed.

## What this fixes (after)
The check-and-set is co-located into one indivisible primitive, `tryClaimSessionGeneration(sessionId): boolean` (`true` = claimed, `false` = busy), plus a symmetric idempotent `releaseSessionGeneration(sessionId)`. Both call sites route through it, so an `await` can never be wedged between the check and the set — the claim is atomic by construction. Single-request behavior is unchanged: same 409 `SESSION_BUSY` body, same lock lifecycle.

## Complexity ledger
- **Net lines:** +~75 (helper pair + JSDoc + dev.md note + new test file ~75); production-code delta is roughly flat — two duplicated 2-statement claim blocks collapse to a single function call each, offset by the ~30-line shared helper they now share.
- **Moving parts:** added one helper pair (`tryClaimSessionGeneration` / `releaseSessionGeneration`); removed two copies of an inline hand-rolled check-then-set. No new table / flag / branch / dependency / abstraction layer. The lock is still the same single `activeSessionGenerations` `Set`.
- **Behavior delta:** **more-reliable** (race-proof by construction). No change to chat outputs, tool selection, prompts, or model defaults.

title: fix(agentMode): B4 — clear progressStore on worker death (no zombie SSE progress)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
`progressStore` (`backend/src/utils/sseProgress.ts`) is the in-memory map backing the AgentMode progress SSE stream. The frontend treats a stored entry whose `status` is not `complete`/`suggestions` as "still generating". Cleanup was **entirely** the controller's job: every terminal path calls `markProgressComplete(sessionId)`. When the generation worker (`generateMarketingResponseWorkerService`, a forked child process) dies mid-iteration, it rejected all pending request promises but did **nothing** to `progressStore`. Cleanup then depended on the *awaiting* controller path reaching a `markProgressComplete` — which the **detached fire-and-forget plan-start path** (`agentModeController.ts` ~5693, a `.then().catch()` not awaited by any HTTP handler) and any future caller don't guarantee. Result: a worker crash mid-run can leave a stale progress entry **forever**, so the user's session streams "Thinking…" indefinitely even after a reload. This is the charter's "crash of a turn must not orphan a stream" invariant.

## What this fixes (after)
Worker death now clears the progress entry **at the source** for every session that had an in-flight request, independent of any controller path:
- New leaf helper `clearTerminalProgress(sessionId)` in `sseProgress.ts` — the single definition of terminal cleanup: emit `complete` *iff* a live entry exists (so it never resurrects an already-cleaned entry), then delete. Active SSE connections are intentionally left registered so a reconnecting client still gets the `complete` signal.
- `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService` calls a new private `clearProgressForInFlightSessions()` (iterates `sessionToRequestId`, best-effort) inside both the `worker.on('error')` and `worker.on('exit')` handlers, before clearing the maps. Also clears the previously-leaked `sessionToRequestId` map on death.

The controller's happy/cancel paths (`markProgressComplete`) are left untouched — this is purely a second, source-level safety net for the crash case.

**Where it actually lives (re-grepped — spec line refs are a map):** `progressStore` is set only in `emitProgress` (`sseProgress.ts:45`); the worker lifecycle is in `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts` (`error` handler ~201, `exit` handler ~216 pre-change).

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx tsc` — **Expected**: clean, exit 0.
2. `cd backend && npm test -- sseProgress.terminalCleanup` — **Expected**: 7/7 pass (3 worker-crash cases, 3 helper unit cases, 1 normal-completion case).
3. `cd backend && npm test -- generateMarketingResponseWorkerService` — **Expected**: existing 17 worker-service tests still pass (no regression in error/exit handling).
4. `cd backend && npm test -- agentModeController.progress` — **Expected**: existing progress-SSE tests still pass, including "emits terminal complete progress after a successful generateResponse".

## Edge cases to check
- A session whose worker request already **settled** (success/error message received) is removed from `sessionToRequestId` before death, so its possibly-post-run `suggestions` progress is NOT clobbered by the crash cleanup. Covered implicitly: cleanup only iterates currently in-flight sessions.
- `clearTerminalProgress` on a session with no entry is a no-op (does not emit a spurious `complete` that resurrects an entry) — covered by the "no-op when no progress exists" unit test.

## Test Evidence
- New tests: `backend/src/__tests__/sseProgress.terminalCleanup.test.ts` — 7 cases (4 passed before the fix, 3 worker-crash cases failed before / pass after).
- Targeted suites run: sseProgress.terminalCleanup (7), generateMarketingResponseWorkerService (17), agentModeController.progress (16) — **40 passed, 0 failed**. Plus agentModeController errorHandling/concurrentRequests/ishareAnonymousSender — **34 passed, 0 failed**.
- `npx tsc`: clean.
- Did NOT run the full ~15min suite (per swarm guardrail — targeted tests only).

## Complexity ledger
- **Net lines:** +51 production (sseProgress.ts +22, worker service +29) + 205 test. Trends toward consolidation: the new helper centralizes the "terminal cleanup" concept that was previously only inline duplication in the controller.
- **Moving parts:** added one pure helper (`clearTerminalProgress`) + one private method (`clearProgressForInFlightSessions`). No new table/flag/dependency/branch in the chat loop. Removed a latent leak (`sessionToRequestId` now cleared on worker death).
- **Behavior delta:** more-reliable. No change to chat outputs, tool selection, prompts, or model defaults.

## Behavior-preserving proof
- Characterization test `AC2: normal completion does not leave the entry orphaned either` (in `sseProgress.terminalCleanup.test.ts`) pins the happy-path cleanup outcome — passes unchanged.
- Existing `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService` error/exit tests (`should handle worker process errors`, `should handle worker process exit with non-zero code`) still assert the same rejection behavior — pass unchanged after the fix (the added cleanup is additive, the rejection contract is identical).
- Existing `agentModeController.progress` test `emits terminal complete progress after a successful generateResponse` passes unchanged — confirms the controller terminal path was not altered.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/utils/sseProgress.ts` — add `clearTerminalProgress` helper
- `backend/src/services/generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts` — clear progress + session map on worker death
- `backend/src/__tests__/sseProgress.terminalCleanup.test.ts` — new repro/characterization tests
- `dev.md` — dated investigation/assumptions note

## What was NOT tested
- A real forked-worker OS-level crash on the live test env (tests simulate the `error`/`exit` events via mocked `child_process.fork`, which is exactly how the worker service receives them — but no end-to-end SIGKILL of an actual child process).
- The frontend SSE consumer's reaction to the `complete` event (out of scope — backend-only PR; the `complete` emission path is unchanged from existing terminal cleanup).

## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Production `ApprovalGate` is still `CaptureGate` (`backend/src/loops/core/gates/captureGate.ts`), whose `pollDecision()` always returns `pending`. So a gated mutation's learning record never gets `shippedAt` stamped, and the attribution cron (`loops/core/learning/attribution.ts`, filter `decision.status in {approved,auto_shipped}` AND `shippedAt` set AND `verdict==null`) has nothing to grade — every loop sits at `pending_approval` forever. This is the dev.md-named #1 learning-loop gap (2026-06-09).

## What this fixes (after)
Adds the real Layer-4 gate that resolves a decision from a Slack reaction on the proposal DM and stamps the Layer-5 `shippedAt` on approval — closing Layer 4→5. **Capability only**: it is NOT wired in as the prod gate. `CaptureGate` stays the live `agentModeGate`; the new gate is built behind `AGENT_MODE_SLACK_REACTION_GATE` (default OFF).

`backend/src/loops/core/gates/slackReactionGate.ts`:
- `requestApproval(mutation)` posts the proposal DM via the injected `SlackPort`, returns a `{channel, ts, approver}` handle.
- `pollDecision(record)` reads reactions and resolves via the pure `resolveReactionDecision(reactions, approver, now)`: ✅ `white_check_mark` from the approver → `approved`; ❌ `x` → `denied` (reject wins when both present, safety-first); none → `pending`. ## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

WS-B / B5 of the AgentMode restructure (`loop-agentmode-restructure.md`).

## What was wrong (before)
Hitting the AgentMode context-window limit fired an oncall alert email on **every occurrence** via `sendAgentModeOncallAlert` (`backend/src/utils/agentModeAlerts.ts`). On a high-concurrency day, one user repeatedly retrying a too-long session generated one oncall email **per request** — flooding oncall.

## What this fixes (after)
`sendAgentModeOncallAlert` gains an **opt-in** `dedupeKey` + `dedupeWindowMs`. When `dedupeKey` is set, at most one alert is sent per key per window (default 10 min); repeats inside the window are suppressed. The two context-limit call sites in `controllers/agentModeController.ts` now pass a `(user, errorClass)` key. When `dedupeKey` is absent the function fires every time, so all other ~14 call sites are byte-for-byte unchanged.

> Note: the **Notion** side was already deduped — `autoReportContextLimitToNotion` sets a per-session `contextLimitReported` flag and skips if set, so Notion only ever files one issue per session. The unprotected flood path was the oncall email, which is what this PR fixes. Left the Notion path untouched to stay contained.

Re-grepped on `origin/harsha/swarm`:

title: fix(agent-mode): clear session→request map on worker crash so the session lock releases immediately (B1)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
On worker `exit`/`error` the crash handlers in `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService` rejected and cleared `pendingRequests` but **never cleared `sessionToRequestId`**. After a crash, a dead session's `requestId` lingered: a later `cancelSession()` for that session mis-fired a `{type:'cancel'}` at the *fresh* worker, and the map grew unbounded across crashes.

## What this fixes (after)
A single `failAllPendingRequests(error)` helper rejects every in-flight request and clears **both** `pendingRequests` and `sessionToRequestId`. The `error`, `exit`, and `shutdown` paths all route through it (dedupes three near-identical handler bodies). Prompt rejection on crash is what lets the controller's `try/finally` release the per-session generation lock (`activeSessionGenerations`) immediately, instead of waiting out `GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS` (~10 min).

## Investigation note (re-grepped — the line refs in the spec were a map)
The literal B1 symptom ("lock only releases after the timeout on crash") is **already fixed** on current `harsha/swarm`: the worker `error`/`exit` handlers (added Feb 2026) reject all pending requests, which unwinds through `runInWorker` → `generateSessionResponse` (`agentModeController.ts:1819`) → the controller's `finally` (`:2356`/`:3032`), releasing the lock immediately. The characterization test added here **passes on the pre-fix code**, confirming that. The genuine remaining defect in the same region was the leaked `sessionToRequestId` mapping — that is what this PR fixes. Full note in `dev.md` (2026-06-14).

Current sites (re-grepped): lock `activeSessionGenerations` = `controllers/agentModeController.ts:40`; `GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS` = `:56`; worker crash handlers = `services/generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts` `error` `:201` / `exit` `:216`.

## Complexity ledger
- **Net lines:** services file +24/−19 (net **+5**, but **−2 branches**: two hand-rolled reject-loops collapsed into one helper call each; `shutdown`'s loop also removed). Tests +222. dev.md +12.
- **Moving parts:** adds one private helper, removes three duplicated reject-and-clear loop bodies and the latent `sessionToRequestId` leak. No new table / flag / dependency / public API.
- **Behavior delta:** **more-reliable.** No change to chat outputs, tool selection, prompts, or model defaults. The only observable deltas are internal: stale session→request mappings are no longer retained, and `shutdown` now also clears that map.

## Behavior-preserving proof
- **Characterization test:** `agentModeController.workerCrashLockRelease.test.ts` — "releases the lock when the worker dies (exit) so the next /generate is accepted (no timeout wait)". Pins the B1 AC; **passes before and after** the fix (the crash→lock-release path was already correct).
- **Repro test (the actual fix):** `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.test.ts` — "clears the session→request mapping when the worker crashes (no stale cancel on the next worker)". **Failed before** (stale `{type:'cancel'}` fired at the fresh worker), **passes after**.

2. `node --max-old-space-size=4096 node_modules/.bin/jest --maxWorkers=2 --forceExit generateMarketingResponseWorkerService` — **Expected:** 18 passed, including "clears the session→request mapping when the worker crashes".
3. `node --max-old-space-size=4096 node_modules/.bin/jest --maxWorkers=2 --forceExit workerCrashLockRelease concurrentRequests` — **Expected:** 8 passed (2 suites).

## Edge cases to check
- `shutdown()` now also clears `sessionToRequestId` (previously only cleared `pendingRequests`) — confirm no caller relies on the mapping surviving a shutdown. Verified: only `cancelSession` reads it, and after shutdown/crash there is nothing to cancel.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 26 passed (18 worker-service + 8 controller), 0 failed.
- Tested as: Jest unit tests only (mocked child_process / worker IPC). No browser/test-env needed — PURE/MOCKABLE.

title: AgentMode C2: verify approval→attribution→verdict end-to-end + fix loop-health pending_approval stall
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

Increment **C2** of the AgentMode restructure (`~/.claude/rules/loop-agentmode-restructure.md` §WS-C2). Verifies the approval→attribution→verdict path end-to-end (mocked) and fixes a `computeLoopHealth` stall found during that verification.

## What was wrong (before)
The closed learning loop "reaches a verdict" but `GET /api/admin/loops/health` never reflected it. The learning store is **append-only**: one logical proposal accumulates a `pending` row → an `approved`+`shippedAt` row (written by the Layer-4→5 approval) → a graded `verdict` row. `computeLoopHealth` (`backend/src/loops/core/health.ts`) counted *every* matching row, so:
- the original `pending` row kept counting as `pendingApproval` even after the human ✅ → state stuck on `pending_approval` forever;
- the pre-verdict `approved`+`shippedAt` row kept counting as `inFlight` even after attribution graded it → state stuck on `in_flight`, never reaching `learned`.

`loopHealthService` reads with no status filter, and both `InMemoryLearningStore` and `DynamoLearningStore` return all rows — so this misreport is real in production, not a test artifact.

## What this fixes (after)
`computeLoopHealth` de-dups by proposal/mutation id (the same key attribution uses in `recordKey`): a `pending` row counts only if no later row has resolved that proposal (approved/auto_shipped/shipped/graded); an `in_flight` row counts only if no graded verdict exists for it. Each logical proposal is now summarized by its **furthest-progressed** row, so the loop visibly moves `pending_approval → in_flight → learned` (or `regressed`). No behavior change for single-row states.

Where I actually found it (line refs are a map): the bug is in `backend/src/loops/core/health.ts` (`isPendingApproval`/`isInFlight` counting in `computeLoopHealth`). The approval contract C2 depends on is `recordLoopApproval` in `backend/src/loops/core/learning/approvalPersistence.ts` (stamps `decision=approved` + `shippedAt`); grading is `runAttribution` in `backend/src/loops/core/learning/attribution.ts`.

2. `npm test -- loops.c2.approvalToVerdict` — **Expected**: 5/5 pass.
3. `npm test -- "loops.health|loops.healthService|loops.attributionCron|loops.approvalPersistence|loops.cooldownAttribution|loops.learning"` — **Expected**: all green (existing health/attribution suites unaffected).

title: fix(loops): kill the daily 'Emma Dev' chirp from the agent-mode reliability loop
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
A recurring "Emma Dev" Slack DM chirped at **seemingly random times**, only from the **AI Reliability loop** (the agent-mode tool-reliability loop). Three compounding issues:

1. **Only loop scheduled + enabled in prod.** Siblings (`ai-eval`, `ai-readiness`, `onboarding-v2`) are env-gated off; only `AGENT_MODE_LOOP_ENABLED` is on.
2. **DM'd on every run, even empty windows.** `ai-eval` guards its post on activity; agent-mode had no such guard. The recorder is gated separately (`AGENT_RUNTIME_SPINE_ENABLED`, off in prod), so every run scanned 0 events and still fired the "healthy/empty" DM — pure noise.
3. **No daily-dedup claim -> felt random.** `ai-readiness` wraps its DM in `claimDailyDigestPost()` (a DynamoDB conditional put keyed on `(date, user)`) so only one process posts per day. Agent-mode has none. Prod runs multiple EB instances + a worker, each with its own boot-aligned 17:30 timer, so redeploys/autoscale/restarts produce **duplicate DMs at staggered, unpredictable times**.

(Correction to the loop's own dev.md note: the `CaptureGate` is not a dead no-op — approval is out-of-band, Harsha reacts ✅ -> `routes/slack.ts` -> `recordLoopApproval`, and `shippedAt` IS stamped. The DM was actionable; the problem is noise + duplication.)

## What this fixes (after)
`onRunComplete` returns before posting unless `AGENT_MODE_LOOP_DIGEST === 'true'` (default off) — a dedicated flag. Because every process checks the flag, it kills the chirp **regardless of instance count** (also sidesteps the missing dedup). The loop still registers, records, runs, and shows in `GET /api/admin/loops/health` — it's just **silent**. No EB env change needed. Set `AGENT_MODE_LOOP_DIGEST=true` to re-enable. Proper follow-up if re-enabled: add the `claimDailyDigestPost()` dedup (noted in dev.md).

## How to test
1. Default (no `AGENT_MODE_LOOP_DIGEST`): run `runAgentModeLoopOnce()` with the loop enabled.
2. **Expected**: no Slack DM, even on a window with failing tools.
3. Set `AGENT_MODE_LOOP_DIGEST=true` and run again.
4. **Expected**: the exact same digest DM as before (wire format unchanged).

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc` clean
- `loops.digestCharacterization` + `loops.agentModeWiring`: 22 passed, 0 failed
- New test: "is silent by default — posts NO digest DM even when tools are failing" (fails before the fix, passes after)

## Files changed
- `backend/src/loops/instances/agent-mode/index.ts` — gate the digest DM
- `backend/src/__tests__/loops.digestCharacterization.test.ts` — silent-by-default test + flag the format tests
- `dev.md` — root-cause writeup (incl. the "why random" multi-process explanation)

## What was NOT tested
- No live prod Slack verification (can't trigger the prod 17:30 cron from here); verified via unit tests against the loop's only DM path.

title: Security: 5 verified-live gaps in main (unauth image-models route, upload XSS, account enumeration, settings/MCP secret exposure)
body:
Five unshipped security fixes (branches `fix/*` + `combined/security-fixes`) were deleted 2026-06-14 as part of branch cleanup — they were 3+ months / ~300 commits stale. But the **underlying gaps were re-verified present in `main` on 2026-06-14** (first-hand `git show origin/main` checks). The fix code was disposable; these holes are not. Filing so they get a fresh, current implementation. **Security = Rui's lane.**

### Verified-live gaps in `main`
1. **Unauthenticated `image-models` route** — `backend/src/routes/image-models.ts:7` is `router.get('/', async (req,res) =>` with **no auth middleware**, mounted publicly at `app.use("/api/image-models", ...)` (`app.ts:291`). Add `authenticateToken` (+ `requireAdmin` if appropriate).
2. **Upload XSS — no file-type validation** — `backend/src/utils/s3Utils.ts` has no `isAllowedUploadType`; image upload handlers only check `mimetype.startsWith('image/')`, so `image/svg+xml` (and other active types) pass and are served inline. Add an allowlist + block SVG/HTML/JS, and/or `Content-Disposition: attachment`.
3. **Account enumeration** — `backend/src/controllers/auth.ts:49` returns `"User already exists"` on register and `:202-204` returns `404 { code: "user_not_found" }` on login. Make non-existent-user login byte-identical to wrong-password (generic `401 "Invalid credentials"`).
4. **Settings GET returns secrets unredacted** — `backend/src/routes/settings.ts` GET responds `res.json(settings)` raw; no redaction util in `main`. Redact API-key/secret-shaped values on read.
5. **MCP server list returns secrets unmasked** — `backend/src/routes/mcpServers.ts` GET does raw `res.json(JSON.parse(settingValue))`. Mask `accessToken`/secrets on the GET path.

_Deleted branches that had (stale) fixes for these: `fix/settings-api-key-exposure`, `fix/file-upload-xss`, `fix/email-enumeration`, `fix/mcp-key-redaction`, `combined/security-fixes`. Re-implement fresh off current `main`; do not resurrect._

title: Onboarding image: feedback loop + managed prompt + reliability telemetry (WS1a/1b/2)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

Onboarding image quality + reliability, on managed/self-improving rails. Backend half of a 2-PR change (frontend: agentweb-customer-portal).

## What was wrong (before)
- Ad-image ♥/✕ in onboarding dead-ended into favorite/archive (gallery state) and **never influenced the next generation** — taste signal on images was thrown away (copy already had this loop; images didn't).
- The image prompt's global scaffolding (style spec + HARD CONSTRAINTS) was **hardcoded in `buildSixLayerPromptForVariant`** — not runtime-editable, couldn't be tuned without a deploy, and `AD_IMAGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` was dead/unused code.
- Image generation + brand-scrape failures were **invisible to the loops framework** — a degraded model or flaky scrape produced a worse onboarding with no telemetry trail.

## What this fixes (after)
- **WS1b — image feedback loop closed.** New `adImageVariantRatingService` stores ♥/✕ under `adImageVariantsRated`; `POST /api/onboarding/ad-image-variant/rate` persists it + logs a PromptSignal; the image orchestrator distills recent rejects into a negative visual-direction block fed into the next generation. Variants now carry their `concept` label so a rejected direction can be named back.
- **WS1a — image prompt fully on managed rails.** Global style spec + HARD CONSTRAINTS extracted to `imagePromptDefaults`, sourced from a new versioned, admin-editable `global-image-directives` row in `promptTemplatesService` (same table, no new table), edited via `GET/PUT /api/admin/prompt-templates/global/image-directives`. **Seeded byte-identical** → behavior-preserving until someone edits it.
- **WS2 — reliability telemetry.** `onboardingTelemetry` emits `image_generation_*` / `brand_scrape_*` started/completed/failed onto the onboarding loop (`Dev-AW-LoopEvents`) with a semantic `errorClass`, so failures cluster on `GET /api/admin/loops/health` and the cluster cron — same rails as everything else.

## How to test
1. **Rating loop:** create a fresh account, reach the Phase-4 image reveal, ✕ a variant. `POST /api/onboarding/ad-image-variant/rate {variantId, rating:"reject"}` returns `{summary:{likes,rejects,total}}`. GET the user → `adImageVariantsRated` has the entry. Regenerate → the new variant prompts contain a "User REJECTED these recent ad image directions…" block.
2. **Managed directives:** `GET /api/admin/prompt-templates/global/image-directives` → seeded styleSpec + hardConstraints. `PUT` a new styleSpec → next generation's prompts use it; `version` bumps.
3. **Telemetry:** run a generation → `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` (loopId=onboarding) has `image_generation_started`/`completed`; force a failure → `image_generation_failed` with `errorClass`.

## Edge cases covered
- Legacy users with no mirror chat-session now still get ratings captured (endpoint needs only variantId+rating).
- Store/Dynamo failure → image gen degrades to the DEFAULT_IMAGE_* constants (never blocks generation).
- Telemetry is best-effort/fire-and-forget — never affects the onboarding cascade.

## Test Evidence
- **616 backend tests pass, 1 skipped (live pipeline), 0 failed.** `npx tsc` clean.
- New suites: `adImageVariantRatingService` (11), `onboardingAdImageVariantRate` (7), `onboardingAdImageNegativeExamples` (10 incl. WS1a override + behavior-preserving), `onboardingTelemetry` (5), `promptTemplatesGlobalDirectives` (7).
- Behavior-preserving proof: existing `onboardingAdImageService` suite passes unchanged; WS1a default output asserted byte-identical to the prior inline strings.

## Files changed (grouped)
- Rating: `services/adImageVariantRatingService.ts`, `routes/onboardingSteps.ts`, `services/adImageStatusService.ts`
- Generation wire-in: `services/onboardingAdImageService.ts`, `services/imagePromptDefaults.ts`
- Managed store: `services/promptTemplatesService.ts`, `routes/adminPromptTemplates.ts`
- Telemetry: `services/onboardingTelemetry.ts`, `loops/instances/onboarding/manifest.ts`, `services/onboardingBrandBuildService.ts`
- Tests: 5 new suites under `__tests__/`

## What was NOT tested
- **Live full-UI new-account E2E with real image generation was NOT run in this autonomous loop.** The running test env is a shared dev box and remote-exec for a clean sync→verify→restore was unreliable from the loop; I did not want to disrupt it unattended or claim verification I didn't perform. Coverage is unit + route-level integration (real handler → persist → response with mocked DB) + a green full backend suite. Recommend a manual run of the "How to test" steps above on the test env before merge.
- Real Gemini image-quality delta from edited directives (that's taste/Harsha).

## Related PRs
- Frontend (image deck repoint): agentweb-customer-portal `defense/onboarding-image-rating` (separate PR)

title: AgentMode reliability: cut run_local_agent_task scope-rejection failures
body:
## Risk: Low / Medium | Priority: High

Internal tool-reliability fix. Targets the `run_local_agent_task` failure cluster — the **internal scope-rejection/routing noise**, not the external Hermes browser agent.

## Real failure modes (evidence)
Queried `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` (us-west-2, `loopId='agent-mode'`, `eventType='agent_tool_failed'`, `dimensions.toolName='run_local_agent_task'`, last 7d): **20 failures**, of which:
- **14 scope-rejections** — dominated by SOFT-WRITE regex **false positives** on read-only tasks:
  - `matched forbidden pattern "\bpost.*comment"` (x9)
  - `matched forbidden pattern "\blog.*in"` (x1)
  - `matched forbidden pattern "\bclick.*button"` (x1)
- **6 genuine relay failures** (`Tool returned success=false`) on the **external Hermes path — out of scope, untouched.**

Two internal root causes:
1. **False positives.** Read-only tasks ("read the comments under this post", "extract text near the login button") matched write-action regexes and got rejected.
2. **Misclassification.** A scope-rejection returned `{success:false}`, which the dispatch layer downgrades to `status:'error'` (via `toolResultError`) → recorded as `agent_tool_failed` → inflates the failure rate and feeds the repeated-failure circuit breaker. The validator did its job; the model just needs a different tool.

## The fix (internal — tool-handler layer only, `backend/src/emma/localAgentTools.ts`)
- Split blocked patterns into **HARD-BLOCK** (shell / credential / file / transaction — always rejected) vs **SOFT-WRITE** (post/comment/click/login/form — only block when the task lacks clear read-only intent).
- Return scope-rejections as a **graceful, model-correctable outcome** (`success:true, rejected:true, guidance, suggestedTool, formattedContent`) instead of `success:false` — so `toolResultError` returns null, the dispatch layer no longer records `agent_tool_failed`, and the breaker does not trip on a legit rejection.
- `suggestAlternativeTool` routes the model to the right tool (`coding_agent` / `perform_data_analysis` / `linkedin_outreach` / `send_email` / `search_web`).

External Hermes execution path, gateway pre-flight, and `agentModeService.ts` dispatch were **not** touched.

## Before / after (sampled failures)
- 5/5 representative false-positive read-only tasks (the `post.*comment`, `log.*in`, `click.*button` cluster) now **PASS** instead of being rejected.
- 2/2 genuine out-of-scope tasks (real write action, credential read) still **REJECT** — safety floor holds.
- Any remaining genuine rejection now returns as a **graceful redirect**, so it no longer counts as `agent_tool_failed`.

**Net effect on target metric:** `run_local_agent_task` failure rate ↓ — the ~14 scope-rejections/7d (the bulk of this tool's ~54% failure rate) either become legitimate successes (false positives fixed) or graceful redirects that are not recorded as failures.

## In-scope success path: behavior-preserving
Legit browsing tasks ("Visit https://example.com and extract the page title", "Scrape product names from …") validate unchanged. The relay request shape, privacy prefix, screenshot upload, and `buildLocalAgentResult` are untouched.

## How to test
1. Unit/integration: `cd backend && npx tsc` (clean) and `npm test -- runLocalAgent run_local_agent agentToolGateway` — see counts below.
2. The new suite reproduces the real telemetry rejection strings and asserts the new behavior.

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0, no errors.
- `jest localAgentScopeRejection localAgentTools agentToolFailureGuidance toolFailureType`: **66 passed, 0 failed**.
- `jest toolDispatch agentToolGateway toolResultError`: **74 passed, 0 failed**.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/emma/localAgentTools.ts` — pattern split + graceful rejection + routing.
- `backend/src/__tests__/localAgentScopeRejection.test.ts` — new, telemetry-derived.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** ~+90 in handler (pattern split + 3 small helpers + comments), ~+150 test. No new tables/flags/deps. Replaced one opaque rejection path with a structured, routed one.
- **Behavior:** AgentMode chat user-visible delta is strictly *fewer errors / better redirects*; legit success path preserved.

## What was NOT tested
- Live end-to-end against the actual relay (external Hermes path — deliberately untouched).
- Production failure-rate measurement (will be observable in `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` after deploy).

**Note (orchestrator-owned doc):** I did NOT edit `backend/docs/AGENTMODE_MIGRATION.md` per instructions.

title: Enrichment: short negative-TTL to stop cache poisoning (WS4)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

Enrichment robustness — fixes the highest-impact driver of "enrichment is bad" (Fangfang). Independent of the other onboarding PRs.

## What was wrong (before)
An **empty** enrichment result (no web results, no LinkedIn data) was cached with the field group's **full 90–180 day TTL**. A lead that couldn't be enriched once was **locked out of re-enrichment for months** — even after the company got a website / the data became findable. This is the "I re-ran enrichment and still got nothing" failure.

## What this fixes (after)
Empty payloads now get a **1-day negative TTL** (clamped to the base TTL) and are flagged `negative: true`. Positive hits keep their full TTL — **behavior-preserving for successful enrichments**. A re-enrich the next day can pick up newly-available data, while a single run that touches the same lead twice still hits cache (no provider hammering).

## How to test
1. Unit: `npx jest enrichmentCacheNegativeTtl enrichmentCacheService` — 57 pass. Covers `isEmptyRawData`, `resolveCacheTtlDays`, and the write path applying short-TTL+flag on empty / full-TTL on hit.
2. Behavioral: enrich a lead with no findable data → cache row has `negative: true` and `expiresAt ≈ now + 1 day` (not +180 days). Re-enrich after a day → providers are re-queried.

## Edge cases covered
- Base TTL smaller than the negative TTL → clamped to base (never extends a TTL).
- Null/garbage payload → treated as empty.
- Any single source with data (web / LinkedIn company / LinkedIn profile) → treated as a hit, full TTL.

## Test Evidence
- 57 enrichment-cache tests pass; `npx tsc` clean. Also **fixed a tautological existing test** that passed an empty payload but asserted the full 30-day TTL — it was locking in this exact bug.

## Files changed
- `services/enrichmentCacheService.ts` (negative-TTL logic), `services/db.ts` (+`negative?` field), 2 test files

## What was NOT tested / follow-ups (deliberately out of scope here)

title: [defense] Org members can manage shared CRM lists (add leads + 9 sibling ops)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## Source
- Issue: Fangfang reported `AGW-37f09247-c951-8198-a361-c00ebe5a1c07` for CRM list `Agentic Growth Era Dinner — Confirmed Guests` (`list_1781301164926_4obaxh7v8`). As an org super-admin she could `update_lead` and enrich existing leads on the org-shared list, but `add_leads_to_list` returned `You do not have permission to add leads to this list`. Expected: write/update access on an org-shared list should also allow adding new leads (and operating on the list generally).

## Root cause
The org CRM-sharing migration (`61658485`) moved the REST route layer and roughly half of `AgentModeService`'s CRM list methods onto the org-aware helper `crmDb.canOrgMemberAccessList(userId, list)` — which returns true when the caller owns the list **or** shares an `orgId` with the owner. The Emma-tool methods were migrated only partially: `add_leads_to_list` and **9 sibling methods** were left on the owner-only `list.userId !== userId` check, so a same-org member who is not the literal list owner was denied. `update_lead` / enrichment already used the org-aware check, which is exactly why those worked for Fangfang on the same list.

## Fix (10 methods total)
All `AgentModeService` CRM list methods now gate on `canOrgMemberAccessList` instead of the raw owner check:
- `addLeadsToList` (the original report)
- `setLeadContactStatus`, `deleteLeads`, `deleteLeadsByFilter`, `updateLeadList`, `getLeadListStatuses`, `configureLeadStatuses`, `deleteLeadList`, `getLeadEngagements`, `addLeadEngagement` (sibling methods carrying the identical bug — same-org members couldn't delete leads, re-status, configure statuses, or view/log engagement on a shared list)

After this change `grep -c "list.userId !== userId"` in `agentModeService.ts` is **0**, and `canOrgMemberAccessList` backs all 18 CRM list call sites.

## Behavior-preserving proof
- For list **owners**, `canOrgMemberAccessList` returns `true` on the owner-id match (first line of the helper), so owner behavior is byte-for-byte identical to the old `list.userId === userId` path. The only observable delta: same-org non-owner members are no longer hard-blocked.
- The REST/UI path was already correct (delegates to `canAccessCrmList`) — untouched.
- No change to chat outputs, tool selection, prompts, or model defaults.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** +27 / −9 source (like-for-like check swap, no new branches), +96 tests.
- **Moving parts:** none added — no new table, flag, dependency, or abstraction. Reuses the existing `canOrgMemberAccessList` helper and **removes 9 divergent owner-checks** in favor of one shared predicate (consolidation, net-negative moving parts).
- **Behavior:** behavior-preserving for owners; widens access to same-org members (the intended fix).

## How to test
1. Log in as an org super-admin who is **not** the list's primary/owner account, in the same org as the owner.
2. Open the org-shared CRM list `Agentic Growth Era Dinner — Confirmed Guests`.
3. Via Emma chat, add a lead (e.g. Kyle Bimm, ktbimm@gmail.com) to that list.
4. **Expected:** the lead is added — no "You do not have permission to add leads to this list".
5. Try delete/edit-status/configure-statuses on the same list as that member. **Expected:** allowed (previously all returned Access denied).
6. As a user in a **different** org, retry. **Expected:** `Access denied`.

## Tests / Checks
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeService.crmTools.test.ts` → **125 passed** (107 existing + 18 new).
- New table-driven coverage asserts, for all 9 sibling methods: a same-org non-owner member clears the access gate (with `canOrgMemberAccessList` called with the caller + list), and an outsider (`canOrgMemberAccessList → false`) gets `Access denied` + the method's error string + **no write performed**.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → clean (0 errors).

## Behavioral assertions verified
- Same-org member can add / delete / update / set-status / configure / view-and-log-engagement on a shared list → `org-shared access — non-owner org member` allow cases.
- Outsider denied with the per-method error string and no write → deny cases.
- Owner path unchanged → existing per-method happy-path tests still pass.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` — 9 sibling permission checks swapped to the org-aware helper.
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.crmTools.test.ts` — regression coverage + deterministic mock default.

## What was NOT tested
- Not run against the live `add_leads_to_list` tool or production DynamoDB; Kyle Bimm not added to the live list (needs your sign-off + a real org session).
- The real `canOrgMemberAccessList` org-membership lookup is mocked in these unit tests; its same-`orgId` logic in `db.ts` has no direct unit coverage in this suite (pre-existing gap).
- Full backend suite not run (known unrelated broader instability); focused CRM suite + `tsc` only.

title: feat(loops): persist loop dispatch tracker to DynamoDB (AW-LoopDispatches)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Low

## What was wrong (before)
The Slack ✅→cloud-dev dispatch idempotency set (`loopDispatchTracker.ts`) lived in an in-memory `Map` that reset on every Elastic Beanstalk redeploy/restart. After a deploy, re-reacting ✅ on an already-dispatched digest DM could launch a **duplicate** cloud-dev EC2 instance. The file header already flagged this as a known v1 limitation with a DynamoDB v2 planned — this closes that TODO.

## What this fixes (after)
The tracker now persists to DynamoDB `Dev-AW-LoopDispatches` via the loops framework's injected `DynamoPort` (mirrors `DynamoLearningStore`). The dedupe set survives redeploys, so a re-✅ across a restart is a no-op. Reads also filter on the stored `ttl` (epoch seconds, now+7d) so a not-yet-swept expired row reads as not-dispatched, preserving v1's exact 7-day semantics. The module singleton degrades to an in-memory `Map` if DynamoDB throws, so a table outage can never crash the Slack events endpoint.

## How to test
This is a backend-only change with no UI surface. Verify via the test suite (CI does not run tests; run locally):
1. `cd backend && npx tsc` → **Expected**: exits 0, no type errors.
2. `npm test -- loopDispatchTracker.test.ts slack.aiEvalReaction.test.ts ensureCriticalTables.test.ts` → **Expected**: 3 suites pass, 37 tests pass, 0 failed.
3. `npm test -- src/__tests__/loops src/__tests__/slack` → **Expected**: 28 suites / 257 tests pass (no regression in the loops/slack subsystem).

Runtime (optional, on the test env): the table self-heals at boot via `ensureCriticalTables`. After a backend restart, react ✅ on a digest DM, restart the backend, re-react ✅ on the same DM → exactly one cloud-dev launch.

## Edge cases to check
- DynamoDB read throws mid-handler → handler logs and degrades to in-memory, does NOT 500 the `/api/slack/events` endpoint (covered by the AC#4 tests).
- Legacy row with no `ttl` attribute → never expires by the passive-expiry guard (forward-compat test).

## Behavioral assertions verified (HUMAN-WRITTEN contract — Notion task, not modified)
1. **Survives restart / dedupe survives redeploy** → `loopDispatchTracker.test.ts` → "AC#1: a brand-new tracker backed by the same table still reports dispatched".
2. **No double-dispatch across simulated restart → launchEnvironment called once** → `slack.aiEvalReaction.test.ts` → "does not double-dispatch across a simulated redeploy (DynamoDB persistence)" asserts `mockLaunchEnvironment` called exactly once across two ✅ with a fresh tracker over the same table.
3. **First reaction still dispatches** → `loopDispatchTracker.test.ts` → "returns true after markDispatched is called (first reaction dispatches)" (unseen ts → false, then true) + the existing dispatch integration tests.
4. **DynamoDB failure is non-fatal (degrade to in-memory)** → `loopDispatchTracker.test.ts` → "AC#4: DynamoDB failure is non-fatal" — a throwing port does not propagate; `markDispatched` resolves, `isDispatched` still dedupes in-memory and returns false for unseen ts.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** +483 / -135 net (~+348). The bulk is tests (+271 in the tracker test, +81 in the integration test). Production source is a behavior-equivalent rewrite of one small service (~+130 net over the v1 Map) — it trades a Map for a persistent, injectable, testable adapter. No new abstraction invented: it reuses the existing `DynamoPort` + the `Dev-AW-Loop*` table/TTL conventions.
- **Moving parts:** +1 DynamoDB table (`Dev-AW-LoopDispatches`), mirroring its two siblings (`Dev-AW-LoopEvents`, `Dev-AW-LoopLearning`) — registered in both `create-tables.ts` and the boot-time `ensureCriticalTables` self-heal. No new flag, no new dependency. The 3 dispatcher call sites became `await` (the handler was already async).
- **Behavior:** dispatch behavior is preserved; the only observable delta is that dedupe now survives redeploys and a DynamoDB outage degrades gracefully instead of behaving exactly like v1. No change to chat outputs, tool selection, prompts, or models.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/loopDispatchTracker.ts` — DynamoDB-backed `DynamoLoopDispatchTracker` + async singleton wrappers with in-memory fallback.
- `backend/src/services/loopSlackApprovalDispatcher.ts` — await the 3 now-async tracker call sites.
- `backend/src/scripts/create-tables.ts` — `createLoopDispatchesTable` + register in `main`.
- `backend/src/services/ensureCriticalTables.ts` — register `LOOP_DISPATCHES_TABLE` for boot-time self-heal.
- `backend/src/__tests__/loopDispatchTracker.test.ts` — rewritten unit tests (fake DynamoPort, all ACs).
- `backend/src/__tests__/slack.aiEvalReaction.test.ts` — inject fake DynamoPort, await isDispatched, add redeploy dedupe test.
- `backend/src/__tests__/ensureCriticalTables.test.ts` — assert the new table name.

## What was NOT tested
- Live AWS DynamoDB round-trip (all tests use an in-memory fake `DynamoPort` per the MOCKABLE charter — no live AWS).
- The manual DynamoDB native-TTL enablement step (documented in code, same manual step as the sibling LoopEvents/LoopLearning + MCP OAuth tables); the in-code `ttl` read-filter does not depend on it.

title: refactor(loops): onboarding loop Phase 2 cutover (PR 1) — V2 live default, no double-fire
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

Phase 2 of the onboarding-loop framework port — **PR 1 of 2: the cutover (flag flip, behavior-preserving)**. PR 2 (follow-up) deletes the now-dormant legacy code (~1k LOC, pure subtraction on this green characterization test).

## What was wrong (before)
The framework V2 onboarding loop (analyst-policy REVAMP) and the legacy threshold heartbeat (`cron/onboardingLoop.ts`) both ran in gated parallel, each behind its own opt-in env flag. When both are on they **double-fire**: two Slack DMs/day + double Bedrock spend. Neither was the default live path.

## What this fixes (after)
A single cutover-policy module (`loops/instances/onboarding/cutover.ts`) owns the "which onboarding loop is live" decision. **V2 is now the live default; the legacy heartbeat is OFF unless explicitly opted back in**, and when it is, V2 yields — at most ONE onboarding loop is ever live, so no double-fire. No legacy code deleted yet (that's PR 2).

Env contract:
- nothing set → `v2` (live default)
- `ONBOARDING_LOOP_ENABLED=true` → `legacy` (explicit fallback; V2 yields)
- `ONBOARDING_LOOP_V2=false` → both off (explicit rollback)

## How to test
This is a backend cron-wiring change — verified by unit/characterization tests (no UI surface). To verify the wiring by reading boot logs:
1. Start the backend with **no onboarding env flags set**.
2. **Expected**: boot log line `[OnboardingLoop] Cutover mode: v2`, then `[OnboardingLoopV2] Initialized — first run at 17:00 UTC`, and `[OnboardingLoop] Disabled (set ONBOARDING_LOOP_ENABLED=true to enable)` (legacy off).
3. Restart with `ONBOARDING_LOOP_ENABLED=true`.
4. **Expected**: `[OnboardingLoop] Cutover mode: legacy`, the legacy `[OnboardingLoop] Initialized` line, and `[OnboardingLoopV2] Not live (...)`.
5. Restart with `ONBOARDING_LOOP_V2=false`.
6. **Expected**: `[OnboardingLoop] Cutover mode: off` and neither loop initialized.

## Behavioral assertions verified (human-written acceptance criteria → test)
The Notion task's confirmed PR-1 acceptance criteria (planner comment, 2026-06-14):
1. **Signal parity** — given a fixed `onboardingEvents[]` fixture containing a skip, a deviation, and a loop-back (`goal_selected` after `channel_selected`), V2 does not lose a funnel signal the legacy heartbeat reported.
   → `loops.onboardingCutover.test.ts` → *"V2 surfaces SKIP, DEVIATION and LOOP-BACK in the digest"*: drives V2 end-to-end (real `UserArrayEventSource` + `LlmAnalystRuleSet` + grounded Bedrock stub), asserts the analyst prompt preserves `onboarding_skipped`, `deviation`, and the `goal_selected → channel_selected → goal_selected` journey, AND the rendered DM references each signal class.
2. **No double-fire** — under the new default env, exactly one onboarding daily job is live; legacy is not invoked unless its flag is explicitly set.
   → `loops.onboardingCutover.test.ts` → the *"no double-fire (criterion #2)"* block: exactly one of {V2, legacy} is live across the env matrix; `resolveOnboardingLoopMode()` returns a single mode.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** +52 new module (`cutover.ts`), +325 new test; wiring is net **+41 / −23** across `server.ts` + `index.ts` (the inline env-string checks are replaced by named policy calls — fewer literal `process.env.X === 'true'` branches scattered, one policy).
- **Moving parts:** **−1 net** at runtime — removes the daily duplicate loop (two DMs/two Bedrock cycles → one). Adds one small pure policy module that **consolidates** two previously-divergent inline gating expressions into a single source of truth. No new table, flag name, or dependency (reuses the existing `ONBOARDING_LOOP_V2` / `ONBOARDING_LOOP_ENABLED` flags; only their defaults/precedence change).
- **Behavior:** behavior-preserving for the loops themselves — only *which one fires* changes. The V2 loop's outputs (sensor, analyst, digest wire format) are untouched.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/loops/instances/onboarding/cutover.ts` (new — policy)
- `backend/src/server.ts` (boot gating → policy + mode log)
- `backend/src/loops/instances/onboarding/index.ts` (runner `isEnabled` → policy; doc)
- `backend/src/__tests__/loops.onboardingCutover.test.ts` (new — characterization)
- `backend/src/__tests__/loops.onboardingInstance.test.ts` (update old gated-parallel assertions → post-cutover)
- `backend/src/__tests__/loops.digestCharacterization.test.ts` (update the V2-off case to the rollback flag)
- `dev.md` (investigation + assumptions to validate)

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc` clean.

## What was NOT tested
- Live, on-deploy verification that exactly one onboarding DM lands per day and that V2's analyst digest is equal-or-better than the legacy heartbeat on REAL traffic (the characterization test proves the sensor preserves signals into the prompt, not LLM behavior on live data). Tracked as assumptions-to-validate in `dev.md`.
- PR 2's legacy deletion (out of scope — pure subtraction follow-up).

title: fix(crm): refresh lastTouch on public webhook merge path
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The public `POST /api/webhooks/forward-lead` route's existing-lead **merge** branch only whitelisted `standardFields` (firstName/lastName/phone/company/title/notes/linkedin) + `customFields` when updating a lead that already exists by email. The `leadData.lastTouch` (and `firstTouch`/utm denorm) computed earlier in the handler were silently dropped, so `lastTouch` was dead-on-arrival — `lastTouch === firstTouch` forever for any lead that came through the webhook more than once. This violated the `LeadAttributionFields` contract ("refreshed on any repeat touch").

## What this fixes (after)
The merge path now propagates attribution to the `updates` object: `lastTouch` always refreshes when the incoming touch carries attribution; `firstTouch` is backfilled only when the existing lead has none (immutability preserved); `utmSource`/`utmMedium` denorm are backfilled only when absent (never overwritten). `crmDb.updateLead()` gains `firstTouch`/`lastTouch`/`utmSource`/`utmMedium` params + SET-expression handling so the merge can persist them.

## How to test
1. POST to `/api/webhooks/forward-lead` for a new email `a@b.com` with `attribution.utm.source=linkedin&campaign=first` against a public-enabled list.
2. **Expected**: 201 `lead.created`; the lead has `firstTouch` and `lastTouch` both pointing at the linkedin touch, `utmSource=linkedin`.
3. POST again for the **same** email `a@b.com` with `attribution.utm.source=google&campaign=second`.
4. **Expected**: 200 `lead.updated`; `firstTouch` unchanged (still linkedin), `lastTouch` now points at the google touch, `utmSource` still `linkedin` (denorm not overwritten).
5. POST a third time with NO attribution but a changed `firstName`.
6. **Expected**: 200 `lead.updated`; no attribution keys touched.

## Edge cases to check
- Existing lead that predates attribution (no `firstTouch`): a touch backfills both `firstTouch` + `lastTouch` + utm denorm (only-if-absent).
- Repeat touch carrying no attribution: attribution fields left untouched, only the standard-field change is written.

## Behavioral assertions verified (from the Notion spec "## Test" section)
| Spec assertion | Test verifying it |
|---|---|
| 1. First touch via webhook → firstTouch + lastTouch both point to first | existing `Attribution (UTM) capture › stamps firstTouch and lastTouch` (createLead path) + merge backfill test |
| 2. Second touch of same lead → firstTouch unchanged, lastTouch updated, utmSource still first | `existing-lead merge path › refreshes lastTouch on a repeat touch, preserves firstTouch + utm denorm` |
| 3. Unit test for the merge path covering the 3 cases | `webhooks.leadForwarding.test.ts › existing-lead merge path` (3 cases) + `crmDb.updateLead.attribution.test.ts` (5 cases) |
| firstTouch immutability (never in updateFields) | merge test asserts `updates.firstTouch` undefined on repeat touch; backfill test asserts it present only when existing lead had none |
| utmSource/utmMedium denorm not overwritten | merge test asserts `updates.utmSource/utmMedium` undefined when existing lead already had them |

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** net +55 src (webhooks.ts +22, db.ts +33), +137 tests. No new files in src; one new test file. No deletion possible (this is a missing-propagation fix, not a refactor).
- **Moving parts:** no new table / flag / dependency / abstraction. `updateLead` gains 4 optional params that mirror the already-existing `createLead` attribution params and the persisted schema — consolidates the create/update attribution contract rather than adding a parallel one.
- **Behavior:** fixes a data-loss bug on an existing endpoint. No change to request/response shapes; the only new observable effect is that `lastTouch`/backfilled `firstTouch` now actually persist on merge (previously discarded). Pure correctness.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 40 passed in the 2 touched suites (`crmDb.updateLead.attribution`, `webhooks.leadForwarding`), 0 failed.
- Broader regression sweep: `crmDb.* | webhooks.* | crm.* | leadSchema | leadCapture` → 1234 passed / 60 suites / 0 failed.
- `npx tsc`: clean (exit 0).
- Tested as: unit/integration with mocked `crmDb` (MOCKABLE — no live services).

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/webhooks.ts` — merge path attribution propagation
- `backend/src/services/db.ts` — `updateLead` attribution params + SET expressions
- `backend/src/__tests__/webhooks.leadForwarding.test.ts` — merge-path attribution tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/crmDb.updateLead.attribution.test.ts` — new updateLead attribution unit tests

## What was NOT tested
- Live DynamoDB round-trip (unit tests assert the constructed UpdateExpression/values, not real persistence). No prod/dev DDB write was exercised — out of scope for AFK/MOCKABLE.
- The `lead = { ...existingLead, ...updates }` in-memory object returned to downstream auto-draft/alert flows is unchanged in shape; not separately re-tested beyond the existing suite passing.

title: feat(mcp): get_account_status tool — plan/status/features/api-key count
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
No MCP tool exposed account info, so agents couldn't tell what plan/features a user has before suggesting features or upgrade prompts.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds a no-arg `get_account_status` MCP tool that returns a curated `{ email, subscription_plan, subscription_status, current_period_end, allowed_features, api_key_count }`. It wraps the existing `GET /api/auth/me` (plan/status/features) and `GET /api/v1/agent/api-keys` (count) self-calls through `mcpFetch`, so it inherits `authenticateToken` and is scoped to the caller.

## How to test
1. As an agent / MCP client authenticated as any user, invoke the `get_account_status` tool with `{}`.
2. **Expected**: a JSON object with exactly these keys — `email`, `subscription_plan`, `subscription_status`, `current_period_end`, `allowed_features` (array), `api_key_count` (number). No other fields.
3. Invoke as a Free user with no Stripe subscription and no API keys.
4. **Expected**: `subscription_plan: "Free"`, `subscription_status: "inactive"`, `current_period_end: null`, `allowed_features: []`, `api_key_count: 0`.
5. Confirm no sensitive fields leak.
6. **Expected**: the output never contains `password`, `stripe_customer_id`, or other raw `/me` fields.

## Edge cases to check
- If the `/api/v1/agent/api-keys` call fails (500), account status still returns with `api_key_count: 0` (best-effort).
- If `/api/auth/me` fails with 401, the tool surfaces the auth error rather than fabricating a status.

## Behavioral assertions verified (from Notion spec)
| Spec acceptance criterion | Verifying test |
|---|---|
| Tool name `get_account_status` | `should register get_account_status and expose it to external MCP clients` |
| Input `{}` (no args) | `should declare a no-arg input schema (object with no required fields)` |
| Output `{ email, subscription_plan, subscription_status, current_period_end, allowed_features, api_key_count }` | `should return exactly the curated output shape ...` |
| Wraps existing `/api/auth/me` | `should call GET /api/auth/me and GET /api/v1/agent/api-keys with the caller context` |
| Registered + reachable by clients | `should register get_account_status and expose it to external MCP clients` |
| No sensitive leak (defensive) | `should never leak sensitive raw fields ...` |
| Free-user defaults | `should default missing plan/status fields to safe values and zero api keys` |
| Robust key count | `should treat a missing/non-array keys payload as zero api keys`; `should still report account status even if the api-keys call fails ...` |
| Auth error surfaced | `should propagate an auth error from the /me call ...` |

## Behavior-preserving proof
No existing tool, route, or chat output is modified — this is purely additive (one new tool registration). All 37 `mcp.apiTools` tests pass (28 pre-existing unchanged + 9 new). 82 tests across `mcp.registry`, `mcp.toolRegistry`, `mcp.mcpServer`, `security.mcpServer`, `mcpServerAuth` still pass, confirming the new registration doesn't disturb registry/server behavior.

- **Moving parts:** +1 MCP tool. No new table, flag, dependency, or branch in the dispatch path. No change to the agent loop.
- **Behavior:** additive only. No change to any existing tool's output or to chat behavior.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 37 passed (`mcp.apiTools.test.ts`), 0 failed. +82 passed across related MCP suites.
- `npx tsc`: clean (exit 0).
- Tested as: mocked `mcpFetch` (Pro user, Free user, missing-keys, failing-keys, auth-error).

## Files changed
- `backend/src/mcp/server/apiTools.ts` — register `get_account_status`

title: fix(landingPages): publish reports stale subdomain (live domain mismatch)
body:
## Problem

Publishing the Every.io Day Zero landing page returned the wrong live domain:

- **Expected:** `https://everyio.agentwebforms.com/every-io-day-zero-pre-seed-fou`
- **Actual:** `https://everyio-day-zero-founders.agentwebforms.com/every-io-day-zero-pre-seed-fou`

## Root cause

The publish (`POST /generated/:id/publish`) and edit (`PUT /github-edit`) endpoints — and `agentModeService.getLeadLists` — reported the page's live URL via `getLandingPageLiveUrl(page)`, which returns the raw stored `customDomainUrl`. That stored managed subdomain (`*.agentwebforms.com`) can go **stale**: it keeps an old subdomain that has silently detached from the Vercel project (re-deploy, or a 409 collision that re-added the subdomain with a different suffix) and now serves a Vercel `DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND` 404.

The `GET /generated` list endpoint already corrects this against `AW-CustomDomains` (the source of truth), but these call sites didn't — so publish surfaced the stale subdomain.

## Fix

Added `resolveLandingPageLiveUrl(page)` to `v0Service` — the single-page equivalent of the list endpoint's correction:

- Looks up the project's attached domains (`listDomains(ownerId, projectId)`).
- Prefers a verified custom domain over a managed subdomain; ties broken by most-recently-updated.
- Only rewrites stored `*.agentwebforms.com` hosts that no longer match the attached domain. **Real custom domains are left untouched.**
- Owner-scoped lookup, so org members editing a shared page see the same URL the owner does.
- Never throws — falls back to the stored value on missing project, no domains, or lookup error.

Wired into the publish endpoint, the edit endpoint, and `getLeadLists`.

## Testing

- **Unit (`services.v0Service.test.ts`):** 11 cases for `resolveLandingPageLiveUrl` — stale-subdomain correction (incl. slug preservation), adopt-when-empty, keep-matching, leave real custom domains, custom>subdomain preference, `updatedAt` tie-break, and all fallback paths (no project / no domains / lookup throws / malformed URL).
- **Integration (`routes.landingPageGeneration.test.ts`):** new `POST /publish` suite asserting the response `live_url` is the resolved attached domain and never leaks the stale `everyio-day-zero-founders` host.
- **Full backend suite:** 12,792 passed, 3 skipped (0 failures).
- **Live verification:** seeded the exact bug scenario into dev DynamoDB (stale stored subdomain + correct `AW-CustomDomains` record) and confirmed both the real `resolveLandingPageLiveUrl` and the live HTTP backend (via an authenticated browser session) return the corrected `everyio.agentwebforms.com` URL. Seed data cleaned up.

title: feat(agent): real background-removal tool for transparent logos (postmortem fix)
body:
## Summary
Postmortem fix for the Aquila transparent-logo workflow. The agent had no way to produce a genuine transparent-alpha logo: `remove_c2pa_from_image` only strips metadata, and `generate_image` redraws the mark (drifting icon/letters/colors). This adds a real, deterministic background-removal tool and fixes the misleading guidance that led to the failures.

## What changed
**New capability — `remove_image_background`**
- `imageGeneration.ts`: `removeImageBackground()` — edge-seeded **flood-fill color key** over raw RGBA pixels via Sharp (already a dependency). Detects the background from the corner median, clears alpha on contiguous border-connected pixels within a tolerance. Produces a **genuine alpha PNG without redrawing the mark**; enclosed regions (e.g. a counter inside a letter, the hole in a logo) are preserved because the fill only follows border-connected pixels. Adds WCAG helpers.
- `agentModeService.ts`: orchestration (download → process → S3) + optional `surface_color` **WCAG contrast check** that warns when a logo would be illegible on the target surface (the "dark wordmark on dark header" mistake).
- `emma/tools.ts`: registers the tool and fixes descriptions — `remove_c2pa_from_image` now states it does NOT remove backgrounds, `generate_image` routes transparent-bg requests to the new tool, `update_html_file` gains container-scoped selector guidance (avoid `:contains+:first` when a brand word appears in both header and footer).

**Bonus bug fix:** filename normalization `lastIndexOf('.') || length` was dead code (`-1` is truthy), collapsing extension-less names like `"logo"` → `".png"`. Fixed at both call sites (new method + the pre-existing `removeC2PAFromImage` twin).

> Note: this is a deterministic color-key, not ML — ideal for the **solid-background logo** case it was built for (crisp, exact, byte-for-byte mark preservation). It is not subject-segmentation for photographic backgrounds; an ML fallback (`@imgly/background-removal-node`) was deliberately deferred to avoid adding a Python/ONNX runtime to the Node backend.

## Testing
- `npx tsc` clean (CI build command, 4GB heap).
- New suites: real-Sharp functional tests (proves alpha, interior-counter preservation, tolerance, corner-median, WCAG helpers); orchestration tests (filename incl. truncation regression, contrast pass/fail/unparseable, error paths); registration/description tests.
- Existing image suites pass (no regressions) — 86 tests across the touched + adjacent suites.
- **End-to-end via Playwright** (customer portal, live agent chat): Emma invoked `remove_image_background` on a real Google-logo PNG with `surface_color #1a1a2e` → returned a `*_transparent.png` S3 URL and contrast 4.39:1 (legible). Downloaded artifact verified: `channels:4 hasAlpha:true`, 70.5% transparent / 26.4% opaque, foreground colors intact.

## How to test manually
1. `http://16.146.115.135:5174`, log in as `test@example.com` / `Test123!`.
2. Agent chat: *"Make the background of this logo transparent: \<URL\> — it will sit on a dark header, surface color #1a1a2e."*
3. Expect Emma to call **`remove_image_background`** (not generate_image/remove_c2pa), return a `*_transparent.png` URL + contrast result. Try a dark logo on `#1a1a2e` to see the low-contrast ⚠️ warning.

title: Fix HubSpot real-time sync: push inbound leads on creation
body:
## Problem

Reported for `lyndi@every.io`: leads only sync to HubSpot on a **manual push**, never in real time. Leads captured today never reached HubSpot.

## Root cause

`externalCrmSyncService.autoSyncLead(...)` is the real-time push to connected external CRMs (HubSpot/Attio). It was only called from the **authenticated UI** lead routes:
- `POST /api/crm/lists/:listId/leads` (manual add)
- `PUT  /api/crm/lists/:listId/leads/:leadId` (manual edit)

The **inbound, unauthenticated capture paths** — how real leads actually "come in" — created the lead (and even auto-enrolled it into drip sequences) but **never called `autoSyncLead`**:
- `POST /api/webhooks/forward-lead` (landing-page / lead-forward webhook) — `webhooks.ts:468`
- `POST /api/crm/public/leads/:listId` (public capture form) — `crmPublic.ts:196`

So a form/webhook lead sat in AgentWeb until someone opened the CRM and hit **Push to HubSpot**, which runs a different code path (`startPushJob`) that iterates the whole list. That matches the symptom exactly: manual push works, real-time doesn't.

## Fix

Both inbound paths now fire `autoSyncLead` for `hubspot` and `attio` immediately after the lead is created/updated, using the **list owner's `userId`** (the request is unauthenticated):
- Webhook: `created` on new lead, `updated` on merge; skipped when the lead is unchanged.
- Public form: `created`.

Fire-and-forget with a `.catch` guard so a CRM outage can never fail or delay lead capture. `autoSyncLead` already no-ops when auto-sync is disabled or the CRM isn't configured for the list, so this is safe for all users.

## Tests

- `webhooks.leadForwarding.test.ts`: syncs created/updated to both providers, skips on unchanged, never fails the request on sync error.
- `crmPublic.leads.test.ts`: syncs new lead to both providers with owner userId, no sync on 403, 201 returned even when sync rejects.
- Full CRM/sync/webhook suite: **1263 tests pass**, `npx tsc` clean.

## Note

EB tail logs had already rotated past today's lead-capture events, so the diagnosis is from the code paths (decisive) rather than a specific log line. Once merged, `[webhooks]`/`[crmPublic]` auto-sync error logs and the existing `[ExternalCrmSync] Auto-sync failed ...` line will surface any per-lead HubSpot API failures.

title: fix(linkedin): auto-trim over-limit invite notes instead of failing/looping
body:
## Problem

When generating LinkedIn connection invitations, the autonomous agent repeatedly produced notes over LinkedIn's hard char limit (200 free / 300 Premium) — observed at 203/204/207/210 chars in a real scheduled session. `sendInvitation()` **threw** on over-limit notes and the agent-mode error guidance told the LLM to "shorten and retry"; because LLMs can't reliably count characters, this looped, burning failed tool calls before correcting (or never sending).

## Root cause

The over-limit text comes from the LLM's tool-call args on the **autonomous agent path**. The human CRM path was already hard-guarded client-side (disabled send button + live counter), so this was exclusively the agent path. The "shorten and retry" loop was the failure mode.

## Fix

Deterministic, consistent length control across **every** invite-note path:

- **`LinkedInOutreachService.trimInviteMessage()`** (shared chokepoint) — trims an over-limit note preferring a **sentence boundary**, then a **word boundary**, surrogate-safe (never emits malformed UTF-16). Byte-identical no-op for any note already within the limit.
- **`sendInvitation()`** — auto-trims instead of throwing, so a send **never fails on length**. The agent inline send path stays pure deterministic trim (it's the path that looped).
- **Draft paths** (CRM `draft-invite-note` route + agent draft-email/message helper) — now run a capped (≤2 attempts) LLM re-generation via the new **`inviteNoteShortener.ts`** when a draft is over limit, then always hard-trim as the guarantee.
- Tool description (`emma/tools.ts`) updated: model is steered to aim ~195 chars and told over-limit notes are auto-trimmed (not rejected).

## Two-layer model, now uniform everywhere
- **Layer 1 (aim short):** prompt instruction in both draft generators + the inline tool description.
- **Layer 2 (deterministic fallback):** every path ends in the same `trimInviteMessage` guarantee.

## Behavioral impact
- **Compliant notes (the common case): zero change** — `trimInviteMessage` returns the input byte-for-byte for any length 0→limit (proven exhaustively).
- **Over-limit notes:** previously failed/looped or cut mid-word → now sent once, sentence/word-clean. Strictly equal-or-better in every case.
- Known trade-off: on the send path the agent isn't told a trim happened (acceptable vs. the retry loop).

## Tests
- Full backend suite: **12,876 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed** (804 suites). `npx tsc` clean. Backend restarted healthy.
- New: `inviteNoteShortener.test.ts` (100% line/branch — JSON parse variants, double-encode, truncated-JSON repair, quote fallback, empty/garbage, attempt capping, candidate rejection), `crm.draftInviteNote.trim.test.ts` (re-gen + trim-to-empty), sentence-boundary + threshold cases in `linkedInOutreachService.test.ts`.

## Not tested live
Did not drive a real LinkedIn invite via Playwright — it would send a real connection request to a third party via Unipile, and the human UI is client-guarded so it can't produce an over-limit input. Evidence is unit/integration + runtime repro of the exact bug lengths (203/204/207/210 → ≤195).

title: fix(templates): preserve fidelity for large HTML email templates
body:
## Problem

When a large branded newsletter (e.g. the ~135K-char Aquila newsletter with base64-embedded images and print/`@page` CSS) was saved as an Email Template via `create_html_template`, the saved template's **HTML Preview did not match the Claude-generated source**.

**Root cause:** `createHtmlTemplate` round-tripped the *entire* user HTML through `generateHTML` (16K output-token cap) to inject `{{variable}}` placeholders. For large docs the model truncated/regenerated the document, dropped base64 blobs, and rewrote print CSS — so the stored `html_content` no longer matched the source and the preview diverged.

### Proven against real prod data
- **Original source** (from prod S3, the `html_source` the session passed): **135,110 bytes**, ends with `</html>`, 3 base64 images, print CSS intact.
- **Corrupted stored template** (`37888b95…`, pulled from prod `AW-Settings`): **22,028 bytes (84% of the document lost)**, **truncated mid-base64-blob**, no closing `</html>` — exactly the 16K-output-cap truncation.

## Fix

Gate behavior on document size:
- **≤50K chars** (~16K output-token ceiling): unchanged full-rewrite path.
- **>50K chars** (`parameterizeLargeHtml`): ask the model only for a small JSON **variable-map** (name + exact source anchor), strip base64 payloads from the prompt, then apply substitutions **deterministically to the pristine original bytes**. The output cap never bites (output is a tiny JSON map), and base64 images, print CSS, layout, and brand colors are preserved verbatim.

**Substitution safety** (`applyVariableMap` + `computeSafeTextRanges`):
- `htmlparser2` parses the doc once to get source-offset ranges of renderable text nodes only (excludes `<style>`/`<script>`/`<title>`/comments/tags/attributes). Replacement splices original bytes — no DOM reserialization — so every occurrence of a repeated value is parameterized consistently without ever corrupting CSS/markup.
- Variable names must match `/^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$/`; empty/unmatched anchors are skipped, not guessed.
- Best-effort: on any LLM failure the document is stored verbatim.

**Known coverage limits** (intentional, fidelity-first; left literal, not corrupted): values in attributes (href/alt/meta), values split across element boundaries, entity/whitespace-normalized anchors, and the subject line. Documented in code and surfaced in the result note.

Adds `htmlparser2` as a direct backend dependency.

## Verification
- ✅ `npx tsc` clean.
- ✅ **19/19** unit tests pass in `agentModeService.createHtmlTemplate.test.ts` (new large-doc fidelity suite: verbatim base64/print-CSS, base64 stripped from prompt, unmatched-anchor skip, malformed-name rejection, all-body-occurrences replaced but never in style/title/attrs, fallback-on-throw, small-path unchanged).
- ✅ **Real end-to-end resave in test env:** ran `create_html_template` on the actual 135K Aquila original against dev DynamoDB → stored result is **byte-for-byte identical to the source** (same SHA256, `diff` empty, ends with `</html>`, all 3 base64 images + print CSS + brand colors intact).
- ✅ **Preview path:** stored HTML rendered through the real customer-portal `buildPreviewSrcDoc` + DOMPurify preserves base64, `@media print`, `print-color-adjust`, and brand colors.

## Post-merge follow-up
The existing prod template `37888b95-b50b-49c2-9eb8-6a82b39c6f30` is still corrupted at rest (this fix only changes the save path). It must be **re-saved from source** in prod to heal its preview.

title: Require human confirmation before Meta Ads writes and image edits
body:
## Summary
Adds a human-in-the-loop confirmation guardrail for destructive/publishing actions in agent mode, fixing the systemic "agent acted on the wrong target" failure from the 2026-06-12 satisfaction review (session: agent regenerated the wrong image set, then published ads to the **Leasing** campaign instead of **Maintenance**).

Two failure modes from the incident are now **hard-gated** (the agent loop physically halts and cannot self-approve — only a new user message resumes the turn):

1. **Wrong-campaign publish** — `call_meta_marketing_api` write actions (CAMPAIGN/AD_SET/AD CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE/COPY_AD, plus AD_CREATIVE CREATE and CUSTOM_AUDIENCE CREATE/UPLOAD_USERS) resolve and echo the exact target (campaign + ad set + asset names/IDs, content/budget changes) and require `confirm=true` to execute.
2. **Wrong-image-set regeneration** — `generate_image` with `inputImages` (i.e. editing existing images) halts, shows the source image(s) as thumbnails, and requires `confirm=true`.

## How it works
- The gate returns `awaitingUserConfirmation: true` + a `confirmationPrompt`; `collectConfirmationPrompt` breaks the agent loop and surfaces the prompt to the user. The model re-calls with `confirm=true` after approval.
- The `confirm` flag is stripped before dispatch so it never reaches the Meta SDK / image service.
- Read-only actions (LIST/SEARCH/UPLOAD_IMAGE/UPLOAD_VIDEO) are not gated.
- Batched edits in one turn collapse into a single consolidated confirmation block.
- The gate flag is preserved through `extractMinimalToolResult` so the frontend renders the correct "Awaiting your confirmation" state on both live-SSE and persisted paths.

## Testing
- `npx tsc`: clean.
- Full backend suite: **13,120 passed / 0 failed** (824 suites, 3 skipped).
- E2E via Playwright (real Emma chat): image-edit gate halt → "Awaiting your confirmation" tool card, no stuck "Generating image…" panel, then confirm → execute. Evidence captured.
- Meta write gate verified via the live HTTP path (`/api/emma/meta-ads/marketing-api`) — no connected Meta account on the test tenant, so the wrong-campaign publish needs a manual pass with a real Meta account before relying on it in prod.

title: fix(agent-mode): cancel orphaned generation on wall-clock timeout
body:
## Problem

When an agent-mode generation exceeds the wall-clock limit (`GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS`), the backend returned `504 GENERATION_TIMEOUT` and released the session lock — but the underlying worker generation **kept running detached**. The original `withGenerationTimeout` only released the lock; its own comment noted *"this does NOT cancel the underlying generation."*

That orphaned run caused two user-facing problems:
1. **Wasted compute + duplicate image write** — the generation finished server-side and wrote a real image nobody asked for anymore.
2. **Stuck/duplicate "Generating image…" UI** — the orphan kept emitting `executing_tools`/`tool_executed` on the shared SSE stream, re-opening the placeholder the user was told had failed, and surfacing a **second image** after they retried.

These are the same root cause (the orphan), so this fixes both.

## Fix

Make the timeout path mirror the existing **manual-stop** path, which already cleanly stops generation:

- **`agentModeController.ts`** — on `isGenerationTimeout`, call `requestCancel(sessionId)` + `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.cancelSession(sessionId)` before re-throwing to the 504 handler. The worker breaks out of its loop and the response is discarded (`response.cancelled`). Applied to **both** the authenticated `/generate` and the interactive-share generate paths.
- **`agentModeService.ts`** — gate the `executing_tools` and `tool_executed` progress emissions on `!isCancelled()`, closing the last race where a tool (e.g. `generate_image`) completing in the same iteration the cancel arrives could emit a late real-image event.

## Verification

- New TDD test `agentModeController.timeoutCancelsOrphan.test.ts` (failed before, passes after): a timed-out `/generate` signals cancellation and still returns 504; a normal error does NOT cancel.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Related suites green (`agentModeController*`, `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService`): 428/428.
- **E2E (Playwright):** timeout → backend logs `cancelling orphaned worker run`, **no orphan SSE after the 504**, shimmer never reappears, no duplicate image written. Happy path → placeholder shows and resolves to the real image (no false suppression).

Pairs with the customer-portal PR (frontend suppression gate) on the same branch name.
