title: fix(agent-mode): expose enriched-field provenance in get_lead_details
body:
## Problem

A customer (founders@agentweb.pro) asked the agent-mode chat *"For the 'June 17th YC founder poker night' lead list, where do you get the funding stage and ARR information from?"* The agent gave a vague answer ("added via web enrichment") and could not cite a precise data source. The reported complaint — "Funding Round + ARR for earlier-stage startups are not accurate, where does this come from?" — is a **data-provenance** problem, not a rendering bug.

## Root cause

Every enriched lead field stores a provenance sidecar `enrichmentMetadata[field]` = `{ source, provider, sourceUrl, sourceQuote, confidence, enrichedAt }`. The customer-portal REST routes already expose this (sanitized) and `EnrichedValue.tsx` renders it on hover. But the agent's `get_lead_details` tool returned `customFields` (the values) and **omitted `enrichmentMetadata` entirely** — leaving the LLM structurally blind to provenance, so it guessed.

Confirmed data sources: Apollo `/organizations/enrich` (funding stage = high conf; annual revenue = low conf, synthesized estimate), Crunchbase/open-web SERP parsing, and LLM web-search extraction via the V3 group waterfall (`provider: 'llm_web_search'`). ARR for leads is a custom field populated by Apollo/web-search — **not** Stripe.

## Fix

1. `agentModeService.getLeadDetails` now runs the lead's `enrichmentMetadata` through the existing `sanitizeEnrichmentMetadataForResponse` (strips cross-tenant CRM-history sibling lineage, rewrites `crm-history`→`agentweb`) and includes it in the response when present.
2. Updated the `get_lead_details` tool description so the agent cites provider/sourceUrl/confidence per field instead of guessing.

`get_leads`/`search_leads` (bulk summaries) still omit metadata by design.

## Testing

- 3 new unit tests (provenance surfaced; cross-tenant lineage sanitized; omitted for manual/legacy leads). Written first, confirmed failing pre-fix, passing post-fix.
- `npx tsc` clean; 143/143 across affected suites; no regressions.
- E2E (Playwright, customer portal → backend): agent invoked "Get lead details" and produced a precise provenance table citing the Crunchbase URL + quote for funding stage (medium conf) and flagging ARR as Apollo-sourced, low confidence, no citation — even surfacing the likely raise-vs-ARR conflation the customer was chasing.

## Risks / notes

- This makes the agent honest about provenance and confidence; it does **not** improve Apollo's early-stage ARR estimates (a data-vendor limitation now made visible rather than hidden). A follow-up could suppress/relabel Apollo's low-confidence revenue for early-stage companies.

title: fix(org): make org-shared ad accounts usable + hide owner-only controls from members
body:
## Problem
Two related org connected-accounts bugs reported on `/settings/accounts`:

1. **Shared ad accounts were visible but unusable.** A teammate's LinkedIn/Meta/Google Ads account marked `sharedWithOrg=true` showed in another member's Settings, but every ad-credential resolver read only the caller's own `connected_accounts`, so using it returned "not connected".
2. **Owner-only controls leaked to members.** The connected-accounts list returned no ownership info, so Share / Stop-sharing / Disconnect rendered on every row for any org member — including teammates' shared accounts. - New `getAccountsWithOwnerIncludingOrgShared(callerUserId)` tags each account with its **owner** userId. `getAccountsByUserIdIncludingOrgShared` is now a thin wrapper over it.
- The three ad-credential resolvers (`getLinkedInAdsCredentials`, `getMetaCredentials`, `googleAdsService.getAccountCredentials`) source accounts from it; token refresh writes back to the **owner's** record (scoped to account_id), not the caller's.
- `GET /api/oauth/connected-accounts` adds an `owned` flag per account; the frontend (separate customer-portal PR) gates owner-only controls on it and shows a read-only "Shared by org" badge otherwise.

## Tests
- Backend: full suite green (13,324 passed, 0 failures); new coverage for owner-tagged resolution, owner-scoped token refresh, and the `owned` flag.
- E2E verified with throwaway org accounts + Playwright.

## Scope note
`getAccountById`-based consumption (social posts/metrics, gmail, hubspot, attio) has the same latent caller-scoped pattern but is out of scope for this Ads-focused fix.

title: fix(agent-mode): work-plan image-resume — asset-aware context, step progression, no regen loop
body:
## Problem
The "LinkedIn Ads Campaign generator" work plan stalled at **Step 3 (Generate 3 Images Per Hook, 18 images)** in production (prod session \`7c8ff5b2-...\`). Root cause — validated against the real DynamoDB session, not the bug report:

- Each agent run has a **10-min wall-clock timeout** (\`GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS\`). An 18-image step exceeds it, so the run times out mid-step and the diagnosis agent tells the user to retry.
- On retry, the still-pending step was re-rendered into LLM context with **no record of the images already generated**, so the model regenerated everything from scratch → timed out again → infinite loop.
- Evidence: \`generate_image\` ran **68×** for ~18 images, cost **$10.86**, Step 3 stuck \`pending\` (duplicate filenames across msg indices confirm regeneration).

## Fix
- **Asset-aware context:** \`extractGeneratedImageFilenames()\` scans the session's \`Image generated:\` system messages (dual-matches a new \`metadata.kind\` marker + legacy string for back-compat) and surfaces them as an **ALREADY-GENERATED ASSETS** block, so the model only generates what's missing.
- **STEP PROGRESSION** guidance for all active plans (not just autocomplete): advance via \`set_work_plan_status\` instead of stalling; don't mark a step complete before its work is finished/approved.
- **Multi-intent handling:** a single batched/conflicting user message is resolved in plan order rather than stalling.
- **Regen carve-out:** the no-regenerate guard yields when the user explicitly asks to regenerate/restart/redo/change.
- **Emma parity:** resume guidance is scoped to agent mode via \`includeResumeGuidance\` (default true); Emma keeps exact production behavior.

## Tests
- **81/81 pass** across the 4 work-plan suites (\`buildWorkPlanContext\`, \`buildMarketingContext\`, \`agentModeService.workPlan\`, \`chatbotService.workPlan\`). \`npx tsc\` clean.

## E2E verification (Playwright, live, Claude Opus 4.8)
Seeded a dev session reproducing the exact prod failure state (Step 3 pending + 6 images already generated). Across **3 independent live runs** (user's manual test + plain "go" + batched multi-intent): **0 regenerations**, plan advanced via \`set_work_plan_status\`, report produced, all steps reached \`completed\`. Pre-fix this exact state looped forever.

## Risks / remaining concerns
- Steers the model via prompt context (not a hard gate) — probabilistic, but 3/3 live runs passed.
- Convergence, not speed: the 10-min timeout is unchanged; a true 18-image step still needs a few nudges but now makes net forward progress instead of looping.
- Adjacent (separate) issue surfaced in testing — Step 2 hook/ad-copy not always persisting into the Step 4 context window — is **not** a regression of this fix; flagged for a follow-up.

title: fix(agent-mode): converge large image batches with a per-run media-generation time budget
body:
## Problem

A predefined work-plan step that generates many images — e.g. the LinkedIn Ads **"Generate 3 Images Per Hook"** plan (6 hooks × 3 = 18 images) — runs the images **sequentially** (required: `addMessageToSession` is read-count-then-write-at-index, not atomic, so the batch cannot be parallelized without corrupting message indices). A single agent run is capped by a **hard 10-min wall-clock timeout** (`AGENT_MODE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT_MS`). 18 images can't finish in 10 min, so the run is killed mid-step, `set_work_plan_status` never fires, and the step is left **pending**.

Validated against the incident session `7c8ff5b2-066a-474c-a0cb-9ec0ac37c2f0` (DynamoDB `AW-ChatSessions`, prod):
- step 3 "Generate 3 Images Per Hook" stuck `pending`; only 2 `set_work_plan_status` calls (steps 1, 2)
- **68 successful** `generate_image` calls, **1** failure — a non-converging *regeneration* runaway, **not** repeated hard timeouts of the image API as the report assumed
- 112 messages, ran 2.5 h

The merged asset-awareness fix (`d4b19f22`, already on main) stops the *regenerate-from-scratch* loop, but — as that commit's own message states — it leaves the wall-clock gap open: a single run still attempts every remaining image and gets hard-killed.

## Fix

A softer **per-run media-generation time budget** in the tool-dispatch boundary (`agentMode/core/toolDispatch.ts`). Once the run is over its deadline (default **7 min**, env `AGENT_MODE_MEDIA_BUDGET_MS`, headroom under the 10-min hard timeout) **and** has produced ≥1 asset this run, further `generate_image` / `generate_video` / `generate_voiceover` calls are **gracefully deferred** instead of executed:

- **deferral is neither success nor failure** — no asset, no pending counter (so `set_work_plan_status`'s `requiredFunctionCalls` gate is untouched), no error, no failed counter (so the gateway repeated-failure breaker is untouched);
- a **tool-role message is still appended** for the orphaned `tool_call_id` (required for the next LLM turn), telling the model to stop, summarize progress, and ask the user to reply **"continue"**;
- the **≥1-asset gate** guarantees a run that starts already over budget still produces one image before stopping — forward progress every turn.

Combined with the existing already-generated-assets context, the next turn generates **only the still-missing assets**, so an 18-image batch converges across a few turns instead of dying mid-step. Opt-in via the deadline input (`0` disables) → no behavior change when unset.

## Testing

**Unit** — 5 new tests in `toolDispatch.test.ts` (no-deadline no-defer, over-budget defer, forward-progress first-asset, non-media never deferred, deferred≠asset). Full related suite: **97 tests pass**, `npx tsc` clean.

**End-to-end (Playwright, customer portal, `AGENT_MODE_MEDIA_BUDGET_MS=1` to force deferral after image 1):**
1. "Generate 3 ad images: coffee1/2/3.png" → **coffee1.png generated**, coffee2/3 **deferred**; Emma reported "1 of 3 saved", listed ✅/⏳ progress, offered a **"Continue"** chip.
2. Clicked **Continue** → generated **coffee2.png only** (distinct S3 URL), did **NOT** regenerate coffee1; reported "2 of 3 saved", deferred again. Confirms convergence + no regeneration.

Test-only env var was removed and the backend restarted on the default 7-min budget after the run.

## Risks / edge cases
- **Scheduled/unattended runs** ("[AUTOMATED UNATTENDED EXECUTION]") can't honor "reply continue", but deferring (graceful stop + persisted partial progress) is still strictly better than today's mid-step hard-kill. Could later auto-continue these; out of scope here.
- Budget is wall-clock from run start; a run that spends its whole budget on non-media work then issues one image still gets one image (≥1-asset gate ensures progress).
- `0` / unset disables entirely, preserving prior behavior byte-for-byte (characterization tests unchanged).

## Manual test cases
1. **Multi-image request** (set `AGENT_MODE_MEDIA_BUDGET_MS=1`): ask Emma for 3+ images → exactly one generates, the rest defer with a "reply continue" message + chip.
2. **Continue** → only missing images generate; already-saved ones are not recreated.
3. **Default budget** (unset / 7 min): a small 1–2 image request completes normally with no deferral.
4. **Disabled** (`AGENT_MODE_MEDIA_BUDGET_MS=0`): behaves exactly as before (no deferral regardless of time).

title: fix(agent-mode): surface enrichment provenance & flag unverified firmographic fields
body:
## Problem

Surfaced in the 24h satisfaction review (session `aac0b28a-3de3-49ae-9197-4246e1e6c23a`): Emma confidently reported a wrong company funding stage ("Slashy = Series C") as established fact. The V3 enrichment engine already computes per-field reliability signals (`confidence`, critic `criticView`, `verifiedBy`), but several agent-facing surfaces dropped that metadata — so Emma stated web-guessed firmographics with no source or confidence.

## Root cause

Small companies' `funding_stage` isn't in Apollo, so it's filled by the web-search/LLM tier (`confidence: 'medium'`), where the LLM can return a plausible-but-wrong value. The metadata existed but wasn't surfaced on:
- the **enrichment preview** summary (`runEmmaEnrichment`) — bare values only;
- **`search_leads`** (list-wide "funding stage for each lead") — returned `customFields` values but not `enrichmentMetadata`;
- **`enrich_lead_custom`** (single-lead on-demand) — returned `enrichedValues` with no provenance.

title: fix(agent-mode): all ishare links stop working after 7 days
body:
## Problem

**All ishare links stop working** ~7 days after they're created — recipients hit `410 Gone` even though anonymous access should work and the share is still active.

## Root cause

Commit `64f9275a` (Mar 15, "expire legacy interactive shares after 7 days from creation") introduced `getInteractiveShareExpiresAt()`, which treats an interactive share with **no `expiresAt`** as expiring `sharedAt + 7 days`.

But every public plan/ishare link is created **without** an `expiresAt`:
- `createSessionWithPlan` (`agentModeController.ts:5874`) sets `isActive`, `token`, `sharedAt` only.
- All pre-March legacy shares likewise have no `expiresAt`.

So each such link silently returned `410` exactly 7 days after creation — i.e. effectively *all* ishare/plan links broke a week out. The helper is used at 8 call sites (get, generate, llm-model, progress, stop, feedback, upload, OG metadata), so the whole anonymous surface was affected.

## Fix

`getInteractiveShareExpiresAt()` now only enforces expiry when an explicit `expiresAt` is set. Shares without one never expire on a timer; their availability is governed solely by `isActive`. Links created via `createConversableShare` (which set a real `expiresAt`) still expire as configured. Removed the now-unused `LEGACY_SHARE_DEFAULT_EXPIRATION_DAYS` constant.

## Verification

Reproduced and verified against the live dev backend:

| Session | State | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| active, `sharedAt` Oct 2025, no `expiresAt` | should work | `410` ❌ | `200` ✅ |
| active, `expiresAt` 2026-06-10 (past) | should expire | `410` | `410` ✅ |

- `npx tsc` clean
- `interactiveShareExpiration.test.ts`: 13/13 pass (legacy-expiry assertions inverted to assert no-expiresAt links stay live)
- Related ishare/share suites: 82/82 pass

## Notes
- Backend-only; no customer-portal changes.
- Sessions already auto-deactivated by the old bug (`isActive: false`) will need re-sharing by their owners; this fix prevents any *active* link from being killed going forward.

title: fix(agent-mode): completion guard blocks generate_image for genuinely-missing assets
body:
## Incident: xCures LinkedIn Ads Campaign (session 7c8ff5b2-…)

One incident with multiple faces, traced across three Notion cards (same user/session/work plan). All hypotheses verified against the **production session record** and the code — not prior reviews.

### Verified ground truth (prod DynamoDB)
- Step 3 "Generate 3 Images Per Hook — 18 total": `requiredFunctionCalls: ["generate_image"]` (×1), `status: completed`.
- `calledFunctions.generate_image = 76`, `failedFunctions.generate_image = 1` — yet the model's own Step 4 note says **only 3 images were verified**. `autocomplete: false`.
- So: the existing completion gate required just **1** generate_image call; the counter was **76**; only **3** assets existed. The gate was satisfied by a polluted counter.

### Root causes (two code bugs + one UX dead-end)
1. **Counter pollution** — `generate_image`'s image-EDIT confirmation gate returns `{success:true, awaitingUserConfirmation:true}` with no asset; `toolDispatch` counted every such return toward `calledFunctions`. That inflated the counter to 76 with 0 new assets.
2. **Completion gate counts the wrong thing/amount** — `setWorkPlanStatus` only checked `generate_image` was called ≥1×, not that 18 assets were actually produced.
3. **Recovery dead-end** — once the plan was (wrongly) all-complete, the done-guard hard-refused the user's "generate the missing 15" request.

## Fixes in this PR

**Recovery (P0, commit 690ae8ae + b6f55780)** — done-branch carve-out re-authorizes `generate_image` for explicit missing-asset requests; verify via `search_user_assets`. Agent-mode only (Emma unchanged).

**Counter integrity (P1, commit 9d5ddd83)** — `mediaGenProducedAsset()` in `toolDispatch.ts`: only count a media-gen success toward `calledFunctions`/asset-budget when it actually produced an asset (not a confirmation pause). `calledFunctions.generate_image` now means "images produced."

**Asset-count completion gate (P2/P3, commit f6a70880)** — optional `expectedAssetCount` on work-plan steps; `setWorkPlanStatus` blocks completion until that many assets are produced (counted from "Image generated:" markers — independent of the counter). Flows through create/modify/applyPredefined + tool schemas. Recovery preserved: gate is opt-in, skip never gated, `modify_work_plan` can lower/clear the count. Prompt surfaces the target and forbids silently completing short.

**Tests (commit 7162e7dc)** — counter-pollution cases (confirmation pause not counted, real success counted, mixed batch) + gate cases (blocks short, allows at target, no field = unchanged, skip not gated).

## Testing
- `npx tsc` clean. Full backend suite: **13,627 passed, 0 test failures** (touched suites 84/84 in isolation).
- **Playwright E2E** (seeded active plan: image step pending, expectedAssetCount 18, only 3 images): asked the agent to complete Step 3 with 3 images. It **refused to silently complete**, explained 3 of 18, proposed lowering the target; on approval it called **`modify_work_plan` (18→3) → `set_work_plan_status` (now passes) → advanced to Step 4**. Exact designed flow; the hard gate held.

## Risks / remaining
- Per-step asset attribution is session-wide (correct for the dominant single-image-step plan; documented). 
- `expectedAssetCount` is opt-in; to prevent recurrence on THIS template, its Step 3 needs `expectedAssetCount: 18` set (template lives in DynamoDB `AW-WorkPlans`, not the repo — data change, flagged separately).
- Timeout reliability (card #1) was already fixed (`retryWithBackoff` + media-budget deferral) — verified present, no change here.

title: fix(agent-mode): enforce per-entity completion in scheduled runs
body:
## Problem

Scheduled lead-engagement runs stopped short of completing all steps. In session `b56a2eac-a534-48ca-8320-4571f700e2df` (Daily Event Lead Engagement Review), the agent extracted guest lists for all 3 Luma events and correctly flagged Harsha's unconnected LinkedIn — but then **skipped LinkedIn research, ICP filtering, and pending-approval checks for Events 2 and 3** instead of completing them.

Judge scores: General 3 (goalCompletion 3), Fangfang 4, Matt 3. Both judges independently confirmed the agent "stopped short of completing the scheduled task, explicitly choosing to skip" the remaining per-entity work.

## Root cause (validated independently)

The scheduled-run system-prompt block `[AUTOMATED UNATTENDED EXECUTION]` (in `agentModeController.ts`) ended with *"If you encounter an unrecoverable error, stop and report it."* It had **no per-entity completion guidance, no blocker isolation, and no pre-output completion gate**. The model over-applied the stop-on-error rule to a single per-entity blocker (one teammate's LinkedIn not connected) and abandoned the rest of the work.

## Fix

Extracted the inline directive into a pure, testable `getUnattendedExecutionDirective()` in `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts` and added four behaviors:

1. **Per-entity completion loop** — complete EVERY workflow step for EACH entity; never stop after the first or collect-all-then-skip.
2. **Blocker isolation** — a single-entity blocker is scoped to that entity; note it and continue the others. Only a truly *global* unrecoverable error stops the run.
3. **Pre-output completion gate** — before the final report, verify every entity has each step completed or explicitly blocked-with-reason.
4. **Surface gaps as actionable items** — every blocked/skipped item appears as a clear next action (e.g. "Connect Harsha's LinkedIn so we can research his guests next run").

All existing continuous-execution behavior (no pausing, full stated volume) is preserved.

## Testing

- **Unit:** 20 new assertions in `agentModeService.scheduledSessionContext.test.ts`; 100% coverage on `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts`. 159 passing across all scheduled-chat suites.
- **TSC:** clean (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npx tsc`).
- **End-to-end (live backend):** Created a scheduled chat via the live API, triggered a real test run, and read the persisted system message from `Dev-AW-ChatMessages`. Confirmed the directive (all four sections + preserved continuous-run rules + `[Schedule Context]`) is present in a real scheduled session, and that the LLM path executes with it.

## Problem
A CRM lead "Slashy" (slashy.com) was enriched with funding data belonging to a different company "Slash" (slash.com). Investigation surfaced three distinct backend defects in the V3 enrichment pipeline.

## Fixes (one commit each)
1. **Critic company identity + drop contradicted** — `runCriticReal` now verifies the source describes the *same* company (name/website/email-domain) and returns `contradicted` for a different company even if similarly named. The orchestrator drops `web_search` fills whose `criticVerdict` is `contradicted` (was previously never dropped). `unsupported`/`partially-supported` are kept at low confidence.
2. **Re-verify Tier 0b sibling copies** — sibling-copy used to strip provenance and bypass the critic. Web-sourced copies are now re-stamped `source:'web_search'` carrying `sourceUrl`/`sourceQuote` so the critic re-verifies them against the destination lead. Added `enrichmentMetadata` to `SiblingLeadResult`.
3. **Register configured custom columns at config save** — `setEnrichmentConfig` registers custom column names into `list.fieldNames` so a configured field (e.g. `funding_stage`) shows in the Configure Fields dialog even when its value is dropped/never found.

## Tests

Verified end-to-end against dev: re-running enrichment now critiques the sibling copy + fresh web fill and drops both; `funding_stage` ends absent (UI shows "—"); re-saving config registers `funding_stage` back into the Configure Fields dialog. title: feat(meta): proactively refresh ad-account tokens so expiry never blocks work
body:
## Problem

Meta Marketing API long-lived ad-account tokens expire ~60 days after connect and Meta issues **no refresh tokens**. The client-side FB SDK's "auto-refresh on use" does not apply to our server-stored copy, so an active user's stored token still died at day 60 and blocked all Meta work until a manual reconnect.

**Incident:** `act_26242538088719416` / `admin@rankai.ai` — token expired ~May 26, stayed broken until a manual reconnect Jun 9.

## Fix

Re-exchange a still-valid token via `grant_type=fb_exchange_token` **before** it expires, as both a proactive cron and an inline self-heal:

- `metaService.extendAccessToken()` — the `fb_exchange_token` primitive.
- `metaTokenRefresh.ts` (new) — `isMetaAdAccount`, `needsMetaRefresh` (14-day window), `ensureFreshMetaAdAccountToken` (refreshes, persists, mutates in-memory config, **never throws**; guards non-positive `expires_in` with a 60-day fallback).
- `agentModeService.getMetaCredentials` + `metaV2.getMetaAccountCredentials` self-heal before throwing "expired".

title: fix(fathom): paginate fathom_get_meetings so agent finds all of last week's meetings
body:
## Problem

Reported bug: *"When searching Fathom to cross-reference who we met in the previous week, the results are not what we expected — it could not find Florence's or Susthmia's record accurately."*

## Root cause

The agent-mode tool `fathom_get_meetings` (`backend/src/emma/fathomTools.ts`) read **only the first page** of Fathom's `/external/v1/meetings` endpoint. That endpoint paginates with `next_cursor` at a **default page size of 10**. Any meeting beyond the first ~10 was silently dropped.

When the user asked the agent to cross-reference who they met last week, the agent called this tool, got back only the first page, and reported it "could not find" people (Florence, Susthmia) whose meetings sat on later pages.

This is the same endpoint that `prospectMeetingService.ts` already paginates correctly — with an explicit code comment warning that skipping pagination "silently loses all but the first 10." The agent-mode tool was missing that loop.

## Fix

`fathom_get_meetings` now follows `next_cursor` until exhausted, aggregating every page. Capped at `FATHOM_MAX_PAGES = 20` (200 recordings), mirroring `prospectMeetingService`. Also removed a leftover debug `console.log` that dumped raw API responses on every call.

## Tests

Added to `emma.fathomTools.test.ts`:
- Multi-page cursor following + aggregation (asserts the `cursor=` param is passed on page 2)
- `FATHOM_MAX_PAGES` safety cap against runaway loops
- Regression test reproducing the exact bug — Florence & Susthmia on page 2 are now found

All 17 fathomTools tests pass; full backend suite: **13,651 passed, 0 test failures**.

## E2E verification (Playwright)

Logged into the customer portal agent-mode chat and asked *"Search Fathom and list all my meetings from the previous week."* The agent correctly invoked the real `fathom_get_meetings` tool, computed the window as Mon June 15 – Sun June 21 2026, and (since the test account has no Fathom connected) returned the proper "Connect Fathom" flow — confirming the full wiring works end-to-end with the fix loaded.

title: CRM enrichment: resolve name-only leads via list-context LinkedIn search
body:
## Problem
Name-only CRM leads (firstName+lastName, no email/LinkedIn/company) failed enrichment with `identityResolutionFailed` for the whole list — even when the list itself carried disambiguating context (e.g. "YC Poker Night", described as YC alumni).

**Root cause:** in `enrichmentIdentityResolver.ts`, Tier 2.7 (the Unipile LinkedIn people-search that turns a name into a LinkedIn URL) only fired when a company was already known. With no company, it was skipped, Apollo couldn't fire, and the company-completeness gate returned `identity_unresolvable`.

## Fix
Thread the lead list's name+description ("listContext") through `runEnrichment → resolveIdentity → findLinkedInUrl`. When company is unknown but list context exists and company fields are requested, run a **name-only** LinkedIn search (folding context into the query collapses LinkedIn results to zero — verified live), then use a cheap LLM to pick the right same-name candidate by context.

## Wrong-person safeguards (defense in depth)
1. **Hard name filter** before the LLM (`unipileNameMatches`).
2. **LLM disambiguation** only when company unknown + context present + >1 same-name candidate; otherwise prior behavior.
3. **Four refuse-guards** in `pickCandidateByContextLLM`: weak-context → refuse; low self-confidence → refuse; ungrounded/hallucinated evidence quote → refuse; out-of-range/declined index → refuse.
4. **Low-confidence taint propagation**: a context-guessed identity downgrades EVERY persisted fill (email/company/title) to low confidence at the orchestrator layer, so a wrong same-name match can never surface a trustworthy-looking email.

## Name matching improvements
The shared `nameTokensMatch` (Apollo gate + Unipile guards) was exact-character. Now normalization (NFKD accent strip + punctuation removal) + initials handling so these MATCH without loosening the wrong-person guard:
- dotted/bare initials `P.`/`P` ↔ `Paul`; concatenated `P.G.`/`P. G.` ↔ `Paul`
- accents `José`↔`Jose`; punctuation `O'Brien`↔`OBrien`; hyphens `Anne-Marie`↔`Annemarie`
- wrong initials (`Q`), wrong names, and real short names (`Bo`, `Al`) still reject correctly
- also fixed an emoji-led display name ("💡 Paul Graham") that let a wrong first name slip through

## Emma guidance
`enrich_leads_preview` no longer flatly declares name-only lists "unenrichable"; it surfaces actionable options.

## Preservation
Every previously-working path (email/LinkedIn/company present; name+company) is unchanged — verified path-by-path against base and via the regression suite. New behavior is reachable only for leads that previously failed outright.

## Testing
- `npx tsc` clean.
- Full targeted suite (`enrichment`/`crm`/`emma`/matcher consumers): 2422 passing, 1 skipped.
- Live end-to-end (real LinkedIn/Unipile/Apollo): name-only "YC Poker Night" lead resolved to Y Combinator at low confidence; weak-context "Imported Contacts" refused; company-anchored control kept medium confidence (not tainted).

title: fix(crm): 'Use my ICP' 404s for org members with org-level ICPs
body:
## Bug

Reported (admin: ruiw@agentweb.pro) on the CRM leads page: **"After clicking on Find Leads, then click Use my ICP does not work."** Reporting user: `info@pmps.ai`.

## Root cause (validated against prod data)

`GET /api/crm/icp/filters` (the "Use my ICP" button) read **only** `user.icpResult`. ICP personas actually live in up to three stores:

1. `user.icpResult` — generated during onboarding / mirrored from Emma's brand build.
2. `user.marketStrategy.icp` — authored on the `/market-strategy` page or by Emma's `update_market_strategy`.
3. **`org.marketStrategy.icp`** — for org members. Per `routes/marketStrategy.ts`: *"If user is in an org, always read market strategy from the org (not the user)."*

The reporting user is an **org owner** with **5 fully-defined ICPs in `org.marketStrategy.icp`**, but **no `user.icpResult` and no `user.marketStrategy`**. So the endpoint returned **404** and the button silently failed — confirmed by querying prod DynamoDB (`AW-Users` + `AW-Organizations`) and reproducing the 404 live in the dev environment.

## Fix

Resolve personas in priority order:
1. `user.icpResult` (preferred — carries the `extractedFilters` LLM cache),
2. else fall back to `marketStrategy.icp` — **org-level for org members**, user-level otherwise — converting to the persona shape via the existing `mapMarketIcpToResult` mapping (the same one Emma's brand-build mirror uses).

The cache write-back is **intentionally skipped** for the `marketStrategy` path: materializing org personas onto `user.icpResult` would shadow later org edits, so `marketStrategy` stays the source of truth and the LLM re-runs on each (rare, explicit, ~3s) click. Also corrected the 404 copy, which pointed users to a non-existent "GTM Plan page" for ICP generation (companion copy fix in customer-portal PR #935).

## Tests

`backend/src/__tests__/crm.icpFiltersRoute.test.ts` — added 7 cases (org fallback, user-marketStrategy fallback, org-beats-user precedence, icpResult-beats-marketStrategy precedence, 404 when neither store has ICPs, out-of-range, no write-back on the marketStrategy path). **24/24 in the file pass; all 58 CRM suites (1255 tests) green. `npx tsc` clean.**

## End-to-end verification (Playwright, dev env)

Dev test user `test@example.com` is an org owner with 3 org-level ICPs and no `user.icpResult` — same shape as the reporting user. Before: `GET /api/crm/icp/filters?icpIndex=0` → **404**. After: → **200 OK**, the modal loaded 3 angle variants ("Founder Title Broad", "CEO Co-Founder SaaS", "Bootstrapped SaaS Keywords") and pre-filled Job Title=Founder, Industry=SaaS.

## Risks / edge cases

- `meta_targeting_brief` for org-derived personas is mapped from `buyerPersonas[0]`; the LLM produced sensible filters from it in testing, but it's a thinner signal than a full onboarding persona's brief.
- No caching on the marketStrategy path means one LLM call per click for those users (acceptable; the action is explicit and infrequent).

title: fix(agent-mode): send one-off emails via configured CRM sender
body:
## Problem

**Reported:** "Configured email sender cannot send email from Emma chat" (High priority, user info@pmps.ai).

A user with a configured email sender could not get Emma to send an email in chat — it appeared to silently fail.

## Root cause (validated against production)

When a user asks Emma / agent mode to send an **ad-hoc** email ("send an email to X"), the only reachable email-send tool is `email` (`backend/src/emma/tools.ts`), whose `send` action routes **exclusively** through connected **Gmail** OAuth accounts (`emailProviderService.resolveEmailAccount`). It has no knowledge of the user's configured CRM senders.

The configured sender is only usable via `send_email_to_lead`, which requires a CRM lead **plus a saved draft** in a list — unusable for one-off sends. So a user who configured a sender (the documented way to set up outbound) but never connected a raw Gmail account had **no tool** to send an arbitrary email.

(`send_email` in `mcp/server/apiTools.ts` is dead — never bridged into the agent/Emma registries.)

### Production evidence
- Session `953c514f-…` (2026-06-25): user asked "Send an email to info@pmps.ai … approved"; Emma called `list_connected_accounts`, found no Gmail, and refused: *"there's no email account (Gmail or similar) connected right now … connect a Gmail account in Settings."*
- That user's configured sender (`info@mail.incentivpay.com`, Resend) **works** — proven by 2 `email.delivered` events that same day.

## Fix

- New `AgentModeService.sendEmailFromConfiguredSender(userId, {to, subject, html/text, senderId?})` — sends a one-off email using the same configured senders `send_email_to_lead` uses (explicit `senderId` → default → first). Routes gmail-type senders through `gmailService`, custom-domain senders through `resendService`.
- New `send_email_from_sender` tool exposing it. Registered as a **foundation tool** and force-merged into `MANDATORY_FOUNDATION_TOOLS` (the prod `foundation_tools` AW-Settings override drops DEFAULT-only additions, so mandatory is required for prod availability).
- Steer the `email` tool description toward `send_email_from_sender` when no Gmail is connected.

## Testing

- **Unit:** 11 new cases in `agentModeService.crmTools.test.ts` (142/142 pass) — happy path, explicit sender, gmail routing, no-senders, unknown sender, validation, Resend-null, gmail misconfig, gmail error propagation.
- **`npx tsc`:** clean.
- **Full backend suite:** 13992/13992 tests pass (the 22 suite-load failures are a pre-existing `axios.create` mock issue, confirmed identical on a clean checkout; none touch changed files).
- **End-to-end (real backend + Resend, dev):** `sendEmailFromConfiguredSender` sent a live email via the configured sender (`harshap@updates.agentweb.pro`), returning a Resend message ID — no Gmail connected.
- **End-to-end (Playwright, customer portal chat):** asked Emma to send via the configured sender → she called `send_email_from_sender` and returned **Sent ✅** (To: delivered@resend.dev, From: harshap@updates.agentweb.pro, Email ID: f6c07e09-…). Generic phrasing ("send an email to …") also routed to the new tool.

## Risks / remaining concerns

- Custom-domain senders still require the domain to be **verified in Resend**; an unverified domain returns null → "Email send failed". This is surfaced (not silent) but without the granular Resend reason. Out of scope for this fix; the reported user's domain is verified.
- The new tool is force-merged into mandatory foundation tools, so it's available regardless of the prod `foundation_tools` override — intended.
- Org/delegated sessions: sender lookup uses the acting `userId` (the target user under delegation), consistent with existing behavior.

title: fix(crm-sync): don't prompt HubSpot reconnect for invalid-email failures
body:
## Problem

On the CRM page, when a lead failed to sync **only because its email was invalid** (e.g. `guylenefanning@mail.com8: invalid email (rejected by HubSpot)`), the sync banner showed *"The connection was rejected"* plus a **"Reconnect HubSpot"** button. The connection was perfectly healthy — reconnecting does nothing to fix a malformed lead email. Reported by ruiw@agentweb.pro (affected user: lyndi@every.io).

## Root cause

`CrmSyncStatusBanner` treats every `lastSyncStatus === 'error'` as a connection failure. But the backend (`autoSyncLead` / `runPush` / push-job) records that same error status for **two different failure classes**:
- **connection** — revoked/expired token, disconnected account (thrown out of `pushLeads`). Reconnect is the right fix.
- **data** — a per-lead rejection caught into `result.errors` (`errorCount > 0`, no throw), e.g. an invalid email. Reconnect cannot help.

The banner couldn't tell them apart, so it always offered Reconnect.

## Fix

**Backend** (this repo):

title: fix(eb): remove custom nginx temp path that breaks startup on AL2023 (prod outage landmine)
body:
## 🚨 URGENT — must merge before the next 02:00 UTC scheduled prod deploy

Prod was recovered today by a **console rollback** to `backend-20260625-pr1955`. That is ephemeral: **`main` still carries the config that broke nginx startup.** The daily scheduled prod deploy (~02:00 UTC) rebuilds from `main` and will re-ship the landmine — every fresh instance will fail to boot nginx and the env will re-enter the same can't-self-heal deadlock, unattended. **This PR removes the landmine.**

## What was wrong (the amplifier in today's "Failed to load users" outage)
A custom `client_body_temp_path /var/tmp/agentweb-nginx/client_body` + a predeploy hook (`01-nginx-client-body-temp.sh`) that created it were added to "keep large bodies off disk." On the **AL2023 platform nginx.service runs with `PrivateTmp=true`**, so nginx gets a *private* `/var/tmp` that does **not** contain the host-created dir. nginx's startup does a non-recursive `mkdir()` of the temp leaf and fails:
```
nginx: [emerg] mkdir() "/var/tmp/agentweb-nginx/client_body" failed (2: No such file or directory)
nginx: configuration file /etc/nginx/nginx.conf test failed
systemd: nginx.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'   → systemctl start exit 1 → EB deploy fails
```
`nginx -t` *passes* when EB runs it out-of-band in the host namespace (the dir exists there), which is why syntax checks looked clean — but the unit's own `ExecStartPre nginx -t` runs inside the private namespace and ENOENTs. (SELinux is refuted: the failing errno is 2/ENOENT, not 13/EACCES, and the only AVC was permissive on `error.log`.)

## What this fixes
Removes the custom temp-path override + the hook, so nginx falls back to its **stock** temp paths under `/var/lib/nginx/tmp` — which `PrivateTmp` does **not** isolate, are RPM-created with correct ownership/SELinux labels, and ran cleanly for months. `proxy_buffers.conf` is **kept as-is** (4 MB in-memory proxy buffers + `proxy_max_temp_file_size 0`), so the ~1.9 MB `GET /admin/users` response stays in memory and **never needs an on-disk temp file** — which is the *correct* fix for the original symptom (the broken hook targeted `client_body`/uploads, the wrong temp path entirely).

One file deleted + one line removed. Zero new moving parts.

## How to test
1. Merge → let the scheduled deploy run (or trigger `deploy.yml`), then watch a **brand-new** instance reach **Health: Green**.
2. On a fresh instance's `eb-engine.log` / `messages`: confirm `nginx ... test is successful` followed by a clean `systemctl start nginx` with **no `[emerg] mkdir() ... failed`**. (This is the boot the console rollback skipped.)
3. `grep -r client_body_temp_path /etc/nginx` → nothing; `GET /api/admin/users` → 200 with users; no `proxy_temp`/`client_body` temp files created for the request.

## Test evidence
- `backend/src/__tests__/nginxStartupTempPath.test.ts` (new) + `nginxProxyBuffers.test.ts` — **4 passed, 0 failed**.

## What is NOT in this PR (deliberately — separate hardening PR to follow)
This stops the immediate bleed + the 02:00 landmine. The **root cause** (what filled the 8 GB disk: a `devEnvService` teardown loop calling `terminateInstances('pending')` and dumping full AxiosErrors at ~79 MB/day) plus **disk headroom + a `RootFilesystemUtil` alarm + instance recycling + log caps** come in a follow-up hardening PR. Full RCA in the incident thread.

## Risk: Low — reverts to the long-proven stock-nginx config; config-only, no app behavior change.

title: fix(prod): disk-fill root cause + headroom/monitoring/recycling (2026-06-26 outage hardening)
body:
## The rest of the 100% fix for the 2026-06-26 "Failed to load users" outage

This is the durable/hardening half. It **includes** the urgent nginx fix from #1971 (so deploying this alone is fully safe), then fixes the *true* root cause and adds the headroom/monitoring/recycling that would have prevented the whole thing. Full RCA in `dev.md`.

> Relationship to #1971: #1971 is the minimal, must-merge-before-02:00-UTC subset. If #1971 merges first, this PR's diff auto-reduces to just the hardening. Either order is safe.

## Root cause this PR fixes — the disk-filler
`devEnvService.teardownEnvironment()` only guarded `if (!instanceId)`, so a dev-env Notion page stuck at the placeholder `"pending"` made it call EC2 `terminateInstances(['pending'])` → `InvalidInstanceID.Malformed` on **every webhook tick (~12,455×)**, and each failure retried commenting on a maxed-out Notion thread, dumping **full AWS-SDK + Axios error object graphs** (request `config` + body) to stdout at **~79 MB/day**. That filled the 8 GB root volume → nginx couldn't write the temp file for the 1.9 MB `/admin/users` response → "Failed to load users."

## What's in this PR
| File | Change | Why |
|------|--------|-----|
| `services/devEnvService.ts` | Require an `i-` instance-id prefix before any EC2 call; clear the page (so teardown stops re-firing) for placeholders; replace full-object error logging with a one-line `errSummary()` | Kills the loop + ~99% of the log volume at the source |
| `.ebextensions/03-root-volume.config` | Root volume 8 GB → **40 GB gp3** | Real headroom (was the AL2023 default 8 GB) — triggers a one-time rolling instance replacement |
| `.ebextensions/04-disk-alarm.config` | Publish `RootFilesystemUtil` + CloudWatch alarm @ **≥80%** → `agentweb-oncall-alerts` SNS | There was **zero** disk telemetry — the outage was silent until users hit it |
| `.ebextensions/05-instance-recycling.config` | Weekly managed instance refresh | No instance lives ~11 days accumulating cruft |
| `.ebextensions/06-log-retention.config` | Stream logs to CloudWatch (14d) + logrotate `/var/log/messages` (50M) + journald cap (200M) | Belt-and-suspenders: no chatty path can fill the disk again |
| `+ #1971 nginx fix` | remove custom `client_body_temp_path` + hook, keep `proxy_buffers.conf` | nginx starts on fresh instances; 1.9 MB response stays in memory |

## How to test
1. **Deploy → fresh-instance boot:** the volume change forces new instances. Confirm each reaches **Green**, with a clean `systemctl start nginx` (no `[emerg] mkdir() ... failed`), and `df -h /` shows **40 GB**.
2. **devEnv guard:** with a Notion dev-env page whose Instance ID is `pending`, trigger teardown → confirm **no** `InvalidInstanceID.Malformed` in logs and the page's Instance ID is cleared; a page with a real `i-...` id still terminates.
3. **Alarm live:** `RootFilesystemUtil` flowing in CloudWatch (`AWS/ElasticBeanstalk`, dim `EnvironmentName`); the 80% alarm is `OK` (not `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`); fire a test SNS notification.
4. **Log bleed stopped:** `/var/log/messages` rotating under 50 MB; no recurring `[devEnv] ... InvalidInstanceID` / `maximum number of comments` in stdout; disk-free trend flat.

## Test evidence
- `backend` jest: **devEnv.test.ts (40) + nginxStartupTempPath.test.ts + nginxProxyBuffers.test.ts — all pass.**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. All 4 `.ebextensions` validated (YAML + embedded ConfigDocument JSON + CFN Resources).

## What was NOT tested
- The `.ebextensions` are validated structurally but only fully exercised by a real EB deploy (the rolling replacement + alarm creation). Recommend deploying to **staging** (`Agentweb-backend-env-1`) first to watch the instance refresh + alarm provision before prod.

## Not in scope (separate follow-up)
The `/admin/users` **latency** time bomb: ~1,181 DynamoDB ops/request (3 scan + 876 COUNT + 292 replay GetItems) → 4.1 s, with a hard 60 s ELB-timeout wall near ~1,000 users. The #1968 payload whitelist (already on `main`) cuts the size 1.9 MB→130 KB; the op fan-out needs a lazy `:userId/stats` endpoint. Filed for a follow-up task.

## Risk: Medium — config-only infra changes + a guarded app fix. The volume bump triggers a rolling instance replacement; deploy to staging first.

title: fix(agent-mode): exclude scheduled cron runs from Live chat history (Live tab showed only 2)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The chat-history list endpoint `GET /api/agent-mode/sessions` returns the most-recently-*updated* `agent` sessions and lets the client split Live vs Scheduled. Scheduled cron runs (`sessionType='scheduled'`) update **daily**, so they dominate the recency-sorted page. A heavy account (`founders@agentweb.pro`, 2,731 sessions) had its first page come back ~48 scheduled / 2 interactive — the Live tab showed **2 chats** out of **~440 real ones**.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds an opt-in `sessionType` filter so each tab fetches its own slice:
- `?excludeScheduled=true` → Live tab (interactive only)
- `?sessionType=scheduled` → Scheduled tab
`exclude-scheduled` uses `attribute_not_exists(sessionType) OR sessionType <> 'scheduled'` so legacy sessions written before `sessionType` existed stay visible. **Behavior-preserving: no query param = identical response.**

## How to test
1. As an account with many scheduled chats (e.g. delegate into `founders@agentweb.pro`), open **Agent Mode → Chat History → Live**.
2. **Expected**: a full page of real interactive chats (not 2), with infinite scroll loading more.
3. Switch to **Scheduled**. **Expected**: scheduled runs only.

## Verified against real prod data (`founders@`, userId `be754b6c…`)
Ran the exact queries this code produces against `AW-ChatSessions`:
- `excludeScheduled`: **50 returned (was 2), 0 scheduled leaked, hasMore=true**
- `sessionType=scheduled`: 50 returned, 0 non-scheduled leaked

## Behavioral assertions verified (tests)
- `chatbotService.scheduledFilter.test.ts`: exclude-scheduled adds `sessionType <> :scheduledSessionType` + keeps `attribute_not_exists(sessionType)`; only-scheduled uses exact equality; no param ⇒ no sessionType clause; combines with portalType via AND.
- `agentModeController.getSessions.test.ts`: `?excludeScheduled=true` ⇒ `exclude-scheduled`; `?sessionType=scheduled` ⇒ `only-scheduled`; neither ⇒ `undefined`; excludeScheduled wins when both sent.

## Complexity ledger
- Net: +1 optional param + one filter branch (service) + one ternary (controller). No new table/flag/index. No schema change, no migration.
- Behavior: AgentMode chat behavior unchanged; only the history-list query gains an opt-in filter.

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc`: clean. `jest` (chatbotService.scheduledFilter, agentModeController.getSessions, infiniteScroll, sessionSearch, chatbot.emmaSessions): **47 passed, 0 failed**.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/chatbotService.ts` (getUserSessions filter)
- `backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts` (getSessions query parsing)

DynamoDB RCU cost: with no GSI yet, exclude-scheduled is a post-Limit filter, so a page does a few extra internal reads (existing pagination loop handles it). A keyed GSI is a planned fast-follow.

title: feat(intake): Linear-first user issue/feature intake + ICM-style dedup (flagged)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

Behind the `FEATUREBASE_INTAKE` flag. Flag **off** = unchanged Notion behavior (the migration default, not an on-error fallback). Migrates user-issue / feature-request intake off Notion onto **Featurebase (customer-facing) + Linear (engineering source of truth)**.

## What was wrong (before)
Every user-filed issue/feature (Emma's `report_product_issues` + the in-app "report a bug" button) and every auto-identified issue became its own **Notion** oncall task. No customer portal, no voting, no dedup — two people reporting the same thing produced duplicate tasks and the "class-action" signal was lost.

## What this fixes (after)
One intake orchestrator (`intakeService`) with three pipes, each behind `FEATUREBASE_INTAKE`:

**1. Feature requests → public, votable Featurebase post (FB-first).**
`POST /v2/posts {integrations:{linear:true}}` creates the post **and** pushes it to Linear for eng in one call. Before creating, an LLM judge dedups against open posts: a confident match **stacks** (adds the reporter as an upvoter + a private eng comment) instead of duplicating; no match → new post. Emma tells the user it's a known request and their vote was added.

**2. Bugs → a private per-reporter Featurebase ticket + ONE canonical Linear issue.**
Each reporter gets their **own private card** (their words, authorOnly). All reporters of the same bug (LLM-dedup against open Linear canonicals) group onto a **single canonical Linear issue** (labels `Bug` + `Customer Reported`, no `Featurebase` label so it never becomes a public post). The canonical **lists every affected user** via a `[reporter-ticket #N <email>]` comment per reporter (email + session) — eng sees exactly who's impacted and works one issue, not N.

**3. Auto-identified issues → private Linear "Auto" issue** (eng-only, deduped by normalized title), never a customer card.

**Notify-on-ship (verified live to a real inbox — both paths):**
- **Features:** native. Marking the post's Linear issue **Done** flips the post to **Completed** and Featurebase emails **every upvoter** automatically (no code of ours runs).
- **Bugs:** the resolve-bridge. A signed Linear webhook (`POST /api/integrations/linear/webhook`) fires when a canonical reaches a completed state → `notifyCanonicalResolved` reads the `[reporter-ticket #N <email>]` comments and **emails each reporter** from our own system address (Resend) + flips their card to Completed. We email reporters ourselves because **Featurebase exposes no API trigger for ticket emails** (a ticket reply/status-change via API stays silent; only *post* status changes email contacts).

**Fail-well, not fall back:** dedup / upvote / comment are best-effort (errors degrade in place — dedup fails → treat as new; stack fails → still filed). A core create failure **propagates** (user is told it didn't file; auto-report failure is logged and never breaks the user's real request). No silent cross-system reroute.

The dedup-judge model is **not hardcoded** — sourced from the settings key `agent_mode_dedup_judge_model` (registry-validated, falls back to the default model). `TODO(ENG-9)`: route this internal LLM call through OpenRouter so model choice becomes gateway config.

## How to test
Backend with `FEATUREBASE_INTAKE=true`. Featurebase dashboard configured (see Config below).
1. **Feature via chat** — Emma: *"add a dark mode toggle."* → **Expected:** Emma confirms tracked; within ~10s a single public Featurebase post appears **and** a linked Linear issue exists.
2. **Feature dedup** — new chat: *"can you add a night mode option?"* → **Expected:** Emma says it's already a known request and your vote was added — **no** new post; the canonical gets an upvoter + private comment.
3. **Bug via UI** (report-a-bug) and **via chat** (Emma: *"the checkout button does nothing"*) → **Expected:** the reporter gets their own private Featurebase ticket; a canonical Linear issue exists listing the affected user + session.
4. **Two reporters, same bug** → **Expected:** 2 private cards, **1** canonical, with a `[reporter-ticket #N <email>]` comment per reporter.
5. **Resolve a feature** (its Linear issue → Done) → post flips to Completed, **upvoters emailed**.
6. **Resolve a bug** (canonical → Done) → **every reporter emailed** ("Resolved: …") + their card flipped to Completed.

## Behavioral assertions verified
End-to-end on the test env (real LLM judge + real Linear + real Featurebase + a **real inbox**):
- **Feature pipe** (UI + chat): FB-first post created + pushed to Linear; dedup stacks voters onto one canonical.
- **Bug pipe** (UI + chat): private per-reporter card + ONE canonical listing all affected users; 2 reporters → 2 cards, 1 canonical.
- **Auto pipe**: private Linear `Auto` issue (no customer card).
- **Resolve bridge**: canonical Done → bridge emails every reporter + flips every card (`notified` count matches reporter count).
- **Emails actually delivered** (checked in Gmail): feature upvoter email from `info@featurebase.app`; bug reporter email from `hi@updates.agentweb.pro`.
- Unit: `npx tsc` clean; **58 tests pass** across the 6 touched suites (dedup match / no-match / low-confidence→new / hallucination-guard / error→new; linearService canonicals + comments + `getIssueComments`; featurebaseService posts/tickets/voters/status; intakeService all three pipes + the resolve bridge with HTML-escaping, dedupe, and per-reporter best-effort).

## Files changed
- `services/intakeService.ts` (new) — orchestrator: `fileUserIssue` (bug vs feature split), `fileAutoIssue`, `notifyCanonicalResolved` (resolve bridge).
- `services/featurebaseService.ts` (new) — posts (`createPost`/`listOpenPosts`/`addComment`/`addVoter`), tickets (`createTicket`/`patchTicketStatus`/`getTicketStatusId`), board/category helpers.
- `services/linearService.ts` — `createInternalLinearIssue`, `addIssueComment`, `getIssueComments`, `listOpenBugCanonicals`, `listOpenIssuesByLabel`.
- `services/dedupService.ts` (new) — source-agnostic LLM dedup judge (features → FB posts, bugs → Linear canonicals).
- `routes/integrations.ts` (new) — Linear webhook (HMAC-verified) → resolve bridge.
- `app.ts` — raw-body middleware for the webhook (before `express.json`) + mount.
- `emma/tools.ts`, `routes/support.ts` — thread `sessionId`, surface the user's tracking link.
- `services/agentModeService.ts` — `getDedupJudgeModel()` (settings-backed).
- `services/emailService.ts`, `cron/onboardingStuckDetector.ts`, `controllers/agentModeController.ts` — route auto / oncall alerts through intake.
- Tests for all of the above.

## Config / secrets / flag
- Flag: `FEATUREBASE_INTAKE=true` to enable (off → unchanged Notion).
- Secrets (created): `prod|dev/AgentWeb/Linear`, `prod|dev/AgentWeb/Featurebase`. Bug-resolve emails reuse the existing Resend system sender.
- **Webhook secret:** `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC for the resolve bridge).
- **Featurebase dashboard:** Linear integration connected (Engineering team); a **"Bug Report"** customer ticket category; sync rule Linear `Done` ↔ Featurebase `Completed` with **Notify = Yes** (drives the upvoter emails); **ticket→Linear sync OFF** for the Bug Report category (so per-reporter cards don't each spawn a Linear issue — the canonical is the only Linear ticket per bug). Linear Engineering team has `Featurebase`, `Auto`, `Bug`, `Customer Reported` labels.

## Deploy-time (the one remaining manual step for bug emails to auto-fire)
**Register the Linear webhook** → `https://api.agentweb.pro/api/integrations/linear/webhook` (Issue events) and set `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` + `FEATUREBASE_INTAKE=true` in prod. The bridge is proven; it just needs Linear to call it. Feature emails need no webhook (native FB↔Linear sync).

## What was NOT tested
- Real Emma **browser** flow (verified via the exact tool/service code path, not Playwright).
- High-volume dedup accuracy / borderline near-duplicates (judge biased to NEW; Featurebase "Find Duplicates" is the backstop).
- The Linear webhook firing in **prod** (verified by invoking `notifyCanonicalResolved` directly on the test env; the HTTP→bridge wiring is unit-tested but the prod webhook isn't registered yet — see Deploy-time).

title: fix(agent-mode): recover perform_data_analysis output when Gemini omits a text part
body:
## Problem

`perform_data_analysis` failed repeatedly in scheduled session `8aa71237` (4 consecutive failures on a ~400KB payload) with the opaque message *"No analysis results received from Gemini."*

## Root cause

`performDataAnalysis` (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`) sends a **single-shot** Gemini `code_execution` request with **no tool-call loop**, then builds its result **only from response parts that carry a `text` field** (plus images). The model's actual computed answer frequently lands in a **`codeExecutionResult.output`** part, which the old extractor mined *only* for file-download markers and never surfaced as analysis.

So when a turn ended after the last code block with **no summary `text` part** — or paused on an internal **`functionCall`** (`run_command` / `python_interpreter`, which `gemini-3.5-flash` does intermittently) — `resultParts` came back empty and the tool failed opaquely, causing the agent to **retry blindly**.

This is **model-independent**: reverting the model (commit `24aee2cd` deliberately moved to `gemini-3.5-flash` to fix a file-materialization/HTTP-500 bug) would risk regressing that fix, and live testing showed both models can emit the failing shape.

### Validated against real captured Gemini responses (old vs. fixed extractor)
- `exec, result, exec, result, fc:python_interpreter` → **OLD=FAIL → FIX=OK** (recovers real analysis)
- `fc:run_command, fc:run_command` (model only peeked, computed nothing) → OLD=FAIL → **FIX=actionable failure**
- response with final text part → OLD=OK, FIX=OK (no regression)

## Fix (`bc08ec7e`)

1. **Surface code-execution output as a fallback narrative** — keep the cleaned `codeExecutionResult.output`; when the turn produced **no** `text` part, surface the **final** stdout block as the analysis (earlier blocks are inspection/debug). When a text part exists, it stays the summary, so normal runs are unchanged and intermediate `print()` noise isn't folded in. Handles both `camelCase` and `snake_case`.
2. **Replace the opaque empty-result message** with actionable, non-retry-inducing guidance (simplify the instruction, keep `file_urls`, don't re-inline) and **log `finishReason` + `sawFunctionCall`** for prod diagnosability.

## Tests (`2c8b5990`) — TDD (written to fail first, then pass)

- code-exec output surfaced when no text part (camelCase + snake_case)
- download-marker blocks still stripped from surfaced output
- `functionCall`-only turn returns actionable guidance, not the old string

## Verification

- `npx tsc`: clean
- `agentModeService.performDataAnalysis` + `toolErrorClassifier` + `toolFailureType`: **89/89 pass**
- Full `agentModeService` set: **93 suites / 1828 tests pass**
- **E2E (Playwright, live backend running this code):** logged into customer portal → agent mode → ran `perform_data_analysis` on an inline CSV → correct totals (Total Tokens 6,700, Total Cost \$18.30, Avg \$3.66), CSV + chart generated with working S3 link. Success path intact.

## Risks / remaining concerns

- **Telemetry class change (intentional):** the new failure message classifies as `Error`→`bug` rather than `empty_result`→`by_design`. This is more correct — a functionCall stall is a genuine transient failure, not a benign empty result.
- **Not addressed (out of scope):** the deeper architectural gap of no multi-turn function-call loop. When the model emits *only* `functionCall`s and computes nothing, there's nothing to recover; the fix returns clear guidance instead. Follow-up candidate.
- **Transient secret error (attempt 1 of the prod session):** real but secondary; not addressed here to keep the PR focused. Easy follow-up mirroring `getGeminiClient`'s env-fallback + retry.

> Note: run backend jest with `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` unset — a leaked `.env` token makes a transitive `WebClient` import hit the test's partial axios mock. Pre-existing harness quirk, unrelated to this change.

title: fix(emma): refresh market strategy during brand re-setup (ENG-44)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium
Linear: **ENG-44** — customer-reported bug where asking Emma to re-setup a brand updated only **Brand Guidelines** while leaving **Market Strategy** stale on `/market-strategy`.

## What Was Wrong
Emma had separate granular tools for brand and market strategy. A broad request like "re-setup my brand" could resolve to `update_brand_guidelines` alone, so the visible brand changed while ICPs/competitors stayed from the old positioning.

## What This Fixes
A broad brand re-setup can now update both sections in one deterministic operation:

- `update_brand_guidelines` accepts `refreshMarketStrategy: true` for broad brand re-setup/refresh requests.
- After writing the updated brand guidelines, the same service call runs the existing `regenerateMarketStrategy` path.
- Regeneration reuses the existing onboarding ICP + competitor generators and mappers; no new generation stack.
- ICPs and competitors are replaced from the updated brand; `businessOverview` is preserved.
- Single-field/brand-only edits leave `refreshMarketStrategy` false/omitted and keep market strategy untouched.
- The tool result returns compact `marketStrategyRefresh` counts so Emma can report what was replaced/generated.

## Complexity Impact
Adds one boolean tool argument and one service call path. Removes the previous conversational dependency where Emma had to ask scope up front and then remember to call a second tool. No new tables, feature flags, dependencies, or UI surfaces.

title: fix(scoring): defer mid-tool-loop sessions from premature evaluation
body:
## Problem

Judge and general scoring could evaluate a scheduled session mid-run. When an agent persists a partial tool-call step (assistant turn with no text + trailing tool result), `hasAssistantTurn()` returned `true` and bypassed the in-flight guard — so the LLM scored an incomplete transcript, producing false 1/5 scores.

The existing guard (`hasAssistantTurn` + `classifyTurnlessSession`) only handled the fully turn-less case (`[system, user]` with no assistant reply at all). The mid-tool-loop case slipped through.

## Fix

**`sessionScoringService.ts`** — adds `transcriptEndsMidToolLoop(messages)`:
- Returns `true` when the last non-system message is a trailing tool result, a pure tool-call assistant turn (no text), or an unanswered user prompt — all states a completed run cannot terminate on
- Returns `false` for a settled assistant turn that carries text (even with aggregated `toolCalls`) — matching the real completed scheduled-run shape in prod
- Both `scoreSessionIfNeeded` and `scoreSessionWithJudgeIfNeeded` now defer (`return null`, no LLM call, no DB write) when mid-tool-loop + within the 60-min grace window; stale mid-loop sessions are scored on the next pass — never skipped permanently

**`sessionScoring.inProgressSession.test.ts`** — replaces the one test that was asserting the buggy behavior and adds 7 new cases:
- Recent mid-loop (tool result) → deferred
- Recent mid-loop (pure tool-call turn) → deferred
- Recent trailing user message → deferred
- Stale mid-loop → scored (not skipped forever)
- Settled (text + aggregated toolCalls) → scored immediately
- Judge path: recent mid-loop → deferred
- Judge path: stale mid-loop → scored

## Test Results

- **Unit tests:** 15/15 pass (`sessionScoring.inProgressSession`)
- **Full suite:** 541/541 pass (scoring + admin.chatSessions + agentModeController)
- **Live HTTP test** against dev DynamoDB + real LLM judge:
  - Mid-loop session → `scores: {id: null}` (correctly deferred, nothing persisted to DB) ✅
  - Settled session (text + toolCalls final msg) → scored at correct index ✅

## Risk

Scope is entirely internal to the scoring/eval pipeline — chat serving, auth, agent execution, and message persistence are untouched. Worst case: a session score is delayed up to 60 min (the existing grace window tunable), never a wrong score or data loss.

title: feat(featurebase): SSO identity endpoint for the in-app widget
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

Backend half of in-app Featurebase SSO. Mints Identity-Verification JWTs so a logged-in user is recognized in the embedded Featurebase widget (their OWN posts + private tickets) with no separate login. Pairs with customer-portal **#940** (frontend identify wiring).

## What this adds
- **`GET /api/featurebase/identity`** (authenticated): signs a short-lived HS256 JWT `{userId,email,name}` (10m) with the board's SSO secret → returns `{ jwt, organization, appId }`.
- `featurebaseService.signFeaturebaseIdentityJwt()` + a new optional `ssoSecret` on the Featurebase credentials.

1. (Once the SSO secret is in `prod|dev/AgentWeb/Featurebase`) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" .../api/featurebase/identity` → `{ jwt, organization:"agentweb", appId }`.

3. No secret → 503 (graceful). No auth → 401.

`npx tsc` clean; **22 unit tests**: signer emits HS256 with the right claims + short exp, verifies with the ssoSecret (and fails with a wrong secret), throws when unset; route returns `{jwt,organization,appId}`, display name best-effort (still mints if the db lookup fails), 401 without a user, 503 when SSO unconfigured.

- New **`ssoSecret`** key in `prod|dev/AgentWeb/Featurebase` = the Featurebase dashboard **Settings → Access & Security → Security** private key. Until it's set, the endpoint 503s and the widget stays anonymous (no breakage).
