title: Trip agent tool circuit breaker on repeated tool timeouts (ENG-167)
body:
## What was wrong

When a user asked to run a newly-created skill, the agent generated a campaign brief via `create_html_file`, which repeatedly timed out. Two distinct bugs compounded this into an unrecoverable loop:

1. **Exact-string breaker (fixed in earlier commits on this PR):** the per-run circuit breaker keyed failures by `(runId, toolName, error-head)`, but each timeout surfaced a slightly different message (raw "connection timed out after Nms", an AbortError, a Bedrock `ModelTimeoutException`), so no single error-head ever reached the trip threshold within one run.

2. **Cross-turn reset (this update):** even after aggregating timeouts by error *class* within a run, the breaker's `runId` is minted fresh on every top-level turn — a user re-sending "try again" gets a brand-new run with a zeroed counter. Verified against the actual production session that filed this ticket (`94253d20-712e...`): `create_html_file` failed **6 times total across 4 separate ~10-minute turns**, never once reaching 3 within a single run. The breaker never tripped; the user instead hit `agentModeController.ts`'s hard 10-minute wall-clock timeout on every turn, each producing the same generic "system timed out, please try again" message — including on the turn where the user said "report bug."

3. **Silent bug filing (this update):** event-level telemetry from that same session showed the model *did* correctly call `report_product_issues` and it succeeded in 5.2s — but nothing told it to stop there. It immediately retried `create_html_file` again in the same run, which hung for 900s (real observed duration, not the nominal 300s — intermittent token trickle resets the idle-timeout clock repeatedly), and the controller killed the turn before the model could ever tell the user the bug was already filed.

## What changed (`backend/src/services/agentToolGatewayService.ts`)

- Timeout-class failures now also aggregate by **session** (`budgetScopeId`) across runs, not just within one run — trips at a lower threshold (2, not 3) since each unit already costs the user up to a full 10-minute controller-bounded turn. The trip check runs before `execute()`, so once tripped, later turns fail fast instead of hanging on another multi-minute timeout.
- Once `report_product_issues` succeeds in a run, a later timeout stop-message says so explicitly and tells the model not to file a second report, instead of repeating the generic "offer to file a bug report" suggestion.

## How verified

- 6 new TDD tests (108/108 in the gateway suite, 194/194 across gateway + classifier + dispatch + retryability suites), `npx tsc` clean.
- **Live-verified against real deployed infra on env1**, not just unit tests: forced a genuine network-level hang (blackhole TCP listener) against the actual synced build and drove the exact reported repro through the real chat UI.
  - Session-scoped breaker: 2 real timeouts, then the 3rd attempt was blocked **instantly** (confirmed via empty log stream — `execute()` never even ran). Model's own words: *"That's a hard stop — the system is now blocking further retries... I won't hammer it again."*
  - Already-filed messaging: forced the exact production sequence (2 timeouts → `report_product_issues` succeeds → retry attempted in the same run) and captured the new stop message firing verbatim in the backend logs. Model's final reply: *"A bug report has already been filed for this failure, so I will not file a duplicate, and I'm stopping retries as instructed."*

## Known limitation

The session-scoped counter is in-memory and has no time-based decay — bounded only by a 500-entry process-wide eviction cap. A long-lived chat session that hits 2 genuine (non-hang) timeouts on some tool across unrelated tasks could see a later legitimate attempt on that same tool blocked early. Fails safe (clear message + fallback offered, never silent/dangerous), but is a real trade-off. Also: this is in-memory per-process state — safe today since prod (`Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`) is pinned to exactly 1 instance, but staging (`Agentweb-backend-env-1`) can scale to 4 with no session stickiness, so a staging re-test could land on a different instance mid-session and appear not to work even though the code is correct.

Fixes ENG-167 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-167/agent-stuck-in-timeout-retry-loop-cannot-execute-any-tool-including

title: Prevent scheduled runs from crashing when the LLM worker receives a process-group SIGTERM (ENG-202)
body:
What was wrong: Scheduled agent runs intermittently produced no assistant response and were flagged as failures. The production session record showed error 'Worker process exited with code null and signal SIGTERM' from generateMarketingResponseWorkerService's exit handler, and the schedule's run history showed the run was killed ~3.7 min in — far under the parent's 10-min graceful-drain ceiling. Root cause: the generateMarketingResponse worker is a forked child sharing the parent's process group; when the platform terminates the instance (EB deploy, autoscaling replacement, health-check restart) it broadcasts SIGTERM to the whole group, and the worker had no SIGTERM handler, so it died instantly, aborting the in-flight run before the parent's drain could let it finish (zero persisted assistant messages).

What changed: Added installWorkerSignalGuards, which makes the worker ignore SIGTERM/SIGINT (its lifecycle is owned by the parent via drain + explicit kill) and exit only on IPC 'disconnect' (orphan safety). Wired it into generateMarketingResponseWorker. Changed GenerateMarketingResponseWorkerService.shutdown()'s post-drain teardown from SIGTERM to SIGKILL, since the worker no longer honors SIGTERM. The existing isCronEnabled() gate already stops NEW scheduled runs from being dispatched during drain, so in-flight runs are now the only ones affected and they get the platform's grace window to complete.

How verified: New unit tests for the signal guards (SIGTERM/SIGINT ignored, disconnect exits, listeners registered once) and an updated shutdown test asserting SIGKILL teardown — 24 tests pass. npx tsc passes with exit code 0.

---
**Automated gates**
Code review: ✅ sound — 2 finding(s) fixed
Deterministic checks: ✅ all passed
Browser verify: ✅ verified

Fixes ENG-202 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-202/scheduled-run-crashed-with-no-assistant-response-xcures-daily-site

title: Keep LLM worker alive through deploy SIGTERM so scheduled runs drain (ENG-201)
body:
What was wrong: Scheduled runs (e.g. Daily Token Usage & Cost Report) intermittently produced a dead session with zero assistant messages and the error 'Worker process exited with code null and signal SIGTERM'. Confirmed against prod session 49e6cdf4-... The zero-downtime deploy feature drains in-flight scheduled chats for up to 10 min on SIGTERM before killing the worker, but the forked LLM worker sits in the same process group/cgroup, so systemd/EB delivers the deploy SIGTERM directly to the worker too. With Node's default signal handling the worker terminated instantly, aborting the in-flight generation before the drain could complete — defeating the graceful drain.

What changed: Added src/workers/workerShutdownGuards.ts installing guards in the worker that ignore SIGTERM/SIGINT (the parent is now the sole termination authority) and exit only when the parent's IPC channel disconnects (so a crashed parent can't orphan the worker). Wired it in at the top of generateMarketingResponseWorker.ts. title: Stop the run-level tool breaker from locking out valid send-invites after invalid_args failures (ENG-197)
body:
## Context — the reported bug is already resolved on `main`

ENG-197 reported: a LinkedIn `send-invite` batch locked the **whole run** out of send-invite after two over-limit notes returned the generic upstream `Invalid parameters` (classified `invalid_args`), which fast-tripped the run-level circuit breaker at 2 — refusing every subsequent send-invite, including corrected notes and invites to unrelated profiles.

Since this issue was filed, **two independent changes landed on `main`** that each resolve the reported scenario:

- **ENG-182 / ENG-222 — per-recipient breaker scope.** `failureScope()` now keys the breaker by recipient (`profile_url` / `provider_id` / `invitation_id`). Failures to different profiles land in different scopes and can no longer aggregate to trip the breaker — directly preventing the cross-profile lockout the reporter hit.
- **ENG-191 / ENG-243 — length gate removed + tier-aware auto-trim.** Over-limit notes are trimmed on the send path (`LinkedInOutreachService.trimInviteMessage`, 200 free / 300 Premium) before dispatch, so they no longer fail with `Invalid parameters` at all.

## What this PR changes

Complementary **breaker hardening**: moves `invalid_args` out of `FAST_TRIP_ERROR_CLASSES` (`errorRetryability.ts`) so an execution-time `invalid_args` keeps the **default** repeated-failure threshold (3 instead of 2), alongside `empty_result` / `not_found`.

This is relevant only when the **same** breaker scope sees ≥2 identical execution-time `invalid_args` (a non-LinkedIn tool, or the same recipient) — it allows one more attempt before the breaker trips, matching how the other "identical text across legitimately different arguments" classes already behave. Spiral protection is retained (the breaker still trips on the 3rd identical failure).

The model-facing retryability verdict is **unchanged**: `invalid_args` stays non-retryable-as-is (separate `RETRYABLE_ERROR_CLASSES` / `NEXT_STEP_BY_CLASS`), so the "fix the arguments first" guidance is intact.

## Verification

- `errorRetryability` unit test asserts `invalid_args` now keeps the default threshold (fails if the change is reverted).
- Two gateway breaker tests, both using real `send-invite` args:
  - **DISTINCT-profile batch** (the reporter's exact scenario): two invites to two different profiles fail with `Invalid parameters`; a third invite to yet another profile still sends. Guards the per-recipient breaker scope (ENG-182).
  - **SAME-profile corrected retry**: two failures on one profile don't lock it out, so a corrected third attempt still sends. This **isolates the one-line change** — reverting `invalid_args` back into `FAST_TRIP` turns this test red (verified locally).
- `npx tsc` clean; the two targeted suites pass (146 tests).

## Bottom line

The customer-reported lockout is fixed on `main` (ENG-182 + ENG-191). This PR is a small, safe hardening of the breaker for execution-time `invalid_args` and does not change the model-facing behavior.

Relates to ENG-197 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-197/send-invite-run-level-circuit-breaker-locks-out-all-valid-invites

title: fix(linkedin): resolve send-invite 'Invalid parameters' (ENG-213)
body:
## ENG-213 — LinkedIn `send-invite` returns 'Invalid parameters' even with a valid <200-char note

Fixes the scheduled-outreach failure where `send-invite` repeatedly returned a generic **'Invalid parameters'** even for valid provider_ids and sub-200-char notes.

### Root causes & fixes
1. **Public-identifier slug not canonicalized** — Unipile's invite endpoint only accepts the canonical member URN, but the send path forwarded a raw slug (e.g. `william-kwak`) straight through. `sendInvitation` now sends the canonical `provider_id` revealed by the connection-check profile fetch, falling back to the passed identifier if the lookup fails.
2. **Spent monthly note quota** — free accounts can only attach a note to ~5 invites/month; once spent, LinkedIn rejects every note-bearing invite with a generic 'Invalid parameters'. `send-invite` now transparently retries **without** the note so the connection request still goes out. Cap/duplicate signals ('cannot resend yet', 'already invited', 'should delay') are explicitly excluded so a real cap is never masked.
3. **Note-drop was recorded as delivered** — the `send-linkedin-invite` CRM route discarded `sendInvitation()`'s result and always cached the original note text. It now records an empty `invitationText` when the note was dropped and returns `noteDropped` in the response so the UI/user knows the personalization wasn't delivered.

### Tests
- Canonical provider_id resolution for send-invite.
- Note-quota 'Invalid parameters' → note-less retry fallback, including exclusion cases (a rejection combining 'Invalid parameters' with an exclusion phrase must NOT retry).
- All 123 tests in `linkedInOutreachService.test.ts` pass; `npx tsc` clean.

title: fix(emma): Drive tool routing, doc-update confirmation/styling, inline style spans
body:
## Summary Investigation from a live "Emma can't see/edit Google Drive files correctly" session surfaced several distinct, compounding bugs in the Google Drive/Docs tooling. This PR fixes the ones not already covered by #2040 (Drive scope widening + update_google_doc plain-by-default, already merged). ## What's fixed **1. Drive tool routing** (`agentModeSystemPrompt.ts`) Emma repeatedly called `list_knowledge_base_files`/`search_knowledge_base` for "in my Google Drive" requests, and claimed zero folders connected without ever calling a real Drive tool — only self-corrected after the user's third, explicit correction. Root cause: no keyword-routing entry pointed "Google Drive" phrasing at `google_drive`/`read_google_doc`, so the model fell back to the adjacent `kb_type="google-drive"` KB filter. Added the missing routing entry. **2. `update_google_doc` confirmation behavior** (`emma/tools.ts`) This tool replaces the entire document and can silently destroy formatting (its sibling `read_google_doc` round-trips content through plain text on read). It now warns and waits for explicit confirmation on the **first** call in a conversation; subsequent calls in the same conversation proceed without re-asking, but still mention Version History recoverability every time. **3. Heading + inline-style composability** (`emma/tools.ts`) Emma was treating "make it a heading" and "color/style it" as mutually exclusive options to present to the user, instead of realizing `# [text]{color=blue}` achieves big+bold (from the heading tag) plus color in one line. Clarified in the tool description. **4. Inline style span — new capability** (`agentModeService.ts`) Added `[text]{attr=value;flag;...}` inline syntax to the markdown→HTML converter, supporting `color`, `font`, `underline`, `italic`, `bold` on a single word/phrase without touching the rest of the document or its document-wide `style_options` accent. Attribute charset is restricted to letters/digits/`#`/`=`/`;`/space, so malformed or hostile values can't break out of the `style` attribute — unrecognized attributes are silently ignored rather than rejecting the whole match. Verified this composes correctly inside headings (`# [text]{color=blue}` → `

text

`). ## How verified - 201 tests across the affected files pass (`googleDriveTools.test.ts`, `agentModeService.googleDrive.test.ts`, `agentModeSystemPrompt.skillResolution.test.ts`, `integrations.googleDrive.test.ts`, `agentModeService.listConnectedAccounts.test.ts`, `googleAdsAuth.test.ts`) - `npx tsc` clean - Manually tested live against the reported failure scenarios (Drive file lookup, doc update, heading styling, multi-attribute styling) via a synced test environment ## Known remaining gaps (not in scope for this PR) - `read_google_doc` exports Google Docs via plain text, so any full-document `update_google_doc` round-trip can still lose original rich formatting (headings/tables/etc. that predate Emma's edits) — mitigated by the Version History mention, not fixed at the root. - No block-level alignment/positioning control (center/left/right a paragraph or table) — the inline style span only affects text runs within a line, not the wrapping block element. - Explicit `**bold**` markdown nested around a color span doesn't compose (bold's regex escapes its captured content directly rather than recursively re-parsing it) — not hit by any request in this session, but a known edge case for future asks.

title: fix(auth): eliminate forgeable JWT_SECRET fallbacks; fail fast at boot
body:
## Summary

`process.env.JWT_SECRET || 'your-secret-key'` (and `|| ''`) appeared at 13 sites covering token signing, verification, password encryption, and OAuth state-param signing. If `JWT_SECRET` were ever unset (new env, config drift, local misconfig), every one of those sites would silently fall back to a publicly-known value — making tokens forgeable and enabling a full auth bypass, including admin. It was latent in prod/staging (the var is set there) but exactly the hidden-fallback failure mode this fix closes.

This PR replaces every fallback with a single `getJwtSecret()` accessor that throws if the secret is missing or empty, and adds a boot-time check so the server refuses to start rather than run insecurely.

## What changed (3 commits)

**1. `fix(auth)` — core fix**
- New `src/config/jwt.ts`: `getJwtSecret()` (throws on missing/empty) + `assertJwtSecretAtBoot()` (logs `[FATAL]`, `process.exit(1)`), called in `server.ts` right after `dotenv.config()`, before the port binds.
- Replaced the fallback at the 13 originally-reported sites: `controllers/auth.ts` (login/OAuth/reset token signing), `middleware/auth.ts` (main verify path), `server.ts` (socket + SSE auth), `routes/admin.ts` (session reissue + delegate tokens), `routes/contractor.ts` (delegate tokens), `mcp/server/httpClient.ts` (internal self-call tokens).
- `utils/crypto.ts`: replaced 4 `process.env.JWT_SECRET!` non-null assertions (password encrypt/decrypt for stored 3rd-party credentials) with `getJwtSecret()`. Added a golden-vector test proving the derived AES key is byte-identical before/after — existing encrypted credentials still decrypt.

**2. `refactor(oauth)` — consolidation, not a vuln fix**
- 13 files (11 OAuth connect routes + `metaAuth.ts` + `unsubscribeUrl.ts`) had their own module-load or call-time `JWT_SECRET` read-and-throw guards. These were already secure (fail closed, no fallback) — this commit just removes the duplication and routes them through the same `getJwtSecret()` accessor for consistency.

**3. `docs`**
- `.env.example`: `JWT_SECRET=your-secret-key-here` → a generation hint (`openssl rand -hex 32`), so nobody copies a weak placeholder into a real environment.

## Scope notes

Two related sites were deliberately left untouched (separate ticket, different risk class — config drift, not forgeable auth):
- `scripts/encrypt-passwords.ts` — standalone migration script, not in the running server's import graph, already fails closed via `!`.
- `utils/stripeConnectCrypto.ts` — `CONNECT_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY || JWT_SECRET`, already fails closed and documented as an intentional dev-convenience fallback.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- grep-clean: no `your-secret-key`, no `JWT_SECRET || ...`, no leftover `STATE_SECRET` or raw `process.env.JWT_SECRET` reads outside `config/jwt.ts` and the two scoped-out files above
- Boot fail-fast verified as a real process: with `JWT_SECRET` unset, exits code 1 with `[FATAL] JWT_SECRET is not set...` before the port binds
- Full test suite: **934/934 suites passed, 15,229/15,232 tests passed (3 skipped), 0 failures**
- Confirmed with the team that `JWT_SECRET` is already set (unchanged) in prod and staging EB configs — this change is behavior-preserving there, no re-login or credential-decrypt impact expected

## Known gap

`attioAuth.ts` and `stripeConnect.ts` have no dedicated unit tests covering their OAuth state sign/verify logic (pre-existing gap, not introduced by this PR). Recommend manually exercising their "Connect" flows on staging before merge as an extra check, since they lack automated coverage.

## Test plan

- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm test` pass locally
- [ ] Boot the backend with `JWT_SECRET` unset -> process exits non-zero with a clear message before the port binds
- [ ] Boot with `JWT_SECRET` set -> normal startup, log in via the portal, confirm an authenticated API call and a Socket.IO chat connection both work
- [ ] Save/re-open a stored integration credential (e.g. a connected account or MCP server) to confirm `utils/crypto.ts` encrypt/decrypt still round-trips
- [ ] Manually reconnect at least Attio and Stripe Connect OAuth flows on staging (the two without unit coverage)

The final implementation is **flag-based**, not regex-based: `agentModeService` sets a deterministic `truncatedByStepBudget` flag when the tool loop hits `maxIterations`, and the completion gate consumes it via the new `scheduledRunSignalsIncompleteResponse()`. title: Fix onboarding brand-build silent stuck, timeout drift, and stale scrapes (ENG-238)
body:
Root-caused the 40-44% onboarding brand-build failure/timeout across three concrete defects.

What was wrong:
1. Silent stuck (AC#2/#4): the brand-build background job is fire-and-forget; when lost (deploy/recycle/crash) the User stays brandBuildStatus='building' forever and the buildingBrand screen polls a spinner with no client timeout — the brand_submitted stuck cohort (~70 days).
2. Timeout drift (AC#1): the status-service + client timeout were a stale 90s but the server session budget is 300s (p95 ~5m), so in-flight builds were reported timed out and the poller abandoned them before the server finished.
3. Stale scrape (AC#3): site fetches sent no cache-control, letting a CDN/intermediary return an old copy of the site.

What changed:
- brandBuildStatusService: buildAutoFailPatchIfStuck() watchdog converts a build stuck past a hard wall (server budget + 30s grace) into terminal 'failed' with a user-visible message; corrected the budget 90s->300s.
- brandBuild GET /status: applies the watchdog on read so stuck builds surface a visible error + retry and long-stuck users reset on next poll.
- cssExtractor + readFileContent: disable browser HTTP cache and send no-cache headers so scrapes return current content.
- useBrandBuildStatus: client timeout aligned to 300s.

Verification: TDD (tests fail before, pass after). npx tsc clean in both repos; targeted jest (60 tests) and the vitest hook test pass.

title: fix(onboarding): regenerate one ICP persona, preserve user edits, and address personas by stable id
body:
Fixes the paid-ads onboarding bug reported by Fangfang Tan (ENG-255): editing a persona and clicking **"Regenerate this one"** returned the same ICP set with the edit discarded.

Companion PR: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#957

## Root cause

Nothing was cached. `POST /api/onboarding/icp/regenerate-one` parsed and validated its `icpId`, then threw it away and called `startIcpDiscoveryForUser` — a **set-level** operation. And `triggerIcpDiscoveryForUser` builds its prompt from `extractIcpBrandContext(user)` alone; it never reads `user.icpResult`. So the user's edits were neither an input to the regeneration nor preserved by it — `icpReadyPatch` overwrote the whole array. Handed identical brand inputs, the model returned the same five archetypes.

From the user's seat: *"it re-ran research and gave me back the same ICPs, ignoring my edit."*

Confirmed against the prod access log for 2026-07-08 (`108.239.226.55`): four `edit-one` calls interleaved with two `regenerate-one` calls between 22:18 and 22:24, each regeneration taking a real ~19s LLM round-trip (`icpDurationMs: 19282`) and returning a full new set. Reproduced by hand on `main`: regenerating one card replaces all five, with or without a prior edit.

## What this changes

**Regenerate exactly one persona.** `regenerate-one` uses the index it resolved. The prompt names the other four personas (so it cannot duplicate them) and asks for a deliberately *different* persona only when the card was never edited — on an edited card that instruction would fight the user's own words. Completion is a read-modify-write, because the ~20s round-trip is long enough for a concurrent `edit-one` on another card. Only `competitorResult.per_icp[N]` is refreshed, since it is a parallel array to the ICP set.

**Treat edits as an immutable anchor.** `ICPPersona.userIntent` records the user's own words per field, written only by `edit-one`, never by generation. Every regeneration of that persona is driven from the anchor rather than from the last generated value, so repeated regenerations cannot walk it away from what the user asked for. A full-set run (`/icp/start`, a cascade) preserves anchored personas whole — an implicit run must never destroy human work.

**Regenerate an edited card as a refinement.** The prompt previously showed the model only the edited field. With no name, pain or desire to work from it reasonably invented a whole new persona around one sentence, so editing `objection` silently replaced the persona's identity. It now sees the card as it stands, is told which fields the user authored, and is asked to keep who the persona is.

**Address personas by stable id, not array position.** `delete-one` splices the stored array and the FE does not refetch (`useIcpStatus` stops polling at `ready`), so the browser kept pre-delete indices: remove card 2, regenerate "card 4", and the server regenerated card 5. Personas now carry a server-minted `id`; the mutators resolve by it and fall back to the legacy `icp-N` form only when no persona carries one. A regenerated persona inherits the id of the card it replaces. `GET /icp/status` backfills ids for records written before they existed — `useIcpStatus` seeds one unconditional fetch on mount, so the browser holds real ids before it can delete anything.

**Read strongly-consistently before regenerating.** The FE fires `edit-one` and `regenerate-one` one second apart, and `getUserById` queries the eventually-consistent `UserIdIndex` GSI, so the regeneration could read a pre-edit row and never see the anchor it is meant to honour.

## Testing

`npx tsc` clean. 656 tests pass across 35 onboarding/ICP suites; the full backend suite (15,643 tests) is green.

Two new suites — `onboardingIcpRegenerateOne` and `icpPersonaIdentity` — cover: regenerating card N leaves the other four byte-identical; an edited persona survives both a regeneration of a different card and a full-set run; the anchor reaches the prompt verbatim; a concurrent edit mid-flight is not lost; mutators resolve the right persona after a delete shifted indices; `GET /icp/status` backfills ids once and still serves the snapshot when that write fails; error paths mark the run failed without rolling back a persisted persona.

**Deliberately not asserted:** whether the model honours *"preserve this meaning exactly"* or *"keep who it is"*. Tests can prove what we send to the LLM, not what comes back. That is the residual the anchor exists to bound — the user's words are never lost and drive every later regeneration, and `applyAnchor` writes them back verbatim regardless of what the model returns.

`onboardingBrandReview.test.ts` asserted that `regenerate-one` calls `startIcpDiscoveryForUser(userId)` — the bug, encoded as an expectation. Rewritten to the per-persona contract rather than deleted.

## Manual verification

Run on a cloud test env against a real Bedrock call:

- Regenerate an untouched card → only that card changes, order intact.
- Edit card 2's name, regenerate card 4 → card 2 keeps its text verbatim.
- Regenerate card 2 itself → the edited field survives, the persona stays recognisably itself.
- Delete card 2, regenerate card 4 → the card the user clicked is the one that changes.

## Not in this PR

Three defects found while investigating, each wanting its own ticket:

- `isReadableContextFile` accepts only `.txt/.md/.markdown/.csv`, so uploaded `.pdf`/`.docx`/`.html` source material never reaches any prompt.
- `mirrorIcpsToMarketStrategy` did not take on one prod account despite logging no error, leaving `marketStrategy.icp[]` stale against `icpResult`.
- `emma.enrichLeads.test.ts` is flaky under parallel-worker load.

Also note: PR #2060 (autofix agent, open) targets `regenerateMarketStrategy`, which is reachable only from Emma's chat tools and never from the onboarding screens. It fixes a real defect in the ENG-44 feature, but not this one.

title: Landing pages: kill the sync-create 300s race, self-heal idempotency locks, sweep abandoned builds (ENG-287/ENG-277)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: URGENT — customer-blocking (RankAI, Opsera, internal evals)

Supersedes #2065 (its commit is merged into this branch with the Dynamo condition tightened). Includes Manan's unmerged `manan/v0-subpage-generation-timeout` (ENG-287) work.

## What was wrong (before)
Landing-page generation failed "routinely" (Matt's 07-10 report; ENG-287/ENG-277) because of three stacked bugs, none of which was credits or account auth (both verified healthy):
1. **`v0.chats.create` ran in sync responseMode** — the HTTP call blocks for the FULL generation (3–15 min in prod evidence) against our own 300s per-attempt timeout. Every slow generation was a guaranteed client-side "failure" while v0 finished anyway, minting an **orphan chat and burning credits on each retry** (~$39 of the $50 on-demand block in 10 days; v0 chat list shows the orphans at a 5-min retry cadence).
2. `withRetry` re-burned the 300s timeout 3× → ~15-minute hangs.
3. The idempotency guard keyed on a volatile prompt hash (never deduped) while `failed`/`reserved` records blocked retries with no TTL → the permanent **"already in flight" wedge** (ENG-277, rankai-book-a-demo), plus eternal `generating` zombie cards for portal builds after any crash/redeploy.

## What this fixes (after)
- Creates use `responseMode: "async"` (chatId in seconds) + a status-gated ~16-min poll (`waitForCompletedV0Version`): a `pending` version is never downloaded, a `failed` version fails fast with v0's verdict. The 300s race and the orphan-chat credit burn are gone.
- Guard self-heals: prompt-independent identity, `failed` never blocks a retry, stale `reserved` (20-min TTL) is reclaimable, succeeded records can never be clobbered (condition scoped: `attribute_not_exists OR failed OR (reserved AND stale)`), lost races resync the local map, corrections get the same reclaim, page delete frees the identity.
- Universal janitor: ANY in-flight record that stops moving past the 30-min ceiling is marked failed with an honest message — portal builds included (poller no longer gated on `DURABLE_LANDING_GENERATION`). Stale in-flight records no longer hold a route hostage in `findReusablePageForRoute`.
- Interactive iterate/correction sends fail fast on our synthetic timeout instead of triple-billing.

## How to test
1. Emma/MCP: `generate_landing_page` for a new sub-page on an existing site.

title: Admin: v0 credit monitor — balance card + low-credit warning (partner portal)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Landing-page generation runs on the v0 API and burns real credits, but the team had ZERO visibility into the balance. A bug (fix in #2066) silently drained the account down to ~$12.76 spendable before anyone noticed.

## What this fixes (after)
Three layers so v0 credits can never silently run out again:

1. **Endpoint** — `GET /api/admin/v0/credits` (admin-only) fetches v0 `user/billing` + `user/plan` + `rate-limits` (response shapes pinned against the live API), normalizes into a stable DTO with a server-computed warn level, caches for 5 minutes, and dedupes concurrent callers into one in-flight fetch (no cache stampede; `?refresh=1` racing a natural expiry shares the same fetch). On any v0 API failure it returns 502 with the error surfaced — never fabricated/zero balances.
2. **Dashboard card** — the partner-portal admin Overview tab shows a "v0 Credits" card: total spendable $ colored green/amber/red by warn level, plan, monthly remaining/total, on-demand remaining/total, last-checked timestamp, refresh button. On fetch failure it keeps the last-known-good numbers (with their stale timestamp) and renders the error inline ("… — showing last known values"); if nothing was ever loaded it shows the plain error with no numbers.
3. **Hourly alert cron** — `checkAndAlert()` runs hourly (registered in `server.ts` like the other crons, `isCronEnabled`-gated) and fires an oncall alert on warn-level transitions into low/critical via the backend's canonical ops-alert path (`emailService.sendOncallAlert` → oncall email list + auto-filed tracked Linear issue; prod-gated so dev/staging never alert). Dedupe: last-alerted level in memory + 24h re-alert window per level; escalation (low→critical) fires immediately; recovery to ok resets state and sends a one-line all-clear. Alert-transport failures are console.error'd, never thrown out of the cron, and retried next tick. Note: the backend has no Slack ops channel — `sendOncallAlert` IS where all existing infra alerts (e.g. AgentMode context-limit) go.

Warn thresholds (named constants in `v0BillingService.ts`):
- **low**: total spendable < $25, or monthly remaining < 20% of allowance
- **critical**: total spendable < $10, or monthly allowance exhausted

At today's real balance ($2.00 monthly + $10.76 on-demand = $12.76) the card shows **amber / "Credits low"**.

## How to test
1. Log in to the partner portal as an admin (test@example.com / Test123!)
2. Go to `/admin` (Admin Dashboard) → **Overview** tab
3. Scroll to the analytics card row (Agent Mode / Tool Calls / GTM Tracker / CRM)
4. **Expected**: a new "v0 Credits" card showing `$12.76` in amber, `Plan: v0-team`, `Monthly: $2.00 / $30.00`, `On-demand: $10.76 / $50.00`, a bold amber "Credits low" line, and a "Last checked" timestamp
5. Click the refresh icon next to the card title
6. **Expected**: a brief spinner, then the same numbers with an updated "Last checked" timestamp (bypasses the 5-min server cache via `?refresh=1`)
7. Kill connectivity to v0 (or point the backend at a bad key) and click refresh
8. **Expected**: the old numbers stay visible with an inline red note "… — showing last known values"; no zeros, no blank card
9. As a non-admin, `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <basic-user-token>" https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/api/admin/v0/credits`
10. **Expected**: 403
11. Alerting (prod only): backend boot logs `[v0CreditAlert] Initialized — running hourly`; with the account currently low, the first prod tick after deploy sends one oncall alert (email to `oncall_emails` + auto-filed Linear issue) — at most one per level per 24h

## Edge cases to check
- Two admins loading the dashboard at the same instant: server makes ONE v0 fetch (in-flight dedup), not two

## Test Evidence
- Backend: `npx tsc` clean; new tests 38 passed, 0 failed (`v0BillingService.test.ts` 33 — normalization, thresholds, cache TTL, in-flight dedup with deferred resolvers, alert transitions/dedupe/recovery/transport-failure; `adminV0Credits.test.ts` 5); full routes suite 14 suites / 145 tests passed
- Partner portal: `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; full `npm test` 34 suites / 278 tests passed (includes 7 `V0CreditsCard` tests, incl. the stale-data-on-refresh-failure path)
- v0 API response shapes verified read-only against the live API (harmless GETs, key from Secrets Manager `prod/AgentWeb/V0`, never printed)
- No real alert was sent during development: the alert transport is mocked in tests and `sendOncallAlert` self-suppresses outside production

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/v0BillingService.ts` (new — fetch + normalize + cache + in-flight dedup + warnLevel + checkAndAlert)
- `backend/src/routes/adminV0Credits.ts` (new — thin admin-only route)
- `backend/src/app.ts` (mount router at /api/admin)
- `backend/src/server.ts` (hourly v0CreditAlert cron registration)
- `backend/src/services/__tests__/v0BillingService.test.ts` (new)
- `backend/src/routes/__tests__/adminV0Credits.test.ts` (new)

- Live end-to-end through the deployed partner portal UI (no test env synced for this branch) — the endpoint's normalization was verified against the real v0 API responses, and the card against mocked responses

title: Emulate dark color-scheme in headless brand extraction (ENG-285)
body:
What was wrong: The design-token/brand extractor (backend/src/services/cssExtractor.ts, extractWithPuppeteer) launched headless Chrome without emulating a color-scheme preference. Headless Chrome defaults to prefers-color-scheme: light, so sites that ship their dark brand behind the OS color-scheme preference (a CSS media query or a client script that toggles a dark class/data-theme) were captured in their LIGHT variant. Confirmed live against rankai.ai: the default read returns body background oklch(0.985 0 0) (near-white) with near-black text, while the real design is matte black with an amber glow — so brand extraction recorded the wrong theme, leading to incorrect brand enforcement on landing pages.

What changed: Added page.emulateMediaFeatures([{ name: 'prefers-color-scheme', value: 'dark' }]) before page.goto so both SSR and client hydration observe a dark preference. Reproduced against the live site that this flips the computed body background from oklch(0.985 0 0)/near-white to oklch(0.175 0 0)/dark with white text and a `dark` class applied — matching the user's screenshot. Light-only sites are unaffected since they have no dark variant to switch to.

How verified: Wrote a failing test first (asserts emulateMediaFeatures is called with prefers-color-scheme dark and before goto), confirmed it failed, then implemented the fix. Full test file passes (27/27) and npx tsc is clean.

title: Inherit org owner subscription tier when accepting an invite (ENG-288)
body:
## Summary

Fixes ENG-288 (org invite recipients get wrong tier / no shared assets) and, as a byproduct, ENG-261's backend half (Twitter connection fails despite Super Premium — the frontend half ships in a companion PR on `agentweb-customer-portal`).

**Root cause:** `getUserSubscriptionType(userId)` read the raw `user.subscriptionType` field with no org-owner resolution. The `/me` route had its own one-off resolution, but every other consumer (connected-accounts gating, Emma's skill auto-install, `get_user_profile`) read the member's own (stale, Free-by-default) record directly.

**Fix:** centralize org-owner tier resolution inside `getUserSubscriptionType` itself, so every downstream consumer (`getAllowedPages`, `getAllowedSkills`, `getAllowedConnectedAccounts`, `getHiddenPages`) inherits correctly with one implementation instead of four disagreeing ones. Resolution is read-time (not snapshotted on invite-accept), so it stays in sync with owner upgrades/downgrades and auto-revokes the moment a member leaves.

## What else this turned up (all fixed here, each independently tested and live-verified against a running test-env instance — not just unit tests)

- **`get_user_profile` (Emma tool)** — same unresolved-call-site bug; member self-reported the wrong tier via chat.
- **`updateUser`'s null-handling** — `leave`/`removeMember`/`deleteOrg` all call `updateUser(id, {orgId: null, orgRole: null})`, but the generic `updateUser` did `SET orgId = :null`, which DynamoDB rejects for a GSI key attribute (`OrgIdIndex`) — every leave/remove/delete-org call 500'd and left the member stuck in the org forever, silently defeating the revocation guarantee this whole fix depends on. Now does `REMOVE` instead of `SET ... = null` for any null field. Audited every other place in the backend that ever nulls a field via `updateUser` (5 fields total) — none rely on the stored-null-vs-absent distinction.
- **Own-active-subscription discriminator** — a member can hold their own independent active/trialing Stripe subscription (accept-invite touches no billing state), so unconditional owner-resolution would silently override a self-paying member's tier. Now resolves to the owner only when the member has no live subscription of their own — matches the existing active/trialing = entitling convention in `stripeService.ts`. Concrete prod case: `pvandervalk@xcures.com` holds his own active Pro sub as an org member.
- **`/me` route inconsistency** — found *while live-testing* the discriminator above: `/me` pre-resolved `subscriptionUserId = org.ownerUserId || userId` itself and passed that into `getUserSubscriptionType`, bypassing the discriminator entirely (a self-paying member's `/me` showed the owner's tier while connected-accounts correctly showed their own — an internal inconsistency). Now delegates to the centralized function with the caller's own id, and skips the owner billing-status overlay for the same case.
- **Org-lookup error isolation** — a transient `orgDb.getOrgById` failure (throttling, network blip) was hitting the outer catch-all and returning hard `"Free"`, discarding the already-fetched user's real own tier. Isolated so an org-lookup failure falls back to the user's own tier instead.

## How verified

- TDD throughout: failing tests first for each fix, `npx tsc` clean after every file, full backend suite green (only 6 pre-existing, unrelated env-config failures — confirmed via `git stash` comparison that they fail identically without this branch's changes).
- Live-verified end-to-end on a cloud test-env instance (not just mocks): join → inherit tier → leave/remove/delete-org → revoke, connected-accounts (Twitter appears/disappears correctly), a real Emma chat message invoking `get_user_profile`, a real Emma chat turn invoking a gated tool (confirms the skill-auto-install call sites), a forced real HTTP 500 to confirm the frontend companion fix's error path, and a real DB-level active-subscription patch to confirm the discriminator.
- Prod data cross-checked read-only (no writes): confirmed no live user is currently stuck from the leave-org bug, confirmed the one real active-subscription-holding org member (`pvandervalk@xcures.com`) isn't affected today (his tier happens to match his owner's), found one unrelated pre-existing stale/orphaned tombstone row (harmless, filtered out by every read path already) — not touched, out of scope.

Fixes ENG-288 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-288/org-invite-recipients-receive-wrong-tier-and-no-shared-assets-landing

title: Return canonical Linear link to internal reporters (ENG-289 Desired behavior #1)
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #2070 (merged). That PR surfaced the canonical Linear link **only in the internal team notification email**. On review of the issue's **Desired behavior**, that misses point **#1**:

> The **submitter** gets the canonical Linear issue link immediately, whether the report created a new issue or deduped/enriched an existing one.

\#2070 deliberately excluded the link from the submitter-facing surface (Emma reply / API response / tool result) because the code review flagged that leaking an internal Linear link to **external customers / external-MCP callers** is a real leak. Those two goals genuinely conflict when the submitter is an external customer.

## What this does (option 2 — surface to internal submitters only)

The submitter now gets the canonical link back **when they are internal** — someone who can actually open a Linear issue:
- an **admin** (`user.isAdmin`), or
- a **delegated-admin** session (a teammate driving on a customer's behalf), or
- an **@agentweb.pro** reporter.

External customers still receive only their Featurebase tracking link, and **all external-MCP callers are always excluded** (even if the caller is an admin) — preserving the leak guard, since the tool result is JSON.stringified to external MCP clients and persisted into Agent Mode LLM/sidebar state. The **internal team email is unchanged** and always carries the link.

### Surfaces
- `emma/tools.ts` `report_product_issues` → `results[].canonicalUrl` (Agent Mode / Slack / Emma), gated `reporterIsInternal && !externalMcp`.
- `routes/support.ts` `/report-ui-bug` → `res.body.canonicalUrl` (in-app Report a Bug), gated on internal reporter.

## Coverage of the rest of Desired behavior (nothing else missing)
- **#1 submitter gets the link** — this PR. ✅
- **#2 canonical enriched with reporter/customer/source** — existing `[reporter-ticket #N]` comments + context lines. ✅
- **#3 customer/blocker rollup visible** — per-reporter comments list each affected user; priority set. ✅
- **#4 dedup comments + returns same link** — existing dedup + same `canonicalUrl` (verified live: two reports → same ENG-296). ✅
- **#5 failed submission surfaced** — REST returns 500; tool pushes `success:false`. ✅

## Tests

title: Fix LinkedIn get-profile retry breaker blocking corrected calls (ENG-313)
body:
What was wrong: The agent-mode same-tool repeated-failure breaker (agentToolGatewayService.ts) keys LinkedIn failures by (tool, recipientScope, errorHead), but get-profile was not in the recipient-scoped action set. title: [blocked: needs expand/contract split] ENG-162: Share HubSpot and Fathom OAuth sessions
body:
> **HELD — database/data-plane gate. Requires Harsha's explicit pre-merge approval.** HubSpot/Fathom pending OAuth payloads move from process memory into durable `AW-OAuthSessions` DynamoDB rows. No schema migration, but it changes the persistence contract for security-sensitive token material, which `autonomous-execution-and-merge.md` reserves to Harsha. Every mechanical gate is already proven green (CI, staging, latest-SHA Greptile 5/5, attribution) — **those do not waive this one.** Gate detail in "Risk and gate classification" below.
>
> *Hoisted to line 1 on 2026-07-31 (Watchdog) — the gate was stated 38 lines down, so the PR read as unexplained `[needs human]` in the queue.*

## Reviewer-first summary

- Replaces process-local HubSpot and Fathom OAuth token-session maps with the existing canonical `AW-OAuthSessions` DynamoDB table.
- Preserves each provider callback, token exchange, account payload, scopes, and webhook behavior while allowing `/finalize` and `/connect` to land on different application instances.
- Stores each pending flow as its own random-keyed, ten-minute TTL row and consumes it with one conditional DynamoDB delete returning `ALL_OLD`; concurrent callers cannot replay token material or overwrite sibling sessions.
- Leaves the existing Gmail/Outlook AW-Settings row format untouched, avoiding mixed-version rolling-deploy coupling.
- This is a bounded phase-1 slice of ENG-162. The parent issue stays open until the remaining eligible OAuth route maps are migrated and the issue-wide grep criterion is clean.

## Acceptance mapping for this slice

1. HubSpot and Fathom pending token sessions use the shared canonical table; no provider-local token map or cleanup timer remains.
2. A session written by one store module instance is consumable from a separately loaded instance.
3. One atomic delete validates user, provider, TTL, and one-time use while returning the payload; missing, expired, mismatched, and replayed sessions return no token material.
4. Same-user sibling sessions use independent rows and cannot clobber one another.
5. Shared-store write/consume failures are explicit and fail closed.
6. Gmail/Outlook storage remains byte-shape compatible because the migrated-provider path does not modify it.
7. HubSpot CRM/Marketing scope behavior and Fathom callback/account/webhook behavior remain regression-covered.

## Behavioral proof

- Initial TDD red: 5 failed / 29 controls passed before the shared-store implementation.
- Store-hardening red: 2 failed / 2 controls passed for delete-failure replay protection and legacy behavior.
- Route failure red: 2 failed because shared-store errors escaped the `/connect` error boundary.
- Greptile rolling-deploy P1: removed the cross-format design entirely; Gmail/Outlook keep their existing storage shape.
- Greptile 3/5 concurrency finding: replaced read/modify/write with one row per pending flow plus atomic conditional delete-and-return.
- Current-main OAuth regression: 8 suites / 117 tests passed.
- Hosted full-suite regression exposed one stale Fathom route harness; it now models the canonical shared-session boundary and passes 9/9 locally.
- Exact-head hosted gate is green: AgentMode backend 10m00s, all-other + coverage 15m22s, and staging deploy/readiness 3m44s.
- Exact-head Greptile review: 5/5, zero comments, required review check passed.
- Direct Dynamo contract tests cover TTL put, collision guard, conditional user/provider/TTL consume, `ALL_OLD`, already-consumed/null behavior, and fail-closed errors.
- Backend TypeScript build/typecheck passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Migrated-route grep is clean; the parent issue all-route grep is intentionally not yet clean.

## Risk and gate classification

- PURE/MOCKABLE test execution: persistence, OAuth HTTP, connected-account, and Fathom webhook interactions are mocked; no live OAuth or external mutation was fired.
- **Existing-table data-plane change:** HubSpot/Fathom pending OAuth payloads move from process memory into the existing `AW-OAuthSessions` DynamoDB table and are consumed atomically. There is no schema migration, but this still changes persistence behavior.
- Therefore this PR requires Harsha explicit database/data-plane approval before merge. CI, staging, latest-SHA Greptile 5/5, and attribution are proven; those checks do not waive the approval gate.
- No external copy, credential, dependency, or new-spend change.

## Complexity ledger

- Deleted both provider-local token maps and cleanup timers.
- Reused the existing canonical OAuth sessions table; no new table, persistence abstraction, fallback, or vendor.
- Production delta: 107 additions / 139 deletions, net -32 lines.

## Attribution

- Linear: ENG-162
- Accountable owner: Harsha Vankayalapati (`142fef82-4d45-4070-99be-c5debe565ac6`, GitHub `harshmoney123`)
- Execution actor: Codex sprint-worker

title: ENG-273: WhatsApp as a peer customer-communication channel (Cloud API)
body:
## Summary

Adds WhatsApp as a **peer customer-communication channel to Slack** ([ENG-273](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-273/support-whatsapp-as-an-outboundcustomer-communication-channel)), on the official WhatsApp Cloud API using a single AgentWeb-owned business number.

Rather than hardcoding a second channel, this introduces the provider-neutral seam Slack now runs through, so Teams ([ENG-272](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-272/support-microsoft-teams-as-a-customer-communication-channel)) lands on the same abstraction instead of becoming a third copy of the same branching. The shape is lifted directly from `emailProviderService`, which solved the identical problem for Gmail/Outlook in ENG-266/302.

## Provider decision

Three paths were compared. **Unipile was rejected despite being the fastest** — days of work, near-zero marginal cost, already a paid dependency wired up for LinkedIn, and the only option that reaches WhatsApp *groups*. It does not use Meta's API; it links an account the way WhatsApp Web does, which violates WhatsApp's consumer terms and risks a permanent, unappealable ban of the connected number. That is not sellable to Manifest Health or Baldwin, who are the buyers driving this request.

## Two platform walls that shaped the design

Neither is a scoping choice, and neither is visible in the request payload:

1. **Meta paused marketing templates to US (+1) numbers on 2025-04-01** — still paused, no announced end date, sends fail with `131049`. AgentWeb's customer base is US-centric, so **WhatsApp is not usable as a campaign/cold-outreach channel** and GTM should not promise it. Utility templates and the 24h service window are unaffected, which is what notifications and approvals actually need. Every template in the registry is deliberately `utility`.
2. **Since 2026-01-15 the Business Solution Terms prohibit general-purpose AI assistants** where the AI is the primary functionality. Structured notifications, approvals and support automation remain explicitly allowed. The inbound webhook therefore deliberately does **not** open an Emma chat session the way `routes/slack.ts` does — and a test asserts it never imports one, because the next person will otherwise "fix" that inconsistency.

## What's in here

- **`messagingChannelService`** — neutral interface, registry, `MessagingChannelError` base class, and a capability model so callers branch on what a channel *can do* rather than on its name. Memoized-promise bootstrap, not a boolean flag (that version had a real concurrency bug — ENG-300).
- **`whatsappService`** — window-aware send routing, approved-template registry, phone-keyed consent, typed mapping for `131049` / `131047` / `131026` / rate limits.
- **`routes/whatsappWebhook`** — raw-body `X-Hub-Signature-256` HMAC, STOP/UNSTOP, delivery-status separation.
- **Two customer-facing surfaces routed through the seam** — ship notifications and lead alerts, both additive to the always-on email baseline.
- **`routes/messagingChannels`** — user-facing config API that refuses a phone number without explicit opt-in.
- **`docs/integrations/whatsapp-contract.md`** — required by `docs/integrations/README.md` before touching an external API.

## Slack is untouched

The Slack refactor is inert by construction: **the pre-existing Slack suites pass unmodified**, which is the whole reason Phase 1 shipped separately from the WhatsApp implementation. `slackChannelAdapter` even omits the thread argument when there is none, because passing an explicit `undefined` is behaviorally identical but changes the call arity those suites assert against.

`humanEvalService`, `leadCaptureFailureService` and the landing-page smoke alert still import `slackService` directly. That is deliberate — they are internal-ops alerts with no customer value on WhatsApp, and `humanEvalService` depends on Slack directory APIs WhatsApp has no equivalent for.

## Three bugs caught during the work

- Deriving the notification candidate list purely from the user record silently broke **org-inherited Slack channels** — Slack resolves through an org/owner fallback. Caught by the existing org-fallback test.
- The webhook originally acked before processing, which raced the work **and would have silently lost STOPs**. It now processes first, and splits failure handling by kind: unparseable payload → 200 (a retry can only fail the same way), storage error → 500 (retry the lost opt-out).
- `clearAllMocks` leaks implementations, so one test's `mockRejectedValue` bled into the next and made a passing assertion depend on test order.

## No data-plane changes

`messagingChannels` is additive and normalized at **read** time from the legacy `slackChannel` / `slackChannels` fields — the same choice ENG-266 made for `senderProvider`. No migration, no backfill, no schema rewrite, so this stays outside CLAUDE.md's database/data-plane approval gate and every existing reader keeps working.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] 282 tests passing across 23 suites (52 WhatsApp service+webhook, 36 channel seam, 18 routing, 13 config API, plus every pre-existing Slack suite unchanged)
- [ ] **95% coverage gate — not yet met.** New files sit at 92.01 stmts / **81.41 branch** / 96.36 funcs / 93.12 lines. Branch coverage is the gap; untested paths are credential-fetch failure, non-JSON Meta error bodies, and org-owner fallback variants. **This blocks merge and is being addressed next.**
- [ ] Live verification against Meta — blocked on ENG-891 (business app, WABA, number, verification, template approval). Meta's sandbox test number works pre-verification and would unblock the full loop ahead of production credentials.

## Deferred, with reasons

Campaign/marketing sends (US pause), multi-tenant Embedded Signup (needs Tech Provider verification + App Review, and its main use case is blocked by the same pause), group messaging (needs an Official Business Account, caps at 8 participants), and conversational Emma (Jan 2026 ToS). All recorded in the contract file and on ENG-273 — ENG-273's Done bar explicitly accepts a documented deferral alongside a shipped workflow.

## Not in this PR

Portal settings card, Emma tool mirror, and approval requests (`revisionService`) — the last needs interactive reply-button templates and inbound button handling, and front-loads template-approval latency.

title: [needs human] ENG-922: halt incomplete image batches before publish
body:
**BLOCKER — unreviewed user-facing copy.** This PR adds three new strings that are persisted as Emma `assistant` messages and rendered to the customer in chat. Material user-visible copy is a permanent Harsha-review gate (`autonomous-execution-and-merge.md` §merge-gate 10, `taste-calibration.md` §gates-that-never-disappear). The swarm may not settle it. **Decision packet with 3 options and a recommendation is on ENG-922** — one reply ("A", "B", "C", or your own wording) clears this and the PR goes through the normal ready/CI/Greptile/merge gate. Nothing else about ENG-922 is open.

## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)

A multi-creative build that hit the per-run media time budget kept going: the model got another loop iteration after an incomplete image batch, and on the Meta ad-creative route that next iteration could start uploading a partial set — leaving orphaned images/creatives. A run that produced **zero** assets got no handling at all and died as a silent generic 504. Dated evidence on ENG-922: a real three-creative build ran ~60 minutes and produced zero images, zero creatives, zero ads, verified against the Graph API.

## What this fixes (after)

A media-budget deferral is now **terminal for the current turn**: completed images are delivered, the exact remaining count is reported, and the loop stops before any follow-on Graph write can publish an incomplete batch. A whole-turn timeout with zero completed assets now returns a same-turn explanation instead of a bare 504.

## Complexity ledger

- **Net lines:** +569 / -13 across 9 files; 4 of the 9 are test files.
- **Moving parts added:** two pure response builders (`buildEmptyMediaTimeoutMessage`, `buildMediaBudgetDeferralMessage`) in an existing leaf util, and one explicit terminal loop boundary.
- **Moving parts removed at runtime:** the model-controlled extra iteration after an incomplete image batch — the path to partial publishing and orphaned Graph state.
- No new service, dependency, setting, table, or data store. No feature flag.
- **Behavior-preserving?** No, deliberately: this changes tool-loop behavior, but only on the two paths where the media budget actually defers or progress proves a zero-asset media timeout. The bounded concurrent four-image path is unchanged and still pinned by its characterization test.

## How to test

1. In Emma chat, ask for a multi-image ad-creative build large enough to cross `AGENT_MODE_MEDIA_BUDGET_MS`.
2. **Expected**: the turn ends with the completed images rendered inline, an exact remaining count, and a `continue` prompt — and no new ad image / creative / ad appears on the Meta account.
3. Verify independently on the Graph API (`/adimages`, `/adcreatives`, campaign ad count) that nothing partial was written.
4. Force a timeout with zero images finished.
5. **Expected**: a same-turn assistant message naming the pending count, persisted so it survives reload; HTTP 504 with `partialMediaDelivery: false`.

## Edge cases to check

- Deferred `generate_video` / `generate_voiceover` (not just images) — nouns must be kind-correct, and "assets" when mixed.
- A read-only tool in the same iteration as a deferred media call must still execute; anything that writes/sends/publishes must defer.
- The `wait_seconds` sequential dispatch path — it was unhardened in the first two commits.
- Non-media timeouts must keep the pre-existing generic 504 handling untouched.

## Test Evidence

Backend jest pattern `"agentMode|timeoutContinuation"`, `--maxWorkers=2 --forceExit`:

| Ref | Result |
|---|---|
| base `8ca97d0078` (merge-base with `main`) | **3996 / 3996 pass**, 236 suites |
| head `616687943` (before the fix commit) | 3997 / 4001 — **4 FAILED**, 2 suites red |
| head `c32e5b76c` (after the fix commit) | **4008 / 4008 pass**, 237 suites |

Three consecutive clean runs on `c32e5b76c` (4008/4008 each) — not one lucky run. `npx tsc --noEmit`: only the 2 pre-existing `twitter-api-v2` module-resolution errors, byte-identical at base. `git diff --check` clean.

The 4 tests red at `616687943`, all now green **unmodified** (the implementation was narrowed to match them, not the reverse):

- `executePreparedTools › media-generation time budget › does NOT defer non-media tools even when over budget` — a pre-existing characterization whose whole purpose was to pin the opposite behavior.
- 3 × `AgentModeController - Error Handling › generateSharedResponse › …`

**Re-run required before ready:** the table above was measured at `c32e5b76c`. Current head is `d0d6c5bc4`, a later merge of `main`. The suite must be re-run at the then-current head when the copy gate clears — this evidence does not carry forward across that merge.

## Behavioral assertions verified

Human-written contract from ENG-922, unmodified:

| # | Acceptance criterion | Proving test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4-image batch completes in one run, no manual "continue" | `core/__tests__/toolDispatch.test.ts` — bounded four-image characterization, still green unchanged (budget was **not** raised) |
| 2 | Zero-asset budget overrun is explained in the same turn with remaining work | `__tests__/timeoutContinuation.test.ts` (`buildEmptyMediaTimeoutMessage`) + `agentModeController.errorHandling.test.ts` persistence/504 assertions |
| 3 | Partial results are delivered on the ad-creative route | `agentModeService.mediaBudgetHalt.test.ts` — real AgentMode loop, 3 completed + 1 deferred |
| 4 | No orphaned state on partial failure | `agentModeService.mediaBudgetHalt.test.ts` scripts a next-turn Graph write and proves it is never reached; `core/__tests__/toolDispatch.test.ts` pins the `wait_seconds` path and the read-vs-write deferral scoping |

## Defects fixed in `c32e5b76c` (self-review of the first two commits)

1. **Over-broad dependent deferral** (`core/toolDispatch.ts`) — marked *every* non-media call deferred, including read-only lookups. Now scoped by the gateway's own `policyDecision.effect`: `read` executes; write/send/publish/mutate defers; anything the gateway cannot classify fails closed to defer. Publish-blocking guarantee unchanged.
2. **Unconditional `getLatestProgress(shareId)`** (`controllers/agentModeController.ts`) — ran in the shared-response `catch` for *every* error, not just timeouts. Moved inside the `isGenerationTimeout` guard, matching this PR's own sibling hunk on the `/generate` path.
3. **`hasWaitTool` path unhardened** (`core/toolDispatch.ts`) — reproduced with `["wait_seconds", "generate_image", "call_meta_marketing_api"]` + `mediaBudgetDeferred: true`: the image deferred and the Meta Graph write still executed. Now covered; new test pins it.
4. **Overclaiming user-facing copy** (`utils/timeoutContinuation.ts`) — "I stopped before starting any follow-on publishing steps, so the incomplete batch was not published" is not something the code can guarantee across iterations within a turn. Reworded to claim only what holds. **This reword was for accuracy, not taste — it is the blocker above.**
5. **Media-kind blind spot** (`utils/timeoutContinuation.ts`) — remaining-work count only counted `generate_image`, so a deferred `generate_video` / `generate_voiceover` returned `null` and dropped the caller into a canned string that lost the completed images. Now counts every budgeted media tool with kind-correct nouns.

## Files changed

Source (5): `controllers/agentModeController.ts`, `services/agentModeService.ts`, `services/agentMode/core/toolDispatch.ts`, `utils/timeoutContinuation.ts`
Tests (4): `__tests__/agentModeController.errorHandling.test.ts`, `__tests__/agentModeController.timeoutCancelsOrphan.test.ts`, `__tests__/agentModeService.mediaBudgetHalt.test.ts`, `__tests__/timeoutContinuation.test.ts`, `services/agentMode/core/__tests__/toolDispatch.test.ts`

## What was NOT tested

- No live Meta ad account and no real spend — image-gen and Graph boundaries are mocked throughout, per the issue's own implementation-test instruction.
- No end-to-end run against staging; the PR has never been ready, so no staging deploy has happened.
- LLM/Emma behavior parity (Okareo baseline-vs-change) for this tool-loop change: not run.
- Greptile has not reviewed any SHA (the required check is `SKIPPED` while draft).

## Autonomous gate status

| Gate | Status |
|---|---|
| Database / data-plane change | **None.** No schema, migration, backfill, index, or key change. Chat messages are written through the existing `chatbotDb.addMessageToSession` contract. |
| Unreviewed external-facing copy | **BLOCKED — this is the gate.** See first line; packet on ENG-922. |
| Unavailable credential | None — everything is mocked. |
| Unresolved product decision on budget behavior | None. AC1 is met without raising the budget; halt semantics are fixed by the human-written AC4. |
| Base current | Merged `main` at `d0d6c5bc4`. Re-verify at ready time. |
| CI / staging / Greptile 5/5 | Not started — draft. |
| Attribution | Passes. All code commits author `harshmoney123`; head `d0d6c5bc4` is a GitHub merge commit authored `harshmoney123`. |
| Ready-flip budget | **Held independently.** `actions-budget.py` exits 2 (CRITICAL): $58.93 of $200 spent on day 10/31, projected **$182.67 = 91% of cap**, and `prevent_further_usage` is on. No PR flips ready while this is non-zero. |
| Auto-merge | Not armed. |

title: Stop sync scoring from silently dropping long sessions (ENG-929)
body:
**What was wrong**

`get_chat_history(sync=true)` promises to score every session that lacks a score, yet completed, expensive sessions came back with `satisfactionScore: null` and were never scored on any later run.

Two defects combined:

1. *Long transcripts could not be scored at all.* `sessionScoringService` raced each scoring call against a flat 20s timeout, and capped the transcript by message COUNT (50) but never by SIZE. Production's configured scoring model (and both custom judges) is a thinking model, whose latency scales with input, so a 30-70 turn scheduled run lost the race, `scoreSession` threw, and the session was left unscored — permanently, since the daily report's window has moved on by the next run. Confirmed against prod: three unscored sessions (msgCount 30/39/69) are missing the satisfaction score AND both judge scores, while a 3-message session in the same later window scored fine in ~3s per judge — so this is a per-session size failure, not the wall-clock budget cutting the batch short.
2. *The failure was invisible.* `scoreBackfill` caught the throw, logged it server-side, and returned the session with a null score — identical to an in-flight run or a session excluded from the cohort by design. The Daily Satisfaction Score Report therefore published an average as if coverage were complete.

A third, aggravating detail: the satisfaction scorer and every judge shared one `try` block, so a single timeout took out all of a session's scores at once.

**What changed**

- `sessionScoringService`: cap the serialized transcript (head + tail preserved, middle elided with a marker); scale the per-call timeout with transcript size from the 20s baseline up to a 60s ceiling; label a score formed on a shortened transcript with `transcriptTruncated` rather than withholding it. The timeout timer is now always cleared.
- `sessionScoringService`: `attemptSessionScore` reports WHY a session was skipped (`in-flight`, `already-scored`, `no-task-session`, `test-run`, `no-user-message`, `admin-override`). `scoreSessionIfNeeded` remains the score-only view for existing callers.
- `scoreBackfill`: returns a per-session outcome (`scored` / `skipped` / `failed` / `not-attempted`, with reason), and runs the judges even when the satisfaction scorer throws.
- `GET /api/admin/chat-sessions`: attaches `scoringOutcome` per session and a `scoringSummary` for the pass (sync mode only).
- `get_chat_history`: passes both through, and its description now states that any non-zero failed/not-attempted count means the satisfaction figures under-sample the window and must be reported as such.

No scoring semantics changed for sessions that already scored; no data migration; the new fields are additive and absent when `sync` is not requested.

**How it was verified**

TDD: the new tests fail on the pre-fix code (8/8 in the new file, plus the outcome assertions in the three existing files). `npm run typecheck` clean; the four touched suites plus the neighbouring scoring suites pass (145 tests).

---
**Automated gates**
Code review: ✅ sound — 1 finding(s) fixed
Deterministic checks: ✅ all passed
Browser verify: ⚠️ environment down (not verified)

Fixes ENG-929 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-929/synctrue-left-4-completed-sessions-with-no-satisfaction-score-get-chat

title: test(qa): fail-closed QA fixture harness (ENG-739)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

**Named gate up front:** the `with-admin` subcommand's grant/revoke adapters perform a runtime compare-and-set on a real users-table row. Per Harsha's closure note on #2239, treat this PR as **data-plane-gated: explicit Harsha approval required before merge**. **Merge** is what that approval gates — not review. The PR is flipped ready so CI and Greptile can produce evidence on the latest SHA; it must NOT be merged without Harsha's explicit data-plane approval. (It was previously worded "must stay draft until that approval", which deadlocked the gate: draft-time runs skip every substantive job and `Require Greptile Review`, so the PR could never accumulate the very evidence the approval decision needs. Two ready-flips were reverted to draft under that reading, cancelling both CI runs.)

## What was wrong (before)
Every documented QA fixture account was dead (401 / 403-deactivated / 404) and QA still reported passes — the signal said pass, the thing never ran (ENG-739). A first implementation (PR #2239) built a correct pure core but was closed 2026-08-07 because nothing could invoke it: interface-only adapters, no CLI, no `require.main`, no consumers, and an error message referencing a `--` flag surface that was never built.

## What this fixes (after)
The harness is now runnable end to end. `preflight` authenticates every required fixture against a configurable real domain and asserts the privilege boundary (non-admin must get 403 on `/api/admin/users`, not 200), emitting structured JSON and exiting nonzero on any mismatch — a dead or missing fixture is a blocking verdict naming the account, never a silent skip. `with-admin -- <command>` runs a command under a temporary userId-pinned conditional admin grant and compare-and-set revokes exactly what this run granted, on normal exit and on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP.

Salvage credit: the pure core (`preflightFixtures`, `runWithTemporaryAdmin`, types — 172 lines) is reused from closed PR #2239 (`swarm/eng-739-qa-fixture-harness`, head `8fedd2e82`), re-committed by this run per the attribution gate. Its two review objections (startChild race, lost CAS) were already refuted on verification there; this PR adds the invokable layer whose absence closed it.

```
npx ts-node src/scripts/qa-fixture-harness.ts preflight
npx ts-node src/scripts/qa-fixture-harness.ts with-admin -- <command...>
```

Credentials/config are environment injection only: `QA_FIXTURE_BASE_URL`, `QA_USER_EMAIL/PASSWORD`, `QA_TIER_EMAIL/PASSWORD`; `QA_USERS_TABLE`, `QA_ADMIN_FIXTURE_EMAIL`, `QA_ADMIN_FIXTURE_USER_ID`. No hardcoded secrets, no table-name defaults.

## Complexity ledger
- Net lines: **+1,585** (724 harness incl. 172 salvaged core, 861 tests). New capability, not refactor; pays for itself by deleting the "QA passes against dead fixtures" failure class and removing any need for a standing prod admin account.
- Moving parts: +1 standalone CLI script under `src/scripts/`. No new service, config system, table, flag, or dependency (uses existing `aws-sdk`, `axios`). The grant-visibility fix adds two injected ports (`readGrantVisibility`, `waitBeforeRetry`) on the existing adapter seam rather than a new abstraction, and both are **required** — an optional visibility check would silently degrade to today's race.
- Behavior-preserving: **zero product-runtime changes** — no product file touched, no product import of this module (AC4). Grep-verifiable: the only consumer is its own test.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/qa-fixture-harness.test.ts` — **Expected:** 41 passed.
2. `npm run typecheck` — **Expected:** clean.
3. Dry CLI check (no env set): `npx ts-node src/scripts/qa-fixture-harness.ts preflight` — **Expected:** one JSON line `{"verdict":"block","phase":"config","detail":"QA_FIXTURE_BASE_URL is not set — preflight has no target domain"}`, exit 1 (fail closed).
4. `npx ts-node src/scripts/qa-fixture-harness.ts with-admin` — **Expected:** usage on stderr, exit 2, no grant attempted.
5. Live smoke (post-approval, staging): export the QA_* vars for `qa-user@`/`qa-tier@agentweb.pro` against `https://api-stage.agentweb.pro`, run `preflight` — **Expected:** `{"verdict":"pass",...}`, exit 0.

## Edge cases to check
- Fixture login returns an unexpected 200-with-admin-access → `phase: "privilege"` block (a non-admin fixture that CAN reach admin routes blocks, not just dead logins).
- Missing one env var of a later fixture → earlier fixtures checked, run still blocks naming the exact var; never partial-passes.
- Network failure (DNS/refused) during preflight → caught, emitted as a block verdict, exit 1 — not an unhandled crash that a wrapper could misread as "no verdict".
- `revokeIfCurrent` hitting a row changed by someone else → returns false → loud `TemporaryAdminCleanupError`, exit 1 (never silently claims cleanup).
- Child killed by signal (no exit code) → mapped to nonzero.

## Test Evidence
- Red run (commit `c97b9276`, tests written before implementation): **15 failed, 7 passed** — the 7 passing are the salvaged #2239 core baseline; all invokable-layer tests fail (`runCli is not a function`, etc.).
- Green run (commit `ea1f3f63`): **30 passed, 0 failed**.
- Grant-visibility red run (commit `ec1bbce2e`): **7 failed, 30 passed** — the 7 new failures are exactly the visibility tests; the 30 pre-existing tests stay green, so the reds are behavioral, not compile errors.
- Grant-visibility green run (commit `027c154c8`): **38 passed, 0 failed** (`npx jest src/__tests__/qa-fixture-harness.test.ts`).
- Signal-during-spawn red run (commit `ac951990b`, test committed before the fix): **3 failed, 38 passed** — one per signal; `child.terminate` recorded `[]` against the post-spawn baseline `[["SIGTERM"]]`, i.e. the command was left running after its grant was revoked.
- Signal-during-spawn green run (commit `5f3ae7837`): **41 passed, 0 failed** (`npx jest src/__tests__/qa-fixture-harness.test.ts`), `npm run typecheck` exit 0.
- The abort-during-poll test was separately proven red: with the abort guard removed, `never starts the child when a termination signal lands during the visibility wait` fails (1 failed / 37 passed), then passes with it restored.
- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0, 0 errors. (It caught a widened-port break in the shared `fakeDocClient` helper that jest did not — the helper now supplies a default `query`.)
- Tested as: no live accounts used — all network/DB boundaries mocked (MOCKABLE class per swarm charter). No real sleeps: `waitBeforeRetry` is injected, so only the real CLI ever calls `setTimeout`.

## Behavioral assertions verified (human-written ACs on ENG-739)
- **AC1** (dead fixture → blocking result naming account+status, never proceeds/omits): `blocks immediately and names a dead fixture login and status`; `exits 1 and emits a blocking JSON report naming the dead account and status, never reaching later fixtures`; `fails closed on missing credential env vars, naming the account, before any login for that fixture`.
- **AC2** (health checked BEFORE use, privilege asserted — 403 not 200): `preflight` is a discrete pre-use subcommand; `blocks when a non-admin fixture unexpectedly has admin access`; `exits 0 with a structured pass report when every fixture authenticates at its expected privilege`.
- **AC3** (no standing admin; grant revoked even on mid-flight kill): `uses the conditional grant token for compare-and-set cleanup on normal exit`; `terminates the child and compare-and-set cleans the grant on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP` (it.each); `exits nonzero when compare-and-set cleanup cannot restore the exact granted value`; `revoke pins the exact row and run: email key, userId + granted value + run id condition`; `terminates the child spawned during the SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP in-flight window instead of leaving it running` (it.each — a signal at ANY point leaves no running child). SIGKILL is outside the signal contract per the PM decision comment (2026-08-01).
- **AC3 (grant visibility, added for the Greptile P1)**: `does not start the child until the grant is visible on the auth read path`; `fails closed without starting the child when the grant never becomes visible`; `bounds the visibility poll by attempts and never waits after the final read`; `never starts the child when a termination signal lands during the visibility wait`; `exits 1 with a structured grant-visibility block, no child, and a completed revoke`; `reads visibility through UserIdIndex, mirroring the auth path getUserById uses`; `reports the grant as not yet visible when the index still serves the old isAdmin`; `treats a missing row on the index as not visible rather than assuming the grant landed`.
- **AC4** (no product-code behavior change): no product file modified; module imports only `aws-sdk`, `axios`, node builtins — no product-runtime imports. Verified by grep: the only importer of this module is its own test.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/scripts/qa-fixture-harness.ts` (new, 724)
- `backend/src/__tests__/qa-fixture-harness.test.ts` (new, 861)

## What was NOT tested
- Live HTTP against a real domain (login/admin routes are mocked; step 5 above is the post-approval smoke).
- Live DynamoDB conditional updates (DocumentClient is faked at the structural seam; the CAS expressions are asserted, not executed).
- A real mid-flight `kill` of the process (signal handlers are unit-tested via the adapter seam; SIGKILL is explicitly out of contract).
- The `require.main` entrypoint block itself (its logic is fully exercised through `runCli`).
- QA-loop wiring (the QA runbook calling `preflight` each run) — rules-side change outside this repo, owned by the parent session.

## Linear issue

Accountable-Linear-ID: 142fef82-4d45-4070-99be-c5debe565ac6
Accountable-GitHub: harshmoney123
Execution-Actor: claude-code
Linear-Issue: ENG-739
