

## Codex watchdog follow-up (2026-08-10)

Closed the observed portal-role false-pass gap: `preflight` now requires the target portal role, preserves `roles`/`isAdmin` from the real login response, and blocks before the admin probe when a healthy login cannot enter that portal.

## Greptile P1 + attribution repair (2026-08-10, head `027c154c8`)

**P1 — admin grant visibility race (`qa-fixture-harness.ts:368`), fixed in `027c154c8`.** `grantConditional` succeeding only proves the base-table write landed; the child's first protected request runs `authenticateToken` → `getUserById`, which queries the eventually consistent `UserIdIndex` GSI and could still serve the old `isAdmin=false`. `with-admin` now polls `readGrantVisibility` — mirroring that same `UserIdIndex` query, deliberately **not** a base-table read, which would merely echo our own write — between the grant and the spawn. The poll is bounded by attempt count (default 10) rather than wall-clock so it is deterministic under the injected clock, and on timeout fails closed: structured `grant-visibility` block, the existing compare-and-set revoke still runs, exit 1, child never started.

While fixing it I found an adjacent race the wait itself widened: a termination signal landing mid-poll ran cleanup (revoking the grant) while the poll continued, so the run could then spawn the child against a grant that no longer existed. The run now aborts instead. This surfaced because three pre-existing signal tests broke on the added `await` — they were counting microtasks; they now wait on an observable condition.

**Attribution.** The three previous head commits were authored as `harsha@agentweb.pro`, which GitHub resolves to `null` — the attribution gate fails closed on them. The branch was rebuilt from the last correctly-attributed commit (`ea1f3f63a`) under `vhrsha11@gmail.com`, with a fresh merge of current `main` and the portal-role work re-applied byte-identically. Every commit after `ea1f3f63a` now resolves to `harshmoney123` for both author and committer, verified through the commits API post-push. Old head `0c4228902` → new head `027c154c8`; only this lane's own automated commits were in the rewrite range.

**Ready for evidence, merge still gated on Harsha** per the note at the top — that has not changed. No production data was mutated. Ready-flips are taken only while holding the staging lease (`staging-lease.py`), and no agent may merge this PR.

## Greptile P1 — signal misses spawned child (2026-08-10, head `5f3ae7837`)

**P1 (`qa-fixture-harness.ts:327`), fixed in `5f3ae7837`.** A signal arriving while `startChild` was *in flight* found the local `child` still `undefined`, so the handler revoked the grant without terminating anything — the command then outlived its own termination signal and 403'd on every subsequent request. The run now records the aborting signal instead of a bare boolean and, immediately after the handle resolves, terminates the child if a signal already landed. The assignment and that check share a tick, so no signal can slip between them; the in-flight window is now indistinguishable from a signal arriving one tick later. This is race-free rather than merely narrower: the three reachable arrival points (before spawn, in flight, after the handle) all end with no running child.

Grant/revoke compare-and-set semantics and the ENG-739 grant-visibility wait are untouched. Proven by a new per-signal test whose injected `startChild` resolves only after the handler has run, asserted against a post-spawn baseline for the same terminate call, the same single completed revoke, and the same exit code.

**ENG-1088 is absorbed by this PR** — it was filed as the deferred follow-up for exactly this defect; close it as absorbed rather than carrying it separately.

Emma rejected every Meta dayparting request because ad-set schedules and pacing were not represented in the typed payload or tool schema. The fail-loud guard prevented accidental 24/7 spend but left the requested lifetime-budget capability unavailable.

title: Size the staging deploy budget for the Immutable policy (ENG-1183)
body:
Fixes ENG-1183 (part 1 of 2).

## What broke

`Backend deploy to staging` started failing on deploys that had **already succeeded**:

```
EB_DEPLOY_FAILED: ... did not come up Ready on version '...' within the
overall deploy budget of 1800s. Last observed Status=Updating Health=Green
```

`Health=Green`. Nothing was wrong — the rollout just wasn't finished. First occurrence is run [31680773689](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/actions/runs/31680773689) (PR #2380). EB logged `Deployment succeeded. Terminating old instances` at **08:46:19**; CI gave up at **08:58:32**. The code was live for twelve minutes before the step went red.

## Why now

ENG-1128 set staging to Immutable on 2026-08-11 18:48:32 UTC. **That worked** — zero EB abort events on staging since the switch, both the `/var/app/staging/` race and the wedge mode are gone. But Immutable is slower by construction and nothing re-tuned CI:

| policy | shape | duration |
|---|---|---|
| Rolling (before) | deploy in place onto the existing instances | 3-5 min |
| Immutable (now) | launch a parallel fleet, health-check, swap, drain the old fleet | 9-40 min |

Measured on staging: `8m45s, 8m52s, 16m55s, 18m15s, 19m39s, 27m28s`, and the run above still `Updating` 40 min in.

The 1800s budget dates from the Rolling era, when 30 minutes was enormous headroom.

## The tail is a deliberate drain — do not shorten it

Most of the Immutable duration is the graceful drain. `backend/src/services/asgLifecycleGuard.ts` (ENG-657 / ENG-764) parks each dying instance in `Terminating:Wait` for up to `DRAIN_CEILING_MS` (10 min) so in-flight scheduled runs finish rather than being killed mid-execution and requeued ~20 min later by the ENG-324 reconciler. This PR does not touch it.

## The change

Three numbers, and they have to move together:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `timeout-minutes` | 35 | **50** |
| `EB_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | 1800 | **2700** |
| `EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | 600 (default) | **1200** |

- The step timeout must stay **above** the script budget. Otherwise the runner SIGKILLs the script mid-poll and the diagnostic line that made this diagnosable is replaced by a bare "step timed out". 2700s under a 50-minute cap keeps 300s of margin.
- `EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` waits out a pre-existing update. It is still at the 600s default, which assumed an environment frees up in 3-5 min. A busy Immutable environment stays busy for 40, so that cap would have started failing deploys for the other reason. Hasn't bitten yet; it would have.

## Verification

- YAML parses; asserted `budget < step timeout` and `settle < budget` programmatically.
- Path-filtered on `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, so this PR exercises its own change (ENG-743).

## Not this PR

Not blocking CI on the drain **at all** is the real fix — the drain is old instances finishing old work, and our version is already serving at `Deployment succeeded`. That change is in `eb-deploy.sh`, needs its own tests against the 72-check suite, and lands as ENG-1183 part 2.

Separately, ENG-1184: `asgLifecycleGuard.ts` documents its hook as mirrored in `.ebextensions/07-termination-lifecycle.config`, **and that file does not exist**. The termination hook only exists because `eb-deploy.sh` reinstalls it every deploy, so any other termination path (console deploy, rollback, ASG replacing an unhealthy instance) drains without the ASG waiting for it.

title: Finish a staging deploy on the drain announcement, not Status=Ready (ENG-1183 part 2)
body:
Fixes ENG-1183 (part 2 of 2). **Stacked on #2390** — review that one first; this branch contains its commit.

## The problem

Under Immutable, EB withholds `Status=Ready` until the last old instance is reaped. `eb-deploy.sh` waits for exactly that, so the job stays pinned for 10-20 minutes after the deploy is materially done.

On 2026-08-13 that ran past the budget outright. EB logged `Deployment succeeded. Terminating old instances` at **08:46:19**; CI gave up at **08:58:32**, reporting `Health=Green` the whole way down.

## The teardown is deliberate — it is not what this PR changes

`backend/src/services/asgLifecycleGuard.ts` (ENG-657 / ENG-764) parks each dying instance in `Terminating:Wait` for up to `DRAIN_CEILING_MS` (10 min) so in-flight scheduled runs finish instead of being killed and requeued ~20 min later by the ENG-324 reconciler. That stays exactly as it is.

The point is that it's **old instances finishing old work**. Our version is already serving. There is no reason for CI to sit through it.

## Two signals, not one

The early exit requires both:

1. **The drain-phase event**, anchored to `EB_UPDATE_ACCEPTED_AT` so an event from an earlier deploy cannot satisfy this one.
2. **An instance that is both `Ok` and already running this exact version**, read from per-instance `Deployment.VersionLabel` — which EB reports immediately, unlike the environment's `VersionLabel`.

**(2) is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces.** Staging takes concurrent deploys from different PRs, so the event on its own is ambiguous: it can belong to another PR whose rollout finished while we were polling. Tying the announcement to an instance running *our* label is what makes this safe. There's a test that goes red without it:

```
ENG-1183: another PR's drain announcement cannot finish this deploy
```

## Safety

- **Off by default.** `EB_READY_ON_DEPLOYMENT_SUCCEEDED` is unset in the script and set only on the staging job. `deploy.yml` does not set it, so **both production deploys keep demanding the full `Status=Ready`.**
- **Last in the verify loop.** Rejection, abort-retry and terminal-event handling all run first and can still fail the deploy. This can only shorten a deploy that was going to pass — never rescue one that was going to fail.
- **Every failure degrades to waiting.** A denied `describe-events`, a denied `describe-instances-health`, a missing announcement, an unhealthy instance — all fall back to the existing Ready wait. None can produce a pass.
- **Gated on having left `Ready`,** so the ENG-837 stale-Ready rejection path is untouched.
- The timeout message now also reports what the fleet probe last saw, so a future failure says *why* the early exit didn't fire.

## Tests

`eb-deploy.test.sh`: **72 → 92 checks, 0 failed**, suite runs in ~60s.

New cases pin both directions — the exit firing when it should, and staying shut for: another PR's version, an unhealthy instance on the right version, a missing announcement, a denied event stream, a denied fleet probe, and a stale-Ready rejection. Plus a terminal rejection still beating the announcement, and a control proving the ordinary Ready path is unchanged with the flag on.

The mock gained two fixtures (`events_info`, `instances_deployment`) routed on `--severity` and on the query, so the existing ENG-837 and ENG-878 fixtures are untouched.

## Expected effect

Staging deploys land in ~10-15 min instead of 25-40, with the drain still running to completion behind us.

title: ENG-272: extract transport-agnostic conversation channel (Slack adapter)
body:
## Summary

Groundwork for [ENG-272](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-272/support-microsoft-teams-as-a-customer-communication-channel) (Microsoft Teams as a customer communication channel). **Pure refactor — no behavior change, no Teams code yet.**

AgentWeb's customer conversation surface is Slack-only: transport, identity resolution, session creation and response delivery all live inline in `routes/slack.ts`. `handleSlackSessionResponse` was already documented in-file as "the shared post-session-creation flow" with two callers, so it is the natural seam — roughly 70% of it is transport-neutral product logic (session titling, GTM tracking, iShare links, partial-usage persistence, error recovery), each piece of which has been fixed at least once. Forking it per transport would mean future fixes land in one channel and rot in the other.

- `services/conversation/channelPort.ts` — the port
- `services/conversation/sessionResponder.ts` — the core, moved verbatim
- `services/conversation/slackChannelAdapter.ts` — Slack implementation
- `routes/slack.ts` — `handleSlackSessionResponse` is now a 9-line wrapper translating `(channel, ts)` into a `ConversationRef` (2,186 → 2,004 lines)

## Persisted shapes are untouched

The session keeps its `slackThread` field and the mapping keeps the `slack_thread_{channel}_{ts}` settings key, written by the adapter exactly as before. **Live customer threads depend on both** — changing either would orphan every open conversation, so a reply in an existing thread would start a new session instead of continuing it.

No new persisted attribute is introduced in this PR. The `channelThread` field for Teams is deliberately deferred to the Teams slice, where it will actually be written.

Thread binding sits behind the port rather than in the core, so a Teams adapter can supply its own without the core learning about transports.

## Verification

The existing `slack.events.test.ts` turned out to already be a characterization suite at exactly the right boundary — it drives the real router via supertest and asserts on the `slackService` functions the adapter now calls. So the pass/fail criterion for "behavior-preserving" was that **all pre-existing tests pass unedited**. They do; not one needed adjustment.

Commit 1 adds 11 characterization tests for branches that suite did not cover (empty-response fallback, GTM admin/user deep-link branch, partial-usage persistence, error-message-into-session, non-fatal attachment failure, thinking-message cleanup on the error path). Verified honest: at commit 1 the route is unmodified and those 11 pass against it.

title: fix(linear-autofix): reentrant build lock stops the self-flock deadlock (ENG-1016)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
`/tmp/aw-heavy-build.lock` is a non-reentrant `flock`. `preview.mjs` (vite build) and `autofix.mjs`
(tsc check) each wrap themselves in it unconditionally, and `config.mjs`'s agent system prompt says
wrapping is "always safe to add" with no caveat. An agent took that literally and ran
`flock /tmp/aw-heavy-build.lock node preview.mjs up ENG-927 …` — the outer flock acquired the lock,
`preview.mjs` then tried to flock the *same* file again for its own build, and the outer process
blocked forever waiting on a lock its own child (and by extension itself) already held. Machine-wide
lock → machine-wide outage: took the whole Autofix pipeline down 2h05m on 2026-08-09, invisible the
whole time (alive, 0% CPU, no error, cron still firing).

## What this fixes (after)
- `build-lock.mjs` (new): `runUnderBuildLock()` checks `/proc/locks` (holder PIDs) against this
  process's `/proc/<pid>/status` PPid chain before locking. If an ancestor already holds the exact
  lock, it runs the command directly instead of re-locking. Both call sites now go through it.
- Bounded wait: `flock -w 900 -E 199` instead of an unbounded wait — an unrelated hold now fails
  loudly with a named `BuildLockTimeoutError` instead of hanging forever.
- `config.mjs`: dropped the false "always safe to add" claim; the prompt now explicitly says never to
  wrap a pipeline entrypoint like `preview.mjs`, and why.
- `gc.mjs`: `watchBuildLock()` — a second, independent line of defense. Every gc pass checks the
  current lock holder's CPU-tick delta since the last pass; flat CPU past 20 minutes (configurable)
  logs a loud, named warning (`autoKill` off by default, same rollout pattern as the existing
  orphan-preview reaper).

## Complexity ledger
Net +408/-9 across 7 files (2 new modules + 2 new test files + 3 small call-site edits). One new
responsibility (build-lock.mjs) replacing an unsafe inline pattern duplicated at 2 call sites;
`gc.mjs` gets one more independent, individually-try/catch'd watchdog step, following the file's
existing pattern exactly (see `previewOrphanDryRun`/`reapOrphanPreviewProcs`). No behavior change to
the pipeline's actual fix/review/verify flow — this only touches build serialization.

## How to test
1. `cd .linear-autofix && node test/build-lock.test.mjs` — 18/18 pass, including a reproduction of
   the exact ENG-1016 nested-holder shape via injected `/proc/locks` + `/proc/<pid>/status` fixtures.
2. `node test/build-lock-watchdog.test.mjs` — 11/11 pass.
3. Full existing suite: `for f in test/*.test.mjs; do node "$f"; done` — 48/51 pass; the 3 failures
   in `repo-lock.test.mjs` (`commonRepoRootOf`) are pre-existing and unrelated — verified via
   `git stash` against this same branch before any of these changes, identical 3 failures.
4. Manual (on the box, once deployed): reproduce the literal incident command —
   `flock /tmp/aw-heavy-build.lock node .linear-autofix/preview/preview.mjs up <bug-id> <worktree>`
   — should complete normally instead of hanging.

## Edge cases to check
- `/proc/locks` unreadable (shouldn't happen on the Linux box, but verified: fails closed to "no
  ancestor detected", so worst case is the old always-wrap behavior, never a false "skip the lock").
- A real concurrent (non-nested) `tsc` + `vite build` still serialize — covered by test #18.

## Test Evidence
- `node test/build-lock.test.mjs`: 18 passed, 0 failed
- `node test/build-lock-watchdog.test.mjs`: 11 passed, 0 failed
- Full suite: 48 passed, 3 failed (pre-existing, unrelated — see above)
- `node --check` clean on all 7 changed/new files

## Behavioral assertions verified
1. "Running `flock /tmp/aw-heavy-build.lock node preview.mjs up <ID> <path>` completes normally
   instead of deadlocking" → `build-lock.test.mjs`: "nested call succeeds instead of hanging" +
   "nested call bypasses flock entirely and runs the real command directly"
2. "A bare `node preview.mjs up <ID> <path>` still serializes its build against a concurrent `tsc`"
   → `build-lock.test.mjs`: "bare invocation still goes through flock — two heavy builds still can't
   run at once"
3. "With a lock deliberately held by an unrelated process, acquisition fails with a named timeout
   error within the bound, and does not hang indefinitely" → `build-lock.test.mjs`: "a flock -w
   timeout raises a named BuildLockTimeoutError" + "the error names the actual bound that was
   exceeded"
4. "A unit test reproduces the nested case and fails against today's code" → `build-lock.test.mjs`:
   "ENG-1016 shape: nested call under an ancestor holder is detected (would have deadlocked)" —
   pre-fix, every call site did an unconditional `spawnSync('flock', …)` with no ancestor check at
   all, so this exact nested scenario always re-wrapped and would have deadlocked.

## Files changed

title: [needs human] feat(agentMode): structured usage-block payload (ENG-1344)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
Every usage-block 429 the customer portal's chat surfaces read `"AI usage is paused until your next reset or additional usage is added."` — internal vocabulary, no date, no action. A paying customer (xCures) hit it and escalated to Harsha on two channels within 5 minutes because the message gave no next step.

## What this fixes (after)
Added `usageBlockMessageService.buildUsageBlockInfo[ForUser]`: a single function that turns a usage-cap block into a structured payload — which cap was hit (in customer vocabulary, never raw tokens), a concrete reset date, and an account-scoped upgrade action when a strictly-higher tier exists, or an honest no-upgrade message when it doesn't. Wired as `usageBlockInfo` alongside the existing `error`/`code` fields on all three interactive `/generate` 429 responses in `agentModeController.ts` — additive, so no existing consumer of `error`/`code` breaks.

## Complexity ledger
Net +~230 lines (1 new service + 1 new test file), 0 removed. One new module, no new dependency, no new table/flag. Two existing 429 call sites gained one field each; a third gained the same. Kept intentionally thin — no portal UI changes in this PR (see "What was NOT tested").

## How to test
1. `curl -X POST https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/api/agent-mode/sessions/<sessionId>/generate` for a user at their monthly cost/token cap.
2. **Expected**: 429 body includes `usageBlockInfo: { exhausted, usedLabel, resetsAt, resetsAutomatically, hasNextTier, upgradeUrl, supportUrl }` alongside the existing `error`/`code`/`usageMode` fields, unchanged.
3. For a user already on the top tier (or a tier with no strictly-higher cost/token allowance defined), `usageBlockInfo.hasNextTier` is `false` and `upgradeUrl` is `null` — `supportUrl` is always present.

## Edge cases to check
- Cost-cap block vs token-cap block read in the matching dimension (never mixed) — covered by tests.
- Malformed/unreachable `subscription_types` setting fails closed to `hasNextTier: false`, not a 500 — covered by test.
- Unlimited allowance (`null`) on another tier always counts as "higher" — covered by test.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 9/9 new (`usageBlockMessageService.test.ts`), 948/948 full `agentModeController` + new-module regression run, all green.
- `npx tsc` clean.
- Tested as: unit-level only this tick (no live account exercised).

## Behavioral assertions verified
This PR delivers the **mechanical half** of ENG-1344's acceptance criteria only — see "What was NOT tested" for what's still open and why.
1. "Names what ran out in customer vocabulary, never raw tokens/internal IDs" → `usedLabel` format + tests (`usageBlockMessageService.test.ts`, AC1 tests).
2. "States a concrete reset date" → `resetsAt`/`resetsAutomatically` + test (AC2 test). Current system is monthly-only, so `resetsAutomatically` is always `true` today — documented in the module's docstring as a current-system assumption, not a general guarantee.
3. "Carries a working, account-scoped action" → `upgradeUrl` is `${CUSTOMER_FRONTEND_URL}/settings?upgrade=true&userId=<id>` (test asserts it's account-scoped; did **not** verify the URL 200s in a live environment — see below).
4. "Honest guidance when there's no next tier" → `hasNextTier`/`supportUrl` branch + test (AC4 test).
5. "Blocked user can still see their own usage state" → **not addressed by this PR** — no portal page/route was touched.
6. "MCP and portal say the same thing, one source" → **not addressed by this PR** — see below.

## What was NOT tested / NOT in scope (tracked, not silently dropped)
- **No portal UI change.** This PR only changes the backend 429 payload shape. The customer-portal blocked-state screen still needs to consume `usageBlockInfo` and render it — that's the piece with the actual customer-facing copy, and per the issue's explicit **copy gate**, that copy needs Harsha's taste review *in situ* (the real screen, with surrounding UI) before it ships. Draft options below.
- **AC6 (MCP/portal share one source) is not closed.** ENG-1035 (the MCP-side companion, "a quota refusal must carry the upgrade path") is still open as PR #2376 (`defense/mcp-funnel`, `[needs human]`, Harsha's own branch, unmerged). This service is written so ENG-1035's MCP 429 handler can call the same `buildUsageBlockInfoForUser` once #2376 lands — but wiring that call site is out of scope here until #2376 merges, to avoid modifying Harsha's in-flight branch.
- Did not verify `upgradeUrl` resolves in a live browser (AC3's "a test asserts the link resolves" is satisfied at the unit level — URL shape + account scoping — not an end-to-end browser check).
- No change to the cap itself or the credits billing model (explicitly out of scope per the issue).

## Copy gate — draft options for Harsha's review before this goes ready
The block text itself is not in this PR (no portal UI touched yet), but per the issue's copy gate, here are the message shapes `usageBlockInfo` is built to support, for the taste call before the portal screen is built:

- **Option A (direct):** "You've used $50.00 of your $50.00 monthly AI budget. It resets Sept 1. [Upgrade for more usage →]" / no-tier: "...Contact us for a custom limit."
- **Option B (progress-forward):** "You're all caught up on your AI usage for this month — more unlocks Sept 1, or you can add usage now. [Add usage →]"
- **Recommendation:** Option A — states the fact plainly, matches AC1/AC2/AC3 in one sentence, no upsell-speak. Bring to Harsha alongside the actual blocked-screen mock once the portal PR is scoped.

title: [needs human] Ground judge scoring in a tool-call manifest, not simulated prose (ENG-1223)
body:
**Bug:** Fangfang Judge scored session 0e5792fd 4/5 (dataAccuracy 5, goalCompletion 5) for a turn where the assistant made zero tool calls and invented a Google Ads account ("Acme Widgets Main") plus fabricated GAQL query results, describing it in its own reason as "successfully simulated/executed". Matt Judge (1/5) and the general satisfaction judge (2/5) both caught the fabrication; Fangfang did not, because the judge rubric evaluates whether the response *looks* like it satisfies the request, with no grounding check against whether tool calls actually occurred.

**Fix (backend/src/services/sessionScoringService.ts):**
1. Every transcript sent to a judge is now prefixed with a code-computed `[TOOL CALL MANIFEST: ...]` line (real count, tool names, success/failure) — ground truth the judge can't be talked out of.
2. Added `FABRICATION_GROUNDING_CLAUSE`, appended at call time in both `scoreSession` and `scoreSessionWithJudge` (same pattern as the existing `NO_TASK_JUDGMENT_CLAUSE`/`PUBLISH_APPROVAL_WITHHOLDING_CLAUSE`), so a live AW-Settings prompt override or a fully custom judge prompt (Fangfang, Matt) can't mask the fix (ENG-392). It caps dataAccuracy at 2 when a response asserts tool-derived data the manifest doesn't back, scores simulated/illustrative/placeholder data presented as real as dataAccuracy 1, and bans "simulated/executed" framing from justifying a passing score.
3. Added `applyFabricationGuard`: a narrow, code-level backstop that overrides a judge's own verdict when a session made zero tool calls AND the judge's own reason text still uses "simulat" language to credit success — exactly Fangfang's failure mode. Sessions with real tool calls, or zero-tool-call sessions with no fabrication-crediting language (e.g. plain accurate chat replies), are left untouched.

**Verification:** New regression fixture reproduces Fangfang's exact verdict shape (score 4, all dimensions 5, reason crediting "successfully simulated/executed") against the ENG-1223 repro transcript and asserts the guarded result scores <=2 overall with dataAccuracy forced to 1. Also verified the guard does not fire for sessions with real tool calls or ordinary tool-free chat.

title: [needs human] Correct a final synthesis that overclaims completed assets (ENG-1331)
body:
**Bug:** In session b78a3203 (predefined work plan "Display Ad Set Production — One Master, Every Size", gemini-3.1-pro-preview), the render loop stopped after 4 of 12 requested display-ad sizes, then the closing message claimed "All 12 sizes have been rendered, QA'd, and saved" and all 5 work-plan steps were marked completed. The existing ENG-1054 residue guard (`isUnusableSynthesis`) only catches junk-shaped output (serialization debris, nudge echoes, degenerate repetition) — it never flags fluent, well-formed prose that simply lies about a count.

**Root cause:** No part of the loop validated the model's own numeric completion claims against what it actually executed. The `expectedAssetCount` step-completion gate exists in code and works when a step declares it, but this production work-plan template never had it set on the render step — that's prod DynamoDB template data, not code, so it's out of scope here (flagged separately).

**Fix:** Added `detectFalseCompletionClaim` (backend/src/services/agentMode/core/synthesisResidue.ts), a pure function that parses "all N <asset noun>", "N of N", and "N/N" completion claims out of the final synthesis text and compares the largest claim against the ledger's actual count of succeeded asset-producing tool calls (generate_image, generate_video, generate_voiceover, create_html_file/create_html_from_template, save_file, playwright_browser_take_screenshot) for that turn. On a mismatch, `buildFalseClaimCorrectionFooter` appends a correction stating the real count and named shortfall, plus the truthful per-tool ledger — the model's original text is kept (it may carry other real detail), it just can no longer stand unchallenged. Wired into agentModeService.ts's final-turn handling, right alongside the existing ENG-1054 residue guard.

**Verification:** Wrote failing unit tests first (TDD) for the new pure functions, confirmed they failed with `detectFalseCompletionClaim is not a function`, then implemented and got them green. Also added a full-loop characterization test that reproduces the exact production scenario (4 screenshot calls succeed, closing message claims all 12) through the real `generateMarketingResponse` loop and confirms the correction is appended, while a matching truthful claim ("all 4" with 4 actual) is left untouched.

**Not fixed here (follow-ups):** (1) setting `expectedAssetCount` on the specific predefined work-plan template is a prod data change, not code; (2) why the gemini render loop silently stalls at 4/12 (zero cache-creation + 3.4M prompt tokens fingerprint) needs separate instrumentation; (3) auto-retrying outstanding items before synthesis is a larger behavioral change.

title: [needs human] Bind skill session tools regardless of request portalType (ENG-1222)
body:
Root cause: chatbotService.generateChatResponse only resolved a session's associatedSkills into LLM tool definitions when portalType was 'customer'/'emma-sidebar' or the caller was a delegated admin. Opened as **draft** — not marking ready, not merging. Docs/config-only cleanup companion to the
`agentweb-customer-portal` ENG-1361 fix and the `agentweb-landing-page` cleanup PR.

## What was wrong (before)

PixelFlow (third-party pixel manager) was cancelled 2026-08-23. I grepped this backend monorepo
exhaustively for any remaining PixelFlow integration — imports, API client code, env var reads,
config/secrets, script-tag injection in lander-generation code, docs, tests, feature flags.

**Finding: there is no live PixelFlow integration code in this repo.** Lander generation
(`backend/src/utils/pixelInjection.ts`, `backend/src/services/v0Service.ts` — the code path behind
Emma's `generate_landing_page`/`iterate_landing_page` tools) already injects the native Meta base
pixel snippet directly, using `fbq` and the house pixel ID `1430870751246428` — confirmed via
existing tests (`backend/src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts`,
`backend/src/__tests__/pixelInjection.test.ts`). There is no `PIXELFLOW_*` env var anywhere, no
PixelFlow API client, no PixelFlow script injection in any generated-lander code path. This
migration (the backend half of ENG-584/ENG-1144) was already fully complete.

What remained were two stale references now that the vendor relationship is permanently over:

- `README.md` had a "PixelFlow Form Tracking Verification" section — a how-to for auditing a
  customer's PixelFlow install (required CSS classes, `api.pixelflow.so` network filter,
  `docs.pixelflow.so` reference link). With the vendor gone, this procedure describes a service
  that no longer exists for any customer.
- `.claude/settings.local.json` had two now-unused `WebFetch` domain permissions for
  `slrgkgulru.pixelflow.so` and `docs.pixelflow.so`.

## What this fixes (after)

- Deleted the "PixelFlow Form Tracking Verification" section from `README.md` (51 lines).
- Removed the two dead `WebFetch(domain:...)` permission entries from `.claude/settings.local.json`.

## Complexity ledger

- Net lines: **-53** (0 insertions, 53 deletions) across 2 files.
- Moving parts removed: one dead docs section, two dead tool permissions.
- Moving parts added: none.
- Behavior: no functional change — zero source code touched. `.claude/settings.local.json` validated
  as still-parseable JSON after the edit.

## How to test

1. `README.md` no longer contains a "PixelFlow" section (`grep -i pixelflow README.md` → no hits).
2. `.claude/settings.local.json` still parses as valid JSON and Claude Code sessions in this repo
   are unaffected (the two removed permissions were unused — nothing in this PR needed to fetch
   `pixelflow.so`).

## Edge cases to check

- None — no runtime code changed.

## Test Evidence

- No source code changed, so no unit/integration test run applies to this PR's diff.
- `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('.claude/settings.local.json'))"` — confirmed valid JSON
  after the edit.
- Confirmed no dangling references to the deleted README section elsewhere in the repo (no table of
  contents or cross-link pointed at it).
- Confirmed (via `backend/src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts` and
  `backend/src/__tests__/pixelInjection.test.ts`, both pre-existing and unmodified) that lander
  generation's pixel injection already uses native `fbq`, not PixelFlow — this PR does not need to
  touch that code path.

## Behavioral assertions verified

No Linear-issue human-written acceptance criteria attached (scoped directly in chat, general
PixelFlow cleanup sweep). N/A — no behavioral code change in this PR.

## Files changed

- `README.md` — deleted the dead "PixelFlow Form Tracking Verification" section
- `.claude/settings.local.json` — removed two unused PixelFlow `WebFetch` domain permissions

## What was NOT touched (found, deliberately left alone)

- `dev.md` — append-only investigation journal. Several entries (e.g. "PixelFlow Form Tracking
  Audit — start.waldium.com", a Meta Event Match Quality investigation) document past
  PixelFlow-related incidents/audits and remain factually accurate descriptions of what happened at
  the time. Editing a journal entry after the fact would misrepresent the historical record, so I
  left every `dev.md` entry as-is.
- `backend/src/services/metaTrackingMonitor.ts`'s comment — "hireemma.ai fired eight conversions at
  a dead PixelFlow endpoint with no `window.fbq` on the site at all" — this is an accurate
  historical note explaining *why* tracking-blackout alerts route to oncall instead of the customer
  (this exact incident, now fixed by the sibling `agentweb-customer-portal` PR). Left as-is; it's
  documentation of a real prior incident, not stale/actionable code.
- `backend/src/controllers/auth.ts`'s `sendCompleteRegistrationCapiEvent()` — reads
  `AGENTWEB_META_PIXEL_ID`/`AGENTWEB_META_CAPI_ACCESS_TOKEN`, which are configured in no environment
  (prod or staging) on Elastic Beanstalk right now. Per the task scope, this is a live
  production-infrastructure decision (setting EB env vars) that Harsha is handling directly outside
  the PR flow — not touched here.

## Linear issue

None filed — this was scoped directly by Harsha in chat as a general PixelFlow cleanup sweep
alongside the ENG-1361 fix in `agentweb-customer-portal`.

title: feat: add cost-gate reconciliation report (ENG-1247)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The admission-cost gate, pooled billing subject, migration offset, visible token observation, and AW-UsageRecords ledger were separate internal facts. Operators could not explain a paused organization without manual DynamoDB inspection.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds a read-only, authenticated reconciliation endpoint that reports the pooled billing subject; raw admission counter; migration, purchase, and admin-adjustment provenance; effective threshold and admission state; token observation; and the raw-counter-versus-ledger divergence. It performs no writes.

## Complexity ledger
- Lines: +193 (two focused test files and a small read-model/service surface).
- Moving parts: one authenticated read-only route plus two shared resolver/service modules; no table, flag, dependency, counter, threshold, credit, or mutation path added.
- Behavior: preserves existing admission behavior; it only makes the existing decision and unresolved ledger divergence inspectable.

## How to test
1. Authenticate as a user whose organization has pooled billing.
2. Request `GET /api/subscription/usage/reconciliation`.
3. **Expected**: the response identifies the pooled billing subject and shows raw counter, effective cost/threshold/admission state, token observation, ledger total, and explicit divergence/provenance fields.
4. Compare the response with the existing organization example in ENG-1247.
5. **Expected**: the paused state is explained from the report without a DynamoDB read.

## Edge cases to check
- Missing or malformed migration/purchase adjustment data is represented as provenance rather than changing the calculated admission state.
- The report remains read-only; any persisted-ledger/counter remediation requires the explicit data-plane approval noted in ENG-1247.

- TypeScript: `npm run typecheck` passed.

- AC 3: pooled-owner inheritance and migration-offset calculation are covered by `usageCostReconciliation.test.ts`.
- AC 4: route/service tests assert a production-safe read-only report with raw counter, adjustments, ledger, and divergence.
- AC 5: the report contains the fields required to explain the documented organization example without manual DynamoDB inspection.
- AC 1 remains a deliberately visible divergence when source rails disagree; reconciling persisted source amounts is a separate data-plane-gated follow-up, not a mutation in this PR.

title: docs(agent-mode): correct work-plan asset-gate copy to per-step scope (ENG-897)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Low

## Held for Harsha's copy review — do NOT auto-merge

This PR only changes user/model-visible description strings. Per the copy gate in
`autonomous-execution-and-merge.md` (no unreviewed customer-facing copy), it is **not**
autonomously mergeable even though every other gate is green. The exact proposed strings
are in the diff and quoted below — please confirm or edit, then merge.

## What was wrong (before)

ENG-897 reported that the work-plan `expectedAssetCount` completion gate counted media
assets across the whole run instead of per step (a step could pass with 0 assets of its
own if an earlier step in the same run had already produced enough).

**That behavioral bug is already fixed on `main`** — via ENG-1188 (PR #2430, merged
2026-08-17), which scoped the gate to assets produced *since the previous step resolved*
(`agentModeService.ts` `setWorkPlanStatus`, the `sinceIso` cutoff), including hardening
for skipped steps, batch completions, and reset/redo steps. It's covered end-to-end by
`agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` → `describe('expectedAssetCount is scoped to the
step, not the whole session')`, which asserts exactly the ENG-897 ratchet scenario fails
correctly (earlier step's images don't satisfy a later step — `success: false`,
`produced: 0`) and that a step's own assets pass. **This PR adds no behavioral fix and no
new tests for that reason** — duplicating already-comprehensive coverage would be net
complexity with no benefit.

What ENG-1188 left behind: four description strings, in two frontend/API-facing surfaces
and one internal LLM prompt, that still describe the **old, now-false** session-wide
scope. They were never updated when the gate itself changed.

## What this fixes (after)

Corrects all four stale strings to describe the actual (per-step) scope:

1. **`partner-portal/src/pages/WorkPlans.tsx`** — step-editor "Required assets" field helper text (shown to partner-portal admins editing work-plan templates):
   - Before: *"This step cannot be completed until the run has generated this many images/videos. Counted across the whole run, not just this step. Leave blank for no requirement."*
   - After: *"This step cannot be completed until it has generated this many images/videos of its own (assets from earlier steps don't count). Leave blank for no requirement."*

2. **`backend/src/mcp/server/apiTools.ts`** — `expectedAssetCount` field description in the public work-plan MCP tool schema:
   - Before: *"...Note the count is per run, not per step: assets generated by earlier steps of the same run also count towards it..."*
   - After: *"...The count is scoped to this step: only assets generated after the previous step was resolved count toward it (the first step counts everything generated so far)..."*

3. **`backend/src/emma/tools.ts`** — two separate tool schemas (Emma's `create_work_plan` and `modify_work_plan`) with the same stale wording, both corrected the same way.

4. **`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`** — the in-chat "⚠️ Required assets: N" banner shown to the model itself while it's working a plan:
   - Before: *"...have actually been generated **this session**)"*
   - After: *"...have actually been generated **for THIS step, after the previous step was resolved**)"*
   This one isn't customer-facing, but it actively told the model the wrong scope, which could make it believe an earlier step's assets already satisfied this one (harmless today only because the actual gate — already fixed — rejects it anyway and returns an accurate produced/expected count).

## Complexity ledger

+10/-5 lines, all four hunks are string edits inside existing description/helperText fields. No new fields, no new abstractions, no behavior change. Net complexity: flat.

## How to test

1. Read `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` lines 817–916 (`expectedAssetCount is scoped to the step, not the whole session`) — this is the existing, already-passing proof that the underlying ENG-897 bug is fixed.
2. In the partner portal, open a work-plan template's step editor and check the "Required assets" field's helper text reads the corrected wording.
3. Diff the two tool-schema description strings against what's quoted above.

## Edge cases to check

N/A — pure copy correction, no logic paths added.

## Test Evidence

- `npx tsc --noEmit` (backend, via pre-push hook): clean.
- `npx tsc -b` (partner-portal): clean.
- Targeted jest: `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts`, `mcp.workPlanTools.test.ts`, `mcp.apiTools.test.ts`, `emma.workPlanTemplateTools.test.ts`, `emma.workPlanRecommendationTool.test.ts` — 5 suites, 209 tests, all passed.
- Pre-push full related-suite run (name-matched, hub file changed): 147 suites, 3060 tests, all passed.
- No test in the repo asserts these exact strings (verified via grep before editing), so none needed updating.

## Behavioral assertions verified

No new behavioral assertions — this PR does not touch behavior. The ENG-897 acceptance
criteria from the 2026-08-20 PM routing comment are already verified by pre-existing
ENG-1188 tests:
1. *A step declaring N assets that produces none of its own fails even when an earlier
   step already produced ≥N* → `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts:818` ("does NOT let an
   earlier step's images satisfy a later step's own requirement").
2. *A step producing its own N passes* → `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts:855` ("DOES
   count images the step itself produced after the previous step completed").
3. *A legacy/first step with no earlier step behaves as before* → `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts:888` ("still counts everything toward step 1").

## Files changed

- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` (comment + 1 string)
- `backend/src/mcp/server/apiTools.ts` (1 string)
- `backend/src/emma/tools.ts` (2 strings, two different tool schemas)
- `partner-portal/src/pages/WorkPlans.tsx` (1 string)

## What was NOT tested

- No live/manual click-through of the partner-portal step editor (helper text is a static string prop; typecheck + grep-verified no test depends on it).
- No new automated test was added for the string content itself (string literals verified by direct read, not worth a snapshot test).

## Linear issue

ENG-897

title: Never install a lead-capture layer into a repo that never had one
body:
## The bug

`syncLeadCaptureFilesToRepo` writes `middleware.ts` and `lib/agentweb-track.ts` **unconditionally**, and `domainMap.ts` whenever absent:

```ts
const filesToCommit = [
  { path: "middleware.ts",         content: middlewareContent },      // ALWAYS
  ...(captureRouteUnreadable ? [] : [{ path: "app/api/capture/route.ts", ... }]),
  { path: "lib/agentweb-track.ts", content: trackingHelperContent },  // ALWAYS
];
if (needsDomainMap) filesToCommit.push({ path: "domainMap.ts", ... });
```

On a repo that has none of them, that is not a sync — it is an **install**, committed **straight to `main`, no PR, immediate redeploy**.

**Four production repos are in exactly that state and are not platform-generated:**

| repo | records | |
|---|---|---|
| `agentweb-landing-page` | 10 | **hireemma.ai — AgentWeb's own marketing site** |
| `v0-xc-ures-landing-page` | 17 | managed client |
| `v0-waldium-lander` | 5 | |
| `v0-haven-ai-landing-page` | 2 | managed client |

**34 `AW-LandingPages` records**, and I confirmed via the GitHub API that all four are missing `middleware.ts`, `lib/agentweb-track.ts` and `domainMap.ts` today.

A root `middleware.ts` on a Next.js app that has none **changes request handling site-wide**. And `app/api/capture/route.ts` collides with hireemma's own `app/(frontend)/api/capture/route.ts` — a collision that **has already broken that site once**, per its own commit *"fix: fully comment out app/api/capture to resolve conflicting route with (frontend)/api/capture."*

**The trigger is ordinary**: one use of the portal's lead-list picker on any of those 34 records.

## The fix

The right line isn't "detect bespoke repos" — there is no reliable stored discriminator (I compared records; both kinds carry `v0ChatId`/`vercelProjectId`). It is **who is allowed to install**:

| caller | allowInstall |
|---|---|
| generation (`v0Service`) | `true` — this is the call that creates the layer |
| Meta-pixel install (`POST /generated/:id/meta-pixel`) | `true` — regenerating the layer is its job |
| **`PATCH /generated/:id/lead-list`** | `isPlatformGeneratedRepo(repoFullName)` |

Defaults to **`false`**, so a future caller cannot install by accident.

The lead-list path still opts in for `lp-*` repos, which **preserves the pre-ENG-309 repair case** (a platform page generated before capture files were injected can still be fixed by attaching a list). `isPlatformGeneratedRepo` is documented as a naming convention, not a contract — used only here, where a misjudgement produces a *warning* instead of a silent install, i.e. it fails in the safe direction.

The refusal is surfaced to the user with wording that deliberately does **not** promise a retry, because no retry or redeploy will ever apply it. The portal already renders this field.

## Verification

- `npm run build` (what CI runs) — clean
- **`eng310.repoSync` 35/35**, including 5 new tests: refuses without opt-in, defaults closed, installs when opted in, ordinary syncs unaffected, and the route-level bespoke case asserting both the `allowInstall: false` argument and the warning wording
- **1172 tests green across all 40 suites** that touch `v0Service` / `landingPageGeneration` / `syncLeadCapture`
- **4 mutations red-checked** — removing the guard, defaulting it open, making the lead-list path always install, and dropping the accurate wording each fail the test that pins them
- Two existing tests correctly caught the new argument and were updated rather than bypassed

## ⚠ Pre-existing failures on `main`, not from this PR

Verified by A/B against pristine `main` versions of the changed files — **identical 28 pass / 6 fail both ways**:

- `landingPageStaging.test.ts` — **6 failing tests** (`POST /publish` → 500)
- `npm run typecheck` — 2 errors, `mockUsersInfo` redeclared across the two `slackService` test files (the second landed today, `516be6c65`)

Neither is caught by CI any more: as of the build-first restructure, **no workflow runs `jest`, `npm test`, or `npm run typecheck`** — `Backend build` compiles `tsconfig.build.json`, which excludes tests. Worth a look separately.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Prevented capture files from being created or overwritten in bespoke repositories without an existing platform capture layer.
  * Added clear warnings and repository-specific guidance when server-side capture setup is unavailable or a capture route is skipped.
  * Preserved existing capture route mappings during synchronization.
  * Ensured platform-generated repositories can install required capture files.
  * Preserved retry behavior for supported synchronization workflows.
  * Prevented publishing until required checks complete successfully.

title: fix(attribution): make lastTouch actually record the last touch (ENG-1499)
body:
## The defect

For a lander-captured lead, `lastTouch` could **never** differ from `firstTouch`. The middleware returned early the moment the first-touch cookie existed, so a returning visitor's later campaign click was recorded nowhere, and the webhook stamped `lastTouch` equal to `firstTouch` at write time.

Every last-touch report on lander traffic therefore showed **first-touch numbers** — silently, with complete-looking data. Confirmed live during the ENG-1157 E2E: the stored lead's `lastTouch` was byte-identical to its `firstTouch`.

## Three hops

1. **middleware** — parses the touch *before* deciding what to write, then writes two cookies under different rules. `aw_first_touch`: written once, never overwritten. `aw_last_touch` (new): overwritten on every **attributed** visit.
2. **capture route** — reads `aw_last_touch`, forwards it as `lastTouch`, separate from `attribution` (which remains first touch).
3. **forward-lead** — accepts and normalises it, falling back to first touch when the lander sent none, so a single-visit lead is unchanged.

## The gate applies to last touch ALONE — this is the whole correctness argument

**Gating last touch is required.** An ordinary internal navigation carries no utm, click id, ref, or external referrer. Counting one as a touch would overwrite a real campaign last-touch with an empty one the moment the visitor clicked to a second page — *actively wrong*, and worse than the useless field it replaced.

**Gating first touch would be a regression**, and ENG-308 says so directly: direct traffic is a real acquisition channel, and `firstTouch` is deliberately not a proxy for "attributed".

My first attempt gated **both**. Two ENG-308 runtime tests caught it — *"still records a touch for an UNTAGGED visit (direct traffic is a real channel)"*. That contract is preserved, and there is now a test pinning the interaction so it cannot regress silently.

## Tests

Follows `eng308.middlewareRuntime`: **transpile and execute** the emitted middleware rather than assert on its source. The claim here is about a two-visit journey, and no string assertion can evaluate that.

**Six of the ten fail against the pre-fix generator**, including the core case — *records a SECOND campaign click without disturbing the first*. The untagged-visit and internal-navigation cases pass either way by design: they are guard rails against exactly the mistake the first attempt made, not evidence of the fix.

Also covered: a direct-then-campaign visitor now gets a last touch that genuinely differs from a direct first touch.

**252 tests green** across middleware/webhook/attribution suites. `tsconfig.build.json` clean.

## ⚠️ Known limit

This changes the **generated** lander source. Existing landers keep the old middleware until regenerated, so their leads continue to carry `lastTouch === firstTouch`. The backend handles both shapes, so nothing breaks — but the fix reaches a given lander only on its next generation. Worth knowing before anyone reads a last-touch report and assumes it is now trustworthy everywhere.

Closes ENG-1499.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - Added separate last-touch attribution tracking for landing-page visits while preserving original first-touch attribution.
  - Campaign parameters, click IDs, referrals, and external visits can now update the most recent attribution.
  - Lead forwarding now includes last-touch attribution when available, with first-touch fallback for single-visit leads.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved attribution handling for rewritten paths, direct traffic, returning campaign visits, and internal navigation.

title: UI Bug: report bug to engineering team that Zetld logo not stored in brand guideline via
body:
Follow-up to #2545 (ENG-933), which fixed the root cause of "Zetld logo not stored in brand guideline" (asset-gating + ICO/SVG rasterisation, both in the onboarding backstop and Emma's `update_brand_guidelines` chat tool). This PR closes two residual gaps identified during hardening review of that fix.

**1. Silent degradation on a dead/flaky logo URL.** When the fetch/rasterise attempt failed (network blip, unreachable host, un-rasterisable SVG), the write still returned `success: true` with no signal that no asset actually landed — Emma had no way to know the Logo & Assets card was still empty. Now surfaces a `logoAutoPinIssue` field on the response (and a note in `formattedContent`), with a distinct message for the SVG case vs. a genuine fetch/upload failure, so Emma can tell the user or retry instead of reporting a false success.

**2. `brandData.logoUrl` drift once an asset already exists.** If a later call touches `brandData.logoUrl` without also providing a fresh `brandAssets` entry (e.g. Emma re-sending the original scraped URL after the asset was already pinned), `brandData.logoUrl` used to silently revert to that stale/raw value while the correct asset stayed in `attachments` — a display/data inconsistency. Now resyncs `brandData.logoUrl` to the actual persisted asset URL in that case.

**Deliberately out of scope:** the concurrent-write race on `updateBrandGuidelines` (plain read-modify-write, no optimistic locking). That's a pre-existing property of the whole function shared by every field it writes, not something the logo work introduced or worsened, and retrofitting real conditional-write semantics here would change behavior for every caller (onboarding + every Emma brand-guidelines edit) — a deliberate design change, not a bounded fix, so it's being left for a separate, dedicated pass rather than rushed into this PR.

**Verification:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- Targeted suite green: `agentModeService.brandGuidelinesUpdate.test.ts` (16/16, incl. 2 new/updated tests for the `logoAutoPinIssue` surfacing — download failure, SVG case — and the `brandData.logoUrl` resync), plus the full brand/logo regression sweep (175/175 across 5 suites)

_Generated by the Linear auto-fix agent — please review._

title: feat(org): gate creation to Starter tier (ENG-957)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Low

## What was wrong (before)
Free and Demo users could create organizations because the API had no entitlement check. The Settings UI offered the create form regardless of plan.

## What this fixes (after)
The backend permits organization creation only for Starter, Pro, Partner, Super Premium, and Managed users. Free/Demo users receive an actionable Starter requirement, and the portal directs them to Pricing before submission.

## Complexity ledger
+ Two small shared tier allowlists (backend enforcement + portal presentation); one focused portal utility; no persistence/model changes. Existing organizations and membership flows are untouched.

## How to test
1. Sign in as a Free or Demo user and open Settings → Organization.
2. Expected: a Starter upgrade explanation and “View Starter plans” link are shown; no create form is offered.
3. Call POST /api/org as the same user with a valid name.
4. Expected: 403 with “Starter plan or higher is required”.
5. Sign in as a Starter user and create an organization.
6. Expected: creation returns 201 and the owner membership is created.

## Edge cases to check
- A subscription state that changes after the portal loads is still enforced server-side.
- Existing Free-owned organizations are not evaluated by this create-only guard.

## Test Evidence
- Backend: 45 focused org-route tests passed; pre-push related suite: 84 tests passed; tsc --noEmit clean.
- Portal: 10 focused access tests passed; npx tsc --noEmit clean.
- Tested as: mocked Free, Demo, Starter, Pro, Partner, Super Premium, and Managed users.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- Free user refusal with named plan: org.test.ts parameterized refusal cases.
- Starter creation success: org.test.ts allowed-tier parameterized cases.
- Existing Free organizations remain unchanged: create guard runs only after the no-existing-org check; existing organization endpoints are unchanged.
- Portal presents upgrade path before submission: orgCreationAccess.test.ts plus conditional Settings rendering.

## Files changed
- backend/src/routes/org.ts
- backend/src/__tests__/org.test.ts
- Portal companion: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal branch swarm/eng-957-starter-org-gate

## What was NOT tested
- Browser QA and live production credentials (QA owns browser smoke).
- Staging deployment and GitHub CI.

## Linear issue
ENG-957

title: UI Bug: report bug to engineering team that Zetld logo not stored in brand guideline via
body:
Second follow-up to #2545 (ENG-933 root cause) and #2591 (first hardening pass: `logoAutoPinIssue` surfacing + `brandData.logoUrl` drift fix).

**Live-verification finding.** After #2591 deployed, I delegated into the actual reported customer's account in production (`p.thayalan@zetld.io`) and asked Emma to save the logo, to verify the fix end-to-end against the real reporter. She called `update_brand_guidelines` with her own `brandAssets` entry built from the raw `zetld.io/assets/logo-CQFsiqmM.ico` URL — not a bare `brandData.logoUrl` — which bypasses the auto-pin entirely (it only fires when `brandAssets` is absent). The "never clobber a caller-supplied asset" guard correctly avoided overwriting it, but can't distinguish a real curated upload from Emma passing through an unprocessed URL as her own asset.

Net effect confirmed live: the "No logos uploaded" symptom was fixed (attachments populated, card renders), but the stored asset was still the unrasterised, unpinned external `.ico` — the exact "logos are embedded into websites and are not .png files" problem this ticket exists to fix, reachable through a third door the first two PRs didn't cover.

**Fix:** when the caller supplies a logo asset whose URL isn't already on our own S3, run it through the same rasterise/pin pipeline (`downloadBrandLogoToS3`) before merging, substituting the pinned result. Skips reprocessing when the URL is already one of our own S3 objects (matches the onboarding backstop's own call shape — no redundant re-fetch). Best-effort: on failure the asset is still stored as provided (never worse than before #2591), and `logoAutoPinIssue` surfaces the gap.

Also fixed an existing test whose fixture URL (`https://s3/brand/logo.png`) never matched the real S3 URL shape `isS3Url` checks against — updated to a realistic pinned URL, which is what made this gap visible in the test suite too once the new check was in place.

title: ci: restore the paths-filter negation guard lost with staging-deploy-gate
body:
## What

Restores a structural CI guard that was lost as collateral in #2588, and wires it into `ci-scripts-tests`.

#2588 correctly deleted `staging-deploy-gate.test.sh` — ENG-1463 removed the `backend-staging-deploy` job it asserted against. But that suite's **final** test was general rather than staging-specific, and it went with its host:

> every `!`-negated `dorny/paths-filter` pattern must sit in a step that sets `predicate-quantifier: 'every'`

## Why it matters

dorny/paths-filter compiles each pattern into its own picomatch matcher and OR-combines them (`patterns.some(...)`; the quantifier defaults to `some`). A negated pattern in a default filter is therefore **not** an exclusion — picomatch returns true for every path *outside* the named one. So:

```yaml
backend_src:
  - 'backend/**'
  - '!backend/**/__tests__/**'   # <-- matches README.md
```

is true for `README.md`, making the whole filter permanently true. A narrowing that reads exactly like an exclusion silently becomes a widening.

ENG-1041 split the deploy decision from the test decision precisely so a test-only diff would stop occupying the single global staging lane. A negation that quietly inverts puts every PR back in that lane while the YAML still reads as a narrowing.

## Why a new file, not back into `pipefail-hygiene.test.sh`

Two reasons, both deliberate:

1. **`pipefail-hygiene.test.sh` declares itself byte-identical across `agentweb` and `agentweb-customer-portal`.** Growing it here forces a cross-repo sync for a rule about workflows it does not otherwise touch.
2. **Subject mismatch.** `pipefail-hygiene` is about scripts piping into early-exiting readers and scans `.github/scripts/*.sh`; this rule scans `.github/workflows/*.yml`. ENG-1412 already made exactly this correction once — moving a structural assertion *out* of `eb-config-conflict.test.sh` because a rule belongs with its subject, not with whichever file the bug was first caught in.

## Two improvements over the deleted version

| | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Scope | scanned only `tests.yml` | scans **every** `.github/workflows/*.yml`, so `deploy.yml` — which also uses paths-filter and was **never covered** — is included |
| Reporting | `<no id>` | `file:step-id` |

The id fix was needed, not cosmetic: `tests.yml` writes `id:` on the dash line, `deploy.yml` as a sibling key, and the original regex matched only the latter — so it printed `<no id>` for the single step it actually scanned.

## Evidence

**Mutation-tested against both real workflows** (injected a negation, confirmed red, reverted):

```
tests.yml  -> FAIL ... tests.yml:filter     (6 run, 1 failed)
deploy.yml -> FAIL ... deploy.yml:filter    (6 run, 1 failed)   <-- never covered before
```

**Four self-checks**, because current exposure is zero (no workflow negates a pattern; none sets `predicate-quantifier`) — so without them a broken auditor and a clean repo are indistinguishable:
- a negation under the default quantifier is flagged
- the same negation under `every` is accepted
- a filter with no negation is left alone
- a **commented-out** quantifier does not satisfy the rule

**All 10 suites green on this branch:**

```
dependabot-config 10 · dependabot-integrity-check 25 · dependabot-only-pr 10
deploy-failure-alert 100 · eb-config-conflict 34 · eb-deploy 79
merge-evidence 107 · paths-filter-hygiene 6 · pipefail-hygiene 18 · trunk-deploy-state 38
```

`pipefail-hygiene` moved 17 → 18 because it globs `*.sh` and now scans one more file — no assertion changed.

`shellcheck .github/scripts/*.sh` (CI's blocking step) exits 0.

## Note

Wired into `ci-scripts-tests` in the same commit. Without that it would be a **third** orphaned suite — the same failure mode that hid this assertion and `coverage-report.test.mjs`.

This is prospective hardening. Nothing is broken today; the guard exists so the hazard cannot be reintroduced silently.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Tests**
  - Added automated checks to ensure workflow path filters correctly handle negated patterns.
  - Added validation for missing or incorrectly configured quantifiers, including commented-out settings and varied workflow formatting.
  - Integrated the new hygiene check into the continuous integration test suite, helping detect configuration issues before changes are merged.

title: fix(google-ads): a tag that reports nothing must not look installed (ENG-1524, ENG-1525)
body:
Two ways a page ends up carrying a Google Ads tag that records **no conversions**, both of which currently succeed silently. They share a shape: the base tag stays on the page, so RULE 7.5 keeps passing and every indicator stays green, while the thing that actually reports is absent.

Found in a deep audit of the Google Ads surface. Closes **ENG-1525** and **ENG-1524**.

---

## ENG-1525 — re-applying a tag deleted the label that makes it work

`updateLandingPageGoogleAds` treated *"field absent"* and *"field explicitly cleared"* as the same request:

```ts
if (conversionLabel) { sets.push(...) }
else removes.push("googleAdsConversionLabel");
```

Re-posting just the conversion id — the natural "re-apply my tag", which the route **deliberately permits** with only a warning because the base tag can be installed before the conversion action exists — took the falsy branch and `REMOVE`d the label and customer id, from this record **and every sibling page**.

`buildTrackingHelper` fires only when id **and** label are both present, so conversions stopped dead behind an HTTP 200. Future sub-pages inherited `googleAds === undefined`; ENG-1325's offline import lost the customer id.

**The hazard was already known one branch away.** The route rejects a *non-string* label with a 400, saying exactly why:
> *"a malformed request would strip a working conversion pair and leave an id that attributes nothing"*

An omitted label did precisely that, unguarded.

**Fix:** `undefined` leaves the stored value alone, `""` removes it. The route stopped collapsing `""` into `undefined` for `customerId` so an explicit clear still works. Clearing the id itself keeps its all-three semantics.

---

## ENG-1524 — nothing checked that the conversion is ever fired

Meta has `validatePixelLeadEvent` with a correction-and-retry loop. Google Ads had **no equivalent anywhere** in `backend/src`. `v0Service` argued none was needed:

> *"Unlike metaPixelId this needs NO validation-retry safety net: v0 does not author the conversion call, it only passes two values into the platform-owned helper."*

It does not author the `gtag` call. It **does** author whether `fireLeadTracking` is called and with which arguments.

So v0 could emit `fireLeadTracking({ email, eventId, pixelId })`, omit `googleAds`, and:

- the pixel validator passes — `pixelId` **is** there
- generation succeeds, `googleAdsTrackingInstalled` is set true
- the pre-flight gate passes **cleanly, with no warning** — the page genuinely carries the tag
- the campaign reports **zero conversions** for as long as it runs

Nothing in the system detects it.

**Fix:** `validateGoogleAdsConversion`, same contract as the pixel check (presence of the argument, not placement), wired into the same retry loop, gated on the conversion **pair** since the helper cannot fire without a label. Never fails generation, matching the pixel path — but the exhausted-retry log now states the page will report no conversions, turning an invisible miss into a visible one.

One deliberate difference: the regex uses a bounded `[\s\S]` window rather than the pixel validator's `[^}]*`. `googleAds` is a **nested object**, so `[^}]*` stops at the first inner brace the moment any other object precedes it. The window also accepts property shorthand, and is bounded so an unrelated mention elsewhere in the file cannot satisfy the check.

---

## Tests

11 new. The **two ENG-1525 cases that describe the bug fail against the pre-fix code**; its three guard rails — explicit clear still removes, supplied values still written, id-clear semantics unchanged — pass either way *by design*, because they exist to stop the fix going too far.

`validateGoogleAdsConversion` is new, so its cases fail before by construction; they pin the shapes that must and must not satisfy it, including that **the base tag alone does not**.

**380 green** across the v0Service, landing-page, google-ads and pixel suites. `tsconfig.build.json` clean.

  * Empty values can explicitly clear saved Google Ads fields.
  * Generated landing pages and sub-pages now validate required Google Ads conversion tracking and retry corrections when needed.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for Google Ads configuration preservation, clearing behavior, and conversion tracking validation.

title: fix(ENG-1528): ask the org authority model, not a userId comparison
body:
## What

Switching a scheduled task from the usage runway returned **404** on production. Measured on the founders account: **8 of the 10 schedules offered were a colleague's, and every one failed.**

## Cause — two halves of the feature disagreed about scope

**Reading is billing-scoped.** `usage-drivers` pools schedules across every org member (`resolvePooledLedgerUserIds`), so an org owner is *shown* colleagues' spend and told it is theirs to reduce.

**Writing compared user ids:**

```ts
if (!schedule || schedule.userId !== userId) throw new ModelChangeNotFoundError(...)
// "No org bypass: an org member does not get to retune a colleague's
//  schedule because they share a bill."
```

That reasoning is right about a **member** and wrong about an **owner** — and `orgAuthz` already draws exactly that line:

```ts
org:content:manage — "Edit or delete another member's items as an org-level override."
                     (owner + admin; withheld from member)
```

The reporting caller holds it twice over: by role, and as the org's billing root (`ownerUserId` **is** their userId). They were refused an authority the org model already grants them.

**Nothing is widened.** `ROLE_PERMISSIONS.member` is empty; a plain member is refused exactly as before. The check just asks the model that already governs this.

Applies to `undo` as well as `apply` — both route through the same loader, or an owner could switch and then be unable to revert.

## Three things this had to preserve or fix

**1. Anti-enumeration — nearly broken by my first pass.** The original 404 was deliberate: *"reports 'not found' rather than 'forbidden' so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which schedule ids exist."* A blanket 403 turns this into an existence oracle for any UUID across tenants. Now only a **same-org** caller gets the honest 403 — the schedule is already listed on their own billing page, so it discloses nothing new. Everyone else still gets 404.

**2. Fail closed.** The authority lookup is wrapped: a failure to read the user or org record is an *absence* of authority — never a grant, never a 500. Found by the integration suite, which surfaced a DB error reaching a customer-facing button as a server error.

**3. Honest status.** `"Scheduled chat not found"` was false for a row the customer is looking at. Same-org refusals now say what actually happened, via `ModelChangeForbiddenError` → 403.

## Tests — 51/51 across all five model-change suites

Mutation-tested:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| revert to bare id equality | **4 fail** |
| forbid unconditionally (breaks anti-enumeration) | **4 fail** |
| ask for a weaker permission (`org:members:read`) | **1 fails** |

That last test exists because `org:members:read` carries **identical role grants today**, so behaviour alone cannot distinguish it. Widening roster reads to members later must not silently hand them model-switching.

## Review note

This changes **who may write to whose schedules**, so it deserves a look at the authorization boundary specifically — particularly the same-org-only disclosure rule in `loadSwitchableSchedule`, which is what keeps the endpoint from becoming an id oracle.

## Not verified in production

The only thing that proves this is switching one of the affected schedules on the founders account and getting a result instead of a 404. Not claiming it works until that happens.

## Follow-up

A plain member will still (correctly) be refused, but the portal has no way to know that in advance and will keep offering them a button that fails. The driver payload needs a `switchable` flag so the UI can explain instead — tracked on ENG-1528.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Unauthorized attempts now receive a clear forbidden response.
  * Missing or inaccessible schedules continue to appear as unavailable.

title: fix(launch-gate): a refused launch must reach the browser (ENG-1523)
body:
RULE 7.5 refuses a launch correctly. The user is shown a **green success checkmark** labelled "Call Google Ads Api".

Three things line up to produce that:

1. **`extractMinimalToolResult` has no branch for `call_google_ads_api`** — 485 lines, zero references to it — so the block payload falls through to `return {}`. The reason is destroyed **server-side**.
2. A block is a **returned value, not a throw**, so `toolCall.error` is never set.
3. The frontend ternary is `error ? 'error' : awaitingUserConfirmation ? 'awaiting_confirmation' : 'completed'` — with neither field present it resolves to `'completed'`, which renders green.

**This PR fixes link 1, which is the prerequisite.** While the backend deletes the payload, no frontend change can recover it. The frontend half (links 2–3) is a separate PR in `agentweb-customer-portal` and lands after this deploys.

Closes **ENG-1523** (backend half).

## What it preserves

- On a refusal: `blocked`, `reason`, `error`, `trackingCheck` (the per-URL evidence, so the UI can say *which* URL failed).
- On a **permitted** launch: `trackingWarning` — the ENG-1358 case where a page is measurable but nothing proves an Ads conversion can be recorded. The gate computes that warning and its callers relay it deliberately, with the comment *"A warning that is computed and discarded is the same as no warning at all"*. The minimizer discarded it one layer later — the same outcome by a longer route.

## Two deliberate design calls

**Keyed on the payload, not the tool name.** `metaLaunchGate` returns this exact block shape in **five places**, so Meta launch blocks were being erased identically — the defect was never Google-only. Keying on `blocked === true` covers both, and any future gate, without another branch here.

**Both branches sit AFTER the confirmation gate.** My first attempt put them first, and a call that both halts for approval *and* carries a warning lost `awaitingUserConfirmation` — which would have broken the Meta approval UI. My own test caught it; the ordering assertion is in the suite so it cannot regress.

Modelled on the `awaitingUserConfirmation` branch directly above, whose comment makes precisely this argument: the per-tool minimizers drop unknown fields, so anything the frontend needs must be preserved here explicitly.

## Tests

8 new. **5 fail against the pre-fix minimizer**, including the Meta block and the ENG-1358 warning.

The 3 that pass either way are guard rails, and are meant to: an ordinary success still minimizes to nothing (the minimizer must not become a hole that preserves everything), a falsy `blocked` is not a block, and the confirmation gate still wins.

**171 green** across the launch-gate, google-ads-tools and confirmation-gate suites. `tsconfig.build.json` clean.

---

*A refusal the operator never sees is indistinguishable from one that never happened — which is the failure the gate exists to prevent.*

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Blocked Google Ads, Meta Ads, and other tool launch results now retain refusal reasons, errors, and tracking details.
  - Permitted launches continue to display relevant tracking warnings and messages.
  - Ordinary successful results remain concise without losing important status information.
  - Confirmation states are now handled consistently when determining which launch details to show.

title: [needs human] Fix industry filter shape in LinkedIn people search (ENG-1299)
body:
**Bug:** The structured LinkedIn people-search path (`linkedInOutreachService.searchPeople`) sent `industry: {include: [id], exclude: []}` to Unipile's classic `/linkedin/search` endpoint. Unipile's schema requires `industry` as a flat array of numeric ID strings (same shape as company/location/school), so every structured search that resolved an industry filter failed with `errors/invalid_parameters` ("Expected union value", HTTP 400). Confirmed against production logs for the reported session (448fb849-4e42-4580-8d6a-02509f64e10c, 2026-08-17T12:15:34Z and 12:15:44Z): two consecutive structured search-people calls failed with this exact error, after which the agent abandoned all structured filters (industry, location) and retried with a bare `keywords: "fintech product manager Bay Area"` query — which surfaced large established employers instead of the requested startups.

**Fix:** Send `industry` as `[resolvedIndustryId]`, a flat array, matching the shape already used for company/location/school and matching Unipile's documented+enforced schema.

**Verification:** Wrote a failing test first asserting the correct flat-array shape (it failed against the unfixed code, reproducing the exact `{include,exclude}` mismatch), then fixed the implementation and confirmed the test passes along with the full existing `linkedInOutreachService` test suite (133/133).
