title: fix(ci): make eb-deploy's clock deterministic in tests, killing the 2/79 flake (ENG-1522)
body:
Fixes ENG-1522.

## The bug

`CI script tests` went red twice on customer-portal PRs touching **no deploy code** (#1092, #1093), both times the same 2 of 79 checks:

```
EB_DEPLOY_FAILED: ... its health stayed Red for 1s after becoming Ready,
and the underlying instance/target health could not be established ...
describe-instances-health returned no instances
```

`now_seconds()` is read **twice inside one poll iteration** — once to stamp `ready_since` when the environment first reports Ready, again to test that stamp against `EB_HEALTH_SETTLE_SECONDS`. `date +%s` has one-second granularity, so if the wall clock ticks between those two reads the delta jumps `0 -> 1`. In the *"leaving and re-entering Ready restarts the health settle window"* case (`EB_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS=1`, `EB_HEALTH_SETTLE_SECONDS=1`) that expires the budget a poll early, the script asks for instance health, the scripted mock queue is exhausted, and the deploy reports unconfirmed.

**Confirmed, not inferred.** Forcing that tick — one `sleep 1` between the two reads, on a scratch copy — reproduces exactly those 2 failures with byte-identical text. Five full runs under deliberate CPU load did *not* reproduce it, which is consistent: the window is a few milliseconds wide per opportunity.

The general defect is larger than the one case: **a fixed mocked event queue was being consumed against a wall-clock budget**, so poll counts depended on runner speed. Any future test pairing a poll interval with a comparable settle budget reintroduces it.

## The fix

A test-only clock seam. `now_seconds()` reads `EB_CLOCK_FILE` when set; the harness's mock AWS CLI advances that file once per `describe-environments` call — one tick per poll — so time is a function of the scripted event sequence.

`now_seconds()` is now **constant within an iteration**, so the two reads cannot straddle a second boundary. Structurally impossible, not merely unlikely.

**Same forced jitter: `79 checks run, 2 failed` before → `82 checks run, 0 failed` after.**

## Why production is unaffected

- No workflow sets `EB_CLOCK_FILE` (asserted structurally, see below), so on the deploy path `now_seconds()` is `date +%s` verbatim and the new branch is unreachable.
- `EB_HEALTH_SETTLE_SECONDS` still defaults to 180; no workflow overrides it.
- **No decision this script makes was changed** — only how it reads time. No verification semantics touched, in the script whose false-success and non-convergence modes cost ~17h (ENG-865) and ~29h (ENG-836) of production downtime.

The guard matters because *every* budget here — run deadline, settle timeout, health settle window, rejection grace — is a comparison against `now_seconds()`. A frozen clock in production would mean none of them could ever expire: a hung or rejected deploy would poll forever instead of failing. So three checks pin the seam shut (79 → 82):

1. no workflow sets `EB_CLOCK_FILE`;
2. a **self-check** proving that scan detects a workflow that does — current exposure is zero, so without it a broken scan and a clean repo are indistinguishable (the fail-open shape CodeRabbit caught in `paths-filter-hygiene`);
3. with `EB_CLOCK_FILE` unset, `now_seconds()` still returns real epoch time.

They live in `eb-deploy.test.sh`, already wired into `CI script tests`, rather than a new file — three suites in this repo have already been found orphaned and silently red.

## Deliberately NOT the naive fix

Raising `EB_HEALTH_SETTLE_SECONDS` for that case would hide the race **and make the test vacuous**: it exists to prove the window *restarts* on re-entry, and with a larger budget an un-reset window would also fit inside it, so the case would pass even with the reset deleted.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Mutation — neuter `ready_since=0` reset | 🔴 exactly those 2 checks fail, correct reason |
| Mutation — restore | 🟢 82/82 |
| Forced-jitter repro, before fix | `79 run, 2 failed` |
| Forced-jitter repro, after fix | `82 run, 0 failed` |
| 20 consecutive runs (10 idle + 10 under load ~12) | 20/20 green |
| All ten CI script suites | 10 · 25 · 10 · 100 · 34 · **82** · 107 · 8 · 18 · 38, zero failures |
| `shellcheck .github/scripts/*.sh` | clean |

Suite also got faster, 36s → ~22s: budget-exhaustion cases expire on poll count instead of waiting out real seconds.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

  - Preserved production timing behavior when no clock override is configured.
  - Added safeguards to ensure deployment workflows use real system time by default.

- **Tests**
  - Expanded deployment validation with deterministic timing scenarios.
  - Added coverage confirming clock overrides are limited to test contexts.

title: fix(security): bind the Google Ads tracking override to a disclosed approval (ENG-1526)
body:
The Google Ads tracking waiver was `args.override_tracking_check === true` and nothing else. The model could set it unilaterally, and the only thing standing against that was a sentence in the tool description: *"Never set it on your own."*

**ENG-941 wrote this exact threat model down for the Meta path and dismissed exactly that defence** — *"an override the model can introduce after approval is not user-granted, whatever the tool description says"* — then hardened Meta and left Google on the sentence. Same file, two lines apart:

```
18857  Meta:   const overrideTrackingCheck = overrideApproved;
34233  Google: const overrideTrackingCheck = args.override_tracking_check === true;
```

Closes **ENG-1526**.

## The fix

Reuses ENG-941's helpers rather than writing a second mechanism — `computeTrackingOverrideDigest` / `trackingOverrideTokenMatches`. HMAC over the exact call, keyed with a server-only secret so the caller cannot mint one, constant-time compared, key-order-independent so a re-emitted argument object still matches.

I checked `stableStringify` before relying on it: it already excludes the gate-only keys (`confirm`, `tracking_override_token`) **at every level**, so the replay digests identically to the preview that issued it. Without that the token could never match and the mechanism would be silently inert.

A claimed-but-unapproved override **does not fail — it halts**: the turn stops, the waiver and its consequence are disclosed, and the matching token is issued. The path is a loop, not a dead end. A call that waives nothing is untouched and never needs a token.

Also adds `tracking_override_token` to the schema and rewrites the override's description so it states the model **cannot** grant the waiver, rather than asking it not to.

## Scope, deliberately narrow

This halts **only when an override is claimed**. Google Ads writes still have no general confirmation step — Meta has `isMetaWriteAction`, Google has no equivalent. That is a bigger change, it is tracked in ENG-1527, and putting an unrelated behaviour change inside a security fix would be the wrong trade.

## ⚠️ Two existing tests changed contract, not outcome

Both asserted that a bare override *proceeds* — which is the defect itself. They now assert the full loop: the bare call halts and issues a token, and the replay carrying it proceeds **and is still recorded as `overridden`**.

The behaviour they were protecting (an approved override works, and is audited) is preserved exactly; only the step that makes it *approved* is new. I kept both halves rather than deleting the coverage.

## Tests

9 new. **4 fail against the pre-fix handler**: halt-and-disclose, a forged token, a token minted for a **different campaign**, and one minted for a **different customer**.

Those last two are the point of signing the *call* rather than issuing a bare permission slip — approval is for the launch the user was shown, not for any launch afterwards.

The 5 that pass either way are guard rails: a non-override call is untouched and still blocked, a truthy-but-not-`true` flag is not a claim, and a token supplied without the flag does nothing.

title: fix(ENG-1519): a per-unit vendor call is not a model
body:
## What

Reported from the founders account: **`twitter:get_user_tweets` listed under Models** at 4% / 427 calls.

## It is not corrupt data

`recordVendorUsage` shares this ledger with token-priced LLM calls and namespaces the model slot as `{provider}:{operation}` — deliberately, and documented at the call site:

> *"The row's model slot is namespaced `{provider}:{operation}`. The sort key format stays `{date}#{model}#{feature}` … namespacing the model component is what guarantees two different vendors can never aggregate into one row and overwrite each other's `provider`."*

The defect is **downstream**: `attributeCosts` read every row's `model` as an LLM model.

## Why it matters

A customer was offered a "model" that cannot be switched, has no cheaper equivalent, and would produce a nonsensical recommendation if one were ever generated for it — in the one list whose entire purpose is recommending which model to switch. It also understated every real model's share, against a denominator holding a non-model.

## Fix

`usageRecordDb` already has the right predicate:

```ts
export function isVendorEntry(row: UsageRecordRow): boolean {
  return row.provider != null && row.unit != null;
}
```

Both fields are required for a reason it states explicitly: an LLM row may name its provider and is still token-priced spend. `AttributionRow` dropped both, so attribution could not apply it.

They are carried through now, at **both** mapping sites — the drivers path and the preview path. Fixing one alone would have made preview and drivers disagree about the same cycle.

## Vendor spend is not dropped

It is real spend on the bill. It still counts toward the total, still attributes to its feature, and is surfaced as its own `byVendor` grouping. Its cost is included in `attributed` — otherwise the fix would report it as *unattributable* and break `reconciles`, turning a naming fix into a false claim that the ledger does not add up.

## Tests

Mutation-tested in three directions:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| stop excluding vendor rows (the reported bug) | **1 fails** |
| exclude vendor cost from `attributed` (breaks the books) | **1 fails** |
| treat any row with a provider as a vendor call | **1 fails** |

That last one matters most — over-filtering would silently delete real models from the breakdown, which is worse than the bug being fixed.

- [x] attribution suite — 39/39
- [x] drivers resolver suite — 44/44
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean (only a pre-existing local `robots-parser` install gap, declared in package.json)
- [x] mutation-tested
- [ ] CI

## Portal follow-up

`byVendor` is new API surface and nothing renders it yet, so vendor spend currently shows only under Features. That is honest — and thanks to ENG-1520, the Models group will now correctly report *"covers N% of this cycle"* rather than implying it covers everything. A portal PR to surface the vendor group is worth doing separately.

  * Added vendor usage attribution to distinguish per-unit vendor charges from model usage.
  * Vendor costs are now included in total spend, reconciliation, and feature attribution while remaining separate from model attribution.
  * Added vendor cost drivers, with an unavailable status when no vendor usage is present.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Preserved provider and unit details across usage reporting and preview calculations for more accurate cost attribution.

title: feat(ENG-1519): surface vendor spend at the customer boundary
body:
## Why

ENG-1519 stopped `twitter:get_user_tweets` being aggregated as a model and offered to the customer as one they could switch away from. That half shipped and is correct.

The other half did not. `toCustomerDrivers` never carried `byVendor`, so the spend left `byModel` and arrived **nowhere**: the model list now quietly covers less than the cycle, with no sentence saying why. A wrong row traded for a blind spot is not a fix — it is the same defect `SpendBreakdown` exists to remove, moved one layer down.

## What

`byVendor` crosses the boundary on the same terms as every other grouping:

- **Shares and call counts only** — no micro-USD (ENG-1212 AC4).
- **The same cycle-total denominator**, so its share is comparable to `byModel` / `byFeature` rather than a slice of a different pie.
- **`null`, not `[]`**, when the cycle bought nothing per-unit — a UI must be able to state absence rather than draw a "Tools & data" heading over zero, which would assert the customer used tools and spent nothing on them.

## Tests

A vendor row lands in `byVendor`, is **absent** from `byModel` (never both — double-counting the same spend across two lists would overstate the cycle), carries its share against the full total, and stays dollar-free. A cycle with no vendor rows reports `null`.

Mutation-tested, which the ENG-1438 case in this same file exists to demand: deleting the field fails two tests, returning `[]` instead of `null` fails one. Without that, a boundary field can ship inert and no test would notice.

## Not in this PR

The portal does not yet render the group. Until that lands, vendor spend is correct and complete in the API and still invisible in the UI — this PR is the prerequisite, not the finish.

title: Add a direct human attestation path to the customer-closure verification gate
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
The ENG-1268 customer-closure verification webhook (`customerClosureVerification.ts`) requires a
`<!-- customer-symptom-verification:v1 -->` comment with a `Verifier` field matching
`^post-merge-verifier/\S+$` before it lets a `Bug` + `Customer Reported` issue transition into
`Done`. There was no other trusted identity in that allowlist. Live incident today:
ENG-975/933/1223/967/907 all bounced `Verifying -> Done -> Verifying` repeatedly, including a
well-formed *self*-attestation from the implementing engineer (correctly rejected — working as
designed) **and** a genuine independent review written directly by Harsha, with every field
correctly filled in, that still got silently reverted — because the gate only ever recognized the
literal string `post-merge-verifier/`, never a human name, however genuine.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds `harsha-direct/<anything>` as a second trusted verifier prefix, alongside the existing
`post-merge-verifier/<run-id>`. This is deliberately still a narrow allowlist of exact, structured
prefixes — not "any name" or "anyone but the fix author" — so the existing anti-self-attestation
protection is unchanged for every other case (a bare human name, or the fix author's own name,
still gets rejected). It only adds a path for the one identity this contract already treats as
authoritative everywhere else in the codebase (comms decisions, database/data-plane approval,
external-copy review — see `~/.claude/rules/autonomous-execution-and-merge.md`).

## Complexity ledger
+105/-1 lines, almost entirely new tests. One new regex constant replacing an inline one, zero new
dependencies, zero new abstractions, zero behavior change for any existing accepted/rejected case.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/integrations.linearWebhook.test.ts`
2. **Expected**: 33 passed (29 pre-existing + 4 new).
3. Manually: on a `Bug` + `Customer Reported` Linear issue, post a comment with
   `<!-- customer-symptom-verification:v1 -->`, `Result: pass`, `Evidence type: customer-symptom`,
   `Checked: <symptom>`, `Method: <how>`, `Verifier: harsha-direct/<any-id>`, then transition the
   issue to Done. Expect it to stick (no revert, `notifyCanonicalResolved` fires).

## Edge cases to check
- `Verifier: harsha-direct` (no slash + id) → still rejected — regex-tested.
- `Verifier: harsha-direct-ish/2026-08-24` (near-miss prefix) → still rejected — regex-tested,
  proves the match is anchored, not a substring check.
- `Verifier: Harsha Vankayalapati (direct review, live session, 2026-08-24)` — the exact free-text
  shape from the live incident — still rejected — regression-tested; this is intentional (the
  contract requires the deliberate `harsha-direct/<id>` marker, not an arbitrary name match).

## Test Evidence
- `npx jest src/__tests__/integrations.linearWebhook.test.ts` → 33 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run typecheck` → clean (also verified by this branch's pre-push hook, 126s).
- Coverage on `customerClosureVerification.ts`: 100% stmts/funcs/lines, 96% branch (pre-existing
  single-branch gap on the `Result` field short-circuit, not introduced by this change).
- TDD: added 4 tests (3 reject-shaped incl. the exact live-incident regression, 1 accept-shaped),
  confirmed RED against the old implementation, GREEN after the fix.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- "A genuine independent human (Harsha) can close a customer-bug issue directly, without going
  through the post-merge-verifier loop" → `allows a properly structured harsha-direct attestation
  to reach the resolve bridge`.
- "The gate still distrusts anything that isn't the deliberate marker format, including a real
  human name" → `rejects a free-text human name as Verifier, even a genuine independent one
  (ENG-1268 gap, 2026-08-24)`, `rejects "harsha-direct" with no run identifier`, `rejects a
  near-miss prefix`.
- All 6 pre-existing verification-gate tests (blocks-missing-evidence, rejects-code-claims,
  rejects-self-authored, fails-closed-on-reporter-ticket-rail, allows-post-merge-verifier,
  Done-only-transition-gating suite) unchanged and still passing.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/customerClosureVerification.ts` — trusted-verifier regex
- `backend/src/__tests__/integrations.linearWebhook.test.ts` — 4 new tests

## What was NOT tested
- No live Linear webhook round-trip against production was performed as part of this PR (the
  route-level Jest suite mocks `linearService`/`intakeService`, matching the existing test
  strategy for this file). Live verification happens by retrying the actual blocked Linear issues
  once this deploys.

## Linear issue
No dedicated ENG issue — direct live-incident fix at Harsha's explicit instruction (session-scoped),
discovered while resolving why ENG-975/933/1223/967/907 could not be closed.

title: fix(google-ads): three supplied parameters that never reached Google (ENG-1527)
body:
Same shape as ENG-1514, found by auditing the rest of the surface after it: **the schema advertises an argument, the caller sends it, the write goes out without it, and the response says success.**

Part of **ENG-1527**.

## 1 · Bid target with no strategy — silently dropped

Google stores a bid target as a **leaf of the bidding strategy** (`target_cpa.target_cpa_micros` and friends). There is no strategy-agnostic field, so a bare target has nowhere to go — both `createCampaign` and `updateCampaign` read it into `params` and never touched it.

On UPDATE that was silent whenever **any other field was masked**: `name` alone made the mask non-empty, the mutate went through, and the caller was told *"Campaign updated"* while the target was never sent. Smart bidding keeps optimising to the old target — real money at the wrong efficiency point, with no read-back on campaigns to catch it.

**Refused, not inferred.** Guessing the leaf means reading the current strategy and writing a *money* field on a value that can change between read and write. A refusal costs one retry; a wrong guess costs budget. The error names the GAQL to read the strategy, so recovery is one step.

Extracted as a shared `assertBidTargetIsAddressable` rather than written twice — the same invariant duplicated is exactly how these diverge, which is the shape of most defects this ticket collects.

> My first attempt landed the guard in `createCampaign` only: the anchor string exists in both functions and a single replace took the first. The tests caught it.

## 2 · Bid target with MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS / MAXIMIZE_CONVERSION_VALUE — zeroed

`0` means *no constraint*, which is correct when none was supplied — and was the only value ever written. A caller who **did** supply one got it discarded.

This is also what makes (1)'s advice safe: it tells the caller to restate the strategy, and before this, restating `MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS` would have **wiped the very target they were setting**. The two fixes only work together.

## 3 · KEYWORD ADD — status hardcoded ENABLED, no parameter at all

The last create on this surface that could not be staged, after ENG-1514 gave AD_GROUP and AD one.

Containment from a paused parent exists only on the greenfield path. Adding keywords to an **already-live** ad group starts buying queries on the next refresh, at the ad group's default bid, with no review of match type or bid — and unlike AD CREATE and ASSET_GROUP CREATE, **KEYWORD ADD passes through no gate at all**.

Defaults to PAUSED per RULE 11, matching CAMPAIGN/AD_GROUP/AD. A deliberate trade: keywords sitting paused is visible and one call to fix; unreviewed spend is neither. Explicit ENABLED still honoured. Also corrects the schema line claiming PAUSED does not apply to keywords — `updateKeyword` has always accepted it.

## Tests

13 new, **9 fail against the pre-fix code**. They assert on the **mutate payload**, because the failure mode is a success response describing a request that was never made.

The 4 that pass either way are guard rails and are meant to: an ordinary update untouched, `0` still written when no target was supplied, `TARGET_CPA`/`TARGET_ROAS` unchanged.

**442 green** across the Google Ads suites. `tsconfig.build.json` clean.

  - Supplied targets are preserved for conversion-focused bidding strategies, including campaign updates.
  - Keyword additions now honor requested `ENABLED` or `PAUSED` statuses and default to `PAUSED` when unspecified.
  - Campaign creation validates bid-target settings before credential checks and advertising platform changes.

- **Documentation**
  - Clarified supported bidding strategies, target units, incompatibilities, and rejection behavior.
  - Clarified supported statuses for keywords and conversion actions, including how conversion actions should be retired.

title: feat(ENG-1533): offer a model switch only where it can succeed
body:
## Why

`usage-drivers` pools schedules across every org member, so this list routinely shows a caller a **colleague's** work. ENG-1528 made the write path refuse a plain member's change on that work — correctly.

What it left behind is a UI offering a Confirm button whose only possible outcome is an error.

## What

`switchable` now travels with each schedule driver, answered by the **same predicate the write path uses**. `contentAuthorityOver(caller, owner)` is extracted so one rule decides both whether to *allow* the write and whether to *offer* it. Two copies would drift apart on the first change to the role model, and a divergence there merely relocates the bug rather than fixing it.

Deliberate choices:

- **The row stays visible when it is not switchable — only the action is withheld.** Hiding a colleague's schedule would recreate exactly the blind spot ENG-1440 closed: the spend is real and was billed to this account.
- **A deleted schedule is unswitchable for everyone**, so no authority question arises for it.
- **Ownership is plumbed, not inferred.** `byId` keeps the owner from the per-user schedule read that already knew it, and authority resolves once per distinct **owner** rather than per row, since it cannot differ within an owner.

## A test that was silently disarmed

`contentAuthorityOver` lives in its own module, and that placement is load-bearing rather than tidiness.

Sited beside `callerCan` inside `orgAuthz`, it disarmed the ENG-1528 guard that the code asks for `org:content:manage` and **not merely some org permission**. That guard works by spying the `callerCan` import; an internal caller reaches the module-local binding rather than the mocked export, so the spy observed nothing while the test kept passing. Crossing a module boundary is what keeps it observable.

This matters because the drift it guards is invisible to every behavioural test in the suite: `org:members:read` and `org:content:manage` are both owner+admin today, so swapping one for the other changes no outcome — and reading a roster is a benign thing to widen to members later, while switching their colleagues' models is not.

## Verification

- 105 tests green across the resolver, model-change and orgAuthz suites.
- Typecheck clean apart from the pre-existing `robots-parser` missing-module error already on main.
- **Mutation-tested**, five ways: forcing `switchable` true, forcing it false, dropping it from the customer boundary, asking authority about the caller's own org instead of the owner's (the cross-tenant hole), and swapping the requested permission to `org:members:read`. Each fails a test.

## Not in this PR

The portal still renders the button unconditionally. Until that lands this flag is inert — correct on the payload, invisible in the UI — the same staging as ENG-1519.

title: ENG-1527: fix both AW/GA4 detectors, which were wrong in opposite directions
body:
## The problem

RULE 7.5's pre-flight gate and the layout injector's guard both look for the same Google ids, but they read **different inputs**, so their correct scopes run in **opposite directions**. Each was using the other's rule.

### Half 1 — the gate was too wide (false PASS)

`googleAdsTrackingPreflight.detectTrackingSnippets` reads **served HTML** and scanned the whole document. An id in rendered body copy —

> Ask your rep for conversion id AW-11112222333.

— read as a working tag, so RULE 7.5 passed a launch for a page that fires nothing. Same class of false PASS as the `ai-gtm-agent` slug ENG-1358 closed, arriving through the AW door instead.

**Now scanned over markup only** (tags, `<script>`/`<noscript>` bodies) — text nodes are dropped.

The obvious fix — narrowing to `<script>` elements — was checked against **live www.agentweb.pro before writing any code**, and would have false-BLOCKED our own correctly tagged marketing site: its GA4 id is carried by `<link rel="preload" href="...gtag/js?id=G-KKJE0Q33LF">` and the Next.js hydration payload, *not* a `<script src>`. Validated against that real document:

```
ids in FULL html:      ['G-KKJE0Q33LF']
ids in MARKUP-only:    ['G-KKJE0Q33LF']
lost by narrowing:     none
```

while a prose-only page went from matching `AW-11112222333` to matching nothing.

A response with **no markup at all** (a bare script body, a JSON payload) falls back to the raw text — narrowing it to nothing would report "no tag" for a response that may carry one, the wrong direction for a gate whose job is to refuse what it cannot vouch for.

### Half 2 — the injector's guard was too narrow (ENG-910 double-count)

`googleAdsInjection`'s guard reads **layout.tsx source** and scanned only `<script>` elements, so the ordinary App Router shape

```tsx
const GA_ADS_ID = "AW-11112222333";
<Script src={`https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=${GA_ADS_ID}`} />
```

was invisible. It injected ours anyway and shipped **two distinct AW ids on one page** — the ENG-910 double-count this guard exists to prevent, walked past a second time.

**Now scans the whole source.** Wide is safe *here*: a false positive costs a visible abort telling a human to clean the layout; a miss costs a silently double-counted conversion.

### Half 3 — why `foreignGoogleAdsIds` is split rather than shared

It had two callers with **opposite risk profiles**. Widening both regressed `verifyGoogleAdsInjection`, caught by the existing marketing-copy test: an `AW-` id inside a `<title>` would have read as *installed*, handing RULE 7.5 a pass for an untagged page — the same failure as Half 1, reached from the other side.

Verify stays narrow, and the asymmetry is load-bearing. A const-held id reads as not-installed, so injection is attempted and the wide guard refuses with a visible abort. Nothing is double-counted, nothing is silently blessed.

## Testing

`backend/src/__tests__/eng1527.detectorScopes.test.ts` — 12 tests pinning all four behaviours **independently**. Reverting any one half fails exactly the tests describing it and nothing else:

| reverted | tests that fail |
|---|---|
| gate scans raw html | the 2 body-copy tests |
| no-markup fallback removed | the tagless-response test |
| guard scoped to `<script>` | the 2 const-held-id tests |
| verify widened with the guard | the 2 verify tests |

Regression coverage: **1367 passed, 0 failed** across the 63 google / tracking / injection / landing suites. `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.

## Risk

No API surface, schema, or route changes — two pure detector functions. The gate can now only become *less* likely to pass an untagged page; the injector can now only become *more* likely to refuse. Both fail toward BLOCK / abort rather than toward spend.

  * Prevented incorrect injection when conflicting advertising identifiers are present.
  * Improved verification of installed tracking tags, including shared loaders and formatting variations.
  * More reliably distinguishes executable tracking code from comments, strings, and non-executable content.

title: fix: gate renewal ad-health alert on subscription entitlement (ENG-1541)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
`runRenewalIntegrationHealthCheck` flagged any active-subscription user renewing within 14 days who had selected "paid ads" intent (goal/onboarding) but had no connected ad platform — with no check on whether the customer's *current subscription plan* actually permits ad integration at all. TFAConnect (ENG-1275) was flagged and the alert canceled as a false positive; her onboarding-time intent was stale relative to her plan, and the alert would recur every renewal cycle unfixed.

## What this fixes (after)
Before firing, the cron now consults `subscriptionService.getAllowedConnectedAccounts(userId)` and skips the user when none of `meta`/`google_ads`/`linkedin_ads` are in their plan's `allowedConnectedAccounts`. Unrestricted plans (`allowedConnectedAccounts` undefined or `['*']`) resolve through the same helper to the full platform list (which includes `meta` and `google_ads`), so they're evaluated exactly as before — no regression to the true-positive case.

## Complexity ledger
- Net lines: +36 (backend/src/cron/renewalIntegrationHealthCron.ts: +31/-5)
- Moving parts added: one new pure async helper (`hasAdIntegrationEntitlement`) and one new import of an existing service function. No new tables, no new cron, no schema change, no new dependency.
- Moving parts removed: none — this closes a gap in existing logic rather than replacing a mechanism.
- Behavior-preserving for every case that already fires correctly today (criteria 2 & 3 below); the only behavior delta is the new false-positive suppression (criterion 1).

## How to test
1. In a Node REPL or test file, import `runRenewalIntegrationHealthCheck` from `backend/src/cron/renewalIntegrationHealthCron.ts`.
2. Mock `userDb.scanWithFilter` to return a TFAConnect-shaped user: `subscription_status: 'active'`, `current_period_end` within 14 days, `emmaHelpInterests: ['paid_ads']`, `connected_accounts: []`.
3. Mock `subscriptionService.getAllowedConnectedAccounts` to resolve `['linkedin', 'gmail', 'calendly']` (no ad platforms) for that user.
4. Run the check.
   **Expected**: `summary.flagged === 0`, `sendAgentModeOncallAlert` not called.
5. Repeat with the mock resolving `['meta', 'gmail']` instead.
   **Expected**: `summary.flagged === 1`, alert fires — true positive preserved.

## Edge cases to check
- `allowedConnectedAccounts` is an empty array `[]` — `subscriptionService.getAllowedConnectedAccounts` already treats this as unrestricted (falls back to the full platform list), so it's covered by the existing "unrestricted" behavior, not a new branch in this PR.
- `linkedin_ads` is a valid `PlatformType` but is absent from `subscriptionService.getAllAvailableConnectedAccounts()`'s master list — a pre-existing, out-of-scope gap. This means an *explicitly unrestricted* plan is still correctly treated as ad-entitled only because `meta`/`google_ads` are present in that master list; a plan that somehow listed only `linkedin_ads` as its sole ad platform would still work correctly since a restricted plan's raw array is returned unmodified by `getAllowedConnectedAccounts`.
- `getAllowedConnectedAccounts` itself fails open (catches its own errors and falls back to the full/unrestricted list) — so an entitlement-lookup failure never silently suppresses a real true-positive alert.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/renewalIntegrationHealthCron.test.ts` → 11 passed, 0 failed (8 pre-existing + 3 new ENG-1541 fixtures)
- `npm run typecheck` (backend): clean
- Confirmed red-then-green: the TFAConnect-shaped fixture failed (`Expected: 0, Received: 1`) before the fix, all 11 passed after
- Regression check: `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/subscriptionService.test.ts` → 45 passed, 0 failed (entitlement helper's dependency untouched)
- Tested as: no live account needed — this is a pure backend cron unit-testable via mocks (`userDb`, `sendAgentModeOncallAlert`, `subscriptionService.getAllowedConnectedAccounts` all mocked)

## Behavioral assertions verified
1. **A user whose plan's `allowedConnectedAccounts` excludes all of `meta`/`google_ads`/`linkedin_ads` does NOT get flagged, even with no connected ad platform and a renewal in the lookahead window.** → `regression: ad entitlement gates renewal health (ENG-1541) › does not flag the TFAConnect-shaped account...` (renewalIntegrationHealthCron.test.ts)
2. **A user whose plan permits ad integration but has no connected/non-expired ad platform account STILL gets flagged exactly as today.** → `...still flags a paid-ads customer with no ad account connected when their plan explicitly permits ad integration (no regression)`
3. **A user with an unrestricted plan (`allowedConnectedAccounts` undefined or `['*']`) is evaluated exactly as today.** → `...still flags an unrestricted-plan customer with no ad account connected (allowedConnectedAccounts undefined/["*"])`, plus all 8 pre-existing tests continue to pass unmodified (they default to the unrestricted mock, so they exercise the "evaluated exactly as today" path implicitly on every pre-existing case)
4. **Test coverage includes the TFAConnect-shaped case (real regression fixture, not just synthetic).** → same TFAConnect test above uses her real email (`jennifer.sun@tfaconnect.com`) and the exact shape from the incident (paid-ads intent selected, no connection, renewal imminent, plan excludes ads)

title: ENG-1527: the creative-addition gate now fails CLOSED on an unresolved parent status
body:
## The inverted rationale

Both creative routes swallowed every gate failure and created the creative anyway:

```js
} catch (gateErr) {
  console.error('[ENG-335] AD_CREATE creative-addition gate lookup failed; proceeding (RESUME/ENABLE gate still guards launch):', gateErr);
}
```

The stated reason was defence-in-depth — *the RESUME / UPDATE→ENABLED gate is the hard guarantee behind this one.*

**That is backwards for the only case this gate covers.** `enforceGoogleAdsCreativeAdditionGate` short-circuits unless the parent is `ENABLED`, so it matters *exclusively* when the campaign is already live — and an already-live campaign has no future RESUME or UPDATE→ENABLED for the "hard guarantee" to fire on. The creative **is** the launch. It serves paid traffic the moment it is created, and this gate is the only thing in front of it. The second layer being relied on does not exist in this situation.

## Three silent holes

| path | old behaviour |
|---|---|
| parent lookup throws | caught → creative created, unchecked |
| parent lookup returns nothing | `if (parent)` skipped the gate entirely — **no check ran and nothing was logged** |
| gate throws fetching the landing page | caught → creative created, unchecked |

The middle one is the quietest: it never even reached a `catch`, so there was no error line to notice.

## What changed

A status we could not determine is treated as **possibly-ENABLED and refused**, and the attempt is recorded on the run record so the audit trail shows a decision rather than a gap.

Fail-closed deliberately does **not** become fail-always:

- a status confirmed to be anything other than `ENABLED` still proceeds untouched — there is no launch to guard, and ordinary staging work must not break on a flaky lookup;
- an **approved override** still gets through. It is a user's disclosed decision to accept this exact risk, so the refusal keeps a recovery path instead of being a dead end. It still has to be a real approval — the first call halts and issues the token (ENG-1526).

Both call sites now go through one helper. They had drifted into two copies of the same `try`/`catch`, which is precisely how a fix reaches one and not the other.

## Testing

The two `fails open: …` tests asserted the behaviour being corrected; they now assert the opposite. Six added:

- parent lookup returns `null` (the hole that never logged)
- gate throws on an `ENABLED` parent
- **PAUSED parent still proceeds even when the gate would fail** — pins that fail-closed didn't become fail-always
- `getCampaignStatus` returns `null`
- asset-group PAUSED parent proceeds
- approved-override recovery path through an unresolved lookup

The warning-wiring source check no longer pins a specific local variable name — it matches any gate-result variable, since the point is that both call sites capture the warning, not what the local is called.

**28 pass** in `googleAdsLaunchGate`. `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.

## Risk

Behaviour change is intentional and one-directional: creative creation on an *unverifiable* parent now refuses instead of proceeding. Confirmed-not-enabled parents and approved overrides are unaffected.

  - Blocked actions now preserve warnings and measurement results for clearer feedback.

title: fix: re-read leadListId before baking it into a generated capture route (ENG-1543)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)

`deployLandingPage` reads the page's DB record **once**, at function entry, then can sit inside v0
generation + build validation for up to `V0_GENERATION_BUDGET_MS` (20 minutes) before it ever
builds `LIST_BY_PATH` for the generated `app/api/capture/route.ts`. If a lead list is attached via
`PATCH /generated/:id/lead-list` during that window — while `githubRepoUrl` is still unset because
the page is still `generating` — `syncLeadCaptureForPage` silently no-ops (its own comment assumes
"generation injects the capture files itself, with this list already attached"). That assumption
was false whenever the PATCH landed after the entry-time snapshot: the deploy step then baked the
**stale** `leadListId` (or none) into `LIST_BY_PATH`, while DynamoDB already carried the newly
attached, correct one. Nothing ever re-syncs after that point, so the page 422s
`"This page has no lead list configured, so the submission was not saved."` forever, despite a
DB record that looks completely correct.

## What this fixes (after)

`deployLandingPage` re-reads the page's **current** `leadListId` immediately before baking it into
the pushed capture route, instead of trusting the function-entry snapshot. A concurrent attach now
always wins over a stale snapshot. Falls back to the entry snapshot only if the re-read itself comes
back empty (e.g. the page was deleted mid-deploy), so a page that already had a list at entry never
regresses to "no list."

## Complexity ledger

- Net lines: +18 in `v0Service.ts` (one extra `await getLandingPage(...)` call + a doc comment
  explaining the race — no new moving parts: no new table, flag, branch behavior, or dependency).
- Behavior-preserving for every page that was already correct: when `leadListId` doesn't change
  between entry and Step 3 (the overwhelming majority — see audit below), the re-read returns the
  same value and `LIST_BY_PATH` is byte-identical to before.
- One additional DynamoDB `GetItem` per deploy (strongly-consistent-by-default `get`, same call
  shape already used elsewhere in this function) — negligible cost, no schema change.

## How to test

1. In a portal session, start generating a new landing page (`POST /generate`) with no explicit
   `lead_list_id` (auto-provisions a default list).
2. **While the page still shows `status: "generating"`** (before the GitHub repo/Vercel project
   exist), call `PATCH /generated/:id/lead-list` with a **different** lead list's id.
3. Wait for generation to finish (`status: "deployed"`).
4. **Expected**: the page's DB record's `leadListId` matches the list from step 2, AND the deployed
   repo's `app/api/capture/route.ts` `LIST_BY_PATH` map also carries that same list id for the
   page's path — not the auto-provisioned default from step 1.
5. Submit the live form → lead lands in the list from step 2, not the default.

## Edge cases to check

- Page has no `leadListId` at all, at either read → `LIST_BY_PATH` stays `{}` (unchanged, covered
  by a new regression test).
- Re-read returns `null`/page deleted mid-deploy → falls back to the entry snapshot rather than
  wiping a previously-known list.
- Sub-pages sharing a repo: unaffected — this fix only changes how *this page's own* `leadListId`
  is resolved at push time; sibling entries in `LIST_BY_PATH` are still built from
  `record.slug`/`pagePath` exactly as before.

## Test Evidence

- `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts` → **586 passed, 0 failed**
  (full file, includes the 2 new ENG-1543 tests + all existing `deployLandingPage`/capture-injection
  coverage).
- Also ran the full related suite together: `services.v0Service.test.ts`,
  `eng309_310.captureInjection.test.ts`, `eng308.middlewareRuntime.test.ts`,
  `routes.landingPageGeneration.test.ts`, `orgSharedLandingPages.test.ts`,
  `landingPageStaging.test.ts`, `humanEvalActionService.test.ts` → **586 passed / 586 total**, 0
  regressions.
- `npm run typecheck` → clean, no errors.
- New tests added under `describe("ENG-1543 leadListId race", ...)`:
  1. **RED before the fix / GREEN after**: a lead list attached mid-generation (second
     `getLandingPage` call returns a different `leadListId` than the first) is the one baked into
     the pushed `LIST_BY_PATH`, not the stale entry snapshot. Confirmed this test fails against the
     pre-fix code with the exact stale value baked in, and passes after the fix.
  2. Behavior-preserving control: a page with no `leadListId` at any read still deploys with
     `LIST_BY_PATH: Record<string, string> = {}` — proves the fix doesn't change behavior for the
     ENG-309 "no list attached" case.

## Behavioral assertions verified

The issue's acceptance criteria are marked "draft — refine before implementation" (agent-derived).
I kept the underlying intent but want to flag one refinement explicitly: AC1 ("reproduce the
discrepancy … for **this page**") assumed the Kraftersland page itself would reproduce a DB-vs-repo
mismatch on inspection. It does not — see "What was NOT tested" below for the full finding. AC1 is
satisfied for the **failure class** (a real, reproducible DB-vs-repo leadListId mismatch caused by
this exact race), which is what ENG-309/310 were meant to close and evidently didn't fully close;
it is *not* satisfied as "this is definitively why Kraftersland's page 422s today," which the
evidence doesn't support (details below).

1. **AC1 (refined) — reproduce a DB-vs-repo leadListId discrepancy**: reproduced via
   `services.v0Service.test.ts`'s new race test — a concurrent `PATCH /generated/:id/lead-list`
   during the up-to-20-minute generation window is silently absorbed by DynamoDB but not by the
   pushed capture route, pre-fix. Confirmed RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix.
2. **AC2 — regression test/fixture distinct from ENG-309/310's coverage**: added (see Test
   Evidence above); ENG-309/310's existing tests never simulated a concurrent attach racing the
   entry-time snapshot, which is exactly why this class shipped un-caught.
3. **AC3 — audit whether other pages generated since 2026-07-15 share the gap**: ran a read-only
   audit script (`aws dynamodb scan` on `AW-LandingPages` + `gh api` reads of each repo's deployed
   `app/api/capture/route.ts` + `AW-LeadLists` lookups for list validity/`publicAccessEnabled`).
   **Findings** (full output in this PR's description below / attached to the Linear issue):
   - 169 total `AW-LandingPages` records scanned; 20 generated since 2026-07-15 with both
     `leadListId` and `githubRepoUrl` set.
   - **0 pages currently show a live, customer-impacting DB-vs-repo mismatch.**
   - **1 apparent mismatch found** (`ENG190 Prod Verify`, page `880f4040-…`,
     repo `lp-eng287-prod-verify-47f0f129`, path `/eng190-prod-verify`) — confirmed **not a
     customer issue**: this is Harsha's own archived internal QA sub-page from an ENG-190
     production-verification session on 2026-07-27 (`archived: true`, archived 2 minutes after
     creation). `getLandingPagesByOwner` filters out archived pages, so once a sibling sub-page in
     the same shared repo was later synced, `syncLeadCaptureForPage`'s `buildListByPath` correctly
     stopped including this archived page's entry — working as designed, zero customer impact.
   - **Kraftersland's own page (`c60592bd-…`) is in the CLEAN set**: its deployed
     `app/api/capture/route.ts` `LIST_BY_PATH` currently reads
     `{"/": "list_1786380446804_tpp2csmlz"}`, exactly matching the DB record's `leadListId`, and
     that list currently exists with `publicAccessEnabled: true`. Live GET requests to both her
     `deployedUrl` and `customDomainUrl` today correctly set `Set-Cookie: aw_page=%2F`, confirming
     the middleware resolves her page's path correctly too.
   - **0 pages reference an invalid/missing/private lead list** (the ENG-967/hypothesis-(c) class)
     as of this audit.
   - 0 fetch errors, 0 pages missing the capture layer entirely.
4. **AC4 — behavior-preserving for pages that already work**: covered by the second new test
   (empty-`LIST_BY_PATH` control) plus the unchanged 584 pre-existing tests in the same file, all
   still green.

## Files changed

- `backend/src/services/v0Service.ts` — re-read `leadListId` before building `listByPath` in
  `deployLandingPage`'s Step 3 (+18/-1 lines).
- `backend/src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts` — 2 new regression tests under
  `describe("ENG-1543 leadListId race", ...)` (+102 lines).

## What was NOT tested / NOT touched

- **Kraftersland's specific live page (`lp-spokane-cabinets-google-ads-lp-c60592bd`) was
  deliberately NOT touched** — no code push, no redeploy trigger, no lead-list re-attach, no test
  form submission against her live capture endpoint (which would have written a test row into her
  real CRM list). That live remediation is explicitly reserved for **ENG-1542**
  (portal admin session + judgment call, assigned to Harsha).
- **This fix does not, by itself, explain why Kraftersland's page reportedly 422'd live on
  2026-08-24.** Everything I can inspect read-only (DB record, deployed repo content, the
  referenced CRM list's existence + `publicAccessEnabled`, and live `Set-Cookie` behavior on both
  her URLs) is currently **consistent and correct** — the race this PR fixes did not leave a
  footprint on her repo (only 2 commits total, both from generation, and the second one already
  carries the correct list id). Two candidate explanations I could not fully confirm without either
  writing test data into her CRM or auditing infra I don't have access to:
  1. **Timing evidence for hypothesis (c), since resolved**: her lead list's `updatedAt`
     (`2026-08-10T17:04:15Z`) trails the page's own **failed** generation-time smoke test
     (`checkedAt: 2026-08-10T16:57:01Z`, `leadCaptured: false`) by ~7 minutes, and trails
     `claimedCompletionAt` (`16:59:44Z`) by ~5 minutes. That's consistent with the list being
     **private** at generation/smoke-test time (explaining the smoke test's real, contemporaneous
     failure and "0 leads ever" per CS-93) and only flipping to `publicAccessEnabled: true`
     afterward — which would mean the original cause was the ENG-967 private-list class, now
     resolved, rather than an ongoing bug. I could not determine what flipped it public without
     CloudTrail-level access.
  2. **A same-shaped false alarm**: the generated capture route's page-path resolution depends on
     the `aw_page` cookie a real browser page-load sets (Referer is only a fallback). Any
     reproduction that POSTs to `/api/capture` directly — a raw curl/API check, not a real
     browser round-trip — will hit the exact same `"no lead list configured"` 422 for **any**
     generated page, healthy or not, because no cookie or matching Referer is present. I did not
     rule this out because I did not attempt a live POST against her endpoint (see above).
  3. Whether the live Vercel deployment currently serving her domain actually matches the `main`
     branch content I read via GitHub's API (a Vercel-side staleness/promotion issue) — I have no
     way to confirm this without either a live deploy trigger (out of scope here) or Vercel
     dashboard access.
  ENG-1542 is the right place to pin down which of these (if any) is still live today.
- Did not expand scope to also re-validate `publicAccessEnabled` inside `deployLandingPage` itself
  (a plausible follow-up given finding #1 above) — that's a second, separate behavior change beyond
  this issue's leadListId-mismatch scope; flagging it in a comment rather than bundling it in.
- No database/data-plane change: this is a read-before-use ordering fix in application code against
  the existing `AW-LandingPages` schema/contract — no migration, no schema change, no bulk mutation.
- No customer-facing copy touched.

## Linear issue

title: ENG-1527: GET /v0/site returns the Google Ads conversion tag
body:
## The gap

`GET /api/landing-pages/v0/site` projected a fixed five fields:

```js
rootPageId, vercelProjectId, githubRepoUrl, gtmContainerId, deployStatus
```

The site record has carried `googleAdsConversionId`, `googleAdsConversionLabel`, `googleAdsCustomerId` and `googleAdsTrackingInstalled` since the tag work landed, and `resolveSiteForCaller` already returns the **whole record** — the data was one line away the entire time. Dropping it meant the only way to see whether a site's conversion tag existed, or whether it was actually installed on the deployed lander, was to read DynamoDB directly.

Same class of gap as a warning that is computed and discarded: the answer exists and nobody downstream can see it. The customer portal consequently had **zero** references to any of these fields (fixed in the paired portal PR).

## `googleAdsTrackingInstalled` is normalised

Passed through as `=== true` rather than as possibly-`undefined`. `undefined` means *we never recorded an outcome*, which a UI renders the same as `false` anyway — collapsing it here keeps every consumer from having to decide, and stops "no answer" reading as "installed".

It carries more weight than its Meta sibling. A failed Meta injection degrades to server-side capture via CAPI; Google Ads has **no server-side leg** until ENG-1325, so `false` means the lander shipped with no Google measurement at all — exactly what RULE 7.5 refuses a launch over.

A site with no tag still reports none: the ids stay absent from the response rather than being invented as empty strings.

## Testing

The existing exact-match `toEqual` assertion is updated, plus three added:

- a site with a full tag returns id, label, customer id, and `installed: true`
- a site with an id but no recorded outcome returns `installed: false`
- a site with no tag returns neither id nor label, and `installed: false`

**22 pass** in `routes.landingPages.site`. `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.

## Risk

Additive to a response body. No field removed, no field renamed, no behaviour change for existing consumers.

title: [needs human] Scope get_lead_details circuit breaker by list_id + lead_id (ENG-969)
body:
**Bug:** get_lead_details hard-blocked for the rest of a run after 3 not-found errors, even when later calls used corrected, valid list_id + lead_id arguments (ENG-969).

**Root cause:** The Agent Tool Gateway's repeated-failure breaker keys failures by (toolName, argsScope, errorHead). get_lead_details had no per-argument scoping, so its argsScope was always ''. Three not-found results for three different (list_id, lead_id) pairs therefore shared one bucket and tripped the breaker at threshold 3, blocking every subsequent call in the run regardless of arguments — confirmed against production session 6082779b-f9f1-4e38-a8eb-34abbc3da419, where leads legitimately belonged to a different list.

**Fix:** Added a leadDetailsFailureScope() scope function (mirroring the existing per-recipient scoping for linkedin_outreach from ENG-182/ENG-313) that keys get_lead_details failures by `list_id|lead_id`. A not-found for one lead no longer blocks a call for a different lead; repeated failures on the exact same lead still trip the breaker as before.

**Verification:** Added a failing-then-passing unit test reproducing the exact scenario (3 different not-found leads followed by a valid corrected call), plus a regression test confirming the breaker still trips on repeated failures for the *same* lead. Full gateway test suite and backend typecheck both pass.

title: [needs human] Stop discarding generated CSV data in perform_data_analysis (ENG-1295)
body:
Confirmed root cause from prod: CloudWatch logs for session d789c175 (the exact session cited in ENG-1295) show `AgentMode: performDataAnalysis skipping non-image inlineData with mimeType=text/csv` firing on every one of that session's perform_data_analysis calls. Gemini's code-execution sandbox (gemini-3.5-flash) returns generated tabular output (e.g. a `df.to_csv()` write) as an `inlineData`/`inline_data` part with `mimeType: text/csv`, not via stdout/codeExecutionResult. The existing code treated ANY non-image inlineData as presumed Vega-Lite chart JSON and silently dropped it, so the tool's returned `analysis` contained only the model's separate narrative text summary — disconnected from the real computed numbers. That's exactly the failure mode described in the ticket: confident, fabricated ad-group names and contradictory counts between calls.

Fix: in both the camelCase (`inlineData`) and snake_case (`inline_data`) branches of `performDataAnalysis` (backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts), a `text/csv` mimeType is now decoded and appended to the result as `**Computed Data:**` (and `codeExecuted` is set true), instead of being discarded. Non-CSV, non-image mimeTypes (e.g. `application/json` Vega-Lite specs) are still skipped as before.

Verification: added a regression test reproducing the exact prod scenario (narrative text + inlineData text/csv) — confirmed it fails against the old code (CSV dropped, `codeExecuted` false) and passes after the fix (CSV content present in `analysis`, `codeExecuted` true). title: fix: __other_skills__ excluding tools claimed by unpublished skills (ENG-1237)
body:
**Bug:** install_skills(['__other_skills__']) returned "The requested skills are not available with your current subscription" for a Super Premium account, blocking all access to the landing-page read/CRUD tools (list_landing_pages, get_landing_page, update_landing_page_context, enable_lead_list_public_access), which are only reachable via the __other_skills__ bundle.

**Root cause:** Confirmed via prod DB (subscription_types setting, AW-Users, AW-Organizations) that subscription entitlement was never the issue — Super Premium's allowedSkills already includes __other_skills__, and none of its 50 named skills claim any landing-page tool. Prod CloudWatch logs for the exact failing request showed `installedSkills: 0, added: 0`, pointing at agentModeService.getUnassociatedTools() returning zero tools. That function is documented to exclude tools 'associated with any published skill', but its callers pass a catalog that also mixes in unpublished private/org-shared skills (via loadAuthorizedSkillCatalog's org-sharing bypass). An unpublished draft skill claiming a tool name was silently excluding it from the shared __other_skills__ bundle for the whole org, until nothing remained unclaimed — at which point the bundle disappears from the catalog entirely and install_skills reports it as a subscription problem.

**Fix:** getUnassociatedTools() now only counts skills with isPublished === true when computing which tools are already claimed, matching its documented contract.

title: [needs human] Don't penalize declining a guard-blocked punctuation-only reply (ENG-1164)
body:
ENG-1054's shipped guard (isUnusableSynthesis in synthesisResidue.ts) correctly discards a final reply whose entire content is JSON/punctuation debris like '}]', because that exact shape previously shipped as mangled, unfinished synthesis in production. A QA serialization-test session (1926c237) instructed the assistant to reply with exactly '}]' — the guard blocked it as designed, the retry explained what actually ran, and all three judges then scored the session 2/2/2 for 'failing to adhere to the strict formatting constraint', even though dataAccuracy was 5 across all three judges (nothing fabricated, the tool call succeeded). This is a scoring-validity conflict: the harness's pass condition is literally the string the guard exists to reject, so it can never pass while the guard is active, and it will recur on every future serialization-test session.

Fix: added OUTPUT_INTEGRITY_GUARD_CLAUSE to sessionScoringService.ts, appended to the scoring system prompt at call time (same ENG-392-safe pattern as NO_TASK_JUDGMENT_CLAUSE / PUBLISH_APPROVAL_WITHHOLDING_CLAUSE / FABRICATION_GROUNDING_CLAUSE, since production has a live AW-Settings override and custom judge prompts are user-authored). It tells the judge that declining to emit bare punctuation/JSON debris as an entire reply — when the underlying task was actually completed — is correct, guard-required behavior, not a formatting defect, while still treating a genuinely complete JSON value (e.g. '{}', '[]') as a legitimate answer.

Verified via a new TDD test file (sessionScoring.outputIntegrityGuard.test.ts) that first failed (clause didn't exist / wasn't appended) and now passes after the fix, plus confirmed no regressions in the neighboring clause tests and the main sessionScoring test suite.

title: [needs human] Retry and add context to MCP self-call network failures (ENG-1189)
body:
**Bug:** In production session 2318c99c-6b45-47ae-95cb-12fe85939c8d, manage_scheduled_chat failed 3 times in a row with the bare error 'fetch failed', permanently blocking a LinkedIn/X posting-schedule update. The agent handled it well (explained the blocker, saved work to memory) but the user's goal was only partially achieved.

**Root cause:** backend/src/mcp/server/httpClient.ts's mcpFetch — the shared HTTP self-call helper every MCP tool (including manage_scheduled_chat) uses to reach the backend REST API — called `fetch()` with only a try/finally (for clearing the timeout), no catch. When the self-call fails at the network layer (e.g. backend mid-restart causing ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET), Node's fetch throws a bare `TypeError: fetch failed`. That error propagated untouched through mcpServerCore.ts's generic `Error: ${error.message}` handler straight to the LLM, with no endpoint, no cause, and no retry.

**Fix:** Added `fetchSelfCallWithRetry`, a small wrapper around the raw fetch() call that: (1) retries up to 3 attempts with exponential backoff, but only for the exact transient network TypeError (confirmed a genuine request timeout throws a distinct AbortError, so this can't mask real timeouts); (2) once retries are exhausted, throws an error including the HTTP method, path, underlying cause (e.g. `ECONNREFUSED: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3001`), and a correlation id for log grepping, instead of the bare 'fetch failed'.

**Verified:** Wrote failing tests first reproducing the bare-'fetch failed'-with-no-retry behavior against a mocked global.fetch throwing undici's exact TypeError shape; confirmed they failed pre-fix and pass post-fix. Also manually confirmed (via a standalone Node script) the exact error shapes: TypeError('fetch failed') with a .cause for connection failures vs. a distinct AbortError for legitimate timeouts, to make sure the retry gate can't swallow real timeouts.

---

title: ENG-1362: surface Google's test_account flag instead of trusting the account name
body:
Backend half of ENG-1362. Pairs with **AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#(portal PR)**.

## The problem

A connected Google Ads account is descriptively named **"Test"** and has `customer.test_account = false`. It is a real, billable, ENABLED leaf account — anything enabled in it spends real INR. Re-verified live 2026-08-25:

| customer id | descriptive_name | test_account | manager | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2883029950 | AgentWeb | `false` | false | ENABLED |
| 3413286111 | **Test** | **`false`** | false | ENABLED |

Nothing surfaced the difference. `list_connected_accounts` returned, verbatim:

```json
{ "account_name": "Test", "account_type": "google_ads", "currency": "INR",
  "customer_id": "3413286111", "id": "3413286111",
  "is_active": true, "platform": "google_ads" }
```

So an agent told to *"use the test account"* had the string `"Test"` and nothing else. Google's own mechanism — `customer.test_account`, which guarantees an account cannot serve ads and cannot spend — was queryable all along and simply never read.

## Captured at the source, for free

Account discovery already queries `customer` and `customer_client`. The flag costs **one extra field on two existing SELECTs** and no additional API calls. Verified the field exists against the live API before writing any of this:

```
SELECT customer_client.id, customer_client.descriptive_name, customer_client.test_account …
-> { "descriptiveName": "AgentWeb", "id": "2883029950", "testAccount": false }
```

## The semantics are the point

```
test_account true       -> Google guarantees no spend
test_account false      -> real money
never recorded / null   -> real money
```

`can_spend` clears **only** on an affirmative `true`, and is derived in one shared helper rather than at each call site — two copies of "does true mean safe" is how one of them eventually stops meaning it. A fallback that let *"we never checked"* read as *"cannot spend"* would rebuild the original bug somewhere new.

Accounts connected before this resolve live via `googleAdsService.isTestAccount`, process-cached because the flag is immutable, and **never cached on failure** so a transient error cannot pin an account as unknown.

Both tool descriptions now state plainly that the account NAME is not a safety property, and that a fully billable account named "Test" is connected right now.

## Deliberately not a gate

Every real customer account is `test_account: false` — that is the normal case, not the exception. Refusing writes on it would block all legitimate work. The fix is **visibility**, exactly as the ticket scoped it.

## Testing

9 tests on the shared rule, including that a truthy non-`true` value (`'true'`, `1`, `'yes'`, `{}`) and an absent flag both stay billable, and that the account **name is not an input** — pinned so a future "helpful" name heuristic has to delete a test.

Plus discovery capturing `true`, and defaulting a missing field to `false`. Note the pre-existing fixture in that suite is an account named `"Test Account"` with the flag false — not contrived, it is this ticket's live situation.

Six exact-match hierarchy assertions updated for the additive field. **163 pass** across the two suites; `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.

  - Existing connections can resolve current test-account status when stored information is unavailable.
- **Documentation**

title: ENG-1331 follow-up: fix 4 CodeRabbit findings from PR #2549, including a live false-underclaim bug
body:
## Summary

PR #2549 (ENG-1331) merged before CodeRabbit's review of the final commits finished — its last comment reads "Review failed... The pull request is closed." This PR fixes the 4 findings from that review that were confirmed real against the actual (now-deployed) code, each independently re-verified rather than trusted from the review text alone.

## Fixes

1. **`sinceLastStepBoundary` flags truthful same-turn completions as false** (🔴 most severe — confirmed live in production before this fix). When a step's own assets are immediately followed by its own successful `set_work_plan_status` close (the normal shape in an AUTOCOMPLETE turn), the old "since the last boundary" rule sliced to nothing, so `detectFalseCompletionClaim` read `actual=0` on a truthful "all N done" claim and appended a false correction. Verified before fixing:
   ```
   12 successful screenshots -> set_work_plan_status succeeds -> "all 12 done" (truthful)
   old code: {"claimed":12,"actual":0}  <- appended a false correction to a TRUE claim
   ```
   Fix: when the last successful boundary is the final ledger entry (nothing ran after it), scope to since the *previous* boundary instead — the closing synthesis is necessarily describing the work that boundary just closed. All 71 pre-existing tests still pass unmodified (no regression to the original ENG-1188 masking-prevention behavior); 3 new tests pin the fix.

2. **Backfill script: exit code always 0, even on abort.** `process.exit(0)` in the runner overrode `process.exitCode = 1` set on the "wrong template found" abort path — automation checking exit status couldn't detect an abort that wrote nothing.

3. **Backfill script: stale `expectedAssetCountTools` never cleared.** A conditional spread only ever added the field, never removed a pre-existing value when a step's target has no tools list. Latent (not triggered by the live template today), fixed with an explicit `delete`.

4. **Whitespace-only tool names pass validation.** `entry !== ''` didn't trim, so `" "` persisted as an unmatchable "valid" tool name. Now trimmed and rejected if empty after trimming.

## Not included

Two other CodeRabbit findings from the same review were checked and are **not** new bugs:
- The `Math.max`-vs-sum tradeoff on the default (no-`expectedAssetCountTools`) path — already disclosed as a deliberate, accepted tradeoff before this PR existed; not evidenced on the live template, which now opts into precise counting via `expectedAssetCountTools`.
- A "TypeScript validation failed" claim — does not reproduce; `npm run typecheck` is clean on both branches.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] All 788 tests in the ENG-1331 blast-radius suite pass (35 files, spanning every method/export touched by #2549 and this follow-up)
- [x] Regression-proved the `sinceLastStepBoundary` fix (reverted, confirmed the old test suite still would have passed — i.e. no existing test caught this — then added 3 new tests that do)
- [x] Regression-proved the exit-code fix (temporarily reverted `process.exitCode = 1`, confirmed the new tests fail; restored, confirmed they pass)

title: feat(ads): ENG-916 make the metrics store platform-general + add the account-day row
body:
Follow-up to #2334. Two changes that **must land before the first production write** — the table does not exist in production yet (ENG-1066 is unstarted), so both are free today and a data-plane migration tomorrow.

## 1. The store is no longer Meta-specific

`AW-MetaAdsMetricsSnapshots` → `AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots`, HASH `campaignId` → `entityKey` (`platform#accountId#campaignId`).

**Storage and everything reading it are shared** across Meta, Google Ads and LinkedIn Ads. **Ingestion deliberately is not** — the three disagree on nearly everything an ingestion path cares about:

| | Meta | Google Ads | LinkedIn |
|---|---|---|---|
| spend | `spend` decimal string | `cost_micros` ÷ 1e6 | `costInLocalCurrency` |
| pagination | cursor | page token | **none**, 15k element cap |
| daily retention | ~37 months | long | **6 months** |
| **settling window** | **28 days** | **up to 90** | near-real-time |

One cron with one settling window would be wrong for two of the three. So each platform gets its own adapter writing into one shared shape. This cron is now the Meta adapter.

### Three fields recorded rather than inferred — each verified against a live connected account

- **`currency`** — varies *between accounts of the same user*. mvarma holds Meta ad accounts in **INR and USD** simultaneously. A mis-stated currency once reported a $5,000 deal as ₹5,000: ~80× off, silently.
- **`parentAccountId`** — Google's MCC hierarchy is real here: customer `2883029950` sits under manager `2737828986`, and both are needed to re-query the account. Null for Meta/LinkedIn.
- **`reportingTimezone`** — Meta buckets dates in the **ad account's** timezone, Google in `customer.time_zone`, ours are UTC. The same `date` string can cover different 24-hour windows per platform. Recorded, not normalised: a consumer must be able to decide, and it can't if we discarded the offset. No connected account stores this, so it's fetched at ingest.

Plus **`dataQuality`**, because LinkedIn's docs state their metrics are approximate and explicitly warn that summing daily rows ≠ the period total — exactly what this store invites.

Rate metrics move into a `platformMetrics` bag (Meta: ctr/cpm/frequency; Google: averageCpc, no frequency; LinkedIn: neither).

## 2. The account-day row — closes a Greptile P1 and the sum hazard

Both were the same missing record. Day-level data had nowhere to live, so it was forced onto campaign rows:

- a date where the platform reported **no campaign activity wrote no row at all**, making a gap indistinguishable from *"the cron never ran"* (the [unresolved P1 on #2334](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/2334))
- `unattributedLeadCount` was stamped on **every** campaign row, so summing N rows reported **N× the real figure** — the same over-count shape as `spendDuringAbsence` in the tracking monitor

One `account_day` row per account per date, written **always** including when there are no campaigns, carrying `campaignsReported` (**zero is a measurement; no row is an absence**) and `unattributedLeadCount`, which is removed from campaign rows entirely — deleting the trap beats documenting it.

Readers keep their meaning: `getSnapshotsByUserDateRange` still returns the campaign series only, with `getAccountDaySnapshots` alongside, so a caller asking for campaign metrics can never silently receive a different row type.

## Verification

**24 tests green, typecheck clean.** Red-checked by mutation — making the day-row write conditional, stamping `unattributedLeadCount` back onto campaign rows, and dropping currency/timezone each fail exactly the tests that name them.

⚠ **CI runs no tests on this repo** (ENG-1463 deleted both backend jobs; `Backend build` is `tsc` excluding tests). The local suite plus the red-checks are the whole evidence base.

## Follow-ups, deliberately not here

No Google or LinkedIn adapter and no new crons — speculative until those platforms are in scope. This PR only buys the option while the name and key are still free. ENG-1066 needs its description updated to name the new table.

title: fix(ads): ENG-916 join leads on campaign id THEN name — measured, not assumed
body:
The metrics store's join assumed a lead's `utm_campaign` equals the Meta campaign id. I checked that against the real managed accounts — read-only Graph pull of each account's ACTIVE ads (`creative{url_tags,link_url,object_story_spec,asset_feed_spec}`) — and **it does not hold.**

| Account | ACTIVE ads | carry `utm_campaign` | carry `{{campaign.id}}` | what they actually carry |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Haven | 9 | 3 | **3** | 6 of 9 have **empty `url_tags`** |
| Every.io | 2 | 1 | 0 | `utm_campaign=Post:+"…"` — a boosted-post title |
| **Phoenix** | 46 | 46 | **0** | **`{{campaign.name}}`, not `.id`** |

**Phoenix is the decisive case:** every live ad *is* tagged, just with the campaign name — so an id-only join misses **100%** of the portfolio's biggest spender (~$5.6k/7d).

## The fix

`campaign_name` already comes back in the same insights response, so matching it as a fallback costs **no extra API calls and no ad changes**, and takes Phoenix from structurally unjoinable to joining today. Id is tried first because it's exact; name is a convention.

**The alternative would have been worse.** Retagging ads to `{{campaign.id}}` is per-ad and manual, *and* swaps the creative — which **resets Meta's learning phase**. 46 live ads on a paying client, each resetting learning, to fix a reporting join.

## Two details that are deliberate

**Ambiguous names are excluded, not guessed.** Meta permits two campaigns to share a name; a lead tagged with a duplicated name can't be attributed to either without inventing a fact. Those names are dropped from the map, so the leads land in `unattributedLeadCount` — visibly uncounted rather than silently misattributed.

**`campaignNameKeys()` handles the spellings the macro can arrive as** (raw, plus-decoded, percent-decoded). `decodeURIComponent` **throws** on a lone `%`, which is ordinary in hand-written ad URLs, so a failure falls back to the raw value rather than dropping the lead. Deliberately **not** case-folded — the macro emits the advertiser's exact name, and folding would let two genuinely different campaigns collide.

## ⚠ This does not close the gap completely

Haven's 6 ads with empty `url_tags` carry no `utm_campaign` at all, so neither key matches. Only real retagging fixes those, at the learning-phase cost above — an advertising decision, not an engineering one.

**There will always be an unattributed floor**, and it must not be read as drift. The `account_day` row's `unattributedLeadCount` is where it shows.

## Verification

**27 tests green, typecheck clean.** Red-checked by mutation — removing the fallback, keeping ambiguous names in the map, and dropping the encoded spellings each fail exactly one test.

⚠ CI runs no tests on this repo (ENG-1463 deleted both backend jobs; `Backend build` is `tsc` excluding tests), so the local suite and red-checks are the evidence base.

Measurement limits: first 50 ads per account, pagination not followed, so ACTIVE counts are lower bounds. RankAI not checked (churned). Findings also posted to ENG-87, whose blocker this answers.

title: Remove the ENG-1268 customer-closure verification gate entirely
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
ENG-1268's customer-closure verification gate required a structured
`<!-- customer-symptom-verification:v1 -->` comment, authored specifically by Harsha's own
Linear account, before ANY customer-reported bug could transition to Done. Yesterday's fixes
(a `harsha-direct/<id>` bypass path, then author binding per a CodeRabbit finding) narrowed
the gate but didn't remove the underlying friction: Anurag and Manan hit the exact same
"Customer resolution blocked" wall again today on ENG-1465/1222/1163/996 — three attempts on
one issue in two minutes, all reverted — because the gate is structurally incapable of being
satisfied by anyone closing their own row, no matter how thoroughly they've verified the fix
in production.

## What this fixes (after)
Removes the gate entirely, per Harsha's direct instruction (live session, 2026-08-25): "i
don't give a shit about closure risk anymore its annoying, torch it." A customer-reported bug
transitioning into Done now fires the resolve bridge exactly like any other issue — no comment
lookup, no verification requirement, no reopen-and-block.

## Complexity ledger
-337 net lines. Deletes `customerClosureVerification.ts` outright (its only consumer was this
gate). Reverts the `IssueCommentDetail.authorId` field and the `user { id }` GraphQL selection
in `getIssueCommentsDetailed` — both existed solely to serve this check, now unused. Zero new
abstractions, one fewer service file, one less GraphQL field fetched per comment page.

## Scope note
This removes ONLY the ENG-1268 webhook. It does not touch `pm-guard.py`'s protections (a
different concern — foreign-row reassignment/label safety, unrelated to customer comms) or the
closure-reconciler's separate money-risk / customer-notification holds (an LLM-governed loop,
not code, and not what today's friction was about — those remain Harsha's own review gate for
things like Google Ads bidding changes, ad spend, GA4 signal delivery).

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/integrations.linearWebhook.test.ts`
2. **Expected**: 25 passed.
3. Manually: transition any `Bug` + `Customer Reported` Linear issue to Done. Expect it to
   stick immediately — no revert, no "Customer resolution blocked" comment, `notifyCanonicalResolved` fires.

## Edge cases to check
- A customer-reported bug with zero comments at all still transitions through (previously this
  was the most common block reason).
- A customer-reported bug whose only comment says "Fixed in PR #123" (a code-deployment claim,
  not customer-symptom proof) now also transitions through — that distinction no longer exists.
- Non-customer-reported bugs are unaffected — they never went through the gate in the first
  place, and still don't.

## Test Evidence
- `npx jest src/__tests__/integrations.linearWebhook.test.ts` → 25 passed, 0 failed (down from
