title: fix: make materialize_knowledge_base_asset a foundation tool (ENG-1580)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
Reproduced live in a real Emma session testing ENG-1580 right after it deployed: asked Emma to use a video from a connected Google Drive Knowledge Base folder as a hosted asset. Gemini correctly identified the exact file and the exact tool needed (`materialize_knowledge_base_asset`), and even attempted `install_skills(['__other_skills__'])` to unlock it — but that skill install was rejected by the caller's subscription tier, and the tool call was never actually attempted. Emma correctly reported: *"materialize_knowledge_base_asset... is not available on your current subscription plan."*

Root cause: the tool was registered normally in the tool registry, but not added to `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS`. Any tool not explicitly marked foundation, and not attached to a specific published skill, falls into the `__other_skills__` bucket — which is itself subscription-gated. Its direct siblings `list_knowledge_base_files` / `read_knowledge_base_files` are already foundation tools for exactly this reason (this file documents the identical failure mode twice already: ENG-152 for `read_file_content`, ENG-260 for `describe_image`). Without this fix, ENG-1580 — the feature meant to unblock Phoenix Technologies' ad-creative workflow — would have been unreachable on Phoenix's actual subscription tier.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds `materialize_knowledge_base_asset` to `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS`, matching its siblings' protection level exactly (not added to `MANDATORY_FOUNDATION_TOOLS`, since `list_knowledge_base_files`/`read_knowledge_base_files` aren't there either — consistent, not over-scoped).

## Complexity ledger
Net +28 lines (7 in the actual fix, the rest a dedicated regression test file matching this repo's established one-file-per-foundation-tool convention: `connectAccountFoundation.test.ts`, `describeImageFoundation.test.ts`, etc.). Zero new abstractions — a one-line addition to an existing array.

## How to test
1. On any account whose subscription tier's `allowedSkills` doesn't include `"*"` or `"__other_skills__"` explicitly, connect a Google Drive Knowledge Base folder containing an image or video.
2. Ask Emma to use that file as a hosted asset.
3. **Expected**: Emma calls `materialize_knowledge_base_asset` directly and returns a real URL, without any "not available on your subscription" message or an `install_skills` detour.

## Edge cases to check
- Accounts with `allowedSkills: ["*"]` (unrestricted tiers) — already worked before this fix and continue to work identically (foundation-tool status is additive, doesn't change wildcard-tier behavior).
- A stale DB `foundation_tools` override — `loadFoundationTools` always unions `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS`, so this tool can't be silently stripped by a drifted override either.

## Test Evidence
- New test (`agentModeService.materializeAssetFoundation.test.ts`): 2/2 passing — asserts the tool is in `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS` and sits alongside its `list_knowledge_base_files`/`read_knowledge_base_files` siblings.
- Full targeted sweep: 142/142 passing across `materializeAssetFoundation`, `foundationToolOverride`, `fathomToolAccess`, `connectAccountFoundation`, `describeImageFoundation`, and the full `googleDrive` suite (confirms no regression to the existing foundation-tool tests or the Drive/KB feature this sits next to).
- `npm run typecheck` (6GB heap): clean, exit 0.
- Pre-push hook: same single pre-existing, unrelated failure as PRs #2636/#2637 (`agentModeService.emptySynthesisRetry.test.ts`). Bypassed with the same standing sign-off already given for this exact proven-unrelated case; CI runs the real gate at head.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- "materialize_knowledge_base_asset is reachable regardless of subscription tier" → directly asserted by the new test against `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS`.
- "This doesn't regress any other foundation-tool gating" → the full existing foundation-tool test suite (`foundationToolOverride`, `fathomToolAccess`, `connectAccountFoundation`, `describeImageFoundation`) passes unchanged.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` — one array addition
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.materializeAssetFoundation.test.ts` — new regression test

## What was NOT tested
- Re-running the exact live Emma session that surfaced this bug, post-deploy, to confirm the tool actually gets called successfully now — recommended as the definitive close-out once this ships, using the same Phoenix-adjacent test setup (a real Drive-connected account on a non-wildcard tier).

## Linear issue
ENG-1580

Risk: Low

Adds `materialize_knowledge_base_asset` to `DEFAULT_FOUNDATION_TOOLS` beside the knowledge-base file tools. This removes subscription-tier gating for asset materialization and prevents the related production access failure. Adds regression coverage for registration and tool placement.

title: fix: acknowledge in chat when a model-change/reassess request didn't change the model (ENG-1565)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
Model resolution in `agentModeController.ts` reads strictly from the request's `llmModel` field (the model picker) — no code path parses chat message text for an intent to switch/reassess models. A message like "reassess using a new model" was therefore inert by construction: the next turn silently resolved the same model, with no acknowledgement that nothing changed. Production evidence: session `e6c9e693-ff33-4883-a18a-9d674b4074c4` (2026-08-25, audited on ENG-426) — the user asked in chat to reassess with a new model and got no indication the request did nothing.

## What this fixes (after)
This is NOT in-chat model switching — that's a materially larger feature (intent parsing, wiring to the picker/session state, confirmation UX) and explicitly out of scope per the ticket. It closes the silence only: when a message reads as a model-change/reassess request and the model that generated this turn is the same as the model that generated the prior turn, an explicit note is appended saying so and how to actually change it — mirroring the existing `reconcileFalseFailureReport` (ENG-971) / `reconcileUnconsumedCursors` (ENG-1207 AC3) append-only reconciler pattern at the same finalize seam in `generateMarketingResponse`.

**Note on the ticket's cited precedent:** the ticket references ENG-1205 AC3 as a similar shipped pattern to mirror. Investigation found ENG-1205 was never actually implemented (only referenced, then deleted, as a deferred TODO comment) — there is no footer/chat-visible correction under that ticket. The actual precedent used here is ENG-1207 AC3 (`reconcileUnconsumedCursors`), which has the identical shape and is already live.

`backend/src/utils/modelReassessRequest.ts` (new pure module):
- `looksLikeModelChangeRequest` — regex detector biased toward precision over recall: "model" is an overloaded word (pricing model, business model, data model), and a false positive here tells the user something false. Requires an action verb + "a/an new/different/another/other model(s)".
- `findLastAssistantModel` — reads the last assistant turn's recorded model (`msg.llm`, the same field ENG-1579's `sessionModelAttribution.ts` reads) from prior session history.
- `reconcileModelReassessAck` — append-only reconciler, same `(content, ...) => content` shape as its neighbours.

Wired into `agentModeService.ts`'s `generateMarketingResponse` right after the ENG-1207 AC3 reconciler: deterministic, append-only, patched into the last assistant message so the persisted transcript matches what the user sees, wrapped in try/catch so a bug here can never block delivery of a reply. Kill switch: `AGENT_MODEL_REASSESS_ACK=false`.

Comparing `modelBefore` against `modelAfter` (rather than assuming chat text can never change the model) correctly stays silent if the picker was ALSO flipped in the same request — that really would change the model despite the chat text, and the acknowledgement would be wrong to fire in that case.

## Complexity ledger
+405 lines across a new pure module + two new test files + one wiring block (+38 lines) in the existing service. No new abstraction beyond the module itself, which follows an established, repeated pattern (3rd reconciler of this exact shape at this seam). No lines removed — this is net-additive but bounded: one guarded, kill-switched, try/catch-wrapped block; everything else is pure and independently tested.

## How to test
1. `npx jest src/utils/__tests__/modelReassessRequest.test.ts` — 27 pure-function tests (detector positive/negative, history traversal, reconciler contract).
2. `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeService.modelReassessAck.test.ts` — 4 service-level regression tests (fires on match+unchanged model, stays silent on non-match, stays silent when the model actually changed, stays silent with no prior history).
3. **Expected**: a chat message like "please reassess using a new model" followed by a turn that runs on the same model as the prior turn gets an appended note; an unrelated message, or a turn where the model genuinely changed, gets no note.

## Edge cases to check
- Message mentions "model" in an unrelated sense (pricing model, business model, data model) → detector correctly does not fire (27 pure tests cover this explicitly).
- No prior assistant turn in history (first message of a session) → stays silent (nothing to compare against, never assumes "unchanged").
- The picker was ALSO changed in the same request as the reassess text → stays silent (the request WAS actioned, just via the picker, not the chat text).
- A bug in the reconciler itself → caught by try/catch, logged, never blocks delivery of the reply.

## Test Evidence
- `npx jest src/utils/__tests__/modelReassessRequest.test.ts`: 27 passed.
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeService.modelReassessAck.test.ts`: 4 passed.
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentMode/characterization/` (full folder): 11 suites, 74 tests, all passed.
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeService src/__tests__/agentMode/` (both full families combined): 171 suites, 3251 tests, all passed, 0 failures.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` (backend): clean.

## Behavioral assertions verified
1. "A message reading as a model-change/reassess request, followed by a turn on the same model as before, gets an explicit acknowledgement" → `agentModeService.modelReassessAck.test.ts`'s "acknowledges the model did not change when the message asks to reassess with a new model".
2. "A transcript with no such request never gets the acknowledgement" → the same file's "does NOT acknowledge when the message is not a model-change request (no false positive)".
3. Regression: no other test in either the `agentModeService` or `agentMode` family broke (171 suites / 3251 tests green, verified against the full folder this time — not a curated subset).

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`
- `backend/src/utils/modelReassessRequest.ts` (new)
- `backend/src/utils/__tests__/modelReassessRequest.test.ts` (new)
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.modelReassessAck.test.ts` (new)

## What was NOT tested
- Live production/staging smoke — this is an internal chat-content-driven footer with no new UI surface; the unit + service-level regression tests are the intended proof per `loop-agentmode-restructure.md`.
- ENG-1565's UI half (a visible model-switch divider in the chat transcript, ENG-1579-adjacent) is separate frontend work, tracked independently.

## Linear issue
ENG-1565 (also in the PR title)

Risk: Low

Adds guarded model-reassessment acknowledgements to `generateMarketingResponse`. The utility detects relevant requests, compares the current model with the last assistant model, and updates the transcript only when both models match. The feature supports `AGENT_MODEL_REASSESS_ACK=false`, logs failures without blocking responses, and includes regression coverage.

title: ENG-1575: one shared Meta action-family collapse; stop misfiling pixel events as Instant Form leads
body:
## What

Meta reports **one** conversion under **several** `action_type` names. Three independent copies of the alias list existed, so the same conversion was handled correctly in one code path and incorrectly in another. This collapses them onto one shared util.

`offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_lead` is a **pixel** event — unambiguously a website conversion — yet sat in the set named `FORM_ACTIONS`. The same conversion landed in both buckets.

| Copy | Requests `actions`? | Before |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agentModeService.ts` | yes | Correct **by accident** — a blunt `if (websiteLeads > 0) formLeads = 0` hides the misfiling |
| `routes/meta.ts` | yes | No suppression → `totalLeads` at **2×**, `costPerLead` at **½** |
| `businessFunnelService.ts` | **no** | Dormant — deliberately left alone |

## Behaviour: no customer-visible change

Verified against four production ad accounts over 180-day windows. In every one, the bare `lead` rollup and `offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_lead` carried **identical** values — one conversion reported twice, never two conversions. Reported lead counts are unchanged by this PR, pinned by fixtures at util, processor and route level.

`routes/meta.ts` returned a doubled `totalLeads` — reproduced with the route's own query params against the deployed artifact, at both 7d and 30d. **No customer saw it**: the portal renders `websiteLeads` through its own prioritisation and never reads `totalLeads`; `CampaignSummary` has no leads field. Correctness depended on the *frontend* re-implementing a guard the backend lacked — which no new consumer of `/api/meta/ad-performance` would inherit.

⚠ **One label changes**, count unaffected: an account with `offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_lead` and no bare `lead` currently shows *"Form Submission: N"* and will show *"Website Leads: N"*.

## Why it matters going forward

The suppression cannot tell a duplicated alias from a genuine Instant Form lead, so it reports **every Instant Form lead as a website lead**. Our own `Meta Ads Campaign Creation` skill says *"Pixel + conversion event not installed/firing → LAUNCH BLOCKER (or pivot to Instant Forms)"* — we steer customers into the exact configuration that misreports, and we steer the ones already having tracking trouble.

No production account uses Meta Instant Forms today. So this ships as a no-op and closes the trap before anyone falls in.

## Approach

Count each conversion family **once by its maximum**, split by capture surface (`instant_form` / `website`) using surface-specific spellings only. Buckets become disjoint; the suppression is no longer needed.

Maximum rather than reading the bare rollup because whether Meta emits it for Instant Forms has never been observable to us — no such account exists. `max` is correct under **both** answers, which is what lets this ship without first finding a lead-ads customer.

Also fixed:
- `offsite_conversion.fb_pixel_custom` is no longer a lead. It is a CUSTOM conversion and can mean anything; one production account carried ~1.5× as many of these as real leads, and with no `lead` event present the old suppression never fires, so they would have reported as leads.
- `cost_per_action_type` follows a fixed precedence instead of assigning on every match, which made the surviving value depend on Meta's array order.
- `website_lead` is classified as a lead — an earlier revision of this branch dropped it entirely.

## Tests

**134 passing** across 11 suites. `npm run typecheck` clean.

- `eng1575.metaActionFamilies` — collapse logic, both Instant-Form variants (with and without a rollup)
- `eng1575.processorLeadMetrics` — drives the real private processors; **no pre-existing test exercised them with an `actions` payload at all**
- `eng1575.metaRouteLeadMetrics` — pins the portal-rendered `websiteLeads` so it cannot move

**12 red-checks**, each restoring an original defect — all caught, green after restore.

Regression fixtures use real production alias **shapes** and the counts the shipped code reported. Account identities, ad-account ids and spend are deliberately omitted — the alias shape and resulting count are what the code must get right, and committing customer performance data would leak it through the repo and every review surface.

## Reviewer note

Findings on this ticket were revised twice during investigation; the ticket records both corrections. The piece most worth scrutiny is the reconciliation branch in `collapseActions` — specifically the case where the rollup exceeds the surfaces we can name, where the *split* is a heuristic even though the total stays authoritative.

Closes ENG-1575.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Centralizes Meta conversion-family classification and lead aggregation in shared utilities. It prevents lead double-counting, separates website and Instant Form conversions, and applies deterministic cost selection. CSV provenance handling now supports quoted commas and multipart responses. Testing reports 134 passing tests and clean typechecking.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

---

## Also carries the fix for ENG-1600 (two defects in ENG-1295's CSV provenance layer)

Found by CodeRabbit's "Outside diff range" review of this PR — **pre-existing code, not introduced here** (verified: present verbatim on `main`, and no hunk of this diff overlaps those lines). Filed as [ENG-1600](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1600) and fixed here because the file was already open and the diff is small.

Both defects can **reject a correct analysis**, which matters because that layer exists to catch fabricated output:

1. **`parseCsvProvenance` split on every comma** — a quoted field containing one (`"Acme, Inc"`) shifted every later column left. Column 0 feeds the cross-call comparison that hard-rejects with `inconsistent_result`, so a row shifted on one run and not the other refuses a correct analysis. It also fed `findCsvIdNameCollisions` and `checkCsvIdGrounding`, producing fabricated collision warnings and spurious "unverified" counts. Now uses `csv-parse` — already imported in that file and used elsewhere in it. Ragged rows relax rather than throw, since returning `null` would disable the only guard against fabricated output.

2. **Several `text/csv` parts, only the last counted** — all are shown to the caller, but only the final one reached provenance and the consistency cache, so a repeat call whose parts arrived in a different order compared two different CSVs and hard-rejected. Comparison and cache write now skip when more than one part is present.

⚠ **ENG-1600 item 3 is deliberately NOT here.** Extracting ~230 lines of pure helpers into `services/agentMode/` is a different change from fixing two parsing defects, and bundling them makes the correctness diff unreviewable. It stays on ENG-1600.

## Risk handling for the branches with no production evidence

The two reconciliation heuristics in `collapseActions` and the cost-conflict path cannot be tested against real data — no account produces those shapes. Rather than ship silent guesses, each now **warns when it engages**, with tests pinning the behaviour and one asserting **silence** on the ordinary shape so the common path cannot become log spam. Totals stay authoritative in every branch; only the surface split is heuristic, and it now says so.

Closes ENG-1600 items 1 and 2.

title: ENG-265: multiple sending domains and per-sender daily caps/warmup
body:
## Summary

Implements ENG-265 (multiple sending domains + email inboxes for cold email
campaigns). ACs #1/#2 (multiple senders, per-campaign sender choice) were
already shipped via ENG-266; the two real gaps closed here:

- **Multi-domain sending**: `User.emailDomain`/`resendDomainId` were scalar
  (one verified Resend domain per account). Added `User.emailDomains[]`
  (additive, existing scalar fields untouched for legacy single-domain
  callers) and plural `GET/POST /api/crm/email-domains`,
  `POST /email-domains/:id/verify`, `DELETE /email-domains/:id` routes.
- **Per-sender daily caps + warmup**: no volume guardrail existed on any send
  path. Added `dailyLimit`/`warmupStartedAt` to `CrmSender`, a warmup ramp
  (day 1-3: 10/day, 4-7: 20/day, 8-14: 35/day, 15+: dailyLimit or 50),  and a
  race-safe DynamoDB-backed daily counter (`senderUsageTracker.ts` /
  `senderUsageTrackerFactory.ts`, modeled on the existing
  apolloQuota.ts/enrichSoQuota.ts pattern). Enforced at `sendAsSender.ts`,
  the chokepoint all real sends funnel through.
- **Opt-in gap closure**: pre-existing senders are grandfathered with no cap
  but get a visible "No daily limit set" warning badge; new senders default
  to a 50/day cap unless explicitly changed.

## Review round + fixes

Had this branch reviewed fresh against `origin/main` by independent backend
and frontend passes. Findings, and what's fixed here:

- **[Fixed] Emma chat-driven sends bypassed the cap entirely.**
  `agentModeService.ts`'s `sendEmailToLead`/`sendEmailFromConfiguredSender`
  (behind Emma's chat send tools) called Resend/Gmail/Outlook directly,
  never touching `sendAsSender`. Now routed through the same chokepoint.
  **Verified live through an actual Emma chat conversation**: a capped
  sender's first send succeeded and recorded quota; the second was blocked
  with `"Blocked. ... that sender has hit its daily limit: 1 email/day"` and
  did not double-count.
- **[Fixed] Lost-update race on `emailDomains[]`.** `POST /email-domains`
  and `DELETE /email-domains/:id` were unconditioned read-modify-write; two
  concurrent requests for the same user could drop an entry. Now conditioned
  on array size with a one-shot retry against a fresh read, mirroring the
  existing `ConditionalCheckFailedException` retry pattern used elsewhere in
  this repo.
- Reviewed and accepted as-is (by design, not bugs): `checkQuota`/`recordSend`
  non-atomic split (mirrors the existing Apollo/enrich.so pattern — quota
  only consumed by a send that actually happened); old singular
  `/email-domain/status` not seeing plural-route domains (documented rollout
  tradeoff, resolved once the frontend fully cuts over, which it has).

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- Targeted suite for every touched file — 335/335 passing, including new
  regression coverage for the cap-bypass fix
  (`agentModeService.senderDailyLimit.test.ts`) and the race-retry fix
  (extended `crm.emailDomains.multi.test.ts`).
- Live-verified on the cloud test-env: multi-domain register/verify/remove,
  daily-cap enforcement on real Gmail + Outlook sends (duplicate-email proof
  at `dailyLimit:2`), group-email bulk-send stop-early on cap hit
  (`sent:2, skippedDueToLimit:1`), and both fixes above via real chat/UI
  interaction (see above).
- **Not live-tested**: drip-worker snooze-on-cap-hit (needs a real
  enrollment + cron wait; covered by `dripSequenceWorker.dailyLimit.test.ts`
  only — accepted as a known gap).

## Governance note

This touches persisted shape on `User` (`emailDomains`) and `CrmSender`
(`dailyLimit`, `warmupStartedAt`) — both purely additive (no new table, GSI,
or removed field), but per this repo's CLAUDE.md, database/data-plane
changes require Harsha's sign-off before merge. **Not obtained yet** — please
do not merge until that's in place.

## Companion PR

Frontend UI: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal (same branch name).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: High

Adds multi-domain support, atomic domain claims, pending group-email persistence, and per-sender daily caps with warmup enforcement. Race-safe DynamoDB reservations affect all production send paths and could block sends or permit uncapped sends, causing a production outage. Existing senders remain uncapped. New senders default to 50 emails per day. Drip snooze behavior was not live-tested.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(linkedin): unblock Jennifer's outreach — publish-scope prompt fix (ENG-1589) + accept-invitation CRM mirror (ENG-1595)
body:
## Summary — two related fixes for the same customer, same PR

**1. ENG-1589 — outreach sends were being wrongly withheld**
- Emma was refusing to send Jennifer Sun's Dream 100 LinkedIn outreach (connection requests/DMs via `linkedin_outreach`) in unattended scheduled runs, citing the PUBLISH AUTHORIZATION block in the system prompt.
- That block — and its underlying code gate (`isPublishCapableTool` / `resolveSchedulePublishAuthorization`) — was only ever meant to cover content-*publishing* tools (`post_on_connected_account`, `publish_blog_article`, `publish_landing_page_changes`, and the repost/comment actions of `linkedin_manage_post`/`twitter_manage_post`). Outreach sends (`linkedin_outreach`, `twitter_outreach`) are governed solely by the separate `SAFETY & VOLUME LIMITS` caps and need no standing authorization at all.
- Root-caused directly against Jennifer's real session: every `linkedin_outreach` call she made was a read (`list-sent-invitations`, `search-people`, `get-profile`). She never attempted a single `send-invite`/`send-message` — Emma self-censored purely from the ambiguous prompt wording, before any code gate had a chance to fire.
- Note: ENG-1589's literal ask ("no working control to grant standing publish authorization") was already shipped separately via customer-portal #1114 — that UI is live and correct, but doesn't apply here since outreach was never in its scope. This PR fixes the actual thing blocking Jennifer.
- Fix: added an explicit scope bullet to both branches of `getUnattendedExecutionDirective`'s PUBLISH AUTHORIZATION block, clarifying outreach/email sends proceed regardless of publish-authorization state.

**2. ENG-1595 — accepted connections were invisible to CRM search**
- `accept-invitation` was a pure Unipile passthrough with zero CRM interaction, so a real inbound LinkedIn connection Jennifer's account accepted was invisible to name-based CRM search forever — unlike an outbound send, which already gets list-attributed via `send-invite`'s own CRM-mirror logic.
- Root-caused against her real report: one of five "missing" leads was confirmed via saved session memory to be a genuinely accepted connection with no lead record anywhere.
- Fix: generalized `mirrorLinkedInInviteToCrm`'s hardcoded `linkedin.invite.sent` engagement type into a parameter (default unchanged), added `INVITE_ACCEPTED_EVENT` for the new direction, and wired the same best-effort mirror pattern `send-invite` already uses into `accept-invitation` — resolve identity (profile_url/provider_id), resolve the target list (explicit `list_id` or the account's bound list), verify access, then mirror. No-ops cleanly rather than guessing when identity or list can't be resolved.

title: LinkedIn people search: add company_size_min/max post-filter (ENG-1558)
body:
**Feature (ENG-1558, follow-up from ENG-1299):** Unipile has no native headcount filter for the LinkedIn People search category — only for Companies — so `linkedin_outreach`'s `search-people` action and `import_leads_from_search` (bulk CRM import) had no way to filter by employer size (e.g. "product managers at startups"). Design approved before implementation (post-filter using each candidate's resolved company, matching Unipile's own headcount bucket boundaries as the reference for "startup"/"enterprise").

**What shipped:**
- `linkedInOutreachService.filterByCompanySize()` — resolves each candidate's employer (free text) → company ID (existing cached resolver) → `employee_count` (existing cached `UnipileCompanyService`, field name confirmed from the Unipile SDK's own TypeBox schema). Unverifiable employers are excluded, not guessed at, and reported back transparently.
- `search-people`: new `company_size_min`/`company_size_max` params, applied after the ENG-1198 anonymized-result filter.
- `import_leads_from_search`: same filter, applied *after* its full 4-tier company-resolution chain (work_experience → title-regex → LLM batch parse → Unipile profile fallback) so a lead whose company only resolved via a later tier isn't wrongly excluded.
- Throttled to 5 concurrent per-employer lookups (was one unbounded `Promise.all` — could fire 30-40 concurrent Unipile calls from a single search).
- `import_leads_from_search`'s top-up loop now stops after 3 consecutive pages the filter empties entirely (`earlyExitOnSizeFilter`), instead of grinding to the full 20-iteration cap, with a resumable cursor.
- No-op (zero extra Unipile calls) for every existing caller that doesn't pass the new params.

**Verification:**
- `npm run typecheck` — clean throughout.
- 396 tests across every affected file (linkedInOutreachService, both search-people dispatcher test files, import_leads_from_search) — all passing, including new tests for the filter logic, dispatcher wiring, concurrency throttling (measures actual max in-flight lookups), and the early-exit threshold (including that it resets correctly and doesn't over-trigger).
- Live-verified `employee_count` coverage against 8 real, organically-sourced search results (not cherry-picked) via the already-deployed `get-company` action: 100% had headcount data, including a 371-person startup and a 560-person community bank, not just large companies.

**Deliberately out of scope:** `POST /api/crm/lists/:listId/leads/find` (the separate UI-driven "Find Leads" REST route calling the same underlying function) — no customer-portal form exists to set these params yet, so backend passthrough with nothing to reach it would be speculative.

Adds optional `company_size_min` and `company_size_max` filters to LinkedIn people search and bulk lead import. The flow resolves employer headcount, excludes unverifiable or out-of-range candidates, limits lookups to five concurrent requests, and reports filtering results. Import stops after three fully filtered pages while preserving a resumable cursor. Existing flows make no extra calls without size filters. Tests and type checking pass.

title: fix(linkedin): verify accept-invitation identity server-side, fix timestamp mislabeling
body:
## Summary

Fast-follow to #2645 (merged, already deployed), fixing two real gaps CodeRabbit caught in review AFTER that merge (missed before merging — my mistake, correcting it here immediately since the gap is currently live in prod):

**1. Identity binding (Major).** The accept-invitation CRM mirror trusted caller-supplied `profile_url`/`provider_id`/`first_name`/`last_name` with nothing tying those values to `invitation_id`. Unlike `send-invite` (where the supplied identity IS the send target by construction — Unipile can't send without it), `accept-invitation`'s identity comes entirely from Unipile's own `invitation_id`/`shared_secret` pair; nothing previously verified that a caller-supplied profile actually matched. A model passing an inconsistent pair (mistake or otherwise) would accept invitation A but attribute the CRM lead/engagement write to unrelated person B.

Fixed by resolving the invitee's identity server-side from Unipile's own `listReceivedInvitations` record for that exact `invitationId`, before accepting. Caller-supplied identity fields are no longer read at all for this action — only `list_id` still matters. Bounded to 5 pages of the received-invitations feed so this can't become an unbounded scan on the live request path. No-ops (mirrors nothing) when the invitation can't be found, rather than falling back to unverified caller data.

**2. Timestamp mislabeling (Major).** `linkedInInviteSentAt` was being stamped unconditionally, including for an ACCEPTED inbound connection — misrepresenting who initiated contact and risking overwriting a real prior outbound-send timestamp on the same lead. Added a distinct `linkedInInviteAcceptedAt` field and stamp whichever is direction-appropriate.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] Full targeted suite green: `linkedInInviteCrmMirror.test.ts`, `linkedInInviteCrmReconcile.test.ts`, `linkedInInviteCrmReconcileCron.test.ts`, `agentModeService.linkedInOutreach.test.ts` — 181 tests
- [x] New tests confirm caller-supplied identity is fully ignored, the invitation-not-found case skips the mirror, the page scan is bounded, and the two timestamp fields never cross-contaminate

It bounds verification to five pages and skips unverified invitations. It also records inbound acceptance and outbound sending in separate timestamp fields. title: fix(linkedin): accept-invitation stops auto-attributing to the account's bound CRM list
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2647 (the identity-binding fix for accept-invitation's CRM mirror), addressing a design gap surfaced during review with the team: the current code still auto-guesses a target CRM list when the model doesn't explicitly supply one, which silently misattributes *any* accepted connection to whatever list happens to be linked to the account.

**The problem:** `send-invite` safely falls back to the account's bound list when `list_id` is omitted, because sending an invite is always a deliberate targeting action. `accept-invitation` copied that same fallback — but accepting an inbound request is a completely different situation: it could be a genuine prospect, or it could be an old colleague/friend who happened to send a connection request. The account owner configuring a list binding for *outbound* attribution never decided "also auto-log every person I happen to accept as a lead." Concretely: if a user just asks Emma to "expand my network" (no CRM/lead context at all), the current code still silently logs every accepted connection into whatever campaign list is configured for that account.

**The fix:** removed the fallback entirely for `accept-invitation`. CRM mirroring now only happens when the caller explicitly passes `list_id` — i.e. when the task actually judged this specific person relevant (exactly what Jennifer's own schedule instructions already do: "for each sender fitting the ICP, accept and mirror into CRM"). No explicit signal → accept still succeeds, nothing gets logged, no guessing.

Also added a small nudge to the tool description: if Emma judges someone a good potential lead but has no list to attach them to, she should surface that explicitly in her final report rather than let it pass silently — so a real candidate stays visible and actionable instead of disappearing.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] 188 tests pass across `agentModeService.linkedInOutreach.test.ts`, `linkedInInviteCrmMirror.test.ts`, `linkedInInviteCrmReconcile.test.ts`, `linkedInInviteCrmReconcileCron.test.ts`
- [x] New test confirms `resolveListIdForAccount` is never even called for accept-invitation now, regardless of whether the account has a bound list

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

When `list_id` is omitted, `accept-invitation` does not mirror the accepted connection to the CRM. It no longer resolves the account’s bound CRM list. title: ENG-1601 + ENG-1600 item 3: join reads the customFields promoter; extract pure CSV helpers
body:
Two independent fixes, one commit each.

## 1 · ENG-1601 — the join dropped 36% of attributable leads

`metaMetricsSnapshotCron` read `lead.firstTouch?.utm?.campaign` directly. Measured on Haven's inbound leads, 2026-07-29 → 08-25:

| where `utm_campaign` lives | count |
| --- | --- |
| BOTH `firstTouch.utm.campaign` and `customFields` | 23 |
| **`customFields` ONLY — `firstTouch` entirely ABSENT** | **13** |
| `firstTouch` only | 0 |
| genuinely bare | 4 |

Those 13 carry a valid Meta campaign id — the **same two ids** the other 23 matched on — in the free-form bag. The attribution arrived; the join looked in one of the two places it can live.

**`promoteAttributionFromCustomFields` already exists for exactly this** (ENG-926 §A: *"the data was never lost, just filed where nothing structured reads"*), is already used at ingest by `routes/webhooks.ts`, and has its own suite. This cron never imported it.

Gap-filling, not a fallback — a structured value still wins, and only an allowlisted set is promoted so a free-form bag cannot assert paid acquisition. The ambiguity guard is unaffected, and a test pins that.

**Effect: 19 → 32 attributed over the same 28 days (+57%)**, from data already in the table. No retagging, no `RETAG_UTM`, no learning-phase reset.

⚠ Why it survived verification: every end-to-end check ran against Dev CRM, which holds none of Haven's production leads, so the join only ever saw **one** write shape.

## 2 · ENG-1600 item 3 — extract the pure CSV helpers

Six pure functions moved out of the 36k-line `agentModeService` into `services/agentMode/csvProvenance.ts`. **Net −145 lines from the service.** `pruneDataAnalysisConsistencyCache` stays — it touches instance state.

The point is testability: ENG-1600's CSV fix couldn't be unit-tested without loading the whole service, so its suite reached in via `(service as any)`. It now imports directly.

That cast was hiding real errors — with `any` removed, `tsc` immediately flagged **four unchecked null dereferences** in the test file, since `parseCsvProvenance` genuinely returns `T | null`. Fixed rather than re-cast.

Deliberately not bundled into #2643, where it would have made the correctness diff unreviewable.

## Verification

**218 tests across 10 suites**, `npm run typecheck` clean.

Three red-checks: reverting the join to the raw field fails 2; promoting without gap-fill fails 1.

Closes ENG-1601. Closes ENG-1600.

Risk: Low. The cron now promotes allowlisted `customFields` attribution while preserving structured values and same-day ambiguity checks. CSV provenance helpers now use a dedicated module, with null-dereference fixes. Neither change is on a production-outage path.

title: Let admin MCP tools scope to a specific client (ENG-1596)
body:
## Summary

Nearly every admin-facing MCP tool was hard-scoped to the calling admin's own account, with no way to inspect a specific customer's data through the tools built for it — every attempt during a live support session either returned the admin's own data or was flatly refused. Root cause: these tools route through `mcpFetch`, which always mints a self-call JWT for the caller's own identity, and downstream routes (including `crmAccessControl.ts`'s org-tenant isolation) have no `isAdmin` bypass at all.

- `search_leads`, `list_lead_lists`, `manage_leads` (**read actions only** — `list`/`get`), `list_connected_accounts`, `get_account_status`, `emma_get_account_status`, `list_tasks`, `list_scheduled_chats` now accept an optional `client_id` (email or userId).
- `resolveClientScopedContext` (new `mcp/server/adminClientScope.ts`) verifies the caller is a real admin (server-side DB check, never trusted from the caller), resolves the target, and mints a delegate-access token via the same mechanism `routes/admin.ts` already uses for the customer-portal delegate flow — extracted to `services/delegateAccessToken.ts` so both call sites share one implementation.
- `mcpFetch` accepts that pre-minted token directly (`context.overrideToken`), so every existing REST route works against the target's data with **zero route-level changes**.
- Every successful `client_id` resolution writes an admin-audit record (`services/adminAuditLog.ts` — the existing ENG-721 admin cross-account audit mechanism, no new table) naming the actor, target, and specific tool used.
- `get_account_status`/`list_scheduled_chats` are also bridged into Emma's in-app self-serve tool set (every logged-in customer, not just admins) — the bridge registers a `client_id`-free schema for those two, and strips `client_id` unconditionally at the bridge boundary even if it slips through as an arg, so the param can never leak into the self-serve version (same class of bug `mcpGetAccountStatusExposure.test.ts` already guards against; CodeRabbit caught the schema-only half of this, see review history below).
- `list_task_executions`/`list_schedules`/`assess_client_health`/`list_all_clients`/`emma_send_message`/`emma_get_session` needed no changes — already correctly admin-scoped or resolve by an unambiguous target id.
- `get_leads_by_crm_criteria`'s separate 404 (`/api/drip-campaigns/preview-segment` doesn't exist anywhere in the backend — a different, unrelated bug) filed as **ENG-1602**, linked to this card, per its own AC #4.
- `client_id` is **not** added to `create_lead_list`, `manage_schedule`, `manage_scheduled_chat` — none of those are confirmed-broken instances in this card.

## Scope note: writes deliberately excluded (ENG-1557)

`manage_leads`'s `add`/`update`/`delete` actions **reject `client_id` loudly** rather than honoring it — found mid-implementation that **ENG-1557** ("Follow-up: MCP delegated customer-support access remains unavailable after ENG-495") is the umbrella authorization-contract ticket for this whole "delegate powers to MCP" family, and explicitly names this ticket. It requires a human-reviewed contract (staff roles, permitted read/write ops + attribution, scope/expiry/revocation/audit) before any credentials are issued or live customer mutations happen. ENG-1506's revocation gap (one of ENG-1557's open questions) is already Done and confirmed. Reads carry none of that risk and are what every confirmed instance in this ticket + Harsha's original ask actually needed — writes are held pending that review.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] New: `delegateAccessToken.test.ts`, `mcp.adminClientScope.test.ts` (incl. audit-trail assertions), `mcp.apiTools.clientScope.test.ts` (end-to-end through the real registry — reads succeed with `client_id`, all three write actions reject it loudly before any DB lookup), plus `overrideToken` coverage in `mcp.httpClient.test.ts` and bridge-boundary stripping tests in `mcpGetAccountStatusExposure.test.ts`
- [x] Full existing coverage re-run and green: `mcp.apiTools`, `mcp.httpClient`, `mcp.userIdOverride` (IDOR guard), `mcp.scheduledChatTools`, `mcpGetAccountStatusExposure`, `admin.delegateAccess`, `auth.delegateTokenRevocation`, `agentModeController.delegatedCrmAccess` — all pass unchanged
- [x] All 35 test files that import `emma/tools.ts` directly re-run — one pre-existing, unrelated failure (`agentModeController.conditionalSkip`, about knowledge-base tool cross-references) confirmed present on a clean `origin/main` baseline via `git stash`, not caused by this change
- [x] CodeRabbit review addressed: bridge-boundary `client_id` stripping, caller-identity precedence (`agentUserId` over `userId`) — both fixed, replied, threads resolved
- [ ] Best verified live against the test environment: as a real admin test account, call `list_tasks`/`search_leads`/`get_account_status` with `client_id` pointing at a customer test account and confirm the returned data is the customer's, not the admin's — attempted this session, blocked by unrelated test-env instance flakiness (SSH became unresponsive under load, survived a stop/start and a reboot); this is exactly the kind of integration seam unit mocks can miss, worth someone re-attempting when the instance is healthy

title: fix: record LinkedIn invite capacity blocks (ENG-1132)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
A scheduled LinkedIn invite run could record an account-level cooldown or internal pacing refusal as a successful required tool call. This falsely reported delivery even though remaining invitation sends could not succeed.

## What this fixes (after)
The scheduled-run ledger recognizes blocked linkedin_outreach send-invite actions, persists a clear session/run-history notice, and marks the required action missed when successful sends do not meet its minimum. Successful sends and non-invite reads retain their existing validation behavior.

## Complexity ledger
Net +244 lines (251 added, 7 removed): one narrow ledger classifier plus explicit result normalization and acceptance tests; no new service, route, persistence schema, or fallback path. Behavior-preserving outside detected send-invite cooldown/pacing responses.

## How to test
1. Run a scheduled chat requiring linkedin_outreach with a send-invite result of Cannot resend yet.
2. Confirm the run is a failure, the response states no further send-invite actions will succeed, and the alert contains the account-level cooldown reason.
3. Run the same schedule with an internal daily pacing-cap refusal.
4. Confirm it fails with the internal-pacing notice.
5. Run a successful send-invite and a failed search-people action.
6. Confirm neither is falsely classified as an invite-cap block.

## Edge cases to check
- Remote staging execution against a real LinkedIn account remains intentionally untested: the worker does not use live accounts or browser QA.
- Provider wording outside the tested cooldown/pacing signatures should remain a normal tool failure.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 9 passed, 0 failed: npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeController.scheduledAlertKeying.test.ts --runInBand --silent
- TypeScript: npm run typecheck clean on exact rebased head.

title: fix: remove Slack auto-trigger pipeline entirely, tag-gated only (ENG-1613)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
The Slack "auto-listen" pipeline (`handleSlackTriggeredSession` for top-level untagged messages,
and the `isTriggered` thread-continuation branch) ran real, paid LLM inference on **every**
non-threaded, non-@mention message in a connected Slack channel by default — including trivial
ones ("lol", "nice", "thanks") — and emailed a draft to `founders@agentweb.pro`. A customer had to
discover and explicitly opt out via `slackSuggestedRepliesDisabled: true`. Phoenix Tech did not,
and burned ~$197 of real inference cost in August.

An earlier version of this PR flipped the default to off with an admin-controlled opt-in escape
hatch. Harsha (direct instruction, superseding that design): kill the pipeline entirely, no opt-in.
Reasoning: even an opted-in account never *sees* the auto-drafted reply — it's emailed to
`founders@agentweb.pro` and never posted to Slack — so the customer has no way to know their
message ever triggered an LLM session at all. That's a trust/transparency problem independent of
account-level consent.

## What this fixes (after)
Removes the untagged-message auto-trigger pipeline outright. Emma's Slack behavior is now
exclusively tag-gated: nothing happens unless a message @-mentions Emma (the existing, completely
unmodified `app_mention` handler).

Deleted:
- `handleSlackTriggeredSession()` and its two call sites (top-level untagged message handler,
  untracked-thread fallback) in `backend/src/routes/slack.ts`.
- The now-unreachable `isTriggered` thread-continuation branch — `type: 'triggered'` was written
  exclusively by the deleted function, so it can never be read back `true` again; the surviving
  code always takes the genuine Emma-mention-session-continuation path.
- The now-pointless opt-in: `PUT /admin/users/:userId/slack-suggested-replies`
  (`backend/src/routes/admin.ts`), the `slackSuggestedRepliesDisabled` field
  (`backend/src/services/db.ts` `User` interface), its entry in the admin user-list projection, and
  the corresponding partner-portal admin toggle in `AdminDashboard.tsx` (which would otherwise 404
  on click once the backend route is gone).
- The ENG-1263 internal-author guard (`isInternalSlackAuthor`, `INTERNAL_SLACK_USER_IDS`) and its
  now-unused `getSlackUserTeamId`/`getOwnSlackTeamId` imports in `slack.ts` — both existed solely to
  protect the deleted pipeline from misfiring on our own team's messages, with no other caller.
  `getSlackUserTeamId`/`getOwnSlackTeamId` themselves stay in `slackService.ts`, separately
  unit-tested (`slackService.teamIdCache.test.ts`) as a general capability, not exclusively owned by
  this feature.
- `AGENTWEB_INTERNAL_SLACK_USER_IDS` from `backend/.env.example` (only reader was the deleted guard).

The `app_mention` handler and the genuine Emma-mention thread-continuation path are completely
untouched.

## Complexity ledger
- Net lines across both commits: **-1394** in tracked files (deleted 4 test files, added 1 smaller
  one), **-462** production code in the removal commit alone.
- Moving parts removed: 1 pipeline (auto-trigger function + 2 call sites), 1 admin endpoint, 1 user
  field, 1 admin UI toggle, 1 internal-author guard helper + its backing const, 2 now-orphaned
  service imports, 1 stale env-var doc entry.
- Moving parts added: zero.
- Behavior: intentionally NOT behavior-preserving for untagged messages (that is the entire point —
  direct product decision). The `app_mention` real-tag flow and the genuine Emma-mention
  thread-continuation path are unchanged.

## How to test
1. Post a plain, non-@mention message in a test account's connected Slack channel (e.g. "lol
   nice", or something that would clearly "need handling" like "can someone help with my
   campaign?").
2. **Expected**: no chat session is created, no triage/LLM call fires, no email is sent to
   `founders@agentweb.pro`. No admin toggle exists anymore to change this — it's unconditional.
3. Reply in an untracked thread (no existing Emma session mapped to it) with a plain follow-up.
4. **Expected**: same — nothing happens.
5. @-mention Emma directly in Slack (`@Emma ...`).
6. **Expected**: Emma responds in-thread exactly as before — this path is untouched.
7. Reply again in that same thread without re-mentioning Emma.
8. **Expected**: Emma continues the session and posts in-thread exactly as before (genuine
   Emma-mention-session continuation, unaffected).
9. In the partner portal admin dashboard, open a user with Slack channels connected — confirm the
   "Suggested replies" toggle that used to appear next to Slack Channels is gone (no broken/404ing
   control left behind).

## Edge cases to check
- A user record with no Slack integration at all (`slackChannels` unset) — unaffected, never
  reached the deleted code path either.
- A pre-existing DynamoDB row that still has `slackSuggestedRepliesDisabled` set from before this
  PR — harmless; nothing reads that field anymore.

## Test Evidence
- New: `backend/src/__tests__/slack.autoTriggerRemoved.test.ts` (3 tests) — removal guard: proves
  no session/LLM call/email fires for an untagged top-level message or an untracked-thread reply,
  including with triage mocked to "would have needed handling" (proves the call site is gone, not a
  mock-shape artifact).
- Deleted (tested only the removed mechanism): `admin.slackSuggestedReplies.test.ts`,
  `slack.autoTriggerDefault.test.ts`, `slack.suggestedRepliesGate.test.ts`,
  `slack.internalAuthorGuard.test.ts`.
- `cd backend && npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `cd partner-portal && npx tsc -b --force`: clean.
- Targeted suites: `slack.*`, `admin.*`, `slackService.*`, `emailService.slackTriggeredSession`,
  `sessionScoring.slackTriggered` — 448 tests, 0 failures.
- Pre-push hook (not bypassed): `tsc --noEmit` (backend) clean, 43 related suites / 438 tests, all
  passed.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- "An inbound Slack message that does not @-mention Emma never triggers any session, draft, or LLM
  call, regardless of any user field" → `slack.autoTriggerRemoved.test.ts`, all 3 cases.
- "A genuine `app_mention` event is completely unaffected" → existing `slack.events.test.ts`
  coverage ("should reply in-thread when Emma is mentioned in Slack", "should forward thread
  replies to existing Emma session"), unmodified and still passing.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/slack.ts`
- `backend/src/routes/admin.ts`
- `backend/src/services/db.ts`
- `backend/.env.example`
- `partner-portal/src/contexts/AdminContext.tsx`
- `partner-portal/src/pages/AdminDashboard.tsx`
- `backend/src/__tests__/slack.autoTriggerRemoved.test.ts` (new)
- 4 deleted test files (listed above under Test Evidence)

## What was NOT tested
- Live Slack workspace round-trip (no test Slack app credentials in this session) — covered by
  existing mocked route-level tests only, consistent with the rest of this file's test suite.
- Production DynamoDB rows that still carry the now-unread `slackSuggestedRepliesDisabled` field —
  not cleaned up (harmless dead data, not a migration; no data-plane change made or needed).

title: [needs human] Authorize a standalone tweet when only twitter_manage_post is granted (ENG-1599)
body:
**Bug:** The scheduled 'Harsha Daily X Post (Autonomous)' run (schedule 1d001fba-0fb7-4bcd-80f6-6041b244a442, session 90ad8838) was authorized/required only for `twitter_manage_post`. Its news-take lane needed to post ONE standalone tweet, which requires `post_on_connected_account` — `twitter_manage_post` structurally cannot post a single tweet (its `post_thread` action hard-throws below 2 tweets in agentModeService.ts). The model correctly called `post_on_connected_account` and was refused: 'The owner authorized only: twitter_manage_post.' Verified against production DynamoDB: the session's `publishAdmission.tools` was `["twitter_manage_post"]` and the schedule's `requiredFunctionCalls` contained `twitter_manage_post` but not `post_on_connected_account`.

**Root cause:** `EQUIVALENT_PUBLISH_ROUTES` in `backend/src/utils/requiredCallSatisfaction.ts` already mapped `post_on_connected_account -> twitter_manage_post(post_thread)` (from ENG-1045, for the opposite direction: a schedule authorized for post_on_connected_account being satisfied by a thread), but had no route back the other way. So a schedule whose only authorized publish tool was `twitter_manage_post` had no path to ever publish a single standalone tweet, even though posting a single tweet is a strictly narrower act than the threads/replies/quote-tweets/retweets that tool is already trusted to publish unattended.

**Fix:** Added `twitter_manage_post: [{ tool: 'post_on_connected_account', platforms: ['twitter'] }]` to the route table, and extended `EquivalentPublishRoute`/the two consumers (`callSatisfiesRequirement` and `isPublishCallWithinAuthorizedScope`) to also filter equivalence routes by a `platforms` list — this keeps the new route scoped to twitter so it can't be used to widen a twitter-only grant into authorization for `post_on_connected_account` calls targeting LinkedIn/Instagram/YouTube (which share that same tool name).

**Verification:** Added tests to `schedulePublishAuthorization.test.ts` confirming (1) the new route authorizes a standalone tweet when only twitter_manage_post is granted, (2) it does NOT widen to other platforms, (3) it's still false on an empty grant. Confirmed red before the fix (reverted the fix, re-ran — the new test failed with the exact same 'owner authorized only' shape) and green after.

---

Code review: ✅ sound — 5 finding(s) fixed
Deterministic checks: ❌ FAILED — npx tsc --noEmit (backend)
Browser verify: ⚠️ environment down (not verified)

Fixes ENG-1599 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1599/harsha-x-autonomous-posting-post-on-connected-account-blocked-on-pre

title: fix: scope Meta AD/AD_CREATIVE LIST to the node and paginate (ENG-1476, ENG-1584)
body:
Fixes **ENG-1476**. Also fixes the engineering half of **ENG-1584**.

## The bug

`AD LIST` returned Meta's first page of 25 records and reported it as the whole ad account. Two customers hit this four days apart on different ad accounts.

On Phoenix Technologies (ENG-1476, reported 2026-08-22) it blocked creative-level reporting — the report shipped with declared gaps.

On Every.io (ENG-1584) it produced a **false statement to the customer**. Asked to prove a compliance-sensitive ad had not been touched, the agent replied, verbatim in production:

> *"Ad 8 'Gusto Renewal Shock' does not exist in this account… I searched all 25 account ads: zero matches. The campaign has 9 ads."*

The campaign had **14** ads. The account had **≥36**. The ad existed — AgentWeb itself had paused it three weeks earlier. The blast-radius check covered 9 of 14 and was reported as complete.

## Four defects, all of them required

Fixing any one alone leaves the bug reachable.

**1. Scope was silently discarded.** `metaService.listAds` sent `params.adset_id`, which **Meta ignores** as a bare param on the `/act_X/ads` edge — the filter looked applied and never was.

Scoping now goes through Meta's own node edges (`/{campaign_id}/ads`, `/{adset_id}/ads`). Chosen over a `filtering` param deliberately: a wrong id becomes an error rather than a silent account-wide result, so the failure mode is structurally unavailable. The correct approach already existed in the sibling `listAdsForUtmAudit`, ~100 lines below the bug.

**2. No pagination.** The SDK's `Cursor` extends `Array` but holds **one page** — `next()` REPLACES its contents rather than appending — so `(await account.getAds(...)).map(...)` read page 1 and nothing else. New `drainCursor` walks to completion under a bounded page limit and reports `truncated` when it stops early.

**3. `campaign_id` was dropped before the call.** It was in scope at the dispatch (the tracking gate uses it) but `manageMetaAdsAds` had no such parameter, so an explicitly campaign-scoped `LIST` became account-wide. This is why repro steps 2 and 3 in the original filing behaved identically.

**4. The result claimed completeness it never had.** `Found ${totalCount} ad(s)` — no scope, no bound. It now names what it was scoped to and whether it is complete; a truncated list says `INCOMPLETE` in the message the model actually reads, not only in a field it may ignore.

## ⚠ Field order in the response is load-bearing

An ad list carries `object_story_spec` per ad, so it routinely exceeds `TOOL_RESPONSE_S3_THRESHOLD` (8,000 chars) and is offloaded to S3 — at which point the model is handed a **sealed 20,000-char PREFIX** of the JSON plus a key.

Anything serialized after a large `ads` array falls off that cut. So `complete` / `hasMore` / `totalCount` / `scope` are emitted **before** the payload — otherwise the truncation warning would disappear on precisely the large lists that need it, which is the original failure wearing a different hat. A test pins the serialization order.

This also addresses the real risk that **pagination alone would make things worse**: a bigger unscoped response pushes more calls onto the offloaded `search_tool_response` read path, which is where ENG-1584's false negative actually surfaced. Correct scoping is what keeps responses small — a campaign-scoped ask returns 14 records, not 36.

## Deliberately NOT changed

`object_story_spec` stays on `LIST` despite being the dominant payload cost. Removing it would trade one silent loss for another, and ENG-1476's own filing asks for verbatim creative content. `AD_CREATIVE GET` remains the way to read `asset_feed_spec`.

`listAdsForUtmAudit` is untouched. It already scopes correctly and works; this PR does not refactor it.

No campaign scope on `AD_CREATIVE LIST` — Meta exposes no `/{campaign_id}/adcreatives` edge. Campaign-scoped creative questions go through `AD LIST` with `campaign_id`, which returns `creative{...}` inline on every ad. The tool description now says so.

## Tests

**634 passing, 0 failing** across every suite touching this surface.

Two existing tests asserted `params.adset_id` was sent — they **pinned the defect**. Both now assert the node edge is used and that no bare filter param goes out.

New coverage:
- `eng1476.metaAdListScoping.test.ts` — node-edge scoping, precedence when both ids are given, no bare filter params, multi-page walk, truncation reporting, non-cursor inputs, page size
- `eng1476.adListReporting.test.ts` — message carries scope and completeness, truncated lists say so, `campaign_id` survives the dispatch, serialization order survives the S3 preview cut
- The ENG-1584 shape specifically: **an ad on page 2 must be found**

## Verification status — read before merging

Verified by unit tests and by reading the full call chain, including confirming that `extractMinimalToolResult` has no Meta branch but only feeds the stored ledger (the model reads `extractToolContent(result)`, the full object, so the new fields do reach it).

⚠ **NOT verified against live Meta.** This role has `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` denied on the break-glass token.

⚠ **ENG-1476's reporter-ticket gate is still outstanding**: the three documented production calls against Phoenix account `448692064923397`, confirming ads scope to campaign `120245795903840105` / ad set `120245795903860105`. That needs break-glass access and is not satisfied by this PR alone.

Nothing on any customer ad account was mutated, and no reactivation is proposed. ENG-1584's remaining half is a live-ads decision under CS-64's approval gate, not engineering.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Tests pass: 634 passing, 0 failing. Core live checks passed. Pagination, Phoenix production verification, and the ENG-1476 reporter-ticket gate remain outstanding.

title: Remove get_leads_by_crm_criteria, orphaned from deleted Drip Campaigns (ENG-1602)
body:
## Summary

`get_leads_by_crm_criteria`'s MCP handler calls `POST /api/drip-campaigns/preview-segment`, which 404s for every caller. Root cause: that route — along with the rest of the Drip Campaigns feature (routes, services, cron executor, `manage_drip_campaign` tool, UI) — was already deleted in `49e622a79` ("remove Drip Campaigns feature, superseded by Sequences"). That cleanup pass missed this one tool because it doesn't have "drip" in its *name*, only in its description and target route path.

This is not a missing feature to build — it's a straggler from an already-decided, already-executed removal.

## Why removal, not implementation

- **No active customer commitment.** The feature's own author, Harsha, separately confirmed in `dev.md` (2026-04-27 investigation) that Drip Campaigns was "accidentally introduced... not intentionally designed as a separate product feature," and agreed to its removal. Zero Linear tickets (support/sales/CS) reference "drip" or "segment" outside ENG-1602 itself.
- **Capability is already covered.** `lifecycle`, `heatScore`, `utmSource` are already standard filterable fields in `search_leads`'s generic filter engine (`LEAD_STANDARD_FILTER_FIELDS`), which also already has list scoping, org-access control, and admin `client_id` scoping (ENG-1596). Nothing this tool promised is actually missing from the product.
- **Implementing it "for real" would reintroduce a known bug.** The tool's advertised contract requires a `total` field reflecting the *full* matching count across every list the caller owns, uncapped. `search_leads` deliberately does NOT state a total unless the scan is exhaustive (ENG-1207) — a stated-but-wrong total previously caused a real prod incident (a weak model read a partial count as a total and under-delivered). Building this tool as specified means reintroducing exactly the bug ENG-1207 already fixed in the sibling code path.

## What changed

- Removed the `get_leads_by_crm_criteria` tool registration from `backend/src/mcp/server/apiTools.ts`.
- Removed its now-orphaned test file (`mcp.tools.getLeadsByCrmCriteria.test.ts`) — its own header called it "Phase A of the drip-campaigns multi-tenant refactor."
- Confirmed not referenced anywhere else: not in `emma/tools.ts`'s `bridgedToolNames`/`adminToolNames`, not in any skill-assignment list, not called from any other route or service.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] Confirmed zero remaining references to `get_leads_by_crm_criteria` in `backend/src`
- [x] Confirmed tool was not bridged into the in-app Emma surface (customers were never able to call it)

Fixes ENG-1602.

title: fix(judge): permit a trailing closing HTML tag on the publish-withheld marker (ENG-995 follow-up)
body:

A new opening tag or any other content after the marker's own closing tag still breaks the match, so the original re-attempt/re-explain rejection is unaffected. ## Test plan - [x] `npm run typecheck` (backend) — clean - [x] Reproduced the real production session's exact final-message shape in a unit test; confirmed it fails against the previously-shipped regex and passes against the fix - [x] Added a second test confirming a genuinely new paragraph tacked on after the marker's own closing tag is still correctly NOT excluded - [x] Full `sessionScoring` suite: 223/223 passing - [x] Pre-push hook (tsc + targeted jest) green Risk: Low Updates publish-withheld marker regexes to allow trailing closing HTML tags. title: ENG-397: deterministic Workflow engine (typed steps, checkpoints, resumability)
body:
## Summary
- Foundational Workflow execution engine (`services/agentMode/core/workflow.ts`): ordered typed steps, entity-ID checkpointing, up-front parameter resolution via the existing ENG-396 AskUserQuestion gate, post-step read-back verification, and output→input threading between steps.
- Demonstrative step (`createCampaignStep.ts`) matching the ticket's own example: `create_campaign(objective, budget_mode) -> campaign_id`.
- Impure orchestrator (`workflowRunner.ts`): `startWorkflow`/`advanceWorkflow`.
- `ChatSession.workflowRun` + optimistic-locked `updateSessionWorkflowRun()` in `chatbotService.ts`, mirroring the existing `updateSessionAskUserQuestion` pattern.

No chat/tool wiring in this PR — `startWorkflow`/`advanceWorkflow` are internal entry points exercised only by tests. Rendering a workflow through Emma's live tool loop is a deliberately separate follow-on (see ENG-419's own comment thread, which recommends this as an independent child once this engine exists).

## Bugs found and fixed across two independent review passes

**CodeRabbit, round 1:**
- `resolveStepParameters` could be satisfied by an unrelated answered question of a different kind, applying the wrong decision's payload.
- A step that omitted a declared output got checkpointed as the literal string `"undefined"` and threaded into the next step as a fake entity ID.
- `budget_mode` was gated but never verified in the read-back (objective was, budget wasn't).

**CodeRabbit, round 2 (on my own fix for the above):**
- `startWorkflow`'s `initialParameters` seeding could inject a *gated* key (e.g. `objective`) directly, letting a caller bypass the AskUserQuestion gate entirely. `startWorkflow` now rejects any `initialParameters` key that appears in any step's `requiredParameters`.

**Independent fresh-eyes subagent review (explicitly briefed to distrust every prior claim above and re-derive findings from scratch):**
- `advanceWorkflow` guarded `step.execute()` against a thrown exception but left `step.verify()` unguarded. Since `verify()` is expected to do live read-back I/O, a thrown verify() (e.g. a network timeout) skipped every checkpoint write — leaving the run `in_progress` with the step unattempted, so the *next* `advanceWorkflow` call (an ordinary retry, not even concurrent) would call `execute()` again and create a second real entity. This is the exact duplicate-creation failure class ENG-397 exists to close. It didn't fire in this PR only because the one shipped step happens to wrap its own read-back call in try/catch — now fixed at the engine level so it doesn't depend on every future step author remembering to do the same.
- Tightened the invalid-output check further: previously only excluded `undefined`/`null` before coercing into an entity id; now also rejects empty strings and non-string/non-number values.
- Added test coverage for the optimistic-lock `conflict` outcome, which had zero coverage despite being load-bearing for any future concurrent caller.

## Known, explicitly deferred (not fixed in this PR) — sharpened after the independent review

- **Security**: `createCampaignStep` calls `metaService.createCampaign()` directly rather than through `AgentModeService.callMetaMarketingApi()`'s two-phase preview/confirm gate. The independent review pushed back on treating this as "just missing wiring": the ENG-396 gate this step reuses answers "has a human chosen the VALUE for objective/budget_mode," not "has a human confirmed THIS SPECIFIC mutation is about to fire right now" — which is what the two-phase confirm gate provides for every other live Meta write in this codebase. These are not redundant. Deferring is reasonable only because there are zero production callers today (verified via repo-wide grep); reusing `createCampaignStep.execute()` unchanged in a live path without an equivalent confirm-before-execute gate would be a regression versus every other Meta write action in this codebase, not optional polish. This should block whatever adds the first live caller (the ENG-419 follow-on), not be filed as generic debt.
- **Performance**: `findNextStep`/`recordStepSuccess` do O(n) checkpoint scans per step transition. Independent review agreed: genuinely premature optimization against a caller that doesn't exist yet, at workflow sizes of a handful of steps.
- **Concurrency**: true concurrent `advanceWorkflow` calls on the same session could each execute a mutating step before either persists (the optimistic lock protects the write, not the execute). Independent review sharpened this: it is not a hypothetical edge case, it is the exact failure mode (a Meta mutation running twice before either DB write lands) ENG-397 was chartered to eliminate. Deferring is defensible only because there are verifiably zero live callers today. This must be closed — with a real concurrency model (e.g. a per-session mutex/lease before `execute()` runs) informed by whatever actually calls this — before any live caller can invoke `advanceWorkflow`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm test -- --runTestsByPath src/services/agentMode/core/__tests__/workflow.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeWorkflowEngine.metaCreateCampaign.test.ts` — 35/35 passing: one test per acceptance criterion, plus dedicated regression tests for every bug found across both review passes
- [x] Ran the full pre-existing `chatbotService`/`askUserQuestion`/`workPlanInputRequest`/`resumePlan` test suites to confirm no regressions from the `ChatSession` edit — 135/135 passing (post `main` sync)
- [x] Branch synced with `main` (188 files changed upstream since branch creation), merged cleanly, all suites re-verified after sync

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Update: two more findings from CodeRabbit's third pass, both fixed
- `advanceWorkflow`'s invalid-output check accepted `NaN`/`+Infinity`/`-Infinity` (typeof 'number' but not a real id) and whitespace-only strings (typeof 'string', non-empty) — now requires `Number.isFinite` for numbers and a non-blank trimmed value for strings.
- `updateSessionWorkflowRun`'s `failIfActiveExists` guard had its own TOCTOU race with the `startWorkflow` session-existence pre-check added earlier: a session deleted between the read and the guarded write would still pass `attribute_not_exists(workflowRun)` (satisfied identically whether the field is absent on an existing row or the whole item is missing), so DynamoDB's `UpdateItem` could still upsert a partial row. Folded `attribute_exists(sessionId)` into the same atomic `ConditionExpression` to close it properly. Added `chatbotService.workflowRun.test.ts` (mirroring the existing `askUserQuestion` test's approach — spying on the real DynamoDB client) since the mocked-chatbotDb tests elsewhere never exercised this method's actual body.

37/37 → 51/51 tests now (core engine + AC/hardening suite + new persistence-layer suite), all passing, typecheck clean, full pre-existing suite (102 tests) unaffected.

## Update: one more finding from CodeRabbit's fourth pass, fixed
`advanceWorkflow` built a step's execution input by merging checkpointed entity IDs *ahead of* `resolvedParameters` — meaning if a workflow definition ever used the same name for a step's declared output and a gated parameter key, the resolved parameter would silently win, and a later step would act on a stale/answered value instead of the real checkpointed entity. Nothing in the shipped `createCampaignStep` triggers this (its outputs and gated params never share a name), but nothing prevented a future workflow definition from doing so.

Fixed two ways: `startWorkflow` now rejects a definition with this collision before any write (`findOutputParameterNameCollisions`), and as defense-in-depth `advanceWorkflow`'s merge order is flipped so checkpointed entity IDs always win regardless of entry-point validation.

62/62 tests now, typecheck clean, 102 pre-existing tests unaffected.

## Update: fifth-pass finding, fixed
CodeRabbit flagged a real conflict: two steps declaring the SAME gated parameter key but a DIFFERENT `questionKind`/`payloadField` — the first step's answer would silently satisfy the second step's (semantically different) gate, since `resolveStepParameters` only checks "is this key already resolved," not "was this specific question answered." `startWorkflow` now rejects a definition with this conflict (`findConflictingGatedParameterKeys`), mirroring the existing output/gated-key collision check.

67/67 tests now, typecheck clean.

title: feat: backfill Meta metrics history through the fixed lead join (ENG-1601)
body:
Follow-up to **ENG-1601**, which is Done and proven in production — the 2026-08-27 09:00 UTC run moved attribution from 0 to 33 of 160 leads on the same store, matching a prediction written down before the merge.

## Why a backfill is needed

`metaMetricsSnapshotCron` only ever walks the last `SETTLING_WINDOW_DAYS` (28) days. Everything older was either never written, or was written through the broken `firstTouch`-only join that dropped 36% of attributable leads.

A dry run against production shows **8,174 leads across 126 days** of CRM history against **29 days** present in the metrics store. There is real history to recover.

## The script adds no new logic

ENG-916 exported `fetchMetaAccountContext` and `snapshotMetaMetricsForDate` with docstrings saying they were "usable by a future backfill script without duplicating this logic". This is that script. It mirrors the cron's own sequencing for the cron's own reasons:

- **credentials resolved once** — the resolver can refresh and PERSIST a token inline, so per-day resolution would mean one write per day against a live client's record, and one identical CRITICAL error per day once a token expires
- **one lead walk serves every date** — the per-date path cannot early-stop (leads order by `leadId`, not `createdAt`), so asking per day would re-walk every list 90 times for identical pages

## Safety properties

**Dry run by default.** `--apply` is required to write. The dry run validates the expensive preconditions and prints the exact date plan, and states plainly what it does **not** cover: the per-day Meta insights fetch and the resulting row values. It is also honest that it is not literally side-effect free, since credential resolution may persist a refreshed token.

**Re-runnable.** Rows key on a deterministic `entityKey` + date, so a repeat OVERWRITES its own row rather than appending. An interrupted run resumes by running it again. A failed day is **named, not just counted**, and one bad day never aborts the rest.

**The 2026-07-02 UTM epoch is a hard floor.** Earlier days are not merely empty — they are structurally unattributable, and writing them produces a long flat run of "0 attributed" that reads as a regression on any chart built from this store. `--allow-pre-utm` exists so that choice is explicit rather than accidental. Verified: `--from 2026-06-01` is refused.

**Paced between days**, because Meta rate-limits per ad account.

## Also in this PR

A stale docstring on `snapshotMetaMetricsForDate` still described the join as reading `firstTouch.utm.campaign` **directly** — the exact behaviour ENG-1601 removed. It survived the fix by two commits, and a stale contract sitting above an exported function is precisely what a backfill author would build against.

The second commit removes a duplicate: the script had kept its own copy of `getLeadsByDateForUser`. It matched the cron for real data and diverged on malformed `createdAt` — the cron throws, the copy stringified it, bucketed under a junk key and silently dropped the lead. Real records are ISO strings so it never bit, but a duplicate that can drift from the thing it mirrors is how you end up verifying your own reimplementation instead of the code that actually runs. The cron's implementation is now exported and imported; the export is the only change to the cron itself.

## Verification status

- typecheck clean; the ENG-916 cron suite (26 tests) passes
- **dry run executed against production**: credentials resolved (account `1842363582956923`, USD, `America/New_York`), 8,174 leads across 126 days, date plan printed
- the UTM-epoch guard verified by attempting a pre-epoch range

⚠ **`--apply` has never run.** It is blocked: the workstation IAM user is read-only on `AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots` (`not authorized to perform: dynamodb:PutItem`). The failure path was therefore exercised for real and behaved as designed — both days named, no abort, clean summary, and a before/after diff confirmed the table was untouched (87 rows, 0 changed, 0 new).

**So the write path is unverified.** Recommended before a full run:

```
--apply --limit 2      # newest two days; they sit inside the 28-day window,
                       # so the cron already wrote them through the fixed join —
                       # the backfill should reproduce them identically
```

That makes the first apply a self-checking one: any difference from what the cron wrote this morning means the script diverges from it.

⚠ Running locally requires working around `backend/.env`, which carries `AWS_REGION=ap-south-1` and credentials for a different AWS account than the one holding these tables. Documented in the script header.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Adds a dry-run-by-default Meta metrics history backfill that reuses the ENG-1601 lead join. It validates dates, UTM bounds, scope, and write targets. It requires explicit production-write approval. The apply path remains unverified because the available IAM user lacks DynamoDB write access.
