title: [needs human] Verify account_id's real platform before failing closed on the ENG-1599 reverse publish route (ENG-1616)
body:
ENG-1599 (PR #2655) added a reverse equivalence route so a schedule authorized only for `twitter_manage_post` can also cover a single standalone tweet via `post_on_connected_account`, scoped to `platform:'twitter'`. That route required the call to omit `account_id`, because `post_on_connected_account` ignores `args.platform` once `account_id` is present and `args.platform` can't be trusted on its own. `list_connected_accounts` pairs every account_id with its platform, so a call shaped `post_on_connected_account(account_id: '...')` is a plausible way this route gets invoked — but the fail-closed rule made it unreachable for that call shape, regardless of whether the account was actually the authorized one.

**Correction to the original PR description:** this is a proactive hardening of a logic gap, not a reproduction of an observed production failure, and it does not fix the incident ENG-1616 was filed from. That incident (session `672b3af7`, 2026-08-27, schedule `1d001fba-0fb7-4bcd-80f6-6041b244a442`) is already resolved — by ENG-1599 itself, which merged later the same day. The session's actual blocked call passed `platform: 'twitter'`, not `account_id`, and it ran ~6 hours *before* ENG-1599 merged (not "the day after ENG-1599 shipped" as originally claimed here) — so it never exercised this route, in either its pre- or post-fix form, and does not evidence this specific gap. No account_id-shaped call has been observed hitting this refusal in production; this PR closes a latent gap defensively, ahead of any confirmed occurrence.

Fix: `isPublishCallWithinAuthorizedScope` now takes an optional `resolvedAccountPlatform` param — the account_id's real platform, looked up from storage rather than trusted from the call's own args — and uses it in place of the caller-supplied platform whenever `account_id` is present. `refuseUnauthorizedScheduledPublish` resolves it via `connectedAccountsDb.getAccountsWithOwnerIncludingOrgShared`, only when it could change the outcome (account_id present, run authorized, exact tool name not already granted), and still fails closed if the lookup errors, returns nothing, or no resolver is supplied at all — fully backward compatible with every existing caller/test.

Verified: unit tests cover the account_id-bearing branch directly — verified-platform match (allow), platform mismatch (refuse), contradictory caller-claimed platform (refuse), no resolver supplied (refuse), lookup error (refuse), and exact-tool-name-match skipping the lookup entirely. Full publish-consent-gate test cluster passes. `npx tsc --noEmit` could not be independently re-confirmed post-merge with `main` due to a local heap-capacity limit on the build box (reproducible OOM at the mandated 4096MB ceiling) — this needs a real CI run once the PR is taken out of draft.

title: fix(agentmode): page oncall on a fully-blocked LinkedIn invite run (ENG-1657)

**What broke, and where.** PR #2653 (ENG-1132) implemented AC1/AC2 — persisting a
plain-language notice when a scheduled LinkedIn outreach run hits an account-level
invite cooldown/pacing cap — but never implemented AC3: an internal oncall alert.
Post-merge verification (ENG-1657) confirmed AC1/AC2 pass 11/11 on the merged head
and that a grep of the merged diff for `alert`/`oncall` returns zero matches. Left
as-is, a fully-blocked LinkedIn-outreach schedule can run silently every day with no
internal signal until a customer complains — the exact 38-day-blind-spot class
`linkedInConnectionHealth.ts` exists to prevent for disconnects, just not wired here.

**What this PR does.** When `detectLinkedInInviteSendBlock` finds a schedule-wide

title: Size the settle cap for the Immutable policy on production (ENG-1183)
body:
Fixes ENG-1183. Supersedes #2390 and #2392 — see *What happened to the original PRs* below.

## The bug

`eb-deploy.sh` waits `EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` for an update that was already running when the deploy arrived. On expiry it does not shrug and proceed — it calls `fail()`:

```
environment '...' was still Updating after waiting 600s for an in-progress
update to finish (pre-update settle 1/3). Version '...' was NOT applied.
```

**Nothing has ever set that variable.** `git grep EB_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS .github/workflows` returns nothing, so both production deploys run on the script's 600s default.

600s is a Rolling-era number — it assumed an environment frees up in 3-5 minutes. `backend/.ebextensions/rolling.config` (the filename is a fossil) switched this environment to `DeploymentPolicy: Immutable` on 2026-07-01 in e1220d523, and nothing re-derived the budgets. Immutable launches a parallel fleet, health-checks it, swaps, then drains the old one.

Measured over the last 24 consecutive production deploys:

| | seconds |
|---|---|
| median own rollout | ~535 |
| max own rollout | **1352** |
| settle cap | **600** |

An in-flight update outlasting 600s is ordinary, not stuck.

## Reachability

Nothing in Actions can leave an update in flight — `deploy.yml` is serialised by `concurrency: deploy-production`, and every sampled run logs `[pre-update settle 1/3] Status=Ready` on its first poll. EB can, though, and does: `05-instance-recycling.config` sets `ManagedActionsEnabled: true` with `InstanceRefreshEnabled: true` and `PreferredStartTime: "Sun:10:00"`. A deploy landing in that weekly window is failed today against a healthy environment, and takes the ENG-865 Slack alert with it.

So this is latent rather than firing — the same honest status #2390 gave it: *"Hasn't bitten yet; it would have."*

## The number

1200s, bounded on both sides, and **both bounds are asserted, not just argued in a comment**:

- **floor — 900s**, the EB command `Timeout` declared in `rolling.config`. Giving up before EB's own timeout means failing a deploy while EB still considers the in-flight command live.
- **ceiling — 1500s left** (`2700 - 1200`) to run our own rollout, above the 1352s worst case measured above.

`partner-deploy` keeps the 600s default deliberately: a different application, no `.ebextensions` in this repo, and ~60s deploys — already 10x headroom. The test skips the Immutable-only bounds for it rather than pretending they apply.

## Tests

`eb-deploy.test.sh`: **82 -> 91 checks, 0 failed.** All ten `CI script tests` suites pass (441 checks), `shellcheck` clean.

The new block is structural, in the shape of the ENG-1522 block above it, and lives in that suite for the same stated reason — it is already wired into `CI script tests`, and orphaned suites in this repo have a habit of going silently red (`staging-deploy-gate`, `coverage-report`, the paths-filter negation).

Every number is **read from the repo**, not duplicated into the test: the EB `Timeout` from `.ebextensions`, the settle default from `eb-deploy.sh`. Fixing this by raising the script default instead of the workflow keeps the suite green.

### Proven to fail

Each check was mutated:

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| remove the fix (back to 600s) | `settle cap 600s gives up before EB command Timeout 900s` |
| over-correct to 1400s | `leaves only 1300s after settling, below the 1400s ... measured` |
| `timeout-minutes: 50 -> 40` | `budget 2700s >= step timeout 2400s; the script can never report why` |
| policy `Immutable -> Rolling` | `no .ebextensions config declares DeploymentPolicy: Immutable` |
| break the extractor | **both** fail-open guards trip |
| script default `600 -> 950` | check reports 950s — the value really is read, not hardcoded |

The `Immutable -> Rolling` mutation initially produced a garbled second failure (`EB command Timeout s`) from an empty variable; the Immutable-only bounds are now skipped in that case, so one clear failure names the cause.

## What happened to the original PRs

Both were written on 2026-08-13 against the **staging deploy job in `tests.yml`**, which ENG-1463 deleted. `main`'s `tests.yml` has seven jobs and none of them deploy.

- **#2390** re-tuned three numbers on that job. Its entire diff has no target left. Its *reasoning* about the settle cap was right, and is what this PR carries forward — moved from staging, where the job is gone, to production, where the policy is the same.
- **#2392** added an early exit on the drain announcement, gated on `EB_READY_ON_DEPLOYMENT_SUCCEEDED` — set only on that same deleted job. Merging it would add ~250 lines of permanently-dead code to the production deploy path. Enabling it for production instead would contradict its own safety argument (*"both production deploys keep demanding the full `Status=Ready`"*), and the data does not ask for it: production deploys are ~9 min against a 45 min budget, 0 failures in 24 runs.

## Deliberately not in this PR

- **The early exit.** Under ENG-1463 the production deploy is the gate that proves the runtime path, so shortening its verification needs its own justification, not a rebase.
- **A runtime test pinned to 1200s.** The settle *mechanism* — wait, then fail at the cap — is already covered by existing cases. Only the number changed, and the number is what the structural checks assert.
- **The `detect-changes` filter gap** — `deploy.yml`'s `backend` filter is `backend/**` only, so a change to `eb-deploy.sh` or `deploy.yml` does not trigger a deploy. That means this PR does not exercise its own change on merge, and eb-deploy.sh changes generally first execute on an unrelated later PR. Same ENG-743 class fixed in the portal in #1095, but closing it here makes CI-only edits trigger production deploys — a policy call, not a cleanup. Flagged for a separate decision.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

Increase the production Immutable deployment settle cap from 600 to 1200 seconds. Keep `partner-deploy` at 600 seconds. Add structural checks for deployment policy, timeout bounds, workflow budgets, and script defaults. No production outage path is changed; rollback remains a configuration revert.

title: ENG-908 / ENG-1298 / ENG-831: make the memory over-length error actionable
body:
Closes **ENG-908**, **ENG-1298** and **ENG-831** — three separately-reported tickets, one cause.

## The bug is the error message

`save_memory` and `save_org_memory` rejected oversized content with:

```
Content must be 2000 characters or less
```

That repeats the limit the schema already declares and adds nothing actionable — not how long the content actually was, not by how much it overran, not what to do instead. With no length to work from, the agent re-sent the identical payload and looped.

It is measured, not theoretical:

| ticket | evidence |
|---|---|
| **ENG-908** | *"the single most repeated tool-level defect in the window"* — 3 of 55 sessions, and the only thing dragging an otherwise-perfect run below a clean score |
| **ENG-1298** | four separate sessions inside one 38-hour window |
| **ENG-831** | `save_org_memory` failed **three consecutive times** on one run; its first listed complaint is *"the error does not report the ACTUAL character count"* |

Every occurrence recovers, so this never surfaces as user-visible harm. It just burns model round-trips on every affected run, quietly and continuously.

## The fix

The message now reports the **actual length**, the **overrun**, and the two ways out — shorten, or split across several memories — and says explicitly *not* to retry the same text, because that was the loop:

```
Content must be 2000 characters or less — this content is 2347 characters,
347 over the limit. Do NOT retry the same text: it will fail identically.
Shorten it to the essential fact, or split it into multiple memories of at
most 2000 characters each, then save again.
```

**Four guards, one rule.** The cap was enforced in four places with four copies of the same throw (user add, user update, org add, org update). They now share one helper, so the wording cannot drift between the path a user hits and the path an org hits — which is precisely how ENG-831 and ENG-908 came to be filed separately about the same sentence.

**Counting is unchanged**: code points via `Array.from`, not UTF-16 code units (ENG-821). An emoji costs one, and the number quoted back is the number enforced — a length the caller cannot reconcile with its own content would be worse than none. Pinned by a test that saves 2000 emoji successfully.

Both tool descriptions now state the limit is a hard **reject**, not a truncation, and tell the model to split across calls rather than re-send.

## Testing

11 tests in `eng908.memoryContentLimit`. Reverting to the old message fails **six** of them — actual length, overrun, no-retry instruction, both remedies, the field name, and the code-point unit.

**1940 pass** across the 117 memory / db / tools / emma suites. `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.

## Risk

Error-text and tool-description change only. No behaviour change to what is accepted or rejected: the same content passes and the same content fails, at the same boundary, counted in the same unit.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

Update `save_memory` and `save_org_memory` length validation. A shared helper now reports actual length and overrun, and advises shortening or splitting content. Validation remains code-point based with unchanged boundaries. Tool descriptions now state that oversized content is rejected, not truncated. Added 11 tests.

title: ENG-1322: bind CONVERSION_ACTION REMOVE to a disclosed approval
body:
Follow-up to ENG-1322, taking **option B** on the `REMOVE` scoping question.

## The problem

`confirm_conversion_action_removal: true` was sufficient on its own — **and the model sets its own arguments.** So the only thing between a model that decided to tidy up a conversion action and a permanent, unrecoverable removal was a sentence in the tool description asking it not to.

ENG-941 already wrote down why that is not a control:

> *an override the model can introduce after approval is not user-granted, whatever the tool description says*

ENG-1526 acted on that for `override_tracking_check`. This is the same shape guarding a **strictly worse** outcome: a removed conversion action cannot be re-enabled, and every campaign bidding toward it as a goal stops counting it — which silently changes how those campaigns bid.

## The fix

The **same primitive** as ENG-1526, not a second mechanism: an HMAC over the exact call, keyed with a server-only secret.

A claimed removal with no matching token **halts**, discloses exactly what will happen, and issues the token. Only a replay presenting it removes anything. The path is a loop, not a dead end.

```
This PERMANENTLY stops a Google Ads conversion action from recording.

It cannot be re-enabled afterwards, and any campaign bidding toward it as a
goal will stop counting it — which changes how those campaigns bid.
Conversions it already recorded stay in your reports, so this is not data
loss, but it is not reversible either.

Conversion action: customers/…/conversionActions/…
```

## The part worth reviewing

The digest covers the conversion action's **resource name**, because that is the destructive argument here. A token minted for a *different* action — or a different customer — is refused rather than honoured, so an approval the user gave for one removal cannot authorise another they never saw. Key order is irrelevant, since the replay is rebuilt by the model.

`LIST`, `CREATE` and `UPDATE` are untouched. The existing `UPDATE status=REMOVED` redirect still routes here, so the back door stays closed.

## Testing

7 tests on the binding, including the case that matters — a token for `conversionActions/222` refused against `conversionActions/111` — plus absent, forged, wrong-customer, wrong-secret, and key-order-independence.

**Two existing matrix tests changed contract, not outcome.** They pinned the old signature and the sentence *"Ask the user before setting the flag"*. That sentence was advice; the assertions now pin the enforced fact — the flag alone does nothing, and the model cannot approve this itself.

**767 pass** across the 27 google / tools / gate suites. `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean.

## Risk

One entity/action. A caller that previously passed only the flag now gets a disclosure halt instead of a removal — which is the intended behaviour change, and fails toward *not deleting* rather than deleting.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: High. `CONVERSION_ACTION REMOVE` now requires a disclosed, action- and customer-bound HMAC token with `confirm_conversion_action_removal=true`. Invalid or mismatched tokens block permanent removal. `LIST`, `CREATE`, and `UPDATE` remain unchanged. The change affects an irreversible production path.

title: [needs human] Recurse into sub-folders for Google Drive KB materialize/read/list (ENG-1624)
body:
**Bug (ENG-1624):** Phoenix Technologies' registered Drive KB folder held only sub-folders (ratio folders like "4x5"); the approved ad creatives lived inside those. `materialize_knowledge_base_asset` returned file-not-found for the 6 approved files and "Not authorized" for the sub-folder itself, blocking a live 6-ad launch at step 9/10.

**Root cause:** every Google Drive query in the KB path (`materializeKnowledgeBaseAsset`, `readGoogleDriveSharedFile`, `listKnowledgeBaseFiles`) was scoped to `'<folderId>' in parents` — direct children of the registered root only, with no recursion. The "Not authorized" message was our own flat allowlist check (`folders.some(f => f.folderId === folderId)`) rejecting a sub-folder ID that was never in the list — not a real Google permission failure. Harsha confirmed live via the service account that Drive access to the sub-folder and its files worked fine once the sub-folder ID was manually added to the allowlist.

**Fix:** added `getGoogleDriveFolderTreeIds()`, a BFS folder-tree walk from a registered root (capped at 500 folders as a backstop). `materializeKnowledgeBaseAsset` and `readGoogleDriveSharedFile` now search across every resolved folder ID via an OR'd Drive query instead of just the root. `listKnowledgeBaseFiles` now lists files across the whole tree and excludes folder mimeTypes from results (previously shown as 0-byte placeholder entries). When a sub-folder genuinely can't be listed (e.g. an unshared shortcut target, surfaced as a 403/401 during the tree walk), the error now names that sub-folder and instructs sharing it with the Drive service account, instead of a bare "not found".

**Verified:** wrote failing tests first against the pre-fix code (confirmed they fail with the exact pre-fix symptoms — file-not-found and a bare "not found" message), then applied the fix and confirmed they pass. Used a mocked root → sub-folder → image Drive fixture per the ticket's acceptance criteria; no live Drive/Meta account needed.

title: Make deploy.yml gate its own changes (ENG-1658)
body:
Fixes ENG-1658. Follow-up to #2673, which found this while closing ENG-1183.

## The bug

`detect-changes` filtered on `backend/**` and `partner-portal/**` only, so **a change to the deploy machinery triggered no deploy**. `eb-deploy.sh` *is* the deploy — it applies the version and decides whether the environment took it — and `deploy.yml` is what runs it.

Confirmed rather than argued. #2673 changed the production settle cap; its own post-merge run on `main` ([33357844871](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/actions/runs/33357844871)):

```
success  Detect changed projects
skipped  Backend deploy to production
skipped  Partner portal deploy to production
```

**21 commits touched these two files in the 34 days to 2026-08-31, and not one of them deployed.** Each first executed on a later, unrelated PR — which is where a mistake in it surfaces, attributed to that PR.

## What that already costs

Five of twelve `eb-deploy.sh` commits are follow-up fixes to the one before, three of them same-day:

```
Aug 4  a610d093b  don't fail a healthy deploy on EB's lagging health rollup
Aug 4  668d7e2c6  fail closed when an ALB reports zero target groups        <- fixes the above
Aug 9  ed494f4d0  let EB_HEALTH_PROBE_DRYRUN exercise the health probe
Aug 9  bc5f38ce2  bound the probe dry run so a stalled diagnostic...        <- fixes the above
Aug 9  07dde650a  kill the stalled probe's AWS call, not just its wrapper   <- fixes the above
```

This is the script whose false-success and non-convergence modes have already cost ~17h (ENG-865) and ~29h (ENG-836) of production downtime.

## The change

Both paths, in **both** filters. `partner-deploy` runs the same script under its own budgets, so the rule is uniform rather than backend-only; partner deploys take ~2 min. `tests.yml` has carried `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh` in its own `backend` filter since ENG-743 — `deploy.yml` was the only workflow that never got this.

### Cost, measured

| | |
|---|---|
| extra backend deploys | **+21 / 34 days** |
| baseline | ~9.5/day (57 in 6 days) |
| increase | **+6.5%** |
| backend prod deploy failures, last 100 runs | **0 of 88** |

The objection this was weighed against — that comment-only edits would trigger pointless deploys — **is not supported by the history**. Across all 26 commits to these two files since June, every one has functional lines. There has never been a comment-only edit.

Four alternatives were investigated and are recorded on ENG-1658, including deploying to staging instead (the environment is still live — `api-stage.agentweb.pro/health` returns 200). Staging lost on its merits, not on sign-off: the deleted staging job carried its **own** budgets against its **own** environment, so it would not have caught ENG-1183, which was production's settle cap being wrong.

## The guard

`paths-filter-hygiene.test.sh`: **8 -> 14 checks, 0 failed.** Two rules, both *derived* rather than hardcoded to today's files:

- **A.** a workflow that filters must be matched by one of its own filters
- **B.** a job gated on `outputs.<f>` that runs `.github/scripts/<s>.sh` must have that script matched by filter `<f>`

Ungated jobs are exempt from B — they always run, so nothing can skip them. Patterns are matched as **picomatch globs, not literals**, so `tests.yml`'s `.github/**` filter satisfies the rule without a redundant entry; comparing literals would have made this rule a nuisance rather than a check.

### Proven to fail

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| revert the change entirely | all **three** violations reported (rule A + both rule-B jobs) |
| remove only the script entry | just the **two** rule-B ones — the rules are independent |
| disable the auditor's fail-open guard | self-check goes red |

Self-checks pin both directions, the glob case, the ungated exemption, and that an auditor parsing zero gated jobs is *reported* rather than passed.

## One thing this PR caught in itself

`pipefail-hygiene.test.sh` went red on the first commit, on my own new line:

```
564: if EXPECT_GATED_JOBS=1 python3 "${GATING_AUDITOR}" ... | grep -q 'fail-open'
```

Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on first match, the writer takes EPIPE, and that status becomes the pipeline's — so a successful match reads as a failure and the branch inverts. Same shape as #2523, in a self-check whose entire job is proving a fail-open cannot hide. Fixed with a here-string in the second commit, and re-verified that the self-check still goes red when the guard it tests is disabled.

## This PR exercises its own change

Unlike #2673, this one touches `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, which the new filter covers — so **the merge should produce a real `Backend deploy to production`** rather than `skipped`. That is the fix demonstrating itself, and I will confirm it on the post-merge run.

All ten `CI script tests` suites pass (447 checks); `shellcheck` clean.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Updates `deploy.yml` so workflow or `eb-deploy.sh` changes trigger the required backend and partner production deploy filters. Adds hygiene checks for filter coverage, gated scripts, undefined outputs, glob patterns, ungated jobs, and fail-open behavior. Fixes a `pipefail` test issue. Reports 15/15 path-filter checks, 18/18 `pipefail` checks, 447 CI script checks, and clean ShellCheck results.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: ENG-1526 / ENG-1322: relay approval tokens through the tool-result minimizer
body:
Found while verifying **#2675** on production. It is **pre-existing**, not introduced by that PR — but #2675 inherits it, so neither approval loop works end to end without this.

## What is broken

Both gates halt, disclose, and issue an HMAC the caller is told to replay *"exactly as returned here"*. `extractMinimalToolResult` discards everything it does not explicitly name, and its confirmation branch named **neither token**.

Verified against production before the fix, driving the real agent:

```
result keys: [awaitingUserConfirmation, confirmationDetail,
              confirmationPrompt, requiresConfirmation, success, summary]

tracking_override_token present: False
```

So the model is handed an instruction it cannot follow. **The tracking override can never be applied**, and a conversion-action removal can never be completed, no matter how many times a user approves.

## Why it went unnoticed

It fails **closed**. The tracking gate simply keeps blocking — which is what it does anyway — so from the outside an unusable override is indistinguishable from a working gate. Nothing unsafe ever happened.

But ENG-1526's own claim that *"the path is a loop, not a dead end"* was untrue in production, and a recovery path callers cannot complete is one they route around.

This is the **ENG-1523 erasure class again**, in the one branch that fix did not touch: blocked results and tracking warnings were rescued from this minimizer; the confirmation branch was not.

## Why the tests did not catch it

The handler-level tests call the dispatcher directly and **never reach the minimizer**. They proved the tokens were *issued* while saying nothing about whether they were *delivered*. Only driving the real agent against prod shows the difference.

The new tests exercise `extractMinimalToolResult` itself, closing exactly that gap.

## Scope

Named explicitly rather than pattern-matched on a `_token` suffix — these two exist to be replayed by the caller, and a blanket rule would eventually relay a field that does not. A test asserts an unrelated `access_token` is still dropped, so the branch stays an allowlist rather than becoming a passthrough.

**5 tests.** Removing the relay fails exactly the two that assert delivery.

## Note on the suite

`agentModeController.consentNarrowsOnEdit` and `agentModeController.inheritedModelRatchet` are **red on clean `origin/main`** — 20 failures, identical with and without this change. Pre-existing and unrelated; flagging rather than folding a fix for them into this PR.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low. `extractMinimalToolResult` now preserves `tracking_override_token` and `conversion_action_removal_token` during confirmation. This enables approved recovery actions to complete. The minimizer explicitly allowlists these tokens and still excludes unrelated `access_token` values. Tests cover both tokens and the exclusion rule.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: [needs human] Auto-retry workplan control-plane flakes (decision card + step status) (ENG-1626)
body:
Production session 822c1ed4-133e-4081-b8c9-ee43547fd463 showed two control-plane flakes forcing manual customer retries:

1. A decision-card (ask_user_question) creation failed mid-workplan. The code already retried once within the same turn, but if that retry also failed, the fallback message told the customer to retry — and the retryable-failure flag stamped on that message was never read on the next turn, so a plain follow-up message (not the literal phrase 'retry creating the card') skipped re-enforcement entirely. Fixed by re-arming the disposition check on the customer's next turn whenever the prior assistant message carries `workPlanDispositionFailure.retryable: true`, regardless of what they typed.

2. `set_work_plan_status` failed twice in the same session with no system-level retry — any exception in its read-modify-write (session read, workPlan persist, associated skill/counter writes) surfaced immediately as a customer-visible failure. Fixed by wrapping it in one automatic retry, gated on the existing errorClass classifier so only genuinely transient failures (timeout/network/rate_limit/upstream_5xx) retry — deterministic validation failures are unaffected. Confirmed via code inspection that failure-cluster telemetry already captures errorClass generically for this tool, so no further plumbing was needed there.

Verified via targeted unit tests covering both fixes (retry-then-succeed, non-transient-fails-immediately, persistent-failure-gives-up-after-two-attempts for the status retry; retryable-metadata detection for the disposition retry) plus the full existing workplan/controller test suites to confirm no regressions.

Note: a third item in the same ticket (a 2026-08-26 Slack-session terminal error) could not be root-caused — this environment's read-only role lacks S3 access to retrieve EB logs that old, and the session's messages are fully offloaded with nothing left to inspect. Left out per the ticket's own guidance to split it into its own issue if unrelated.

title: Name the mechanism, not a file that never existed (ENG-1184)
body:
Fixes ENG-1184 — but **not the way the ticket proposed**, and the difference is the point.

## The ticket's premise inverted

ENG-1184 was filed because `asgLifecycleGuard.ts` said:

> Fixed hook name, mirrored in `.ebextensions/07-termination-lifecycle.config`.

That file is not on `main` and never has been. The ticket reasonably concluded the graceful drain therefore exists only as a side effect of the deploy path, and proposed adding the missing config.

**The pointer was wrong, not the setup.** `eb-deploy.sh` already records the reasoning, above `ensure_termination_lifecycle_hook()`:

> This belongs in the deploy path, not `.ebextensions`: an `.ebextensions` resource delta cannot ride an immutable application deploy, while a one-time manually created hook disappears if Elastic Beanstalk ever replaces the ASG. The API is idempotent, so every deploy repairs the hook before `update-environment` is allowed to retire an instance.

So the proposed fix is precisely what that design rejected, for a reason with an incident behind it — a resource-config delta cannot ride a bundle change *at all*, proven on 2026-08-04 at the cost of **~50 minutes of undeployable `main`** (ENG-818 #2277). I had already flagged that on the ticket in August; what I had not established then is the second half.

**A lifecycle hook is ASG state, not instance state.** It persists on the group once installed and applies to every `EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING` transition thereafter — including the ASG replacing an unhealthy instance, which the ticket listed as the case that "needs nothing unusual to happen". Under Immutable, EB moves new instances into the *original* ASG and terminates the temporary one, so the hook survives deploys too. The residual window is an ASG the deploy script has never run against, and `eb-deploy.sh` refuses to deploy if it cannot install the hook first.

That materially lowers the severity from "correctness hole in run durability" to "a comment pointing at the wrong place".

## What actually changed

**1. The pointer now names the mechanism, not a filename** — `ensure_termination_lifecycle_hook()` in `eb-deploy.sh`, with the reasoning inline so this ticket cannot be re-filed. For the same reason it cites the function, not a line number: a line number rots exactly like a filename does.

**2. A second stale claim of the same class**, in `eb-config-conflict.sh`:

> Staging cannot catch this: staging is `AllAtOnce`, which has no resource/instance restriction, so it accepts the identical change and reports green.

Both halves stopped being true and nothing noticed. **ENG-1128 switched staging to Immutable on 2026-08-11**; **ENG-1463 then removed the staging deploy job entirely**, so nothing in CI deploys to staging at all.

This one is worse than a comment, because the script **logs** it:

```
log 'Staging will NOT reproduce this: staging is AllAtOnce and accepts it.'
```

That reaches an engineer at the exact moment they are deciding whether a green run means anything, and tells them the opposite of the truth.

A deployment policy is an environment-level setting in AWS, not something this repo can read, so *any* assertion about one here is a claim that can silently invert. Replaced with what stays true:

```
No staging run is evidence either way: CI has not deployed to staging
since ENG-1463 removed that job. This gate is the only check for it.
```

**3. The test that let it rot.** `eb-config-conflict.test.sh` asserted the literal string `'staging is AllAtOnce'` and kept passing through both changes — because it pinned the **wording**, not the claim. Now asserts the new message, and mutation-verified: restoring the old log line turns it red.

## Verification

- `eb-config-conflict`: **34/34**, and proven to fail — reverting the log line reports `FAIL ENG-836: and warns that no staging run is evidence about this`
- All ten `CI script tests` suites green; `shellcheck` clean
- Backend build (`npm run build`, the CI command) **exit 0**

## Left open on the ticket, deliberately

Two things I am not doing here, both genuinely blocked on AWS rather than on a decision:

- **`.platform/hooks/predeploy`** installing the hook on every instance launch would narrow the residual window further, but the instance role holds only `CompleteLifecycleAction`, `RecordLifecycleActionHeartbeat` and `DescribeAutoScalingInstances` — no `PutLifecycleHook`. That is a capability we do not have, not a call we can make.
- **Harsha's ENG-1341 evidence** — a scheduled chat lost to `Worker shutdown — drain ceiling exceeded`. The drain *ran* and hit its ceiling, so it is a `DRAIN_CEILING_MS` sizing question, independent of the hook. Belongs with ENG-1341.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

Updates termination lifecycle hook documentation and staging validation messages. The change affects comments, shell-script warnings, and tests. It does not change deployment behavior or production paths. Rollback is simple because the change is limited and localized. Verification reports 34/34 related tests passing, all ten CI script suites passing, clean ShellCheck results, and a successful backend build.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: test(ENG-1533): prove both authority answers in one payload
body:
Closes the one AC1–AC4 case the ENG-1533 suite could not distinguish.

**The gap.** Every existing case in the `ENG-1533` block puts exactly one schedule owner in play. With a single owner, a per-row authority lookup and a collapsed one produce identical output, so none of them can tell the two apart. AC1–AC4 describe the mixed case: a plain member reading a list containing both their own scheduled work and a colleague's, where the two rows must answer differently in the same response.

**Mutation-verified, because a passing test proves nothing on its own.** Replacing the per-owner lookup with a single collapsed value:

```ts
switchable: meta ? ([...authorityByOwner.values()][0] ?? false) : false
```

passes **all six** other cases in the block and fails **only** the new one. That is the shape a "look it up once" refactor naturally takes, so it is worth a guard.

For contrast, and recorded so the next reader does not redo it: the cruder mutation — resolving authority from the caller rather than each row's owner, `contentAuthorityOver(userId, userId)` — is already caught by two existing cases. It was not evidence of a gap, and I checked before claiming one.

**No production code changed.** 65/65 in the suite, backend typecheck clean apart from the pre-existing `robots-parser` error on main.

This does not replace the real-domain UI evidence Harsha is holding ENG-1533 for — that still needs the ENG-739 fixture. It closes the deterministic half so the fixture only has to prove the rendering.

title: call_meta_marketing_api transient failure surfaced raw to customer mid-deploy ("call to Meta Marketing API failed") instead of auto-retrying quietly
body:
**Root cause (verified against prod DynamoDB `AW-ChatMessages` and CloudWatch `web.stdout.log` for the exact incident window — corrected from this ticket's original description; full correction posted as a Linear comment on ENG-1625):**

No CAMPAIGN or AD_SET CREATE ever failed during the 2026-08-27 Phoenix Technologies deploy. The one real error in the incident window (17:19:56Z) was a `CAMPAIGN LIST` post-deploy read-back requesting `effective_status` and `special_ad_categories` — both real Meta Campaign GET fields, but missing from this file's `CAMPAIGN_READ_FIELDS` allow-list, so they were rejected LOUDLY by local argument validation (the deliberate ENG-398 "reject loudly, never silently drop" behavior) before the call ever reached Meta. The model self-corrected 6 seconds later with a valid field list and succeeded.

**What changed:** widened `CAMPAIGN_READ_FIELDS` to include `effective_status` and `special_ad_categories`, so this exact read-back no longer fails at all — fixing the trigger at the source rather than only how a fired-and-recovered error renders (that UI-layer defense is the companion fix in `agentweb-customer-portal` PR #1125).

**Behavior-change note (not a defect, but undocumented until now):** `listCampaigns` uses this same allow-list as its DEFAULT field set when no `fields` param is given (`resolveReadFields(...) ?? [...CAMPAIGN_READ_FIELDS]`), so every plain `CAMPAIGN LIST` call — not just ones that explicitly ask for these two fields — now also returns `effective_status` and `special_ad_categories` by default. Payload growth is small (a short status string and typically `["NONE"]`), well within the existing tool-result size handling, but it is a real shape change to the default response, worth knowing about for anything downstream that iterates campaign field keys.

**Tests:** 4 new cases in `metaService.configFields.test.ts` following the existing ENG-398/ENG-785 pattern — explicit selection, new default-set membership, single-campaign read, and an ENG-398 regression pin (still rejects a genuinely unsupported field loudly). title: [needs human] Fix update-conversation-history deadlock for never-messaged 1st-degree connections (ENG-1623)
body:
**Bug:** send-message enforces a gate requiring update-conversation-history to have synced within 24h. But update-conversation-history itself threw a generic 'LinkedIn outreach action failed' for 1st-degree connections who have never been sent a LinkedIn message — a permanent deadlock blocking all first-touch DMs to accepted connections (ENG-1623).

**Root cause:** Unipile only creates a `chat_attendee` record once a chat/thread exists. `getMessagesWithContact` (linkedInOutreachService.ts) called `client.messaging.getAllChatsFromAttendee` expecting either a populated or empty `items` array, but for an attendee with zero message history Unipile's API 404s instead. That raw, unclassified `UnsuccessfulRequestError` (whose `.message` is always empty) propagated straight up through the `update-conversation-history` tool-dispatch case in agentModeService.ts to the generic catch-all error message.

**Fix:** Wrap the `getAllChatsFromAttendee` call in a try/catch that runs the error through the same `handleError` classification already used elsewhere in this file. If it classifies as `NOT_FOUND` (404), treat it as 'no conversation exists yet' and return an empty message list (matching the existing behavior for `items: []`), which lets update-conversation-history succeed, stamp the sync timestamp, and unblock send-message. Any other error (auth, session, 5xx, etc.) still propagates with its full structured message instead of the old blank one.

**Verification:** Reproduced the failure with a new unit test mocking a 404 `UnsuccessfulRequestError` from `getAllChatsFromAttendee` — it failed before the fix (uncaught `UnsuccessfulRequestError` with empty message) and passes after. Also added a test confirming non-404 errors (e.g. 401) still throw a structured, informative error rather than being swallowed. All 154 tests in the file pass, and `npx tsc` compiles clean.

---

title: Fix create_html_file/save_file JSON parse failures on quote-rich and truncated tool calls (ENG-1477)
body:
**Bug:** `create_html_file`/`save_file` calls were failing with `Failed to parse arguments: Expected ',' or '}' after property value in JSON at position N`, and the customer-reported session showed this happening repeatedly on a scheduled report (7 failed attempts in one run).

**Root cause (confirmed against the real reported prod session, `02ab5f5e...`, via direct DynamoDB reads):** the actual failures were NOT an unescaped-quote formatting mistake — every one of the 7 failing calls was a syntactically clean JSON *prefix* that stopped dead mid-property, missing the required `content_draft` field entirely, with `completion_tokens` far under the output cap (so not the `finish_reason: 'length'` case the existing ENG-403 guard already handles). Something interrupted the model stream without reporting `length`, and the incomplete JSON reached `JSON.parse` raw.

**What shipped, across this PR's history:**
1. `repairUnescapedQuotes` / `parseToolCallArguments` (`repairToolCallArguments.ts`) — a defensive repair pass for the secondary, more classic failure mode: an unescaped inner quote in a title/content string (a quoted phrase, or HTML markup like `class="..."`). Walks the raw text like a JSON tokenizer and escapes a quote in place only when it isn't a legitimate string terminator, with container-aware handling so embedded CSS `font-family:"Arial",sans-serif` lists and JS/JSON array/object literals inside prose don't get misparsed.
2. **Real root-cause fix:** `isTruncatedJsonPrefix` + `TruncatedToolCallArgumentsError` — detects a genuinely truncated stream (distinct from a formatting mistake) and tells the model to retry the exact same call instead of "fix your arguments" (ENG-124's default), which was actively wrong guidance when there's nothing to fix. Wired through `toolErrorClassifier.ts` / `errorRetryability.ts` as a new `truncated_response` class.
3. **Security fix:** `hasDuplicateObjectKeys` — the quote-repair heuristic could be tricked by untrusted echoed content (e.g. scraped text in `content_draft`) shaped like `..., "title":"HACKED"` into treating it as real JSON structure, letting `JSON.parse` silently keep the last occurrence of a duplicate key and overwrite a legitimate argument. Reproduced directly; now any repair that would produce a duplicate key at any nesting depth is rejected, falling back to the honest original parse error instead.
4. **Defense-in-depth:** `create_html_file`/`save_file` schemas now set `additionalProperties: false`, so even a non-duplicate injected key is rejected by the existing gateway validator rather than relying on the handler simply not reading it.

**Verification:**
- Live preview, both ticket scenarios (quoted-phrase title, HTML attribute quotes in `save_file`) — succeed on the first call, fetched artifact byte-identical/quote-intact
- Live preview, the review-flagged edge cases (CSS `font-family` list, embedded array literal) — succeed on the first call
- Targeted suite: 332+ passing (repairToolCallArguments, toolDispatch, toolErrorClassifier, errorRetryability, agentToolGatewayService, plus the new schema-hardening test importing the real tool registry)
- `npm run typecheck` — clean

Fixes ENG-1477 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1477/create-html-file-and-save-file-reject-large-argument-payloads-with-a


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Improved tool-call JSON parsing for `create_html_file` and `save_file`. The backend repairs unescaped quotes, detects truncated argument prefixes, rejects duplicate keys after repair, and classifies truncation as retryable. It also hardens both tool schemas with `additionalProperties: false`.

title: docs: add the Google Ads launch gate and conversion tag contract
body:
Adds `docs/integrations/google-ads-launch-gate-contract.md`, a companion to `meta-ads-contract.md` using the same template. Registered in the folder README and the integrations map.

## Why

The integration-memory folder had a Meta contract and no Google Ads one, while the Google Ads write surface accumulated a set of rules that are actively counter-intuitive. The next person or agent to touch them will "fix" them into bugs without this.

## The section that matters most

**Two Detectors, Opposite Scopes.** Two functions look for the same `AW-` ids. They read different inputs, so their correct scopes run in opposite directions:

| | Reads | Correct scope | False positive costs | Miss costs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RULE 7.5 detector | served HTML | **narrow** | a launch passes on a page that fires nothing | a recoverable block |
| injector guard | layout source | **wide** | a visible 422 | two AW ids on one page |

The obvious fix to the gate, narrowing it to `<script>` elements, would have **false-blocked our own marketing site**, whose GA4 id lives in a `<link rel="preload">` and the hydration payload rather than a `<script src>`.

## Other rules recorded with the reason attached

- **Case sensitivity is load-bearing.** A nav link to `/ai-gtm-agent` read as container `GTM-AGENT` and passed an untracked page.
- **Element detection is a JSX parse, not a regex.** A commented-out tag block read as installed, and comments cannot be regex-stripped here because the loader URL contains `//`.
- **Approval tokens must survive `extractMinimalToolResult`.** Both approval loops were dead ends in production. Handler tests passed because they never reach the minimizer, so they proved the tokens were issued and not that they were delivered.
- **`createCampaign` and `updateCampaign` duplicate their strategy branches.** A fix applied to one and not the other already shipped once.
- **Offline import is closed by Google**, gated on the developer token, with our code shipping two months after the window closed.

## Also included

title: Adopt Unipile account_status webhook for real-time disconnect detection (ENG-1197)
body:
## Summary

ENG-1197's investigation (this session) confirmed why LinkedIn/Unipile sessions repeatedly die for high-volume automated-outreach accounts (Jennifer Sun, Sue Xu/ENG-1654): LinkedIn's own automation detection revokes the session, surfacing on Unipile's side as their `CREDENTIALS` status — confirmed directly against Unipile's docs, not just inferred from correlation. That's not fixable in our code.

What IS fixable: today we only detect this via polling (`linkedInConnectionSyncCron.ts`, ~10 min while healthy, backing off to 30 min once flagged dead). Unipile offers a push webhook (`source: "account_status"`) that fires near-instantly on exactly these transitions. This PR adopts it as a faster detection path.

**Not a replacement for the polling cron** — that stays on unchanged as a safety net for a missed/mis-registered delivery. **Not a fix to the root cause** — a `CREDENTIALS` disconnect still requires the end user to manually re-authenticate; this only makes us find out sooner.

## What shipped

- `backend/src/routes/unipileWebhook.ts` (new) — receives `POST /api/webhooks/unipile/account-status`. Maps Unipile's `AccountStatus.message` to our own health signal, mirroring `isProvenDisconnectError`'s conservative philosophy: only `CREDENTIALS` may claim disconnected; `ERROR`/`STOPPED` (Unipile's own "investigate" status) routes to a separate internal-only deduped oncall alert, never the customer-facing pipeline.
- Deliberately reuses the existing, already-idempotent `recordUnipileAccountHealth` pipeline (`linkedInConnectionHealth.ts`) instead of building a second notify path — avoiding a repeat of the ENG-1351-vs-ENG-1197 mistake (two independently-built "notify on disconnect" implementations with conflicting flag defaults, discovered this session, left untouched/out of scope here).
- Auth: plain shared-header comparison (Unipile doesn't sign payloads — confirmed against their docs), SHA-256 + `timingSafeEqual`, same technique as `fathomWebhook.ts`. **Fails closed** (deliberate deviation from Fathom's fail-open): a forged `CREDENTIALS` delivery could false-alarm a paying customer, a forged `OK` could silently clear a genuinely-dead account's disconnect flag — both worse than rejecting traffic while misconfigured.
- `account_id → ownerUserId` resolution reuses the existing `getAllUnipileAccountIds()` full-scan (now exported, one-line change) rather than building a new reverse-index — matching the precedent already running in production for Calendly's webhook receiver (`getAccountsByCalendlyUserUri` does the identical scan on every delivery). At today's scale (16 total Unipile accounts) a reverse index would be premature optimization.
- `backend/src/scripts/register-unipile-account-status-webhook.ts` (new) — one-time per-environment provisioning script, reuses `linkedInOutreachService.getClient()`'s existing Secrets-Manager-backed credential path. Safe to re-run (skips creation if a webhook already targets the same `request_url`).
- New env var `UNIPILE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (`.env.example` updated).
- No `asyncJobQueue` — `recordUnipileAccountHealth`'s own compare-and-swap write already makes redelivery safe, and Unipile's own 5x/30s retry already provides the crash-durability a queue would exist for. Processing is fully synchronous.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] New suite (`unipileWebhook.test.ts`, 22 tests): exhaustive message-mapping coverage, auth boundary (missing/wrong header, fail-closed when secret unset), route wiring (owner resolution, ignore-messages never reaching the health pipeline, non-LinkedIn accounts ignored, thrown errors surface as non-200 so Unipile retries)
- [x] Existing `linkedInConnectionSyncCron` (8/8) and `linkedInConnectionHealth` (58/58) suites still pass unchanged after the export change
- [ ] Manual: run the registration script against a test environment and confirm a real disconnect/reconnect cycle reaches the webhook faster than the polling cron would have caught it (can't unit-test a third-party push delivery)

Fixes ENG-1197 (fast-follow item; the alert + auto-pause asks were already shipped, root-cause investigation is documented on the ticket).

title: fix(meta): paginate and correctly scope listCampaigns/listAdSets/listAdsForUtmAudit/listCustomAudiences/listPixels (ENG-1625)
body:
**What was wrong:** PR #2656 (ENG-1476/ENG-1584) fixed `listAds`/`listAdCreatives` in `backend/src/services/metaService.ts` — pagination, deadlines, and truthful `truncated`/`scope` reporting so a bare `Found 25 ad(s)` could never again read as "these are all the ads" (that exact sentence told an Every.io customer a protected ad did not exist). That fix was scoped to two edges; the identical defect was still live on five others.

**What changed** (mirrors the reference implementation in #2656 exactly — that PR is untouched here):

1. **`listAdSets` (highest priority — two defects at once)**:
   - Campaign scoping went through a bare `campaign_id` param on `/act_X/adsets`. Meta's own docs for the account-level adsets edge list only `date_preset`/`effective_status`/`is_completed`/`time_range` as supported params — `campaign_id` is not among them, the same shape ENG-1476 found and fixed for the ads edge. Scoping now goes through the campaign **node** edge (`Campaign(id).getAdSets(...)`) instead, which makes the scope structurally impossible to ignore.
     - ⚠️ **Not confirmed live** against a real Meta ad account — no path to a valid Meta access token was available from this workspace (DynamoDB `Query`/`Scan` denied on the connected-accounts table, Secrets Manager `GetSecretValue` denied). Corroborated only against Meta's public API documentation. If this needs live confirmation before being trusted further, that's a follow-up someone with credential access should run.
   - No pagination at all.
2. **`listCampaigns`, `listAdsForUtmAudit`, `listCustomAudiences`, `listPixels`**: no pagination (`listCustomAudiences` additionally hard-capped at `limit: 50`). `listPixels` also bypassed the SDK entirely via a bespoke `fetchWithRetry` call that never followed `paging.next` — switched to the SDK's `AdAccount.getAdsPixels`, a proper Cursor, so it now shares the exact same `withReadDeadline`/`drainCursor` path as everything else in the file.

All five now return `{ items/campaigns/adSets/audiences/pixels, truncated, pagesFetched, scope? }` instead of a bare array. Every caller updated — tool-facing ones (`listMetaAdsCampaignsNew`, `listMetaAdsAdSets`, the DATASET/PIXEL LIST action, CUSTOM_AUDIENCE LIST) rebuilt through `buildListResult`/`buildListMessage` so the `Found N X(s)` sentence always states scope and completeness in prose, not just a field the model can skip; internal callers (routes, `metaLaunchGate`'s tracking pre-flight, `metaCapiKeyCoverage`, `metaAccountCredentials`) just destructure the new shape.

`META_LIST_PAGE_SIZE` (100) / `META_LIST_MAX_PAGES` (25) / `META_LIST_MAX_MS` (45s) / `META_READ_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s) are unchanged — tuned in #2656 against live Phoenix data (1300+ creatives across 13 pages) and shared verbatim by all five methods here.

**Tests:** new `eng1625.metaListPagination.test.ts` modeled on `eng1476.metaAdListScoping.test.ts` — pins the concrete regression this ticket asked for (an ad set that exists in the account but not in the requested campaign is absent from a campaign-scoped result), pagination walk + truncation for all 5 methods, and the cross-account tenancy refusal on the new campaign-node path. `eng1476.metaListScope.test.ts` extended for the 4 new `payloadKey`s and noun phrasing. Every pre-existing test asserting the old bare-array shape or old single-arg Graph call updated to the new contract (these are not implementation bugs being papered over — they were asserting the ENG-1476/ENG-1584 defect shape as correct, which this fix deliberately changes).

**Verification:** `npm run typecheck` clean; full Meta-related suite green — 20 files / 557 tests (`metaService.test.ts`, `metaService.spendCap.test.ts`, `metaService.configFields.test.ts`, `metaLaunchGate.test.ts`, `metaV2Routes.test.ts`, `adUtmAuditAdapters.test.ts`, `agentModeService.meta*.test.ts`, plus the ENG-1476 reference suites and the new ENG-1625 pagination suite).

Fixes the remaining scope of ENG-1625 (filed from a review conducted on that ticket's original PR #2682, already merged) — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1625/call-meta-marketing-api-transient-failure-surfaced-raw-to-customer-mid

title: fix(test-env): terminate instance + SG on failed SSH launch (ENG-1425)
body:
## What
Fixes ENG-1425: test-env launch left a billable EC2 instance and a permanently-open security group running whenever the SSH readiness check failed, because the failure path just exited without cleanup.

## How
- Adds `cleanup_failed_launch` (ERR trap): terminates the instance, deletes the launch security group, and removes launch state on any failure after resources are created.
- Adds `diagnose_ssh_failure`: on SSH timeout, dumps instance state/status and the security group's ingress rules to stderr before cleanup runs, so a real failure is still debuggable.
- SSH-timeout branch now triggers the ERR trap instead of a bare `exit 1`.

## Complexity ledger
+42/-1 lines in one file, additive-only (a failure-path safety net); no new abstractions, no config surface.

## How to test
1. `bash test-env/test-test-env-launch.sh` — asserts the safeguards are present in the script (shell-only regression check; the AWS/SSH boundary itself is intentionally exercised in cloud-dev, not unit tests).
2. `bash -n test-env/test-env.sh` — syntax check, passes.
3. `shellcheck test-env/test-env.sh` — no new findings introduced by this diff.

## What was NOT tested
- Did not launch a real EC2 instance / force an actual SSH timeout against AWS — this repo's dev-loop instruction is to keep heavy/cloud verification off Harsha's laptop and this is a one-tick headless run with no live AWS launch budget approved. The regression script instead pins the specific code shapes (trap installed, cleanup function defined, diagnostics message present) that the original bug lacked.

## Rollback
Revert the single commit; restores the prior (leaky) failure path with no data/schema impact.

title: Meta/Drive read hardening: scope, completeness, and honest failure reporting
body:
Follow-ups from reviewing #2656, #2676 and #2689, plus one bug found while testing. One theme runs through all of them: **a read must not lie about its own scope, its own completeness, or what it put in the logs — and a refusal must name a remedy that can actually work.**

Each change is small and independent. None alters a happy path.

---

## 1. Single-entity Meta reads were not bounded by the selected ad account

`new Campaign(id)` / `new AdSet(id)` address a **global** node id. Unlike the `/act_X/` edge, nothing about that construction ties the read to an ad account — and one Meta OAuth token routinely spans several. So `listCampaigns({ campaignId })` and `listAdSets({ adSetId })` could return an object from an account the caller never selected: the selected-account scope was advisory, not enforced.

#2656 added `assertNodeInAccount` to the campaign-**scoped** list paths for exactly this reason; the single-entity fetches never got it.

`account_id` is a readable field on both nodes, so it is requested **alongside** the caller's fields and ownership is answered by the same response as the payload. One round trip, no separate probe that could fail on its own and refuse a read that would otherwise have succeeded. The field is stripped from the result unless the caller asked for it, so the payload shape is unchanged. Both ids also now pass through `resolveScopeId`, so a supplied-but-empty id is refused rather than silently widening the read.

The refusal names the remedy — *select the owning account* — which discloses nothing (that is the only way forward) while keeping the non-oracle rule: it never names the account that actually owns the node.

## 2. The launch pre-flight treated a truncated ad read as a clean one

`metaLaunchGate` destructured `{ items: ads }` and discarded `truncated`. Campaign/ad-set-level activation puts every ad in scope live at once and is judged on the whole campaign's destinations, so a bounded read was **fail-open** in two ways: an empty `destinationUrls` returned `proceed: true` when it may just be the pages never fetched, and a non-empty one cleared a launch whose unread ads were never checked.

Both now block, naming the real cause; an explicit override still passes and records as `overridden`. Ad-level activation is deliberately unaffected — it is judged on that ad's own destination.

The not-found branch also stops asserting the ad *"may belong to a different campaign"* when the search was truncated. Not found in a partial search is not absent, and naming the wrong remedy is the ENG-1636 failure. (Refined further in **#10** below — the first version of this collapsed two different reads into one flag.)

**Verified live** that this cannot fire spuriously: `filtering` on `campaign.id` **is** honoured server-side (79 ads / 1 campaign, vs 463 / 15 account-wide), so tripping the bound needs >2,500 ads in a *single* campaign.

## 3. Drive query literals escaped quotes but not backslashes

Drive's grammar requires both. A file named `report\` produced `name = 'report\'`, whose trailing `\'` reads as an escaped quote and leaves the literal unterminated — an opaque Drive 400 rather than a match. The same gap lets a crafted value manipulate quote parity and reach past the parent-folder clause the query is scoped by, so this is a scoping fix as well as a correctness one.

Four inline `.replace(/'/g, …)` sites now share one `escapeDriveQueryValue`; backslash is replaced first, since escaping the quote first would double-escape the backslashes that step introduces.

## 4. Drive requests had no per-request deadline

`DRIVE_LIST_WALK_MAX_MS` is checked **between** requests, so it bounds how many calls the walk makes but cannot interrupt one already issued that never answers — Node's `fetch` applies no default deadline.

The timeout is the **remaining walk budget**, not a fixed value. A fixed ceiling is arbitrary in both directions: too low fails a legitimately slow call the walk still had time for, too high is meaningless because the walk stops at its own deadline anyway. Derived, it can never fail a call the walk would not have abandoned regardless. A 1s floor prevents `timeout: 0`, which gaxios reads as *no* timeout.

## 5. Paged Graph URLs were logged, and the paging recursion was unbounded

`fetchWithRetryAndPaging` logged `paging.next.substring(0, 100)`. A Graph paging URL carries `access_token` in its query string — often first — so that wrote credential material to application logs on every paged read. `drainCursor` already refuses to log Meta error objects for this reason.

It also followed `paging.next` recursively with no ceiling: unbounded work on the stack, and a stop with no signal is indistinguishable from a complete result. Now bounded with a `pagingTruncated` flag that propagates through the page merge.

## 6. The UTM audit reported a clean bill of health from a bounded read

`adUtmAuditAdapters` discarded `truncated`, so the tool could say **"✅ All N campaign(s) carry UTM tracking"** — a claim about everything — from a read that saw part of it. The ENG-1584 sentence shape again.

The port return type is **widened** to `PortRead<T> = T[] | { items; truncated? }` rather than switched to an object. Google and LinkedIn expose no completeness signal, so those adapters keep returning plain arrays and are **left completely untouched** — the only way to be certain this cannot regress them. `truncated: undefined` means *"this platform does not report completeness"*, never *"complete"*.

`auditCampaigns` takes an optional completeness out-param rather than a wider return type: `CampaignAuditReport[]` is destructured at ~30 call sites, and unwrapping an envelope at all of them mostly risks silently weakening assertions.

## 7. A skill-gated tool could be substituted, and the result presented as a PASS

Found while testing, in a live delegated session on a real customer account (`a1a6345a`, Phoenix): the gate refused `audit_ad_utm_coverage`, `install_skills` was refused by subscription, and the model then ran an unrelated `AD LIST` and presented a confident **"UTM Tagging Audit Summary — PASS, 6/6 ads tagged (100%)"** table built from it.

Three inputs the model reasons from were wrong, and all three are fixed here:

- The gate error said *"install the required skill first"* and said **nothing** about the install itself failing, so the model improvised. It now says what to do when the install fails, and explicitly forbids running a different tool and presenting its output as this tool's result. The error **prefix is unchanged** (`classifyToolErrorClass` keys `tool_unavailable` off it), pinned by a test.
- `installSkills` returned a bare `{ message }` on a subscription refusal while the success path returns `success: true` — so `success` was `undefined` and the refusal did not necessarily read as a failure. Now `success: false` on every refusal path.
- A **partial** install returns `success: true` because *something* installed, so the ledger asserted a clean install on exactly the shape where the one skill the gated tool needed was the one refused. `rejectedSkillIds` is now a field on the result and survives `extractMinimalToolResult`, so the outcome is legible rather than buried in prose inside `message`.

## 8. The unavailable-capability notice has moved to its own branch — **draft #2705**

This PR previously also carried `buildUnavailableCapabilityNotice`: an unconditional banner prepended above the answer stating that a gated tool never ran. **It has been removed from this PR and moved, unchanged, to `manan/unavailable-capability-notice` (#2705, draft), together with a full write-up of why it does not work.**

It was wrong in three separate ways across three review rounds, each time defeated by a different part of a pipeline it does not control, and each round was paid for by the read hardening above — which is the actual subject of this PR. Rather than attempt it a fourth time under review pressure, it is parked with the diagnosis so the next attempt starts from what is known instead of from the code. In short, and in full on #2705:

- `executePreparedTools` pushes **all preflight failures before any executed result** (`toolDispatch.ts` prepare loop vs Phase 3), so a skill-gate refusal is *always* at a lower ledger index than an `install_skills` entry. The notice's `if (installSucceededAfter > i) return;` therefore suppresses it on the real incident shape, and no index-based ordering between the two can mean anything.
- The earlier "inert in production" diagnosis was **wrong**: `toolResultError` downgrades `success: false` to an `Error` *before* `extractMinimalToolResult` runs, so a hard refusal does reach the ledger with an `error`. Fixes built on that diagnosis aimed at a hole that is not there.
- The arm/disarm narrowing is **turn-global rather than per-tool**, so an unrelated failed install can arm the notice for a tool nobody tried to install.
- The rule that defeated all three attempts: **hand-built ledger fixtures pass while the feature is dead.** Any future test must build the entry through `executePreparedTools`. This is not a new lesson — `extractMinimalToolResult`'s own ENG-1207 comment records `reconcileUnconsumedCursors` failing in exactly this way.

**Kept here deliberately** — none of it is the notice, and none of it is inert: the skill-gate error text, `installSkills` returning `success: false`, and `rejectedSkillIds` surviving minimization (all in #7 above). They act *before* a fabrication rather than annotating one after it, and each is justified on its own without the banner. `buildFalseClaimCorrectionFooter` is unchanged and still does its ENG-1188 job.

## 9. A capped Drive read told the model to retry a read that can never succeed

The `capped` branch of the Drive name search (`readGoogleDriveSharedFile`, `materializeKnowledgeBaseAsset`) ended **"Retry the read."**

Reaching `capped` with no `failed` has exactly one cause here: `queryDriveFilesAcrossFolders` crossing `DRIVE_LIST_WALK_MAX_MS`. (Its other capping path, `batchCount >= perBatchTarget`, cannot fire on a zero-result search.) That is a **wall-clock** bound spent walking a folder tree whose size does not change between attempts — and it is the *second* such budget, after `getGoogleDriveFolderTreeIds` already spent one enumerating sub-folders. A tree large enough to exhaust it exhausts it again, in the same place, on every retry.

So the instruction was a loop, and not a cheap one: each pass burns up to two more 15s budgets out of the turn. The capped branch now says not to retry and names the only variable that can move the outcome — a **smaller search scope** (the file's direct Drive link, or a sub-folder registered as its own source) — and, failing that, to tell the user the folder is too large to search rather than dressing a deterministic limit up as a glitch.

The neighbouring `failed` branch **keeps** "Retry the read": a request error *is* transient. Both branches now share one helper so that distinction cannot drift between the two call sites — which is exactly how one of a duplicated pair gets fixed and the other does not.

## 10. The launch gate collapsed two different reads into one truncation flag

`const searchWasIncomplete = adsTruncated || accountWideTruncated;`

The account-wide fallback only runs when the **campaign-scoped** read has already come back without the ad. So when that campaign read was *complete* (`truncated: false`) and only the fallback truncated, the block reported *"The ad list for campaign X was too large to read completely"* — about a read that had finished — told the user to narrow to an ad set that does not contain the ad, and **suppressed** the one accurate sentence, that the ad may belong to a different campaign.

The flags stay apart now, so each message names the read that actually stopped short. Refines #2 above; the campaign-truncated wording is unchanged.

## 11. A tenancy refusal softened the confirmation prompt instead of blocking the write

`buildMetaWriteConfirmation` resolves ids to names through best-effort resolvers:

```ts
// Best-effort resolvers — each guarded so a Meta lookup failure never blocks the gate.
try { return await metaService.getAd(accessToken, id, account_id); } catch { return undefined; }
```

That `catch` was written for a transient Graph blip, and for that it is right. But the ownership check from **#1** throws through the *same* catch, and it means the opposite of a blip: not "we could not look" but "we looked, and this node is not in the selected ad account".

Swallowed as a hiccup, the refusal's only effect was a vaguer prompt — the summary degraded to `ID <id>` and the gate went on to ask the user to approve a write to a node the guard had already refused. An approval there is precisely what unlocks the confirmed replay that performs it. **A guard whose sole consequence is a less informative prompt is not a guard.**

The two are now told apart by `isMetaAccountScopeRefusal`, keyed off the one sentence every ownership refusal carries. That sentence is a **shared constant**, not a literal retyped at the read site: if the wording drifts, the reader fails silently and in the permissive direction. It deliberately does *not* match `assertNodeInAccount`'s "could not verify … please retry", which is a genuine transient and must keep degrading.

On a refusal the gate returns `success: false` / `ACCOUNT_SCOPE_REFUSED` and never builds the prompt. The refusal discloses **nothing** about the node — no name, no owning account, no id — only the selected account the caller already supplied. `assertOwnedByAccount` withholds those because a block that answers *"which account owns this?"* is the oracle it exists to prevent, and relaying them through the confirmation gate would hand back the same answer by a longer route.

**Scope, stated rather than implied.** This closes the reachable path **at the confirmation gate**. The underlying hole is wider and pre-existing, and belongs in its own PR: `updateAd` / `deleteAd` / `updateAdSet` / `deleteAdSet` / `updateCampaign` / `deleteCampaign` in `metaService.ts` take no ad-account id at all, and four `getAd` callers (`copyMetaAdsAd`, `handleCreativeContentUpdate`, `verifyCreativeSwap`, `retagMetaAdUtm`) do not pass one.

---

## Two regressions this branch introduced, caught in self-review and removed

- **`META_PAGING_MAX_PAGES` was set too tight, by me.** 25 pages mirrors `metaService` — but that value pairs with an explicit `limit=100`, so it means 2,500 rows. The six `routes/meta.ts` callers set **no** `limit`, so Meta serves 25/page and the bound was **625 rows against previously-unbounded behaviour**: dashboards would silently shrink for any account past that. Exactly the defect the bound was added to prevent, reintroduced by the guard itself. Raised to 500 and documented as a runaway guard, not a page-size policy.
- **The tenancy guard originally cost an extra Graph call per read** and added a failure mode of its own. Folded into the payload read instead (see #1).

Also found while re-auditing: **six full access tokens in application logs.** `routes/meta.ts` logged whole Graph URLs built with `&access_token=${accessToken}` — an entire token per line, where the paging log fixed in #5 leaked only a 100-character prefix. All six redacted; a repo-wide sweep for the pattern now returns nothing.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean. **The full backend suite passes: 3,782 tests across 167 suites**, run in one process on the pushed head.

Every new test group was run against the pre-fix code and **fails** there, so they pin behaviour rather than describe it. For the three fixes added in this round, specifically:

- **#9** — reproduced through the real helper, not by calling the message builder: fake timers advance the clock inside the *name query only*, so the folder walk finishes inside its own budget and the read reaches `capped: true, failed: undefined`, which is the only shape that reaches the branch. Pre-fix, both call sites returned *"…This is an INCOMPLETE read… Retry the read."*
- **#10** — campaign read mocked complete, fallback truncated. Pre-fix it produced *"The ad list for campaign 120200000000000 was too large to read completely"*, about a read that had finished.
- **#11** — pre-fix, the summary read *"UPDATE ad ID ad\_from\_another\_account"*: the confirmation prompt asking a user to approve a write to a node in someone else's ad account. Five of the six new assertions fail there; the sixth is the deliberate opposite-error guard.

The cases that pass either way are deliberate opposite-error guards: a complete read with nothing to measure must still pass; an ordinary healthy audit must still say "All N"; a plain apostrophe was already escaped; a plain-array port must not gain a fabricated warning; a *transient* Meta failure must still degrade to a prompt rather than block; the `failed` Drive branch must still say "Retry the read".

Live, read-only, against Phoenix `448692064923397`:
- `filtering` on `campaign.id` is honoured server-side — bounds the blast radius of #2.
- `account_id` confirmed readable on both `Campaign` and `AdSet` in the SDK field enums — the premise of #1.

### Existing assertions changed, and why
None blesses new behaviour; each pinned an invariant that is unchanged:
- Fixtures that answered `account_id` only for a bare `['account_id']` probe, which no longer happens.
- Four assertions that pinned call **arity** or an exact string/array rather than the thing they protect — that an unavailable tool is *counted as failed*, that the caller's field selection is *honoured*, that the shared-drive flags are *passed*, that the audit routes to the right platform/port.
- One direct port call now normalises through `readPortResult`.
- Two `install_skills` assertions dropped their call into the removed notice; the minimization behaviour they actually protect (`success: false` and `rejectedSkillIds` surviving `extractMinimalToolResult`) is asserted directly instead, and still fails when that branch is disabled.

## Not in scope
- **Caching the Drive folder-tree walk.** A naive cache reintroduces the bug #2676 just fixed — a stale tree makes a newly added sub-folder resolve as not-found. It needs invalidation design, so it is deliberately left out.
- **Ad-account scoping on the Meta write methods themselves**, and the four `getAd` callers that pass no account id — see the scope note under #11.
- **The unavailable-capability notice** — draft #2705.

## Deploy note
The new refusals are all fail-closed — tenancy mismatch (now blocking the write, not just the prompt), truncated launch gate, empty scope id. Each names its cause and its remedy, and the launch gate keeps its override. That is the right direction, but it is a behaviour change: some users will see a block they did not see before.
