title: fix(eng-1215/eng-1212): dangling org owner 500, /usage dollar leak, non-prod email guard
body:
Three defects found by the read-only verification passes on ENG-1215. Each was investigated to root cause before any code was written; none was assumed.

Commits are split per defect, fix and tests separately.

---

## 1. A dangling org owner 500s the account — and blocks chat

`resolveBillingUserId` guarded a missing ORG (`if (!org) return userId`) but not an unresolvable OWNER. Two shapes exist in real data:

| Shape | Example |
|---|---|
| `ownerUserId` names a user that no longer exists | org `member-test-tc20260525` → `placeholder-owner-tc20260525`, which has no `AW-Users` row |
| `ownerUserId` absent from the org row entirely | org `dabd0425-…`, `memberCount: 2` |

Both returned an id nothing resolves, and `getUserTokenUsage` (`tokenUsageService.ts:148`) then threw `User not found`, surfacing as the 500 on `/usage-runway`.

**The blast radius is wider than the endpoint it was found on.** This function also resolves the billing subject for `checkTokenUsage` — the gate on the chat path — and for `stripe.ts`. A member whose own record is perfectly healthy is locked out of the product by a defect in a row they cannot see or repair.

Falls back to the member’s own partition, exactly as the `!org` case does. With no billing root there is no org counter to pool onto, so the member is quota’d on their own — the restrictive direction, never uncapped.

**Production is currently unaffected**: all 17 prod orgs resolve to a real owner. This is latent, not a live outage.

## 2. `/usage` shipped internal dollars to customers (ENG-1212 AC4)

AC4: *"No internal USD amounts are returned by customer APIs."* The ticket outcome says it plainer — forecast *"without exposing dollar ceilings"*.

`/usage-runway` honoured this from day one via `toCustomerRunway`. `/usage` returned `checkTokenUsage` verbatim, so `costUsed` and `costAllowance` went out in plain USD to every authenticated customer. Two chatbot 429 bodies shipped the same object.

This was **not** a deliberate product choice — the portal states the opposite intent in two places:

- `SubscriptionCard.tsx:32` — cost quota surfaced *"ONLY as a percentage bar (never the dollar figures)"*
- `SubscriptionCard.tsx:620` — *"Dollars stay admin-only; to the user this is simply usage"*

and `costUsed` has **no non-test reader anywhere in the portal**. `costAllowance` is only ever null-checked, never rendered, so `hasCostAllowance` carries the one bit the client used.

`costPercentUsed` is kept deliberately: a percentage is not a dollar amount, and it is what the bar renders. Verified unaffected: the scheduled-limit email renders only percentages, and the partner portal builds admin dollar figures from subscription-type policy, not from this endpoint.

Portal counterpart: **agentweb-customer-portal#1129**. `hasCostCeiling()` there tolerates both API shapes, so the two can deploy in either order.

## 3. Non-production could email real customers

Staging and every preview run `NODE_ENV=development` (verified on `Agentweb-backend-env-1`) against `Dev-` tables, and `Dev-AW-Users` is a clone of production holding real customer addresses. The only environment check in the entire email stack guarded `sendOncallAlert` — an internal alert to our own oncall — while every customer-facing send went straight to the provider. A preview booting the full cron stack could mail a real customer.

Guards `ResendService.sendEmail`, the single chokepoint all 28 callers and `sendSystemEmail` funnel through, so a sender added later is covered without anyone remembering to.

An **allowlist**, not a blanket block, because staging still has to prove mail leaves the box:

- `NONPROD_EMAIL_ALLOWLIST` — exact addresses or `@domain` suffixes; defaults to `@example.com`, which is what existing fixtures already use, so nothing breaks
- `NONPROD_EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL=true` — separate, deliberate opt-in for a delivery test

A send is suppressed whenever every primary recipient is blocked: delivering to an allowlisted cc alone would silently change who the message was addressed to.

**No-op in production**, asserted rather than assumed — a guard that suppresses real mail is a worse outage than the one it prevents.

---

## Verification

Every fix is mutation-verified, several in both directions:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Remove the dangling-owner guard | 3 of 4 fail |
| Collapse to `return userId` always | the pooling case fails instead |
| Redaction becomes a pass-through | 2 fail |
| Redaction also drops `costPercentUsed` | the meter case fails |
| Email guard active in production | the no-op case fails |
| Domain suffix match → `includes()` | the `example.com@evil.com` case fails |
| Guard disabled at the chokepoint | both suppression cases fail, delivery cases stay green |

Suites run: `tokenUsageService` (75), `orgBilling` ×4, `chatbot` + `usage-runway.e2e` (250), `subscription` routes, all email suites (61). `npm run typecheck` clean apart from the pre-existing `robots-parser` TS2307.

One existing-test change, called out explicitly: three `checkTokenUsage` mocks used positional `mockResolvedValueOnce` chains, so adding one `getUserById` call shifted every value by one. They are now id-keyed. **No assertion was changed** — and the mutation run confirms they still fail when pooling breaks, so they were not weakened to pass.

It redacts internal cost fields from customer responses and blocks non-allowlisted non-production email recipients. Production email behavior remains unchanged. Type checking still reports the pre-existing `robots-parser` TS2307 error.

title: ENG-929 follow-up: fix sync=true throughput under budget pressure, guard the manifest/cap composition
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2305 (merged, deployed). During a post-deploy risk review I identified 4 residual risks in that fix; 2 had real, well-scoped code fixes and are in this PR. The other 2 (transcript truncation occasionally changing a score for very large sessions, and downstream drift in what the Daily Satisfaction Score Report concludes) are inherent tradeoffs of the original fix, not defects — forcing a "fix" for those would risk reintroducing the original bug or over-engineering without evidence it's needed, so they're left as monitor-worthy, not code changes.

- **Throughput under budget pressure**: `backfillSessionScores`' scaled-up per-session timeout (up to 60s vs. the old flat 20s) means a few large sessions can now consume much more of the shared 4-minute wall-clock budget each. Left in array order, a window with a few large sessions up front could starve many small, fast sessions of any attempt at all. Now dispatches smallest-first (by `messageCount`) while keeping the documented "outcomes in same order as input" contract intact — only *which* session a worker picks up next changes.

- **Hand-merge regression guard**: #2305 required three rounds of hand-resolving merge conflicts against a fast-moving main, twice in the exact spot where this ticket's transcript cap composes with ENG-1223's tool-call manifest (`${manifest.text}\n\n${capped.text}`, in both `scoreSession` and `scoreSessionWithJudge` — two separate, non-shared functions). Added tests pinning that composition with a tool call placed outside both the 50-message scoring window and the truncated transcript's surviving head/tail, so a future merge silently dropping either piece fails a test instead of quietly reintroducing an already-shipped bug.

title: ENG-1669: stop a bad judge response from silently becoming NaN, raise scoring token ceiling
body:
## Summary

Fixes ENG-1669, discovered incidentally while live-verifying ENG-929/#2694 against real production data (2026-09-01). Two custom scoring judges were technically failing their LLM call on ~6% of scored sessions — not a rubric/judgment quality issue, a mechanical failure of the call/response itself.

**Bug 1 — NaN silently reaching persistence.** `Math.round(parsed.score)` had no guard against a missing or non-numeric `score` field in the judge's JSON response. This produced `NaN`, which then flowed through `applyFabricationGuard` untouched and only failed once `chatbotDb.updateSessionSatisfactionScore`/`updateSessionJudgeScore` tried to persist it — as an opaque DynamoDB SDK error (`"The parameter cannot be converted to a numeric value: NaN"`) far from the actual cause. Confirmed against 2 real production sessions. Fixed by validating at the source (reusing the existing `finiteNumber` helper) in both `scoreSession` and `scoreSessionWithJudge`, throwing a message that says what's actually wrong. This is caught by the same per-session try/catch #2305 added to isolate a scoring failure from the rest of the batch — no behavior change there.

**Bug 2 — genuinely truncated/malformed JSON.** Confirmed against 2 other real production sessions (`"Unterminated string in JSON..."`, `"Expected ',' or '}' after property value..."`) on judges with long (8k-10k char) system prompts. The existing comment on `SCORING_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS` already documents this exact "thinking model" truncation risk — 2000 was evidently still not generous enough for the judges configured in production today. Doubled to 4000; exported so a test can reference it instead of a hardcoded literal.

- [x] New `sessionScoring.judgeScoreValidation.test.ts` reproduces the exact ENG-1669 failure mode (missing/non-numeric score) for both `scoreSession` and `scoreSessionWithJudge`, asserting each throws instead of persisting NaN

title: fix(agent-mode): scheduled-run 429 misclassified as system error (ENG-1670)
body:
Auto-fix for ENG-1670: Scheduled runs lose 429 rate-limit context when wrapped, mis-classified as system error (LinkedIn Post Factory)

Looks identical to ENG-845/ENG-826 (same schedule, same zero-output symptom) but is a distinct, still-active bug — verified directly from prod `AW-ChatSessions`/`AW-ChatMessages`/`AW-TaskSchedules`, not inferred. ENG-826's Gemini union-schema fix is unrelated to this failure.

**Root cause:** the scheduled pipeline fires bursts of near-simultaneous parallel tool calls, which trips a Gemini rate limit (429) on gemini-3.7-flash. `generateMarketingResponse` correctly classifies this and preserves `.status`/`.code` on the error it throws — but that signal was silently dropped crossing the worker's IPC boundary back to the parent process, so `classifyZeroAssistantFailure` in `agentModeController` could never see it, and the transcript shown to the user read "unexpected system error" instead of the accurate "rate limit, retrying."

**Fixes:**
1. Preserve `.status`/`.code` across the `generateMarketingResponseWorker` ↔ `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService` IPC boundary, so the failure is classified correctly downstream.
2. Extend `callLLM`'s OpenRouter transient-error retry from 2 to 3 attempts with exponential backoff (1.5s, 3s) — a single 1.5s retry wasn't enough to clear the burst-triggered 429 in the sessions that hit it.

title: [needs human] Stop stale-model-id migration from rewriting updatedAt (ENG-1333)
body:
Root cause: backend/src/scripts/migrateStaleModelReferences.ts's applyCandidate() included `updatedAt = :now` in the UpdateExpression whenever it corrected a stale llmModel reference on a scanned table (AW-ChatSessions, AW-TaskSchedules, AW-ScheduleTemplates, AW-WorkPlans). This script was run with --apply against production on 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18 (commits 014453543 and fde4c3084), touching ~841 rows. Because updatedAt is also the sort key of AW-ChatSessions' AdminUpdatedAtIndex GSI (used by get_chat_history for time-range queries), this made months-old sessions appear as if they'd just been 'touched', so a 24-hour window query returned 763 rows instead of the true 36. Confirmed by reading the reporting session (cea8b5a5-24b5-45a6-9d84-27fab3337cd4) — a scheduled Daily Satisfaction Score Report — whose own analysis and judge scores independently diagnosed 'bulk updatedAt rewrite' as the contamination source, and by the migration script's own commit history explicitly stating the writes were applied to production.

Fix: applyCandidate()'s scanned-table write path now sets a new modelMigratedAt field to record when the migration touched the row, and no longer touches updatedAt at all. This is a forward-looking fix (prevents future corruption from any re-run or new stale-model discovery); it does not retroactively repair already-corrupted rows, which is a data-plane operation outside the scope of a code change.

Verified with a TDD test: wrote a new test asserting applyCandidate's UpdateExpression never references updatedAt, confirmed it failed against the old code (UpdateExpression was 'SET #field = :new, updatedAt = :now'), then fixed the source and confirmed it passes.

title: [needs human] Preserve 403 code on mapped X List scope error (ENG-1300)
body:
The X List read endpoints (getOwnedLists/getListMembers/getListTweets) already convert a 403 into an actionable 'reconnect your X account for list.read' error via mapListScopeError. That rewrite constructs a plain new Error() without copying over the original .code=403, so classifyToolErrorClass (which reads .code to classify HTTP errors) falls back to a generic 'Error' class, and classifyToolFailureType in turn falls back to 'bug' instead of 'config'. This is why a persistent, well-understood X List permission gap was invisible to quality/scorecard telemetry even though the agent-facing error message was already clear — the classification layer that other systems key off of never saw it as an auth/config issue. Fix: attach code=403 to the rewritten error so it classifies correctly downstream. Verified with a new unit test asserting classifyToolErrorClass/classifyToolFailureType return 'auth'/'config' for the mapped error, plus the full existing twitterService and agentModeService twitterOutreach test suites.

title: fix(ENG-1344): name the reset date on every block surface, from one producer
body:
Companion to customer-portal #1134. **Draft** — the block wording is material user-visible copy and ENG-1344's own *Copy gate* says it "does not ship without Harsha's review… before the PR is marked ready" (ENG-1442).

## Why

Three customer-visible surfaces said "reset" and never said **when**:

| Surface | Was |
|---|---|
| Interactive 429 × 3 (`agentModeController`) | *"AI usage is paused until your next reset or additional usage is added."* |
| Scheduled-chat run notice | *"…paused until the next reset or additional usage is added."* |
| Scheduled-chat email | *"Your usage allowance resets at the start of each billing period."* |

The first is a near-verbatim match for what the xCures escalation quoted back on 2026-08-18 — *"a block that I can't use Emma until I reset or add new usage. What does that mean?"* — so the portal-only draft could never have fixed the sentence he actually read.

## AC6: one producer

AC6 requires the portal copy and the ENG-1035 429 payload be *"generated from one source, so they cannot drift into two different explanations of the same block."* There is no shared package between the repos and no cross-repo import, so that can only mean one **runtime** source:

- `usageBlockCopy.ts` composes `{ resetDate, headline, body, resetSentence, message }`
- `toCustomerTokenUsage` ships it as `usageBlock`; the three 429s carry it beside the flat `message`
- `usagePausedMessage` **delegates** rather than re-composing, so the flat string cannot fork
- the portal renders it and derives nothing (portal commit `978ffd23`)

## Deliberate non-changes

**The shared-session 429 gets no date.** That route already withholds usage detail because anyone holding the share link can call it, and the reset date is the *owner's* billing cycle. The viewer is not the billing subject and cannot act on it.

**Every message falls back to the pre-existing undated wording** when the month is unparseable — vague, which is the defect, but true.

## `formatResetDateLong` does string surgery, not `toLocaleDateString`

A date-only ISO string parses as UTC midnight, so a host west of the line renders the previous day. Pinning `timeZone: "UTC"` fixes it but only reproduces on a negative-offset host — on this fleet (IST) a test asserting the pin **passes whether or not the pin is there**. I found that by mutation: removing the pin passed all 10 tests. There is no `Date` in that path now, and the mutation restoring one fails on IST too.

## Verification

- Full suite: **27,881 passed**, 20 skipped. The 2 failing suites / 3 tests are **pre-existing on clean `main`** — verified by stashing: `siteLinkCrawlerService` (missing `robots-parser` dep) and `bedrockSdkCacheTtlCapability` (ENG-893: installed Bedrock SDK is older than 3.972.0, so `cachePoint.ttl` never reaches the wire — worth its own look, given it is a caching/cost guard).
- `npm run typecheck` at its pre-existing baseline (same `robots-parser` error, nothing new).
- Mutations all failing correctly: the Date-based formatter, an off-by-one month name, a fabricated date in place of the fallback, the email keeping its vague sentence, and `usagePausedMessage` forking its own wording.

## Known limit

Nothing binds the two repos in CI. The portal's fixture spells out the strings this emits, but if these are reworded that fixture goes stale silently. That is a stale-fixture problem, not a production one — the portal renders whatever the server sends.

title: fix(agentmode): answer an in-chat request for a named model (ENG-1205 AC3)
body:
Closes the **named-model** half of ENG-1205 AC3, plus an adjacent silent correction found while verifying it.

## Why this is not already done

ENG-1565 (#2642) closed the *generic* half — "reassess using a new model" now gets an acknowledgement. Its detector requires `new|different|another|other` next to `model`, so it never fires on a message that **names** the model it wants. That is what ENG-1205's production session actually contained:

> "Use Opus 5 model, and make sure you sort all of the 107 leads..."

Verified against the merged detector — that message, `switch to Opus 5`, `can you use claude opus 5 for this` and `run this on opus please` are all misses today. The request and the nine turns after it were answered with nothing (session `d5898ffd`, 2026-08-14), and the user reported the product as broken. #2642's own PR comment says the same thing: *"the ticket's cited precedent (ENG-1205 AC3) was never actually implemented."*

## What this does

`backend/src/utils/modelMentionRequest.ts` — a pure, registry-driven detector wired at the same append-only finalize seam as its neighbours (`reconcileFalseFailureReport` ENG-971, `reconcileUnconsumedCursors` ENG-1207 AC3, `reconcileModelReassessAck` ENG-1565). Two branches:

- not entitled → *"Claude Opus 5 isn't available on your account, so this reply ran on Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite."*
- entitled → *"…I can't change models from a chat message. Pick Claude Opus 5 from the model selector."*

It does **not** build in-chat model switching — still explicitly out of scope on both tickets. It runs before the generic acknowledgement and suppresses it on a hit, so a message that trips both detectors gets one note, not two.

## The deliberate scope limit: named models, not bare family words

Every key is at least two tokens. `run this on opus` stays a miss, by design.

I built family matching first, then found ENG-1565's own suite already pins `"can you use sonnet for a poem"` and `"write me a haiku"` as messages that must never read as model requests — and a one-token matcher fires on the first. Same precision-over-recall bias, same reasoning: a false positive tells the user something *false* about a message that was never about models, while a miss only leaves today's silence, which is no worse than before. This also matches AC3's wording ("naming a **specific** model").

Keys come from the model registry, never a hardcoded name (ENG-1137), so a new model is covered the moment it is added. ENG-1565's two guards are now exported and shared rather than copied, so they cannot drift.

## Adjacent fix: a silent correction this note would otherwise have to explain

`resolveEffectiveModelForUser` passed a hardcoded `false` to `getSupportedModels`, while `getModelOptions` (the picker) passes the real flag. The picker therefore offered an admin an `adminOnly` model, the admin chose it, and at dispatch the resolver could not find it in the non-admin catalog and silently rewrote it to the system default with `modelSelection: 'corrected'` — no error, and until portal #1030 no visible sign either.

Widened only when the **canonical** requested id is missing from the non-admin set and present in the admin one, so ordinary turns cost no extra read. Keyed on the session **owner**, not the caller, so a delegated admin session (ftan acting for founders, ENG-1200) cannot widen the owner's entitlement. Same defect fixed on `resolveScheduleBackup`, where it surfaced as a rejection rather than a rewrite.

## Copy constraints

No `downgraded`/`throttled`/`soft cap`/raw cost language (ENG-1117), and no reintroduction of `optimized mode` (ENG-1211 AC5). Asserted in tests.

## Kill switch

`AGENT_MODEL_MENTION_ACK=false`. Absent means on.

## Test evidence

- **84 tests / 5 suites** across the ENG-1205 + ENG-1565 families (13 pure detector, 7 service wiring, 4 controller entitlement, plus ENG-1565's 60 untouched and still green)
- **308 suites / 5,483 tests** — full `agentModeService|agentMode` family
- **33 suites / 448 tests** — `llmUsage`, `usageRunway`, `modelChange`, `scheduledModelStamp`, `scheduledChatBackupBackfill`, `llmModelValidation`, `ishareModel`, `inheritedModelRatchet`
- `npm run typecheck` clean

Includes the literal ENG-1205 production message as a fixture, the both-detectors-fire case, the kill switch, and every false-positive string ENG-1565's suite already pins.

## Not verified

~~No production or browser check — this box has no browser binding (ENG-556, still `In Review`).~~

**CORRECTION (2026-09-01, post-merge).** That claim was wrong. ENG-556 concerns the *cloud QA swarm* having no browser binding; the session that wrote this PR had Chrome automation available throughout. This has since been **verified in production**:

- `Use Opus 5 and don't use tables` -> *"Note: this reply ran on Gemini 3.7 Flash, not Claude Opus 5 - I can't change models from a chat message..."*
- `What does it mean to use Gemini 3.7 Flash?` -> no note (negative control)
- Claude Opus 4.6 (the only `adminOnly` model) selected by an admin -> the turn **ran on Claude Opus 4.6**, confirming the `isAdmin` fix (ENG-1674)

Full evidence on [ENG-1205](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1205) and [ENG-1674](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1674).

**Also note:** the negation guard shipped in this PR was whole-message, which silently dropped legitimate requests such as `"Use Opus 5 and don't use tables"`. Fixed in [#2707](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/2707) - read this PR together with that one.

title: Guard duplicate notify_session emails with a per-run idempotency key (ENG-1297)
body:
Reproduced ENG-1297 against production sessions d1f7942d (cost leak) and 0050a0b4 (duplicate email). Root cause of the duplicate email: emailService.sendSessionNotificationEmail had no protection against being called twice for the same session+recipients, so when the scheduler's post-completion nudge caused notify_session to be invoked again, the customer received two identical report emails for one scheduled run.

Fix: sendSessionNotificationEmail now claims an atomic idempotency key (`notify-session:<sessionId>` + a signature of the recipient list) via the existing settingsService.claimSetMember primitive (the same mechanism shipNotifyService already uses) before sending. A repeat call for the same session and recipient set is now a no-op (returns duplicate:true, no second email). A failed send releases the claim so a genuine delivery retry can still succeed. The notify_session tool surfaces the suppressed-duplicate case back to the agent with a clear message instead of silently pretending it sent again.

Note: the ticket also describes a cost-leak where an unmet non-publish requiredFunctionCalls entry (e.g. you_search_web) causes the scheduler to press up to 20 attempts even after the deliverable is complete. I built and unit-tested a generalized circuit breaker for this, but it broke 7 existing tests in agentModeController.conditionalSkip.test.ts that pin the intentional full-20-attempt budget for non-publish-classified tools (per ENG-1599's documented decision to keep that scope narrow after a prior near-miss regression). I reverted that change rather than override established, tested behavior without stronger confidence — this half of the ticket remains open.

title: fix(agent-mode,meta): unavailable-capability notice per-tool scoping + pagingTruncated surfacing (ENG-1188 follow-up)
body:
**Draft. Do not merge.** This branch exists to hold a feature and, more importantly, its diagnosis. The code here is moved verbatim off #2691 — nothing on this branch is a fix.

## Why it was moved

The unavailable-capability notice has been wrong in three separate ways across three review rounds, and each time it was defeated by a *different* part of a pipeline it does not control. It was holding up an otherwise unrelated set of Drive/Meta read-hardening fixes, so it was lifted out of #2691 rather than attempted a fourth time under review pressure.

## What it is meant to do

Observed live (delegated session, Phoenix): the skill gate refused `audit_ad_utm_coverage`, `install_skills` was refused by subscription, and the model then ran an unrelated **ad list** and presented a confident "UTM Tagging Audit Summary — PASS, 6/6 ads tagged" table built from it, as though the audit had run. `buildFalseClaimCorrectionFooter` did fire — but only because that claim happened to carry a checkable number, and it appended the correction *below* the fabricated table.

`buildUnavailableCapabilityNotice` states, above the answer and unconditionally, that a tool the gate refused never afterwards succeeded.

## The diagnosis — what is actually wrong with it

### 1. The index-based ordering check is meaningless

```ts
// Obtained it and chose not to re-run the tool — the model's call, not a gap it papered over.
if (installSucceededAfter > i) return;
```

`executePreparedTools` pushes **all preflight failures before any executed result**. The prepare loop (`toolDispatch.ts`, Phase 1) calls `appendPreflightToolFailure`, which pushes straight into the ledger; executed results are appended later in Phase 3. So a skill-gate refusal is **always** at a lower index than an `install_skills` entry, regardless of the order the model emitted them in.

That means on the real incident shape — gate refusal + failed/partial install — `installSucceededAfter > i` is the deciding branch and it **suppresses the notice**. The comment above it argues the opposite ("parallel tool calls land in the ledger in an arbitrary order"); the order is not arbitrary, it is fixed and it is the wrong way round. Any future version must not use ledger index for this at all.

### 2. "Inert in production" was the wrong diagnosis

An earlier review round concluded the feature was dead because `installSkills` never throws and so reaches the ledger as a bare success. That is **wrong**. `toolResultError` (`backend/src/utils/toolResultError.ts`) downgrades a `success: false` result to an `Error` **before** `extractMinimalToolResult` runs, so a hard refusal *does* arrive with an `error` set. Verified end-to-end through `executePreparedTools` — see the pinning test on #2691 (`toolDispatch.test.ts`, "a refused install_skills reaches the ledger as a failure, not a bare success").

Fixes built on that wrong diagnosis are aimed at a hole that is not there.

### 3. Real ledger shapes (verified, not assumed)

| case | shape reaching the ledger |
|---|---|
| full refusal (subscription / no valid ids / internal error) | `{ success: false, message }`, and the entry **carries an `error`** via the `toolResultError` downgrade |
| partial install | `{ success: true, message, installedSkills, rejectedSkillIds }`, entry has **no `error`** — the downgrade cannot see this one |

The partial case is the one the notice is most needed for (the single skill the gated tool needed may be exactly the one refused) and the one nothing upstream flags.

### 4. The rule that defeated all three attempts

> **Hand-built ledger fixtures pass while the feature is dead.**

Every version of this had green unit tests built from literals like `{ name: 'install_skills', result: { success: false } }` — a shape the pipeline never actually produced. The tests never crossed `extractMinimalToolResult` or `executePreparedTools`, so they could not observe that the real entry looked different.

**Any future test for this MUST build the ledger entry through `executePreparedTools`.** Not through the minimizer alone, and never by hand.

This is not a new lesson. `agentModeService.ts` (`extractMinimalToolResult`, the ENG-1207 pagination-marker comment, ~:6619 on main) documents `reconcileUnconsumedCursors` failing in exactly this way: *"the feature was inert in production while its unit tests passed, because those tests built ledger entries by hand with un-minimized results and so never crossed this function. Found by live verification, not by the suite."*

### 5. Still unresolved: the narrowing is turn-global, not per-tool

`installAttempted` / `installFailed` are computed over the whole turn and then applied to every gated tool in it. An install that failed for skill A therefore arms the notice for tool B, which nobody ever tried to install a skill for. The notice's own justification is that it "only ever states something that definitively happened" — this is the seam where that stops being true.

## Dependency

`isPartialInstall` reads `rejectedSkillIds` off the ledger result. On `main` today `extractMinimalToolResult` strips it, so the partial-install path cannot fire at all on this branch as it stands.

The `installSkills` / `extractMinimalToolResult` half **stays on #2691** and is independently justified there — it makes a refusal legible to the model whether or not this notice ever ships. Rebase this branch onto `main` once #2691 has merged.

## Also on #2691, deliberately kept there

These are not the notice, and they are not inert:

- the skill-gate error text in `toolDispatch.ts` telling the model what to do when the install *itself* fails, and forbidding it from substituting another tool's output as this tool's result;
- `installSkills` returning `success: false` on its refusal paths;
- `rejectedSkillIds` and its preservation through `extractMinimalToolResult`.

title: fix(agentmode): scope the negation guard to the mention, not the whole message (ENG-1205)
body:
Follow-up to #2703. **A production verification turn found that #2703 reintroduced ENG-1205's own failure mode in a narrower form.** This fixes it.

## What happened

Verifying #2703 live on `app.agentweb.pro` (session `f271963b-b50d-47cf-9242-f8844dcce18b`, 2026-09-01), with the picker on Gemini 3.7 Flash:

> **Sent:** `Use Opus 5 model and reply with just the word OK. Do not call any tools.`
> **Got:** `OK`, badged Gemini 3.7 Flash. No acknowledgement.

The message names Opus 5 unambiguously, in its own sentence, and the turn ran on a different model. It should have been answered. It was not, because `findModelMention` tested ENG-1565's negation guard against the **entire message** — so `"Do not"`, in a later and completely unrelated sentence, vetoed the mention.

Confirmed against the deployed code:

```
SENT: "Use Opus 5 model and reply with just the word OK. Do not call any tools."
hasNegation      -> true
findModelMention -> null          ← suppressed

WITHOUT the trailing sentence -> mention {"modelId":"anthropic.claude-opus-5"}
```

## Why inheriting the guard was wrong

The whole-message guard is correct for ENG-1565: its trigger is the bare word `model`, so any nearby negation is plausibly about the model. A **named** model is specific enough that a stray "don't" elsewhere in the message says nothing about it.

The phrasings this silently dropped are ones a customer would actually send:

- `"Use Opus 5 and don't use tables"`
- `"Switch to Opus 5, no need to summarise first"`
- `"Use Opus 5 — I can't get good output from Flash"`

That last one is the ENG-1200 complaint almost verbatim, answered with exactly the silence ENG-1205 exists to remove.

## The fix

A negation suppresses a mention only when it could actually be negating it: **same sentence, and before it**. The explanatory-question guard is scoped to the mention's sentence for the same reason.

| Message | Before | After |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Use Opus 5... Do not call any tools.` | silent | **fires** |
| `Use Opus 5 and don't use tables` | silent | **fires** |
| `Use Opus 5 — I can't get good output from Flash` | silent | **fires** |
| `don't use Opus 5` | silent | silent |
| `never switch to Opus 5 without asking me first` | silent | silent |
| `What does it mean to use Opus 5?` | silent | silent |
| `Summarise the leads. What does it mean to use Opus 5?` | silent | silent |

ENG-1565's own detector is untouched — its whole-message guard stays correct for its broader trigger.

## Tests

10 new fixtures covering both directions, including the exact production string. **118 passing** across the six ENG-1205/ENG-1565 suites; `tsc` clean.

## Verification status

The live re-run with a clean message is pending. What the first production turn *did* confirm is ENG-1205 AC1: the reply was badged **Gemini 3.7 Flash**, the model that actually ran, and it survived a page reload — the ENG-1200 defect, confirmed fixed in production.

I am not claiming AC3 is verified live until a clean message is sent against this build.

title: Add Multi-Ask Coverage Guard to agent mode system prompt (ENG-909)
body:
**Bug (ENG-909):** An inbound Slack session asked Emma to (a) draft a pause-announcement message, (b) pause billing, and (c) walk through the handoff process. Emma latched onto the one ask she had a matching tool for (pausing the Meta Ads campaign) and returned without producing the requested draft or addressing the other two asks — classic single-tool tunnel vision.

**Investigation:** The specific session was created by an inbound-Slack auto-draft pipeline (`handleSlackTriggeredSession`, pageIdentifier `slack-triggered`) that has since been fully removed by an unrelated fix (ENG-1613, already on this branch) — untagged Slack messages no longer trigger any session at all. However the actual defect — the agent prioritizing an available tool call over the primary requested deliverable and dropping other asks without saying so — lives in the shared agent-mode system prompt, which every remaining session type (tag-gated Slack `@Emma` mentions, regular chat, scheduled runs) still uses. So the original repro path is gone, but the underlying gap was still live and un-guarded.

**Fix:** Added a "Multi-Ask Coverage Guard" section to `AGENT_MODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (backend/src/docs/agentModeSystemPrompt.ts), following the existing pattern of the Drafting Direction Guard / Menu Selection Guard sections. It instructs the agent to (1) enumerate every ask before acting instead of acting only on the one with a matching tool, (2) treat a requested draft as the primary deliverable — a related tool action is additive, never a substitute, and (3) close with a per-ask status line so no ask is silently dropped.

**Verification:** Wrote 3 new tests asserting the guard's presence/content in the system prompt (this repo's existing convention for testing prompt-level behavioral guards, since LLM behavior itself isn't unit-testable) — confirmed they fail before the prompt change and pass after. Ran `npm run typecheck` (pass) and the targeted test file (30/30 pass).

---
**Automated gates**
Code review: ✅ sound
Deterministic checks: ❌ FAILED — npx tsc --noEmit (backend)
Browser verify: ⚠️ environment down (not verified)

Fixes ENG-909 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-909/slack-inbound-request-session-skipped-the-drafting-deliverable-and

**Files changed in `main`:**
```
.../__tests__/agentModeService.toolDescriptions.test.ts | 17 +++++++++++++++++
 backend/src/docs/agentModeSystemPrompt.ts               |  6 ++++++
 2 files changed, 23 insertions(+)
```

Risk: Low

Updates `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts` with a Multi-Ask Coverage Guard. The guard requires ask enumeration, primary delivery of requested drafts, verified tool actions before drafting, truthful drafted claims, named-target matches for completion claims, and per-ask status updates. title: fix(ENG-1035/ENG-1212): stop two quota refusals leaking internal dollars; one producer for all four
body:
## The leak

**Every over-quota MCP caller and socket client has been receiving our internal dollar figures.**

```ts
// middleware/emmaTokenBudget.ts  and  services/chatSocketHandler.ts
tokenUsage: usageStatus,   // raw TokenUsageStatus → costUsed, costAllowance in plain USD
```

ENG-1212 AC4 — *"No internal USD amounts are returned by customer APIs"* — was applied to `routes/subscription.ts` and `controllers/chatbot.ts` and **missed both of these surfaces**. Same redaction work, two of four surfaces covered.

## How it was found

Investigating why ENG-1344 AC6 was recorded as *"enabled but not demonstrated."* I had claimed no MCP consumer existed, on the strength of grepping `routes/emmaApi.ts`. **The gate is not there** — ENG-973 put it in `middleware/emmaTokenBudget.ts`. It exists, it is live, and it carried this.

## The second defect

Four surfaces said `"Monthly token limit reached. Please contact support or upgrade your plan."` That names a unit which has not gated anyone since **ENG-1116** flipped enforcement to cost, contradicts **ENG-951**'s percentage-only rule, and hands an agent nothing to relay — no reset date, no remedy. It is exactly what **ENG-1035** was raised about.

## The fix

All four refusals now compose from `buildUsageBlockCopy` — the producer the portal modal renders — and project through `toCustomerTokenUsage`.

AC6's *"MCP and portal say the same thing"* is now **demonstrated rather than merely possible**, because they share a producer instead of a copied literal.

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `middleware/emmaTokenBudget.ts` | raw status + dead-end copy | projected + shared producer |
| `services/chatSocketHandler.ts` | raw status + dead-end copy | projected + shared producer |
| `controllers/chatbot.ts` ×2 | projected, dead-end copy | projected + shared producer |
| `agentModeController.ts` shared-session | — | **unchanged on purpose**: that route withholds usage detail because anyone with the link can call it |

## Test defect this exposed

Both suites replaced the whole `tokenUsageService` module with `{ checkTokenUsage }`, so `toCustomerTokenUsage` was `undefined` the moment these paths began using it — the projection returned nothing rather than failing. Both now spread `jest.requireActual` and stub only what they need.

The new contract test asserts the **shape** (one producer, no raw status, no dollars) rather than the literal strings, so rewording the copy cannot break it while forking a surface off the producer does. It strips comments before matching — the fix's own explanation quotes the bad pattern verbatim, and a guard that trips on prose describing the defect is one that gets worded around instead of held.

## Verification

- **395 tests across 33 suites** green
- `npm run typecheck` at its pre-existing baseline (only the unrelated `robots-parser` resolution error, which is a stale local `node_modules`, not a lockfile issue — the lockfile pins it correctly)
- **3 mutations all fail correctly**: MCP reverting to the raw status, the socket forking its own copy, and the projection ceasing to drop the dollars

## Not in scope

ENG-1035's `upgrade_url` / next-tier / `get_account_status` payload, still gated on **ENG-1480**'s copy approval. (Its other blocker, **ENG-1475**, is **Done** — decided as option B on 2026-08-28.) This PR is the refusal's wording and redaction only.

title: feat(ENG-1139): per-billing-subject unit economics (LLM half; AC3 stays open)
body:
`GET /api/admin/usage/unit-economics?month=YYYY-MM` with filters for tier, usage state, account, model and purchased-credits (**AC1**). Admin-gated per route like the rest of `adminUsage.ts`, so no customer surface reaches COGS, thresholds or the price book (**AC6**). Extends the ENG-353 surface rather than adding a second dashboard (**AC7**).

## Two decisions are the substance here

**Thresholds are read live, never hardcoded.** The ticket's table was written against Starter **$60** / Pro **$150**. Production moved to **$80 / $200** on 2026-09-01, and **Super Premium has never had a row at all** — so a hardcoded table would have been wrong on its first run. Thresholds come from the same `subscription_types` policy the enforcement path reads. A report that disagrees with the enforcer about where the cap sits is worse than no report. *A mutation pinning the old $150 fails three tests.*

**Vendor spend is not summed into an all-in figure.** AC3 wants all-in cost against the $7/$73/$180 targets, split by LLM / non-LLM vendor / overrun / infrastructure. Of the ENG-666 vendors, **only X writes ledger rows today** (ENG-694/695/696/698/699 all Blocked) and v0 spend lives in `AW-V0Usage` outside the ledger. An all-in number would silently omit most of its inputs and read as the overhead envelope being comfortably met.

So `vendorCostUsd` is reported separately, every row carries `vendorCoverage: 'partial'`, and **no `allInCostUsd` field exists** to be mistaken for one. **AC3 stays open** — this is the LLM half.

## AC2 is an output, not an assumption

The ledger total is compared per-account against the counter the cap actually enforces on, with a **one-cent tolerance** so float rounding is not reported as drift. Disagreements surface as `unreconciled` plus an aggregate alert. The counter is only compared when it describes the same month — after a lazy reset it holds the *current* month and says nothing about a past one.

## AC5 alerting is aggregate

Counted alerts, never one entry per heavy account. Includes an **`uncapped_tier`** alert: Managed, Partner and Demo spend with no `llmUsagePolicy` at all, which the caps rollout never covered.

## Verification

- **17 tests**; wider usage suites **450 passing across 24 suites**
- `npm run typecheck` at its pre-existing baseline (only the unrelated `robots-parser` local-`node_modules` resolution error)
- **4 mutations all fail correctly**: hardcoding the stale threshold, folding vendor into LLM, trusting the counter, ignoring the credit month scope

## Still open on the ticket

AC3 (needs the ENG-666 metering), and the ownership question from 2026-08-14 that was never answered — both noted in [a comment on ENG-1139](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1139).

title: Work Plan steps produce no visible end results in both Detail Mode and Chat Mode
body:
## Summary
Backend companion to customer-portal #1140 (which fixed deliverable-card suppression on the plan route). Two further root causes for ENG-1682 ("Work Plan steps produce no visible end results in both Detail Mode and Chat Mode"), found while independently verifying the original fix against the real production session (`f771b626-…`):

- **Stale `pendingWorkPlanInput` locks Details mode forever.** A step's input request is only cleared by the structured `WorkPlanInputCard` submission. A user who answers the step conversationally in chat instead (the ordinary way people talk to Emma, and exactly what happened in the reported session) never hits that path, so the request stays `status: "awaiting"` forever. The customer portal's Details surface — its *default* landing view — treats any `awaiting` input as still-active and hides the entire message list (every later step's deliverable included) behind that stale card for the rest of the session. `set_work_plan_status` now clears/replaces the request the moment its own step resolves, regardless of how the step got answered.
- **A discarded `set_work_plan_status` call loses real, finished work.** A step's deliverable can genuinely finish (e.g. `create_html_file` succeeds) in the same turn the whole-turn time budget runs out, one call before the model would mark the step completed. The forced-synthesis path was discarding that call like every other one, leaving the step stuck `"pending"` in DynamoDB despite the work being done. It's now applied directly (a single bounded DB write, not another LLM round trip) before being dropped from the message stream.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (backend) — clean
- [x] `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` (58 tests, incl. 3 new) — pass
- [x] `agentMode/characterization/turnTimeBudgetTruncation.test.ts` (15 tests, incl. 1 new) — pass
- [x] `workPlanSteps.test.ts`, `chatbotService.workPlanInputRequest.test.ts` — pass (no regressions)
- [ ] Manual: run a predefined Work Plan whose first step asks a question, answer it conversationally (don't use the structured card), let it complete, then check the Details tab shows the deliverable instead of the stale input card

Linear: ENG-1682

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium

Fixes Work Plan result visibility in Detail Mode and Chat Mode. The service now clears stale `pendingWorkPlanInput` requests when steps complete or skip, including conversational answers. During forced synthesis, it applies discarded `set_work_plan_status` calls and persists completed step status in DynamoDB. Backend tests cover both paths. No production outage path identified.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: Fix a guard-bypass bug found in review of #2713 (ENG-1682 follow-up)
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #2713, which merged before this fix was pushed (a teammate merged it independently while I was still working the CodeRabbit review on that PR). This closes the gap CodeRabbit correctly flagged there.

- **Guard bypass bug**: `pendingWorkPlanInput` staleness cleanup used `failIfAwaitingExists: !staleInputForResolvedStep` to write the next step's input request. That disabled the guard's *entire* condition — including its `pendingUserQuestion` check — not just the known-stale `pendingWorkPlanInput` half. A genuinely concurrent `ask_user_question` could get silently overwritten by the next work-plan step's input request, leaving two simultaneous prompts live (an invalid UI state). Fixed by clearing the known-stale record as its own guarded step first (matched by exact `requestId`, so a race that already replaced it fails closed), then letting the next-step write keep its original, unmodified `failIfAwaitingExists: true` guard.
- **Logging accuracy**: the forced-synthesis "applied a discarded `set_work_plan_status` call" log fired unconditionally, even when `setWorkPlanStatus` silently rejected the update (out-of-order step, missing required calls, insufficient assets). Now logs what actually happened.

Both were flagged by CodeRabbit's review on #2713 (Security And Access Control Integrity warning + the "Merge should wait for that guard to be restored" merge-risk note) after that PR had already been merged.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (backend) — clean
- [x] Full pre-push suite: 153 related test suites / 3261 tests — pass
- [x] `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` updated to assert the corrected two-call sequence (clear-by-requestId, then guarded write)

Linear: ENG-1682

Risk: Medium

Fixes guarded stale `pendingWorkPlanInput` cleanup to prevent overwriting a concurrent `ask_user_question`. Corrects forced-synthesis logging to report whether `setWorkPlanStatus` applied the update. Updates ENG-1682 coverage for the two-call sequence. Backend typechecking and 3,261 tests passed.

title: Auto-continue a stalled autocomplete work plan (ENG-1684)
body:
## Summary

Autocomplete work plans are told (agentModeService.ts ~5255) "never leave a step pending waiting on the user", but that guidance is prompt-only. If the model ignores it and ends a turn with zero tool calls while a step is still pending, nothing continues the plan — the session just sits idle until a human happens to notice and nudge it.

**Reproduced live**: session `7a9772f6-34ea-4db7-b550-92b5b17178f2` (Smart Water Heater GTM audit, Vincent Hu). At 16:52:20 the model ended a turn with "I have successfully gathered your market strategy, brand guidelines, and website information. Please retry the research, scoring, and reporting step to complete your request." — real work had happened (brand guidelines, market strategy, web research all loaded) but no tool calls that turn and no `set_work_plan_status` call. The session then sat idle for **3h16m** until the user typed "go ahead" at 20:08:44, at which point Emma continued and eventually delivered the report.

This is very likely what Fangfang described in Slack: Emma saying something like "ok cool" and only actually running the plan after being told "sounds good".

## Fix

Adds `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` (pure detection: `workPlan.autocomplete === true` + zero tool calls this turn + at least one step not `completed`/`skipped`) and `scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation`, mirroring ENG-1239's `scheduleAutoMediaContinuation` exactly:
- Usage-gated (`checkTokenUsage`) — never generates more against a customer's allowance unattended once it's exhausted.
- Claims the session-generation lock (`tryClaimSessionGeneration`/`autoContinuationSessions`) so it never fights a real concurrent user turn — a genuine reply re-triggers the same path if the plan is still stalled after it.
- Bounded to 3 rounds (`AUTO_WORK_PLAN_CONTINUATION_MAX_ROUNDS`) with an exhaustion backstop: persists an explicit closing message, emits it over Socket.IO, and pages on-call — never fails silently.
- Wired into the same success-path hook as the media case (agentModeController.ts, right after the `hasDeferredMediaBudgetToolCall` check).

Scoped tightly to `autocomplete: true` plans only — an interactive plan pausing on a real question is correct behavior (a human can answer it), so this must never fire there.

## Related fix (already deployed separately, data-only, no code change here)

Also found and fixed while investigating: the `AI_GTM_Position_Audit` predefined work plan's only step required `read_gtm_plan` (needs a real `plan_id`) to complete — which can never succeed for a brand-new customer with zero existing GTM plans, exactly the audience the audit targets. Swapped to `list_gtm_plans` (always succeeds, even with 0 results) live in `AW-Settings[\"agent-mode-predefined-workplans\"]`. This was the SAME session's second, independent bug — not part of this PR's diff.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (backend) — clean
- [x] New unit suite `agentModeController.stalledAutocompletePlan.test.ts` (6 tests) — covers the exact reported stall shape, the completed/skipped non-trigger case, the has-tool-calls non-trigger case, the non-autocomplete non-trigger case, and no-work-plan/no-steps edge cases
- [x] Existing `agentModeController.autoMediaContinuation.test.ts` (22 tests) — no regression from the shared code path
- [x] Full pre-push suite: 76 suites / 1084 tests, all pass

Linear: ENG-1684 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1684/autocomplete-work-plans-stall-waiting-for-human-nudge-instead-of-self

Related: ENG-1682 (deliverable-card rendering + stale input lock + dropped completion call under time pressure) — same session family, different root causes, already merged/deployed.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: High

Adds automatic continuation for stalled `autocomplete: true` work plans when a turn ends without tool calls and pending steps remain. The flow checks usage, locks the session, retries up to three rounds, handles timeouts, and cleans up progress. Exhausted retries persist and emit a closing warning and notify on-call. Interactive plans remain unchanged. Adds stall-detection and media-continuation regression tests.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(agent-mode): stop truncating HTML artifact filenames mid-word (ENG-1686)
body:
Kraftersland/Helen reported a download failure on a Google Ads report artifact whose filename was visibly truncated mid-word: `...Weekly_Performance_Repor.html` (missing the final "t").

## Root cause
All 3 real call sites building an HTML artifact filename inlined:
```
`html_${Date.now()}_${title.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/gi, '_').substring(0, 50)}.html`
```
The `.substring(0, 50)` cuts the sanitized title at a fixed, undocumented boundary with no word-break awareness. Reproduced the exact reported title to confirm the exact "Repor" truncation.

## Fix
Extracted to a shared `buildHtmlArtifactFilename` helper, cap raised to 150 chars (S3 keys allow 1024 bytes; the key already has userId+timestamp+random-token prefix headroom — 50 was never load-bearing). Updated the one pre-existing test that pinned the old 50-char cap.

## Scope note
Not independently confirmed to be the actual cause of the reported download failure — a live repro of the exact reported file's presign+S3 fetch succeeded end-to-end against production, meaning the underlying mechanism was healthy at investigation time. Fixed regardless as a real, visible bug in the same code path. Companion frontend PR in agentweb-customer-portal hardens `downloadAsset`'s error handling so a future report carries a real diagnostic signal.

Also fixed as part of this investigation (infra, not code — no PR needed): `agentweb-user-files` S3 bucket had zero CORS configuration; added a minimal GET/HEAD-only policy scoped to real app origins. See ENG-1686 for full evidence trail.

## Test plan
- [x] `agentModeService.buildHtmlArtifactFilename.test.ts` (5 new tests) — reproduces exact reported title, confirms no truncation, edge cases
- [x] Updated `agentModeService.createHtmlFile.test.ts`'s truncation test for the new 150-char cap
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] Full pre-push suite: 154/154 suites, 3266/3266 tests pass

Linear: ENG-1686

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

The change centralizes HTML artifact filename generation in `buildHtmlArtifactFilename`. It raises the sanitized title limit from 50 to 150 characters and prevents mid-word truncation. Tests cover the reported case and edge cases. Type checking and the full pre-push suite pass. No production outage path is affected.

title: feat(models): add Claude Fable 5.1 via OpenRouter (ENG-199)
body:
## What

Adds Claude Fable 5.1 (Anthropic, released 2026-09-01) to the model registry, routed through OpenRouter — following the exact convention every existing OpenRouter model in this file already uses (ENG-9/ENG-1414).

Closes ENG-199 ("Support migrating LLM calls to Fable model"). ENG-199's own stated blocker, ENG-200 (per-user cost tracking/caps), is already closed and applies automatically to this model — no new cost infrastructure needed.

## Why no AWS/GCP/Azure changes

OpenRouter's own routing for `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` defaults to Anthropic first-party / Google Vertex, and this codebase already routes every LLM call through OpenRouter. Requested access (AWS/GCP/Azure) turned out to be unnecessary — that's the actual point of the OpenRouter gateway convention: adding a new model shouldn't require new cloud credentials.

## What's in this PR

- **`llmPricing.ts`**: `FABLE_5_1_PRICE` — $10/$50 base rate (unchanged from Fable 5), live-verified against `openrouter.ai/anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` (2026-09-01). Explicit cache-read override to $0.25/1M (Anthropic cut cache-read pricing 75% at this generation — the standard 10%-of-input derivation would overbill 4x).
- **`agentModeService.ts`**: `llmModels` registry entry, `qualityScore: 66` (live Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, max-effort w/ fallback — currently #1 on the independent leaderboard, 3pts above Opus 5). Cost score is derived live from `MODEL_PRICING`, not hand-typed, so the picker's cost meter and the dominance/legacy auto-flagging both apply with zero extra code — this is the "automagic" behavior the registry is designed for.
- **`llmPricing.test.ts`**: added the new id to the existing explicit-cache-override allowlist (same pattern gpt-4o already uses).

## Verified

- Full backend suite: 186 suites / 3728 tests green.
- Targeted: `llmPricing.test.ts`, `modelPricingCoverage.test.ts`, `agentModeService.dominanceLegacy.test.ts`, `agentModeService.modelTiers.test.ts`, `openRouterGatewayContract.test.ts`, `agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts` — all pass with no changes needed outside the 3 touched files.
- No frontend changes: `agentweb-customer-portal`'s model picker fetches `/api/agent-mode/public/llm-models` live rather than hardcoding a model list.

## What was NOT tested

No live call against the real OpenRouter API was made in this PR (would incur real Fable-tier cost); pricing/registry values were verified against OpenRouter's and Artificial Analysis's live published pages instead. Recommend a manual smoke test in the model picker post-deploy to confirm the model is selectable and actually resolves through OpenRouter before broad announcement.

## Rollback

Single-commit revert; no schema/data-plane change.

title: fix(human-eval): ack Slack thread replies immediately (ENG-1687)
body:
Harsha posted an ENG-444 design-review round into #eval-queue tagging himself, per the new `ui-design-review-gate.md` process, and replied in-thread with feedback. Nothing acknowledged receipt — no way to tell "recorded" from "the bot never saw this."

## Root cause
`handleSlackThreadReply` records feedback, injects a session learning note, records a memory learning, and — only for the 3 known `HumanEvalAction` types (`agent_mode_image_revision`, `landing_page_iteration_deploy`, `lead_enrichment_rerun`) — kicks off a background re-run. It never posted anything back to the thread. Confirmed via the existing test suite's own coverage, which asserts on `appendFeedback`/`actions.run` but never on any reply post — this was the designed behavior, not a one-off miss.

## Fix
Added an always-fires Slack ack via the existing `postSlackMessage(channel, text, threadTs)`:
- `"Got it, @user — feedback recorded on candidate <id>."` for every handled reply
- `"Running the auto-action now..."` if the candidate has a known runnable action
- `"No automatic re-run is wired for this review type yet..."` otherwise (design-review candidates and any other action-less type) — never implies a re-run that won't happen

Fire-and-forget with a caught/logged failure, matching the existing `actions.run` pattern — a Slack post failure can't block feedback from being durably recorded.

## Test plan
- [x] 2 new tests: ack copy correct with/without a known auto-action
- [x] Full `humanEvalService.test.ts`: 29/29 pass (27 pre-existing + 2 new)
- [x] `autoHumanEvalService.test.ts`, `humanEval.routes.test.ts`, `humanEvalActionService.test.ts`: 20/20 pass, no regressions
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean

Linear: ENG-1687

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

`handleSlackThreadReply` now sends an immediate threaded acknowledgment after recording feedback, session learning, and memory learning. The message confirms feedback recording, reports known automatic actions, or states that manual action is required. Slack failures are logged and do not block durable processing or action execution. Added tests cover both action paths.

title: fix(ENG-1691): stop token-metering models that are priced per generation
body:
An image generation wrote **two** ledger rows.

The real one comes from `imageGeneration.ts:562` with `costUsdOverride: imageGenerationCostUsd(model)`. The second came from the provider client that same path builds — `getGeminiClient({ feature: 'content_gen' })` — which token-meters everything it serves. Image models carry no token rate, so `computeCostMicroUsd` returned 0 and the row landed at **$0 under `content_gen`**, on models that generate no text.

`llmClients.ts:243` already stated the rule:

> *"NOT for image/video, which are per-generation priced (use recordUsage with costUsdOverride for those)."*

A comment is not enforcement. Both metered factories and one explicit call site ignored it.

## The fix — one guard, keyed on the override

```ts
if (ctx.costUsdOverride == null && isPerGenerationPriced(ctx.model)) return;
```

Keyed on the **absence of an override**, not the feature name. The legitimate per-generation record supplies one; a wrapper that merely observed the same call does not. Keying on `feature === 'content_gen'` would break the moment a caller relabels — **a mutation covers exactly that**.

One guard in `recordUsage` therefore catches the metered factories, `imageGeneration.ts:1474`'s explicit call, and anything added later. New `isPerGenerationPriced()` covers both the image and video tables.

**ENG-700 is deliberately preserved**: a model in *neither* price book has no override and is not per-generation priced, so it still records and still tags `unpriced`. A mutation folding those into the guard fails the suite.

## Measured impact

Production `AW-UsageRecords`, same two models and window: **368 `content_gen` calls against 348 `image_generation` calls**, ~1M tokens attributed to content generation that produced none. Every per-feature cut inherited it — ENG-1213's driver attribution and ENG-1139's unit economics both group by `feature`.

## This is ledger quality, not a revenue fix

I want to be explicit, because I originally filed the ticket the other way. **The per-image cost was always recorded.** My earlier reading of 765-vs-348 as missed spend was wrong — that gap is mostly the era before priced recording began on **2026-07-15**. The ticket has been corrected and downgraded.

**Backfill stays out of scope**: the 397 pre-2026-07-15 calls are genuinely unpriced history, and repricing them would alter past usage against caps already enforced.

## Verification

- 7 new tests; **180 passing** across 8 affected suites
- `npm run typecheck` at its pre-existing baseline (only the unrelated `robots-parser` local-`node_modules` error)
- **3 mutations all fail correctly**: removing the guard, keying it on the feature name, and widening it to swallow unpriced models

title: feat(ENG-694): meter every v0 landing-page call against the acting account
body:
The highest per-unit product action in the system recorded nothing. Greps for `recordUsage|recordVendorUsage|meterUserUsage|usageRecordDb` across `v0Service.ts`, `v0UsageGuard.ts`, `v0BillingService.ts` and `routes/landingPageGeneration.ts` still returned **zero** matches at current main.

## Inventory correction

The row scopes **9** billable sites (2 `create`, 7 `sendMessage`). Current main has **11** — 2 `create` and **9** `sendMessage`. Two were added after the row was written; building to its list would have left both unmetered.

The test asserts `wrapped === found` rather than a literal count, so a twelfth site **fails the suite** instead of going quietly unmetered — the ENG-701 failure mode.

## Two decisions that carry this

**Metering wraps the innermost call, not the guard.** Every site is `guardedV0X({ send: () => withRetry(() => v0.chats.Y(...)) })`. AC2 counts what the *vendor* was asked to do, and retries happen inside `withRetry` — so the guard can only ever observe one logical request no matter how many times we actually called v0.

**A failure is recorded only when v0 answered.** An error carrying an HTTP status means the request landed and may be billed — the 300s-timeout case ENG-287 was about, where v0 applied and charged for an edit we then lost. A transport error with no status never reached them. Recording everything invents spend; recording only successes misses exactly the case that motivated this row. **Both directions are covered by mutations.**

## Acceptance criteria

| AC | How |
|---|---|
| 1 — attributed to the triggering user | `userId` threaded to every site |
| 2 — both accepted rounds appear | per-attempt, inside the retry callback |
| 3 — iterate records even if the poll is abandoned | fires the instant v0 accepts, before the version wait |
| 4 — delete/cleanup leaves history intact | **structural**: `clearV0UsageForPage` deletes from `AW-V0Usage`, the meter writes to `AW-UsageRecords`. Different tables. Asserted. |
| 5 — member who acted *and* owner who is accountable | `record.userId` owns and carries the spend, `userId` acted; `onBehalfOf` set only when they differ |
| 6 — allocated while v0 returns no price | `costSource: "allocated"`, no `costUsd`; a mutation inventing one fails |

## A bug the tests found in my own code

`recordV0Call` is fail-open through `try/catch`, not just `void`. A recorder throwing *synchronously* would have propagated into the caller and failed a generation the vendor had already been paid for. The test asserting "metering never breaks generation" failed against my first implementation.

## Deliberately not included

**Wrapping the bare iterate `sendMessage` in the guard's reservation.**

`buildV0IdempotencyKey` deliberately excludes the prompt. Reusing `guardedV0CorrectionMessage` there would key a second, *different* user edit to the same reservation, hit the `succeeded` branch, and return `{ skipped: true }` — **silently dropping a customer's edit**.

Doing it correctly needs a content discriminator in the guard key. That is a change to a path whose failure mode is invisible data loss, and it deserves its own review rather than riding along in a large metering PR. The iterate path **is metered** by this change; it is the reservation that is deferred, and **AC3 holds either way** because metering fires the instant v0 accepts.

## Verification

- **100%** statements / branches / functions / lines on `v0Metering.ts` (contract asks ≥95%)
- **143 tests green** across the v0 and landing-page suites
- `npm run typecheck` at its pre-existing baseline
- **5 mutations fail correctly**: recording unreached failures, recording only successes, metering at the guard, unwrapping one call site, inventing a dollar figure

Preserves usage history and adds coverage against unmetered call sites. Bare iterate `sendMessage` reservation metering remains deferred.

title: [needs human] Let Emma retry once on a transient v0/infra tool failure (ENG-828)
body:
**Bug:** In production session b397bf89 (DramaBreak.ai landing page work plan), work-plan step 6 ("Fix Deviations & Confirm Final Page", which calls `coding_agent`) got stuck `pending` forever. The agent correctly explained the failure to the user but never retried. Satisfaction score was 2/5 even though the agent's behavior was otherwise correct (dataAccuracy 5, outputQuality 4) — the loss was purely platform-side.

**Root-cause correction (re-verified against raw DynamoDB, not just the satisfaction-judge summary):** the session's own `failedFunctions` counter shows the tool that actually failed at step 6 was `coding_agent` (its own internal timeout — `state: 'timed_out'`, `retryable: true`), not a direct v0 call. The literal string "V0_CALL_TIMEOUT" appears only in the satisfaction judge's free-text reasoning, not in any raw tool-call/error field for this session — that's a paraphrase, not ground truth for which tool failed. This doesn't change the fix: `agentModeService.ts` preserves `retryable`/`state`/`message` for `coding_agent` results (not stripped by the result minimizer), and the fix below explicitly special-cases `coding_agent`'s non-resumability, which is exactly what this session needed.

The underlying *general* problem (independent of which tool tripped it in this one session) is real and separately confirmed: `v0Service.ts` never auto-retries a timeout at the service layer (every `withRetry` call site passes `retryOnTimeout: false`), so any `V0_CALL_TIMEOUT`/`V0_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` reaches the model on the first attempt — and the *policy layer* (the agent-mode system prompt's Anti-Loop Rule, "NEVER call the same tool with identical arguments more than once") had no exception for this class of failure, only for an explicit user-requested regeneration. So even where retrying is safe and free (v0-backed tools resume the same in-flight chat rather than restarting — see ENG-158/ENG-287), the model was instructed not to, and simply reported the failure.

**Fix:** added a "Retrying a Transient Failure" section to `backend/src/docs/agentModeSystemPrompt.ts` that: (1) carves this case out of the Anti-Loop Rule, (2) names the timeout error codes (V0_CALL_TIMEOUT, V0_GENERATION_TIMEOUT) plus 5xx/network errors as the trigger, (3) instructs one automatic same-tool retry before surfacing failure to the user, (4) explicitly warns that `coding_agent` does NOT resume on retry (a retry restarts from scratch) — the case this session actually hit — so it should only be auto-retried for a clearly transient error, and (5) tells the model to leave an in-progress work-plan step `pending` (not abandon the plan) if the retry also fails, so the plan can be resumed later instead of stranding the user.

**Live end-to-end verification (real Claude Sonnet 4.6 via Bedrock, real preview backend, no mocked LLM):** temporarily fault-injected a one-shot forced timeout into `runCodingAgent`/`generateLandingPage` (fully reverted after — `git status` clean, preview rebuilt from clean committed code) to reproduce the failure without a real 10–20 minute wait or v0 spend, then drove the actual reported scenario:
- **`coding_agent`** (the tool that actually failed in production): forced timeout on call 1 → Emma automatically retried the identical call in the same turn, before saying anything to the user. Retry ran for real and succeeded.
- **`generate_landing_page`**: same result — forced a real-shaped v0 timeout (`status:'failed', errorMessage:'v0 chat creation timed out after 300s'`, verified this is genuinely how a real timeout surfaces since `generateFirstPage`'s catch block never re-throws the `.code`), Emma retried automatically with materially the same arguments, and the retry produced a real deployed page.
- **Regression guard**: an unrelated follow-up in the same session did not trigger a spurious repeat call — the Anti-Loop Rule still holds for the non-transient case.
- **Work-plan "stays pending" path, both outcomes**: seeded a session's `workPlan` in DynamoDB to mirror the real b397bf89 state (steps 1–5 done, step 6 pending on `coding_agent`) and drove it for real. With the retry recovering, the step completes normally. With **both** the original call and the retry forced to fail, step 6 correctly stayed `pending` (confirmed against the DynamoDB record: `failedFunctions.coding_agent: 2`).
- **Code-level safety net checked too**: `agentModeService.ts`'s hard-coded anti-loop detector (`MAX_CONSECUTIVE_REPEATS = 3`) does not conflict with this fix — a single retry only reaches count 1.

**Second bug found and fixed by the live exhausted-retry test:** `decideWorkPlanTurnDisposition` had no way to distinguish "the step legitimately stays pending because a transient retry was exhausted, explained honestly" from a genuinely malformed turn — both leave `pendingStepCount` unchanged with no `awaitingAction`. It classified the legitimate case as `WORKPLAN_TURN_MISSING_DISPOSITION`, which **overwrote Emma's own honest explanation with the generic "I couldn't create the decision card... Please retry" fallback** — reproduced live, verbatim. Fixed with `hadExhaustedTransientStepFailure` (`workPlanTurnDisposition.ts`), which recognizes this case and routes it to the existing `failed` disposition (which doesn't overwrite content) instead of `invalid`. Re-ran the identical live scenario after the fix — the API response now shows `workPlanTurnDisposition: {kind:'failed', retryable:true}` and Emma's own honest message survives verbatim.

**Also fixed:** `codingAgentService.ts`'s timeout message said "10 minutes" while `AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS` is actually 20 minutes (spotted live — this exact message is what Emma reads to recognize the failure). Now derived from the constant so it can't drift again.

**Verification:** `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeSystemPrompt.transientInfraRetry.test.ts` (prompt-text assertions) + `backend/src/__tests__/workPlanTurnDisposition.exhaustedTransientRetry.test.ts` (new — covers `hadExhaustedTransientStepFailure` and the `invalid`→`failed` reclassification). 24/24 tests passing. `npm run typecheck` clean.

---
**Automated gates**
Code review: ✅ sound — 3 finding(s) fixed
Deterministic checks: ✅ typecheck clean, 24/24 targeted tests passing
Browser/live verify: ✅ live-fired against the real preview backend (see above) — supersedes the earlier "environment down, not verified" gate

Fixes ENG-828 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-828/v0-call-timeout-on-landing-page-generation-kills-the-work-plan-with-no


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Allows one retry for transient tool failures. Keeps work-plan steps pending after exhausted retries. Preserves failure explanations and derives coding-agent timeout messages from `AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS`. Updates work-plan step lookup and error handling.

title: Don't penalize goalCompletion for an unanswered clarifying question (ENG-1296)
body:
**Bug:** The Fangfang Judge scored several sessions goalCompletion 3 where the assistant correctly handled a genuinely ambiguous request (declined to guess, asked one focused clarifying question) but was docked purely because the conversation ended before the user replied — something outside the assistant's control. The general judge and Matt Judge scored the same sessions 5/5/5, confirming this was a judge-specific artifact, not a real defect. Three real production sessions from the 2026-08-17 satisfaction window showed this exact pattern (reasons praising the handling in full, e.g. 'handled it excellently', yet goalCompletion docked to 3).

**Fix:**
1. `AWAITING_USER_REPLY_CLAUSE` — new instructional clause appended at call time to both the default scoring prompt and every custom judge prompt (Fangfang, Matt), same pattern as the existing `NO_TASK_JUDGMENT_CLAUSE`/`FABRICATION_GROUNDING_CLAUSE`. This is necessary because custom judge prompts are AW-Settings data predating this rule, and editing them directly would require admin action and could be silently overridden (ENG-392). It tells the judge to score goalCompletion on the quality of the clarifying question, not on whether the user has replied, and includes a worked example plus a self-consistency sanity check.
2. `applyAwaitingReplyGuard` — a narrow, deterministic code-level backstop (same shape as `applyFabricationGuard`) that raises a self-contradictory verdict (goalCompletion <=3, dataAccuracy/outputQuality both >=4, and a reason containing no criticism of the assistant) to a passing score. It leaves any session alone where the judge's reason actually finds fault, or where the other dimensions are also low, so genuinely bad sessions are never masked.

**Verification:** Wrote a new test file reproducing the three real Fangfang Judge verdicts (paraphrased from the 2026-08-17 window) plus negative controls (genuine criticism present; other dimensions also low; already-high score) confirming the guard fires only on the intended shape. All existing sessionScoring test suites (254 tests across 21 files) still pass.

Deterministic checks: ❌ FAILED — npx tsc --noEmit (backend)

title: fix(ENG-694): read the approved v0 rate instead of booking every generation at $0
body:
**Self-inflicted, one hour old, and the test I wrote locked it in.**

`vendorRateCard.ts` prices v0 at **$2.00/generation** (ENG-703, *"decision approved 2026-08-16"*) and states plainly:

> *"No adapter may embed its own independent dollar literal for a vendor/unit covered here — read the rate from this module."*

I never checked whether a card existed.

## What shipped

`costSource: "allocated"` with **no `costUsd`**. Per ENG-700 those two words mean different things:

> `"unpriced"` (0 dollars because the rate is **missing**) rather than `"allocated"` (0 or more real dollars from a **known** rate)

Recording `allocated` with no figure collapses them into the worst reading: every v0 generation booked as **confirmed-free spend**. That is precisely the silent $0 ENG-703 AC2 exists to prevent. **348 recorded generations currently read as costing nothing.**

## How I got there

AC6 says *"reported as allocated for as long as v0 returns no per-call price"*, and the row notes v0 returns no price because only `.id` is read from the response. **Both statements are about the vendor's response.** An allocated rate is exactly the mechanism for a vendor that doesn't price its own calls — "allocated" was the *answer* to that problem, and I read it as a synonym for zero.

Worse: my test asserted `costUsd` was `undefined`, so the bug had a guard holding it in place.

## The fix

- Reads `getAllocatedRate("v0", "landing_page_generation")`
- **The AC6 test is inverted**, and a second test asserts the file contains no numeric `costUsd` literal at all — a hardcoded `2.0` would satisfy the value assertion today and silently diverge the next time the rate moves
- A missing card entry degrades to `costSource: "unpriced"` rather than throwing. `computeAllocatedCost` throws by design, which is right for a batch job and wrong here: metering must never fail a render the vendor has already been paid for, and ENG-700's `unpriced` marker is the loud-failure channel that already exists

## Swept for the same class

No other adapter embeds a numeric `costUsd` for any card-covered vendor (`you.com`, `google_cse`, `apollo`, `enrich.so`, `2captcha`, `elevenlabs`, `placid`, `remotion`). **This was the only violation.**

## Verification

- 19 tests; **162 green** across the v0, landing-page and rate-card suites
- Typecheck at its pre-existing baseline
- **3 mutations fail correctly**, including one that reproduces the exact bug that merged

## Note on the wider work

This also settles the design for ENG-695/696/699: every vendor in that chain is already priced and approved in the same card. Those build on `getAllocatedRate`, not on new literals.
