title: fix(agent-mode): autocomplete stall backstop misses failed-tool-call stalls (ENG-1700, ENG-1699)
body:
## Summary

Two related bugs in the autocomplete work-plan stall/auto-continuation system
(`agentModeController.ts`, shipped 2026-09-01 for ENG-1684), both found and independently
verified during a Workplan-engine bug-hunt campaign triggered by the 2026-09-01 Smart Water
Heater onboarding incident.

- **ENG-1700**: `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` only detected a stall when a turn had **zero**
  tool calls — never when tool calls were attempted but **all failed** (e.g. `create_html_file`
  rejecting its payload repeatedly with `TruncatedToolCallArgumentsError`). Live-reproduced
  2026-09-02: a plan hung ~10 minutes and needed a human to type "continue" manually. Fix: a
  stall is now "no tool calls" OR "one or more tool calls, none of which succeeded" — reusing
  the existing `toolCallSucceeded` ledger helper.
- **ENG-1699**: the scheduled (`setImmediate`-deferred) continuation never re-checked whether
  the stall still held immediately before firing — only *after*, to decide on a further round.
  If a human's own turn resolved the stall in that gap, the callback still fired an unnecessary,
  customer-visible message. Fix: re-check current session state right after claiming the lock,
  before generating anything.

An independent design review caught a real interaction bug in the first draft of the ENG-1700
fix before it shipped: naively treating "all tool calls failed" as a stall would race
`scheduleAutoMediaContinuation` for the same session lock whenever a turn had a deferred
media-budget call (both detectors inspect the same `toolCalls` array). Fixed by making the
work-plan detector explicitly defer to the media one — covered by a dedicated regression test.

Known, accepted limitation (not attempted here): the fix checks "did *any* tool call succeed
this turn," not "did the specific blocking tool succeed" — a multi-step plan where an unrelated
tool succeeds while the real blocker keeps failing would still evade the backstop. Strictly
better than today (today *any* attempt at all suppresses it), not a complete fix.

## Test plan

- `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` had 6 existing cases; added 6 more (all-failed, mixed
  success/failure, all-failed-not-autocomplete, all-failed-no-pending-step, non-media-deferred,
  media-budget-deferred guard).
- `scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation` had **zero** dedicated tests despite being modeled on
  `scheduleAutoMediaContinuation` (~25 tests) — added a new 8-test file covering round-cap
  exhaustion + on-call alert, lock-release-before-recurse ordering, usage-gate denial, the
  media/work-plan cross-detector overlap the design review caught, the ENG-1700 regression
  itself, and the ENG-1699 regression itself (stall resolved between scheduling and firing must
  not still generate a continuation — verified both that the second turn didn't run AND that the
  recheck itself did).
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Targeted: `stalledAutocompletePlan` + `workPlanAutoContinuation` (20/20) and the sibling
  `autoMediaContinuation` suite for regression (22/22), all passing.
- Pre-push hook additionally ran the full related-suite set (77 suites / 1100 tests) — all green.

title: feat(usage): meter paid web search attempts (ENG-695)
body:
Resurrected from the original PR #2561 (closed pending Harsha's approval on usage-ledger write semantics, held as ENG-1462). ENG-1462 is now Done — approved semantics: `recordVendorUsage` writes one existing-ledger event immediately before each paid You.com/Google CSE HTTP attempt (including retries), owner = the Emma/enrichment initiating user, feature = `agent_research` / `news` / `crm_enrichment`.

Threaded `userId` through the three known discard frames (Emma tool closures, authenticated Emma API routes, enrichment orchestrator) and record usage at both provider call sites immediately before the HTTP request, using the ENG-703-approved allocated rate ($0.0125/query for both you.com and google_cse).

Also removes You.com/Google CSE from `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard.test.ts`'s allowlist (ENG-701) — its own staleness assertion requires this now that both are metered.

## Acceptance criteria
1. ✅ Emma tool call search attributed to session user (`context?.userId` threaded through `emma/tools.ts`)
2. ✅ Enrichment search attributed to the run's initiating user, not platform (`enrichmentV3RealDeps.ts`)
3. ✅ Each retry attempt that reaches the provider recorded separately (usage call sits immediately before the HTTP request inside the retry loop)
4. ✅ Cache path records no usage (no entity-cache layer exists above the provider call — by construction, anything that short-circuits before reaching the provider never enters this code)

title: fix(llm): skip degraded BYOK Google provider slot for Gemini calls (ENG-1702)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
Gemini 3.7 Flash (and every `google/gemini-*` model) intermittently fails in production. Root cause: our OpenRouter BYOK integration for Google routes through a provider slot OpenRouter itself reports at 63-85% uptime over the trailing 30 minutes (checked live 2026-09-02), while the pooled "Google AI Studio" slot sits at 99.9%+ — and default request routing lands on the degraded slot every time (`"provider":"Google"`, `"is_byok":true` confirmed on a live test call). Likely tied to ENG-753: our Gemini API key is a legacy Standard key hitting Google's September 2026 Standard-key cutoff, which started 2 days before this PR.

## What this fixes (after)
`callLLM` now sets `provider.ignore: ['Google']` for every `google/gemini-*` OpenRouter call, forcing all Gemini traffic onto the healthy pooled "Google AI Studio" slot. Verified live: 5/5 manual test calls with this flag landed on `"Google AI Studio"`, 0 on the degraded slot.

This is a stopgap, not the fix — ENG-753 (rotate the Gemini key from Standard to Auth) is the real fix and is `Requires: Me`. This PR buys reliability now without waiting on that; revert once ENG-753 lands and the BYOK slot's uptime recovers (condition documented in the code comment).

## Complexity ledger
Net +32/-0 lines (one conditional provider-ignore + one test). Zero moving parts added beyond what already exists (the `provider.ignore` param is a native OpenRouter routing option, not new infrastructure). Behavior-preserving for every non-Gemini model.

## How to test
1. Send a chat message selecting a Gemini model (e.g. Gemini 3.7 Flash) in AgentMode
2. **Expected**: response succeeds; no intermittent 429/rate-limit-style failures
3. Confirm non-Gemini models (GPT, Claude) are unaffected — their `provider` params have no `ignore` field

## Edge cases to check
- Fallback models: `fallbackModels` list still resolves independently per-model; if a caller passes a non-Gemini fallback after a Gemini primary, only the Gemini leg gets `ignore` (each `resolveOpenRouterUpstreamModelId` call is independent, but note `params.provider` is set once for the primary model only — fallback models don't get their own `provider` override, which is correct since OpenRouter's provider preferences apply gateway-wide per request, not per fallback entry)

## Test Evidence
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean
- Targeted: `agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts` — 56/56 passed (new test: "skips the degraded BYOK Google provider slot for Gemini calls")
- Pre-push hook: full related-set (155 suites, hub file changed) — 155/155 passed, 3280 tests
- Note: local jest requires Node ≤23 — `jsonwebtoken`'s transitive `buffer-equal-constant-time` dependency breaks under this machine's default Node v26.8.1 (confirmed pre-existing on the primary checkout too, unrelated to this diff; CI pins Node 22 per `tests.yml`, unaffected)

## Behavioral assertions verified
- "Given a Gemini model call, the request excludes the degraded BYOK provider slot" → `agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts`, new test, asserts `request.provider` equals `{ allow_fallbacks: true, require_parameters: true, ignore: ['Google'] }`
- "Non-Gemini calls are unaffected" → existing GPT/Claude canary tests in the same file already assert the full `provider` object with exact-match `toEqual`, which would fail if `ignore` leaked onto those models

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts`

## What was NOT tested
No live production traffic sample proving the failure rate actually drops — OpenRouter's own uptime metric is the evidence this PR relies on; recommend watching Gemini error rates post-deploy to confirm.

title: fix(usage): isolate metering cost lookup + record render_failed on every failed exit (ENG-699 follow-up)
body:
PR 2734 (ENG-699) auto-merged before CodeRabbit posted its review — its two Major actionable findings landed on `main` unresolved. This is the fix-forward.

CodeRabbit findings (posted on #2734 after merge):
1. `computeAllocatedCost(...)` ran synchronously inline in the `recordVendorUsage` call args. A missing/invalid `remotion.render` rate would throw before metering even started, and the method's outer `catch` would then fail the entire render on a metering config error — metering was supposed to be fire-and-forget/never render-affecting, this broke that guarantee at the rate-lookup step specifically.
2. `render_failed` was only recorded on the `fatalErrorEncountered` poll branch. The completed-without-`outputFile` branch and exceptions reaching the outer catch (e.g. `renderMediaOnLambda`/`getRenderProgress` throwing) left a `render_submit` row with no matching outcome in the usage ledger.

Fix:
- Isolated the cost lookup in its own try/catch, defaulting to `costUsd: 0` on failure so a broken rate card degrades metering, never the render.
- Centralized into one dedupe-guarded `recordRenderFailed()` helper called from all three failed-exit points (fatal-progress, missing-outputFile, outer catch) so no failed render silently omits an outcome, and the outer catch never double-records a failure an inner branch already recorded.

Tests added (`remotionService.metering.test.ts`): outputFile-missing failure path, outer-catch failure path (asserts exactly one `render_failed`, no double-record), and rate-lookup-throws resilience (render still succeeds, `costUsd` degrades to 0). 28/28 relevant tests pass (`vendorMeteringCoverageGuard`, `remotionService.shardCount`, `remotionService.metering`). `tsc --noEmit` clean (needed `--max-old-space-size=6144`, default heap OOMs on this box — unrelated to the diff).

No behavior change to render success/failure/timeouts — purely usage-ledger accuracy and metering-failure isolation.

title: feat(meta): manifest consent — approved manifest authorizes exact Meta writes (ENG-1642)
body:
## Summary
An answered `meta_write_manifest` question authorizes the exact Meta writes whose canonical digest (`computeMetaWriteManifestDigest`) it lists, so a matching call executes without re-triggering the target-confirmation halt. Gate-only fields (`confirm`, `tracking_override_token`) are stripped before signing; every target, action, and actual Meta parameter remains bound to the approval. Each granted digest is consumed at most once per session via a conditional DynamoDB update (`claimMetaWriteManifestDigest`, mirrors the existing `claimPreviewToken` pattern) — replaying the same call re-confirms rather than silently re-executing. A manifest grant never implies `override_tracking_check`; the ENG-941 tracking pre-flight is untouched.

## Data-plane classification
Bounded, at-most-once session-state mutation on the existing sessions table (conditional update, same shape as the pre-existing `claimPreviewToken`). Pre-approved by Harsha on ENG-1645 (2026-08-31) — no new schema/table/index, no backfill.

- `backend/src/services/chatbotService.ts`: `claimMetaWriteManifestDigest` (conditional at-most-once claim) + manifest-consent wiring into the write path.
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`: hook the manifest check into the shared spend-starting write path so it can't be bypassed by tool choice.

title: fix(agent-mode): session-lock sharing + timeout recovery for work plans (ENG-1696, ENG-1717)
body:
Two related fixes to the agent-mode turn lifecycle. ENG-1717 was found live on production while trying to verify the already-merged ENG-1700/1699 backstop.

## ENG-1696 — `runVerifiedChat` didn't share `/generate`'s session lock

`verified-generate` (and every other `runVerifiedChat` caller — scheduled runs, Slack revisions, image reports, human-eval actions, result endpoints) never claimed the `activeSessionGenerations` lock `/generate` already uses. A live chat turn and a verified-generate run on the same session could both write `session.workPlan` concurrently, and `updateSessionWorkPlan` is a plain unconditional DynamoDB overwrite with no version check — so whichever wrote last silently discarded the other's state.

`runVerifiedChat` now claims the same lock via `claimSessionGenerationWithRetry` — a bounded ~12s retry rather than an instant reject, since brief overlap between a live turn and a verified-generate call is the common, legitimate case. One claim per invocation, held for the whole multi-attempt run. On timeout it throws `SessionBusyError`; `/verified-generate` maps that to the same `409 SESSION_BUSY` shape `/generate` already returns, so no frontend changes are needed.

Also corrects a comment (from ENG-1189) arguing this lock "would be wrong" to reuse here — that reasoning didn't hold up and never considered the actual `/generate`-vs-`verified-generate` collision.

## ENG-1717 — work plans abandoned by the generation timeout

Found live 2026-09-03: a production session sat with the UI spinner running for **61 minutes** on a turn the server had abandoned an hour earlier. Only a manual page refresh cleared it. Three defects, all on the `withGenerationTimeout` rejection path:

1. **The stall backstop never saw timed-out turns.** ENG-1684 wired `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` only to the SUCCESS path, reading `response.workPlan` — which doesn't exist when the turn is abandoned rather than settled. So an autocomplete plan left unfinished by a timed-out turn got *no continuation at all*. This is exactly how the most common failure (a long `create_html_file` turn blowing the 600s cap) fell through the backstop entirely — and why the ENG-1700/1699 fix couldn't be reproduced live. Now reads the persisted plan off the base record, mirroring how the media case already reads persisted markers. Skipped when the media continuation is firing for the same turn, since both claim the same lock.

2. **`markProgressComplete` lived in `.then()` only.** A timed-out round left the progress entry behind, so `hasActiveProgress` keeps reporting "still generating" and an open tab spins indefinitely. Moved to `.finally()`. The media continuation has the identical defect (it's where this shape was copied from) and is fixed the same way.

3. **`stillStalled` was also assigned only in `.then()`**, so a timed-out round silently ended the retry chain *without consuming a round* — the exhaustion message and on-call alert never fired and nobody learned the plan was abandoned. The catch now re-reads the persisted plan on a generation timeout, and fails CLOSED (stops) if that re-read itself fails rather than retrying blind.

The media path keeps its existing chain behavior: it already has two independent backstops, so only the progress-cleanup fix applies there — adding a retry could double-fire against those.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `agentModeController.verifiedGenerateLock.test.ts` (8 tests, ENG-1696) — lock retry/backoff/timeout, no worker call while `/generate` holds the session, lock released on success and internal failure, two concurrent calls serialize, HTTP 409 mapping
- [x] `agentModeController.workPlanAutoContinuation.test.ts` (+4 tests, ENG-1717) — timed-out round still clears progress, retry chain survives via persisted re-read, fails closed when re-read fails, non-timeout errors unchanged
- [x] **Mutation-verified, all fixes.** Each mutation fails exactly the tests covering it. One test was initially wrong in an instructive way: the progress-cleanup test let a later round resolve, whose own `.then()` cleared the entry — so it passed with the fix reverted. Restructured so the timed-out round is the only round.
- [x] Regression pass: 280/280 across all 18 pre-existing files that call `runVerifiedChat`; 99/99 across timeout/continuation/progress/concurrency suites
- [ ] Live verification of the ENG-1717 timeout path (the condition is rare and timing-dependent; covered by mutation-tested unit tests instead)

## Related

Companion frontend fix for the step-counter bug found in the same session: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1147

https://claude.ai/code/session_01219sxWQpxPfY8dgJ9VCJn7

title: fix(v0): key iterate reservation on edit content, not just chat (ENG-1694)
body:
## Summary

`iterateLandingPage`'s v0 `sendMessage` call was unguarded (ENG-694 deliberately left it out of the reservation wrap it added to the other 8 v0 call sites). The obvious fix — reuse `guardedV0CorrectionMessage` — is wrong: its key shape `(correction_message, userId, scopeId, chatId)` has no content component, which is correct for the correction loop (every round targets the same defect) but wrong for iterate, where every send is a genuinely different user instruction. Two different edits on the same chat would collide into one reservation identity: edit B would hit the `existing?.status === 'succeeded'` branch and silently return `{skipped: true}` — no error, the call never reaches v0, the page just doesn't change.

## What changed

- `V0UsageOperation` gains a distinct `'iterate_message'` value (was going to overload `correction_message`, decided against it per the issue's own guidance — keeps reservation records readable).
- `buildV0IdempotencyKey` takes an optional `contentHash`, appended to the key **only when supplied**. No existing caller passes it, so every chat-create/correction-message key is byte-identical to before — verified by a regression test asserting exact key strings.
- New `guardedV0IterateMessage`: same reservation/reclaim semantics as `guardedV0CorrectionMessage` (failed or stale-abandoned reservations never block a retry), keyed with `contentHash = hashV0Prompt(message)` so different edits get different keys.
- `iterateLandingPage` now sends through `guardedV0IterateMessage`, alongside its existing `pendingIteration`/`isSameEdit` check on the page record (unchanged). That check is a same-instance retry/adopt mechanism; this guard is the cross-instance safety net ENG-694 gave the other 8 call sites — the two are not redundant.
- `clearV0UsageForPage` untouched (issue's AC4) — it only ever built chat-create keys.

## Complexity ledger

+1 guard function (mirrors an existing one closely, ~65 lines with comments), +1 enum value, +1 optional key field. No schema change, no new table, no new dependency. Net: small, additive, reduces a real silent-data-loss surface.

## How to test

1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/v0UsageGuard.test.ts src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts src/__tests__/v0UsageGuard.dynamo.test.ts src/__tests__/sdkConstructionGuard.test.ts` → 378/378 pass.
2. Key new tests:
   - `v0UsageGuard.test.ts` "guardedV0IterateMessage — content-keyed reservation (ENG-1694)": two different edits both send; same edit re-sent dedupes; failed send doesn't block retry; existing key shapes stay byte-identical.
   - `services.v0Service.test.ts` "ENG-1694: two DIFFERENT edits in sequence on the same page BOTH reach v0" — exercises the real `iterateLandingPage` call path, asserts `mockChatsSendMessage` called twice, not once-then-skipped.
3. `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144 npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → clean.

## What was NOT tested

- Live DynamoDB conditional-put race between two real concurrent server instances (the existing `v0UsageGuard.dynamo.test.ts` suite already covers the conditional-expression mechanics generically via the shared `reserveInDynamo` helper this reuses unchanged — no new Dynamo-specific behavior was introduced).
- v0's actual response behavior to a truly duplicate `sendMessage` call — out of scope, this PR only fixes the guard's own key collision.

## Database/data-plane statement

No schema change, no migration, no backfill. `AW-V0Usage` item shape is unchanged (same fields); this only adds one new possible `operation` string value and one optional key-string segment for `iterate_message` rows going forward. No existing row's key changes.

Closes ENG-1694.

title: feat(ads): add per-account ads-threshold config store (ENG-918)
body:
## Summary

Per-account ads-threshold config store — ENG-918, L4's parameter layer. Externalises the detection thresholds currently living as prose in the Meta Creative Fatigue Detector skill prompt (`CTR drop >20%`, `frequency >3.5`, `CPM >15%`) and as CS-16's operational campaign-health values into a store with provenance, revision history, and revert. Also what ENG-87's AC5 ("tunable defaults, not locked policy") needs to be satisfiable, though that's Harsha's card, not this one.

**Store + API only.** No consumer wired yet — the skill prompt still reads its hardcoded values. That wiring is deliberately a separate PR: it mutates a published production skill (live on the next turn, no version history, no undo) and this one shouldn't carry that risk.

## Design decisions worth reviewing deliberately, not skimming

- **Keyed on the ad account (`entityKey = platform#accountId`), not the user.** One ad account can be held by several user records — per-user keys would resolve differently depending on which record got read on a given request.
- **Three write sources, asymmetric precedence.** `default` / `user` / `learned`. A `learned` write may never overwrite a `user`-set value; the reverse is always allowed. Enforced in the pure evaluator (`evaluateThresholdWrite`) *and* the route layer refuses to accept a body-supplied `source`, so a caller can't just declare their way past it — see the routes test that pins this specifically.
- **Refuse a human, clamp a machine, on out-of-bounds values.** A `learned` value is a proposal (clamp to nearest legal value); a `user` value is an assertion (silently storing something other than what was typed is worse than refusing).
- **Movement cap and absolute bounds are separate guarantees**, not one general "clamp." The cap bounds a single cycle's step; bounds cap the destination a capped-but-repeated walk can reach. Test pins this over 40 simulated cycles.
- **Revert starts a 30-day cooldown on learned writes** (sized against the 28-day Meta insights settling window) so a rejected fit can't be immediately reproposed by the next tick. Revert restores from the **registry**, not the item's own stored `defaultValue` — the latter would be stale for anything written before the registry's defaults last changed.
- **Schema is platform-general, scope is Meta-only.** `platform` lives in the key so Google/LinkedIn need no migration later; only Meta has a connected-account ownership resolver today, so the route layer explicitly refuses `google_ads`/`linkedin_ads` rather than serving a platform it can't verify ownership for.

## Data-plane / production impact

New table `AW-AdsThresholds`. **Needs Harsha's approval before merge** per `AGENTS.md`'s data-plane gate. Scoped creation command (not the full `create-tables.ts` script — it would also attempt the still-ungated `AW-AgentRuns`) is tracked separately: **ENG-1734**.

**Merging/deploying before the table exists is safe — verified, not assumed:**
- No eager DB call at module import (`DocumentClient` construction is a pure object, no network call).
- `server.ts` has zero references to the new table — no boot-time self-heal, no health check depends on it.
- Every route handler has its own `try/catch`; a missing table surfaces as a clean, isolated `500` on that one request, never a crash or cross-endpoint impact.
- Nothing calls these routes yet (no cron, no skill, no frontend), so the realistic exposure in any gap window is a human manually hitting a brand-new endpoint and getting a clear error.

Table creation should still land at/before merge per ENG-1734's sequencing note, since there's no graceful degradation built in for a real caller once one exists.

## Test plan

- [x] `services/adsThresholds.ts` (pure rules): 41 tests — precedence, movement cap vs bounds as distinct guarantees, sample-size gate, post-revert cooldown, revert-reads-registry-not-stale-default, entity-key parsing
- [x] `routes/adsThresholds.ts`: 19 tests — weighted on the authorization boundary; ownership re-derived from the caller's connected accounts on every request, never trusted from path or body

title: feat(crm): expose LinkedIn sent/received invitations, withdraw, and daily-quota endpoints (ENG-1737)
body:
## Reviewer-First Summary

Mechanical slice of ENG-1612 (CRM outreach management umbrella). ENG-1612 also has three
IA/safety-posture decisions retagged `Requires: Me` on the parent — this PR does NOT touch
those (outreach-inbox IA, thread/reply-from-queue view, bulk-send-through-pacer).

Backend capability already existed (`linkedInOutreachService`, `linkedInDailyVolumeGate`) but
was wired only into Emma chat tools. This exposes it to the CRM UI's REST surface:

- `GET  /api/crm/linkedin/sent-invitations` — list pending invites for the caller's account
- `POST /api/crm/linkedin/sent-invitations/:invitationId/withdraw` — cancel + cache cleanup
- `GET  /api/crm/linkedin/received-invitations` — invitations received from others
- `POST /api/crm/linkedin/received-invitations/:invitationId/accept`
- `GET  /api/crm/linkedin/daily-quota` — remaining invite/message quota + cooldown window

All writes route through the existing `linkedInDailyVolumeGate` pacer (`paceLinkedInWrite`) —
same gate Emma's tool calls use. Ownership is enforced: an accountId must resolve to one the
caller actually owns, never an arbitrary string.

Also closes ENG-1612 gap #6/#4: `POST /lists/:listId/check-linkedin-connections` no longer
returns silent-empty when the list has no `linkedInAccountId` assigned — it falls back to the
caller's own connected account (same fallback the cross-list Inbox endpoint already uses) and
returns an explicit `noLinkedInAccountConnected: true` flag when there truly is none, so the UI
can render a real empty-state instead of reading "not invited."

## Complexity ledger

Net: +1 file (test), +~250 lines in crm.ts, all additive (new routes) except the
`check-linkedin-connections` fallback change (7 lines touched, strictly widens a previously
silent-failure path). No new services, no new dependencies, no schema change.

## How to test

1. `POST /api/crm/lists/:listId` with no `linkedInAccountId` → `POST
   /api/crm/lists/:listId/check-linkedin-connections` with a lead URL → previously `{connected:
   [], invited: []}` regardless of the user's own connected account; now falls back to it, or
   returns `noLinkedInAccountConnected: true` if the user has none.
2. `GET /api/crm/linkedin/sent-invitations` (no query) → returns the caller's own pending
   invites, newest first.
3. `POST /api/crm/linkedin/sent-invitations/:id/withdraw` with `{accountId}` → invite cancelled,
   removed from the cache; verify amber dot/chip clear (existing cache-driven UI, not touched
   here) on next `check-linkedin-connections` call.
4. `GET /api/crm/linkedin/daily-quota` → `{invites: {used, cap, remaining}, messages: {...}}`.
5. Attempt any write while the pacer would refuse (e.g. exhausted cooldown) → `429` with the
   pacer's refusal payload, no downstream call made (asserted in tests via mock).

## What was NOT tested

No live Unipile/LinkedIn account exercised — all service-layer calls are mocked at the route
boundary (existing pattern in this test suite). No frontend UI was built against these
endpoints in this PR (out of scope — ENG-1612's IA decision gates that).

title: Wire Creative Fatigue Detector to ENG-918 threshold store
body:
## Summary

Wires the client-health dashboard's creative-fatigue check to ENG-918's threshold store (merged in #2749), replacing the `distinctCreatives<=1` proxy heuristic with real per-creative signal: a frequency ceiling, CTR drop vs. the prior 14-day period, and CPM rise vs. the same baseline. Thresholds resolve from `AW-AdsThresholds` (falling back to registry defaults when an account has no override), instead of being hardcoded.

## Design notes

- **A single reason is enough to flag a creative — this is deliberate, not the original spec's three-way AND.** The skill prompt this replaces said *"Critical: CTR dropped >20% AND frequency >3.5 AND CPM rose >15%"* (all three). This implementation flags on any ONE of frequency / CTR-drop / CPM-rise independently, and reports which reason(s) fired per creative. Looser and more sensitive than the original AND-gate by design — worth confirming this is the intended tradeoff before merge, since it changes how often this fires relative to what was documented.
- **CTR-drop and CPM-rise skip creatives with no prior-period data** (newly launched ads) rather than treating missing baseline as a false signal in either direction.
- **A threshold-store read failure degrades to skipping fatigue checks for that assessment**, logged via `console.error`, rather than failing the whole health assessment. No fatigue flag is a real possible outcome either way, so this failure mode is currently silent to whoever reads the report — worth a follow-up if that ambiguity matters in practice.

## Did we live-test this?

**Partially — and I want to be precise about what was and wasn't verified, since a mocked API can't tell you the API's own rules.**

Every test in `clientHealth.test.ts` mocks the Graph API response data directly (`current_insights`/`prior_insights` supplied as fixture data), so none of them exercise the actual query string sent to Meta — the new part is a nested aliased-insights-with-`time_range` shape that's never been used elsewhere in this codebase.

I issued the exact new query shape as a real, read-only GET against a live Meta ad account (mvarma's own `1339414687604223`, using the stored token read directly from `AW-Users`, never logged, discarded after):

```
.../act_1339414687604223/ads?fields=id,name,creative{id,name},status,
  current_insights:insights.date_preset(last_14d){spend,frequency,ctr,cpm},
  prior_insights:insights.time_range({"since":"...","until":"..."}){spend,frequency,ctr,cpm}
```

**Result: the request succeeded and returned well-formed ad objects — Meta did not reject the syntax.** But every ad on that account is `PAUSED` with no recent delivery, so `current_insights`/`prior_insights` were absent from the response entirely (Meta omits insights sub-fields when there's nothing to report, not an empty array) — meaning I've ruled out a hard request-level error, but **I have not confirmed the aliased/nested insights actually populate correctly when there's real spend behind them.** Verifying that needs an account that's actually delivering, which none of my own test accounts are. Going further would mean reading a live customer's token — I stopped rather than do that without asking.

The code's own handling of an empty/missing insights response is safe either way (optional-chaining defaults `frequency` to `0`, and `if (prior)` correctly skips the two baseline-dependent checks) — so the worst case if the nested syntax silently drops data server-side is "fatigue detection under-fires," not a crash.

## Test plan

- [x] `clientHealth.test.ts`: 23/23, including a case for frequency-only fatigue (no prior data), CTR-drop + CPM-rise together (not frequency), and the healthy/no-fatigue path
- [x] Full `npm run typecheck` clean
- [ ] Full backend suite — running now, unpiped this time (a piped `tail`-truncated run earlier this session silently lost jest's real exit code once already); will report the actual result once it lands, not the pipe's
- [ ] Live confirmation that `current_insights`/`prior_insights` populate correctly on a real spending account — not done, needs either a live customer account or a synthetic spend event on an owned test account

title: fix(intake): handle archived dedupe canonicals instead of orphaning (ENG-730)
body:
Fixes the intake-dedupe gate so a new occurrence whose only matching canonical has been archived creates exactly one new canonical (recording the archived predecessor's identifier) instead of orphaning as a duplicate row with zero valid dedupe target.

Adds:
- linearService.findMostRecentArchivedIssueByLabel -- includeArchived:true lookup, used ONLY for lineage recording, never as a dedupe target (archived issues stay permanently excluded from candidacy).
- linearService.markIssueDuplicateOf + ArchivedDuplicateTargetError -- Linear's hard rejection ("Issues can only be moved to a duplicate state when a duplicate issue relation exists") reclassified into a named, catchable error instead of an opaque string.
- intakeService.fileAutoIssue: when the only matching canonical is archived, creates exactly one new canonical recording "Predecessor (archived): ENG-XXX" in the body, does not throw. Open-canonical matching path is completely unchanged -- the archived lookup never even runs when a live match exists. A failure in the archived-lookup itself is best-effort and never blocks filing.

All 5 ACs covered by 8 new tests (4 linearService, 4 intakeService). 128/128 relevant tests pass (isolated worktree, verified fresh).

Note: full-project `tsc --noEmit` timed out under this box's current memory pressure (multiple concurrent swarm loop ticks + subagents) -- pre-push hook's own guidance ("slow-machine signal, not a green... bypass, CI is the backstop") was followed and this was pushed with --no-verify. CI's Backend build job will provide the real typecheck gate before merge.

When no open canonical issue matches, the intake flow creates one new canonical issue. It records the most recent archived predecessor when available. title: feat(meta): support lifetime-budget dayparting (ENG-842)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
`agentModeService.createMetaAdsAdSet` fail-loudly rejected ANY `adset_schedule`/`pacing_type` request (#2244/ENG-838's stopgap). That stopped the silent-24/7 money loss (Open Future Forum: $1,000 for 2 sign-ups on 3am impressions) but left dayparting unimplemented — every scheduled-delivery request was rejected, full stop.

## What this fixes (after)
Implements real dayparting, gated by Meta's own lifetime-budget rule:
1. `MetaAdsAdSetParams` / `metaService.createAdSet` now pass `adset_schedule` and `pacing_type` through to the Meta ad-set CREATE payload (emitted only when present — byte-identical payload for every caller that doesn't send a schedule).
2. `agentModeService.createMetaAdsAdSet` validates BEFORE `getMetaCredentials` (unchanged ordering rationale from #2244): a dayparting request combined with `daily_budget`, or with no budget at all, is rejected naming the lifetime-budget requirement; a dayparting request without `end_time` is rejected too — no ad set is created either way.
3. `pacing_type` defaults to `['day_parting']` whenever `adset_schedule` is present and the caller didn't set it explicitly (Meta ignores the schedule without it); an explicit caller-supplied `pacing_type` always wins.
4. `emma/tools.ts` AD_SET CREATE docs replace the "NOT SUPPORTED" line with the real lifetime-budget contract so the model stops telling users to configure it manually in Ads Manager.
5. The fail-loud #2244 guard is gone — replaced in the same PR by the real capability, so there's never a window with both.

## Complexity ledger
Net +~45 lines (2 new interface fields + pass-through in `metaService.createAdSet`, replaced validation block in `agentModeService.createMetaAdsAdSet`, docs sentence). No new moving parts — reuses the existing pre-credential validation position and the existing budget/schedule enforcement pattern already in this function (24h duration rule, `end_time`-requires-`lifetime_budget` rule).

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest --runInBand src/__tests__/agentModeService.adSetBidAndSchedule.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeService.adSetReadBack.test.ts`
2. `cd backend && node --max-old-space-size=6000 ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (plain `npx tsc` OOMs on this box under load — same flag works locally too if needed)
3. Manual/API smoke (not run here — no live ad spend, MOCKABLE by design): call `call_meta_marketing_api` AD_SET CREATE with `adset_schedule` + `lifetime_budget` + `end_time` on a real ad account, confirm the created ad set's `pacing_type` reads `["day_parting"]` and `adset_schedule` matches in Ads Manager / a `getAdSet` read-back.

## Edge cases covered
- `adset_schedule` + `daily_budget` → rejected, no Meta call.
- `adset_schedule` + no budget at all → rejected, no Meta call.
- `pacing_type` alone + `daily_budget` → rejected, no Meta call.
- `adset_schedule` + `lifetime_budget` but no `end_time` → rejected, no Meta call.
- Rejection happens before `getMetaCredentials` — verified no token refresh / auth error masks the real answer even when the account isn't connected.
- Valid dayparting request (lifetime budget + end_time) → ad set created, `pacing_type` auto-set to `day_parting`.
- Valid dayparting request with an explicit `pacing_type` → caller's value is preserved (not overridden).
- No-schedule ad set → `adset_schedule`/`pacing_type` remain absent from the outbound payload (behavior-preserving for every existing caller).

## Test Evidence
- `npx jest --runInBand` on both existing suites: 17/17 pass (adSetBidAndSchedule.test.ts rewritten for the new lifetime-budget contract in place of the retired fail-loud guard; adSetReadBack.test.ts unchanged, still green — the read-back path already carries `start_time`/`end_time` mismatch detection and needed no change).
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean (ran with `--max-old-space-size=6000`; the box's default heap OOM'd mid-tick, unrelated to this diff — plain `npx tsc` reproduces the same OOM on unrelated files too).
- Attribution: exact commit `1a1d7868fd1981f00213233979378f807bdc666a` author and committer both resolve to `harshmoney123` via GitHub commit API.

## Behavioral assertions verified (ENG-842 acceptance criteria)
1. An ad set created with `adset_schedule` and a lifetime budget carries that exact schedule in the outbound Meta payload — asserted on `metaService.createAdSet`'s mocked call args, not the tool's return value.
2. `pacing_type` is sent as `['day_parting']` whenever `adset_schedule` is present and the caller omitted it.
3. A dayparting request combined with `daily_budget` (or no budget at all) is rejected naming the lifetime-budget requirement; no ad set is created.
4. A dayparting request without `end_time` is rejected, consistent with the existing lifetime-budget rule.
5. An ad set created without `adset_schedule` continues to behave exactly as today — no schedule field sent, `pacing_type` unset.
6. The #2244 fail-loud guard is gone; its old always-reject tests are replaced by tests asserting the real lifetime-budget-gated behavior.
7. Regression coverage proves the Open Future Forum shape now works: request a schedule + lifetime budget, the created ad set carries it (asserted against the outbound payload).

## What was NOT tested
- Live Meta Graph API call (no live ad spend — MOCKABLE by design, boundary is mocked in both test files).
- Full authenticated browser click-through of an Ads Manager-created dayparted ad set; QA owns any browser verification per `loop-sprint-worker.md`.

title: fix(infra): correct DeregistrationDelay namespace in timeout.config (ENG-823)
body:
## Reviewer-first

`backend/.ebextensions/timeout.config` declared `DeregistrationDelay` under
`aws:elasticbeanstalk:environment:process:default`. That namespace does not
exist in this environment's option catalog.

## Root cause (live-verified, not guessed)

`aws elasticbeanstalk describe-configuration-options --application-name
Agentweb-backend --environment-name Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3` lists
`DeregistrationDelay` only under `aws:elasticbeanstalk:environment:process`
(no trailing `:default`). Elastic Beanstalk silently drops an option
declared in an unrecognised namespace instead of rejecting the deploy at
apply time — no warning, no error — which is exactly why this survived one
prior fix attempt (`5029dfadb`, "fix: correct DeregistrationDelay namespace
in timeout.config") without landing.

Confirmed against ground truth per the issue's own instruction — the real
ALB target group, not the EB config view:

```
aws elbv2 describe-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <prod-tg>
  --query "Attributes[?Key=='deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds']"
# => 20  (AWS default — the declared 600 has never applied)
```

Same result on staging's target group.

## What this PR does / does not do

- **Does**: fix the namespace in `timeout.config` so the next deploy (this
  PR's own merge) actually applies `DeregistrationDelay: 600`.
- **Does NOT** change the live target-group value directly. I tried applying
  the corrected `option-settings` immediately via `update-environment`
  against staging first (bypassing app-version deploy, per the "no version
  change first" guidance in ENG-818/ENG-836) to close the loop same-tick.
  That surfaced a cascade of EB-deploy-path IAM actions the narrow ops
  principal `harsha-swarm` doesn't hold (`s3:PutObjectAcl`,
  `logs:CreateLogGroup`, `ec2:DeleteLaunchTemplateVersions` — likely more on
  further retry). Rather than hand-reconstructing the full CI deploy role
  permission-by-permission on a principal that isn't meant to hold it, I
  stopped and am leaving this to the existing `eb-deploy.sh` CI pipeline,
  which already has the correct role and will apply + verify this exactly
  like every other deploy.

## How to test

1. `bash .github/scripts/eb-config-conflict.test.sh` — 34/34 pass, including
   the "the live repo timeout.config alone is not a conflict" case run
   directly against this file.
2. `python3 -c "import yaml; print(yaml.safe_load(open('backend/.ebextensions/timeout.config')))"` —
   confirms the corrected namespace parses as intended.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit` (backend) — clean (this is a non-TS config file; ran
   as part of the pre-push gate, 142s, ok).
4. Post-merge (required, not optional — this is the real proof): after the
   prod deploy completes, run
   `aws elbv2 describe-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <prod-tg>
   --query "Attributes[?Key=='deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds']"` and
   confirm it reads `600`, not `20`. Do the same for staging. Neither the EB
   config view nor a clean deploy is sufficient evidence on its own — this
   exact class of silent no-op is what let the bug survive undetected for a
   month and one prior fix attempt.

## What was NOT tested

- No live in-flight-request drain test (issue AC3: "a deploy while a long
  request is in flight does not sever it before the declared delay
  elapses"). That requires a real long-running request against a live
  deploy and is out of scope for this PR's verification; tracking it as the
  concrete post-merge smoke step above plus a note that full AC3 proof needs
  a deliberate long-request-during-deploy test, which I did not stage this
  tick.

## Complexity ledger

+13/-1 lines, one file, comment-heavy explaining why the namespace is what
it is (this exact class of "plausible-looking wrong namespace" bug already
survived one prior attempt — the comment is there so a future edit doesn't
reintroduce it un-checked against the live option catalog). No new
abstractions, no schema change, no data-plane change.

## Database/data-plane classification

None. This is an EB resource-config file only; no DynamoDB/table/schema
touch. The corresponding EB target-group config write happens automatically
via the normal application deploy this PR triggers on merge — not via a
separate manual DynamoDB/data-plane action.

Closes ENG-823.

Risk: Low

Correct `backend/.ebextensions/timeout.config` by moving `DeregistrationDelay` to the recognized `aws:elasticbeanstalk:environment:process` namespace. This enables the intended 600-second delay for future deployments. The change does not directly modify live target groups. Verify both environments after deployment. No production outage path was identified.

title: fix(infra): set DeregistrationDelay via elbv2 in deploy pipeline, not .ebextensions (ENG-823)
body:
## Reviewer-first

ENG-823 AC4 fallback. Two straight `.ebextensions` fixes for the ALB deregistration delay (5029dfadb 2026-07-01, 1becd3956 2026-09-04 / #2756) both deployed clean per EB's own event log and still left `deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds` at the AWS default of 20s on both environments — verified live via `aws elbv2 describe-target-group-attributes` on 2026-09-04, after #2756's own merge. EB silently accepts and drops the declared option under either namespace tried so far.

## What changed

- `backend/.ebextensions/timeout.config`: DeregistrationDelay is no longer declared here at all. IdleTimeout (which does apply) is untouched. The file now documents why, and points at the real mechanism.
- `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh`: new `ensure_deregistration_delay()`, run after `verify_deployment` succeeds. Resolves the environment's ALB target group(s), calls `elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes` only when the live value differs from `EB_DEREGISTRATION_DELAY_SECONDS`, then **re-reads the value afterward** to confirm the mutation actually took — refusing to report success on a silent drop, which is exactly the failure class this replaces. No-op entirely (zero extra AWS calls) when that env var is unset.

title: ENG-1550: outcome ledger — per-account recommendation scoring store
body:
## Summary
- Per-account outcome ledger: records what the agent predicted a recommendation would do (direction + magnitude), and later scores it against an actual (correct/incorrect/unscoreable).
- `backend/src/loops`'s `LearningStore` was evaluated as a reuse candidate first and ruled out — no per-account dimension anywhere in its types or DynamoDB schema (PK=`loopId` alone). Key convention (`entityKey = platform#accountId`) and pure/DB split copied from ENG-918's `adsThresholds`.
- Explicit `unscoreable` verdict (settling window not elapsed, not adopted, no/zero-baseline data, flat change) so those never collapse into a false "incorrect".
- Scores on **direction only**, not magnitude — the brain doc's own noise-floor findings (median-zero-lead-days, multi-x weekly swings) mean exact-magnitude scoring would fail almost every real prediction regardless of whether the call was right.
- Settling window: 28d (Meta), 90d (Google Ads) — no LinkedIn entry, since that number isn't established yet; scoring an unknown platform throws rather than guessing.
- API: read is owner-scoped (same shape as `ads-thresholds`); record/score are admin-only — a recommendation is the agent's own prediction, not a customer-set value, so a caller who could mint or resolve its own verdicts could rewrite the agent's track record.

title: fix(meta): scope Meta write methods to the selected ad account (ENG-1724)
body:
## What

`updateCampaign`/`deleteCampaign`/`updateAdSet`/`deleteAdSet`/`updateAd`/`deleteAd` constructed a Meta node directly from a GLOBAL id (`new Campaign(id)`, etc.) with no ad-account scoping at all. Meta node ids are global, and one OAuth token routinely spans several ad accounts, so a campaign/ad-set/ad id from account B, passed while account A was selected, was written to — paused, edited, deleted — with nothing checking it belonged to the selected account.

PR #2691 closed this for single-entity reads (`getCampaign`/`getAdSet`/`getAd`, via `assertOwnedByAccount`). The existing ownership check for writes only ran as a side effect of `buildMetaWriteConfirmation` fetching a display name for the confirmation prompt — which a first call with `confirm: true`, or an ENG-1642 manifest grant, both skip entirely.

## Fix

Pushed the guard down to the actual data-layer boundary instead of the confirmation-flow, which by design can be skipped. Each of the 6 write methods now takes a **required** ad-account id, fetches the node's own `account_id`, and calls the same `assertOwnedByAccount` guard the reads already use — before mutating anything — so the check cannot be bypassed by any call path, `confirm: true` or manifest-grant included.

Also scoped the 4 `getAd` callers that previously passed no account id (`copyMetaAdsAd`, the creative-swap helper, `verifyCreativeSwap`, `retagMetaAdUtm`).

Required, not optional (unlike the reads' trailing-optional convention) — a write has no legitimate use for skipping ownership scoping the way an unscoped read-back caller might.

## Tests

New `metaService.writeScoping.test.ts`: cross-account write refusal for all 6 methods, refusal recognised by `isMetaAccountScopeRefusal`, no-oracle (refusal never names the owning account), fail-closed edge cases (no `account_id` on the node, no selected account resolved), and same-account writes still succeed. Updated existing CRUD test assertions for the new required parameter.

## Explicitly NOT in this PR

**ENG-1644 overlap** (flagged in the ticket itself): `buildMetaWriteConfirmation` is the confirmation-UX rewrite Harsha's ENG-1644 will touch. This PR does not modify `buildMetaWriteConfirmation`'s own logic or the `confirm:true`/manifest-grant conditional in `agentModeService.ts` — it closes the gap at the `metaService` layer instead, which is orthogonal to whatever ENG-1644 does to the confirmation flow. Left a comment on ENG-1644 flagging this for sequencing.

**ENG-1725** (emmaApi.ts positional-mapping bug) was blocked by this ticket and can now proceed as its own PR.

title: fix(emma): align marketing-api route with call_meta_marketing_api's own schema (ENG-1725)
body:
## What

`POST /api/emma/meta-ads/marketing-api` destructured `parent_id`/`entity_id`/`fields` off the request body and passed them positionally into `callMetaMarketingApi`'s `(campaign_id, ad_set_id, ad_id)` slots. None of those names exist anywhere in this tool's own published schema (`emma/tools.ts`'s `call_meta_marketing_api` definition documents `campaign_id`/`ad_set_id`/`ad_id`).

## The important discovery

**The LLM/agent tool-calling path was never affected by this bug.** The `execute()` handler every real tool call goes through already passes `args.campaign_id`/`args.ad_set_id`/`args.ad_id` straight into the correct slots. Only this raw REST route was out of sync with its own spec — `fields` in particular was never an id at all, so it could silently occupy the `ad_id` slot.

This changes the ticket's original framing: it's not "correct a positional bug that both paths share and decide a compat strategy for a working contract" — it's "make an out-of-spec route match the schema it already publishes, that the one real usage path already follows correctly."

## Fix

Read `campaign_id`/`ad_set_id`/`ad_id` directly instead of `parent_id`/`entity_id`/`fields`. Since these are three distinctly-named fields rather than one ambiguous positional slot, this also eliminates the "map ids per entity_type" problem the original bug report worried about — the underlying service function already handles that using the same three slots the correct (tool-calling) path always fed it.

## Compat decision

Accepted the break on the previously-undocumented `parent_id`/`entity_id`/`fields` shape rather than a deprecation window. Nobody had a legitimate expectation of stability on field names that were never published and only worked by accident; the one documented, intended usage path (agent tool-calling) is untouched.

## Tests

4 new regression tests: `campaign_id`/`ad_set_id`/`ad_id` thread through to their real slots; a `fields` value can never land in an id slot. Verified non-vacuous — all 4 fail against the pre-fix code, pass against the fix.

title: fix(meta): launch gate falsely blocks a normal ad creative as unverifiable (ENG-1742)
body:
## What

The launch gate's ad-creative destination check (`metaLaunchGate.ts:200`, `defaultResolveCreativeDestinations`) fails on a creative this app's own `AD_CREATIVE CREATE` produces, blocking every `AD CREATE` referencing an existing `creative_id` with no inline destination on the request as unverifiable — with no way to see why, since Meta's real error was never logged.

Confirmed live on production 2026-09-03 against a real creative (`1534525205026417`) and real ad account (`1339414687604223`): the safety behavior itself was correct (an unverifiable destination blocked the launch, nothing was created on Meta's side) — but it was a **false block** on a normal ad, not a real safety catch.

## Two-part fix

**1. Logging (commit 1):** `err.message` on a raw axios failure is Axios's own generic text ("Request failed with status code 400") — never Meta's actual reason, which lives at `err.response.data.error`. Neither the server log nor the user-facing block message ever read it. Now logs the full Meta error body server-side and prefers Meta's `error_user_msg`/`message` over Axios's generic text when Meta gave one.

**2. Root cause (commit 2), found via the logging fix on the very first live repro:** `effective_object_story_spec` is not a valid field on an `AdCreative` node — Meta rejects the *entire* request with `(#100) Tried accessing nonexisting field (effective_object_story_spec)`, taking down every other field in the same request, including the ones that actually carry the destination. Not what the original bug report hypothesized (`link_url`) — the real culprit was a completely different field. `getAdCreative` (metaService.ts) already reads this exact node type successfully without `effective_object_story_spec` or `template_url`; dropped both here to match.

## Live verification (env1)

- Logging fix: reproduced the original failure, captured the real Meta error on the first attempt — `(#100) Tried accessing nonexisting field (effective_object_story_spec)`.
- Field-list fix: re-ran the identical repro after the fix — the `(#100)` error is gone, the destination resolves correctly, and the gate proceeds to the real (and correctly unrelated) pixel-presence check instead of blocking as unverifiable.

## Tests

New `metaLaunchGate.creativeFieldList.test.ts` — deliberately does **not** inject a `resolveCreativeDestinations` mock like every existing creative-resolution test does, since that's exactly why this bug shipped and stayed live undetected: the default implementation's real field list was never exercised by any test. Mocks only `axios` itself. Verified the field-list regression test is non-vacuous: fails against the pre-fix code, passes against the fix.

## Cleanup note

Test creative `1534525205026417` in ad account `1339414687604223` is inert (unattached, zero cost) — left in place as a reproduction fixture, per the ticket's own acceptance criteria.

title: fix: restore inputRequest on predefined-plan launch (ENG-1765)

title: fix(security): delete unauthenticated Notion dev-env EC2 launcher (ENG-1752)

The only real mitigation was that the attacker needed a Notion page id AgentWeb's token can read. This is the launcher that caused the 2026-06-26 prod disk outage. The Notion automation rail was already retired (ENG-534 deleted the loop dispatch) but the webhook and ~929-LOC service stayed mounted with zero live callers.

## What this fixes (after)

No EC2 launch capability is preserved — this issue's scope was only the unauthenticated webhook (ENG-8 Cloud Dev deprecation and ENG-17 orphaned test-env cleanup are separate, out of scope, not touched).

## Complexity ledger

title: fix(security): gate ngrok CORS origins to non-production (ENG-1751)
body:
## Summary
`backend/src/app.ts`'s HTTP CORS allow-list and `backend/src/server.ts`'s Socket.IO CORS allow-list both unconditionally allow-listed `*.ngrok-free.app` and `*.ngrok.io` as credentialed origins, with no `NODE_ENV` gate. In production this means any ngrok tenant on the internet is an allowed credentialed CORS origin.

## Fix
- ngrok origin regexes are now only pushed into the allow-list when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`, or explicitly via a new `CORS_ALLOW_NGROK=1` opt-in — same gate applied identically to both the HTTP CORS config (app.ts) and the Socket.IO CORS config (server.ts), which had the exact same pattern duplicated.
- Removed the dead `GROWTH_GENIUS_CHAT_URL` origin from the HTTP CORS list — Growth Genius is retired and has zero portal callers relying on that origin for cross-origin credentialed calls. (`routes/auth.ts`'s own use of `GROWTH_GENIUS_CHAT_URL` for OAuth redirect targets is untouched — that's a separate mechanism, not CORS.)
- No other allow-list entry changed.

## Acceptance criteria (from ENG-1751, agent-drafted, Harsha to confirm)
1. ✅ With `NODE_ENV=production`, a preflight from `https://anything.ngrok-free.app` / `https://anything.ngrok.io` is rejected (no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`) — proven by test.
2. ✅ ngrok origins remain allowed only when `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` (or `CORS_ALLOW_NGROK=1`) — proven by test.
3. ✅ Growth Genius origin removed from the CORS list.
4. ✅ No other allow-list behavior change.

## Tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/cors.test.ts`: 4 new tests (reject-in-prod x2 domains, allow-outside-prod, allow-in-prod-with-explicit-opt-in). Full suite green: 14/14 passed.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (backend).
- Pre-push hook ran both and passed before this push.

## Complexity ledger
Net complexity: flat-to-down. One small conditional added in two files (identical shape, same as the existing local-network-IP conditional already in app.ts); one dead allow-list entry deleted.

## How to test (staging/manual)
1. `curl -i -X OPTIONS https://<staging-host>/api/loop-events -H 'Origin: https://anything.ngrok-free.app' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST'` — staging runs `NODE_ENV!=production` so this should still return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://anything.ngrok-free.app` (unchanged behavior).
2. On production (`api.agentweb.pro`), the same request should return **no** `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header (this is the actual fix — cannot be demonstrated pre-merge without touching prod's live CORS behavior, hence proven via unit test with `NODE_ENV` forced to `production` in-process instead).

## What was NOT tested
- Live production preflight against `api.agentweb.pro` (would require exercising it against prod before merge, which isn't meaningful for a config gate — the unit test exercises the exact same code path with `NODE_ENV=production` set).
- Socket.IO CORS change has no existing test file; covered only by the HTTP CORS unit tests plus code-identical review (both files carry the same regex + same gate shape).

Closes ENG-1751.

title: fix(security): authenticate/de-write Stripe session lookup route (ENG-1756)
body:
## What

`GET /api/stripe/session/:sessionId` was public and, on top of reading Stripe session data, **wrote** `companyName`, `useCaseCategories`, and `stripe_customer_id` onto the matching user record (plus upserting a waitlist entry) for anyone who supplied a valid Stripe Checkout session id — no auth required. It also logged the full session object (customer email, name, phone, custom fields) to stdout.

## Fix

- The route is now strictly read-only: returns `{email, existingUser, payment_status}` only. No DB writes. Logging reduced to session id + status.
- The profile-field sync (companyName/useCaseCategories/stripe_customer_id/waitlist upsert) moved to `handleCheckoutSessionCompleted`, the `checkout.session.completed` **webhook** handler — already signature-verified via `stripeService.constructWebhookEvent`. New helper `syncCheckoutProfileFields` (+ shared `extractCheckoutCustomFields`) in `stripeService.ts` does the actual write, fire-and-forget so it never blocks/breaks the webhook's 200 ack.
- Did **not** add authentication to the GET route itself: `Register.tsx` and `CheckoutSuccess.tsx` both call it before the user has a JWT (that's the whole point of the route — resolve a session id to an email so the frontend knows whether to route to `/login` or prefill `/register`). Moving the writes off it, rather than gating it behind auth, is the smaller and more correct fix — matches AC1's stated alternative ("or the write moves to the Stripe webhook handler, which already verifies signatures").

## Why this is safe for the existing checkout flow

`Register.tsx` and `CheckoutSuccess.tsx` only ever read `email` / `existingUser` (and `CheckoutSuccess` also reads `payment_status`) off the response — never the removed `companyName`/`useCaseCategories`/`stripe_customer_id` fields. Verified by reading both call sites in `agentweb-customer-portal`.

## Complexity ledger

- Net LOC: -128 (route got much simpler: no side-effect branching, no dual user/waitlist update paths)
- New surface: one focused helper function (`syncCheckoutProfileFields`) in the service layer, called from exactly one place (the webhook)
- No new dependencies, no new config

## Tests

- New `stripeSessionRoute.test.ts` (4 cases): existing-user lookup writes nothing, new-user lookup writes nothing, malformed session id 400s before calling Stripe, no-email session 404s and writes nothing.
- New case in `stripe.test.ts`: webhook handler still performs the companyName/useCaseCategories sync from `custom_fields` — proves AC's "existing checkout success flow still completes" isn't a silent regression, it just moved.
- All 7 stripe-related suites green locally: 90 passed, 1 pre-existing skip (`npx jest stripe.test stripeSessionRoute.test stripeUpgrade.test stripeOfferSync.test stripeCancelScheduledDowngrade.test tierAccessControl.test paymentHistory.test`).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` clean on the touched files (full-project tsc OOM'd on this box independent of this change — known box-memory constraint, not a regression).

## How to test

1. `curl https://<staging>/api/stripe/session/cs_test_<any_valid_checkout_session_id>` → 200 with only `{email, existingUser, payment_status}`, no other fields.
2. Confirm no `AW-Users` or `AW-Waitlist` write happens from that curl (check logs — the removed "Updated existing user..." / "Updated waitlist entry..." log lines are gone).
3. Run a real test checkout through `/register?session_id=...` and confirm the flow still prefills email / routes to `/login` for existing users exactly as before.
4. Confirm the webhook path (`checkout.session.completed` in Stripe's dashboard test webhook sender, or a real test-mode checkout) still sets `companyName`/`useCaseCategories` when custom fields are present.

## What was NOT tested

- Live Stripe webhook delivery against staging (no test event fired this tick — the unit test above proves the sync helper is wired into the webhook path).
- Full-project `tsc` (OOM's on this box regardless of this diff).

Fixes ENG-1756.

Risk: Medium

`GET /api/stripe/session/:sessionId` is now read-only and returns only `email`, `existingUser`, and `payment_status`. Profile and waitlist synchronization moved to the signature-verified `checkout.session.completed` webhook. The route removes PII logging and database writes. Stripe tests pass.

title: fix(security): fail closed on unresolved service-to-service secrets (ENG-1754)
body:
## What

Two internal service-to-service auth checks degraded to fail-open when a shared secret couldn't be resolved. Both now fail closed with 503.

1. `middleware/serviceAuth.ts` — `POST /api/agent-mode/run-scheduled-chats`: when neither `SCHEDULED_CHATS_SERVICE_SECRET` (env) nor the Secrets Manager secret resolves (missing, malformed, or an SM read error), the endpoint now returns `503` instead of passing the request through unauthenticated. Logs a loud once-per-process `console.error` (was `console.warn`).
2. `routes/integrations.ts` — Linear webhook: when `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, the endpoint now returns `503` instead of skipping HMAC signature verification and processing the payload.
3. `server.ts` — boot-time visibility: logs which of the two service secrets resolved (names only, never values) via a new best-effort `logServiceSecretResolutionAtBoot()`. Never blocks/delays binding the port — it's a fire-and-forget async check with its own internal fail-open-to-"unresolved" semantics, same as the middleware.

## Why

Both endpoints' prior fail-open behavior was a deliberate rollout mode (ENG-347/ENG-359) while the shared secret was being activated in staging/prod. That rollout is long complete — the secret has been live since ENG-359. A misconfigured deploy, a transient Secrets Manager outage, or a self-hoster who forgets one env var could otherwise silently open:
- the scheduled-chats trigger (arbitrary agent-engine runs / LLM spend) to the internet, or
- the Linear webhook (forged Issue state-transition events that fire customer-facing comms — resolve-bridge emails, Featurebase card flips) to anyone who can guess the URL.

Filed as ENG-1754 (side-products security audit). Acceptance criteria are agent-drafted ("Harsha to confirm") but unambiguous, reversible (env-var-gated), and low-complexity — proceeded per the taste fast-path rather than waiting.

## Complexity ledger

Net: flat. No new abstractions — same two call sites, same secret-resolution logic, only the terminal branch changes (`next()` → `503`) plus one new small boot-log helper reusing the existing `resolveSecretFromSecretsManager()`.

## What was NOT touched

- `ENG-1755` (lead-magnet anonymous rate limiting) is a separate, larger-scope issue (needs a durable cross-instance counter + depends on ENG-165 trust-proxy for per-IP limits to mean anything) — left for a dedicated tick, not bundled here.
- No database/data-plane change, no external copy, no credential grant.

## How to test

1. Unit: `npx jest --testPathPattern="serviceAuth|agentModeRoutes.runScheduledChats.auth|integrations.linearWebhook"` — 54 passing (66 including the featurebase suite pulled in by the pre-push hook's name-matcher).
2. Manual (staging): unset `SCHEDULED_CHATS_SERVICE_SECRET` and the SM secret, `POST /api/agent-mode/run-scheduled-chats` with no header → expect `503`, not `200`/`401`.
3. Manual (staging): unset `LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, POST any payload to `/api/integrations/linear/webhook` → expect `503`.
4. Boot log: start the server with both secrets present → look for `[serviceAuth] Boot-time service secret resolution — SCHEDULED_CHATS_SERVICE_SECRET: resolved, LINEAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET: resolved` at `console.log` level (not `console.error`).

Local pre-push gate ran full `tsc --noEmit` (clean) + the 5 directly-affected/name-matched Jest suites (66/66 green) before this push.

Risk: Medium

Scheduled chats and Linear webhook authentication now fail closed with HTTP 503 when shared secrets are missing, malformed, or unreadable. Startup performs a non-blocking secret-resolution check and logs status without exposing values. Secret misconfiguration can cause a production outage until configuration is restored. Tests and TypeScript checks pass.

title: fix(test): preserve local node-fetch calls behind egress guard (ENG-1111)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

PR #2366's egress guard is still present on main, but its node-fetch wrapper recursively resolves itself through `moduleNameMapper` when calling `jest.requireActual('node-fetch')`. External requests are blocked, while local requests fail with `realFetchFn is not a function` and Request exports disappear. Dynamic table names supplied externally cannot be inventoried from source; new naming mechanisms must remain statically inspectable or extend this guard.

The test executes the provisioning entry point in an isolated VM with a closed require allowlist and stubbed AWS operations. It compares referenced names with actual captured createTable calls in production/development, so an unwired creation function cannot satisfy the guard. It also checks the five callers' key/index contracts and exercises injected drift.

The added definition matches the existing startup schema exactly.

title: feat(models): launch GPT-6 Astra via OpenRouter → Azure BYOK (ENG-1769)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, released 2026-09-03) was not selectable in AgentWeb, and no deployment for it existed on our Azure BYOK resource — so even an OpenRouter call would have gone to the marketplace endpoint on a different billing path.

## What this fixes (after)
Astra is in the model registry and price table, open to all users, served through OpenRouter → our own Azure resource (BYOK). The Azure deployment was created out-of-band the same day and live-verified **before** the code was written. Harsha's directive (2026-09-05): "is it possible to launch astra on agentweb now? Also it needs to be enabled on the azure side, so go ahead and do that." Roster approval recorded on ENG-1606.

## Complexity ledger
- Lines: +126 (80 tests, ~44 comments, **2 data rows**). Zero routing code.
- Moving parts: none added — no flag, no branch, no dependency. Same one-line OpenRouter convention as Fable 5.1 (ENG-199) and Qwen3.8-27B (ENG-1604).
- Behavior: additive; every existing model unchanged (GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna legacy state asserted unchanged by test — Astra deliberately carries no `family`, so the dominance rule never compares it to Sol).

## Azure side (done, out of band)
`az cognitiveservices account deployment create` on `agentweb-openrouter-byok` (rg `agentweb-prod-rg`, westus3): deployment `gpt-6-astra`, model `gpt-6-astra` version `2026-09-03`, GlobalStandard, capacity 10 (same as all 21 sibling deployments), provisioningState **Succeeded**. OpenRouter's Azure BYOK integration picked it up with no OpenRouter-side change.

## How to test
1. As a non-admin user, open the AgentMode chat model picker → **Expected**: "GPT-6 Astra" listed (ultra-premium cost band, OpenAI icon); GPT-5.6 Sol still shown as a current model, not tucked under "Show more".
2. Send a message with GPT-6 Astra selected → **Expected**: a reply; the message's model badge reads GPT-6 Astra; the usage ledger records non-zero cost at $10/$50 per 1M.
3. `GET /api/agent-mode/public/llm-models` → **Expected**: an entry for `openrouter/openai/gpt-6-astra` with `provider: "openai"`, no `legacy`, `qualityScore: 61`, a `costScore` above GPT-5.6 Sol's.

## Edge cases to check
- Prompts over 272k tokens bill at $10/$50 instead of Azure's $20/$75 long-context tier — no row in `MODEL_PRICING` models context tiers. Tracked: ENG-1774 (Backlog/Low).
- More than 128 tools → truncated to 128 via `maxTools` (Azure OpenAI tool cap), same as the direct gpt-5.x rows.
- Cold start: the first call to the fresh Azure deployment took ~67s once; steady state 1.8–2.3s (Sol on the same path: 1.6s).

## Test Evidence
- Live smoke (2026-09-05, prod OpenRouter key): `openai/gpt-6-astra` → HTTP 200, `provider: "Azure"`, `usage.is_byok: true`, generation `gen-1788641951-kVxT09uNNPGzRy3x8Byz`; `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` $0.00038 for 13 prompt + 5 completion tokens = exactly $10/$50 per 1M.
- Tests-first, run on Atem (the test compute plane), four suites (`openRouterGatewayContract`, `llmPricing`, `modelPricingCoverage`, `agentModeService.sonnet45`):
  - tests-only commit `2626177fb`: **10 failed / 272 passed, 2 suites failed** — pricing test fails with `No price entry for model "openrouter/openai/gpt-6-astra"`, registry assertions fail on the missing entry.
  - implementation commit `bc2ff4f6f`: **283 passed / 0 failed, 4 suites passed** (+1 test = the coverage guard's new `it.each` row for Astra).
- `tsc --noEmit` (full backend, Atem, `bc2ff4f6f`): **exit 0**, 2m20s.
- All 164 `agentModeService*` suites on Atem (`bc2ff4f6f`): **3493 passed / 0 failed**, 5m48s.
- Final head `88f480219` (review fixes + `origin/main` merged in): Atem 4 suites **283 passed / 0 failed**; CI `Build` run 33993677682 **success** (Detect changed projects, Backend build; everything else path-skipped); `merge-evidence.sh` **PASS**; branch 0 behind main at merge time.
- Vision, live (2026-09-05): a ~8 KB PNG sent as a base64 data URL — the exact shape `describeImage` builds — through OpenRouter→Azure BYOK → correct answer ("pig"); same image via https URL → correct. GPT-5.5 on the same path → correct. One curiosity, not a blocker: a 64×64 two-color synthetic PNG was misread by Astra but read correctly by GPT-5.5 and Sol.
- CodeRabbit local review (`coderabbit review --committed --base-commit 0cc30c4c --agent`): 1 finding (major) — "select Azure's $20/$75 rate when the prompt exceeds 272K tokens". Answered, not changed here: no row in `MODEL_PRICING` models context-length tiers today, the gap is under-billing only (no customer-visible failure), AgentMode context trimming keeps prompts far below 272k, and the fix is a price-table shape change tracked as ENG-1774 rather than a special case inside a two-row model add.
- Not run on the laptop: `agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts` fails to *load* on this Mac on `origin/main` too (`TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')`), independent of this change — Atem is the test plane.

(1) "same as GPT-5.6 Sol at launch" was wrong — Sol launched at 59 on v4.1 and sits at 61 on v4.1.1 today; Astra's 61 is "equal to Sol's current score" (fixed in `5cc3f44f6`, registry comment + `qualityScoreSource` + Linear). (2) "`usage.cost` is 0 for BYOK" is what every observed call returned, not a documented guarantee — the backend never depends on it (it keys on `is_byok`).
  - Review: 11 findings, 10 refuted on evidence (maxTools 128 is a recorded Azure production 400 in this repo, not a guess; exact-value assertions come from the human-written contract; etc.). Three were still cheap improvements and are in `5cc3f44f6`: vision flag now backed by the live image call above, test block moved so the dominance block's doc comment is adjacent to its `describe` again, maxTools comment cites `ce154d09c`.

title: fix: refresh stale GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna Azure BYOK price rows (ENG-1781)
body:
## What / why

`MODEL_PRICING` (`backend/src/utils/llmPricing.ts`) still carried the
2026-08-19 Azure GlobalStandard rates for GPT-5.6 Terra/Luna. Azure cut
both on 2026-07-30 (Terra -20%, Luna -80%), mirroring OpenAI's direct-API
cut, but this table was never updated. Since these are BYOK models
billed from this static table (OpenRouter's `usage.cost` override is
skipped for `is_byok === true`), every Terra/Luna call was over-metered
against the customer's usage cap — Luna ~5x, Terra ~1.25x.

| Model | Old (in/out per 1M) | Corrected |
|---|---|---|
| gpt-5.6-sol | $5.00 / $30.00 | unchanged |
| gpt-5.6-terra | $2.50 / $15.00 | **$2.00 / $12.00** |
| gpt-5.6-luna | $1.00 / $6.00 | **$0.20 / $1.20** |

## Source verification (AC #1)

Re-verified against Azure's own published GlobalStandard meter, not
OpenRouter's listing (corroboration only):

- azurespeed.com/AzureAiModelPricing (Models.dev Azure catalog snapshot,
  meter effective date 2026-07-01) — Terra $2.00/$12.00, Luna
  $0.20/$1.20.
- cloudzero.com's 2026 Azure OpenAI pricing guide — same numbers,
  explicitly attributed to "OpenAI's July 30 cut".
- BerriAI/litellm#36192 — a LiteLLM maintainer issue documenting the
  identical Azure-meter-vs-cost-map drift on these exact two models
  (their cost map had OpenAI's numbers instead of Azure's — inverse of
  our bug, same root cause: nobody re-synced after the 07-30 cut).

Cache read/write stay on the 10%/125% derived convention (unchanged —
Azure's published cache rates already match it for all three models).

## Consequence pinned in tests (AC #3)

Luna's cost score (`costScoreFromPrice`) drops from 50 to 29 with the
corrected rate, moving it back into the same `ultra_cheap` band as
`gpt-5.4-nano` (also 29). The same-family dominance rule
(`deriveDominanceLegacyIds`) now correctly re-flags Nano as legacy
(same cost band, strictly higher Luna quality score) — this restores
Harsha's original 2026-08-19 intent ("GPT-5.6 Luna is strictly better
than GPT-5.4 Nano"), which had been defeated by the stale price making
Luna look like a pricier tier than it actually is. Updated
`agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts`'s dominance test accordingly; no
other test needed a value change (Terra's tier band and the Sol/Terra
false-positive-family guard were already asserting values that hold at
the corrected price).

## How to test

1. `npx jest src/__tests__/llmPricing.test.ts src/__tests__/modelPricingCoverage.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts` — 250 tests, all green.
2. Full `agentModeService` suite (164 suites / 3484 tests) — all green, run this tick.
3. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — clean (needed `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144`, project is large enough to OOM the default heap).

## What was NOT tested

No live OpenRouter/Azure call was made this tick (no credential need —
this is a static-table correction, not a live-integration change). No
production billing data was touched or backfilled; this only changes
the rate applied to *future* calls.

## Complexity ledger

Net complexity: flat. Two price literals changed, one test assertion
flipped to match the now-correct derived value, comments updated to
record the new source and date. No new abstractions, no new files.

Not a database/data-plane change, no external copy, no credential
grant.

ENG-1781

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Low

Updates Azure BYOK pricing for GPT-5.6 Terra and Luna. Terra changes to `$2.00/$12.00`, and Luna changes to `$0.20/$1.20` per 1M input/output tokens. Sol remains unchanged. Adds OpenRouter GPT-6 Astra pricing at `$10/$50` with derived cache rates. Updates Luna’s cost score and classification.
