title: ENG-1551: lead volume & attribution monitor
body:
## Summary
- New distribution-aware lead-volume drought detector: flags a campaign only when its trailing 7-day lead average falls below **that campaign's own** 5th-percentile historical floor (computed from a baseline excluding the trailing window itself) — not a fixed day count, which fires ~50% of weeks on a low-volume account per the card's own measured data (Haven's Maintenance Triage: 39 of 59 days had zero leads).
- `services/leadVolumeMonitorService.ts` resolves client→ad-accounts identically to `assessClientHealth` (`platform === 'meta' && account_type === 'ad_account'`) — deliberately, not a second slightly-different resolver.
- New MCP tool `monitor_lead_volume`, registered in `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES` and `CROSS_ACCOUNT_USER_DATA_TOOLS` (so the scheduled-report distribution guard treats it as sensitive, same as `assess_client_health`).
- Account-level `unattributedLeadCount` kept strictly separate from every campaign's totals — never read as evidence a campaign's volume collapsed.
- **New prod skill created and published**: "Lead Volume & Attribution Monitor" (not in this PR — a DynamoDB item in `AW-Skills`, verified via read-back, all 9 attributes matched). Hard-requires a Conversion Tracking Validator pass before reporting any drought as real, with an explicit third "unconfirmed" state so CTV-unavailable never silently defaults to a false positive or negative.

## Not done, deliberately
- No schedule wired to use this skill yet — the card's own instruction is to force activation via a schedule's run prompt (`functionCallMinCalls`), not by editing the published skill; that's a per-schedule decision for later.
- No live end-to-end confirmation that a real Emma session picks up the new skill — no direct prod API access from this session, only the DynamoDB write itself (verified) and test-env1 (which reads a separate `Dev-AW-Skills` table, so it can't see this).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean throughout
- [x] Pure logic: 19 tests. Mutation-tested — a red-check caught a real bug (baseline percentile computed over the whole history including the trailing window let an ongoing collapse dilute its own floor and mask itself); fixed, then confirmed the fix via a second mutation (reverting it) before restoring.
- [x] Orchestration: 10 tests. Mutation-tested — dropped `account_type` filter (caught: Instagram Business account leaked in) and dropped per-account row filter (caught: one account's campaigns leaked into another's report).

title: fix(agentMode): modify_work_plan can no longer silently drop a failed required function call (ENG-1793)
body:
## Summary

Fixes [ENG-1793](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1793/work-plan-steps-marked-completed-despite-requiredfunctioncalls-never): work plan steps were being marked `completed` despite their `requiredFunctionCalls` never firing or failing.

**Root cause (verified against live DynamoDB data, not guessed):** the completion gate in `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt` (which checks `session.calledFunctions` against `step.requiredFunctionCalls`) was already correct and working as designed. The actual bug is in `modifyWorkPlan`: when merging an existing step's `requiredFunctionCalls`, it used `newStep.requiredFunctionCalls !== undefined ? newStep.requiredFunctionCalls : <old value>`. In production session `a90b38fc-a641-4e11-b5af-219d1fa39145` (launched from the "Meta Ads Performance Report" predefined plan), the "Create HTML report" step's required `create_html_from_template` call FAILED (`failedFunctions.create_html_from_template: 1`, absent/zero in `calledFunctions`). A mid-run `modify_work_plan` call for that step happened to pass `requiredFunctionCalls: []` — a defined, non-`undefined` value — which silently replaced the template-authored requirement with an empty array. The completion gate then had nothing left to check, and the step was marked `completed` anyway.

Confirmed by comparing the live session's `workPlan.steps[2].requiredFunctionCalls` (`[]`) against the source template `plan_1770258894323_mhftrt1jc`'s step 3 (`["create_html_from_template"]`), plus `calledFunctions.modify_work_plan: 1` showing the tool was actually invoked mid-run.

## Fix

`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`, `modifyWorkPlan`:
- `requiredFunctionCalls` can still be freely modified (added to, reordered, or have functions removed) — **except** it may no longer silently drop a function that has already failed for the session (`failedFunctions[fn] > 0`) and has not since succeeded (`calledFunctions[fn]` is 0/absent). That specific removal is re-added to whatever the caller requested.
- A function that was never required, or that failed and later succeeded, or that never failed at all, is unaffected — genuine scope reduction (e.g. user explicitly agrees to drop a step's requirement) still works exactly as before.
- The session is now read with `consistentRead=true` (same `getChatSession(sessionId, true)` pattern `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt` already uses per ENG-1188), so a required call's failure recorded earlier in the same turn is never missed by the check.

This is general — it is not keyed to the specific session, plan, or function name from the incident, and does not touch steps with an empty/no `requiredFunctionCalls` list or steps whose required calls succeeded normally.

## Tests

Added to `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts`:
- `ENG-1793: modify_work_plan cannot silently drop a failed required function call` (new describe block, 5 tests):
  - re-adds a required function that already failed and never succeeded, even when the update omits it
  - reads the session with consistentRead so a same-turn failure is never missed
  - still allows a genuine scope reduction: dropping a required function that never failed
  - does not re-add a required function that failed but has since succeeded
  - end-to-end: modify_work_plan cannot be used to bypass set_work_plan_status's completion gate
- `ENG-1793: fails to complete a step whose required function was called but failed, never succeeded` — pins the `setWorkPlanStatus` half of the ticket title directly (already correct pre-fix; guards against a future regression).

## Mutation test

Reverted only the `agentModeService.ts` fix (kept the tests), re-ran the suite: the 3 tests that exercise the new merge/consistentRead behavior failed with clear signals (e.g. `Expected: ObjectContaining {"requiredFunctionCalls": ["create_html_from_template"]}` vs `Received: {"requiredFunctionCalls": []}`; the end-to-end test got `Expected: false, Received: true` for the bypassed completion). Restored the fix — all 67 tests in the file pass again.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` — 67/67 passing
- [x] `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts` — 20/20 passing (unaffected launch path, sanity check)
- [x] Mutation-tested the fix (see above)

title: fix(agent-mode): match predefined work plan titles separator/case-insensitively (ENG-1794)
body:
## Summary

Fixes [ENG-1794](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1794/launch-predefined-work-plan-silently-launches-wrong-template-when-two): `launch_predefined_work_plan` could silently launch the wrong predefined work-plan template when two templates have near-identical titles (e.g. an `_Eval`/`_Audit` suffix pair).

**Root cause** (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`, `applyPredefinedWorkPlan`, ~line 32536): the `planTitle` argument was matched against the stored template title with a plain `.toLowerCase()` equality check. Templates are stored with underscore-joined titles (`Founder_Linkedin_Sales_Readiness_Eval`), but natural chat phrasing uses spaces and mixed case (`Founder LinkedIn Sales Readiness Eval`) — these never matched.

Live-verified via the session transcript (`sessionId 3fce3c5a-6b25-4167-987b-b5bd8c7f4c5b` in `AW-ChatMessages`): the model's first `launch_predefined_work_plan` call with the natural phrasing failed "not found" (exactly as the strict-equality code predicts). Per the tool's own error message ("verify the identifier/name first"), the model fell back to `list_predefined_work_plans` + `search_tool_response`/`read_tool_response` to grep the full (370KB+) plan listing for a title to retry with. Because the two LinkedIn templates share byte-identical `welcomeMessage` text, the model's search snippets didn't clearly distinguish them, and it retried with the literal title `Founder_Linkedin_Sales_Readiness_Audit` — a real title that then matched exactly, launching the wrong template with no error. The sibling `AI_GTM_Position_Eval`/`_Audit` pair "worked" only because their *differing* `welcomeMessage` text made the fallback search's result unambiguous — not because the first-call matching logic was actually more permissive.

**Fix**: normalize both sides (case, underscores/hyphens → space, whitespace) before comparing, so natural-language phrasing resolves directly on the first call for every template — bypassing the risky fallback-search path entirely. `planId` continues to win first on an exact match. This is separator/case normalization only, not fuzzy/substring matching, so two templates whose titles genuinely differ (the `_Eval`/`_Audit` suffix itself) never collide.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts`:
  - `ENG-1794: near-duplicate titles sharing an identical welcomeMessage` → `resolves a spaced, mixed-case title argument to the matching Eval template, not the Audit one`
  - same describe block → `resolves a spaced, mixed-case title argument to the matching Audit template, not the Eval one`
  - `ENG-1794: still resolves correctly when near-duplicate titles have DIFFERING welcomeMessage text` (regression guard for the already-working AI_GTM_Position pair)
- [x] Mutation-tested: reverted the `agentModeService.ts` fix only (tests kept) → all 3 new tests failed with `Expected: true / Received: false` on `result.success`; all 20 pre-existing tests in the file still passed. Restored the fix → all 23 pass.
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts` — 23/23 pass
- [x] Also ran the other test files that exercise `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` (`agentModeController.createSessionWithPlan.test.ts`, `emma.workPlanTemplateTools.test.ts`, `agentModeController.acceptWorkPlanRecommendation.test.ts`) — 48/48 pass

Not merging — per campaign convention, a human reviews and merges after this is verified.

Slice 1 of the ENG-1250 usage-accounting rewrite — **the store only**. Nothing reads it yet and no enforcement moves.

## The approval

Harsha approved the data-plane change on ENG-1250 on 2026-09-03, naming every parameter:

> Approved. Create `AW-SpendEvents` as spec'd: HASH=billingUserId, RANGE=eventId · GSI: billingUserId + occurredAt · No TTL (auditable ledger; storage cost is negligible) · 18 fields per Architecture §1. Go ahead and build the store + charging API interface.

Verified on 2026-09-07 that the table does **not** exist in `992382574572` — so the approval authorized creating it, rather than recording that it had been created. This PR is that creation.

## Why not reuse `AW-LlmChargeEvents`

It opens by declaring itself *"deliberately LLM-only: it is not the future cross-vendor wallet"* — committed 89 minutes after ENG-1250 was filed, so that scoping was a decision made with this row already open. Repurposing it would have spent a data-plane approval to arrive somewhere that still is not the destination, leaving ~10 required fields and the reservation lifecycle unbuilt.

## What the store enforces

These are the invariants that turn into money bugs and cannot be repaired after the fact:

| Invariant | Why it is enforced at the write |
|---|---|
| A replayed idempotency key adds $0 and returns the **original** event | §1's requirement. Returning the retry would book a second, different amount under an already-charged key |
| `costMicroUsd` is a non-negative **integer** of micro-dollars | §3's invariant is exact to one micro-dollar; float dollars cannot hold that over ~1.4M rows |
| `billingMonth` must agree with `occurredAt` | They index one row into two months; afterwards nothing can tell which field lied |
| `costSource` has no `"unpriced"` member | The billing boundary says an unpriced unit must fail closed, never "become a silent $0 charge" |
| `allocated` costs require a `rateCardVersion` | §5: historical events retain the rate version used |
| A lifecycle only advances out of `reserved` | A settled amount cannot be rewritten, a void cannot be resurrected |

## Retention

**No TTL**, per the approval. `AW-LlmChargeEvents` expires rows at 365 days; this store is the evidence behind *"a pause is explainable to the cent"*. Its absence is the decision, not the usual missed manual console step — and the provisioning test asserts nobody later adds a `TimeToLiveSpecification` believing `CreateTable` honours one. (It does not; the existing tables carry comments saying so.)

## Provisioning

Registered in `scripts/create-tables.ts` and in `services/ensureCriticalTables.ts` — the latter because, as that module documents, the script is never run on deploy and three incidents in two days came from exactly that gap. The table is therefore created at the next server boot.

## Testing

41 tests. Every invariant above was mutation-tested — **all 12 mutations fail the suite**, including "replay returns the retry not the original", "sum counts reservations as spend", "settled becomes re-voidable", "write a ttl like the LLM table does", and "list stops after the first page".

`npm run typecheck` is clean. (One pre-existing unrelated error, `robots-parser` in `siteLinkCrawlerService.ts`, is local `node_modules` staleness — the dep is pinned at `^3.0.1` in `package.json`.)

## Out of scope

The charging API (§2), the monthly projection (§3), dual-write and reconciliation are later slices. **No enforcement moves onto this rail** — ENG-1250 AC6 keeps that transition with Harsha, gated on shadow-reconciliation evidence, and we will come back for it separately.

## Note on the title

This PR deliberately names **ENG-1796**, not ENG-1250. A branch or title matching the epic would auto-transition all nine sections of it to `Merged` when this lands — the same integration behaviour that regressed ENG-1212 and mis-moved ENG-1035 and ENG-1139.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium. Adds the `AW-SpendEvents` immutable DynamoDB ledger with provisioning, idempotent writes, lifecycle transitions, retrieval, pagination, aggregation, and UTC timestamp validation with canonicalization. No production path reads the store. Rollback requires removing the table and deployment wiring.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(billing): add the single spend charging API (ENG-1798)
body:
Slice 2 of the ENG-1250 rewrite — the single charging API of Architecture §2.

> **Stacked on #2787.** This PR targets `anurag/eng-1796-spend-event-store`, not `main`, because it builds on that store. Review/merge #2787 first and this retargets to `main` automatically.

Covered by the same 2026-09-03 approval: *"Go ahead and build the store + charging API interface."*

## The contract

§2's rule is that *"all paid egress goes through one service; callers may not write the ledger or monthly counter directly"*. This is that service.

| Step | Where |
|---|---|
| 1. resolve the billing subject | `resolveBillingSubject` |
| 2. classify the call | `classify` |
| 3. resolve measured cost or allocated rate + version | `resolveCost` |
| 4. reserve | `reserveSpend` |
| **5. check admission** | **absent — deliberately** |
| 6. execute the vendor call | `chargeForCall`'s callback |
| 7. settle or void | `settleSpend` / `voidSpend` |
| 8. persist idempotently | via #2787's store |

## Step 5 is not built, and that is the point

Admission needs the monthly projection of §3 (next slice), and wiring admission at all is what **AC6 reserves for Harsha** behind shadow-reconciliation evidence. Nothing here reads a balance, blocks a call, or can pause an account.

There is a test asserting the module exports no `admit`/`admission`/`balance`/`remaining`/`enforce`/`pause`/`block` surface, so a future change that adds one trips a tripwire rather than sliding in.

## Decisions

- **An unpriced vendor throws rather than booking $0.** ENG-700 drew the line this preserves: `allocated` means real dollars from a known rate; a missing rate is not $0, it is unknown. The billing boundary says unpriced egress *"must never become a silent $0 charge"*.
- **A vendor-reported cost beats the card**, per §5.
- **This module throws where `usageRecorderService` swallows.** That inversion is deliberate: a swallowed failure on an *observation* rail loses a data point; the same on a *charging* rail loses revenue with no counter of what was lost — the defect ENG-702 exists for. Whether to run fail-open during the observe-only phase is a per-call-path decision that belongs at the call site.
- **`onBehalfOf` is stamped only when payer and actor differ**, so an ordinary self-serve call does not read as delegated.
- **`billingMonth` is derived from `occurredAt`, never the clock.**

## A test caught a real inefficiency

`chargeForCall` was calling `settleSpend` with no amount, which reads the event back from DynamoDB to recover the reserved cost — a number it had computed moments earlier. Every fixed-price charge would have paid for that read, and round-tripped the amount through float to do it. It now settles from the reservation in hand.

## Rate card

Two additive exports on `vendorRateCard.ts`: `VENDOR_RATE_CARD_VERSION`, because §5 requires historical events to retain the rate version used and the card had none, and `getRecordingUnit`, so a call site takes its unit from the card rather than restating it where it can drift from the rate it describes.

## Testing

52 tests across the two suites; `npm run typecheck` clean apart from the pre-existing `robots-parser` local-`node_modules` staleness. **All 12 mutations fail the suite**, including "unpriced vendor books $0", "customer-paid work gets charged anyway", "vendor failure settles instead of voiding", and the AC6 tripwire "an admission check appears".

## Not wired to anything

No adapter calls this yet. Bringing the already-metered paths onto it in observe-only dual-write is slice 4.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: High. Adds `spendChargingService` for billing subject resolution, cost calculation, reservation, settlement, and voiding. It preserves vendor errors and successful results, handles settlement failures, and adds rate-card metadata. The service can affect production billing, but no adapters call it yet. Admission checks remain excluded.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(agent-mode): work plan completion gate bypass + template name mismatch (ENG-1793, ENG-1794)
body:
## Summary
Combines two related fixes found during the round-3 exhaustive production sweep of all 28 predefined work-plan templates, shipping together in one PR per request.

- **ENG-1793**: `modify_work_plan` could silently drop a step's `requiredFunctionCalls` entry for a function that had already failed and never since succeeded, letting `set_work_plan_status` mark the step complete anyway. Fix: a failed-and-not-since-succeeded required call can no longer be silently dropped, regardless of what the caller passes. Also switches to `consistentRead=true` (ENG-1188 precedent) so a same-turn failure is never missed.
- **ENG-1794**: `launch_predefined_work_plan`'s title matching was strict case-sensitive equality against the stored underscore-joined title, so natural phrasing never matched on the first call and fell back to a fragile truncated-search recovery path — where near-duplicate titles sharing identical `welcomeMessage` text got confused (e.g. `Founder_Linkedin_Sales_Readiness_Eval` resolving to `..._Audit`). Fix: `normalizeWorkPlanTitleForMatch()` (lowercase, fold `_`/`-` to space, collapse whitespace) applied to both sides — separator/case normalization only, no fuzzy logic, so real title differences still never collide. `planId` exact match still wins first.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Both fixes mutation-verified independently (fix reverted, tests fail with clear signal; fix restored, tests pass)
- [x] Full pre-push suite: 159 suites / 3486 tests passing
- [x] Targeted files: `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` (67 tests incl. 6 new for ENG-1793) + `agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts` (23 tests incl. 3 new for ENG-1794) — 90/90 passing

title: feat(billing): derive the monthly spend projection and prove its invariant (ENG-1803)
body:
Slice 3a of ENG-1250 §3 — the monthly projection, **derived rather than stored**.

> **Stacked on #2787**, a sibling of #2788 (they touch disjoint files). Both retarget to `main` once #2787 merges.

## Why §3 splits in two

§3 asks for an atomic `billingUserId + month` projection. *Persisting* one is a second data-plane gate and a second round-trip to Harsha. So this builds the derivation first — a pure function over immutable spend events producing the §3 shape, plus the invariant check, with **no new table and no writes**.

When we do ask for the stored form (3b), we arrive with a working derivation and measured reconciliation behind it rather than a design sketch. That is what got the parent unblocked in the first place.

## What it produces

`projectMonth(...)` — settled spend, active reservations, included allowance, purchased credits, admin grants/reversals, migration adjustment, usable allowance, remaining balance, overspend, policy mode, and event counts.

`reconcileProjection(...)` — §3's invariant: summing settled events reproduces the projection within one micro-dollar. With integer micro-dollars throughout, a non-zero drift is never rounding; it means events were lost, double counted, or written to the wrong month.

Allowance inputs are **parameters, not fetched**. They live in subscription policy and the credit ledger; wiring them is a later slice, and keeping them parameters is what makes the invariant testable.

## Two things this deliberately does not invent

**The policy boundary.** §3/§4 say the mode is `full_choice | optimized | paused`. That text is dated 2026-08-15. **ENG-1211 then shipped on 2026-09-04 and removed the optimization boundary outright** — `evaluateLlmUsageMode` can no longer return `optimized`, and `optimizationCostThresholdMicroUsd` is now an alert level that *"can never again change, block, or rewrite a model"*.

Deriving three modes here would quietly reintroduce a gate the team deleted. So this **delegates to `evaluateLlmUsageMode`** rather than reimplementing the comparison — one boundary, one definition, no way for the two rails to disagree. A test asserts `optimized` is never produced, and the mutation that reimplements the old boundary fails three tests.

**The spend basis.** The live gate counts LLM cost only; this rail counts every AgentWeb-paid vendor. For the same account the new basis is `>=` the old one and reaches the hard cap sooner. That gap is not a bug to paper over — measuring it is precisely what the §8 shadow reconciliation is for, and AC6 forbids moving enforcement before it has been. **`policyMode` here is a shadow computation that nothing reads.**

## Structural guarantees

§3's *"raw spend is always preserved"* is enforced by shape, not by discipline: credits, admin reversals and migration adjustments only ever touch the allowance side, and adjustments cannot drive the allowance below zero into phantom spend. Reservations count against the remaining balance but never against settled spend.

Events are filtered to the subject and month rather than trusted, and the number dropped is reported as `excludedEventCount` — a caller passing a neighbouring month's events would otherwise get a plausible-looking total that no reconciliation could match, and §8 would read it as vendor drift.

## Testing

17 tests; typecheck clean. **All 9 mutations fail the suite**, including "credits added to spend instead of allowance", "reservations counted as settled spend", "mode reimplemented with the removed boundary", "allowance may go negative", and "reconciliation tolerance made infinite".

## Out of scope

3b (persisting the projection — needs the gate), dual-write, and enforcement. No enforcement moves anywhere.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Low

Adds a pure monthly spend projection with no persistence or writes. It filters events by billing user and month, calculates spend, allowances, balance, overspend, policy mode, and event counts, and reports exclusions. Shadow policy errors do not abort projection generation. No enforcement path or production outage path changes.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: Fix monitor_lead_volume unreachable from real Emma chat sessions
body:
## Summary
- `monitor_lead_volume` (ENG-1551, PR #2784) was registered in `mcpToolRegistry` and `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES` (agentModeService.ts — controls session-level access grant) but missing from `adminToolNames` (emma/tools.ts) — the list that actually bridges MCP-registered admin tools into Emma's in-app chat tool loop.
- Both other registration points were correct; only this bridge was missed. One-line fix.

## How this was found
Live-testing ENG-1552's internal validation work plan on prod (a private, admin-only work plan, not customer-facing) via a real scheduled-chat test run against Haven's actual account. The route worked fine when hit directly via curl earlier, and the tool was "grantable" per `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES` — but a real Emma chat session calling it got `Unknown tool: monitor_lead_volume`.

The run itself handled this gracefully — it did not fabricate lead-count data or silently drop the requirement; it explicitly noted the tool was unavailable, called out the gap in its final report, and refused to substitute placeholder numbers. That's a separate, encouraging finding about the model's behavior under a broken tool, not something this PR needed to fix.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] New regression test (`eng1552.monitorLeadVolumeEmmaBridge.test.ts`, 3 tests): asserts the tool resolves via `mcpToolRegistry`, is actually bridged into `emmaToolRegistry`, and the bridged handler is the identical `execute` function, not a stub. Deliberately narrow — `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES` and `adminToolNames` already have a small pre-existing asymmetry (`inspect_orphaned_org_join_requests` / `list_predefined_work_plans`) this test isn't confident enough to assert away, so it checks this one tool specifically.
- [x] Mutation-tested: removed the entry, confirmed exactly the two bridge-specific tests failed (the mcpToolRegistry-only test correctly still passed), restored.

title: feat(billing): dual-write metered vendor usage into the spend ledger (ENG-1804)
body:
Slice 4 of ENG-1250 — §9 step 2, *"dual-write old and new rails in observe-only mode"*.

> **Stacked on #2788** (it needs `VENDOR_RATE_CARD_VERSION` from that PR). Retargets to `main` once #2788 merges.

## Where it mirrors, and why there

At `recordVendorUsage`, not at each adapter. That function is already the single choke point every metered vendor path funnels through — You.com, Google CSE, Apollo, enrich.so, Remotion, v0, X — so **one seam covers all of them and any vendor added later**, instead of seven edits that a new adapter can silently miss.

Adapters calling the charging API directly is the end state (§2). This is the shadow phase that earns the right to get there.

**Nothing reads these rows.** No enforcement, no admission, no balance. AC6 keeps that transition with Harsha, gated on the reconciliation this data produces.

## A crash bug the wiring test caught

The first version was `void mirror(...).then(...)` with no rejection handler. A rejection there is an **unhandled promise rejection, which takes the Node process down** — the shadow ledger killing the API it observes, which is far worse than losing a shadow row.

Fixed on both layers: `mirrorVendorUsage` is now total (the flag read and event construction are inside its `try`, not just the store call), and the fire-and-forget call site has its own `.catch`. Both guards are mutation-verified — removing the call-site `.catch` crashes the suite outright.

## Decisions

| | |
|---|---|
| **Fail-open** | Inverts `spendChargingService`, which throws. That one is a *charging* rail and must not lose revenue silently; this is a shadow of an *observation* rail and must never break the metering it mirrors. |
| **Kill switch defaults ON** | `SPEND_LEDGER_DUAL_WRITE=false` stops it. Inverted from the repo's opt-in convention because the point is to accumulate the evidence AC6 needs — a flag defaulting off means discovering in a week that none exists. Blast radius: a fire-and-forget write to a new, empty, unread table at a few hundred rows a day. |
| **Retries not deduplicated** | Call-site tokens are ENG-702's scope. The live rail is *also* non-idempotent, so a retry double-counts on both sides and the totals still reconcile. A shadow rail that deduplicated while the live one did not would diverge by design, and every retry would read as unexplained drift in §8. Call sites can adopt `idempotencyKey` incrementally. |
| **`unpriced` skipped, not $0** | The billing boundary forbids an unpriced unit becoming a silent $0 charge. |
| **X/Twitter labelled `caller:twitter`** | ENG-703 deliberately excludes X from the card; stamping the card's version would claim a provenance the amount does not have. |

## Parity with the row it mirrors

Both rows are stamped from **one instant**, so they cannot straddle UTC midnight, and the shadow uses the **identical** micro-dollar arithmetic. If those two roundings ever diverge, every §8 comparison reports drift that is really one number rounded two ways.

## Testing

167 tests across the seven related suites; typecheck clean. **All 12 mutations fail the suite.**

Worth flagging: the rounding mutation initially did *not* fail. The test used $0.0495, which rounds and floors to the same value — so it would have passed against the wrong implementation and proved nothing. Retested with values that discriminate ($0.0000125 → 13 rounded, 12 floored; and a negative, which floors to negative money).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Adds an observe-only, fail-open dual write from `recordVendorUsage` to the spend ledger. It runs after successful live writes, covers all vendor paths, skips unpriced usage, preserves shared arithmetic and timestamps, labels X/Twitter usage, and prevents unhandled rejections. Ledger rows do not affect enforcement or balance decisions.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix: work-plan completion-gate bypasses + title-match gaps (ENG-1799, ENG-1800, ENG-1802)
body:
## Summary

Fixes two production completion-gate bypasses found in the same sweep that produced ENG-1793 (already merged, PR #2076/#2789), each in `modifyWorkPlan` (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`) — the same function ENG-1793 patched, but for two gaps ENG-1793 didn't close.

### ENG-1799 — `requiredFunctionCalls` could be silently dropped for a never-called function

**Root cause:** ENG-1793's `mergeRequiredFunctionCalls` protects a required function from being silently dropped by a mid-run `modify_work_plan` call only if it had already **failed** at least once (`failed > 0 && succeeded === 0`). A required function that was simply **never called at all** (`failed === 0`, `succeeded === 0`) — exactly the shape live-verified in production session `3fce3c5a-6b25-4167-987b-b5bd8c7f4c5b` ("Founder_Linkedin_Sales_Readiness_Audit") — fails the `failed > 0` test trivially and could still be dropped, leaving `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt`'s completion gate nothing to check.

**Fix:** broadened the invariant (`backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`, `modifyWorkPlan`) — a required function can only be dropped once it has **succeeded** at least once, regardless of whether it previously failed or was never attempted. A step that has already resolved (`completed`/`skipped`) is exempt, since the gate that mattered already ran its decision.

### ENG-1800 — `expectedAssetCount` had no drop/reduction protection at all

**Root cause:** unlike `requiredFunctionCalls`, `expectedAssetCount`/`expectedAssetCountTools` in `modifyWorkPlan` had **zero** protection — the field is explicitly documented as freely overridable so a user can legitimately reduce scope. Live-verified in production session `ca06a9e0-9499-42e1-98ce-72b5bb7b4d04` ("Display Ad Set Production — One Master, Every Size", planId `a513e5c9-5e8a-49a8-97a3-1a771a7f81c2`): "Render the Full Size Matrix" required 12 assets (gated on `expectedAssetCountTools: ["playwright_browser_take_screenshot"]`); `set_work_plan_status` correctly blocked with `workplan_insufficient_assets` (1 of 12 produced). The model then called `modify_work_plan` **twice in the same run**, shrinking `expectedAssetCount` first to 1, then to 0 — nothing distinguished that self-serving edit from a genuine user-approved reduction — after which the step completed with 1 real screenshot, and the closing synthesis falsely claimed "✅ Deliverables Generated & Verified" across "all 12 units".

**Fix:** mirrored the same invariant used for `requiredFunctionCalls` — `expectedAssetCount` can still be freely raised, lowered, or cleared, **except** it may never be silently lowered while the step's own actual produced-asset count (computed the same way the real completion gate computes it, including the same per-step `sinceIso` cutoff walk) has not yet met the *existing* (pre-edit) requirement. Once the step has genuinely produced enough assets, or once it has already resolved, edits are unrestricted.

### False "✅ Verified" claim (ENG-1800) — not separately fixed

The closing synthesis's false "Deliverables Generated & Verified" claim is a direct downstream consequence of the numeric gate being bypassed: with the fix, `modify_work_plan`'s attempt to shrink `expectedAssetCount` to 0 is rejected, so `set_work_plan_status` keeps returning `workplan_insufficient_assets`, and the step can never reach `completed` on a 1-of-12 production run — so the model has no path to reach the "all 5 steps completed" closing synthesis that carried the false claim in production. A pre-existing `detectFalseCompletionClaim`/`buildFalseClaimCorrectionFooter` mechanism exists elsewhere in the codebase for catching overclaiming prose, but it did not fire on this specific turn's wording — flagged as a possible separate follow-up, intentionally left out of scope here per the gate fix removing the precondition for the false claim to ever reach the user.

### ENG-1802 — title matching only normalized separators/case at one of four call sites

**Root cause:** the ENG-1794 fix (already merged) added `normalizeWorkPlanTitleForMatch()` (lowercase, fold `_`/`-` to space, collapse whitespace) but wired it into exactly one call site, `applyPredefinedWorkPlan`. Three other title-matching sites in `backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts` still did raw `.toLowerCase()`-only comparisons: `getAllPredefinedWorkPlans`' dedup key, `getPredefinedWorkPlan`'s GET-by-title lookup, and `createSessionWithPlan`'s POST `:planTitle` URL param lookup — so a template stored with an underscore-joined title (the common shape) never resolved against the natural, spaced phrasing a user/model would type at those three sites, and two templates differing only by separator could dedupe as separate list entries.

**Fix:** exported `normalizeWorkPlanTitleForMatch` from `agentModeService.ts` and switched all three sites to it — same separator/case normalization as the already-merged fourth site, no fuzzy/substring matching added.

This is a separate, already-scoped follow-up ticket (found during PR #2789's review) added to this PR at the user's request; unrelated to the ENG-1799/ENG-1800 completion-gate work above but small and mechanical enough to ship together.

## Root-cause verification

Both root causes were verified against live production data (read-only, `AW-ChatSessions`/`AW-WorkPlans`, via `aws dynamodb`/`aws dynamodb query` against `AW-ChatMessages`), not just code inspection:
- ENG-1800: the exact `modify_work_plan` calls reducing `expectedAssetCount` 12 → 1 → 0 for step 3, and later 0 for steps 3/4/5, were found in the session's persisted tool-call ledger, immediately following two `workplan_insufficient_assets` blocks.
- ENG-1799: confirmed the analogous code-level gap (never-called functions bypass the ENG-1793 `failed > 0` check) by reading `mergeRequiredFunctionCalls`; the specific production session referenced in the ticket did not itself exercise `modify_work_plan`, so this fix is verified via the demonstrated code gap plus regression tests rather than a literal reproduction in that one session's ledger — see the PR discussion / final report for full detail.

## Tests

Added to `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts`, mirroring the existing ENG-1793 test style:
- `ENG-1799: modify_work_plan cannot silently drop a never-called required function call` (4 tests: re-adds a never-called requirement, still allows dropping an already-succeeded one, exempts already-resolved steps, end-to-end gate-bypass-attempt test)
- `ENG-1800: modify_work_plan cannot silently clear the expectedAssetCount gate` (5 tests: refuses a reduction below produced count, allows reduction once genuinely satisfied, allows raising freely, exempts already-resolved steps, end-to-end gate-bypass-attempt test mirroring the exact production sequence)
- Updated the existing ENG-1793 "genuine scope reduction" test, whose invariant intentionally tightened (dropping now requires the function to have *succeeded*, not merely never failed)

Added to `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeController.{getAllPredefinedWorkPlans,getPredefinedWorkPlan,createSessionWithPlan}.test.ts` for ENG-1802 (1 test per site), plus a fix to `createSessionWithPlan.test.ts`'s `../services/agentModeService` module mock, which only stubbed the `agentModeService` object — the controller now imports `normalizeWorkPlanTitleForMatch` directly from that module, so the mock factory needed to forward the real implementation via `jest.requireActual` or every test in that file broke.

**Mutation-verified** (all three fixes): reverted each fix commit in turn (`git stash`), ran the corresponding new tests, confirmed they fail against pre-fix code (4/4 ENG-1799 assertions fail without the fix; ENG-1800 correctly fails the 4 tests asserting the new protection while the ones asserting pre-existing/exempt behavior still pass; all 3 ENG-1802 tests fail without the fix), then restored the fix and confirmed all tests pass.

`npm run typecheck` run after every `.ts` edit per CLAUDE.md; full targeted suite green on the final state (146 tests across `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts`, `agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts`, and the three `agentModeController.*` files above).

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` — 76/76 passing
- [x] `agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts` — 23/23 passing

- [x] Root causes verified against live production DynamoDB data (read-only) for ENG-1799/ENG-1800

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

## Update: fresh-eyes review found and closed a real regression + a real gap

A fresh-eyes adversarial review of this PR (post-push, pre-merge) found the "step resolved (completed/skipped) exempts from protection" carve-out described above for both ENG-1799 and ENG-1800 is **unsafe, not just conservative**: a resolved step can be reset back to `pending` (a real, already-supported transition — see the existing ENG-1188/CodeRabbit PR #2430 cutoff-timestamp handling in `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt`, which explicitly documents "a step that was completed/skipped and later reset to 'pending'") without restoring `requiredFunctionCalls`/`expectedAssetCount`. The review reproduced the exploit directly: complete a step legitimately → clear its requirement via `modify_work_plan` while `completed` (exempt, so no protection ran) → reset to `pending` → re-complete with **zero** of the real required work redone, gate silently skipped.

The same review also found `expectedAssetCountTools` had **zero** protection at all — the ENG-1800 fix only guarded the numeric `expectedAssetCount`. A model could leave `expectedAssetCount` unchanged and instead retarget `expectedAssetCountTools` to an unrelated tool it had already called enough times for other reasons, achieving the identical "dodge a failing gate" bypass through a field the fix never touched.

**Both independently verified against the actual code** (not taken on the review's word) before fixing: confirmed the reset-to-pending transition is real via the pre-existing PR #2430 code comment, and confirmed `expectedAssetCountTools`'s lack of an allowlist check directly in `synthesisResidue.ts`'s `countProducedAssets`.

**Fix (2 new commits):**
- Removed the resolved-step exemption from `mergeRequiredFunctionCalls`/`mergeExpectedAssetCount` entirely — protection now applies regardless of step status. This is a no-op for a step that resolved normally (everything it needed had already genuinely succeeded), and only bites the reset-then-clear-then-recomplete abuse path.
- Added `mergeExpectedAssetCountTools`, applying the same produced-vs-required guard to the tools list that `mergeExpectedAssetCount` already applied to the number.

**Tests:** rewrote the two tests that pinned the now-removed exemption into tests proving the opposite; added an end-to-end reset-abuse regression test for `requiredFunctionCalls` mirroring the review's exact exploit sequence; added two new tests for the `expectedAssetCountTools` guard. All 4 new/rewritten tests independently mutation-verified against pre-fix code (`git stash`, rerun, confirm failure, restore) — genuinely fail with clear signals. Full 149-test targeted suite green on the corrected code; `npm run typecheck` clean; full 162-suite/3577-test pre-push hook green on the branch (rebased onto latest `main`) before this push.

---

## Update: live-testing on test-env1 (post-correction) found a third, distinct bypass — fixed

While live-testing the reset-to-pending fix above on test-env1, the model organically (unprompted, not a scripted repro) restructured a `Meta_Ads_Perf_Report` session by calling `modify_work_plan` with `removeStepCounts` including a stepCount, and a new step reusing that exact same number, in the same call — consolidating two steps into one. Because `removeStepCounts` filters `workPlan.steps` **before** the update-or-add loop runs, the re-added step landed in the "add new step" branch, which none of this PR's protection covered — a third, distinct bypass mechanism beyond the never-called-function and reset-to-pending cases, since neither touched the `removeStepCounts` interaction.

**Fix (2 more commits):** snapshot every step's pre-removal state (`originalStepsBeforeRemoval`), keyed by `stepCount`. When a "new" step reuses a stepCount that was just removed in the same call, treat it as an edit for protection purposes — apply the same merge guards using the pre-removal step as the baseline. A genuinely new stepCount (never existed before this call) is unaffected.

**Deliberately scoped**, not generalized: a broader N-to-M consolidation (a removed step's number never reused by any replacement) can still lose that step's requirement — filed as ENG-1808, not fixed here, since a general fix risks over-blocking unrelated, legitimate step deletions without more careful design (distinguishing "this new step replaces that removed step's scope" from "this removed step is just obsolete, unrelated to whatever else got added this call" isn't safely inferable from call-adjacency alone).

**Test:** one new regression test pinning the exact reused-stepCount pattern observed live. Mutation-verified (reverted the fix, reran, failed with a clear signal; restored, full 80-test suite passes). Full 162-suite/3577+-test pre-push hook green on the branch (rebased onto latest `main` again) before this push.

---

## Update: second fresh-eyes review round (post live-testing) found and closed a real regression

Requested a second, focused review since two rounds of un-reviewed changes had landed since the first review (the Finding-1/2 correction, and the live-discovered `removeStepCounts` fix) — self-review has a known blind spot, and this PR had already twice shown that a closer look finds something new.

**Blocking, reproduced:** the `removeStepCounts`-reuse fix correctly protected `requiredFunctionCalls` unconditionally (the merge function always runs, correctly handling `requested === undefined` by keeping the existing value), but `expectedAssetCount`/`expectedAssetCountTools` kept the old "only merge if the caller explicitly supplied the field" gate. A model reusing a removed stepCount and simply **omitting** `expectedAssetCount` (never explicitly lowering it — the only case earlier tests covered) skipped the merge entirely, leaving the re-added step with **no `expectedAssetCount` property at all** — a complete, silent removal of the asset-count gate, strictly worse than an explicit lowering, through exactly the surface that fix claimed to close. The reviewer reproduced this independently before reporting it; I re-verified with my own mutation test before fixing (fails pre-fix with `Expected: 12, Received: undefined`, matching the reviewer's finding exactly).

**Fix (2 more commits):** mirrored `requiredFunctionCalls`'s unconditional pattern for both `expectedAssetCount` and `expectedAssetCountTools` — the merge functions already correctly preserve the existing value when the caller's field is `undefined`. Also corrected a code comment the same review flagged as inaccurate (non-blocking): the resolved-step protection isn't a pure no-op for every normally-resolved step, since `session.calledFunctions` decrements toward 0 once a step's own credit is consumed on completion — clarified as intentional fail-closed behavior.

The reviewer also independently re-verified the `originalStepsBeforeRemoval` snapshot timing/staleness and the `mergeExpectedAssetCountTools` read-ordering — both correct, no issues found. Full 161-suite/3520-test pre-push hook green on the branch (rebased onto latest `main` again) before this push.

title: feat(linkedin): withhold a scheduled run with no daily invite budget (ENG-1717)
body:
Delivers **ENG-1609 AC #9**. First of an 8-PR stack; base is `main`.

## Problem

A scheduled LinkedIn outreach run with no daily invite budget left still ran: it burned a full generation, attempted sends the pacer was always going to refuse, and reported the result as a failure indistinguishable from a real one.

## Change

`utils/scheduledRunCapacityGate.ts` — a pure pre-run decision (injected deps, no I/O of its own), following the `scheduledRunAccountGate` (ENG-1197) and `scheduledRunPreCheck` (ENG-1259) pattern. When every usable account is out of daily invite headroom, the run is withheld with a distinct `skipped_send_capacity_exhausted` status and a plain-language reason naming the account and when its window renews.

- `promptCouldPinAnAccount()` pre-filters on the prompt, so a schedule that cannot pin an account never pays for an account read at all.
- Pending counts are fetched **after** the verdict and only on a block — LinkedIn publishes no pending cap to compare against, so they inform the report and never decide it.
- Fail-open throughout: an unreadable account or a failed count never withholds a run.

The customer portal renders the new status as a skip rather than a red "Test Failed" (see the paired portal PR).

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; 40 new tests; full backend sweep green apart from 6 suites proven pre-existing on `a54b424b2` by checkout-and-rerun.

Evidence comment with the full reasoning is on ENG-1717.

The gate checks owned and shared accounts, records `skipped_send_capacity_exhausted`, and fails open on read errors. It adds daily headroom and pending-invitation queries. title: fix(linkedin): list-sent-invitations can no longer report an unreadable backlog as an empty one (ENG-1718)
body:
Delivers **ENG-1609 AC #7**. Stacked on `anurag/eng-1717-presend-capacity-gate` — review that first; this PR's own diff is the second commit.

## Problem

`list-sent-invitations` could return `{}` for an account carrying a real backlog. The handler asked one question — `Array.isArray(items)` — and the Unipile SDK runs at `validateRequestPayloadLevel: 'warn'`, so a non-conforming body passes straight through. The model then reported "no pending invitations" to a customer whose sends were being throttled *by* those invitations.

This also corrects ENG-1132's own diagnosis: production evidence shows the ledger held 126 pending rows for iTrials at incident time. The tool never read it.

## Change

`services/agentMode/linkedInSentInvitationsView.ts` — `getSentInvitationsView()` returns one of three **named** outcomes and never a bare empty result:

- `live` — read from LinkedIn just now;
- `cache` — our own ledger, when the live read was unavailable or empty while we still hold records;
- `none` — with `liveUnavailable` distinguishing "we could not read it" from "there is genuinely nothing tracked".

Always carries a non-empty `notice`. `sent_at` is restored to each row so stale invitations can be picked by age (which is what ENG-1719's bulk withdraw needs). Cached rows are ordered oldest-first; capped at 50 with `totalPending` reporting the true backlog size.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; 14 new tests; full sweep green apart from the 6 known pre-existing suites.

## Noted, not absorbed

The SDK's `'warn'` validation level is platform-wide — raising it to `'error'` would affect every LinkedIn action, so it belongs in its own scoped issue rather than riding along here.

Risk: Medium

Updated `list-sent-invitations` to distinguish live, cached, and unavailable results. The tool validates live responses, falls back to ledger records, preserves `sent_at`, sorts cached invitations oldest-first, caps output at 50, and reports pending counts. Added 14 tests and confirmed typecheck success. Unreadable responses no longer appear as empty lists.

title: fix(linkedin): a send requirement is satisfied by a send that happened, not by any call to the tool (ENG-1720)
body:
Delivers **ENG-1609 AC #4 and #11**. Stacked on `anurag/eng-1718-sent-invitations-truthfulness`.

## Problem

`linkedin_outreach` multiplexes reads (`search-people`, `get-profile`) and sends (`send-invite`, `send-message`, `send-inmail`) behind one tool name, and a schedule can only name the **tool** in `requiredFunctionCalls`. The final verdict counted successful calls by name — so a run that made one successful `search-people` and had **every** `send-invite` refused satisfied `min: 1`, kept `runDelivered` true, and reported success to an owner whose outreach sent nothing.

All 8 production schedules declaring this requirement resolve to `min: 1`, so a single successful read defeated every one of them. This is the false success ENG-1132 AC #2 was filed to catch.

The check also only engaged when a cooldown/pacing phrase was recognised, so a send failing any other way — "recipient cannot be reached", provider errors, the class ENG-1640 reported live — never reached it at all.

## Change

`utils/linkedInSendRequirement.ts` decides on the **action**:

- a run that attempted **no** send keeps the name-keyed count, so a read-only LinkedIn schedule is not newly broken;
- a run that attempted **≥1** send is scored on its **succeeded** sends alone.

That demotes `LINKEDIN_INVITE_CAP_BLOCK_RE` to choosing which sentence the owner reads rather than whether the run passed. Deliberately **not** wired into the `runVerifiedChat` nudge loop — pressing harder against an account that is refusing sends is the amplification ENG-1715 (later in this stack) exists to bound.

## Three things found while building it

1. **The underscore spelling was invisible.** The dispatcher opens with `action.replace(/_/g, '-')`, so `send_invite` really sends — but the ledger stores the raw argument and the old helper folded case only. Neither the block detector nor the counter recognised it.
2. **The generic oncall page would have gone silent.** It was suppressed on the requirement verdict, which was identical to the block condition before this change and diverges after it — an unclassified all-sends-failed run would have missed the requirement, fired no dedicated page, *and* had its generic page suppressed. Re-keyed to the condition that actually fires the dedicated page.
3. **`functionCallDetails.actual` is now action-aware on passing send runs too** — leaving the name count persisted `{actual: 7, required: 1}` for a run that sent once.

## AC correction

The ticket's AC #5 is self-contradictory: it asks that all 11 existing ENG-1132 characterization tests keep passing **and** that the read-plus-blocked-sends case fail. The test at `agentModeController.scheduledAlertKeying.test.ts:339` **is** that case, asserting `passed: true` — the defect written down as expected behaviour. It is inverted here, along with one `actual` detail at `:368`. The other 9 pass unchanged.

## Behaviour change, stated plainly

Runs that pass today will now fail: any run where every LinkedIn send failed. That is AC #2's intent. All 8 affected production schedules are currently paused, so nothing flips overnight.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; 15 new unit tests; the ENG-1132 characterization suite goes 19/19; full sweep green apart from the 6 known pre-existing suites.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: High — This change makes LinkedIn send requirements action-aware. Successful reads no longer satisfy a send requirement when attempted sends fail. It supports underscore-form actions, updates alerts and `functionCallDetails.actual`, and adds 15 unit tests. Production schedules are paused because this can change customer-visible run outcomes.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(scheduling): stop pressing an unmet SEND requirement for 20 attempts (ENG-1715)
body:
**Blocking sibling of ENG-1609** (blocks ENG-1722). Stacked on `anurag/eng-1720-action-aware-send-counting`.

## Problem

`runVerifiedChat` re-sends *"Please try again. Make sure to `<tool>` (N more time(s) needed)."* until `maxAttempts` — 20. Two circuit breakers stop that early, and they are gated on mutually exclusive tool classes: `isPublishName` (ENG-947) and `isReadOnlyToolName` (ENG-1297). **Every `SEND_TOOLS` entry is in neither** — `linkedin_outreach`, `send_email`, `linkedin_manage_post`, `twitter_outreach`, `delete_leads`, `enrich_leads_execute`, and the rest — so a run that cannot satisfy a send requirement got the full 20-attempt press with no breaker at all.

The press argues directly against the run's own correct behaviour: a `send-invite` refused by an account-level cooldown returns *"DO NOT keep trying other recipients"*, and the loop then asks for it up to 19 more times. ENG-1297 recorded both outcomes of that pressure on a merely read-only tool — the model refuses every press (86 messages, $28.70, ~3.8M cache-creation tokens), or it complies and re-runs the run's primary action. Here that action is an irreversible external contact to a real person, on an account the provider is already throttling.

## Change

`utils/sendPressCircuitBreaker.ts`, modelled on the read-only sibling. Budget **2** (initial turn + one press), matching read-only rather than publish's 3 — a send refused by a cooldown or pacing cap is refused identically on every later attempt in the same run. Counts presses, not the run-wide attempt counter.

Unlike the read-only breaker it returns `success: false` with a `sendPressExhausted` marker: ENG-1297 *waives* its requirement and reports the run successful, and a send that did not happen must never be waived.

## Two corrections to the ticket, both verified in code

1. **AC #4 says a tool that is both publish and send is "none today". There are two.** `send_email_from_sender` and `twitter_manage_post` are both `isSendName` **and** already claimed by the publish breaker — through `EQUIVALENT_PUBLISH_ROUTES` (ENG-1599), not through `isPublishName`. Excluding only `isPublishName` would have left both breakers claiming the same turn and cutting a publish stall short at the smaller budget. The publish module now exports its own claim check (`isPublishPressClaimedName`, a pure extraction of the condition `isPublishOnlyUnmet` already applied) and this defers to it — one definition, not a second classifier.
2. **The press is triggered by UNDER-CALLING, not blocked sends.** `callSatisfiesRequirement` credits an exact name match for a non-publish tool even when the call **failed**, so one refused `send-invite` already satisfies `min: 1` and no press ever starts. AC #5 as filed cannot be reproduced literally; the tests use the real trigger.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; 21 unit tests including a drift guard that asserts which of the three breakers claims each `SEND_TOOLS` entry by name; 8 integration tests over `runScheduledChat`; full sweep green apart from the 6 known pre-existing suites.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium

Adds a send-specific circuit breaker to `runVerifiedChat`. It permits the initial send and one retry, then returns `sendPressExhausted: true`. It excludes publish-claimed tools, preserves existing breakers, and adds unit, integration, and ownership-drift coverage. This affects scheduled-chat retry behavior but does not directly indicate a production outage path.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(linkedin): seed the Daily LinkedIn Connection + Outreach Agent system schedule template (ENG-1722)
body:
Delivers **ENG-1609 AC #1, #2, #3, #5** — the ticket's headline. Stacked on `anurag/eng-1715-send-press-breaker`.

## Why this ships after the others

It is the switch that arms ENG-1132. That fix's block-detection / fail-the-run / page-oncall chain is gated on a schedule declaring `linkedin_outreach` in `requiredFunctionCalls` — a production scan of all 523 `AW-TaskSchedules` rows found 8 that do, **all paused**. The merged fix protects nobody today. Seeding this template turns it on platform-wide, which is why it lands behind ENG-1720 (action-aware counting) and ENG-1715 (the send-press breaker): without those it would arm a validation mechanism that does not work and a press loop that does harm.

## A seed script, not the API

`createScheduleTemplate` hardcodes `visibility: 'private' as const` and ignores the body's field, so the user route **cannot** produce a system template. Create-then-`PUT`-visibility does work, and that it works is the authorization bug ENG-1716; this deliberately does not rely on it. Follows the `seed-eng615/616/617` house pattern: idempotent, explicit, version-controlled.

## Design decisions worth reviewing

- **`functionCallMinCalls: { linkedin_outreach: 1 }`.** Before ENG-1720 a minimum of 1 was worthless here — the verdict counted by name, so one successful `search-people` satisfied it while every send was blocked. Action-aware counting changed what 1 *means*: "at least one send actually succeeded". A **higher** minimum would be worse, not stricter: the press loop still counts by name and fires on under-calling, so mandating several calls is exactly what drags a cooldown-stopped run into the press ENG-1715 had to bound.
- **The variable list is derived from the prompt's own placeholders**, with a test pinning the two in both directions. A hand-passed array that disagrees is silently overwritten on the API route, and an undeclared placeholder reaches the model as literal `{{x}}`.
- **No optional variables.** A declared variable left blank hard-fails the run before the model is called, so the two the parent ticket calls optional carry documented literal defaults — `"default"` and `"create new"` — handled by the prompt, with a test asserting the description and prompt name the same literal.
- **No numeric per-run volume cap in the prose**, asserted by a test. A prompt-level "max 5 invites/run" outliving its backend cap is what ENG-1631 had to run a production migration over.
- **The ENG-1640 signal-channel ladder** — engagement mining, then employer-event two-hop, then announcement-text demoted to last — order asserted by a test.
- **It does not promise the warm-up ramp** (ENG-1721, next in this stack); a test asserts the word does not appear, since the backend enforces it and a prompt describing it would be the same prose drift.
- `createdBy: 'system'` and a non-empty `category`, because those are the `CreatedByIndex` hash key and the `VisibilityCategoryIndex` range key respectively — a blank category makes the row invisible to the very listing AC #1 requires it to appear in.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean. 22 tests. Beyond unit tests: seeded **twice** against `Dev-AW-ScheduleTemplates` (second run skipped, leaving exactly one row — AC #6), then queried back through `VisibilityCategoryIndex`, the same GSI `getScheduleTemplates` uses, confirming visibility, category, all four variables and the validation wiring survive the round trip. Two tests drive the real seeded template through `createScheduleFromTemplate` to prove variables alone yield a live daily schedule with nothing left unsubstituted.

Full sweep green apart from the 6 known pre-existing suites.

## Not done

**The production seed has not been run.** It publishes a platform-wide template to every customer, and `createScheduleFromTemplate` **copies** `startingMessage` rather than referencing it — so every schedule created before any later fix keeps the old prompt permanently. That is a one-way door and wants an explicit decision:

```
NODE_ENV=production npx ts-node src/scripts/seed-eng1609-linkedin-outreach-template.ts
```

Incidental correction: the parent ticket says `list_schedule_templates` returns one platform template. Production has 6 templates and **zero** with `visibility: 'system'` — the Meta Ads one is `public`. This will be the first system template.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Adds an idempotent seed for the system-visible “Daily LinkedIn Connection + Outreach Agent” template. It uses a stable template ID and conditional creation to prevent duplicates during concurrent runs. It adds optional `onlyIfAbsent` support to `scheduleTemplateDb.createTemplate`. The production seed has not been run.

title: fix(linkedin): ramp the daily invite cap by connection age, not just the configured cap (ENG-1721)
body:
Delivers **ENG-1609 AC #6**. Stacked on `anurag/eng-1722-linkedin-outreach-template`.

## Why this is core scope

Harsha queried Unipile directly for the account behind ENG-1132: `premiumId: null`, no premium features — a **free** LinkedIn account — and `created_at` ~24 hours before the block. It was refused at a target well under the 30/day ceiling. His conclusion: *"this is very likely the DEFAULT new-customer failure mode, not an edge case"*, and the ramp *"should be treated as core scope, not a nice-to-have."*

LinkedIn throttles a freshly-connected third-party integration materially harder for roughly its first one to two weeks, independent of our cap. A flat cap cannot model that.

## Change

`resolveEffectiveDailyInviteCap = min(ramp, resolveDailyInviteCap(configured))` — `min`, never `max`; the ramp only ever lowers. ~5/day through the first week, 15 through day 14, then the account's own cap with no ramp. Same shape as `senderUsageTracker`'s `WARMUP_RAMP` / `effectiveDailyLimit` (ENG-265).

**Age is the only input**, per the ticket's constraint: `is_premium` and `daily_invite_cap` are self-reported and provably wrong in the field — the account above carries `is_premium: true` and `daily_invite_cap: 30` while being free. `created_at` matched Unipile's own record to the minute and survives re-OAuth, so an established account that reconnects does not restart its ramp.

## It had to reach three call sites, not one

1. `reserveDailyVolumeSlot`'s cheap pre-check;
2. the **durable re-check** inside `updateAccountConfig`'s CAS callback — it re-derives from freshly-read config, and `created_at` lives on the account row rather than in its config, so missing it there would have committed a reservation the first check had just refused;
3. `remainingDailyInvites`, so ENG-1717's capacity gate measures headroom against the same ramped cap instead of waving a run through for the pacer to refuse.

`connectedAt` is **required** on `ResolvedLinkedInAccount` so a future call site cannot silently drop the ramp.

## Two boundaries that needed explicit handling

- **The operator escape hatch is checked before the ramp.** When `resolveDailyInviteCap` returns `Infinity` the mechanism is off (`LINKEDIN_DAILY_INVITE_ABSOLUTE_MAX <= 0`) — layering `min(5, Infinity)` on top would reintroduce a cap exactly where an operator disabled it. That is also Jest's default, so the naive version would have newly throttled every suite.
- **A warm-up cap must not be described as a configurable one.** The refusal said *"raise it in Settings or ask Emma to update it if you have LinkedIn Premium"* — advice that cannot work here, and acting on it (self-reporting Premium) is what gets a new account throttled harder. Warm-up refusals now say so.

## Correction to AC #4

AC #4 says the ramp is "a no-op for existing accounts (median connection age 132 days)". Read-only production scan, 2026-09-07 — 16 unipile accounts, **zero missing `created_at`**, ages: `4, 12, 18, 41, 59, 116, 117, 124, 136, 136, 138, 143, 156, 158, 170, 176`. Median 136 holds, but **two live accounts are inside the window** and get ramped the moment this deploys. Intended behaviour, but "no-op" is the wrong expectation for a deploy review.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; 22 new tests. Every value assertion sets `LINKEDIN_DAILY_INVITE_ABSOLUTE_MAX` explicitly — it is 0 under Jest, which reads as "disabled → Infinity", so an unguarded assertion passes vacuously; that trap is itself pinned by a test. Full sweep green apart from the 6 known pre-existing suites.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Adds a connection-age warm-up ramp for LinkedIn invite limits. The ramp applies to pacing, daily headroom, and durable reservations. It uses `created_at`, preserves limits after re-OAuth, and distinguishes warm-up refusals from configured-cap refusals.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(linkedin): bulk-withdraw stale invitations to reclaim pending capacity (ENG-1719)
body:
Delivers **ENG-1609 AC #8**. Stacked on `anurag/eng-1721-warmup-ramp`.

## Problem

Reclaiming pending-invitation capacity required `cancel-invitation` one `invitation_id` at a time, each first obtained from `list-sent-invitations`. No scheduled run completes that and no person does it by hand. Requested on ENG-1132 on **2026-08-11** and still unbuilt: Hannah K ~105 pending; TFA Connect / Jennifer Sun **539**, dropping to 393 between 08-29 and 08-30 by means nobody could account for, still throttling her sends (ENG-1640).

## Change

New `withdraw-stale-invitations` action taking `older_than_days` plus optional `max_withdrawals` and `list_id`, driven off the ledger's `sentAt` + `invitationId` (both restored/made trustworthy by ENG-1718 earlier in this stack). Selection logic is a pure function; the drain takes injected deps, so neither needs Unipile to test.

**Oldest first**, capped at 40 per run — the drain size `linkedInWritePacer`'s own comment names as the realistic target, and a wall-clock bound, since at `minGapMs` spacing an unbounded drain would hold one request open for minutes.

## Paced, never bypassed

Every withdrawal goes through the same `paceLinkedInWrite` the single-shot action uses, reserved **individually rather than once for the batch** — reserving one slot and looping is precisely the burst that gets an account's session revoked. On a refusal it **checkpoints**: reports what it withdrew, what remains and why it stopped, and the next run continues from the oldest. Verified against the real pacer with `LINKEDIN_WRITE_MAX_PER_HOUR=2`.

Because it routes through `paceLinkedInWrite` rather than reimplementing the checks, **AC #3 falls out rather than being restated**: `dailyVolumeClassFor` returns `null` for cancel, so a drain does not consume the day's invite budget. Pinned by a drift guard that drains 40 and then asserts the full send allowance is intact — if that classification ever flipped, a drain would silently eat the whole day's sending.

## Honesty rules carried over from ENG-1718

- An unparseable or future `sentAt` is **never** treated as stale — age is the entire basis of the decision, so unusable means "do not touch", not "assume old".
- Old rows with no withdrawable `invitationId` are counted and reported, not dropped.
- A `notice` is always present, including when nothing qualified.
- A ledger-cleanup or CRM failure never turns a completed withdrawal into a reported failure.

## CRM consistency (AC #4)

Each withdrawal drops the ledger row — which is what the CRM's "invitation pending" indicator reads from — and appends a `linkedin.invite.withdrawn` engagement to an **existing** lead. Deliberately narrower than `mirrorLinkedInInviteToCrm`: it never creates a lead and never changes lead status. A withdrawal is not an act of outreach, so manufacturing a CRM record for someone who has none would invent a contact out of undoing one; and we really did contact the people who do have records, so un-marking them `contacted` would falsify history rather than correct it.

## Not oversold

The module docblock and the tool description both state that this does **not** lift the new-account trust throttle — that gate is about account age, not pending count, and is ENG-1721's ramp. The model is the thing choosing which remedy to offer, so it needs to know.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; 20 drain tests + 7 driving the real tool handler; full sweep green apart from the 6 known pre-existing suites.

Risk: Medium

Adds `withdraw-stale-invitations` to reclaim pending-invitation capacity. The action selects valid stale invitations oldest first, withdraws up to 40 with pacing, retries CRM provenance writes, checkpoints refusals, updates the ledger, and records CRM engagements without creating leads or changing invite budgets.

title: feat(onboarding): auto-create the LinkedIn outreach schedule behind a default-off flag (ENG-1723)
body:
Delivers **ENG-1609 AC #10** — the last of the eight. Stacked on `anurag/eng-1719-bulk-withdraw-stale-invitations`. **Nothing is enabled by this PR.**

## The undefined term

AC #10 originally read "for any customer whose plan promises a daily outreach volume". That has no referent in code: `SubscriptionType` carries `allowedPages`, `allowedSkills`, `allowedConnectedAccounts`, `allowedFeatures` and token/cost allowances — no outreach-volume concept — and tier definitions live in an admin-managed DynamoDB setting. Rather than add a billing field to serve one trigger, it is resolved into three checkable predicates:

| Predicate | Resolved as |
|---|---|
| LinkedIn connected | the customer's **own** unipile account |
| ICP known | the lead list onboarding just minted from it — also the `lead_list_id` the template needs |
| outreach-capable tier | `scheduled_chats` enabled **and** `unipile` a permitted platform |

Own accounts only, not org-shared: an org-shared account belongs to someone else, and auto-enrolling a colleague's LinkedIn into unattended outreach is exactly the consent this must not assume.

## Why the flag is not optional

This creates a **live** schedule that sends real connection requests from a real person's LinkedIn account with no chat interaction. A wrong predicate means unrequested outreach under someone's own name — irreversible and reputational. ENG-1721's ramp and the daily cap bound the blast radius, but bounded is not acceptable.

Default-off behind `OUTREACH_SCHEDULE_AUTO_CREATE_ENABLED`, plus a **dry run that works regardless of the flag** so the whole trigger can be proven before it is flipped — the `MANAGE_LEADS_CROSS_ACCOUNT_ADD_ENABLED` pattern from ENG-1557 v1. A dry run still respects every real predicate.

## Fails closed, and distinguishes "denied" from "don't know"

`isSubscriptionFeatureEnabled` returns `boolean | null`, where null means the admin setting could not be resolved. Background jobs elsewhere may treat null as "retry later"; this one refuses with its own `tier_unresolved` reason. Collapsing null into false would hide a broken admin setting behind a legitimate-looking denial, on the one path that creates outreach under someone's own name. Every dependency that throws degrades to a refusal, never to an unguarded create.

Every path returns a named reason (AC #5) — "nothing happened" and "nothing happened because the tier could not be resolved" are different facts.

## Other review points

- **Idempotency (AC #4) is a stamped `autoCreatedFromTemplateId`**, not an inference from the schedule's name — renaming is explicitly allowed by AC #6, and inferring would produce a duplicate.
- `already_exists` short-circuits every other predicate, because it is the only reason that means the system is working correctly.
- **AC #6**: an ordinary active `scheduled_chat` — no hidden flag, no undeletable marker, visible/editable/pausable like any other.
- All four template variables are filled; a blank one hard-fails the run before the model is called, which is why the template documents literal defaults.
- Split in two: the decision module has no I/O and no environment reads, so every predicate combination is testable without mocking DynamoDB or the subscription service; a wiring module holds the real deps.
- Hooked into `POST /api/onboarding/outreach/save` as **best-effort** — the prospects are already saved by then, so a failed auto-create must never turn a successful save into a customer-visible error. **With the flag off the response is byte-identical to before.**

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean; 19 tests; full sweep green apart from the 6 known pre-existing suites.

## Two deliberate stops

1. `OUTREACH_SCHEDULE_AUTO_CREATE_ENABLED` is unset — the shipped default.
2. ENG-1722's production template seed has not been run either, so `template_missing` is the honest answer in production today regardless of the flag.

Recommended order if enabling: seed the template → run with `dryRun: true` against a real customer → flip the flag.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Adds default-off, best-effort LinkedIn outreach schedule creation after onboarding prospect saves. Creation requires a connected LinkedIn account, an ICP lead list, eligible tier access, and a valid template. The service supports dry runs, fail-closed decisions, idempotency, and editable schedules. Failures do not affect prospect saving.

title: feat(billing): internal spend reconciliation, fidelity and basis divergence (ENG-1809)
body:
Slice 5 of ENG-1250 — the internal half of §8, and the evidence AC6 is waiting for.

Branches off `main` directly (slices 1–4 are all merged), so unlike the last three this one gets a real CodeRabbit review rather than being skipped for a stacked base.

## Two questions, not one

§8's internal check is really two questions with **opposite expected answers**:

| | Question | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| **Fidelity** | Does the shadow reproduce the vendor rows the live rail already writes? | **Zero drift.** Anything else means the mirror is losing, duplicating or mispricing events |
| **Basis divergence** | How much larger is all-vendor spend than the LLM-only figure the live gate enforces on? | **Non-zero** — quantifying it is the entire point |

Reporting one number for both would be useless. A large value could mean the mirror is broken (stop everything) or that vendors are simply a large share of spend (the expected finding). Those demand opposite responses.

The divergence figure is the one AC6 is actually waiting for: **how much sooner an account would hit its cap if enforcement moved to this rail.**

## Design decisions

- **Fidelity compares per (date, provider, operation), never as one total.** A single total nets a $5 overcount on one vendor against a $5 undercount on another and reports zero — the one answer that would wrongly clear this rail for enforcement. There's a test asserting exactly that: the netted total reads `0` while the verdict is still `false`.
- **Three failure kinds stay distinct** — ordinary drift; live vendor spend never mirrored (§8's *"a successful vendor call without a settled/voided event is an operational error"*); and shadow events with no live row, which is the inverse case and the more alarming one, since the shadow leading the live rail is exactly what #2793's ordering fix exists to prevent.
- **LLM rows are excluded from fidelity.** They were never mirrored, so counting them would manufacture drift equal to the entire LLM bill. Their comparison *is* the divergence check — which is the point of separating the two.
- **The divergence report carries `trustworthy`.** A divergence computed over a mirror that loses events **understates** the answer, and understating it argues for a cutover on false evidence.
- **An account with no LLM spend reports 0%, not `Infinity`.** Both are inventions; only one of them looks like a measurement.
- **`readyForCutoverEvidence` says the data is trustworthy and nothing more.** §9 also requires seven days of shadow running plus boundary and concurrency tests, and AC6 requires Harsha's explicit approval. Green is a precondition, not a verdict — a test pins that it tracks fidelity, not the size of the divergence.

## Scope

Pure functions over rows the caller fetches. No persistence, nothing scheduled, nothing that can move enforcement. The external invoice check is separate work.

## Testing

18 tests; typecheck clean. **All 11 mutations fail the suite**, including "verdict from the netted total", "LLM rows counted as vendor rows", "unmirrored vendor still counts as clean", "divergence always claims trustworthy", and "readiness driven by divergence size".


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

Adds pure billing spend reconciliation functions. The implementation compares shadow and live vendor spend, measures all-vendor versus LLM-only basis divergence, applies fidelity trust checks, and supports monthly reports. It changes no persistence, scheduling, or enforcement paths, so it does not create a production outage path.
