title: fix(billing): scope reconciliation fidelity to the dual-write period (ENG-1810)
body:
Follow-up to #2804, found by running the §8 reconciliation against production for the first time. Both bugs are invisible until real data with real history goes through it, which is why this exists rather than a unit test.

## The first run looked like a disaster and was not

Every vendor row reported **NOT MIRRORED** — 39 groups, twitter alone showing 21 unmirrored calls on 2026-09-07.

Correct arithmetic on the wrong question. The dual-write deployed at **~15:09Z** that day; twitter's last write was **08:20:50Z**, seven hours earlier:

```
twitter:get_user_tweets  calls=8  updatedAt=2026-09-07T08:19:52.714Z
twitter:post             calls=1  updatedAt=2026-09-07T08:20:50.875Z
you.com:query            calls=3  updatedAt=2026-09-07T15:30:28.625Z   <- first mirrored batch
```

Nothing was broken. The mirror did not exist yet for any of that traffic.

**The real defect is that fidelity could never go green.** History the mirror never saw is unmirrored by construction and always will be, so the check was permanently red — useless as the AC6 precondition it exists to be.

## Fix

- `mirrorStartedAt` scopes the check to the period the dual-write actually ran.
- Days wholly before it → `preMirrorGroups`, excluded from the verdict.
- The changeover day → `partialGroups`, also excluded. The live rail aggregates **per day**, so that row legitimately holds calls from both sides of the deploy and cannot be split; a shortfall there is expected, not a finding.
- **Totals now cover assessed groups only.** A large pre-mirror drift printed beside `ok: true` would make a reader who trusts the number over the verdict conclude the ledger is broken when it is merely young.

## The second bug, which the first fix exposed

With everything excluded, `fidelity.ok` was **vacuously true** — and the divergence printed as trustworthy while resting on no comparison at all.

I had guarded `readyForCutoverEvidence` against exactly this and missed the same hole in `trustworthy`. Both now require `assessedGroupCount > 0`. A green light produced by having no data is the worst failure this module could have, and worse than a red one, because it looks like evidence.

## Also lands

`scripts/spendReconciliationReport.ts` — read-only terminal report, so the shadow phase can be checked without hand-reading DynamoDB (§7's *"no admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause"*).

## The finding worth keeping

Divergence varies enormously by account:

| Subject | LLM-only | Vendor | New basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| `1743956381327` | $0.81 | $18.99 | **+2333%** |
| `e86420f2…` | $117.85 | $0.37 | +0.31% |

Not yet trustworthy — no full day assessed — but directionally this is the AC6 evidence, and it already says a flat cutover would hit some accounts vastly harder than others.

## Testing

25 tests; typecheck clean. **Six mutations fail the suite**, including "pre-mirror days still counted as failures", "totals include pre-mirror history again", "empty assessment counts as evidence", and "vacuous ok counts as trustworthy".


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium

Scopes billing reconciliation to the active dual-writing period. Excludes pre-mirror and changeover-day groups, limits totals to assessed groups, and prevents empty assessments from passing. Adds a read-only reconciliation report with pagination and cutover evidence. Includes 25 tests and passes typechecking.

- Pure discrimination gate (`l2Diagnose.ts`): evaluates all look-alike causes for a symptom, reaches `determined` only when exactly one cause is `supported`, otherwise honest `could_not_determine` with reason. Three verdict states (`ruled_out`/`supported`/`unchecked`) — `unchecked` causes are disclosed but excluded from the ruled-out requirement, so one permanently-unchecked cause (e.g. `budget_exhausted`, no evidence source in this codebase) never blocks a `determined` diagnosis when another cause is genuinely confirmed.
- Orchestration service (`l2DiagnoseService.ts`): composes evidence from `monitor_lead_volume` and `runMetaTrackingMonitor` (in-process, no HTTP self-call) for `leads_at_zero`. title: feat(billing): idempotent vendor usage writes, retry, and loss alerting (ENG-702 AC1/AC3/AC6)
body:
ENG-702 **AC1, AC3 and AC6** — the three criteria this row still had open.

> **Do not merge yet.** This row is headed *"data-plane gate — stop before merge for Harsha's explicit approval"*, and I have asked him on the ticket whether that still applies. See below.

## The ticket's evidence was six weeks stale

Re-verified every AC against `main` @ `8a3f7c4e2` before writing code. The row's evidence is dated `211045f2e` (2026-07-29):

| AC | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Same vendor event twice → spend once | **OPEN — this PR** | `RecordVendorUsageContext` had no idempotency field; `incrementUsage` is an unconditional `ADD` |
| 2. Retried internal batch doesn't double-count | already met | ENG-1251 |
| 3. Retry then surface | **OPEN — this PR** | `logRecorderFailure` swallowed; no retry, no counter |
| 4. LLM never blocks the caller | holds, preserved | untouched |
| 5. Reconcile spend vs vendor calls | already met | ENG-1809/1810 |
| 6. One alert per window | **OPEN — this PR** | the 60s throttle was a log line, not an alert |

## Why a transaction, not just a conditional put

`incrementUsageWithSpendEvent` writes the daily aggregate row and the immutable spend event in **one transaction**, conditional on the caller's token.

That's the property worth having: a replayed token no-ops the spend event **and** skips the aggregate's contribution *together*, never independently. Deduping only the new rail would have reproduced, on the vendor path, the exact defect ENG-1251 was raised to close on the LLM side — a retried batch deduping its charge event while its ledger contribution landed a second time.

Targets `AW-SpendEvents`, not `AW-LlmChargeEvents`, which declares itself *"deliberately LLM-only: it is not the future cross-vendor wallet"*. No TTL, since `AW-SpendEvents` is retained by decision.

## Adoption is incremental by design

A vendor context **without** an `idempotencyKey` keeps today's behaviour exactly — unconditional aggregate write, then the fail-open shadow mirror. Seven adapters can adopt one at a time rather than a flag day, and each becomes correct independently.

## Two deliberate choices

- **The idempotent path never throws.** Every caller invokes `recordVendorUsage` fire-and-forget, so a rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection and takes the process down — the crash I hit and fixed in #2793. AC3's *"surfaced rather than silently discarded"* is served by a counter and an alert, not by throwing into a caller that cannot catch it.
- **An unpriced call falls back to the plain write.** The billing boundary forbids an unpriced unit becoming a $0 spend event, so there is no event to make the aggregate idempotent against, and inventing one would be the silent $0 charge the boundary exists to prevent.

## On the data-plane gate

The row is headed *"creates a new persistent store"*, justified by *"a day's worth of call identifiers cannot live on the existing daily aggregate row."* That was true when written. It is not now: **`AW-SpendEvents` already is that store** — approved, created and deployed under ENG-1796 last week. This PR adds no table, no key change, no index and no retention change.

I have **not** waived the gate on my own reading — it is flagged for Harsha on the ticket. Holding until he answers.

## Testing

250 tests across nine affected suites; typecheck clean. **Ten mutations fail the suites.**

One initially did not, and it's worth recording why: the `CancellationReasons` index check is byte-identical in `incrementUsageWithChargeEvent`, so a whole-file substitution mutated the *LLM* function and the vendor test correctly ignored it. Re-targeted at the second occurrence, it fails as it should — a flaw in my mutation harness, not a gap in the test.


---

# AC3 and AC6

The defect, quoted from the row: *"a DynamoDB outage produces one log line and unbounded unattributed revenue loss, with **no counter of what was lost**."*

The missing counter is the real problem. A throttled log line tells you something failed; it cannot tell you **how much money stopped being recorded**, which is the only question worth asking during an outage. Drops are now counted with their micro-dollars, aggregated per provider, and reported.

## Two design points that are not obvious

**Surfaced is not thrown.** Every caller invokes `recordVendorUsage` fire-and-forget, so a rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection and takes the process down — metering killing the product it meters, a crash already shipped once in #2793. AC3 is served by a loud, countable, aggregated alert instead, which AC4's *"never blocks or fails the caller's operation"* points at anyway.

**Retry is gated on idempotency, and only the token path gets it.** There, AC1's conditional transaction makes a replay a no-op, so retrying costs nothing. On the tokenless legacy path the aggregate write is an unconditional `ADD`: if the first attempt landed and only its *response* was lost, a retry double-counts — the exact failure AC1 exists to prevent.

That path therefore **counts the loss but never retries**, failing toward under-counting, which reconciliation detects, rather than toward over-charging a customer, which it cannot undo.

## Other decisions

- **Permanent failures are not retried.** A `ValidationException` retried is just a slower failure, and it delays the alert saying spend is going unrecorded.
- **A transaction conflict *is* retried** — the write did not happen at all, so it is a transient nothing rather than a lost charge.
- **Three attempts, exponential backoff.** This runs inside a request's lifetime; a longer ladder turns a brownout into latency the customer feels for a row nothing reads synchronously.
- **AC6 aggregates per window**: a burst of a thousand failures in one minute produces **one** alert carrying all thousand — not a thousand alerts, which is the failure mode AC6 names and the reason nobody reads them.
- **The first successful write after an outage flushes the final window.** Windows otherwise close only when a *later* drop arrives, so when failures **stop** — exactly when someone starts investigating — the last and often largest batch would never be reported. Cheaper and more reliable than a timer, since it fires precisely when there is evidence the rail is healthy again.

## Testing

279 tests across ten affected suites; typecheck clean. **Nineteen mutations fail across both halves**, including "permanent errors retried too", "alert per record not per window", "lost money not accumulated", "final window never flushed" and "recovery flush removed".


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium. Adds transactional, idempotent vendor usage writes and retry handling. Adds provider-level dropped-write monitoring with recovery-aware alerts. Legacy tokenless and unpriced-call behavior remains unchanged. The fail-open path limits production outage risk, but billing writes and alert state require careful rollback validation.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix: modify_work_plan cross-call removeStepCounts bypass + full ENG-1808 closure (ENG-1811)
body:
## Summary

Fixes a critical, live-discovered regression on top of PR #2794 (already merged/deployed): the `removeStepCounts` drop-protection shipped there only survives within a single `modify_work_plan` tool call. Splitting a remove-then-re-add across two separate, ordinary tool calls defeats it completely — and this happened organically, unprompted, on test-env1 while live-testing the previous PR.

## ENG-1811 — cross-call bypass

**Root cause:** #2794's fix snapshotted pre-removal step state (`originalStepsBeforeRemoval`) and checked `removeStepCounts?.includes(newStep.stepCount)` — both scoped to a single `modifyWorkPlan` invocation. Each tool call is an independent function call with its own fresh session read and its own `removeStepCounts` argument. Live-observed sequence on test-env1 (session `88fd7752-828a-4158-b837-0ee22a7fe200`):

1. Model tries 3x to complete a step requiring `list_html_templates` (never succeeds). Correctly blocked each time.
2. `modify_work_plan` call A: `removeStepCounts: [2, 3]`, no re-add.
3. A **separate, later** `modify_work_plan` call B re-adds steps 2 and 3 with `requiredFunctionCalls` omitted — call B has no `removeStepCounts` (it isn't removing anything), so it has zero memory of call A's removal.
4. Both steps complete with `requiredFunctionCalls: []`. `list_html_templates` never succeeded, ever, the whole session.

**Fix:** replace the per-call snapshot with a session-level, stepCount-agnostic debt ledger (`workPlan.pendingRequiredFunctionCalls`). Since `workPlan` is read fresh and written back on every call, this survives any number of separate invocations. `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt` refuses to let a batch resolve the last remaining pending step(s) — finish the plan — while any ledger entry hasn't genuinely succeeded, regardless of which step (if any) still lists it. Unrelated, still-in-progress steps keep completing normally; only the moment the plan would otherwise look done is gated. Entries auto-clear once satisfied.

## ENG-1808 — fully closed, not just narrowed

The user asked to close ENG-1808 (N-to-M consolidation: remove steps 2 AND 3, re-add only step 2, step 3's number never reused) fully in this same PR, since the ENG-1811 fix's design generalizes to it directly. Since the ledger isn't scoped to stepCount reuse at all — only to whether the function has genuinely succeeded before the plan finishes — this closes ENG-1808's `requiredFunctionCalls` case completely, not just for the reused-number pattern.

`expectedAssetCount`/`expectedAssetCountTools` have no equivalent session-level ledger yet (the "produced count" calculation is inherently step-relative, harder to genericize) — the existing per-call reattachment is kept as a best-effort guard for same-call reuse; this narrower residual is called out explicitly, not silently left unaddressed.

## Tests

Six new tests replacing the one that pinned the now-superseded per-call mechanism:
- Same-call remove+reuse, `requiredFunctionCalls` omitted — debt recorded, plan-finish blocked.
- **Cross-call** (the exact live exploit): removal and re-addition in two separate `modifyWorkPlan` calls — debt survives.
- Debt clears once genuinely satisfied, unblocks plan-finish.
- Debt does NOT block an unrelated, still-in-progress step — only plan-finish.
- **ENG-1808's exact original scenario** — fully blocked, then correctly unblocks once both debts are paid.
- (Existing suite: 85 tests in the ENG-1799/1800 describe blocks, all still passing.)

**Mutation-verified:** reverted the fix (`git stash`), reran — 3 of 4 directly-dependent new tests fail with clear signals (the "unrelated step" negative control correctly passes either way), the ENG-1808 test also fails cleanly. Restored, full 85-test file passes. `npm run typecheck` clean. Full 186-suite/3769-test pre-push hook green (hub-file triggered since `chatbotService.ts` is touched too), rebased onto latest `main`.

## Not merging yet

Per explicit instruction: fresh-eyes review (subagent) + live-testing on test-env1 both still pending before merge.

  - Re-added steps maintain accurate asset requirements without duplicating same-call requirements.
  - Work-plan completion is prevented until all outstanding required actions are fulfilled.
  - Fulfilled requirements are cleared automatically, allowing plans to complete normally once all required work is finished.
  - LinkedIn sent-invitation listings now more reliably combine available live and cached results.
- **New Features**
  - Added the `diagnose_leads_at_zero` tool to the admin skill set.

<sub>⚠️ Note: Your high-level summary instructions were not applied because this feature is currently available only on Essentials plans or higher.</sub>
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

---

## Update: fresh-eyes review found and fixed a real regression

**Blocking, reproduced:** the `pendingRequiredFunctionCalls` debt check compared against `calledFunctionCounts`, a local copy that gets decremented in-place (once per required call) as this same batch's own steps pass their gates above (the pre-existing ENG-1698 credit-consumption mechanic). If a debt name is **also** genuinely required and satisfied by the step currently completing in the exact same batch, that step's own gate consumes the shared credit and drives the local copy to 0 — making a real, same-turn success look like it never happened, and **permanently** blocking the plan from ever finishing (a blocked gate persists nothing, so retrying the identical batch fails identically forever).

The reviewer reproduced this independently before reporting it — a session with a pending debt for `list_html_templates`, a single pending step whose own `requiredFunctionCalls` is exactly that function, called once and genuinely succeeding, got permanently blocked. I re-verified with my own mutation test before fixing (fails pre-fix with `Expected: true, Received: false`, matching the reviewer's exact reproduction).

**Fix:** read `session.calledFunctions` directly for this specific check — the raw snapshot captured once at the top of the function, confirmed via grep to never be mutated in-place elsewhere. A debt is a "did this genuinely happen, ever" fact check, not a shared-pool credit-consumption check like the per-step gates are.

Everything else the reviewer checked (ledger population/union correctness, enforcement placement and all-or-nothing persistence discipline, the "doesn't block unrelated in-progress steps" claim, auto-clear reaching persistence, type consistency on both read/write sides, no regression to the existing `existingIndex>=0` edit path, and confirmation that the `expectedAssetCount`/`expectedAssetCountTools` scope limit is genuinely disclosed not hidden) came back clean.

Full 164-suite/3571-test pre-push hook green on the branch (rebased onto latest `main`) before this push. Still not merged — live-testing on test-env1 for this specific fix next.

## Update: round-3 & round-4 review — one more real bypass found and fixed, one narrower gap disclosed and ticketed

**Round 3 finding (blocking, reproduced with an executed repro):** the debt ledger's only *enforcement* point is `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt`, which only runs on a `set_work_plan_status` call. A caller could bypass it entirely by deleting the last remaining `'pending'` step(s) via `modify_work_plan` and simply never re-adding them or calling `set_work_plan_status` again — since no step is left `'pending'`, every other "is the plan done" check in the codebase (`workPlan.steps.every(completed|skipped)`, with no debt awareness) would report the plan fully done. Confirmed independently before fixing.

**Fix:** `AgentModeService.buildWorkPlanContextMessages` (and its `buildMarketingContext`/Emma callers) and two `workPlanCompleted` checks in `agentModeController.ts`'s scheduled/verified-chat retry loop now resolve `pendingRequiredFunctionCalls` against real `calledFunctions` instead of inferring completion from step status alone. A genuinely-done-but-debted plan now gets an explicit "❌ This plan is NOT actually finished" banner instead of "✅ ALL STEPS ARE DONE".

**Self-caught regression while fixing this:** first attempt called a new `AgentModeService.isWorkPlanFullyResolved` static from `agentModeController.ts`. ~150 test files in this suite mock `'../services/agentModeService'` as a bare `{ agentModeService: {...} }` object with no `AgentModeService` class export — calling the class from this heavily-mocked controller file broke 2 real suites (`agentModeController.publishPressBreaker.test.ts`, `agentModeController.workPlanScheduledChat.test.ts`, 11 tests). Caught via a full (non-`--bail`) local run before it reached CI, reverted to a local, self-contained `workPlanCompletedWithoutDebt()` function in `agentModeController.ts` (same logic, zero cross-module dependency) — full 271-suite/5041-test pre-push hook green after the revert.

**Round 4 (this newest fix) findings, each independently verified:**
- No drift between the two now-separate implementations (`isWorkPlanFullyResolved` vs `workPlanCompletedWithoutDebt`) — read both bodies side by side, byte-identical logic.
- `calledFunctions` freshness at both controller call sites — correct, no new race.
- `buildWorkPlanContextMessages`'s new early-return branch vs the old "all done" branch — mutually exclusive, exhaustive, correctly ordered.
- **Real test-coverage gap:** `workPlanCompletedWithoutDebt` (the controller's own copy, actually gating the scheduled-chat retry loop) was never exercised directly — only its service-level twin was tested. Added two tests driving it through the real retry loop. First draft of one test passed even under a reverted (debt-blind) mutant — a stale keyword fixture was gating it, not the debt check — caught via the mutation-test discipline and fixed by isolating the schedule's keyword/function requirements.
- **Real but narrower gap, deliberately NOT fixed here:** `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan`/`workPlanHasPendingStep` (the *autocomplete self-continuation* trigger, a different mechanism from the enforcement gate above) has no debt awareness either. If an autocomplete plan's model deletes its last pending step in the same turn (creating debt) and that `modify_work_plan` call succeeds, the autocomplete loop's own "did this turn make progress" short-circuit fires before it would ever check for debt, so no further auto-continuation round gets scheduled — the run just goes quiet. This does **not** reopen the core guarantee: the ledger is still correctly persisted, `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt` still correctly blocks the plan from ever being reported finished, and the now-fixed context banner is still correct on the next turn — it only means the *unattended self-nudge* loop specifically won't chase the debt down on its own. Filed as [ENG-1813](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1813/hasstalledautocompleteworkplan-doesnt-check-eng-1811-debt-an) rather than expanding this already-twice-self-corrected, urgent PR further.

Full 271-suite/5041-test pre-push hook green on the branch (rebased onto latest `main`) after each of the above. Still not merged — live-testing this newest fix on test-env1 next, per the standing "test until satisfied, then merge, then live-verify on production" instruction.

title: feat(billing): adopt the vendor idempotency token in v0 (ENG-1812)
body:
First adapter to adopt [[ENG-702]] AC1's idempotency token. Part of [[ENG-1250]] §6.

## Why v0 first

[[ENG-702]] names it as one of the two dangerous retry-heavy paths: *"the v0 code documents in its own comments that a retried correction can be applied and charged twice"*, and *"the v0 retry loop books duplicates under one reservation"*. It is also the only adapter that already had a canonical idempotency notion to reuse, so it sets the shape for the other eight.

## The unit of charge is one per RESERVATION, not per attempt

`meteredV0` returns a **thunk**, and `withRetry` re-invokes it. So every retry inside one reservation booked another charge — exactly the defect the row names.

The token now comes from `v0UsageGuard` itself, via a new `meteringKeyFor(guardKey, reservedAt)`:

* Every `withRetry` attempt inside one reservation shares the key → the transactional write collapses them into **one** charge.
* A guard-permitted retry after a failure mints a **new** reservation, so a new key, and is charged in full — because it really did call v0 again.

Deriving it from the guard rather than inventing a parallel notion is the point. Two independent definitions of "the same v0 call" would drift, and the failure would be silent: the guard deduping while the ledger charged twice, or the reverse.

## Adoption shape for the remaining adapters

The guards' callbacks now receive the key (`create(meteringKey)` / `send(meteringKey)`). A plain `() => Promise<T>` stays assignable in TypeScript, so this was backward compatible and adoption stays per-call-site — 11 of 11 v0 metering sites threaded, verified by grep, with no change to retry or guard semantics.

## Testing

59 tests across the four v0 suites, 239 across all fourteen affected; typecheck clean. Four mutations fail, including "reservation time dropped from key" and "guard key dropped from key" — the two ways the identity could silently become too coarse or too fine.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium. The v0 billing adapter now uses reservation-scoped vendor idempotency keys. Retries within one reservation share one charge. New reservations receive new keys. All 11 v0 metering sites pass the key without changing retry or guard semantics. Typecheck passes; four mutation tests fail.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(security): only an admin may publish a schedule template platform-wide (ENG-1716)
body:
Closes the authorization gap found while scoping ENG-1609. Base is `main`; independent of the ENG-1609 stack.

## The hole

`PUT /api/agent-mode/schedule-templates/:templateId` wrote whatever `visibility` the caller sent, behind an **ownership check only**:

```ts
if (visibility !== undefined) updates.visibility = visibility;
```

So any authenticated user could promote their own private template to `system` or `public` and put it in every user's template picker — skipping the review workflow that exists for exactly this decision (`submitForReview` → admin `approveTemplate`) and is reachable one route over. The sibling **create** route gets this right: it hardcodes `visibility: 'private' as const` and ignores the body field. Only update leaked.

**Why it's worse than a normal authz slip:** a schedule template carries a `startingMessage` — an agent prompt — plus `requiredFunctionCalls`, so a platform-wide one is prompt-injection surface reaching every customer's agent. And `createScheduleFromTemplate` **copies** `startingMessage` onto the schedule at creation, so revoking the template afterwards does not undo schedules already made from it. There is no clean rollback.

## The fix

`utils/scheduleTemplateVisibility.ts` — the decision as a pure function, no I/O:

| Target | Who |
|---|---|
| `system`, `public` | admin only |
| `private` ⇄ `pending_review` | the owner (mirrors `submitForReview`, plus withdrawing a submission) |
| anything else | rejected, not persisted |

Refused **explicitly** (403/400), never silently dropped — AC #1 calls that out specifically, because a silent drop is how the `manage_schedule_template` confusion started.

## Two things beyond the ticket

- **The legacy `platform` alias was a live bypass.** `scheduleTemplateService.normalizeVisibility` rewrites a stored `'platform'` to `'system'` on **read** — so a non-admin could write `'platform'`, which is not in the enum and not obviously a promotion, and every reader would then report `'system'`. Aliases are folded **before** the authorization decision, not after.
- **The route accepted any string at all**, so `visibility: 'nonsense'` became a stored value no reader understands. Now a 400.

## AC #4 — the MCP schema

`manage_schedule_template` advertised all four values while routing `create` to an endpoint that hardcodes `private`, so Emma asking for a `system` template silently got a private one. Its enum is now the two values the route can honour, and the description states that `create` always produces a private template and that `system`/`public` are admin-only.

## AC #5 — audit of existing non-private rows

Read-only production scan: **6 rows — 5 `private`, 1 `public`, 0 `system`.**

The `public` row ("Multi-Campaign Performance Report") is owned by a **non-admin** and carries **no `reviewFeedback` attribute** — which `submitForReview` always writes (`reviewFeedback: ''`). So it never passed through the review workflow. It was set public either by an admin via the admin route or by its owner via this unprotected PUT; the stored data cannot distinguish those.

**Not demoted.** AC #5 says report rather than demote, and it has live usage — pulling it would break schedules referencing it.

## Unchanged

The admin route (`adminScheduleTemplateRoutes`, `isAdmin`-gated) is untouched and remains the way a `system` template is created (AC #3).

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean. **1675 suites / 29576 tests pass, zero failures.** 16 policy tests (the promotion refusal, the `platform` alias, unknown values, each permitted self-service transition, admins, and that restating an unchanged value needs no privilege so a whole-object PUT keeps working) plus 6 driving the real route.

⚠️ **Note for the next authz test in `scheduleTemplates.test.ts`:** its default `mockUser` has `isAdmin: true`, so a non-admin case must name its caller explicitly. The first cut of these tests passed against unprotected code because of it.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium. The schedule-template update route now enforces visibility authorization. Non-admins can use only `private` and `pending_review`; admins can set valid values. Invalid values and `platform` are rejected. MCP schema guidance now matches policy. Tests and type checking pass.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix: hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan doesn't check ENG-1811 debt ledger (ENG-1813)
body:
## Summary

Fixes ENG-1813, found during round-4 review of PR #2808 (the ENG-1811 debt-ledger fix): `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` has no awareness of the ENG-1811 debt ledger (`workPlan.pendingRequiredFunctionCalls`).

## The bug

An autocomplete work plan's `modify_work_plan` call that deletes the last pending step while creating genuine ENG-1811 debt (a removed step's required function call that never actually succeeded) is itself a *successful* tool call. The pre-existing ENG-1684/1700 short-circuit (`calls.some(toolCallSucceeded) -> not stalled`) called this turn "not stalled" even though no real required work got done — so no further auto-continuation round ever fired to go satisfy the debt. The unattended run just goes quiet.

**Does not reopen ENG-1811's core guarantee.** The session-level `pendingRequiredFunctionCalls` ledger is still correctly populated and persisted; `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt` still correctly blocks the plan from ever being reported "finished" while debt is outstanding; `buildWorkPlanContextMessages` still correctly surfaces the debt on the next turn. This only restores the autocomplete self-nudge loop's ability to chase the debt down on its own instead of going quiet.

## Fix

Two new helpers in `agentModeController.ts`:
- `workPlanHasUnresolvedDebt(workPlan, calledFunctions)` — resolves `pendingRequiredFunctionCalls` against real `calledFunctions`.
- `workPlanHasUnfinishedAutocompleteWork(workPlan, calledFunctions)` — combined "pending step OR unresolved debt" check.

`hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` now checks debt *before* the succeeded-call short-circuit (media-deferral exclusion still takes priority over both). The other 3 call sites that previously used the bare `workPlanHasPendingStep` (`scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation`'s pre-fire re-check, its timeout-catch re-read, and the whole-turn-timeout branch) now use the combined check, each threading `calledFunctions` from the session object already in scope.

## Tests

5 new tests in `agentModeController.stalledAutocompletePlan.test.ts`:
- Fires when a `modify_work_plan` call succeeded this turn but left genuine debt unresolved (and confirms the OLD behavior really would have missed it, via the same scenario with debt stripped out).
- Does not fire once the debt function has genuinely succeeded.
- Never fires on an interactive (non-autocomplete) plan.
- Media-budget deferral still wins over unresolved debt.
- An empty `pendingRequiredFunctionCalls` array behaves exactly like no debt.

**Mutation-verified:** reverted the fix, confirmed the key regression-guard test fails cleanly (`Expected: true, Received: false`), restored, all pass. Full local suite green both before and after the merge onto latest `main` (80 suites / 1159 tests via the path-filtered pre-push hook). `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Scope note

This branch was originally intended to also cover ENG-1814 and ENG-1807. ENG-1807 is being handled separately by another agent. ENG-1814's fix is still in design (root-caused, direction decided — A: shrink `list_predefined_work_plans`'s response using the existing ENG-1469 safe projection, B: add an ambiguity/confirmation check in `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` — not yet implemented) and will land in its own follow-up PR.

title: ENG-1807: reconstruct real tool-call ledger on a mid-run scheduled-chat exception
body:
## Summary
`runScheduledChat`'s catch block used to persist a permanently-wrong `test-history` record — `actualFunctionCalls: []`, `passed: false` — whenever the run hit ANY exception (e.g. a worker-drain mid-deploy), even when the run had already completed everything required and `persistIncrementally` had already written it to the session before a later step (title generation, etc.) hit the error. For production runs this got masked later by the resume/reconciler path; test runs never get that lease (`isTest` gate, deliberate — "never requeued"), so the wrong empty result was permanent, not interim.

- Reuses `reconstructPriorToolCalls` (already used by the ENG-657 resume path) to rebuild the real ledger from the session's own persisted messages before writing the error result, then recomputes `functionCallMatches`/`functionCallMisses`/`passed` against it.
- Guarded on `recoveredToolCalls.length > 0` — a schedule with zero required function calls can't flip to `passed:true` merely because there's nothing to miss; only genuine evidence of recovered activity produces a pass.
- **Same-class follow-up fix**: a resumed run's persisted `actualFunctionCalls` (the raw audit list) didn't prepend `resumePriorToolCalls`, unlike the `passed` verdict computed from it a few lines below — under-reporting what actually happened on a correctly-scored, passing run.
- Deliberately NOT touched: the `isTest`/lease/resume-marker gates that decide whether an interrupted TEST run gets auto-resumed later — that's a separate, documented policy choice ("Skipped for test runs, which are never requeued"), not part of this bug.

title: feat(billing): route every vendor write through the atomic path (ENG-1250 §6)
body:
Finishes §6 adoption for the six remaining adapters — **by not threading a token through them**.

## Why the original plan was wrong

I planned one PR per adapter. Investigating the first showed that shape buys nothing:

| Adapter | Retry behaviour |
|---|---|
| You.com / Google CSE | **no retry at all** — bare axios, no interceptor |
| X/Twitter | `withRetryOn401` meters **only on success**, so a 401 attempt is never charged |
| Apollo / enrich.so | the `attempt < 3` loops are **DynamoDB quota bookkeeping**, not vendor retries |
| Remotion | no retry |

None has a natural pre-call identifier, and none re-enters metering on a retry. A call-site token there would be a freshly minted nonce — exactly what `buildShadowEvent` already mints — delivered by editing **eleven sites across six files for no semantic gain**.

Worth recording: ENG-702's claim that *"You.com retries up to 4× on the provider's own throttle signal"* is **not true of today's code**. It was verified at `211045f2e` in July.

## What this does instead

Every vendor call takes the atomic path, token or not. That buys the six adapters something real:

- the aggregate row and the spend event move together in **one transaction** instead of two independent writes
- **AC3's retry becomes safe on every path**, because a replay cannot double-count. Before this the tokenless path could not be retried at all — its unconditional `ADD` would double-count after a lost response

Both now extend to any vendor added later with no further edit.

A call-site token still wins where one genuinely exists: v0 supplies the guard's key (#2809) and collapses retries within one reservation. This doesn't replace that — it raises the floor for everyone else.

## Fallback, so this cannot make things worse

If the transaction fails after retries, the pre-ENG-702 path still runs and lands the **live** row. A spend-ledger outage must not also stop the metering that predates it, turning one table's problem into lost attribution on both. The fallback leaves the rails divergent — live row, no event — which §8 already reports as `unmirroredGroups`. Detectable and honest.

**A test caught a bug in that fallback:** when the fallback *also* failed, both catches recorded the loss — counting one failed write twice and inflating the lost-dollars figure AC3 exists to make trustworthy. The fallback now suppresses its own counting.

## Testing

273 tests across the 15 affected suites; typecheck clean. Three mutations fail, including "fallback double-counts the loss" and "tokenless skips the atomic path".

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium

Route all vendor usage writes through the atomic aggregate-plus-spend-event path, including tokenless calls. If atomic retries fail, fall back to the legacy aggregate write and record lost ledger writes once. This preserves metering behavior and prevents duplicate loss accounting. Testing covered 273 tests across 15 suites, with typechecking passing.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: [needs human] Stop misclassifying publisher refusals as AgentWeb auth failures (ENG-1162)
body:
**What was wrong:** In the ENG-1162 reference session, `read_file_content` hit HTTP 403 twice on files.gao.gov and `playwright_browser_navigate` hit `net::ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` on ramaonhealthcare.com. Both errors flowed through `classifyToolErrorClass` (backend/src/utils/toolErrorClassifier.ts), where any message containing a bare 401/403 status is swept into the generic `auth` class, whose model-visible next-step guidance says 'Tell the user to (re)connect the account or fix permissions.' That's nonsensical for an anonymous external URL fetch (there is no AgentWeb account involved), and — more importantly — it gave the model no signal that a failed read is NOT evidence the content doesn't exist, so the run silently degraded to search-based verification instead of reporting the source as unverified.

**What changed:**
- `readFileContent` (backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts) now tags a 401/403 from its external-URL (non-S3, non-Drive) fetch branch with an explicit 'The publisher refused this fetch...' marker in both the `message` and `error` fields it returns.
- `classifyToolErrorClass` (backend/src/utils/toolErrorClassifier.ts) now recognizes that marker, plus any `net::ERR_*` browser-navigation failure text (Chromium/Playwright's stable network-error prefix), and classifies both into a new `publisher_refused` class — checked ahead of the generic embedded-HTTP-status regex so it isn't shadowed by the literal '403' in its own marker text.
- `errorRetryability.ts` adds model-visible guidance for `publisher_refused`: not an AgentWeb account problem, not evidence the content is missing, try an alternate path once or report the source as unverified rather than silently dropping the candidate.
- A bare, unmarked 401/403 (e.g. from a real connected-account API like Meta/LinkedIn) is untouched and still classifies as `auth` — verified with existing + new tests.

**How verified:** Reproduced the misclassification directly (classifyToolErrorClass on 'net::ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE...' and on read_file_content's real HTTP-403 error text both returned 'auth'/unclassified with the wrong 'reconnect the account' guidance before the fix, confirmed the guidance became correct after). Added a failing-then-passing unit test for read_file_content's 401/403 handling and for the classifier's new `publisher_refused` routing (including a regression check that unrelated bare 401/403 messages still classify as `auth`). Ran the full affected test surface (readFileContent, toolErrorClassifier, agentToolGatewayService, toolDispatch characterization, and both read_file_content Emma-tool test files) — 258/258 passing — plus `npx tsc` clean.

title: [needs human] Configure Express trust proxy for ALB -> nginx -> Node topology (ENG-493)
body:
**Bug:** Express never called `app.set('trust proxy', ...)`. In prod (ALB -> nginx -> Node, nginx proxying to Node over loopback) this meant `req.ip` was always the loopback socket address for every request, regardless of the real client — confirmed via a live prod nginx access log (nginx's `$remote_addr` is always one of a small set of internal ALB private IPs, while the real client IP is separately present via the ALB's own `X-Forwarded-For`). Any IP-keyed control — including `authRateLimiter` in `routes/auth.ts`, `leadMagnet.ts`'s 5/day IP limiter, and `waitlist.ts`'s 5/minute signup limiter — was a de facto single global bucket shared by every caller instead of one per client.

**Fix:** `app.set('trust proxy', 2)` in `backend/src/app.ts`, trusting exactly 2 hops (nginx's loopback connection, then the ALB's private address that nginx appends via `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`) so `req.ip` resolves to the real client IP. Verified the hop-count math against `proxy-addr`/`express`'s actual numeric-trust semantics in `node_modules` rather than assuming, and separately re-confirmed live against prod by spoofing `X-Forwarded-For` and reading the raw header chain Node actually received (exactly 2 trailing hops, no CDN/WAF in front). Also refreshed stale code comments in `routes/leadMagnet.ts` and `routes/webhooks.ts` that described trust proxy as unset/deferred — `webhooks.ts`'s forward-lead handler intentionally still reads `x-forwarded-for` manually (leftmost, for Meta CAPI match quality) rather than `req.ip`, which is correct either way and unrelated to this fix.

**Known dependency, documented in code, not enforced by it:** the hop count is only correct as long as the ALB's own `routing.http.xff_header_processing.mode` stays `"append"` (default) and `xff_client_port.enabled` stays off — both confirmed live-current, but they're AWS load balancer attributes, not app code, so nothing here guards against future infra drift. See the comment above `app.set('trust proxy', 2)` for the full reasoning.

**Verification:**
- `backend/src/__tests__/trustProxy.test.ts` — imports the real app, proves the pre-existing `auth.ts` login/register limiter now gives distinct real callers independent budgets, including a spoofed-leftmost-XFF boundary case (fails at hop count 3, passes at 2).
- `backend/src/__tests__/leadMagnetTrustProxy.test.ts` — same proof for `leadMagnet.ts`'s IP limiter, the endpoint the issue's own manual-test plan named but which had no prior automated coverage.
- `backend/src/__tests__/waitlistSignupTrustProxy.test.ts` — same proof for `waitlist.ts`'s signup limiter, a third `req.ip`-keyed consumer found by sweeping the codebase, not originally named in the issue.

title: fix: launch_predefined_work_plan can silently launch the wrong near-duplicate template (ENG-1814)
body:
## Summary

Fixes ENG-1814: `launch_predefined_work_plan` can silently launch the wrong near-duplicate template. Live-reproduced on production (2026-09-07) while re-verifying ENG-1794's fix — asked for "Founder LinkedIn Sales Readiness **Audit**", the model instead launched "...**Eval**". This is the exact same template pair ENG-1794's own incident report cites, hit a second time via a different mechanism.

## Root cause (3 compounding issues, all confirmed by direct code read — see full trail in the commit message and `workplan-brain/nodes/bug-eng1814.md`)

1. The system prompt itself instructs the model to call `list_predefined_work_plans` before `launch_predefined_work_plan` for the most common phrasing — not an edge case.
2. `list_predefined_work_plans` returned every accessible template's full legacy shape (description, userInstructions, skillIds, requiredFunctionCalls per step) *alongside* the already-built ENG-1469 safe `display` projection, redundantly, with no cap — trivially exceeds the platform's fixed 8,000-char tool-response-to-S3 threshold, forcing the model into a fragile multi-step `search_tool_response`/`read_tool_response` detour just to find a title.
3. That detour has zero disambiguation logic — when two near-duplicate titles both match a plausible query, nothing tells the model which one it meant. The matching logic in `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` itself is not at fault — it correctly launches exactly the title it's given; the wrong title gets picked upstream, during the detour.

## Fix — two changes, both reusing already-proven patterns in this codebase

**A.** `list_predefined_work_plans` (`apiTools.ts`) now returns only the compact ENG-1469 `display` shape plus a few top-level fields, instead of the full bloated legacy shape. `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` never consumed this tool's output anyway (it re-fetches its own candidates independently), so nothing needed the bloated shape. Reduces how often the detour triggers at all.

**B.** `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` (`agentModeService.ts`) now detects when a title-based match (not a stable planId) has a near-duplicate sibling in the accessible set — same word count, exactly one differing token, narrow by design to avoid over-triggering on genuinely distinct templates — and returns `{success:false, requiresConfirmation:true}` instead of launching, reusing the exact response shape the pre-existing "plan already active" guard in this same function already established. A planId-based match is exempt (unambiguous by construction) — that's also the retry path the response message points the model at once a human disambiguates.

A third direction (threading the raw user message down for a verbatim-provenance check) was considered and rejected — higher plumbing cost across 4-5 files for a weaker guarantee than B, since natural phrasing legitimately never contains the literal stored title anyway (the same gap ENG-1794's normalizer exists to smooth over).

## Blast-radius review

Checked every real caller and adjacent path:
- The "accept recommended plan" endpoint always calls `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` by planId (pre-validated via `resolveAccessiblePredefinedWorkPlan`, which itself never matches by title) — architecturally exempt already.
- `recommend_predefined_work_plan` takes planId only — same exemption.
- `createSessionWithPlan` (customer-portal `:planTitle` URL route) has its own fully independent inline title-matching, never calls `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` — out of scope, since that route is driven by a URL param (a human/marketing link), not an LLM reading a search result.
- Confirmed the new failure response integrates correctly with the existing `toolCallSucceeded`/`hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` machinery (same-day ENG-1813 fix) — a blocked launch during an autocomplete plan correctly triggers a retry nudge rather than going silently unretried.

## Tests — deliberate behavior change, handled explicitly, zero silent regressions

Three existing tests in `agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts` (2 for the LinkedIn Eval/Audit pair, 1 for the GTM Eval/Audit pair) previously asserted a **direct launch** for these near-duplicate pairs — updated to assert the new confirmation-required behavior instead, with the reason recorded inline (per this repo's own testing rule: an invariant that no longer applies is updated with the reason, not quietly forced green). Added:
- Coverage for the planId-retry escape hatch (both pairs).
- Two guards proving the ambiguity check does **not** over-trigger — different word count, or differing in more than one token — so genuinely distinct templates are unaffected.
- Dedicated `mcp.workPlanTools.test.ts` coverage proving the bloated legacy fields are actually stripped (zero prior coverage existed for this).

**Mutation-verified both A and B independently** — reverted each fix, confirmed the dedicated tests fail cleanly (exact expected-vs-received mismatches, not crashes), restored, all green again.

Full local suite green both before and after merging onto latest `main`: 163 suites / 3644 tests via the path-filtered pre-push hook. `npm run typecheck` clean throughout.

title: fix: report an unwritten CRM engagement as unwritten, and never skip the visibility CAS (ENG-1719, ENG-1716)
body:
Two Major defects CodeRabbit surfaced against **already-merged** code. Both are live on `main`; neither is in the PR whose review turned them up.

## 1. An unwritten CRM engagement was reported as written (ENG-1719, `3bed557d0`)

`recordInviteWithdrawnInCrm` returned `{ leadId, listId }` even when it appended **nothing** — the lead vanished mid-retry, or contention outlived `MAX_ATTEMPTS`. The stale-invitation drain sets `recorded = true` on any non-throw, so a missing `linkedin.invite.withdrawn` entry landed in the run report as a successful CRM write.

That is a hole in the exact code added to *stop* swallowing these failures: `crmRecordFailed` exists precisely because nothing re-runs this write, and it was under-reporting.

The recorder now returns `engagementLogged` — the same signal `mirrorLinkedInInviteToCrm` has always returned — and the drain treats an explicit `false` as not-recorded, while still treating `null` (no lead to attach to) as nothing-to-miss.

## 2. The visibility no-op skipped the compare-and-swap (ENG-1716, `326727eb7`)

`resolveVisibilityUpdate` returned a **write** for a canonical no-op. For a legacy stored `'platform'`, both sides canonicalize to `'system'` — so the route wrote `visibility` while its own is-this-changing test, comparing those same canonical values, found them equal and **skipped the CAS**.

An owner's stale request could then restore `system` after an administrator had demoted the template: an authorization regression on the one path where the CAS was load-bearing.

The no-op branch now emits no write at all. Normalising a legacy value belongs in a migration, not in an unguarded write on the user route.

## Verification

`npm run typecheck` clean · **1680 suites / 29694 tests, zero failures**.

New tests: the drain classifies `engagementLogged: false` as not-recorded (and `true`/`null` as recorded); the policy emits no write for every same-value restatement, including both spellings of the legacy alias. Two existing assertions updated for the new shapes.

## How these were found — worth knowing

[#2797](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/2797)'s GitHub **merge-base was stale**: `base.ref` said `main` while `base.sha` still pointed at a superseded branch head, so CodeRabbit reviewed a **46-file** diff instead of that PR's actual **4**. Most of what it raised was other people's merged code and is deliberately **not** actioned here. These two were ours, and were real.

If you retarget a stacked PR, check `pulls/:n` `base.sha` actually moved before trusting any review of it.

Risk: Medium

CRM withdrawal recording now reports `engagementLogged` accurately, including missing-lead and retry-exhaustion outcomes. CRM retries now back off after each failed attempt without delaying the final attempt. Visibility updates suppress canonical no-op writes, including legacy `'platform'` values. Tests cover both fixes. Verification passed typecheck and 1,680 suites with 29,694 tests.

title: fix(ci): teach the metering coverage guard to see helper indirection (ENG-1797)
body:
The guard could not see metering that goes through a helper, so `v0Service.ts` was **simultaneously metered in reality and allowlisted as unmetered** — and a change removing that metering shipped green, which is the one thing ENG-701 exists to prevent.

## Cause

`isMetered` required a **direct** import of `recordUsage`/`recordVendorUsage` from `usageRecorderService`. `v0Service` meters all eleven of its call sites through `meteredV0` and never imports the recorder itself, so the check returned false, the staleness detector never fired, and the allowlist entry claiming *"none record usage yet"* stayed as a standing amnesty.

## Fix

It now follows **one hop**: a module counts as metered when a local helper it imports is itself directly metered **and** the imported name is actually called there.

One hop is deliberate — it covers the helper pattern in use and keeps this a pure, terminating function over the in-memory file map. Arbitrary depth would need cycle handling and would start calling a module "metered" on the strength of a relationship no reader of that file could see. **A fixture asserts the second hop is not followed.**

The imported name must be *called*, not merely imported — the same strictness the direct check already applies after ENG-701's own review finding.

With the guard now seeing it, the `v0Service` allowlist entry is genuinely stale and is removed. The coverage summary reduces to ENG-698's three vendors, which is the real remaining gap.

## Proof, by mutation against the real repo

Removing every `meteredV0` reference from `v0Service.ts` now fails:

```
services/v0Service.ts calls v0 (Vercel) and records no usage (no allowlist entry).
```

**The identical mutation passed 14/14 before this change** — which is how the defect was found.

## Testing

21 tests; typecheck clean. Seven new fixtures cover the mechanism: helper-metered detection, unused import, unmetered helper, second-hop refusal, parent-relative import, staleness detection, and the inverse regression the amnesty used to hide.

title: ENG-1801: admin client_id scoping for Meta-ads reporting tools
body:
## Summary
- `list_meta_ads_campaigns`, `get_meta_ads_metrics`, and `call_meta_ads_insights_api` resolved `account_id` only against the calling session's own connected Meta accounts, with no way for an admin/internal run to reach a named client's account. Worse, an omitted `account_id` silently fell back to the caller's own account/token instead of erroring — risking a report generated against the wrong company's data and misattributed to the named client (the highest-severity finding in the original bug report).
- Adds an admin-only `client_id` param (email or userId) to the 3 tools, matching the identical contract already live on 7 other admin-scoped tools. Resolves in-process (no delegate token, no HTTP self-call) via the same pattern already proven by `assessClientHealth`/`diagnoseLeadsAtZero`: admin-gate the caller, resolve the target, read *their own* connected accounts — no fresh OAuth grant needed.
- A `client_id`-scoped call never auto-selects an account and never falls back to the legacy shared-token account — it must resolve the target's real account or throw.
- Only the 3 read-only wrapper methods ever construct the new `clientScope` argument passed into the shared `getMetaCredentials` resolver — the other 28 call sites (all Meta write/mutate operations: create/update/delete campaign, ad set, ad, creative) are untouched, so this cannot become a latent cross-tenant-write path.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] Full regression run across all Meta-ads-related test files — zero behavior change on the unscoped (ordinary customer) path
- [x] New/extended tests: admin-gate reject, blank/not-found/non-customer-role reject, successful cross-tenant resolve + audit log, both silent-fallback branches proven suppressed under scope

title: ENG-1818: fix agent-engine task creation crashing on every model
body:
## Summary
- `create_task_from_template`/`create_task_from_prompt` has been failing 100% of the time for at least 2+ days, for every model, with a misleading `datetime.utcnow()` deprecation error
- Real root cause: every model routes through OpenRouter via `langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI`, so `browser-use`'s `Agent` always sees the class name `"ChatOpenAI"` and its memory subsystem (mem0) infers an OpenAI embedder needing a real `OPENAI_API_KEY` that doesn't exist anywhere in this codebase — that construction isn't exception-contained and aborts every task before real work starts
- This is a regression from `83f22aadd` ("eliminate gateway credential race"), which removed a process-env `OPENAI_API_KEY` shim for a real safety reason — an apparently unintended side effect broke mem0's embedder construction
- Fix: `enable_memory=False` in `web_agent.py`'s `agent_kwargs` (memory was never an intentionally used feature here — nothing in this codebase reads `Agent.memory`), plus a cleanup of the misleading `datetime.utcnow()` deprecation noise in `create_jwt_token` (confirmed not the actual cause)

## Verification
- Live-verified before/after via a direct repro against the real production VM: extracted the real systemd service's exact environment (`/proc/<pid>/environ`), called `WebAgent.setup()` directly to bypass the broad exception handler that hides the real traceback in production. Captured the full stack trace on the original code (matches production logs exactly); confirmed the fixed code succeeds (`enable_memory: False`, `memory: None`, `Agent()` constructed).
- New regression test (`tests/test_eng1818_memory_disabled.py`), mutation-tested on the VM (reverted the fix, confirmed the test fails cleanly, restored).
- Full existing test suite (`pytest tests/`) run against both the fixed and unmodified checkouts on the VM: **identical 30 pre-existing failures on both** (unrelated dependency/version-drift issues, confirmed pre-existing, not introduced by this change) — zero new failures, +1 new pass (this fix's own test).
- No GitHub Actions CI exists for `agent-engine` — this VM-based testing is the primary verification gate for this subsystem.
- Independent fresh-eyes review (background agent) traced the root cause line-for-line against the actual pinned `browser-use==0.1.48` source and confirmed the fix is correct, minimal, and loses no functionality anything in this codebase depends on.

## Deploy
`agent-engine` deploys manually (not via GitHub Actions) per `agent-engine/deploy/RUNBOOK.md` — `git pull` + `systemctl restart agent-engine` on `agentweb-agentengine-instance-prod2`. Will deploy promptly after merge given customer impact.

title: ENG-1820: fix agent-engine task execution failing at first real action
body:
## Summary
- After ENG-1818's memory fix (agentweb#2821), agent-engine tasks reach Step 1 but then fail 100% of the time on their first real action, with a 404 from OpenRouter: "No endpoints found that can handle the requested parameters"
- Root cause: `browser-use`'s real per-step call always uses `with_structured_output(method="function_calling")`, which LangChain auto-sends as `parallel_tool_calls: false` — a parameter essentially no model in OpenRouter's catalog declares as supported. `openrouter_gateway.py`'s `require_parameters: true` made OpenRouter hard-reject the request instead of ignoring the unsupported param
- Not model-specific — confirmed via direct reproduction against both `gpt-5.6-terra` and `gpt-4.1` (actively used in production)
- Fix: drop `require_parameters: true`. `tool_choice` (forcing one specific function) still guarantees single-tool-call behavior regardless
- Also: fixed 4 pre-existing tests hitting the same mem0 crash ENG-1818 fixed elsewhere (they construct `Agent()` directly, bypassing `web_agent.py`'s fix), and removed confirmed-orphaned dead code found along the way (`deep_research_agent.py`, `memory_fix.py`/`memory_fix_v2.py` + their tests/configs)

## Verification
- Root cause confirmed via direct reproduction on the real production VM: captured the actual outgoing request payload via an `httpx` event hook, replicated `browser-use`'s exact call shape, confirmed identical 404 against `gpt-5.6-terra` and `gpt-4.1`
- Mutation-tested the fix on the VM (reverted, confirmed the updated test assertion fails cleanly, restored)
- Full `pytest tests/` suite run on the VM against both this fix and the current deployed checkout: identical 30 pre-existing failures on both (unrelated, confirmed pre-existing), zero new failures — the 192→174 passed delta is fully accounted for by the 18 tests deliberately deleted (dead `memory_fix*` test files)
- Independent fresh-eyes review (background agent) traced the exact request shape against the real pinned `langchain_openai`/`browser-use` source and confirmed the fix is safe with low residual risk; found one real gap (a 6th untouched `Agent(llm=None, ...)` call site) which I independently verified doesn't need the fix — `llm` is Pydantic-validated as a required field, so passing `None` raises `ValidationError` (a `ValueError` subclass) before any memory/embedder code is ever reached
- No GitHub Actions CI exists for `agent-engine` — this VM-based testing is the primary gate

## Deploy
Manual, per `agent-engine/deploy/RUNBOOK.md` (`git pull` + `systemctl restart agent-engine`). Will deploy and run a real end-to-end task-completion test on production after merge — the actual bar that matters here is a task finishing successfully, not just reaching Step 1.

title: fix(agent-engine): bound OpenRouter request timeout (ENG-1822)
body:
## Summary

- `create_openrouter_llm`'s `ChatOpenAI` client had **no effective request timeout at all** (not even the `openai` SDK's own 600s default) -- confirmed by reading and empirically testing the exact package versions running in production (`langchain-openai==0.3.11`, `openai==1.109.1`, `httpx==0.28.1`). `ChatOpenAI.request_timeout` defaults to `None`, and langchain forwards that `None` *explicitly* to `openai.OpenAI(timeout=...)` rather than omitting it -- which skips openai's own `NotGiven`-based fallback to its 600s default and reaches `httpx.Client(timeout=None)`, which httpx's own docs define as "No timeouts."
- Live-verified in production (execution `1788877994807`, right after ENG-1820 removed `require_parameters`): a single browser-use per-step `get_next_action()` call on a trivial ~7K-token request took **~7m45s** to return an empty/malformed response. browser-use's own retry then got back a fast but structurally garbage response (one action object carrying *every* possible action key simultaneously), and because `"done"` happened to be the first key, the agent self-terminated claiming false success without ever navigating anywhere -- reported `completed`/`success: true` to the customer.
- Adds `REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120` to `create_openrouter_llm`'s `ChatOpenAI` construction. browser-use's per-step call is a single `tool_choice`-forced structured-output call with a small bounded JSON output (not a long streaming generation), so a short bound is correct -- and live-confirmed generous, since the failing call only carried ~7K input tokens. The gateway's two other call sites (a short comparison in `task_utils.check_new_information`, and an end-of-task knowledge-base regeneration in `task_monitor.py`) are both non-interactive/backgrounded and already wrapped in broad `try/except`, so one shared bound is safe for all current callers.
- Investigated whether `require_parameters` (removed in ENG-1820) should come back in some scoped form to also guard the malformed-response failure mode. Confirmed against OpenRouter's own provider-routing docs that it's genuinely all-or-nothing across every request parameter -- there's no way to require `tool_choice`/`tools` support while excluding `parallel_tool_calls`, so re-enabling it would resurrect the ENG-1820 404. Left out of this change; documented as a plausible follow-up (`provider.order`/`provider.only` allow-listing known-good providers per model family) that needs live OpenRouter traffic to validate, which this investigation didn't have API-key access to do.

## Root cause confidence

- **Unbounded timeout**: confirmed, not suspected -- read the exact installed source of `langchain_openai`/`openai`/`httpx` (matching production's pinned versions, verified via SSH `pip show`) and empirically constructed a real `ChatOpenAI` instance to observe `client._client.timeout == None` before the fix and `== 120.0` after.
- **Why removing `require_parameters` surfaced it now**: plausible, not proven with certainty -- `require_parameters=True` previously made bad/incompatible providers 404 immediately (ENG-1820's bug) instead of being selected at all. With it off, OpenRouter can route to slower or non-compliant providers, and the always-unbounded timeout meant nothing ever cut such a request short. I could not make live authenticated OpenRouter completions to directly reproduce which provider got selected (no `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` access), so this is reasoned from documented OpenRouter routing/parameter semantics plus the one live production incident, not independently reproduced against multiple providers.
- **Malformed "kitchen sink" action response**: real and directly observed (production log inspected via SSH), but its root cause (provider not correctly enforcing single-tool-call JSON schema shape) is a distinct, harder problem from the timeout/hang. This PR's fix does not address it -- documented as an open follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_openrouter_gateway.py` -- added `test_gateway_sets_an_explicit_bounded_request_timeout` (mocked `ChatOpenAI`, asserts a concrete finite `timeout` kwarg is passed) and `test_gateway_client_has_no_unbounded_timeout` (real `ChatOpenAI` construction, no mocking, asserts the underlying `httpx` client's `.timeout` is not `None`) -- run against production-pinned `langchain-openai==0.3.11`/`openai==1.109.1`/`httpx==0.28.1` in an isolated scratch venv (no network calls, no production access touched).
- [x] Mutation-tested: reverted the fix locally, reran the new tests, confirmed both fail against the unfixed code (one directly reproducing `assert None is not None`), then restored the fix and reran to confirm all 9 tests in the file pass.
- [x] Full existing `test_openrouter_gateway.py` suite (7 pre-existing tests) still passes unmodified.
- [x] Related suites that construct/mock this gateway also still pass: `test_task_utils.py::TestOpenRouterDoesNotExportEnvVar`, `test_stale_model_retirement.py` (all `check_new_information`/knowledge-base call-site tests), `test_eng1818_memory_disabled.py`.
- [x] Inspected the real production hang's log (`execution_1788877994807_web_agent.log`, read-only via SSH to `agentweb-agentengine-instance-prod2`) to independently confirm the sequence of events described in the ticket.
- [x] No production processes, the live checkout, or the live systemd service were touched -- all verification used an isolated `/tmp` scratch venv with production-pinned package versions, plus read-only SSH inspection (`pip show`, log reads).

title: test(agent-mode): give the describe-image timeout tests real headroom
body:
Test-only. These three tests flaked inside a full parallel sweep while passing in isolation at **8.9s against a 10s per-test budget**.

## The flake is not in the timeout path

`beforeEach` sets `AGENT_MODE_DESCRIBE_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS = '50'`, so the code under test finishes in milliseconds. What consumes the budget is `new AgentModeService()` — importing and constructing a ~37k-line module — **once per test**. At 10s that left roughly a second of headroom, which a loaded machine erases.

## Why a wider budget rather than a shared instance

Moving construction to `beforeAll` would be faster, but it shares service state across tests in a file that mutates `process.env` and spies on instance methods per test. That trades a timing flake for an isolation one, which is harder to diagnose. The reason is recorded at the constant so the next person does not "optimise" it back.

title: fix(security): withhold the admin bit from delegated sessions on the template visibility route (ENG-1716)
body:
## What

`PUT /api/agent-mode/schedule-templates/:templateId` decided the visibility authorization with `user.isAdmin === true`. This switches it to `isRealAdmin(req)`.

## Why — found during production verification of ENG-1716

ENG-1716 closed the hole where any authenticated user could promote their own template to `system`/`public` and put its agent prompt in every customer's picker. That fix is confirmed working in production (see the ENG-1716 verification comment: non-admin gets 403 on `system`, `public`, the legacy `platform` alias and case variants; the sanctioned `pending_review` route still works; nothing partially applied).

Verifying it turned up a remaining path to the same outcome. `authenticateToken` rebuilds `req.user` for a delegate session from the **target** user's DB record:

```ts
isAdmin: targetUser.isAdmin || false,
```

So a session delegated into an account that happens to be an admin carries `isAdmin: true`, and the raw check accepted it. A contractor may hold a delegate token for a user in their assigned list (`middleware/auth.ts`), so this is the difference between *"admins may publish"* and *"anyone who can delegate into an admin may publish"*.

`isRealAdmin` is the codebase's existing answer, documented on the helper itself:

> When an admin delegates to another admin user, the delegated session should NOT inherit admin privileges. Use this helper instead of checking `req.user.isAdmin` directly.

Elsewhere in `agentModeController` the raw flag only widens a **read** (view another user's session). This is the one place it grants platform-wide **reach**, which is why it is the one place that needs the stricter helper.

## Behaviour change

None for a non-delegated session, and none for a delegated session into a non-admin account — in both cases the two expressions agree. The only difference is a delegated session into an admin account, which is now refused, and which the helper's own docstring says should never have had the privilege.

A delegated session keeps every non-privileged power it had (rename, submit for review), so support workflows are unaffected.

## Tests

Two cases added to `scheduleTemplates.test.ts`, which does not mock `middleware/auth`, so the real `isRealAdmin` runs:

- a delegated session into an admin account is refused `system`, `public` and `platform`, with no partial write
- the same session can still rename and submit for review

Verified failing against the pre-fix controller (1 failed / 37 passed) and passing after (54 passed across both template suites). `npm run typecheck` clean.

title: fix(agent-engine): enforce real wall-clock deadline on OpenRouter calls (ENG-1822 follow-up)
body:
## Summary

PR agentweb#2823 (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=120`) was merged, deployed, and then proven insufficient by a live production re-test — the task still hung ~8 minutes. Root cause: `httpx`/`httpcore`'s `timeout` is enforced per-chunk-received, not as a total-request deadline — confirmed directly against the installed `httpcore==1.0.9` source (`sock.settimeout(timeout)` called fresh before every single `recv()`). A provider that trickles response bytes slowly enough never lets any single read exceed the configured timeout, no matter how long the overall call runs.

This PR adds `_enforce_hard_deadline`: dynamically subclasses `ChatOpenAI`, wrapping `ainvoke` in `asyncio.wait_for(timeout=HARD_DEADLINE_SECONDS)` and `invoke` in a bounded daemon thread — enforcing a genuine wall-clock ceiling independent of httpx's own timeout semantics. `HARD_DEADLINE_SECONDS = REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS * 2 + 15` = 255s, matching the already-documented worst-case retry envelope.

Live-traced on production that browser-use's actual call pattern (`llm.with_structured_output(AgentOutput, include_raw=True, method="function_calling").ainvoke(...)`, a `RunnableMap`/`RunnableSequence` composition, not the raw `ChatOpenAI` instance) genuinely routes through the overridden `ainvoke`.

An independent fresh-eyes review (isolated worktree, re-derived everything from scratch) found and this PR fixes:
- The dynamic subclass was named `HardDeadlineChatOpenAI`, silently breaking browser-use's `REQUIRED_LLM_API_ENV_VARS.get(self.llm.__class__.__name__, [])` lookup (keyed on the literal string `"ChatOpenAI"`) — now preserves `__name__`/`__qualname__`/`__module__`.
- `pytest-asyncio` is not a project dependency (not in `environment.yml`, not installed in the real deployed conda env) — every `@pytest.mark.asyncio` test was silently not executing there. Converted all async tests to plain sync tests using `asyncio.run()` internally.
- Added a regression test exercising the exact `with_structured_output(...).ainvoke(...)` composition against a real trickling-socket test server (previously only proven via a one-off manual production trace).
- Comment accuracy: the sync `.invoke()` path's daemon thread isn't actually bounded by the client's own timeout (this module's own findings contradict that claim) — browser-use calls `.invoke()` on every task via `_verify_llm_connection()`, so this is real, non-theoretical exposure, now documented accurately rather than overclaimed.

Full test suite reran fresh on a clean VM scratch copy against the real deployed conda env: 21/21 pass in `test_openrouter_gateway.py`, 26/26 unaffected in `test_browser_use_integration.py`.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_openrouter_gateway.py`: 21/21 pass on the real production conda env (no `pytest-asyncio` available)
- [x] `test_browser_use_integration.py`: 26/26 pass, unaffected
- [x] Mutation-tested the new `with_structured_output` regression test (removing `_enforce_hard_deadline`'s wiring makes it hang instead of pass)
- [x] Live-traced `with_structured_output(...).ainvoke(...)` on production to confirm it routes through the override
- [ ] Deploy to production and rerun the real end-to-end task-completion test that surfaced ENG-1822 — pending merge

Not calling ENG-1818/ENG-1820/ENG-1822 done until that live test passes.

title: fix(agent-engine): report task success from is_successful(), not is_done() (ENG-1823)
body:
## Summary

`web_agent.py`'s `execute_task` drove both the ENG-859 partial-extraction salvage gate and the customer-facing/persisted success field off a single `result.is_done()` check. `is_done()` only answers "did the agent invoke the `done` action at all" — it says nothing about that action's own `success` field. A run whose final `done` call explicitly reported `success: false` (or a malformed/hallucinated result the agent itself flagged as not real) still got reported as `status: completed`, since nothing downstream ever looked past "did done get called".

**Confirmed live in production three times on the same day** (executions `1788877994807`, `1788881552500`, `1788897303516`): the agent's own `done` action said things like *"No real action was performed yet... sample HTML5 report for demonstration purposes only"* with a fabricated report, and DynamoDB showed `status: completed` regardless every time. This is the exact mechanism behind the "task redirects but does nothing" incidents surfaced while live-testing ENG-1818/1820/1822.

## Fix

Splits the two questions into `task_completion_status.py`'s `determine_task_completion_status(result)`, returning `(task_is_done, task_succeeded)`:
- `task_is_done` keeps gating the ENG-859 salvage path unchanged — that logic only cares whether the run finished, not whether it succeeded.
- `task_succeeded` now drives the returned `"success"` field and the `"summary"`/`"error"` key choice — the customer/DynamoDB-facing signal.

The `output_as_json` validation gate stays on `task_is_done`, deliberately out of scope for this fix — unrelated to the customer-facing success signal this ticket tracks.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests (`test_task_completion_status.py`, 4 cases) pass locally and on the real production conda env
- [x] Mutation-tested: reverting to the old `task_succeeded = task_is_done` behavior makes `test_done_but_reported_failed_is_the_eng1823_bug` fail as expected
- [x] `web_agent.py` confirmed to still import cleanly against the real installed `browser_use`
- [x] No regressions: `test_browser_use_integration.py` (26/26), `test_eng1818_memory_disabled.py` (1/1), `test_partial_extraction.py` (9/9) all still pass

title: feat(x): score post performance against X's real ranking weights via Grok (ENG-56)
body:
## Summary
- Adds `assess_post_performance`, a new `twitter_manage_post` action that scores an X post using **X's real ranking weights and combination formula**, ported from `xai-org/x-algorithm`'s source (not approximated).
- **Predicted mode** (`text`): scores a draft via Grok (`openrouter/x-ai/grok-4.6`) before it's posted.
- **Actual mode** (`tweet_id`): scores an already-published post from its real `getTweetMetrics` counts — no LLM call.
- Returns a score plus `netPositive` — a real, source-derived boolean (not an arbitrary tier), true iff predicted positive engagement outweighs predicted negative feedback.
- v1 is deliberately compute-on-demand: no new DynamoDB table/field, no new frontend.

## What's faithfully ported vs. what's out of reach (read `xPostRankingScore.ts`'s header for the full breakdown)
An earlier version of this PR linearly summed 6 hand-picked weights — that materially misrepresented X's algorithm. After reading `ranking_scorer.rs` in full (not just the params list), this now ports the **real nonlinear formula**:
- Every text-estimable weight (15 of ~26 named signals) pulled verbatim from `home-mixer/params/param.rs`, confirmed against `ValueModelMode`'s default (`"weighted"` — the mode this ports is the live default, not a fallback).
- The real `pos`/`neg` split + `offset_score` transform from `RankingScorer::compute_weighted_score`, not a flat weighted sum.
- **Explicitly excluded, and documented why:** telemetry-only signals (dwell time, click-dwell, watch time — require an actual serving event, unknowable pre-publish), media-view signals (photo/video expand, only relevant with attached media), and per-request/per-viewer ranking context (author cold-start, diversity, out-of-network discount, per-request weight perturbation — a post has no single "the" score outside a specific viewer/pool/request). The score is for comparing draft A vs draft B, or a post's predicted vs. actual — not a literal X placement prediction.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] `xPostRankingScore.test.ts` — the ported formula is cross-checked against an **independently hand-rolled reference implementation** of the same math (not just re-asserting the code's own output), plus clamping, fail-closed parsing, fail-closed on missing impressions, and the net-positive/negative ordering guarantee
- [x] Dispatcher wiring tests in `agentModeService.twitterOutreach.test.ts` — both modes, both failure paths
- [x] Full pre-push suite green (160 suites / 3564 tests)
