title: fix(models): stop sending tool_choice to Claude Fable 5.1 — every agent-mode turn 404s (ENG-199)
body:
## What

Claude Fable 5.1 no longer sends `tool_choice` to OpenRouter. Gated behind a new optional `supportsToolChoice` (default **true**), so nothing changes for any other model.

## Why — it was 100% broken in production, not partially

ENG-199 shipped the model into the picker. Every agent-mode turn on it returned a 500. From the production log, captured live while verifying the ticket:

```
AgentMode: OpenRouter call failed for model "openrouter/anthropic/claude-fable-5.1":
404 No endpoints found that can handle the requested parameters
```

OpenRouter's own metadata explains it — `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1`'s `supported_parameters`:

```
include_reasoning, max_completion_tokens, max_tokens, reasoning, reasoning_effort,
response_format, stop, structured_outputs, tools, verbosity
```

No `tool_choice`. And **parity with the sibling does not hold**: `anthropic/claude-fable-5` and both `:batch` variants *do* list it, so this is a genuine per-model difference rather than a listing quirk.

An unsupported parameter is not ignored. OpenRouter's provider router finds no endpoint able to serve the request and 404s, which is why this failed louder than the `temperature` defect CodeRabbit caught pre-merge — one parameter over, same class.

`params.tool_choice` was set whenever caller tools existed, and agent mode always supplies caller tools, so the parameter was sent on every single call. Consistent with the usage data: **0 sessions on this model across 18,611 scanned** — nobody could have completed a turn.

`tools` itself is still sent. The model supports tools; it does not support the selection field.

## Scope — audited, not assumed

Cross-referenced every `openrouter/*` model in the registry against OpenRouter's live `supported_parameters`. **Fable 5.1 is the only one** that omits `tool_choice`; the other fourteen all support it. The new flag is therefore carried by exactly one entry, and a test asserts that so the default-true gate cannot quietly become a registry-wide regression.

One unrelated observation from the same audit, **not** changed here: `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.8-max` no longer appears in OpenRouter's model list (only the dated `qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902` does). Three production sessions used it in August with real cost recorded, so it resolved fine then and I am not touching it on an unverified hunch — flagging it as a latent risk for whoever owns ENG-1604.

## Tests

`agentModeService.fableToolChoice.test.ts`, 6 cases: the flag is set; `tool_choice` is dropped with caller tools present and when explicitly passed; `tools` is still sent; `temperature` stays omitted; a supporting model still gets `tool_choice: auto`; and Fable 5.1 is the only flagged entry.

Verified **failing (2 of 6) against the ungated call path** and passing after. `npm run typecheck` clean; 320 passed across the five model/registry suites.

## Verification after deploy

The "before" is already captured — the 404 above, from production logs at 09:34:32Z. After deploy I will re-run the same single minimal turn and confirm it completes.

Requests still include caller `tools`. Tests cover omission, preservation, temperature behavior, supported models, and registry configuration. Typechecking passes with 320 tests.

title: fix(agent-engine): reject malformed multi-action browser-use responses (ENG-1828)
body:
## Summary

`browser-use`'s per-step call asks the LLM for one `ActionModel` per item in `AgentOutput.action` — a single dynamically-built pydantic model with every registered action (`done`, `go_to_url`, `search_google`, `write_file`, ...) as an optional sibling field, not a discriminated union. Nothing in the JSON schema enforces "exactly one populated field" — that invariant is only ever *assumed* by the framework's own code, never validated. `Controller.act()` iterates the populated fields and executes whichever it finds first, silently discarding the rest.

**Observed 5 times in production** (2026-09-08/09, across the ENG-1818/1820/1822/1823 investigation): the LLM populates several action fields at once instead of exactly one. Since `done` is registered *first* in `Controller.__init__` (confirmed via direct source read, before any navigation action), it always wins — the agent self-terminates on step 1 with a fabricated result, never getting a chance to perform any of the other populated (possibly genuine) fields. A customer-trust issue: a fabricated "completed" result for a task the agent never actually did.

## Fix

`StrictActionController` — a `Controller` **subclass** (not a monkeypatch; confirmed via grep that `Controller.act(` has exactly one call site in the whole installed `browser_use` package, and `self.controller` is the only meaningful instance) that raises a descriptive `ValueError` before delegating when more than one action field is populated. That exception flows into browser-use's own existing `Agent._handle_step_error` (confirmed: feeds the error back into the model's context via `include_in_memory=True` for a self-correcting retry), bounded by the same `max_failures`/`retry_delay` already configured — no new retry machinery needed.

Zero-populated fields are deliberately **not** rejected — falls through to a harmless no-op in the real `Controller.act()`, not observed in production, not worth guarding against.

**Process note**: went through 4 explicit self-critique passes before implementing (caught and corrected 2 real design issues — monkeypatch→subclass, and a debunked `StopIteration` justification that had led to an overly-broad `!= 1` check, correctly scoped down to `> 1`), then an independent review (fresh subagent, re-derived everything from scratch against the real installed `browser_use` 0.1.48 source, byte-identical-verified between scratch and production) which found the docstring's remaining safety-reasoning claim was still subtly wrong and a test-fidelity gap — both fixed in a follow-up commit.

## Test plan

- [x] Two-layer tests: `test_describe_populated_actions.py` (fast, dependency-free, duck-typed) + `test_strict_action_controller.py` (constructs a *real* dynamically-built `ActionModel` via `Controller().registry.create_action_model()`, including a case with a custom agent-engine-style action registered, mirroring `web_agent.py`'s own pattern)
- [x] Mutation-tested (`> 1` → `> 2`): confirmed the multi-field test correctly fails, restores clean
- [x] Full regression: 77 tests across the affected surface, all pass individually against the real production conda env — zero regressions
- [x] Independent review: no blocking issues, verdict "safe to merge and deploy as-is"

title: fix(schedules): template-created schedules never run — stamp variableValuesUpdatedAt (ENG-1609)
body:
## A schedule created from a template never runs

Found by actually running the ENG-1609 seeded template end to end in production, rather than by inspecting the row it writes. The row was correct in every field.

The schedule fired **exactly on time** (`lastRunTime 10:57:19.070Z`, target `10:57:17Z`) and then, instead of running:

- emailed its owner asking for the variables it already held (`Scheduled chat variable request email sent to recipients: aseth@argusoft.com`, Resend id `a8372a92…`, delivered)
- set `variableRequestStatus` back from `provided` → `pending`
- advanced `nextRunTime` a full day

No session, no `runResult`, no LLM call. It would have repeated that every day forever.

All four variables were populated:

```
icp_description         = "Founders and heads of growth at seed-stage B2B SaaS companies…"
daily_connection_target = "2"
message_template        = "default"
lead_list_id            = "list_1788951189817_xuxjmjnww"
```

## Cause

`runScheduledChats` accepts prefilled variables only through:

```js
const prefilledWithoutRequest = !hasVariableRequestSentAt && hasVariableValuesUpdatedAt;
const isVariableRequestSatisfied = schedule.variableRequestStatus === 'provided'
  && hasAllVariableValues
  && (prefilledWithoutRequest || (valuesProvidedAfterLatestRequest && valuesProvidedAfterLastRun));
```

`variableValuesUpdatedAt` was **absent from the record**, so `prefilledWithoutRequest` was false and the whole predicate failed — despite `variableRequestStatus: 'provided'` and every value present.

The gate is not wrong. Its own comment says *"Pre-filled defaults (no email request ever sent) are valid for all runs."* The creation paths just never stamped the timestamp it reads.

| creation path | stamps `variableValuesUpdatedAt` |
|---|---|
| `createScheduledChat` | ✅ |
| `updateScheduledChat` | ✅ |
| `submitScheduledChatVariables` / `…ByAccessToken` | ✅ |
| **`createScheduleFromTemplate`** | ❌ |
| **`outreachScheduleAutoCreate`** (ENG-1723) | ❌ |

## Why this is urgent

ENG-1723's auto-create **went live today** with `OUTREACH_SCHEDULE_AUTO_CREATE_ENABLED=true`. The next customer to complete outreach onboarding would get a schedule that silently never fires and instead emails them asking for the ICP they had just typed in — the exact "self-serve" promise ENG-1609 exists to deliver, inverted.

It also breaks ENG-1609 AC #2 (*"create_schedule_from_template works with variables alone"*) for every template, not just this one.

## Tests

One per path: the timestamp is stamped and parseable, and `variableRequestSentAt` is left unset — both halves of the predicate the gate reads. Verified **failing (2 of 63)** against the unstamped paths and passing after. `npm run typecheck` clean.

## A note on how this was missed

I verified ENG-1723 earlier by checking the written row and the idempotency guard, then deleted the schedule **before its first fire**. Every field was right. The behaviour was not. title: fix(agent-mode): echo messageIndex/clientId so optimistic bubbles don't remount (ENG-1495)
body:
## Summary

Root cause of ENG-1495 (React key drift): the frontend's optimistic message bubbles have no server identity until a later session refetch resolves `messageIndex`. `getMessageKey`'s old `messageIndex ?? index` fallback therefore changes across that refetch, React unmounts+remounts the message component, and any local state set moments earlier (e.g. `WorkPlanRecommendationCard`'s "already applied" flag, correctly set by the accept response) resets against now-stale-relative props — producing "This workplan is already active." instead of "Workplan started." on the very first accept of a session.

**Backend investigation, independently verified against the real code (not trusted from the report alone):**
- The server's message array is genuinely append-only — `messageIndex` is a mutex-guarded (`withKeyedMutex`), monotonic, never-reassigned sort key (confirmed: `AW-ChatMessages` is keyed on `{sessionId, messageIndex}`). No delete/truncate/splice path exists anywhere against the persisted table.
- The backend already computed `messageIndex` when persisting a message, but discarded it before responding — `addMessageToSession`/`addMessagesToSession` returned the raw message reference instead of the stamped one.

**Fix**: stamp the `messageIndex` these functions already compute onto the message they return, thread an optional client-generated `clientId` through `generateSessionResponse` (for the user's own optimistic bubble, which has no server round-trip yet to get an id from), and echo both synchronously in `generateResponse`'s and `generateSharedResponse`'s responses plus the 2 `session-message-appended` socket emits whose `resolved` value already carries a `generateSessionResponse` result (auto-continuation retries). Skipped the other 4 socket emit sites deliberately — background exhaustion/completion notices that arrive fresh via socket, never competing with a prior optimistic bubble.

Companion PR in `agentweb-customer-portal` (branch `manan/eng-1495-message-id-echo`) stamps `clientId` at creation and updates `getMessageKey` to prefer it.

Additive-only: new optional `ChatMessage.clientId` field, new optional `generateSessionResponse` parameter, new optional response fields. No schema/table/index/key change.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Full backend suite: 1432/1432 pass (108 suites) — verifies nothing broke in either of the two central, ~40-call-site functions this touches
- [x] New test file (`agentModeController.messageIndexEcho.test.ts`, 4 tests) — mutation-verified: reverting the res.json echo fails exactly the echo test; reverting the clientId attachment fails exactly the persistence test
- [x] Defensive-coding fix included: the new code doesn't throw when `addMessageToSession`/`addMessagesToSession` resolve `undefined` (the shape most of the existing test suite already mocks) — caught by cross-referencing an existing test file's mock convention before this ever hit CI

title: fix: unbreak landing-page publish — cert-length subdomains (ENG-1839) + unsatisfiable Tests gate (ENG-1488)
body:
Fixes ENG-1839.

## Problem

A landing page whose subdomain label exceeds 46 characters produces an `agentwebforms.com`
FQDN longer than 64 characters. Certificates cap the Common Name at 64, so no certificate can
ever be issued. DNS resolves fine; the TLS handshake is closed. The page is unreachable in a
browser while its DB record still reads `status: deployed` — which is why this went unreported.

Validation was applied to the **label** and permitted 63 (the DNS limit), but the certificate
is issued for `<label>.<SUBDOMAIN_BASE>` — label + 18. The real ceiling is 46.

Two live customer pages are already in this state, both `status: deployed`:

- `create-a-high-converting-mobile-first-emergency-home-servic.agentwebforms.com` (77 chars)
- `build-a-single-page-pricing-focused-landing-page-called-pro.agentwebforms.com` (77 chars)

Measured against existing production subdomains, the failure tracks FQDN length, not label
length:

| FQDN length | result |
|---|---|
| 28, 34, 57, 59 | 200 |
| 77 (both pages above) | TLS handshake closed |

Known-good ceiling 59, known-bad floor 77. The exact boundary is not pinned — no existing
subdomain falls between 60 and 76 — but 64 is the documented CN limit and is consistent with
every observation.

## Change

- Ceiling derived from `SUBDOMAIN_BASE` (`Math.min(63, 64 - 1 - SUBDOMAIN_BASE.length)`)
  rather than hardcoded, so it stays correct if the apex domain changes.
- Validation rejects on the FQDN, with an error naming the actual computed length and limit.
- **Collision-retry fix:** `${label}-${suffix}` was truncated *after* joining, which could cut
  into the suffix and destroy the uniqueness it exists to provide. Now truncates the base to
  leave room, so the suffix always survives.
- **Trailing-hyphen fix:** truncation could land on a hyphen and produce a label that
  `validateSubdomain`'s own pattern rejects. Truncation now strips it.

The last two are adjacent defects in the same code paths, found while making this change.

## Tests

The prior assertion was `result.length <= 63` — not the binding constraint. It passes even
when the FQDN is too long to certificate, so it would not have caught this defect and would
not catch a regression. Replaced with assertions on the FQDN, on the ceiling being derived
rather than hardcoded, on trailing hyphens, and reproducing the two labels that shipped broken.

Verified the new tests actually fail against the old behaviour: hardcoding the ceiling back to
63 fails 4 of them.

`npm test -- --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/services.customDomainService.test.ts src/__tests__/services.customDomain.pagesubdomain.test.ts` → 45/45 pass.
`npm run typecheck` → clean.

## Not included

Repairing the two already-broken pages is a data-plane change (DynamoDB records + Vercel
domain mutation on live customer sites) and needs separate approval. This PR only stops new
ones being created.

ENG-1839 also suggests surfacing cert-provisioning failure on the page record — both broken
pages read `deployed`, which is the reason nobody noticed. That is a separate design change,
not a validation fix, and is deliberately out of scope here.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01SMV1NbXXW6yS1b73fzvSqF

---

## Update: domain-health surfacing was added and then reverted

An earlier revision of this PR added background re-verification plus a "this page may not be
reachable" warning, intending to fix the silent-failure mode that let these three pages sit
broken unnoticed. **It was reverted, because it could not detect this bug.**

`verifyDomain` reads exactly two signals: Vercel's `verified` flag (ownership) and
`misconfigured` from `/v6/domains/<d>/config` (whether DNS points at Vercel). Neither fails
for an over-length domain. Verified against all three broken records — every one resolves
correctly to `cname.vercel-dns.com` / `66.33.60.129`, so `misconfigured` is false and
ownership is inherent for our own apex. The pipeline would have reported all three as
**healthy**.

Shipping it would have been worse than not shipping it: it creates a warning system whose
silence reads as "verified fine" while the failure it was built for goes straight through.

It also carried real risk, since `isDomainMisconfigured` returns `true` on ANY thrown error
(429, 5xx, timeout). That was safe when the result could only withhold an upgrade; once it
drove a write, a transient Vercel blip would have persisted a false "unreachable" state and
shown customers a factually wrong reason.

The goal remains valid and needs a **reachability** signal rather than a **configuration**
one — an actual TLS handshake attempt, or a certificate-status field if Vercel exposes one.
That is a different design and belongs in its own change.

The add-and-revert commits are left in history deliberately, so the next attempt starts from
what was learned rather than repeating it.

# ADDED 2026-09-10: the publish "Tests" gate (was PR #2846)

#2846 has been folded into this PR and its branch closed. Both fixes are needed to publish a
landing page at all, and shipping them separately cost an extra merge→deploy→verify cycle for
no review benefit. **Rollback note:** they now revert together.

## Problem

The publish route required a check run named exactly `"Tests"` on the draft SHA:

```js
const testsCheck = (checksRes.data.check_runs || []).find(c => c.name === "Tests");
if (!testsCheck || ...) return res.status(409).json({ error: "required_tests_pending" });
```

Generated landing-page repos contain **no `.github/workflows` at all**, so that check can never
appear. Verified against the GitHub API:

| Repo | `actions/workflows` total_count |
|---|---|
| `lp-create-a-high-converting-mobil-f80e1869` | **0** |
| `lp-taskflow-test-page-249d7f67` | **0** |
| `AgentWebPro/agentweb` | 5 |

So publish returned `409 required_tests_pending` permanently, and the error told the operator to
*"retry publish after GitHub starts it"* — describing something GitHub would never do.

The gate was introduced 2026-08-23 by `6470eb409` (ENG-1488). This PR fixes that
implementation; it is the correct linkage for this change.

## Change

The gate is correct for a repo that runs tests. It is now skipped **only when GitHub positively
reports zero workflows**, and is deliberately **fail-closed**: if the workflow list cannot be
read for any reason — 5xx, timeout, revoked token, or a 200 whose `total_count` is absent — the
count defaults to `1` and the gate stays in force. An unreadable API never opens the gate.

The check-runs fetch stays in its original position. An earlier draft moved it, which shifted
the ordered mock queues in `landingPageStaging.test.ts` and silently broke 10 tests in a suite
that **CI does not run** — the ordering is load-bearing, please keep it.

## Correction: this does NOT close ENG-1536

An earlier version of #2846 claimed this likely closed ENG-1536
("publish_landing_page_changes fails in 4 of 5 observed calls"). **That was an unverified
inference from the failure signature and it is now disproven:**

| | |
|---|---|
| Tests gate shipped | **2026-08-23** |
| Most recent prod call to `publish_landing_page_changes` | **2026-08-13** |

Established by scanning `AW-ChatSessions` (18,642 items) on
`attribute_exists(calledFunctions.publish_landing_page_changes)` — 48 matching sessions,
2026-03-26 → 2026-08-13. `updatedAt` is the session's last update, so true call times are ≤
those dates, which only widens the gap.

**No publish call has occurred in production since this gate existed**, so it cannot have caused
any observed failure. The gate is still a real defect — it would break the next publish — but its
severity is "will break", not "has been breaking". **ENG-1536's cause remains unknown and
unfixed; do not treat this PR as closing it.**

---

# Review round 6 (2026-09-10) — two independent reviewers

One full pass over the whole change, one scoped to the parts prior rounds structurally could
not have covered (three commits written after round 5 reported; two cherry-picked from a
different base). Both verdicts and every finding below were re-verified before acting.

## Fixed in this round

**HIGH — the repair script could delete a customer's own domain** (`cac3914e8`). The scope
filter was `d.domain.endsWith(SUBDOMAIN_BASE) && d.domain.length > MAX_FQDN`. No `type` check,
so a customer's own over-length custom domain was in scope (`addCustomDomain` applies no length
ceiling — `validateDomain` is format-only); and no leading dot, so
`…division.myagentwebforms.com` matched too. With no page referencing it, `classifyRecord`
returned `isOrphan: true`, and the ORPHAN branch of `--remove-old` requires neither `--map` nor
a per-record opt-in — it deletes from Vercel irreversibly. Now `isRepairableSubdomain`,
extracted so it is testable, with the predicate mutation-verified.

*Five prior rounds all examined `classifyRecord` and none checked what was fed into it. The
scope filter was inline, unexported, untested; the exported function was the one that got
reviewed.*

**MEDIUM — an unverified custom domain alone became the reported host** (`543b9eb18`). Found
independently by both reviewers. `rank` is a comparator, not a filter, and both winner loops
seed unconditionally — so rank 0 means "loses a comparison", never "is rejected". When a
pending custom domain is a project's only attached row there is nothing to lose to, so it won
and the page reported a host with no DNS. Exactly the failure the three tiers exist to prevent,
surviving in the one shape where ranking never runs. Reachable via `DELETE /api/domains/:id`,
the cascade cleanup, a failed `assignManagedSubdomain`, and this PR's own repair script.

**MEDIUM — the sweep's write path had no test** (`d23bd60b4`). The "never write to `status`"
invariant is the one a previous attempt on this branch got wrong, and its failure mode is
silent: a malformed UpdateExpression throws inside the per-record try, bumps `errors`, logs at
warn, and the sweep does nothing forever. Five tests now cover it; mutation-verified.

## Known gaps, deliberately not fixed here

- **No prober-health circuit breaker.** A prober-side fault (egress DNS, NAT/proxy, security
  group) fails every probe at once. Bounded today because every code such an outage produces —
  `ENOTFOUND`, `ECONNRESET`, `ECONNREFUSED`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `EAI_AGAIN`, `TIMEOUT` — is SUSPECT,
  never DEFINITIVE, so nothing reaches a customer until three consecutive hourly rounds fail.
  The real fix needs a two-phase restructure; documented in the cron.
- **`status` is a stale add-time signal.** Nothing refreshes it except an explicit verify call
  or the portal panel being open. A customer who adds DNS an hour later and never reopens the
  panel keeps `pending_verification` forever, and now sees the managed subdomain rather than
  their branded domain. Deliberate trade — never show a dead host — but it changes behaviour
  for existing records.
- **The portal still deletes before adding.** The new guard covers only the over-length cause;
  any other POST failure still strands a page. Pre-existing, not a regression.
- **`addCustomDomain` has no length ceiling.** The only Vercel-reaching path without one.

## ⚠️ Needs someone with prod AWS access before this is called done

The Tests-gate fix depends on the org token being able to read
`GET /repos/:owner/:repo/actions/workflows`. A fine-grained PAT without `Actions: read` returns
403 → the catch keeps the gate → **publish stays 409 forever and fix (B) is a no-op in
production**, with only a `console.warn` as signal. Safe either way, never wrong — but possibly
inert. I could not verify: reading `prod/AgentWeb/GitHub` is denied to my IAM user.

title: feat(admin): broaden Usage & Cost from X-only to every metered vendor (ENG-1837)
body:
Closes ENG-1837.

## Why

The admin **Usage & Cost** tab was built under ENG-664 as the reference implementation for vendor metering, and its provider machinery (`providersInData`, `userRowForProvider`, `providerLabel`) was deliberately kept generic so it could broaden. It never did — the tab pinned `const provider = TWITTER_PROVIDER_KEY`.

Six more vendors have since landed on the same ledger — v0 (ENG-694), You.com + Google CSE (ENG-695), Apollo + enrich.so (ENG-696), Remotion Lambda (ENG-699). Their spend is recorded, priced and queryable, and invisible to every admin. `getCostAggregation(start, end, limit, provider)` already accepted `"llm" | "all" | <vendor>`; what was missing was the control and an option list.

## Backend

**`METERED_VENDOR_PROVIDERS`** — the vendors with a live `recordVendorUsage` adapter. Deliberately *not* derived from `vendorRateCard`'s `VendorRateProvider`: that card also prices ElevenLabs, 2captcha and Placid, which are priced but **not yet metered** (ENG-698, blocked on the ENG-1598 Placid credential). Offering them would render a permanently empty view, and "no rows" reads as *this vendor costs nothing* rather than *we don't measure this vendor yet* — the silent-zero failure ENG-693 AC4 exists to prevent.

**`availableProviders` on the aggregation response** — computed over the **unfiltered** window, so the picker keeps offering every vendor while one of them is selected. Free: the scan already happened. It is the union of the registry and the providers actually present, and the union matters in both directions — the registry keeps a vendor discoverable before it accrues any spend (the reason ENG-664 always offered `twitter`), and the window scan surfaces a vendor whose adapter shipped after the registry was last edited. "Present" reads both signals `recordVendorUsage` writes (`provider` and the `"{provider}:"` model namespace), because the filter matches on either.

**Coverage guard** — `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard` now asserts the registry and the real adapters agree in both directions, in the same spirit as its existing staleness assertion. A registry key with no adapter, or an adapter missing from the registry, fails the build.

## Partner portal

- **Provider dropdown, default `all`.** The tab answers *"who spent our vendor budget"*; opening on a single vendor hides the total. X is one click away and keeps its own panels.
- **Server-scoped re-fetch, not client-side filtering.** `userCount` exists precisely because summing the capped `topUsers` slice understated the headline past 100 spenders (ENG-664 review round) — re-deriving it in the browser would reintroduce the bug that field was added to fix.
- **The allocated caveat is now unconditional; the X dedup caveat is not.** `providerIsAllocatedEstimate` hardcoded `"twitter"`, so every other vendor's cost read as vendor-measured. Every figure here is allocated, LLM dollars included (ENG-693 AC3). Deleted rather than generalised — a predicate that is always true is a lie with a signature. Only X dedups a repeat read of the same resource within a UTC day, so only X is an upper bound.
- **An all-vendor total states that it is an undercount** while ENG-698 is open. A figure silently omitting three vendors would read as the overhead envelope being comfortably met.
- **The X reconciliation panel and the by-X-account rollup no longer render under a non-X vendor.** Both compare against X's own billing cycle / connected accounts, which say nothing about Apollo — and the panel fired a second request on every tab open regardless of selection.
- **The drill-down column is named for what the rows are** (`Tool` / `Model` / `Tool / model`), using the `provider` prop `UserUsageRow` already accepted and ignored. Labelling a `twitter:post` row "Model" is the mis-read ENG-1519 was filed for.

## Scope boundaries

No enforcement, no schema change, no customer surface. Vendor spend still does not draw down any cap — that is ENG-1250 §9 and stays behind AC6 and Harsha's sign-off. The `?tab=costs` LLM dashboard is untouched and its `"llm"` default still keeps vendor rows out.

## One superseded test

`UsageCostByUserTab.test.tsx` asserted *"is X-only by default: allocated caveat shown, no provider selector"*. That encoded ENG-664's deliberate scoping, which AC1 reverses. Rewritten naming the supersession rather than deleted, so the history stays readable.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Backend suites | **517 passed / 25 suites** (`usage*`, `spend*`, `vendorMetering*`, `routes/adminUsage`, `twitterPricing`) |
| Partner portal suites | **131 passed / 20 suites** (`components/admin/__tests__`, `pages/__tests__`) |
| Backend production build | green |
| Partner portal production build | green |
| Guard failure modes | checked by actually breaking the registry in both directions, not assumed |

Note CI runs production builds only — it contains no jest job — so the suite results above are local, per `CLAUDE.md`.

Post-deploy verification on production against a real range with known vendor spend before the ticket closes.

title: fix(linkedin): a de-duplicated send counted as a delivery — run reported success having contacted nobody (ENG-1720)
body:
## A run that contacted nobody reported success

Found by running the seeded template against two profiles that already had **pending** invitations, on `aseth@argusoft.com`. Both sends were skipped as duplicates. Production log:

```
17:16:26 send-invite: skipping .../danielkoukol/ — invitation already pending (sent 2026-09-09T13:32:45.644Z)
17:16:30 send-invite: skipping .../iwcrosby/     — invitation already pending (sent 2026-09-09T13:32:45.644Z)
```

Nothing was delivered — `daily_volume.invite.count` stayed at 2 and the sent-invitations ledger stayed at 2 rows. The run was nevertheless stored:

```
status               success
passed               true
functionCallMisses   []
functionCallDetails  { linkedin_outreach: { actual: 2, required: 1 } }
```

The owner is told their outreach ran when no one was contacted, and the run's own record contradicts both the pacer and the ledger.

## Cause

`send-invite` de-duplicates against the sent ledger and returns a success-shaped result:

```js
return withRouting({
  success: true,
  alreadyInvited: true,
  message: `…Skipped to avoid a duplicate — no invite quota was used…`,
  data: { alreadyInvited: true, sentAt: … },
});
```

`toolCallSucceeded` rejects only an `error`, `result.success === false`, or a call that never executed — so a deliberate no-op counted as a delivery:

```js
const successfulSends = sendCalls.filter(toolCallSucceeded).length;  // 2
```

**This is ENG-1720's own founding bug, one layer down.** That ticket closed the tool-NAME loophole — a successful `search-people` satisfying a send requirement — and left open the send that does not send. The module docblock describes the exact failure it has just reproduced.

## Fix

`isDeliveredSend`: a send call is a delivery only if it succeeded **and** did not report `alreadyInvited` (checked at the top level and nested under `data`, since the handler sets both).

A skip still counts as an **attempt**, deliberately. That keeps `isSendRun` true so the run is scored on sends rather than silently falling back to the name-keyed count — otherwise an all-skipped run would pass again by that second route. It therefore fails its requirement, which is correct: it contacted no one. That is also exactly the looping case **ENG-1715**'s send-press breaker exists to stop — and ENG-1715 could not be verified before this fix, because the requirement was wrongly satisfied and the breaker never engaged.

## Tests

Four cases in `linkedInSendRequirement.test.ts`: two skips must not satisfy `min: 1`; a real delivery alongside a skip counts once; an all-skipped run stays a send run; and both `alreadyInvited` shapes are rejected.

Verified **failing (3 of 19)** against the pre-fix predicate and passing after. `npm run typecheck` clean; 59 passed across `linkedInSendRequirement`, `sendPressCircuitBreaker` and `requiredCallSatisfaction`.

## Behaviour change worth stating

A run whose every target is already pending now **fails** instead of reporting success. That is the intent — it delivered nothing — but it does mean a schedule working a fully-exhausted lead list will start reporting failures rather than silent no-op successes. Given ENG-1132 was filed about exactly that silence, surfacing it is the point.

Adds `isDeliveredSend` to exclude `alreadyInvited` no-ops from delivered-send counts while retaining them as send attempts. Runs with no delivered invitations now report failure. Regression tests cover skipped, mixed, and both response shapes.

title: feat(admin): render the cross-vendor spend ledger in the partner portal (ENG-1838)
body:
Closes ENG-1838.

## Why

[ENG-1250](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1250) §7 states the requirement bluntly: *"No admin should need direct DynamoDB inspection to explain a pause."* The API that satisfies it shipped in #2811 and **nothing rendered it**, so the answer still lived in a table scan.

This adds the drill-in, as a sibling of the LLM and X cost breakdowns already on the admin user card. Unlike those two it reads the immutable `AW-SpendEvents` ledger rather than the daily aggregate: per-call, every metered vendor at once, and the only one that can show reservations.

## Backend — resolve the billing root before reading the ledger

The route's parameter is named `billingUserId`, but nothing made callers pass one, and spend events are partitioned by billing root. An org **member's** id therefore matched nothing and produced a complete, well-formed, entirely **empty** breakdown — the worst failure available on a screen whose job is explaining a pause: it would answer *"this account has spent nothing"* about an account that has spent plenty.

That is not hypothetical. The admin cost tables are keyed by the **acting** user (`usageAnalyticsService` groups `topUsers` on `item.userId`), so drilling in from one hands this route a member id routinely. It now resolves through the same `resolveBillingUserId` the live gate bills through — a no-op for a root, correct for a member, and impossible to disagree with the enforcer about who pays. Both ids come back so the UI can say whose ledger it is showing.

## Backend — the route had no route-level test at all

`spendReadModel` was unit-tested as pure functions and every *other* route in `adminUsage.ts` was covered, but this route's composition — billing resolution, the `BILLING_USER_ID_RE` / `MONTH_RE` guards, and stitching breakdown + allowance + projection + pause into one payload — was asserted nowhere. Added, with only the true boundaries mocked and the read model running for real, so the tests exercise the composition rather than restate it.

## Portal — three rules the component exists to keep

- **A reservation is not spend.** Committed-but-unresolved money is reported beside settled spend and never added into it.
- **Raw spend, adjustments and usable balance are three figures.** §3: *"Credits and migration adjustments change available allowance; they never erase or rewrite spend."* A single net number would hide which of the two moved.
- **Absence is stated, never rendered as zero.** A month with no events reads as "nothing recorded", and says that is not the same as \$0.00 spent — this ledger only covers calls made after it started recording (2026-09-07).

Also handled, each because the alternative asserts something false: an uncapped tier reads **Uncapped** rather than a zero allowance it has blown through; a malformed stored policy is flagged so the state is not read as measured; a non-zero `excludedEventCount` is surfaced because it should be impossible; and sub-cent vendor units keep four decimals, since an X owned-read is \$0.001 and would otherwise render as \$0.00 on exactly the rows this screen exists to itemise.

**One defect the tests caught while being written:** a negative admin reversal formatted as `\$-5.00`, which reads as a malformed figure rather than money taken back. The sign now sits outside the symbol.

## Scope boundaries

Read-only. No enforcement, no schema change, no customer surface. The component takes a payload and renders it — ENG-1250 AC6 keeps enforcement with Harsha, and a read model must never become the thing that pauses an account.

Open question **D6** in \`docs/vendor-cost-metering-brain.md\` §7 — whether this surface or the \`AW-UsageRecords\`-backed Usage & Cost tab is the long-term admin home — is deliberately not settled here. This makes the shipped API visible; it does not retire anything.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Backend suites | **487 passed / 23 suites** (\`routes/adminUsage\`, \`spend*\`, \`usage*\`) |
| Partner portal suites | **152 passed / 21 suites** |
| Both production builds | green |
| Billing-resolution fix | verified by reverting it and confirming the test fails |

CI runs production builds only — it contains no jest job — so the suite results above are local, per \`CLAUDE.md\`.

title: fix(admin): keep LLM providers out of the vendor picker (ENG-1837 follow-up)
body:
Follow-up to #2841 (ENG-1837). Found in the post-deploy production check, not by tests.

## What was wrong

The Usage & Cost picker offered `azure-openai`, `bedrock`, `gemini`, `openai` and `openrouter` alongside the seven metered vendors. Those are **LLM token providers**.

The picker's entire framing is per-unit vendor spend — the allocated caveat, the ENG-698 undercount warning, the `METERED_VENDOR_PROVIDERS` registry that decides what is selectable — and none of it means anything for a token provider. The LLM Costs tab (`?tab=costs`) already answers that question, and provider isolation between the two tabs was an explicit ENG-664 deliverable.

## Cause

`providerOfRow` returned `row.provider` for any row that had one. ENG-693 gave **LLM** rows a `provider` too, so every token provider in the window looked like a vendor.

The discriminator is the one the `"llm"` scope already filters on — `isVendorEntry` needs provider **and** unit. The option list and the filter now share one definition of "vendor" and cannot drift apart.

## Why the tests missed it

Every fixture that set `provider` also set `unit`, so no test ever presented the shape that breaks it: a row with a provider and no unit, which is what an ordinary LLM call writes. That is the gap, and it is worth naming rather than just patching — the fixtures were too clean to be representative.

The regression test now uses real LLM row shapes (`bedrock` / `gemini` / `azure-openai` on unnamespaced models) and asserts they are absent **while a genuine vendor row is present**, so it cannot pass vacuously. Verified failing against the old one-line predicate.

The client-side fallback is unaffected: it derives options from the model string, where an LLM id has no vendor namespace, and never reads the provider attribute.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Affected suites | **102 passed** (`usageAnalyticsService`, `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard`, `routes/adminUsage`) |
| Typecheck + production build | green |
| Regression test | confirmed failing against the old predicate |

Production re-check after deploy before ENG-1837 closes.

title: fix: publish no longer waits for a Tests check that cannot exist
body:
One of the three blockers that stopped a customer's rebuilt landing page from being published
at all. Separate from ENG-1839 (#2840), which fixes a different defect found during the same
investigation.

## Problem

The publish route requires a check run named exactly `"Tests"` on the draft SHA:

```js
const testsCheck = (checksRes.data.check_runs || []).find(c => c.name === "Tests");
if (!testsCheck || ...) return res.status(409).json({ error: "required_tests_pending" });
```

**Generated landing-page repos contain no `.github/workflows` at all**, so that check can never
appear. Verified against the GitHub API:

| Repo | `actions/workflows` total_count |
|---|---|
| `lp-create-a-high-converting-mobil-f80e1869` | **0** |
| `lp-taskflow-test-page-249d7f67` | **0** |
| `AgentWebPro/agentweb` | 5 |

So publish returned `409 required_tests_pending` permanently, and the message told the operator
to *"retry publish after GitHub starts it"* — describing something GitHub would never do.

This is also the most likely explanation for **ENG-1536** ("publish_landing_page_changes fails
in 4 of 5 observed calls"), which reads like a flaky handler but behaves exactly like a
deterministic refusal.

## Change

The gate is correct for a repo that runs tests. It is now skipped **only when GitHub positively
reports zero workflows**.

Deliberately **fail-closed**: if the workflow list cannot be read for any reason — 5xx, timeout,
permissions — `hasCi` stays `true` and the gate applies exactly as before. "Could not determine
whether this repo has CI" must never be mistaken for "it has none".

## Tests

- publishes a no-CI repo, and asserts it does not even request `check-runs`
- keeps the gate when the workflow list is unreadable (fail-closed)
- keeps the gate for a repo that has CI whose `Tests` check is still running

Verified the first fails if the skip is removed. Every pre-existing publish test needed its
axios mock chain extended, since the route now makes one additional GET before `check-runs`.

## Not included

The other two blockers from the same investigation: the publish tools being refused by
`install_skills` (ENG-1795), and no human having push access to generated repos since
~2026-07-10. Both still open.

title: fix: skill-refusal cause reporting (ENG-1795) + reachability sweep cadence & multi-instance safety (ENG-1839)
body:
Fixes ENG-1795.

## Problem

`install_skills` returned ONE message for every rejected skill id:

```
The requested skills are not available with your current subscription.
Tell the user plainly that this capability is not on their plan.
```

That text does not merely misreport the cause — it **instructs the model to state the plan
limitation to the customer as fact**. So any lookup failure reached a paying customer as a
billing statement, sending them to the one team that cannot help them.

A rejected id has three causes and only one of them is billing:

| Cause | Reality | Who can fix it |
|---|---|---|
| **unentitled** | The skill exists; the account is not granted it | Sales |
| **unavailable** | The id is right and the account IS permitted, but nothing is installable behind it — an empty `__other_skills__` pool, a visibility filter, the admin-only bundle | Support |
| **unresolved** | No such skill id: retired, renamed, a typo, or invented by the model | Support / the model retrying |

### This is not hypothetical

The ENG-1237 repro already in this suite records a real production session
(harsha@agentweb.pro) where an unpublished org-shared skill claimed the last unassociated
tools, `__other_skills__` dropped out of the catalog, and the refusal surfaced to the user as a
subscription limit.

ENG-1237 fixed the *cause* of that particular case (one line in `getUnassociatedTools`). Its
commit message called the resulting message "misleading" — and left it. Any other route to the
same state still produced the same false billing claim.

## Change

Each cause gets its own message and its own error class, so the failure policy can cluster them
apart:

- **unentitled** → `subscription_blocked` (unchanged text — this is the branch where the plan
  claim is TRUE)
- **unavailable** → `empty_result` (retrying the same id cannot succeed, so `invalid_args`
  would be wrong too)
- **unresolved** → `invalid_args`

A mixed refusal keeps the ids in separate response fields and classifies as the unknown-id
case, because pooling them would put a typo back under a billing verdict — the exact conflation
being removed.

If the catalog lookup itself fails we cannot know why an id was rejected, so it falls to the
branch that makes **no claim about the customer's plan**. An unproven absence is never reported
as an entitlement failure.

Admin Tools is excluded from the entitlement branch entirely: it is gated on
`isAdmin`/delegation, so an entitlement verdict would tell an ordinary user to buy a plan that
grants admin.

## The tests were part of the problem

`getAllowedSkills` is mocked to `['*']` suite-wide. **Every pre-existing test asserting the
subscription message ran against a user entitled to everything** — the message was pinned in
five places while the condition it describes was never once constructed. That is how the
conflation survived: the tests could not tell the branches apart either.

Added: a genuinely un-entitled skill (published, deliberately absent from `allowedSkills`); a
mixed refusal keeping its ids separate; a catalog-lookup failure making no billing claim.

Updated five existing expectations to the branch each fixture actually exercises — notably
`should return error for invalid skill IDs`, which asserted the SUBSCRIPTION message for an id
it names invalid.

Two org-private cases now read "could not resolve", which is also **less leaky**: the old
wording implicitly confirmed to an outsider that another org's private skill exists and is
merely unpurchased.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean
- Full backend suite: **1693 suites / 29,954 tests, 0 failures**
- Mutation: collapsing the classifier back to a single subscription verdict **fails 6 tests**

## Note

The Linear ticket's own title/description still frame this as a subscription/plan issue, which
is the framing this PR disproves. It needs correcting — I don't have Linear access from here.

  - Correctly classifies unknown skills as invalid requests and unavailable skills as unavailable tools.
  - Preserves categorized skill details in installation failure records.
  - Correctly identifies subscription-related installation refusals.
  - Prevents the skill installer from being incorrectly reported as an unavailable capability.

title: fix: take the hourly domain sweep off production, and correct two defects #2847 shipped
body:
Carries the six commits that did not make it into #2847 before it merged, plus corrections to
two defects that #2847 put into production.

## Why this exists

#2847 merged at `ec302c623` while later work was still in review. Everything below was already
written, reviewed and mutation-verified against that branch — it just never landed.

## 1. Corrects two defects now live from #2847

**The install refusal tells the model to do something impossible.** `unavailable`/`forbidden`
refusals classify `tool_unavailable`, whose guidance is appended directly beneath the refusal:

```
[Retryable: no — this tool is not available in this session. Do NOT retry it —
 install the required skill via install_skills, ...]
```

`install_skills` DID run — it ran and refused — and the remedy points at the call that just
refused. For an admin-only bundle it also contradicts the refusal's own text, which says not to
suggest support or an upgrade.

**Catalog defects drop out of triage.** `tool_unavailable` maps to failure type
`model_uninstalled_tool` ("not a tool bug; fix the catalog"), so the `unavailable` bucket — which
IS the ENG-1237 catalog defect — is excluded from the investigate set.

Both fixed by a dedicated `skill_install_refused` class: fast-trip like its siblings, failure
type `bug`, and guidance whose only job is the verdict, since the refusal text already names the
cause and the ids. Additive, not a rename. All 16 files consuming error classes were traced;
only three hardcode names and none are in this path.

An admin-only refusal further resolves to `by_design` rather than `bug` — a role boundary is not
a defect to investigate — distinguished by message, since both callers already pass it. A mixed
refusal stays `bug`, because the catalog half is real.

## 2. Takes the hourly sweep off production

The reachability monitor currently makes an unsolicited HTTPS request to **every customer
domain, 24 times a day**. Now daily at a fixed 06:15 UTC, matching the other crons in
`server.ts` — boot-relative scheduling meant "hourly" reshuffled on every deploy.

A domain checked within the last 20h is skipped, which makes the sweep safe to run more than
once per period: it covers staggered multi-instance runs, restart storms, and a sweep that dies
partway (the next run picks up exactly the remainder — self-healing, no lease to leak). It is
NOT a substitute for a lock and the comment says so: simultaneous instances both scan before
either writes.

The probe now identifies itself (`AgentWeb-DomainMonitor/1.0 (+https://agentweb.pro)`). A
header-less HEAD from an unknown IP is what bot protection exists to refuse, and a 503 from a
WAF counts as a failed probe — so an anonymous prober can decide a healthy customer site is
broken.

Confirmations 3 → 2. Two consecutive DAILY failures cannot both be caught by one transient
incident, so a lower count buys more confidence at this cadence, not less.

## 3. A monitoring gap and a fleet-wide false-accusation risk

`CERT_HAS_EXPIRED` was briefly promoted to DEFINITIVE to cut reporting latency. Reverted: that
code is OpenSSL's verdict on **any** certificate in the chain at any depth, not the leaf.
Verified locally — a leaf valid for another year, chained to an expired root, yields
`error 10 at 1 depth lookup: certificate has expired`. So an expired root in Node's bundled
store, the OS ca-certificates package, or an egress proxy's CA makes every domain report expiry
at once, with a correct clock. As DEFINITIVE it bypasses the confirmation threshold, so one
sweep would write "The SSL certificate has expired." to every affected customer's portal. That
is the DST Root CA X3 shape.

Separately: a FUTURE `lastReachabilityCheckAt` made `now - last` negative and skipped the domain
until wall-clock caught up — one write from a skewed clock silently retiring a domain from
monitoring, with no log and no error. In a monitor whose premise is that silence must not be
read as health.

## Verification

- Full backend suite green on this branch
- Every fix mutation-verified: removing the notice guard fails 5; adding `bug` to
  `NON_DISPATCHABLE_FAILURE_TYPES` fails 1; collapsing the `by_design` branch fails 1; reverting
  the future-timestamp guard fails 1; cadence → weekly fails the latency bound; `CERT_HAS_EXPIRED`
  → DEFINITIVE fails 1
- The detection-latency bound derives the cadence from the scheduler's own constant rather than
  hand-copying it, and fails at both 999 (dead monitor) and 1 (single blip reaches the customer)

## Known, not fixed here

Two items from the last review, both filed rather than bundled:

- The mixed-refusal rule keys on prose in `describeRejections`. Rewording the `unavailable`
  sentence flips a mixed refusal from `bug` to `by_design` with no test failing — the fixture is
  a hand-written approximation rather than derived from real output.
- Simultaneous-instance coordination. Production runs one instance; a real lease is owed if that
  environment ever scales out.

* **New Features**
  * Domain monitoring now performs daily reachability checks and avoids rechecking recently verified domains.
  * Reachability probes provide clearer identification to monitored services.
  * Skill installation refusals now provide more specific error handling and guidance.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Certificate-related reachability failures require repeated daily confirmation before a domain is marked unreachable.
  * Prevented repeated retries and alternative-tool suggestions when skill installation is explicitly refused.
  * Improved handling of admin skill-access refusals and lookup failures.

title: fix: honor explicit user 'stop' during work-plan auto-continuation (ENG-1819)

body:

title: fix(linkedin): preserve alreadyInvited through the tool-ledger minimizer — #2842 was inert without it (ENG-1720)
body:
## The other half of #2842 — without which that PR does nothing

PR #2842 added `isDeliveredSend`, keyed on `result.alreadyInvited`. I re-ran the production test on the deployed build and the result was **identical**: `actual: 2`, `passed: true`, `misses: []`, for a run that delivered nothing. The predicate was never seeing the flag.

## Why

`extractMinimalToolResult` has no general `linkedin_outreach` branch. Its own ENG-1299 comment states the consequence plainly:

> *linkedin_outreach has no branch below, so its stored tool-ledger result is the `{}` default*

Two things follow, and the second is worse than the bug I set out to fix:

1. `result.alreadyInvited` never reaches the ledger, so `isDeliveredSend` cannot see it.
2. **`toolCallSucceeded({})` returns `true`** — no `error`, no `success: false` — so *every* `linkedin_outreach` ledger entry reads as successful, whatever actually happened.

So ENG-1720's action-aware counting could tell **which** calls were sends (arguments survive the minimizer) but could not tell a delivered send from a skipped or failed one. The earlier run that scored 2-of-2 was correct by coincidence: both sends genuinely succeeded, so the wrong measurement produced the right number.

## Fix

```ts
if (toolName === 'linkedin_outreach' && result?.alreadyInvited === true) {
  return { success: result?.success, alreadyInvited: true };
}
```

`success` rides along for the same reason the sibling `degraded` branch keeps it — a bare marker with no outcome is not enough to score on.

## The testing mistake worth recording

#2842's unit tests passed against a fix that did nothing, because I built the ledger entry by hand with `result.alreadyInvited` present — **a shape production never produces**. The tests were self-consistent and measured nothing.

The two tests here assert the marker survives `extractMinimalToolResult` itself, which is the boundary that was actually broken. Typecheck clean; 44 pass across the minimizer and requirement suites.

## Still worth a look afterwards

This preserves the de-dupe outcome specifically. The broader issue — that a `{}` ledger entry reads as success for *any* `linkedin_outreach` failure mode — is untouched here and deserves its own consideration, since it means a genuinely refused send may also be scoring as delivered. I would rather land the narrow fix and file that than widen this PR.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

`extractMinimalToolResult` now preserves `alreadyInvited` and `success` for `linkedin_outreach` results. This allows `isDeliveredSend` to distinguish duplicate invites from delivered sends. Tests confirm duplicate markers survive minimization and delivered sends remain unmarked. Typecheck and 44 minimizer and requirement tests pass.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(admin): spend-by-provider cut, and name what an unattributed row is (ENG-1859, ENG-1860)
body:
Closes ENG-1859. Closes ENG-1860.

Both were found while verifying ENG-1837 on production, not from a spec.

## ENG-1859 — spend by provider

The LLM Costs tab breaks spend down by **model** (49 rows on production) and not by **provider**, so *"Bedrock vs Gemini vs OpenRouter vs Azure"* was unanswerable anywhere in the admin UI. The ledger has carried `provider` on LLM rows since ENG-693; nothing read it for this cut.

It briefly *was* answerable: for about thirty minutes the vendor picker accidentally offered `bedrock`, `gemini`, `openai`, `azure-openai`, `openrouter` — removed in #2844, because that picker is for per-unit vendors. Removing it also removed the only place the question could be asked. **This is the right home for it**: provider-level LLM spend is a model-routing question, not a vendor-spend one, so each surface keeps meaning exactly one thing.

`byProvider` is a new cut over rows the scan already loaded — no new query, no schema change.

**Keyed on the `provider` attribute, deliberately not derived from the model id.** The same model is reachable through more than one upstream — `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` via Bedrock and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` via OpenRouter — which is precisely why `byModel` cannot answer this. There is a test for exactly that case.

**Rows predating ENG-693 have no provider.** They bucket as `PROVIDER_UNRECORDED` and render as *"Not recorded"* with a sentence explaining what that means. Attributing them to an upstream would invent data; dropping them would make the provider rows sum to less than the headline with nothing saying why. A test asserts the cut reconciles to the total.

## ENG-1860 — name the unattributed rows

`(no email on file)` collapsed four materially different situations into one blank-looking string. Measured on production, 2026-08-11 → 2026-09-10:

| Row id | Calls | Cost | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system` | **10,830** | $10.86 | the recorder's no-user fallback |
| `anon_<uuid>` × ~45 | ~250 | ~$12 | anonymous / pre-auth sessions |
| `workplans` | 10 | $0.67 | a feature name in the user-id slot |
| `eng1223-live-readonly-check` | 3 | $0.04 | a test-harness id |

The label was not *wrong* — there genuinely is no email — but it **hid the row that matters**. `system` is the largest call count on the page, 29% of all metered calls in the window, and read like a data-quality nit rather than an attribution gap. That gap is filed separately as **ENG-1858**; this change only makes it legible.

Classified on the id's shape, so it costs no extra lookup, and the raw id keeps rendering beneath. An unresolved id is labelled *"Unknown or unresolved user"*, never *"deleted"* — we know the lookup missed, not why, and asserting a cause we have not established would be a different kind of wrong. There is a test asserting the label never claims deletion.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Backend | **93 passed** (`usageAnalyticsService`, `routes/adminUsage`) |
| Partner portal | **161 passed / 22 suites** |
| Both production builds | green |

`CostDashboardTab` had **no test file at all**; it has one now, covering the new cut including the two-upstreams case and the old-backend-omits-the-field case.

CI runs production builds only — no jest job — so these are local, per `CLAUDE.md`.

Post-deploy production verification before either ticket closes.

body:

- Behavior: production push deployment remains unchanged; staging gains an explicit-ref control rail

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. title: fix(oauth): harden and verify Hermes native callback exchange (ENG-1869)
body:
## Risk: High | Priority: High

Hermes native headless discovery requires interactive orchestration to present an OAuth URL and receive the later pasted callback. No Emma server interoperability failure was reproduced: the native fixture also passed the unchanged base. This PR hardens the security defects found during that investigation and documents the required persistent CLI flow.

Tracking: [ENG-1869](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1869). **Do not merge or deploy**, per Harsha. This changes persistence behavior and remains a draft.

## Behavior and security

- Validate confidential-client credentials and PKCE before consuming an authorization code. Wrong verifier/secret attempts preserve the code. The atomic DynamoDB update checks unused state, expiry, PKCE challenge/method, client identity and any supplied exact redirect; simultaneous valid exchanges issue one pair. OAuth 2.1 omission of the redundant token-request redirect remains supported.
- Bind refresh to the issuing client and authenticate confidential clients through their registered Basic or POST credential transport. Reject missing/unknown clients and malformed/unsupported registration auth methods.
- Rotate refresh tokens with one DynamoDB transaction: consume the old token, put one successor, and check the family root. Use the existing GSI only as a locator, then read current token/family state consistently. Retry recognized transaction conflicts with a bound; propagate other storage failures without orphan successors.
- Authenticated, correctly bound replay revokes the family root, disabling descendant access and refresh tokens. A concurrent loser is also replay: one response succeeds, but that family becomes unusable. No grace window preserves a potentially stolen successor. This implements [RFC 9700 §4.14.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html#section-4.14.2).
- Preserve the original PR's registered-redirect validation on denied consent, S256 consent requirement, scalar input guards, state preservation and no-store token responses. Raw tokens remain absent from storage/callback URLs.

## Persistence compatibility and rollback

No table/key/index changes, TTL configuration changes, migration, backfill, provisioning or token wire-format changes. Existing token items gain `familyId`, root-only `familyRevoked`, and `accessExpiresAt`. Their existing `expiresAt` TTL retains replay evidence through a fixed 30-day family deadline; access validity remains at most one hour. Rotation does not extend that deadline. This increases storage retention and transaction/consistent-read work.

**Legacy refresh tokens require reauthentication:** old records have no recoverable ancestry, so adopting them could leave prior ancestors able to replay without disabling their descendants. Existing legacy access tokens retain their original expiry. Missing/TTL-deleted evidence also fails closed. No production data was mutated.

**Rollback is not a blind revert:** after new records exist, old readers would misinterpret retention TTL as access expiry and ignore family revocation. Retain the new access-expiry/family checks during a partial rollback, or explicitly revoke affected families before reverting readers (separate approved data-plane work). Prefer a forward fix; reverting refresh writers reopens the original vulnerabilities.

## Strict TDD evidence — Atem, this worktree

Tests were written and run before each implementation step:

| Round | RED | GREEN |
|---|---|---|
| PKCE/secret preservation and refresh protection | 17 failed, 6 passed | 23 security cases passed |
| Malformed storage, legacy lineage, expiry | 11 failed, 33 passed | 44 security cases passed |
| Transaction/revocation conflicts | 2 failed, 44 passed | 46 security cases passed |
| Registration auth-method review | 5 failed, 46 passed | 51 security cases passed |
| Registered credential transport | 4 failed, 51 passed | 55 security cases passed |

Final focused verification: **6 suites passed, 164 tests passed** (OAuth routes/service/security, native Hermes, MCP authentication and MCP security). The neighboring existing MCP suites emit a timer-teardown warning; the native fixture exits cleanly. `npm run build`: **exit 0**. `npm run typecheck`: **exit 0**. Tested and committed as `621696d650b4c2a7239f47d34722523a31a39d95`; author and committer are both `deploy@agentweb.pro`.

The native replay now retries with the original valid verifier. Its corrected baseline passed before runtime changes. Concurrency tests assert the exact DynamoDB condition and evaluate predicates against mutable storage; two service refreshes reach the transaction with the same unused snapshot. Further cases cover stale GSI reads, ancestor replay, revocation racing rotation, missing roots, rejected-client/secret preservation, fixed expiry, and atomic failure.

Commands and operational steps: [`backend/docs/HERMES_MCP_OAUTH.md`](backend/docs/HERMES_MCP_OAUTH.md). RED/GREEN/build/typecheck/review/push transcripts are retained in `.scratch/eng1869-review/` inside the specified worktree on Atem; they are not repository artifacts.

## Scope and verification limits

No Slack callback bridge exists or is implemented. Hermes orchestration must keep the original `hermes mcp add ... --auth oauth --connect-timeout 315` PTY or `hermes mcp login emma` stdin alive and forward a later Slack callback URL plus Enter into that same persistent process. Posting in Slack alone cannot finish OAuth. No Hermes repository files were changed.

The native fixture imports installed Hermes SHA `7d13442bd0987c3936158fc9855114c0cef6e896` read-only and exercises real Emma routes/service, MCP auth/transport, native stdin paste and an authenticated fixture tool. DynamoDB transactions are a stateful expression-evaluating double, not a live DynamoDB or IAM proof. Portal login/UI, telemetry and business inventory are mocked. No live Slack adapter, real browser login, production refresh transaction, or production token/tool round-trip was tested. Earlier production discovery/DCR/authorization-redirect probes did not issue production tokens.

After a separately authorized deployment, perform the runbook's native flow and verify wrong-verifier preservation, valid replay rejection, one refresh, and ancestor replay disabling the successor. No merge/deployment is part of this delivery.

## Complexity and attribution

Review corrections: +614 / -219 lines, net +395; runtime net +99. Added a shared client-auth helper, family-state checks and transaction conflict handling; no new service, table, dependency or external auth path. Shared expression-aware test storage replaces the native fixture's permissive mock. A write-count-only refresh test was replaced by behavioral transaction/replay tests.

Accountable owner: Harsha (unchanged Linear assignee). Execution actor: Codex. Author and committer: `deploy@agentweb.pro`.

## Local review

CodeRabbit suggested a refresh-replay grace period. Declined: it would preserve a potentially stolen successor and conflicts with the requested family replay protection. The registration/lookup auth-method mismatch (reported twice) was fixed after five failing regression tests. Registered Basic/POST transport enforcement was fixed after four failing tests across authorization-code and refresh grants. The follow-up review identified a minor fixture gap in two old revoked/expired refresh tests. Their GSI lookup now resolves complete primary records and asserts the intended revocation/expiry branch; all 164 tests pass. Follow-up CodeRabbit review completed with one minor test-fixture finding (fixed as above) and no runtime findings. No zero-findings claim is made for that review snapshot.


## Push / remote state

Pushed `621696d650b4c2a7239f47d34722523a31a39d95` to the existing `fix/emma-mcp-hermes-oauth` branch; push exited 0. PR remains **OPEN / DRAFT**, unmerged. GitHub build jobs are **SKIPPED** for the draft; no CI-green or deployment claim is made. Verification above is direct local execution on Atem, not inferred from the push hook or skipped CI.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: High

Hardens Hermes native OAuth callback exchange security. The change validates client credentials, PKCE, redirect bindings, authentication methods, and refresh-token client binding. It adds atomic refresh-token rotation with replay-family revocation and preserves authorization codes after invalid attempts. It also documents the persistent CLI flow and verification limits. No production outage path was identified.

title: feat(evaluation): isolated workspace with connector-free Meta simulator (ENG-1870)
body:
**DO NOT MERGE OR DEPLOY. Harsha explicitly requested this continuation be pushed for review only.**

## Problem and resulting behavior

The first ENG-1870 implementation isolated the evaluator but only supported inspect/analyze/generate/upload. It did not satisfy the required connector-free Meta simulator.

The Evaluation workspace now lets candidates query the frozen approved dataset and create/update/inspect simulated campaigns, ad sets, ads, creatives/uploads, budgets, and schedules through Emma/MCP and the evaluation page/API. Publish, activate, and pause return validation, warnings, and resulting object/effective state with **“Simulation complete — not sent to Meta”**. All simulator persistence stays in the existing evaluation table; every object ID is synthetic and evaluation-scoped. No Meta connector/API, production ad table, org resource, URL fetch, or connector credential path is available.

Provisioning accepts a bounded positive-schema approved `simulationPacket`, maps local packet references to synthetic IDs, and freezes a separate starting case. Reset restores that case, wipes disposable artifact access/bytes, retains audits, and never refunds generation spend or reactivates access. Revision/epoch checks reject concurrent lost updates and pre-reset generation output. Cleanup intent survives failures; repeating reset completes interrupted cleanup.

The provisioning administrator and explicitly assigned active reviewers can inspect simulations/audits and private artifacts, including after candidate revoke. Unrelated administrators, organization members, candidates, and delegated/ambient transports cannot use that review grant. Candidate inspection uses a safe projection without reviewer assignments or cleanup metadata. Existing auth, tool allowlists, MCP session ownership, credentials, and revoke barriers remain in place.

No candidate-specific code/email is embedded. Operational naming and disclosure are approved in Harsha's continuation request.

- Real **Dev-AW-Evaluations** transaction smoke passed frozen-query/edit, create/publish/activate, private artifact round-trip, concurrent edits (1 accepted / 1 rejected), reset/reseed, stale epoch rejection, foreign review denial, and revoked query/reset/write denial. title: feat(agentmode): add reasoning effort mechanism (ENG-1788)
body:
## Reviewer-first

Makes OpenRouter reasoning effort explicit and testable without changing any default. A model registry row may opt in, an empty-by-default task-class map may override it, and capability metadata fails closed before `reasoning` is added to the request. The effective served effort is attached to response/message usage and the run trace.

Scope is ENG-1788 option 1 only. No effort default is configured, no task override is configured, and no user-facing policy or UX changes.

## Acceptance contract

- Registry effort is sent only when explicitly configured and supported.
- Unset effort preserves the existing request shape with no `reasoning` field.
- Task-class override wins; the default override map is empty.
- Unsupported models and fallback chains receive no reasoning field.
- Effective served effort reaches message usage, success logs, and run tracing.

## Behavior-preserving proof

- Characterization test confirms the unset response/request path remains unchanged.
- Fixed model + mocked OpenRouter transcript preserves the existing final response; only opted-in telemetry gains `reasoning_effort`.
- No model row declares `reasoningEffort`; production request behavior is therefore unchanged.
- `npm --prefix backend run typecheck`: pass.
- Focused AgentMode/OpenRouter/gateway/tracing run: 179 suites, 3,792 tests passed.
- Exact pre-push affected run: 163 suites, 3,642 tests passed.

## Complexity ledger

- Lines: +180/-3, of which +130 are acceptance/characterization tests.
- Moving parts: no dependency, service, flag, table, or runtime process added. One typed resolver centralizes capability validation and precedence rather than branching at callers.
- Behavior: no default or output change; the mechanism is dormant until a registry effort or task override is configured.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is low and bounded to OpenRouter request construction/telemetry. Capability checks fail closed, including fallback targets. Rollback is reverting commit `42ec8dc9f53f84a40088ac1b392b4b9c968993f8`; no persistent data or configuration migration exists.

## How to test

1. Run `npm --prefix backend run typecheck`.
2. From `backend`, run `npm test -- --testPathPattern='agentModeService\\.|openRouter|gatewayAdapter|agentMode/characterization|observability/tracing'`.
3. Confirm the no-effort case omits `reasoning`, the configured case sends it, task override wins, unsupported/fallback cases omit it, and tracing records the effective effort.

- No live provider request: the change is behavior-preserving and fully mockable.
- No browser QA: no UI changed.
- No policy/default activation.

title: fix: self-healing domain registration + Tests-gate bypass fix (ENG-1839, ENG-1856)
body:
## Summary

Two related fixes found while live-testing whether the publish flow actually works end-to-end.

**1. Self-heal domains that skip `customDomainUrl` registration (ENG-1839 follow-up)**

A page's `customDomainUrl` is only visible to the reachability sweep because it's matched
against an `AW-CustomDomains` record — an invariant that holds only while every write goes
through `addCustomDomain`/`addSubdomain`. It broke in production: a standing DynamoDB grant
issued for an unrelated repair (last night's ENG-1843 fix) was reused to repoint a live
customer's domain via a direct table write. The page kept reading `deployed`, no domain record
was ever created, and the domain went completely unmonitored — no log, no error, nothing, until
traced by hand.

`reconcileUnregisteredDomains` runs at the top of every sweep: finds deployed pages whose domain
host has no matching record, registers it through the real `addCustomDomain` path (genuine
Vercel-side verification, not an assumed status), folds newly-created records into the same run.
Deliberately excludes `agentwebforms.com` hosts — an unregistered managed subdomain is a
different bug in `addSubdomain`, not this kind of drift.

**This is a data-plane change (automated production record creation) — needs Harsha's sign-off
per CLAUDE.md before merge. Not merging on my own.**

**2. Tests-gate bypass no longer requires an empty check-runs list (ENG-1856)**

The prior fix (ENG-1488 follow-up, `f9ca39ef2`) only skipped the required-Tests gate when a repo
had BOTH zero check runs and zero Actions workflows. That reasoning doesn't hold for this repo
population: Vercel's GitHub integration auto-deploys and posts a check run for ANY PR on a
connected project, unconditionally, and the publish route always opens a PR as its first step —
so `checkRuns.length` is never actually 0 on a real attempt. The workflow-count check never ran,
and publish reproduced the exact unsatisfiable-gate bug the fix was built to close.

**Confirmed live: a random sample of 7 generated repos had zero merged publish PRs, ever, since
this gate shipped.** Not a partial-availability issue — total, for every generated landing page,
for roughly the last 2.5 weeks.

The workflow count is now consulted whenever no check literally named "Tests" exists, independent
of what else has reported.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Full `landingPage*`/`cron.*`/`domainReachability*`/`customDomain*` test slice — 672 tests,
      all passing (253 for the reconciliation fix, 419 for the Tests-gate fix)
- [x] Existing test that pinned the OLD (now-incorrect) behavior rewritten to test the new,
      intentional tradeoff, with reasoning — not just made to pass
- [x] Verified the fix is not a tautology: the new pinning test fails if the old
      `checkRuns.length === 0` condition is restored
- [x] Harsha review + sign-off on the data-plane piece (fix #1) — verbal go-ahead, see note below

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved custom-domain monitoring by automatically recognizing eligible domains on deployed pages when their records are missing.
  - Updated publishing checks so repositories without test workflows can proceed when only non-test automated checks are present.
  - Custom domains that are invalid or managed by the platform continue to be excluded from reconciliation.

<sub>⚠️ Note: Your high-level summary instructions were not applied because this feature is currently available only on Essentials plans or higher.</sub>

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Attribution

Accountable-Owner: Manan Varma
Accountable-Linear: ENG-1839, ENG-1856
Execution-Actor: Claude (claude-sonnet-5)
Data-plane sign-off: Harsha Vankayalapati, verbal go-ahead, 2026-09-11


## Rollback

Standard git revert — no data migration, no schema change, no destructive write.
The reconciliation fix only ever creates new AW-CustomDomains records for hosts
that currently have none; reverting removes the code path, any records it already
created remain valid, harmless, orphaned-but-correct rows (same shape a normal
addCustomDomain call would produce). The Tests-gate fix is a pure logic change to
an existing route with no persisted state of its own.
