title: fix(schedules): auto-created outreach schedules cannot be edited — scope the email-notification check (ENG-1836)
body:
## A customer cannot edit the schedule the system created for them

ENG-1723 auto-creates outreach schedules at onboarding with `emailNotifications: []`. `updateScheduledChat` then refuses **every** edit to them. Reproduced in production 2026-09-09 on a schedule created by the live auto-create path:

```
PUT /api/agent-mode/scheduled-chats/60c5c825-…   { nextRunTime: "…" }
-> 400 {"error":"At least one email notification is required for scheduled chats"}
```

The customer never asked for this schedule — the system made it during onboarding. So adjusting it is the *first* thing many will want to do: narrow the ICP, rename it, change the cadence. Each of those returned a 400 until they also handed over an email address they never chose to give, for notifications they never requested.

## Why the check was wrong rather than the auto-create

The blanket check assumed every schedule carries an address. That was true when it was written — `createScheduledChat` requires one — and stopped being true the moment ENG-1723 began creating schedules without one. The stored data already violates the invariant the check enforces.

Now scoped to where the invariant actually held:

```ts
const hadEmailNotifications =
  normalizeEmailList(existingSchedule.emailNotifications || []).length > 0;
if (effectiveEmailNotifications.length === 0 && hadEmailNotifications) { … 400 … }
```

Clearing the last address off a schedule that **has** one is still refused. Only a schedule that never had one is allowed to stay that way.

## Two existing tests retargeted, not deleted

Both asserted that an empty list is refused when the **stored** list is also empty. That is precisely the auto-created shape, and under it the customer can never edit their own schedule — so the tests encoded the bug. Rather than delete the protection, their fixtures now start with an address, so they cover what still applies: you cannot clear the last one.

Recording that explicitly because changing a test to make an implementation pass is normally the wrong move. Here the invariant genuinely stopped holding when auto-create shipped, and the tests were written before it existed.

## Verification

New test verified **failing (1 of 147)** against the unscoped check and passing after. `npm run typecheck` clean; 147 pass in `agentModeController.scheduledChat.test.ts`.

Built in an isolated git worktree — this repo clone is shared with another concurrent session that has uncommitted work in it.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

Update scheduled-chat email-notification validation. The check now rejects clearing the final email address only when the existing schedule has an address. Onboarding-created schedules with `emailNotifications: []` can remain without email notifications. Tests cover both cases. Type checking and all 147 scheduled-chat controller tests pass.

title: feat(metering): meter ElevenLabs and 2captcha (ENG-1878, split from ENG-698)
body:
Closes ENG-1878. Unblocks two thirds of ENG-698 without waiting on ENG-1598.

## Why now

ENG-698 bundles three vendors, but only **Placid** needs Harsha's credential (ENG-1598 — a 1–2 minute authorization). ElevenLabs and 2captcha have no such gate, and the whole ticket has been Blocked behind Placid since 2026-08-26.

That block was costing measurable accuracy. Over **2026-09-04 → 09-11** — the first window in which all seven live adapters were writing — vendor spend is **$89.51 of $670.85: 13.3% of total metered spend, a 15.4% uplift on LLM**. Every one of those figures was a floor while these two were missing, and the cap decision this epic exists to enable cannot be taken on a knowingly incomplete number.

> An earlier read put vendor spend at 3.9%. **That was wrong.** Four of seven adapters only began writing on 2026-09-02, so most of that 30-day window had partial coverage. The corrected figure is **3.4× higher** — the difference between "rounding error" and "one dollar in seven".

## ElevenLabs

One call site, `userId` already a required parameter, `script.length` is the quantity. `model_id` is hardcoded `eleven_turbo_v2_5`, so the Flash/Turbo rate applies unconditionally — noted at the call site, because if a caller ever picks the model the rate key must move with it or the cost silently halves against multilingual.

Characters are sent as a **fraction** of 1k rather than rounded up, so a 200-character clip is not billed as a whole unit. Metered **after** the response (a request that returned no audio was not billed) and **before** the S3 upload (losing the bytes must not lose a billed call). Both have tests.

## 2captcha — and the one real judgement call

Metered at `submit2CaptchaTask`, the single submit+poll helper all five call sites funnel through. AC3 asks for failures the vendor still billed, and the three failure shapes are **not** equivalent:

| Shape | Billed? | Recorded? |
|---|---|---|
| Submission rejected (`status !== 1`) | never accepted | **no** |
| `ERROR_CAPTCHA_UNSOLVABLE` while polling | 2captcha documents as free | **no** |
| Our 165s poll deadline | **indeterminate** — task accepted, may have been solved and charged after we stopped waiting | **yes** |

Recording the timeout makes 2captcha's allocated total an **upper bound** — the same shape X's already has — which is the honest side to err on when the alternative is under-reporting spend we may have incurred. The outcome is carried in `feature` (`captcha:solved` / `captcha:timeout`) so the two stay distinguishable. All four cases have tests.

## A defect my own test caught

Both meters are wrapped in `try/catch`, and that is load-bearing rather than defensive habit: **`computeAllocatedCost` throws on an unpriced unit by design** (ENG-703 AC2). Calling it inline — as I first did, and as the existing adapters do — would let a rate-card key rename break every voiceover and every captcha solve. AC5 forbids exactly that. It still fails loud, into the log; it just no longer fails the user's request.

## Coverage

Both vendors removed from the `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard` allowlist and added to `METERED_VENDOR_PROVIDERS`, so they appear in the admin picker. The guard's two-way assertion (ENG-1837) fails the build if either is forgotten. **Placid remains allowlisted against ENG-698**, which keeps its credential scope and its human-written ACs unmodified.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Affected backend suites | **144 passed / 7 suites** |
| Portal picker suite | 28 passed |
| Both production builds | green |

CI runs production builds only — no jest job — so these are local, per `CLAUDE.md`.

Post-deploy production verification before the ticket closes: both vendors selectable in the picker, and spend appearing once a real call occurs.

title: fix(agent-mode): stop reporting the brand-logo content gate as an outage (ENG-1844)
body:
## Summary
- Emma told a real customer landing-page generation "is currently unavailable... the underlying tool service is temporarily unreachable" and offered to file a product issue — for a real, immediate, non-flaky 422 from the correctly-working ENG-326 brand-logo gate (no persisted logo saved).
- Root cause, traced and verified directly: the `missing_brand_logo` marker never survived to classification. `httpClient.ts`'s self-call error construction picks `data.message` over `data.error` in a `||` chain, and separately `classifyToolErrorClass`'s embedded-status regex requires whitespace before the status digits — the message contains `"(422)"` with no preceding whitespace, so it doesn't match either. Both gaps together left this in the generic unclassified bucket, whose default guidance is exactly the shape that produced Emma's wrong framing.
- Fix: `httpClient.ts` now preserves the route's own `error` code on `.code` (separate from `.message`, left exactly as a human UI caller would see it — confirmed this only touches the internal Error used for the agent pipeline, never the JSON response body a real customer-portal call reads). `classifyToolErrorClass` adds a `missing_brand_logo` class keyed on that code, imported from `brandLogo.ts` as the single source of truth (not a second independent literal). `errorRetryability.ts` gives it dedicated guidance forbidding the outage framing. `toolFailureType.ts` classifies it `by_design`.

## Review round 2 (commissioned before merge)
Found one real, evidenced gap: `formatToolError`'s `isConnectionTimeout` branch matched on bare substrings `'Connection timeout'` / `'service temporarily unavailable'` with no tool-name or errorClass gate — and its own guidance text contains the literal phrases from Emma's observed wrong wording. Didn't fire on the current brand-logo message, but any future message merely containing either fragment (regardless of tool or cause) would get "external service unreachable" framing — zero test coverage existed for this branch. Tightened to match the complete, real phrases both actual origins (`mcpClientService.ts` MCP-connection failures) always emit; added coverage proving both the real-trigger and no-longer-triggers cases. Also closed a constant-drift risk (classifier now imports `MISSING_BRAND_LOGO_ERROR` instead of an independent literal copy).

## Bundled finding (same bug class, found while working a different ticket)
`toolDispatch.ts`'s install_skills preflight gate used to pre-emptively tell the model "if install_skills cannot install it — for example it is not available on this subscription — tell the user plainly unavailable on their plan" BEFORE install_skills ever runs. ENG-1795 exists specifically because install_skills refuses for 4 distinct reasons and only one is billing — this pre-empts its own accurate, bucketed reason with a guess. Replaced with an instruction to defer to install_skills' own response message. **Honest gap**: no dedicated automated test — the existing characterization harness only records success/error outcome, not message text, so covering this would need harness changes disproportionate to this bundled fix. Verified manually; confirmed zero existing tests assert the old wording.

title: feat(agent-mode): distinguish launch-ready from deployed for landing pages (ENG-1868)
body:
## Summary
- Generated landers can be handed off as launch-ready despite an unresolved Meta pixel and a failed post-deploy smoke test. Found while surveying the full ENG-18xx range — a real, separate defect from the publish pipeline. Directly relevant to a real customer page: generated with `metaTrackingInstalled: false`, `trackingInstalled: false`, and an initial `smokeTestResult: { ok: false, leadCaptured: false }` — still presented as launch-ready.
- Root cause: a reporting/handoff gap, not a missing write-blocker. `smokeTestResult` is computed fire-and-forget AFTER deploy already returns — the deploy step structurally cannot gate on it. `trackingInstalled` IS known synchronously at deploy time, but nothing downstream checked either signal before claiming success:
  - `reconcileLandingDeploymentReport` force-appended "deployed successfully" for any deployed URL, gated only on `status`/`buildStatus` — zero awareness of `smokeTestResult` or tracking.
  - `extractMinimalToolResult`'s allowlist stripped `smokeTestResult`/tracking fields before the ledger even had a chance to carry them to the reconciler.
  - `getDeploymentStatus` never read or returned either signal.
  - The frontend already had a working precedent for exactly this (`trackingInstalled`/`metaTrackingInstalled` badges) that was just never extended to `smokeTestResult`.
- Re-verified every claim above against fresh `main` myself before implementing (not trusted from the original research pass) — all held up, plus a bonus discovery: the list route already spreads the full record, so `smokeTestResult` reaches the frontend today with zero extra backend plumbing needed for the badge.

## Fix
1. New `getLandingPageLaunchReadiness()` in a standalone, dependency-free `utils/landingPageLaunchReadiness.ts` — NOT in `v0Service.ts` (heavy at import time: aws-sdk, axios) or inline in `agentModeService.ts` (required by most of the test suite per ENG-1277, so anything it imports at module scope should stay cheap).
2. Deliberately excludes `metaTrackingInstalled` from the readiness verdict — corrected from an earlier draft that would have flagged every customer with no Meta ad account connected as "not ready", which is a legitimate, deliberate outcome (ENG-1141/ENG-449), not a defect. Only a failed smoke test and missing GTM tracking count.
3. `getDeploymentStatus` returns `launchReadiness` on every branch. `extractMinimalToolResult` computes/carries it for all 5 landing-deployment tools instead of stripping the underlying signals.
4. `reconcileLandingDeploymentReport` appends a truthful "Not launch-ready yet" caveat when readiness fails — append-only, the existing "deployed successfully" line is never rewritten or removed (the build really did succeed even when the page isn't launch-ready).
5. `generate_landing_page` / `get_deployment_status` tool descriptions now tell Emma "deployed" != "launch-ready".
6. Frontend: a `smokeTestResult?.ok === false` badge next to the two existing tracking badges, same established pattern (separate PR in the customer-portal repo, branch `manan/eng-1868-launch-readiness-badge`).

**Deliberately NOT doing**: a hard 409 gate on `/deploy` (smoke test doesn't exist yet at that point) or a blanket rule on unresolved Meta tracking (would punish a legitimate, deliberate outcome). Sized to the actual symptom — a reporting gap, not a missing gate.

## Test plan

title: fix(admin): withhold the allowance comparison from the spend ledger (ENG-1874)
body:
Closes ENG-1874. Live defect on production.

## What was wrong

The spend-ledger panel showed settled spend beside a **usable allowance**, a **remaining** balance and a **"% of allowance committed"**. Those two sides have different bases:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Numerator** | `AW-SpendEvents` — holds **vendor spend only** |
| **Denominator** | `llmUsagePolicy.hardCostThresholdMicroUsd` — the tier's **LLM** cost cap |

So it rendered **"Remaining $199.93 · 0.0% of allowance committed"** on production for a billing subject whose LLM spend had already consumed most of that same $200. On a screen whose entire purpose is *explaining a pause*, the headline figure tells an admin the pause is wrong.

## Why the ledger is vendor-only

Verified in code, not inferred. `AW-SpendEvents` has exactly two writers — `incrementUsageWithSpendEvent` (`usageRecorderService.ts:296`) and `mirrorVendorUsage` (`:458`) — and **both sit inside `recordVendorUsage*`**. The LLM path calls plain `incrementUsage` and stops. ENG-1804's title scopes it that way ("dual-write metered **vendor** usage"); ENG-1250 §6 is where it changes.

## Withheld, not relabelled

A caveat under a confident `0.0%` does not work: the number gets read, the footnote does not.

**Removed:** usable allowance, remaining/overspent, % committed, and the allowance adjustments — an adjustment shown beside no balance invites the reader to reconstruct the very comparison this removes. **The pause explanation goes too**, because `explainPause` builds its reason from the same invalid comparison, so it is *wrong* rather than merely weak.

**Kept:** settled spend, in-flight, every slice, the daily trend, and the excluded-event and policy-error warnings. All describe the ledger's own contents and are unaffected.

An explicit note replaces them — saying nothing would leave an admin to read the omission as a bug and try to restore it.

## Tests

Four tests asserted the removed figures, i.e. they encoded the defect. Rewritten to assert the opposite, each naming what it supersedes so the history stays legible:

- pause explanation is withheld while the ledger cannot substantiate it
- no allowance, remaining or percentage figure renders at all — not "Uncapped", not a floored $0.00
- the absence is explained rather than left as a hole
- adjustments are withheld with the allowance

## What this does not fix

The underlying basis gap is ENG-1250 §6 — bringing LLM rows onto the ledger. When that lands, these figures become correct and should be restored; the comments at each removal site say so. This PR only stops production asserting something false in the meantime.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Portal suites | **162 passed / 22 suites** |
| Production build | green |

CI runs production builds only — no jest job — so these are local, per `CLAUDE.md`.

title: fix(agent-mode): stop restarting the shared worker on every unrelated transient failure
body:
## Summary
Found while investigating ENG-1852 (`__other_skills__` bundle intermittently empty). A diagnostic (PR #2868, live) caught the tool registry flip-flopping between 0 and 264 tools across 5 calls within one 6-second window of a single turn, all in the same worker process's log stream. Traced the real mechanism, confirmed by reading the code directly:

`agentModeController.ts`'s fire-and-forget first-attempt-failure retry path called `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.restartWorker()` **unconditionally** whenever any first attempt failed for any reason — the only justification was a comment ("the current worker may be unresponsive"), no actual check. `restartWorker()` SIGKILLs the worker process, which is a **shared singleton serving every concurrent session** — and the exit handler's `failAllPendingRequests()` rejects **every other session's in-flight turn** on that worker too, not just the one that triggered the restart. So a single transient hiccup (a provider rate limit, a bad tool call — anything unrelated to the worker process itself) was taking down every concurrent user's turn. The freshly-restarted worker also needs to re-run its own tool registration before it's ready, which plausibly explains ENG-1852's observed flip-flop.

## Fix
An `isWorkerHealthy()` ping/pong health check already existed in `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts` but was never called before restarting. Gated the restart on it: only restart (and thus only collaterally affect other sessions) when the worker genuinely doesn't respond — matching `restartWorker()`'s own doc comment ("used when the worker is detected as unresponsive"), just actually detecting that instead of assuming it. When the worker IS healthy, skip both the restart and the 3-second wait, and retry directly.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] Two new tests in `agentModeController.createSessionWithPlan.test.ts`: confirms `restartWorker` is NOT called when the health check reports healthy (the common case — a single session's transient failure no longer affects concurrent sessions), and IS still called when the health check reports unresponsive (the genuinely-broken-worker case is unchanged)
- [x] Full existing suite (38 tests) passes, including the pre-existing failure-handling test, with no regression

title: fix(agent-mode): break chatbotService/agentModeService circular import (ENG-1852)
body:
## Root cause, confirmed via a captured construction stack trace

`agentModeService.ts` imports `chatbotDb`/`ChatMessage`/`searchPlatformKnowledgeBase`
from `chatbotService.ts` at module scope. `chatbotService.ts` also imported
`AgentModeService` back as a top-level **value** import — a real circular require.

Inside the shared marketing-response worker process, that circularity caused
`agentModeService.ts`'s own module-level singleton line
(`export const agentModeService = new AgentModeService();`) to execute a **second
time** in the same process — once via the worker's own direct import, once via
`chatbotService.ts`'s back-reference — each producing a genuinely separate object.
The second instance never had `.initialize()` called on it, so its tool registry
stayed permanently empty. Whichever instance happened to answer a given
`getUnassociatedTools()` call determined whether
`install_skills(['__other_skills__'])` succeeded or failed — explaining the
intermittent, previously unexplained "0 tools / 264 tools" flip-flop within a
single session (ENG-1852/ENG-1865, and the coding_agent narration bug self-filed as
ENG-1899).

Live prod evidence, same OS process (pid 4847), two different instances:
```
[Worker] [ENG-1852-CTOR] {"pid":4847,"instanceId":"ndmzasqc",...}
  at new AgentModeService (agentModeService.js:1492:20)
  at Object.<anonymous> (generateMarketingResponseWorker.js:15:26)   ← the real, expected instance

[Worker] [ENG-1852-CTOR] {"pid":4847,"instanceId":"ffqa4l4y",...}
  at new AgentModeService (agentModeService.js:1492:20)
  at Object.<anonymous> (agentModeService.js:36810:28)               ← the module-level singleton line...
  ...
  at Object.<anonymous> (chatbotService.js:58:28)                    ← ...re-executed via chatbotService's back-import
```

## Fix

`chatbotService.ts` now imports only the **type** at module scope
(`import type { AgentModeService as AgentModeServiceType }`) and resolves the
runtime value with a lazy `await import('./agentModeService')` at the point of use
inside `generateChatResponse` — the same pattern `emmaApi.ts`'s
`getAgentModeService()` already uses to avoid this exact class of cycle.

`agentModeService.ts` is untouched — it has 49 usages of
`chatbotDb`/`ChatMessage`/`searchPlatformKnowledgeBase` scattered through the file;
the cycle only needed breaking from the lighter side (`chatbotService.ts` uses
`AgentModeService` in exactly 3 places, all within one function).

## Tests

New regression test, `chatbotService.noCircularAgentModeImport.test.ts` (AST-based
via the TypeScript compiler API, not regex, matching this repo's
`sdkConstructionGuard.test.ts` idiom):
- Asserts no top-level **value** import of `AgentModeService` from
  `agentModeService.ts` exists in `chatbotService.ts`.
- Asserts the lazy `await import('./agentModeService')` pattern is actually present
  (not just that the import was removed).

Verified both assertions fail against the pre-fix code and pass on the fix (not
just written to pass vacuously).

48 existing tests across the 3 suites that exercise `generateChatResponse` and this
exact skill/tool-binding logic
(`chatbotService.skillSessionToolBinding.test.ts`,
`chatbotService.modelRouting.test.ts`, `chatbotService.doubleCharge.test.ts`) still
pass unchanged.

## Not done in this PR

The temporary diagnostic instrumentation (`instanceId` + construction-stack
logging, shipped across #2877/#2878/#2879) is intentionally left in place — one
more live repro should confirm this fix actually resolves the flip-flop before
that cleanup PR.

title: fix(agent-mode): use the module singleton in the worker, not a fresh instance (ENG-1852)
body:
## Root cause, confirmed live (not the theory from the closed #2880)

The shared marketing-response worker process constructed its own local
`new AgentModeService()` instead of using `agentModeService.ts`'s own exported
module-level singleton (`export const agentModeService = new AgentModeService();`).
Both objects are live in the same worker process at once — importing
`agentModeService.ts` at all (which the worker does at its own top level) already
constructs the singleton as a side effect of module load; nothing needs to call for
it explicitly. The worker's own local instance correctly gets `.initialize()` called
on it. The module's own singleton never does.

`emma/tools.ts` and `apiTools.ts`'s tool handlers (`install_skills`,
`getUnassociatedToolNames`, and ~135 others) import and call methods on that plain
module-level singleton directly — not on the caller-scoped `context.service` the
`ToolContext` interface documents for exactly this purpose. Most of those methods are
stateless proxies to external APIs and don't care which instance answers.
`install_skills`/`getUnassociatedToolNames` DO depend on per-instance state populated
only by `.initialize()` (`this.toolRegistry`) — so whichever of the two live objects
happened to answer a given call determined whether
`install_skills(['__other_skills__'])` saw the correctly-populated 264-tool registry
or the permanently empty one.

Live prod evidence, same worker pid (4847), two distinct instances:
```
instanceId ndmzasqc (264 tools) ← generateMarketingResponseWorker.js's own `new AgentModeService()`
instanceId ffqa4l4y (0 tools)   ← agentModeService.ts's own module-level singleton line
```

## Correcting the record on the closed PR #2880

An earlier attempt at this fix assumed a circular import between
`agentModeService.ts` and `chatbotService.ts` caused the singleton's construction
line to execute twice, via Node re-entering the module body on a circular require. A
commissioned review built a real repro of that exact file structure under Node and
refuted it directly: Node's require cache returns the same (possibly incomplete)
exports object on a circular re-entry — it does not re-execute the module. That PR is
closed, unmerged.

## Fix

The worker now imports and uses `agentModeService.ts`'s own exported singleton
instead of constructing a redundant second instance. This matches what
`emma/tools.ts` and `apiTools.ts` already assume, so there is only ever one live
`AgentModeService` object per process again — zero changes needed to either of those
files' ~139 call sites.

## Tests

Two existing worker tests updated: their `jest.mock('../services/agentModeService',
...)` mocked `{ AgentModeService: jest.fn()... }` (the class constructor), matching
the old `new AgentModeService()` call. Now mocks `{ agentModeService: {...} }` (the
value the real import resolves to). Both verified to fail against the pre-fix code
and pass on the fix.

Full backend suite: **1719/1721 suites, 30489/30512 tests pass.** The 2 failing
suites (`createTablesDrift`, `mcp.userIdOverride`) fail identically on a clean
`origin/main` checkout — confirmed unrelated to this change and to ENG-1852, out of
scope for this PR.

## Process note

Following the standing rule for this fix specifically: review → live test on
test-env-1 → re-review if anything changes → merge only once satisfied → post-deploy,
live-test properly on production across cases, not just one repro. Not merging until
all of that is done.

## What was wrong (before)
`generateMarketingResponse` threw a generic "I apologize, but I encountered an error processing your request" on the same customer (Smart Water Heater / Vincent Hu) session **8 times over 9 days**, across 4 distinct OpenRouter failure signatures, with no fix ever landing despite being routed to `autofix` on day one (2026-09-02). Two of the four signatures were never retried at all:

- The SDK's own response-body JSON parse failing: `invalid json response body ... reason: Unexpected end of JSON input`.
- A 200 response with no `choices` array, which the unguarded `response.choices[0].message` downstream turned into a bare `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading '0')` — zero signal that the cause was an upstream response shape, not a caller bug.

## What this fixes (after)
`callLLM`'s existing retry loop (already handles `rate_limit`/`network`/`upstream_5xx`) now also retries both of the above:
- Widened `isRetryableLlmCallError` to match the raw JSON-parse-failure message pattern.
- Added an explicit, retryable check right after the OpenRouter call returns: if `res.choices` is not an array (missing entirely, not merely empty), throw a clear `MALFORMED_OPENROUTER_RESPONSE` error instead of letting it reach the unguarded downstream access.

**Deliberately NOT touched**: the other two reported signatures (`400 Provider returned error`, `404 No endpoints found that can handle the requested parameters`) are OpenRouter routing/config failures, not transient glitches — retrying the identical request would 404 identically. That needs separate, verified investigation into the specific model/parameter combination this account hit, not a guessed fix bundled in here.

## Complexity ledger
Net +116 lines (mostly tests). One new guard clause + one widened regex check in existing code; no new dependencies, no new files, no change to the shared `classifyToolErrorClass` taxonomy (kept scoped to this one call site so 400/404 stay non-retryable everywhere else, which is correct for other tools).

## How to test
1. `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts` (or run the whole `agentModeService.*` suite)
2. **Expected**: all pass, including the 4 new tests under `describe('retries a malformed/empty OpenRouter response (ENG-1681)')`

## Edge cases to check
- An empty-but-present `choices: []` (the shape dozens of other tests in this file already mock) must NOT be treated as malformed — pinned by its own explicit test so a future change can't silently widen this check's blast radius.

## Test Evidence (run on swarm box, Node 24 — Mac Node 26 is a known jest/jsonwebtoken landmine on this repo)
- **Regression proven first**: reverted just the fix (kept the new tests) and confirmed 3 of the 4 new tests fail for exactly the expected reason. Restored before proceeding.
- `agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts`: 75/75 passed (with fix in place).
- Full `agentModeService.*` suite: **168 test suites, 3674 tests — all passed, zero regressions.**
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`
- `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts`

## What was NOT tested
- The `400`/`404` OpenRouter routing-failure signatures — explicitly out of scope.
- Live production traffic (backend-only reliability fix with full unit coverage).

## Linear issue
ENG-1681


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium. `callLLM` now retries malformed OpenRouter responses caused by SDK JSON parse failures or missing `choices`. Empty `choices: []` responses keep their existing behavior. Validation and retry classification moved to a pure module. Production retry behavior can change, but rollback is localized.

title: feat(sandbox): real portal + real Emma for eval principals — phase 1 (ENG-1907)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
ENG-1870 shipped a second mini-product for evaluations: an 81-line server-rendered `/evaluation` page dumping raw case files, a single-shot Gemini call with no tools or memory, a toy simulator with `sim_*` ids, and an HTTP allowlist + socket refusal + single-tool restriction that kept an `eval_` principal out of the real portal and the real Emma entirely. Harsha rejected it on 2026-09-12: the candidate never touches the product.

## What this fixes (after)
Phase 1 of ENG-1906 (sandbox mode = real portal + real Emma with a simulated Meta connection). An `eval_` principal is now a normal customer-portal account with a policy record: the boundary is a **denylist** of connector-OAuth / MCP / API-key / billing / org / Featurebase / sharing / transfer / replay routes (Stripe test mode: outbound side effects off by default), the socket admits active sandbox principals on the same policy check, tool denial is **class-based** (`lifecycle`, `connectors`, `sends`, `social`, `publish`, `third_party_writes`, `browser`, `automation`) and enforced in all three dispatchers, provision requires the `Sandbox` tier row and seeds brand guidelines, Admin → Access Portal opens the account in the real portal, `/api/auth/me` carries `sandboxInfo`, and every fleet sweep (`getAllUsers` default exclusion + the direct scans), oncall alerting, reliability telemetry and CRM engagement skip sandbox accounts. The mini-UI, single-shot Emma, toy simulator and generation counter are deleted.

No Meta simulation yet (phases 2/3, ENG-1908/1909): a phase-1 sandbox account has no Meta connection. No portal change (phase 5, ENG-1911).

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** 57 files, +1,791 / −1,504 (net +287). Production code net **−14** with three modules deleted (`routes/evaluationPage.ts`, `services/evaluationService.ts`, `services/evaluationSimulation.ts`) and the candidate routes/tool actions removed; three small modules added (`utils/socketEvaluationAuth.ts` 59, `services/agentMode/sandboxTelemetry.ts` 43, `scripts/ensure-sandbox-tier.ts` 54). Tests net +373 (four retired suites −568, twenty-four new/extended +1,086). Docs net −72 (`EVALUATION_WORKSPACES.md` rewritten shorter, `dev.md` +43).
- **Moving parts removed:** a second frontend runtime, a second Emma, a second usage meter, a toy simulator, an HTTP allowlist. **Added:** one tool-class table, one `includeSandbox` option on `getAllUsers`, one tier row (data, applied by an idempotent script).
- **Behavior:** unchanged for every non-sandbox user — every gate is keyed on the `eval_` prefix and the pre-existing normal-user assertions in the touched suites are untouched. AgentMode chat outputs untouched; the only monolith change is the telemetry recorder skipping sandbox runs.

## How to test
1. From `backend/`: `NODE_ENV=development npx ts-node scripts/ensure-sandbox-tier.ts` — prints `added` the first time, `present` after (idempotent, compare-and-set; never edits an existing `Sandbox` entry).
2. `POST /api/admin/evaluations` as a real (non-delegated) admin with `{ email, displayName, password, expiresAt, brandGuidelines: { brandName } }` → 201 `{ userId: "eval_…", expiresAt, audit }`. The `AW-Users` row has `subscriptionType: "Sandbox"`, `brandGuidelines.brandData.brandName`, and **no** `adAccount` / `connected_accounts`.
3. Log into the customer portal as that account → lands on the app (no `/onboarding/v2` redirect); `GET /api/auth/me` includes `sandboxInfo: { isSandbox: true, label: "Sandbox", datasetId: null, datasetVersion: null, expiresAt }`.
4. Ask Emma anything → streaming works (socket `session-message-appended`).
5. Ask Emma to send an email / connect LinkedIn / deploy a landing page → the tool returns `Tool "…" is not available in this sandbox workspace (<class>).`; `POST /api/oauth/meta/init` → 403 `{ error: "Not available in this sandbox workspace" }`; `POST /api/agent-mode/share` → 403.
6. Partner portal → the sandbox user is listed → Access Portal opens the **customer portal** (`/oauth-callback?token=…`), not `/evaluation`.
7. `POST /api/admin/evaluations/<id>/revoke` → the account's next request is 401; `GET /api/admin/evaluations/<id>` as the provisioning admin still returns `{ userId, status: "revoked", audit, truncated }`.
8. With the tier row absent (dev only): step 2 → 412 whose `error` names `scripts/ensure-sandbox-tier.ts`.

## Edge cases to check
- A legacy `AW-Evaluations` row (Ryan's, provisioned under ENG-1870) still carrying `simulation` / `artifacts` / `materials` / `remaining` loads without error and denies every tool class (fail closed).
- `/api/agent-mode/ishare/<id>/generate` on a sandbox-owned session (public route, no token) → 403 before any generation spend.
- `install_skills` is allowed (deliberately outside the `connectors` `install_` prefix — denying it strips every non-foundation tool).

## Test Evidence
- Local (Mac, Node 20 — the default Node 26 cannot load `jsonwebtoken`): 26 targeted suites / 578 tests green at `f275db4f2`; `npm run typecheck` clean.
- Pre-push hook: **all 357 backend suites green** (6,022 tests, 232s, Node 20) on the first pushed head `a920167ab`, and the 268 affected suites green (106s) on `f275db4f2`. The very first push attempt saw one supertest "socket hang up" in a 60-request matrix on a slow worker (passes alone and in-band); both boundary matrices now allow 30s per case, assertions unchanged.
- Atem (exact head `f275db4f2`, Node 24, worktree `~/.agentweb-swarm/wt/eng-1907`): the same 26 suites / 578 tests green (8.4s, `--maxWorkers=2`); `npm run typecheck` exit 0.

- RED→GREEN per slice: policy/store 80 failed → 223 pass; boundary/socket/admin/me/share 67 failed → 142 pass; fleet/alerts/telemetry 17 failed → 205 pass (each recorded in the slice's test commit message).

2. *Every denied class fails closed through the portal, in-process Emma and external MCP* → `evaluationAccess.test.ts` (40 denied routes), `evaluationBoundary.test.ts` (28 denied names × `ToolRegistry` + `McpToolRegistry` + `enforceEvaluationTool`, 18 allowed names, lifecycle always denied, legacy row denies all), `agentModeController.sandboxShare.test.ts`.
3. *Fleet sweeps never include a sandbox account; no oncall/alert/CRM/nudge/telemetry rows; no share link* → `db.deletedAccounts.test.ts` (default exclude / opt-in), `eng916.metaMetricsSnapshot`, `metaTokenRefreshCron`, `activationAnalysisCron`, `renewalIntegrationHealthCron`, `cron.domainReachabilitySweep` + `Reconcile`, `clientHealth`, `metaTrackingMonitor.dryrun`, `utils/agentModeAlerts.test.ts` (userId / session owner / fail-open / dedupe window), `chatbot.lastActiveAt.test.ts`, `agentModeService.sandboxTelemetry.test.ts` (5), `admin.usersPerformance.test.ts` (roster opt-in), `agentModeController.sandboxShare.test.ts`.
4. *Usage cap from the Sandbox tier row; provision refuses without it* → `evaluationLifecycle.test.ts` (`SandboxTierMissing` before any write; tier + brandGuidelines + no `adAccount`), `evaluationAdminRoutes.test.ts` (412). The cap itself is the product's existing `checkTokenUsage` gate on `monthlyTokenAllowance` — not re-tested here.
5. *Access Portal opens the real portal; revocation invalidates all sessions/tokens in one request; reviewer access survives* → `admin.delegateAccess.test.ts` + `evaluationDelegateAccess.test.ts` (portal callback URL, evaluation scope, 11 fail-closed token kinds), `evaluationLifecycle.test.ts` + `evaluationCredentials.test.ts` (revoke + cleanup unchanged), `evaluationAdminRoutes.test.ts` (review after revoke).
6. *ENG-1870's nine criteria remain green* → 1: `evaluationLifecycle` provision (no org); 2: superseded — case material is now brand guidelines + (phase 4) KB files, not `materials`; 3: real Emma (phase 2/3 add Meta); 4/5: `evaluationAccess` + `evaluationBoundary` + `evaluationTools` (eval principal cannot provision/revoke/review, cannot install connectors/MCP, cannot reach org/admin); 6: tier-bounded usage (`evaluationLifecycle`); 7: `evaluationLifecycle` + `evaluationCredentials` (revoke bumps `sessionVersion`/`delegateTokenEpoch`, cleans five credential tables); 8: the suites above; 9: `evaluationTools.test.ts` + `evaluationAdminRoutes.test.ts` (Emma tool + admin REST).

## Files changed
- Policy/store: `services/evaluationPolicy.ts`, `services/evaluationStore.ts`, `mcp/server/evaluationTools.ts`, `routes/evaluation.ts`, `app.ts`, `scripts/ensure-sandbox-tier.ts`; deleted `routes/evaluationPage.ts`, `services/evaluationService.ts`, `services/evaluationSimulation.ts`.
- Boundary/auth: `middleware/evaluation.ts`, `utils/socketEvaluationAuth.ts`, `server.ts`, `routes/admin.ts`, `routes/auth.ts`, `controllers/agentModeController.ts`.
- Fleet/alerts/telemetry: `services/db.ts`, `cron/{activationAnalysis,domainReachability,metaMetricsSnapshot,metaTokenRefresh,renewalIntegrationHealth}Cron.ts`, `services/{metaTrackingMonitor,clientHealthService,chatbotService,agentModeService}.ts`, `utils/agentModeAlerts.ts`.
- Tests (23 new/extended, 4 retired), `docs/EVALUATION_WORKSPACES.md`, `dev.md`.

## What was NOT tested
- No live browser session against a deployed environment (phase 6 is the production proof with a disposable persona).
- The usage-cap block itself (existing `checkTokenUsage` path; the tier row values — 2M tokens, $25 LLM, $20 extra — are a first setting Harsha can change in the admin `subscription_types` editor).
- Meta behaviour (none exists for sandbox accounts until ENG-1908/1909).

## Review disposition (local CodeRabbit, pre-PR)
Fixed: `/me` converts only `EvaluationDenied` to 401 (a store outage is a 500, not a lockout); the email-first client-health lookup rejects sandbox principals; the alert path resolves the session owner with the record-only `getChatSessionRecord`; the boundary denies the whole share/ishare/conversable-share family and the public readers refuse on the session owner; socket delegates must match `delegateTokenEpoch` exactly like HTTP; terminal/claim-check telemetry callbacks receive the identity explicitly (the marked-run set is no longer the only source) and the tracking lives in `services/agentMode/sandboxTelemetry.ts`; a new invariant test pins that every gateway-known outbound tool is sandbox-classified.
Answered: (1) *persistence-model change needs data-plane approval* — recorded below; (2) *delegate token in the query string* — pre-existing behaviour of the customer portal's `/oauth-callback?token=` for every delegate, not a sandbox regression; moving all delegates to a fragment token is scoped into ENG-1911 (portal phase) with an acceptance criterion.

## Data-plane note
Approved by Harsha 2026-09-12 (ENG-1906 decision 7): policy rows stay in the existing `AW-Evaluations` table with the same key shape; the `Sandbox` tier row is a prod `AW-Settings.subscription_types` data change applied by the idempotent script — no schema, index, or IAM change. Legacy attributes are left in place on the one existing row (Ryan's), never deleted; that row is re-provisioned from scratch in phase 6 (ENG-1912), so no cleanup pass is needed. Approval for this reinterpretation is part of the same decision.

Revoke every active sandbox via `POST /api/admin/evaluations/<id>/revoke` (instant deny), then revert the merge commit. Policy and audit rows are retained. The `Sandbox` tier row is inert without provisioned accounts.

title: sandbox: Meta interceptor, dataset store, insights engine, Graph simulator (ENG-1908)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The ENG-1907-shipped sandbox account had a real customer portal and real Emma, but no simulated Meta connection: any Graph API call from a sandbox account either hit `denyByTier`/route denylist noise or, if it slipped through, would have to reach `graph.facebook.com` for real. There was also no dataset to answer from and no way to compile one from a take-home packet.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds the process-level Meta interceptor and everything behind it: a Graph request matcher, a frozen dataset store with a read-time date shift (the dataset's last delivery day always reads as "yesterday UTC"), an insights engine (sync breakdowns + the async report-run flow), a Graph read simulator answering `me/adaccounts`, `campaigns`, `adsets`, `ads`, `adcreatives`, `adspixels`, and insights with real Graph wire shapes, sentinel-token provisioning (the sandbox connection row never carries a real `adAccount`), a refresh-guard so sandbox tokens are never sent to Meta's OAuth refresh endpoint, and 18 real Graph transcripts recorded against AgentWeb's own ad account for parity testing.

## Complexity ledger
Net +~3,600 lines, all additive and namespaced under `services/sandbox/`; zero changes to non-sandbox request paths (the interceptor's real-traffic branch is a hostname check that returns before any sandbox logic runs). Two small unrelated fixes surfaced by running the full suite for the first time on this branch (see below) — both root-cause, not workarounds.

## How to test
1. `npm run typecheck` — clean.
2. `node node_modules/.bin/jest src/__tests__/sandbox src/__tests__/evaluationLifecycle.test.ts src/__tests__/evaluationAdminRoutes.test.ts src/__tests__/sandboxToolClasses.invariant.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeService.insights.test.ts` — 13 suites, 179 tests, all pass.
3. Full backend suite (Node 20, `env PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`): 1737 total, 1732 passed, 2 failed unrelated to this diff (see "Edge cases" below), 3 skipped (pre-existing e2e/twins exclusions).

## Edge cases to check
- **Sanitization gap found and fixed before push**: the transcript recorder kept URL pathnames verbatim (the `adcreatives` paging `next` link carried the real ad-account id), paging cursors decoded to real object ids, and image hashes named real assets. Fixed in `244c33761` — the recorder now remaps ids in URL paths, emits synthetic cursors/hashes, and refuses to write a fixture with any un-mapped 9+ digit run; all 13 affected fixtures repaired; the transcript test tightened to assert this and shown to fail against the old fixture.
- **Pre-existing schema-drift gap** (`createTablesDrift.test.ts`, ENG-1758 AC3): `evaluationStore.ts` has referenced `AW-Evaluations` since phase 1 (already merged/deployed), but the table was never registered in `create-tables.ts`. This test already failed on `main`; it just never ran there (CI's Backend build doesn't run this suite, and phase 1 only ran targeted tests). Fixed here by registering the table with its actual live schema — no schema/data/IAM change, `createTable` no-ops against the existing table exactly like every other entry in the script.
- **Two full-suite-only failures are pre-existing, unrelated flakiness** (`webhooks.leadForwarding.test.ts`, `mcp.userIdOverride.test.ts`): both pass in isolation with 100% of their individual tests green; the "failed" suite status only appears in the 1737-suite full run, matching the documented cross-file Jest teardown/shared-state cascade (ENG-1286-class — a file elsewhere in the run corrupts shared module state for whichever suite runs after it in the same worker). Neither touches anything this PR changes.
- Stale `@types/axios@0.9.36` devDependency was shadowing axios's own bundled types and broke `tsc --noEmit` the first time any file (this PR's `metaInterceptor.ts`) imported `AxiosAdapter`/`AxiosResponse`/`InternalAxiosRequestConfig`. Removed; no other file referenced it.

## Test Evidence
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Targeted sandbox surface: 13 suites, 179 tests, 0 failed.
- Full backend suite (Node 20): 1737 suites, 30846 tests — 1732/1734 non-skipped suites green, 30825/30846 tests green; the 2 red suites and 21 non-run tests are documented above as pre-existing and unrelated.
- Portal is unaffected (backend-only PR).

## Behavioral assertions verified
ENG-1908's acceptance contract is architectural (the interceptor/simulator exist and answer with real Graph shapes) — verified by `metaGraphMatcher.test.ts` / `metaInterceptor.test.ts` (F1, 31 tests, merged separately) plus this PR's `dateShift`, `sandboxDatasetStore`, `insightsEngine`, `graphReads`, `metaSimulator`, and `graphTranscripts` suites, each asserting the specific behavior named in its filename against the recorded real-account transcripts.

## Files changed
`backend/src/services/sandbox/*` (new: dateShift, sandboxDatasetStore, insightsEngine, graphReads, metaSimulator, objects, graphError, metaInterceptor, metaGraphMatcher, sentinel, types), `backend/src/services/evaluationStore.ts`, `backend/src/services/metaTokenRefresh.ts`, `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` (one line: skip the insights poll delay for sandbox tokens), `backend/scripts/record-graph-fixtures.ts` (new), `backend/src/scripts/create-tables.ts`, `backend/src/__tests__/sandbox/**` (new, incl. 18 recorded+sanitized fixtures), `backend/src/__tests__/evaluationAdminRoutes.test.ts`, `backend/package.json`/`package-lock.json`.

## What was NOT tested
Parity between the simulator's output and the recorded transcripts is proven per-endpoint by each module's own tests reading the same fixtures; a dedicated cross-cutting parity harness comparing every simulator response byte-for-shape against every transcript is deferred to the phase-3 simulator PR (ENG-1909) once create/update/delete exist too, per the phased plan.

## Linear issue

title: spike(agent-mode): Agentic Fabriq Gmail connector behind a flag (ENG-1685)
body:
## Risk: High | ENG-1685 | Draft, default off — no canary or rollout approval

This spike evaluates a managed Gmail connector against the existing direct path.
The previous draft guessed tool names/argument shapes and accepted insufficiently
constrained network and callback inputs. This revision adds the
pre-canary security boundaries and an offline-verifiable paired experiment runner.
It does not establish live vendor compatibility or a performance improvement.

The existing environment flag and explicit user allowlist remain off/empty by
default. Keep PR #2887 draft. No credentials were read, live vendor calls made,
deployment started, or production data modified for this revision.

## Security and experiment behavior

- REST and MCP destinations require exact HTTPS vendor-origin approval. Reject
  URL credentials, fragments, nonstandard ports, unrelated/public lookalikes,
  private/link-local targets, and redirects before forwarding bearer credentials.
  DNS resolves and checks public addresses before dispatch, then pins the approved
  address to the connection to prevent a second-lookup rebinding. Streaming reads
  enforce a byte limit and deadline through body consumption. The shared SSRF
  guard has one small normalization fix for expanded/mixed IPv6 notation; the
  change is not confined entirely to the new adapter directory.
- OAuth challenges use random single-use state bound to the initiating user,
  owned account, Gmail provider and connection. Verification uses constant-time
  comparison and atomic compare/delete; repeated initiation does not overwrite a
  live challenge. Callback input and the reread connection must match the binding.
- The canary rejects send/reply before acquiring credentials or contacting the
  vendor. Tool selection requires exact reviewed identity and schema compatibility;
  heuristic keyword matching and speculative argument mapping are removed.
- **The reviewed tool manifest is intentionally empty.** No live descriptor or
  mapping has been reviewed; discovering a plausible tool does not authorize its
  execution. The bridge currently refuses calls until that contract is reviewed.
- Strict REST/token/MCP validation bounds TTLs and descriptors and checks JSON-RPC
  version/id. Errors and spans omit raw identifiers, account values, token bodies
  and concrete endpoint paths. Hostile route and network fixtures exercise failure
  paths, not just clean synthetic-account responses.
- `pairedBenchmark.ts` accepts read-only actions below the LLM with fixed fixture
  adapters, alternating AB/BA per action/cache stratum, cold reset and recorded warm
  primers, every attempt/failure, fixed stage timings and semantic verdicts. Its
  report excludes payloads, identifiers, hashes of content, tokens and raw errors.
  Samples are configurable; p99 is inconclusive below 100 actual measured
  executions per stratum.
  See `backend/src/integrations/agenticFabriq/PAIRED_BENCHMARK.md` for precise timing,
  failure and percentile interpretation.

## Complexity ledger

<!-- DIFF_LEDGER_START -->
Snapshot of this revision against merge-base
`e22f7186423d50298c849a558208b7320e7b909b` (`origin/main`), including all
implementation, test, configuration, and benchmark documentation.
This PR-body draft itself is excluded to avoid a self-changing count.
Counts are physical diff lines, including comments and blank lines.

| Category | Files | Added | Deleted | Net |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Production/configuration | 19 | 1,711 | 28 | +1,683 |
| Tests | 13 | 1,277 | 0 | +1,277 |
| Documentation | 1 | 66 | 0 | +66 |
| **Total** | **33** | **3,054** | **28** | **+3,026** |
<!-- DIFF_LEDGER_END -->

This remains additive engineering, not a demonstrated simplification. New moving
parts include the vendor REST/MCP adapter and transport boundary, scoped token
cache, in-process single-use connect challenges, default-off route/dispatch wiring,
and offline benchmark runner. Existing direct integration machinery remains.
Removing the spike also requires reverting the small app/dispatch/env wiring; it
is not literally one directory deletion.

**Deletable existing production LOC today: 0.** Nothing in this read-only spike
replaces the full existing Gmail integration or shared infrastructure.

| Existing area | Current physical LOC | Realistic deletion assessment |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `routes/gmailAuth.ts` | 233 | Future candidate only after all direct Gmail connect/reconnect flows and existing-account migration are replaced; not deletable by this spike. |
| `services/gmailService.ts` | 590 | About 81 LOC of token refresh/client setup (lines 82–162) may become unnecessary after a complete Gmail auth replacement. The full 590 includes read shaping, batching, quota handling and send/reply behavior and is not an auth-only saving. |
| `services/emailProviderService.ts` | 386 | Retain provider abstraction, account authorization and Outlook support. |
| `routes/connectedAccounts.ts` | 712 | Retain shared multi-provider account management. |
| `services/connectedAccountsDb.ts` | 1,219 | Retain account data model and persistence; no schema/data migration is part of this revision. |
| `services/oauthTokenSessionStore.ts` | 241 | Retain shared OAuth session handling for other integrations. |
| `utils/secretsManager.ts` | 1,130 | Retain shared secret access. Even the Gmail credential helper is reused by YouTube. |

At most approximately **314 gross physical LOC** (233 + 81) are concrete,
conditional future Gmail auth candidates, before replacement/compatibility code
and only after a broader approved cutover. This is not a net-savings estimate.
Do not count all OAuth routes, the full Gmail service, or shared secrets/account
infrastructure as removable for replacing one read-only connector.

## Validation for this revision

- TDD: hostile security and experiment tests were run and observed failing before

No active safety incident: no sandbox account exists in production yet (phase 4/ENG-1910 hasn't compiled a dataset), so the failure mode without this fix would be functional once one did (a sentinel token isn't a real Meta credential, so every Graph call from that account would 401 for real), not a leak — but this must land before phase 4 ever provisions a real account.

## What this fixes (after)
Adds `services/sandbox/bootstrap.ts`, wiring the interceptor's `handle` to `createMetaSimulator` with real dependencies (policy lookup via `requireActiveEvaluation`, dataset via `getSandboxDatasetStore()`, overlay as `EMPTY_OVERLAY` until phase 3/ENG-1909 ships the write path), and calls it once from `server.ts`'s boot sequence.

## Complexity ledger
Net +~80 lines (one new small wiring module + its test + a 12-line addition to server.ts). Zero new moving parts — this connects two things that already exist and were built to be connected (per the design doc: "Interceptor. Process-level, installed once at boot").

title: fix(sandbox): launch gate destination check, CAPI safety proof, sandbox management links (ENG-1909)
body:
## Risk: High | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The Meta launch gate's destination pre-flight check (`runMetaTrackingGate`) always made a real
outbound fetch to verify a Meta pixel is installed on the ad's landing page — meaningless for a
sandbox (evaluation) account whose ads point at fictional/example.invalid destinations, since it
would always fail with no way to pass. `sendCapiLeadEvent`'s reachability from a sandbox account
had never been verified end-to-end (only reasoned about). The four `adsmanager.facebook.com?act=`
management-link build sites sent every account, sandbox included, to a dead Meta URL for an
account that was never real.

## What this fixes (after)
1. **Launch gate**: `MetaGateDeps` gained an optional `fetchHtml` override, threaded through to
   `preflightMetaTrackingGate`. A new `buildSandboxFetchHtml(userId)` (`sandboxTrackingPreflight.ts`)
   resolves to `undefined` for any real account (byte-for-byte unchanged — the real fetcher runs)
   and to a dataset-backed answer for a sandbox account, built from that account's own frozen
   `SandboxDataset.landers`. The gate stays genuinely live: an undeclared/unmeasured destination
   still returns no pixel and still blocks the launch — this is signal, not bypassed.
2. **CAPI safety (investigation + proof, ENG-1909 finding)**: traced all four callers of
   `sendCapiLeadEvent` (`webhooks.ts`, `calendlyWebhook.ts`, `metaConversionRelay.ts`, `auth.ts`).
   A sandbox account's own lead list IS reachable (no `SANDBOX_TOOL_CLASSES` entry covers CRM/lead
   tools, and `isSandboxDeniedRoute` doesn't cover public inbound webhooks), and
   `getMetaAccountCredentials` resolves that account's own sentinel token — so this is a genuinely
   reachable path, not a hypothetical. It is already safe: the process-level Meta interceptor
   classifies `graph.facebook.com` traffic carrying the sentinel and simulates it before it ever
   reaches the real network. Proved directly against the real `sendCapiLeadEvent`, not left as an
   inference — see `sandboxCapiSafety.test.ts`.
3. **Management links**: `routes/meta.ts:892` and the three sites in `routes/metaV2.ts` (272/366/438)
   now route a sandbox account to a portal-internal `sandboxManagementUrl()` →
   `${CUSTOMER_FRONTEND_URL}/meta-campaigns?campaign=<id>` instead of the real Meta Ads Manager URL.
   Real accounts are unaffected — the ternary's else-branch is the exact original expression.

## Complexity ledger
Net +413/-8 lines. New moving parts: one optional `MetaGateDeps.fetchHtml` field (default-safe,
`??` falls through to the real fetcher), one new pure module (`sandboxTrackingPreflight.ts`), one
tiny URL-builder module (`sandboxManagementUrl.ts`). No abstraction added beyond what each of the
three deliverables needed; nothing removed because nothing here was previously duplicated.
Behavior-preserving for every real account at every one of the touched call sites — see proof below.

## Behavior-preserving proof
- `MetaGateDeps.fetchHtml` is optional; `runMetaTrackingGate` passes `{ fetchHtml: deps.fetchHtml }`
  into `preflightMetaTrackingGate`, whose own `MetaPreflightDeps.fetchHtml ?? defaultFetchHtml`
  already existed and falls back to the real fetcher when `undefined`. A real account's call is
  therefore byte-for-byte the old hardcoded `{}` — proved directly in
  `metaLaunchGate.test.ts`'s new `describe('fetchHtml threading (ENG-1909)', ...)`.
- `buildSandboxFetchHtml(userId)` short-circuits to `undefined` on `!isEvaluationUser(userId)`
  *before* touching the evaluation store or dataset store at all — proved in
  `sandboxTrackingPreflight.test.ts`'s first test, which asserts `requireActiveEvaluation` was
  never called for a real user id.
- Both `agentModeService.ts` call sites (`callMetaMarketingApi`, `executeAudienceCampaignLaunch`)
  now always pass a 6th `{ fetchHtml: sandboxFetchHtml }` argument; for a real userId this resolves
  to `{ fetchHtml: undefined }`, which is `toEqual`-equivalent to the old `{}` (Jest treats
  undefined-valued keys as absent). One pre-existing exact-argument-count assertion in
  `metaLaunchGateWiring.test.ts` needed updating to include the now-always-present 6th argument
  (comment explains why); the other three assertions in that same file needed no change because
  they already used `{}` explicitly and it collapses the same way.
- Each management-link site's real-account branch (`isEvaluationUser(userId) ? sandboxManagementUrl(...) : <original expression, byte-for-byte>`) is unchanged from before this PR. `sandboxManagementUrl.test.ts` drives both a sandbox and a real userId through the live `/api/meta/v2/create-image-ad` route and asserts each gets the correct URL shape.
- `sandboxCapiSafety.test.ts`'s second test proves a real-token CAPI send reaches a locally
  substituted `fetch` stub untouched — the interceptor's `handle` is never invoked, audit counters
  stay at 0 — i.e. a real account's CAPI path is completely unaffected by any of this PR's changes
  (it isn't touched at all; this test exists purely to prove that by contrast with the sandbox path).

## How to test
1. Run the combined relevant suite: `npm test -- src/__tests__/sandboxManagementUrl.test.ts src/__tests__/sandboxCapiSafety.test.ts src/__tests__/sandboxTrackingPreflight.test.ts src/__tests__/metaLaunchGate.test.ts src/__tests__/metaTrackingPreflight.test.ts src/__tests__/metaV2Routes.test.ts src/__tests__/googleAdsLaunchGate.test.ts src/__tests__/metaLaunchGateWiring.test.ts src/__tests__/metaLaunchGate.creativeFieldList.test.ts`
   **Expected**: 9 suites / 272 tests pass.
2. `npm run typecheck` — **Expected**: clean, no errors.
3. As a sandbox (`eval_*`) account with an active evaluation policy and a pinned dataset, attempt to
   launch a Meta campaign whose landing page is declared in the dataset with a pixel id.
   **Expected**: gate passes without any real outbound fetch.
4. Same, but pointed at an undeclared/unmeasured destination. **Expected**: gate still blocks —
   this proves the sandbox path is still a live gate, not bypassed.
5. As a sandbox account, create an image/carousel/video ad or hit `/api/meta/create-ad`.
   **Expected**: `managementUrl` in the response is `<CUSTOMER_FRONTEND_URL>/meta-campaigns?campaign=<id>`, never `adsmanager.facebook.com`.
6. As a real (non-sandbox) account, repeat steps 3–5. **Expected**: identical behavior to before this PR — real outbound fetch for the gate, real `adsmanager.facebook.com` management link.

## Edge cases to check
- A sandbox account whose evaluation record has no dataset pinned (legacy row) — `buildSandboxFetchHtml` returns `undefined`, gate falls back to the real (always-failing-for-fictional-urls) fetcher rather than throwing.
- A declared lander with zero pixel ids — must NOT be treated as an always-pass; covered explicitly in `sandboxTrackingPreflight.test.ts`.
- Dataset load failure — falls back to `undefined` rather than throwing and blocking an otherwise-legitimate flow.

## Test Evidence
- Unit tests: 272 passed, 0 failed across the 9 relevant suites (see "How to test" #1).
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- Same suite + typecheck also run on Atem (swarm box) — see PR comment for the exact output.

## Behavioral assertions verified
This is a fork-directive implementation (ENG-1909 phase-3 F2 slice), not a Linear-issue-driven
acceptance contract; the three deliverables and their hard "real accounts unchanged" invariant are
each mapped to a specific test above.

- `backend/src/services/metaLaunchGate.ts` — `MetaGateDeps.fetchHtml`, threaded into the preflight call
- `backend/src/services/sandboxTrackingPreflight.ts` (new) — `buildSandboxFetchHtml`
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` — both `runMetaTrackingGate` call sites
- `backend/src/services/sandboxManagementUrl.ts` (new) — `sandboxManagementUrl()`
- `backend/src/routes/meta.ts` — sandbox-aware `adManagementUrl`
- `backend/src/routes/metaV2.ts` — sandbox-aware `managementUrl` (3 sites)
- `backend/src/__tests__/sandboxTrackingPreflight.test.ts` (new)
- `backend/src/__tests__/sandboxCapiSafety.test.ts` (new)
- `backend/src/__tests__/sandboxManagementUrl.test.ts` (new)
- `backend/src/__tests__/metaLaunchGate.test.ts` — fetchHtml threading tests
- `backend/src/__tests__/metaLaunchGateWiring.test.ts` — one pre-existing assertion updated (6th arg now always present)

## What was NOT tested

title: feat(sandbox): write simulator — create/update/delete, effective_status, adimages, overlay CAS store (ENG-1909)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Phase 2 (ENG-1908) built the sandbox Meta interceptor and read simulator but rejected every write with a hard "sandbox does not support writes yet" error (`graphErrors.sandboxWrite`). AC1/AC3 of ENG-1909 require Ryan's simulated sandbox account to accept realistic campaign/adset/ad/adcreative/customaudience create/update/delete calls, with effective_status cascades and a PENDING_REVIEW→ACTIVE review-window derivation, backed by a real optimistic-concurrency store — not just reads.

## What this fixes (after)
- New `sandboxOverlayStore.ts`: one DynamoDB item per sandbox principal (`evaluation/<userId>/sim` in the existing `AW-Evaluations` table), CAS via `ConditionExpression: 'attribute_not_exists(evaluationKey) OR revision = :expected'` (same pattern as `settingsService.ts`'s ENG-965 `setSettingIfValueMatches`), with bounded retry and a best-effort audit-row append.
- New `metaWriteSimulator.ts`: `handleGraphWrite` — create/update/delete for campaign/adset/ad/adcreative/customaudience, collision-proof id generation (`9` + 16-digit counter, never colliding with the `1…`-prefixed seeded/fixture ids), the backward-shift timestamp fix so "now" writes read back as the real current time through the existing forward date-shift on reads, a simulated PENDING_REVIEW→ACTIVE review window, and `/adimages` upload via the existing S3 upload util.
- `metaSimulator.ts` now dispatches non-GET/non-insights requests to the write simulator when `deps.mutateOverlay` is present, and preserves the phase-2 hard-refusal behavior when it's omitted (e.g. a read-only test harness).
- `objects.ts` / `types.ts`: added `customAudiences` to the resolved-objects merge and the overlay shape (parallel to every other object type).
- `bootstrap.ts`: wired `getSandboxOverlayStore()` for both `loadOverlay` and `mutateOverlay` at boot.
- **Fix found while landing this PR**: `graphReads.ts`'s `customaudiences` list edge read `this.dataset.customAudiences` (the frozen fixture array) instead of the resolved `this.objects.customAudiences` map, so an overlay-created or -deleted audience never showed up in a list call even though direct by-id reads already went through the merged view. Every other write-capable object type already listed through the resolved view — this was the one holdout, caught by this PR's own `metaWriteSimulator.test.ts` customaudiences test.

## Complexity ledger
Net +~430 lines across 2 new modules (overlay store + write simulator) plus their tests. No new dependencies. One new DynamoDB table registration (`AW-Evaluations`, already created and approved in an earlier phase — this PR just adds the `create-tables.ts` entry that was missing, closing a pre-existing schema-drift test failure). Behavior-preserving for every existing read path; the only new moving part is the write path AC1/AC3 explicitly require.

## How to test
1. `POST act_<account>/campaigns` with `{name, objective}` on a provisioned sandbox account → 200 with a new `9…`-prefixed id.
2. `GET <that id>` → reflects the posted fields; `GET act_<account>/campaigns` → the new campaign appears in the list.
3. `POST <that id>` with `{status: 'PAUSED'}` then `GET act_<account>/ads?fields=effective_status` for a child ad → cascades to `CAMPAIGN_PAUSED`.
4. `DELETE <that id>` → `{success: true}`; subsequent list no longer contains it.
5. `POST act_<account>/customaudiences` → create, read back by id, appears in list, delete, disappears from list (this exact path is what caught the bug above).

title: fix(sandbox): install the Meta interceptor in the AgentMode worker process (ENG-1912, CRITICAL)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Urgent

## What was wrong (before)
Found live in production during the ENG-1912 phase-6 proof: a disposable sandbox persona's `call_meta_ads_insights_api` tool call reached the **real** `graph.facebook.com`, carrying its sentinel token, and got Meta's own real `(#190) Bad signature` OAuthException back. Confirmed directly from production logs — the request object logged `url: 'https://graph.facebook.com/v25.0/act_.../insights'` and `access_token: 'sbx.eval_....'`.

Root cause: `generateMarketingResponseWorkerService.ts` runs all AgentMode tool execution in a **separate forked child process** (`generateMarketingResponseWorker.ts`), with its own V8 isolate and its own `globalThis`. `server.ts`'s `installSandboxMetaInterceptorAtBoot()` call only runs inside the main process's `server.listen()` callback — it never executes in this worker, so the worker's `fetch`/axios/`https` were never patched. Same bug class as ENG-1917 (interceptor never installed at boot), in a second, previously-undiscovered process.

No real Meta data or real customer was exposed — Meta's own signature validation rejected the sentinel token outright (it's not a real credential). But the core invariant this whole feature depends on ("zero requests leave the process for `graph.facebook.com`") was actively violated for **every** AgentMode tool call touching Meta — the primary way a candidate/Emma interacts with Meta data in the sandbox.

## What this fixes (after)
Installs the interceptor at the top of the worker entry script too, guarded by the same `shouldBootstrapBackgroundJobs()` check `server.ts` uses (skip under the Jest test-boot path — this worker module is imported directly by two existing test files, and `metaInterceptor.test.ts` owns the module-level singleton's install/uninstall lifecycle itself).

## Complexity ledger
Net +24/-0 lines in the worker file (mirrors the exact pattern already in `server.ts`) + a new focused test file. No new dependency, table, or behavior change for real accounts — this worker serves real accounts identically; the guard is a pure no-op for them.

## How to test
1. Provision a sandbox persona, send an Emma chat message that triggers a Meta insights/campaign-list tool call.
2. Before this fix: real `graph.facebook.com` request, real `Bad signature` OAuthException (reproduced live in prod).
3. After this fix + deploy: simulated Meta-shaped success from the frozen dataset, zero real network egress.

## Edge cases to check
- Worker install failure doesn't crash the worker (logs and continues) — covered by the new test's third case.
- Jest test-boot path never double-installs against the same module-level singleton — covered by the new test's second case, and the two pre-existing worker test files (unaffected, still 8/8 green).

## Test Evidence

title: fix(sandbox): reset() clears chat history and generated content (ENG-1924)

`evaluationStore.reset()` only restored the simulated Meta dataset overlay to its seed hash — it never cleared chat sessions/messages, tasks, work plans, or generated files. `purge()` clears all of that, but also permanently deletes the account (and its already-issued login), which isn't the "make it fresh for reuse" operation an admin actually wants.

## What this fixes (after)
`reset()` now runs the same `SandboxArtifactCleanup.preparePurge(userId)` cleanup engine `purge()` already uses (chat sessions/messages, tasks, work plans, agent runs, leads, skills, memory, deals, templates, S3/GCS files), minus purge()'s separate account-deletion transactWrite — so the account, its credentials, and its policy/audit trail survive while every piece of candidate-produced content is cleared. Zero new moving parts — this swaps one existing, already-tested cleanup call (`deleteSandboxPrefix`, S3-only) for another existing, already-tested one (`preparePurge`, which is a superset covering S3 *and* every DynamoDB table a sandbox account can touch). Removed the now-unused `deleteSandboxPrefix` requirement from the `SandboxLifecycleDeps` interface (the underlying `SandboxArtifactCleanup` method and its standalone export are left in place — still independently useful/tested, just no longer required by this interface).

2. As admin, on `/sandbox-accounts`, click "Reset" on that account and confirm.

title: fix(linkedin): say which gate stopped a stale-invitation drain (ENG-1873)
body:
## ENG-1873, AC2: a stale-invitation drain now says which gate stopped it

`withdraw-stale-invitations` withdrew **nothing** on three production runs across 14 hours (2 invitations, both >1 day old), each time reporting:

> *Stopped early: this account is at its write-pacing limit…*

That wording was asserted, not known. `paceLinkedInWrite` refuses from **three** independent sources, and the drain threw away the refusal it was handed and hardcoded the write-pacer message:

| gate | source |
|---|---|
| `daily_volume` | the daily connection-request cap, including the durable re-check |
| `write_pacer` | the hourly ceiling / queue in `reserveWriteSlot` |
| `reservation_persistence` | both checks passed, but the daily reservation could not be written |

So the defect's one investigation went to the wrong subsystem, and couldn't be narrowed because the refusing gate's log line was unobtainable (EB log retrieval was returning stale bundles).

## Change

- Every `paceLinkedInWrite` refusal carries a machine-readable **`gate`** — no string-matching on prose.
- The drain's `pace` dependency returns `{ gate, reason }`; the result exposes **`pacedGate`** and **`pacedReason`**.
- The notice names the gate that actually refused and relays its first line. "write-pacing limit" appears **only** when the write pacer refused.
- The action logs the gate, so **one drain run now diagnoses itself from its own tool result**.

Compatibility: `pace` still accepts a bare string (reported as `unknown`, claiming no specific gate). The new `gate` field is additive on refusal objects `routes/crm.ts` also returns.

## Why this is the first step, not the whole fix

This is AC2. AC1 — the drain actually withdrawing — needs the real cause, which this PR exposes. The leading suspect is worth stating: a cancel consumes no invite budget but still goes through the **durable daily-volume commit**, so a persistence failure there refuses every withdrawal while both pacing checks allow. That commit is the one step the original local reproduction never exercised. Once deployed, one run confirms or rules it out.

## Tests

- **Gate:** one assertion per refusal source, plus the drain's own path (`cancel-invitation` still commits the reservation; a persistence failure refuses it as `reservation_persistence`).
- **Drain:** a paced stop names its gate; daily-volume and persistence refusals never claim write-pacing; a bare string is `unknown`; an unpaced run has no gate fields.
- **One existing test retargeted, not deleted.** It asserted "write-pacing limit" from a bare, *unidentified* refusal string — the exact assumption behind the misreport. It now supplies a genuine `write_pacer` refusal, the only case where that wording is correct.

Verified **failing (9 of 56)** against `main`'s pacer and drain, passing after. 77 pass across the drain, gate and CRM outreach suites. Typecheck: no errors in changed files (the only local errors are in `sandbox/metaInterceptor.ts`, untouched here, from the local dependency tree lagging current `main`).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium

The change identifies why stale-invitation draining stopped `paceLinkedInWrite`. It propagates refusal gates and reasons, reports them in notices and logs, preserves bare-string compatibility as `unknown`, and adds targeted tests. The change affects LinkedIn pacing and drain control flow but does not fix the underlying withdrawal failure.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(billing): delete-protect the AW-SpendEvents money ledger (ENG-1250)
body:
`AW-SpendEvents` is the immutable, no-TTL, seven-year audit ledger for money, and it was created with **deletion protection off** (the account-wide default — verified `DeletionProtectionEnabled=false` on the live table). One accidental console/API delete is unrecoverable: no TTL to rebuild from, and per ENG-1758 no backups or PITR either.

## Two changes

1. **Spec** (`create-tables.ts`, `ensureCriticalTables.ts`) now sets `DeletionProtectionEnabled: true`, so any fresh creation (dev, disaster recovery) is protected from birth.

2. **`ensureCriticalTables` now reconciles protection on the already-exists path.** `createTable` never updates an existing table, so a flag added *after* the table was created would never reach production. On `ResourceInUseException` for a spec that requests protection, it describes the table and enables protection only if off — **describe-first**, so an already-protected table costs one read and no write (this runs every boot and must not churn `UpdateTable`).

**Fail-safe:** any error — including the runtime role lacking `dynamodb:UpdateTable` — is logged and swallowed. The flag is purely additive (prevents a delete; cannot orphan, expose or lose data), so not applying it is the status quo, and a missing safety flag must never take startup down.

## Not a data-plane gate

This is the *opposite* of what that gate guards — it makes data harder to lose, not easier — and it's reversible.

## Live table

Still shows protection off: the `vendor-argusoft` IAM user lacks `UpdateTable`. It flips on the next deploy where the EB role runs `ensureCriticalTables`, or via one manual `UpdateTable` by anyone with the permission. The describe-first guard makes repeated runs safe.

## Testing

11 tests. Three mutations fail: skipping the reconcile, dropping the describe-first guard, letting `UpdateTable` errors escape.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

Enable deletion protection for `AW-SpendEvents` during creation and startup reconciliation. Describe existing tables first, then update only when protection is disabled. Log and swallow reconciliation errors, including missing `dynamodb:UpdateTable` permission, to prevent startup blockage. Production remains unprotected until deployment or manual update.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(accounts): retry a config write that collides with an in-flight transaction (ENG-1873)
body:
## ENG-1873, AC1: the root cause of the drain withdrawing nothing

With AC2 deployed (#2897), a production drain finally named its own refusal — `pacedGate: reservation_persistence`. The exception behind it, from a production log bundle:

```
[linkedInDailyVolumeGate] failed to reserve daily volume for FtFMgtmhQdezRcG6PJaqMw:
TransactionConflictException: Transaction is ongoing for the item
```

## Cause

`TransactionConflictException` means another request holds a DynamoDB transaction on the same item. On the users table that is **`applyMonthlyChargeAtomic`**, which `tokenUsageService` runs for each LLM completion.

A tool call executes as soon as its completion returns — frequently while that completion's charge transaction is still committing on the very user record the tool then writes. `updateAccountConfig` retried only `ConditionalCheckFailedException`, so the collision threw, `paceLinkedInWrite` failed closed, and the drain stopped before its first withdrawal.

**Not deterministic.** A later run in the same session won the race and withdrew both invitations (ledger 2 → 0, no invite budget consumed). That's also why earlier investigation could reproduce "both gates allow" locally and still see production refuse.

**Not specific to withdrawals.** This helper backs **25 call sites** — including sends and token refreshes — so any connected-account write made from a tool call could lose the same race.

## Fix

AWS documents the error as transient, and `paymentHistoryDb` and `usageRecordDb` already classify it that way. `updateAccountConfig` now retries it with a short bounded backoff — **4 retries, ~50–450 ms each** — and **re-reads before every retry**, re-applying the merge exactly as the CAS path does, so a retry can never write a stale snapshot.

The retry budget is **separate** from the CAS budget:
- a genuine concurrent overwrite still gives up with `ConnectedAccountChanged` after three tries
- any other error still propagates immediately
- worst case adds under a second before the original error is rethrown

## Tests

title: feat(metering): meter Placid image renders (finishes ENG-698)

The **last unmetered paid vendor** in the codebase. ElevenLabs and 2captcha shipped in ENG-1878; Placid waited on its credential migration (ENG-1598), which Harsha authorized 2026-09-11. With that unblocked, this wires the metering.

The file's other two Placid endpoints — the editor access-token mint and the template list — are **deliberately not metered**: they aren't renders and Placid doesn't bill them.
