title: feat(metering): meter Placid, the last unmetered paid vendor (ENG-698)
body:
Closes ENG-698. With this, every known paid-vendor egress module records usage.

## The ticket named the wrong calls

ENG-698 said to meter Placid's editor-token and rendered-image-fetch calls. Reading the code, only **one** Placid call in the codebase is billable, and it is neither of the two that use the private token:

| Call | What it does | Billable | Uses private token |
|---|---|---|---|
| `getPlacidEditorToken` | mints an editor JWT | no rate | yes |
| `listPlacidTemplates` | catalogue read | no rate | yes |
| `generateFromTemplateToExecution` | **URL API image generation** | **`image_render` $0.095** | **no** |

So the credential migration and the metering apply to **different calls**. Metering the two token consumers would book spend Placid never charged.

## 1 · Token from Secrets Manager

Harsha created `prod/AgentWeb/Placid` on 2026-09-11 (ENG-1598). `getPlacidPrivateToken` reads it first.

He described it as holding *"a non-empty `PLACID_PRIVATE_TOKEN` value"* — which fits both a JSON object keyed by that name and a bare token string. The secret isn't readable from here, so **both shapes are accepted** rather than guessing one and breaking production on the other. A test proves this bites: without JSON handling, the entire `{"PLACID_PRIVATE_TOKEN":…}` string would be sent as the bearer token.

It falls back to `process.env.PLACID_PRIVATE_TOKEN` when the secret is absent — the normal case in development, where no `dev/AgentWeb/Placid` exists. The fallback is **logged, not silent**: the point of the migration is that production stops depending on the env var.

## 2 · Render metering

Recorded after Placid returns the image and **before** the S3 upload, so a storage failure can't lose a render Placid already charged for. Placid's URL API serves an identical parameterised URL from cache while we record every successful response, so this allocated total is an **upper bound** — the same shape X's already has. Wrapped in `try/catch` because `computeAllocatedCost` throws on an unpriced unit by design (ENG-703 AC2).

## 3 · Coverage is now complete

- The `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard` allowlist is **empty**. The scan and staleness checks still run, so a *new* unmetered vendor fails the build exactly as before — an empty amnesty list is the goal state, not a switched-off guard.
- `placid` joins `METERED_VENDOR_PROVIDERS`, so it appears in the admin picker.
- **The "Placid is not metered yet" undercount warning is deleted**, as its own marker instructed. Leaving it would tell admins usage is absent when it is present — the stale-caveat mistake from #2864, at full scale.

## Commits

Split per `CLAUDE.md`: credential migration · metering · tests.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Affected backend suites | **140 passed** |
| Portal admin suites | **93 passed** |
| Portal production build | exit 0 |
| Backend typecheck | no errors in changed files |

**One honest caveat on the backend build.** It fails locally, but **only** on `services/sandbox/metaInterceptor.ts` — pre-existing, not in this diff. My local `node_modules` has a stray `@types/axios` that isn't in `package.json`; those axios-0.x typings shadow axios 1.x's own. CI builds from the lockfile with `npm ci` and won't have it, so the **CI Backend build is the proof** here, not the local one.

Both negative tests were checked by breaking the code: removing JSON handling fails the token test; removing the metering call fails exactly the two metering assertions while the "does not meter" tests keep passing.

## Post-deploy verification

Needs an admin view: confirm a `provider = placid` ledger row appears after a real render, and that the picker lists Placid. Not yet verifiable without browser access.

title: feat(admin): compute actual all-in cost now that vendor coverage is complete
body:
AC3 of ENG-1139 asks for actual all-in cost split into LLM, non-LLM vendor, admitted-work overrun and infrastructure. It was **blocked on the vendor half not being measurable** — that's no longer true.

## Why it's unblocked

As of 2026-09-14 **every paid vendor writes to `AW-UsageRecords`** (v0, X, You.com, Google CSE, Apollo, enrich.so, Remotion, ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid) and the coverage guard holds **zero** allowlisted vendors. Verified on production: all five vendors with September traffic write to the ledger, **v0 included** — the header's claim that v0 lives in `AW-V0Usage` outside the ledger was stale.

So `vendorCostUsd` is now **complete**, not a sample, and the reason all-in was withheld (a figure silently omitting most of its inputs) no longer applies.

## What's added

- `allInCostUsd` = LLM + vendor (per row and per tier)
- `admittedWorkOverrunUsd` = LLM spend past the **effective** cap (threshold + credits + grants), clamped at 0; $0 for an uncapped tier
- `infrastructureUsd` = 0, **deliberately** — the billing boundary excludes shared platform overhead from per-account attribution without a reviewed policy, so allocating it per account would be an invention. Separated and honest rather than omitted.
- `vendorCoverage`: `'partial'` → `'complete'`; stale header and coverage note rewritten.

## The one test rewritten, not deleted

It asserted the old invariant ("coverage partial, so never sum an all-in"), which genuinely no longer holds. Rewritten to the enduring AC3 invariant: all-in still **separates** its parts.

## What this does NOT close

ENG-1139 stays open: AC3's *target comparison* (/3/80) needs the authoritative COGS numbers, which are stale and are a business decision (**ENG-1688**). This ships the measurement; the comparison layers on once those exist. Row-id kept out of the title deliberately so the integration doesn't auto-move a still-open row.

## Testing

21 tests. Four mutations fail: all-in omitting vendor, overrun ignoring the threshold, overrun not clamped at 0, infrastructure invented as nonzero.

title: Record LLM spend in the spend ledger alongside vendor spend (ENG-1934)
body:
## What

LLM spend now reaches `AW-SpendEvents` alongside vendor spend (ENG-1250 §6). Until now the ledger held vendor spend only, about 13% of what AgentWeb pays for, so a cap or credit price could not be sized from it.

**Observe-only.** Enforcement does not change: the live cap still reads `AW-Users.tokenUsage.totalCost`.

## Both LLM write paths

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `recordUsage` (every in-process call) | plain aggregate `update` | aggregate + spend event in **one** conditional transaction, same as `recordVendorUsage` |
| `POST /internal/usage` (agent-engine batches) | 2-item txn: aggregate + `AW-LlmChargeEvents` | + one spend event **per priced portion**: `llm:<id>` for price-book records, `llm:<id>#engine` for engine-priced records. Unpriced records get none, and a group nobody priced is labelled `unpriced` |

## Event shape

| Field | Token call | Image/video (`costUsdOverride`) |
|---|---|---|
| `unit` / `quantity` | `llm_token` / all tokens | `llm_generation` / number of generations |
| `operation` | model id | model id |
| `eventId` | `llm:<call id>`, or `gen:<uuid>` built once before retry | same |
| `rateCardVersion` | `llm-price-book:2026-09-10` | book when priced from llmPricing; `caller:openrouter` / `caller:agent-engine` otherwise |

- An unpriced model writes the aggregate only, never a $0 event.
- A ledger failure falls back to the plain aggregate write and is counted by `usageWriteFailureMonitor`. The LLM call is never failed or slowed.
- Aggregate date and event instant come from one clock read, so a call can't split across UTC midnight.
- Engine transaction: `duplicate` stays keyed on the charge item. A spend-event-only condition failure throws, so the route's fallback writes the usage instead of skipping it.

## Kill switch

`SPEND_LEDGER_LLM_DUAL_WRITE`, **default ON** (product decision: we need a full billing cycle of data before sizing a cap). Only `false` disables it, which restores today's writes exactly. It's separate from the vendor `SPEND_LEDGER_DUAL_WRITE`. Both tables are PAY_PER_REQUEST (checked).

## Reconciliation (§8)

Without this change every LLM event would read as an ORPHAN. `reconcileVendorFidelity` gains `llmMirrorStartedAt`. When it's absent, LLM data is excluded on both sides, same as before. LLM groups key on `(date, model)`, because pre-ENG-693 rows have no provider. Unpriced LLM rows are excluded. The report script defaults the start date to `LLM_SPEND_LEDGER_STARTED_ON` (`2026-09-14`).

## Admin spend ledger

The breakdown route returns `llmLedger { recording, startedOn, month: none|partial|full, missingLlmMicroUsd }`. Coverage is **measured**: settled LLM events are compared with the aggregate rail's LLM rows for the same billing subject and month. That catches the days before recording began, kill-switch gaps and fallback writes alike. An unmeasurable month is `partial`, never `full`. The panel brings back the allowance figures ENG-1874 withheld (usable allowance, remaining, %, adjustments):
- **full month:** shown, labelled as LLM + vendor spend against the allowance.
- **partial:** shown, with *"Understated: $X of LLM spend is not in the ledger"* (or *"Unverified"*) in the figure's own caption, including for uncapped tiers.
- **earlier months, or a backend without the field:** still withheld, with the reason shown.
- **Pause explanation stays withheld.** The live gate counts LLM only and this total counts both (ENG-1886).

Deploy order is safe either way: the portal treats a missing `llmLedger` as vendor-only.

## CodeRabbit review (head f74870a07): all 5 findings fixed
Engine generation count; mixed pricing in one engine group; coverage inferred from config; reconciliation inferring "unpriced" from a $0 cost; caption hidden for uncapped tiers. Details are in each thread.

## Verification
- Backend typecheck clean (only the pre-existing `metaInterceptor` errors from a stray local `@types/axios`; CI build is the gate).
- 62 related backend suites, 1,594 tests pass. Portal ledger suite: 33 tests.
- Mutation checks: dropping the call id or the fallback write fails the recorder suite; dropping the generation count or collapsing engine provenance fails the engine suite; changing one price without bumping the version fails the price-book fingerprint test.
- `usageRecorderService.test` and `routes/internalUsage.test` now run with the switch OFF. That makes them the proof that OFF is unchanged; with it ON, the recorder suite's mock would have passed every test through the failure fallback.

## Post-deploy check
1. `AW-SpendEvents` contains `unit=llm_token` events for real traffic within minutes of deploy, with `costMicroUsd` matching the aggregate.
2. EB logs show no `[usageRecorder]` / dropped-write alerts.
3. From 2026-09-15: `npx ts-node src/scripts/spendReconciliationReport.ts 2026-09` shows no LLM drift on full days.
4. Partner portal spend ledger for September shows the allowance with the "Understated" caption.

## Rollback
Set `SPEND_LEDGER_LLM_DUAL_WRITE=false` on EB (no deploy needed), or revert the PR. Events already written are immutable and are ignored by every reader when fidelity's LLM start is unset.

Refs ENG-1250 §6, ENG-1874, ENG-1886.

Adds LLM spend-event dual writes while preserving `AW-Users.tokenUsage.totalCost` enforcement. Updates reconciliation, coverage reporting, admin allowance display, retries, and fallback monitoring. Production usage writes could cause spend-recording gaps, but rollback is available through `SPEND_LEDGER_LLM_DUAL_WRITE`.

title: ENG-1831: extract OpenRouter request-param decision + guard registry against supported_parameters
body:
## Why
ENG-199 shipped Claude Fable 5.1 with `tool_choice` unsupported on OpenRouter; because callLLM sends `provider.require_parameters: true`, every agent-mode turn 404'd (`No endpoints found that can handle the requested parameters`) for its whole time in the picker. Nothing checked the registry against OpenRouter, so the next model could repeat it. This is Phase 1 of ENG-1831.

## What
- **`agentMode/openRouterRequestParams.ts`** (pure): `selectOpenRouterSamplingParams` (tool_choice / temperature), `openRouterIgnoredProviders` (the ENG-1702 Gemini ignore), `assertOpenRouterToolsSupported`. callLLM now calls these instead of the inline block.
- **Fallback-aware**: `tool_choice` and `temperature` are sent only when the primary AND every `models` fallback accept them — the chain gets one parameter set. Reasoning effort already worked this way. Only current fallback caller is deep research (Sonar → Sonar), where nothing changes.
- **`supportsTools` registry flag**, false on `perplexity/sonar-deep-research` and `sonar-pro-search` (no OpenRouter endpoint lists `tools`). callLLM throws a named error before the network call if tools (incl. web search) reach such a model, instead of the routing 404. Deep research never sends tools, so no production path changes.
- **Guard test** `openRouterRequestParams.registryGuard.test.ts`: for every non-live registry model, at least one non-ignored endpoint in the committed snapshot must accept the widest parameter set callLLM can send it. Checks only the dangerous direction. Includes mutation cases proving it catches ENG-199 and an undeclared tool-less model.
- **Snapshot** `fixtures/openRouterSupportedParameters.json`, refreshed with `npm run refresh:openrouter-params` (public `/models/{id}/endpoints`, which follows aliases — e.g. `qwen/qwen3.8-max` → `qwen3.8-max-0902`, which the `/models` list no longer shows).

title: ENG-1718: label list-sent-invitations sent_at as approximate (false 'burst' reported to a customer)
body:
## Why — found verifying ENG-1718 against real production runs
TFA Connect's daily Dream 100 schedule hit LinkedIn's account-level cooldown on 09-11 and 09-13 (CloudWatch: `Armed invitation cooldown breaker` for `ofGscnIrR5qZYZ00ovNsTQ`). On both runs `list-sent-invitations` worked as ENG-1718 intends: a real live list, `Pending backlog ≥100 (cursor not exhausted)`, both pages read.

Both runs then told the customer about an **"unexplained anomaly — ~50-invite batch all sent within ~16 seconds"**, and asked them to check LinkedIn. That anomaly is ours:

- LinkedIn exposes only relative ages ("Sent 6 days ago"). Unipile resolves the label to an absolute `parsed_datetime` **at request time** (already documented by the ENG-875 drift test).
- The 09-11 run's list call ran at **17:17:36Z**. The "burst" it reported was **2026-09-05T17:17:37Z**, six days earlier to the second. The other "burst" (09-10 17:16–17:17) is one day before its 17:16–17:17 calls.
- TFA's ledger (read-only check): **681 rows, 39 distinct `sentAt` values**; every row an exact 0/1/2/7/14/31/61/92/122/181 days before its sync time.

ENG-1718 is what added `sent_at` back to this action's output, so presenting it as a precise send time is a defect in that work.

## What
- `live` and `cache` results carry `sentAtIsApproximate: true`. Their `notice` now includes `SENT_AT_PRECISION_NOTE`: identical timestamps are not a burst and must not be reported as an anomaly, and older dates can be weeks off.
- The `list-sent-invitations` tool description says the same thing.
- No data or selection changes. `source: 'none'` results are unchanged.

## Not in this PR (filed separately)
The ledger's `sentAt` quality: 450/681 TFA rows fall back to first-sync time when Unipile omits `parsed_datetime`. That makes the ENG-1719 drain **under**-withdraw for large-backlog accounts. It never over-withdraws, because an estimate is never older than the real send. Correcting stored `sentAt` also moves CRM invite-sent dates and follow-up cadence, so it needs its own decision.

## Tests
- 3 new view tests (live flagged + note, cache flagged + note, absent for `none`); the view suite passes 18/18.

title: fix(agent-mode): create_html_from_template variable values as plain text
body:
## Summary — corrected 2026-09-15, see comment history

**This PR was originally aimed at the wrong call site.** The first version patched `performDataAnalysis`'s prompt, based on an initial (wrong) assumption that its raw output was the source of HTML markup leaking into a customer report. An independent review caught this; pulling the real Haven session's actual `AW-ChatMessages` data confirmed it definitively:

- `performDataAnalysis`'s real raw output is rich **Markdown** (`### headers`, `| tables |`, `**bold**`) — never HTML. It was never the source.
- The actual `<ul><li><strong>` HTML that reached the customer report came from a **separate LLM turn** — the one composing `create_html_from_template`'s own `variable_values_json` — which reformatted the Markdown-formatted analysis into HTML on its own initiative, because that tool's description gave no formatting guidance at all.

The original `performDataAnalysis` fix was reverted (`git revert 3ac064586` → `dfcf4314a`) since it addressed nothing and risked regressing `performDataAnalysis`'s other real callers (chat, `POST /api/crm/lists/:listId/analyze`, the public `/data-analysis` Agent API) that legitimately want its Markdown output.

## The real fix

`create_html_from_template`'s tool description and both its `variable_values_json`/`array_variable_values_json` parameter descriptions (`backend/src/emma/tools.ts`) now explicitly forbid HTML tags and Markdown syntax in variable values — values are inserted as literal text, so this is where the formatting contract actually needs to live.

## Test plan
- [x] New test (`emmaTools.createHtmlFromTemplate.plainText.test.ts`) asserts the tool's registered description text directly.
- [x] Mutation-tested: reverted just the `tools.ts` change, confirmed exactly 3/4 of the new tests fail (the 4th, "tool is registered", correctly still passes), nothing else; restored, reverified clean.
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean; 99/99 across the 3 affected suites.
- [x] Live-verified on test-env1 against the actual mechanism, not a proxy: called gemini-3.7-flash directly (the same model that produced the real bug, confirmed via the real session's llm field) with only the corrected tool schema and a device-breakdown prompt structurally identical to the real one — model composed clean plain-text sentences, zero HTML, zero Markdown bold.
- [x] Root-caused against ground truth: pulled the real Haven session's actual tool-call arguments from prod AW-ChatMessages (sessionId 9a1c837f-1517-4656-b943-4bdb9442affe) to confirm exactly which LLM turn produced the HTML, rather than assuming.

title: autofix: raise maxConcurrent 1→3 to match the box's proven-safe forced-run cap
body:
## What was wrong (before)
`maxConcurrent` (non-forced bugs run in parallel) was stuck at 1, even though `maxForcedConcurrent` on this same box has safely run 3 concurrent forced bugs since 2026-07-21. The box (t3.2xlarge, 8 vCPU/32GB) had already earned this headroom; the config just never caught up.

## What this fixes (after)
`maxConcurrent: 1 → 3`, matching the already-proven-safe `maxForcedConcurrent` cap. Comment updated in place to record why (kept the 2026-07-02 OOM history, added the 2026-07-21 forced-run evidence).

## Complexity ledger
One config value + comment. No new moving parts, no EC2 change.

## Why no hardware change
Checked CPU utilization on `i-0cb38aac2332941dc` over the trailing 7 days via CloudWatch: **1.4% average, 72.9% peak**. The original OOM (2026-07-02, 16GB box) and the forced-run OOM (2026-07-21, this 32GB box at 5-wide) were both memory pressure, not CPU. The box already supports 3-wide safely — that's what `maxForcedConcurrent: 3` proves in production today. This PR just extends that same proven ceiling to ordinary (non-forced) bugs.

## What was NOT changed
`maxPicksPerCycle` stays at 1/cycle — so this mainly widens the crash-recovery/backfill parallelism path and normal per-cycle concurrency once a pick happens, rather than immediately tripling backlog drain rate. Flagged in the comment as a natural next question, not bundled into this change.

1. Deploy this branch to the runner (or let the next sync pick it up).
2. Trigger 2-3 non-forced bugs in the same poll window (or wait for organic backlog).
3. **Expected**: up to 3 run concurrently via `poll.mjs`'s `Promise.all` pool (see `processNewBugs`), no OOM/load spike, `htop`/CloudWatch stays well under what the 2026-07-21 5-wide incident showed.

title: [needs human] Unlock a skill's tools in the same batch that installs it (ENG-1945)
body:
**Bug**: install_skills reported success, but a tool it unlocked (e.g. playwright_browser_navigate) called in the SAME model response was rejected as 'not available'. Root cause: the tool-dispatch loop's allowedToolNames gate validates every call in a batch against a snapshot taken before that batch's install_skills call has actually executed; the refresh only happened at the start of the NEXT loop iteration. Confirmed against the reported production session, which shows the model declaring browser tools broken then self-correcting a turn later once the async refresh caught up.

Added an `installedToolNames` field to installSkills' success result (mirroring the existing rejectedToolNames field) so the eager check can resolve what was unlocked.

title: ENG-1938: keep the earliest sentAt estimate so the stale-invitation drain sees old invites
body:
## Why
Found verifying ENG-1718 on production (ENG-1938). `AW-UnipileSentInvitations.sentAt` froze its **first** observation:

```ts
sentAt: item.parsed_datetime ?? cached?.sentAt ?? now   // and sentInvitationChanged ignored sentAt
```

LinkedIn exposes only relative ages. Unipile resolves "Sent 3 months ago" at request time, and the value is `now` when `parsed_datetime` is missing. Production ledgers today (read-only):

| account | rows | sentAt == sync time | look ≤21 days old |
|---|---|---|---|
| largest affected account A | 679 | **449** | 445 |
| affected account B | 369 | **256** | 256 |

One of these accounts' own run reports shows pending invites from March and May. The stale-invitation drain (ENG-1719) selects by this field, so for exactly the large-backlog accounts it exists for, most of the backlog was invisible to it.

## What
- `resolveLedgerSentAt(cached, item, now)`: store the **earliest** estimate ever observed.
  - A relative label resolved at request time is never earlier than the real send, so the earliest resolution is the tightest estimate.
  - Rows stamped with their sync time heal as soon as Unipile supplies a date; bucket rollovers ("1 week" → "1 month") lower it.
  - **Never moves later**: request-time drift causes no rewrite, so the ENG-875 write-amplification guard still holds (its test is unchanged and passes), and rows from our own `send-invite` keep their exact instant.
  - A **different `invitationId`** is a new invitation to the same person, so the old date is discarded.
  - Unparseable or future provider values are ignored.
- `sentInvitationChanged` now also counts a sentAt that moved **earlier**. That's what lets existing rows heal on the next sync, including incremental walks, which stop only on unchanged pages.

## Effects to expect (accepted on ENG-1938)
- **Drain**: more genuinely stale invitations become selectable for large backlogs. Selection logic is untouched.
- **CRM**: `reconcileSentInvitationsToCrm` rewrites a lead's `linkedInInviteSentAt` from the ledger on each pass, so those dates move **earlier** (toward truth) once. Engagement records are unaffected: they're appended once per `invitationId`, and `createdAt` is never rewritten.
- **One-off write burst**: each healing row is rewritten once (see scope below), then back to steady state.

## Assumption, stated
LinkedIn's relative label floors the age. The ledger evidence supports it: every observed offset is an exact 0/1/2/7/14/31/61/92/122/181 days. I'll verify it after deploy: no send-path row (exact time known from CloudWatch) may move earlier than its logged send.

## Tests
- New `linkedInSentInvitationsSync.earliestSentAt.test.ts` (9): heal, drift = no write, rollover, exact send kept, re-invite resets, send-path row without id, bad/future values ignored, first-sight fallback, change detection.
- One existing assertion reversed on purpose ("prefers parsed_datetime" moved sentAt **later** on any rewrite) and paired with its earlier-wins counterpart.
- 105 suites touching sentAt / sent invitations / linkedin_outreach: 2859 passed. `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Data change: scope, rollback, verification (for the pre-merge approval check)
**Table:** `AW-UnipileSentInvitations`, field `sentAt` only. Rows are rewritten through the existing sync upsert; no migration script. Nothing else in the row changes.

**Scope (full scan, 2026-09-15 06:50Z, read-only):** 6,376 rows across 23 accounts.
- **1,080** rows carry their sync time as `sentAt`. These heal on the next sync that sees a `parsed_datetime`.
- Any other row whose LinkedIn age bucket has since rolled over is also lowered, once. Upper bound: every row rewritten **once**, spread across hourly full walks; afterwards writes return to today's steady state.
- 0 rows lack an `invitationId`, so every row takes the matching-id earliest-wins path.

**Effects downstream:**
- The stale-invitation drain can select genuinely old invitations.
- `reconcileSentInvitationsToCrm` moves each lead's `linkedInInviteSentAt` earlier on its next pass.
- CRM engagement `createdAt` is unchanged (appended once per `invitationId`).

**Rollback:**
- A pre-deploy snapshot of every row's `accountId, invitedUserPublicId, invitationId, sentAt, syncedAt` is held locally (not in the repo).
- Reverting this PR alone won't restore values: earliest-wins never moves a date later, but the old code also never revisits `sentAt`, so lowered values would simply persist.
- A full rollback is revert + restoring `sentAt` from the snapshot for rows whose `invitationId` still matches. That needs a credential with DynamoDB write on this table; the verifying IAM user is read-only.

**Post-deploy verification plan:**
1. Before/after counts of rows with `sentAt` == sync time, per account. Expected to drop.
2. **The safety property, against real data:** 40 invitations sent through AgentWeb in the last 7 days have exact send times in CloudWatch. After the next full walks, no such row may have `sentAt` earlier than its logged send. Today all 40 sit 43–563 s after it, meaning LinkedIn's label floors. A violation means reverting.
3. A read-only `withdraw-stale-invitations` dry-run is not available, so the drain's candidate count is computed offline from the post-heal ledger with `selectStaleInvitations`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium. Updates LinkedIn invitation synchronization to retain the earliest valid `sentAt` estimate, handle invitation identity changes, and ignore invalid or future provider dates. This improves stale-invitation and CRM accuracy while preventing unnecessary rewrites. Nine focused tests and typecheck pass.

title: Ignore type-only provider SDK imports in sdkConstructionGuard (ENG-1937)
body:
## What

`backend/src/__tests__/sdkConstructionGuard.test.ts` fails on `main`:

```
Direct provider SDK import in services/agentMode/llmModelRegistry.ts: openai.
```

`a0fdb3c85` (#2906) moved the model registry out of the allowlisted `agentModeService.ts` into `agentMode/llmModelRegistry.ts`. That file only **names** the SDK's type:

```ts
import type OpenAI from 'openai';
client: OpenAI | null;
```

`findDirectProviderSdkImports` matched every import declaration of a provider module, type-only or not. CI runs builds only, not jest, so the failure reached `main` unnoticed.

## Fix

The guard exists to stop client construction and runtime SDK use that bypass metering. A type-only declaration is erased at compile time and can do neither, so it's now skipped. I chose this over allowlisting the file because an allowlisted file could later gain a real value import that nobody notices.

The skip is narrow: a declaration counts as type-only only when **nothing** in it is a value.

| Allowed | Still rejected |
|---|---|
| `import type OpenAI from 'openai'` | `import { type ClientOptions, OpenAI } from 'openai'` |
| `import { type A, type B } from 'openai'` | `import OpenAI, { type ClientOptions } from 'openai'` |
| `export type { OpenAI } from 'openai'` | `import 'openai'` |
| `export { type OpenAI } from '@azure/openai'` | `import * as sdk from 'openai'` / `export * from 'openai'` |

## Verification
- `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/sdkConstructionGuard.test.ts`: 30 passed (was 1 failed / 19 passed on `main`). The existing alias-resistance cases and the stale-allowlist check still pass.
- Backend typecheck clean (apart from the known local `metaInterceptor` noise).

Test-only change; nothing ships to production.

title: Price vendor calls inside the recorder so a missing rate can never fail the request (ENG-1929)
body:
## Problem

Vendor metering call sites computed cost **inline, as an argument**:

```ts
void recordVendorUsage({ ..., costSource: 'allocated', costUsd: computeAllocatedCost('you.com', 'query', 1) });
```

`recordVendorUsage` never throws. Its arguments, though, are evaluated **before** it is called, and `computeAllocatedCost` throws on a missing rate by design (ENG-703 AC2). So a rate-card key rename, or a new operation with no rate, would fail the user's request itself, not just the metering. On You.com and Google CSE the throw even lands **before** the search call.

No call site throws today, since every key in use is priced. The risk is the next rate-card edit.

## Fix: pricing moves inside the recorder

`recordVendorUsage` takes a `rateKey` and resolves the rate within its never-throw boundary:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Priced key | cost computed at call site | recorder computes `quantity × rate` → `allocated` |
| Missing key | **throws into the vendor request** | recorded `unpriced` (no $0 spend event) + loud `[vendorRateCard] UNPRICED vendor unit …` log, once per key per process |
| Pre-priced figure (X's own pricer, measured) | `costSource` + `costUsd` | unchanged |

`RecordVendorUsageContext` makes `rateKey` and `costSource`/`costUsd` mutually exclusive.

**ENG-703 AC2 still holds:** an unpriced unit is never booked as $0. What changes is where it fails (in metering, not in the user's request), not whether.

## Call sites

Migrated to `rateKey`: You.com, Google CSE, Apollo, enrich.so, ElevenLabs, 2captcha, Placid, Remotion.

- **Remotion had a real bug.** Its guard caught a missing rate and recorded the submission as **$0 `allocated`**, the silent $0 AC2 forbids. It now records `unpriced`.
- **X (`twitterService`):** checked and left as is. Its pricer is typed (`TwitterOperation`) and already inside a try/catch.
- **`computeAllocatedCost`:** no callers remain, so it's removed.

## Guard (AC3)

`vendorMeteringCoverageGuard` gains an AST check: any `recordVendorUsage({ costUsd: <expression containing a call> })` in `backend/src` fails the build. Literals, identifiers, property access and arithmetic on those are allowed. Mutation-checked: putting `costUsd: getAllocatedRate('you.com','query')!` back into `youSearchProvider` fails it at `youSearchProvider.ts:104`.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-1929)
1. No vendor call can fail because its own cost could not be computed: pricing happens inside the never-throw boundary. A test proves an unpriced key throws neither synchronously nor as a rejection.
2. An unpriced unit is still reported loudly and never recorded as $0: it's tagged `unpriced`, gets no spend event, and logs a marker line. Tested.
3. A new call site can't reintroduce the inline path without failing the coverage guard.

## Tests
- New `usageRecorderService.vendorRateKey.test.ts`.
- Call-site tests now assert the `rateKey`, plus the dollar rate that key resolves to (e.g. ElevenLabs Flash/Turbo $0.125 per 1k characters), instead of a `costUsd` the call site no longer computes.
- The Remotion test that asserted the old $0 fallback is replaced, with the reason recorded inline.
- 117 related backend suites, 2,945 tests pass. Typecheck clean.

## Rollback
Revert the PR. There's no data or schema change; the only effect is which `costSource` a missing rate produces.

title: Keep fractional vendor quantities on the usage aggregate (ENG-1878)
body:
## Found in production verification (2026-09-15)

I triggered one real ElevenLabs voiceover via Emma ("AgentWeb metering check.", 24 characters).

| Rail | quantity | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `AW-SpendEvents` | **0.024** ✅ | 3,000 µ$ ✅ |
| `AW-UsageRecords` aggregate | **0** ❌ | 3,000 µ$ ✅ |

`usageRecordDb.buildIncrementUsageUpdate` wrote `Math.max(0, Math.round(inc.quantity || 0))`. That rounding predates ENG-1878, which made ElevenLabs quantities fractional on purpose (priced per 1,000 characters). So every clip under 500 characters counted as **zero** usage on the aggregate, and longer clips rounded to whole thousands. Cost was always right; usage volume wasn't, and the two rails disagreed on quantity.

## Fix

Write the quantity as-is, still clamped to a finite, non-negative number. DynamoDB numbers are exact decimals, so `ADD` accumulates fractional values without float drift. The readers I checked (`usageAnalyticsService` summing, the X breakdown's `toLocaleString`) already handle non-integers.

## Tests

`usageLedgerVendorDimension.test.ts` pinned the old behaviour ("never writes … a fractional quantity", 2.6 → 3) from ENG-693, when every unit was a whole count. That assertion is superseded with the reason inline:
- the never-negative-cost half is kept as its own test
- a new test checks 0.024 is kept exactly
- a new test checks negative / NaN → 0

Mutation-checked: restoring `Math.round` fails the fractional test. Related suites pass (96 tests); typecheck clean.

## Post-deploy check

Trigger one voiceover; the aggregate row's `quantity` should equal the spend event's.

title: Show whether an account is actually paused, from the enforcer itself (ENG-1886)
body:
## Problem

No admin screen showed whether an account is **actually paused**. The spend ledger panel's `pause` came from `explainPause`, a shadow computation over the ledger that nothing enforces (`spendProjection.ts`: "SHADOW ONLY … Nothing consumes this"). It was withheld in ENG-1874 for that reason. An admin asking "why has this customer stopped working?" had nowhere to look.

## Fix: show the enforcer's own decision, re-labelled, never recomputed

**Backend.** `GET /api/admin/users/:billingUserId/spend/breakdown` now returns `enforcement`, built from `checkTokenUsage(billingUserId)`, the same function that admits or refuses a user's work (read-only). `describeEnforcement` only re-labels its result:

| field | from `checkTokenUsage` |
|---|---|
| `paused` | `!allowed` |
| `usageMode` | `usageMode` |
| `gatedBy` | `costEnforced` → `cost`, else token cap → `tokens`, else `none` |
| `used` / `limit` / `percentUsed` | cost figures when cost gates, token figures otherwise |
| `resetsOn` | first day after `month` |
| `usagePolicyVersion` | `usagePolicyVersion` |

- **Past months:** the enforcer only knows the current month, so a past month returns `{ available: false, reason: "not-current-month" }` instead of an inferred pause.
- **Failed reads:** return `{ available: false, reason: "unreadable" }`; the breakdown itself still returns.

**Portal.** A card at the top of the spend ledger panel:
- **Paused:** "Paused now by the usage cap (mode: paused)"
- **Not paused:** "Not paused: the usage cap is admitting work"
- **Counter line:** "Enforcer's counter (LLM cost): $204.10 of $200.00 (102.1%) · resets Oct 1"
- **Qualifier:** *"This is the counter that decides admission (AW-Users), not the ledger total below. The two can differ."* ENG-1247 measured those two differing in both directions.

The shadow `explainPause` result is still never rendered.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-1886)
1. **An admin can see whether a billing subject is paused, and against which threshold:** the card shows paused state, counter, limit, % and reset date.
2. **The value is the one the enforcement path returns:** it's `checkTokenUsage`'s own result. Mutation-checked: deriving `paused` from the percentage fails the test.
3. **The screen separates what the enforcer measured from what the account spent:** the qualifier sits on the card.
4. **No shadow field is shown as an enforcement outcome:** `explainPause` stays unrendered, and a test covers a shadow "paused: true" beside a real "not paused".

## Tests
- `enforcementStateView.test.ts` (5)
- route tests (3 new: billing subject, past month, failed read)
- portal tests (8 new)
- Backend typecheck clean; portal suite 42 passed.

Admin-only; no data-plane change.

title: ENG-1854: pause default #eval-queue Slack fan-out, decouple persistence
body:
## Summary
- Adds a Slack-posting toggle (`human_eval_slack_posting_enabled`) for `#eval-queue`, defaulting **ON** (flipped mid-session once the two real noise sources below were independently fixed) — a single explicit `'false'` is a genuine kill switch, checked first and unconditionally, overriding everything else including the exception list.
- Adds a keyed exception list (`human_eval_slack_posting_exception_user_ids`) — with the default now ON, its practical role is selecting a concise message format for specific accounts, not deciding whether posting happens at all. Ships empty.
- **Lead-enrichment anomaly gate**: a routine, zero-failure enrichment completion never becomes a review candidate at all, unconditionally — independent of the toggle. This was the confirmed dominant source of `#eval-queue` noise (a real Slack dump showed 7+ near-identical "processed N, failed 0" posts in one day).
- **Cross-path artifact dedup**: the same artifact can no longer get posted twice via two different trigger mechanisms (auto-trigger vs. manual Emma tool vs. admin API) — all three claim the artifact URL atomically before creating a candidate, and release the claim if candidate creation subsequently fails.
- Gate/dedup logic lives inside `HumanEvalService.createCandidate()` / `autoHumanEvalService.ts`, so every entry path is covered uniformly.

**Real bug found and fixed along the way**: candidate persistence used to be coupled to the Slack post succeeding — a Slack failure silently dropped the candidate entirely. Reordered so the record always persists first; Slack posting is a best-effort side effect that can never prevent it.

Context: ENG-1854, per Harsha (2026-09-14) — Matt and Fangfang weren't reviewing `#eval-queue`, it was overwhelming context-free noise. ENG-1853 (a proper reviewer portal) is a separate, larger ticket gated behind a Harsha-approved prototype.

## Rollback / config

- **Config location**: `AW-Settings` DynamoDB table.
  - `human_eval_slack_posting_enabled` — `'false'` is a real, unconditional kill switch (checked before the exception list). Absent/anything else = posting enabled (the default).
  - `human_eval_slack_posting_exception_user_ids` — comma-separated userIds; selects the concise message format when posting is already happening. Ships empty.
- **Full code rollback**: revert this PR's commits; no schema/data migration, plain revert is safe.
- **Effective timestamp**: not yet deployed to production — will be added here once merged and the deploy completes.

## Known open item

ENG-1854's own text asks to "use the Haven + Every packet as the only current exception." Traced precisely: Haven/Every's real approval flow (hand-built HTML packet on S3, approved via Linear card CS-64) never touches this pipeline at all — the literal instruction can't be satisfied as written. Posted the full finding on ENG-1854 asking Harsha for direction rather than guessing.

## Review history (4 independent adversarial rounds)

- **Round 1**: found the toggle-lookup fail-safe gap (fixed), a narrow partial-failure window between a successful Slack post and its DB update (documented, low-severity, left as-is), and a test-coverage gap on `humanEvalActionService`'s optional-field guard (fixed).
- **Round 2**: found the reviewer-Slack-ID lookup had the identical fail-safe gap as round 1's first finding (fixed, and additionally live-fault-injected on env1 — a temporary marker-gated throw was deployed, triggered, confirmed the catch engaged and the candidate still persisted, then reverted).
- **Round 3** (run after the anomaly gate, cross-path dedup, and default-flip were added): found two real issues, both fixed — (a) the artifact-claim dedup marked artifacts claimed *before* candidate creation succeeded and never released the claim on failure, permanently blackholing that artifact from ever being sent again on nothing more exotic than a transient DynamoDB error; rewritten to use `settingsService.claimSetMember`/`releaseSetMember`, an existing atomic primitive built for exactly this "claim, release on failed delivery" shape; (b) the exception list could bypass an explicit `'false'` kill switch — reordered so the kill switch is checked first, unconditionally.
- **Round 4** (scoped to round 3's two fixes): found one real issue in the claim/release rewrite itself, fixed — `enqueueAutoHumanEval`'s try/catch wrapped both `createCandidate` and the subsequent sourceKey dedupe-marker `setSetting` write under one catch; if `createCandidate` succeeded but that housekeeping write then threw, the shared catch still released the artifact claim, reopening the cross-path duplicate window this claim exists to close for an artifact a real candidate had already consumed. Fixed by giving the marker write its own non-fatal try/catch. Confirmed the kill-switch reorder and the other two call sites (`emma/tools.ts`, `routes/humanEval.ts`) have no equivalent issue. Also flagged, not fixed (non-blocking): `artifactClaimsSettingName()` independently computes the UTC-month bucket at claim time and release time rather than sharing one captured value — a claim made in the last moment of a month whose release fires just after rollover would silently target the wrong bucket and no-op. Astronomically unlikely in practice; left as a known, documented edge case.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] 102 tests across `humanEvalService`/`humanEvalActionService`/`autoHumanEvalService`/`humanEval.routes`/`emma.enrichLeads`/`emmaTools.enqueueHumanEval`, all passing
- [x] Every fix in this PR mutation-verified: the exact historical bug reintroduced, confirmed the relevant test fails, restored — done for the persistence/fail-safe fixes (both settings lookups), the anomaly gate, the cross-path dedup, the claim/release fix, the kill-switch-ordering fix, and round 4's marker-write-scope fix
- [x] Live-tested on env1 repeatedly across the full session: default-off persistence, default-on posting attempts, exception-list override, message-format distinction (concise vs. verbose, real posted text captured via temporary debug instrumentation, cleanly reverted), fail-safe fixes live-fault-injected with real thrown errors, cross-path dedup proven against real DynamoDB (one row survives after the same artifact is posted twice)
- [x] Four independent adversarial review rounds, all findings addressed except one genuinely deferred (documented, low-severity, round 1) and one genuinely blocked on Harsha (posted to ENG-1854, awaiting his answer)

title: [needs human] Use fresher Market Strategy ICPs in lead-discovery filters (ENG-1955)
body:
GET /api/crm/icp/filters (used by the CRM "Use my ICP" Find Leads flow) always preferred user.icpResult (the one-time onboarding ICP snapshot) over marketStrategy.icp whenever icpResult was non-empty. Edits made on the Market Strategy page, or by Emma's update_market_strategy tool, only ever write marketStrategy.icp — nothing mirrors them back onto icpResult — so a user who corrected wrong onboarding ICPs kept getting lead searches built from the old, wrong personas forever.

Confirmed against production data for the reporting user: onboarding generated icpCompletedAt=2026-09-12T00:25:01Z with badly-mismatched personas; the user's corrected personas were saved to marketStrategy.icp at updatedAt=2026-09-12T00:36:22Z (11 min later), but /icp/filters kept serving the stale icpResult personas since they were non-empty.

Fix: the route now falls back to marketStrategy.icp whenever it was saved more recently than icpResult was last generated (marketStrategy.updatedAt > user.icpCompletedAt). When either timestamp is missing (older accounts), behavior is unchanged. Cache write-back to icpResult is correctly skipped in this case, same as the existing marketStrategy-fallback path.

Verified via TDD: added a failing test reproducing the prod scenario, confirmed it failed against the old code, implemented the minimal fix, and confirmed the full icpFiltersRoute test suite (26 tests) plus tsc typecheck pass.

title: Bound the spend-breakdown read without truncating its totals (ENG-1841)
body:
## Problem

`GET /api/admin/users/:billingUserId/spend/breakdown` read a whole subject-month from `AW-SpendEvents` with **no ceiling** (`listSpendEvents` pages to exhaustion). It also returned one row per session and per open reservation, both unbounded. The ledger is growing: LLM events are on it since ENG-1934, and ENG-1858 attributes more calls to real customers.

**Measured on production (2026-09-15):** 2,450 events across every subject for all of September; the largest subject-month has 542.

## Fix

The ticket's constraint is that **a truncated aggregate is a wrong aggregate**, so no total is ever computed from a partial set.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Read | unbounded | `listSpendEventsBounded(…, SPEND_BREAKDOWN_MAX_EVENTS = 50,000)` stops paging past the ceiling. The route answers **422 `spend_breakdown_too_large`** with no totals, and the portal dialog already shows that message. |
| Detail rows | unbounded | `boundBreakdownRows(breakdown, 100)`, applied **after** `buildSpendBreakdown` |
| Totals, daily trend, pause explanation, LLM coverage | whole month | **unchanged: still the whole month** |
| What was cut | n/a | `omitted.{byProvider,byFeature,byMember,bySession,inFlight}` = `{ rows, eventCount, settledMicroUsd, reservedMicroUsd }`; listed + omitted reproduces each total |

- `listSpendEvents` still pages to exhaustion, because the §8 reconciliation must see every event.
- Open reservations keep newest-first order (the screen labels them "most recent").
- The portal's "Showing the N largest of M — K more not shown" notes now include server-omitted rows.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-1841)
1. **Response size and work are bounded:** the read stops at 50,000 events and each list returns at most 100 rows. The test proves the next page is never requested (mutation-checked).
2. **Every total stays exact:** totals are summed before the cut, and past the ceiling the endpoint refuses rather than summing a partial set.
3. **Rows beyond the bound are stated as omitted, with exact counts and dollars:** covered in both the route and the portal.
4. **The screen is unchanged for a subject-month under the bound:** `omitted` is all zeros, and the existing 43 portal tests pass untouched.

## Tests
- `spendEventDb` (3 new): fits; stops at the ceiling; exactly at the ceiling.
- `spendReadModel` (4 new): small breakdown untouched; totals kept; omitted sums exact; reservation order.
- Route (2 new): 422 past the ceiling; 107 sessions → 100 listed + 7 omitted.
- Portal (4 new).
- Suites: backend 107 passed; portal 47 passed; typecheck clean.

**Not done here:** the persisted monthly projection (§3b), which would remove the full read entirely. That's a data-plane change for later.

title: Attribute helper LLM calls to the user who triggered them (ENG-1858)
body:
## Problem (ENG-1858)

Production booked **2,392 of 8,787 metered LLM calls (27%, 2026-09-08→15) to `userId: "system"`**. Callers of `AgentModeService.callLLM` omitted `usageContext`, so `recordUsage` fell back to `system` and `meterUserUsage` skipped the per-user cap charge. That spend was recorded but never reached any customer's balance.

Traced (read-only mapping of every call site): 2,256 of those calls were feature `agent_task`, the default when no context is passed. The biggest sources are the suggested-reply chips after every turn, session titles, session summaries and `describe_image`.

## Decision
The product owner chose to **attribute and charge**: these calls count against the triggering user's cap, like every other LLM call they trigger (ENG-1250: every AgentWeb-paid call deducted once).

## Change

**1. Call sites pass the triggering user**, as a plain `{ userId, sessionId, feature }` with nothing awaited before the LLM call (`billingUserId` too inside the agent loop, where it's already resolved):

| Path | Feature |
|---|---|
| suggested-reply chips (agent loop) | `suggested_replies` (+ `:interactive` / `:scheduled:<id>`) |
| session title | `session_title` |
| session summaries (session list, account summary) | `session_summary` |
| describe image (tool, generate_image fabrication check, Emma API) | `describe_image` |
| live-voice tool summaries | `live_voice_tool_summary` |
| finalize-guard judge / correction | `finalize_guard_judge` / `finalize_guard_correction` |
| scheduled continuation judge, run summary, pre-check | `scheduled_continuation_judge`, `scheduled_run_summary`, `scheduled_run_precheck` |
| diagnostic message, stop-request judge | `diagnostic_message`, `stop_request_judge` |
| report classification, HTML templates | `report_classification`, `html_template` |
| CRM enrichment field mapping / config classification | `crm_enrichment_field_mapping`, `crm_enrichment_config` |
| onboarding ad copy / competitors / creative direction (+ ICP regenerate) | `onboarding_*` |

When no user is in scope the context is feature-only; no user is ever invented.

**2. Billing owner resolved at metering time, not at the call site.** Resolving the ENG-1217 billing subject at each call site would put two DynamoDB reads, and a new failure mode, in front of every helper call. (A first attempt did that and broke ~20 controller suites: exactly the coupling to avoid.) Now `callLLM`'s metering step:
- **Already has `billingUserId` (the agent loop) or has no user:** metered synchronously, unchanged.
- **Otherwise:** resolves the owner **after the response exists**, fire-and-forget and fail-open (bills the acting user on error), with a **60s bounded cache** and in-flight dedupe.
- **The enforced cap charge** (`incrementUserTokenUsage`) resolves the org pool itself and never reads this cache.

**3. Platform-funded paths are named, not anonymous:** `platform:onboarding_loop`, `platform:eval_rca`, `platform:slack_admin_intent` (no userId).

## ENG-1858 acceptance criteria
1. **Every `system` row traced to a named call path:** done, see the mapping in the ticket.
2. **Each path attributed or classified as platform-funded, with the reason:** the table above.
3. **The remainder is named and tracked:** ENG-1961 (workplan thumbnails, intake dedup, `describeVideo`, one tasks-route call, an eval script, dead code).
4. **No metering write removed or made lossy:** attribution only adds context; every fallback still meters.

## Tests
- New `eng1858.usageAttribution.test.ts` (17 tests):
  - call sites pass the right context
  - an org member is metered with the org root, and `callLLM` doesn't wait for the lookup
  - a lookup failure still meters (acting user) and never rejects
  - the cache resolves once within the TTL, including for concurrent calls
  - a context with `billingUserId` or no user isn't resolved
  - platform features carry no user
- Existing suites updated to assert the **exact** new context (strengthened, not loosened): diagnosis, describeImage ×2, generate_image fabrication check, enrichment smart-field classification, eval RCA.
- **268 affected suites run in 11 batches, all green;** the 4 suites that failed before the test updates pass (168 tests). Typecheck clean.

## Post-deploy check
Re-measure the `system` share over the following days (was 27% of calls). New rows for `suggested_replies`, `session_title`, etc. should appear under real user ids with correct `billingUserId`.

title: feat(agent-mode): ENG-1880 Phase B — scheduled reports on Harsha's account
body:
## Summary
Per the 2026-09-14 call decision (Harsha + Manan): before ENG-1880's autonomous Meta ads report ever reaches a real customer, run it as a scheduled chat on **Harsha's own account** (not a customer's, not the founder's), **weekly**, for every real client currently running active Meta ad spend — so real report accuracy and per-report LLM/API cost can be monitored over a month-or-a-few-weeks window before deciding on customer opt-in (Phase C).

## What this creates
6 new `AW-TaskSchedules` rows, one per client, all owned by `harsha@agentweb.pro` (userId `1743956381327`), weekly at 09:00 UTC (after that day's metrics-snapshot cron writes fresh data), targeting the private `Meta_Ads_Perf_Report_Autonomous` work plan.

**Cadence — reconsidered after review, not the original pick.** Daily was the first instinct, but this report is a rolling 30-day window: day-to-day content barely shifts, so daily runs would mostly regenerate near-identical reports — little new accuracy signal, real cost spent on redundant output. The real monitoring window is a month or a few weeks (not literally "a few days"), so weekly still yields 4+ genuinely-spaced samples across it.

**Client list — not picked arbitrarily.** Ranked by real 30-day spend from `AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots` (checked 2026-09-15): Phoenix Technologies ($32,090.54), Haven AI ($13,292.91), My Health Surveys ($3,996.96), Omega Tech MS ($703.20), Kraftersland ($310.31), Toa Works/Bodylever ($275.72). 4 other connected accounts showed $0 spend across the same window and were excluded — not "major clients running Meta ads."

**Message wording — not invented.** Copied from a real, already-live schedule (`scheduleId 1816cb76-...`) that already proved this exact "run the private work plan titled X, target client Y" phrasing correctly resolves via the model's own `launch_predefined_work_plan` tool call. `AW-TaskSchedules` has no `planId` field — the target plan is identified by exact title match inside the message text, confirmed against real prod data, not assumed.

- [x] Live-tested on test-env1: running the script creates all 6 rows correctly with `frequency: "weekly"` and the right `nextRunTime`; re-running correctly no-ops on all 6 (idempotent, no duplicates).
- [x] Root-caused the actual schedule-to-work-plan resolution mechanism against real prod `AW-TaskSchedules` data rather than assuming a `planId` field existed.

## Not done in this PR, flagged for follow-up
- **A real, already-live schedule** (`1816cb76-...`, monthly, targeting the earlier internal-validation plan variant, owned by Manan's own account) was found while researching this — a leftover test artifact, not part of this rollout. Left untouched pending a decision on whether to deactivate it.
- **Running this script against prod** needs someone with prod DynamoDB write access (same class of blocker as ENG-1734/ENG-1879/ENG-1939) — not done as part of this PR.

title: Enigma card-revenue adapter: dormant, metered, cached

## What
Adds a cache-first Enigma client that looks up a US brand's 12-month **card** revenue by website. It ships **dormant**: nothing calls `getEnigmaService()`, and without the `dev|prod/AgentWeb/Enigma` secret the service is never initialised. That means no spend and no lead data from this PR.

Refs ENG-1388 (phase 1 of the Enigma integration).

- `services/enigmaService.ts` (pure, fail-closed):
  - unusable, social or site-builder domains → skipped, no call
  - a brand whose own websites don't match our domain (TLD included) → not_found
  - null, negative or undated values are never repaired
  - typed errors for 401, 402, 429 and GraphQL errors; errors are never cached
- `services/enigmaServiceFactory.ts`: `fetch` client (so the ENG-1111 egress guard covers it), AW-EnrichmentRawCache store (`cacheType: 'enigma'`), and ledger metering per billed value via ENG-1929 `rateKey`.
- `services/enigmaGraphql.ts`: side-effect-free request builder.
- Registrations:
  - `getEnigmaApiKey`
  - boot init
  - rate card `enigma.{card_revenue_12m, card_revenue_yoy_growth_12m, brand_attribute}` (placeholder list prices; allocations pending ENG-1956)
  - `METERED_VENDOR_PROVIDERS`
  - metering-guard signature
- `docs/integrations/enigma-contract.md`

### What changed in the contract
New contract: `docs/integrations/enigma-contract.md`.

## Verification

- Suites `enigmaService`, `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard`, `vendorRateCard`, `usageAnalyticsService` and `usageRecorderService.vendorRateKey` pass: 146/146.

title: Enigma card revenue in V3 lead enrichment, behind a flag
body:
## What
Refs ENG-1388 (phase 2). Acceptance criteria: ENG-1932.

Adds the `company_card_revenue` field group (`card_revenue_12m`, `card_revenue_period_end`, `card_revenue_yoy_growth`; 30-day TTL), filled **only** by Enigma. **Off by default.** Calls require all of:
- `ENIGMA_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED=true`
- the user on `ENIGMA_ENRICHMENT_USER_ALLOWLIST` (empty = nobody)
- a user-initiated run (enrich-v3 route or Emma; never the cron)
- a config that explicitly names a card field

Safeguards, which must ship together:
- **Fail closed:**
  - the waterfall's card tier returns before Tiers 2–5, so no web or LLM guess is possible
  - the V2 `splitFieldsByGroup` drops card fields, and `llmEligibleFields()` strips them from every V2 LLM unit including the linkedin and `no_context` fallbacks
  - the per-field refresh route (`.../fields/:field/refresh`, which ran the web/LLM path with `forceOverwrite`) refuses card fields with a 400
- **No implicit opt-in:**
  - card columns default to `include:false`
  - aliases and smart-field dependencies onto card fields are stripped, for saved configs and for preview runs' inline configs (`stripImplicitCardRevenueRouting`)
  - the group is left out of the LLM alias and classifier prompts
  - V3 never injects card fields as deps
- **Spend:**
  - industry card-adoption gate (low adoption skips)
  - per-run cap `ENIGMA_MAX_CALLS_PER_RUN` (default 100)
  - daily cap `ENIGMA_DAILY_LIMIT_PER_USER` (default 150, AW-Configs `system:enigmaUsage`)
  - **monthly credit budget** `ENIGMA_MONTHLY_CREDIT_BUDGET` (default 1,800 of the 2,100-credit Pro plan; AW-Configs `system:enigmaCreditBudget`). The live spike (ENG-1933) measured ~19 credits per call, 52 at worst, so call caps alone cannot bound spend. Checked before each call, recorded after it from the billed values; a spent budget halts the run as a `budget_reached` skip
  - run circuit breaker on the first 402/401
  - blocked hosts (AgentWeb form hosts, profile pages, site builders) skip before taking a run slot
- **No cross-customer copy:** Tier 0b sibling copy skips card fields and any `provider: enigma` value.
- **Provenance:**
  - string values
  - `provider: enigma`, `confidence: medium`
  - new optional `EnrichedFieldMeta.asOf`
  - a `sourceQuote` stating it is not total revenue
- **Accounting:**
  - `result.enigma` summary; skips never count as failures
  - tier and source breakdowns gain an `enigma` key only when Enigma filled, so other runs keep their existing shape
- **Cron:** `isUnenriched` ignores card fields.
- **Emma:** requests card fields only for an explicit card-revenue ask, always says "card revenue, 12 months to <date>", describes YoY as a signed change, and is warned when an Enigma run halted (credits, key or budget) so that is never reported as "no card revenue found".

### What changed in the contract
`docs/integrations/enigma-contract.md`: Enigma is now reachable from V3 enrichment behind the flag. The update adds lead field shapes, opt-in and exclusion guards, the quota row, new failure modes and open gaps.

## Verification
- Typecheck passes.
- Every suite related to the changed files: 1,310 suites, 23,390 tests passed. One suite, `mcp.userIdOverride`, fails to load (`McpToolRegistry is not a constructor`) identically on `origin/main`, so it is unrelated.
- Deliberately breaking the early return, the sibling provider check, the default exclusion, the credit-budget check, the run halt, the refresh guard and the LLM-eligibility filter each made a test fail.
- **Live-checked** against the real API by the ENG-1933 spike (35 lookups, 664 credits): matching, billing counts and response shapes hold. The enrichment path itself has not run live; that is the post-merge check below.
- ENG-1932 acceptance criteria audited line by line against the code; the gaps it found (refresh route, preview aliasing, Emma seeing halts, blocked hosts using run slots) are fixed here.

## Data plane / spend
- New persisted lead attributes: `customFields.card_revenue_*` plus metadata `asOf`.
- New AW-Configs row types `system:enigmaUsage` (per user, daily) and `system:enigmaCreditBudget` (platform, monthly).
- Spend is only possible after the flag is set **and** a user is allowlisted.
- Decision recorded: the PR owner (Anurag) is proceeding without a separate data-plane sign-off; the flag ships off.
- Not in this PR: a query-side filter that would stop Enigma billing per-platform rows we discard (cuts the per-call ceiling from 52 to 32 credits). Enigma's docs don't show null-filter syntax, so it needs one live test call first; the budget bounds spend meanwhile.

## Rollback
- `ENIGMA_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED=false` stops all calls immediately with no deploy.
- The fields are additive strings that nothing else reads.

## Live verification after enabling for an internal test user
1. Add `card_revenue_12m` explicitly to a test list and include three leads: a US consumer brand, a B2B SaaS company and a personal-email lead.
2. Run enrich-v3. Expected:
   - consumer brand filled, with metadata and a ledger row
   - B2B lead skipped (`low_card_adoption`)
   - personal-email lead skipped (`unusable_domain`)
3. Re-run and expect zero new Enigma calls.

title: fix(agent-mode): close the other half of ENG-1852 — chatbotService singleton, construction guard, diagnostics removal
body:
## What this does

Closes the other half of ENG-1852, plus the two follow-ups that ticket deferred.

ENG-1852 was two live `AgentModeService` objects in one worker process — the worker's own (initialized) and the module singleton (never initialized, empty registry). Whichever answered a given `getUnassociatedTools()` call decided whether the `__other_skills__` bundle resolved. PR #2881 fixed the worker half. `chatbotService` was still constructing a fresh instance **per chat message**, so `backend/src` still had two production construction sites and the bug class remained reachable.

Three things, in order:

1. **`chatbotService` uses the module singleton.** Per gate-open message it was running a full `initialize()` — `registerTools` over ~264 tools, `initializeMcp`, `ensureBuiltInSkills`, downstream singleton bootstrap — then discarding the instance. And because `startFileCacheCleanup()` set an un-unref'd interval whose closure retained the instance, **each discarded one stayed reachable for the process lifetime.** That's a real leak, not just waste.
2. **AST guard** so a second construction site can't silently reappear.
3. **ENG-1852's temporary diagnostics removed** — their job is done and the structural tripwire now lives in a test.

## Scope note worth reading before reviewing

The local instance was used at **six** call sites, not one — three of them outside the `skillToolGateOpen` block, including `callLLM`, which owns provider transport, retries/fallback and exactly-once metering. So this reroutes the widget's LLM path onto the process-wide singleton. That is the part that deserves scrutiny.

Checked: all three post-gate calls are safe on an uninitialized instance today (module constant / settings lookup / `this.llmModels`), so this fixes waste and a latent footgun, not a live bug.

`initialize()` is now idempotent for the expensive registration pass, which this change **requires** rather than merely benefits from: `server.ts` starts boot init deliberately non-blocking, so a request can land mid-init. `loadFoundationTools()` deliberately stays **outside** that latch — it writes the process-global `FOUNDATION_TOOLS` static that `PUT /foundation-tools` mutates per-process, and latching it would mean an admin-added tool never reaching a process until restart (the ENG-280/ENG-404 class). Behaviour there matches `main` 1:1.

## Two rounds of review, and what they caught

Both found real defects. Round 2 found that **round 1's fix for the blocking defect was itself broken** — worth knowing before trusting any of this.

- **Round 1** — the latch marked init successful on mere completion. But every step of the init body swallows its own errors, so it can't reject; a silently-degraded init latched **permanently**, where the old per-message instance re-ran registration and self-healed. Strictly worse than the bug being fixed.
- **Round 2** — round 1's replacement signal, `getAllTools().length > 0`, **can never be false.** `registerTools()` registers four built-ins unconditionally after both try/catch blocks and `ToolRegistry.register` is a `Map.set` that cannot throw. Confirmed independently by fault injection on test-env-1, which logged `Error registering tools to instance` one line before `Agent Mode Tools initialized successfully`.

The latch now requires both registration halves to have actually succeeded — `toolsRegistered` (step 1's side-effect imports, which POPULATE `emmaToolRegistry`) and a new per-instance `emmaToolsRegistered` (step 2's copy). They fail independently: if step 1 throws, step 2 still "succeeds" by copying zero tools without error.

Round 2 also defeated the guard again — `import().then(m => new m.X())` (a live idiom; `server.ts` loads two modules that way), subclassing, plain rebind, namespace-member alias, assignment-form `require`. All closed with regression cases. The `src/scripts` exclusion is removed: it rested on "scripts are one-shot CLI processes", false for `seed-eng1609-linkedin-outreach-template`, which `outreachScheduleAutoCreateWiring.ts` imports as a library into the long-lived server.

## Verification

- **Backend build** (the CI gate): exit 0.
- **Full suite**: 1767 suites passed, **0 failed tests** (31,513 passed). The single failing suite, `mcp.userIdOverride`, fails identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree — verified by running one. Arithmetic: 1764 there + 3 new test files = 1767.
- **Live-tested on test-env-1, all seven cases pass**: widget chat end to end; concurrent-session isolation (two simultaneous sessions, distinct markers, no cross-bleed); `install_skills(['__other_skills__'])` succeeding; foundation-tools propagation 58→59 picked up on the next turn with the container never restarting (setting restored byte-identical); diagnostics absent; degraded-init detection by fault injection in both directions; clean deploy.

The result I'd point at: **`File cache cleanup started` stayed at 2** — one per process — across six real chat turns. The old per-message behaviour would have added six more. The leak is confirmed gone against live traffic, not inferred from a diff.

Every new test is mutation-verified against the code it guards, including the ones that pin regressions this branch itself shipped and then fixed.

## Also included

`evaluationPersistenceRace`'s `expired root` case set `expiresAt = Date.now()` to simulate expiry, but the guard is `expiresAt > :now` with `:now` captured earlier — so it only denied the write while under a millisecond elapsed. Pre-existing; this branch surfaced it by shifting jest's split across `maxWorkers: 2`. Now dated unambiguously in the past.

## Not done here

Backend CI runs `npm ci` + `npm run build` only — no jest, and `tsconfig.build.json` excludes the test directories. So the guard in this PR, like the ~30 other architectural guard tests in this repo, does **not** gate a merge. Wiring jest into backend CI is a separate infrastructure decision and deliberately not made here.

---

**Accountable-Owner:** Manan Varma
**Accountable-Linear:** none — deliberate. Follow-up to ENG-1852 closing gaps in our own prior work, not customer-facing scope.
**Execution-Actor:** Claude

title: feat(ads): close the Meta shadow outcome-learning loop (ENG-502)
body:
## Shadow outcome learning — approved contract, verification in progress

Harsha explicitly approved the additive data-plane contract and cautious model-visible wording on 2026-09-15. Merge after isolated baseline/changed-build Okareo comparison and current-head gates. No manual production data mutations or fabricated outcome evidence.

ENG-502 captures scoped predictions from health assessments, records adoption only from verified execution/explicit decline, evaluates settled Meta campaign evidence, and retrieves supported qualitative guidance. Explicit client-scope review can promote/revert the existing account-wide ENG-918 threshold. Numerical evidence stays in the ledger; guidance stays in account memory. No new persistence key, table, index, dependency or LLM call.

### Evaluation boundaries

- Only recognized ENG-502 version-1 `assess_client_health` shadow contexts with valid client attribution enter evaluation. Contextless legacy/manual rows remain untouched unless explicitly migrated. Selection, fresh cron reads, evaluator and conditional transaction enforce this boundary.
- Production capture, execution receipts, due adapter and completion are **Meta-only**. Google has **pure-evaluator early-settlement guard coverage only**, not a settled evaluation integration.
- Settlement requires a final refresh after the end of each reporting calendar day in its valid IANA timezone plus the provider window (Meta: 28 elapsed days). Invalid/unsupported zones fail closed; positive/negative offsets and spring/fall DST boundaries are tested.
- Complete tenant-matching campaign windows, receipt timing, sample, stable-spend and campaign-specific noise checks distinguish correct/incorrect/inconclusive/unscoreable. Ad-level predictions are never scored against campaign snapshots. Comparisons are observational, not causal proof.
- One bounded GSI page (50 rows) per 15-minute tick. Atomic pending-to-scored writes compare the full context; concurrent receipts/context changes cannot be overwritten. Capture has one total 100 ms deadline.

### Truthful learning scope

- Only **correct, adopted campaign outcomes** produce guidance. Incorrect/inconclusive/unscoreable outcomes remain in the ledger; old unsupported lessons are excluded from retrieval.
- Campaign/channel approval, including default campaign scope, changes **qualitative guidance only** and returns `parameter: null`. Its revert changes guidance only. A transaction cannot pair narrow-scope guidance with an account-wide parameter write.
- Only explicit `scope: "client"` approval may promote an **account-wide** threshold. Thirty independent supported outcomes, sole client ownership, ENG-918 bounds/caps, user precedence, revision history and rollback/cooldown are required. Shared-account promotion fails closed. No campaign/channel numeric scope is claimed.
- Deterministic global → client → campaign → channel retrieval retains provenance, confidence, review history and expiry. Generic memory edits/deletes cannot erase structured history.
- Receipt/promotion lookup refuses incomplete pages beyond 100 ledger rows. Guidance reads up to 100 items and returns up to 20; saturation is observable, not complete fleet coverage.

### Validation and approvals

Harsha explicitly approved the additive data-plane contract and cautious customer/model-visible wording. No manual production data mutation is authorized.

- **464 tests / 15 focused suites passed on Atem**, production TypeScript no-emit and diff check pass. Latest route boundary regression: 5 red / 24 green before fix; all pass afterward.
- Separate `dd16f89a0` fixes the exact retired Greptile status allowlist with **112 passing pipeline tests**. Active checks and positive execution evidence remain required; no status spoofing.
- Actionable review corrections cover final settled snapshot availability, bounded ownership reads, decline write budget, safe diagnostic logs, and early malformed/oversized key validation (including sibling score route). Valid-request behavior and approved wording are preserved.
- CodeRabbit N+1 advisory disposition: keep sequential fresh reads and conditional writes for receipt/verdict race safety. Bound a tick to 50 records / 555 seconds of network budgets within 900 seconds. Batching distinct campaign/date ranges would add coordination without evidence of a capacity defect; no unbounded loop or user-table count scans remain. Docstring coverage is advisory, not a reason to add boilerplate.
- Official **Okareo SDK + REPS passthrough driver**: same 4 read-only scenarios × 3 pinned checks, zero failures on baseline and changed isolated staging builds. Tool selection 5.000 → 4.993; no hallucinated capabilities 1.000 → 1.000; actionability 4.939 → 4.589 (every score ≥4, manually reviewed). This establishes tested safety boundaries, not identical text or statistical equivalence.
  - [Baseline c59c293](https://app.okareo.com/project/0d5558f2-1829-4990-b4a2-78dd6f9c9798/eval/d3f355e1-e0ca-4f46-8e85-115b4b250f81)
  - [Changed 16e35bc](https://app.okareo.com/project/0d5558f2-1829-4990-b4a2-78dd6f9c9798/eval/2ee4833f-2a91-4616-a76e-e8f473de8aa6)
  - [Isolated changed deployment](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/actions/runs/35045210008): Ready/Green, development/Dev stores. Final subsequent changes are logs, 75→50 cron page size and invalid HTTP key rejection; deterministic tests cover that delta. No later model-facing changes.
- Changed staging smoke: health 200, unauthenticated learning 401, authenticated unowned-account learning and ledger reads 403.
- Final head `25e76d9fabab4d021506c3e28a043cb8bb067ecc` passed [CI/build](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/actions/runs/35046228624) and `merge-evidence.sh` (exit 0, three executed green jobs). Merged as `d110f6583064bc56fff30cb97cdab17514dcfe7a` at 2026-09-16 02:02:53 UTC. Production deployment and safe read/privacy smoke are verified. Final version `backend-20260916-pr2933` also includes the late-review fix in #2933; [final deployment](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/actions/runs/35047079951) succeeded and EB reached Ready/Green. See the final evidence comment for acceptance gaps. **Organic production capture→receipt→settled learning remains not exercised** until eligible records exist. No synthetic finding, adoption, promotion or production data repair.
- [Detailed evidence and limitations](backend/docs/verification/ENG-502-capture.md).

### Rollback and complexity

`ADS_LEARNING_MODE=off` stops capture/receipt/evaluation. Preserve privacy filters and readers once records exist. Revert promoted thresholds through the review/ENG-918 path while retaining provenance; never restore ambiguous legacy reads.

Overall PR adds the evaluator, receipt observation, structured learning/review and one scheduler, reusing existing stores/GSI/cron/threshold governance. This correction removes legacy terminal scoring and unsupported guidance, restricts account-wide writes to explicit client review, and adds reporting-calendar settlement plus qualitative-only review. **No new keys/schema for narrower thresholds.**

title: fix(ads): distinguish learning review outages from conflicts (ENG-1968)
body:
Learning review and decline currently return HTTP 409 even when ownership lookup or DynamoDB fails. This follow-up to #2931 distinguishes explicit domain/conditional conflicts (409), recognized dependency outages (503), and unexpected failures (500), while keeping the approved response wording, privacy-safe logs, and persistence behavior.

The finding arrived in CodeRabbit's late review of `efc10a3d1` after #2931 merged; its separate ID-validation finding was already fixed in #2931's final head. Both mutation-route callers now share the error classifier. No error text is parsed, and mixed/unknown transaction cancellation reasons do not masquerade as domain conflicts.

Validation: 7 failing route regressions / 26 passing before implementation; **473 tests across 15 focused suites pass**, production TypeScript no-emit and diff check pass on Atem. Cases include dependency failures on approve/revert/decline, unchanged explicit conflict results, domain refusals, conditional races, throughput cancellations, malformed cancellation metadata, and sanitized diagnostics. No model-facing successful path, data contract, dependency, schema, or write policy changes. The isolated Okareo before/after comparison for #2931 remains applicable to those unchanged paths; no production write was used to test the failures.
