title: fix(placid): render Emma-chat images instead of 404ing (ENG-1957)
body:
## Problem

In the customer app, **Images → open an ad image → Edit with Placid → pick a template → Create** returns **404** for any image generated inside an Emma chat, and nothing renders. On the reported account that is *every* image (17 groups, 67 images).

The Images page groups chat images under **synthetic** ids minted by `getExecutionsWithAssets`:

```
taskId      = agent-mode-<sessionId>
executionId = <sessionId>-images
```

`generateFromTemplateToExecution` opens with `taskDb.getTaskById(taskId)`. No `AW-Tasks` row matches, so it 404s `Task not found` before Placid is called. The execution lookup would miss too, and the closing `updateTaskExecution` would have nowhere to write: chat images are not execution rows at all, they are `upload_image` / `generate_image` tool-call results in `AW-ChatMessages`, projected into `AW-ChatSessions.assetCache`.

The sibling Placid endpoints (`placid/templates`, `placid/editor-token`) appear to work on the same ids only because they never read `req.params.id`.

This is also why production has **zero** Placid renders and zero Placid spend events, which blocks verifying ENG-698's render metering.

## Change

`generateFromTemplateToExecution` resolves a synthetic pair to its chat session and takes a session path; everything else is unchanged.

| | task path (unchanged) | agent-mode path (new) |
|---|---|---|
| resolve | `AW-Tasks` + `AW-TaskExecutions` | `AW-ChatSessions` |
| authorize | owner, or platform admin | owner, or platform admin |
| bill | task owner (`onBehalfOf` = caller) | **session owner** (`onBehalfOf` = caller), plus `sessionId` on the ledger row |
| store | `tasks/<taskId>/executions/<executionId>/edits/...` | `uploadFileToS3` under the **session owner**, as other agent-mode images |
| persist | append to `result_files` | append a session message with an `upload_image` tool call |

- **Authorization** matches the house predicate used by `favorite-image`, `uploadImageToSession` and `generateResponse`: 404 when the session is missing, 403 when it is someone else's. Plain equality is delegation-safe, since `middleware/auth.ts` already resolves `req.user` to the target user.
- **Why a message, not a cache write:** the Images page derives agent-mode images by scanning session messages, so writing one message keeps a single source of truth and the existing `assetCache` refresh surfaces it. The portal already calls `fetchExecutionsWithImages()` after a successful render, so no frontend change is needed.
- **`parseAgentModeImageIds`** (new, `utils/agentModeAssetIds.ts`) requires both ids to name the *same* session — the session-path equivalent of the task path's `execution.taskId !== taskId`, without which a caller authorized for one session could aim the write at another. It strips affixes positionally, so a session id containing `-images` is not mangled the way the favorite/archive endpoints' `.replace()` would.

## Acceptance criteria
1. **Chat image renders and appears on the Images page** — session path renders, stores and persists as a scannable message.
2. **No cross-user renders** — 403 before Placid is called and before anything is metered; 404 for a missing session.
3. **Exactly one Placid ledger event per render, billed to the session owner** — unchanged single `recordVendorUsage`, now with `billingUserId` = session owner and `sessionId` set.
4. **Real task executions unchanged** — same S3 key, same `result_files` append, no session touched.

## Tests
- New `placidAgentModeRender.test.ts` (15 tests): the four ACs above, admin-renders-for-customer billing, the S3-failure path, mismatched id pair, and the parser (including the `-images`-in-session-id case).
- Existing `placidMeteringAndToken.test.ts` (20 tests) passes unmodified — the task path is byte-identical in behaviour.
- `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard`, `tasks.videoFavorites`, `tasks.agentModeMessageLoading`, `tasks.parallelAssetLoading`: all green (43 tests).
- Typecheck: no errors in the changed files. (21 pre-existing errors remain locally in `metaService.ts` / `sandbox/metaInterceptor.ts`, from a stale `@types/axios` in this machine's shared `node_modules`; untouched by this PR.)

## Post-deploy check
Render a Placid template from an Emma chat image, confirm it appears on the Images page, and confirm exactly one `placid` / `image_render` spend event lands for the session owner — which also unblocks the ENG-698 verification.

title: fix(agent-mode): supply current run id as ground truth for report_product_issues gate
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #2915. Live production verification (real admin account, real LLM) of the `claimed_unavailable_tools` gate surfaced that it was unusable for its primary case: the model has no legitimate way to learn its own `agentRuntimeRunId` (never surfaced in any tool result or prompt text), so requiring it as a `run_id` argument meant even an honest same-turn claim could never be verified. Confirmed live: asked to file a claim about its own current run, the model invented the placeholder `"current-run"` instead of a real id, and the gate correctly (but unhelpfully) rejected it as unverifiable.

- Thread `agentRuntimeRunId` from `toolDispatch.ts`'s `executePreparedTools` through `executePreparedAgentTool`/`executeTool` into the tool context as `context.currentRunId` — a value the **server** supplies because it already knows, unambiguously, which run is executing this exact tool call.
- `report_product_issues` now defaults to `context.currentRunId` whenever the model omits `run_id`, so a same-turn self-diagnosis claim verifies correctly with zero model-side cooperation required.
- An explicit `run_id` argument still takes priority when supplied, preserving ENG-939's citing-a-different-run case (a reviewer analysing another session) unchanged.
- Verified `context.currentRunId` cannot be spoofed by any caller: traced the external MCP path (`mcpServerCore.ts`) — its `context` object is a fixed literal that never accepts a `currentRunId` field from request args — and the internal agent-mode path keeps the model's tool arguments and the server-built `context` strictly separate.
- Side effect: the "always attach ground truth" dossier enrichment now fires automatically for any bug report filed from within a live run, not only when the model happened to supply `run_id` explicitly.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc` clean
- [x] 1000/1000 targeted tests pass post-merge-with-main (agentMode/, systemPrompt, report_product_issues family, sessionScoring, codingAgent smoke)
- [x] Live-verified on production with a real admin account: the original false-claim rejection still works; this PR's fix specifically addresses the honest-claim path the live test exposed

Risk: Medium

`report_product_issues` now falls back to `context.currentRunId` when `run_id` is omitted. Server run IDs flow through tool execution. Explicit IDs retain priority for cross-run analysis. Live-run bug reports receive dossier enrichment. Tests cover fallback behavior, rejection, cross-run IDs, and prose claims.

title: feat(human-eval): show the originating user's email on the #eval-queue card
body:
## Summary

Adds a `*User:*` line to the `#eval-queue` Slack card showing the email of the account whose chat produced the artifact.

Matt's ask, direct from the channel: the card names the review type, category and reviewer, but nothing about *whose* work it is — so telling one customer's creative from another means opening the chat link first. That's the same context-free-noise complaint ENG-1853/1854 exist to fix, and it's a one-line fix on the card we already post.

Before / after:

```
 *Human eval: creative image*
 *Category:* Ad
 Reviewer: @Matthew Wilmer
+*User:* founder@haven.com

 *Output:* open output
 *Chat:* open associated chat
```

## Design notes

- **Resolved only for the Slack message, never persisted.** The email is looked up at post time from the candidate's `userId` and used to render the line. No new field on the `AW-HumanEvalQueue` record — this stays out of data-plane territory, and the candidate's `userId` was already the durable identity.
- **Its own try/catch, deliberately.** `userDb.getUserById` is a GSI query that re-throws on a transient DynamoDB error. Without a local catch, that error lands in `createCandidate`'s posting try/catch and costs the *entire notification*, not just this one line — the mutation test for this fails with `Number of calls: 0`, i.e. no Slack post at all. Same fail-safe shape as the settings-lookup fixes in #2923.
- **Verbose card only.** The concise exception format (`buildConciseExceptionMessage`) is untouched — it is deliberately one mention plus one link, per ENG-1853's "Slack contains only a concise assignment/reminder and one portal link; it is not the review database." Adding fields there would defeat its purpose.
- **Degrades quietly.** Candidates with no `userId` (e.g. automatic lead enrichment) skip the lookup entirely and render exactly as they do today.

## Review

One independent adversarial round, briefed with the invariants established across #2923's four rounds. **No blocking defects**; the reviewer independently re-ran both mutation exercises and reproduced them exactly. Three low findings, each re-verified against the real code before fixing:

- **Spy leak (fixed).** `spy.mockRestore()` sat as the last statement of each new test, so a failing assertion leaked the stub — `jest.config.js` sets `clearMocks` but *not* `restoreMocks`, so `mockResolvedValue` survives between tests. Replaced with a central `afterEach(jest.restoreAllMocks)`.
- **Untested deleted-account path (fixed).** `getUserById` returns `undefined` both for a missing user and for any account tombstoned with a `deleted_` userId prefix (`db.ts:1190`) — likelier in practice than the transient throw that *was* covered. Added a test, mutation-verified.
- **`userDb` is not constructor-injected (not fixed).** All eight other collaborators are injected; this one is reached as a module singleton, which is why the tests need `jest.spyOn`. A real inconsistency, but restructuring the constructor is out of proportion to a one-line card change.

Also fixed a **pre-existing** issue the review surfaced: the toggle's JSDoc still described a "default-off switch" while the code has defaulted ON since #2923's flip, and sat as an orphaned second doc block. Comment-only, no behavior change.

Verified clean by the reviewer and worth recording so they aren't re-raised: no import cycle (verified transitively by BFS over the import graph — the only paths back are dynamic `import()` hops that form no load-time cycle); **module-load cost is exactly zero** since `db.ts` was already statically loaded via `chatbotService`; `getUserByIdConsistent` correctly *not* used (`email` is the base table's partition key, so it never changes); delegation is correct (under delegate access `userId` is the target customer, so the card names the right party); and PII is consistent with existing convention (`slackService.ts:895` already posts *lead* emails to Slack). The unescaped `${email}` interpolation introduces no new injection class — the same card already interpolates raw user-typed chat text.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] 42 tests in `humanEvalService` passing, including four new ones: the email renders; a thrown lookup still posts the card without the line; a deleted/missing account omits the line; a candidate with no `userId` never calls the lookup
- [x] Every behavior mutation-verified — dropping the `*User:*` line fails the render test; dropping the local try/catch fails the fail-safe test with `Number of calls: 0` (i.e. the entire Slack post is lost); making the resolver return a value for a missing user fails the deleted-account test and only that test
- [x] **Live-verified on env1** against real DynamoDB — the thing unit tests cannot prove, since they mock `getUserById`. Temporary instrumentation captured the actual built card from container logs:

  ```
  *Human eval: creative image*
  *Category:* Ad
  Reviewer: <@U08TWRHKCG4>
  *User:* test@example.com
  *Output:* <https://example.com/env1-probe-2.png|open output>
  ```

  Instrumentation fully reverted (zero probe strings in the diff; working tree matches committed HEAD, so what ran on env1 is what is committed). Both test candidate rows deleted from `AW-HumanEvalQueue` and confirmed gone.
- [x] env1 also re-proved #2923's core fix incidentally: env1's Slack token is stale, so `postSlackMessage` threw `invalid_auth` for real — and the candidate still persisted, exactly as designed.
- [ ] Production verification on the real `#eval-queue` (clearly-marked test post, reviewers given a heads-up, cleaned up after)

## Related

Follow-up to #2923 (ENG-1854). Same surface, same reviewer complaint; ENG-1853 replaces this card with a real portal later.

title: ENG-1550: record_ads_recommendation — the outcome ledger's missing write path
body:
## What and why

The ENG-1550 outcome ledger shipped its store, service and REST routes — but **nothing any agent could call ever wrote to it**, so prod's `AW-AdsOutcomeLedger` held zero rows. Established three ways:

- the only non-test importer of `outcomeLedger` in the backend is the route mount at `app.ts:409`
- no registered tool name matches recommendation/ledger/outcome/predict (`workplan_recommendation` is the unrelated work-plan system)
- there is no generic HTTP/fetch tool a skill could use to reach the admin routes

The route file names its intended consumer as *"the loop system that actually generates recommendations … once it exists"* — it does not exist. So the 5 ads skills stayed **architecturally amnesiac**: advice emitted as prose, then gone. That is the gap ENG-885 calls *"where nearly all the value sits"*.

This adds the missing write path.

## Two deliberate design constraints

**Record-only.** `routes/outcomeLedger.ts` gates *both* record and score behind `requireAdmin`, reasoning that letting a caller "mint or resolve its own scored verdicts would let them rewrite the agent's track record". That risk is real but **asymmetric**: recording a *pending* prediction is the agent committing to a falsifiable claim before the outcome is known — the entire point of the ledger. *Scoring* is where a model could launder its own record. So the tool can only create a pending row; there is no scoring tool, and scoring stays admin/cron-only. A test fails if a scoring sibling is ever added.

**Owner-scoped, no `client_id`.** `getMetaCredentials` carries an explicit ENG-1801 warning that client-scope *"must never be wired from a write/mutate tool without its own fresh authorization decision"*. This is a write, so it takes the ownership check (same shape as `get_ads_thresholds`) rather than routing around the warning. Admin cross-tenant recording is deliberately **not** inherited.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` clean; 13/13 tests pass — both re-run on this branch after rebasing onto current `main`.
- **Red-checked**: disabling the ownership check makes the ownership test fail, and it passes again on revert — the tests are not decorative.
- **Live-tested end to end on test-env1**, not just unit-tested. Wired the tool into the *Meta Creative Fatigue Detector* skill in `Dev-AW-Skills` (atomic `ADD`; attribute count 9→9, `systemPrompt` SHA identical, nothing removed — the ENG-917 checklist), then ran a real agent turn through a scheduled-chat test run: `passed: true`, `actualFunctionCalls: ["record_ads_recommendation"]`, zero misses. A genuine row landed in `Dev-AW-AdsOutcomeLedger` (4 → 5 rows) with `status: pending`, correct metric/direction/magnitude/date, real `createdBy`, server-minted id — **byte-shape identical to a row written by the REST route**.

**This is the first time an agent has ever written to the outcome ledger.**

## Rollout note (not in this PR)

Deploy must land before any prod `AW-Skills` row references the tool, or a live skill carries a dangling tool name. Verified all 3 intended skills (Meta Creative Fatigue Detector, Cross-Channel Budget Engine, Weekly Executive Ads Report) are present in **every** real prod subscription tier, so the wiring will actually reach customers. Note `getPublishedSkills` is cached, so a prod skill edit needs a cache expiry or restart to take effect.

title: ENG-1938: merge the ledger estimate into live list-sent-invitations rows
body:
## Why — the last gap, found checking #2916 on production
After the ledger fix, a live `list-sent-invitations` on a real account returned:

```
source: live   totalPending: 99 (lower bound)   sentAtIsApproximate: true
oldest sent_at: 2026-09-02T11:27:37.376Z
newest sent_at: 2026-09-02T11:27:37.376Z    distinct sent_at values: 1
```

Every row on the page carried the same timestamp — exactly 14 days before the call, i.e. LinkedIn's "2 weeks ago" resolved at request time. Our ledger held **9 distinct values for the same account, the oldest 44 days**, because it keeps the earliest estimate ever observed (ENG-1938). The view preferred live and discarded the better data, so "withdraw the oldest" is unrankable from this action's output and a human reading the list sees a flat wall of identical dates.

## What
- Read the ledger alongside a usable live page and serve `earliestSentAt(live, ledger)` per invitation. Both are upper bounds on the real send, so the earlier value is tighter and still never earlier than the send — the same rule #2916 verified on production (38 invites with exact logged send times, 0 earlier).
- Live rows are returned **oldest first**, like cache rows already were, and the notice says "showing the N oldest".
- A ledger read failure on the live path is logged and ignored: the live page is served unchanged.
- The cache read that the fallback path already performed is now done once and shared, so no extra read on the fallback path.

**Read-only.** No stored data changes, so this does not touch the data-plane approval gate that #2916 needed.

## Tests
- 4 new: ledger earlier wins + oldest-first ordering + untracked row keeps its live value; live wins when the ledger is later; ledger failure still serves live; `earliestSentAt` edge cases.
- 106 suites touching sentAt / sent invitations / linkedin_outreach: **2870 passed**. Typecheck shows only `origin/main`'s pre-existing `metaService.ts` / `metaInterceptor` errors.

## Post-deploy check
Re-run the same live call: distinct `sent_at` values must exceed 1 and the oldest must match the ledger's oldest (~44 days), not the label date.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: ENG-1550: reject a backdated evaluationDate (retroactive prediction)
body:
## The bug

`createRecommendation` validated only that `evaluationDate` **parses** — never that it sits after `createdAt`. `scoreRecommendation` treats a row as settled once `now >= evaluationDate + windowDays`, so a recommendation created today with `evaluationDate: '2020-01-01'` is **born already past its settling window** and can be scored immediately, returning a real `correct`/`wrong` verdict about a period that ended before the prediction was made.

This store exists to be a **falsifiable** track record of whether the agent's advice works. Accepting a backdated evaluation date permits recording "predictions" whose outcomes are already known and scoring them correct. That doesn't just add one bad row — it makes the aggregate record untrustworthy, which is the single property the ledger exists to provide.

Pre-existing and reachable today through the admin REST route, independent of any one caller.

## It has already happened in production

`AW-AdsOutcomeLedger` currently holds a row `6dabc0fb` with `evaluationDate 2026-07-01` against `createdAt 2026-09-16` — backdated two and a half months, scored `verdict: correct`. I wrote it myself while live-testing the route. The bug demonstrating itself.

**That row should be deleted** when someone with prod write access is next in there; it is a falsely-correct entry in the track record. I have no `DeleteItem` permission.

## The fix

`evaluationDate` may not precede `createdAt`. Equality is allowed deliberately — predicting about this instant is not a claim about the past, and the settling window still withholds scoring for `windowDays`.

`createdAt` is now validated too, and is load-bearing rather than decorative: every comparison against an Invalid Date is `false`, so an unparseable `createdAt` would silently **disable** the new bound instead of tripping it — the same trap the existing `evaluationDate` parse check already documents.

## Verification

- **Written failing-first**: 4 of 8 new tests failed against the old code, including one that creates a backdated row and scores a real verdict about 2020.
- **252/252 pass** across every ledger / learning / capture / thresholds suite — ENG-502's `captureFatigueRecommendations` path included, since it is the ledger's live producer.
- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- **No migration needed** — pure validation, effective on deploy.

### One thing worth a reviewer's eye

The route suite's fixtures were a hardcoded `'2026-01-01'`, which went stale the moment the wall clock passed it, so its **authorisation** tests began failing on fixture data rather than the behaviour they exist to check. Now derived from `Date.now()`.

Deliberately split into two constants: rows POSTed to the create route need a **future** date, while rows read back as already-created for the scoring tests need a **settled (past)** one. Collapsing both into "future" would have left those scoring tests green while silently exercising the `unscoreable` path — they assert only status 200, so that weakening would not have surfaced as a failure.

title: fix(placid): render through the REST API instead of the URL API (ENG-1972)
body:
## Problem

Every Placid render in production fails, so **no ad image can be created at all** — from a task image or an Emma-chat image — and production has recorded **zero** Placid renders and zero Placid spend events, all time.

The renderer used the **URL API**: `GET api.placid.app/u/<template_uuid>?<layers>`. That endpoint answers **403 Forbidden** for this project. Observed twice in production on 2026-09-16 (06:50, 06:51 UTC) after ENG-1957 shipped:

```
POST /api/tasks/agent-mode-1b7f2131-…/executions/1b7f2131-…-images/generate-from-template  500
web[4650]: Error in generateFromTemplateToExecution: Request failed with status code 403
```

**It is not our request shape.** A parameter-free GET of the same template, from an unrelated machine with no credentials, returns the same 403:

```
$ curl -sI "https://api.placid.app/u/issqexguamokx"     # 403, HTML "Forbidden"
```

Meanwhile the REST calls beside it succeed on the same account and the same ids: template listing 200/304, editor token 200. Placid's docs note a project can be **restricted to signed URLs only** on the URL API, which fits exactly.

## Change

Render through **`POST /api/rest/images`**, authenticated with the private token this backend already holds and already uses successfully — so the render no longer depends on that project setting, and no dashboard change or URL-signing scheme is needed.

- `create_now: true` asks for a synchronous render, but Placid documents it as best-effort ("may fail under high load"), so a `queued` response is **polled**, not treated as a failure. Bounded at 10 polls × 1.5s because this runs inside a user's request; a stuck queue fails cleanly instead of hanging.
- The REST API returns a URL, so the bytes are fetched before the existing S3 upload. Everything downstream — S3 layout, result file, ENG-1957's session message — is unchanged.
- Layers pass straight through: the REST body takes the same `{layer: {prop: value}}` shape the client already sends, and values keep their own types instead of being stringified into the URL API's query notation. The `source_image_url` convenience mapping is restated as `layers.image.image`.

**Metering moved with the egress.** ENG-701's coverage guard holds every paid-vendor call site to booking its own usage — and after extracting the render, this file is the one that knows whether an image was actually produced. So `recordVendorUsage` now sits beside the call that spends the money (the same pattern `voiceoverService` uses), taking the billing subject from the controller: task owner, or chat-session owner for a chat image, never the caller. The controller's own metering block and its now-unused import are gone.

## Acceptance criteria
1. **A render succeeds** from a task image and from an Emma-chat image — provable only in production, see below.
2. **Exactly one `placid` / `image_render` event per successful render**, billed to the owner with `onBehalfOf` for an admin — unchanged contract, now asserted where the call lives.
3. **A render that produced no image books nothing** — error status, missing polling URL, polling ceiling, and HTTP failure all covered.

## Tests
- New `placidRenderService.test.ts` (12): token header, layer pass-through, queued→polled→finished, id-derived polling URL, error on create, error while polling, polling ceiling, HTTP failure propagated as-is (so a refused render stays distinguishable from a slow one), one charge per image including for a polled render, `onBehalfOf`/`sessionId` carried through, nothing booked on failure, and ENG-698 AC6 (a throwing recorder still returns the image).
- `placidMeteringAndToken.test.ts` and `placidAgentModeRender.test.ts`: invariants unchanged, updated only where the transport is — "before Placid is called" now watches the POST. One test added: an unconfigured private token is refused before any request and books nothing.
- `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard` green — the new egress file books its own usage rather than being allowlisted.
- 81 tests across the four suites; typecheck clean for the changed files.

## Post-deploy check
Render a template from a chat image and from a task image; confirm both produce an image and that exactly one `placid`/`image_render` spend event lands per render for the owner. That is also the first Placid spend event in production, which unblocks **ENG-698**'s render-metering verification and **ENG-1957** AC1.

If the 403 turns out **not** to be the signed-URL restriction, this change still stands: the REST API is the documented, token-authenticated path and is the one already proven to work for this project.

title: fix(billing): dedupe keyed unpriced vendor writes so a retry counts once (ENG-1958)
body:
A bug in my own ENG-702 AC1 work.

## The bug
`recordVendorUsageIdempotent` guards a retried **priced** call with a conditional spend event. An **unpriced** call has no spend event (the billing boundary forbids a $0 one), so it fell back to a plain unconditional `ADD` — and a retried unpriced call with the same `idempotencyKey` **double-counted its quantity/callCount**. Cost is unaffected ($0); usage volume isn't, and §8 reads the extra as unmirrored.

Exposure is small today (only v0 passes a stable key, and its key resolves to a *priced* rate) but grows as more call sites adopt keys.

## The fix
`incrementUsageWithDedupeMarker` pairs the aggregate ADD with a conditional `Put` of a tiny dedupe marker in the **same transaction** — same table, same key schema (`userId`/`sk`), **no new table/index/key shape**. The marker:
- lives in its own `idem#<billingUserId>` partition, so it can never collide with a real usage row
- carries no provider/unit/cost, so `isVendorEntry` and the spend reads ignore it
- self-expires on the table's native `ttl`

A replay fails the condition → transaction cancelled → aggregate untouched → reported `duplicate`.

**Scoped to keyed calls only** (AC3): an unkeyed unpriced call keeps the plain write — a replay is undetectable without a key, and a marker would never match. Conflicts retry as transient, matching the priced path.

## Data-plane
New item shape in an existing table under its existing key schema — not a schema/table/index/key change. It's part of the ENG-702/ENG-1250 idempotency rail, which **Harsha's 2026-09-15 approval on ENG-1250 explicitly unblocked** (the ticket's "needs Harsha" note predates that).

## Testing
202 tests across ten suites. Mutations fail: reverting the keyed-unpriced path to the plain ADD, and not classifying the marker's condition failure as a duplicate.

title: fix(metering): attribute the residual system-booked paths (ENG-1961)
body:
## Problem

ENG-1858 threaded the triggering user through the high-volume LLM paths and cut unattributed spend from **27% of calls to 0.1%**. This closes the remainder.

Every `callLLM` site outside tests (57) and every `recordVendorUsage` / `recordUsage` / `meterUserUsage` / `meterUsageFromResponse` site (45) was re-classified against `main` first. That corrected four rows of the ticket's table and found two paths it did not list — see the [mapping comment](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1961) on the ticket.

## Change

**User-triggered — now charged to whoever triggered them**

| path | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| intake dedup judge (`dedupService.findDuplicate`) | no usage context at all — the only such production `callLLM` | `intake_dedup`, billed to the acting user, with the session |
| `inlineEmailStyles` (`utils/emailVariables.ts`) | its own comment: *"no userId reachable in this utility"* | `content_gen`, billed to the importing user |

The dedup judge needed no identity resolution: both live callers already hold a userId (the support route computes one for the report fingerprint, the Emma tool resolves one before filing). `FileUserIssueParams` gains `actingUserId`, threaded to all three `findDuplicate` sites.

**`actingUserId` is deliberately not `userEmail`.** Under ENG-939 `userEmail` is the *affected* user of a cross-user telemetry review — someone who asked for nothing. Billing them would charge a customer for an admin's triage, which is the same mistake ENG-1957 fixed on the Placid path. Who pays is who spent the tokens.

**A bucket path stops standing in for a user id**

`workPlanThumbnailService` calls the image service with `userId: 'workplans'`. That string is an **S3 folder** (`users/workplans/files/...`) — but `userId` also feeds five metering points in `imageGeneration.ts`, so a literal that is not an account has been landing in the userId slot of usage rows, and renaming it would move every existing object.

`ImageGenerationParams` gains `meterUserId` / `meterFeature`: the charge and the file owner are now separate. Omitted, the charge follows `userId` exactly as before, so no other caller changes. An explicit `null` books no user — the honest shape for platform-funded generation. Thumbnails pass `meterUserId: null` with `platform:workplan_thumbnail`, S3 path untouched.

**Platform-funded paths say so**

- `describeVideo`: attribution was already right (ENG-200); the gap was *shape*. It booked under the catch-all `agent_task` with no session — now `describe_video`, with the chat session threaded, matching what describeImage got in ENG-1858.
- `scripts/compareJudgeModels.ts` → `platform:judge_eval`.
- `fathomOnboardingIngestionService` → `platform:fathom_onboarding_ingestion`. This held the **only hardcoded `userId: 'system'` literal in the codebase**. It was nearly honest — extraction runs before `matchFathomOnboardingTarget` resolves an account, so no user exists yet — but a literal that reads like an account is worse than a named feature.

**Dead code**

`triageSlackMessage` is deleted; ENG-1613 removed its only call site. Its mock stays in `slack.autoTriggerRemoved.test.ts`, now documented as a trap for the **call site** rather than the method — which is what that regression test was always guarding. A stale doc reference to it elsewhere is updated.

## Acceptance criteria
1. **Every path attributed or recorded as `platform:`** — table above; nothing is left anonymous.
2. **No non-user string reaches the userId slot** — `'workplans'` is now only an S3 path.
3. **The `system` share is re-measured after this lands** — post-deploy, below.

## Not changed
`cron/onboardingLoop.ts`, `rcaEnricher.ts` and `routes/slack.ts` already record `platform:*` (ENG-1858) and are correct as-is. `routes/tasks.ts` ~1393 already passes usage context — that row of the ticket was stale.

## Tests
- `dedupService.test.ts`: the judge's context, and feature-only metering when no user is in scope (no invented user).
- New `eng1961.residualAttribution.test.ts`: `inlineEmailStyles` charges the importer, meters feature-only without one, and does not call the LLM when no inlining is needed; the workplan thumbnail asserts all three of `meterUserId: null`, `platform:workplan_thumbnail`, and the unchanged `workplans` folder.
- `slack.autoTriggerRemoved`, `intakeService` ×4, `adminWorkPlanThumbnail`, `vendorMeteringCoverageGuard`: green.
- Typecheck clean for the changed files.

## Post-deploy check
Re-measure the `system` share over a full traffic day; the residual should be platform-named rows only. One specific row to watch: an untraced `agent_task` call booked to `system` on 2026-09-16 00:47 UTC (gemini-3.8-flash, 3,684 tokens) best fits the dedup judge — single call, default model, and `agent_task` is exactly what a missing usage context produces. If it stops appearing, that identifies it.

title: chore(agent-mode): log-only probe for tool dispatch outside the offered set
body:
## What this is

A **log-only** probe. Seven lines of code, no behaviour change. It answers a question we currently can't answer any other way.

## The question

Entitlement is enforced in exactly one place: **visibility**. `getFilteredTools()` decides which schemas the model is handed, and `availableToolNames` in `chatbotService` is literally `toolDefinitions.map(t => t.function.name)` — the set offered on that turn.

**Dispatch never re-checks it.** The model's raw `toolCall.function.name` goes straight into `executeTool`.

To be fair to the code, dispatch is not unguarded. `executeTool` and `ToolRegistry.execute` carry five real guards between them: evaluation-account, arg/contract validation, ENG-803 publish approval, ENG-822 anonymous refusal for `requiresUserAccount` tools, ENG-827 scheduled-publish consent, plus an unknown-tool throw. **None of them is entitlement.** And the registry holds every registered tool with no entitlement filter, so a name that arrives resolves and runs.

The Agent Tool Gateway that looks like the backstop runs with `enforce: false` in production — `AGENT_TOOL_GATEWAY_ENFORCE` is not set in the prod EB configuration.

So the only thing preventing an unentitled call is the model being constrained to the schemas it was given — **a provider-side guarantee, not ours.**

## Why probe instead of fix

That guarantee is probably holding. I couldn't verify it: forcing the case needs a genuinely restricted account (the test-env admin has everything, so nothing is unentitled for it), and probing entitlement bypass against live prod wasn't an appropriate thing to do.

Two reasons not to just assume it: this codebase routes through OpenRouter across providers of differing strictness, and this model has previously fabricated a UI control (ENG-1855) and an audit table (ENG-1625) with complete confidence.

And two reasons not to enforce right now: refusing could break a flow that legitimately dispatches outside the offered list — delegated admin, internal tooling, the sandbox path — and we have no evidence about what those are. Enforcing something that never fires is also just dead code that reads as protection.

## What it settles

- **Silent** → the provider constraint holds. Enable enforcement knowing it's inert, or close the finding as defended-by-construction.
- **Fires** → real gap, and the log names the tool, session and portal, so enforcement can be scoped rather than guessed.

Same make-the-failure-observable-before-gating-on-it pattern the ENG-1852 follow-up (#2930) took six review rounds to arrive at.

## Tests

Added to the existing skill-session tool-binding harness rather than duplicating 165 lines of mocks: silent when the tool was offered, warns **and still dispatches** when it wasn't.

Mutation-verified: removing the probe fails 1 test, inverting its condition fails 2.

Build exit 0 · `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 · 34 suites / 321 tests pass across chatbotService and the chat socket path.

## Note on the diff size

Seven lines of code; the rest is the reasoning above kept next to the check, so the next reader doesn't have to re-derive why it warns instead of refusing.

---

**Accountable-Owner:** Manan Varma
**Accountable-Linear:** none — follow-up to ENG-1852's investigation, closing a question rather than a ticket
**Execution-Actor:** Claude

title: ENG-1978: record unconfirmed wildcard tool grants (observation only, no behaviour change)
body:
## Summary

**Observation only — no behaviour change.** Every code path returns exactly what it returned before. This makes four currently-invisible cases visible so we can decide what to do about them with data instead of assumptions.

Four paths through `subscriptionService` resolve to `["*"]` — grant *every registered tool* — and only one of them is deliberate:

| Path | Deliberate? |
|---|---|
| A tier config explicitly listing `["*"]` | **yes** — left alone |
| Unknown tier name, or a malformed `subscription_types` row | no |
| An empty `allowedSkills` list | no — almost certainly inverted |
| Any thrown error in `getAllowedSkills` / `resolveSkillsToToolNames` / `getAllowedFunctionCalls` | no |
| A tier that could not be *confirmed* for this user (missing user row, unreadable org owner, org-lookup blip) | no |

The empty-list case is the clearest: `FREE_TIER_FALLBACK` is `allowedSkills: []`, commented *"No premium skills on Free tier"* — and resolves to the entire tool registry.

## Why observation first, rather than just fixing it

**Whether any of these fire in production is currently unknowable.** The error cases log a bare `console.error` with no user and no marker; the rest log nothing at all. "We have never had a problem here" is therefore not evidence of safety — a silent over-grant is indistinguishable from normal operation from the outside.

The fix is written, tested and mutation-verified on `manan/eng-1978-tool-entitlement-fail-closed`, and is **deliberately not proposed for merge**, because:

1. It converts a *rare, silent over-grant* into a *visible broken session* ("Emma can't do anything"). That is the right direction for security, but the failure becomes user-facing.
2. `settingsService.getSetting` is **uncached** — a live DynamoDB read on every entitlement check. Higher read volume means more chances to trip a fail-closed path.
3. An earlier revision of that branch would have **stripped every tool from paying org members during routine org-lookup blips**, by gating on a `resolved: false` flag that is overloaded across four cases — two of which still carry a real, usable tier. The original author had handled that deliberately and said so in a comment three lines above the code I changed. Caught and reverted before it reached a PR.

That last one is the argument for this PR existing: a tradeoff like #1 should be made against a measured rate, not an assumed one.

## What to do with it

In ~2 weeks, grep production logs:

```
[entitlement] WILDCARD-GRANT
```

Each line carries `reason`, `userId`, and context. The `reason` breakdown answers the question directly:

- **Effectively never fires** → cherry-pick the fail-closed branch; it's a free win.
- **Fires regularly** → a blind flip would have caused visible outages. Add a cache or retry on that uncached settings read first, then flip.

## Scope note — this does not address ENG-1978's title

The ticket is titled *"a new tool that isn't wired to a skill is exposed to every customer via `__other_skills__`"*. That is the catch-all **working as designed**, not a defect, and we are deliberately not changing it. Measured against the live database: **31 tools** currently reach customers only via that bundle, and they include the entire landing-page product (`generate_landing_page`, `deploy_landing_page`, `publish_landing_page_changes`, and 8 more). Inverting that default would delete a shipped feature for every customer.

The ticket's own question #2 — *"Defaulting to full access on error is a fail-open"* — is the real defect, and is what this PR instruments.

Two factual corrections for the ticket while we're here:
- It says only `Sandbox` omits the bundle, implying Sandbox is the safe tier. **Sandbox is `["*"]`** — a full wildcard, strictly *more* permissive than the catch-all.
- A tier can reach the bundle three ways: listing `__other_skills__`, `"*"`, or **being empty**. The ticket names only the first.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] **All 46 pre-existing tests in `subscriptionService.test.ts` pass completely unmodified** — including `getAllowedSkills returns wildcard for "*" or empty`, which asserts the empty-list inversion. That test passing untouched is the proof this PR changed no behaviour. (The fail-closed branch had to rewrite it; this one does not.)
- [x] 190 tests green across `subscriptionService` / `tierAccessControl` / `chatbotService.skillSessionToolBinding` / `agentModeService.skills` / `agentModeController.functionCallsSubscription` / `auth.subscription`
- [x] 4 new tests, each asserting **both** that the grant is recorded **and** that the return value is unchanged — the second half is what catches a future edit to a return value made while believing only logging was being touched
- [x] Full pre-push suite green

## Rollback

Revert the two commits. No schema change, no config, no data migration — the only runtime effect is additional log lines.

title: fix(agent-mode): prepend a ground-truth notice when coding_agent's acceptance check fails (ENG-1899)
body:
## Summary

Customer-reported (mvarma, session `b0967189`, 2026-09-12, HIGH priority). `coding_agent` was asked to fix transparent CTA buttons twice. Attempt 1 claimed the fix was applied while its own `text_present` acceptance check failed and the live page still showed the bug. Attempt 2 claimed *"visual verification passed with screenshot"* while its own `selector_exists 'form'` check failed **and** it reported button copy matching neither the approved brief nor the deployed page.

**Root cause:** the boolean gate is correct; the text is not. `codingAgentService.ts` already forces `success: false` and carries structured `acceptanceStatus`/`acceptance` when a check fails — but the human-readable `message` is built as a concatenation (`${result.message}\n\n${acceptance.summary}...`), which puts the model's own possibly-false claim *first* and the real failure *after*. That string flows through unmodified to Emma and to the agent-mode ledger; nothing downstream ever read the structured fields to correct what the synthesizing LLM says next.

## Fix

One new function, `buildAcceptanceFailureNotice` (`agentMode/core/synthesisResidue.ts`), wired into the main loop immediately after the existing `buildUnavailableCapabilityNotice` guard (`agentModeService.ts`) — same file, same pattern, built for a different tool but the *identical* failure class (a refusal papered over by a confident fabricated summary).

That guard's own documented lesson is the reason for this shape: an earlier guard in the same file (`detectFalseCompletionClaim`) only caught its incident because the false claim happened to contain a checkable number, and appended its correction *below* the fabrication. `buildUnavailableCapabilityNotice` fixed both problems by being:
- **Unconditional** — states a fact already in the ledger (a specific check failed), never tries to detect that the prose claims success, so a claim phrased any other way still can't slip through.
- **Prepended** — the true state is seen before the model's own claim, not after.

`buildAcceptanceFailureNotice` does the same for `coding_agent`, and is simpler to build: `coding_agent` already emits a clean `acceptanceStatus` per call — no partial-install-style inference needed.

**Deliberately not doing** (real, complementary hardening, out of scope for this fix): reordering `codingAgentService.ts`'s own message concatenation, or adding evidence-gating to `report_to_user`'s free-text `status` field. This fix is the smallest change with the most direct precedent already proven in this codebase; the ticket's stated symptom is fully addressed by making the true state impossible to miss at synthesis time.

**Ruled out, not assumed:** the real session's `calledFunctions` shows `playwright_browser_take_screenshot: 1` — a screenshot genuinely was taken, so this isn't pure hallucination-from-nothing, it's an inaccurate summary surviving into the final message ahead of the real check. And `coding_agent`'s draft/preview-vs-production branch split is real and correctly designed (a fresh load of the *production* URL legitimately showing the old bug is expected) — but `verifyAcceptanceChecks` runs against the *same* preview URL the model claims to have checked, so that architecture doesn't explain this ticket's symptom and isn't touched.

## Two bugs found and fixed during review + live-test iteration

1. **Duplicate banner across turns** (env1 live-test finding, commit `c32a407b6`): a session that hits two consecutive `coding_agent` failures — the ORIGINAL incident's own shape — can have the model echo its own prior (already-decorated) turn from conversation history, duplicating the banner. Fixed with an idempotency check against the exact computed notice text (refined further in point 3 below).
2. **Stale failure surviving a same-turn retry pass** (independent review finding, commit `c32a407b6`): a failed `coding_agent` call was still reported even after a LATER call in the same turn retried and passed. Fixed: a failure superseded by a later same-turn pass is no longer reported.
3. **Marker-substring false negative** (independent review finding on the point-1 fix itself, commit `ffc953a6d`): the original duplicate-suppression check matched on the bare marker phrase anywhere in content, which could also suppress a genuinely NEW, different failure if the model's prose merely recapped an older incident. Fixed by comparing the exact computed notice text instead of the generic marker — verified via a dedicated regression test the reviewer's own probe predicted would fail, and did.

## Rollout

Own env-var kill switch (`AGENT_CODING_AGENT_ACCEPTANCE_NOTICE`, default ON), per this block's own stated convention: an unconditional guard most needs one, since a false positive prepends a banner to an otherwise-correct answer.

title: fix(placid): log the vendor's own error, not just the status code (ENG-1972)
body:
## Problem

The render path logged `err?.message`. For an axios failure that is the bare string `Request failed with status code 403` — the response body, which carries the actual reason, was thrown away.

That is not hypothetical cost. Investigating why no Placid render has ever succeeded in production took three rounds because of it:

1. First 403 → read as Placid's documented "restrict URL API to signed URLs" setting.
2. The render was migrated from the URL API to the REST API on that theory (PR #2943) — a change that stands on its own merits, but did not fix the symptom.
3. The REST API returned 403 as well. Only calling the API by hand surfaced what had been in every response body from the start:

```json
{"message": "Requires Subscription and Credits"}
```

The Placid account has no subscription, so **no render could ever have succeeded, by any transport**. One log line would have said so on day one.

## Change

`describePlacidError(error)` renders a failure as `HTTP <status>: <body> (<message>)`:

- **Bounded** at 500 characters, so a vendor HTML error page cannot flood the log.
- **Falls through unchanged** for non-HTTP failures (`socket hang up` stays `socket hang up`).
- **Never throws** — a circular/unserializable body degrades to a placeholder rather than turning a logging call into a second failure.
- **No credentials.** Only `error.response` is read. The request headers, which carry the Bearer token, are never touched.

Wired into `generateFromTemplateToExecution`'s catch, the one place that swallowed it.

## Tests
Four cases in `placidRenderService.test.ts`: the real 403 body is surfaced with its status; a non-HTTP error passes through unchanged; a 5,000-character body is truncated with an ellipsis and stays under the cap; a circular body does not throw and still reports its status. 18 tests in the suite, typecheck clean for the changed files.

## Context
This does not unblock rendering — that needs a Placid subscription, and whether we want one at all is [ENG-2009](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2009). This is the diagnostic debt that made the blocker expensive to find, fixed so the next vendor refusal reports itself.

title: ENG-2011: §4 admission reservation & concurrency gate
body:
## ENG-2011 — §4 admission reservation & concurrency gate

Part of ENG-1250 (Usage accounting v2). Builds the admission gate that decides whether a new call is admitted and reserves its cost atomically, so two concurrent calls cannot both spend the last of a balance.

### What this adds
- **`spendAdmission.ts`** — `admitAndReserve` / `settleReservation` / `voidReservation` over `AW-SpendProjection`.
- **`spendProjectionDb.ts`** — `PersistedProjection` gains an unfloored `availableMicroUsd`, seeded in `putProjection` as `usable − settled − reserved`.

### The concurrency guarantee
DynamoDB condition expressions cannot do arithmetic across attributes (`settled + reserved + :est <= usable` is invalid). So the balance is materialised as one attribute, `availableMicroUsd`, and admission conditions on it alone:

```
ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(billingUserId) AND availableMicroUsd >= :est
UpdateExpression:    ADD reservedMicroUsd :est, availableMicroUsd :negEst
```

The conditional `UpdateItem` **is** the guarantee — DynamoDB serialises it, so two racing admissions cannot both pass when only one fits. A rejected admission writes nothing and leaves the balance intact for the call that does fit.

- **settle** moves `reserved → settled` and returns `(reserved − actual)` to the balance — a cheaper call refunds, a dearer one drives `available` honestly negative (overrun). Never gated: a reservation that happened always settles.
- **void** returns the whole reservation to the balance.
- `allowOverrun` skips the balance condition (admitted work may finish) but still requires the row — reserving against a missing projection is a seeding bug, not an overrun.

### Observe-only
Nothing wires to enforcement. The live gate stays on the legacy counter until the cutover (§9.6), which **AC6 keeps with Harsha**. This slice makes the gate exist and proves it correct.

### Verification
- 11 admission + 15 projection-store tests; full affected set **108 passing** (spendAdmission, spendProjectionDb, spendProjection, spendReconciliation, ensureCriticalTables).
- Mutation-tested: drop the balance condition, don't decrement available, flip the settle sign, treat a condition-fail as admitted, collapse missing/insufficient, remove the estimate guard — **all six killed**.
- `npm run typecheck` clean for both changed files.

title: fix(security): sanitize LLM-authored HTML before it reaches S3 (ENG-1997)
body:
## Summary

`createHtmlFile` (passthrough/render/deterministic-fallback branches) and the sibling `update_html_file`/CSS-selector editor upload LLM-authored or LLM-edited HTML straight to S3 with zero sanitization. If the model faithfully reproduces untrusted quoted text (a CRM note, a client quote) containing markup, or a tool call directly sets a dangerous attribute (`setAttribute`/`replace`/`append`), it lands live and unescaped in a public S3 `.html` file — **confirmed exploitable on real prod**, live payload still there until someone with S3 access removes it.

Sibling to ENG-1877 (`createHtmlFromTemplate`), but that fix doesn't transfer here — there's no `{{variable}}` boundary to escape values into, since the model authors/edits the whole document freeform.

## Fix

`sanitizeGeneratedHtml` (`backend/src/utils/htmlSanitizer.ts`, via `sanitize-html`) at the shared upload chokepoint in all 4 call sites, stripping only constructs that can execute script or hijack the page:
- `<script>` tags, except a path-scoped Chart.js CDN allowlist this tool's own prompt documents
- any `on*` event-handler attribute, on any tag
- `srcdoc` (browsers HTML-decode any attribute value on parse, then reparse a decoded `srcdoc` as its own document — entity-escaping it is not enough, unlike an ordinary attribute)
- `<base>`, `<meta http-equiv="refresh">`
- `<style>`/`style=` containing `@import` or a non-`data:` `url()`

Everything else (structure, tables, images, inline styling, the `<!DOCTYPE>` sanitize-html otherwise silently drops) passes through unchanged.

`sanitize-html`'s own declared `htmlparser2@^12.0.0` is ESM-only and breaks under this repo's ts-jest/CommonJS setup; overridden to `10.1.0`, already used elsewhere in this tree by `cheerio`.

## Verification

- **Two independent adversarial reviews** (round 1 found the sibling `update_html_file` gap + 4 sanitizer bypasses: `srcdoc`, CSS injection, `<base>`, an overly-broad CDN allowlist — all fixed; round 2 found one more, `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` — fixed) plus everything each round tried that did *not* work.
- **Live-fire tested against a real test-env1 EC2 instance** — real S3 uploads, real fetch-back, across all 4 upload paths (`createHtmlFile` passthrough, render via a real LLM call forced to embed raw markup, deterministic fallback, and `uploadUpdatedFile`) — every attack payload neutralized, every legitimate construct (Chart.js CDN script, benign inline styles, benign meta tags, the doctype) preserved.
- **Full backend suite** run before and after all fixes: identical 3 pre-existing, unrelated failures both times (`slack.events.test.ts`, `slack.aiEvalReaction.test.ts`, `mcp.userIdOverride.test.ts` — zero diff vs `origin/main` on any of those files), zero new failures.
- `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Test plan

title: ENG-1250 §9.6: enforcement cutover wiring (dark, reversible)
body:
## What

Wires the ENG-1250 §9.6 enforcement cutover **dark** behind a reversible flag, and adds the would-pause capture the flip gate needs. **No behaviour changes until the flag is flipped.**

The legacy paid-call gate counts LLM cost only (`AW-Users.tokenUsage.totalCost`). The cutover moves the *spend basis* of that same gate onto the spend ledger's monthly projection (`AW-SpendProjection.settledMicroUsd`), which counts every AgentWeb-paid vendor.

## How — a one-number swap

Both live gates (`checkTokenUsage`, `getEffectiveLlmUsagePolicy`) run the identical `applyLlmUsageCredits → evaluateLlmUsageMode` pipeline. `spendEnforcementBasis.resolveEnforcementCostBasisMicroUsd` changes exactly one input to it — the raw cost — to the ledger's settled all-vendor total, and leaves credits, threshold, and predicate untouched. So credits are still applied **exactly once** and the only divergence from the legacy decision is vendor inclusion (the single intended divergence `spendProjection.ts` documents).

## Flag — dark, reversible, canary-able

`AW_SPEND_LEDGER_ENFORCEMENT`:
- unset / `legacy` / `false` (**default**) → legacy LLM-only basis. Ships inert.
- `allowlist` → only `AW_SPEND_LEDGER_ENFORCEMENT_ACCOUNTS` (a canary).
- `true` → every account.

A missing/unreadable projection **fails open** to the legacy figure — a partial dual-write can never harden enforcement on absent data. Rollback is unsetting the variable; both rails stay dual-written, so no migration either way.

## Blast radius at cutover (2026-09)

`spendWouldPauseSnapshot.ts` captures the would-pause list as durable evidence (JSON + Markdown, flag state + git head) to run immediately before a flip. Current run: **51 subjects, 1 newly paused** — the Starter account `bb07579b…` ($115.74/$150 today → $218.24 once its $102.49 of Apollo vendor spend counts), covered by the signed-off **1(b) grandfather-notify** remedy.

## Tests

Billing-critical, so retained:
- `spendEnforcementBasis.test.ts` — the switch: dark default, reversible, allowlist canary, fail-open on missing/failed read.
- `spendCutoverAdmission.test.ts` — the full admission chain, pinning the 2026-09 Starter case: admitted today, paused once vendor counts, credit-resumed on the same model, fails open with no projection.

Not wired to reserve/settle (§4 `spendAdmission`) yet — this cuts over the pause *decision*; concurrency-safe reservation stays a later increment.

title: fix(agent-mode): "Keep chatting" on a workplan recommendation now tells Emma it was declined (ENG-1974)
body:
## Summary

Filed by `pheonix` (another session) while live-testing unrelated approval-deck work (ENG-1635/1644) — filed separately, assigned to Manan.

**Confirmed via real repro, both historically (pulled the real session `add6415c-245c-4c48-8e6c-f8555579d410` from `Dev-AW-ChatMessages` on env1) and freshly live-recreated on env1 with network-log verification:** Emma recommends a predefined work plan via `recommend_predefined_work_plan`, rendering a card with two buttons — "Use this workplan" (real accept, `POST .../work-plan-recommendations/:id/accept`) and "Keep chatting". The second was, by explicit original design (ENG-1472), a pure client no-op: `setCollapsed(true)` + a focus-event dispatch, zero network calls (confirmed via a captured network log on a fresh env1 session — zero requests fired on click). Because it left no trace anywhere, the LLM had no signal the user declined. The recommendation's tool-call result just sits in `session.messages` as permanent context. Any vaguely on-topic next message (real repro, twice: "lets crearte the campaign" / "lets create the campaign", neither an accept-button click nor one of the suggested reply chips) got Emma to self-initiate `launch_predefined_work_plan` for the declined plan — that tool is independently callable by the model, fully decoupled from the accept endpoint.

**Structural reason this bug existed, not just a UI oversight:** unlike `pendingUserQuestion` / `pendingWorkPlanInput` (each a real session-level field with `status: 'awaiting' | 'answered'`, mutated via a dedicated handler with an optimistic-locked DynamoDB write), the workplan recommendation had **no pending-state field at all** — no `status` on `PersistedWorkPlanRecommendation`, found only by scanning `session.messages`. No existing decline/reject concept anywhere in either repo to copy (confirmed via broad grep) — only the *transport patterns* are reusable. (The ticket's own text cites a `deckAnswer` mechanism as precedent — **this does not exist anywhere in the codebase**, confirmed via exhaustive grep; not a real thing.)

**Key de-risking finding, verified against code:** `recommendationId` is not random — it's a deterministic hash, `agentModeService.ts`:
```ts
const recommendationId = createHash('sha256').update(`${sessionId}:${plan.planId}`).digest('hex').slice(0, 32);
```
This means a decline correlates back to any later `launch_predefined_work_plan` call **exactly** (recompute the same hash once `planTitleOrId` resolves to a concrete `planId`), not via fuzzy title matching — which matters because the repro itself showed the model getting confused between planId and title in its own tool arguments (a title-collision validation error before a successful retry).

## Fix

- New session-level state: `declinedWorkPlanRecommendations` — a **map** keyed by `recommendationId`, not a single slot like `pendingUserQuestion`. A single slot would let declining a *second* plan silently erase protection for the *first*, reopening this exact bug. Direct precedent for this shape already on the same type: `consumedMetaWriteManifestDigests`.
- New dedicated endpoint `POST /api/agent-mode/session/:sessionId/work-plan-recommendations/:recommendationId/decline`, mirroring `accept`'s own shape (a discrete out-of-band state mutation with no chat-turn semantics — not the `questionAnswer`/`workPlanInputAnswer` generate-body-field pattern, since decline carries no message). `accept` always passes `skipDeclineGate: true` — the user's own explicit accept click must never be blocked by an earlier decline of any recommendation.
- **Two enforcement layers:**
  - **A — dynamic prompt context** (primary signal): a new per-turn context message naming the declined plan(s), wired into `buildMarketingContext`, same discipline as the ENG-1899 acceptance notice shipped earlier tonight — state the real fact before the model's own read of the conversation forms.
  - **B — deterministic gate** (backstop): a third `requiresConfirmation: true` guard inside `applyPredefinedWorkPlan`, same shape as its two existing guards (active-plan conflict, ambiguous title). Recomputes the deterministic hash for the *resolved* planId, so it correlates correctly whether `launch_predefined_work_plan` was called with a title or an id. New `confirmedDeclinedPlan: boolean` tool argument, mirroring the existing `force: true` retry flag — same risk tier (reversible, conversational).
- Static system-prompt cross-reference sentence added to the Work Plan Capabilities section.

**Not doing** (flagged, not silently dropped): reload persistence for the collapsed state (a declined card currently re-expands after a page refresh, since `collapsed` is local React state) — the data is already fetched once this ships, low-cost follow-up, out of this PR's literal scope.

## Companion PR

Frontend half (the actual "Keep chatting" click firing the decline call): AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1173

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean after every file change
- [x] New `agentModeController.declineWorkPlanRecommendation.test.ts` (401/404/403/RECOMMENDATION_NOT_FOUND/happy path, explicit assertion `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` is never called)
- [x] New declined-recommendation-gate suite in `agentModeService.applyWorkPlan.test.ts`: blocked when declined, same plan resolved by planId instead of title still blocks identically (proves the hash correlates on the resolved planId, not the tool-call argument form), unblocked with `confirmedDeclinedPlan: true`, unaffected by `skipDeclineGate: true` (accept path), unrelated declined entry never blocks a different plan
- [x] New write-helper suite (`chatbotService.declinedWorkPlanRecommendation.test.ts`) exercising the real `dynamodb.update` spy, not a mocked `chatbotDb`, covering the init-then-retry-once shape
- [x] New context-builder suite (empty when nothing declined, names the plan, plural phrasing for multiple)
- [x] Extended system-prompt and emma-tool-wiring suites for the new sentence and the new `confirmedDeclinedPlan` argument
- [x] Updated the pre-existing accept-endpoint test's exact-call assertion for the now-always-present `skipDeclineGate` option
- [x] Mutation-verified the two highest-risk pieces: the deterministic gate (disabling it fails exactly the two tests that exercise it) and the context builder's plural phrasing
- [x] Full pre-push suite: 312 suites / 5342 tests green
- [x] env1 live test: recreated the exact original repro (recommend -> decline via the new endpoint -> ambiguous continuation "lets create the campaign") and confirmed Emma no longer calls launch_predefined_work_plan, correctly treating it as a new request instead. Also confirmed the accept path is fully unaffected on a fresh session (200, success:true, real workPlan).
- [x] Fresh-eyes independent review: found 1 real bug (decline endpoint discarded the write's boolean result, so a failed write silently returned a false-positive 200) -- verified, fixed, mutation-tested. title: fix(ENG-1875): don't ledger work-plan debt for user-authorized step removals
body:
## Summary
- `modify_work_plan`'s `removeStepCounts` ledgered ENG-1811 anti-gaming debt for a removed step's never-called `requiredFunctionCalls` unconditionally -- with no way to tell a legitimate user-authorized scope cut from a model gate-dodge, since both hit the exact same code path with identical arguments. That debt could make `hasStalledAutocompleteWorkPlan` see "unfinished" and fire auto-continuation, silently re-doing work on scope the user had just explicitly removed.
- Adds an LLM-judge check (`wasStepRemovalUserAuthorized`), sibling to ENG-1819's `userExplicitlyRequestedStop`, run only on the rare path where a removal would create genuinely *new* debt. If the user's most recent real message explicitly authorized the cut, that debt is never written in the first place -- so none of the 3 independently-duplicated downstream debt-check sites (`workPlanHasUnresolvedDebt`, the inlined `workPlanCompletedWithoutDebt`, `AgentModeService.isWorkPlanFullyResolved`) need to change.
- Fails safe toward "not authorized" (debt ledgered exactly as before) on any judge error/timeout/no-message, preserving ENG-1811's anti-gaming guarantee unconditionally.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] New tests in `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` (5 cases): judge "yes" -> debt skipped; judge "no" -> debt ledgered (regression guard); judge throws/times out -> fails safe; no real user message -> fails safe without calling the judge LLM; an authorized removal never clears already-standing debt from an earlier, unauthorized removal in a separate call
- [x] Mutation-tested: forcing `authorized = false` unconditionally made exactly the 2 "yes"-path tests fail, confirming they exercise the fix
- [x] Full 170-suite related jest run green pre-push (3648 tests)
- [ ] env1 live test: recreate the ENG-1875 repro (step 1, then `modify_work_plan removeStepCounts` with an explicit authorizing instruction in the same message) and confirm no silent re-add / no auto-continuation
- [ ] env1 live test: recreate the original ENG-1811 gaming scenario (no authorization) and confirm debt still ledgers and the plan still correctly stalls (must-not-regress case)
- [ ] Fresh-eyes review

Fixes ENG-1875 (https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1875).

## Why
Emma should resolve 'I don't know what to do next' from the public AgentWeb documentation before improvising or dumping a generic handoff. Voice onboarding needs the same behavior when a connection or setup step cannot be completed without user input.

- `search_user_guide` reads the legacy Notion guide.
- It appends five hard-coded Mintlify integration links, but does not search or retrieve the Mintlify corpus.

5. When a safe browser-automation capability is available, Emma uses it for routine navigation and form completion; the user retains login/OAuth consent, 2FA, payment, legal acceptance, and irreversible-action confirmation.
6. Voice onboarding surfaces at most one best-fit guide at a time and continues the spoken interview instead of dumping documentation.

title: ENG-1552: recipient preflight + verified scheduled-report delivery state
body:
## ENG-1552 — recipient preflight + verified scheduled-report delivery state

Scheduled reports could generate successfully and then never reach anyone, because recipient authorization was only discovered at send time, after the expensive run, and nothing was recorded. This wraps the existing ENG-500 authorization decision (global `isAdmin`, applied only to reports that used a cross-account tool) in preflight, persisted state, remediation, dedup and read-back. What counts as "authorized" is unchanged.

**Approved to ship** by Manan, 2026-09-18.

### 🔒 Shadow mode by default: no customer-visible change
Reports are being generated and watched internally first, so **everything below that a customer could notice only takes effect with `SCHEDULED_REPORT_DELIVERY_ENFORCEMENT=true`**. With it unset (the default, including prod), schedules are never refused, runs are never skipped, empty reports and digests are sent exactly as before, test-history has no new field, and the confirm endpoint 404s. Each decision is still computed and logged as `[ENG-1552 shadow] would have …` (grep EB logs), and delivery state is still recorded in `deliveryLog`, so the rules can be watched and tuned before anyone turns them on. Always on, because they're internal only: the oncall alert dedup and `deliveryLog` recording.

### What changes (when enforcement is on)
- **Alert dedup (ENG-1825):** withheld-report oncall alerts carry an Alert Class + Schedule ID, so every occurrence lands on one canonical Linear defect; per-schedule 24h dedupe. No no-login share link to the withheld report is ever put into Linear.
- **Preflight before generation:** a schedule that produces cross-account data (previous run's `lastKnownSensitive` breadcrumb, or it *requires* a cross-account tool, so the first run is gated too) with no currently-authorized recipient is skipped before any session or model call. Records `withheld/no_authorized_recipients` and returns a `remediation` object. Silent schedules (no recipients) are unaffected.
- **Empty reports (xCures/ENG-1504):** a run with no content is no longer emailed; it's recorded `withheld/empty_content`.
- **Activation gates:** create, toggle-to-active, and update (active schedule, when recipients or required tools change) return 400 + remediation instead of letting such a schedule go live. The MCP `manage_scheduled_chat` actions call the same handlers. No bare "≥1 recipient" gate was added: create already falls back to the requester and ENG-1836 already refuses clearing the last address, and ENG-1723 outreach schedules are recipient-less by design.
- **Truthful delivery:** `sendEmail` still never throws, but now resolves to `'sent' | 'suppressed' | 'failed'`. `delivered` is recorded only for a send the provider accepted; otherwise `delivery_attempted` with `provider_error` / `suppressed_nonprod`.
- **Digest parity:** `sendDailyDigestEmail` had no recipient check at all; it now uses the same guard (a digest is sensitive if any run in it is).
- **Read-back:** `GET …/test-history` carries each run's latest `delivery` state as an additive field (array shape unchanged). New owner-only `POST …/delivery-log/:runId/confirm` records ENG-1821's "recipient confirmed receipt" step, and only for a delivered run and only for recipients it actually went to.
- **No new customer email.** Reports are in an internal review period, so the preflight, digest and empty-report paths record state and alert oncall only. The one pre-existing owner notice (single report withheld after generation) is kept. The planned automatic test run after a recipient edit was dropped for the same reason (it's a full run that really publishes/sends).

### Data
New additive attributes on `AW-TaskSchedules`: `deliveryLog` (capped at 100 entries), `lastKnownSensitive`, `lastKnownSensitiveAt`. No migration, no backfill. Writes go through `scheduleDb.appendDeliveryLogEntry`, which is conditioned on `attribute_exists(scheduleId)` so a schedule deleted mid-run is never recreated.

### Verification
- `npm run typecheck` clean; the 111 suites the pre-push hook selects all pass.
- **Real DynamoDB (dev table, throwaway row, deleted afterwards):** append creates the log; breadcrumb in the same write; `updatedAt` untouched; read-back returns `delivered`; cap trims oldest at 100; a missing schedule is not recreated.
- **Live on an autofix preview of the final head, both modes** (dev DB; mail allowlist set to only Resend's test inbox `delivered@resend.dev`, verified in the backend's environment; every other address suppressed):
  - **Shadow (flag unset) — 15/15:**
    - cross-account create → 201; adding a cross-account tool → 200; re-enabling a sensitive schedule → 200 (each only logs `[ENG-1552 shadow] would have …`)
    - the sensitive run still generates, and a real send records `generated → delivered`; the breadcrumb is re-derived
    - test-history has no `delivery` field; confirm → 404; the schedule list carries none of the internal fields
    - a whole-form portal save that changes nothing keeps the flag; a manual resend records nothing
    - a cross-account digest still goes to the configured non-admin (only logged)
  - **Enforced (flag on) — 18/18:**
    - create / update / toggle → 400 + remediation; a rename is never refused; a whole-form save that changes nothing is not refused
    - the sensitive run is skipped before generation and records `withheld`, read back through test-history
    - a stuck schedule recovers after a prompt edit
    - an ordinary send records `delivered`; confirm → `recipient_confirmed` for the delivered address only; confirming a withheld run → 409
    - a manual resend records nothing; the digest goes only to the admin owner
  - **Previously unit-only cases, now live — shadow 9/9, enforced 10/10:**
    - the create-from-template gate
    - a first run gated only because the schedule *requires* a cross-account tool (no breadcrumb yet)
    - a recipients-only edit
    - a delegated admin's edit, gated exactly like the owner's
    - a delegated create with no email, which falls back to the admin's address (allowed)
    - a delegated confirm, which records the admin as the confirmer
    - the exemptions: a silent pre-filled schedule, and re-enabling a no-recipient schedule
    - a single report withheld *after* generation: not sent, the existing owner notice kept, `withheld` recorded
  - All test schedules and templates deleted; delegate tokens revoked; preview torn down.
  - Still unit-only by nature: the empty-report path (a model can't reliably be made to return nothing) and the oncall Linear dedup (oncall is a no-op outside production).
- Covered by unit tests only: an empty report (a model can't be made to return nothing reliably) and the oncall Linear dedup (oncall is a no-op outside production).
- `emailService.strict.test.ts`: the swallow-failures test now asserts `'failed'` instead of `undefined`. The invariant (never throws) is unchanged.

### Independent review
**Round one:** a fresh-eyes reviewer went over the diff, and each finding was verified before acting on it:
- **Fixed:**
  - the schedule list (and Emma's `list_scheduled_chats`) leaked the internal fields; they are now stripped;
  - the digest placeholder was visible with the flag off; it is now enforcement-only;
  - a flagged schedule could never recover; an edit to its tools or prompt now clears the flag;
  - the delivery log is now one write per send and capped at 30;
  - the resend path now records the right run ID; the skip path reuses the lease run ID.
- **Round two** (a second fresh reviewer, which re-verified every round-one fix as correct):
  - **Fixed:**
    - the portal submits the whole form, so "field sent" was being treated as "changed" (a rename cleared the flag and re-ran the gate); the gate and the reset now compare the actual lists;
    - create-from-template skipped the activation gate; it now goes through it;
    - a manual resend could overwrite a run's real delivery state; manual resends now record nothing;
    - a non-string response can no longer throw outside the function's try/catch.
  - **Accepted:** the log counts toward the row budget (bounded by the cap of 30); shadow-mode digest classification reads (no digests were sent in 14 days); 30 entries cover about 15h of an hourly schedule.
  - The branch is merged with current `main`; the pre-push hook ran typecheck plus 279 suites, all green.
- **Round three** (focused on the round-two fixes and the main merge): no blockers. The merge applies main's changes byte-for-byte and touches none of this branch's functions.
  - **Fixed:** the recipient comparison normalized only the incoming list, so an older row stored as a string or a JSON-array string counted as "changed" on a no-op save. Both sides are now normalized, with a test that fails against the old comparison.
  - **Left as-is:** two nits about pre-existing input-type laxity.
- **Rejected as false positive or not a defect:** the digest UTC-vs-local run ID (servers run in UTC, and a digest spans runs by design); the oncall alert routing (internal and intended); the always-empty allowed-recipients list (correct by construction).

### Approvals
- **Data-plane rule** (new additive `AW-TaskSchedules` attributes `deliveryLog`, `lastKnownSensitive`, `lastKnownSensitiveAt`; no migration, no backfill): covered by Harsha's standing approval for such changes, as confirmed by Manan on 2026-09-18.
- **Customer-facing copy:** none is live. The remediation sentence only appears once enforcement is turned on.

### Turning it on later
Set `SCHEDULED_REPORT_DELIVERY_ENFORCEMENT=true` on the backend environment after the shadow logs look right. Unset it to go back to shadow.

### Rollback
Revert the PR. The new attributes are additive and ignored by older code.
