title: fix(smoke): trustworthy post-deploy lead capture + synthetic-lead suppression (ENG-449)
body:
Post-deploy smoke test filled only `input[type=email]` and polled the CRM by email. Modern landers are React-controlled multi-field forms whose validation blocks submit until every required field passes, so the test false-negatived on working pages.

Verified live 2026-09-18: `campaign.waterheater.app` root (name/phone/zip + 4 selects + symptom checkbox, POSTs `/api/hero-estimate`, redirects to `chat.waterheater.app/text?handoff_id=...`) and `/voice-ai-agent-free-estimate-w` (POSTs `/api/capture`, shows inline success) — both submit fine for real visitors, both smoke-tested FAIL.

## What changed

**Filling the form**
- Discovery scores the page's forms and drives the most lead-like one, stamping it with a marker attribute so the fields that get filled and the submit button that gets clicked belong to the same form. A form containing `input[type=password]` is never chosen; a lone email input is treated as a subscribe box, not a lead form.
- Values are chosen from each field's *hint* (name/id/placeholder/autocomplete/label), never its selector — every `[name="..."]` selector contains the substring `name`, which previously sent `[name="zip"]` down the person-name branch.
- Covers `textarea` and `number`/`url`/`date`/`search` inputs, required checkboxes, and one radio per required group.
- Skips what a real visitor cannot fill: hidden/disabled/readonly/`aria-hidden` controls, off-canvas and named honeypots. A control carrying `required` is never skipped on its name — a working honeypot cannot be required.
- Reads `form.elements`, so a `form=`-associated required control and a sticky-footer submit button outside the form are both seen.
- Selectors address ids via `[id="..."]`; `#:r0:` (React `useId`, used by shadcn form primitives) is rejected outright by Playwright's CSS parser.
- Synthetic phone is `415-555-0100..0199`, the NANP's reserved fictional range inside a real area code. A bare `555` area code is unassignable and real validators reject it.
- Explicit per-interaction timeouts; Playwright's default is 30s, so one unreachable control used to burn 30s of the run, silently, per field.

**Deciding whether a lead was captured**
- Chat-handoff landers redirect instead of writing a CRM row, so `pollForLead` always missed them. A redirect now counts as a capture only when **all** of: the navigation is cross-origin; `handoff_id` is present as a real query parameter (read via `searchParams`, not matched as raw text); that id was not already in the deployed URL; and the submit produced a **final 2xx** same-origin non-GET response whose body carried this run's synthetic data.
- That last condition is the load-bearing one. The redirect is written by the page's own JS, so on its own it proves nothing — a lander whose `fetch(...).catch(() => {})` swallows a 500 redirects identically, and URL evidence alone would mark a silently-broken capture endpoint as passing forever.
- Attribution matches encoding-stable fingerprints against both the raw and percent-decoded body, because a native form POST escapes the synthetic email's `+` and `@` as `%2B`/`%40`.
- The CRM poll is unconditional: it is the cleanup path as much as the verification path, and skipping it strands a synthetic lead in the customer's list.
- `smokeTestResult.handoffId` persists the id so a handoff can be checked against the chat backend by hand.

**Reporting**
- Failure reasons carry submit diagnostics (fields filled, submit path, navigation, whether capture evidence was seen) instead of one identical string for every cause.
- The pixel reason names the `fbq('track','Lead')` call rather than a `facebook.com/tr` request, which the implementation stopped watching.

## Tests

- `landingPageSmokeTest.test.ts` — 33 cases covering the capture-evidence boundaries (redirect hop, GET, unattributed same-origin POST, urlencoded escaping), submit fallbacks, and diagnostics.
- `landingPageSmokeTest.discovery.test.ts` (new) — 17 cases running the real page-side discovery against a real DOM. jsdom's ESM chain cannot load under this jest config (`cssExtractor.test.ts` mocks it out for the same reason), so it runs in a child process that extracts the declaration via the TypeScript compiler API — which also enforces the self-containment `page.evaluate` requires.
- Written from mutation testing: 12 single-point mutations that earlier revisions of this suite did not catch now each fail it.

**597 tests pass across the 9 suites that exercise this change**, with every behaviour below pinned by a mutation pass. `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` is clean in every changed file (14 errors remain repo-wide, all pre-existing: 12 axios-typing in `metaService.ts`/`sandbox/metaInterceptor.ts`, 2 `sanitize-html` in `htmlSanitizer.ts`).

## Synthetic leads no longer leak into customer CRMs

The smoke test submits a **real** lead through a customer's **real** form. Deleting the row afterwards does not unsend an email or un-fire a conversion, so anything that escapes recognition has already done its damage.

- **Recognition by either marker.** A lander with no email field cannot carry our address — it substitutes its own placeholder (observed live: `noemail+<timestamp>@waterheater.app`). `isSmokeTestEmail` never matched that, so HubSpot/Attio sync, drip enrolment, auto-send email, owner notification and a Meta CAPI conversion all fired on a synthetic lead. `isSmokeTestLead` now also recognises the synthetic **phone** (415-555-0100..0199, the NANP's reserved fictional range, which no real visitor can hold). Applied at all three suppression sites: the `webhooks.ts` CAPI guard, the `webhooks.ts` side-effect cascade, and `metaConversionRelay`.
- **Cleanup that reaches the row.** When no email was filled, cleanup polls the list by that phone instead, matched on digits **and** a `createdAt` at or after this run's submit.
- **A start-of-run sweep.** The per-run poll has only ~8s to find the row it created; when the capture write lands later, the row was never deleted. That is how 45 synthetic leads accumulated across nine lists in August, four of them in a paying customer's CRM. Each run now clears what the previous one stranded, so the failure is self-correcting rather than cumulative. Bounded to 3 pages / 20 deletes, and any list failure is swallowed rather than changing the verdict.

## Controls the old discovery could not see

- **ARIA widgets.** shadcn/Radix renders a checkbox as `<button role="checkbox" aria-checked>` with an `aria-hidden` proxy input, so keying on `input[type=checkbox]` made the control invisible — never filled, never even counted as unreachable. Now discovered by role, reading `aria-required` / `aria-checked`.
- **`skippedRequired` is exact**, derived from what discovery actually emitted rather than re-deriving `usable()`. It now counts required controls of types outside the fillable set (`datetime-local`, `color`, `file`) and ones with no addressable id, name or index — the cases that made it report `0` on precisely the pages the diagnostic was added for.
- **Value constraints**: `step` is honoured, and `min` is applied after `max` so contradictory bounds land on `min`.

### The phone marker had to accept the shape landers actually post

`+1 415-555-0142` normalises to 11 digits while the pattern demanded exactly 10, so it did not match. A lander using a libphonenumber-style phone component emits E.164 and nothing in the platform normalises what it posts — **13,072 real leads carry a phone and 91% of them normalise to 11 digits**, so this was the dominant shape, not an edge case. That single gap defeated suppression, the per-run cleanup and the stranded-lead sweep simultaneously. Normalisation now lives in one exported `phoneDigits`. Widening is safe: country code 1 IS the NANP, so `1` + `4155550142` can only be the reserved fictional number.

### ARIA widgets, and the ways they misbehaved

`HTMLButtonElement.type` resolves to `"submit"` when the attribute is absent, so a typeless `<button role="checkbox">` satisfied both the checkable match and the submit-control find — `submitSelector` resolved to the checkbox rather than the real submit button, and `check()` would click it mid-fill. A `role="switch"` could also occupy the single-checkable fallback slot, toggling "SMS updates" while leaving the consent box the lander gates submit on. Both fixed; `<div role=checkbox>` is discovered via a subtree scan since `form.elements` lists only form-associated elements.

### The sweep is auditable

It deletes rows from a paying customer's CRM and previously logged nothing — `console.*` appeared zero times in the file and the catch was empty. Every deletion and every failure is now logged, and rows younger than two minutes are left alone so a run on another backend instance cannot have its in-flight row deleted out from under its poll.

## Merge gate

`smokeTestResult.handoffId` is a new optional field persisted on `AW-LandingPages`, tracked as ENG-2044. It reuses the existing update expression on the same row — no new table, key, index, migration or backfill.

## Verified against the live pages (observe-only)

Run with real Chrome against both landers the PR cites, with every non-GET request aborted at the browser so no lead, chat handoff or conversion event was created.

**`/voice-ai-agent-free-estimate-w` — works end to end.** The right form is marked, 5/5 fields are filled with correct hint-derived values (`firstName`→`Smoke`, `lastName`→`Test`, `zip`→`94025`, phone in the reserved range), and the submit produces:

```
POST https://campaign.waterheater.app/api/capture
body: {"firstName":"Smoke","lastName":"Test","email":"smoke-test+...@agentweb.pro","phone":"4155550180","zip":...}
attribution would match: true
```

**Root `campaign.waterheater.app/` — now works too.** It did not, through several revisions of this PR: the required symptom group is a set of shadcn/Radix checkboxes whose inputs are permanently 0x0 with the label as their only clickable surface, sitting behind a collapsed disclosure. Discovery now opens a disclosure whose `aria-controls` panel actually holds checkables, reaches the control through its visible label, and clicks rather than `check()`s it:

```
POST https://campaign.waterheater.app/api/hero-estimate
body: {"full_name":"Smoke Test","phone":"4155550163","zip":"94025","symptoms":["water_leaking"],"heater_type":"tank_gas",...}
attribution would match: true
```

The disclosure rule is deliberately narrow. `aria-expanded` also marks Radix **Select** triggers, and clicking one opens a listbox overlay that swallows every later click including the submit — which turned the working voice page into a total failure until the rule was restricted to panels containing a checkbox or radio.

**Form selection, checked across the fleet.** The real discovery was run against 42 live landers from `AW-LandingPages` (load, discover, report — no filling, no submitting). 26 carry one form, 11 carry none, 5 carry more than one. Of those 5, four are hero/footer pairs or exact duplicates where either choice is equivalent. The fifth was wrong, and is fixed in this PR:

```
lp-5star-co-hosts-free-str-perfor-9.vercel.app
  form[0] controls=6 usable=0 box=0x0     <- was chosen
  form[1] controls=6 usable=6 box=512x405
  form[2] controls=6 usable=6 box=448x405
```

Responsive v0 landers ship the same form two or three times and collapse the inactive variants to a 0x0 box. Scoring every control made the duplicates tie on every term, so the collapsed one won on DOM order and discovery returned zero fields — nothing filled, guaranteed FAIL on every deploy. Scoring now counts only controls that pass the same usability test the fill loop applies.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The `navigatedAway` conjunct is redundant given the cross-origin check, and can discard a real handoff PASS when the chat app's `load` takes longer than 8s.
- Synthetic values ignore `min`/`max`/`step`/`pattern`/`maxlength`, so a constrained `date`/`number` field can still block submit.
- The `opacity === "0"` visibility check is stricter than Playwright's own and samples once, so a control mid-fade is dropped rather than waited for.





<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

The smoke test now supports modern multi-field forms and chat-handoff redirects. It fills usable controls, handles disclosures, scopes submission, validates exact cross-origin `handoff_id` values, records capture evidence, polls CRM, and cleans up synthetic leads. Smoke-test detection covers email and reserved phone markers. `handoffId` persistence remains pending data-plane approval.

title: feat(backend): report the running build version on /health
body:
## Why

`/health` returns `{"status":"healthy"}` and nothing else, so there is no way to tell from outside **which build** an instance is serving.

"The deploy workflow succeeded" and "this instance is running that code" are different claims, and during an incident telling them apart is usually the whole question. Today the only way to answer the second is to read the EB console and trust that nothing has cycled since.

## What

- The deploy workflow writes `dist/build-info.json` immediately before packaging — **inside** `dist`, so the file travels within the artifact and describes the code beside it. Anywhere else would be a claim *about* a build rather than a property *of* one. It records the version label, the commit and the build time.
- `/health` now returns `{"status":"healthy","version":"backend-20260919-pr2990"}`.

## The one judgement worth reviewing

**`/health` reports the version label only — deliberately not the commit SHA.**

The endpoint is unauthenticated, so anything in it is world-readable, and a full SHA names precisely which code is running to anyone matching against known issues. The label carries a date and a PR number: enough to answer *"is my change live?"*, and materially less useful to someone who is not us. The SHA stays in `build-info.json` on the instance, readable by anyone who can already read the disk.

If the team would rather have the SHA on the endpoint, it is a one-line change in `healthPayload()`.

## Details

- Read **once at module load**, not per request. Monitoring hits this endpoint constantly and a per-request file read would add disk I/O to a health check for no reason.
- A missing file yields `null` rather than throwing — the normal case locally, in tests, and on every build that predates this change. Pinned by a test.
- `Object.keys(healthPayload())` is asserted to be exactly `["status","version"]`, so the commit cannot leak back in by accident later.

## Testing

`backend/src/__tests__/buildInfo.test.ts` — 3 tests, passing. The three changed/added TypeScript files produce no `tsc` errors.

One caveat stated plainly: a full backend typecheck was run in a git worktree with `node_modules` borrowed from another checkout, which reports pre-existing failures for `robots-parser` and `sanitize-html` — dependencies added to `main` after the borrowed modules were installed. The same check is clean in a normal clone. CI installs dependencies for the actual commit and is the real verification here.

## Context

Found while building an autonomous bug-fixing agent that watches its own deploys: it can currently prove the Deploy workflow succeeded for a merge commit, but not that the fix is live. This closes that gap, and is worth having regardless of that agent.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

The deploy workflow stores version label, commit SHA, and UTC build time in `dist/build-info.json`. `/health` returns the version label with healthy status. The backend reads build information once at module load and returns `null` fields when unavailable. The commit SHA remains private.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(slack): Emma answers 1:1 DMs without @mention
body:
## Problem
DM-ing Emma in Slack went nowhere. The events route only handled `app_mention` (channels/threads) plus replies in already-tracked threads. Slack never emits `app_mention` for DM text, so a 1:1 DM fell through every branch and was silently ignored.

## Change
New `message`-event branch in `backend/src/routes/slack.ts` for `channel_type === 'im'` (with D-channel fallback):
- Strips the bot mention, normalizes Slack formatting (same as mention path)
- Resolves sender via verified Slack email exact-match only — never fuzzy, so a DM sender can never resolve to someone else's account; tombstoned (`deleted_*`) users skipped; mapping cached per DM channel (1:1 channel = one human side)
- Creates a `slack-dm` agent session and reuses `handleSlackSessionResponse` (title, thread mapping, thinking msg, response, postback)
- Unknown identities get a helpful error message, not a silent drop
- Threaded DM replies keep riding the existing thread-mapping handler
- README: bot events now list `app_mention` + `message.im` (Slack app config change needed on deploy)

## Verification
- `slack.events.test.ts`: 27/27 green, incl. 2 new cases (DM creates `slack-dm` session via cached mapping; unknown DM identity rejected with error post, no session)
- `slack.autoTriggerRemoved.test.ts`: 3/3 green (ENG-1613 untagged top-level/thread behavior unchanged — DMs are 1:1 conversations, not channel auto-listen)
- Full-project `tsc --noEmit` OOMs on this box (2GB heap); scoped check: the edited route file's tests compile and pass under jest/babel, and the patch only uses already-imported helpers

## Deploy note
Subscribe the Slack app to `message.im` bot events, then deploy backend (path-filtered prod deploy on merge). Post-deploy smoke: DM Emma from an account with a matching AgentWeb email, confirm a reply; DM from an unknown email, confirm the helpful error.

Risk: High

Adds Slack 1:1 DM support without `@mentions`. It also adds an Enigma card-revenue integration with caching, billing, validation, typed errors, and startup initialization. The broad change surface spans Slack routing, server startup, enrichment, metering, secrets, and deployment configuration, which increases rollback complexity.

title: [ENG-1390] Harden skill mutation writes with conditional DynamoDB guards
body:
Linear source: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1390/harden-skill-mutation-writes-against-concurrent-visibilityownership

## Problem
`SkillService` does read-then-unconditional-write across skill mutations, so a concurrent change between the read and the write can be silently clobbered. `withdrawFromReview()` was already hardened (ENG-932) with an `expectedUpdatedAt` optimistic-concurrency guard; `deleteSkill`, `submitForReview`, `approveSkill`, `rejectSkill` were not.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `skillService.deleteSkill()` (or a new variant) accepts an optional condition (e.g. expected `ownerId` and/or `visibility`) and uses a DynamoDB `ConditionExpression` on delete; a failed condition surfaces as a distinct, catchable error (not a generic 500).
- [ ] `DELETE /:skillId` passes the values read at authorization time as the delete condition, and maps a conditional failure to 409, mirroring the withdraw-review route pattern.
- [ ] `submitForReview`, `approveSkill`, `rejectSkill` each pass `expectedUpdatedAt` into their `updateSkill()` call, and each maps `ConditionalCheckFailedException` to a distinct error the calling route turns into 409.
- [ ] A test per method proves: normal-path unaffected, and a simulated concurrent change (mocked `ConditionalCheckFailedException`) surfaces as a 409, not a silent overwrite.

title: [ENG-741] Voice lab: Start talking deletes saved interview snapshot before session confirmed
body:
Linear source: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-741/voice-lab-start-talking-deletes-the-saved-interview-snapshot-before

## Problem
The voice-lab "Start talking" control deletes the persisted interview snapshot BEFORE awaiting the session start. A mis-click destroys a saved in-progress interview — with no confirmation prompt, and no fallback if the session then fails to start. The user loses answered discovery questions and cannot get them back.

title: ENG-1250 §3b: production projection writer + backfill (unblocks §9.6)
body:
## What

Ships the **missing production writer** for `AW-SpendProjection` (ENG-1250 §3b) — the gap that made the merged §9.6 enforcement switch a no-op. `AW-SpendEvents` was filling (~11.6k rows) while `AW-SpendProjection` stayed empty because `putProjection` had no non-test caller, so `spendEnforcementBasis` read an empty table and always fell through to legacy. Verified 2026-09-21 against `origin/main` and prod (`Count=0`).

Still **observe-only**: this populates the projection; nothing new enforces until `AW_SPEND_LEDGER_ENFORCEMENT` is flipped.

## How

**1. Event-driven writer** (`spendProjectionDb.applySettledSpendEvents`)
- Atomic `ADD settledMicroUsd` (+ `settledEventCount`, `SET computedAt`) per settled event. An ADD creates the row on first touch and **never clobbers** `reservedMicroUsd`/`availableMicroUsd`/allowance — safe alongside §4 admission, and not the whole-item `putProjection` that would race reservations.
- Hooked at the single `usageRecordDb` transaction seam both rails funnel through (`incrementUsageWithChargeEvent` + `incrementUsageWithSpendEvent`), fired only on `"applied"` so a deduped replay never double-adds, and **never throws** — observe-only maintenance can't break the charging transaction.
- Boundary: the hot path owns **only** settled spend; allowance/`availableMicroUsd` seeding is the backfill's, reservations are §4's.

**2. Backfill** (`scripts/spendProjectionBackfill.ts`) — seeds the full current month from the ledger for subjects whose events predate the writer. Sources from `AW-SpendEvents`, idempotent, **dry-run by default** (`--write` to persist), asserts each row reconciles ≤1µ$.

**3. Observability + freshness** (`spendEnforcementBasis`) — logs the previously-silent `projectionMissing` branch (so a canary can prove readback), and adds a `computedAt` staleness guard (`AW_SPEND_PROJECTION_MAX_STALENESS_MIN`, off by default) that fails **open** to legacy on a stale snapshot.

## Verification

- Typecheck: clean for all touched files (only pre-existing unrelated errors remain).
- Tests: `spendProjectionWriter.test.ts` (no-clobber, grouping, kill switch, never-throws) + staleness cases in `spendEnforcementBasis.test.ts`; **41 spend-suite tests pass**, and **176 existing usage/recorder/dual-write tests still pass** (hook is non-breaking).
- **Prod dry-run** of the backfill (read-only, 2026-09): 40 subjects, **worst reconciliation drift 0µ**, all within tolerance.

## Not in this PR
The prod backfill run itself (data-plane write) and the flag flip — both deliberate, deferred to after merge+deploy.

title: [needs human] Force autocomplete on work plans for scheduled sessions (ENG-2058)
body:
**What was wrong:** The failing scheduled session (Luma Event Lead Engagement — Daily) called `create_work_plan` without specifying `autocomplete`, which defaults to `false` (interactive: 'present results after each step and wait for user approval'). On a scheduled/unattended run there is no human to approve, so the model's final turn kept presenting results and implicitly waiting for approval. The completion-gate classifier (`classifyScheduledContinuationAsync`) detected this as a 'confirmation' halt, exhausted its retry/continuation budget (20 attempts), and the run was recorded as `deferredUnresolved` -> a validation failure, recurring daily and firing the oncall alert each time even though 'Missing function calls' and 'Keyword misses' were both 'none'.

**Fix:** In `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`, both `createWorkPlan` and `modifyWorkPlan` now force `workPlan.autocomplete = true` whenever the session's `sessionType === 'scheduled'`, overriding whatever value (or absence of one) the model passed. This guarantees a scheduled run's work plan is always hands-off, matching the [AUTOMATED UNATTENDED EXECUTION] directive already given to the model elsewhere, but enforced in code rather than relying on the model to remember to pass `autocomplete: true`.

**Verification:** Added tests in `agentModeService.workPlan.test.ts` reproducing the bug (autocomplete omitted or explicitly `false` on a scheduled session) — confirmed they failed before the fix and pass after. Confirmed a non-scheduled session's explicit/omitted autocomplete value is unaffected (zero regression).

title: fix(smoke): a combined name field is no longer filled with just a surname (ENG-449)
body:
Found by the **first production run** of the post-deploy smoke test after #2982 shipped.

## The bug

`"fullname"` contains the substring `"lname"` (`ful|lname`), so the surname branch claimed it before the generic name branch could — and a combined name field was filled with `"Test"` instead of `"Smoke Test"`. The real POST body from a freshly generated lander:

```json
{"fullName":"Test","phone":"4155550144","zip":"94025"}
```

No fixture had a `fullName` field, which is why the unit tests never caught it. It took a real generator producing one.

## The fix

Two independent guards, because either alone suffices and both are cheap:

- a combined-name branch checked **first** (`full name` / `your name` / `contact name`)
- the short aliases `lname` and `fname` now require a word boundary, so they match only as their own token rather than anywhere inside a longer hint

Verified across the hint set:

```
fullname / full_name / your name  -> "Smoke Test"
lastname / family-name / surname  -> "Test"
lname                             -> "Test"     (still works as its own word)
firstname / given-name / fname    -> "Smoke"
```

Mutation-checked: reverting either guard alone still passes (the other covers it); reverting **both** reproduces the original bug and fails the suite.

## About the run that found this

The smoke test's own verdict was **correct**. The generated lander collects name/phone/zip and no email, and the capture endpoint requires one (`webhooks.ts:533` → `400 "Email is required"`), so no lead row can ever be created for that page. `ok=false` was a true negative.

That v0 can generate a lead-capture form the platform cannot accept is a **separate product issue** and is not addressed here.

## Verification

109 tests pass across the three smoke-test suites; `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean in changed files (14 pre-existing errors elsewhere, unchanged).

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved synthetic data generation for name-related fields.
  - Combined-name fields now receive “Smoke Test,” while standalone surname and given-name fields receive “Test” and “Smoke,” respectively.

title: fix(agent-mode): scope false-completion-claim guard to sessions that use its tools (ENG-2076)
body:
## Summary
- Fixes [ENG-2076](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2076/meta-ads-false-0-of-n-produced-completion-claim-correction-derails): the ENG-1331 false-completion-claim guard has no vocabulary for Meta Ads tools (`call_meta_marketing_api`), so it always reads `actual: 0` for a Meta Ads session and falsely corrects true claims — a live session truthfully recapped "3 creatives created" and got told "0 of 3 were actually produced", derailing the user right before the publish-confirmation step that would have made the ads go live.
- Gates the guard on `assetProducingToolsInPlay(toolCalls, currentSession?.calledFunctions)` — true only when an asset-producing tool (`generate_image`, `generate_video`, `create_html_file`, etc.) was actually used either this turn or earlier in the session — so it stays confined to the domain it can reason about instead of firing on every non-media tool conversation.
- Root cause writeup and full session trace (`65abb8aa-3732-4be0-9281-edf28de3027c`) are in ENG-2076.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (backend) — clean, aside from a pre-existing unrelated failure in `landingPageSmokeTest.discovery.test.ts` already on `main`
- [x] `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/services/agentMode/core/__tests__/synthesisResidue.test.ts src/__tests__/agentMode/synthesisResidueGuard.test.ts src/__tests__/agentMode/synthesisResidueKillSwitch.test.ts src/__tests__/agentMode/synthesisResidueLedger.test.ts` — 118/118 passing, including the original ENG-1188/ENG-1331 same-turn shortfall case

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low. The false-completion guard now runs only when supported asset-producing tools were used in the current turn or session. This prevents false corrections in Meta Ads sessions. The change adds a safe history check and preserves same-turn detection. Type checking and four targeted Jest suites passed with 118 tests.

title: fix(agent-mode): close ENG-2076 residual gap + second unprotected call site
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #3012 (already merged/auto-deployed). Post-merge verification found #3012's fix was incomplete in two ways:

1. **Reintroduced a narrower version of the same bug.** #3012 gated the guard on "did this turn OR the session's persisted `calledFunctions` ever use an asset-producing tool." `detectFalseCompletionClaim`'s `actual` count is computed from the CURRENT turn's `toolCalls` only, never from history — so a session that generates real images earlier and later truthfully recaps that count on an unrelated turn (no new tool calls) still got a false "0 of N produced" correction, just narrower than before (any session that ever touched an asset-producing tool, not every session). Simplified the gate to check only the current turn's own ledger.
2. **`sessionSummaryService.ts` was never fixed.** It runs the identical `detectFalseCompletionClaim` check against the whole-session tool-call ledger, with no domain gate at all — a Meta Ads (or any non-media) session whose LLM-written summary happens to phrase a true result with a digit near an asset noun would have its accurate summary silently **replaced** by a false "0 of N... not yet complete" line that persists to `session.sessionSummary` and is served verbatim by the `account_summary` Emma tool. Same fix applied there, scoped to the whole-session ledger (consistent with what `actual` is computed from at that call site).

Also adds regression coverage at both call sites, including an end-to-end scenario through the real `generateMarketingResponse` loop reproducing session `65abb8aa-3732-4be0-9281-edf28de3027c`'s exact turn shape.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` (backend) — clean, aside from the pre-existing unrelated failure in `landingPageSmokeTest.discovery.test.ts` already on `main`
- [x] `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/services/agentMode/core/__tests__/synthesisResidue.test.ts src/__tests__/agentMode/synthesisResidueGuard.test.ts src/__tests__/agentMode/synthesisResidueKillSwitch.test.ts src/__tests__/agentMode/synthesisResidueLedger.test.ts src/__tests__/sessionSummary.test.ts` — 138/138 passing

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium

Limits false-completion guards to current-turn asset-producing tool calls. Preserves truthful recaps and non-media summaries, including Meta Ads results, in responses and `session.sessionSummary`. Adds regression coverage. Targeted tests pass: 138/138. Backend typecheck still has a pre-existing unrelated failure. No production-outage path is indicated.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: [needs human] Stop logging raw Slack event body and headers (ENG-2054)
body:
ENG-2054 reported that /api/slack/events accepted unsigned requests. Investigation showed that vulnerability was already fixed on main (commit 2d2952153, 2026-09-16) via verifySlackRequest()'s HMAC-SHA256 check over the raw body with replay protection, and is covered by existing tests. What remained was the ticket's secondary finding: two console.log calls right after signature verification logged the full JSON body and all request headers at info level on every event, leaking third-party tokens and customer message content into the application log. Removed both log lines — the existing 'Event callback received, event type' log a few lines below already covers routine debugging. Added a regression test that sends an event with a secret header and sensitive body text and asserts neither ever appears in console.log output; verified it fails before the fix and passes after.

---
**Automated gates**
Code review: ✅ sound — 2 finding(s) fixed
Deterministic checks: ❌ FAILED — npx tsc --noEmit (backend); npx jest src/__tests__/slack.events.test.ts (backend)
Browser verify: ⚠️ environment down (not verified)

Fixes ENG-2054 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2054/slack-events-endpoint-accepts-unsigned-requests-forged-events-can

**Files changed in `main`:**
```
backend/src/__tests__/slack.events.test.ts | 27 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 backend/src/routes/slack.ts                |  4 +---
 2 files changed, 28 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)
```

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low

The `/api/slack/events` route no longer logs full request bodies or headers. App-mention diagnostics log only the event timestamp. This prevents tokens and customer message content from entering application logs. HMAC-SHA256 signature verification and replay protection remain unchanged.

title: fix(landers): ENG-2078/2079/2080/2081/2082/2083/2087 — the landing-page generation pipeline
body:
Four defects in the landing-page generation pipeline, all found while live-verifying the post-deploy smoke test. Each one surfaced the next.

| | Issue | |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | [ENG-2078](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2078) | smoke test races the capture-route sync build |
| 2 | [ENG-2079](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2079) | an unanswered v0 correction fails the whole page |
| 3 | [ENG-2080](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2080) | corrections fire on pages with no capture form, burning ~17 min |
| 4 | [ENG-2081](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2081) | smoke diagnosis computed but never persisted |
| 5 | [ENG-2082](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2082) | a phone-only lander can never capture a lead |
| 6 | [ENG-2083](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2083) | undeployable page returns 500 instead of 409 |
| 7 | [ENG-2087](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2087) | unparseable generated code bricks the whole site's builds |

---

## 1. ENG-2078 — smoke test races the capture-route sync build

Adding a sub-page pushes a **second** commit regenerating `app/api/capture/route.ts` — the new page's path only enters the deployed `LIST_BY_PATH` there (ENG-483). That build was fire-and-forget with its promise dropped, while the smoke test was dispatched immediately after the deployed write. The submit hits a route with no entry for `/slug`, gets `422 "This page has no lead list configured…"`, no lead, `ok: false`.

Deterministic — every sub-page add. Root pages unaffected.

```
14:52:24  generate returns     api=404   dpl_DWLBfz
14:52:59  ...                  api=404   dpl_CNUT5i   <- rollout mid-flight
14:53:39  ...                  api=422   <- route exists, path not in map yet
```

**Fix:** retain the poll promise, await it in the already-detached smoke dispatch. Request path unchanged.

## 2. ENG-2079 — an unanswered correction fails the whole page

The enhancement corrections each end in an explicit `proceeding without it` fallback — a page missing them is degraded, not broken. That fallback was unreachable when v0 answered with no new version, because the failure happened at the **await**, not the check: `waitForCompletedV0Version` throws, the outer catch marks the page `failed` after ~17 minutes, blaming v0.

**Fix:** `awaitOptionalV0Correction` returns `undefined` instead of throwing; `undefined` falls through to the existing fallback. Applied to all six enhancement sites. Deliberately **not** applied to the `validateV0Output` correction — un-correctable output must still fail, so those two waits stay fatal.

## 3. ENG-2080 — the wait itself

ENG-2079 stopped the failure; it did not stop the wait. The corrections were gated only on the *feature* being configured, never on whether the page has a form to attach to. A form-less page still took ~17 minutes to deploy (measured live: fired 09:45:40Z, deployed 10:05).

**Fix:** `hasLeadCaptureForm(files)`, keyed on the POST to `/api/capture` — the platform-owned contract every generated capture form uses, not a `<form>` tag (which a login form or search box also satisfies). All six sites now additionally require it.

## 4. ENG-2081 — the diagnosis was thrown away

`runGenerationSmokeTestNow` classifies *why* a submit produced no lead, then puts it only in the Slack alert. The persisted record couldn't distinguish:

- **no lead form at all** — capture is fine, the PAGE is the problem
- **form submitted, no row landed** — a real capture/CRM fault

Both read `ok:false, leadCaptured:false`. The code's own comment argues exactly this point, then says it only in the alert — whose Slack transport is currently dead, which is how it surfaced. Live, a page verified to contain zero `<form>`, `<input>`, `<button>` persisted as `noFormOnPage=None`.

**Fix:** persist `noFormOnPage` / `authFormOnly` / `iframeCount`, only when true/non-zero.

---

## Tests

**4851 passed** across 210 suites (the capture change touches a core public route, so the net was widened well past the 6 directly-affected suites). `tsc --noEmit` clean.

All four mutation-checked — revert the fix, the test fails with the real production symptom:

| Fix | Symptom on revert |
|---|---|
| ENG-2078 | `Received number of calls: 1` — smoke fired immediately |
| ENG-2079 | `Expected "deployed" / Received "failed"` |
| ENG-2080 | `Received number of calls: 1` — the correction, and its wait |
| ENG-2081 | `Received: undefined` |
| ENG-2082 | `Expected: 201 / Received: 400` — phone-only refused |

Two existing fixtures were form-less pages used as a convenience to make the pixel and bridge-out checks fail. Under the ENG-2080 gate they'd no longer exercise the correction loop they assert on, so they now carry a real capture form missing only the thing under test — which is also the actual production scenario.

## Live verification (env1 + env2)

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| happy path | `ok=true, leadCaptured=true` (+31s gate) |
| `fullname` field | `ok=true, leadCaptured=true` (+36s) |
| side-effect suppression | no CRM sync / sequence / auto-send / owner-notify — **no emails fired** |
| phone-only lander | correctly still `ok=false` — verified email-less, capture verified rejecting |
| stranded-lead sweep | planted lead confirmed swept |
| ENG-2079 reverify | same input that produced `failed` now `deployed`, `pixelVerified=False` |
| ENG-2082 phone-only | `201`, `leadId lead_ph_4d4be7fa83dae4aa5996c2a3` |
| ENG-2082 dedupe | `+1 (415) 555-0142` then `4155550142` -> `200 lead.unchanged`, same leadId |
| ENG-2082 neither | `400 "Email or phone is required"` |
| ENG-2083 redeploy | `409` (was `500`); a missing page still `404` |
| ENG-2081 `authFormOnly` | `True` on a real login-only page (1 password input, no `/api/capture`) |
| ENG-2081 `iframeCount` | `2`, matching the 2 real iframes; `noFormOnPage=True` alongside |
| ENG-2080 bridge-out twin | form-less page with `bridge_out_url`: **2m04s**, both pixel and bridge-out hit `proceeding without it`, zero correction round-trips |
| ENG-2082 dedupe race | 4 concurrent identical phone submits -> one `201`, three `200` adopting the same leadId, **1 row**, no 500 |
| ENG-2080 reverify | same form-less prompt: **~20 min -> 2m47s**, `deployed`; log shows `proceeding without it` with no pixel correction round-trip |
| ENG-2081 reverify | same page now persists `noFormOnPage=True` (was `None`) |

## Fifth commit

`origin/main` did not typecheck — the discovery test's local type had drifted from `DiscoveredCheckable` (missing `isAria`), failing TS2339 and blocking the pre-push `tsc` hook for everyone. Unrelated, fixed here because it blocked the push.

## 5. ENG-2082 — a phone-only lander can never capture a lead

`/api/capture` required an email, so a phone-only lander — an ordinary thing to want, and something the generator will happily build — was structurally incapable of producing a lead. Every submission was refused before a row was even constructed, with nothing warning the owner until the leads never arrived.

Nothing downstream actually required one:

| Consumer | Already handled it |
|---|---|
| `createLead` | dedupes only `if (leadData.email && leadData.email.trim())` |
| `autoEnrollLeadInSequences` | opens with `if (!leadEmail) return;` |
| auto-send | already reports `skipped_no_email` |
| Meta CAPI | `metaUserDataNormalisation.ts` already normalises `ph` as a first-class match key |

**Fix:** the gate takes an email **or** a phone, refusing only a submission carrying neither.

Dedupe is the one real gap — email has the `email-index` GSI, phone has no index. Rather than add a second GSI, a phone-only lead keys on its own normalized number and lets the conditional create dedupe: the ENG-787 mechanism `createLead` already exposes for "a caller that keys a lead on a stable identity", the same way the LinkedIn invite mirror uses it. Losing that create is the dedupe *succeeding*, so it adopts the winning row rather than 500ing, and `isNew` stays false so new-lead side effects don't fire twice for one person.

`email` is omitted from the item entirely rather than written as `''` — it keys the GSI, and DynamoDB rejects an empty string for an index key attribute.

Generator check became `validateCaptureFormHasContactField`, since phone-only is now legitimate; it flags only a form collecting neither.

**Deliberate:** a phone-only lead that later submits with an email becomes its own row — the same thing that already happens for two different emails. Merging needs the phone index this avoids.

## 6. ENG-2083 — undeployable page returns 500

```
POST /generated/:id/deploy  ->  HTTP 500  {"error":"Cannot deploy a landing page with status: deployed"}
```

The route's only classifier was `error.message?.includes("not found") ? 404 : 500`, so a deliberate precondition failure surfaced as a crash — polluting error monitoring and telling retry logic the request was worth repeating when it can never succeed.

`LandingPageNotDeployableError` carries `code: "LP_NOT_DEPLOYABLE"` and `httpStatus: 409`; the route matches on the **code**, not `instanceof`, so it survives re-wrapping across a throw boundary (same reason `V0OutputValidationError` carries one). Message text unchanged — callers and an existing test match on it.

## 7. ENG-2087 — unparseable generated code bricks the whole site

Found while closing live-test gaps. A generation committed this as its entire `page.tsx`:

```tsx
"use client"

import  from ".."

export default function SyntheticV0PageForDeployment() {
  return < />
```

Not valid JavaScript. It doesn't render blank — it fails `npm run build`, so **every subsequent deploy of that site fails, for every sibling page**, until someone deletes it. Seen live: one bad generation, then an unrelated page two minutes later failing with a syntax error pointing at a file its author never touched.

Checks 1–7 in `validateV0Output` are shape heuristics — they ask whether the text *looks* like React. This stub passes all of them. `detectIncompleteSyntheticPage` recognised the marker but requires a second gate (≥1 orphaned section); this generation produced no sections at all, so the gate could never fire.

**Two independent nets:**

1. `findUnparseableModule` rejects any generated module that doesn't parse. Syntax-only — `transpileModule` reports no type/resolution diagnostics — so unresolved imports are fine and TSX generics (the classic false positive) aren't flagged. `typescript` is already a runtime dependency.
2. `detectIncompleteSyntheticPage` now also reports the marker page when zero sections were generated, counted with the same `ui/` and provider-name exclusions the orphan loop uses — counting `theme-provider` as a section is exactly what let this through.

Both mutation-checked independently.

## Remaining gaps, stated plainly

- **Root-page path.** Every change has a twin in `deployLandingPage`; all live runs were sub-pages. Reaching it needs an account with no existing site — on env2 that means creating an account or deleting a shared 30-page site. Unit-tested only.
- **Google Ads correction twin.** Same code shape as the pixel and bridge-out twins, both of which are live-proven; it's gated on the site having a conversion pair configured.
- **Phone-only through a real lander.** Generated landers bake `BACKEND_URL` pointing at env1's ngrok, so their submissions reach a different backend. Verified against the capture endpoint directly instead.
- **ENG-2087 live.** Can't make v0 emit invalid code on demand; covered by unit + mutation tests using the exact source observed.

## Known tradeoff

The ENG-2078 gate delays the smoke test by ~30-40s, widening the window where a backend restart loses the result outright — the page keeps `deployed` but gets no `smokeTestResult`. Pre-fix it completed in ~0.5s (wrongly, but it completed).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(config): strip encryptedPassword from config API responses (ENG-2056)
body:
GET /api/config (and its sibling GET /shared and GET /api/:appName routes) stripped `password` from each config object before responding but never stripped `encryptedPassword`, so the encrypted credential shipped to the browser on every config listing. The same deny-list pattern (`const { password, ...rest } = config`) was repeated in 5 places across the file, all with the same gap.

**Fix.** Added `encryptedPassword` alongside `password` in each of the 5 destructures. While live-testing against real preview data, also found and fixed a pre-existing crash: `GET /api/config` 500'd whenever a shared config pointed at a since-deleted user, because the `sharedWith` filter only excluded `null`, not the `undefined` that a not-found user lookup actually returns. Finally, centralized all 5 destructures into one `omitSensitiveConfigFields` helper so a future sensitive field can't repeat this bug by being missed at one of several call sites.

Verified with a failing-then-passing TDD cycle for both fixes (regression tests added and confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code), against real prod-cloned data in a live preview (API + browser UI, including the create/list/delete round trip), and via direct DynamoDB inspection of the account that surfaced the crash.

---
**Automated gates**
Code review: ✅ sound
Deterministic checks: ✅ `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx jest routes.config.test.ts` (18/18) pass
Browser verify: ✅ verified live against a preview environment (API responses + Settings UI)

Fixes ENG-2056 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2056/get-apiconfig-returns-encryptedpassword-to-the-browser

title: [needs human] Distinguish attended vs unattended turns for work-plan autocomplete forcing (ENG-2072)
body:
**Problem:** ENG-2058 made createWorkPlan/modifyWorkPlan/applyPredefinedWorkPlan force `workPlan.autocomplete = true` whenever `session.sessionType === 'scheduled'`. But sessionType records how a session was CREATED, not whether the current turn is attended — a user can reopen a schedule-created session from the customer-portal 'Scheduled' sidebar tab and keep chatting in it live (useAgentModeChat reuses the same sessionId). If that live message triggers create_work_plan/modify_work_plan/launch_predefined_work_plan, it ran hands-off with no per-step approval even though a real person was watching, exactly the confusion ENG-803 already hit and fixed for the publish-approval prompt block.

**Fix:** Added a tri-state `isUnattendedRun` signal (mirroring ENG-803's publishAuthorized pattern) threaded from runScheduledChat (and the shared 'Test run' path) — true only there, false from the interactive verifiedGenerate endpoint, undefined elsewhere — through generateSessionResponse, the generateMarketingResponse worker process (IPC), executePreparedTools, and into ToolContext. The three work-plan methods now call a new `shouldForceScheduledAutocomplete(session, isUnattendedRun)` helper: an explicit true/false signal wins; when undefined (callers not yet migrated, e.g. the direct emmaApi.ts HTTP route) it falls back unchanged to the original sessionType-only check, so no existing caller's behavior silently changes.

**Verification:** Wrote new unit tests first confirming the bug (an attended turn on a scheduled session forced autocomplete=true), then implemented the fix and confirmed they pass, plus a regression test that the unattended path still forces autocomplete and that omitting the signal falls back to old behavior. Ran the full chain of affected/adjacent test suites (work-plan tests, worker arg-order test — updated for the new trailing parameter — toolDispatch, toolRegistry, runVerifiedChat/verifiedGenerate, scheduled-chat suites, publish-approval/ENG-803/827 suites, Slack/emmaEmailService callers of generateSessionResponse) — all green. Full backend typecheck (npx tsc) passes clean.

Browser verify: ⚠️ environment down (not verified)

title: feat(enigma): re-ship ENG-2070 vars under the CFN size limit
body:
## What
Re-ships ENG-2070's two Enigma env vars, this time under CloudFormation's 4,096-char `EnvironmentVariables` limit that broke #3013 (reverted in #3016).

**Exactly one file, five settings, nothing else:**
- `ENIGMA_ENRICHMENT_ENABLED=true`
- `ENIGMA_ENRICHMENT_USER_ALLOWLIST=<one internal admin id>`
- `OPENROUTER_GATEWAY_TASK_CLASSES=""`, `DISCORD_INVITE_URL=""`, `GCS_BUCKET=""` — blanked to free room. All three confirmed to have zero references anywhere in the repo (full-tree grep, not just `backend/src`).

## Why this frees enough room
Live EB config measured right before this commit: 67 variables, 4,057 chars. Blanking the three above frees 199 chars of *value*, but `.ebextensions` can only override a value, not delete the option entirely, so each name stays (~62 chars total). Net: 4,057 − 199 + 62 + 99 (the two new vars) = **4,019 / 4,096, 77 chars of margin.**

## Why `.ebextensions` and not the EB console
The direct config-update API/console path fails at CloudFormation staging with an S3 Access Denied error, for every identity tried, on both additions and removals (ENG-2071, still unexplained, not blocking on it here). Bundling into a normal deploy via `.ebextensions` is the route that's actually proven to work, as long as the result fits under the size limit — which this now does.

## Not done here, and why that's fine
A true deletion of the three dead variables (reclaiming the ~62 chars their blanked names still cost) needs `update-environment --options-to-remove`, which hits the same ENG-2071 staging error. Leaving them blank is a correct, safe state either way — they're unused, so an empty value changes nothing functionally.

## Scope
Internal admin account only (`ENIGMA_ENRICHMENT_USER_ALLOWLIST` is one id). No customer accounts affected. No code changes — config only.

title: fix(landers): ENG-2079/2080/2081/2082/2083/2087 — v0 correction loop, capture contract, parse gate
body:
Follow-on to #3017, which merged early carrying only ENG-2078 + the `isAria` typecheck fix. These five commits were pushed after that merge and were therefore never attached to an open PR.

| Issue | |
|---|---|
| [ENG-2079](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2079) | an unanswered v0 correction fails the whole page |
| [ENG-2080](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2080) | corrections fire on pages with no capture form, burning ~17 min |
| [ENG-2081](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2081) | smoke diagnosis computed but never persisted |
| [ENG-2082](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2082) | a phone-only lander can never capture a lead |
| [ENG-2083](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2083) | undeployable page returns 500 instead of 409 |
| [ENG-2087](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2087) | unparseable generated code bricks the whole site's builds |

---

## ENG-2079 — an unanswered correction fails the whole page

The enhancement corrections (pixel Lead event, Google Ads conversion, bridge-out redirect) each end in an explicit `proceeding without it` fallback — a page missing them is degraded, not broken. That fallback was unreachable when v0 answered with no new version, because the failure happened at the **await**, not the check: `waitForCompletedV0Version` throws, the outer catch marks the page `failed` after ~17 minutes, blaming v0.

`awaitOptionalV0Correction` returns `undefined` instead of throwing; `undefined` falls through to the existing fallback. Applied to all six enhancement sites. Deliberately **not** applied to the `validateV0Output` correction — un-correctable output must still fail.

## ENG-2080 — the wait itself

ENG-2079 stopped the failure, not the wait. The corrections were gated only on the *feature* being configured, never on whether the page has a form to attach to.

`hasLeadCaptureForm(files)` keys on the POST to `/api/capture` — the platform-owned contract every generated capture form uses, not a `<form>` tag (which a login form or search box also satisfies).

## ENG-2081 — the diagnosis was thrown away

`runGenerationSmokeTestNow` classified *why* a submit produced no lead, then put it only in the Slack alert. The record couldn't tell "no lead form at all" from "form submitted, no row landed" — both read `ok:false, leadCaptured:false`. Now persists `noFormOnPage` / `authFormOnly` / `iframeCount`.

## ENG-2082 — phone-only landers

`/api/capture` required an email, so a phone-only lander was structurally incapable of producing a lead. Nothing downstream required one: `createLead` dedupes only `if (leadData.email && …)`, `autoEnrollLeadInSequences` opens with `if (!leadEmail) return;`, auto-send reports `skipped_no_email`, and Meta CAPI already normalises `ph`.

Gate now takes email **or** phone. Dedupe: email has the `email-index` GSI, phone has none — so a phone-only lead keys on its normalized number via the ENG-787 deterministic-leadId + `failIfExists` mechanism `createLead` already exposes. Losing that create is the dedupe *succeeding*, so it adopts the winning row rather than 500ing.

## ENG-2083 — 500 for a precondition failure

The route's only classifier was `error.message?.includes("not found") ? 404 : 500`. `LandingPageNotDeployableError` carries `code: "LP_NOT_DEPLOYABLE"` + `httpStatus: 409`, matched by **code** so it survives re-wrapping.

## ENG-2087 — unparseable code bricks the site

A generation committed `import  from ".."` / `return < />` as its whole `page.tsx`. Not valid JavaScript — it fails `npm run build`, so **every later deploy of that site fails, for every sibling page**. Seen live: one bad generation, then an unrelated page two minutes later failing with a syntax error pointing at a file its author never touched.

Two independent nets: `findUnparseableModule` (syntax-only, so unresolved imports and TSX generics aren't flagged), and `detectIncompleteSyntheticPage` now also reporting the marker page when zero sections were generated.

---

## Tests

**4851 passed across 210 suites.** `tsc --noEmit` clean. Every fix mutation-checked — revert it and the test fails with the real production symptom:

| Fix | Symptom on revert |
|---|---|
| ENG-2079 | `Expected "deployed" / Received "failed"` |
| ENG-2080 | `Received number of calls: 1` — the correction, and its wait |
| ENG-2081 | `Received: undefined` |
| ENG-2082 | `Expected: 201 / Received: 400` |
| ENG-2087 | both nets checked independently |

## Live verification (env2)

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| ENG-2079 | same input that produced `failed` now `deployed` |
| ENG-2080 | same form-less prompt: **~20 min → 2m47s**, no correction round-trip |
| ENG-2080 bridge-out twin | `bridge_out_url` + form-less: 2m04s, pixel *and* bridge-out both `proceeding without it` |
| ENG-2081 `noFormOnPage` | `True` (was `None`) |
| ENG-2081 `authFormOnly` | `True` on a real login-only page |
| ENG-2081 `iframeCount` | `2`, matching the 2 real iframes |
| ENG-2082 phone-only | `201`, `lead_ph_4d4be7fa…` |
| ENG-2082 dedupe | two formats → same leadId; 4 concurrent submits → one `201`, three `200`, **1 row** |
| ENG-2082 neither | `400 "Email or phone is required"` |
| ENG-2083 | `409` (was `500`); missing page still `404` |

## Known gaps

- **Root-page path.** Every change has a `deployLandingPage` twin; all live runs were sub-pages. Reaching it needs an account with no existing site. Unit-tested only.
- **Google Ads correction twin.** Same shape as the pixel and bridge-out twins, both live-proven; gated on the site having a conversion pair.
- **Phone-only through a real lander.** Landers bake `BACKEND_URL` pointing at env1, so their submissions reach a different backend.
- **ENG-2087 live.** v0 can't be made to emit invalid code on demand.

## Tradeoff worth a reviewer's eye

ENG-2078 (already in main) delays the smoke test ~30–40s, widening the window where a backend restart loses the result entirely — page stays `deployed` with no `smokeTestResult`.

title: fix(landers): correct two capture-route gate defects now live in main
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **DRAFT ON PURPOSE — DO NOT MERGE, DO NOT MARK READY.**
>
> The two PRs before this one (#3017, #3023) were each merged while work was still in flight, stranding later commits on a closed PR and leaving a defect live in `main`. This stays a draft until the author explicitly says otherwise. If you think it should ship, please ask first rather than marking it ready.

Follow-on to #3023, which merged at `c05540f47` carrying the **first-round** review fixes. These corrections were pushed after that merge and so were never attached to an open PR.

## Why this matters now

Two defects from the first-round fix commit are **in `main` today**, and they compound:

```
IN MAIN:  buildStatus !== "ready"           v0Service.ts
IN MAIN:  captureRouteGateMaxMs = 90_000
```

**1. `!== "ready"` is always true.** `pollVercelDeployment` returns `success | error | timeout` — never `"ready"`. Every other comparison in the module uses `"success"`. So the settle window fires on **every** sub-page add, including the builds that just proved the capture route was live, adding a flat 45s to each one. The branch meant to distinguish "route known live" from "we don't know" does nothing.

**2. The 90s cap can re-open ENG-2078.** `pollVercelDeployment` budgets `60 × 5s`, and the ENG-483 comment describes these builds running to that full window. A 90s race doesn't bound a wait — it releases the smoke test **before the route is live** for any build over 90s, which is the exact false `ok:false` ENG-2078 was merged to fix.

Together they're worse than separately: the always-on 45s settle pushes any build over 45s into the 90s cap.

The reason neither was caught is that the shipped test config sets `settleMs` to `0`, zeroing out the exact value the first bug lives on, and the gate shipped with no test at all.

## What this PR does

- `buildStatus !== "success"`, so the settle fires only when the outcome genuinely doesn't prove the route live.
- Cap sized to the poll's own budget (300s) — a backstop for the pathological case (the poll is bounded by *attempt count*, so axios timeouts can stretch it), not a truncation of real builds.
- `sleepMs` timers `unref()`'d. They were holding the event loop; rtk jest was force-exiting workers over it. The module already sets that precedent twice (`withTimeout`, `startBuildHeartbeat`).
- Adopt-path merge no longer writes a fresh `forwardedAt` over the stored one. It was rewriting the lead's capture time whenever anything else changed, contradicting the invariant stated at the stamp site and visible in the owner alert.
- ENG-449 gap #3 suppression no longer keys on `isNew`. The adopt path can now set `isUpdated`, which made a synthetic smoke-test lead able to drive HubSpot/Attio sync, sequence enrolment and an agent-mode draft.
- **Reverted the dead-end rethrow.** Rethrowing `V0_VERSION_FAILED` failed a page whose output had already passed `validateV0Output`, over an optional enhancement — precisely what ENG-2079 exists to stop. The dead chat is still acted on: it's reported, and the remaining corrections skip rather than spending more billed messages on a chat that can't answer.
- `hasLeadCaptureForm` / `validateCaptureFormHasContactField` now read `.jsx`/`.js` too; a page emitted as `app/page.jsx` was invisible to the gate.

## Deliberately not done

Tightening the zero-section guard to "reaches only non-sections". A stub importing one provider and a healthy marker page rendering one real component whose name merely matches the **unanchored** `NON_SECTION_COMPONENT_NAME` (`service-types.tsx` matches `types?`) are statically indistinguishable — same directory, both rendered in JSX by the entry. Flagging fails the generation outright; missing ships a thin page other checks may still catch. The cheap failure is the right one to prefer. The gap is documented where the decision lives.

## Tests

Both defects shipped with **zero** coverage, which is why the first was wrong. Both now have regression tests, mutation-checked:

| Test | On revert |
|---|---|
| a successful build releases the gate with no settle | reinstate `"ready"` → `Expected 1, Received 0` |
| classification survives a throw after the fill | move assignments back → `Expected 2, Received undefined` |

```
4945 passed across 222 suites
tsc --noEmit clean
```

Note: backend ESLint arrived via #3022 while this was in flight. CI lints only CI scripts, not backend source, and the repo reports issues across 2000+ files — nothing here is a new violation.

title: fix(observability): load OKAREO_API_KEY from Secrets Manager (ENG-2070)
body:
## What
Boot loads the Okareo trace-exporter token from Secrets Manager (`prod/AgentWeb/Okareo`) instead of the EB env. Same pattern as `getEnigmaApiKey`.

## Why
`OKAREO_API_KEY` is 856 chars, which puts the EB env payload over CloudFormation's 4096-char limit. That's why ENG-2070 (Enigma) and ENG-2071 (spend-ledger canary) can't persist env config.

## Already done (infra)
- Secret `prod/AgentWeb/Okareo` created with the current prod value. Readback authenticates against `api.okareo.com/v0/projects` (201; bogus key → 401).
- `aws-elasticbeanstalk-ec2-role` gets inline `AgentWebOkareoSecretRead` (GetSecretValue on that secret only). Simulated: allowed.

## Behavior
- Env var set → used as before (safe to deploy before the EB var is removed).
- Env var unset + secret present → loaded at boot, before the lazy `initTracing`.
- Secret missing → warning; Okareo exporter stays off (same as today with no key). Never blocks boot.

## Rollout / rollback
1. Merge + deploy (no behavior change; env var still wins).
2. Remove `OKAREO_API_KEY` from the EB env; confirm boot log `Okareo API key loaded from Secrets Manager`.
Rollback: revert this PR and re-add the env var from the secret.

Complexity: +1 small helper, +1 guarded boot block; −856 chars of EB env.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low — the Secrets Manager lookup only enables optional trace export; if it fails, boot continues with export disabled.

When `OKAREO_API_KEY` is unset, startup loads the environment-specific Okareo key from AWS Secrets Manager. A configured environment key takes precedence. The secret value is trimmed, and lookup failures produce a warning without blocking boot.

## What
`website` is a first-class `LeadRecord` attribute — enrichment's domain resolution (`resolveApolloMatchDomain`, used by Enigma card revenue and others) reads `lead.website` directly, and a "Tier 0.5" resolver writes it back. But `createLead`, `updateLead` and `batchCreateLeads` never accepted it as an input, so a caller-supplied website (single-lead create, the PUT update route, or a bulk/CSV/LinkedIn import) was always silently dropped — only that one internal resolver could ever populate the field.

**Found live** while re-testing ENG-1388/ENG-1932 (Enigma card revenue): a lead created with an explicit website ended up with none stored, so domain-keyed lookups had nothing to resolve against.

Adds `website` to all three functions' accepted fields, following the exact pattern already used for `company`/`title`/`notes`: plain string, defaults to `''` on create, SET-or-REMOVE on update. title: fix(ENG-2119): batch landing-page preview edits behind a syntax gate
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Landing-page `coding_agent` calls committed each file immediately, exposing incomplete multi-file changes to Vercel. The reported production sample had 20 ERROR builds out of 88 previews. The agent had no pre-commit parse gate, and preview checks could accept an older build on the reusable branch.

## What this fixes (after)
`edit_file`, `edit_files`, and `revert_file` share an in-memory workspace. Reads, searches, and listings see staged changes. `check_deployment` validates the entire changed TS/TSX/JS/JSX/CSS batch, then sends one request to the existing `update-files` endpoint, which already uses GitHub blobs/tree/commit/ref APIs. Syntax diagnostics include file/line/column and return to the model; both report-to-user and plain-text completion must pass the same gate. Failed or exhausted sessions leave invalid edits uncommitted.

A successful build closes the edit batch. A real Vercel ERROR still permits an atomic repair batch. Reverts and automatic recovery are batched as well. Preview polling and the final URL refresh use the committed SHA, retain the initial draft-PR fallback, and reject malformed API data.

## Complexity ledger
- Production/config: **+192 / -152 lines (net +40)**. Entire PR: **+506 / -187 (net +319)**, including focused regression coverage.
- Removed immediate per-file writes and per-file rollback writes from the coding loop; one commit path reuses existing authorization, GitHub retry/rebase/idempotency, and deployment polling.
- Added one per-run workspace and one parse-only helper. PostCSS was already locked transitively at 8.5.10; it is now a declared direct dependency. No new installed package versions, API endpoints, queues, Vercel configuration, or persistence.
- Behavior intentionally changes: intermediate edits stay private until validated; only a failed build permits further commits in the same session. Model routing and accounting remain unchanged.

## How to test
1. Ask the coding agent to edit two landing-page files using separate edit calls, including revising the first file again.
2. Verify no file-write request occurs before `check_deployment`, and one atomic commit contains both final files.
3. Introduce `const value = ;` or an unclosed CSS block. Verify the model receives the exact parse location, no commit is created, and it can fix the staged file and retry.
4. Return a Vercel ERROR for that commit. Verify the model receives its build error and can submit a complete repair batch; an older READY or ERROR deployment must not satisfy the new commit's poll.

## Test evidence
All commands ran on Atem with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048` and Jest `--runInBand --forceExit`:
- Coding-agent service, staging, and Emma tool suites: **147 passed**.
- Acceptance, run state, subpage, and tool-dispatch smoke suites: **34 passed**.
- GitHub atomic commit/retry, preview service, and preview route tests (`commitFilesToRepoMain|getPreviewDeploymentUrl|GET /preview-url`): **23 passed**.
- **204 focused tests passed**. The new acceptance regression started at **3 failing / 1 passing** before implementation.
- Standalone strict TypeScript check of `codingAgentSyntax.ts`: passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- Local CodeRabbit review completed: all three findings addressed (commit-metadata compatibility, ensuring an open preview PR for a new SHA, and the valid status-only response for pages without a Vercel project), with regression coverage. Review was not rerun after those fixes.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- One final commit for a normal editing session: separate/repeated edit test plus the real Git Data helper's multi-file tree/commit/ref assertions.
- Parse errors prevent commit and reach the model: five supported syntax extensions, repair-and-retry, report-to-user bypass, and plain-text bypass tests.
- Build feedback/self-repair retained: ERROR-to-repair loop, exact-SHA lookup, old READY/ERROR rejection, and first-preview PR fallback tests.
- Read-your-writes, deletion/revert, no-op create/delete, read-only/error exits, authorization denial, and malformed content coverage.

## Edge cases and limits
- Additional repair/rollback commits are necessary after a real Vercel failure. The existing pre-session synchronization of a stale preview branch with main can also create a maintenance commit; preserving it avoids reverting newer main changes.
- Parsing does not check imports, types, or Next.js server/client semantics. The proposed event-handler heuristic is deliberately omitted: a component can belong to an importing client's module graph without its own `'use client'` directive. Vercel remains the authoritative build check.
- Existing update-files request size/20-file batch limit and concurrency semantics remain in place. Staged changes are intentionally ephemeral until commit.

## What was NOT tested
No full repository/backend build or full Jest run, no live Vercel deployment, and no live model/Okareo simulation. This is a draft PR as requested, with no production merge or deployment. The pre-push broad typecheck/related-suite hook is bypassed to honor the explicit scoped-compute constraint; focused evidence is above.

## Rollback / post-deploy verification
Revert this PR to restore the previous write behavior. After a future approved deployment, use a QA landing page, perform a two-file revision, inspect the single edit commit and its matching READY preview, then repeat with malformed syntax and verify there is no push until repaired. No database/data-plane change.

## Files changed
- Coding loop/workspace and syntax parser: `codingAgentService.ts`, `codingAgentSyntax.ts`.
- Commit-specific preview lookup: `v0Service.ts`, `landingPageGeneration.ts`.
- Dependency declaration: backend package manifest/lock.
- Focused regression suites: coding-agent service/staging, v0 service, landing-page staging.

## Design references
Reuses [GitHub's tree → commit → ref flow](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/git/trees#create-a-tree), [TypeScript compiler APIs](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/Using-the-Compiler-API), and [PostCSS parsing](https://postcss.org/api/#parse).

title: ENG-2117: Move ClickUp connection management to org admins
body:
## Summary

ClickUp connection management now requires the existing `org:accounts:manage` permission (org owners/admins) instead of Brand Knowledge editor access. This applies to `/init`, `/callback`, `/finalize`, `/connect`, `/save-token`, and `/disconnect`. Browser callbacks authenticate signed state and reload the actor's current org role; state/token sessions are bound to the org.

Existing org and legacy user tokens remain readable without migration or reconnect. Status reads the connected identity from [ClickUp `/user`](https://developer.clickup.com/reference/getauthorizeduser) and workspace names from `/team`. Both OAuth and personal-token writes compare identity before replacing the token; a different/unavailable prior identity returns 409 and a short-lived confirmation bound to actor, org, and both tokens. Connect/disconnect use the existing structured admin audit logger with actor and ClickUp identity. Disconnect also removes the acting admin's legacy fallback token, preserving unrelated secrets.

**Frontend companion:** https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/1194 — the Brand Knowledge and Organization settings UI lives in that repo, not the monorepo's partner portal. Deploy this backend first, then the frontend. Both remain **draft**, per request.

## Acceptance checklist

- [x] Org-admin-only connect/disconnect/reconnect; Brand Knowledge read-only status + admin link in companion PR.
- [x] Identity (email/username) and workspace displayed from existing credentials.
- [x] Negative tests: members, including KB editors, receive 403 before provider calls or writes. Callback/finalize and org changes are covered.
- [x] Different identity requires warning/confirmation; cancel/no confirmation leaves existing credentials unchanged.
- [x] Connect/disconnect audit events include actor + ClickUp identity; unavailable identity explicitly recorded on disconnect.
- [x] Existing token read precedence and read-only docs/tasks routes preserved; no reconnect or data migration required.
- [x] No schema/table/index/model changes, new database resources, or live data repairs.

## Test evidence

Backend source: `dd56b7adab5ca1c746ec6ce06d41139f188bd889`; companion source: `4498f6ca4c3d4a5aeecbd4da215524a350c853f5`.

- Before implementation, acceptance regression suite: **11 failed, 1 passed**.
- Scoped Jest, final backend source: **102 passed / 4 suites**, serial, 1.5 GB heap cap:

```sh
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1536 backend/node_modules/.bin/jest \
  --config backend/jest.config.js --runInBand --runTestsByPath \
  backend/src/__tests__/clickupAuth.admin.test.ts \
  backend/src/__tests__/clickupAuth.test.ts \
  backend/src/__tests__/orgClickupIntegration.test.ts \
  backend/src/__tests__/clickupService.test.ts
```

- Coverage includes admin/owner success, non-admin 403 at all connection routes, signed callback/org binding, forged/stale/candidate-mismatched confirmations, OAuth warning → confirmation → session consumption, invalid token/provider shapes, audit fields, and existing org/user token resolution.
- Companion: **12 scoped Vitest tests passed**, five changed production files passed scoped TypeScript diagnostics, and Chromium fixture checks passed with no runtime errors.
- Screenshots: [admin](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/blob/4498f6ca4c3d4a5aeecbd4da215524a350c853f5/docs/qa/eng-2117/admin.png), [member](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/blob/4498f6ca4c3d4a5aeecbd4da215524a350c853f5/docs/qa/eng-2117/member.png), [Brand Knowledge](https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/blob/4498f6ca4c3d4a5aeecbd4da215524a350c853f5/docs/qa/eng-2117/brand-knowledge.png). - CodeRabbit local review completed with one redirect-origin finding; resolved by restricting OAuth frontend origins and adding negative tests. Review is advisory, not a merge proof.

## Complexity / risk

Net production code **−124 lines**: one authorization helper and one connection/confirmation/storage/audit path replace duplicated PAT/OAuth branches. No new dependency or persistence field. Obsolete tests authorizing solo/KB-editor writes and unsigned callbacks were replaced with the new human-requested org-admin acceptance contract; read-only regression tests were retained.

Existing connections are not rewritten by status. OAuth flows already in flight before deploy must restart because state now binds org membership. Token sessions retain the existing process-local lifetime. Identity API outages leave existing status connected when workspace access succeeds; a replacement with unreadable prior identity requires explicit confirmation. Customer-facing copy is included for review in these drafts.

## Rollback / post-deploy smoke

Revert the frontend companion and this commit, then redeploy. No migration/backfill to undo; existing stored token format is unchanged. Code rollback does not recover a token intentionally replaced/disconnected by an admin; recovery then requires reconnecting the intended integration account.
