title: ENG-2118: Org-admin ClickUp and Google Drive access inventory
body:
## Summary

ENG-2118 adds a read-only inventory of metadata actually returned by the organization's connected ClickUp and Google Drive credentials. Refresh retrieves names, IDs and parent relationships from the provider rather than inspecting the Brand Knowledge index.

- `GET /api/source-access` lists available sources; `?source=<id>` checks one live. Fresh persisted org membership and `org:accounts:read` are required. No arbitrary target org/user is accepted; private teammate connections are excluded.
- ClickUp traverses teams, active/archived spaces, folders, lists and paginated Docs. Drive lists non-trashed files/folders across drives with an explicit metadata field mask. Live connected identity and check time accompany the tree.
- Every scan is capped at 2,000 items, 80 provider requests, 20 seconds, 5 seconds/request and 2 MiB/response. Repeated cursors, malformed metadata, provider failures and Drive `incompleteSearch` produce a visibly incomplete result. Route rate limit: 12 requests/minute/authenticated user/process.
- Backend-only scope: customer-facing UI lives in `agentweb-customer-portal`. This PR contains no `partner-portal/` changes. It is independent of ENG-2117.
- Existing ClickUp credentials and OAuth routes are untouched. Drive refresh is in-memory only. No new storage, schema, migration, index, dependency or background worker.

## Acceptance checklist

- [x] Live token-scoped ClickUp and Drive metadata enumeration; no document content returned or content-read endpoints called.
- [x] API returns connected identity, last-checked time and hierarchy per available source; live checks refresh provider metadata.
- [x] Non-admin 403, fresh membership enforcement, cross-org denial and foreign/private source isolation.
- [x] Safe pagination/caps and explicit incomplete results; malformed data fails closed.
- [x] Reuse existing connections without reconnect or persistent writes.
- [x] Independent of ENG-2117; draft targets `main`.
- [ ] Live xCures check of `agentwebintegration@xcures.ai` and Eric's subsequent scope change. No production token was exercised in this run; fixture tests are not claimed as live customer evidence.

## Test evidence

Validated head: `e266d1007f1d7de4fbb40aa72d2bf33879996861`.

- Scoped backend Jest on Atem: `node --max-old-space-size=1536 backend/node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --config backend/jest.config.js --runTestsByPath backend/src/__tests__/sourceAccess.test.ts --runInBand --silent` — 1 suite, 19 tests passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Backend tree is identical to the previous head (`785628c0270328f86b94170ce2cadb264cbd9f91`). The cleanup removes 195 lines across five partner-portal files; no partner-portal changes remain in the PR diff.
- Scoped backend TypeScript validation passed at the previous head; backend files are unchanged. No full-repo typecheck, build, broad test suite or live customer check was run for this cleanup.
- Repository-supported `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` keeps this push scoped to the requested validation. This draft is not a release/merge proof.
- CodeRabbit local review (partial advisory pass; stopped after five minutes without a final verdict): embedded ClickUp lists are retained before additional requests. Explicit archived-list queries remain intentionally: removing those without documented completeness guarantees could hide archived reachable metadata. Nested folder parent IDs and numeric Doc parent types are covered. The suggestion to narrow shared Drive inventory to Brand Knowledge folders is intentionally not applied: this ticket explicitly asks for actual token reach, not the KB index; fresh org-admin authorization and existing org-sharing consent delimit the audience.

Provider contracts: [ClickUp Docs](https://developer.clickup.com/reference/searchdocspublic), [ClickUp folders](https://developer.clickup.com/reference/getfolders), [Google Drive files.list](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/files/list).

## Risk, limitations and complexity

Medium: security-sensitive metadata enumeration. Auth checks precede token use; credentials and raw upstream errors are never serialized or logged. Only own/org-shared Drive OAuth connections and the org ClickUp secret are inspected, not the global Drive service account. Read-only visibility does not alter provider permissions or Emma's existing execution paths. Large sources can be incomplete and must not be interpreted as an exhaustive access audit. Live customer verification remains outstanding; customer-facing UI is owned by `agentweb-customer-portal`.

Complexity ledger: one isolated metadata crawler, one authenticated route, one focused backend test file and two backend wiring lines (388 added lines across four files). Zero frontend changes, persistent models/tables, token migrations or duplicated OAuth connection flows.

title: [needs human] Grow turn time-budget reserve for slow tool dispatch, not just slow LLM calls (ENG-2121)
body:
**Bug:** During a Meta ad-creative work-plan step, heavy knowledge-base reads (design tokens/media assets) completed but the turn was cut off by the whole-turn hard cap before `generate_image` could even be issued. The user saw the ungraceful "I hit the time limit" 504-style fallback instead of a graceful partial answer.

**Root cause:** `evaluateTurnTimeBudget`'s adaptive synthesis reserve (ENG-907) only widens using the slowest *LLM call* observed this run (`longestLlmCallMsThisRun`). It has no visibility into how long the *tool-dispatch* phase of an iteration takes. A slow non-media tool call (e.g. a batch `read_knowledge_base_files`) can burn several minutes of wall clock that the reserve never accounts for, so the budget kept reading as "normal"/"wrap_up" long after most of the turn's time was gone, and a second equally slow tool call then ran the turn straight past the controller's hard cap — before the in-loop `final_synthesis` nudge ever got a chance to force a graceful partial answer. (Media-generation tool calls already have an equivalent protection via `generationHardCapMs`/`longestMediaCallMsThisRun`; generic tools like KB reads had none.)

**Fix:** Track the tool-dispatch phase's wall-clock duration each iteration the same way the LLM call's duration is already tracked (`longestToolDispatchMsThisRun`), and feed `Math.max(longestLlmCallMsThisRun, longestToolDispatchMsThisRun)` into the reserve calculation. A slow KB read now grows the synthesis reserve exactly like a slow LLM call would, so the loop forces a graceful, nudge-driven partial answer with enough margin to actually complete before the hard cap fires.

**Verification:** Added a regression test that models fast LLM calls but a slow (`~6.3min`) `read_knowledge_base_files` tool dispatch. Confirmed (by stashing the fix) that the unfixed code overruns the 600s hard cap at 775s; with the fix, the loop forces final synthesis at 385s and delivers within the cap.

---

title: ENG-1250: fail loud on unresolvable allowance in the projection backfill
body:
## What
Hardens the ENG-1250 §3b projection backfill so it can never again silently persist wrong allowance data.

## Why
On 2026-09-21 a perms-starved backfill run couldn't read AW-Users / the subscription config, so `getUserById`/`getSubscriptionTypeConfig` returned null and the script **silently seeded every subject as `unlimited` (usableAllowance=0)** — wrong allowance written to all 40 prod rows before it was caught and re-run with the correct grant. A genuinely uncapped tier and an unreadable one looked identical. (No §9.6 impact — enforcement reads only `settledMicroUsd`, which was always correct — but it blocks §4, which reads the allowance/available fields.)

## Change
- `allowanceFor` now **fails loud**: a null user, a missing `subscriptionType`, or a null subscription config is a *resolution failure* and throws; only a config that resolves and has no `llmUsagePolicy` is a real uncapped tier.
- `main()` **skips** an unresolvable subject (never writes a guessed `unlimited`), records it, and **exits non-zero** listing them — one bad subject can't abort the rest, and can't silently persist wrong allowance.

## Tests
Added: `allowanceFor` throws on null user / missing tier / null config; returns `unlimited` only on a resolved no-policy tier; returns the real credit-adjusted cap for a capped tier. Full suite 9/9 green; typecheck clean.

Addresses the Gap-2 follow-up recorded on ENG-2068. `settledMicroUsd` is unaffected.

title: F1: Shared funding skeleton (RunFunding, LlmTransport, RunBackend, recordLlmUsage, decideFallback, AttemptUsageJournal)
body:
## Summary

Lands the seven ENG-1816 funding contracts under `backend/src/services/funding/` with **zero behavior change** — `route` is always `agentweb` today. Every later ENG-1816 ticket fills one pre-made slot instead of touching `callLLM` again.

- `RunFunding` — resolved once per run, ambient via `AsyncLocalStorage`, carried across the worker fork as plain data (same shape as `publishAuthorizationOverride`)
- `LlmConnection` — type + store interface only
- `LlmTransport` / `OpenRouterPlatformTransport` — today's OpenRouter send/validate/retry loop relocated unchanged out of `callLLM`, not rewritten
- `RunBackend` / `EmmaLoopBackend` — wraps `generateMarketingResponse` unchanged; unwired seam for a future Claude-subscription backend
- `recordLlmUsage` — funding decided **above** the fire-and-forget metering funnel, not inside it (that funnel is fail-open by design, so a check inside it would fail silently)
- `decideFallback` — signature + one invariant only (never returns `switch_to_agentweb` when the run's fallback is `stop`), not wired into any path yet
- `AttemptUsageJournal` — no-op port for a future per-attempt usage table

Also fixes 3 LLM call sites that booked spend to `"system"` (same bug class as ENG-1858): `wasStepRemovalUserAuthorized`, `restyleContent`/`generateBlogContent`, and the chatbot KB embeddings client — all now read the run's owner from the ambient store instead.

Flags (`LLM_BYOK`, `LLM_CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION`) read from one `AW-Settings` row, not EB env vars — prod EB is already at CloudFormation's 4096-char `EnvironmentVariables` limit, so no env-var-based flag can ship today regardless.

One unrelated fix bundled as its own commit: `growthGeniusService.ts` had a pre-existing implicit-`any` that fails `tsc --noEmit` on current `main`, blocking every push from this base. Fixed as a one-line type annotation, unrelated to ENG-1816.

## Two real regressions caught before this ever reached CI

1. **Sleep-spy break.** The transport extraction initially replaced `this.sleep(ms)` with a transport-local timer, which broke 8 tests in `agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts` that spy on `AgentModeService.prototype.sleep` to assert exact backoff values without waiting — 2 of them by letting real 7.5s/20s timers run. Fixed by injecting `sleep` as a caller-bound closure, same pattern as the other decision closures (`isRetryableError`, `computeBackoff`).
2. **Eager AWS SDK import.** `runFunding.ts` originally imported `fundingFlags.ts` (which pulls in `settingsService.ts`, which constructs a real `AWS.DynamoDB.DocumentClient` at module load) at the top level. That made merely importing `currentRunFunding` — now used in `blog.ts` and `chatbotService.ts`, files with no other reason to touch AWS — eagerly load the AWS SDK graph, breaking `blog.test.ts`'s deliberate avoidance of an aws-sdk mock. Fixed with the same lazy-`require` idiom `deferredBillingMetering.ts` already uses for `tokenUsageService`, for the identical reason.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] New unit tests: `recordLlmUsage`'s branch logic (agentweb route meters unchanged; any other route touches no existing rail, writes only to the journal — asserted on exact call args), `decideFallback`'s stop invariant, `fundingFlags`' all-off fallback on a missing/malformed/unreadable row, `RunFunding`'s `AsyncLocalStorage` isolation between two concurrent runs

title: ENG-1250 F5: durable projection delivery inside the charging transaction
body:
## What
Makes the ENG-1250 spend-projection update **durable** by writing it inside the *same* DynamoDB `transactWrite` as the ledger + spend events, replacing the previous fire-and-forget writer.

## Why
The writer was fire-and-forget after the charge committed: a crash between the commit and the projection write permanently under-counted the projection until a backfill re-ran. Before broadening the enforcement rollout beyond the canary, the projection must not be able to silently drift from the ledger.

## How
- `settledProjectionUpdateItems(events, now)` (replaces the async `applySettledSpendEvents`) returns the projection-maintenance items — one atomic-`ADD` `Update` per subject+month (a transaction may not touch an item twice) — to append to the charge transaction.
- Wired into both `incrementUsageWithChargeEvent` and `incrementUsageWithSpendEvent`, **appended last** so the existing `CancellationReasons` index mapping (0=ledger, 1=charge, 2+=events) is unchanged.
- **Atomic + idempotent by construction:** the projection commits with the ledger, and a duplicate replay (whose transaction is canceled) can't double-add — strictly better than the old "only on applied" guard.
- **Unconditional** Update: a failing condition would abort the charge, so the standalone writer's monotonic-`computedAt` guard is dropped — in the transactional path the projection never lags the ledger, so it's unnecessary (the staleness guard stays default-off).
- **Reversible:** `SPEND_PROJECTION_WRITER=false` returns no items, leaving the transaction exactly its ledger+event items.

## Tradeoff (accepted)
A projection-write failure now fails the charge. It's one more atomic `ADD` on an existing table (no schema change), the same contention class as the ledger item already in the transaction, and the kill switch reverts it instantly.

## Tests
214 green across all affected suites (writer + both charge-txn suites + the 6 other charge-path suites), typecheck clean. New/updated coverage asserts the projection Update rides in the transaction, groups same-subject events into one item, is unconditional, and is absent when the kill switch is off.

Phase A of ENG-1644 (durable approval inbox + exact runtime resume) — the child ticket to ENG-1635, which is fully shipped/Done. Builds the backend foundation only: no Slack, no new tool, no Emma wiring yet (Phases B–E, tracked in the approved plan, follow on top of this).

**⚠️ Data-plane change — needs Harsha's sign-off before merge** (new `AW-ApprovalDecisions` table, per this repo's own merge gate).

- **Security-relevant fix, not just prep**: `metaWriteDispatch` stored only the *raw* `account_id` argument, never the account `getMetaCredentials` actually resolved — every claim/dispatch re-derived it live from the user's *current* connected accounts. Safe today only because claim happens seconds after preview, same session. Unsafe for ENG-1644's days-later Slack resume, where connected accounts can drift in between and silently target a different real account than what was shown/approved. Adds `resolvedAccountId` alongside the unchanged raw `account_id` (digest-matching still needs the raw value) and dispatches against the frozen id. Digest computation itself is untouched — byte-identical, regression-tested.
- **New `AW-ApprovalDecisions` table**: `decisionId` HASH key — for `gateType='meta_write'` it *is* the `metaWriteManifestDigest` itself (per `metaLaunchGate.ts`'s own comment: "Child ENG-1644 uses this same digest as its pending-approval store key"), so a changed payload is structurally a new record, never an in-place edit. GSIs: `ApproverIndex`, `CustomerIndex` (Phase E), `StatusExpiryIndex`.
- **`approvalInboxService.ts`**: `createDecision` (idempotent), `claimDecision` (atomic conditional update — deliberately no pre-read, since a read-then-write here would itself be a race the pure condition doesn't have), `getDecision`, `listPendingForApprover`, `listPendingForCustomer`. Enforces the team/customer audience+status invariant (ticket point 6) as a hard check, not a naming convention.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean after every file
- [x] 36 tests passing (23 existing manifest-suite + 13 new `approvalInboxService` unit tests) — resolvedAccountId population, digest-unchanged, simulated connected-account drift proving dispatch uses the frozen id not a re-derivation, pre-migration fallback, idempotent create, atomic claim/expiry/already-resolved outcomes, option-shape validation, audience/status invariant
- [x] **Live env1 replay**: drove a real Meta write end-to-end through the existing, live-in-production ENG-1635 approval-deck flow (natural prompt → real halt → real approve → real dispatch) — ad renamed, full read-back confirmed correct ad/ad-set/campaign, proving this change doesn't regress the already-shipped flow

title: ENG-1644 gap-closing: expiry sweep + credential-reconnect auto-claim
body:
## Summary

Post-launch honest audit of the approval-inbox feature (ENG-1644, Phases A-E — already merged/deployed to prod, PR #3059) found two real gaps in a direct review with Manan. Closes both.

1. **A decision nobody ever answers just died silently.** `StatusExpiryIndex` was provisioned in Phase A specifically for this and had zero consumers. Adds `expireDecision`/`listDuePending` (same race-free atomic-conditional-update shape as `claimDecision`), `notifyOriginSessionOfExpiry`, and a new `approvalExpirySweepCron.ts` wired into `server.ts` hourly, following the exact existing pattern (`setInterval` + `cronJobRegistry.track`, ~20 other jobs already do this).

2. **`customer_credential` decisions could never resolve to "done."** The email goes out and that's it — nothing detects the customer actually reconnecting. Adds `credentialPlatform`/`credentialAccountId` to the decision schema (required for this gate type), `findPendingCredentialDecision`, and `autoResolveCredentialDecisionOnReconnect`, wired into the real Meta and LinkedIn OAuth reconnect callbacks right after a real reconnect succeeds.

Deliberately deferred (see plan file for full reasoning): idempotency dedup for non-`meta_write` decision creates (same-turn duplicates already handled by Agent Mode's existing content-keyed dedup elsewhere), and a multi-select-and-submit-once Slack UI (re-read the ticket's own wording — concluded it means no back-and-forth per item, not batch-submit N items).

Also, separately (no code, already applied): set `approval_inbox_fallback_slack_user_ids` in prod to Matt's real Slack ID — previously unset on purpose during testing.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean after every file
- [x] 103 unit tests passing (expiry race/resilience, credential-decision matching, auto-resolve flow including lost-claim-race and never-throws cases)
- [x] Caught and fixed two pre-existing test-mock gaps the new dynamic-import wiring exposed (`metaAuth.test.ts`/`linkedinAuth.test.ts`'s `INTEGRATION_CONFIG` mocks didn't cover `linkedinAds`, silently swallowing the new code path)
- [ ] Live env1 verification (expiry sweep, reconnect auto-claim, multi-item Slack queue rendering) — in progress

**This PR stays in draft — do not mark ready or merge without explicit go-ahead.**

`linkedin_ads` is a fully live platform — own OAuth flow (`/api/oauth/linkedin-ads/init`), own Settings card, real active customer connections (e.g. ThinkingAI's `rw_ads` connection) — but it's missing from two hardcoded entitlement allow-lists:

- `partner-portal/src/components/admin/SubscriptionTypesTab.tsx` → `AVAILABLE_CONNECTED_ACCOUNTS` — the Partner Portal toggle list for subscription-type entitlements

Net effect: `linkedin_ads` could never be toggled on for any subscription type in Partner Portal, and never appeared in the customer Settings grid regardless of plan — even for customers with an active, working connection.

Add `'linkedin_ads'` to both arrays.

Updated the existing drift-detection suite (`subscriptionService.calendly.test.ts`, which asserts an exact list length and cross-checks backend vs. partner-portal lists by reading the frontend source live) and `renewalIntegrationHealthCron.test.ts`'s unrestricted-plan fixture, since both previously hardcoded "14 items, no linkedin_ads" as expected state.

- `tsc --noEmit` on backend — no new errors (pre-existing unrelated `sanitize-html` module-resolution failure on `main`, not touched by this PR — see note below)

- Did not touch the customer-portal `connectedAccountsCatalog.ts` (already correctly includes `linkedin_ads`; this PR only fixes the two lists that were missing it).

These two lists — plus the customer-portal `CONNECTION_CATALOG` — are three hand-maintained copies of the same platform list. title: fix(agent-mode): don't send inline screenshots to models without verified vision support (ENG-2132)
body:
## Summary
- `toolDispatch.ts`'s playwright-screenshot handling only checked `!isGeminiModel` before embedding a base64 `image_url` block in a tool-role message — added in a0e5523ce for a *different*, Gemini-specific reason (Gemini's OpenAI-compat endpoint 400s on `image_url` in a tool-role message regardless of vision capability). It silently assumed every other model accepts inline images.
- `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` has no verified vision support (no `supportsVision` entry in `LLM_MODEL_REGISTRY`), so OpenRouter has no endpoint for it that accepts image input — the next LLM call 404s with `"No endpoints found that support image input"`.
- Root cause confirmed against real prod DynamoDB messages for the session in the oncall alert (`ffe0e1ad-16f4-4ca6-ada2-3bc87c3d3761`, filed as a comment on ENG-2086 by the auto-triage grouping on stack-trace shape, but confirmed unrelated — split out as ENG-2132).
- Fix: gate the inline-image branch on `LLM_MODEL_REGISTRY[llmModel]?.supportsVision === true` (the same flag `getVisionModelOptions` already trusts), in addition to excluding Gemini for its separate reason. Falls back to the existing text+URL-only path (already used for Gemini) for any model without verified vision support.
- Live-reproduced against the real OpenRouter endpoint: the old inline-image shape 404s for `deepseek-v4-flash` with the exact production error (`"failed_routing_step":"Filter by Image Support"`); the text+URL fallback returns 200.
- Also includes one unrelated, pre-existing fix: a stale pinned-list test (`agentModeController.conditionalSkip.test.ts`'s redirect audit) hadn't been updated for the `stage_pending_decision` tool a separate, already-merged PR added — its own description makes the classification obvious (hands off to a named approver over Slack, doesn't block the session — not a same-requirement substitute), matching the same reasoning already on record for `present_question_deck -> ask_user_question` right above it.

Linear: ENG-2132

## Test plan

title: D78: a narrow, read-only credential for GET /api/admin/agent-runs
body:
## Summary
- `AW_AGENT_ADMIN_JWT` (aw-agent's admin-API credential) is a full 90-day admin login session token — the backend re-reads the user from the DB per request, so it carries that account's whole privilege set (~195 admin handlers, ~108 state-changing) even though aw-agent makes exactly one read-only call with it (`GET /api/admin/agent-runs`, filtered to a single `sessionId`, `limit=3`).
- Adds `authenticateAgentRunsSecretOrAdmin`: a dedicated header-secret credential (`x-aw-agent-runs-secret` / `AW_AGENT_RUNS_SECRET`), constant-time compared, fails closed (401 wrong secret, 503 unconfigured — a valid admin session is never an accepted substitute). On a match, the request is narrowed server-side to what the caller actually needs (`sessionId` required, `limit` clamped to 3) before reaching the route handler directly.
- No header sent → unchanged behavior: falls through to `authenticateToken`, `isAdmin` exactly as before, so `partner-portal`'s `AgentRunsInspector` (which browses this route on a real admin session, unfiltered) is untouched.
- Purely additive: `AW_AGENT_ADMIN_JWT` is not removed or changed anywhere. Nothing on the live aw-agent box has been touched by this PR — `AW_AGENT_RUNS_SECRET` isn't set there yet, so aw-agent keeps using the JWT exactly as today until an operator sets the new secret (a separate, later step, tracked in `.aw-agent/DECISIONS.md` D97).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/agentRunsAuth.test.ts src/__tests__/agentRuns.routes.test.ts` — 15/15 passing (10 new + 5 existing route tests, unaffected)

title: fix(client-health): never-connected ad account is onboarding, not at-risk/blocked (ENG-2133)
body:
## Why
ENG-2128 (Eval System v2) slice 1 / **ENG-2133**: "Not connecting an ad account is flagged as churn risk. That is an onboarding/activation state, not churn." Two live paths produced the label:

- `assess_client_health` (Emma admin tool + MCP) returned `status: 'blocked'` with "No Meta ad account connected" for any client without a Meta ad account (CS-77 quoted exactly this).
- Partner-portal Client Health `deriveQuickStatus` returned red **At Risk** for no ads (and **Blocked** when nothing was set up), although an `onboarding` status already existed and was never used.

It also counted an ad account whose token had **expired** as "ads connected", because the record still exists.

## What
- `classifyMetaAdConnection()` (pure, no live API call; same timestamp rule as `isTokenNotExpired`): `never_connected | connected | expired`. A legacy `adAccount`, a refresh token, or a missing expiry all count as connected.
- `assess_client_health`: never_connected → **`onboarding`** ("Activation incomplete…"); expired → **`at-risk`** with the expiry timestamp; connected → unchanged logic.
- `list_all_clients` gains `ad_connection`; `has_ads` keeps its meaning for existing callers.
- MCP tool descriptions tell the model that onboarding is not churn.
- Partner portal: rule moved to `utils/clientHealthStatus.ts`; Onboarding chip + summary tile; neutral ads icon for not-yet-connected; falls back to `has_ads` when talking to an older backend.

## Safety
- Additive: no table, setting, flag or data change. Rollback = revert.
- Deploy order independent: the old portal ignores `ad_connection` and already renders `onboarding`; the new portal falls back to `has_ads`.
- No other readers of these fields in either repo or the customer portal (grep). ENG-502 fatigue capture (which calls `assess_client_health`) stays green.

## Tests
- TDD: 9 new backend tests red before the fix, green after.
- `clientHealth.test.ts` + `eng502.capture.test.ts`: 76/76. Adjacent suites (scheduledReportAccess, eng1967.evaluator, mcpGetAccountStatusExposure, agentModeService.skills): 154/154. Portal `clientHealthStatus.test.ts`: 5/5.
- Backend `npm run typecheck` and partner-portal `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- **Removed expectation:** `clientHealth.test.ts` asserted that a client with no ad account is `blocked|at-risk`. That was the defect ENG-2128 reports, so the test now asserts `onboarding`.

## Post-deploy check
Open Admin → Client Health: a client that never connected Meta shows **Onboarding** (not At Risk). `assess_client_health` for such a client returns `status: onboarding`.

Linear: ENG-2133 (parent ENG-2128)

title: fix(agent-mode): describe_image fictional-model claims + session model-decision drift
body:
## Summary

Two bugs found in a reported Emma agent-mode session, investigated against prod DynamoDB and raw EB logs for the incident window.

**Bug 1 — describe_image asserted unverifiable "fictional" claims.** A user uploaded a screenshot of AgentWeb's own model picker (real, currently-registered models) and asked which to use. `describe_image` had no system prompt, so the vision model rendered an unverifiable authenticity judgment ("these models don't exist... fictional mockup") off its training-data cutoff, and Emma repeated it to the user as fact.
- `agentModeService.ts`: added a system-message guardrail constraining the vision call to factual, observable description only.
- `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts`: added a Truthful Reporting rule against repeating a tool's own unverified opinion as settled fact.
- Live-reproduced against the real vision provider with the exact image + prompt from the incident: without the fix, the model calls the models fictional; with the fix, purely factual description, and Emma answers the actual question (even recommending a specific model).

**Bug 2 — session.llmModel and llmUsagePolicyDecision could silently drift apart.** The session's `llmModel` picker field read `gemini-3.8-flash`, but every turn's actual `llm` field (and raw EB logs for the window) show `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` ran the whole time. Root cause: `updateSessionLlmModel()` has several call sites (task-type model overrides, the picker's own PATCH endpoint, admin/plan swaps) that update `llmModel` alone, leaving a now-stale `llmUsagePolicyDecision` in place — a recurrence of the bug class documented at `agentModeController.ts:9042` (ENG-892/ENG-1313/ENG-1565/ENG-1579).
- `chatbotService.ts`: `updateSessionLlmModel` now `REMOVE`s the stale decision whenever `llmModel` changes without a fresh one, so a session record can never pair a decision with a model it doesn't describe.
- Verified live against the real dev DB: PATCHing a session's model through the actual 2-arg endpoint now correctly clears the decision instead of leaving it stale.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Targeted jest (24 suites / 346 tests covering describe_image, model routing, truthful-reporting prompt sections, toolDispatch) — all pass
- [x] New regression test `chatbotService.updateSessionLlmModelDrift.test.ts` covering both branches of the fix
- [x] Live end-to-end verification via the real `/api/agent-mode/generate` endpoint on a synced preview, using the actual reported screenshot and question
- [x] Live verification of the session-decision-clearing fix against the real dev DB
- [x] 360° review of every `describeImage()` caller and `updateSessionLlmModel()` call site — no other consumer relies on the old (buggy) behavior

**Note:** the local pre-push hook's broad jest run (225 suites, hub-file triggered) surfaced one unrelated pre-existing failure in `agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts` (model-catalog dominance scoring, from the separately-merged "refresh model catalog" work). Confirmed via diff that none of this PR's commits touch the registry/supersession files or that test — it's byte-identical to `main`'s current tip. Pushed past it per the hook's own printed bypass guidance; flagging here for visibility.

## Summary
Follow-up to #3069, which merged and deployed but did not actually work in production.

`app.use("/api/admin", adminRoutes)` applies `router.use(authenticateToken)`, `router.use(isAdmin)` with no path filter, so it ran for **every** request under `/api/admin/*`, including `/agent-runs`, before Express ever reached the D78 gate mounted later in `app.ts`. An unauthenticated request — with or without a correct `AW_AGENT_RUNS_SECRET` header — got rejected by this earlier catch-all's `authenticateToken` ("No token provided") before `authenticateAgentRunsSecretOrAdmin` ever ran.

**Found live**, after #3069 deployed, by smoke-testing the real production endpoint with the secret header before setting the actual secret value anywhere — not caught by `agentRunsAuth.test.ts`, which exercises the gate against an isolated Express app and never exhibited the real route-mounting interaction.

**Fix:** mount `/api/admin/agent-runs` *before* the catch-all `/api/admin` router, so the gate's own logic decides (secret header, or its own `authenticateToken`/`isAdmin` fallback identical to before), and the request never reaches the catch-all a second time either way.

## Test plan
- [x] New `agentRunsAuth.mountOrder.test.ts` imports the **real** `app` (not an isolated instance) so a future reordering of these mounts fails a test instead of silently regressing again.
- [x] Verified the new test actually catches the bug: ran it against the pre-fix mount order first (1 failure, exactly the correct-secret case), then restored the fix (3/3 passing).
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] All three agent-runs test files together — 18/18 passing

title: feat(eval): eval registry + audit with a validated-only gate (ENG-2134)
body:
## Why
ENG-2128 (Eval System v2) slice 1 / **ENG-2134**: "Audit current judges + account-health rules; list every metric, grader, and known false-positive", plus the eval registry from ENG-2128 §D. Principle 2: *unvalidated judges cannot gate or alert*.

## What
- `backend/src/loops/eval/evalRegistry.ts`: one typed list of every grader: 3 session judges, finalize guard, run verdict, Okareo hallucination check, enrichment golden set, #eval-queue, image like-rate, LP smoke test, and 4 account-health classifiers. Each entry records surface, grader type, source, model and family, consumers and known false-positive issues.
- `mayGate(id)` returns true only with a recorded validation of κ ≥ 0.6 on n ≥ 30 plus an evidence link. **No grader qualifies today.** ENG-2136 (the agreement harness) produces those validations.
- `backend/docs/evals/EVAL_REGISTRY.md`: the audit behind it.

## Audit findings (2026-09-25, origin/main + read-only prod)
1. The **Matt Judge** prompt is byte-identical to `default-scoring-prompt` and runs on the same model, so it is not an independent judge.
2. Every session judge runs on Gemini, and so does the agent default (`gemini-3.8-flash`). ENG-2128 requires a different family.
3. Only 44% of sessions have a score (8,462 of 19,293), written lazily when someone opens the dashboard or runs the `get_chat_history` backfill.
4. Only 10 sessions carry a human `adminOverride` score, and there is no agreement code anywhere.
5. The Daily Satisfaction Score Report schedule has been paused since 2026-08-18.
6. The finalize guard is off in prod. Okareo checks exist only inside Okareo. There is no automated creative grader.

No customer content or prompt text is committed, only ids, lengths and dates.

## Scope / safety
Adds a module, a doc and a test. The registry isn't imported by runtime code yet, so behaviour is unchanged. Rollback = revert.

## Tests
`evalRegistry.test.ts` 4/4: unique ids; no gate without a qualifying validation; every validation has an evidence link; every code source path exists. `npm run typecheck` clean.

title: feat(eval): judge-vs-human agreement metrics — kappa, P/R, CIs (ENG-2136)
body:
## Why
ENG-2128 (Eval System v2) / **ENG-2136**. Principle 2: every judge reports agreement with humans (Cohen's κ ≥ 0.6, precision/recall per failure class), and an unvalidated judge cannot gate or alert. Principle 4: report confidence intervals and sample counts, and compare variants pairwise. The ENG-2134 audit found no agreement code anywhere in the repo.

## What
`backend/src/loops/eval/agreement.ts` (pure, no I/O):
- `cohensKappa` for nominal labels, and `weightedKappa` (linear or quadratic) for ordinal 1–5 judge scores
- `perClassMetrics`: precision/recall/F1/support per class, with human labels as truth; `null` instead of 0/0
- `wilsonInterval`, a seeded percentile `bootstrapCI` (reproducible), and `agreementReport` (n, observed agreement, κ with CI, per-class)
- `pairwiseWinRate`: ties count half, with a Wilson CI on decisive comparisons
- `toGraderValidation`: builds the record the eval registry's `mayGate()` reads (#3073). It's structurally typed, so this PR doesn't depend on #3073.

The runner that feeds golden-set cases through a grader lands with the golden-set store (ENG-2135 / ENG-2147).

## Safety
Nothing imports this module yet, so runtime behaviour is unchanged. Rollback = revert.

## Tests
`agreement.test.ts` 14/14. Expected values are the textbook 2×2 case (κ = 0.4) and independently computed reference values (3-class κ 0.4286, quadratic 0.3846, linear 0.4074, Wilson 8/10 = [0.4902, 0.9433]). None of them were read back from the module. `npm run typecheck` is clean.

title: ENG-2139: advisory creative gates (placement spec, size, broken render) + Story/Reel label fix
body:
## Why

ENG-2139 (ENG-2128 T7). Nothing checked generated creatives automatically. `imageGeneration.ts` silently turned an unsupported ratio or an unparseable size into 1:1, and a pixel size like 1200x628 was snapped to 16:9 without any signal (brain §2.3, F8). The ENG-421 audit also found that `onboardingAdImageService.ts` called 1080x1350 "Story/Reel". Real Story/Reel is 9:16 1080x1920; 1080x1350 is the 4:5 feed portrait.

## What

1. **Label fix (ENG-421).** In the Brick 8 system prompt and the per-variant Layer 1 line, 1080x1350 is now labelled "Meta Feed — portrait 4:5". The size itself is unchanged, so only the placement name the model sees is different.
2. **Placement spec table** (`services/creativePlacementSpecs.ts`):
   - Meta feed 1:1 1080x1080
   - Meta feed 4:5 1080x1350
   - Meta story/reel 9:16 1080x1920
   - The two Google image field types the Ads integration attaches: `SQUARE_MARKETING_IMAGE` 1200x1200 and `MARKETING_IMAGE` 1.91:1 1200x628

   Each entry has a minimum size, an aspect tolerance and the platform upload limit (Meta 30 MB, Google 5120 KB). Meta uploads are also downscaled to 1936px / 8 MB by `resizeImageForMeta`, so that internal cap is not treated as a defect.
3. **`services/creativeGates.ts`** is pure (`evaluateCreativeGates(measurement, request)`). `runCreativeGates(buffer)` measures the image with sharp, which is already a dependency, and never throws. The checks are:
   - `decode`: the bytes don't decode, or the image has no dimensions
   - `blank_render`: luminance std-dev on a 64x64 thumbnail is below 4, which catches flat white/black and fully transparent images
   - `aspect_ratio`: compared with the requested placement or ratio
   - `dimensions`: at least the placement minimum
   - `file_size`: within the platform limit
   - `aspect_fallback`: the Gemini 3 path substituted the requested shape

   `fitsPlacements` lists every placement the image would be accepted for.
4. **Silent-fallback detection.** `convertSizeToAspectRatio` now delegates to `resolveGeminiAspectRatio`. That function keeps the original snap values and tie order and also reports `unsupported_ratio`, `unparseable_size` or `nearest_ratio` (more than 3% off). A sweep of 74,018 WxH sizes gave identical output to the old code.
5. **Runs at generation time, advisory only.** `ImageService.generateImage` runs the gates on the final bytes, logs failures with `console.warn`, and returns the verdict as `result.gates`. A failing or erroring gate never fails generation. The results are stored on:
   - the agent-mode `generate_image` human-eval candidate, as `AW-HumanEvalQueue.creativeGates`
   - each onboarding `adImageResult` variant, as `gates`

   Both are additive optional attributes on items the app already writes. There is no new table, key or index.
6. **Registry.** `creative-deterministic-gates` is added to `evalRegistry.ts` (graderType `code`, no validation recorded, so `mayGate` stays false) and to `docs/evals/EVAL_REGISTRY.md`.

### Deferred (on purpose)

- **OCR text-area ratio / spelling.** tesseract.js is not a backend dependency. By default it downloads its language data from a CDN at runtime. Doing this cleanly would mean adding tesseract.js plus its wasm core, vendoring `eng.traineddata` (several MB of binary) into git, and spending seconds of CPU per image on the API instances. That doesn't meet the "offline, no runtime download" bar, and a partial OCR would give misleading scores, so it is left for a follow-up.
- **Landing pages.** Smoke-test and launch-readiness results are already stored with pass/fail and reasons on `AW-LandingPages` (`smokeTestResult`, `getLandingPageLaunchReadiness`). Nothing reads a combined gate shape yet, and the LP human-eval candidate is created before the smoke test finishes. An adapter would be dead code, so it waits for its consumer (T4 / dashboard).
- **Runway.** Runway returns a remote URL rather than bytes, so no gates run there. Nothing is fetched just to check it.
- **Archetype layout text.** The seeded `AW-PromptTemplates` rows still head the portrait layout "Story 4:5:". Those rows live in prod and are admin-edited, so changing the constants in `brick5Archetypes.ts` would not change prod. Editing the rows is a prod config write, so it is out of scope here.

## Safety

- Advisory only: nothing blocks, and every gate path is wrapped so an error returns `undefined`.
- No prod data or config writes and no schema change. The new attributes are optional, and older items read as absent.
- Cost: one extra sharp decode per generated image. Measured at about 135 ms for a 4096² PNG, and it runs on the libuv threadpool, not the event loop.
- Rollback: revert the PR. Stored `creativeGates` / `gates` attributes are ignored by older code.

## Tests

- New: `creativeGates.test.ts` (14 tests) and `imageGeneration.creativeGates.test.ts` (3 tests). Fixtures are rendered in-process with sharp, with no binary files in git:
  - clean pass
  - wrong aspect (a 4:5 request that came back square)
  - undersized
  - oversized (tested through the measurement)
  - blank
  - fully transparent
  - undecodable bytes
  - Gemini substitution cases
- Extended: `onboardingAdImageService.test.ts` (label fix and gates kept on each variant), `humanEvalService.test.ts`, `autoHumanEvalService.test.ts` and `agentModeService.generateImage.test.ts` (gate result reaches the candidate).
- **Red → green:** with the five changed service files restored to `origin/main`, 8 of the new tests fail, including the "labels 1080x1350 as a 4:5 feed portrait, not Story/Reel" test. The two new test files fail on main because the modules don't exist there. With the branch, all pass.
- Suites run on the branch, all green: creativeGates, imageGeneration.creativeGates, imageGeneration, imageGeneration.likeness-fixes, imageGeneration.backgroundRemoval, onboardingAdImageService, humanEvalService, humanEval.routes, autoHumanEvalService, emmaTools.enqueueHumanEval, agentModeService.generateImage(.brandLogo), agentModeService.removeC2PA, eng1961.residualAttribution, evalRegistry.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean. `lintdiff` found 0 added-line findings.
- I pushed with `--no-verify`. The pre-push hook failed only on `agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts` › ENG-1786 legacy rows, and that test fails the same way on plain `origin/main`.

Linear: ENG-2139 (parent ENG-2128)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Low — creative gates are advisory and do not block image generation. The change adds placement specifications, evaluates generated images, and optionally stores gate results. It relabels 1080×1350 onboarding ads as Meta Feed portrait 4:5.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(eval): offline agent graders — task success, tool correctness, groundedness, cost per success (ENG-2137)
body:
## Why

ENG-2137 (T5 of ENG-2128, Eval System v2, surface A). Today the only agent-side code grader is the run verdict (`runRecorder.computeRunVerdict`). It is a heuristic over failure counts and it does not check whether the task got done. The finalize guard, which would give us groundedness data, is off in prod, so there are zero `claim_mismatch` rows (F5). Nothing flags the ENG-286 class either: a Google Ads write that returns `success: true` and changes nothing. ENG-592's boundary contract was never built.

## What

All of it is offline and read-only. No runtime behaviour changes.

- **`loops/eval/agentGraders.ts`**: pure, typed graders.
  - `gradeTaskSuccess`: returns `success | failure | excluded` plus a reason. It applies the ENG-1710 relaxed rule: the plan counts as complete with at most one pending step, and only if that step is the last one. It excludes runs that ended on a crash placeholder, sessions with no work plan, sessions with zero tool calls, and plans that were never engaged. To avoid relying on the agent's own report, a completed step whose `requiredFunctionCalls` never succeeded fails. So does a plan finished while ENG-1811 removed-step debt is still outstanding.
  - `gradeToolCorrectness`: flags `invalid_args`, `policy_blocked`, `uninstalled_tool` and `repeated_failure` (3+ in one run, the runRecorder threshold) from `Dev-AW-LoopEvents`. From the session ledger it flags `write_without_read_back` and `repeated_mutation` (the ENG-286 retry). A write counts as read back when the tool read the object itself (`readBackVerified`, `spend_cap_verified`, `verified`, `drift`), or when a later successful read on the same account either names the object's id or reads every object of that type. For a create, a later successful call that uses the new object's id also counts. A later read of the same type that only names other objects (usually a parent, such as keywords read by campaign id) is reported as `write_read_back_unconfirmed` and does not fail the session.
  - `gradeGroundedness`: uses the finalize guard's own lexicon and claim-to-tool matchers, with no LLM call. Every lexicon hit counts as a claim, so it over-reports compared with the runtime guard, which asks a judge. Treat it as an upper bound until ENG-2150 shadow data exists.
  - `efficiencyMetrics` / `aggregateByModelAndTaskType`: turns, tokens and cost (settled `AW-SpendEvents` by `references.sessionId`) plus tool latency p50/p95 (LoopEvents `durationMs`) per successful task. Groups are model × task type, with n and a Wilson CI from ENG-2136's `wilsonInterval`.
- **`loops/eval/agentGraderLoader.ts`**: a thin loader behind a port that only exposes `query`/`scan`. Its normalizers are pure and tested.
- **`scripts/evalAgentGraders.ts`**: CLI, `--from/--to [--limit] [--per-session] [--json]`. It prints ids, tool names and counts only, never message text or plan titles.
- **Registry**: `agent-task-success`, `agent-tool-correctness` and `agent-groundedness-offline` are added as unvalidated code graders, so `mayGate` is false for all three. `EVAL_REGISTRY.md` is updated to match.
- `finalizeGuard.claimLooselyMatchedByLedger` is now **exported** so the grader can separate ambiguous claims from unbacked ones the same way the guard does. That export is the only change to runtime code, and the guard behaves the same.

### Where this departs from the ticket text (checked against the code)

- **Signature of the tool-correctness grader.** The ticket says `gradeToolCorrectness(runEvents)`. It takes `{ events, ledger }` instead, because `agent_tool_succeeded` rows carry no arguments. Tool args, and so the object being written, exist only in `AW-ChatMessages` `metadata.toolCalls`. I checked the field names on prod rows, read-only and printing names only.
- **Where the model comes from.** The session's `llmModel` is the model picker, not the model that ran (ENG-892). The model is taken from `agent_run_verdict.llmModel` (the end-of-run model), then `agent_run_started`, then the operation with the most spend.
- **Task type.** Sessions store no category, so task type is a keyword heuristic over the plan title, as in ENG-1710.

### First run on prod (read-only, 2026-09-11..25, 600 sessions)

- **Task success:** 39 success (35 complete, 4 with one trailing pending step), 12 failure, 549 excluded (537 had no work plan).
- **Ad-platform writes:** 402 in 17 sessions. 33 were never read back at all (8%). 137 were read-back unconfirmed (34%). 2 were repeated identical writes.
- **Loop-event findings:** 260 invalid_args, 56 repeated_failure, 53 policy_blocked, 13 uninstalled_tool.
- **Groundedness:** 45 sessions ungrounded by the lexicon, including 21 `schedule_created` and 10 `post_published`. This is an upper bound.
- **Cost:** most graded groups have n < 20, so the per-model × task-type cost numbers are not yet comparable.

## Out of scope

- **pass^k:** needs re-running tasks in the sandbox (ENG-1906).
- **Enabling finalize-guard shadow mode:** OPS-5 / ENG-2150.
- **Changing the Google Ads / Meta tool implementations:** the runtime half of ENG-592.
- **κ against human labels:** needs the T3 golden set (ENG-2135) plus the T4 harness. The registry records the validation once it exists.

## Safety

- No writes anywhere. The loader's port has no put, update or delete.
- No flags, config or tables change. There is no OPS step.
- Nothing calls the graders at runtime.
- Rollback: revert the PR.

## Tests

- `agentGraders.test.ts` (43) covers every grader rule. It includes an ENG-286-shaped success-but-no-op that `computeRunVerdict` grades `ok` and the new grader flags. The same case is replayed through the ENG-591 harness (`evaluateReplayCase`): it is **red** on the run verdict and **green** on the grader.
- `agentGraderLoader.test.ts` (10) covers the ledger, final reply, placeholder, events, spend and model normalizers, plus pagination, limit and lookback against a fake read-only reader.
- **Red before the change:**
  - With `finalizeGuard.ts` restored to `origin/main`, 4 groundedness tests fail.
  - Without the new modules, both suites fail with "Cannot find module".
- **Green after:** 7 suites / 85 tests pass, including `evalRegistry`, `agreement`, `failureReplaySuite` and both finalize-guard suites.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean. Diff-scoped lint (`lintdiff.py`) reports 0 findings on 7 files.

Linear: ENG-2137 (parent ENG-2128)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Low

Adds offline, read-only graders for task success, tool correctness, groundedness, and efficiency, plus a session loader and reporting CLI. Registers the graders as unvalidated. Exports `claimLooselyMatchedByLedger` without changing its behavior. The graders do not add a runtime path, so production impact and rollback complexity are limited.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: ENG-2143: account-health classifier (activation / at-risk / healthy) + backtest, inert behind flag
body:
## Why

ENG-2143 (ENG-2128 T11). Supersedes ENG-2016, ENG-1342 and ENG-1913. The ENG-2128 brain findings behind it:
- **F1:** three code paths say "at risk" when an ad account was never connected. The renewal cron (`renewalIntegrationHealthCron.ts`) is off in prod because it alerted from stale onboarding intent and re-alerted every 24h. The ENG-1342 wiring in `metaTrackingMonitorCron` only logs with `console.warn`.
- **F10:** we have very few churn positives, so the backtest has to report n and confidence intervals, not just a point estimate.
- **F15:** a signal we did not read must never become a confident negative.
- **Decision D6:** the current ads requirement is recorded on `AW-AccountCapabilityRequirements` (written by OPS-4), and activation nudges go to CS, never to oncall.

## What

1. **`services/accountHealthClassifier.ts`** is a pure classifier. It returns `activation_incomplete | at_risk | healthy | insufficient_evidence` plus an evidence list (`risk / activation / gap / context`) and a confidence grade.
   - **Connection:** Meta is read through the existing `classifyMetaAdConnection`. Google Ads and LinkedIn Ads use the same token rule, now exported as `hasUsableAdToken`. No connection logic is copied.
   - **Never connected:** always `activation_incomplete`, even when ads are contracted. The acceptance criterion says no account is labelled at-risk or churn only because it never connected an ad account.
   - **Expired connection:** `at_risk` only when the ads requirement is current:
     - `requirementSource: contracted`, or
     - `recent_ads_action` verified within 30 days, or
     - ad spend in the last 30 days.

     Onboarding intent alone, a stale ads action, or a missing field all give `insufficient_evidence` (ENG-2016 AC1/AC2).
   - **Zero delivery (ENG-1913):** an enabled campaign with a positive approved budget and 0 impressions and 0 clicks more than 24h after going live counts as stuck. Paused campaigns are excluded.
   - **Payments:** an unresolved `payment_failed` within 35 days, or `past_due`, is a risk.
   - **Activity recency:** context only (ENG-2016 AC5). Engagement never creates a risk and never hides one.
2. **`cron/accountHealthClassifierCron.ts`** replaces the log-only path, behind `ACCOUNT_HEALTH_ALERTS_ENABLED` (default off).
   - `at_risk` goes to `sendAgentModeOncallAlert` only once `mayGate('account-health-classifier')` is true (ENG-2128 principle 2: unvalidated graders cannot alert). Until then it is a `needs_review` log line, which escalates to oncall on the first run after a validation is recorded. It fires at most once per account + billing cycle (`current_period_end`) + episode. It fires again only for new risk evidence, a new cycle, or a leave-and-return transition (ENG-2016 AC3). Each account keeps one tracked issue via `Alert Class: account-health:<userId>`.
   - An active ENG-1541 correction downgrades a connection- or delivery-only risk to needs-review (AC4).
   - The alert body carries the requirement, previous state, transition reason, billing cycle, next actor, confidence, and every evidence item (AC6).
   - `activation_incomplete` produces a `cs_nudge` log line only. `insufficient_evidence` produces a `needs_review` log line and does not end an open episode, so one failed read cannot trigger a second alert.
   - Dedupe state lives in its own `account_health_signal` row per account, claimed with a version check. Every instance runs the cron, and an in-memory window would reset on each deploy.
3. **`scripts/eng2149-backfill-requirement-source.ts`** is the OPS-4 backfill (see Safety).
4. **`scripts/eng2143-account-health-backtest.ts`** is a read-only backtest (results below).
5. **Eval registry:** added `account-health-classifier` (graderType `code`, no validation). The registry test stays green and `mayGate` stays false.

### Why I did not touch `metaTrackingMonitorCron`
The ENG-1342 block is left as is, and this sweep is the visible signal. Two reasons:
- Its pixel flags repeat faults that the tracking monitor already alerts through its own alert sink.
- Its connectivity check (`evaluateAdConnectivity`) needs a numeric future `token_expires_at`. That flags every Google Ads account that relies on a refresh token as disconnected: all 16 Google Ads connections in prod have an expired access-token timestamp and a refresh token. Surfacing that check would be a false-positive generator.

## Backtest (read-only against prod, 2026-09-25, counts only)

Setup:
- Five back-to-back 30-day windows, with cutoffs 2026-04-28, 05-28, 06-27, 07-27 and 08-26.
- **Churn** = a dated `subscription_canceled` event in AW-PaymentHistory within the window.
- **Signals** are rebuilt as of each cutoff. Current `subscription_status` is not used, because it would leak the outcome.

| | n (account-cutoff pairs) | churned | predicted at_risk | TP | precision [95% Wilson] | recall [95% Wilson] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pooled | 92 | 8 | 1 | 1 | 1.00 [0.21, 1.00] | 0.13 [0.02, 0.47] |

State by truth (pooled):
- **churned (8):** activation_incomplete 4, at_risk 1, healthy 3
- **retained (84):** activation_incomplete 61, healthy 23

**How to read this:**
- There is one prediction and 8 positives. The precision point estimate of 1.00 means nothing, because the interval runs from 0.21 to 1.00. The ticket's precision ≥ 0.8 target cannot be confirmed or refuted on this data.
- 18 accounts are `canceled` with no dated cancel event (they cancelled before PaymentHistory existed), so they are excluded. Pairs from the same account across cutoffs are not independent.
- Recall is low by design: at-risk needs hard behavioural evidence.
- Known gaps in the historical data:
  - No stored per-campaign delivery data, so zero delivery is never evaluated in the backtest.
  - The requirement fields do not exist yet.
  - Refresh tokens and the legacy `adAccount` field are read as current values.
- Half the churners never connected an ad account. That is not predictive: 73% of retained accounts also never connected one. It supports keeping "never connected" as an activation state, not a risk state.

**Dry run of the live sweep (read-only, today):** 24 paying accounts, of which 14 are `activation_incomplete`, 1 is `at_risk` (past due) and 9 are `healthy`. Turning the flag on today would log 1 needs-review line (the at-risk account; oncall stays closed until the classifier is validated) and 14 CS nudge lines on the first run, then nothing until something changes.

## Safety

- **Inert.** `server.ts` schedules the sweep only when `ACCOUNT_HEALTH_ALERTS_ENABLED=true`. A direct non-dry run refuses to write or send without the flag, or on an instance that graceful shutdown is draining. Even with the flag on, oncall is closed until the registry records a qualifying validation. `RENEWAL_HEALTH_ALERTS_ENABLED` stays unset. Nothing in this PR writes to prod.
- **OPS-4 (ENG-2149).** New optional fields on `AW-AccountCapabilityRequirements` rows keyed `(userId, capability='ad_platform_integration')`:
  - `requirementSource`: `contracted | recent_ads_action | onboarding_intent`. Absent means unknown.
  - `requirementVerifiedAt`: ISO timestamp. `recent_ads_action` counts as current for 30 days after it.
  - `requirementSetBy`: an admin email or `eng-2149-backfill`.

  Run order:
  1. `npx ts-node --transpile-only src/scripts/eng2149-backfill-requirement-source.ts [--contracted=<userId,...>]`. This is a dry run. Today it plans 7 rows as `onboarding_intent`, with 0 already set.
  2. `ENG2149_BACKFILL_APPLY=AW-AccountCapabilityRequirements npx ts-node --transpile-only src/scripts/eng2149-backfill-requirement-source.ts --apply [--contracted=...]`. Writes are conditional on the row existing and `requirementSource` being unset.
  3. Rollback: the same command with `--rollback --apply` and the same `--set-by` the apply run used. It removes only the fields that run wrote.

  Deciding which accounts are `contracted` is a human call. The backfill marks everything `onboarding_intent` unless ids are passed.
- **Enabling the flag (OPS; I have not set it).** Set `ACCOUNT_HEALTH_ALERTS_ENABLED=true` on `Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`. After that the sweep also writes rows `(userId, capability='account_health_signal')` holding `state`, `stateSince`, `lastEpisodeKey`, `lastSignalCodes`, `lastSignalAt`, `lastSignalChannel` and `version`. Rollback: unset the flag. Those rows are ignored by every other reader and can be deleted.

## Not in this PR (remainder, precise)

1. **Live campaign-delivery input for ENG-1913.** AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots only stores campaigns that delivered, with no status or budget. Filling `CampaignDeliveryInput` needs a new read-only adapter: Meta `act_<id>/campaigns?fields=status,daily_budget,start_time,insights{impressions,clicks}` and Google Ads GAQL `campaign.status, campaign_budget.amount_micros, metrics.impressions, metrics.clicks`. title: feat(eval): golden-set store, seed builder, labelling API and validation runner (ENG-2135)
body:
## Why

ENG-2135 (ENG-2128 T3): every judge needs a labelled golden set before it may gate or alert (principle 2). Decision D2: case ids + labels live in a private production store and content is fetched at run time, never in git (generalises ENG-1314 option 3; supersedes ENG-1314 and ENG-972). Brain findings used: F4 (no human session labels; 10 `adminOverride` rows), F7 (judge false-positive catalogue), F13/F14, F10 (account ground truth).

This is PR 1 of 2: backend store, seed builder, labelling API, replay-fixture source and validation runner. The partner-portal labelling page is a separate PR.

## What

- **`loops/eval/goldenSet.ts`**: the case schema `{caseId, surface, taskType, sourceRef, criteria[], labels{criterion: pass|fail|na}, notes, labeller, labelledAt, split, version, schemaVersion, seedSource, createdAt, replay?}` with validation. Criteria per surface: agent = task_success, tool_correctness, groundedness, instruction_compliance. Creative = the 7 ENG-421 criteria. Account = activation_incomplete / at_risk / healthy, where `pass` means the state applies. The dev/test split comes from a sha256 of the case id, with 60% going to test so a 50-case surface can reach the registry's `MIN_VALIDATION_N` (30).
- **`loops/eval/goldenSetStore.ts`**: a typed DynamoDB adapter. It takes its table name from **`EVAL_GOLDEN_CASES_TABLE`**. While that is unset the store reports not provisioned, and every read and write throws `GoldenSetStoreNotProvisionedError` without calling DynamoDB. Seed writes are idempotent (`attribute_not_exists`) and never overwrite labels. Label saves use optimistic concurrency on `version`.
- **`scripts/create-tables.ts`**: `createEvalGoldenCasesTable` (`AW-EvalGoldenCases`), following the script's existing pattern.
- **`loops/eval/goldenSetSeed.ts` + `scripts/seedGoldenCases.ts`**: builds the case lists from projected, read-only scans (ids and flags only):
  - agent: sessions named in the F7 false-positive catalogue, plus `adminOverride` sessions, plus the sessions behind the ENG-1312 replay fixtures.
  - creative: AW-HumanEvalQueue image and landing-page candidates that have feedback from their own reviewer (Matt).
  - account: canceled vs active AW-Users by userId, balanced between the two, admins excluded.

  The catalogue input is an **off-repo** JSON file because it holds production session ids. Selection is deterministic and independent of the split. The script is a dry run by default; `--write` refuses and exits 1 when `EVAL_GOLDEN_CASES_TABLE` is unset.
- **`routes/adminGoldenSet.ts`**, mounted at `/api/admin/eval/golden-cases`. Endpoints: `GET /status`, `GET ?surface=&split=`, `GET /:caseId`, `PUT /:caseId/labels`. Access is `authenticateToken` + `isAdmin` (delegated sessions are refused). Until the store is provisioned it returns 503 `golden_set_store_not_provisioned`; a stale `expectedVersion` returns 409.
- **`loops/eval/agentModeReplayFixtureSource.ts` + `scripts/runReplayFixtures.ts`**: for every ENG-1312 fixture that a golden case links to (`replay: {fixtureId, messageIndex}`), the real turn is read from AW-ChatMessages at run time. This is a direct read-only query; it does not go through `chatbotDb.getChatSession`, which can migrate or repair rows. Fixtures with no store or no link keep their synthetic placeholders. The checker and thresholds are unchanged. `agentModeReplayFixtures.ts` changes only in its doc comments.
- **`loops/eval/runValidation.ts` + `scripts/runGraderValidation.ts`**: for a registry grader id, the runner loads that surface's test split, gets the grader's verdicts, and prints `agreementReport` per criterion plus `toGraderValidation` for the grader's primary criterion. It never edits the registry. Pairs are binary only: human `na`/unlabelled cases and grader abstentions are counted separately and never scored as agreement. Adapters included:
  - `session-judge-general`, `-fangfang`, `-matt`: their stored verdicts; a dimension ≥ 4 on the 1–5 scale counts as pass.
  - `agent-task-success`, `agent-tool-correctness`, `agent-groundedness-offline` (#3076): run live on the case's session through a read-only loader.

## Findings / deviations

- **Split and selection were correlated in the first draft.** Ordering candidates by the same hash as the split put 29 of 30 account cases in test. Selection now uses a salted hash. There is a test for this, and it fails against the old ordering.
- **`length-limit-ignored-1` is not linked to real content.** Its ENG-1309 threshold (≤ ~6,000 chars; 10,524 at the time) measures the *produced document*, which lives in a tool artifact. The chat reply at that turn is 1,043 chars, so real content would pass. Linking it would need a harness change, which is out of scope, so it keeps its placeholder.
- **Pending fixtures are not linked either.** `unnecessary-permission-1` and `pushback-not-rewarded-1` have no numeric threshold, so linking them adds nothing yet.
- **Account test split is small.** With 30 account cases, about 18 land in test, below `MIN_VALIDATION_N` = 30. The account classifier cannot qualify for gating on this set alone; F10's small n applies.
- **ENG-1710's 225 labelled sessions** are off-repo (Harsha's machine) and are not included; the catalogue input can take them later.
- **Pre-existing, not changed here:** `GET /api/human-eval/candidates/:candidateId` has no admin check, unlike its list route. The labelling UI uses it; worth a separate fix.

## Safety

- **Inert until OPS-2.** With `EVAL_GOLDEN_CASES_TABLE` unset, the API answers 503 and the scripts refuse to write. Nothing reads or writes the store at runtime otherwise; there is no cron or hook.
- **No production writes in this PR.** Every production read was a projected, read-only scan or query. Output is counts only.
- **No customer data in git.** A grep of the added lines for UUIDs, the known session prefixes and customer names finds only synthetic `@example.com` addresses.
- **Rollback:** revert the PR. After OPS-2, unsetting the env var makes the store inert again.
- **Data-plane note (CLAUDE.md):** this PR adds a table definition. It is created only by OPS-2.

## OPS-2 (ENG-2147): exact steps

Do **not** run the whole `create-tables.ts` against production: it would also try to create every other table in the script that does not exist. Create just this table:

```bash
aws dynamodb create-table --region us-west-2 --table-name AW-EvalGoldenCases \
  --attribute-definitions AttributeName=caseId,AttributeType=S AttributeName=surface,AttributeType=S \
  --key-schema AttributeName=caseId,KeyType=HASH \
  --global-secondary-indexes '[{"IndexName":"SurfaceIndex","KeySchema":[{"AttributeName":"surface","KeyType":"HASH"},{"AttributeName":"caseId","KeyType":"RANGE"}],"Projection":{"ProjectionType":"ALL"}}]' \
  --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST
aws dynamodb wait table-exists --table-name AW-EvalGoldenCases
aws dynamodb update-continuous-backups --table-name AW-EvalGoldenCases \
  --point-in-time-recovery-specification PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true
```

- **Keys:** `caseId` (S) HASH, no sort key. GSI `SurfaceIndex`: `surface` (S) HASH, `caseId` (S) RANGE, projection ALL.
- **IAM for the backend role (EB instance profile):** `dynamodb:GetItem`, `PutItem`, `UpdateItem`, `Query` on `arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:<acct>:table/AW-EvalGoldenCases` and `.../table/AW-EvalGoldenCases/index/SurfaceIndex`. No Scan and no DeleteItem are needed. For the Atem runner and seed host: the same, plus read access it already has on AW-ChatSessions, AW-ChatMessages, AW-HumanEvalQueue, AW-Users and Dev-AW-LoopEvents.
- **EB env:** `EVAL_GOLDEN_CASES_TABLE=AW-EvalGoldenCases` on `Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`, after the table exists.
- **Verify:** `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin>" https://api.agentweb.pro/api/admin/eval/golden-cases/status` should return `provisioned: true`. Then put, get and delete one synthetic row (for example `caseId=agent#sessionId#ops2-probe`) with the CLI.
- **Seed (after OPS-2):**
  ```
  EVAL_GOLDEN_CASES_TABLE=AW-EvalGoldenCases npx ts-node --transpile-only src/scripts/seedGoldenCases.ts \
    --fp-catalogue <off-repo catalogue JSON> --write
  ```
  The catalogue file is at `~/.cache/eng2128/eng2135-fp-catalogue.json` on the ENG-2128 box (never commit it).
- **Rollback:** delete the (empty or seed-only) table and unset the env var.

## Tests

- **New suites:** 6, 50 tests (`goldenSet`, `goldenSetStore`, `goldenSetSeed`, `agentModeReplayFixtureSource`, `runValidation`, `routes/__tests__/adminGoldenSet`). They cover schema validation, the store adapter with mocked DynamoDB, not-provisioned behaviour, route auth (401 with no token, 403 for a customer, 403 for a delegated admin; admin OK; 503; 409), the deterministic split, and the runner math on fixture labels (kappa 0.70 on a known 2×2).
- **Also run:** `agentModeReplayFixtures`, `evalRegistry`, `agreement`, `agentGraders`, `agentGraderLoader`. All 11 suites, 140 tests, green.
- **Red→green:** on `origin/main` all 6 new suites fail, because the modules do not exist. The seed split-independence test fails against the unsalted ordering and passes after.
- **Read-only checks against production data:**
  - Seed dry run: agent 50/50 (eligible 64: 2 replay, 10 adminOverride, 38 catalogue selected); creative 50/50 (eligible 62); account 30/30 (eligible 53). 38 catalogue ids matched no session; they are user ids and other non-session ids in the tickets.
  - Replay with real content: `yesno-terse-1` FAILS at 3,271 chars > 600 and `yesno-terse-2` FAILS at 215 words > 150. The gate catches the real ENG-1309 regressions, which closes ENG-1312's AC3 gap. With the store unset, all fixtures stay placeholders and pass.
  - The agent-grader and judge adapters were run on three real sessions. The first draft's loop-events filter on the `tsSession` sort key was rejected by DynamoDB; it now filters on `dimensions.sessionId`.
- **Checks:** `npm run typecheck` clean; `lintdiff` 0 findings on added lines; `eslint --max-warnings 0` clean on every touched file.

title: feat(portal): admin Eval Labelling page for golden sets (ENG-2135)
body:
## Why

ENG-2135 (ENG-2128 T3), PR 2 of 2. This adds the admin page for binary per-criterion labelling of golden-set cases. The backend API (store, seed, `/api/admin/eval/golden-cases`) is in PR #3078. **Merge that one first**: until it is deployed, this page shows a load error instead of cases.

## What

- **New page:** `partner-portal/src/pages/EvalLabelling.tsx` at `/eval-labelling`. It is behind `AdminRoute`, is registered in the navigation catalog (Operate group, after Agent Runs), and has a page title. It follows the AgentRunsInspector pattern: the `useAuth()` token (never `localStorage`), an admin check, and MUI.
- **Case list:** shows one surface at a time (agent / creative / account health), ordered least-labelled first, with split and labelled counts.
- **Source view:** each case's source is fetched **at view time through existing admin APIs** and nothing is stored:
  - agent: `GET /api/admin/chat-sessions?sessionId=` (transcript, plus a link to the AgentRun Inspector)
  - creative: `GET /api/human-eval/candidates/:id` (request, output, image, reviewer feedback)
  - account: `GET /api/admin/users/:userId` (a whitelist of account fields, plus a profile link)
- **Grader verdicts are hidden on purpose.** Judge scores and client-health status are not shown, because the labels are the truth those graders are validated against.
- **Label form:**
  - Pass / Fail / N/A toggles for each criterion, with a one-line definition for each. Agent: task success, tool correctness, groundedness, instruction compliance. Creative: the 7 ENG-421 criteria. Account: activation incomplete, at risk, healthy.
  - A note field.
  - Save calls `PUT …/labels` with `expectedVersion`. A 409 tells the labeller to reload instead of overwriting.
- **Inert until OPS-2 (ENG-2147).** `/status` returns `provisioned: false`, and the page then shows "golden-set store is not provisioned yet (OPS-2, ENG-2147)" and loads nothing else.

## Safety

- Admin-only in the UI (`AdminRoute` plus a page-level check) and in the backend (`authenticateToken` + `isAdmin`, which refuses delegated sessions).
- The page only reads existing admin APIs and writes through the new admin route. It adds no new data exposure.

title: fix(human-eval): candidate lookup is admin-or-owner only (ENG-2154)
body:
## Why
**ENG-2154** (child of ENG-2128), found while building ENG-2135's labelling page (#3079): `GET /api/human-eval/candidates/:candidateId` required only a login. Any authenticated user could read any candidate by id, including the originating user's email (added in ENG-1854 / #2939), session ids, the artifact URL and reviewer feedback. Candidate ids are random UUIDs, which limits exposure, but it is still an authorization gap on customer data.

## What
- Admins read any candidate. A user can read only candidates whose `userId` is theirs.
- Everything else gets **404** (not 403), so a guessed id does not confirm that the candidate exists.

## Safety
Neither portal calls this route on main (grep of partner-portal, customer-portal and backend), so nothing that works today breaks. ENG-2135's admin page (#3079) is the first consumer, and it runs as an admin. Rollback = revert.

## Tests
`humanEval.routes.test.ts` 21/21. The 5 new cases cover admin, owner, another user (404), an ownerless candidate (admin only) and an unknown id. The two cross-user cases fail on origin/main and pass with the fix. Typecheck is clean, and lint reports 0 findings on added lines.
