title: feat(creative): ENG-421 rubric judge — 7 binary criteria + pairwise, advisory and off by default (ENG-2140)
body:
## Why

ENG-2140 (ENG-2128 T8). Nothing scores a generated creative today; creative feedback is free-text Slack replies to one reviewer (ENG-2128 F8). ENG-421 produced a 7-criterion launch-ready floor that Harsha adopted on 2026-08-17 (hook clarity, offer specificity, proof integrity, brand fidelity, format readiness, policy/compliance risk, media-buyer usefulness). It was never implemented. This PR encodes that floor as an LLM rubric judge. It stays advisory and is off by default.

## What

- **`services/creativeRubricJudge.ts` + `creativeRubricJudgePrompt.ts`**
  - The 7 criteria are yes/no questions. The judge writes a rationale before each verdict.
  - Inputs: the image (URL or bytes), optional copy, the ENG-2139 gate result, and a brief (goal, audience, CTA, offer, placement, generation request, and a brand profile from `brandGuidelines.brandData`, without founder details).
  - When a criterion needs an input the brief does not have (no offer, no brand profile), the judge must fail it and name the missing input. This follows ENG-421's rule: ask, don't invent.
  - The prompt and parser follow the customer portal's offline pairwise judge (`scripts/evalOnboardingQualityPrompt.ts`): the prompt is versioned in the repo, the output must be strict JSON, and a code fence is tolerated but nothing else.
  - Unparseable output, a missing criterion, an invalid verdict, an empty rationale, an LLM error or an unreadable image each return `status: 'error'` with a `kind`. An error result has no `criteria` and no `passed`, so it can never be read as a pass.
- **Pairwise mode.** `judgeCreativePair(A, B, brief)` compares two creatives against the same brief.
  - The two images are shown in random order as "1" and "2", then mapped back to A/B.
  - The result has an overall preference plus a preference and reason per criterion. `preference` is the agreement harness's `PairwiseChoice` (`'A' | 'B' | 'tie'`), so a list of results goes straight into `pairwiseWinRate`.
  - `selectPriorBest` picks the prior creative: same user, same placement, created earlier; most rubric passes first, then the most recent.
- **Judge model.** Defaults to `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`, which is registered, vision-capable, and priced at $3/$15 per million tokens. Generation runs on Gemini and gpt-image, so the judge refuses any Google or OpenAI model and any model missing from the registry (`model_not_allowed`, no call is made). `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_MODEL` overrides the model.
  - Calls go through the OpenRouter gateway (`AgentModeService.callLLM`) and are metered as `feature: creative_rubric_judge`. No new SDK.
  - Our own S3 images are private, so they are read from S3 (with a size cap), shrunk to at most 1568 px and inlined. Any other https URL is passed to the provider unchanged, so the backend never fetches an arbitrary URL. Plain http is refused.
- **Runtime hook** (`creativeRubricJudgeRuntime.ts`).
  - Runs after agent-mode `generate_image` has enqueued its human-eval candidate.
  - Judges `category: 'ad'` creatives only, and only when `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_ENABLED=true` and the creative falls inside `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE` (0–1, default 0).
  - The judge runs only when the deterministic gates passed. When the gates failed or did not run, a `skipped` result is stored and no model is called.
  - The result is stored as a new optional attribute, `creativeRubric`, on the existing `AW-HumanEvalQueue` item. The update uses `SET … attribute_exists(candidateId)`, so it never creates an item. No table, key or index change.
  - The hook is not awaited and never throws, so it cannot delay or fail generation or the enqueue.
- **Offline script** `scripts/scoreCreativeRubric.ts --ids a,b,c [--pairwise] [--dry-run]`.
  - Read-only. It calls OpenRouter directly instead of `callLLM`, so not even spend-ledger rows get written.
  - It prints verdict counts, pass counts, error kinds and tokens. It never prints copy, requests, rationale text or image URLs.
- **Registry.** Adds `creative-rubric-judge` (LLM judge, creative, Claude, no validation, so `mayGate` stays false) and updates the audit doc.

### Deviations and deferrals

- **Pairwise does not run at runtime.** `AW-HumanEvalQueue` is keyed only by `candidateId`, so finding the prior best at generation time would mean scanning the table on every generation. Pairwise is available in code and through the offline script (`--pairwise`). Running it at runtime needs the creative-lineage record from ENG-2128 slice 4c.
- **κ per criterion is not computed here.** That needs the T3 golden set and the T4 harness run on it. Registry validation stays empty until then.
- **Agent mode's brief is thin.** The only brief it has is the generation request plus the placement from the gates; there is no structured offer, CTA or audience. So `offer_specificity` will usually fail on agent-mode ads. That is intended under ENG-421's floor ("no stored offer → fail").
- **Onboarding ad images are not judged.** They have no human-eval candidate to store the result on.

## Safety

- **Inert on merge.** Production sets neither `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_ENABLED` nor `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE`, so no model is called and nothing is written.
- **Advisory only.** Nothing reads `creativeRubric` to block generation.
- **Rollback.** Unset the flag or set the rate to 0, or revert this PR. The extra attribute on existing items is harmless.

### OPS step (for the matching OPS ticket; this PR does not set it)

Set these on the EB environment `Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`:

| Variable | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_ENABLED` | `true` | |
| `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE` | `1` (suggested) | `0.25` if you prefer to start small |
| `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_MODEL` | unset | Default is `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` |

- **Estimated cost per creative:** about **$0.02** at the price-book rate for `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` ($3 in / $15 out per million tokens). That assumes ~2k image tokens for a 1080×1350 image, ~1.5–2k prompt tokens and ~700 output tokens. The script's dry run on 5 real candidates estimated $0.020–$0.022 each. A pairwise comparison costs about $0.03.
- **Volume:** 125 agent-mode ad creatives were enqueued in the last 30 days (a read-only count), so a rate of 1 costs about **$2.50–3 a month**. A rate of 1 is suggested because the judged set also feeds the κ validation.
- **Verify** in `AW-HumanEvalQueue` that newly enqueued ad candidates carry `creativeRubric.status` (`ok` / `skipped` / `error`), and look for `[creative-rubric]` warnings in the logs.

### Offline run on real candidates

- **Dry run only.** I ran the script with `--dry-run` (read-only) on the 5 most recent `creative_image` ad candidates. All 5 had an S3 image, a brand profile and a generation request. None had a gate result yet, because ENG-2139 had only just deployed, so the runtime hook would have recorded `skipped` for them.
- **No live judge call.** The OpenRouter key sits in Secrets Manager (`<env>/AgentWeb/OpenRouter`), and the local IAM user has no access to it (`AccessDeniedException`). Running the judge would need a new credential, so I skipped it. After deploy, OPS can run `npx ts-node src/scripts/scoreCreativeRubric.ts --ids <5 ids>` wherever the key is available.

## Tests

New: `creativeRubricJudge.test.ts` (27), `creativeRubricJudgeRuntime.test.ts` (14). Extended: `autoHumanEvalService.test.ts` (+3), `agentModeService.generateImage.test.ts` (+1). The LLM is mocked throughout.

What they cover:
- verdict parsing: valid, fenced, malformed, missing criteria, invalid verdict and empty rationale, the last four each returning an explicit error with no verdicts
- refusing Google, OpenAI and unregistered models without making a call
- image handling: S3 download plus downscale, https passed through, plain http refused
- pairwise: order mapping for both orders, and output fed into `pairwiseWinRate`
- flag off, unsampled and organic creatives: no call and no brand read
- failed or missing gates: a recorded skip
- storage on the candidate (`SET creativeRubric`, conditional)
- the enqueue unaffected when the judge hangs or rejects

**Red → green.** I restored `autoHumanEvalService.ts`, `agentModeService.ts` and `humanEvalService.ts` to `origin/main` and removed `creativeRubricJudge.ts`.
- Red: all 4 affected suites failed. The hook and brief tests failed, and the new suites could not find the module.
- Green with the change: 7 touched suites, 187/187 tests. The pre-push hook passed 176 suites and 3,813 tests.

**Checks:** `npm run typecheck` is clean, and `lintdiff.py` reports 0 findings on added lines.

Linear: ENG-2140 (parent ENG-2128)

Risk: Low. Adds an opt-in, sampled creative rubric judge with seven binary criteria and pairwise comparison. It runs after deterministic gates pass, stores advisory results on existing human-evaluation queue items, and does not block generation. It also adds an offline scoring CLI and evaluation registry entry. The author reports both runtime flags are unset in production.

title: fix(oauth): isolate per-item createAccount failures in multi-account connect
body:
## Bug

`metaAuth.ts`'s `POST /connect-ad-accounts` and `linkedinAuth.ts`'s `POST /connect-accounts` (personal + organizations loop) each connect multiple accounts inside one outer try/catch. A single item's `createAccount` failure aborted the whole request with one blanket 500 — even when an earlier item in the same request had already durably connected, and, if a matching pending `customer_credential` decision existed for it (ENG-1644's approval inbox), already been auto-resolved (claimed + executed + origin session notified). That resolution can't be undone by a retry, and the client had no way to know the earlier item actually succeeded.

Predates ENG-1644 — its auto-resolve wiring (PR #3062, merged) just made an existing response-contract weakness consequential rather than introducing it. Found and deferred during ENG-1644's round-4/5 code review as its own scoped fix.

## Design decision

No existing multi-item response pattern exists elsewhere in this codebase to match, so this is a first pass — happy to revisit the shape if there's a preferred convention.

Chose: keep the loop running past a single item's failure (collect per-item results) instead of aborting; respond 200 whenever at least one item actually succeeded, with the accounts that succeeded in the existing `connectedAccounts`/`accounts` field plus new, additive `partialFailure: true` and `failed: [{account_id, error}]` fields. Only fall back to the existing 500 shape when literally nothing succeeded.

This is **fully backward compatible** — checked both real frontend callers (`customer-portal`'s `AdAccountSelectionHandler.tsx` and `Settings.tsx`) directly: both only ever read `response.data.success` + `.connectedAccounts.length`/`.accounts.length` on the happy path, and `error.response.data.error` on any non-2xx. Neither needs a code change — the all-succeed and all-fail response shapes are byte-identical to before this fix, and a genuine partial success now correctly shows an accurate count instead of a misleading total-failure toast. The new fields are there for a future UI update to use, not required by this fix.

## Scope

Only the two loop-shaped call sites this bug actually lives in. Did **not** touch `linkedInAdsAuth.ts`'s `/connect` (single-account, not affected) or any of the ~12 other connected-account platforms — explicitly out of scope for ENG-1644 and not part of this bug either.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` clean after every file touched.
- `metaAuth.test.ts`: added a partial-failure test (account 1 succeeds, account 2 throws — asserts 200, only account 1 in `connectedAccounts`, `partialFailure`/`failed` populated correctly, account 1's auto-resolve still fires) and an all-fail regression test (asserts the exact pre-fix 500 shape, unchanged). All 22 tests in the file pass, including the 20 pre-existing ones untouched.
- `linkedinAuth.test.ts`: fixed a stale mock name (the route now calls the consolidated `safeAutoResolveCredentialDecision` wrapper, not the raw function directly, from an earlier round of ENG-1644 review fixes — the mock still referenced the old name). Could **not** add a new success/partial-failure test for the org loop specifically — this file's own existing comments already document that `/connect-accounts`' in-memory `tokenSessions` Map is internal, not exported, and can't be seeded from a unit test; that's a pre-existing structural gap this fix doesn't change either way. All 24 tests pass.
- Full typecheck + both touched suites + adjacent suites (`linkedInAds.oauthRoutes.test.ts`, `approvalInboxCustomerNotify.test.ts`) all green, no regressions.

Draft per standing instruction — stays draft until explicitly told otherwise.

title: Fix stage_pending_decision result silently dropped by extractMinimalToolResult
body:
## Bug

`extractMinimalToolResult` (agentModeService.ts) minimizes every tool result before persisting/passing it onward. It had no case for `stage_pending_decision` (ENG-1644), so a genuinely successful call — decision written, Slack notified — fell straight to the function's default `{}` and silently lost its result (`decisionId`, `success`, `message`, `expiresAt`) on every call.

Same recurring bug class already documented in this function's own comments (`metaWriteManifestDigest`, `metaWriteDispatch`, `questionDeckPayload` — each hit the same default-`{}` trap before being fixed). `stage_pending_decision` is a 4th victim, found live-driving a real Emma turn through production during ENG-1644 post-merge verification — never caught by unit tests, since they call the tool's own `execute()` directly and never route through this minimizer.

Not confirmed as the direct cause of any specific production error (no dedicated downstream consumer of these specific fields was found), but it's real, confirmed data loss independent of anything else — worth shipping regardless.

## Fix

Added an explicit case preserving `success`/`decisionId`/`expiresAt`/`message` when present, matching the shape every other minimized halt-marker case in this function already uses.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- New tests in `agentModeService.extractMinimalToolResult.test.ts` (both fields-present and fields-absent cases) — verified they actually execute against the new branch, not just pass vacuously.
- Full targeted suite (171 suites, 3705 tests, via the pre-push hook) — all green.

title: Require subjectLabel on every approval-inbox decision (ENG-2159)
body:
## Bug

A real TriCityAI campaign-activation decision got mistakenly rejected on production today (ENG-2158) — the Slack card gave the reviewer no clear indication of which account/customer the decision was about, only whatever happened to land in free-form `businessImpact` prose. Root cause, confirmed via code read: `customerId`/`customerName` on `ApprovalDecision` are structurally forbidden on team-audience decisions (`validateCreateRequest` explicitly rejects them for `plan_choice`/`meta_write`), so decisions in an approver's own Slack queue have no dedicated field for "what account is this" at all. Separately, `decisionItemBlocks` never rendered `customerId`/`customerName` even when they *are* set (customer-audience decisions), so the gap existed on both paths.

## Fix

New required field `subjectLabel: string` on `ApprovalDecision`/`CreateApprovalDecisionRequest`, allowed regardless of audience (unlike `customerId`, which stays customer-audience-only by design):
- `validateCreateRequest` rejects any decision with a missing/blank `subjectLabel`.
- `stage_pending_decision`'s tool schema makes it a required parameter — Emma can't omit it.
- `decisionItemBlocks` (Slack) renders it as its own distinct, always-present line above `businessImpact`.
- Both customer-facing email templates (`notifyCustomerOfPendingCredentialDecision`, `notifyCustomerOfExpiredCredentialDecision`) include it for parity.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- New tests: validation (missing/blank rejected, persisted correctly), tool-arg threading, Slack render (distinct line, not replacing businessImpact), both email templates.
- Targeted suites (86 tests, 4 files via pre-push hook) — all green.

title: fix(agent-mode): diagnosis-honesty fixes + MCP schema relax + admin-activity redaction + Luma schedule migration
body:
Bundles the defects found during the ThinkingAI Luma investigation (2026-09-25/26) plus the migration script to stand up ThinkingAI's daily screening schedule. Each fix is its own commit; each has a mutation-checked test. `tsc --noEmit` clean; all touched suites green.

## Commits

**1. ENG-2160 — empty success ledger (original PR)**
Diagnosis agent narrated tool steps that never ran when the success ledger was empty (session `7adc834c-…`: a 429 killed the turn before any dispatch; user told "I have successfully loaded your browser cookies and navigated…"). Now states the absence explicitly and forbids inferring steps from the user's request. Reverses two assertions (ENG-971, ENG-1133) that had characterized the omission — neither ticket required it; both real requirements preserved.

**2. ENG-2161 — succeeded tool ≠ achieved goal**
Same function, non-empty ledger. `search_tool_response` ran but returned nothing; agent wrote "I have successfully analyzed the guest data… Please retry the browser evaluation step." Adds a rule: a succeeded tool RAN, not that its goal was met; never claim what a tool found/returned/analyzed/produced; never tell the user to run/retry an internal step.

**3. ENG-2163 — redact admin/support activity from a customer's own view** ⚠️ security-adjacent, review closely
Admin-only tools (get_pr_digest, read_linear_issues, manage_user_notes) run in a session delegated into a customer's account leaked internal data into the customer's view via the assistant's *narration* (raw tool results were already stripped; the narration was not). Prod: ThinkingAI's account (`e278986c-…`) got a 203-PR digest + Linear issues + internal notes in its history.

Decision (2026-09-26, product owner): persist as-is, mark admin activity, filter from the customer view. Implemented **serve-side**: `filterMessagesForClient` drops, for a non-admin viewer, the assistant messages of any "admin-tainted" turn (a turn whose stream contains an admin-tool RESULT). Keyed off the tool-result message actually present — **not** `metadata.toolCalls`, which a timed-out turn (the incident) lacks.
- New pure util `utils/adminOnlyMessageFilter.ts` (unit-tested); controller delegates with the real `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES`.
- `viewerIsAdmin` **defaults to false → fails closed**. `getSession` opts in for admin/delegated; public share + conversable endpoints keep the default (redacted).
- Serve-side only: no schema change, no backfill, and it **retroactively redacts the existing incident session**.
- Reviewer note: `getSessions` returns no message bodies (preview from first user message only); `filterMessagesForClient` is the sole full-message serve chokepoint. Any new serve path must pass through it.

**4. ENG-2162 — relax over-strict MCP tool schemas**
`playwright_browser_network_requests` declares `requestBody`/`requestHeaders` required though listing requests needs neither, so the gateway rejected the natural call pre-execution (sessions `81d208b8-…`, `e278986c-…`). Same class as ENG-821. Pure sanitizer at both `listTools()` ingest sites in `mcpClientService`, keyed on original (unprefixed) tool name. Never mutates input.

**5. Migration — ThinkingAI daily Luma schedule**
`scripts/seed-thinkingai-luma-daily-schedule.ts`: run once post-deploy (prod write) to create the daily scheduled chat driving the published "Luma Event Lead Engagement" skill on `daniel.liu@thinkingai.io`. Modeled on `seed-eng1880-phase-b-scheduled-reports` — NODE_ENV guard, name-based idempotency, minimal `requiredFunctionCalls` (pull-path only; ENG-480). Draft-only; disable after 2026-09-28.

## Not included, on purpose
- **ENG-2164** (customer-installable Luma skill) — not code; shipped as an `AW-Skills` catalog row.
- The retry-policy "mismatch" first suspected — invalid (that release note documents image generation, which is accurate; the interactive 2-attempt policy is deliberate).

## Test plan
- New: `agentModeService.diagnosisEmptyLedger`, `…diagnosisOutcomeInflation`, `adminOnlyMessageFilter`, `mcpToolSchemaSanitizer` — all mutation-checked (fail without the fix).
- Unregressed: 3 diagnosis suites (17 tests), 3 filter/getSessions suites (30 tests).
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors (default heap OOMs on this repo, unrelated).
- Pushed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` (hook's local CI OOMs in this env; verification run manually; CI is the backstop).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

## Review round (2026-09-26) — fresh-eyes adversarial review + fixes

An independent reviewer found the ENG-2163 redaction was **incomplete**: it covered the three agent-mode serve paths but NOT the Emma chatbot endpoints (`controllers/chatbot.ts`: getChatSession, listEmmaSessions, sendMessage, sendMessageStream), which read the same session store owner-gated-only and returned raw messages — a customer could fetch their own admin-touched session there unredacted. Also `sessionSummaryService` summarized the raw transcript, served to the customer via the `account_summary` tool (paraphrase leak). **Both verified against code and fixed** in commit `aae4f5f9`:
- new scoped `redactAdminActivity` (drops only admin-tool results + admin-tainted narration, no base-strip → no chatbot UI regression), applied to all four chatbot serve returns;
- summary input redacted before summarization.

Findings intentionally not changed: allowlist drift (the cited `list_predefined_work_plans` is deliberately non-admin-gated — redacting it would over-hide legit content; single-source-of-truth noted as follow-up), and the ENG-2160 lost-counter-write double-action (narrow, pre-existing, documented in a comment).

Verification after fixes: 10/10 util tests, 107 tests across the chatbot/summary/filter suites, tsc 0 errors; live-verified on env1.

title: [ENG-2131] Ability to manually set/override CRM display time zone (e.g., to PT)
body:
Mirror of [ENG-2131](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2131) (Linear, status: Backlog, Featurebase). Source of truth stays in Linear — comment here and update Linear on progress.

## What
The CRM automatically displays times in the browser's local time zone, with no user-facing setting to force a specific zone (e.g., PT) globally across the CRM UI regardless of browser location.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A user-facing setting (Settings or CRM preferences) lets the user pick/override the CRM display time zone (e.g., force PT).
2. Once set, timestamps across the CRM UI render in the chosen zone, not the browser default.
3. The override persists across sessions; clearing it restores browser-local behavior.
4. Existing timestamp rendering is unchanged when no override is set.

Good first scope: UI preference + a time-zone-aware formatting helper with unit tests using fixed instants across zones. Keep it UI + mockable data; no prod data/auth/billing/security exposure.

title: [ENG-2127] Lifecycle-filtered enrolment queries the status attribute, so it can never match
body:
Mirror of [ENG-2127](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2127) (Linear, status: Todo). Source of truth stays in Linear — comment here and update Linear on progress.

## What
`routes/sequences.ts` passes a **lifecycle** value into `crmDb.getLeadsByStatus(listId, lifecycle)`, which queries the `status` attribute on the `listId-status-index` and never reads `lifecycle`. The two vocabularies are disjoint, so a lifecycle-filtered enrol returns zero leads, always — silently (empty array looks like a legitimate result).

## Acceptance criteria
1. Decide what the lifecycle filter is supposed to mean, then either query a `listId-lifecycle-index` (or equivalent lifecycle read path) or remove/stop offering the filter.
2. A lifecycle-filtered enrolment returns the matching leads in tests with fixtures covering both vocabularies — never a silent empty result for a populated filter value.
3. If the filter is kept, failing/empty-filter paths surface a clear signal rather than masquerading as "0 leads enrolled".
4. No production data mutation in tests; use mocks/fixtures. Backfill of existing rows, if any, is a separate Linear-directed step.

Good first scope: bounded query-path fix + unit tests with fixtures. Keep it mockable; no prod data/auth/billing/security exposure.

title: Resolve every matching credential decision on reconnect, not just the oldest
body:
## Bug

Follow-up to ENG-1644's gap-closing round (the reconnect-auto-resolve fix shipped earlier today). Found live-testing that same fix on production: `findPendingCredentialDecision` used `.find()`, returning only the FIRST matching pending `customer_credential` decision for a given customer+platform+account.

Confirmed live on prod: two pending decisions existed for the same customer+platform+account —
- `558e9b59-7563-4dd7-bede-b96268ec167b` (created 13:29Z)
- `0c7f761c-ce3c-4b26-b0e2-c29fdb1f35f0` (created 17:55Z)

both `gateType=customer_credential`, `credentialPlatform=meta`, `credentialAccountId=1339414687604223`, same `customerId`. A real Meta reconnect only resolved the older one — the newer decision stayed `pending_customer_response`. Left alone, it would sit until it expires, at which point the expiry sweep sends the customer a false "your reconnect window has closed" email despite them having already reconnected.

## Fix

- `findPendingCredentialDecision` → `findPendingCredentialDecisions` (plural), `.find()` → `.filter()`. Same matching/normalization logic, just returns every match instead of the first.
- `autoResolveCredentialDecisionOnReconnect` now loops over every match, claiming and executing each independently. Each decision gets its own try/catch — one failed claim (lost race, transient error) never stops the rest from being attempted. Outer function stays self-contained (never throws), same as before.
- Only one caller existed (`approvalInboxCustomerNotify.ts`); confirmed via grep, updated consistently.

## Not in scope

A separate, unrelated stale test decision (`2713f0df-a8a4-4094-8a61-810cd55f0b4c`, no `credentialAccountId` at all) was found in the same investigation — that's a live production data cleanup, not a code fix, and is explicitly out of scope for this PR.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` clean after every file touched.
- Renamed/updated existing tests for the plural return shape.
- New regression test: two pending decisions for the same account both resolve on one reconnect (the actual bug this fixes) — previously only the oldest would.
- New test: a lost claim race on one decision doesn't block a second matching decision from resolving.
- New test: a transient failure resolving one decision doesn't stop the others from being attempted.
- Full targeted suite for both touched files: 59/59 passing (verified via direct jest binary run, not just individual `it()` blocks).

Linear: follow-up to ENG-1644 (no new ticket filed — this PR description is the record, per the parent session's instruction).

title: ENG-2144: online eval sampler + Eval v2 dashboard; satisfaction demoted to unvalidated
body:
## Why

ENG-2144 (ENG-2128 T12, slice 6). Session scoring today is lazy: a session gets a score only when an admin opens it on the partner-portal dashboard (`AdminDashboard.tsx` → `POST /api/admin/chat-sessions/score`) or a `get_chat_history sync=true` backfill touches it. Coverage is 44% overall and 0–96% by bucket (ENG-1710), so any rate built on those scores carries that selection bias. The satisfaction judge is also unvalidated (AUC 0.67 against task completion, 83.6% of scores are 5), yet its red/green badges are what the dashboard puts in front of people.

This PR adds a daily uniform random sampler that does not depend on who opened what, grades the sample with the deterministic ENG-2137 graders, shows the results with n and a CI on every number, and moves satisfaction to a secondary position labelled unvalidated.

## What

**Backend**
- `cron/evalV2SamplerCron.ts` (daily, 17:15 UTC, only when `EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED=true`):
  - **Frame:** sessions whose last activity (`updatedAt`) fell on the previous UTC day. It comes from a `AdminUpdatedAtIndex` query and never a scan. By run time every session in the frame has been idle for at least 17 hours.
  - **Sample:** a seeded uniform random draw of `EVAL_V2_SAMPLE_SIZE` sessions (default 50) using partial Fisher–Yates. The seed is `eval-v2:<day>`, and the frame is sorted by id first, so the draw does not depend on query order.
  - **Grading:** task success, tool correctness and offline groundedness (`agentGraders.ts`). This is deterministic, with no LLM call.
  - **Writes** go to `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` through the existing loop-event row shape and `DynamoPort.putItemIfAbsent`:
    - `eval-v2` / `eval_v2_sample_run#<day>`: frame size, seed and the sampled ids. This row claims the day before grading, and a resumed run reuses the same draw.
    - `eval-v2` / `eval_v2_scored#<day>#<sessionId>`: one row per session with flat dimensions only (verdicts, reasons, counts, surface, model, task type) and `graders: agent-task-success@1,agent-tool-correctness@1,agent-groundedness-offline@1`. It stores no message text.
    - `eval-v2-daily` / `<day>#1d` and `<day>#7d`: the aggregate per surface × task type × model. Each grader gets n, passes, rate, a 95% Wilson CI, a not-applicable count, versions and `mayGate`.
  - **Idempotent per (day, session):** scores are conditional puts on a deterministic key, and a day already marked complete is skipped.
  - **Flag contract:** a live run refuses without the flag (`{status:'refused', reason:'flag_off'}`) before any I/O. A dry run is allowed.
- `AGENT_GRADER_VERSIONS` in `agentGraders.ts`. Bump a grader's version in the same change that alters its verdict logic.
- `agentGraderLoader.ts`: the I/O tail is split into `listSessionsUpdatedBetween` and `loadSessionItems(…, {includeSpend})`. `loadSessionsForGrading` behaves as before. The sampler passes `includeSpend: false`: AW-SpendEvents has no session index, so reading spend would need a scan. The sampler's reader also refuses scans outright.
- `GET /api/admin/loops/eval-v2-trend?days=&window=7d|1d` sits on the existing admin-only `/api/admin/loops` router. It returns the snapshots, each grader's version and `mayGate`, and whether the sampler flag is on.
- `scripts/evalV2Sample.ts` dry-runs any day read-only and prints counts only. `--live` behaves like the cron and refuses without the flag.
- Eval registry: the sampler and the new tab are recorded as consumers of the three graders.

**Aggregate choice:** I added a sibling daily snapshot (`eval-v2-daily`) instead of extending the reliability snapshot. The reliability snapshot is one scalar row per window, built from agent-mode events. Eval v2 needs nested per-cell metrics over sample days, written after the day's sample exists. The layout mirrors `agent-reliability-daily` (a deterministic `<date>#<window>` key with overwrite).

**Alerts:** none are added. Every sampled grader has `mayGate() === false` today, so under ENG-2128 principle 2 none may alert. Each metric carries its `mayGate` value so a future alert path can check it, but no alert path exists.

**Partner portal**
- New **AI configuration › Eval v2** tab (`EvalV2Tab.tsx`), which uses the `useAuth()` token. It has a per surface × task type × model table: every cell shows rate, `[CI]` and `n=`, and a cell with no labelled sessions shows `– (n=0)` instead of 0%. There is also a daily trend (7d or 1d window) and frame coverage. Every grader carries an "unvalidated" chip in the legend and column header while `mayGate` is false, a banner says the rates drive no alert, and an info note shows when the sampler flag is off.
- **Satisfaction is no longer the headline.** In chat history the Satisfaction column moves after Actions, and its header gains an "unvalidated" chip with the reason. Its chips lose the red/amber/green colours so an unvalidated 1–5 score does not read as a verdict. The cell is extracted into `SatisfactionBadges.tsx`. Scores, custom judges, admin override, lazy scoring and retry are unchanged. No data or judge was deleted.
- The Daily Satisfaction Score Report schedule (`AW-TaskSchedules d0dd32ee…`) is already `paused` (last run 2026-08-18). Nothing in the DB was changed.

## Safety

- **Inert until OPS-7 (ENG-2152):** the cron is not scheduled unless `EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED=true`, and a live run refuses without the flag. The new tab and endpoint only read, and show "no snapshots yet" plus "sampler is off" until OPS-7.
- No production writes were made building this. I checked `eval-v2` and `eval-v2-daily` in prod after the dry runs, and both have 0 rows.
- **Rollback:** unset the flag. The `eval-v2*` partitions are separate from all existing loop partitions and can be left in place or deleted.

**OPS-7 step:** set EB env `EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED=true` on `Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`. Optionally set `EVAL_V2_SAMPLE_SIZE=50`, which is the default. Expected writes to `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` per day: at most k scores plus 2 puts on the run row plus 2 snapshot rows, about 54/day (roughly 1.6k/month, each row about 1 KB). Expected reads per day: one index query for the day's frame (about 50 sessions), one agent-mode partition query covering the sampled sessions' lifetime (capped at 14 days, typically one day, about 3.2k items), and one messages query per sampled session. The first 17:15 UTC run samples the previous day; I did not add a catch-up. Verify with `GET /api/admin/loops/eval-v2-trend`, where `samplerEnabled` should be true and one snapshot should appear.

**Read-only prod dry run** (`npx ts-node --transpile-only src/scripts/evalV2Sample.ts --date …`, counts only):

| day | frame | sampled | task success/failure/excluded | tool pass/fail | grounded/ungrounded/no_claims |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-24 | 56 | 50 | 2 / 0 / 48 | 41 / 9 | 4 / 3 / 43 |
| 2026-09-23 | 47 | 47 | 7 / 0 / 40 | 34 / 13 | 7 / 4 / 36 |

Daily volume is about 45–58 sessions, so k=50 is close to a census. Task success labels only sessions that have a work plan (about 10%), so its n will stay small, which is why every cell shows n.

## Tests

New suites:

| Suite | Tests | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| backend `evalV2Sampler.test.ts` | 16 | Seeded uniform sampling: deterministic, independent of query order, inclusion rate k/N within 5 sd over 4000 seeds. Row round-trip, with no message text. Aggregate math: n, passes, Wilson CI, not-applicable excluded from n, null rather than 0 when n=0, 1d/7d windows, coverage, mixed versions. `mayGate` follows the registry and an injected gate. |
| backend `evalV2SamplerCron.test.ts` | 8 | Refuses with the flag off before any I/O. A dry run with the flag off writes nothing. Refuses on day-not-over and invalid dates. Frame comes from the index and there is no scan (the fake reader throws on scan). Second run writes nothing. A resumed run reuses the draw, writes one row per session, and reads a moved session back by key. Snapshots are served by the trend read. |
| backend `loopEvalV2TrendEndpoint.test.ts` | 4 | Real `isAdmin` returns 401 unauthenticated and 403 for a non-admin or a delegated session. An admin gets n, CI and `mayGate:false` per grader. |
| portal `EvalV2Tab.test.tsx` | 8 | useAuth token, n/CI in every cell and trend row, "unvalidated" labels and banner, a validated grader, empty and flag-off states, window switch, no token. |
| portal `SatisfactionBadges.test.tsx` | 3 | "unvalidated" header, no red/green chip colours, override still works. |

`adminNavigation.test.ts` is updated for the new `eval-v2` slug (27 slugs).

**Red → green:**

title: feat(creative): creative lineage + ad-level metrics + score/CTR/CPA correlation, inert until OPS-3 (ENG-2141)
body:
## Why

ENG-2141 (ENG-2128 T9, decision D3). ENG-2128 asks whether creative scores correlate with live performance (reported coefficient and n). Today that cannot be measured:

- No generated image has an ID. Images are only S3 URLs, and agent-mode Meta publish does not record which generated image became which ad. Only the legacy task flow stores `meta_ad{adId, creativeId, imageHash}`.
- `AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots` holds campaign rows and account_day rows only. Ad-level insights are fetched live and not stored.
- Meta keeps revising insights for 28 days (ENG-1550), so the comparison has to use settled rows only.

## What

**(a) Creative lineage** (`services/creativeLineage.ts`, off by default)
- `generate_image` writes one record per generated image with these fields: `creativeId`, `userId`, `s3Key`, `artifactUrl`, `sessionId`, `category`, `promptHash` (sha256; the prompt text is never stored), `generatorModel`, `gatesSummary` (ENG-2139) and `humanEvalCandidateId`.
- **How the creativeId is resolved.** `creativeId = cr_ + sha256(S3 key)[:32]`. Every generated image gets its own S3 key, so any later step that holds the S3 URL finds the record with a GetItem.
- **Publish stamping** follows the order Emma actually works in:
  - `UPLOAD_IMAGE(url)`: the URL resolves to the creative, which gains Meta's `imageHash`.
  - `CREATE ad creative`: each of our S3 `image_url`s resolves directly. Each `image_hash` resolves through the same user's creatives that carry that hash. The Meta creative id is appended.
  - `CREATE ad`: the `creative_id` resolves through the same user's creatives that carry it. Then `{adId, metaCreativeId, imageHash, via, linkedAt}` is appended to `metaAdLinks`.
  - **Copy ad** and **creative swap** stamp the creative and the ad in one step.
  - Lookups are scoped to the user (GSI `userId-createdAt-index`, 180-day window), so a hash never links across users. Every call is fire-and-forget and never throws.
- **The rubric result is not copied.** ENG-2140 writes `creativeRubric` onto the human-eval candidate asynchronously, and only for a sampled share of creatives. The record keeps `humanEvalCandidateId` and the report joins on it. Copying the result would add a second writer that races the judge.

**(b) Ad-level metrics** (`cron/metaMetricsSnapshotCron.ts`, `services/adsMetricsDb.ts`, off by default)
- `rowType: 'ad'` rows come from one `level=ad` insights call per account per date. Each row has spend, impressions, clicks, CTR/CPM/frequency, Meta-reported leads (the lead family counted once, via `metaActionFamilies`) and video p25/thruplay when Meta returns them.
- The rows use the same 30-day overwrite window as the campaign rows. A failed ad read never costs the campaign rows for that day.
- **Join pitfall found and avoided.** Ad rows carry `ownerUserId`, not `userId`, so they stay out of the sparse `userId-date-index` GSI. `leadNotificationLookup.campaigns` reads at most 100 rows from that index and gives up when the read is truncated. One row per active ad per day would silently switch off campaign enrichment on lead notifications. Ad rows are read by `entityKey = meta#<account>#ad#<adId>` instead.
- `isMetaRowSettled(row)` counts a row as settled only if it was **captured** at least 28 days after the latest possible end of its reporting day (UTC-12). This matches the cron: the 09:00 UTC run on day +30 captures a settled row, and the run on day +29 does not.

**(c) Correlation**
- `agreement.ts` gains `spearmanRho` / `spearmanReport`. It is tie-correct (Pearson on average ranks) and the bootstrap CI is seeded. Resamples on which ρ is undefined are dropped and counted. `bootstrapCI` behaves exactly as before for kappa.
- `loops/eval/creativePerformance.ts` together with `scripts/creativePerformanceCorrelation.ts` form a read-only report: rubric passed-count vs settled CTR, and vs CPA **per currency**.
  - Ranking INR CPAs against USD CPAs would be meaningless, hence the per-currency split.
  - Only rows from the day the ad carried the creative count. For a swap, the shared link day is excluded.
  - Every exclusion is printed. The report writes nothing.
- Registry: `creative-performance-correlation` (outcome grader, unvalidated) is added to `evalRegistry.ts` and `EVAL_REGISTRY.md`.

## Safety

- **Inert until OPS-3 (ENG-2148).** Nothing reads or writes `AW-Creatives` unless `CREATIVE_LINEAGE_ENABLED=true` **and** `CREATIVE_LINEAGE_TABLE` is set. No ad rows are written unless `META_AD_LEVEL_SNAPSHOTS_ENABLED=true`. None of these is set in prod.
- There is no change to `AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots` schema or its GSI. Existing readers filter by `rowType === 'campaign' | 'account_day'` or read by campaign `entityKey`, and ad rows are not in the user index.
- **Cost once enabled:** one extra Meta Graph call per account per date in the 30-day window, plus one DynamoDB put per active ad per date.
- **Rollback:** unset the flags. The table and the rows are additive.
- **Data-plane:** this adds a new table definition, so it needs Harsha's approval per CLAUDE.md. Production creation is OPS-3.

### OPS-3 (ENG-2148): exact steps (do not run the whole `create-tables.ts`)
```bash
aws dynamodb create-table --region us-west-2 \
  --table-name AW-Creatives \
  --attribute-definitions AttributeName=creativeId,AttributeType=S AttributeName=userId,AttributeType=S AttributeName=createdAt,AttributeType=S \
  --key-schema AttributeName=creativeId,KeyType=HASH \
  --global-secondary-indexes '[{"IndexName":"userId-createdAt-index","KeySchema":[{"AttributeName":"userId","KeyType":"HASH"},{"AttributeName":"createdAt","KeyType":"RANGE"}],"Projection":{"ProjectionType":"ALL"}}]' \
  --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST
aws dynamodb wait table-exists --region us-west-2 --table-name AW-Creatives
aws dynamodb update-continuous-backups --region us-west-2 --table-name AW-Creatives \
  --point-in-time-recovery-specification PointInTimeRecoveryEnabled=true
```
1. Confirm the backend's DynamoDB principal can use `GetItem`, `PutItem`, `UpdateItem` and `Query` on `arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:992382574572:table/AW-Creatives` and `.../table/AW-Creatives/index/*`. It is `aws-elasticbeanstalk-ec2-role` unless the env uses access keys. I could not read the role's policies.
2. Set these on EB `Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`: `CREATIVE_LINEAGE_ENABLED=true`, `CREATIVE_LINEAGE_TABLE=AW-Creatives`, `META_AD_LEVEL_SNAPSHOTS_ENABLED=true`.
3. Verify each of these:
   - After an agent-mode `generate_image` with category `ad`, an `AW-Creatives` item exists.
   - After Emma publishes it (UPLOAD_IMAGE, then CREATE creative, then CREATE ad), that item has `metaAdLinks`.
   - After the next 09:00 UTC Meta snapshot run, `AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots` has `entityKey = meta#<account>#ad#<adId>` rows with `rowType = ad`.
4. The correlation report (`CREATIVE_LINEAGE_TABLE=AW-Creatives npx ts-node --transpile-only src/scripts/creativePerformanceCorrelation.ts`) has data only once linked ads pass 28 days of settling. It also needs the ENG-2140 judge enabled so creatives carry a rubric score.

## Tests

The new or changed suites, plus the covering agent-mode and ENG-916 suites, pass: **12 suites, 278 tests**. `npm run typecheck` is clean. `lintdiff` reports 0 findings on added lines (15 files).

Red→green: each production file was restored to `origin/main`, or the fix was mutated back, and the new tests were run:
| Restored / mutated | Result |
|---|---|
| `agentModeService.ts` at origin/main | `agentModeService.creativeLineage.test.ts` 6/6 fail |
| cron + `adsMetricsDb.ts` at origin/main | ad-row suites 12 of 21 fail |
| `agreement.ts` at origin/main | Spearman 7 of 23 fail |
| `collectCreativeMedia` counting a URL next to a hash (swap mis-credit) | 1 fails |
| ad rows written with `userId` (GSI pitfall) | 2 fail |
| settled-row check disabled | 2 fail (settling-window exclusion) |

- Spearman is checked against textbook values: IQ vs TV hours gives ρ = −29/165. The tie case is hand-computed as 8/√95.
- The ad rows are tested from a recorded-shape `level=ad` fixture with synthetic ids and values. No live Meta calls are made in tests.

## Found, not fixed (separate bug)
In `updateMetaAdsAd`, a creative swap that passes a new `image_url` also carries over the old creative's `image_hash`. `MetaService.createAdCreative` uses the hash first, so the ad keeps serving the **old** image. Lineage follows Meta's hash-first rule, so it does not credit the new image. The swap itself should be fixed in its own ticket.

Linear: ENG-2141 (parent ENG-2128). Ops: ENG-2148.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Adds opt-in creative lineage from generated images through Meta ads, optional ad-level metric snapshots, and a read-only report that correlates rubric scores with settled CTR and CPA by currency. Lineage and snapshots require environment flags. The report uses tie-correct Spearman correlation with a seeded bootstrap confidence interval.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: Fix generate_image confirmation gate blocking unrelated calls (ENG-2166)
body:
Three fixes bundled deliberately into one PR to reduce review/deploy cycles today.

## 1. ENG-2166 — generate_image confirmation gate stuck open

Real customer-reported bug (Vincent Hu, High priority). Root cause: `isApprovedImageSourceForRevision` (`toolDispatch.ts`) gated every `generate_image` call whenever `approvedRevisionImageSources` was non-empty for the run, not just edit attempts. Once one confirmed edit succeeded, every later unrelated `generate_image` call — including plain text-to-image with no `inputImages` — got wrongly rejected. Fixed: a call with no `inputImages` isn't an edit and now always passes this gate. The real protection (rejecting an edit against the wrong source) is unchanged.

## 2. Duplicate customer_credential decisions only resolving the oldest on reconnect

Found live-testing ENG-1644's reconnect-race fix on prod today: two pending `customer_credential` decisions existed for the same customer+platform+account, and a real reconnect only auto-resolved the older one — the newer stayed stuck until it would expire and trigger a false "your window closed" email. `findPendingCredentialDecision` (singular, `.find()`) renamed to `findPendingCredentialDecisions` (plural, `.filter()`); `autoResolveCredentialDecisionOnReconnect` now resolves every match, with its own try/catch per decision so one failure never blocks the rest.

## 3. linkedin_ads missing from the connected-accounts allowlist

`getAllAvailableConnectedAccounts()` never had `linkedin_ads` added, so the customer-portal Settings page's LinkedIn Ads card never rendered for any customer without an explicit subscription override — confirmed live: a real account connected LinkedIn Ads via onboarding (a separate, ungated flow) weeks ago, disconnected it today, and had no self-service path back. Added `linkedin_ads` to the allowlist. Also caught and fixed a second, duplicated hardcoded platform list in the partner-portal admin UI via a cross-repo drift-detection test.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck` clean throughout.
- All three fixes have dedicated regression tests reproducing the exact reported/observed bug.
- Full targeted suite across all touched files: 160+ tests passing, confirmed via pre-push hook (ground truth, not hook-filtered).

Supersedes #3090 (closed, folded in here).

title: ENG-2142: weekly pairwise creative calibration (~20 pairs, one click, golden-set labels)
body:
## Why

ENG-2142 (ENG-2128 T10). Creative eval today is the `#eval-queue` firehose: one Slack post per creative to one reviewer, free-text replies (brain F8). ENG-2128 asks for a small weekly calibration sample instead: about 20 pairwise A/B items, one click each. The labels go into the golden set, not the gating path, and they validate the rubric judge's pairwise mode (ENG-2140).

## What

**Pairwise golden cases** (`goldenSet.ts`): a creative case can now carry a `pair`. Creative A is `sourceRef.id`, the newer creative. B is the prior creative of the same account. The case has one criterion, `pairwise_preference`, labelled `A` / `B` / `tie`. It stores ids, the ISO-week batch, position and stratum only. It stores no content. The **existing** `PUT /api/admin/eval/golden-cases/:id/labels` route validates the choice, so there is **no new route**. `runValidation` leaves pairwise cases out of the binary agreement.

**Weekly sampler** (`loops/eval/creativeCalibration.ts`, pure):
- **Pairs:** each creative from the previous ISO week is paired with the creative `judgeCreativePair` would compare it to. That is `selectPriorBest` when the placement is known. Otherwise it is the latest earlier creative of the same account and category.
- **Deterministic per ISO week:** ties are broken by a hash of batch + pair.
- **Stratified:** round-robin over category × placement, with a per-account cap of ceil(20 / accounts).
- **Priority:** pairs where the stored judge result is contested or close come first. `disagree` means the judge passed a creative that a reviewer still replied to. `uncertain` means the pass counts are within 1. Next come `unscored` pairs, then `clear` ones.
- Pairs from earlier batches are never drawn again.

**Weekly job** (`cron/creativeCalibrationCron.ts`, scheduled in `server.ts` only with the flag):
- Writes the batch through the golden-set store.
- Posts **one** Slack message with the portal link, never one per pair.
- Idempotent across instances and days. Only the instance whose conditional put created the batch's first case posts. A completed week stops after one store query.

**Scripts:**
- `scripts/creativeCalibrationBatch.ts`: dry run by default, prints counts only.
- `scripts/creativeCalibrationReport.ts`: read-only weekly judge-vs-human agreement. It runs the pairwise judge on the labelled pairs (unmetered, nothing stored) and prints: n; A/B/tie agreement with a Wilson 95% CI; Cohen's κ with a bootstrap 95% CI; decisive-only agreement; each side's A win rate (`agreement.ts`).

**Portal** `/eval-labelling/calibration` (admin only, `useAuth()` token):
- Two creatives side by side, sides shuffled per pair.
- The generation request is shown as context. No judge result, feedback or date is shown. This is less customer data than the existing Eval labelling creative view.
- One click for Left / Tie / Right, plus an optional note, then the next unlabelled pair opens.
- Buttons and note are locked while saving, so a double click saves once. The saved confirmation clears on the next edit (the CodeRabbit #3079 lesson). A conflict gets a 409 message.
- `?batch=` from the Slack link selects the week.
- Eval labelling now hides pairwise cases and links to the new page.

### Host: why not ENG-1853 or `/batch-review`

- **ENG-1853** (Manan, In Progress) is a per-campaign approval packet: approve-all, manifest, branch edits. On main it is still only an S3 HTML prototype. Calibration is a different job: blind A/B labels for judge validation. So this is **linked, not absorbed**. If the packet portal lands, a calibration tab could link to this page.
- **`/batch-review`** lives in the customer portal repo and is customer-authenticated. Its approve/reject triggers `triggerAutoRevision`. It is the wrong audience, and it has side effects.
- The admin golden-set page (ENG-2135) is the natural host: same store, same label route, same auth.

## Safety: inert until OPS

Three independent switches, all off. Nothing in prod changes on merge.

| Switch | Effect | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `CREATIVE_CALIBRATION_ENABLED=true` (EB env) | `server.ts` schedules the daily check; a live run refuses without it | unset |
| `EVAL_GOLDEN_CASES_TABLE` (OPS-2 / ENG-2147) | golden-set store; unset means nothing is written and the page says "not provisioned" | unset |
| `CREATIVE_CALIBRATION_SLACK_ENABLED=true` (EB env) | the one weekly Slack message; the ENG-1854 kill switch `human_eval_slack_posting_enabled='false'` still wins | unset |

Optional AW-Settings `creative_calibration_slack_channel` is used first. The fallback is `human_eval_slack_channel`, then `HUMAN_EVAL_SLACK_CHANNEL`. The mention comes from `human_eval_reviewer_matt_slack_user_id`, and the link from `FRONTEND_URL`.

Rollback: unset the flags, or revert. There is no migration. Pairwise cases already written are ordinary golden-case rows; `runValidation` and Eval labelling ignore them.

## Tests

- **Backend:** 115 tests in the touched suites. New: `creativeCalibration.test.ts` (16), `creativeCalibrationCron.test.ts` (14), `creativeCalibrationScripts.test.ts` (5). Added to `goldenSet`, `adminGoldenSet` (admin-only pairwise save), `runValidation` and `humanEvalService`. Related suites (`goldenSetStore`, `goldenSetSeed`, `agreement`, `creativeRubricJudge*`, `scoreCreativeRubric`) are green: 193 total.
- **Portal:** 28 tests. `CreativeCalibration.test.tsx` (11), plus Eval labelling and the route catalog.

**Red → green:** each check below failed on the old code and passes on this branch.
- `runValidation.ts` from main → the pair-exclusion test fails.
- `adminGoldenSet.ts` from main → the pairwise PUT test fails.
- `goldenSet.ts` from main → 3 schema tests fail.
- `humanEvalService.ts` from main → the uncapped-pool test fails.
- The Eval labelling pair filter reverted → its test fails.
- `catalog.ts` from main → the route inventory fails.
- Mutation checks, each caught by its test:
  - Removing the Slack flag check.
  - Letting any instance post, instead of only the first-case owner.
  - Removing the save lock.
  - Removing the clear-on-edit.
  - Removing the auto-advance.
- The new modules do not exist on main.

**Read-only prod dry run** of the sampler against `AW-HumanEvalQueue`. Store unset, counts only:
- 2026-W39: 21 eligible pairs → 20 drawn, 5 accounts.
- 2026-W38: 36 → 20, 5 accounts; ad 17 / organic 3.
- 2026-W37: 70 → 20, 7 accounts; ad 9 / organic 11.

All pairs are `unscored`, because the rubric judge is off in prod. Placement is still `unknown` for almost every creative: only 5 have ENG-2139 gate results so far.

`npm run typecheck`, portal `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint on added lines (`lintdiff`, 0 findings; the portal files also pass `--max-warnings 0`) are all clean. The pre-push hook passed.

title: fix(meta): creative swap no longer keeps the old image_hash when given a new image_url (ENG-2169)
body:
## Why

ENG-2169 (found while building ENG-2141). This is the success-but-no-op class from ENG-592. In the agent-mode Meta creative swap (`updateAdViaCreativeSwap`), the single-image and video branches built:

```ts
image_hash: params.image_hash || ld.image_hash,   // video: || vd.image_hash
image_url:  params.image_url  || ld.picture || ld.image_url,
```

When the caller passes only a new `image_url`, which is the normal case for a freshly generated image, the old creative's hash is carried over. `metaService.createAdCreative` prefers `image_hash` over `image_url`, the same way Meta does. So the new creative was built with the **old** image, the swap reported success, and the ad kept serving the image it was supposed to replace.

## What

1. **Stop inheriting the hash.** In the single-image (`link_data`) and video (`video_data` thumbnail) branches, a new `image_url` without an `image_hash` no longer inherits the old hash. The URL goes to Meta as `picture` / thumbnail `image_url`, which is what `AD_CREATIVE CREATE` already does with a URL. The swap does not upload the image itself: the CREATE path doesn't either, and an upload would add a download failure mode to a live path.
2. **Read back the image before attaching.** When an image was requested, the swap now reads the created creative back (`getAdCreative`, which names `image_hash` explicitly) **before** attaching it to the ad. It returns `success:false, error:'SWAP_NOT_REFLECTED'` and leaves the ad on its current creative when:
   - a hash was requested and the live hash is different, or
   - only a URL was requested and the live hash still equals the old one.

   The read-back is best-effort, the same as `verifyCreativeSwap`: if the read throws, the swap goes ahead. Only positive evidence of a stale image blocks it.

Branches checked and left alone:
- **Carousel (`child_attachments`):** cards keep their own hashes, and top-level `image_hash`/`image_url` are not applied to cards at all. So this bug is not present there. That a top-level image is ignored on a carousel is a separate behaviour and is out of scope here.
- **`placement_assets`:** there is no hash carry-over, and URLs are already resolved through `resolvePlacementAssetHashes`.
- **`creative_id` path:** not affected.

ENG-2141 (`stampMetaPublish(... via: 'swap_creative')`) is not on `main` yet. The new early return is placed before the attach step, so a lineage stamp added after the attach and verify steps stays correct: an unattached creative is never stamped.

## Safety

- No flags, config or prod data involved.
- Behaviour only changes when `image_url` or `image_hash` is passed to an ad UPDATE on a single-image or video creative.
- For those calls there is one extra `getAdCreative` read before the attach. Every other swap makes the same Meta calls as before.
- Rollback: revert the PR.

## Tests

Added 6 tests to `agentModeService.metaAdsCRUD.test.ts`, all with mocked Meta and no live calls:

| Test | origin/main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| new URL only, single image → old hash not sent, URL sent | ✕ | ✓ |
| new URL only, video thumbnail → old hash not sent | ✕ | ✓ |
| created creative still has the old hash → `SWAP_NOT_REFLECTED`, no attach | ✕ | ✓ |
| requested hash not on created creative → `SWAP_NOT_REFLECTED`, no attach | ✕ | ✓ |
| new hash → used (regression guard) | ✓ | ✓ |
| neither → old image carried over, no extra read (regression guard) | ✓ | ✓ |

The two regression guards pass on `main` by design. They pin behaviour that must not change.

- Red run: the old `agentModeService.ts` was put back against the new tests, giving `4 failed, 66 passed, 70 total`.
- Covering suites on this branch: `metaAdsCRUD`, `metaLaunchGateWiring`, `metaWriteManifestConsent`, `metaWriteManifestProducer` and `eng1476.adListReporting` gave **124/124 passed**.
- `lintdiff`: 0 findings. `npm run typecheck` is clean. The pre-push hook passed.

Linear: ENG-2169 (parent ENG-2128)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium — this affects Meta ad creative updates, but leaves carousel and other paths unchanged. When a new image URL is supplied without a hash, the swap drops the old hash and checks the created creative before attachment. A confirmed stale image blocks attachment; inconclusive read-back allows attachment with `image_verified: false`.

title: Channel-aware sequence enrolment + worker skips undeliverable steps (split from #3026)
body:
Split out of #3026 so it can be reviewed as the feature change it is, rather than as a footnote to a landing-page smoke-test PR.

## Why this is its own PR

In #3026 this work went through six review rounds and the severity went **up**, not down: round 4 found one narrow bug, round 5 found two blockers, round 6 found a **cross-tenant lead disclosure**. Every one was a defect in the fix from the round before, and all of them lived in these same three files.

The cause was scope. What began as one line — *don't enrol a lead with no address* — had become channel-aware enrolment, worker skip semantics, a shared reachability module, a `delivered` flag threaded through two DB writers, and a CRM read with an authorization boundary. Each fix reached into riskier territory than the last. So it moves here, whole.

`dripSequenceWorker.ts` and `dripSequenceDb.ts` are byte-identical to `main` in #3026; only the ENG-2127 lifecycle-filter guard stayed behind, because it is audit work unrelated to enrolment.

## What it does

**Enrolment is channel-aware.** `SequenceChannel` is `'email' | 'linkedin'`, and `dripSequenceWorker.sendLinkedInStep` reaches the lead through `lead.linkedin` after loading it by `leadId` — it never touches the address. A LinkedIn-only lead in a LinkedIn sequence *was* being messaged, and an `l.email` test removed that capability. Enrollability now comes from the sequence's own steps: reachable on **at least one** channel it uses.

**The worker skips a step the lead cannot receive**, instead of throwing. It used to throw, and the throw propagated out, so the enrollment retried the same undeliverable step forever and never reached the steps it *could* receive. Configuration failures (no sender, no LinkedIn account, empty message text) still throw — those resolve when the user fixes them.

**The dedup identity moved.** `leadEmail` is the partition key of `leadEmail-index`; an empty one is invisible to `getExistingEnrollment`, so the row was re-created — and the lead re-messaged — on every run. A lead with no address now uses its LinkedIn URL there.

## Known gaps, stated rather than filed

- **ENG-2165** — the dedup key is a mutable lead attribute, so identity churn (a LinkedIn-only lead later gaining an email) misses the lookup and creates a second active enrollment → duplicate DMs. Needs a stable `listId#leadId` key, which needs a new GSI plus a backfill.
- `crm.ts`'s three auto-enroll sites are still email-only. Making them channel-aware would **start** auto-sending LinkedIn invites to people who currently receive nothing — a new outbound behaviour, not a restoration. Deliberately not done here.
- A mixed email+LinkedIn sequence now enrols anyone reachable on either channel and skips the steps they cannot receive. That is a product decision worth confirming.

## State

Branched on top of #3026, so its diff collapses to just these files now that #3026 has merged. Needs a rebase onto current `main` and a fresh full-suite run before review — **do not merge on the strength of #3026's verification**; the last review of this code found a security defect.

Draft deliberately.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**

title: Lead notifications: per-org lead-type filter (default form fills only) + Emma tools
body:
## Summary

Org Slack notifications currently fire for every CRM insert, including prospect discovery and imports. Default delivery now selects only inbound form fills and new-lead Calendly bookings. ENG-2177.

- Carry a server-assigned `LeadOrigin` separately from lead/form fields through single/batch inserts and the existing queue. Missing/unknown origins fail closed.
- Validate optional `leadTypes` on the existing org JSON config. Absent selects `form_fill` + `booking`; explicit arrays replace defaults; `[]` silences all types. Check before enqueue and reload settings before delivery/recovery.
- Add foundation Emma tools `get_lead_notification_settings` and `update_lead_notification_settings`. Return effective settings/options without credentials; scope to the authenticated user's org; writes require existing `org:configure` authority. Preserve channel/sources/masking and reject concurrent config edits.
- Document behavior, all origin mappings, and tool examples. No migration, new table, or lead-record origin field.

## Origin mapping per call site

| Origin | Call sites |
| --- | --- |
| `form_fill` | `routes/webhooks.ts`: forward-lead create + accepted repeat dispatch; `routes/crmPublic.ts`: public capture |
| `booking` | `routes/calendlyWebhook.ts`: new lead on booking |
| `linkedin` | `services/linkedInInviteCrmMirror.ts`; `services/agentModeService.ts`: `importLeadsFromSearch` |
| `enrichment_import` | `routes/crm.ts`: bulk-import, CSV import, LinkedIn-file import; `services/agentModeService.ts`: `addLeadsToList`; `services/outreachOnboardingSaveService.ts`: prospect-list save |
| `manual` | `routes/crm.ts`: single CRM UI/API add |
| `integration` | `utils/attioPersonWebhookEvent.ts`; `routes/webhooks.ts`: HubSpot record-sync create; `routes/crmWebhook.ts`: HubSpot record-sync create; `services/signupAutoEnrollService.ts`; `services/onboardingLeadSync.ts`; Attio/HubSpot adapter batches; `services/crmAutoSyncService.ts`; `cron/activationAnalysisCron.ts`; `routes/admin.ts`: CRM sync; `routes/crm.ts`: subscriber sync |

`crmWebhook.ts` contains provider record sync, not form capture, so it uses `integration`. The DB layer forwards each caller's explicit origin into `dispatchLeadCreated`/`dispatchLeadsCreated`; it never derives origin from a field in a submitted lead.

## Behavior change

Existing enabled orgs without `leadTypes` immediately stop receiving LinkedIn/import/manual/integration alerts. Old queued jobs without origin are suppressed. Opting in applies to subsequent events; no historical replay. Existing-lead Calendly updates retain existing behavior. Tools require an already configured valid notification channel to update settings.

“Only form fills” sets `["form_fill"]`; “also notify me about LinkedIn leads” reads the current list and adds `linkedin`. A valid disabled config can be re-enabled. Draft only, as requested; no production settings changed and no live Slack messages sent.

## Validation

- Before implementation: filter acceptance contract reproduced 7 failures + 1 passing inbound case.
- 304 focused Jest tests passed across 10 suites (notification service, tool validation/auth, DB single/batch boundary, forward-lead repeat capture, public capture, LinkedIn mirror/reconcile, Attio, Calendly booking-list). Final changed-path rerun: 148 passed.
- Additional changed-origin caller suites: 220 tests passed across 8 suites. Foundation override regression + final public-form spoofing test: 14 passed. All 22 production single/batch create call sites audited for literal server origins.
- Scoped `tsc --noEmit --strict --target es2018 --module commonjs --skipLibCheck` on `leadNotificationConfig.ts`; TypeScript syntax checks for all changed TS files; `git diff --check`.
- Jest/tsc capped at 768 MB. No full typecheck, build, or full test suite, per request. The broad pre-push hook is explicitly skipped for this scoped-check draft.
- Local CodeRabbit review disconnected with `WebSocket closed` before a final verdict. Its one returned finding suggested extracting the two foundation registry entries and caller origin literals from `agentModeService.ts`. Kept the existing foundation registration convention and direct caller literals: the config validator and tool authorization/handlers already live in focused modules; another indirection adds complexity without changing behavior.

## Complexity and rollback

One shared origin/config validator and two small tool handlers; reuse existing DB JSON, auth policy, registry, and async queue. Added enum/options and explicit origin arguments; no new service, infrastructure, migration, or polling loop. Excluded batches stop before per-lead reads; opted-in delivery now rechecks current routing/settings per job.

Rollback: **revert this PR**. Disabling the existing org config also stops pending jobs at processing. After deployment, smoke one form fill/booking (delivers), one import/LinkedIn lead (silent by default), then opt in via Emma and verify only the chosen origin delivers in the caller's org.

title: refactor(auth): share HubSpot/Fathom OAuth pending sessions via AW-OAuthSessions (expand) (ENG-162)
body:
## What
ENG-162 phase-1 EXPAND step for HubSpot + Fathom: pending OAuth token sessions (between /finalize and /connect) are now written to the existing `AW-OAuthSessions` table (Meta's proven pattern) and consumed atomically via conditional delete (`userId`, `provider`, `ttl > now`). The in-memory Map is still written, and /connect falls back to it, so sessions created by old instances during a rolling deploy still complete.

Data-plane classification: Harsha approved in ENG-1547 (Option 1) — existing table, key, row shape, 10-min TTL and consume authority; no table/schema/key/retention/IAM change. `create-tables.ts` untouched.

## Reviewer-first
- `backend/src/services/oauthFlowSessions.ts` (new): store/consume + payload validation at the persistence boundary; persisted local shadows cannot resurrect a session consumed on another instance.
- `db.ts`: `oauthSessionDb.consume` (conditional delete, ALL_OLD); Dynamo errors rethrown -> route 500, not treated as a missing row.
- Routes: `/connect` now rejects non-string/empty `tokenSessionId` with 400.

## Complexity ledger
+337 / -61 overall; routes net -48 (86 -> 38 changed lines of boilerplate removed); the new lines are the shared helper + tests. Net-negative across the phase comes with the CONTRACT step (drop Maps) and remaining providers.

## How to test
`cd backend && npx jest --runInBand src/__tests__/oauthFlowSessions src/__tests__/db.oauthSessions src/__tests__/hubspotAuth src/__tests__/fathom` — 30 suites / 772 tests pass locally at d055105b. Includes instance-A-finalize / instance-B-connect, one-time-use and expired-session negatives. Existing characterization tests unchanged (db mocked via setup.ts).

## Rollback
Revert this PR; any in-flight rows expire in 10 min via TTL condition. No data migration.

## Post-deploy verification
Connect HubSpot and Fathom once on prod; confirm success and no `oauthSessionDb.consume` errors in EB logs.

## Not tested
Live provider OAuth round-trip; real multi-instance deployment. Contract step (remove Maps, remaining providers) is a follow-up.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium — HubSpot and Fathom OAuth connections now rely on DynamoDB session operations. A DynamoDB failure makes these routes return 500 and blocks connections until service recovers. The change leaves table and IAM configuration unchanged.

The shared service stores OAuth sessions in DynamoDB and consumes them with a conditional delete. It validates stored payloads and keeps a local fallback for eligible sessions from older instances during a rolling deploy. Both `/connect` routes return 400 for empty or non-string session IDs.

title: fix(mcp): finish drain admission + in-flight tracking (A-019)
body:
## Summary

Completes the still-missing A-019 drain invariants against current `main` without reviving the obsolete parts of the old research plan.

- new **external** MCP `tools/call` requests get JSON 503 once this instance starts draining
- internal MCP self-calls from already-admitted AgentWeb turns stay allowed, so the existing ENG-1189 drain can actually finish them
- every MCP `CallTool` handler is registered in `cronJobRegistry` until the tool settles
- `generateResponse` refuses a fresh interactive turn before STT, idempotency/session claims, deck writes, or provider work
- drain admitted cron/MCP calls, interactive sessions, and live-voice tool executions **before** shutting down the response worker; both phases share the original drain deadline
- MCP `SERVER_RESTARTING` failures explicitly warn that the message may have been saved and to check the session before retrying (no automatic retry)
- after the worker drain, MCP session transports close before the HTTP listener

## Why this is narrower than the old A-019 plan

Later shutdown work already landed the worker/session drain, listener ordering, and MCP usage-event metering. This PR only fills the residual admission + in-flight tracking gap.

## Invariants

- `GET /mcp` behavior is untouched.
- No SSE-shaped 503 and no retry middleware.
- Existing internal loopback MCP calls are **not** rejected during drain.
- No ALB/nginx/deployment configuration changes.

## Tests

Adds retained drain-invariant coverage for:
- external `tools/call` → 503 while draining
- internal loopback tool call remains admitted
- `CallTool` remains visible in the in-flight registry until settlement
- MCP shutdown ordering relative to drain/listener close
- `generateResponse` drain guard occurs before the session-generation claim

## Opslane regression verification

- Reproduced the early worker shutdown in a failing test executing the production drain block: shutdown was called while the MCP registry drain was unresolved.
- Regression now asserts worker shutdown waits for both registry and interactive-session drains, and receives only the remaining budget.
- Worker deadline tests cover exhausted (0 ms) and short (25 ms) budgets.
- MCP error test asserts saved-message warning and exactly one fetch (no unsafe replay).
- Local scoped Jest, after merging current main: **4 suites / 91 tests passed** (`gracefulShutdown`, `mcp.mcpServer`, `security.mcpServer`, `mcp.httpClient`). Existing MCP mock timer teardown warnings remain; exit status is 0.
- Removed the obsolete fake concurrent-worker test: it duplicated `Promise.all` rather than exercising production sequencing and contradicted this reproduced regression.

## Rollback / post-deploy

Revert this squash commit if admission or drain regresses; no database, schema, or infrastructure changes. Verify the exact main deployment completes and public backend health returns 200. A destructive production SIGTERM/message replay is not part of the smoke test; deterministic regression coverage verifies that ordering without creating customer messages.

Tracks: kvnloo/agentweb#23 (A-019).
