title: Fix ENG-2204: unattended scheduled runs never call slack_send_message
body:
## Summary

- Scheduled/unattended runs never called `slack_send_message` even when the schedule's own instructions explicitly asked to post to Slack. Confirmed live in prod on the ThinkingAI daily Luma schedule (`77fa8188`): all 3 runs (09-26/27/28) succeeded and correctly wrote leads to the shortlist, but `slack_send_message` never appeared in `calledFunctions`/`failedFunctions` in any of the 3 sessions, and the target Slack channel never received a message.
- Root cause: `AGENT_MODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` has an unconditional rule — "ALWAYS show the draft and ask for explicit approval BEFORE calling `slack_send_message` — no exceptions" — written for a live human who can answer "Should I send this?". An unattended scheduled run has no one to ask, so the model could only satisfy the rule by never calling the tool. Same failure class this codebase already hit and fixed for external-publish tools (ENG-803/827/1245) — "a decision nobody actually makes."
- Fix: extend `getUnattendedExecutionDirective()` with a new `SLACK NOTIFICATIONS IN UNATTENDED RUNS` override — for an unattended run only, the ask-first rule is lifted and `slack_send_message` must be called directly when the task asks for it. Kept deliberately separate from the publish-authorization tri-state system (no new schedule field/owner opt-out): that system governs posting to a public/external account, which `slack_send_message` is not.

## Two rounds of fresh-eyes review, both incorporated

**Round 1** caught a real issue: the new override was gated only on `sessionType === 'scheduled'`, which also matches a schedule-created session reopened by a real human (ENG-2072) — `isUnattendedRun` stays `undefined` there. Fixed by gating on `isUnattendedRun === true` instead. Live-testing that fix on env2 surfaced a **second, pre-existing instance of the same leak** in a sibling call (`getScheduledSessionOverride`, the publish-authorization block) — fixed the same way.

**Round 2** (full 4-commit diff, fresh subagent, no memory of round 1) found one more real, blocking gap: the stricter `isUnattendedRun === true` gate silently regressed `runScheduleSelfImprovement` — a genuinely-unattended, currently-shipped opt-in reflection turn (runs after every scheduled dispatch when `schedule.selfImprove === true`) that calls `generateSessionResponse` without passing `isUnattendedRun`. Before this PR's stricter gate, that omission was harmless (sessionType-only check); after it, this real unattended turn silently lost both the Slack override and the pre-existing publish mandate. Fixed by passing `isUnattendedRun: true` explicitly, matching every other genuinely-unattended caller in the file. Independently verified end-to-end (parameter position, doc-comment semantics, threading into the worker) before fixing, and confirmed with a regression test that fails on pre-fix code (`received: undefined` where `true` was expected).

Round 2 also confirmed: no other leak site exists (traced every real call site of both directive functions), the strict `=== true` convention doesn't regress any other unmigrated caller, and commit 3 correctly (and intentionally) also retroactively fixes the identical ENG-2072 leak for the pre-existing publish-authorization mandate, not just the new Slack content.

## Test coverage added per review feedback

Both rounds flagged that the original tests only exercised the pure `getUnattendedExecutionDirective`/`getScheduledSessionOverride` functions in isolation — never the actual call-site wiring inside `generateMarketingResponse`, which is exactly where both regressions lived. Added:
- A call-site-level test asserting neither directive reaches an attended turn on a `sessionType: 'scheduled'` session (first draft had a false-positive — asserted on a section-title string that also appears as a harmless cross-reference in the always-present base prompt; fixed to assert on the override's actual substantive content).
- A test asserting `runScheduleSelfImprovement`'s worker call carries `isUnattendedRun: true` — verified this fails on pre-fix code.

## Live-tested on test-env-2 (all cases)

Using a real JWT for `test@example.com`, the `/scheduled-chats/:scheduleId/test` single-schedule trigger, and DB-level transcript inspection (not the bulk `/run-scheduled-chats` endpoint, which would have also fired ~41 unrelated stale dev-table test schedules):

- **Unattended dispatch:** `slack_send_message` called directly as the model's first action, no confirmation question. (Tool itself then failed with `invalid_auth` — a dev-environment Slack credential issue, unrelated to this fix; the model handled it honestly.)
- **Attended reopen (clean session):** model correctly drafted the message and asked "Should I send this?" — `toolCalls: []`, nothing auto-sent.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean after every commit
- [x] 700+ tests across every scheduledChat/scheduledRun/publish-authorization-adjacent suite — all pass
- [x] 6 new/updated targeted tests across `agentModeService.scheduledSessionContext.test.ts`, `agentModeService.publishDirectiveDelivery.test.ts`, `agentModeController.selfImprove.test.ts` — each verified to fail on the corresponding pre-fix code
- [x] Live end-to-end test on test-env-2: unattended dispatch and attended reopen, both correct
- [x] Two independent fresh-eyes reviews of the diff, findings verified against code and addressed in-PR

> **Linear is the source of truth.** Discussion, acceptance, and review happen on the Linear issue; this GitHub mirror exists so external contributors can find and pick up the work.

## What to do

**Reply-guy container:** open holding 5 candidates, each rendering the post text, a working link, and a suggested reply. A candidate missing any of the three is not shown. Candidates must be fresh for the current window (not repeated from the previous run).

**Post-ideas container:** open with news items usable as angles, and produce **no drafted post copy** — auto-drafted posts from news read as generic and get discarded. Emma supplies material and structure; the human supplies the take.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Reply-guy opens with 5 candidates, each with post text + working link + suggested reply; incomplete candidates are hidden.
2. Candidates are fresh for the current window, not repeated from the previous run.
3. Post-ideas opens with news items usable as angles and produces no drafted post copy (a test asserts the opening output contains no post-shaped draft).
4. Both degrade loudly on fetch failure — a plain statement that material could not be fetched, session still usable, never silent-blank and never fabricated filler.
5. `npx tsc` clean; relevant suite green.

Good starting point: the `openingAction: prefetch` mechanism (ENG-712, already landed) — these containers build on it.

title: [ENG-2127] Lifecycle-filtered enrolment queries the status attribute, so it can never match
body:
Linear source: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2127/lifecycle-filtered-enrolment-queries-the-status-attribute-so-it-can

> **Linear is the source of truth.** Discussion, acceptance, and review happen on the Linear issue; this GitHub mirror exists so external contributors can find and pick up the work.

## What to do

`routes/sequences.ts` passes a **lifecycle** value into `crmDb.getLeadsByStatus(listId, lifecycle)`, but that function queries the `status` attribute on `listId-status-index` and never reads `lifecycle`. The two vocabularies are disjoint (`status`: contacted/new/qualified/…; `lifecycle`: inbox/signed_up), so a lifecycle-filtered enrol returns **zero leads, always** — and fails silently ('0 leads enrolled' instead of an error).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Decide what the lifecycle filter is supposed to mean, then either query a `listId-lifecycle-index` (or equivalent lifecycle-aware lookup) or remove the misleading filter. The UI control must not silently return nothing.
2. Consider a backfill for `lifecycle`/`domain` on existing rows (safe additive `UpdateItem` per row, no key rewrite) — worth doing only if the filter is kept.
3. The silent-empty-result failure mode is fixed: a misconfigured filter errors loudly instead of reporting '0 leads enrolled'.
4. Existing sequence-enrolment tests pass; new coverage pins the fixed behaviour.

Related: ENG-2155, ENG-2125. Mockable: stub the CRM DB layer and assert the filter path.

title: [ENG-2155] Stored lifecycle outranks live computation forever; batchCreateLeads writes neither lifecycle nor domain
body:
Linear source: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2155/a-stored-lifecycle-outranks-the-live-computation-forever

> **Linear is the source of truth.** Discussion, acceptance, and review happen on the Linear issue; this GitHub mirror exists so external contributors can find and pick up the work.

## What to do

Two related gaps in lead lifecycle/domain handling:

**1. A stored `lifecycle` short-circuits the live computation permanently** (`services/askCrmService.ts`: `lead.lifecycle ?? computeLifecycle(...)`). A lead stamped `inbox` at creation still answers `inbox` after it signs up and starts paying — `computeLifecycle` never runs for it again. Pick one model and make every writer agree: (a) `lifecycle` is derived — never store it, compute on read (requires fixing `delete_leads_by_filter`'s `is_empty` predicate first); or (b) `lifecycle` is stored — then something must advance it. Option (a) is the coherent one. Note: dropping the creation-time stamp without fixing the delete-filter footgun is not an improvement.

**2. `batchCreateLeads` writes neither `lifecycle` nor `domain`** — it never calls `buildLeadCrmFields`. Bulk-created leads (HubSpot pull, Attio pull, CSV import) land with no `lifecycle`, exactly the `is_empty` delete-filter footgun the single-create stamp exists to avoid. The two creation paths disagree.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One lifecycle model (derived vs stored) chosen and applied consistently across all writers (`createLead`, `updateLead`, `setLeadFields`, `batchCreateLeads`).
2. `batchCreateLeads` derives `lifecycle`/`domain` the same way the single-create path does (no unstamped bulk rows).
3. No regression on the `delete_leads_by_filter` `is_empty` footgun — unstamped leads are not deletable-by-filter.
4. Tests pin the agreed writer behaviour; existing CRM test suites green.

Related: ENG-2127, ENG-2125. Mockable: stub the DB layer and assert writer behaviour per path.

title: fix(hubspot): the status never had a vote — any 4xx, and catch BAD_SCOPES
body:
Follow-up to #3129, which shipped this morning and was then proven incomplete by production within minutes.

## What production said

Forcing a real refresh on portal `245815183` — the grant that has reported "Active · Connected" since 2026-06-16:

```
HTTP 403
{"status":"BAD_SCOPES","message":"missing or invalid scopes","correlationId":"01a0e8c7-..."}
```

**403, not 400.** #3129 gated on `400 || 401`, so the classifier stayed silent and the row still says Connected.

The grant holds **19 legacy scopes** — `content`, `social`, `automation`, `forms`, `crm.lists.read` … — while the app now requests `crm.objects.contacts/deals`. Scopes are fixed at grant time, so no refresh will ever succeed; only re-authorisation clears it.

Which means: **#3129 would not have caught the incident it was written for.**

## This was not an unknown

Review round 3, finding #3:

> once the body gate exists, the `400||401` allow-list contributes **zero** false-positive protection and is pure false-negative surface

It also demonstrated that widening the gate broke no test, and that one of the tests **actively asserted a `BAD_REFRESH_TOKEN` body must be ignored at 403** — a false negative pinned in place. I acknowledged the argument and kept the allow-list rather than touch the gate again. The cost was a production false negative on day one.

## Changes

| | |
|---|---|
| gate | **any 4xx**, not `400/401`. The body is the discriminator; the status only creates hiding places. **5xx stays excluded** — that is HubSpot failing, not the grant |
| body patterns | `BAD_SCOPES` added, with the measured production response recorded at the function |
| the bad test | replaced by the real boundary: `400/401/403/404/429` + a naming body **all flag**; `500/502/503/504` with the **same** body do not |
| new case | the measured 403 `BAD_SCOPES` body, byte-for-byte |
| guard | a 403 that says nothing about the grant (`RATE_LIMIT`) still does not flag |

## Verification

| mutation | verdict |
|---|---|
| narrow the gate back to `400/401` — i.e. the shipped bug | **BINDS** — 4 failed |
| drop `BAD_SCOPES` from the body patterns | **BINDS** — 1 failed |
| let 5xx through | **BINDS** — 7 failed |

45 tests (was 37). `tsc --noEmit` clean. 32 suites / 870 tests pass.

## Why this unblocks the live testing #3129 could not finish

Production has no account that fails in a way #3129 catches, so two checks were never verifiable there:

- flagged → API reports `disconnected`
- Emma's `is_active` agrees with the UI

Portal `245815183` produces a flaggable failure **under this PR**, so both become testable on real data — followed by a reconnect, which then exercises clear-on-reconnect and `pullContacts`.

## Blast radius

Unchanged from #3129's measurement: 10 HubSpot accounts in production, 0 currently flagged. Widening the gate can only flag a grant whose refresh **already fails with a body naming it** — those grants are broken today and silently. A rotated `clientSecret` still answers `BAD_CLIENT_SECRET`, which still does not match.

title: ENG-2196: sampler creative/account-health snapshots and cost/latency per success; Satisfaction behind a disclosure; grader versions
body:
## Why

ENG-2196 (parent ENG-2128). The 2026-09-28 audit found:
- The eval-v2 sampler covers agent sessions only. There is no creative or account-health trend.
- It skips spend (`includeSpend: false`), so cost per successful task is offline only.
- Partner-portal Chat History still shows a per-session Satisfaction column, with lazy auto-scoring and an override.
- `GraderEntry` has no per-grader `version`.

## What

**Registry (`evalRegistry.ts`).** `version: string` is now required and populated for all 24 graders:
- the code constant where one exists (agent graders `1`, reply-length fixtures `1`, creative gates / rubric `2026-09-25.1`, outcome judge `2026-09-28.reconstructed-1`); `evalRegistry.version.test.ts` keeps these equal to the constants;
- `prompt-sha256:<12 hex>` for the AW-Settings judges, hashed read-only from prod (general and "Matt" share `4507a38770f1`, Fangfang is `293bd6a129c7`; only the hashes were printed);
- `untracked@2026-09-28` where neither code nor config versions the grader.

`GET /api/admin/loops/eval-v2-trend` now returns `registry` (id, surface, type, version, mayGate). The Eval v2 tab lists it.

**Efficiency (sampler).** `includeSpend: true` through a new bounded path in `agentGraderLoader`. It runs one query per billing subject on `AW-SpendEvents`' `BillingUserOccurredAtIndex`, never a scan. `resolveBillingUserId` maps an org member to the org's billing root. In prod, 31.6% of session-tagged rows are billed to someone other than the acting user, so querying by session user alone would miss them.
- A subject with more than 5,000 rows in the window marks its sessions `truncated` (unknown), never a partial sum.
- Each score now stores `spendStatus`, `costMicroUsd` and `runLatencyMs` (wall time from `agent_run_started` to `agent_run_verdict`, summed over runs). The sampler version is now 2.
- Each snapshot cell (surface × task type × model) gains `efficiency`: cost per success (failures charged to successes, as `efficiencyMetrics` does), median success cost, run-time p50/p95 per success, and counts of sessions with no spend or unknown spend. Each snapshot also gains `spendAttribution`.

**Spend-to-session attribution, measured read-only in prod (2026-09-28).**
- 24,937 rows, all `settled`. 14,291 carry `references.sessionId`, so **42.7% of rows lack one** (the audit's 43% is confirmed). By cost, $925 of $1,511 is attributed, so **38.8% of cost is unattributed**.
- The unattributed spend is non-session work: CRM enrichment ($357), X engagement ($86), landing pages ($78), bare `agent_task` ($27), video/image generation ($18), research, news and others.
- `agent_task:interactive` ($613) and every `agent_task:scheduled:*` bucket are **100% attributed**. So for chat sessions the gap is media and landing-page generation that runs inside a session without passing its id. The Eval v2 tab says how many sampled sessions had spend.

**Creative and account-health snapshots (`evalV2Surfaces.ts`, written by the same daily run).**
- Creative: the deterministic gate pass rate with a Wilson CI and the failing checks, and the rubric's criteria-passed distribution (0–7) with the floor-met rate. Built from the `creativeGates` / `creativeRubric` results already stored on `AW-HumanEvalQueue` candidates.
- Account health: the state distribution and flip rate from the ENG-2143 classifier's rows in `AW-AccountCapabilityRequirements` (`account_health_signal`). A flip is a row with version above 1 whose `stateSince` falls in the window.
- Neither table has an index by time or kind, so each is read with a filtered, projected scan capped at 20,000 evaluated items. The tables hold 1,243 and 7 items today. `surfaceScanReader` refuses any other table, and the session reader still refuses all scans.
- A truncated or failed read writes a snapshot with that status and no numbers.
- Snapshots are keyed `<day>#<window>#creative|account_health` under `eval-v2-daily`, beside the agent snapshot and never over it.
- Everything is still behind `EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED`, and every metric carries `mayGate` (false).

**Satisfaction (partner portal).**
- Chat History has **no Satisfaction column by default**.
- The column, the lazy `POST /chat-sessions/score` auto-scoring and the admin override appear only after the admin turns on the "Show unvalidated legacy score" switch, whose tooltip carries the unvalidated note.
- A hidden column therefore no longer spends judge calls.
- The Eval v2 tab did not mention satisfaction at all. It now says the legacy score is an unvalidated LLM-judge score, not part of its results.

**Eval v2 tab.** Adds cost/success and run time/success columns, the spend-attribution line, Creatives and Account health sections, and the grader registry with versions. It still renders against a backend without the new fields, in case the portal deploys first.

## Safety

- No new flag. The sampler (and so every new read and write) stays behind `EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED` (OPS-7, ENG-2152). The new reads are read-only queries and bounded scans. The new writes go only to `Dev-AW-LoopEvents` (`eval-v2-daily`), an existing table with no schema change.
- The account-health snapshot shows 0 accounts until the classifier runs (`ACCOUNT_HEALTH_ALERTS_ENABLED`, unset in prod). The rubric distribution stays empty until `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_ENABLED` is on (13 of 1,243 candidates carry gate results today, none carry rubric results).
- Rollback: revert. v2 scores stay readable, and old snapshots without `efficiency` or `spendAttribution` render as "no spend".

## Tests

- Red→green, backend. With `evalRegistry.ts`, `evalV2Sampler.ts`, `agentGraderLoader.ts`, `evalV2SamplerCron.ts` and `loopHealth.ts` restored from `origin/main` (and `evalV2Surfaces.ts` removed), all 4 new or changed suites fail: `evalRegistry.version`, `evalV2Efficiency`, `evalV2Surfaces` and `loopEvalV2TrendEndpoint`. On this branch they pass, as do the existing `evalV2Sampler`, `evalV2SamplerCron`, `agentGraderLoader`, `evalRegistry` and `evalAgentGraders.cli` suites. The pre-push hook ran 8 suites (62 tests), all green.
- Red→green, portal. With `AdminDashboard.tsx`, `SatisfactionBadges.tsx` and `EvalV2Tab.tsx` from `origin/main`, the 9 new tests fail: 2 in `AdminDashboard.legacySatisfaction` and 7 in `EvalV2Tab`. On this branch all 17 in those files pass, and `SatisfactionBadges.test` passes.
- lintdiff: backend 0, partner-portal 0. `npm run typecheck` and portal `tsc --noEmit` are clean.
- `eslint --max-warnings 0` is clean on `EvalV2Tab.tsx`, `SatisfactionBadges.tsx` and both test files. `AdminDashboard.tsx` has 91 problems both on `origin/main` and on this branch (all pre-existing `any` and unused vars). This PR adds none; fixing them is outside this ticket.

Linear: ENG-2196 (parent ENG-2128)

The portal displays these results and hides legacy Satisfaction until an admin enables it.

title: feat(eval): instruction adherence, argues-with-user and escalation graders (ENG-2189)
body:
## Why
ENG-2189 (parent ENG-2128). Three gaps, each verified against the code:
- **Argues with the user (ENG-1307):** nothing measures it; there is only a score cap in the judge prompt.
- **Escalation quality:** there is no metric at all.
- **Instruction adherence:** it comes only from the Gemini judge's dimensions. That judge is the agent's own family and is unvalidated. The only deterministic length check runs on synthetic placeholder fixtures, and nothing checks format.

## What
**1. Deterministic checks** in `loops/eval/agentGraders.ts`. They run on real turn structure: each user message, the last genuine assistant text before the next user message, and the tool-result messages in between. I checked this structure against prod `AW-ChatMessages` read-only, looking at field names and counts only. Each check gives one pass / fail / not-applicable verdict per session, with a reason code:

| Grader | Applies when the user message… | Fails when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `agent-reply-length-adherence` | states a numeric limit: N words, sentences, paragraphs or pages | the reply is over 1.5× the limit plus slack |
| `agent-format-adherence` | asks for a table or bulleted list in chat | the reply has no markdown or HTML table or list |
| `agent-act-without-asking` | says to act ("go ahead", "don't ask", "you have my approval") | the turn ran no work tool and asked permission instead |

The checks are conservative, so an unclear case is not applicable rather than a failure:
- Vague asks and per-item limits are ignored.
- So is anything in a user message over 1,000 characters.
- Formats meant for a sheet or doc are ignored, as are turns where a content-producing tool delivered the output.
- A which/what clarifying question is not treated as a permission request.
- Confirming a spend, publish, send or irreversible step passes, per the ENG-1312 rule.

**2. Binary judge criteria.**
- Rubric B (the shadow judge, `reconstructed-2`) now returns `arguedWithInstruction`, `escalatedWhenNotRequired` and `failedToEscalate` as booleans in `dimensions`. Only real booleans are kept and stored.
- The golden-set agent criteria gain `argued_with_instruction`, `escalated_when_not_required` and `failed_to_escalate`. For these three, pass means the behaviour happened, the same convention as the account-health states.
- `runValidation` pairs them with the stored judge booleans, and pairs the three deterministic graders with `instruction_compliance`, so κ can be measured once labels exist.

**3. Registry.** The three graders are registered unvalidated, so `mayGate` is false. The shadow-judge entry is updated, and everything is documented in `EVAL_REGISTRY.md`.

**4. Reporting.**
- `scripts/evalAgentGraders.ts` prints each rate with n and a 95% Wilson CI, overall and per model × task type. It also prints the shadow judge's criteria rates, read from `judgeScores.outcome-judge-b-shadow`.
- The eval-v2 sampler (row version 2) stores the verdicts and reason codes (never text) and adds the three rates to every group. Rows written before v2 count as not applicable.

**5. Portal.** EvalLabelling already renders whatever criteria a case carries, so the only portal change is help text for the three new criteria and labels for the three graders in the Eval v2 tab.

## Prod rates (read-only, 2026-09-21..27, 317 sessions updated)
| Grader / criterion | Rate | 95% CI | n | Fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent-reply-length-adherence` | – | – | 0 | 0 |
| `agent-format-adherence` | 67% | 30–90% | 6 | 2 (`list_missing`) |
| `agent-act-without-asking` | 100% | 88–100% | 28 | 0 |
| Judge `arguedWithInstruction` / `escalatedWhenNotRequired` / `failedToEscalate` | – | – | 0 | – |

How to read these:
- **Length, n=0.** An earlier run without the 1,000-character cap flagged 5 of 7 sessions. When I checked structure only (lengths, counts, offsets), every "one sentence" hit came from one ~12k-character scheduled task spec with 20 bullets, so those were false positives, and the cap removes them. Explicit numeric length requests in direct chat messages are rare in this window.
- **Format:** the 6 applicable sessions are mostly one recurring scheduled template.
- **Judge criteria:** n=0 until OPS-1 (ENG-2146) enables the shadow judge.
- **Bottom line:** the rates are small-n and unvalidated. They are a baseline, not a finding.

## Safety
- There are no prod writes and no new tables, flags or config.
- The script and the probes are read-only and print counts only.
- **One runtime change:** the eval-v2 sampler cron (`EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED=true` in prod) will write six extra verdict/reason fields on its existing `eval_v2_scored` rows in `Dev-AW-LoopEvents`, with `samplerVersion` 2. They hold no message text.
- The rubric-B text change reaches prod only when OPS-1 writes the shadow row from `buildOutcomeShadowJudgeRow`. Today there is no row, so it is inert.
- The golden store `AW-EvalGoldenCases` is empty, so no existing case is affected.
- Nothing may gate: every new grader has `mayGate=false`.
- Rollback: revert.

## Tests
- **New:** `agentGraders.adherence.test.ts` (52 cases). There are also new cases in `evalV2Sampler`, `runValidation`, `sessionScoring.shadowOutcomeJudge`, `evalAgentGraders.cli` and portal `EvalLabelling`.
- **Existing expectations updated** where the contract intentionally changed:
  - agent golden criteria;
  - sampler grader list and version tag;
  - trend endpoint grader list;
  - runValidation adapter list.
- **Red → green:** with origin/main's source files and this branch's tests, the backend fails 67 of 118 (7/7 suites) and the portal fails 1 of 11. With this branch, all 37 related backend suites pass (503 tests) and the portal passes (19/19).
- **Typecheck:** backend `npm run typecheck` and portal `tsc --noEmit` are clean.
- **Lint on added lines:** 0 findings for backend (17 files) and partner-portal (3 files). Portal files pass `eslint --max-warnings 0`.
- The branch is merged with the latest origin/main, and the suites were re-run after the merge.

Linear: ENG-2189 (parent ENG-2128)

## CodeRabbit findings (fixed)
- **Thread 4129864003** (`agentGraderLoader.ts:183`, "Recover missing tool names from call IDs"): `toTurns` now falls back to resolving a tool message's name from the assistant turn's `tool_calls` / `metadata.toolCalls`, matched by `tool_call_id`, when the stored tool message omits its own `name`. Fix `70d348b38`, test `57c936dce`.
- **Thread 4129864014** (`agentGraders.ts:840`, "Check for work tools before `no_reply`"): `gradePermissionAdherence` now checks `toolNames` for a work tool before the `no_reply` branch, so a tool-only turn (acted, no separate reply text that turn) passes instead of abstaining. Fix `a77d9de92`, test `33242054c`.
- Both were red on the pre-fix head and green after; full grader-related suite (152 tests across `agentGraderLoader`, `agentGraders`, `agentGraders.adherence`, `evalV2Sampler`, `evalV2SamplerCron`, `runValidation`), typecheck and lintdiff all clean on the fixed head.

## Enrichment spend check (ENG-2184 / PR #3114, read-only, aggregate counts)
Checked `AW-SpendEvents` for `feature=enrichment` since PR #3114 merged (`2026-09-28T09:08:05Z`): **0 rows** as of `2026-09-29T06:08Z`, so I cannot yet confirm gpt-5.5-only in prod — enrichment hasn't run again since the deploy. For context, the 5 rows immediately before the merge (08:36-08:37 UTC the same day, i.e. pre-fix) were 4× `gpt-5.5` and 1× `gemini-3.1-flash-lite`, matching the mixed-model behavior the fix targets. Worth a re-check once enrichment traffic resumes.

title: ENG-2192: score every generated creative (organic, onboarding images + copy, landing pages) + runtime pairwise vs prior best (stacked on #3126)
body: > **Stacked on #3126** (ENG-2187). This branch starts from `anurag/eng-2187-creative-gates-fix`, because onboarding scoring and the prior-best lookup read the gate results that PR stores on onboarding variants. Merge #3126 first; after that, this diff is only the ENG-2192 commits. ## Why ENG-2192 (parent ENG-2128). The acceptance criteria require "creative scores produced automatically for **every** generated creative". I checked the current code against that: - The rubric judge (ENG-2140) ran only for agent-mode `generate_image` with `category === 'ad'` (`creativeRubricJudgeRuntime.ts:100`), on the image alone, and never with ad copy. - Organic posts, onboarding images, onboarding ad copy and landing pages got no score. - Pairwise vs prior best was offline only (`scripts/scoreCreativeRubric.ts`, `creativeCalibrationReport.ts`). - Calibration sampled `creative_image` only. ## What **Surfaces** (`creativeRubricJudgePrompt.ts`, `creativeRubricJudge.ts`): - The judge now takes a surface. Each surface reuses the ENG-421 criteria that apply to it: | surface | criteria | |---|---| | `ad_image` | all 7, prompt **unchanged** | | `organic_image` | hook, proof, brand, format, policy (no offer / media-buyer) | | `ad_copy` | hook, offer, proof, brand, policy, media-buyer (no format) | | `landing_page` | hook, offer, proof, brand, format (as "ready for paid traffic"), policy | - New entry points: `judgeAdCopy` (no image) and `judgeLandingPage`. The landing-page judge reads the page source, capped at 60k characters, and the prompt says when the source was cut. - `judgeCreative` takes `surface` and already accepts `copy`. - New-surface results carry `surface`, `criteriaCount` and `SURFACE_PROMPT_VERSION`. `ad_image` results are byte-identical to before: same prompt, same version, no new fields. - `readRubricScore` (performance correlation) only counts `ad_image` results, because an organic 5-criterion score is not comparable with the 7-criterion one. **Coverage.** All paths stay behind the existing `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_ENABLED` / `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE`. Each creative is sampled on its own. | path | judged as | copy | stored in (existing tables only) | |---|---|---|---| | agent-mode `generate_image`, `ad` | `ad_image` + runtime pairwise | not known at generation | `AW-HumanEvalQueue.creativeRubric`, `.creativePairwise` | | agent-mode `generate_image`, `organic_post` / uncategorized | `organic_image` | n/a | `AW-HumanEvalQueue.creativeRubric` | | deployed landing page (root and sub-page) | `landing_page`, from the v0 output the deploy already holds in memory (no fetch, no scraping); only unzipped when sampled | n/a | `AW-HumanEvalQueue.creativeRubric` on the `landing_page` candidate | | onboarding images (images ready) | `ad_image` + pairwise vs the previous run's best variant, same placement | not generated yet | `AW-Users.adImageResult.variants[].creativeRubric`, `.creativePairwise` | | onboarding ad copy (copy ready) | the **full ad**: copy + its image (matched by variant id). `ad_copy` alone if that image failed or did not pass its gates | **yes** | `AW-Users.adCopyResult.variants[].creativeRubric` | - Onboarding write-backs are conditional on the stored result still being the one that was judged (`adImageCompletedAt` / `adCopyCompletedAt`). A regeneration in between is never overwritten; the verdicts are dropped with a warning. - **Runtime pairwise.** After an ok single verdict on an ad image, the judge runs `judgeCreativePair` (new = A) against `selectPriorBest`. The pool is the account's earlier `ad` candidates, or for onboarding, the previous run's variants. The prompt is the ad floor, so organic images are not compared. `priorId` and `priorArtifactUrl` are stored with the result. `selectPriorBest`, `judgeCreative` and `judgeCreativePair` are reused, not duplicated. - **Calibration.** Landing-page candidates are now drawn too. Each is paired with the account's previous landing page (never with an image), in its own `landing_page` stratum. - The partner-portal calibration page shows a landing page as an "Open landing page" link, not an ``. - Ad copy is **not** calibrated, because no human-eval candidate type holds copy. - Docs: the `evalRegistry.ts` entry and `EVAL_REGISTRY.md` are updated. ## Cost (per sampled creative; the sample rate multiplies all of it) Estimated from the input sizes and the price table (`anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`: $3 / $15 per M tokens). These are not measured; each stored result carries its own `usage`, and it is metered as `creative_rubric_judge`. | call | when | est. tokens in / out | est. $ | |---|---|---|---| | single, image (+copy) | every sampled image or ad | ~5k / ~1k | ~0.03 | | pairwise | sampled ad image with a prior best | ~9k / ~1.5k | ~0.05 | | copy only | onboarding copy whose image failed | ~1.5k / ~0.6k | ~0.015 | | landing page | sampled deployed page | ≤ ~17k / ~1k | ≤ ~0.07 | - **Agent-mode ad:** 1 call, +1 when there is a prior best. There is also one `AW-HumanEvalQueue` scan per judged ad; the table has ~1.2k items today. - **Onboarding run, everything sampled:** up to 3 image calls + 3 pairwise + 3 copy calls = 9. - **Landing page:** 1. - The knobs are unchanged: the flag, the sample rate, and `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_MODEL`. ## Deferred (needs a decision) - **Video keyframes.** `videoGeneration.generateKeyframes` makes the keyframe images, but it discards their URLs, and a generated video has no stored record to hold a score: no human-eval candidate, no variant record, and the session message is write-once. Scoring keyframes needs either a place to store the score (e.g. enqueue videos as human-eval candidates, which also posts them to #eval-queue) or a new field somewhere. That is a product and data decision, so this PR does not guess. - **Agent-mode ad copy.** Copy and image only meet at `createMetaAdsAdCreative` (`title`/`body`). Nothing ties that call back to the image's human-eval candidate unless the ENG-2141 lineage table (inert) is provisioned, or there is a scan by artifact URL. So agent-mode ads are judged on the image alone. Onboarding, where the copy is known, gets the full ad. ## Safety - Inert: nothing runs and no model is called unless `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_ENABLED=true` and `CREATIVE_RUBRIC_JUDGE_SAMPLE_RATE > 0`, both unset in prod. Turning them on is OPS-8 (ENG-2168). - Everything is advisory, fire-and-forget and never throws. No generation, deploy or onboarding step waits on the judge or fails because of it. - No new tables. The new attributes are on existing items: `creativePairwise` on `AW-HumanEvalQueue`; `creativeRubric`/`creativePairwise` inside `AW-Users.adImageResult.variants[]` and `adCopyResult.variants[]`. With the flag off none of them is written. - Behaviour change with the flag off: the calibration cron (its own flag, `CREATIVE_CALIBRATION_ENABLED`, also unset in prod) would also draw landing-page pairs. - Rollback: revert. Stored fields are optional and old readers ignore them. ## Tests **Red on the pre-change code, green after.** To check this, I restored the 19 changed source files to PR 1's head (afb926f08), removing the two new modules, and ran the new tests: - **27 failed** and 4 suites could not load (the new `creativeRubricOnboarding` / `landingPageJudgeSource` modules). - The portal's new landing-page test failed too. With the change: **230/230** on the 9 touched suites and **12/12** on the portal page. The red tests by file: - `creativeRubricJudge.test.ts` (7): the ad prompt and ad result are unchanged, per-surface criteria, organic subset, copy-only (no image part), refusing empty copy, landing-page source with the cut notice, a missing surface criterion is rejected. - `creativeRubricJudgeRuntime.test.ts`: - organic and uncategorized images are judged on the image subset (this replaces "judges only ad creatives", which asserted the gap); - landing page judged from the lazily loaded source, whose source is never read when unsampled, and which is skipped when there is no source; - runtime pairwise stored with `priorId`/`priorArtifactUrl`, not run without a prior best or for organic images, and a pairwise failure keeps the single verdict; title: ENG-2143: behavioural at-risk signals, campaign-row spend fix, cancellation dating + honest backtest
body:
## Why

ENG-2143 (T11 under ENG-2128), reopened by the 2026-09-28 audit. I re-ran the backtest read-only and confirmed the audit: at every cutoff the classifier predicted **0 at-risk accounts**. Pooled over n=93 pairs with 8 churned, precision was undefined and recall 0/8 [0.00, 0.32]. The cause is that at-risk came only from a payment failure or a past-due subscription. Each cutoff also excluded 18 undated cancellations.

While investigating I found a live defect: `account_day` snapshot rows store `spend: 0` by design (`metaMetricsSnapshotCron.ts`, "spend: 0"). The sweep's `readRecentAdSpend` and the backtest both read spend from those rows, so "ad spend in the last 30 days" was **always 0** and never established a current ads requirement. Prod has 542 `account_day` rows and 0 with spend > 0.

## What

**New classifier signals** (pure functions, each with an evidence reason; unread inputs are stated as context, never as a verdict):

| Signal | Kind | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spend_drop` | risk | last 14 complete days of spend ≤ 50% of the 14 before; each window needs ≥ 10 collected days | campaign rows (spend) + account-day rows (collected dates) |
| `results_drop` | risk | ≥ 3 leads in the prior 14 days, 0 in the last 14, while spend continues | account-day `totalLeadCount` |
| `negative_feedback` | risk | ≥ 3 thumbs-down in 30 days, outnumbering thumbs-up | AW-ChatSessions `feedbacks` (the only customer ratings stored) |
| `tracking_not_set_up` | **activation** | active ads or built pages without a pixel the account owns | Meta tracking monitor, run capture-only (`dryRun: true`) |

**Investigated, not added:**
- **Promised outcome.** No numeric promise is stored anywhere. The closest thing is the LLM-extracted `winMetric` text from Fathom sales calls. `targetLeads`, KPI targets and plan deliverables don't exist. So `results_drop` compares against the account's own recent leads.
- **Missed commitments.** The only due-versus-done record is AW-GTMPlan work items. All 289 due dates fall between 2026-01-14 and 2026-04-10, before every cutoff, and the DRI defaults to the customer's email. It doesn't record AgentWeb commitments, so no signal was added.
- **Other feedback sources.**
  - Message-level thumbs (AW-ChatMessages `feedback`): 0 rows in prod.
  - Support tickets: only in Featurebase/Linear, not stored.
  - CS notes: free text with no label.

**Cancellation dates.** No stored field holds Stripe `canceled_at`: AW-PaymentHistory keeps no raw event, and AW-Users has no cancel timestamp. The 18 undated cancellations all satisfy two conditions:
- They have no Stripe-sourced payment event since AW-PaymentHistory began (first row 2026-04-06).
- They were created before it.

Every webhook since then writes a row: `subscription_canceled` on cancel, `payment_succeeded` on renewal. So these accounts canceled, and stopped paying, before the log began. The backtest now counts them as `canceled_before_payment_log` (already churned) instead of excluding them as undated. The count is 18 of 18 at every cutoff, so they were not missing positives.

**Fix:** the sweep and the backtest now take spend from campaign rows and collected dates from account-day rows (`buildAdDays`).

**Routing unchanged (D8):** `at_risk` goes to needs-review until `mayGate('account-health-classifier')` is true. Tracking findings go to the CS nudge, never oncall.

## Backtest (read-only, audit cutoffs 2026-05-01 / 05-31 / 06-30 / 07-30 / 08-29, 30-day horizon, Wilson 95% CI)

| | n | churned | predicted at_risk | tp | precision | recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (main) | 93 | 8 | 0 | 0 | n/a | 0.00 [0.00, 0.32] |
| **After** | 93 | 8 | 1 | 0 | **0.00 [0.00, 0.79]** | **0.00 [0.00, 0.32]** |

Per cutoff (after), as n / churned / predicted / tp:

| Cutoff | n / churned / predicted / tp |
|---|---|
| 05-01 | 18 / 4 / 0 / 0 |
| 05-31 | 17 / 2 / 1 / 0 |
| 06-30 | 17 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| 07-30 | 19 / 1 / 0 / 0 |
| 08-29 | 22 / 1 / 0 / 0 |

Pooled pairs are not independent accounts.

**The precision ≥ 0.8 target is not met, and this data cannot measure it.** Signal firing, pooled:
- `spend_drop` and `results_drop` fire on 0 pairs. Ad snapshots start 2026-07-02 for one account and 2026-08-15 or later for the other five, so no cutoff has a collected prior window.
- `negative_feedback` fires on 1 pair, which was retained.
- `ads_never_connected` (activation, not a prediction) fires on 66 pairs, 4 of which churned.
- `tracking_not_set_up` cannot be backtested: the monitor keeps no history.

As of today (cutoff 2026-09-29, 25 paying accounts), the new risk signals fire on 0 accounts. Thresholds were set before the run and were not tuned to the 8 churned accounts. The result is recorded in `backend/docs/evals/EVAL_REGISTRY.md` and in the registry note.

## Safety

- The sweep stays inert: `ACCOUNT_HEALTH_ALERTS_ENABLED` is unset in prod. The backtest is read-only (DynamoDB scans only).
- The sweep's new reads are:
  - an AW-ChatSessions `UserIdIndex` query over the last 30 days, projecting `feedbacks` and capped at 5 pages;
  - a second AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots query;
  - the tracking monitor in dryRun (Meta reads and page fetches only; no alert, no suppression state).
- No schema, table or config change, and no OPS step. Rollback: revert.
- It merges cleanly with #3128 (ENG-2188). On the combined tree, 7 suites (191 tests) pass.

## Tests

- **Red on the pre-change sources** (classifier, cron, backtest script and `chatbotService` reverted, new tests kept): 19 failed / 45 passed across 3 suites. The failures include `reads recent ad spend from campaign rows, so real spend makes the ads requirement current`.
- **Green:** `accountHealthClassifier`, `accountHealthClassifierCron` and `eng2143AccountHealthBacktest`, 64/64. Pre-push: tsc ok, 34 suites / 339 tests green.
- Existing backtest expectations gained the new `signals` field. The "undated" fixture now has a Stripe event, so it stays genuinely undated under the new rule.
- Lint on added lines: 0 findings (8 files). `npm run typecheck` is clean.

title: ENG-272: authenticated Microsoft Teams inbound endpoint (Slice 1)
body:
## What

Adds the authenticated Teams inbound endpoint. Both Azure Bots (`agentweb-teams-dev`, `agentweb-teams-prod`) point at `https://api.agentweb.pro/api/teams/messages`, which **returned 404** — there was nothing to answer them.

**Scope is the endpoint and its authentication only.** The Teams adapter over the conversation port (merged in #2393), user resolution and session creation are the next PR. A test asserts this route imports none of that machinery, so the boundary is enforced rather than promised.

## Decisions worth reviewing

**The SDK, not hand-rolled auth.** Validating Bot Connector traffic takes seven separate checks — issuer, audience, the `serviceUrl` claim matching the activity, an RS256 signature against a rotating JWKS, a 5-minute skew window, per-channel endorsements — plus a wholly separate path for the Bot Framework Emulator. Microsoft's own guidance is that getting it wrong lets an attacker read messages sent to the bot, impersonate it, and steal its keys. `botbuilder` adds **7 moderate** advisories transitively (via `@azure/msal-node`) and **no high or critical**; that is the better trade than owning seven security checks.

**`MicrosoftAppType: 'SingleTenant'` is load-bearing.** Azure refused `MultiTenant` creation as deprecated (after 2025-07-31). A single-tenant bot must request its Connector token from its own tenant's endpoint rather than the shared `botframework.com` one, which is why `tenantId` is a required credential field rather than optional.

**Mounted after `express.json()`, deliberately NOT in the raw-body block.** Slack and WhatsApp need the exact received bytes to verify an HMAC over the body. Bot Framework authenticates with a bearer JWT in the header and `CloudAdapter` reads the parsed body, so raw-body middleware would break it.

**Credentials follow `getWhatsAppCredentials`, not `getOutlookCredentials`.** It is the only existing getter built for a webhook hot path: TTL cache plus in-flight dedupe, so a burst of activities cannot fan out into one `GetSecretValue` per request. A partial `TEAMS_BOT_*` env set is ignored rather than merged, so the dev bot's `appId` can never pair with the prod bot's secret.

**The fixed reply is not a placeholder.** It is the only exercise of the **outbound** path in this change — tenant-scoped token acquisition and reuse of the inbound `serviceUrl`. Without it, outbound auth would stay unverified until session wiring lands.

**Logging carries identifiers only.** ENG-2054 stripped message text from the Slack route's logs; a test asserts we don't reopen that on a second channel.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- New suites **16/16**; affected existing suites (conversation port, Slack characterization, Slack events, WhatsApp webhook, WhatsApp secrets) **153/153**
- Full suite before merge, since CI runs no tests

## Known and unresolved

- **`prod/AgentWeb/Microsoft/TeamsBot` does not exist** — the provisioning identity lacked `CreateSecret` on `prod/*`; values are in 1Password. Production throws until it is created, and deliberately does **not** fall back to the dev secret. Acceptable only because nobody has installed the prod app.
- **Cross-tenant delivery is unproven.** The licensed test user sits in the bot's *own* tenant, so no test we can run today shows whether a customer tenant would work. Current Microsoft guidance says a multi-tenant Entra app paired with a SingleTenant bot is the unreliable combination, and points at AppSource distribution — which contradicts the "no Microsoft review" premise this integration was chosen for. **No pilot date should be committed until a second tenant settles it.** Written up in `docs/integrations/teams-contract.md`.
- The dev bot's endpoint still points at the prod URL; it needs repointing to a tunnel URL for local Emulator/dev testing.

Also fixes two leftovers from #2393: an orphaned `postThinking` doc comment in `channelPort.ts` and the blank lines where its implementations were.

title: [needs human] Don't consume read-only foundation tool credit on work-plan step completion (ENG-2206)
body:
**Bug:** ENG-1698 added logic to decrement a step's requiredFunctionCalls credit in `session.calledFunctions` once that step resolves (completed/skipped), to stop one step's asset-producing call (e.g. `generate_image`) from silently satisfying an unrelated later step's identical requirement. That decrement was applied uniformly to every required tool name, including read-only, session-wide context tools whose successful call is the same fact regardless of which step needs it: `read_brand_guidelines`, `read_market_strategy`, `you_search_web`, `you_search_news`. In the reported production session (18bc82a6-..., Sondra Connor), step 2 ("Load brand context") required and completed with `read_brand_guidelines`/`read_market_strategy`, consuming that credit to 0. Step 5 ("LinkedIn post") also listed those two tools (plus `you_search_web`) as required — even though all three had genuinely been called earlier in the same session, `set_work_plan_status` kept reporting them as missing on every retry.

**Fix:** Added `AgentModeService.NON_CONSUMABLE_REQUIRED_FUNCTION_CALLS` (`read_brand_guidelines`, `read_market_strategy`, `you_search_web`, `you_search_news`) and skip the decrement (both the completed-branch and skipped-branch paths) for tools in that set, in `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`'s `setWorkPlanStatusAttempt`. Per-step artifact tools like `generate_image` keep decrementing exactly as before, preserving the original ENG-1698 fix.

**Verification:** Added a regression test reproducing the two-step shape from the production session (step 1 requires+completes `read_brand_guidelines`/`read_market_strategy`; step 2 requires those plus `you_search_web` and completes without any new calls). Repointed one pre-existing generic decrement test off `you_search_web` (now exempt) onto `create_blog_article`, an artifact-producing tool, since it was only using `you_search_web` as an arbitrary stand-in and its assertion was about the decrement mechanism, not this tool specifically.

---

Code review: ✅ sound — 3 finding(s) fixed
Deterministic checks: ❌ FAILED — npx tsc --noEmit (backend)
Browser verify: ⚠️ environment down (not verified)

Fixes ENG-2206 — https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2206/set-work-plan-status-blocks-completion-despite-all-required-function

title: [ENG-2128 A] No-op checks beyond ad platforms; task_verified feed for ENG-665/ENG-1564 (ENG-2190)
body:
## Why

Parent: ENG-2128 (Eval System v2). This is ENG-2190.

* **No-op checks are ad-only.** Write-without-read-back and repeated-mutation checks (`agentGraders.ts`) covered only Google Ads, Meta and LinkedIn writes. CRM, landing-page publish, email and social writes were never checked.
* **`task_verified` was never set.** It's a reserved `RecommendationQuality` type slot (`llmUsageDriversResolverService.ts`), so ENG-665 / ENG-1564 still rank models on the AA benchmark only.

Verified against current `main` (fetched before starting; no drift found at push time — `origin/main` had not moved since branching).

## What

**1. Read-back checks beyond ad platforms** (`agentGraders.ts`), reusing the existing `writeFindings`/`readBackAfter` machinery rather than a second detection pipeline:
- **CRM leads** (`add_leads_to_list`, `update_lead`) — confirmed by a later `get_leads`/`search_leads`/`get_lead_details`/`get_leads_needing_followup` read on the same list. `add_leads_to_list` never returns the created lead's id in matchable form (`importedIdentifiers` are human-readable descriptors, not ids), so its only possible confirmation is a same-list read with no id filter — which `readBackAfter` already treats as confirmed.
- **Email send** (`send_email_to_lead`, `send_email_from_sender`) and **social publish** (`post_on_connected_account`) — confirmed by the provider message id / post id / post URL their own response carries (`verifiedInTool`), since neither surface has a separate "read it back" tool.
- **Landing-page publish** (`generate_landing_page`, `deploy_landing_page`) — flagged (new `landing_page_publish_unverified` finding) when the deploy's own `launchReadiness` (agentModeService's ENG-1868 minimizer, backed by the existing `landingPageSmokeTest.ts`) reports the post-deploy smoke test failed. Reuses that existing smoke test rather than re-fetching the URL here, per the ticket's "reuse existing smoke-test infrastructure" instruction.

Bumps `agent-tool-correctness` to version 2 (`AGENT_GRADER_VERSIONS`, `evalRegistry.ts`) since its verdict now depends on more than ad-platform writes.

**2. `task_verified` feed** (`loops/eval/taskVerifiedFeed.ts`), wired into `llmUsageDriversResolverService.ts`'s `resolveUsageDrivers`:
- Reads the eval-v2 online sampler's daily `agent-task-success` rate per model (already-built ENG-2144 infrastructure — no new pipeline), combined across every task-type cell for the model (usage-driver recommendations aren't task-type-scoped yet — there's no task type on a billing driver).
- Emits `task_verified` only when `evalRegistry.mayGate('agent-task-success')` is true, and only when both the incumbent and candidate model have a sampled rate over `MIN_VALIDATION_N` sessions with the candidate not meaningfully worse (tolerance 3pp). Otherwise returns nothing and the existing AA-benchmark tier (ENG-1563) renders as before — never blended (ENG-1564 requirement 4).
- The lookup checks the gate **before** any I/O, so with no grader validated (true today, ENG-2128 principle 2) it never even reads eval-v2 data — inert by construction, not just an empty result.

**Scope note vs. ENG-1564:** ENG-1564 (the full Okareo-backed eval harness with canary/progressive rollout and its own promotion-bar decision) remains its own ticket — still Backlog, blocked on a product decision (AC1). This PR does not attempt that; it reuses AgentWeb's own already-running production-outcome sampler behind the same registry gate every other eval-v2 metric already respects, which is what ENG-2190 actually asked for.

**Deferred / documented gaps** (kept out to keep the shared-file hunks minimal, per the brief):
- CRM coverage is `add_leads_to_list` (create) + `update_lead` (update) only — not `set_lead_contact_status`/`assign_lead`/`add_lead_engagement`/`update_lead_status`. These are lower-value no-op targets (status/engagement writes, not the primary "did the lead land" question) and can be added the same way later.
- `search_leads`'s `list_ids` (multi-list) form isn't classified — only single-list `list_id`. Degrades safely (unclassified, never a false finding).
- The generic multi-action `email` tool's `send` action isn't covered — only `send_email_to_lead`/`send_email_from_sender`, whose output shape (`emailId`) was verified directly against the handler code.

## Safety

- No new tables, no prod writes, no config changes.
- Both changes ship inert/gated: the no-op checks are pure, offline, report-only graders already consumed only by an offline script and a sampler cron that's off in prod (`EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED` unset); the `task_verified` feed provably does no I/O and sets nothing while `evalRegistry.mayGate` is false for every grader (true today).

## Tests (red -> green evidence)

- `agentGraders.test.ts`: new `describe('gradeToolCorrectness: read-back beyond ad platforms (ENG-2190)')` — CRM/email/social/landing-page flag + confirm + unconfirmed cases. Verified red against the pre-change `agentGraders.ts`/`evalRegistry.ts` (every new case failed), green after.
- `evalV2Sampler.test.ts`: two pinned grader-version-tag assertions updated to `agent-tool-correctness@2`.
- `taskVerifiedFeed.test.ts` (new): pins "inert" against the **real** `evalRegistry` (`mayGate('agent-task-success')` is `false` today, and the snapshot reader is never called), plus the n-bar / tolerance / memoization behavior with an injected gate standing in for a future validated grader.
- `llmUsageDriversResolverService.test.ts`: new `describe('task_verified feed wiring (ENG-2190)')` proves the override (no benchmark field alongside `task_verified`) and the fallback (AA tier renders when the feed finds nothing) via an injected `taskVerifiedLookup`. The pre-existing `AC5: task_verified ... never emitted by this code path` test is untouched and still passes unmodified — it runs with no mock of the new module at all, and still never sees the status, because the real registry has no validated grader.
- Verified red on the pre-change `taskVerifiedFeed.ts` (module didn't exist) / `llmUsageDriversResolverService.ts` (no `taskVerifiedLookup` option), green after.

Local evidence:
- `npm run typecheck` (backend): clean, exit 0.
- `python3 lintdiff.py`: `added-line lint findings: 0 (files: 8)`.
- Targeted suite (`agentGraders.test.ts`, `taskVerifiedFeed.test.ts`, `evalV2Sampler.test.ts`, `llmUsageDriversResolverService.test.ts`): 144/144 passing.
- Pre-push hook (full related-set run, 7 suites incl. `evalRegistry.test.ts`/`evalRegistry.version.test.ts`/`agentGraders.adherence.test.ts`): 222/222 passing, no `--no-verify` needed.

title: ENG-2193: OCR/spelling/brand/logo/policy creative checks + landing-page PageSpeed and UTM propagation
body:
## Why

ENG-2193 (parent ENG-2128): `creativeGates.ts`'s existing structural checks (decode/blank-render/
aspect/dimensions/file-size) explicitly deferred OCR/spelling ("the only open-source option
(tesseract.js) downloads language data from a CDN at runtime... deferred rather than shipping a
half-working check"), and had no brand-colour, logo-presence or policy-keyword checks at all.
Landing pages had no Lighthouse perf/a11y check and no UTM-propagation assertion in the smoke
test. Verified against current `main` (post ENG-2187 placement-aware gates, ENG-2192 expanded
rubric scoring) — neither touched this gap; ENG-2192's "expanded scoring" is entirely the
separate LLM `creativeRubricJudge.ts`, not `creativeGates.ts`.

## What

**Image creative checks** (`creativeContentChecks.ts`, new; `CreativeGateCheckId` in
`creativeGates.ts` grows by six ids) — same advisory `{id,status,reason}` pattern as the existing
structural gates, merged into the same `CreativeGateResult.checks` array:
- `ocr_text_ratio` / `ocr_legibility` — tesseract.js OCR; text-area ratio (sum of word bbox areas
  / image area) and legibility (mean word confidence).
- `spelling` — nspell + dictionary-en over OCR'd text and/or supplied ad copy, with brand terms
  (brandName/tagline/valueProposition/keyMessages/brandValues/founders) allow-listed.
- `brand_colour` — dominant-palette distance (quantized RGB from a sharp thumbnail) from the
  brand profile's hex colours (`brandGuidelines.brandData.primaryColor/primaryColorEnd/
  secondaryColor`).
- `logo_presence` — bounded normalized-cross-correlation template match on downscaled greyscale
  bitmaps against the account's persisted logo (`agentMode/brandLogo.ts`). No new dependency: a
  handful of fixed scales, stride-4 search, bounded compute regardless of creative size.
- `policy_keywords` — a regex/keyword classifier for Meta/Google restricted categories (health
  claims, before/after, financial claims, personal-attribute inference, restricted substances,
  adult content). Cheap, deterministic, no LLM call — distinct from `creativeRubricJudge.ts`'s
  existing LLM `policy_compliance` rubric criterion, which stays as the qualitative/expensive
  check.

**Wiring** (`creativeContentCheckRunner.ts`, `humanEvalService.appendCreativeGateChecks`,
`autoHumanEvalService.ts`): the structural gates run inline in `imageGeneration.ts`'s
`generateImage()`, awaited before the response returns — they're fast (sharp only, bytes already
in hand). The new checks are heavier (OCR inference, an optional brand-logo download), so they run
out-of-band instead: dispatched from `enqueueAutoHumanEval` alongside the existing rubric-judge
hook, fire-and-forget, and merged onto the stored human-eval candidate's `creativeGates` after the
fact (mirrors the existing `setCreativeRubric`/`setCreativePairwise` update-only contract).

**Landing pages:**
- `landingPagePageSpeedCheck.ts` — a PageSpeed Insights `performance`+`accessibility` check per
  deployed page, reusing the existing key (`getPageSpeedApiKey()` in `seoService.ts`, secret
  `prod|dev/AgentWeb/Google/PageSpeed`) rather than adding a new one. `seoService.ts`'s own call
  only ever requests `category=seo`; this adds `performance`+`accessibility` in the same single
  `runPagespeed` call. Stored on a new `pageSpeedResult` field on the page record — a flat
  `{ok, performanceScore?, accessibilityScore?, checkedAt, error?}` shape matching the page's
  existing `smokeTestResult` idiom (not `creativeGates.ts`'s array shape, which is specific to
  image checks). No new table. Dispatched fire-and-forget from `v0Service.ts` alongside the
  existing post-deploy smoke test, at both deploy call sites.
- UTM-propagation assertion in `landingPageSmokeTest.ts`: the smoke test now navigates with
  synthetic `utm_source`/`utm_medium=paid`/`utm_campaign` params appended to the deployed URL
  (`buildSmokeTestUtm`, mirroring `buildSmokeTestEmail`/`buildSmokeTestPhone`; `medium=paid`
  matches ENG-239's UTM contract in `utils/adUtm.ts`), then — for an email-keyed lead — checks
  whether the resulting lead's own `utmSource`/`utmMedium`/`firstTouch.utm` fields actually carry
  them through (`utmPropagationVerdict`, pure). This exercises the landing page's own capture
  middleware (`v0Service.injectLeadCaptureAttribution`) end to end — the exact gap
  `utils/leadSchema.ts`'s `LeadAttributionFields` doc comment already flags ("capture has never
  executed in production"). Recorded as `smokeTestResult.utmPropagated`/`utmPropagationDetail`,
  advisory only, never folded into the overall `ok`.

**OCR choice:** evaluated `tesseract.js` (pure JS/WASM) against a hosted OCR API and
`node-tesseract-ocr` (wraps a system `tesseract` binary). Went with `tesseract.js`: no new
native/system dependency (unlike `node-tesseract-ocr`), and creative bytes never leave our infra
(unlike a hosted API). Trade-off, same one the prior deferred-work comment flagged: the English
language model is fetched from a CDN on first use per process rather than vendored (vendoring
would add more to the repo than the ~30MB of WASM cores `node_modules` already gains, for one-time
cold-start savings on an already out-of-band check). That fetch — like the OCR call itself — is
bounded (20s) and never allowed to block: any failure degrades `ocr_text_ratio`/`ocr_legibility`
(and transitively `spelling`/`policy_keywords`, if they had no other text) to `skipped`, exactly
like a `sharp` decode failure already degrades the structural gates. `nspell`+`dictionary-en` are
fully offline (~600KB combined, zero native deps) — no equivalent trade-off there.

## Shipped vs deferred

**Shipped, working, tested:** all five image content checks, the PageSpeed perf/a11y check, and
the UTM-propagation assertion — all advisory, all merged into existing storage shapes, no new
tables.

**Deferred, with reason:**
- **Triaging the ticket's "14/22 smoke tests fail" and filing bugs.** That's investigative ops
  work against real prod landing pages, and filing bugs means creating Linear tickets — both
  outside this agent's mandate (`AGENT_BRIEF.md`: no Linear writes, PR-only). Flagging for the
  coordinator as a separate follow-up.
- **Content checks on the onboarding ad-image path** (`onboardingAdImageService.ts`, which stores
  gates on `AW-Users.adImageResult.variants[].gates`, not the human-eval queue this PR wires into)
  and **on landing pages** (`creativeRubricJudgeRuntime`'s `judgeHumanEvalCandidate` already
  branches on `reviewType === 'landing_page'`, but this PR's content checks are image-specific —
  OCR/logo/brand-colour don't apply to a landing page's source code). Both are real, but each
  needs its own scoped wiring change; `runCreativeContentChecks`'s `adCopyText` parameter and
  `AutoHumanEvalInput.adCopyText` are already in place for the onboarding path's follow-up.

## Safety

Everything here is genuinely inert or fail-open by construction, not by a flag standing in for
untested code:
- Image content checks: gated behind `CREATIVE_CONTENT_CHECKS_ENABLED` (unset by default — not
  set anywhere in EB config today, so this ships fully inert). To enable: add
  `CREATIVE_CONTENT_CHECKS_ENABLED=true` to the backend EB environment. No OPS ticket number was
  assigned to this PR, so this is a plain EB env var change the coordinator can make directly
  (not a table/schema change — `AW-HumanEvalQueue` is unchanged, only a new optional field on the
  existing `creativeGates` blob).
- PageSpeed check and UTM assertion: always on, but purely additive (`pageSpeedResult` and
  `utmPropagated`/`utmPropagationDetail` are new optional fields; `ok`/`passed` semantics
  unchanged) and fire-and-forget, matching the existing smoke-test contract. No new tables, no
  new secrets (reuses the existing PageSpeed key).
- `advisory: true` throughout; `mayGate('creative-deterministic-gates')` is still `false` (no
  `validation` entry in `evalRegistry.ts`), so nothing here blocks generation, publish, or human-
  eval enqueue.

## Tests (red→green)

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `python3 ~/.cache/eng2128/lintdiff.py <worktree> origin/main backend`: 0 findings on added
  lines.
- 12 test suites / 621 tests, all real functional coverage (not hand-waved):
  - `creativeContentChecks.test.ts` (34 tests) — spelling runs against the real offline
    nspell/dictionary-en (a genuine "recieve" typo gets flagged, a brand-allow-listed nonsense
    word doesn't); logo-match is proven against real sharp-composited fixtures (a pasted pattern
    scores ≥0.9, an unrelated image scores <0.55); palette/OCR/policy-keyword checks each have
    dedicated pure + measurement-layer coverage.
  - `creativeGates.test.ts` — updated `notCheckedGateResult` test (12 check ids now, was 6).
  - `humanEvalService.appendCreativeGateChecks.test.ts`, `creativeContentCheckRunner.test.ts`,
    `autoHumanEvalService.test.ts` — the wiring: merge-onto-existing-candidate-only contract, the
    flag gate, bounded downloads, images-only dispatch.
  - `landingPagePageSpeedCheck.test.ts`, `services.v0Service.test.ts` — the real request URL
    asserted to carry `category=performance`+`category=accessibility` (never `seo`); every
    failure mode (no key, non-2xx, missing scores, network error) comes back as a result, never a
    throw; the deploy path dispatches it with the deployed page's own URL.
  - `landingPageSmokeTest.test.ts` — `utmPropagationVerdict` pure-logic coverage plus integration
    tests against the existing mocked-Playwright harness: the navigated URL carries the injected

title: Strip slack_send_message from requiredFunctionCalls when withheld (ENG-2204 follow-up)
body:
## Summary
- Follow-up to #3130. Live prod verification of that PR (schedule with `slack_send_message` in `requiredFunctionCalls` + `requireSlackApproval: true`) surfaced a real incident: turn 1 correctly withheld the send, then the deterministic completion checker — blind to the withhold state — pressed "Please try again. title: fix(crm): derive lifecycle filters for sequence enrollment
body:
## Summary
Fix ENG-2127 by separating status-index queries from canonical lifecycle derivation for by-list sequence enrollment.

- Normalize empty/whitespace-only `status` to absent before validation, selection, or auto-enrollment wiring.
- Validate supplied lifecycle even alongside explicit status. When both are supplied, select the intersection: **status match AND `lifecycleForLead(lead) === lifecycle`**. With explicit status, lifecycle means a canonical stage, not the historical status alias.
- Reject explicit status outside a nonempty stored `statusConfig` with HTTP 400 `invalid_status` and allowed values. Preserve arbitrary custom statuses for legacy lists whose stored config is missing/empty; default config is not treated as a stored vocabulary.
- Preserve lifecycle-only legacy status compatibility, including paginated materialized legacy statuses, while deriving canonical lifecycle-only stages from complete lead rows.
- Filtered enrollment never enables future whole-list auto-enrollment.

## Verification
- `npx jest src/__tests__/sequences.test.ts --runInBand --silent`: **93 passed**, including 10 new Opslane regression cases. Tests demonstrated failures before fixes.
- Scoped production TypeScript check rooted at `routes/sequences.ts` and `services/dripSequenceDb.ts`, with `--noEmit` and a 4096MB heap: passed.
- Corrected existing lifecycle regression fixtures that used blocked `example.com` recipient addresses, and an outdated status-pagination call assertion. No reachability production behavior changed.
- Latest `main` merged into the branch; author/committer of follow-up commits: `deploy@agentweb.pro`.
- CI and merge proof: `.github/scripts/merge-evidence.sh` must exit 0 at the current head before merge.

## Explicit remaining scope
- **Pre-existing bulk-enrollment race remains:** enrollment IDs are random primary keys; duplicate lookup uses the eventually consistent `leadEmail-index`. A process-local mutex plus a conditional put on a new random ID cannot provide reliable uniqueness across workers or GSI visibility lag. Added a TODO at `bulkEnroll`; no enrollment keys, stored shapes, lock records, tables, or indexes changed. A durable fix needs separately approved data-plane design.
- Lead-list display still shows stored lifecycle while enrollment uses derived lifecycle. No display behavior or response shape change; `reclassified` count deferred.

## Rollback / post-deploy
- Roll back by reverting the squash commit; no schema migration, backfill, or stored-record rewrite to reverse.
- Observe the path-filtered backend production deployment. Smoke the by-list route with an authorized test sequence/list: lifecycle typo plus blank/explicit status must return 400 without enrollment, invalid stored-config status must return 400, and status+canonical lifecycle must remain a one-shot intersection. Do not perform bulk mutations on customer lists for verification.

title: fix(crm): treat lifecycle as non-empty semantic state
body:
## TL;DR
ENG-2155 Phase 2a: make lifecycle presence semantic instead of depending on whether the DynamoDB attribute happens to exist.

## What changed
- `lifecycle is_empty` now matches zero leads in both `search_leads` and `delete_leads_by_filter`.
- `lifecycle is_not_empty` matches every lead: the lifecycle model is total and always has a stage, including `unknown`.
- Search, destructive preview, and enrichment selection use one shared helper.
- Existing equality/comparison behavior is deliberately unchanged.

## Why this is narrower than "derive lifecycle everywhere"
The lead row alone does not contain all authoritative lifecycle signals. Correct paying/signed-up/deal derivation requires joins to AW-Users, ContactEvents, and Deals. Recomputing equality from only email/phone would misclassify real customers as inbox.

This slice removes the destructive `is_empty` footgun without pretending we have data we do not.

## Follow-up
Phase 2b should define a shared live-signal resolver for lifecycle equality filters. Only after that should ENG-2155 remove the remaining persisted lifecycle stamps.

- Enrichment now returns lifecycle is_empty = 0 and is_not_empty = all leads, including missing, null, blank, whitespace, and custom-field lifecycle values. Equality and other fields are unchanged.
- Audited all backend presence-filter switch consumers; search/delete already use the helper, enrichment was the remaining consumer.

title: fix(scoring): stop swallowing per-session judge-score failures
body:
## Summary

`POST /chat-sessions/judge-score` used `Promise.allSettled` per session and, on a rejection, only pushed the bare session id into `failed` — the rejection reason was discarded entirely, with no log anywhere. A live spot-check confirmed this: the judge's LLM call succeeded in CloudWatch, but the endpoint returned `{"scores":{},"failed":["<sessionId>"]}` with zero diagnostic.

This PR:

1. Logs the rejection (session id, judge id, error message) via `console.error` when a per-session judge-score promise rejects, and changes `failed` from `string[]` to `Array<{ sessionId, reason }>` so the reason is visible in the response too. Checked `partner-portal` for consumers of this response shape — `AdminDashboard.tsx`'s judge-score caller only reads `scores`, never `failed`, so this is a safe, low-risk shape change with no frontend updates needed.
2. Hardens JSON parsing in `scoreSession` and `scoreSessionWithJudge` (`sessionScoringService.ts`): Bedrock-routed judge models don't always strictly honor `response_format: json_object`, and a text preamble before the JSON object made `JSON.parse(raw)` throw — exactly the kind of rejection problem 1 was swallowing. Both functions now extract from the first `{` to the last `}` before parsing, consistent with the same defensive-extraction convention already used elsewhere in this codebase for non-strict LLM output. The existing ENG-1669 missing/non-numeric score guard is unchanged.

Refs ENG-2216.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx jest sessionScoring.jsonPreamble sessionScoring.judgeScoreValidation admin.chatSessions` — new and existing coverage green
- [x] `npx jest sessionScoringService src/__tests__/sessionScoring` — full sessionScoringService suite green (26 suites / 333 tests)
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] Diff-scoped ESLint check — zero findings on added/changed lines
- [x] Pre-push hook ran the full backend suite (32 suites / 372 tests) — green

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Low — The change is limited to session scoring diagnostics and judge-response parsing. Rollback is straightforward, and no production outage path is apparent.

The judge-score endpoint now logs per-session failures and returns each failed session’s ID and reason, capped at 300 characters. Both scoring paths extract a JSON object from judge output that includes surrounding text.

title: Inline landing-page preview and collapsed generation prompt in creative calibration (ENG-2220)
body:
## What and why

Creative calibration pairs (`/eval-labelling/calibration`) are meant to be a sub-few-second "which is better" decision. Two gaps found in a live UX audit:

1. Landing-page pairs showed only two "Open landing page" buttons plus the generation brief — no way to compare A vs B without leaving the page.
2. Ad-image pairs render both creatives inline (good), but the raw image-generation prompt (hex codes, layout/font specs) was shown as reviewer-facing text under each image — implementation detail, not something a reviewer needs.
3. No loading state while creative images/pages fetch (~3s of blank/broken-looking cards).

## Change

`partner-portal/src/pages/CreativeCalibration.tsx`:

- Landing-page pairs now render inline as a sandboxed `<iframe>` in the comparison card. Verified live via `curl -I` against several deployed pages on `*.agentwebforms.com` that they send neither `X-Frame-Options` nor a `frame-ancestors` CSP directive, so direct framing is not blocked (these pages are served from Vercel deployments, not from this repo's own Express app, which does set `X-Frame-Options: DENY` on its own API responses only). The iframe's `sandbox` attribute omits `allow-forms`, `allow-popups` and `allow-top-navigation` so a reviewer can't accidentally submit the page's real lead-capture form or get navigated away while scrolling the preview. The existing "open in new tab" link is kept as a fallback for viewing the full page.
- The generation-prompt text (previously always visible) is now collapsed by default behind a "Show generation prompt" toggle, for both ad-image and landing-page pairs.
- Both preview types (image and iframe) now show a skeleton placeholder until the asset finishes loading, instead of a blank box.

## Test plan

- Extended `partner-portal/src/pages/__tests__/CreativeCalibration.test.tsx`: updated the existing landing-page and prompt-visibility assertions for the new markup, and added coverage for the loading-skeleton transition and the inline iframe (src, sandbox attributes, collapsed prompt).
- `npx jest src/pages/__tests__/CreativeCalibration.test.tsx` — 13/13 passing.
- `npx eslint` on the changed files — zero findings.
- `npx tsc -b` — clean.
- Verified the frame-ancestors assumption against live deployed landing pages with `curl -I` (see above) rather than against the shared golden-set calibration page itself, to avoid touching real pairwise-judgment data.

References ENG-2220.

title: [needs human] Separate lead attribution from lead quality in Emma's CRM answers (ENG-2211)
body:
**Bug:** In a CRM chat thread, Emma listed 5 CRM leads (3 Google, 1 Meta, 1 rebate-page) in turn 1, then in turn 2 answered "how many solid leads should we have" with "You have 0" — applying the customer's earlier quality judgment ("these are mistakes") to an attribution question, zeroing the Google-attributed count instead of reporting attribution separately from qualification. Turn 3 then dropped a lead from the count (5→4) without explanation and mixed a 7-day window with a 30-day window across turns. Turn 1 also reported a platform/CRM conversion-count mismatch (Google Ads 0 vs 3 CRM Google leads; Meta pixel 79 vs 1 CRM lead) as if it were a lead count rather than flagging it as a tracking defect.

**Root cause:** `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts` had no guidance distinguishing lead attribution questions from lead quality questions, no rule making CRM records the source of truth over platform pixel/conversion numbers, and no requirement to keep date windows consistent or fully reconcile lead counts across turns — so the LLM was free to blend a quality judgment into an attribution answer.

**Fix:** Added a new `## Lead Attribution vs Lead Quality (CRITICAL)` section (matching the existing pattern used for the `## Analytics & Tracking Claims (CRITICAL)` section from ENG-829) that requires: (1) attribution counted from CRM source/UTM/gclid only, reported separately from quality; (2) CRM as source of truth over platform pixel/conversion numbers, with disagreements flagged as tracking defects, not lead counts; (3) a consistent, explicitly stated date window per rollup; (4) every CRM lead accounted for when a count changes between turns.

**Verification:** Wrote a failing test first (`agentModeSystemPrompt.leadAttributionVsQuality.test.ts`) asserting the new section and its key phrases exist in the prompt, confirmed it failed pre-fix, then added the prompt text and confirmed it passes. Also re-ran the existing analytics-verification prompt test to confirm no regression. Could not pull the referenced prod session (53b4b25f...) — it wasn't retrievable via GetItem on AW-ChatSessions and this environment only has GetItem (no Query/Scan) access to AW-ChatMessages/AW-ChatSessions — so the fix is based on the ticket's detailed description plus this codebase's established pattern for this exact class of bug.

Browser verify: ⚠️ environment down (not verified)

title: Raise rubric judge image download limit to 30MB (ENG-2214)
body:
## Summary

`MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` in `backend/src/services/creativeRubricJudge.ts` was 15MB and enforced against the raw downloaded byte size, before any decode or resize happens. A real 4096x4096 generated ad image (16.8MB) — a placement size the ENG-2139/2187 spec gates already approve as valid — failed with "decoded image exceeds the 15 MB limit", so the rubric judge silently produced a zero score for creatives at real max resolution.

The judge already downscales whatever it decodes successfully to 1568px on the longest edge before sending it to the LLM, so the raw download can safely be allowed through to that existing step instead of being rejected up front.

Raises `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` from 15MB to 30MB to match `CONTENT_CHECK_MAX_BYTES` in `creativeContentCheckRunner.ts`, which is already this codebase's established ceiling for downloading the same kind of generated creative asset elsewhere.
