title: Add creative and account-health adapters to the validation harness
body:
## Summary

ENG-2226. `backend/src/loops/eval/runValidation.ts`'s `defaultGoldenCaseGraders()` only had adapters for agent-surface graders (the session judges and the ENG-2137 agent graders). Creative and account-health had none, so `runGraderValidation.ts` could never succeed for a creative or account-health grader, no matter how many golden cases get labelled on those surfaces -- there was nothing to compare the human label against.

Adds two `GoldenCaseGrader` adapters:

- **`creative-deterministic-gates`**: reads the stored `CreativeGateResult` `humanEvalService` keeps on the human-eval candidate (`creativeGates`, extended by `appendCreativeGateChecks`) and maps `passed`/`failed` onto the `format_readiness` golden criterion -- the ENG-421 floor these gates actually check (decode, blank-render, aspect, size, file size).
- **`account-health-classifier`**: rebuilds an account's current signals the same way `accountHealthClassifierCron.ts`'s `gatherAccountHealthSignals` does, classifies with `classifyAccountHealth`, and maps the resulting state onto the three `account_health` criteria (`activation_incomplete`, `at_risk`, `healthy`), with `at_risk` as the primary criterion since that's what `mayGate('account-health-classifier')` actually unlocks (the oncall page). `insufficient_evidence` and a missing classification both abstain on every criterion rather than guessing.

Both readers use a dynamic `import()` at the call site so `humanEvalService`'s and the cron module's own heavy dependencies (Slack, S3, email, oncall alerting) never load into `runValidation.ts`'s static module graph, matching the existing pattern in `scoreCreativeRubric.ts` and `creativeCalibrationReport.ts`. Both adapters are read-only, keeping this file's existing invariant ("All adapters read only").

## Test plan

title: Guard scoring-judges create/update against concurrent write loss (ENG-2223)
body:
## What

`POST /scoring-judges` and `PUT /scoring-judges/:judgeId` in `backend/src/routes/settings.ts` did a plain read-then-write (`getSetting('scoring-judges')` -> mutate the in-memory array -> `setSetting('scoring-judges', ...)`). Two admin saves landing close together could lose one's update (last-write-wins on the whole array, not per-judge). Found during ENG-2218's review; not introduced by it.

## Fix

Both routes now write via `setSettingIfValueMatches` (the existing conditional/CAS write primitive in `settingsService.ts`, ENG-965), conditioned on the exact raw value each attempt read, inside a bounded retry loop (re-read, re-apply the same field-level change, re-write) on `ConditionalCheckFailedException`. Retry budget is `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5`, matching the codebase's other read-modify-write caller of this primitive (`htmlTemplateService.upsertPublicTemplate`). Exhausting retries throws a descriptive error (logged, 500 response) instead of looping forever or silently dropping an update.

POST's very-first-write-ever case (no row yet) still falls back to a plain unconditioned `setSetting`, since there's nothing to condition on yet — same documented bootstrap gap `upsertPublicTemplate` already accepts.

## Same write path ENG-2218 just hardened

This touches the exact same read-modify-write path that ENG-2218 (P0 shadow-judge data-loss fix) hardened to merge fields onto the existing stored judge object in place, rather than replacing it wholesale, so fields the request body doesn't carry (`shadow`, `sampleRate`, ...) survive an update. That merge-in-place logic is **unchanged** here — it's the same code, just reindented inside the new retry loop. Worth a careful look in review given how recently and how sensitively that logic was fixed.

## Tests

Added to `backend/src/__tests__/settings.scoringJudges.test.ts`:
- POST and PUT: a CAS-conflict test that simulates two concurrent writers via a stale first `getSetting` read vs. a fresh retry read, asserting the retry is conditioned on the fresh value and that **both** writers' changes are preserved in the final write (never a silent overwrite).
- POST and PUT: a retry-exhaustion test asserting a persistent conflict fails loudly (500) after exactly `MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts rather than looping or dropping data.
- Existing tests updated to assert against `setSettingIfValueMatches` instead of `setSetting` where a row already exists, including the ENG-2218 shadow-judge merge-preservation test, which still passes unchanged in behavior.

`npx jest src/__tests__/settings.scoringJudges.test.ts` — 20/20 passing. Full `settings.*` suite (7 files, 87 tests) also green via the pre-push hook.

## Scope

Only POST and PUT for scoring-judges were changed, per the ticket. `DELETE /scoring-judges/:judgeId` was left as-is (out of scope here).

`POST /scoring-judges` and `PUT /scoring-judges/:judgeId` now use compare-and-set writes with up to five retries after conflicts. This limits the change to admin scoring-judge writes and returns HTTP 500 if retries are exhausted. POST still bootstraps a missing setting; PUT retains its field-level merge behavior.

title: Add Google Ads metrics snapshot cron (ENG-2215)
body:
## Summary

Adds a read-only Google Ads campaign / account_day metrics snapshot pipeline, writing to the existing shared `AW-AdsMetricsSnapshots` store (`services/adsMetricsDb.ts`) alongside Meta and LinkedIn.

- `backend/src/cron/googleAdsMetricsSnapshotCron.ts` — mirrors `metaMetricsSnapshotCron.ts`'s overall shape (account enumeration, per-day re-pull/overwrite window, isolation per account/day) but with Google Ads' own specifics:
  - **Units**: converts `metrics.cost_micros` *and* `metrics.average_cpc` (also reported in micros despite its field name) from micros to currency; never stores a raw micros value.
  - **Pagination**: reuses `googleAdsService.search`'s existing page-token walk rather than re-implementing it, and refuses to write a day if that walk's own page cap ever reports the read as truncated.
  - **Settling window**: re-pulls the last 92 days (Google's own conversion attribution window is configurable up to 90 days, per Google Ads Help; +2 days for the same worst-case-timezone buffer Meta's own window uses), not Meta's 28-day window — the two are not the same thing.
- Off by default behind `GOOGLE_ADS_METRICS_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED`, same pattern as every other cron added this cycle (`EVAL_V2_SAMPLER_ENABLED`, `FAILURE_REPLAY_NIGHTLY_ENABLED`, `CREATIVE_CALIBRATION_ENABLED`, `CREATIVE_CONTENT_CHECKS_ENABLED`). Wired into `server.ts` daily at 09:15 UTC, right after the existing Meta cron.
- `backend/src/scripts/googleAdsMetricsSnapshotDryRun.ts` — standalone runner, dry-run by default (reads real accounts and logs what would be written, writes nothing); `--write` makes it live.
- `backend/src/__tests__/eng2215.googleAdsMetricsSnapshot.test.ts` — 18 tests covering: micros→currency conversion for both `cost_micros` and `average_cpc`, correct `AdsPlatform`/entity-key shape, multi-row aggregation, refusal on a truncated page read, the always-written `account_day` row (including zero-campaign days), `parentAccountId` (manager/MCC) handling, dry-run write-suppression, account enumeration/dedupe, and the flag being a complete no-op (no API calls, no writes) when unset.

Ad-level rows and CRM lead attribution are not implemented here — only campaign and account_day rows. More importantly, **linking a generated creative to the Google Ads ad it became (creative lineage) is explicitly out of scope for this PR** and is tracked separately; this PR only covers the data/snapshot half of the original ask.

title: [ENG-2231] LLM call timeout can be non-integer ms, crashing the OpenAI SDK call
body:
Linear: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2231/llm-call-timeout-can-be-non-integer-ms-crashing-the-openai-sdk-call

## Summary
`turnTimeBudget.ts`'s synthesis reserve calculation (`totalMs / 2`) can produce a non-integer millisecond value, which flows unrounded into the per-call LLM timeout. The OpenAI SDK's `validatePositiveInteger` rejects it (`Error: timeout must be an integer`), forcing a degraded final-synthesis fallback or a cancelled orphaned worker run — the user gets a partial or missing answer.

Root cause (located, not yet fixed):
- `backend/src/utils/turnTimeBudget.ts`, `evaluateTurnTimeBudget`: `const reserveMs = Math.min(Math.max(baseReserve, slowestCallReserve), totalMs / 2);` — fractional when `totalMs` is odd.
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` (~line 4309): fractional `reserveMs` can make `llmCallTimeoutMs` fractional; nothing downstream rounds it before `openRouterPlatformTransport.ts` passes `{ timeout: timeoutMs }` to the SDK.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `reserveMs` / final `llmCallTimeoutMs` is always an integer (e.g. `Math.floor`/`Math.round`) before use as a deadline or SDK timeout.
- [ ] Regression test on `evaluateTurnTimeBudget` with an odd `totalMs` pins the integer invariant.
- [ ] Existing related unit tests pass.

## Note
Linear (ENG-2231) is the source of truth. Sync status there; do not treat this GitHub issue as authoritative.

title: [ENG-1728] v0 iterate guard: persist pre-send version + serialize concurrent edits on same chat
body:
Linear: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-1728/v0-iterate-guard-persist-pre-send-version-serialize-concurrent-edits

## Summary
Follow-up from CodeRabbit review on PR #2745 (ENG-1694). Two related gaps in `guardedV0IterateMessage` / `iterateLandingPage`:
1. If the process dies between the guard recording success and `pendingIteration` being stored, a retry reads the post-edit version as `baseVersionId`, the guard skips the already-sent message, and the retry waits for a newer version no send will create -> `V0_GENERATION_TIMEOUT`. Fix: persist the pre-send version durably with the reservation, or return it from the guard, so a skipped retry resumes against the original base version.
2. Two DIFFERENT edits (different content hashes) can both pass the guard concurrently after reading the same `baseVersionId`. Fix: atomic per-chat/page iteration lease; queue or retry a distinct message only after the active iteration reaches a terminal state.

Source: https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb/pull/2745#discussion_r3923783500

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Skipped retry resumes against the original pre-send base version (no V0_GENERATION_TIMEOUT on retry-after-crash).
- [ ] Concurrent distinct edits on the same chat/page are serialized via a per-chat/page lease.
- [ ] Related existing tests pass.

Linear (ENG-1728) is the source of truth. Sync status there; do not treat this GitHub issue as authoritative.

title: fix(ENG-2215): enumerateDistinctGoogleAdsAccounts avoids getAllUsers() fan-out
body:
## Problem

Found while doing live production verification of ENG-2215 (PR #3167): `enumerateDistinctGoogleAdsAccounts()` calls `userDb.getAllUsers()`, which internally fans out three full secondary-index scans (AW-Tasks, AW-Workflows, AW-ChatSessions) per user, purely to compute admin-dashboard display counts this code never uses. Isolated the call against real prod data and it ran past 60s with zero output — not even the first `console.log`, since the hang is inside the single `await userDb.getAllUsers()` call.

The cron is flag-gated off (`GOOGLE_ADS_METRICS_SNAPSHOT_ENABLED`) by default, so this hasn't affected production directly yet, but it would make every run of this cron unacceptably slow (and likely timeout) once the flag is enabled.

## Fix

Switch to `userDb.scanWithFilter('attribute_exists(connected_accounts)', {})` — the same pattern `connectedAccountsDb.ts`'s `getAccountsByAttioWorkspaceId` already documents and uses to avoid this exact fan-out. Re-added the eval/sandbox user exclusion explicitly, since `scanWithFilter` (unlike `getAllUsers()`) doesn't apply it by default.

## Verification

- Updated/added unit tests (20/20 passing), including new coverage for eval-user exclusion and for using `scanWithFilter` with the correct filter expression.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Re-ran against real prod data: enumeration now completes in ~11s (previously timed out past 60s) and correctly finds 11 distinct connected Google Ads accounts.

title: Seat-based billing — Phase 3: LLM usage credit grant
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of seat-based billing (ENG-2247): orgs on Starter/Pro can buy extra
team seats at $50/month each, and $30 of that becomes additional shared LLM
usage credit for the org. This PR grants that credit monthly, for every
organization with `purchasedExtraSeats > 0`.

- `backend/src/services/orgSeatCreditGrantService.ts` — for each org with
  `purchasedExtraSeats > 0`, calls the existing
  `grantMonthlyLlmUsageCredit` (`llmUsageCreditService.ts`, merged in Phase 1)
  with `source: 'purchase'`, `amountMicroUsd: 30_000_000 * purchasedExtraSeats`,
  `billingUserId: organization.ownerUserId`, and a deterministic grant id
  `seat-credit:{orgId}:{usageMonth}` (reusing the existing
  `getCurrentUsageMonth()` for the month key). Orgs with `purchasedExtraSeats`
  absent or ≤ 0 are skipped before any call is made — no wasted or
  zero-amount grants.
- `backend/src/cron/orgSeatCreditGrantCron.ts` + a registration block in
  `server.ts` — a daily sweep, anchored to a fixed UTC hour via the existing
  `utils/dailySchedule.ts` helper.

## Where/how I found and hooked into the existing reset cadence

I read `tokenUsageService.ts` looking for a scheduled job that resets the
org's monthly usage/cost counters, and traced every lead (`cron/`, `scripts/`)
back to the conclusion that **there isn't one**: the per-user token/cost
counters reset *lazily*, in place, the moment `getUserTokenUsage` /
`incrementUserTokenUsage` notice the stored `month` no longer matches
`getCurrentUsageMonth()`. There is no central "month rolled over" event and
nothing to extend directly — a hypothetical edit at those lazy-reset call
sites would only fire for a user who happens to incur usage that month, which
is backwards for a credit that must land for every org with purchased seats
whether or not anyone used anything yet.

So this ships as a **sibling scheduled sweep** running at the identical
*monthly* granularity: it keys off the exact same `getCurrentUsageMonth()`
the usage ledger itself resets on, scoping the grant id to it so a daily
sweep (or any number of process restarts within the same calendar month) is
a no-op after the first grant. The daily cadence itself (rather than some
finer or coarser interval) matches the existing `metaTrackingMonitorCron` /
`accountHealthClassifierCron` pattern of anchoring to a fixed UTC hour via
`dailySchedule.ts`, since (per that file's own comment) a naive 24h
`setInterval` never elapses in this environment — PRs merge every 1-2 hours
and each merge restarts the process.

Idempotency itself is **not** reimplemented — it's entirely delegated to
`grantMonthlyLlmUsageCredit`'s own grantId ledger +
`ConditionalCheckFailedException` retry loop. This PR's only job is deciding,
once per org per sweep, what to call that function with.

## Judgment calls

- No scheduled "month reset" trigger exists to extend directly (see above) —
  added a sibling daily cron instead, matching this codebase's existing
  pattern for monthly-cadence crons that must survive frequent redeploys.
- Deliberately did **not** touch `llmUsageTopUpService.ts` /
  `validateLlmUsageTopUpConfig` — settled product decision that seat credits
  run at a different, lower margin than ordinary top-ups.
- `purchasedExtraSeats` is floored and must be a finite positive number
  before anything is attempted; a negative or non-finite value is treated
  the same as absent/0 (skip), not an error.

## Mutation-check results

- Changed `SEAT_CREDIT_MICRO_USD_PER_SEAT` from `30_000_000` to `25_000_000`
  → the reconciliation test (and both idempotency tests, which also assert
  exact amounts) failed as expected. Reverted, confirmed green.
- Broke the idempotency guard by appending `Math.random()` to
  `seatCreditGrantId` → both idempotency tests failed as expected (second
  run granted again instead of being a no-op). Reverted, confirmed green.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd backend && npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm test -- --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/orgSeatCreditGrantService.test.ts` — 4/4 passing
      (reconciliation: sum of credited amounts across orgs with 0/absent/1/7
      purchased seats exactly equals `30_000_000 * sum(purchasedExtraSeats)`;
      idempotency: running the sweep, and the per-org grant call, twice for
      the same org/month does not double-grant)
- [x] Existing `llmUsageCreditService.test.ts`, `llmUsageCreditDebit.test.ts`,
      `orgSeatService.test.ts`, `admin.llmUsageCredit.test.ts` — all still
      passing (58/58 across the combined run)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Risk: Medium — the daily sweep grants shared LLM usage credit, and correcting an issued grant may require ledger changes. Month-scoped grant IDs prevent duplicate grants, and per-organization failures do not stop the sweep.

Adds a daily sweep at 10:00 UTC. It grants $30 per floored purchased seat to the organization owner for the current usage month. Mid-month seat increases are not back-filled; the updated seat total applies next month.

title: Seat-based billing — Phase 2: Stripe billing plumbing
body:
## Summary

Phase 2 of seat-based billing (Phase 1 — `purchasedExtraSeats` and `orgSeatService.ts` — already merged on `main`). This PR wires that cap math up to real Stripe billing:

- **`backend/src/services/subscriptionService.ts`**: `SubscriptionType.seatPricing?: { priceCents, usageCreditMicroUsd, baseSeats }` — admin-configurable, no hardcoded dollar amounts.
- **`backend/src/routes/admin.ts`**: `GET`/`POST /api/admin/subscription-types` whitelist, validate (positive-integer `priceCents`/`usageCreditMicroUsd`, non-negative-integer `baseSeats`), and persist `seatPricing`, mirroring the existing `llmUsageTopUp` pattern exactly.
- **`partner-portal/.../SubscriptionTypesTab.tsx`**: a seat-pricing form section (price $/mo, usage credit $/mo, base seats), modeled on the top-up UI's state/input/save-mapping pattern.
- **`backend/src/services/orgSeatBillingService.ts`** (new): the Stripe-facing core —
  - `setOrgSeatQuantity(orgId, totalExtraSeats)` — finds the org owner's live subscription's seat line item by matching `price.product` against `STRIPE_EXTRA_SEAT_PRODUCT_ID` (no stored item-id field to drift), and creates/updates it with fresh `price_data` from the *currently* configured `seatPricing`, or deletes it when `totalExtraSeats === 0`.
  - `purchaseExtraSeat(orgId)` / `removeExtraSeat(orgId)` — read the live Stripe quantity (never the DB mirror), adjust by one, and delegate to `setOrgSeatQuantity`. `removeExtraSeat` refuses (descriptive error) if the result would drop below the org's currently-occupied extra seats, computed from live member count and `orgSeatService.baseSeatsForTier`.
  - Every `price_data` update also passes `quantity` explicitly — Stripe's own type docs confirm updating a subscription item's price resets `quantity` to 1 otherwise.
  - Does **not** write `Organization.purchasedExtraSeats` — Stripe stays the source of truth; the DB mirror is the webhook's job.
- **`backend/src/services/stripeService.ts`**: `handleSubscriptionUpdated` (the real `customer.subscription.updated`/`.created` handler, invoked from `controllers/stripeController.ts`) now mirrors the seat item's quantity onto `Organization.purchasedExtraSeats` when the subscription belongs to an org's billing owner — idempotent, and a no-op when the product id is unconfigured.
- **`backend/src/routes/org.ts`**: `POST`/`DELETE /api/org/:orgId/seats`, gated by `orgAuthz.isBillingRoot` (403 otherwise), returning `{ newTotalSeats, effectiveCap }`. A `removeExtraSeat` occupied-seat refusal surfaces as 400.
- **`.env.example`**: documents the new `STRIPE_EXTRA_SEAT_PRODUCT_ID` var.

Covers Linear tickets **ENG-2243 through ENG-2246**.

## Judgment calls (please review)

1. **Webhook file location**: the spec pointed at `backend/src/routes/webhooks.ts` for "the existing Stripe subscription-updated webhook handler," but that logic actually lives in `stripeService.handleSubscriptionUpdated` (invoked from `controllers/stripeController.ts`'s `handleWebhook`, routed via `routes/stripe.ts`). I extended it there instead of adding a second, divergent handler in `webhooks.ts`.
2. **New endpoint location**: put the two seat endpoints in `routes/org.ts` (already `/api/org/:orgId/...`-shaped, already `authenticateToken`-gated at the router level, already has an `isBillingRoot`-eligible owner-only precedent in its `DELETE /:orgId` route) rather than a new router file.
3. **`effectiveCap` computed from the service's return value, not a re-read of the org**: since `Organization.purchasedExtraSeats` is only updated by the webhook (which can lag), the route computes `effectiveCap` from the `newTotalSeats` `purchaseExtraSeat`/`removeExtraSeat` actually returned, not a fresh DB read, so the response is never stale relative to the write that just happened.
4. **`removeExtraSeat`'s "currently needed" formula on an unlimited tier**: when `baseSeatsForTier` returns `null` (no cap — e.g. Managed), I treat "currently needed extra seats" as 0, so the refusal never fires for such a tier (it shouldn't have purchased seats via this path in the first place, but this keeps the function total rather than throwing on a tier it wasn't designed for).
5. **Stripe client construction**: followed `mrrCollectionGapService.ts`'s lazy-singleton + `createStripeClient` pattern exactly (same as the test mocking pattern in `mrrCollectionGapService.test.ts`) rather than reusing `stripeService.ts`'s private (unexported) `getStripeOrThrow`.
6. **No Stripe webhook test added**: the existing `handleSubscriptionUpdated` call sites in `stripeUpgrade.test.ts` / `stripeOfferSync.test.ts` / `stripe.test.ts` / `stripeDowngrade.test.ts` don't set `user.orgId`, so the new seat-sync branch is inert in all of them (confirmed green — no regressions) but isn't itself exercised by a new test; the core sync logic (`findSeatLineItem` matching, quantity read) is already covered by `orgSeatBillingService.test.ts`, and the webhook glue is a few straightforward lines. Flagging in case you want a dedicated webhook-level test added.

## Test plan

- [x] `cd backend && npm run typecheck` — clean after every `.ts` edit
- [x] `npm test -- --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/orgSeatBillingService.test.ts` — 21/21 pass, including a hand-verified mutation check (temporarily dropped the explicit `quantity` from the update call — 4 tests failed as expected — restored)
- [x] `npm test -- --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/orgSeatBillingRoutes.test.ts` — 8/8 pass (owner-only gating, 400/403/404/500 mapping)
- [x] Regression check: `src/__tests__/org.test.ts`, `orgCrossTenant.proof.test.ts` (57/57) and `stripeUpgrade/stripeOfferSync/stripe/stripeDowngrade.test.ts` (51/52, 1 pre-existing skip) all still pass
- [x] `partner-portal`: `npx tsc -b --force` clean

title: Seat-based billing — expose seat info and enforce the cap on new memberships
body:
## Summary

This is the final backend piece of seat-based billing. All groundwork (`Organization.purchasedExtraSeats`, `orgSeatService.ts`, `orgSeatBillingService.ts`, admin-configurable `seatPricing`, owner-gated purchase/remove endpoints) is already on `main`. This PR:

1. **Exposes seat info on `GET /api/org/me`.** Adds a `seatInfo` object (`baseSeats`, `purchasedExtraSeats`, `effectiveCap`, `currentMemberCount`) computed from the org owner's resolved tier via the existing `baseSeatsForTier`/`effectiveSeatCap` helpers. `seatInfo` is omitted entirely (not sent as `null`) for an uncapped tier, so the frontend's already-built paywall/usage UI — which has been silently inert because the backend never sent this field — works with zero frontend changes. The extra `getOrgMemberCount` read only happens for a capped tier.
2. **Enforces the seat cap on new membership creation.** Wires `orgSeatService.assertSeatAvailable` into all three paths that create a membership: `POST /:orgId/invite`, `POST /accept-invite`, and `POST /:orgId/domain-requests/:requestToken/approve`. A `SeatLimitReachedError` maps to `409 { error, code: "SEAT_LIMIT_REACHED" }`; every other error keeps its existing handling.

**No data migration and no automatic Stripe/billing change for any existing org.** Nothing is backfilled, nothing is auto-charged. This covers ENG-2250, and — per the updated product decision — effectively closes the scope of ENG-2248/2249 differently than originally planned: there was never any data to backfill, so there is no migration ticket to do. An org that is already over its effective cap today (there was never a cap before this feature) keeps every existing member untouched; it simply cannot add a new one until the owner purchases enough extra seats to cover current headcount, or removes someone. This is the confirmed, intended behavior for an over-cap org going forward, not a gap to soften.

## Judgment calls

- **Invite-time vs. accept-time vs. both**: checked at **both**. The invite-send check (`POST /:orgId/invite`) gives the owner the paywall immediately, at the point they're deciding whether to invite. The accept-time check (`POST /accept-invite`) is the one that actually prevents overfill, since a pending invite doesn't occupy a seat and time can pass between send and accept during which the org can fill up some other way (another invite accepted, a domain-join auto-approved). `POST /:orgId/domain-requests/:requestToken/approve` gets the same re-check, for the same reason — a domain-join request can also sit pending for a while.
- **Where exactly to place each check**: right before the action that actually creates/reserves the membership (token generation for invite; `userDb.joinOrg` for accept-invite and domain approval), after all the existing cheap/authz checks, so a seat check never runs before a 400/403/404 that would've fired anyway.
- **Error mapping**: added a small shared `respondIfSeatLimitReached` helper rather than duplicating the `instanceof SeatLimitReachedError` check three times, mirroring the existing `mapSeatBillingError` pattern already used by the purchase/remove-seat endpoints in this file.
- **Stale test invariant removed**: `org.test.ts` had a test literally titled "does not cap org size — an invite succeeds well past the old limit of 5," seeded with a Starter-tier org at 13 members. That invariant is exactly what ENG-2250 intentionally reverses for capped tiers, so I replaced it with the required "already over-cap before this feature" 409 test (and added a below-cap success case alongside it) rather than leaving a red test or working around it.
- **Stale comment cleanup**: `orgSeatService.ts`'s header comment explicitly said `assertSeatAvailable` must not be wired in before an "existing-org rollout backfill" — exactly the plan this task's updated product decision supersedes. Updated it to describe current reality (wired in, no backfill, no auto-billing) rather than leave a misleading comment next to the code it was warning against.
- **New test file vs. extending existing ones**: added `orgSeatEnforcement.test.ts` for accept-invite and domain-join-approval cap coverage, since neither existing file for those routes (`org.test.ts`'s accept-invite section, `org.domainAutoJoin.test.ts`) had `subscriptionService` mocked in a way that made the owner's tier controllable — easier to add a small focused file than retrofit two others. `assertSeatAvailable`'s own boundary math (exact-at-cap, purchased-seat arithmetic) is already covered by the pre-existing `orgSeatService.test.ts` and isn't re-derived at the route layer.

title: Stop Emma inferring a paid channel for untagged CRM leads (ENG-2260)
body:
**Bug:** Emma folded a lead sourced only as "via the Mountain View Heat Pump Rebate page" (no UTM source, gclid, or other click ID) into Google Ads attribution — reasoning from the page name via domain-knowledge pattern-matching ("rebate pages are a Google Ads thing") rather than an actual tag. The lead was correctly categorized the first time a real CRM tool call returned its (untagged) attribution, but drifted into "Google Ads" on a later turn when Emma re-derived the rollup from her own prior conversational prose instead of the tool data, because that prose never flagged the lead as untagged in the first place.

**Root cause:** found live-testing the ENG-2211 fix in production (read-only, test account only) — a faithful reproduction of the real incident surfaced this adjacent bug. ENG-2211 fixed Emma using a *quality* judgment to override an *attribution* count; this is a different mechanism — contextual inference filling in for a missing tag, and that inference surviving into later-turn rollups once the original "untagged" signal is lost in translation to prose.

**Fix:** two rules added to the same `## Lead Attribution vs Lead Quality (CRITICAL)` section:
1. Never infer a paid channel from a landing page name, campaign-adjacent wording, or similar context — only an explicit UTM source/gclid/click ID counts as a tag. An untagged lead is its own distinct "source unknown / untagged" bucket, and the untagged status must be stated explicitly on first mention (not just the page/campaign name) so it survives into later turns even when Emma is summarizing from conversation history rather than re-querying the CRM.
2. When recomputing a rollup in a later turn from memory rather than a fresh tool call, trust the CRM tag over earlier prose — never let an untagged lead drift into a specific channel through pattern-matching, and re-check with the CRM tool if unsure.

**Verification:**
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeSystemPrompt.untaggedLeadAttribution.test.ts` — new test, pins both rules' key phrases
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeSystemPrompt.leadAttributionVsQuality.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeSystemPrompt.analyticsVerification.test.ts` — no regression
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- Live-tested on preview with real CRM data (3 leads: Google-tagged, Meta-tagged, and an untagged lead sourced only by page name): first mention correctly bucketed the untagged lead as "Source Unknown / Untagged" with explicit "no tracked click ID" language; a later-turn follow-up answered purely from memory (zero tool calls) and still correctly held the untagged lead out of Google Ads.

Related: ENG-2211 (parent incident), ENG-2260 (this ticket)

title: Seat-based billing — observability for purchases, removals, and credit grants
body:
## Summary

Adds structured observability for seat-based billing's three money-relevant operations, per ENG-2256. Purely additive — no business logic, return values, or API responses changed.

- **`orgSeatBillingService.ts`**
  - Logs `[orgSeatBillingService] seat purchased` (`orgId`, `newTotalSeats`, `priceCentsCharged`) and `[orgSeatBillingService] seat removed` (`orgId`, `newTotalSeats`) at `console.info`, placed inside `setOrgSeatQuantity` — the single function that actually talks to Stripe for extra seats — derived from comparing the seat line item's quantity before/after the mutation. This avoids re-fetching tier/pricing data a second time in `purchaseExtraSeat`/`removeExtraSeat` just for logging, and keeps `setOrgSeatQuantity`'s return type (`Promise<void>`) unchanged.
  - Logs the two expected refusal paths at `console.warn` (not error — these are handled, customer-facing walls, not system failures): "owner has no Stripe subscription" (shared by both purchase and removal, since both route through `getOwnerWithLiveSubscription`) and "seat occupied, can't remove" (in `removeExtraSeat`'s occupied-seat floor check).

- **`orgSeatCreditGrantService.ts` / `cron/orgSeatCreditGrantCron.ts`**
  - Checked whether the sweep's summary (`scanned`/`eligible`/`granted`/`idempotent`/`failed`/`totalGrantedMicroUsd`) is logged after each run. It already is — `runOrgSeatCreditGrant` in `cron/orgSeatCreditGrantCron.ts` logs `console.info('[OrgSeatCreditGrantCron] completed', summary)` on success and `console.error(... 'completed with failures' ...)` when `failed > 0`. No change needed here.

- **Metrics/analytics system**: searched `llmUsageCreditService.ts` and `usageRecordDb.ts`/`usageRecorderService.ts` for a structured logger, a dedicated metrics client, or an analytics-emission pattern for financial events. Found none — money-relevant operations in this codebase (`usageRecorderService.ts`'s `[usageRecorder]`/`[spendLedgerShadow]`/`[vendorRateCard]` failure/warn logs, `orgSeatCreditGrantService.ts`'s existing `[orgSeatCreditGrantService]` idempotent-skip log) all use tagged `console.log`/`console.warn`/`console.error`/`console.info`, not a separate metrics/analytics system. Matched that convention rather than introducing new logging infrastructure.

## Convention matched

Bracketed-module-name-tagged `console.*` calls with a structured fields object as the second argument (e.g. `console.info('[AdsLearning] capture confirmed', { recommendationId, mode })`, `console.warn('[approval-inbox-slack] ...', ...)`), `console.error`/`console.warn` reserved for failures/refusals and `console.info`/`console.log` for routine/expected events — consistent with `orgSeatCreditGrantService.ts`'s own existing idempotent-skip log and `usageRecorderService.ts`'s throttled failure logs.

title: Fix revenueService.ts and stripe.ts items.data[0] hazard (ENG-2257)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to seat-based billing's code review, which fixed the `items.data[0]` hazard in `stripeService.ts` (a subscription can now carry a second, seat-billing extra-seat line item alongside the plan item, and Stripe doesn't document `items.data` as stably ordered). That review added `findBasePlanItem()` to `stripeService.ts` and fixed every plan-mutating call site there, but the bug class existed in a few places outside that feature's scope. This covers **ENG-2257**.

## Call sites found and what was done

| File | Site | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `services/revenueService.ts` | `getMonthlyAmount()` — `sub.items.data[0]` | **Fixed.** Now uses `findBasePlanItem()`. This function prices every MRR/ARR/churn/cohort/ARPU/LTV figure computed in this file, and is also called by `mrrCollectionGapService.detectMrrCollectionGaps()` for its "below contracted price" check — so this was the highest blast-radius site found. |
| `routes/stripe.ts` | `/upgrade` endpoint — `currentPriceId = currentSub.items.data[0]?.price?.id` | **Fixed.** Now uses `findBasePlanItem()`. This value gates the "already on this plan" short-circuit and the cached `scheduledChange.toTier` on a downgrade — a seat item sorting first could previously compare the seat's price instead of the plan's. |
| `routes/crm.ts` | lead-enrichment `getStripeSubscriptionForCustomer()` — `sub.items?.data?.[0]?.price` used to compute `mrrCents` | **Fixed.** Same MRR-pricing hazard as `revenueService.ts`, just for a CRM lead card. Imported `findBasePlanItem` dynamically (matching `routes/stripe.ts`'s existing pattern) so this route doesn't eagerly pull `stripeService`'s transitive import graph (notably `waitlistDb`'s module-load-time `AWS.config.update`) into requests that never hit this branch — a static import here broke an existing, unrelated test (`crm.cardRevenueRefresh.test.ts`) that partially mocks `aws-sdk`. |
| `controllers/stripeController.ts` | `recordSubscriptionEvent()` — `data.items?.data?.[0]?.price?.id` | **Fixed.** Records the `priceId` into the payment-history audit trail for `customer.subscription.{created,updated,deleted}` webhooks; a seat purchase fires `subscription.updated` too, so this could log the seat's price instead of the plan's. |
| `services/stripeService.ts` | `findBasePlanItem()` | Already exported by the seat-billing review — no change needed. |

## Left alone (not an items.data[0]-identifies-the-base-plan hazard)

- `routes/stripe.ts` — three `current_period_end` reads (`items?.data?.[0]?.current_period_end`). `current_period_end` is the same across every item on a subscription (same billing cycle), unlike price — reading it off any item is safe regardless of seat-item ordering. Matches the existing `getSubscriptionPeriodEndIso()` precedent in `stripeService.ts`.
- `stripeService.ts`'s four previously-reviewed "low-risk" sites (`syncSubscriptionFromStripe`, `handleSubscriptionDeleted`, `deriveSubscriptionType`, `reconcileStripeUser`) — already carry `NOTE` comments from the seat-billing review explaining why a wrong read there only skips an additive tier-sync/backfill rather than corrupting billing state or misreporting revenue. Left as-is per that review's reasoning.

## Tests

- Added `services/revenueService.test.ts`: `getMonthlyAmount()` against a single-item sub (unaffected), a two-item sub in both orderings (plan-then-seat, seat-then-plan), the no-seat-env-var fallback, yearly-price conversion, and discount application — all pinned to price off the plan item.
- Extended `stripeUpgrade.test.ts`'s existing seat-billing describe block with two tests covering the `routes/stripe.ts` fix: "already on this plan" detection and a genuine plan change, both with the seat item sorting first in `items.data`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx jest src/__tests__/revenueService.test.ts` — 7/7 pass
- [x] `npx jest --testPathPattern="stripe|revenueService|mrrCollectionGap"` — 18 suites / 172 tests pass (incl. `stripe.test.ts`, `stripeUpgrade.test.ts`, `stripeDowngrade.test.ts`, `admin.stripeCustomerId.test.ts`)

title: Require a fresh CRM query before restating a lead total (ENG-2262)
body:
**Bug:** Emma answered a lead-count rollup purely from memory of an earlier turn, with no signal that the underlying CRM list had changed out-of-band (a lead deleted directly via the API, simulating the customer removing it via the CRM UI mid-conversation). She confidently restated the stale total with zero tool calls and no caveat.

**Root cause:** found live-testing the ENG-2260 fix with a deeper multi-case scenario. ENG-2211's existing "account for every lead" rule only fires once Emma already knows a count changed (`"if a count changes between turns... name which lead moved"`) — it never required her to proactively re-check before stating a total as current in the first place. A silent out-of-band deletion gives her no such signal.

**Fix:** a new rule requiring a fresh CRM query before restating a total or breakdown as current. Explicitly scoped to counts of the mutable dataset itself — distinct from an individual lead's own already-established attribution tag or quality note, which stays safe to recall from memory (the behavior ENG-2260 just fixed and tested). The rule is careful not to regress that: it only fires on "how many / total / right now / any rollup" questions, not on recalling an already-discussed lead's channel.

**Verification:**
- `npx jest src/__tests__/agentModeSystemPrompt.crmRollupStaleness.test.ts` — new test, pins the rule
- Full `agentModeSystemPrompt.*` suite (27 files, 195 tests) — no regression, confirmed via pre-push hook
- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- Live-tested on preview with the exact failing scenario reproduced: 3 real CRM leads, established a baseline rollup, an unrelated distraction turn, then deleted one lead directly via the API (simulating a UI deletion mid-chat), then re-asked the same "how many total" question. Before this fix: confidently restated the stale count, zero tool calls. After this fix: fresh `get_lead_lists`/`get_leads` calls fired, and the response explicitly reconciled — *"shows we now have 2 leads in total (down from 3, as Jordan Lee was removed from the list)."*

title: Floor the synthesis-reserve budget so it's always an integer ms (ENG-2231)
body:
**Bug:** `reserveMs` in `evaluateTurnTimeBudget` could come out fractional two independent ways — `totalMs/2` on an odd `totalMs`, or `slowestCallReserve`'s `*1.25` multiplier on an odd `longestLlmCallMs`. `reserveMs` is handed straight through to `llmCallTimeoutMs` a few calls downstream in `agentModeService.ts`, which is passed as the OpenAI SDK's `timeout` option — the SDK's own `validatePositiveInteger` throws `"timeout must be an integer"` on anything fractional, killing the LLM call and forcing a degraded "final synthesis" fallback mid-run.

**Found:** during the ENG-2211 investigation — reproduced twice on the WaterHeater.app account's own production logs (`LLM call timed out for session ... at iteration 2 — forcing a final synthesis`), independently confirmed not the trigger for that specific incident but a real, separate, reproducible defect.

**Fix:** floor the whole `reserveMs` expression once at the source in `evaluateTurnTimeBudget`, rather than patching the one downstream call site that happens to crash — `reserveMs` has multiple consumers (3 call sites in `agentModeService.ts`), and flooring at the source guarantees the integer invariant for all of them, not just the one that's currently exercised.

**Verification:**
- Two new unit tests pin the exact failure mode: an odd `totalMs` forcing a fractional `totalMs/2`, and an odd `longestLlmCallMs` forcing a fractional `*1.25` result — both now assert `reserveMs` is an integer.
- `npx jest src/utils/__tests__/turnTimeBudget.test.ts src/__tests__/agentMode/characterization/turnTimeBudgetTruncation.test.ts` — 37 tests pass, including the existing characterization test that already exercises the "LLM call timed out → forcing final synthesis" path end-to-end.
- `npm run typecheck` — clean.

This is a deterministic code bug, not an LLM-behavior question — the unit tests directly reproduce and prove the fix for the exact fractional-input conditions. Live-reproducing the original crash in production isn't practically forceable (it depends on wall-clock timing landing on an odd ms value), so this one is proven by direct test coverage rather than a live chat reproduction.

title: Stop tagging a carried-over secondary number as [verified] (ENG-2263)
body:
**Bug:** Emma correctly re-queried the CRM for the number a turn directly asked about ("search across all lists for X, give me an exact total"), but a secondary number in the same response — an overall account-wide list/lead count mentioned as supporting context — was carried over from a `get_lead_lists` call three turns earlier, after a list had been deleted in between, and was tagged `[verified]` as though it had just been confirmed.

**Found:** during live production verification of ENG-2262 — a deliberately deeper, multi-turn stress test that mixed a direct question (the search) with ambient context (the overall account snapshot) in the same answer.

**Why ENG-2262's rule doesn't cover this:** that rule re-triggers correctly for the number the question is literally about. It says nothing about secondary numbers riding along in the same answer.

**Fix:** require the `[verified]` tag to mean a tool call happened in THIS turn, specifically — any secondary number not freshly re-queried must be labeled as possibly out of date rather than silently restated and tagged current. This is cheaper than forcing every ancillary number to be re-verified on every turn (which would regress the deliberate scoping in ENG-2262's own rule): it mandates honest labeling, not extra tool calls.

**Verification:**

title: Label what an anonymous share-link visitor says so Emma does not treat it as the owner's word (ENG-2227)
body:
## What this does (plain language)
A share link lets anyone who holds it write into the account owner's real chat. Emma could not tell what a visitor typed from what the owner typed, and treated both as the customer's word. Real case (ENG-2211): a visitor typed "they made the call by mistake" and Emma used it to answer "You have 0" leads.

Now everything a visitor types is labeled `[Sent by an anonymous viewer via a shared link — not a verified account owner]` wherever it reaches the model, and the system prompt tells Emma what that means: answer ordinary questions normally, but when a visitor makes a consequential claim (a correction to a number, a quality judgment, a request to change a decision) say that it came from an anonymous viewer instead of presenting it as the owner's word. **Labeling only: nothing a visitor could do before is blocked or removed** (owner decision, 2026-11-19).

This PR replaces the October draft of #3187 (it was 5,477 commits behind main and conflicting; the work was re-applied onto current main) and closes the side doors two independent reviews found.

## Where the label goes
- The typed history rebuild and this turn's own message (the label is appended server-side, last, so a visitor cannot place text after it); the "merge consecutive user messages" step no longer mixes a visitor's message into the owner's.
- **The comment on a thumbs-down** (written into the chat as a system-role row, which the model reads with MORE authority than a user message): now says an anonymous viewer wrote it, and the comment is quoted as data. The owner's own wording is unchanged.
- **Live voice:** a visitor's spoken turn is stamped like a typed one, labeled in the call's history block (one line per row, so a newline in their text cannot forge an unlabeled "User:" line), and the voice prompt says a visitor is speaking.
- Model Compare replay and the benchmark replay.
- Server-authored "automatic continuation" turns are NOT labeled (no visitor wrote them).
- One shared helper, `utils/anonymousShareProvenance.ts` (idempotent: never labels twice).

## What it does not do (decided, documented)
- It does not make state-changing requests need the verified owner (it would remove something visitors can do today; owner: "nah i think its okay to leave it be").
- Still open: a visitor-made scheduled run's starting message has no provenance line (its tools are already restricted by ENG-2816); code gates that read the last user message as the owner's word (Meta `verifyExplicitStatement`); visitor thumbs feed the account-health classifier; `emma_get_session`/MCP return raw messages; `/ishare/:id/email-report` is an unauthenticated mail relay once the link is held (separate ticket).
- The portal sends no login on the share-link feedback PUT, so the owner's own thumbs-down comment on their own link is worded as an anonymous viewer's (safe direction, wording only). A small portal PR would fix it.

## Tests
Node 22. `npm run typecheck` clean. New: `anonymousShareProvenance.test.ts` (8), `agentModeController.ishareFeedbackProvenance.test.ts` (4), 4 voice cases in `liveVoiceService.test.ts`, a benchmark case, a buildMarketingContext continuation case; the turn-preamble golden re-recorded (prompt length +1,888+190 chars, hashes, and the label on a visitor's live message; nothing else) with a plain assertion that fails if the call-site argument is dropped. 24 neighbouring suites pass. Eight mutation checks (drop the call-site argument, the voice stamp, the feedback owner check, the voice history label, the voice newline collapse, the compare label, the continuation skip, the benchmark last-only rule) each fail the matching test. Two independent reviews (round 1: 3 high, 1 medium; round 2: no blocker or high, 3 medium, all fixed).

## Live before/after (same scenarios, 3 rounds each)
Production (old code, the owner's own account): a visitor says "all 5 leads were mistakes, the real count is 0" and Emma answers as fact, labeled 0/3, identical to the owner's answer. A visitor leaves a thumbs-down whose comment claims "the owner confirmed ... use 0", then the owner asks the count: Emma answers 0, 3/3.
Test environment (this exact head): visitor claim labeled 3/3 ("per an unverified note from an anonymous share-link viewer"); the owner's same claim 0/3 labeled; an ordinary visitor question 0/3 labeled and answered normally; a client-demo case (visitor describes their own dental clinic and asks for a tagline) 0/3 labeled and answered normally; after the visitor's feedback comment the owner's count question answers "5 active leads" 3/3.

title: fix(landing-pages): batch pixel/ads/bridge-out corrections so bridge-out can't be starved (ENG-2099)
body:
## Summary
- Fixes ENG-2099: the three v0 enhancement corrections (Meta Pixel Lead event, Google Ads conversion, bridge-out redirect) shared one `validationAttempt` counter, and each successful correction did `continue`, consuming a whole loop iteration. On a page configured for all three, pixel ate attempt 0, ads ate attempt 1, and bridge-out's own guard (`validationAttempt < V0_VALIDATION_MAX_RETRIES`) was already false by attempt 2 — structurally unreachable, not merely unlucky. That customer's bridge-out redirect (the whole point of a bridge-out funnel) would silently never get fixed.
- The "obvious" fix (raising the retry ceiling, or giving each correction its own budget) was explicitly rejected in the ticket — it either costs more billed v0 messages/wall-clock on every page, or just changes *which* correction gets starved without fixing the structural issue.
- Actual fix: run all three checks up front each attempt, batch whichever are still failing into **one** v0 correction message + **one** wait, then `continue` once. No correction can consume another's turn anymore. Applied identically at both correction sites — `addPageToExistingRepo` (sub-page path) and `deployLandingPage` (root-page path).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] New regression test reproducing the exact starvation: all three (pixel/ads/bridge-out) missing and never fixed — asserts the batched message mentions all three on every attempt sent, and all three are accurately reported unverified after retries exhaust. Assertion is content-based, not just a call count, since the old buggy code also sent exactly 2 messages in this scenario (both pixel-only) — a count alone wouldn't have caught the regression.
- [x] New test: pixel gets fixed after attempt 0 while ads/bridge-out don't — confirms attempt 1's batched message drops the already-fixed pixel instructions but keeps asking for the other two.
- [x] Full `services.v0Service.test.ts` (370 tests) green, plus the 3 related validator test files (22 tests) and the 3 other name-matched v0Service test files pre-push picked up (35 tests) — all green.

title: [ENG-2264] createAccount platform matching misses legacy 'facebook' rows, creating orphaned duplicates on reconnect
body:
Linear: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2264
Source-of-truth: Linear — Linear-is-source-of-truth. Discuss and close in Linear; this GitHub mirror is for external contributors.

## Problem
`connectedAccountsDb.createAccount` matches existing entries only on the exact platform string passed in (`acc.platform === platform && acc.account_id === input.accountId`). Reconnect flows that hardcode `platform: 'meta'` (e.g. Meta Marketing POST /api/oauth/meta/connect-ad-accounts) never find an existing row still stored under the legacy `'facebook'` platform value — even though read paths (e.g. `getMetaCredentials` in agentModeService.ts) already treat 'facebook' and 'meta' as the same account.

Impact: users with a legacy 'facebook' row get a brand-new 'meta' entry on every reconnect; the old row is orphaned (access token, capability flags, sharedWithOrg, engagement memory do not migrate).

Reference: backend/src/services/connectedAccountsDb.ts, createAccount existingIndex lookup. Related: ENG-2232 / PR #3171 (read-side fallback only).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] createAccount's existing-entry lookup matches across the meta/facebook platform alias set (or a centralized alias list shared by read and write paths so they cannot drift again).
- [ ] Reconnecting a 'meta' account updates the legacy 'facebook' row in place instead of creating a duplicate.
- [ ] No behavior change for platforms without aliases; existing connectedAccountsDb tests pass plus a new regression test for the alias match.
- [ ] npx tsc clean on touched files; relevant jest suite green.

title: fix(v0): persist iterate base version before send (ENG-1728)
body:
## What
ENG-1728 gap 1. `iterateLandingPage` now writes `pendingIteration` (with `unsent: true`) BEFORE calling v0, then clears `unsent` after v0 accepts. The original base version is kept on that second write.

## Why
Before this, `pendingIteration` was only written after the send. If the process died after v0 accepted the message but before the write, the retry read the post-edit version as its base. The usage guard then skipped the already-sent message, and the retry waited for a version nothing would create, ending in V0_GENERATION_TIMEOUT.

## Behaviour
- Recorded edit without `unsent`: resume the wait and don't send again. This also covers legacy records, which were only ever written after a send.
- Recorded edit with `unsent`: the process crashed around the send. The edit goes through `guardedV0IterateMessage`, which dedupes by content hash. A send that already happened returns `skipped` with no second charge; a send that never happened goes out now.
- The wait is always anchored to the original pre-send base.

## Not in this PR
Gap 2: a per-page lease to serialize distinct concurrent edits. It needs a conditional-write lease on the page record, so it stays open on ENG-1728.

## Complexity ledger
+1 optional field and one extra DynamoDB update per iterate. No schema, table, or index change; `pendingIteration` is an existing schemaless attribute.

## How to test
`cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts`. Result: 370/370 locally, including 2 new ENG-1728 tests (the pre-send write happens before the v0 call, and a crashed unsent retry still sends).

## Rollback
Revert this commit. Records left with `unsent: true` are read by old code as an ordinary pending edit, which is the old behaviour.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium — the change affects persisted retry state on the production v0 send path. A code revert is straightforward.

`iterateLandingPage` writes the original base version with `unsent: true` before sending an edit to v0. After v0 accepts the send or the usage guard confirms prior acceptance, it saves the pending iteration without `unsent`. Retries preserve the original version anchor and use the guard to avoid duplicate sends.

title: feat(meta): write rate shaping - budget-edit throttle, coalesce, burst score (ENG-2280)
body:
## What
ENG-2280 (ENG-2046 A3): in-memory Meta write rate shaping on the shared authorized-write path (`dispatchAuthorizedMetaWrite`, used by both model calls and approved-deck dispatch).
- Per-object budget-edit throttle: a 5th budget edit (daily_budget/lifetime_budget/spend_cap/budget_amount on CAMPAIGN/AD_SET UPDATE) inside an hour is never sent; returns `throttled` + `retryAfterMs`.
- Coalescing: re-sending the object's last budget values inside the window returns success without a Graph call or a slot.
- Burst score per ad account: read=1, write=3, 60 points / 60s sliding window; over threshold, writes are refused with retry-after.
- Meta subcode 1487225 maps to a throttle message in `enrichMetaError`; campaign/ad-set UPDATE errors now go through `enrichMetaError` (they previously returned the raw message).
- A failed/throw write releases its budget slot.

## Acceptance
- 5th edit not sent, retry-after: tested (unit + dispatch-path test asserting updateMetaAdsAdSet called 4x)
- 1487225 -> throttle message: tested

title: ENG-2286: bill org members' spend to the org owner, not the member
body:
## What
The usage recorder now resolves the **org billing root** when a caller doesn't name a `billingUserId`, so an org member's spend is recorded against the account the enforcement gate actually checks.

## The problem (verified in prod, 2026-10-05)
The gate pools an org member onto the org owner (`resolveBillingUserId`) and never looks at the member's own id. The recorder's fallback was `ctx.billingUserId || userId`, and these vendor call sites pass only `userId`: Apollo, enrich.so, Enigma, voiceover, Remotion, You.com, Google CSE, reCAPTCHA (only v0, Placid and Twitter resolve it). So an org member's vendor spend was recorded against the **member**, outside the owner's cap and outside enforcement.

A scan of all 32,742 ledger events: **7 org members, $301.64 billed to themselves, 97% vendor.** The impact model's three "would pause" accounts were this artifact, so the Free-tier flip paused nobody and a grandfather credit went on a member record where it had no effect. Correct pooling would not have capped any owner in October (max $53.07 of an $80 cap); September exposure was larger (one member $235 against a $200-cap owner).

## The fix
The recorder is the one place every record passes through, so the owner is resolved **there**, not at ~15 call sites:
- Resolved **once** per call at the two public entry points (`recordUsage`, `recordVendorUsage`) and written back into the context. The aggregate row, spend event, legacy fallback and dropped-write alert then all read the same id, so one call can't be split across two owners. (The priced write's `catch` falls back to `recordVendorUsageLegacy`, which would otherwise re-derive it independently.)
- An explicit `billingUserId` always wins. `system` and `anon_` ids are not resolved.
- **Never loses a record:** on any resolver failure it bills the acting user (the old behaviour) and logs, throttled.
- Cached 60s per user (bounded, 2,000 entries) so it adds no lookup to every vendor call.
- **Kill switch** `SPEND_RECORDER_RESOLVE_ORG_OWNER=false` restores the old behaviour without a deploy.
- Reuses `resolveBillingUserId`, the same predicate the gate uses (incl. `inheritsOrgBilling`), so recording and enforcement cannot disagree.

## Things worth a reviewer's eye
- `tokenUsageService` is **lazy-required**, matching the existing use in this file: a static import would drag `db.ts` and `config/aws` into every consumer and break suites that mock `aws-sdk`.
- Under `NODE_ENV=test` resolution is a no-op unless a test installs a resolver. Without that, the 55 suites that run the recorder over an unmocked data layer would reach a live DynamoDB. This follows the precedent in `llmUsagePolicyResolverService`.

## Scope / what this does not do
- **Forward-only.** Spend events are immutable; already-written records keep their id. No backfill, no data change.
- Customer effect: new vendor spend by org members now counts against the owner's cap. None would cross a cap today (October scan), but an owner could in future, which is the intended enforcement.

## Verification
- Typecheck: zero errors in touched files (38 pre-existing unrelated errors unchanged).
- New suite: 11 tests. **Mutation-checked**: restoring the old fallback fails the 6 resolution-dependent tests; the 5 that pin unchanged behaviour still pass.
- Regression: all **55 suites / 1,258 tests** that touch the recorder pass, in 71s (no slowdown, so no live calls).

## After deploy
Verify new events for org members carry the owner's `billingUserId`, and re-run the impact model: the false "would pause" accounts should no longer appear.

Refs ENG-2286, ENG-1250.

Resolution is cached for 60 seconds and can be disabled with `SPEND_RECORDER_RESOLVE_ORG_OWNER=false`.

title: ENG-2286: pool the impact model by billing owner, as the gate does
body:
## What
`spendCutoverImpact` and `spendWouldPauseSnapshot` now pool spend onto the **billing owner the gate checks** instead of the id the spend happened to be recorded under. Follow-up to #3218 (which fixes the recorder going forward).

## Why
The gate resolves an org member onto the org's billing root (`resolveBillingUserId`) and never looks at the member's own id. The model summed by the **recorded** `billingUserId`, which was often the member's, so it modelled a gate that does not exist. On 2026-10-05 it reported three "newly paused" accounts. All three were org members, and I repeated that claim to you and to the Harsha agent.

## How
- `poolSpendByOwner(perSubject, ownerOf)` in the tested service: pure, re-keys spend onto the owner. An id absent from the map or mapped to itself stays its own subject; an owner with no spend of its own still appears, built from its members; inputs are not mutated.
- Both scripts resolve each id's owner with `resolveBillingUserId` (the same predicate the gate uses), pool, then evaluate the **owner's** tier, credits and cap. An unresolvable id stays its own subject (the restrictive direction, as `resolveBillingUserId` does).
- `spendCutoverImpact` prints which members were folded in, so the output explains itself.
- `spendWouldPauseSnapshot` had the same copied aggregation and got the same fix; otherwise the flip-time evidence file would still list accounts the gate never measures.

## Before / after against prod (read-only)
**October 2026**: subjects 31 → 26, **newly paused 1 → 0**. The Free org member (614% of a $5 cap) is one Starter subject at 66.3% of $80, matching my independent ledger scan ($53.07 of $80).

**September 2026** is the more important result. Pooling does not just remove false positives, it exposes two **real** owner-level overages the old model could not see:

| owner | tier | cap | LLM | vendor | all-in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `be754b6c` | Super Premium | \$500 | \$370.88 | \$244.81 | **\$615.70 (123%)** |
| `36496472` | Starter | \$90 | \$74.08 | \$22.72 | **\$96.79 (107.5%)** |

\$236 of the first is a member's vendor spend; the second includes a Free member's \$22.33. September is over and caps have reset, so nothing can be paused now. This is the leak's actual cost: two owners ran past their caps and the gate never saw it. The 3 accounts the old model flagged (`0d1b79d9`, `22342fe2`, `1743956381327`) were the artifact.

## Not in this PR
No change to enforcement or to any recorded data. Read-only scripts plus a pure function.

title: fix(eng-2293): unblock daily OpenRouter model-catalog refresh pipeline
body:
## Summary

The daily `refresh-model-catalog.yml` workflow (PR #3065, tracked retroactively in ENG-2292) has failed every scheduled run since at least 2026-09-27 — zero draft PRs ever created, blocking onboarding of 7 already-discovered models including `gpt-6.1-sol`. See ENG-2293 for the full root-cause writeup.

**Commit 1 — stop clobbering curated pricing.** `modelCatalogRefresh.ts`'s pricing-refresh loop unconditionally applied any live OpenRouter quote to *existing* registry entries, discarding hand-researched cache rates (promo adjustments, confidence caveats) with zero review. Existing entries now only get drift *reported*; only brand-new additions are priced directly from a live quote.

**Commit 2 — decouple guard tests from live, mutable data.** `llmPricing.test.ts`'s cache-convention check and `modelCatalogRefresh.test.ts`'s score-matching assertions were both coupled to production data that the automation itself mutates, so they broke whenever the automation did its normal job.

**Commit 3 — surface price-drift reports.** An independent review found the drift reports from commit 1 only reached the uploaded JSON artifact, not the step summary / PR body / Slack. Folded into the step-summary markdown.

**Commit 4/5 — self-maintain the override allowlist, then make it quote-agnostic.** The same review flagged that commit 2's exemption (sniffing the registry's `description` field) was fragile, since the workflow's own draft-PR body instructs reviewers to rewrite that exact field. Replaced with the writer registering each addition directly into `explicitCacheOverrides` at add time. A **second** independent review pass on that fix then found its inner extractor only recognized single-quoted entries — silently dropping all existing overrides (no error) if that line is ever reformatted to double quotes (no lint rule guards against it). Fixed by extracting the merge into its own `mergeSetLiteral` function, made quote-agnostic, with a regression test locking in both the quote-style contract and idempotency.

Verified end-to-end at each step: ran the complete real `refresh-model-catalog.yml` step sequence (write → refresh-openrouter-params → guard tests → degraded-check), verbatim, against live OpenRouter data, with zero mocking — every step exits 0. Confirmed previously-clobbered curated entries are left untouched, confirmed the step-summary now actually contains drift-report lines, confirmed the override-merge survives both quote styles and repeated runs without duplication.

Intentionally **not** bundling the actual model additions (gpt-6.1-sol, claude-sonnet-5.5, etc.) into this PR — those are real model launches affecting customer-facing pricing/capability, and should go through the workflow's own draft-PR review step, same as the original design intended. Once this merges, the next scheduled (or manually dispatched) run of `refresh-model-catalog.yml` should open that draft PR.

Refs: ENG-2292 (retroactive tracking for PR #3065), ENG-2293 (this bug)

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npx jest` on the 3 guard-test files: 66/66 pass
- [x] Full live replay of all 4 real workflow steps against real OpenRouter data, verbatim commands, zero mocking: all exit 0
- [x] Confirmed previously-clobbered curated pricing entries are left untouched after the live write
- [x] Confirmed the override-set merge survives single- and double-quoted source and is idempotent on a repeated run
- [x] Two independent fresh-eyes subagent reviews (first on commits 1-2, second specifically on commits 3-4 in response to the first) — both verdict: safe to merge; every finding from both reviews is now fixed
- [ ] Next scheduled/dispatched `refresh-model-catalog.yml` run opens a draft PR (can't verify pre-merge — the workflow's checkout step hardcodes `ref: main`, so this is the acceptance criterion from ENG-2293, checked post-merge)

title: feat(meta): stateless MCP endpoint for the Meta Toolkit (ENG-2295)
body:
## What
Adds `POST /api/meta-toolkit/mcp`: a stateless MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0) endpoint. With it, Claude or any other MCP client can add the Meta Toolkit as a remote server with `claude mcp add --transport http <api>/api/meta-toolkit/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer aw_..."`. ENG-2268 child 5.

## Why
ENG-2282, ENG-2283 and ENG-2288 shipped the manifest, the gateway and a REST shape. MCP clients cannot speak that REST shape, so the parent's "callable by Claude" outcome had no protocol surface until this change.

## How
- The endpoint lives in `routes/metaToolkit.ts` and runs behind the same per-IP rate limiter.
- `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list` (auth required, manifest only) and `tools/call`, which goes through `handleMetaToolkitCall`. Gateway auth, account binding, ENG-2046 write guards and metering are unchanged, and there is no bypass path.
- A refusal comes back as an `isError: true` tool result. Auth failures return HTTP 401/403 with JSON-RPC -32001 and `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`. Unknown methods return -32601, a missing tool name returns -32602, and a malformed body returns 400/-32600. Notifications return 202 with an empty body.
- No session state, storage, schema or external copy is involved.

## Risk / rollback
Security-adjacent: this adds a new ingress, but it reuses the existing authenticated gateway, and negative tests cover a missing token, a wrong account and refusals. To roll back, revert this commit; the route is additive.

## Tests
- `jest eng2295 eng2288 eng2283 eng2282`: 4 suites, 42/42 passed.
- Scoped `tsc` is clean. The full `tsc` OOMs on this box.
- `worktree-doctor`: OK.

## Not tested
Live MCP handshake against staging with a real API key and a connected Meta account. Post-deploy smoke: `curl -X POST <api>/api/meta-toolkit/mcp -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize"}'` should return serverInfo, and `tools/list` without a bearer should return 401.

## Complexity ledger
+1 route handler, roughly 80 LOC, with no new modules or dependencies.

title: ENG-2286 / AC7 stage 1: the ledger is the only enforcement basis (no legacy fallback by default)
body:
## What
Stage 1 of retiring the legacy counter (ENG-1250 AC7). `spendEnforcementBasis` stops falling back to `AW-Users.tokenUsage` when the spend projection is **missing or unreadable**. Behind a flag, default off, instantly reversible.

## Why
AC7: the legacy counter is retired "rather than maintained as fallbacks". §9.8 then stops writing it, after which it would be a stale number, so nothing may still read it as a basis. This is the first step because it has to land before the writes stop (stage 3).

## Behaviour with `AW_SPEND_LEDGER_LEGACY_FALLBACK` unset (new default)
- **No projection row → counts $0.** That is the normal state of an account's first request in a new month (the row is created by its first settled event), and the legacy counter, which also resets monthly, would have said $0 too. Logged once per subject+month instead of on every request.
- **Read error → fail open:** counts $0, admits, and logs loudly. Availability over precision, matching the rest of the metering path. (An over-cap account is admitted for as long as the read keeps failing, which is why it logs at error level.)
- A projection that exists is used exactly as before.

`AW_SPEND_LEDGER_LEGACY_FALLBACK=true` restores the old fallback with no deploy.

## Evidence it changes nothing today
Checked against prod (read-only, 2026-10-05): **all 24 subjects with legacy October spend already have an October projection row**, so no current account reads differently. Prod has `AW_SPEND_LEDGER_ENFORCEMENT=true` with no tier exclusion and no staleness guard, so these are the only fallbacks in play.

## Not in this PR (deliberately)
Two other legacy fallbacks stay until stage 4 deletes the code: the opt-in staleness guard (default off, never enabled) and a subject the mode flags leave dark or exclude by tier (neither configured in prod). Stages 2 to 4 (move the readers off the counter, stop the writes, delete the code after a clean boundary) are separate PRs.

## Verification
- Typecheck: zero errors in touched files (38 pre-existing unrelated errors unchanged).
- Four existing tests described the old fallback and are updated on purpose; new tests cover the default, the once-per-subject log, the fail-open path and the rollback flag. 117 tests pass across the enforcement, admission, token-usage and credit suites.

title: ENG-2286 / AC7 stage 2b-2: the admin cost modal's 'counted' reads the ledger, not the counter
body:
## What
The org rollup behind the partner portal's per-user cost modal showed the org **owner's legacy `AW-Users.tokenUsage` counter** as "Counted", meaning what counts against the cap. It now reads the owner's settled **LLM spend from the ledger**.

## Why
Since enforcement moved to the ledger (2026-09-28) the counter is no longer what counts against the cap, and once its writes stop (stage 3) this modal would read stale. I first thought this reader dead; it is not: `CostBreakdownBody.tsx` displays it (counted, coverage %, the "uncharged" and "counter ahead" notes).

## How
- `countedForMonth` reads the owner's ledger via `listSpendEventsBounded`, summing **settled** `llm_token` + `llm_generation` events. It stays LLM-only because this rollup's gross burn is LLM-only, so both sides of the coverage ratio measure the same thing.
- **Months up to and including 2026-09 keep reading the archived `tokenUsageHistory`.** The LLM ledger only started on 2026-09-14, so September is partial. History is frozen, complete pre-retirement data and what the modal showed for those months before.
- **Fails loud on a truncated read:** the ledger read is bounded (50k events) and throws when exceeded instead of reporting a wrong total, matching the rollup's own rule.
- Only the owner's ledger is read; events a member billed to themselves are ignored, as the cap does.

## Not changed
The modal's explanatory copy still says "counter" in places; it is admin-only and the behaviour it describes (the ledger running ahead of or behind the usage records) still reads correctly. Happy to reword in a follow-up.

## Verification
- Typecheck run from `backend/`: no errors in touched files (38 pre-existing unrelated errors unchanged).
- 74 tests pass across the three usage-analytics suites. **Mutation-checked:** skipping the ledger branch fails 7.
- New cases pin the boundaries: member-billed events ignored, only settled LLM events count (vendor units, reservations, voids do not), September uses history, an over-bound read rejects, and an empty covered month reads as `none`.

Part of ENG-2286 / ENG-1250 AC7. Remaining readers (selfActivity, client-health export, MCP account-status tool, admin list fields) follow separately.

title: [ENG-899] Work-plan AI thumbnail job reverts concurrent edits (stale whole-plan write)
body:
Linear: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-899/work-plan-ai-thumbnail-job-reverts-concurrent-edits-stale-whole-plan

## Problem
The fire-and-forget AI thumbnail job (`generateAIThumbnail(plan)`) is kicked off from the create handler holding the plan as it looked at creation. Image generation + S3 upload take ~40s. It finishes by calling `workPlanService.updateWorkPlan(updated)` — a whole-item `put` of that stale snapshot. Every edit made in the window is silently overwritten.

## Acceptance criteria
- Thumbnail job performs a single conditional write touching only `thumbnail_*` + `updatedAt`, conditioned on `attribute_exists(planId)` and a job-start marker; no whole-plan put.
- A concurrent title/steps edit made during the job survives (test).
- Plan deleted mid-job is not resurrected (test).
- Admin upload during job is not overwritten, incl. clear->upload->clear ABA (test).
- Manual regenerate returns the plan as actually stored; skipped write is not reported as success.
- No table/index/schema change (attribute-scoped UpdateExpression only).

## Constraints
- `removeThumbnail` is specified as *clear and regenerate*, not *clear and stay blank* (`workPlanThumbnailService.ts:154` kicks a regeneration). A blanket guard on `none` breaks it.
- The manual regenerate is synchronous — the admin waits on the response. A skipped write must NOT be reported as success; return the plan as actually stored.
- Do not key ordering on `updatedAt` alone: an unrelated edit to the plan steps would discard a perfectly good generated thumbnail.
- Suggested direction: a single-write protocol. Capture a marker at job start, condition the final write on it, no separate claim.

Related: ENG-889 / PR #2266.

---
*Linear (ENG-899) is the source of truth. This GitHub mirror is for external contributors; status and acceptance are tracked in Linear.*

title: ENG-2286 AC7 stage 2c: admission gate stops reading the legacy counter
body:

**Behaviour change (explicit, accepted by the ticket owner)**
Token volume no longer gates. A tier with no enforced versioned policy and no cost gate is now **uncapped**; 25 accounts were identified on such tiers. For them `used`/`allowance`/`effectiveAllowance`/`percentUsed` report 0/null, which already hides the customer `UsageMeter`. **What changes**

With the ledger live in prod the counter is never read at admission. The per-request ledger-vs-legacy canary line is removed (it forced the read).
- `checkTokenUsage`: month from the clock, bonus from the user record, token gate and token warning removed.

title: ENG-2286: recorder resolves a supplied billingUserId to the org owner too
body:
Follow-up to #3218, found while checking ENG-2286 completion against live data.

**Observed (production, read-only)**: after the #3218 deploy (old instance gone 11:11Z 2026-10-05), org member `1743956381327` still wrote 82 X/Twitter spend events ($4.37, 16:46-16:54Z) into **their own** ledger partition. Other member spend since the fix is correctly in the owner's partition (76 events in owner `be754b6c`'s), so #3218 works for LLM and for vendors that pass no payer.

**Cause**: `twitterService` passes `billingUserId: ownerUserId`, the owner of the connected X account, which for a member's connection is the member. #3218's resolver returned any supplied id verbatim (`if (supplied) return supplied`), so these events skipped org-owner resolution and stayed outside the owner's cap.

**Fix**: resolve the supplied id as well. Idempotent for an id that is already a billing root (owner, solo user, member holding their own subscription), so callers that pass a resolved payer, including the LLM path, are unaffected. `system`/`anon_` are never resolved. The `SPEND_RECORDER_RESOLVE_ORG_OWNER=false` kill switch is unchanged.

**Scope note**: forward-only, like #3218. The $4.37 and earlier leaked X spend stay in the member partitions (historical data, not rewritten); the 2026-10 pooled impact model showed no owner near its cap.

**Verification**: typecheck at the 38-error baseline; 13 recorder tests (new: member-as-supplied-payer resolves to owner, system/anon never resolved, explicit root unchanged); 64/65 related suites pass (the one failure is the pre-existing unrelated `v0Metering`). Mutation (restoring 'supplied wins') fails 2.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium. The change affects production billing attribution, but the existing kill switch supports rollback. It does not indicate a production outage path.

When `billingUserId` is supplied, resolve it to the organization owner unless it is already a billing root or is `system` or `anon_`. The kill switch and resolution-failure fallback preserve the selected ID. Historical spend is unchanged.

title: ENG-1816 F2 follow-up: GTM phase-ID exposure + work-plan diagnostic logging
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to F2 (ENG-2103, PR #3188) — fixes two of the three anomalies found during F2's exhaustive post-deploy production live-testing, and instruments the third (confirmed pre-existing, not an F2 regression, but could not be reproduced on demand).

- **GTM phase-ID exposure** (`readGTMPlan`'s formatted output never exposed a phase/work-item's real `id`, only its 1-based display position — so `add_gtm_work_items`/`update_gtm_phase`/`update_gtm_work_item`/`delete_gtm_items` had nothing valid to target, and the model sometimes declined the request entirely claiming the capability didn't exist). Fixed by appending `(id: ...)` to both the phase and work-item lines, and pointing the four tools' `phase_id`/`work_item_id` schema descriptions at `read_gtm_plan`'s output.
- **Work-plan session-state diagnostic** — a production session reported `No work plan found in this session` immediately after an earlier step on the same session had completed successfully. Live-reproduced the exact sequence against production (real API calls + direct DynamoDB verification between each step) and could not trigger the failure — the round trip is reliable every time. Rather than ship a guessed fix for an unreproduced bug, added targeted diagnostic logging at both call sites that can hit this (`setWorkPlanStatus`, `modifyWorkPlan`), capturing session existence/age and whether `calledFunctions` shows `create_work_plan` was ever invoked despite the plan being absent — the one signal that would distinguish real data loss from "never created." This turns the next real occurrence into something diagnosable.
