title: feat(eng-2293): price-outlier warning + Slack alerts on PR creation and job failure
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to ENG-2293 / PR #3221. After that merged, the system's weak points were discussed directly — this PR addresses the ones agreed on, deliberately **not** including auto-merge (ruled out: this touches customer billing/capability, and the registry's own history shows human review has already caught real pricing mistakes that would otherwise have shipped).

**Commit 1 — price-outlier warning, never a gate.** Compares each addition's blended price against its family. Deliberately a report, not a failing test — a hard gate here would recreate the exact deadlock ENG-2293 fixed.

**Commit 2 — Slack alerts on the job's own outcome.** Notifies on PR creation/update and on job failure/timeout — previously the job only alerted on frontier lag, which is exactly how it died silently for 9+ days.

**Commit 3 — price-outlier check compares to the closest sibling, not a skewed family average.** An independent second review pass found real families already sit close to the 3x cutoff using only their existing, correctly-priced members — e.g. gpt-sol's two real tiers alone span 2.81x. A family-wide average is the wrong baseline when a family legitimately spans multiple price tiers; comparing to the single closest sibling fixes both the false-positive risk (a normal new tier member near either end) and the false-negative risk (a bad quote landing near a skewed average). Verified with a test built from the real numbers that motivated the fix — confirmed it fails under the old logic, passes under the new, and the real outlier caught earlier (deepseek-v4.1-flash) is still caught.

**Commit 4 — surface Slack notification failures instead of swallowing them.** The same review found both new Slack steps ended in a blind `|| true` — a rotated/revoked webhook would fail silently forever, in direct tension with this PR's own purpose. Now uses `curl -f` plus a `::warning::` annotation on failure, visible in the run summary, while the step still never fails the job.

## Known limitation, out of scope for this PR

A repo Settings permission ("Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests") still blocks the PR-creation step itself — separate, pre-existing, not fixable via any PR (see ENG-2293 comments).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npx jest` on the 3 guard-test files: 70/70 pass
- [x] Live-verified the price-outlier logic against real OpenRouter data twice (before and after the closest-sibling fix) — still catches the real outlier both times
- [x] Independently recomputed the family-spread numbers that motivated commit 3 directly from the live registry, not taken on the reviewer's word
- [x] For both commit 3 and the earlier zero-baseline fix: reverted just the fix, confirmed the regression test fails, restored, confirmed it passes — proving each test is load-bearing, not vacuous
- [x] Verified `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v8`'s actual output field names against its real `action.yml`
- [x] Two independent fresh-eyes subagent reviews — every finding from both verified and either fixed or explicitly confirmed as a non-issue

title: feat(ENG-2311): add 'session' list type and suppress lead side-effects
body:
## Summary
ENG-2311 (S1 of epic ENG-2309). Adds `listType: 'session'`: a list whose rows are one-per-landing-page-visitor-session telemetry, not contacts or deals.

- **Vocabulary**: `LEAD_LIST_TYPES` / `isLeadListType` in `utils/leadSchema.ts` is now the single source of truth. Accepted (set-once, unchanged semantics) at `GET /crm/contacts`, `POST /crm/lists`, `PUT /crm/lists/:id`, Emma create/update list tools (now also validated server-side), MCP tool description, and the db/agentMode types.
- **`utils/sessionList.ts`**: `isSessionList(list)` (S2 and later slices import it), `suppressLeadSideEffects(list)` (the one policy gate), `excludeSessionLists(lists)`.
- **`defaultStatusConfigFor('session')`** = one non-terminal `new` entry. Not empty: an empty config makes `mapStatusToMetaEvent` fall back to the SALES defaults (which contain `won` => a Meta Purchase), and `sequences.ts` treats "no statuses" as a 400. A single `active`-type entry cannot express a conversion (asserted in a test).
- **Side effects suppressed for session lists** (decision always from the DB list row, never the request body): HubSpot/Attio `autoSyncLead`, `autoEnrollLeadInSequences`, auto-draft/auto-send, owner alert email + Slack (`leadListAlertService.notifyLeadListOwnerIfConfigured`, `orgLeadNotificationService.routingContext` chokepoints), Meta CAPI, `sendRoadmapDeliveryEmail`, `dispatchLeadCreated`, and the `attribution.first_touch` event-log write in `db.createLead` (new opt-in `suppressSideEffects`, only set by callers that hold the list). Call sites: webhooks.ts forward-lead, crmPublic.ts, crm.ts single-lead create/update. Non-session lists get byte-identical inputs (the flag key is only added when true).
- **Cross-list aggregates now exclude session lists** (sales/customers/unset unchanged): Inbox/contacts (`contactDedupService`; `listType=session` is the explicit opt-in), Emma ask_crm + heat ranker loaders, Meta attribution coverage / CAPI divergence / reconcile, Meta metrics snapshot cron, account summary, business funnel, admin CRM analytics.

## Follow-up (review round): sequences + Meta relay
- Sequences: PUT /sequences/:id rejects `autoEnrollListIds` containing a session list; by-list and explicit-lead enrol routes reject session lists (400). crm.ts import routes holding the list row skip list auto-enrol. The autoEnroll* functions and the LinkedIn import route have no list row in scope, so are unguarded (configuration is closed upstream).
- Meta relay: `listType` is threaded into the relay context; `dispatchLeadStatusConversion` and `relayLeadStatusEvent` refuse session lists (covers retagged lists that still carry the sales statusConfig, and already-queued jobs).

## Not changed (deliberately / could not safely)
- Calendly still calls `autoSyncLead` without a list in hand (it writes to its own sales list). Emma `update_lead` is now gated (it already loaded the list).
- `GET /crm/lists` returns session lists (the UI needs them); any client that sums `leadCount` across lists will include them. Customer portal types/filters are out of scope (see ticket for the portal list).
- Existing prod session lists have `listType` unset: they are NOT covered until tagged once (`PUT /crm/lists/:id {listType:'session'}`), and until then still appear in Inbox / aggregates.

## DATA-PLANE NOTICE
Per AGENTS.md this needs **Harsha's explicit approval before merge** (introduces a persisted list-type value that changes how stored lists are interpreted). DO NOT MERGE without it.

## Rollback
Pure code revert. No schema/index change and no data written by this PR. Lists already tagged `listType: 'session'` after deploy keep that attribute; on revert, old code would treat an unknown listType as the sales default for status config (via `defaultStatusConfigFor` fallthrough) and would reject re-setting it. Existing rows are untouched.

## Post-deploy smoke
1. `PUT /api/crm/lists/<test list> {listType:'session'}` -> 200; repeat with `'sales'` -> 400 "already set"; `{listType:'bogus'}` -> 400.
2. POST forward-lead to that list with a synthetic email -> 201, row exists; confirm no HubSpot/Slack/owner-email/sequence enrolment fired.
3. POST forward-lead to a sales list -> unchanged behaviour (alerts/sync still fire).
4. `GET /api/crm/contacts` excludes the session list; `?listType=session` returns it.

## Tests
New: `sessionListType.contract.test.ts`, `webhooks.forwardLead.sessionList.test.ts` (5 of 30 fail against pre-change gating, pass after). Updated `crm.routes` (message now lists `session`; added accept + set-once cases) and `crm.contacts`.

Slice S3 (ENG-2313) of epic ENG-2309: ONE versioned, server-side traffic-source classifier + a pure tagged-link generator, so channel names stop drifting per LP.

- `utils/trafficSource.ts` - `classifyTraffic({ landingUrl, utm, clickIds, referrer, userAgent, hostname })`, taxonomy constant (`CHANNELS`, groups, organic mediums), `TRAFFIC_CLASSIFIER_VERSION = 2.0.0`. Port of the LP's V1 client classifier (LP PRs #30/#31) first, then justified fixes.

- Parity harness (outside repo): V1 JS extracted verbatim from `public/guilty-before-the-mic-v2.html` and run next to the TS port over 142 input combinations: 146 inputs, 89 identical, 57 different (refreshed after the fbclid change); every difference intentional and test-pinned; every difference is intentional and pinned by a test.

(With the shared symlinked node_modules, origin/main itself shows 37 typecheck / 22 build errors from stale deps; identical with and without this PR.) eslint was not run.
- Round trip: every link preset (tiktok, instagram, youtube, facebook, linkedin, x, reddit, pinterest, newsletter, agency:<name>) classifies back to its intended channel with no referrer, with the platform's referrer origin, with a contradictory referrer, and with the in-app UA where one exists.

## Intentional differences vs V1
See the PR comment / test names in `trafficSource.test.ts` ("intentional differences"). Summary: utm_source aliases (ig/fb/yt/tt/li/x/twitter, bare gemini/claude/copilot/google/meta, newsletter); host matching replaces substring regexes (no more bayou.com/xmeta.ai/dubbing.com/youtube.com.evil.com/path-or-query keyword hits); mail.google.com + Gmail app = Email, news.google.com = Referral; bing.com/chat anchored to host (still needs a path-bearing referrer); android-app referrers; internal/parent-domain referrers ignored; free-text referrers ignored; `agency-<slug>` outranks the referrer; click id with no other signal names its platform instead of Direct/Paid; whitespace/`undefined` handling; fbclid weak signal (above); path-only landing URL has no host; `non-paid`/`no_ads` not paid; cpv/retargeting/remarketing/sponsored paid.

title: feat(ENG-2314): admin dry-run dedupe/merge + delete for session rows
body:
## What
Admin-only, dry-run-first tool (ENG-2314, epic ENG-2309) to MERGE duplicate LP session rows (forward-lead race) and delete explicitly-named junk/test rows.

- `POST /api/admin/session-cleanup/preview` `{listId}` -> read-only plan (all pages, grouped by `customFields.sessionId`, fallback synthetic email; keeper = earliest createdAt/smallest leadId; merged diff; counts; deterministic `planHash`). With `leadIds[]` -> explicit-delete plan.
- `POST /api/admin/session-cleanup/apply` `{listId, planHash, expectedRowsToDelete, confirm:true [, leadIds[]]}` -> recomputes the plan and REFUSES (409) unless hash + count match and `confirm === true`; <=500 deletes per call (re-preview to continue); per-group result; full JSON backup of every deleted row in the response (+ keeper-before) and a write-ahead `[session-cleanup-backup]` console line.
- Mounted `authenticateToken, isAdmin` like the other `/api/admin/*` routers (isAdmin rejects delegated sessions). `routes/crm.ts` delete paths are untouched.
- Added `crmDb.deleteLeadGuarded` (additive; `deleteLead` unchanged): conditional on `updatedAt`, returns ALL_OLD, decrements `leadCount` only when it really removed a row (the existing `deleteLead` decrements even if the row was already gone, which breaks leadCount under overlapping runs).

## Merge rules (mirror what a non-raced row holds: the live writer overwrites scalars per event)
| Field(s) | Rule |
|---|---|
| journey, eventCount | row with the highest eventCount (tie: latest updatedAt, then keeper order) |
| clickLog, clickCount, showsClicked | row with the highest clickCount (tie: eventCount, updatedAt, keeper order) |
| dwellSec, activeSec, videoWatchSec, maxScrollPct | numeric max |
| `*_at`, `*At` (incl. capiLastSentAt, page_exit_at) | LATEST |
| forwardedAt | EARLIEST (forward-lead keeps the first) |
| every other scalar (lastEvent, furthestStage, lastEp, lastClick*, capi status, channel, ...) | from the highest-eventCount row (same tie-break), blanks filled from the other rows in that order |
| top-level firstTouch/lastTouch/clickIds/utm* | keeper wins; filled via `ifNotExists` when missing |

Keeper = earliest createdAt, then smallest leadId.

## Safety guards
- **Idle guard**: a group is eligible only if EVERY row's `updatedAt` is strictly older than `minIdleMinutes` (default 30, 5..1440, validated). Others are reported `skipped_active` (`counts.groupsSkippedActive`), never mutated, and excluded from `rowsToDelete` and `planHash` (a live row's moving updatedAt would make the plan unstable run to run). `minIdleMinutes` is in the hash; a group turning idle between preview and apply changes the hash and forces re-review. Missing/unparseable updatedAt = active.
- **Positive marker**: dedupe only groups rows with `customFields.source === 'lp-session'` plus a sessionId or synthetic email; others count as `rowsWithoutIdentity`. Explicit-ID mode is unchanged. The synthetic-email domain is a documented constant (generalising for other tenants is S5).
- **Run order**: run this AFTER S2 (atomic upsert) is deployed.
- **PII**: console `[session-cleanup-backup]` lines contain FULL rows. Admins must not use explicit-ID mode on real customer leads without saving the returned `backup`.

## DATA-PLANE NOTICE (needs Harsha's explicit pre-merge approval)
This PR adds a code path that hard-deletes rows (bulk mutation / production data repair) per AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md. **Do not merge without Harsha's explicit approval.** No apply has been, or will be, run against prod by this PR. No new table/index/schema.

## Rollback
Route is additive and inert unless an admin calls it; revert the PR to remove it. Data restore path for any apply = the returned `backup[]` (full original items of every deleted row) plus per-group `keeperBefore`; the same data is logged to the app console as `[session-cleanup-backup]` before each group is mutated. Restore by hand with `PutItem`, then fix `leadCount`.
No persistent audit store exists in the repo for admin actions (`recordAdminAudit` is console-only; `AW-ModelChangeAudit` is LLM-model-specific); persisting audits is proposed as a separate follow-up (needs its own data-plane approval).

## Verification
- Jest (sequential, `timeout 900`): `sessionRowCleanupService.test.ts` 33 + `adminSessionCleanup.test.ts` 14 = 47 passed.
- Clean install in a throwaway dir outside the repo (`npm ci`): `npm run build` (tsconfig.build.json, `--outDir` temp) exit 0, 0 errors; `npm run typecheck` 0 errors. (The worktree's symlinked node_modules is stale and shows 37 unrelated errors.)
- dynamodb-local (`amazon/dynamodb-local`, real AW-Leads/AW-LeadLists schema, 696 rows / 1.6MB, real 1MB LastEvaluatedKey paging, loopback-only SDK guard): 64 assertions pass: preview leaves the table byte-identical; hash identical across page sizes; e7c97874-style merge; LIVE pair skipped_active; marker-less pair untouched; reserved-word keys through the real expression parser; object top-level fields persist as DynamoDB Map (`M`), not strings; concurrent double-apply deletes each donor once and leadCount equals the real row count; idempotent re-apply; explicit mode.

## Post-deploy smoke (READ-ONLY)
As an admin: `POST /api/admin/session-cleanup/preview {"listId":"list_1791263007033_gbtv2org"}` (Organic list) and expect `counts.duplicatedSessions: 2`, `rowsToDelete: 2`, no writes. Do NOT call `/apply` without approval. Also confirm non-admin -> 403.

title: feat(ENG-2312): atomic session upsert on (listId, sessionId) for session lists
body:
Stacked on #3259 (ENG-2311) — **base is the S1 branch**; do not retarget to main until S1 merges.

## Problem
Custom LPs write one CRM row per visitor session through `POST /api/webhooks/forward-lead`. Dedupe was `getLeadByEmail` (eventually-consistent `email-index` GSI) then `createLead` (random id, non-atomic pre-check). Events 3–128 ms apart each missed the other and created their own row (prod V2 list: 2399 rows / 47 extra; one pair split a journey across two rows). `updateLead` also full-map-overwrites `customFields`, so concurrent events lose keys.

## Change
Gated STRICTLY on `isSessionList(<list row from DB>)` AND a valid body identity; otherwise the existing path runs byte-for-byte (legacy LPs without `sessionStartMs` unchanged; a body can never opt a non-session list in — tested).
- **Identity**: `sessionId` (top-level or `customFields`, `^[a-z0-9-]{8,64}$`/i) + `sessionStartMs` (integer, within [now-48h, now+5min]); either invalid/missing => legacy path.
- **leadId** = `lead_<sessionStartMs>_<first 12 hex sha256(listId:sessionId.toLowerCase())>` — keeps the ordinary `lead_<13-digit ms>_` shape so `getLeadsByListId` (ScanIndexForward:false) recency ordering holds. Nothing in the repo parses leadId (grepped).
- **Create exactly-once**: conditional put (`attribute_not_exists(leadId)` via `failIfExists`) with new opt-in `skipEmailDuplicateCheck` (default unchanged). Only the winning request reaches createLead's create-time work (leadCount ADD, fieldNames); a loser throws `leadAlreadyExists` before any of it.
  *Chosen over UpdateItem-ALL_OLD upsert*: that would need all of createLead's item construction (lifecycle, domain, attribution, GSI attrs) re-expressed as `if_not_exists` SETs, and DynamoDB cannot create `customFields` and `customFields.k` in one expression (path overlap), so it needs a bootstrap write anyway.
- **Merge (losers / later events)**: `crmDb.mergeSessionLeadEvent` — no read-modify-write. One document-path SET per `customFields` key (all names+values via placeholders), last-write-wins; the cumulative journey group (`journey, eventCount, clickLog, clickCount, showsClicked`) is a separate UpdateItem guarded by `attribute_not_exists(#cf.#ctr) OR NOT attribute_type(#cf.#ctr, :N) OR #cf.#ctr <= :n` on `eventCount`, so an out-of-order older event cannot regress it (stale => no-op, not an error). `forwardedAt` is never rewritten; `source` is written only if the caller named one (same as the existing merge paths).
- `sessionStartMs` added to `HANDLED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS` (no junk passthrough); `sessionId` intentionally NOT added (LPs already post it and read it back from customFields).
- Response codes/messages unchanged (201 created; 200 updated/unchanged).

## Verification
- Jest: new `crmDb.mergeSessionLeadEvent`, `sessionUpsert.contract`, `webhooks.forwardLead.sessionUpsert` tests (exact expression/condition shapes + a static placeholder validator); adjacent suites (`webhooks*`, `crmDb*`, `eng239.attributionE2E`, `eng309_310.captureInjection`, `crm.routes`, `crmPublic*`) green. Handler tests fail against the pre-change `webhooks.ts` (5 failing).
- **Real DynamoDB** (docker `amazon/dynamodb-local`, 127.0.0.1, throwaway script outside the repo; AW-Leads/AW-LeadLists keys+GSIs copied from `create-tables.ts`), driven through the real express handler + real `crmDb`: 20 concurrent events for one session => exactly 1 row (deterministic id), exactly one 201 / nineteen 200, `leadCount` == 1, key-union of all 20 distinct customFields keys, journey group == highest event whatever the arrival order, reserved-word keys (`domain`, `system`, `name`, `a.b`, `with space`) written, no ValidationException; 6 sessions x 8 concurrent events => 6 rows, leadCount 6; out-of-order 5,3,4,1,2 => journey stays at 5; missing-`customFields` row recovers; stale counter is a no-op; 400-key hostile body bounded. 4 runs, all 25 checks green each. For contrast, the unchanged legacy path with 20 concurrent same-email events produced **20 rows** in each of 3 runs (the read-then-create is not atomic even without GSI lag). Note dynamodb-local does not reproduce GSI eventual consistency; the new path never reads a GSI, so that axis is moot for it, and atomicity rests on the primary-key conditional put, which local enforces identically.

## DATA-PLANE NOTICE
Needs **Harsha's explicit approval before merge** (AGENTS.md): introduces a deterministic-key write scheme for lead rows and a new atomic-write path on AW-Leads. No schema/index change, no migration, no backfill.

## Rollback
Revert this PR (S1 can stay). Rows already written keep their `lead_<ms>_<hash>` ids — still valid ordinary rows; on revert the legacy path finds them by their stored email (same as any row) and merges into them with the old full-map update, so the old race/lost-update behaviour returns for new events but nothing is lost or corrupted. Existing rows are untouched.

## Post-deploy smoke
1. On a `listType: session` list, POST 5 concurrent forward-lead events with the same `sessionId` + `sessionStartMs` and distinct fields => one 201, four 200, one row with the deterministic `lead_<ms>_<12hex>` id, list `leadCount` +1, union of fields.
2. POST the same body without `sessionStartMs` => legacy behaviour (random id).
3. POST the same body to a sales list => legacy behaviour.
4. Confirm no ValidationException / 5xx in logs for `forward-lead`.

## Caveats / follow-ups
- The LP must send the SAME `sessionStartMs` for every event of a session (and a numeric, non-decreasing `eventCount`); a changing start time yields different ids (duplicates). Rows created before the LP rollout keep random ids; a session straddling the rollout could produce one extra row.
- List-level `fieldNames` is still the existing read-modify-write in createLead (creator only), so two different sessions created concurrently can drop each other's *new* field names from `list.fieldNames` (self-heals on later creates). Not changed here; `mergeFieldNames` is the atomic alternative.
- Scalars are last-write-wins by arrival, so an out-of-order older event can lower e.g. `dwellSec`; only the journey group is monotonic-guarded, per the spec.

title: fix(onboarding): atomically claim onboarding start routes and make the eager pipeline race-safe (ENG-2308)
body:
## Summary

Fixes [ENG-2308](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2308/outreach-onboarding-double-fires-icpstart-duplicating-the-icp-llm-call), found during ENG-2276 production testing. The onboarding `/start` routes (icp, competitor, creative-dir, ad-copy, ad-image, plus brand-build) launched a duplicate paid LLM/image run whenever a retry or double-fire reached them, and the eager-pipeline orchestrator had its own variants of the same race.

The PR grew over several rounds of live testing and independent review. Several of the later fixes correct my own earlier changes, and that is called out below rather than smoothed over.

## The core bug and fix

`/icp/start` and its siblings wrote their `running` start-patch unconditionally. A concurrent or retried call that read a stale non-running status also "won" and launched a second parallel generation. Confirmed live: `OutreachIcpPick`'s 8s watchdog re-firing `/icp/start` while a normal (>8s) generation was in flight.

Every axis now claims its non-running -> in-flight transition with a DynamoDB `ConditionExpression` (same primitive as `designSystemBuild.ts`, ENG-328), via an exported `claim<Axis>Run`. A caller that loses gets the in-flight snapshot instead of launching a second run. A stale-claim clause (`startedAt <= now - <axis>_TIMEOUT_MS`, reusing each axis's existing constant) keeps a genuinely crashed run retryable.

## What else this PR changes

**Eager-pipeline orchestrator**
- The orchestrator's runners called `trigger<Axis>ForUser` directly and nothing flipped the axis to in-flight, so every result past the first was silently dropped. Runners now claim then trigger.
- Route-level `start*ForUser` claimed first and then handed off to `reconcileForUser`, so the orchestrator's own claim for the same axis always lost. They now skip claiming on the eager branch.
- A runner that loses its claim now **joins** the run that holds the axis: it waits for it to finish and adopts its real result or failure, instead of reporting a stale placeholder as `ready` (which fired downstream steps on empty context) or leaving the step stranded `running`. If the other run outlives the axis timeout, the step is recorded `failed` and the next reconcile retries it.
- `reconcileForUser` dedups concurrent calls per user (in-process), and a request that arrives mid-walk schedules exactly one follow-up pass so it is not lost.

**Run ownership on completion**
- Each axis's completion and failure writes are conditioned on the run's own `<axis>StartedAt`, so a superseded ("zombie") run cannot overwrite or drop a newer run's result.

**Brand build**
- A brand-build Emma session now names its claim in its existing `pageIdentifier` (`brand-build|claim:<startedAt>`). `update_brand_guidelines` and `update_market_strategy` refuse writes from a superseded session before writing anything, and condition the writes of the current one on its claim. Nothing new is persisted.
- The refusal reaches the model as a deliberate policy block with the stop instruction in `error`.
- A superseded session is refused while a newer build is in flight, or when no human has ever written in it (a zombie: only the build's own opening prompt). A chat a human has since written in is ordinary chat again, so reopening the chat that built your brand still works. This is decided by content, not age: an earlier 15-minute bound assumed a 10-minute agent turn cap that does not apply to the brand build's direct call, so a slow zombie outlived it.
- `regenerate_market_strategy` and `update_brand_guidelines` with `refreshMarketStrategy:true` now pass the session through, so their minutes-long regeneration write is guarded and conditioned too.
- A run reclaimed mid-session stops writing once its session returns, instead of mirroring stale ICPs/competitors over the newer run's.
- `/brand-build/start` returns its claim patch directly instead of re-reading the eventually-consistent GSI.

## Bugs found in my own fixes (so reviewers know where to look)

- `/icp/regenerate-one` was first guarded with the per-user claim. That broke ENG-255's intentional "two persona cards regenerate concurrently" flow, so it was **reverted** and a regression test added. Two rapid clicks on the *same* card remain unguarded (needs a per-persona claim).
- Brand-build ownership was first kept in an in-process map. A live run showed it never worked: the agent loop runs in a forked worker process. It was then derived from session age, which blocked innocent ordinary sessions, and finally replaced by the explicit marker above.
- A lost claim first threw an error that left the step `running` forever. Reproduced, then replaced by the join behavior above.
- Unit tests passed in each of these cases and missed them. They were caught by live runs and review, which is why the live matrix below exists.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` (backend): clean
- [x] Targeted jest: 691 passed across 18 suites (all onboarding services, orchestrator + wiring, brand-build hook, routes, delegation tests)
- [x] Mutation-checked the newest guards: removing the refusal shape, the org re-check, the market-strategy guard, the post-session skip, or the claim conditions each fails the intended tests
- [x] **Live (dev preview + real DynamoDB), counting real outbound LLM calls:**
  - legacy and eager paths each ran a full cascade
  - 3 concurrent `/start` per axis stayed at the single-run call count (icp 1, competitor 5, creativeDir 1, adImage 3, adCopy 3; one competitor run showed 6 calls, matching the logged JSON-extraction retry, not a duplicate run)
  - a fresh `running` claim blocked a new run (0 calls); a 10-minute-stale claim was reclaimed
  - a superseded icp completion was dropped with no result overwrite and no cascade
  - eager account with icp held by another run: the orchestrator waited, resumed when it finished, and all six steps ended `ready` with real outputs and correct ordering
  - two concurrent `/brand-build/start` on an eager account ran one build
  - a zombie brand-build session was refused across the worker boundary: the newer run's guidelines survived intact, status stayed `building`, and the stale run wrote nothing afterwards; on the model side it made exactly one `update_brand_guidelines` call and stopped
  - re-run on the merged code (after syncing with `main`): legacy and eager full cascades with zero ownership drops; a days-old zombie-shaped session refused vs a reopened chat a human wrote in allowed, using real DynamoDB messages
- [x] Branch synced with `main` (0 behind)

## Known limits

- The reconcile dedup and coalescing are in-process; they do not cover two backend instances (the per-axis DynamoDB claims still do).
- Org members' brand data lives on the org record, which has no claim to condition on, so the guard is a consistent re-read just before the write (a single read-to-write gap), not an atomic condition.
- If the session lookup in the hook fails, the call is treated as an ordinary session (original behavior).
- A user can forge the marker on their own session; the only effect is on that user's own writes.

title: fix(crm): close the bulk-enrollment race with a claim transaction
body:
## Summary
ENG-2127's explicitly-named remaining scope (the core index-mismatch bug was already fixed in #3151): `enrollLead`'s only duplicate guard was a query against the eventually-consistent `leadEmail-index`, so two concurrent callers for the same lead+sequence (webhook resubmission racing a bulk import, two workers, etc.) could both pass the check and both write — the whole sequence delivered twice to the same lead.

## Fix
`enrollLead` now atomically claims every identity candidate against `AW-SequenceEnrollments`' own primary key (strongly consistent — no GSI lag) in the same `TransactWriteItems` call as the real enrollment write. Either every claim and the enrollment land together, or none do.

- Claim items are namespaced `claim#<sequenceId>#<identity>` — never collides with a real `generateEnrollmentId()` value (always `enr_...`).
- They deliberately carry **none** of this table's GSI key attributes (`leadEmail`; `sequenceId`+`status`; `userId`+`nextSendAt`) and never set `status: 'active'`, so they're invisible to every existing query *and* the one `scan` (`getAllDueEnrollments`) — verified against every read path against this table before relying on it.
- **No new table, index, or key changed** — satisfies the original TODO's own caution ("do not change keys or add persisted lock records without separate data-plane approval") by reusing the existing table's primary key in a new, deliberately-invisible shape, not by introducing new infrastructure.
- Mirrors an existing pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase (`llmUsageCreditService.ts`'s `isTransactionalConditionalFailure`).

Also fixed `linkedInConnectionSyncCron.ts:360` — a third call site with its own copy of the same race, calling `enrollLead` directly, and missing `identityCandidates` entirely (so even after this fix it would only have claimed one of up to three identities its own pre-check already looks across).

**Deliberately not touched**: the other named gap in #3151's "Explicit remaining scope" (lead-list display still showing stored lifecycle while enrollment uses derived lifecycle) is cosmetic and architecturally coupled to ENG-2155's own in-progress live-signal derivation work (PR #3152, open, by another engineer) — fixing it now would risk duplicating or preempting that design.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [x] New dedicated suite (`eng2127.enrollmentRaceClaim.test.ts`): claim-item shape/namespacing/GSI-invisibility, null-on-conditional-failure, rethrow-on-unrelated-error, and a genuine concurrency test (two simultaneous `enrollLead` calls sharing mock claim state) — confirmed failing against the pre-fix code first (both callers won)
- [x] Updated one pre-existing test file whose mock lacked `transactWrite`; added two cases to the cron's test file for the `identityCandidates` pass-through and null-handling
- [x] Full affected suite green (320 tests across 16 files)
- [x] **Live-verified against real dev DynamoDB, not mocks**: fired 5 truly concurrent `enrollLead` calls for the identical lead+sequence from a standalone script hitting `Dev-AW-SequenceEnrollments` directly — exactly 1 of 5 won, confirmed independently via `getExistingEnrollment`'s own GSI query. Test data cleaned up after (enrollment + both claim items deleted).

title: feat(tracking): tracker SDK + public session ingest + tracking config (ENG-2315)
body:
## ENG-2315 (S5 of epic ENG-2309): tracker SDK + public ingest + tracking config

Productises the DramaBreak one-off (`app/api/track/route.ts` + the inline tracker in `guilty-before-the-mic-v2.html`): any landing page pastes one tag and gets one session row per visit in a **session list**, classified server-side.

```html
<script src="https://api.agentweb.pro/sdk/v1/aw.js" data-aw-list="<listId>" async></script>
```

**Stacked.** Base is `anurag/eng-2312-atomic-session-upsert` (S1+S2). The branch also merges S3 (`anurag/eng-2313-traffic-source-classifier`, PR #3260) as its first commit because S3 is not merged yet, so this PR's diff against the base shows S3's files until #3260 lands; the S5 work is the 4 commits after that merge (+ the base merge commit).

### DATA-PLANE NOTICE: needs Harsha's explicit approval before merge
- **New persisted list attribute** `trackingConfig { allowedOrigins[<=10], pageLabel<=60 }` on `AW-LeadLists` rows of session lists. No new tables, no GSIs, no migration, no backfill; absent on every existing list.
- **New public, unauthenticated, CORS-open endpoint** `POST /api/track/event` (+ public `GET /sdk/v1/aw.js`). It can only write session rows into lists that are `listType:'session'` AND `publicAccessEnabled===true` AND have allow-listed origins.
- `createLeadList` gains an optional `initialAttributes` argument (additive; no existing caller changes) so a tracker list is public and configured from its first write.

### What changed (one logical change per commit)
1. `refactor(crm)`: the exactly-once create + atomic merge loop moves **verbatim** from forward-lead's session branch to `services/sessionUpsertService.ts`; both forward-lead and the ingest call it. Zero behaviour change: forward-lead's existing tests pass **unmodified** (no test file under `src/__tests__/webhooks.forwardLead.*` is touched).
2. `feat(crm)`: `trackingConfig` validation (`utils/trackingConfig.ts`) + `updateLeadList`/`createLeadList` hooks.
3. `feat(tracking)`: `POST /api/track/event`. 16kb body (own parser mounted before the global 50mb one), event allow-list, bounded allow-listed fields only (`clean()` discipline of the LP route), list resolved server-side, Origin must be in `allowedOrigins` (empty list = no browsers), per IP+list rate limit that drops with 429, answers 204. The SDK sends **raw signals only**; the server classifies with S3's `classifyTraffic` and overwrites `trafficType/channel/channelKey/channelGroup/referrerHost/sourceLink/sourceDetail`, stamps `classifierVersion`, `device` (from the UA header) and `page` (from config).
4. `feat(tracking)`: `GET /sdk/v1/aw.js` + the SDK. Shipped as a **TS string constant** (`src/sdk/awSdkSource.ts`): `tsc` copies no `.js`/assets and the EB bundle is `dist` + package.json, so a `public/` file would pass CI and 404 in prod. Verified in a clean `npm ci` build that `dist/sdk/awSdkSource.js` exists and parses.
5. `feat(tracking)`: enable-tracking API: `POST /api/tracking/session-lists` (creates the list in one write: `listType:'session'`, `isSystemManaged`, `publicAccessEnabled:true`, `alertEvents:[]`, session `displayFields`; returns the embed tag) and `PUT /api/tracking/session-lists/:listId/config`. Gate: `canDestructiveCrmList` (owner / org owner / listed CRM editor), the same gate `PUT /api/crm/lists/:listId` uses for list settings; `canAccessCrmList` is read-level and would let any org viewer widen the allow-list. Unknown body fields are a 400.

### Decisions / deviations to review
- **Responds 204 after the write completes** (not before): a DB failure is a real 500 instead of a lost event nobody sees, and tests/monitoring are deterministic. Latency is one conditional put.
- **Out-of-order safety beyond S2's journey group.** `buildSessionMergePlan` takes an optional `journeyKeys` (default unchanged for forward-lead); the ingest widens the guarded group with `lastEvent`, `furthestStage`, `lastCustom*`, `lastClick*`. The SDK sends cumulative `lastEvent`, `clickCount`, `clickLog` on **every** event. Real-DynamoDB testing found both failures (an older play_start overwriting a newer state; a later event overtaking the click events and the click log being rejected by the guard).
- **First-touch channel**: the SDK cannot know a channel (no client classifier), so it stores the first landing URL + referrer host in localStorage (`aw_ft_url`, `aw_ft_ref`) and the server classifies them (`firstTouchChannel`). A client-sent `firstTouchChannel` string (older page-local trackers set `aw_ft_ch`) is still accepted as a cleaned string.
- **Do-Not-Track**: NOT honoured by default (consistent with the existing LPs). A page can opt in with `data-aw-respect-dnt` (also honours GPC). **Harsha: please confirm the default.**
- **Custom events** (`awTrack('x', props)`) never mint new columns: one bounded `lastCustomProps` JSON blob + `lastCustomName`, so a caller cannot grow a customer's list schema (`createLead` adds every new key to `fieldNames`).
- **Two rate limiters, IP-wide first**: 600/min per IP across all lists (`INGEST_IP_RATE_LIMIT`, 2.5x the per-list cap, room for a shared NAT), then 240/min per IP+list. The per-list key comes from the body, so on its own rotating listIds gave a fresh bucket per id and every request cost an unauthenticated DynamoDB read; the IP limiter drops those before any read or per-list key. Both are `express-rate-limit` in-memory stores: per-instance, not global; idle keys are swept every window (previous/current rotation), so growth is bounded by what the IP cap lets through. Keys use `req.ip` (`app.set('trust proxy', 2)`; if the hop count were wrong the key would be the ALB/proxy address, throttling everyone together, or a client-forgeable XFF entry, making the limiter bypassable), **not** the first X-Forwarded-For hop (client-forgeable). The stored visitor `clientIp` uses the first hop as specified (same as forward-lead; spoofable, write-once).
- A request with **no Origin header** (server-side/curl) passes the origin gate (it is not a cross-site browser request) and is bounded by every other gate; it cannot write anything a browser could not.

### Verification
- Mutation-checked unit/contract tests: 39 targeted mutations across SDK / ingest / config / API / service plus 8 follow-ups. Initial survivors: 4 were real test gaps (counter derived from journey length, active-time double count, payload-size shedding, whole-body spread) and are now killed by added tests; 2 were equivalent mutants (a storage write that is guarded twice; a client `trafficType` that the field allow-list already cannot carry).
- Test: 12 requests with 12 different listIds from one IP get 429 after the IP cap and make no `getLeadListById` call for the dropped ones (mutation: IP limiter removed or keyed per list -> fails).
- Real DynamoDB (`amazon/dynamodb-local`, 127.0.0.1, https blocked in the harness) through the **real express routes + real crmDb**: one session delivered 10x per event, shuffled, concurrent (60 requests) -> exactly 1 row, `leadCount` 1, final cumulative journey, server classification; hostile payloads (2MB, wrong types, 50 junk keys, `__proto__`) bounded with no 5xx; gates write nothing; the **real aw.js in jsdom** posting to the real route stored the row. The **real compiled `app.ts`** (clean install) was exercised for the CORS exception, 16kb-before-50mb parser order, mounts and an unaffected forward-lead.
- Clean `npm ci --ignore-scripts` copy outside the repo: `npm run build` exit 0, `npm run typecheck` exit 0 (the shared symlinked node_modules is stale and hid 2 real type errors that this caught and fixed).

### Rollback
- Revert this PR. Nothing else depends on it: forward-lead returns to its inline session branch (identical behaviour). Existing `trackingConfig` attributes on lists are inert once the endpoint is gone (no reader), and need no cleanup.
- Kill switch without a deploy: set a tracker list's `allowedOrigins` to `[]` (PUT config) to deny every browser, or turn `publicAccessEnabled` off for it (ingest returns 403).

### Post-deploy smoke
1. `curl -sI https://api.agentweb.pro/sdk/v1/aw.js` -> 200, `content-type: application/javascript`, `cache-control: public, max-age=300`, `access-control-allow-origin: *`, an `etag`.
2. `POST /api/tracking/session-lists` (user JWT) with a test origin -> embed tag; `curl -X POST .../api/track/event -H 'Origin: <allowed>' -d '<json>'` -> 204; with a foreign Origin -> 403 `origin_not_allowed`; a 20kb body -> 413.
3. Open a page with the tag in a real browser; confirm one row appears in the list with `channel/trafficType/classifierVersion` and `dwellSec` after leaving the tab. Confirm `POST /api/webhooks/forward-lead` is unaffected.
4. Check the ALB/nginx serves `/sdk/v1/*` (only `/api` and root paths like `/batch-review` have precedent; I could not verify this path pre-deploy).

### Not verified here
Prod routing of `/sdk/v1/*`, real browsers (Safari ITP, in-app browsers), the portal's rendering of the new `displayFields` (custom-field column keys), and any customer page CSP (`script-src`/`connect-src` need `api.agentweb.pro`).

title: feat(tracking): segment routing into child session lists (ENG-2316)
body:
## ENG-2316 (S6 of epic ENG-2309): segment routing into child session lists

**Stacked on #3266 (ENG-2315, S5)**; base is `anurag/eng-2315-tracker-sdk-ingest`. 2 commits.

A session list can copy each session into child session lists by traffic segment, e.g. "organic sessions also go to the Organic list" (the DramaBreak requirement, today hard-coded as `ORGANIC_LIST_BY_PAGE` in the LP route):

```jsonc
// PUT /api/tracking/session-lists/:listId/config
{ "routing": [ { "id": "organic", "match": { "trafficType": "organic" }, "childListId": "list_..." } ] }
```

### DATA-PLANE NOTICE: needs Harsha's explicit approval before merge
- Extends the **new persisted list attribute** `trackingConfig` (S5) with `routing: RoutingRule[]` (<=5 rules). Still no new tables/GSIs/migrations; absent on every existing list.
- At ingest, a session is **also written into other lists** (the children). Same row shape and same exactly-once upsert as the parent; the parent is unchanged and still has every session.

### Behaviour
- Rule = `{ id: slug, match: { trafficType?: 'paid'|'organic', channelGroup?: ChannelGroup, channel?: channelKey }, childListId }`. A rule needs >=1 match field; **all** given fields must match; rules are independent (a session can land in several children); each child once.
- **PUT validation** (shape first, then against the DB rows): max 5 rules, unknown fields rejected, each child exists / is a session list / has the **same owner** (`userId`) / is not the parent / has **no routing of its own** / is targeted by one rule only; the caller must also pass `canDestructiveCrmList` for **every child** (copying sessions into a list is writing to it); and the list must not already be another list's routing target (reverse check through the existing `userId-index`, no new GSI). `routing: null` or `[]` clears it. An update that does not mention `routing` leaves stored rules untouched.
- **Ingest fan-out** (`services/trackerIngestService.ts`): parent upserted always; every matching child upserted concurrently with the SAME `sessionId`/`sessionStartMs` (its own deterministic `leadId`, since the hash includes the list id). Children are re-read on the write path and skipped (logged) unless still a session list with the parent's owner. **A child failure is logged and never fails the request or the parent**; a parent failure still 5xx. Only the list the event was posted to is consulted (one level), so a stale or racing config can mis-route but cannot loop.
- **Self-healing and its limit.** The journey is cumulative and every event upserts again, so a child that missed a write converges on the next event. Scalar fields only a missed event carried (e.g. `lp_view_at`) stay missing on that child. Verified against DynamoDB-local (child missing at the first event, created before the second).

Also carries the S5 IP-wide rate limiter fix (merged from the S5 branch).

### Decision to review
- "Same owner" is strict `child.userId === parent.userId`; I did not extend it to "any list in the org the caller can edit", because the ingest re-checks ownership on every write and a cross-owner copy would silently stop working if either side changed. Easy to relax later.

### Verification
- Mutation-checked: 24 mutations on the routing util, API and service (AND vs OR, empty-rule-matches-all, every validation rule, reverse-chain, child permission, failure isolation, owner / session-list re-checks, parent-as-child, shared row object, per-child session identity). All killed; one initially survived (the "parent named as its own child" test never returned a parent row from the mock) and the test was fixed.
- Real DynamoDB (`amazon/dynamodb-local`, real express routes + real crmDb), 120 concurrent shuffled deliveries (10x each event, 2 sessions): the parent has both sessions; **paid -> parent only (with the one-organic-child config), organic Instagram -> parent + organic child**; `leadCount` exact on all lists; child rows carry the same cumulative journey/classification/`sessionStartMs`; 3 of 4 broken children (missing / other owner / sales list) -> parent 204, healthy child written, broken ones untouched; self-heal check as above.
- Clean `npm ci --ignore-scripts` copy: `npm run build` exit 0, `npm run typecheck` exit 0 at this head.
- forward-lead, `sessionUpsert*`, `eng239.attributionE2E`, `eng309_310.captureInjection`, `crmDb.mergeSessionLeadEvent`, `crm.routes`, `sessionListType.contract`: all pass at this head (23 suites / 495 tests in the targeted run).

### Rollback
Revert this PR. Ingest then ignores any stored `routing` (it is only read by the fan-out), and the parent behaviour is exactly S5's. Rows already copied into children stay (they are ordinary session rows) and can be deleted from the children's CRM views if unwanted. Per-list kill switch without a deploy: `PUT .../config { "routing": [] }`.

### Post-deploy smoke
1. Create two session lists with the S5 API; `PUT` routing `organic -> child`.
2. Post one event with `utm_medium=paid&fbclid=x` landing URL, then one with `utm_source=instagram`: parent has 2 rows, child has 1 (the Instagram one), `leadCount` 2 / 1.
3. `PUT` a rule whose child already has routing -> 400 `routing_chain`; a self-targeting rule -> 400 `routing_self`.

### Not verified here
Production list volumes (each event now costs 1 list read for the parent + 1 per matching child; there is no list cache yet), a cross-org-owner scenario in the portal, and the portal UI for editing rules (not in scope).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Adds optional routing rules to session-list `trackingConfig` and fans matching events out to validated child session lists. The parent write remains authoritative, and child-write failures do not fail ingest. Reverting or disabling routing stops future copies; existing child rows remain.

title: fix(forward-lead): a lost duplicate-email race adopts the existing lead instead of returning 500
body:
## Problem (ENG-2309 / T1)
Measured on PRODUCTION (ordinary, non-session list): 12 concurrent forward-lead submissions of the SAME email -> `{201: 9, 200: 2, 500: 1}` and **9 rows for that one email**. The 500 body is exactly `{"success":false,"message":"Lead with email \"<email>\" already exists in this list"}`: `getLeadByEmail` (email-index GSI) missed, then `createLead`'s own pre-check found the concurrent row and threw a plain Error -> outer catch -> 500 + `api.lead_failed` owner alert, and the visitor's lead/event was dropped.

## Change (4 commits)
1. `createLead`: the duplicate-email pre-check throws the SAME message, now with `err.duplicateEmail = true` and `err.existingLead = <row>`.
2. `routes/webhooks.ts` forward-lead: the existing-lead merge is extracted, unmoved, into one `mergeIntoExistingLead` routine used by both the start-of-request `getLeadByEmail` hit and the typed-error adopt in the create branch. title: fix(session-upsert): guard funnel-state and click fields against out-of-order delivery
body:
## Problem (ENG-2309, in production)
`POST /api/webhooks/forward-lead` on a SESSION list guarded only `journey, eventCount, clickLog, clickCount, showsClicked` (by `eventCount`); every other key was last-write-wins by arrival. Measured in prod on a throwaway session list, events delivered `[count 3 app_cta_click, count 2 play_start, count 1 lp_view]` gave final `eventCount=3`, `journey` correct, but `furthestStage = lp_view` and `lastEvent = lp_view` (wrong). DramaBreak funnel analytics read `furthestStage`.
Second weakness: click data is carried only by click events, yet shared the `eventCount` group, so a click event (count N) overtaken by a non-click event (N+1) had its whole group rejected and the click data was lost.

## Fix
`mergeSessionLeadEvent` now takes one or several independently guarded groups; each is its own conditional UpdateItem (`attribute_exists(leadId) AND (attribute_not_exists(c) OR NOT attribute_type(c,:N) OR c <= :incoming)`), a failed condition is a no-op for that group only. forward-lead default (`SESSION_GUARD_GROUPS`):
- PROGRESS by `eventCount`: journey, eventCount, furthestStage, lastEvent, lastEp
- CLICKS by `clickCount`: clickLog, clickCount, showsClicked, lastClickLabel, lastClickShow, lastClickSection, lastClickUrl

A group whose counter is absent/non-numeric in the event falls back to last-write-wins. Digit-string counters are coerced for both counters. The tracker ingest still passes `journeyKeys` (INGEST_GUARDED_KEYS): one eventCount group, plan output shape unchanged, its tests untouched. Non-session lists and identity-less events do not reach this code.

## Evidence
- Fail-first on origin/main: new `sessionUpsert.outOfOrder.test.ts` 4 failed / 2 passed; pass with the fix.
- Adjacent suites (webhooks.forwardLead.*, sessionUpsert*, crmDb.mergeSessionLeadEvent, trackIngest*, trackerIngest*, sessionList*, eng239, eng309_310): 17 suites / 282 tests pass.
- Mutation checks (12 mutants): all killed (one initial survivor, guardApplied "any group" semantics, got its own test).
- dynamodb-local, real express route + real crmDb: baseline origin/main fails (i) `furthestStage=lp_view`, (ii) 5/5 rounds wrong, (iii) click data lost; fixed passes all (i)-(iv) incl. 3 sessions x 12 shuffled concurrent events x 5, exact leadCount; SDK/ingest harness (scratch-s5) still ALL PASSED.
- Clean `npm ci --ignore-scripts` copy: `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` exit 0.

## Rollback
Revert this PR; the row shape is unchanged (only which events win), no migration. Rows written meanwhile stay valid.

## Post-deploy smoke (safe on prod)
Throwaway session list; POST to forward-lead with the same sessionId/sessionStartMs and flat customFields, in order: `{eventCount:"3", lastEvent:"app_cta_click", furthestStage:"app_cta_click"}`, `{eventCount:"2", play_start}`, `{eventCount:"1", lp_view}`. Expect final `furthestStage=lastEvent=app_cta_click`, `eventCount=3`. Then a click `{eventCount:"5", clickCount:"1", clickLog:["a"]}` after `{eventCount:"6", page_exit}` must keep clickCount 1 / clickLog. Delete the list afterwards.

title: No LinkedIn account available for import_leads_from_search lead discovery
body:
## Summary

Juan (juan@usehaven.ai) reported `import_leads_from_search` failing with "No LinkedIn account is available..." Prod logs showed this was actually a 4-day Unipile-side outage (502s for every connected account platform-wide), not a missing connection. Root cause: the account-resolution fallback used a binary connectivity check that collapsed "proven dead" and "probe couldn't tell" into the same `false`, so the outage made the whole account pool look unconfigured.

## Fix, iterated through four independent reviews + an automated live-app verification bot (Opslane)

1. `resolveAccountIdWithSource`/`resolveAccountIdForEnrichment` now use the tri-state `probeAccountSession` instead of the binary check.
2. Added a reactive backstop in `import_leads_from_search` to correct the probe cache on a genuinely dead account; switched its disconnect check to the canonical `isProvenDisconnectError` (excludes a bare 403 — permission/plan restriction, not a dead session).
3. Fixed the same `ownerUserId` misattribution bug (site-wide pool accounts can never resolve an owner under an unrelated caller's userId) in both the `import_leads_from_search` and `linkedinOutreach` reactive handlers — confirmed live against the real dev DB.
4. Fixed a flaky cross-file jest interaction (`jest.requireActual` on a module with real `unipile-node-sdk` imports colliding with another file's virtual mock) — root-caused via stash-and-bisect, not worked around.
5. **Opslane** (an automated bot that actually runs the built app and drives real HTTP requests against it) found a genuine P1: `POST /api/onboarding/outreach/preview-prospects` returned a raw 500 instead of a clean 502/503 when the real Unipile search call failed. Root cause: `searchProspectsPreview`'s only error-detection path checked for `searchPeople` resolving with `{ error }` — but `handleError` is typed `Promise<never>` and always throws, so that check was dead code and nothing caught a real rejection. This became far more likely to trigger because of this PR's own change (an outage used to resolve to `null` and short-circuit cleanly; now it falls through to a real, unverified account, into this already-broken path). Fixed by wrapping the call in try/catch. Confirmed live by reproducing Opslane's exact scenario against the real dev DB.
6. Opslane also flagged a second case (`import_leads_from_search` still showing "no account available" with a pool configured) that I could **not** reproduce via the literal scenario described — my own live repro of "credential fetch throws" correctly falls through to the pool account. The far more likely explanation is a genuinely bad/rejected Unipile API key producing a real 401 from every account probe, which is correctly classified as a *proven* disconnect per the pre-existing ENG-281 contract (unchanged by this PR) — not a regression, since every account being truly dead is the one case where "no account available" is the honest answer.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] 462/462 tests pass across all 7 affected suites
- [x] Live-verified end-to-end against the real dev DB at every stage of every fix, including reproducing both of Opslane's exact reported scenarios
- [x] Four independent fresh-eyes code reviews plus independent verification of each review's own claims (not taken on their word) — three real findings fixed and re-verified, the fourth round found nothing further
- [x] Opslane's live-app verification re-runs on every push; the P1 it found is fixed and reproduced-then-resolved locally

Closes ENG-2205.

title: fix(ingest): a skewed device clock no longer loses the whole session (ENG-2324)
body:
## What / why (ENG-2324, epic ENG-2309)
`POST /api/track/event` answered `400 invalid_session` for every event whose `sessionStartMs` (minted from the **device** clock by the SDK) was outside `[now-48h, now+5min]`. A skewed device (or a tab left open for days) therefore lost **all** its events. forward-lead is untouched (still strict); the DramaBreak LP route validates its own window.

## Fix (server, ingest only) + one additive SDK field
1. **Commit 1 (server)** `resolveIngestSessionIdentity` (utils/sessionList.ts): an in-window start is used unchanged (byte-identical to before, zero extra reads). A *well-formed* integer start outside the window is no longer a rejection; it is replaced by `substituteSessionStart(sessionId, now)`:
   `generation = latest instant <= now of the form k*24h + phase`, `phase = sha256("start:"+lower(sessionId)) mod 24h`. So the substitute is in `(now-24h, now]` (inside the window, 13 digits, never ahead of the clock, ordering stays time-prefixed per ENG-2123), identical for every event of the session, and advances once per 24h at a session-specific instant (no shared midnight).
   Existing rows are found, not duplicated: for a *substituted* event only, the service does exact-key **consistent** `getLeadById` probes, in order: the device start if it had merely **aged out** of the window (row was created while it was inside), then the two previous generations; the first hit is the row used (so `customFields.sessionStartMs` follows the row actually written). Normal events do not read. Malformed sessionId / non-integer / non-numeric start is still a 400.
2. **Commit 2 (SDK)** adds `clientNowMs: Date.now()` to every event. Server uses it only as a "device clock is >5 min ahead" signal that pushes the session onto the substitute **for the whole session**. Without it a +10 min device flips mid-session: its start is rejected as future until the clock catches up (5 min later), then becomes in-window and would create a 2nd row. The field can only push a session onto the (bounded) substitute, never off the window rule, and is not stored on the row.

## Bounded abuse
A caller could already choose any position in the last 48h with an in-window start. The substitute lets it choose a position in the last 24h by grinding sessionIds (phase); nothing new, nothing in the future, nothing pinned above `now` or below `now-24h`. A caller cannot make a row sort at the top/bottom forever (the ENG-2123 failure). Extra cost for an attacker forcing substitution: <=3 consistent exact-key GetItems per target list per request, behind the existing per-IP (600/min) and per-IP+list (240/min) limiters.

## Design alternatives (honest comparison)
| Option | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Hash of sessionId only as the prefix (no clock) | not recent -> breaks ordering (ENG-2123); rejected |
| Substitute = "server now at first event" | non-deterministic: every event gets a different id -> row split; rejected |
| Stateless day-bucket only, no probe | splits every session that crosses the boundary; the probes fix this |
| First-seen time stored (alias item / new table / GSI by sessionId) | needs infra / data-plane change or pollutes the list; out of scope |
| SDK learns server time (response `Date`, time endpoint) | beacons ignore responses; needs first-event gating; does nothing for cached/old SDKs; riskier to prod pages. Only the 1-line `clientNowMs` is taken |
| Trust any future start up to +24h | lets a caller pin rows to the top for a day; rejected |
**Chosen**: stateless generation + exact-key probes + a sticky device-ahead signal: no new infra, deterministic, bounded.

## Evidence
* Unit/route/service: `npx jest` over utils, sessionUpsert, forward-lead, tracking, SDK: **52 suites / 1343 tests pass** (new: `sessionList.ingestIdentity.test.ts` incl. a 5000-case property test; route tests for +3d/-3d/+10min; probe tests; SDK test).
* **dynamodb-local** (real express router + real `crmDb`, https patched to throw), 3 waves x 5 concurrent events (15 requests) per session:

| device clock | statuses | rows | leadCount | leadId prefix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | all 204 | 1 | 1 | device start (unchanged) |
| +4min | all 204 | 1 | 1 | device start (in window) |
| -6h | all 204 | 1 | 1 | device start (in window) |
| +10min | all 204 | 1 | 1 | server time, 92 min old (< 24h) |
| +3d | all 204 | 1 | 1 | server time, 498 min old |
| -3d | all 204 | 1 | 1 | server time, 1171 min old |
Funnel state merged (eventCount 15, `page_exit_at`, `lp_view_at` present) in every row: no event lost.

Long-running (server clock moved forward with a Date.now patch; 5 concurrent events per step):
| scenario | rows |
|---|---|
| +10min device, new SDK, steps 0..6h | 1 |
| +3d device, new SDK, 0..47h (crosses 1-2 daily advances) | 1 |
| -3d device, OLD SDK (no clientNowMs), 0..47h | 1 |
| -47h59m device (start ages out of the window after 1 min), to +40h | 1 |
| correct clock, tab open 3 days (start ages out at 48h) | 1 |
| **+10min device, OLD SDK** (crosses the +5min edge) | **2 (documented residual)** |
| **+3d device, session alive >48h** | **2 (documented limit)** |
Malformed (`1.5`, `"soon"`) still 400.
* **Mutation checks** (16 mutations, each re-run against the targeted suites; all KILLED after two added tests for the first run's survivors): out-of-window rejected again; substitute = server now; phase fixed 0; substitute may exceed now; device-ahead stickiness removed; clientNow sign ignored; aged-out start not probed; future start probed; only one previous generation; forward-lead window dropped; probe loop removed; probe not consistent; probe on every event; row `sessionStartMs` not following the chosen row; parser drops clientNowMs; SDK drops clientNowMs.
* Clean-copy gate on head `4b125041e`: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` -> `npm run build` exit 0, `npm run typecheck` exit 0 (copy deleted).

## Known limits / risks (not hidden)
* An OLD/cached SDK (<=5 min cache, or a customer-pinned copy) has no `clientNowMs`: a device ahead by 5 min..24h keeps all events (the old behaviour lost them) but its row can split ONCE at the moment its start enters the window (shown above).
* A session alive >48h on the substitute path can start a 2nd row (probes are 2 generations deep). A device clock within ~jitter of exactly +5 min can alternate between the two classifications.
* A race of two concurrent events for one session straddling that session's own daily phase instant (once a day, ms-wide) with the first event's write not yet visible can create two rows. Not provable away without stored state.
* The stored `customFields.sessionStartMs` of a substituted session is the server substitute, not the device value (nothing in the repo reads it besides ingest).
* Existing sessions in flight at deploy keep their ids (in-window starts are unchanged).
* A persisted first-seen store (alias row/table) would remove the residuals but is a DATA-PLANE decision.

## Rollback
Revert the PR (two independent commits: the SDK field is additive and ignored by the server if absent; reverting only commit 2 is safe too). Rows written under substitute ids stay valid ordinary session rows.

## Post-deploy smoke (throwaway session list only)
Create a throwaway session list with a test origin; `curl -X POST /api/track/event -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' -d '{"listId":"<throwaway>","event":"lp_view","sessionId":"smoke-clock-0001","sessionStartMs":<now+3d>,"eventCount":1}'` twice -> both `204`; list shows ONE row, leadId prefix within the last 24h, leadCount 1. Delete the throwaway list.

## Update after merging main (#3282 list cache, #3287)
Merged `origin/main` into this branch (head `4a0f8d82b`); the only conflict was `trackerIngestService.write`, resolved keeping BOTH: `write(listId, ownerUserId)` (owner from the cached row passed to createLead) and the async probe loop. Re-verified on the merged head: 17 suites / 300 tests (ingest, route, sessionList, ingestListCache, db.ingestListCache, SDK, forward-lead, sessionUpsert) pass; clean-copy `npm ci --ignore-scripts` -> build -> typecheck exit 0; dynamodb-local skewed-clock proof unchanged (all 204, 1 row each for 0/+4m/+10m/+3d/-3d); NEW combined proof: 150 events over 5 sessions with clocks 0,+4m,+10m,+3d,-3d -> all 204, 5 rows (1 per session), leadCount 5, **1 ingest list read inside the TTL window** (the substitute probes read AW-Leads, not the list) and exactly 1 more after the TTL.
