title: ops(nginx): add request_time to access log for per-route p99 alarm
body:
**Updated after Manan's review:** EB's prod-3 nginx.conf already has `access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;` in the server block, so the original version logged every request twice (reproduced locally with prod-3's exact nginx.conf: 3 requests → 6 lines). The timing log now goes to a separate `/var/log/nginx/access_timing.log`; `access.log` is untouched (3 requests → 3 lines in each file). A new `.ebextensions/07-nginx-timing-log.config` ships the new file to CloudWatch (`/aws/elasticbeanstalk/<env>/var/log/nginx/access_timing.log`) by appending to EB's CloudWatch agent config. Rotation is covered by EB's existing `/var/log/nginx/*` hourly logrotate rule.

## What
Logging-only nginx change on the backend EB env.
- `backend/.platform/nginx/conf.d/access_log_timing.conf` (http context): `log_format main_timing` = EB's default `main` format **plus** appended `rt=$request_time urt=$upstream_response_time`.
- `backend/.platform/nginx/conf.d/elasticbeanstalk/access_log_timing.conf` (server context): `access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main_timing;`. This replaces the inherited http-level `access_log … main`, so each request is still logged **once**, to the same file CloudWatch already streams.

No routing, timeout, proxy, or traffic behavior changes.

## Why
The `prod3-p99-latency` alarm uses ALB `TargetResponseTime`, which can't exclude routes, and long-running `/api/agent-mode/*` and `/mcp` requests (p99 up to ~280s) dominate it. It's on an interim 60s threshold. With timing in the log, a CloudWatch metric filter can feed a per-route p99 alarm that leaves those routes out.

## Verification (local, nginx 1.31.6)
- `nginx -t` passes with the repo's conf.d plus an EB-style server include.
- Sample line: `127.0.0.1 - - [07/Oct/2026:01:33:16 -0700] "GET /api/x?y=1 HTTP/1.1" 401 179 "-" "curl/7.81.0" "-" rt=0.000 urt=-`
- The http-level `main` log got **0** lines, so there's no double logging.
- The status code stays in field 7, so the existing `prod3-auth-401-403` metric filter (`[ip, id, user, ts, tz, req, status=401 || status=403, ...]`) still matches; the new fields fall into `...`.

## Rollback
Revert this PR. nginx goes back to the EB default `main` format.

## Post-deploy
- Confirm new lines in `/aws/elasticbeanstalk/Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3/var/log/nginx/access.log` end with `rt=… urt=…`.
- Confirm the `prod3-auth-401-403` metric keeps reporting.
- Then create the per-route p99 metric/alarm and retire the 60s interim threshold.

Draft per Manan; Manan marks it ready and merges.

title: fix(v0): serialize landing-page iterations per page (ENG-1728)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
`iterateLandingPage` wrote `pendingIteration` unconditionally. Two distinct edits on the same page could both read "no pending edit", then each overwrite the other's recorded base and both send to v0. `finishIteration` also ran `REMOVE pendingIteration` unconditionally, so finishing one edit could erase another active edit's marker, and that edit's retry would then re-send.

## What this fixes (after)
This is ENG-1728 gap 2 only. It serializes iterations per page using DynamoDB `ConditionExpression`s on the **existing** `pendingIteration` attribute:
- **Pre-send write:** `attribute_not_exists(pendingIteration) OR pendingIteration.startedAt < :staleBefore` (stale = older than `V0_GENERATION_BUDGET_MS`). If the condition fails, the call throws `ITERATION_IN_PROGRESS` before v0 is called. The route maps that to **409**.
- **Post-send stamp:** `pendingIteration.messageHash = :h`. Retrying the same content still keeps the original base. If another edit has taken over a stale marker, the stamp doesn't overwrite it, and the wait continues because our message is already with v0.
- **Finish:** `attribute_not_exists(pendingIteration) OR pendingIteration.messageHash = :h`. If the condition fails, the iteration is still counted and set to `draft`, but the other edit's marker is left alone.

No new persisted fields, no schema/table/index change, and no change to persisted data shape. The only persistence change is that writes are now conditional.

## Complexity ledger
- Non-test lines: about +45 / −15 in `v0Service.ts`, plus a one-line route status mapping.
- Moving parts: no new tables, fields, flags, or dependencies. It adds 3 condition expressions and 1 fallback write in `finishIteration`.
- Behavior: a distinct edit sent while another is active now gets a 409 instead of racing. Every other path is unchanged.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts --runInBand -t "iterateLandingPage"`
2. **Expected:** 15 passed.

## Edge cases to check
- Two concurrent requests with the same content and no prior marker: the second gets a 409. It's a duplicate, so the user just retries.
- After a stale takeover, the earlier edit still finishes and counts its iteration without clearing the new marker.

## Test Evidence
- TDD: two new regressions failed first. The race test failed because no `ITERATION_IN_PROGRESS` was raised. The finish test failed because the unconditional REMOVE was used.
- After the fix: `-t iterateLandingPage` → 15 passed, 0 failed (362 skipped in the 377-test file). The full suite was deliberately not run (scoped run), and neither was full `tsc`/build. ts-jest compiled `v0Service.ts`.
- The existing test "a DIFFERENT message still sends" now uses a **stale** `startedAt`. With a fresh marker it described the race this PR removes; a distinct edit during an active iteration is now covered by the new rejection test.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- A distinct edit is rejected or retried while an iteration is active → `ENG-1728: a DIFFERENT edit racing an active iteration is rejected before v0 is called`
- A same-content crash retry keeps its original base → existing `ENG-1728: the pre-send base version is persisted BEFORE v0 is called` and the unsent-retry test (the stamp keeps `anchorBaseVersionId`)
- Finishing doesn't clear another active iteration → `ENG-1728: finishing an iteration never clears ANOTHER edit's active pendingIteration`

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/v0Service.ts`
- `backend/src/routes/landingPageGeneration.ts`
- `backend/src/__tests__/services.v0Service.test.ts`

## What was NOT tested
- The full backend suite, full typecheck/build, and staging. No production writes or v0 spend.
- Real DynamoDB evaluation of the conditions; the tests use mocks.

## Database gate note
This doesn't change the schema or persisted model. It does change write semantics on `AW-LandingPages`-style records (conditional writes). Flagging it so the reviewer can confirm it's outside the data-plane gate.

## Linear issue
ENG-1728 (gap 2)

title: feat(agent-mode): compare models side by side in a chat (ENG-55)
body:
## What

Backend for an **opt-in "Compare models"** option on the chat page (ENG-55 / ENG-113): the user chooses 2–4 models, sends one prompt to all of them, sees the answers side by side, and can continue the chat from the answer they prefer.

- `POST /api/agent-mode/compare` — tool-less, read-only fan-out over `agentModeService.callLLM`.
- `POST /api/agent-mode/compare/select` — "Continue with this answer": persists the chosen answer as a normal user/assistant turn.

Portal UI: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal (companion PR, linked below). **Deploy this PR first**; until it is live the portal button just shows a generic error.

Linear: ENG-55, ENG-113. Not covered here: ENG-112 (branching, needs a new persisted field → Harsha), ENG-110 (separate portal PR).

## Why this shape
- A Work Plan run is one session with one model and a linear message log; there is no fork/parallel-output concept, and an agent loop run N times would duplicate external side effects (email, posts, publishes). So the comparison is **tool-less** and **stateless until the user picks one**.
- **No schema, table, key or persisted-field changes.** Select writes the same message shapes `/generate` already persists.

## Behaviour and safety
- Never passes `tools`, `webSearch`, `tool_choice` or `fallbackModels` to `callLLM` (asserted by a test). `/compare` never writes to the session and never takes the generation lock.
- **No role logic, and only the selected model may answer.** Every user and admin can compare any model they can select; compare refuses only internal and live-voice models (not chat models for anyone). Who may select what is decided in one place (registry + usage-policy resolver), never here and never by a model's name.
- **No silent substitution:** a model runs only if the usage policy honours it as requested (`resolveEffectiveModelForUser` can otherwise rewrite it to the default). Unknown, live-voice, unpriced and internal-only models are returned as `rejected`. **The answering model is verified**: the gateway-reported model must be the selected one (exact id or a dated snapshot of it; `gpt-5.5-pro` is *not* `gpt-5.5`), otherwise that column is discarded as `model_mismatch` — never shown, never signed for "Continue".
- Response contains **no usage, token, cost or upstream ids** (customer surfaces never show dollars).
- `finish_reason: "length"` → `error / output_limit`, never a selectable answer (so Continue can't persist half a sentence).
- Limits: 2–4 unique models (after alias resolution), 8000-char prompt, 8192 output tokens per model (includes reasoning tokens), per-model isolation, 2 concurrent compares per user (per instance).
- Usage gate identical to `/generate` (429 `usage_paused`, same body shape). `409 compare_session_not_started` is returned **before any spend** for a chat with no first turn.
- `/compare/select` verifies an **HMAC select token** before any write (binds session owner, session, compareId, prompt, model, sha256(content), issuedAt; key derived from the JWT secret; 24 h expiry; constant-time compare), so a client cannot forge an assistant message or its `llm` attribution. It takes the session generation lock (409 `SESSION_BUSY`), is replay-safe, and does **not** emit `session-message-appended` (the portal appends from the HTTP response).
- Kill switch: AW-Settings `model_compare_enabled` — only the value `false` disables (503 `model_compare_disabled`); an unreadable setting leaves the feature on.

## Cost envelope (decision needed)
Worst case per compare is **2 × N calls × 8192 output tokens** (`callLLM` retries once; it has no AbortSignal, so a client disconnect doesn't stop spend). The usage gate runs once before the fan-out against a lagging ledger, so a compare near the cap can overshoot by about that amount. Available to every authenticated user (Opus included); the kill switch exists. Compare calls run inside the same run-funding scope as `/generate`. **Harsha: please confirm the envelope (tokens / concurrency).**

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit`: exit 0 (real `npm ci`; the shared `node_modules` in the main clones is stale — see below).
- 128 new tests (incl. strict served-model verification, mutation-checked); with every existing suite that imports the controller/routes + `sdkConstructionGuard` + `tokenUsageService`: 121 suites / 1,936 tests pass and `tsc --noEmit` exits 0, re-run after rebasing on current `main`.
- Mutation checks (guard removed → tests fail): select-token verification (9 fail), tools passed to `callLLM` (1), truncation ignored (1), ownership check (1).
- Independently reviewed by a separate adversarial pass; its MEDIUM findings (truncation, pre-spend first-turn guard, consistent read under the lock, prototype-key model ids, context normalisation, cost-bound wording) are fixed.

## Opus
The session model-picker endpoint still refuses any model id containing `opus` to non-admins (added 2026-04-03 when Opus 4.6 was the only Opus at $15/$75; never updated when Opus 4.8 became public on 2026-05-28; ENG-2028 ruled it stale against the ENG-744 public-catalog contract; the fix is Harsha's #2963, open and unmerged, bundled with unrelated work). **This PR does not touch that rule** (no conflict with #2963) and does not copy any such rule into Compare: Opus 4.8 / 5 / 5.5 are comparable by everyone. The only remaining admin-only model, Opus 4.6, is handled in a separate draft PR.

## Not verified
- **No live call to any model** (no gateway key available locally). The risk that reasoning models (GPT-5.5 / Opus 5 / Gemini 3.x) exhaust 8192 tokens → `output_limit` is untested.
- No staging/browser run; multi-instance behaviour unverified.
- Pre-existing, intentionally untouched: global body-parser errors return 500 not 400 (`app.ts` error handler); `normalizeModelId` returns prototype members for ids like `constructor` (guarded locally in this feature).

## Rollout / rollback / post-deploy smoke
- **Rollback:** set `model_compare_enabled` = `false` in AW-Settings (immediate, no deploy), or revert this PR. No data migration, nothing to repair.
- **Post-deploy smoke** (as the QA user, on a chat that has at least one turn): `POST /compare` with two cheap models → 200, two `ok` results each with a `selectToken`, no usage/cost fields; with one model → 400; as a non-owner → 403; `POST /compare/select` with a tampered `content` → 400 `invalid_select_token`; with the real token → 200 and two new messages in `GET /session/:id`; then flip the kill switch → 503 and flip it back. **Run one hard prompt on each reasoning model and check for `output_limit` before widening use.**

## Review notes
- Customer-portal companion (UI): AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1223. Separate, independent portal fix for ENG-110: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1224.
- Note for reviewers: `CLAUDE.md`'s "run `npm run typecheck`" was done via the repo's tsc invocation; the shared `node_modules` in the main clone is stale (missing `tesseract.js`, `botbuilder`, `sanitize-html`), so a symlinked install gives spurious tsc errors.

## Design decisions the verifier flagged (intended)
- **Every public model, Opus included, is comparable by every user and admin.** Compare has no role logic: it refuses only internal models and live-voice models. Who may *select* a model is decided in one place (the registry flags + the usage-policy resolver), never by a model's name. The session model PATCH still refused ids containing "opus" to non-admins; that name-based deny is removed in #3334, after which the picker, PATCH, `/generate` and Compare all agree.
- **The answering model is verified**, not assumed: an answer produced by a different model than the one selected is discarded as `model_mismatch` (never shown, never signed for Continue). OpenRouter reports its *canonical slug* (e.g. `anthropic/claude-4.8-opus-20260528` for the id `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`), so the check compares vendor + name tokens ignoring order and a trailing date, and still rejects lookalikes such as `gpt-5.5-pro`.

title: feat(models): no role-gated models — open Opus 4.6 and drop the name-based Opus denies (ENG-2028)
body:
## What

Removes `adminOnly: true` from `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`, the **last** registry model still gated to admins. After this no model is role-gated: the user catalog and the admin catalog are identical.

The principle (Anurag, 2026-10-07): *every user and admin can select the model of their choice, and the model they select is the one that runs.* The `adminOnly` mechanism itself is unchanged and still available; nothing sets it now.

## Why Opus 4.6 was gated, and why that no longer holds
- Added 2026-04-03 ("restrict opus models to admin users only", Opus 4.6 then the only Opus at $15/$75) — no reason recorded in the commit.
- Kept on 2026-08-19 when Harsha opened the OpenRouter roster to everyone ("not just isadmin"); the registry note and a test called it *"gated for unrelated reasons... still Bedrock-Claude-tier-gated"*.
- That reason predates routing every LLM call through the gateway. It is mapped to `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` in `openRouterGatewayContract.ts`, priced `withDerivedCache(5, 25)` — **identical to Opus 4.8 and 5** — and flagged `legacy: true` (quality score 26).

**This reverses a documented, tested exception, so it needs Harsha's explicit ack.** It is a separate PR on purpose so it can be reviewed or reverted on its own.

## Change
- `llmModelRegistry.ts`: drop the flag; update the comment that documented the exception.
- Tests: the three `getSupportedModels` tests, the "does not touch an adminOnly gate" test, the vision-options test and the role-resolution test that pinned Opus 4.6 as admin-only now assert the opposite (and a new test asserts the admin and user catalogs are identical and no registry model is `adminOnly`). The `adminOnly` mechanism is still covered via a synthetic flagged entry that is removed after each test.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit`: exit 0.
- Every backend test that touches the catalog (`getSupportedModels`, registry, `adminOnly`, model options, vision/report options, Opus 4.6): **44 suites / 1,401 tests pass**.
- Mutation: putting the flag back makes 6 of those tests fail.

## Not verified
- **Opus 4.6 has not been called live** (no gateway key available locally). It is mapped and priced, but whether the gateway currently serves `anthropic/claude-opus-4.6` should be confirmed with one real call before merge. If it is no longer served, the right fix is to retire the model, not to keep it admin-only.
- Interaction with the open ENG-2028 PRs (#2963 / portal #1184) is none: this touches neither `isModelSelectableBy` nor the PATCH rule. Note that the session model-picker still refuses any id containing `opus` to non-admins until #2963 lands, so Opus 4.6 will appear in the catalog but is still refused by that PATCH until then.

## Rollout / rollback
- **Rollback:** one line — put `adminOnly: true` back on the entry.
- **Post-deploy smoke:** `GET /api/agent-mode/model-options` as a non-admin now lists `anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1`; `GET /api/agent-mode/public/llm-models` includes it; one real completion on it succeeds.

## Update after review (CodeRabbit + independent review + Opslane)
Opening Opus 4.6 alone was not enough: the model picker lists Opus 4.8 / 5 / 5.5 for everyone (none is `adminOnly`) while the session model **PATCH** refused any id containing the word "opus" to non-admins (the ENG-2028 symptom, after which the user's first prompt was lost). This PR now also removes the remaining **name-based** "opus" denies (`updateSessionLlmModel`, `updateSharedSessionLlmModel`, `isModelSelectableBy`, `getReportsModelOptions`). Selection is gated **only** by the registry flags (`adminOnly` / `internalOnly` / live), so the catalog, the picker, the PATCH, Compare and `/generate` all agree. Same approach as #2963 for the PATCH blocks. By design **every public model, Opus included, is selectable and comparable by every user and admin**; a non-admin PATCH to Opus now returns 200 (previously 403).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium — More users can select Opus 4.6, but live gateway availability is unverified; rollback is a registry flag change.

The registry no longer marks Claude Opus 4.6 as admin-only. Admin-only gating remains supported. The session model picker still rejects `opus` IDs for non-admins until PR `#2963` lands. The author reports passing backend tests and type-checking.

title: feat(agent-mode): an explicit model selection runs on that model or not at all (ENG-903)
body:
## The issue

A model the user (or a schedule) **explicitly chose** was silently replaced by the default, so the model that ran was not the model that was selected:

- `resolveGenerationModel` turned an id the registry no longer has into the default and reported `fellBack`. Inside `resolveEffectiveModelForUser` that happened *before* the usage policy looked at it, so the policy saw the default, called it `honored`, and nothing was flagged.
- `selectPolicyModel` returned `corrected` (→ default) for a valid id that wasn't selectable.
- A scheduled run did the same and only sent an oncall email. ENG-903: *Harsha Daily X Post (Autonomous)* pins `claude-sonnet-4-5` (retired), so every daily run has been running on `anthropic.claude-opus-5`, a model nobody chose. ENG-892: 6 of 117 sampled sessions were booked to a model that never ran.

## The rule
**An explicit selection runs on exactly that model or does not run, and the caller is told.**
- *Explicit* = the **request carries a model** (`llmModel` on `/generate` or session creation, trimmed; a blank value means none) or a **schedule pin**.
- A model merely *stored* on a session is **not** explicit: no persisted flag can tell a user's pick from a system-stamped default, and none is added (that would be a data-plane change). So `/generate` without `llmModel`, `verified-generate`, and shared/conversable chats fall back to the **current default** when the stored model is retired or not selectable, as before. The portal always sends the picker value, so portal users still get the 422 and an "Unavailable" badge (companion PR agentweb-customer-portal#1225).
- No selection at all ⇒ the configured default. Usage-paused ⇒ the existing 429. Registry legacy aliases still map forward. User-configured **backup models are unchanged** (see below).

## Change
`resolveEffectiveModelForUser` throws `ModelUnavailableError` (`services/agentMode/modelUnavailable.ts`) for an explicit model that is not served or not selectable. `allowSilentSwap` is true only when nothing was explicitly selected.

| Entry point | Now |
|---|---|
| `/generate`, session creation | HTTP 422 `{ error, code:'model_unavailable', requestedModel, reason }`, validated **before any session write** (a pending deck/work-plan answer is not consumed), no LLM call, no metering, stored `llmModel` untouched, lock + idempotency claim released. The policy decision is computed once per turn and reused at dispatch. Paused accounts still get the plain 429. |
| An explicit **live voice** model in a text chat | 422 `not_selectable` before the user message is persisted (it used to 500 late, after saving the message and paging oncall). |
| Padded ids (`" gpt-5.5"`) | trimmed at intake; blank = no selection. |
| Shared / conversable chats, `verified-generate` | stored-only ⇒ fall back to the current default (never run on a stored model the owner cannot select, **including a stored live-voice model**). |
| Non-string `llmModel` (array, object, number) | 422 `model_unavailable` with a sanitised label (an array used to 500 on `/generate`). `null`/blank = no selection. |
| `/model-options` | no longer lists live-voice ids in `allModels` / `selectableModels` / backups (all consumers are text-chat pickers). |
| Scheduled runs | fails the run **before** any session, resume claim or lease work, recorded as a failure with `model_unavailable: pinned model "<id>" is not served` (or `not selectable`), **no requeue** (a throw would be requeued 3× with a false "will be retried" message). The oncall alert is kept and says nothing ran. Unpinned schedules keep the old alert-only behaviour. |

One producer (`modelUnavailable.ts`) builds every body; the echoed label is sanitised and capped at 120 **code points** (no split surrogate pairs). **No new persisted field, table, key or index.**

## Deploy prerequisite (read before merging — merge deploys to prod)
Every **schedule pin** (and any explicit request) naming a model that is neither served nor an alias **starts failing the day this ships**. Run `scripts/migrateStaleModelReferences.ts` first: its dry-run is the default and read-only; `--apply` is a data mutation (needs Harsha). Known example: the ENG-903 schedules pinning `claude-sonnet-4-5`.

## Verification
- `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 on the rebased head.
- 297 affected suites on the rebased head (over merged #3334 and #3329): 296 pass, 1 skipped, 0 failing (5704 tests). `agentModeService.sonnet45` failed 69 tests on an older `main`; it passes on current `main`.
- Four existing assertions encoded the silent swap and now assert the failure (each with the reason in a comment).
- Independent adversarial review + CodeRabbit + the Opslane verifier all found real issues, each fixed or answered below.

## Opslane Verify findings (first run, commit f9b8841) — disposition
1. *Never-picked chats get 422 once the default is retired* — **fixed by design**: a stored model is not an explicit selection (rule above).
2. *verified-generate on stored internal/admin-only models* — **fixed**: falls back to the default, never runs on the stored model.
3. *Backup model not tried after a 503 → 500* — **pre-existing, not a regression**: on `origin/main` the service and worker never read a backup model at all (`backupModel`/`llmBackupModel` appear only in the controller, which resolves, stores and echoes it; OpenRouter fails over inside the single request). Unchanged by this PR.
4. *Padded / whitespace ids give a false 422* — **fixed** (trim at intake).
5. *Scheduled failure says "not served" for admin-only* — **fixed** (reason-specific text).
6. *Live voice model in a text chat → 500* — **fixed** (422 `not_selectable` before persistence).
7. *Truncated id ends in a lone surrogate* — **fixed** (code-point truncation).

## Final-head review (independent, evidence-based) and Opslane round 2
Fixed from them: stored live-voice model in text chat, array `llmModel` 500, `/model-options` offering live ids, comments that contradicted the rule, and **"stored retired model fell back to the code constant instead of the configured default"** (Opslane run 203): the fallback is now the SAME default a brand-new session gets (`getDefaultModel()` = admin setting `agent_mode_default_model`), reported as a correction, not "honored". A configured default that is itself internalOnly / adminOnly / live falls back to the code constant with one `console.warn` (found by review: it would otherwise have failed every no-model turn).
Unchanged and identical on `main` (verified): backup models are never retried by the service (OpenRouter fails over inside the one request).

## Not verified / decisions
- The turn-generation lock is an in-memory per-instance set, as everywhere else in this controller; not changed here.
- No owner email for a failed scheduled run (new customer copy needs review); the signals are the failed run-history row and the oncall alert. A failed run still consumes `runCount` like any other failed run.
- Out of scope, unchanged: emma-email, work-plan `defaultModel` launch fallback, htmlCreation, the scoring judge, session types whose model comes from admin config, Slack/session responder (system-assigned model).
- Companion portal PR: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1225.

## Rollback
Revert the PR (no data to repair).

title: ENG-2104: RunBackend emitter seam and attempt-finished terminal event (PR 1 of F3)
body:
## What

First, deliberately small slice of ENG-2104 (F3). Adds terminal-event reporting at the `RunBackend` seam so any backend, including B4's future `ClaudeCodeBackend`, can report how a run ended through one typed sink.

- `RunBackendCallbacks` gains an optional, caller-owned `emitter` (the caller owns runId and seq; one emitter per run).
- New `attempt-finished` stream part (`outcome`: completed / failed / cancelled, optional `toolCalls`).
- `emitBestEffort` swallows sink failures. `RunEmitter.emit()` deliberately throws on sink failure (there is a test for that), so callers next to a live turn must not call it directly.
- `EmmaLoopBackend` emits `attempt-finished` then `finish` for completed / failed / cancelled runs and rethrows the original error unchanged. `cancelled` comes from the loop's own `result.cancelled` (not from `isCancelled()` after the fact, which could mislabel a run that finished and was stopped during tail work).
- The other 7 part types named by the ticket are described in a comment only, with the blocker for each. Giving them payload shapes now would be guessing.

## What this PR does NOT do (ENG-2104 stays open)

- **Terminal events only, not the whole stream.** `generateMarketingResponse` still builds its own internal `RunEmitter` (different runId) that only forwards legacy progress. The loop's text/tool/approval events do not flow through the new emitter, and nothing correlates the two runIds. Unifying them is left on the ticket.
- **No production caller:** `pickRunBackend` / `EmmaLoopBackend` are not used by the worker until B4 cuts it over (same shape as F1's `RunBackend` and `decideFallback`). Deployed behaviour is unchanged (checked by grep: only `runBackend.ts` references them).
- Not built: ambient emitter for `usage-observed` / `funding-changed` / `approval-requested`; persisted sequence numbers and replay cursor; reconnect protocol with an ownership check on the run id. Tracked on the ticket.

## Also in this PR (test-only, both fail on clean `main`)

- `agentModeService.adSetBidAndSchedule`: the source-scan test read `emma/tools.ts`; the Meta tool text moved to `emma/metaTools.ts` (ENG-2282).
- `calendlyWebhook`: four assertions now include the `'booking'` origin argument `createLead` is called with.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`: clean (Node 22).
- Unit tests plus `runBackend.integration.test.ts`, which drives the real `EmmaLoopBackend` against the real `agentModeService` (dependencies and the one model call stubbed). Mutations (remove the swallow; skip the completion emit; read `isCancelled()` instead of `result.cancelled`) each make tests fail.
- An independent fresh-context review of this diff found: cancellation derived from the wrong signal (fixed), an overclaiming emitter comment (fixed above), `finish` coupled to `attempt-finished` (split), a dead exported type (removed), full error object logged (now message only).
- Full backend suite earlier (Node 22): 2111 suites passed; the failing suites also fail on clean `origin/main`.
- Deployed this branch to test-env-1 and exercised it through the real API as an admin account and a throwaway non-admin user (deleted afterwards): plain turn, follow-up, tool calls, stop mid-run, 3 concurrent sessions, same-session busy lock, work plan, approval deck via the structured `deckAnswer` channel, scheduled chat test run, image attachment with a real vision call. No crash-class errors in the logs. This is a regression check only: the new emitter code is not reachable from the environment.
- The pre-push hook currently fails on `agentModeService.sonnet45` (69 tests of pinned model quality/cost scores), identically on clean `origin/main` after the model-catalog refresh; not touched here.

title: fix(linkedin): handled 503 instead of raw 500 when Unipile infrastructure fails (ENG-2205 follow-up)
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3275 (ENG-2205, merged). #3275 made `resolveAccountId*` return an account whose probe was only *indeterminate* (instead of `null`) so a Unipile outage no longer reads as "no account configured". Opslane's runs on this branch (135, 199) found the side effects below; each was verified against the code before being acted on.

## What changes

**1. Handled 503 instead of a raw 500 when Unipile infrastructure fails** (credential fetch, gateway/5xx, timeout, transport)
- New dependency-free `isLinkedInInfraError` (`utils/linkedInInfraError.ts`).
- `send-linkedin-message`, `send-linkedin-invite` and `sync-linkedin-connections` answer `503 { code: 'linkedin_unavailable' }` with a generic message. Business errors keep their existing handling (400 `Cannot send message:`, otherwise 500). Nothing is recorded on a failed send.
- The onboarding prospect preview maps an infrastructure rejection to `search_unavailable` (already rendered as a friendly 503); other rejections stay `unipile_error`.
- `import_leads_from_search` gives the agent the generic message instead of the raw internal text, and logs the raw error locally.

**2. Enrichment behaviour is deliberately UNCHANGED from before #3275**
- CRM enrichment (`crmEnrichmentService`) resolves its account with `resolveAccountId(userId, { verifiedOnly: true })`: when no account is *proven* live it gets `null`, skips the LinkedIn source with the existing warning, and keeps its normal parallelism (20, not 5).
- `resolveAccountIdForEnrichment` (v3 enrichment) is restored byte-for-byte to its pre-#3275 body.
- Consequence, intended: during a Unipile outage enrichment skips LinkedIn exactly as it did before #3275. Both original resolvers treated an inconclusive probe as "not connected" (`null`). Opslane run 199 findings 1 and 2 flag exactly this as a difference from #3275's behaviour, because an earlier version of this description said the opposite; that text was wrong.
- The skip warning now distinguishes the two causes: "LinkedIn (Unipile) is temporarily unreachable — linkedin source skipped" when an account exists but could not be verified (e.g. an outage), and the original "No LinkedIn (Unipile) account connected — linkedin source skipped" when there is none. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

**3. Authorization: a client-supplied LinkedIn account id was never checked** (pre-existing)
- `send-linkedin-message` and `send-linkedin-invite` passed the body `accountId` straight to Unipile, so any authenticated user could send from any account id they could name, including the site-wide pool account (its id is disclosed in agent tool responses as `sharedAccountId`). Both now require the account to be the caller's own or org-shared (`resolveLinkedInAccountForWrite`, the check withdraw/accept-invitation already use) and return 403 otherwise. The portal sends the user's own default account, so the normal flow is unchanged.
- Sequence steps: `POST`/`PUT /api/crm/sequences` stored each step's `linkedInAccountId` unvalidated and the drip worker sent from it. Create/update now refuse a new or changed pin the caller does not own or share (403). On `PUT`, pins already stored on the caller's own sequence are not re-validated, so an unrelated edit still saves after an account is disconnected. The drip worker re-checks the pin at send time, so a stale or foreign pin cannot send.

**4. Smaller behaviour changes (all covered by tests)**
- `send-linkedin-message`: the post-send engagement write is retried twice (keyed put with a fixed event id, so a retry overwrites rather than duplicates); if it still fails the route returns `{ success: true, engagementRecorded: false }` rather than a failure that invites a duplicate message.
- Ownership gate: a stored row is named by either its `account_id` or Unipile's `config.unipile_account_id` (they differ on legacy rows; the sync cron and scheduled-run gate already treat both as one account), so a user's own account is not wrongly refused. Access is not widened - both ids belong to a row already scoped to the caller's own/org-shared accounts.
- `import_leads_from_search`: an account is recorded as disconnected immediately only for Unipile's explicit `errors/disconnected_account`; a bare 401 needs a fresh probe to confirm first, since recording pauses scheduled runs and emails the owner.
- `isLinkedInInfraError` treats `SERVER_ERROR` as infrastructure only for gateway statuses 502/503/504 and Cloudflare-style 520-524; a plain 500 can be request-specific, so it keeps its normal error.
- Drip worker: a step pinned to an account the owner no longer owns/shares is snoozed 30 minutes (not retried every 5-minute tick). A failed ownership lookup keeps the normal retry.
- Sequence create/update validate pins on LinkedIn-channel steps only (a pin left on an email step is inert); a transient read failure on update is a retryable 500, not a misleading 403.
- The 403 for a non-owned account id carries `code: 'linkedin_account_not_connected'` and points the user to Settings → Connected Accounts.

## Deliberately NOT changed (tracked in ENG-2347)

- **`send-linkedin-message` auto-resolve still falls back to the shared pool** for users with no account of their own (own account first, then pool), exactly as before this PR. An earlier commit here removed that fallback; it was reverted because it is a behaviour change (pool-only users got a 400; Opslane run 199 finding 3) and this PR must not regress behaviour. Note `send-linkedin-invite` and the message-sync route do *not* borrow the pool, and `resolveUserOwnedAccountId`'s doc says user-initiated outreach should not — so this is an inconsistency; the product decision, plus the drip-worker pool use, is tracked in **ENG-2347**.
- The drip worker's auto-resolved account (no pinned account) can still use the pool; by design.
- `get_leads` wiring test updated for the `include_all_fields` option added in ENG-425 (unrelated stale test, fixed so the suite is green).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] 60 affected suites pass (1785 tests) on the merged tree
- [x] Non-vacuous: neutering each new guard fails its tests (503 branch, verifiedOnly, ownership checks, sequence checks, pinned-account exemption)
- [x] Live on a branch preview (real dev DB + Unipile): 403 for pool/foreign/made-up account ids on both send routes and on sequence create/update; own account passes; control run on the pre-fix code shows the hole was real; 503 paths with a forced credential-fetch failure; a sequence whose stored pin no longer resolves still saves
- [x] Independent reviews of each fix commit (fresh-context reviewers)
- [ ] Opslane re-run on the final head

Refs ENG-2205.

title: ops(nginx): bare request_time in access_timing.log for per-route p99 metric
body:
## What
Follow-up to #3324. A small format change to the **timing log only** (`/var/log/nginx/access_timing.log`): the line now ends with a bare `$request_time` as the LAST field (no `rt=` prefix). `$upstream_response_time` is dropped: it can be `-` or a comma-separated list on upstream retries, which would shift fields. `access.log` is untouched.

## Why
A CloudWatch metric filter can only use a log field as a metric value if that field is a plain number. `rt=0.006` isn't one, so the per-route p99 alarm can't be built on the current format. With bare numbers, this filter will work:

`[ip, id, user, ts, req != "*/api/agent-mode/*" && req != "*/mcp*", status, bytes, ref, ua, xff, rt]` → metric `RequestTime` = `$rt`

## Verification
Tested locally on prod-3's exact nginx.conf layout:
- `nginx -t` passes.
- 3 requests produce 3 lines in `access.log` and 3 in `access_timing.log`.
- Sample timing line: `... "GET /x3 HTTP/1.1" 401 179 "-" "curl/7.81.0" "-" 0.000`

## Rollback
Revert this PR. Only the timing log's format changes back.

## Post-deploy
- Confirm new lines in the `access_timing.log` log group end with a bare number.
- Then create the metric filter, the per-route p99 alarm, and retire the 60s interim `prod3-p99-latency` threshold.

Draft per Manan.

title: feat(agent-mode): log-only detector for [verified: <CRM tool>] tags no CRM call can back (ENG-2263)
body:
## Why
PR #3185 added a prompt rule: `[verified]` on a CRM number must mean a tool call happened in THIS turn. A scripted A/B replay (old vs new prompt, a one-line difference, ~290 runs, 8 models) showed the rule has **no consistent effect**. Cheaper, user-selectable models restate a stale overall CRM total about half the time and tag it `[verified: get_lead_lists]` with no such call that turn. The production default model (`gemini-3.8-flash`, checked on a fresh session) and the strong models (`claude-sonnet-5.5`, `gpt-5.5`) did not do it: 0 of 79 runs. (`gemini-3.1-flash-lite` is the cost-policy fallback, not the default.)

A prompt sentence can't fix that. This is the deterministic half, **measurement only**.

## What
- `utils/crmFreshnessGuard.ts` (pure, no LLM): checks each `[verified: ...]` tag against this turn's tool ledger using the existing `toolCallSucceeded` (so errored / `success:false` / duplicate / deferred calls don't count).
  - `cited_tool_not_run`: the tag names a CRM tool and none of the tools it names succeeded this turn.
  - `bare_tag_no_crm_tool`: a bare tag beside CRM wording, with no CRM tool that turn.
  - Tags that already say earlier / previous / stale are skipped.
- Wired in `agentModeService.ts` right after the existing always-on guards (ENG-736/971), same seam. It logs `[crm-freshness-shadow] ... (message NOT modified)` with `{sessionId, model, kinds, findingCount, tagsSeen, crmToolsSucceeded, sample}`.
- **It never edits the reply.** Always on, try/catch-wrapped (cannot throw into the turn), kill switch `AGENT_CRM_FRESHNESS_GUARD=off`.

## Evidence
- 26 unit tests; I broke each rule in turn (ignore the cited-tool check, drop the honest-tag skip, ignore `toolCallSucceeded`, ignore the kill switch) and each break fails tests.
- Replay of the saved outputs through the real detector: flags **49 of 83** bad answers from weak models (59%); **0 of 79** flags on the default and strong models. The one flagged message I inspected had a genuinely unbacked second tag; its honest `[verified: previous turn]` tag was correctly skipped.
- Typecheck clean.

## Deliberately not in this PR
- **No enforcement / rewrite.** Waits on production data (`grep '\[crm-freshness-shadow\]'`, split by `model` and `kinds`).
- **No caveat for untagged totals** (the other ~40% of bad answers). `get_lead_lists` returns `lists[].leadCount` and `totalLists` but no total-leads field, so the model sums it itself and a "number appears in the tool result" check has to accept sums. That needs its own design.

## Limits
- The replay used simulated CRM tool results and the real system prompt, not the full runtime scaffolding; the phrasings were deliberately tempting, so real-world rates will be lower.
- I could not confirm from deployed config that the older LLM-based finalize guard is off in production (config read was access-denied); this detector doesn't depend on it.

ENG-2263 stays open until the production data is read.

title: ENG-903: validate scheduled-chat model pins at write time
body:
## Summary
ENG-903: scheduled-chat model pins (`llmModel`, `llmBackupModel`) were stored unvalidated, so a bad pin only failed at run time (failed run + oncall alert). They are now validated at the write site with the same rules as the picker/resolver (`resolveGenerationModel` alias/served check + `isModelSelectableBy(canonical, isAdmin)`), via one helper `validateScheduleModelPin`. Failure returns HTTP 422 with the shared `buildModelUnavailableBody` (`code: model_unavailable`). Run-time behaviour is unchanged.

## Behaviour
| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| empty / absent / `''` | no pin (unchanged; `''` on update clears) |
| padded valid id | stored trimmed |
| honoured alias | accepted |
| not a registry key / alias | 422 `not_served` |
| internalOnly, live-voice | 422 `not_selectable` (also for admins) |
| adminOnly, non-admin | 422 `not_selectable`; admin accepted |
| non-string (array/object) | 422 |

## Compat rule
On update a model/backup is validated only when being SET to a different non-empty value. Absent, unchanged, or `''` are never rejected, so old schedules with a since-retired model can still have unrelated fields edited. An unchanged since-retired backup is kept as stored.

## Write paths
Covered: `createScheduledChat`, `updateScheduledChat`, `createScheduleFromTemplate` (per-use model/backup override). MCP/Emma schedule tools call these HTTP handlers, so they are covered transitively.
Left alone: template create/update (user + admin) and a template's own stored `llmModel` (not re-validated on instantiation); admin routes; work-plan `defaultModel` (already filtered by `getSupportedModels` at apply); internal `scheduleDb.updateSchedule` callers (llmModelChangeService, scripts, LinkedIn health). Portal not changed: its save handler shows a generic toast and drops the server message (follow-up).

## Verification
- New suite: 17 tests (13 fail without the change, all pass with it).
- Existing scheduled-chat suites (21 suites, 475 tests) green.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: feat(compare): Compare models as a plan-gated add-on (server-enforced, switch-off by default) [ENG-55]
body:
## Summary
Makes "Compare models" a plan-gated add-on, enforced on the server. It is OFF until an AW-Settings switch is set, so deploying this changes nothing. Companion portal PR: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1227.

- New subscription feature id `model_compare` ("Compare models") in `subscriptionService`; the partner-portal Subscription Types editor and the admin save filter are driven by `getAllAvailableSubscriptionFeatures()`, so no partner-portal code change is needed.
- New optional `isEntitled` dep in the existing compare/select deps seam, checked right after the `model_compare_enabled` kill switch and before any session read, usage check, lock, model call or write. Logic in `services/agentMode/modelCompareEntitlement.ts`.
- `GET /api/auth/me` gains an additive, non-persisted `modelCompareEntitled` boolean (same function as enforcement; chosen over model-options because `/me` is already loaded into the portal's auth state, carries `allowedFeatures`, and is the single boot call).

## Behaviour
| Switch `model_compare_requires_entitlement` | Caller | /compare and /compare/select |
|---|---|---|
| absent, or anything but `true` | anyone | unchanged (tier never consulted) |
| `true` | admin | allowed |
| `true` | effective tier (org-owner aware) includes `model_compare`, or legacy tier with no feature list | allowed |
| `true` | tier has an explicit list without the id | 403 `{error, code:'model_compare_not_entitled'}` |
| `true` | tier unreadable / lookup throws | 403 (fail closed) |
| settings read fails | any | last-known value (60s cache); cold start = not required |

Delegated sessions: `req.user` is the target customer, so the customer's plan applies.

## Rollout steps
1. Deploy. Nothing changes (switch absent).
2. In the admin Subscription Types editor tick "Compare models" on the tiers that should have it and save. A saved tier with an explicit list lacking the id loses Compare when the switch flips; legacy rows with no list keep it.
3. Set AW-Settings `model_compare_requires_entitlement` = `true` (effective within ~60s per instance).
4. Rollback: set it to anything else / delete it. `model_compare_enabled=false` stays the separate global kill switch.

## NOT changed
No DB schema or migration, no new table, no change to existing tiers or `model_compare_enabled`, no billing/usage metering, no model-call path, no prod/AWS config. Partner portal untouched.

## Deviations from the design
- Entitlement is evaluated for the requester (admin short-circuits; a non-admin non-owner already gets 403 `forbidden`), which equals the session owner's plan for every allowed case. `isEntitled` is a new optional dep rather than a changed `isFeatureEnabled` signature (that one is global and has no user).
- The one existing assertion that legacy rows with no list resolve to all features now also includes `model_compare` (expected).

## Verification
- Failing-first tests, then implementation: `modelCompareEntitlement.test.ts`, `modelCompare.entitlement.routes.test.ts` (real router + auth), `authMeModelCompareHint.test.ts`, additions to `modelComparison.test.ts` and `subscriptionService.test.ts`.
- Jest, targeted suites (modelCompare*, modelComparison, sdkConstructionGuard, subscriptionService*, authMe*, admin.subscriptionTypes): 12 suites, 360 tests, all pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` (backend, full): exit 0.
- Not verified: behaviour against live DynamoDB/AW-Settings (no prod access); user-facing strings need owner review.

Dev note: `dev/pending/eng-55-model-compare-addon.md`.

title: ENG-110: per-user cap on concurrent interactive generations
body:
## Summary
ENG-110 remainder, backend half. Adds a per-user soft cap on concurrently generating INTERACTIVE Emma chats. No data-plane change (no schema, table, migration or persistence change); state is in memory. Companion portal PR: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1229.

- New module `backend/src/services/agentMode/concurrentGenerationCap.ts` holds the counter (userId -> distinct sessionIds), the setting reader and the 429 body. `agentModeController.ts` changes stay thin.
- `/generate` takes a slot right after `tryClaimSessionGeneration` succeeds (inside the existing try/finally) and releases it in the same `finally` as the session lock.
- `/verified-generate` takes the slot inside `runVerifiedChat` after its claim, only when the interactive handler passes `capInteractiveUserId`; the handler maps the thrown `TooManyConcurrentRunsError` to 429.
- Not counted and never blocked: scheduled runs, auto-continuations, Slack, email, approval-inbox, result endpoints and other system `runVerifiedChat` callers (they do not pass the option). ishare/conversable generate is not touched. Compare keeps its own separate cap of 2.

## Behaviour
| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| 1st to 3rd concurrent chat (distinct sessions) for a user | admitted |
| 4th concurrent chat | `429 {error, code:'TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_RUNS', message:'You have 3 chats generating at once. Wait for one to finish, then try again.', limit:3}`; session lock and idempotency key released |
| Same session twice | 409 SESSION_BUSY as before; never counts twice |
| Setting `max_concurrent_generations_per_user` = 0 | unlimited |
| Setting absent / garbage (`abc`, `-1`, `2.5`) | default 3 |
| Setting read fails | last-known value, else 3 (cached ~60s) |
| Success, throw after claim, early return, 409, client disconnect | slot released in `finally` |
| Admins | not exempt (the setting is the knob) |

## Rollout
- AW-Settings key `max_concurrent_generations_per_user`, default 3 when unset. No feature flag needed.
- Rollback: set the value to `0` (takes effect within ~60s), or revert.
- Caveat (accepted, bounded): the counter is in-memory per instance and resets on restart. Prod is 1 instance, but Immutable deploys briefly run two, so during the deploy overlap a user can hold up to `limit` slots on each. This is a soft cap against tab-spamming, not a billing control.
- Client disconnect before headers still cancels the run (unchanged).

## Verification
- New: 20 unit tests (`concurrentGenerationCap.test.ts`), 8 controller tests for /generate (`agentModeController.concurrentGenerationCap.test.ts`: cap boundary, leak-free release on throw / between-claim-and-work throw / disconnect / 409, 0, garbage, per-user isolation), 3 for /verified-generate (`agentModeController.verifiedGenerateCap.test.ts`: 429, throw release, scheduled path exempt).
- Existing: 7 suites / 301 tests (concurrentRequests, verifiedGenerateLock, errorHandling, runSurvival, failLoudSelectedModel, autoMediaContinuation, modelComparison) and 15 further suites / 121 tests that call generateResponse/verifiedGenerate all pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean. Dev note: `dev/pending/eng-110-concurrent-sessions.md`.

title: ENG-112: branch a chat from a message (flag chat_branching_enabled, default off)
body:
## Summary
ENG-112: branch a chat from an assistant reply so the user can continue on a different model and compare. `POST /api/agent-mode/session/:id/branch {messageIndex, llmModel?, idempotencyKey?}`. Behind AW-Settings `chat_branching_enabled` (DEFAULT OFF: only the exact value `true` enables it; absent/unreadable = 404 `chat_branching_disabled`), so merging changes nothing. Companion portal PR: https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/1230.

## Design
A branch is an ordinary new session built by `createChatSession` from an ALLOWLIST, plus the source rows `[0..k]` appended through `addMessagesToSession`. Provenance is one free-form key, `metadata.branchOrigin`, on row 0 (the stored system prompt). No new session field, index or table. Logic in `services/agentMode/chatBranching.ts` (injected deps, like `modelComparison.ts`); wiring in `controllers/chatBranchController.ts`; `/model-options` gains an additive `chatBranchingEnabled` hint.

## Phase 0 proof table
| Claim | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| (a) ChatMessage.metadata is free-form, not stripped on write/read | PROVEN | `shrinkMessageForPersistence` touches metadata only when >350KB (keeps timestamp/toolCalls). Verified post-write by the service (row 0 re-read must carry branchOrigin). Test: provenance survives `getChatSession` and `filterMessagesForClient`. |
| (b) system row safe; no visible bubble | PROVEN with a CHANGED representation | A separate system provenance ROW at index 0 is DISPROVEN: the source's real prompt would sit at index 1, inside the model context (`buildMarketingContext` `startIdx = 1`). Instead branchOrigin rides row 0's metadata; row 0 is never sent to the model, compare reads only user/assistant, `ChatMessageItem` renders null for system. Test builds the LLM context and asserts no provenance/system row. |
| (c) admin taint | PROVEN | Tool rows copied; an admin branching inside a tainted turn gets the whole turn copied so narration + prompt stay redacted; customer cannot name a tainted (hidden) row. Mutation-checked. |
| (d) idempotency | PROVEN | In-process in-flight/replay map + the `AGENT_RUN_STORE` idem lane createSession uses; released on every failure. Limit: with the run store off only same-instance retries dedupe. |
| (e) allowlist | PROVEN | Test asserts every defined key on the new item is in the allowlist, with a source carrying ~45 forbidden fields incl. share tokens. |
| (f) concurrency/auth | PROVEN | Source claim held for whole copy, 409 SESSION_BUSY otherwise, never releases a foreign lock; owner-or-admin; consistent re-read under lock; headroom of 10 under the 1000-message cap; owner's model/entitlement via `resolveEffectiveModelForUser`. |
| (g) data-plane | See below | |

Hazards found: copying `usage` would bill the branch (addMessagesToSession runs `incrementTokenUsage`) so `usage`, `metadata.feedback`, `clientId`, stale `messageIndex` are stripped; `addMessagesToMessagesTable` silently swallows unprocessed batch items, so the copy is re-read and verified (dense indices, messageCount, provenance) and a half-built branch is archived (existing soft-delete).

## Copy hazards
| Copied | Not copied (why) |
|---|---|
| Rows `[0..k]` incl. hidden tool rows, tool ledger, llm | `usage`, feedback, clientId, messageIndex (billing/attribution/indices) |
| llmModel (request or source), associatedSkills, selectedStartupId, portalType agent, pageIdentifier only `agent-mode`/`skill-*`, sessionType forced regular | share tokens/shareMetadata/interactiveShareMetadata (a copy must not be public), totals/costs, llmUsagePolicyDecision (fresh one made), scores/summary/feedbacks/favorites/archives/publishStatuses, workPlan, calledFunctions*, pending* slots, workflowRun, publishAdmission, execution/email/slack/gtm/result bindings, delegateInfo (this request's is used), archived/error, assetCache/assetScanIndex (rebuilt lazily), pageContent |
Refused: non-`regular` sessions, non-agent portals, archived (404). Admin branching keeps the branch owned by the source owner.

## Flag / rollout / rollback
Default off. Enable by setting AW-Settings `chat_branching_enabled` = `true`. Rollback: set anything else; endpoint 404s and portal hides the action. Existing branches are ordinary sessions.

## Data-plane determination
AGENTS.md gates "table, schema, index, key, ORM/persistence-model changes ... and anything that can reinterpret, orphan, expose, or make stored data unrecoverable". This adds no table/index/key/session attribute; it writes ordinary session items and message rows via existing methods, plus one optional key inside the existing free-form `metadata` map (and `idem#` rows in AW-AgentRuns via the existing lane). It is a bounded per-request write (<=990 rows), not a backfill/bulk mutation. I read it as outside the Harsha gate. Residual risk: it introduces a new reader contract for `metadata.branchOrigin`, and analytics/CRM see a branch as a new session with copied history; this is the one judgment call a reviewer may want to confirm.

## Verification
New: 80 service tests (real ChatbotDB over an in-memory DocumentClient) + 15 route tests + 4 model-options tests; existing suites touching sessions/messages (16 suites, 497 tests) green; mutation checks (keep usage, no taint extension, no release, copy delegateInfo) each fail the suite. Backend `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Adds `POST /api/agent-mode/session/:id/branch` to create a session from a selected history prefix, with optional model selection and idempotency. The service checks eligibility, applies rate limits, and verifies copied rows before revealing the branch. Model options include a branching hint, and shared views omit branch provenance.

title: ENG-2107 (B1): claude -p runner — pinned binary, clean env, lockdown flags, kept-open session per conversation
body:
## Summary

B1 of ENG-1816 Track B (Claude subscription). A kept-open `claude -p` process per conversation, with every lockdown rule the ticket requires enforced by the module itself, not by caller discipline.

`backend/src/services/funding/claudeCliRunner.ts`:
- **Allowlisted env built from scratch per spawn** — never `process.env`. A stray `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in the backend's real env can never reach the child and silently convert a subscription run into API billing.
- **Lockdown flags**: `--tools "" --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources ""`, `--system-prompt-file` (not `--system-prompt` — Emma's real prompt exceeds the OS arg-length limit), `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_THINKING=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` pinned explicitly.
- **Kept-open pool keyed by conversationId**, idle-close timer, concurrency cap with a FIFO queue.
- **`prewarm()`** — a named entry point for spawning ahead of the first real turn (e.g. on chat open), proven for real to deliver the warm-session latency the ticket claims (see Evidence).
- **`apiKeySourceFor()`** captures the `system/init.apiKeySource` field, so the ticket's own named requirement — *"add an adapter contract test on every version bump that asserts `system/init.apiKeySource == 'none'` with a subscription-mode login"* — is a real, checkable thing (`claudeCliRunner.live.test.ts`, gated behind `CLAUDE_CLI_LIVE_TEST_CONFIG_DIR`, never runs in CI, run by hand on every version bump).
- `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` pinned **exact** (`2.1.294`, no caret) as a deliberate exception to this repo's usual caret convention — the ticket documents that `--bare` may become the `-p` default in a future release with no announced opt-out.

**Explicitly deferred, not built here** (same boundary the design doc verifies against B2/B3's real scope): the MCP tool bridge (B2/ENG-2109), the real `claude_subscription` credential store (A1/B3/ENG-2110), worker-host provisioning (B5/ENG-2114), and `pickRunBackend` cutover (B4/ENG-2113). `prewarm()` wiring to a real chat-open signal is also out of reach until B3/B4 land — there's no live connection to warm yet and no caller.

## Evidence

- Typecheck clean, 15 unit tests green (mocked process boundary): env-lockdown invariant (tested with a real stray `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set on the test's own env, proving it never reaches the child), flag construction, turn round-trip, pool reuse, `prewarm()` reuse, concurrency queueing, idle-close, apiKeySource capture, failure containment.
- Four live model probes this session (haiku×2, sonnet, opus) on the pinned binary — all succeeded honestly (no Claude Code identity spoofing), confirming `claude -p` passes identity checks on every tier.
- Ran the ticket's own "real payload, not trivial" bar for real, through this module: Emma's real `AGENT_MODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (not synthetic) + a clearly labeled size-matched placeholder for the tool-schema payload B2 doesn't build yet, ~53.1k tokens total, sonnet model — `prewarm()` then two real turns: turn 1 (cold) 3603ms, turn 2 (same session, now warm) 2093ms, a real ~42% speedup; peak RSS 227MB (holds under the design's own ~250MB estimate).
- Every live probe used an isolated copy of the already-authenticated login, never the live path — verified via mtime, every time, that the real session's credential file was never touched.

Design doc with the full verification trail: `eng-1816-brain/evidence/drafts/b1-claude-p-runner-design.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `claudeCliRunner.test.ts` (15/15, mocked process boundary)
- [x] `claudeCliRunner.live.test.ts` run by hand against a real login (gated, skipped in CI)
- [x] Real at-scale probe against the live binary (sonnet, ~53k tokens) — see Evidence
- [x] Synced with `main` before push, pre-push hook green (typecheck + related suite)

title: ENG-903: Work Plan launch and save fail loudly on an unavailable pinned model
body:
## Summary
Product rule: the model a user/admin selects is the only one used. A Work Plan's non-empty `defaultModel` is an explicit pin, but launch silently dropped an unsupported pin for the account default (console warning only). Now the launch fails loudly with HTTP 422 `model_unavailable` (shared `buildModelUnavailableBody`) before any session or side effect, and the pin is validated at save time like schedule pins (#3365). The pin rule set is extracted verbatim into `services/agentMode/modelPin.ts` and `validateScheduleModelPin` delegates to it, so schedules, plan writes and plan launches cannot drift. Empty `defaultModel` = account default (unchanged). No new persisted field/table/index.

Companion portal PR: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1232 (display + surfaces the 422 message).

Admin determination: the launching user. `createSessionWithPlan` = the signed-in caller (anonymous = non-admin); `applyPredefinedWorkPlan` = the session owner (launch/accept routes enforce owner == caller; Emma tool uses context.userId). adminOnly clears only for an admin; internalOnly/live-voice fail for everyone. Plan writes: user route = writer's admin flag; admin route = admin.

## Behaviour (path -> before / after)
| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| POST plan session (`createSessionWithPlan`, public) | session + plan created, pin silently replaced by default | 422 before `createChatSession`; alias stored canonically |
| `POST /session/:id/work-plan` (launchWorkPlan) | via applyPredefinedWorkPlan: plan applied, model left unchanged silently | 422, nothing applied |
| accept recommendation | same | 422, nothing applied |
| Emma `launch_predefined_work_plan` | launched, model silently unchanged | `success:false, errorType:'model_unavailable'`, message = the shared sentence; no mutation |
| Unattended/scheduled launch (model tool call inside a scheduled run; no separate server-side plan-launch path exists) | silent | refused as above + deduped oncall alert |
| Plan create/update (user + admin routes; MCP goes through them) | any string stored | 422; unchanged stored value tolerated; '' clears (field removed); trimmed; non-string 422 |

## Item 4 classification (read-only; nothing changed)
| Place | Class | Evidence / decision |
|---|---|---|
| agentModeController ~4136 task-type override (report/image/video required fn) | system task-type override, persisted onto a session | only when `params.llmModel` absent; callers are system flows (revisionService, humanEvalAction, imageReports) not a request model; added in 7cea339 as per-feature admin models. Not a request selection; behaviour change is a product decision (it does persist onto a user session) - left, flagged |
| createSession ignoring explicit `requestedLlmModel` for skill/emma-sidebar/report/image/video | explicit-selection ignore (documented intentional) | not tiny: needs the portal to stop sending the picker value for these types, else 422 would break them; left, flagged |
| Slack/email/sessionResponder `session.llmModel \|\| getDefaultModel()` | system default | leave |
| emma/tools.ts 7616/7636 `'anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6'` | system default | only when `context.llmModel` is absent (no session model); leave |
| htmlCreation ~1351 template fallback | stored session model (ENG-46, already recorded) | the turn model already passed the resolver; leave |

## Verification
- New: `workPlanModelFailLoud.test.ts` (25), plus cases in createSessionWithPlan (44 total), accept/launch (15), applyWorkPlan suites. Fails without the fix (10 failures on pre-change src), passes with it.
- Cases: retired, internalOnly, live, adminOnly non-admin/admin, alias, empty/blank, valid, non-string; no session/skills/plan/model writes on 422; write-time unchanged-stale tolerated, clear, trim.
- 15 suites / 334 tests green before final edits: work-plan, #3365 schedule validation, failLoud*, adminOnlyModelEntitlement. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

## Review follow-ups (be3931d3f)
- The plan's model is now written FIRST; if that write fails the launch returns `model_save_failed` (HTTP 503, Emma `success:false`) with nothing else written (createSessionWithPlan also deletes the empty session best-effort). 422 stays for genuine `model_unavailable` only.
- Anonymous 422 body is `{error, code:'model_unavailable'}` only (no model id, name or reason), produced by `buildAnonymousModelUnavailableBody` in `modelUnavailable.ts`. Signed-in callers keep the detailed body.
- Admin plan route: admin status is applied only to a private plan owned by an admin (PUT); POST and system/public/shared/other-owner plans validate as non-admin, so an adminOnly pin there is 422 `not_selectable`.
- Plan-pin wording no longer says "you selected"; the Emma tool message adds a do-not-retry hint.

## Production check
On 2026-10-08 all 42 plans in AW-WorkPlans were checked read-only (projection of model + visibility). 24 pinned plans use only anthropic.claude-sonnet-5 (17), gemini-3.7-flash (5) and anthropic.claude-opus-5 (2), all registry entries with no adminOnly/internalOnly/isLive/legacy flag, so no existing plan is refused by the new launch check today; 18 plans have no pin. A stale-model dry-run immediately before deploy is still advisable because the old dry-run script flags only ids missing from the registry, not live/adminOnly/internal pins.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium — changes span launch, write, and scheduled-run paths, but rollback is limited to Work Plan model handling.

Work Plan launches reject unavailable pinned models before session setup and return 422; anonymous responses omit model details. Create and update routes validate pins while allowing unchanged values and blank values to clear them. Failed model saves return 503. Scheduled launches refuse unavailable pins and alert on-call. An empty pin uses the account default.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->


## Round 3 changes (review follow-ups)
- applyPredefinedWorkPlan: plan structure (sequential stepCount) validated BEFORE the model write; previous llmModel + llmUsagePolicyDecision captured and restored if the plan write throws (restore failure logged with session id; caller still gets the failure).
- createSessionWithPlan: structure validated before createChatSession (422 workplan_invalid, no session); new session deleted (logged on failure) if model or plan write fails. Refused model launches already create no session.
- Admin pin scope: only private + admin-owned + no orgId; org-scoped plans validated as non-admin (user and admin POST/PUT); admin PUT widening visibility re-validates the stored model as non-admin (422).
- Emma tool for anonymous sessions: anonymous-safe wording, no model id/name/reason.
- Portal surfacing: the 422 body carries both `error` and `message`; the customer-portal Work Plans settings editor reads `message` today and a companion portal PR makes it read `error` (wording true whichever merges first).
- Known unrelated failure: mcp.publicToolInventory (manage_crm_sequence unclassified) fails on origin/main too.


## Round: final-review fixes
- `createSessionWithPlan`: every write after `createChatSession` (model, plan, first input request, interactive-share metadata, default-model lookup) now sits in one try/catch that deletes exactly the session just created (best effort) and returns 503 `model_save_failed` (model write) or the generic 500. Previously only a plan-write failure cleaned up.
- Launch compensation race: the restore after a failed plan write is now `chatbotDb.restoreSessionLlmModelIfUnchanged`, a single UpdateItem with `ConditionExpression llmModel = :planModel`. A model the user PATCHed in the window is preserved (ConditionalCheckFailed logged at info). A session with no prior explicit model gets `REMOVE llmModel` (back to its exact prior state). Other restore failures still log CRITICAL. NOT a schema change: existing attributes, a conditional write only; no new field, table or index.
- User plan PUT: the adminOnly check uses the plan owner's admin status (`plan.ownerId`), as the admin PUT does; org-scope rule unchanged.
- Tests: failing-first tests for each later write, the race, the REMOVE case (exact expressions asserted in a chatbotService unit test), the owner-based matrix row, and the stepCount 422 body `{error, code:'workplan_invalid'}`.
- Verification: 113 suites / 2013 tests green, backend tsc clean; rebased onto current main.


## Round: canonical pin storage (CodeRabbit)
- `validateModelPin` (shared by work-plan user/admin POST/PUT and schedule create/update/template overrides, llmModel and llmBackupModel) now returns the CANONICAL registry id instead of the requested alias. Partial registry doubles still return the requested value. Blank clears, trim, non-string 422 and unchanged-stale tolerance (incoming equal to stored, or to the stored value's canonical form) unchanged; an unchanged stored alias is not rewritten. ## Review notes (added by hand; the bot rewrites the section above on its next run)

**Review of this PR's new model (`claude-haiku-5.5`)**: flags match the endpoint data, price matches OpenRouter's listing at all 10 endpoints, the Artificial Analysis score is the right slug, a live tool-bearing request routed via Bedrock in about 1 s, and it stays admin-only. **Not yet safe to open to customers:** OpenRouter bills 5x above 100k prompt tokens and the price book is flat (known gap, ENG-1774). It also needs a real description/tier, and `supportedReasoningEfforts` / `supportsVision` decided.

**This PR also upgrades the generator so the next PR needs less review:**
- display names lose the "Vendor: " prefix (this entry now reads "Claude Haiku 5.5")
- a much cheaper model is information, not a warning; a $0 quote still warns
- long-prompt and time-of-day price tiers are detected and warned about
- each new model's listed price is cross-checked against its endpoints
- a live smoke test per new model (needs repo secret `OPENROUTER_SMOKE_API_KEY`; without it the PR is not eligible)
- the PR body leads with an explicit auto-merge verdict and collapses the ~150 "AA unmatched" lines

Script changes take effect only once this PR is merged, since the workflow runs from `main`.


**Independent review of this PR (fresh-eyes subagent) and what was done about it:** the verdict now fails closed. A fake +60 score on an existing model, an Artificial Analysis outage, and an unknown report line each previously still said ELIGIBLE (reproduced) and now block. Existing-model score moves of more than 3 points or a changed Artificial Analysis slug block. A non-blocking capability-guard step feeds the verdict (it caught nothing today: 51 checks passed). The smoke step is `continue-on-error`, parallel and capped. Third-party text is flattened to one line, and the body is size-guarded under GitHub's limit. Left as is, on purpose: one-word display names such as "GPT-5.5" are the registry's own style; the smoke test cannot prove production BYOK routing (it says so); a verdict cannot be bound to a SHA the bot does not yet have.

title: fix(emma): document valid operators for quality_info.* GAQL fields (ENG-2354)
body:
Live-testing the ENG-2354 fix (ad_relevance field-name guess, PR #3360/#3371) in a fresh Emma session surfaced a second, separate issue: asked naturally for "Quality Score with ad relevance" on a test campaign, and Emma correctly picked the right field names this time (confirming #3371 works), but then tried `ad_group_criterion.quality_info.search_predicted_ctr IS NOT NULL` in a WHERE clause, which Google Ads rejects:

`IS NOT NULL is not a valid operator to use with 'ad_group_criterion.quality_info.search_predicted_ctr' in WHERE clause. Valid operators: =, !=, IN, NOT IN.`

She retried 7 times before self-correcting and landing on a correct final answer, so this didn't actually fail the user's request — but it's the same symptom (visible repeated failures) as the original bug, from a different cause.

Fix: one line added to the Quality Score GAQL guidance stating the valid operator set for `quality_info.*` fields, and that unpopulated scores should not be filtered with a null check.

No running code changed, same as #3360/#3371 — this only edits the tool description Emma reads.

title: ENG-273: WhatsApp approval notifications + STOP/UNSTOP acknowledgement
body:
Closes the two gaps left after WhatsApp landed, both found while verifying the channel live against Meta's sandbox on 2026-10-08.

## 1. Approval requests over WhatsApp

`agentweb_approval_request` had been in the template registry since the channel shipped but **had no caller** — `revisionService` and the three other approval paths all went straight to Slack. This was the last Slack-parity gap.

It is a **notification, not a second place to approve from**. WhatsApp has no Block Kit, and reply buttons need a pre-approved interactive template plus inbound button handling the registry deliberately lacks. The reviewer is told an approval is waiting and linked to the asset; approving still happens in Slack or the portal, so exactly one surface stays authoritative.

Hooked into `sendApprovalRequestWithTracking` rather than the four call sites — the one choke point every approval already passes through, so a new caller cannot forget it. Additive by construction: the Slack send and approval record complete first, and the notifier never throws.

## 2. STOP / UNSTOP were answered with silence

The webhook recorded an opt-out correctly and then said nothing. From the sender's side, a STOP that works and a STOP that was dropped look identical — the one thing a consent mechanism cannot afford to be ambiguous about. The code already anticipated it (`handleInboundMessage` carries the comment *"including a STOP, that is what makes the opt-out confirmation deliverable"*); the confirmation was never written.

`sendOptOutConfirmation` is a separate narrow export, not a `force`/`ignoreOptOut` flag — a bypass any caller can pass is one that eventually gets passed by accident. It takes no text and no template, so it cannot be repurposed to message someone who opted out, and it still honours the service window the inbound STOP just opened. The opt-out is recorded **before** the acknowledgement is attempted, and the attempt can never throw.

## Verification

Exercised end to end against Meta's sandbox from `api-stage.agentweb.pro`:

- Meta delivered inbound to the staging webhook; signature verified against the real app secret
- `Verify <CODE>` bound the number with `optIn.source: inbound_verification`
- Service-window row written with a TTL exactly 24h ahead, in epoch seconds
- Confirmation reply arrived on the handset
- `STOP` recorded the opt-out; `UNSTOP` cleared it and service resumed without re-verification

This also settled the open design risk: **Meta's test number does accept a first inbound message** from an allowlisted recipient, so the inbound-first verification flow needs no outbound priming.

## Docs

The contract's Live Verification section claimed the sandbox runbook was "how this was exercised". It had not been — until 2026-10-08 not one message had flowed. Corrected to what was actually observed. Also records that the business is now **verified as a Tech Provider**, which clears one of the two gates on multi-tenant Embedded Signup (App Review remains).

## Tests

306 passing across all WhatsApp/messaging suites. The existing Slack approval suites (`slack.agentModeRevision`, `slack.aiEvalReaction`) pass unmodified, confirming the approval change is inert for Slack.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium — The change adds WhatsApp notifications and consent handling. Both are additive: WhatsApp failures do not fail approval processing, and confirmation failures do not undo recorded consent.

After Slack sends an approval request and records it, the shared tracking path sends a WhatsApp notice only to a user whose linked Slack destinations include the approval channel. The notice links to the asset; approval remains in Slack or the portal. STOP is recorded before a fixed acknowledgement attempt. UNSTOP uses the standard send path.

title: feat(google-ads): device bid adjustments (ENG-2036)
body:
## What / why (ENG-2036)
xCures asked Emma to set device bid adjustments (e.g. -100% Mobile/Tablet for desktop-only B2B). `call_google_ads_api` had no device criterion support. Adds `CAMPAIGN_CRITERION` action `SET_DEVICE_BID_ADJUSTMENT`.

- Campaign scope: updates Google's auto-created DEVICE campaign criteria (`customers/<c>/campaignCriteria/<campaignId>~<30000|30001|30002|30004>`) `bid_modifier`, one atomic `campaignCriteria:mutate`.
- Ad-group scope: creates `adGroupBidModifiers` with `device.type`.
- `bid_modifier_percent` -100..900 → modifier `1 + pct/100` (-100 = 0 = exclude).
