title: ENG-2107 (B1): fix 5 concurrency/pipe-robustness bugs found by independent review
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #3374 (merged). After merge, I asked for a fresh, independent review of the diff — one that hadn't been part of building it — and it found 5 real defects, all verified against the actual merged code before acting on any of them. None affect production today (B1 still has zero callers — B4 hasn't wired anything to it), but all are real correctness gaps that would surface as soon as a real caller exists.

1. **TOCTOU race in `spawn()`/`prewarm()`.** Concurrent calls for the same `conversationId` could both pass the pool check before either claimed the slot, spawning two real `claude -p` processes for one conversation. `closeSessionInternal` also deleted its pool entry **by key**, not by object identity — the orphaned loser closing first could erase the live winner's entry. Fixed: concurrent spawns for the same `conversationId` now serialize onto one in-flight promise; `closeSessionInternal` now checks identity before deleting.
2. **`close()`/`closeAll()` couldn't touch a queued or mid-flight spawn.** A spawn still waiting behind the concurrency cap wasn't in the pool yet, so `close()` was a silent no-op on it — it would complete as an orphaned, unreachable process. `closeAll()`'s queue release only *schedules* the queued spawn's continuation as a microtask, so new processes could spawn asynchronously right after a caller believed shutdown had finished. Fixed with a `pendingCloseRequests` set that queued/mid-flight spawns check before (and immediately after) committing to a real process.
3. **Idle-close could kill an actively in-flight turn.** The timer was armed at the start of `send()` and never re-armed until the next call — a turn genuinely outliving `idleCloseMs` (the ticket's own stated concern: a real ~54k-token prefix under load) would be killed mid-turn and misreported as "idle". Fixed: the timer now checks for a pending turn before closing and reschedules instead of killing; it's also re-armed the moment a turn actually completes.
4. **`child.stderr` was never consumed.** With `--verbose` passed and a long-lived kept-open child, an OS pipe-buffer fill could stall the child's stdout flush entirely. Fixed: stderr is drained into a bounded tail, for diagnostics without the deadlock risk.
5. **`stdin.write()` had no error handling.** A synchronous throw rejected that turn correctly (the Promise constructor's own behavior), but never cleared `session.pending` — permanently wedging all future `send()` calls behind the "already in flight" guard. Fixed with an explicit try/catch, plus a `stdin` `'error'` listener for the async case (an unhandled `EventEmitter` `'error'` there would otherwise crash the whole backend process, not just this session).

## Evidence

- 7 new unit tests, one per fix (plus the identity-vs-key regression and the stderr-drain smoke test) — all 22 tests green, typecheck clean.
- Re-verified live against the real binary after the fix (`prewarm` → `send` → `close` round trip, isolated credentials, real `is_error`/`apiKeySource` fields) to confirm nothing regressed.
- Full review transcript and verification trail recorded in `eng-1816-brain/nodes/initiative-eng-1816.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `claudeCliRunner.test.ts` (22/22)
- [x] Live regression probe against the real binary post-fix
- [x] Synced with `main` before push, pre-push hook green

title: ENG-2361: GET /api/crm/leads cross-list pending_review leads
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The CRM Inbox could only filter by `pending_review` one list at a time. Users with drafts spread across several lists had no single place to review them.

## What this fixes (after)
New `GET /api/crm/leads?status=pending_review` returns pending-review leads from every list the caller can access (own lists plus org-shared lists, same enumeration as `GET /lists`, each re-checked with `canAccessCrmList`). Each lead carries `listId` and `listName`, and its `messageDraft` comes through unchanged. Results are sorted by `updatedAt` desc.

- `status` is required, and v1 accepts only `pending_review` (anything else → 400).
- Lists are fetched 5 at a time via the existing `fetchAllLeadsByStatusIndex`, with an overall cap of 500 leads. Response: `{ leads, total, truncated }`.
- Each lead's status is re-checked after the fetch, because that helper's fallback path returns the whole list when the status index fails.
- Registered as the exact path `/leads`, ahead of `/leads/:leadId/enrichment`, so the two can't collide.

This is the backend slice only. The portal quick filter and approve/reject UI (AC 3) are separate work.

## Complexity ledger
- Lines: about +65 route, +130 test. No new dependencies, tables, flags or indexes.
- Moving parts: one read-only route that reuses existing helpers (`getReadableOrgMemberIds`, `canAccessCrmList`, `fetchAllLeadsByStatusIndex`, `sanitizeLeadForResponse`).
- Behavior: existing routes are untouched, including the per-list `GET /lists/:listId/leads?status=`.

title: fix(meta): set campaign bid_strategy on CBO create so ad sets don't fail 1815857 (ENG-2364)
body:
## Reviewer first

Every.io (ENG-2364): Emma created a CBO "master" Meta campaign. Meta then rejected all 7 ad sets under it with `error_subcode 1815857` ("Bid amount required"), even though each ad set sent `bid_strategy: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP`. Under campaign budget optimization the bid strategy belongs to the campaign. `createCampaign` sent a CBO `daily_budget` without a campaign `bid_strategy`, so Meta's default demanded a `bid_amount`.

Prod evidence (web.stdout, 2026-10-08): campaign 120244709961670395 was created at 20:46:29 with `daily_budget: 25000` and no bid_strategy. 7× AD_SET CREATE were rejected 20:47:16–23 with 1815857. Emma then patched the campaign's bid_strategy at 20:47:51.

Fix: whenever `createCampaign` sets a campaign budget (on either the `daily_budget` path or the `advantage_campaign_budget + budget_amount` path), it also sends `bid_strategy: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP`. This is Meta's no-cap default, and the same value the ad-set layer already defaults to. ABO campaigns (no campaign budget) are unchanged.

Risk: low. The value is the documented default and only applies to newly created CBO campaigns. Existing campaigns are untouched. Bid-capped CBO (a campaign-level cap) was never supported on CREATE before this change and still isn't.
Rollback: revert. No data/persistence change.

## Evidence
- RED→GREEN: `eng2364.cboBidStrategy.test.ts` went from 2 failed / 1 passed to 3/3.
- Neighbouring suites (metaService.*, metaCampaignsCRUD, metaSpendCap, metaObjectiveGate, workflowEngine.metaCreateCampaign): 20 suites, 405 tests, all passing.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p backend`: clean.

Gmail: written into the raw RFC 2822 message (CR/LF stripped). **Outlook: not sent** — Graph `internetMessageHeaders` only accepts `x-` prefixed headers, so the field is ignored there (documented in `sendAsSender.ts`/`emailProviderService.ts`); the body link still works.
2. Same HMAC signature as the body link (test asserts identical `sig`). The header targets the backend route `POST /api/crm/public/lists/:listId/leads/:leadId/group-email-unsubscribe` because the body link is a frontend page that can't receive a one-click POST. The route now reads `email`/`sig` from the query string when the form-encoded body is just `List-Unsubscribe=One-Click` (global `express.urlencoded` already parses it). Forged sig → 403 (negative test).
3. One-off `send-email` unchanged; test asserts no `headers`.
4. New tests fail on main (4 failed with prod code reverted) and pass here.

## Evidence
jest: crm.groupEmail, crmPublic.unsubscribe, crm.routes, sendAsSender, resendService.* → 212/212.

## Risk / rollback
Security-adjacent (public unsubscribe route): authorisation unchanged — still HMAC-verified or legacy email-match; query params only fill fields the body omits. Rollback = revert commit. No schema/data change, no copy change. Header base URL = `BACKEND_URL` (default `https://api.agentweb.pro`).

## Complexity ledger
+2 small helpers, +1 optional param threaded through 3 send paths, +5 tests.

## How to test
Staging: send a group email to a test inbox via Resend/Gmail sender; inspect raw headers for `List-Unsubscribe`; `curl -X POST -d 'List-Unsubscribe=One-Click' '<header url>'` → 200, lead shows unsubscribed.

## Not tested
Full local `tsc` (OOMs on the box); CI typecheck is the proof. Live provider delivery.

title: fix(eval): tighten outcome-judge-b-shadow rubric calibration (ENG-2138)

## Summary
- ENG-2356's replay (2026-10-08) measured the reconstructed outcome-judge rubric at AUC 0.58 and 28.6% of scores at 5, against targets of >=0.75 and <15%. Of 77 scored sessions, 22 were labelled failures and none scored 1 or 2.

## Summary
Fixes found by testing #3263 in production.
- Regenerate-one failed ~1 in 3 (model omitted meta_targeting_brief): prompt now requires all five fields, plus one retry.
- Concurrent regenerates could erase each other's card (whole-list read-modify-write). Each card is now written to its own list slot via a new `elementSets` option on `userDb.updateUser`, conditioned on the card id; competitor entry and marketStrategy mirror follow the same rule.
- A full ICP run overlapping a regenerate had its result dropped or hidden; the regenerate now leaves the status to the full run.

- Review fixes: mirror failure no longer fails a saved card; a deleted card while joined no longer flips status; a joined card is retried, not dropped, if the claim it joined was another card's regeneration.

Same-card edit during its own regeneration is still overwritten; `edit-one`/`delete-one` still write whole lists from a lagging read.

title: ENG-903: refuse an explicit model on fixed-model session types
body:
## ENG-903: refuse an explicit model on fixed-model session types

`createSession` silently ignored a request `llmModel` for skill, emma-sidebar and every non-`regular` session type (report_generation, image-generation, video-generation, book-generation, scheduled, any other string). They now return HTTP 422 `model_not_selectable_for_session_type` ("This kind of session uses a fixed model and does not accept a model choice.") before the skill lookup, idempotency claim and any write. Absent/blank model and ordinary chat sessions are unchanged.

**Merge order: NO portal PR is needed.** Evidence the portal never sends `llmModel` at creation: ChatSupport (emma-sidebar), ResearchReports, Images, Videos, Books, CRM, VoiceOnboardingLab and useAgentModeSessions all POST without it (the chat model is applied via PATCH /session/:id/llm-model). The portal never calls `/skill/:id/session`. MCP `emma_create_session`/workflowTools send no `sessionType` (ordinary chat). Merge after portal PR: n/a (none exists); this PR is safe to merge on its own. Unknown external API clients that send `llmModel` with a non-regular type will now get the 422 (intended).

Not changed (reported): `runVerifiedChat` (~L4170-4195) overwrites the stored session model with the task-type model when `requiredFunctions` include update_html_file/read_file_content/create_blog_article/generate_image/generate_video and no `params.llmModel` is passed. Interactive /verified-generate passes none, so it keys on required functions, not session type, and can overwrite a model the user picked in the same chat.

Tests: failing first (7 failed), then failLoudSelectedModel 57/57; createSession* suites 86/86; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: ENG-55: Compare requests no-data-collection providers (switch, default off)
body:
## Summary
Compare models sends the prompt plus up to ~24k chars of history to several vendors via OpenRouter with no data policy. This adds `provider.data_collection = "deny"` for Compare calls only, behind AW-Settings `model_compare_deny_data_collection`. Existing `order` / `allow_fallbacks` / `require_parameters` / `ignore` are kept. No new persisted field, table or index.

## Behaviour
| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Setting absent / not exactly `true` | Request unchanged (no `providerPolicy` key, provider object identical) |
| Setting `true` (trim, case-insensitive) | Compare calls add `data_collection: "deny"` to the merged provider object |
| Normal chat / loops / coding agent | Never carry it (only Compare passes `providerPolicy`) |
| Settings read error | Last-known value; cold start = off. Cached 60s, retry after 5s on error |
| Policy on + OpenRouter "no endpoints" 404 | That column gets `provider_policy_unavailable`; other columns still answer |
| Policy off + same 404 | Unchanged `upstream_error` |

## Parameter sources verified
- https://openrouter.ai/docs/features/provider-routing: request-level `provider.data_collection` is `"allow" | "deny"`, default `"allow"`; unsatisfiable provider constraints fail with a 404. Sibling fields `order`, `allow_fallbacks`, `only`, `ignore`, `zdr` also listed.
- The repo has no reference for `data_collection` (registry guard covers `supported_parameters` only). NOT verified: the exact 404 wording for the data-policy case, and that every Compare model has a deny-compliant endpoint (no credentials). Classifier reuses ENG-2293 `isProviderNoEndpointsError`.

## Rollout
Merge with the switch absent (no behaviour change). Owner sets the AW-Settings row to `true` after a live Compare check. Portal shows the generic "This model could not answer this time." for the new code until a copy entry is added to `RESULT_ERROR_COPY` in CompareResultCard.tsx.

## Rollback
Set the row to `false` or delete it; effective within ~60s per instance. Or revert the PR.

## Verification
- New `compareProviderPolicy.test.ts` plus new cases in `modelComparison.test.ts` and `agentModeService.openRouterClient.test.ts`.
- Mutants: applying the policy to all calls fails 7 tests; dropping the policy-on guard in the classifier fails 2.
- Suites run: modelComparison, modelCompare.routes, modelCompare.entitlement.routes, openRouterClient, openRouterRequestParams (+registryGuard), sdkConstructionGuard: 399/400 pass. The 1 failure (sdkConstructionGuard stale allowlist entry `services/videoGeneration.ts`) fails identically on origin/main.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Low — the change is opt-in, limited to Compare requests, and can be rolled back by disabling or removing the setting.

When `model_compare_deny_data_collection` is exactly `true` after trimming and case normalization, Compare requests to OpenRouter set `provider.data_collection` to `"deny"`. A matching no-endpoints 404 maps to `provider_policy_unavailable`. Other request types remain unchanged. Provider availability and exact 404 wording were not verified. Reported checks: targeted suites had 399/400 passing; `tsc --noEmit` was clean. The failing guard reportedly also fails on `origin/main`.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->


## Review round 2 (head 4c82de9ad)
- `provider_policy_unavailable` is now conservative: only when the policy is ON, the model is a registry id, and the error is the generic no-endpoints 404 whose text does not mention "parameter" and is not "No endpoints found for <slug>". The require_parameters 404 and unknown/retired-model 404 stay `upstream_error`. No data-policy keyword is used (no OpenRouter docs sentence to cite for the 404 wording).
- Setting parse is exactly the string `true` (no trim/lowercase).
- Cache refresh is single-flight (4 parallel columns => 1 settings read); unused message constant removed.
- New controller-wiring tests (modelCompare.routes): row 'true' => callLLM gets providerPolicy deny; absent/'false' => absent. Mutant (delete `getProviderPolicy` line) fails it.
- Portal copy should not assert a cause; suggested: "No provider for this model was available with the current privacy setting. Try again later or pick another model."

## What

First of two PRs for ENG-2109 (the tool bridge that lets a `claude -p` session reach Emma's tools). This one is the harness-agnostic core, with no caller and no route.

- `funding/runToolToken.ts`: per-run opaque token (32 random bytes, stored only as a SHA-256 hash), idle-based expiry, bound to a run id, revoked when the run closes.
- `funding/toolBridge.ts`: `openRun` / `closeRun` / `listTools` / `callTool`. What a tool is, how it runs and what counts as read-only are injected.

Under `claude -p` the CLI owns the agent loop, so three controls Emma's loop enforces around tool dispatch live here instead:

- The model gets exactly the run's filtered tool list, and each call is checked against that list again at execution time.
- A result that asks for the user's confirmation locks the session. No tool runs until a new user turn clears it. Several tools hand the model the token that confirms their own preview and rely on the loop ending the turn; without this lock the model could preview and confirm in one turn.
- Tools not known to be read-only run one at a time per run, in arrival order.

## Risk

None in production: nothing imports these files yet. The second PR (stacked on this branch) wires them in.

## Tests

47 unit tests. 18 mutations of the guards were each caught by a test. An independent review round found six issues (lock cleared on reopen, stale tool list trusted, a hung call wedging the queue, fixed-clock token expiry, raw error text returned, test gaps); all fixed here.

## Rollback

Revert the PR. No data, schema or config change.

title: ENG-2109 (B2): tool bridge wiring — Emma dispatcher, internal MCP route, runner
body:
## What

Second of two PRs for ENG-2109, stacked on the core PR. Connects the bridge to Emma's real tool dispatcher and to the `claude -p` runner. Merge the core PR first; this one then retargets to `main`.

- **Executor** (`funding/emmaToolBridgeExecutor.ts`): runs each bridge call through `executePreparedTools`, so policy, argument repair, the gateway, budgets and telemetry are Emma's own code. Tool list comes from a new `agentModeService.resolveRunToolAccess`, which calls the same helpers the loop calls.
- **Internal MCP route** (`/internal/tool-bridge/:runId/mcp`): streamable HTTP. Two guards: direct loopback connections only (no forwarding header), and the run token bound to the run id in the URL on every request. A request that fails either is passed on untouched and gets the app's normal response for a path with no route.
- **Runner** (`funding/claudeCliRunner.ts`): takes the bridge as its one MCP server. The token goes in a 0600 config file, never on the command line. If the CLI does not report the server connected, the turn is rejected and the session closed; otherwise the CLI carries on with zero tools and reports success.
- **Same-message duplicates**: an identical call repeated in one model message runs once, as in Emma's dispatcher. The runner reports each tool call's message id from the CLI's event stream.
- **Same-turn new tools**: after a skill install, the install call's answer waits (max 2 s) for the CLI to re-read its tool list, so the new tool is usable in the same turn.
- **Lock after restart** (`funding/sessionHaltState.ts`): read from the session's own last assistant message. No new storage.

Two fixes to already-merged B1 runner code, each its own commit: a failed process start left an unhandled promise rejection; a killed CLI re-created its scratch folder, leaving one empty folder in `/tmp` per closed session.

## What changes in production

- One edit on the live chat path: Emma's loop now gets its dispatch ports from `buildToolDispatchPorts` instead of an inline object. Same functions, same values.
- A new route is mounted. Nothing opens a bridge run until ENG-2113, so no token can exist and every request falls through to the normal 404.

## Evidence

- 163 tests in `funding/`; 4,569 tests across funding, tool dispatch, the agent service, approval decks and CRM freshness pass on the rebased head.
- Integration test against the real `agentModeService` and dispatcher: the bridge offers exactly the tools the loop sends the model (legacy and skill-gated sessions); a real confirmation preview locks the session and the model's own confirm is refused.
- Mutation checks on the route guards, adapter, executor and duplicate logic: every mutation caught.
- Independent review: no critical or high findings, no self-approval or cross-run path. Its findings are fixed in this PR.
- Live, real `claude -p` 2.1.294, locally and inside the test environment's backend container, with test tools behind the real runner, route and bridge: parallel reads start within 5 ms; an identical write twice in one message runs once; a tool installed mid-turn is usable in that turn; the model's attempt to confirm its own preview is refused and the session stays locked; a forged token stops the turn and leaves no process.
- Test environment: a normal Emma chat ran two tools and answered normally; the route is byte-identical to a missing path from outside and from inside the container.

## Known limits

- No single run yet has the real CLI and Emma's real tools together; that needs the caller from ENG-2113.
- The forwarding-header half of the local-only guard relies on nginx adding `X-Forwarded-For`, which is the platform default and is not pinned in this repo. The test environment has no nginx in front, so only the loopback half ran there. The token check stands behind it either way.
- Posting the approval deck, the step budget, cancellation, the loop breaker, the citation registry and the CRM freshness observer stay with the loop's caller (ENG-2113).
- A legacy session that installs a skill becomes skill-gated one turn earlier than in the loop.

## Rollback

Revert the PR. No data, schema or config change.

title: fix(eval): serializeMessagesForScoring crashes on content: undefined

## Summary
- `JSON.stringify(undefined)` returns the JS value `undefined`, not the string `"undefined"` -- so `typeof m.content === "string" ? m.content : JSON.stringify(m.content)` silently evaluated to `undefined` for a message with `content: undefined`, and the chained `.trim()`/`.length` then threw `TypeError`.

title: fix(compare): qwen3.8-max renamed upstream, alias to -0902 (ENG-55)
body:
## Summary
Compare column `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.8-max` returned `model_mismatch`. OpenRouter's public catalog no longer lists `qwen/qwen3.8-max` (only `qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902`, canonical `qwen/qwen3.8-max-20260902`, and `-prime`), but still routes the old id as an alias. Our registry kept the stale id, so the strict served-model check (a base id must not accept a registered sibling's MMDD snapshot) refused the response. The refusal was correct for a stale id; the registry was wrong.

**Fix (option a):** registry + pricing key renamed to `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902` (same $2/$6), old id added to `LEGACY_MODEL_ALIASES`. `isSameServedModel` is untouched.

## Audit (public catalog 2026-10-09, 44 non-live/non-internal/priced OpenRouter registry ids; script kept outside the repo)
| result | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| ok (id listed, canonical slug accepted) | 43 | 44 |
| stale (not in catalog) | 1: `qwen/qwen3.8-max` | 0 |
| false rejects | 0 | 0 |
| false accepts | 3 | 2 |

False accepts before: `gpt-4o-mini` accepting `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18` (benign: OpenRouter lists it as the same snapshot, equal canonical slug), `deepseek-v4-flash` accepting `-0731`, `qwen3.8-max` accepting `-0902`. The last disappears with this change. `deepseek-v4-flash` vs `-0731` only occurs while `-0731` is unregistered (it is rejected once the catalog refresh adds it; sibling protection depends on the registry knowing siblings). Modelled with and without `discoverNewModels` additions (the static registry is the runtime registry here; refresh writes additions into the source). Only the qwen row changes between before/after.

## Decision and alternatives rejected
- (a) alias + rename: keeps existing pins working on the same model and keeps the strict identity guarantee.
- (b) teach identity about provider aliasing: rejected, weakens "the selected model is the only one used"; the alias target can change under us.
- (c) retire with migration: rejected, pins to this still-registered id (not flagged by the earlier stale-id dry-run) would fail loudly.
Risk accepted: none for pins; the alias is read-time only, no data migration, no new persisted field.

## Why the guard missed it
`openRouterRequestParams.registryGuard` snapshots `/models/{id}/endpoints`, which follows aliases, and only checked parameters. The snapshot already recorded `qwen/qwen3.8-max -> resolvedId qwen/qwen3.8-max-0902`. New guard test: a registry id must resolve to itself in the snapshot (fails on main for exactly this id). Snapshot key renamed (same endpoints).

## Behaviour
Before: Compare column errors `model_mismatch`. After: ok; a different served model (e.g. `-prime-20260923`, other date, bare alias) is still `model_mismatch`. Old pins resolve to `-0902` without fallback.

## Portal follow-up
Add `'openrouter/qwen/qwen3.8-max'` to `LEGACY_MODEL_ALIAS_IDS` in `src/lib/modelUnavailable.ts` (hand-copied mirror), else saved chats show "Unavailable".

## Verification
New tests failed first (3/4 in `modelCompare.renamedModel`, 1 guard test). Now 14 suites / 772 tests pass (modelComparison, modelCompare.routes, entitlement.routes, compareProviderPolicy, openRouterRequestParams*, alias/registry, llmModelValidation, migrateStaleModelReferences, modelCatalogRefresh) plus pricing 48; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Compare now uses the `qwen3.8-max-0902` snapshot for registry and pricing entries. The old model ID resolves through a legacy alias. The registry guard rejects IDs that resolve to a different ID in the endpoints snapshot. The change affects model selection and pricing for this model.

title: fix(agent-mode): provider 5xx is not an unknown error (ENG-2381)
body:
## Summary
Oncall ENG-2381: a final `503 Provider returned error` from OpenRouter (after its in-request provider failover and callLLM's transient retry) fell through agentModeService's catch to the generic "I encountered an error" message, so the controller paged oncall as **Agent Mode: Unknown Error in Generate Response**.

## Change
- `agentModeService.generateMarketingResponse` catch: a 5xx status (or `upstream_5xx` class) now wraps with `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE_USER_MESSAGE`.
- `agentModeErrors`: `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE_USER_MESSAGE` + `isProviderUnavailableError`.
- `agentModeController`: at all three error handlers (generate, shared generate, third site), answer `503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE / wait_and_retry` before the unknown-error oncall branch. Genuinely unknown errors still alert.

## Risk / rollback
Error-path classification only; no retry/model behaviour change, no data-plane. Rollback = revert.

## Tests
- Controller: provider-unavailable -> 503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE and no Unknown-error oncall alert (new).
- Helper positive/negative cases (new).
- Related suites: 7 suites / 191 tests green locally; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Not tested
`agentModeService.contentFilter.simple.test.ts` harness throws a TypeError before reaching callLLM (pre-existing: its 429 case passes only via the generic fallback), so the service-side 5xx branch is not unit-exercised there.

## How to test

## Complexity ledger
+1 branch in service catch, +1 helper, +3 controller guards (same shape as the existing high-demand branch).

title: fix(agent-mode): hold state-changing calls after media-budget deferral (ENG-922)
body:
## What / why (ENG-922)

When the per-run media time budget defers an image, a state-changing call in the same turn (e.g. `call_meta_marketing_api` uploading to `/adimages`) could still run against the incomplete set. That is how a partial batch leaves orphaned images or creatives on an ad account. This change holds those calls back. It replaces closed #2294 (stale and conflicted) with a fresh branch from main that changes **no user-visible strings**, per the 2026-10-11 re-scoped acceptance criteria.

- `toolDispatch.ts`
  - Mixed media and non-media batches now run media first and other calls after, and results stay in emission order.
  - After a deferral (in this iteration, or carried over from an earlier iteration via the new `priorMediaBudgetDeferred` input), state-changing non-media calls are deferred instead of executed. They still get tool_call_id answers; this uses the existing `deferred` result path.
  - Read-only calls (policy `effect === 'read'`) still run. If a call's effect can't be classified, it is deferred.
  - Covered on all three dispatch paths: sequential, bounded batch, and parallel.
- `agentModeService.ts`: a new sticky `mediaBudgetDeferredThisRun` flag is passed into each later iteration.

## Acceptance criteria mapping
1. 3 completed + 1 deferred image -> zero Graph writes after the deferral. Tested in the same iteration and in a later iteration.
2. Zero-image timeout: no copy change. The existing on-main timeout and continuation path is untouched.
3. A normal 4-image + Graph batch under budget still runs everything (test added). The existing ENG-510 characterization tests still pass.
4. Fresh branch from main. No DB or data-plane change.

## Evidence (head ad70cf747)
- RED: 3 of the new ENG-922 tests fail against unpatched main.
- GREEN: `toolDispatch.test.ts` 133/133. `src/services/agentMode` + timeoutContinuation + agentModeService: 228 suites / 4986 tests.
- Pre-push hook: 187 suites / 4071 tests.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Complexity ledger
+1 input field and +1 local predicate. The bounded batch path is restructured into a media pass followed by an other-calls pass. Nothing is removed.

## Risk / rollback
This is an AgentMode-path change. A Graph write that the model chains in the same turn as a deferred media batch now waits for the continuation turn. Rollback: revert this one commit.

## How to test (staging)
1. Set `AGENT_MODE_MEDIA_BUDGET_MS` low on staging (e.g. 1000) and ask Emma for 4 ad image variants uploaded to a test Meta account.
2. Expect: at least 1 image delivered, the rest deferred, and no `/adimages` POST for the incomplete set until continuation.

## Scope / not done

- No live Google Ads call. All fixtures are mocked. Not checked in staging.
- One unverified assumption: `campaign.bidding_strategy_type` echoes the enum we send (MAXIMIZE_CONVERSIONS, TARGET_SPEND, …). TARGET_SPEND is reported as TARGET_SPEND in GAQL, which matches.

## Tests

title: ENG-273: WhatsApp interactive approvals, support hand-off, and one platform per customer
body:
Makes WhatsApp a complete, independent channel. Slack and WhatsApp are separate features: a customer connects one of them, and neither depends on the other.

## What changes for a customer on WhatsApp

- **Approvals with real buttons.** Inside the 24-hour window they get Approve / Reject reply buttons (a service message, so no Meta template is needed). Outside it, the existing template with a link.
- **A WhatsApp-only customer can be asked to approve approvals the agent engine creates.** Three Slack assumptions used to prevent it: the engine only asked when the task had a Slack channel, `POST /api/slack/send-approval` rejected a request without one, and the approval was posted to Slack first and aborted if that failed.
- **Approving emails the task's subscribers**, exactly as a Slack approval does.
- **Writing in gets an answer.** A non-command message gets a fixed greeting (once per 12h) and is forwarded to the team by email, with a media message's caption, filename and media id. No model is involved.

## One platform per customer

`customerChannelPolicy` is the single definition of which platform an account is on. Enforcement and every screen read it.

- A second platform is refused at every entry point: starting or completing WhatsApp verification for an account with its own Slack channel; an admin assigning a Slack channel, the `link this channel` command, and Slack Connect provisioning for an account on WhatsApp.
- **An account with a verified WhatsApp number is on WhatsApp everywhere.** `resolveDestination` returns no Slack destination for it (own channel or inherited), and Emma's Slack allow-list and the legacy lead alert, which bypassed the resolver, follow the same rule. This settles every way the two can come to coexist in one place.
- An organisation's shared channel is a default the account inherited, so it does not block a member connecting WhatsApp. A Slack Connect support room is not a delivery destination, so it is not a platform.
- One number belongs to one account.
- The admin dashboard shows each customer's platform (WhatsApp number masked to four digits), and can disconnect WhatsApp on a customer's behalf.

## Design points worth a reviewer's attention

- **Button taps are one atomic conditional write** (`approvalDb.answerIfOpen`, `attribute_exists AND status IN (pending, needs_changes)`). WhatsApp can never remove a button, so every tap arrives as a fresh message, possibly from someone who already answered elsewhere. Exactly one wins; only the winner emails subscribers. An earlier claim-row design guarded WhatsApp taps only and was replaced.
- **A failed send to a reachable customer is a different answer from "no channel".** `409 no_channel` means nobody to ask; `502 delivery_failed` means they can be reached and were not. The engine holds output for the second, as it does when a Slack send fails, and also fails closed if the account cannot be read.
- **A caller may only approve what is theirs.** `assetUrl` is the approvals primary key and the record is written with a put, so the check blocks replacing (or, on a failed send, deleting) another account's approval, or pointing at another account's execution. Enforced on the new route for everyone and for any WhatsApp customer through `requestApproval`.
- **Meta returns a template quick-reply's LABEL as its payload**, so a tap is correlated only through `context.id` against the outbound message id stored at send time.
- **Shared Slack code is touched in two places**, both behaviour-preserving for Slack: the subscriber email fan-out moved out of the `approve_asset` handler into `approvalSubscriberNotify`, and `sendApprovalRequestWithTracking` is a thin delegate to `approvalRequestService`. `send_task_approval_request` in the engine is byte-identical to `main`.

## Verification

Two independent review passes and three CodeRabbit rounds found real problems (listed in the commit messages); each was verified against the code before fixing.

- Latest push (2026-10-13): the related set of 1,652 suites has 1,648 passing; the 4 failing (`admin.announcements`, `mcp.publicToolInventory`, `crm.groupEmail`, `tracking.sessionLists`) fail identically on a clean `origin/main` in the same environment, which is why this branch was pushed with the pre-push hook's documented `--no-verify`. CI is the backstop. Earlier: 162 suites / 2,447 tests on the affected set. Typecheck: 0 errors across the backend. Engine tests: 21 pass. Dashboard: `tsc -b` and `vite build` pass; lint count for the file is unchanged from main.
- **Three suites that failed on `main` independently of this work are fixed in their own commit** (`admin.gtmPlans`, `admin.crmAnalytics`, `slackLeadNotificationCompact`): a table prefix read once at import while the tests change `NODE_ENV`, and a test that asserted two calls in the same millisecond on a payload that embeds a timestamp.
- **Full backend run:** the only failures in this branch that were not already failing on `main` were one suite whose mock lacked the new export (fixed) and two that depend on my local `.env`'s `BACKEND_URL` (they pass with it unset). The remaining 8 fail identically on a clean `origin/main` (6 `agentModeController.*`, `mcp.publicToolInventory`, `sdkConstructionGuard`).
- Live on staging against Meta's sandbox from a real handset: approval delivered by WhatsApp alone, Approve recorded against the right account, the other button refused afterwards with the recorded verdict, greeting delivered, one-platform refusal on the connect endpoint, platform shown in the admin list with no full number.

Tests replaced because their premise was removed on purpose, not to make anything pass: `leadListAlertService.whatsapp` ("independently when both configured") and four `shipNotifyService.whatsapp` "peers" tests asserted the double delivery the rule forbids.

## Added in the 2026-10-13 round (all gaps found by a fresh audit)

- **A failed re-request no longer erases an earlier verdict.** The pending record is written ahead of the WhatsApp send, replacing any record for the asset; the cleanup used to delete it. It now restores the earlier record, conditionally (only over the record this request wrote). A failed read of the earlier record aborts instead of falling back to delete.
- **`/api/approval-requests` answers 502 `delivery_failed` for a failed Slack send** (it was a generic 500 against the documented contract). The legacy Slack route keeps the raw error.
- **Approvals outside the 24-hour window can now be answered.** A second template, `agentweb_approval_request_buttons`, carries Approve / Reject quick replies. Until Meta approves it the notifier falls back (error 132001) to the link-only template. **The template still has to be created and approved in the WABA that owns the sending number.**
- **ENG-2413 interaction (found while merging main):** the new Slack entitlement check on `/api/slack/send-approval` would 403 a WhatsApp customer whose task still names an old Slack channel (they are entitled to none), so they would never be asked and their output would be held. Such customers are exempted, and the route hands `requestApproval` no channel for them so a disagreeing second read fails closed instead of posting to the caller's channel.
- **A refused verification no longer looks like "waiting".** `other_platform` / `number_in_use` set the row to `refused` with a reason; the status endpoint returns it; the code stays retryable.
- **Failed delivery receipts are logged** (message id suffix and Meta error code, never the number). **Opt-out** also matches `Stop.`, `please stop`, `stop all`. Dashboard shows "Unknown" when the platform lookup failed rather than "Not connected". Stale comments corrected.

## Not done / needs action

- **Customer-facing wording needs review before this ships:** the greeting, the STOP/UNSTOP and disconnect messages, the approval texts, and the portal consent text (companion PR).
- **Create and get approval for the button template** (and the other three templates) in the production WABA; there is no production number yet (ENG-891).
- **Query forwarding by email was not seen end to end.** Staging's `nonProdEmailGuard` suppresses all mail because `NONPROD_EMAIL_ALLOWLIST` is unset on `Agentweb-backend-env-1`.
- **The agent-engine change is deployed by hand** (GCP VM, `agent-engine/deploy/RUNBOOK.md`); CI does not deploy it. An engine that runs ahead of the backend gets a 404 and treats it as no channel.
- **An approval that cannot be delivered, or goes to a customer who has opted out, holds the task output** and nothing retries it. It is logged at error level (`could not deliver an approval to user …`) for an alarm.
- Accepted and documented in the contract: Slack, the portal and batch review still write approval status unconditionally, so a later answer there can overwrite a WhatsApp verdict; the legacy `/api/slack/send-approval` has the same ownership exposure for Slack customers; a failed support forward is logged, not retried (failing the webhook on a mail error makes Meta redeliver for up to 7 days).

Companion PR for the customer portal: `AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1243` (now also: WhatsApp approvals from Images / Videos / Research Reports, the task "Require approval" toggle, refused-verification messaging).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: High

WhatsApp is now an independent customer channel for agent-engine approvals, support hand-off, and platform enforcement. Approval taps use atomic updates so only one response wins. **Production risk:** failed WhatsApp delivery or an opted-out recipient holds task output without retry; failed support-email forwarding is logged without retry.

The admin dashboard shows the platform and masked WhatsApp number, and supports disconnection. Portal-started approvals remain Slack-only. Production WABA template approval and customer-facing wording remain outstanding. The author reports 1,648 of 1,652 related suites passed, plus successful typechecks and builds; the reported failures reproduce on clean `origin/main`. Staging email forwarding was not verified.

body:
## What
Follow-up to #3408. That PR stops `serializeMessagesForScoring` crashing on `content: undefined`, but does it with `JSON.stringify(m.content ?? "")`. `JSON.stringify("")` is the two-character string `""`, which is truthy, so:

- a tool-calls-only assistant turn renders as `assistant: ""` followed by `[called tools: x]`, instead of `assistant: [called tools: x]` (what `content: ""` already renders as);
- a genuinely empty assistant turn is no longer skipped, contrary to the existing comment;
- user and tool messages render `user: ""` / `tool result (name): ""`.

That changes the judge's input on the most common turn shape, and we calibrate judges against exact transcripts. #3408's tests only assert `not.toContain('undefined')`, so they pass with the artifact.

## Fix
One `textOf()` helper (null/undefined become empty text, strings pass through, other values are JSON-stringified) used by the user, assistant and tool branches.

## Verification
- `sessionScoring.undefinedContent.test.ts` (9 cases) pins the exact rendered lines, that no literal `""` or `undefined` reaches the prompt, that content blocks and objects are stringified exactly as before, and that an undefined-content assistant turn renders identically to `content: ""`. Against the current main code 7 of 9 fail (the 2 that pass are the "worked before" cases); against this change all 9 pass. #3408's own 3 tests also pass.
- Independent read-only review (separate reviewer, not the author) compared old vs new output for `""`, whitespace, strings, content-block arrays, objects, numbers, booleans and NaN: identical for everything except null/undefined.
- Read-only replay of the deterministic sample that exposed the original crash (window 2026-07-10..10-07, seed `eng-2138`, 40 sessions, real production messages, mocked model reply): 22 judged OK, 0 TypeErrors. Before any fix: 6 TypeErrors in 16.
- Pre-push hook (tsc plus related suites) passed. CodeRabbit was rate-limited (3 included reviews per hour), so the independent review above stands in for it.

## Deliberately not changed: other `?? ""` sites with the same quirk
These predate #3408 and use `JSON.stringify(x ?? "")`, so undefined content becomes the truthy `""`:

| Site | Effect |
|---|---|
| `hasAssistantTurn` (~L907) | an empty assistant message counts as a real turn; feeds failed-run classification |
| `isNoTaskSession` (~L832) | user text becomes `""` rather than empty |
| `lastAssistantText` (~L1194) | last assistant text is `""` (truthy) rather than empty |
| `transcriptEndsMidToolLoop` (~L1310) | a tool-calls-only last turn is NOT treated as mid-loop, although the comment says it should be |
| `describeToolOutcome` (~L93) | harmless: `JSON.parse('""')` yields no outcome either way |

Switching them to `textOf` is the consistent fix, but it changes in-flight and failed-run classification for production sessions, so it should land separately with the number of affected sessions measured first. Follow-up ticket filed.

Risk: low. Scoring input only, no schema or write-path change.

title: fix(domains): authorize page-subdomain before Vercel side effect (ENG-2412)
body:
## What / why
`POST /api/domains/page-subdomain` called `setPageSubdomain` (Vercel POST with AgentWeb's team token) using a body-supplied `vercelProjectId` + `mainDomain` before it checked whether the caller owned the landing page. Any authenticated user could attach a hostname to another customer's Vercel project. ENG-2412.

## Change (backend/src/routes/domains.ts)
Every authorization check now runs before any Vercel call:
1. Load the page by `landingPageId`; 404 unless `page.userId === caller` (this check already existed but ran after the Vercel call; now it runs first).
2. 403 when `page.vercelProjectId !== body.vercelProjectId`.
3. 403 unless `mainDomain` (case-insensitive) is in the caller's `listDomains(userId, vercelProjectId)` records.
The owner's happy path is unchanged.

## Tests
`routes.domains.test.ts`: 45/45 pass. New negative tests cover a foreign page, a mismatched project and an unowned mainDomain; each asserts no `setPageSubdomain` call and no middleware/DB write. One positive test covers a case-insensitive owner match. `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

## Risk / rollback
Risk: an owner whose `mainDomain` has no custom-domain record on this project now gets a 403. That is intended (AC3). The portal only offers a mainDomain it read from the project's own domains. Rollback: revert this commit. No database or data-plane change.

## Complexity ledger
+1 guard block in one handler, no new helpers.

## Not tested
Live staging call against a real Vercel project.

title: test: fix stale agentModeErrors mocks breaking lock/cap release tests
body:
## Summary
On origin/main 12 tests in 6 suites failed with `TypeError: isProviderUnavailableError is not a function` (controller error handler, agentModeController.ts ~L10606, added by ENG-2381). Their `jest.mock('../utils/agentModeErrors', ...)` factories hand-listed exports and omitted it, so the handler threw instead of responding.

Test-only. In all 17 controller test files whose factory was a hand-listed object, prepend `...jest.requireActual('../utils/agentModeErrors')` so future exports never break these mocks. The existing overrides remain.

title: UI Bug: Luma agent usage is not successful. could the session login be handled more auto
body:
## Summary
ENG-2338: Luma's "Verifying Your Browser" gate cannot be passed from our automation browser, so a browser login to Luma is unreliable. This adds a **Luma calendar API key** connector: a user with a Luma Plus key connects it once and the agent reads events and guest lists through Luma's public API, with no login at all. **Users without a key see no change** — the browser/session-cookie path stays as the fallback.

**Root cause (verified).** Prod session `bf7f3c5f` was a first-ever Luma login (the user's cookie jar held only anonymous Luma cookies, no `luma.auth-session-key`). I reproduced the gate from our server with the production launch args + stealth script across headless/headed × spoofed/native UA: all 4 variants show the gate after "Continue with Email" and none reach the code step in 90s. So it is not the headless flag, the UA or the stealth script; the likely cause is datacenter-IP reputation (untested). Related history: ENG-475 / 505 / 507 / 1022 / 1953.

## What changed
- **Connector.** `platform: 'luma'` connected account; `POST /api/oauth/luma/connect` validates the key against Luma, then stores it. Tools `luma_list_events` / `luma_get_guests` (`public-api.luma.com`, header `x-luma-api-key`, 200 req/min per calendar).
- **Agent behaviour.** Prompt tells the agent to try the API tools before a browser and offers connecting a key as the durable fix. Also: bot-gate handoff now uses the right tab name ("Session Cookies"), requires a final snapshot before declaring the gate stuck, and gives the cookie how-to inline.
- **Status.** A key Luma rejects (401) sets `needs_reconnect` and shows as "Reconnect required"; a 403 on one event does not kill the key.
- **Tier lists.** `luma` added to the all-platforms list and the partner-portal tier editor. Portal side never tier-gates the card (see portal PR) because tiers saved earlier carry explicit lists that cannot contain it.
- **Test-only override** `LUMA_API_BASE_URL`, ignored when `NODE_ENV=production`, so a preview can exercise the connector against a fake Luma.

## Key storage — please read
The key is encrypted with `encryptPassword(key, userId)` (AES-256-GCM, key derived from `JWT_SECRET`) in `config.access_token` of the user's connected account — the **same scheme as Foreplay and login credentials**. It is never returned by any endpoint (the accounts list returns fixed fields; `/connect` runs `redactAccountSecrets`), never logged, and never reaches the model. **It is not KMS envelope encryption** (that does not exist in the repo yet — `AW-LlmConnections` is not provisioned and `llmConnection.ts` is types only). KMS was considered and declined for this PR; a later migration can swap the single encrypt/decrypt pair. No new table and no migration.

## Verification
- Backend typecheck clean; 50 suites / 555 tests pass (Luma, key storage with the **real** crypto, accounts list, prompt, tier lists, cursor guard). Partner portal: type check 0 errors, build OK, tier-editor tests pass (incl. a new one on the real component).
- **Independent fresh-eyes review ×2** (subagent, full context). Findings verified against code; real ones fixed, others noted below.
- **Live in the branch preview** (real backend + browser + real agent) against a **fake Luma that follows Luma's OpenAPI**: bad key → 422 and not saved; good key saved with no key in any response; the agent listed events and pulled guests with a date cutoff (exactly the expected 25); a 230-guest read took 4 calls through a 429 and finished with all 230; connect, list and disconnect were exercised through the real routes. Real Luma accepts our header and returns JSON 401 for a bad key on both endpoints.
- Live testing found what unit tests could not: the card was hidden by the tier allow-list, a 429 was worded so the dispatcher said "do NOT retry", and a cursor guard printed "0 row(s)" for this tool. The review found that a default guest page (~27k chars) exceeded the 20k the model is shown and cut off the paging fields; paging fields now come first and calls are capped.

## NOT verified
- **A successful authenticated call to real Luma** — nobody has a Luma Plus key. Field names and paging are taken from Luma's published OpenAPI. Please connect a real key once after deploy and pull a guest list.
- Whether Luma answers 403 for another calendar's event (fix is defensive).
- Not done: the published "Luma Event Lead Engagement" skill row (prod data, Harsha) still describes the browser path; `report_product_issues` on the bot-gate handoff.

## Merge order
Merge **this PR first**, then the portal PR (https://github.com/AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal/pull/1247) — its Luma card calls `POST /api/oauth/luma/connect`. Merging deploys to production automatically.

* **Improvements**
  * Luma connections that need attention are marked disconnected, with guidance to reconnect.
  * Session-cookie instructions now point to **Settings > Session Cookies** and include updated steps for login and bot-protection challenges.

title: ENG-112: branch family link and GET /session/:id/branches
body:
## Summary
ENG-112 gap: a branch was only linked back via `metadata.branchOrigin` on its first message row, so a source chat could not list its branches and the sidebar could not group them. This adds a session-level family link and a listing endpoint.

## Contract (portal is built against this)
1. New optional session attribute `branchedFrom: { sessionId, rootSessionId, messageIndex, branchedAt }`. `sessionId` = immediate source; `rootSessionId` = `source.branchedFrom?.rootSessionId ?? source.sessionId` (branch of a branch stays in one family); `messageIndex` = raw fork index sent to the branch endpoint; `branchedAt` = ISO. Added to `ChatSession`, allowed in `createChatSession`'s `initialState` Pick (like `archived`), written by `chatBranching`'s createSession call (so the born-archived branch already carries it). Never copied from the source: a new branch computes its own.
2. `GET /api/agent-mode/sessions` and `GET /api/agent-mode/session/:id` pass it through for the owner. Not exposed by the share (`getSharedConversation`), conversable (`getConversableSession`) / ishare serializers (they pick fields by name; tests pin it) nor by MCP (`emma_get_session`, `emma_list_sessions` strip it via `omitBranchedFrom`).
3. `GET /api/agent-mode/session/:sessionId/branches` (authenticateToken, owner only, same `chat_branching_enabled` flag, 404 `chat_branching_disabled` when off). Returns `{ rootSessionId, sessions: [{ sessionId, title, llmModel, messageCount, updatedAt, createdAt, branchedFrom? }], truncated? }`: the root plus every non-archived session of the same owner with that root, createdAt ascending, max 50. One paginated, projected `UserIdIndex` query walk (no scan, no GSI), at most 20 pages, newest-first (`ScanIndexForward=false`, so a capped walk drops the OLDEST sessions); stops once a 50th match proves there are more. `truncated: true` is exact (a further match exists, or the page cap hit with index left). Cost: one indexed pass over the owner's sessions (typical user <1000). Legacy branches made before this change have no `branchedFrom` and are NOT grouped (finding them would need message-row reads per session).
4. Per-user lookup throttle (in memory, per instance, sliding minute): AW-Settings `branch_family_max_per_minute`, default 20, `0` = unlimited, garbage = default, cached ~60s with last-known fallback; over the limit -> 429 `TOO_MANY_BRANCH_LOOKUPS`.
5. Hourly branch cap and all other branch behaviour unchanged.

## User-facing consequences
- A branch of a LEGACY branch (made before this attribute) starts a NEW family root.
- Reads are eventually consistent: a just-created branch may be missing from the endpoint; the portal adds it client-side.
- `UserIdIndex` projects ALL attributes, so each page reads up to 1 MB of full rows (worst case 20 pages) even though the response is projected.

## Data-plane note
Owner-approved additive optional attribute; no GSI, no backfill, rollback = stop writing/reading.

## Rollback
Flip `chat_branching_enabled` off, or revert: the attribute is ignored by every other reader; existing items carrying it are harmless.

## Verification
Review round: failing tests first for newest-first order (ScanIndexForward) and exact `truncated`; mutation (remove ScanIndexForward) fails the test. 16 suites / 451 tests pass; tsc clean.
Backend CI does not run jest; run locally. Failing tests first (23 failed before the implementation). Mutation checks each fail the tests: dropping the MCP strip (2), exposing it on the share serializers (2), dropping the owner filter (1), writing sessionId instead of root (2). Targeted suites (chatBranching*, ishare, mcp.apiTools, getSessions, sessionLoading): 336 passed; wide run (chatBranching*, adminOnlyMessageFilter, ishare*, mcp.apiTools*, every suite referencing addMessagesToSession/createChatSession/filterMessagesForClient/getSharedConversation/getRecentSessionsPage): 142 suites, 2822 tests passed. `tsc --noEmit`: clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium — The change adds persisted branch metadata and an authenticated session-listing endpoint. The metadata is additive, but rollback must account for sessions created with branch links.

Record branch provenance when creating sessions. Add `GET /session/:sessionId/branches` to return the owner-visible branch family. Strip branch metadata from MCP session responses.

title: fix(emma): tenant-scope read_file_content S3 reads + SSRF guard (ENG-2420)
body:
## What / why
ENG-2420. `readFileContent` (shared impl behind `POST /api/emma/read-file`, `POST /api/emma/read-page`, and the Emma `read_file_content` / `read_page_source` tools) streamed any key in the shared private bucket and fetched arbitrary URLs with plain `axios.get`.

- S3: caller `userId` is now threaded from all four entry points; a key is readable only under `users/<userId>/` or `sandbox/<userId>/` (no `..`). Otherwise a single non-leaking "File not found or you do not have access to it." — no S3 call made. No admin bypass added.
- External: new `ssrfSafeGet` uses `resolvePinnedPublicAddress` per hop, pins the socket to the validated IP (`lookup`), `maxRedirects: 0` with manual re-validated redirects (max 5). Blocked → `URL blocked: private or internal address`.

## Risk / rollback
Security fix, no data-plane change. Risk: legitimate reads of S3 objects under other prefixes (e.g. `tasks/<id>/attachments/`) are now refused for the agent; those owners have their own routes. Rollback = revert this commit.

## Tests (local, exact head)
- readFileContent + tool + routes.emmaApi + misc.moduleIsolation + toolResultError + htmlTools: 6 suites, 119/119 pass.
- New negatives: other-tenant key (no S3 call, no key echo), no caller, foreign prefix, traversal, `user-ab` vs `user-a` prefix collision; 169.254.169.254, 127.0.0.1, localhost, DNS→10.x; public→302→metadata refused. Positives: own `users/` and `sandbox/` keys, public URL with relative redirect + pinned lookup.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Complexity ledger
+1 small helper pair (`isS3KeyOwnedByUser`, `ssrfSafeGet`) in misc.ts; optional `caller` arg on one function. No new modules.

## How to test (staging)
1. As user A, upload a file in chat, ask Emma to read it → content returned.
2. `POST /api/emma/read-file {file_url: <user B's S3 URL>}` as A → `success:false`, "File not found or you do not have access to it."
3. `POST /api/emma/read-page {url:"http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"}` → `URL blocked: private or internal address`.
4. `read-page` on `https://example.com` → HTML returned.

Not tested: live staging (pending CI deploy).

title: ENG-110: expose /generating + isGenerating for reload re-attach (no cancel change)
body:
## Summary
ENG-110 reload-survival (backend). Adds `GET /api/agent-mode/generating` (the caller's own running sessions) and an owner-only `isGenerating` on `GET /session/:id`, so the portal can re-attach to a chat that is still replying after a reload. Portal PR: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1244.

**No cancellation behaviour changes and there is no switch.** An earlier revision of this PR gated a cancel-suppression behind an AW-Setting; investigation showed the premise was false (see FACTS), so it was removed.

## FACTS (investigated with a real http server; safe to paste into ENG-110 / ENG-2424)
- `POST /generate` registers `req.on('close', ...)` after `express.json()` has consumed the body. On Node >= 16 the request stream is already closed then, so that listener never fires on a client abort; `res.on('close')` and the socket 'close' do. Reproduced with plain Express + a client that destroys its socket mid-request: Node 20.19.2 and 22.23.3 never emit req 'close'; Node 14.6.0 does.
- Production Node is 22: the EB platform is '64bit Amazon Linux 2023 v6.11.10 running Node.js 22' (the repo itself pins nothing: no .nvmrc / engines; CI uses 22.x). The listener is dead on Node 22 (verified), so it is dead in production.
- Nothing else cancels on disconnect: no res 'close' / 'aborted' / AbortSignal in the /generate path; nginx (`.platform/nginx/conf.d/agent-mode-timeout.conf`, 600s) and the ALB (IdleTimeout 600, `.ebextensions/timeout.config`) only close sockets, which the handler ignores; the portal has no beforeunload/pagehide/unmount stop and aborts its fetch only in `handleStop`, which also calls `POST /session/:id/stop` (the real canceller).
- So a running chat already keeps running and persists its reply when the tab is closed or reloaded TODAY. What was missing was visibility after the reload.
- Same dead listener in the conversable-share generate (cancel never fires) and `/verified-generate` (`clientDisconnected` never true; harmless). The SSE GET `/progress` listener is a bodyless GET and does fire.
- Do not repair these to `res.on('close')` without a product decision: it would make every reload kill the run.

## Changes
- `GET /generating` (auth): `{ sessionIds }` for the CALLER only, from the cap module's per-user map (`getGeneratingSessionIdsForUser`) intersected with `activeSessionGenerations`. Added on claim, removed by the existing `finally`.
- `GET /session/:id` adds `isGenerating` only for the genuine owner; admins/delegates and share views never get it.
- A comment at the dead listener records the fact. State is in-memory per instance (Immutable deploy overlap hides the other instance's runs; accepted). No table/attribute/index.
- Cost: an abandoned run holds its cap slot until it finishes (cap x 600s per user) - already today's behaviour.

## Tests (run locally; CI does not run jest)
- New: `agentModeController.generateDisconnect.socket` (2, REAL http server + express.json + socket destroy: worker not cancelled, reply persisted once, lock + slot released, /generating lists the run, explicit Stop cancels), `agentModeController.generating` (10), `agentModeRoutes.generating` (2, real router + real auth middleware + real controller: 401 without a token, 200 with the caller's ids only, never another user's; removing the route registration fails it). `sessionLoading` updated for the additive `isGenerating`.
- Mutation: switching the listener to `res.on('close')` fails the socket test.
- Slice (agentModeController*, concurrentGenerationCap*, sessionLoading, agentModeRoutes*, generate*; rebased on main incl. #3463/#3467): 121 suites, 1749 tests green. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Rollout: none needed (no flag); merge order independent of the portal PR.

title: ENG-113: save unchosen Compare answers behind compare_save_alternatives (multiverse view)
body:
## Summary
ENG-113 (multiverse view), backend half. Today "Continue with this answer" appends ONE user+assistant pair and the unchosen Compare columns are lost. Behind the new AW-Settings switch `compare_save_alternatives` (exact `true`; absent/other/cold-start failure = off = today's behaviour; ~60s cache + last-known fallback, same pattern as `compareProviderPolicy.ts`), the unchosen answers are saved on the chosen assistant row and can be branched from. Portal half: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1246.

**Owner-approved additive metadata key; no schema/index/table change.** (`metadata.compareId`, `metadata.compareAlternatives`, `metadata.compareAlternativesOmitted`, `metadata.branchedFromAlternative` are free-form message metadata.)

## Design
- `POST /compare` returns `alternativesToken`: HMAC (select-token key derivation + a `kind` tag) over user, session, compareId, prompt, issuedAt and the sorted SET of `{model, sha256(content)}` of every ok column. The switch is not part of it.
- `POST /compare/select` accepts optional `alternatives:[{model,content,latencyMs?}]` + `alternativesToken`. Stored only if the switch is on and the token verifies (constant time) over alternatives + the chosen answer (so the set is exactly the server's ok columns), models distinct, max 3, each content <= 200k. name/provider come from the server registry (`getModelCompareInfo`), never the client. Any failure: alternatives ignored + logged, select still succeeds for the chosen answer. Replay returns the existing pair and never rewrites; 409 `compare_already_selected` unchanged; no model call in select, so usage/cost unchanged.
- Branch endpoint: copied rows strip `compareAlternatives`/`compareId`/`compareAlternativesOmitted`; new optional `alternativeModel` ("Branch with this answer") replaces row N's content + `llm` with the alternative's, drops the alternatives, adds `branchedFromAlternative:{model}`, sets the new session's model to it (explicit model resolution = entitlement/usage policy). Idempotency scope appends `alternativeModel` only when present (existing scopes byte-identical). Lock, cap, born-archived verification, allowlist unchanged.
- Hint `compareSaveAlternatives` (boolean) on `GET /api/agent-mode/model-options` next to `chatBranchingEnabled`.

## Risks designed out
- (a) Size: serialized alternatives <= 120,000 UTF-8 bytes AND whole assistant row <= 341,808 bytes (`MAX_MESSAGE_CONTENT_SIZE` 350,000 minus 8,192 headroom, derived from the shared `MAX_PERSISTED_MESSAGE_BYTES`). The headroom matters because a later like/dislike re-runs `shrinkMessageForPersistence`, which truncates the chosen answer BEFORE dropping metadata (a review probe at 349,990 bytes lost answer characters). Accepted rows are returned untouched by the guard, now and after a feedback write (both tested, plus cap+1 => marker). Otherwise NONE stored (never partial) + `metadata.compareAlternativesOmitted:'size'`; if even the marker would not fit under the cap the message is stored exactly as today. Bytes are JSON-escaped UTF-8 (CJK/emoji/control chars tested). Chosen answer never touched.
- (b) Exposure: `filterMessagesForClient({omitBranchOrigin:true})` (share/ishare `getSharedConversation`, `getConversableSession`) also drops `compareAlternatives`. MCP admin transcript / summarizer / judge / replay inputs build `{role, content}` from explicit fields; a tripwire test fails if any file outside a 5-file allowlist mentions the key.
- (c) Trust: set token (above); client text is never stored unless it hashes into the signed set.
- (d) LLM context: `buildCompareMessages` and `buildMarketingContext` produce identical output with/without alternatives (hostile text tested).
- (e) Branch strips (above).

## Flag / rollout / rollback
Ship dark (switch absent = off). Enable: set AW-Settings `compare_save_alternatives` = `true` (portal reads the hint within ~60s cache). Rollback: set it to anything but `true`; already-saved alternatives remain on their rows (owner-only, stripped from non-owner views). Deploy order is free: old portal ignores the new response fields; old backend ignores the new request fields.

## Deviations
- Hint lives on `/model-options` (where `chatBranchingEnabled` is), not `/me`.
- `latencyMs` of an alternative is NOT bound by the token (clamped display value), only model+content are.
- Branch rows 0..N-1 also get the generic alternatives strip (leaner), rather than being byte-verbatim.
- `llmModel` + `alternativeModel` that disagree is a 400 `invalid_request`.
- Added `export` to `MAX_MESSAGE_CONTENT_SIZE` so a test pins the budget to the real cap.

## Tests (run locally; backend CI does not run jest)
- New: `compareSaveAlternatives` (65), `chatBranching.alternatives` (15), `compareAlternatives.contextExclusion` (3); extended: `modelCompare.routes`, `adminOnlyMessageFilter`, `agentModeController.ishareModel`, `agentModeController.scheduledModelStamp`.
- Failing first: against origin/main source the new/extended suites show 29 failed tests + 2 suites failing to compile.
- Mutations (each fails tests; git diff clean after): skip token verify (11 fail), client name (2), drop non-owner strip (4), store over budget (5), budget-only/no row cap (2), branch keeps alternatives (3), branch ignores alternative content (2), builder referencing the key (tripwire, 1).
- Suites after rebase on origin/main: 59 suites / 1009 tests pass (modelComparison, modelCompare*, compareProviderPolicy, chatBranching*, messageSizeGuard, adminOnlyMessageFilter, ishare*, chatbotService*, buildMarketingContext, scheduledModelStamp, filterMessages, session loading/list, admin.chatSessions). `tsc --noEmit` clean (single run, 6144MB heap).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



Review round 2: headroom fix (above); `stripOrigin` renamed `stripOwnerOnlyMetadata` with a comment (flag name kept, tripwires kept); route-level test that a set token is rejected as selectToken (the `kind` mutant stays equivalent: the payload shapes already differ); branch-with-alternative writes `branchedFrom` with the root preserved. Rebased on main (#3463 family endpoint). Mutation: headroom=0 fails 3 tests.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium — The opt-in setting limits exposure, but the change affects answer persistence, token verification, and branch creation.

When `compare_save_alternatives` is enabled, `/compare` signs successful answers and `/compare/select` saves verified alternatives within size limits. Non-owner views filter alternatives. Users can branch from a saved alternative. Model options expose the feature hint. The author reports 59 suites and 1,009 tests passed, with `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: ENG-2105 (A1): LlmConnection store, api_key kind (KMS-encrypted customer keys)
body:
## What

First BYOK (bring-your-own-key) PR for ENG-1816, Track A. Real CRUD for the `LlmConnection` type F1 declared, `api_key` kind: a customer's own Anthropic/OpenAI/Google key, add / live-validate / list (masked) / share / revoke.

## Storage

- New table `AW-LlmConnections`: one row per connection, indexed by owner, by the org it's shared with (sparse), and by provider (for incident response, e.g. "every connection using provider X" if a provider reports a compromise).
- Each key gets its own KMS data key (envelope encryption); the key itself is encrypted locally with AES-256-GCM and only the wrapped data key + ciphertext are stored. Both layers are bound to connection id, owner and provider, so a ciphertext copied onto another row can't be decrypted.
- KMS is called with instance-role credentials explicitly — the key policy grants the instance role, and the SDK's default credential chain would otherwise pick the backend's static keys and fail. Staging and production share that role, so the key *alias* chosen by `NODE_ENV` (not IAM) is what keeps staging/test data off the production key.
- Revoking deletes the encrypted key in the same conditional write. PITR is deliberately off: with it on, a "revoked" key's ciphertext would stay restorable from a backup for up to 35 days.
- The raw key leaves the service in exactly one place (`getKeyMaterial`), not reachable over HTTP, which re-reads the connection fresh every call so a revoke takes effect on the very next use.

## Rules (per Manan's decisions)

- A user may hold several keys, any provider, several per provider, tried in the order added.
- A user with no org manages their own keys. In an org, only the owner may add a key or share it with the org; a shared key is usable by every member's runs for as long as the sharer stays an owner.
- Anyone may revoke a key they own; another owner may revoke a key shared with the org.
- A delegated admin acts as the customer and is recorded on what they add or revoke.
- Gated by `eng1816_funding_flags`' `byok` switch (`isByokEnabledFor`): off by default; list/revoke always work so a customer can always remove a key.

## API

`/api/llm-connections`: `GET` list, `POST` add, `POST /:id/validate`, `PATCH /:id` (share toggle), `DELETE /:id` revoke. Session-derived user only — no caller-supplied user/org id. Per-user rate limit, no caching. The key appears in exactly one request body, never a response, log line, or error (including an error the HTTP client library itself raises, which can carry request headers).

## Review and fixes

One independent review pass found no critical/high issues. It found and I fixed:
- **Medium** — the per-owner connection cap (10) was enforced by counting then creating as two separate calls; concurrent adds could each see a fresh count under the cap and all succeed. Now atomic: a per-owner slot counter is checked and incremented in the same DynamoDB transaction as the create.
- **Low** — `validate()`'s provider round-trip can take seconds; a revoke landing during it could be papered over, reporting a revoked connection as still active. Closed by re-reading after the provider call and checking the final write's own result.
- **Low** — `list()` kept showing a key as "shared" after its sharer stopped being an org owner, though it was already unusable. Now filtered through the same check the usable-key path already applies.
- **Low** — added a regression test for the "org fails to load" fail-closed branch, previously untested.

All four fixes are mutation-tested: 9 mutations across two rounds, 9/9 killed.

## Live verification

Against real infrastructure, not mocks, inside the test environment's backend container:
- The table created automatically at boot, exactly matching the approved spec (3 GSIs, delete-protected, on-demand, PITR off).
- Real KMS seal/open round-trip against the dev key; a wrong encryption context is refused by KMS itself.
- Real HTTP calls to Anthropic, OpenAI and Google with a deliberately invalid key — each correctly classified as `invalid_key`, and `add()` refused to store it.
- The real table's owner and provider indexes, `getKeyMaterial`, and revoke (including that it deletes the encrypted key and `getKeyMaterial` afterward fails) all verified end to end.

## What changes in production

Nothing can use this yet. The route is mounted and reachable, but:
- adding or validating a key requires the BYOK flag enabled for that specific user, off for everyone by default;
- nothing in the funding/money path (A2/A4) reads from this table — that's later work.

So blast radius today is effectively zero: no customer is affected unless an admin has explicitly opted them into the BYOK allowlist, and the only durable state a customer can create is a key they added themselves, which they can revoke at will.

## Known follow-up

PR 2 (OpenRouter key + BYOK credential provisioning on add/revoke) is separate and currently blocked on ENG-2383 (an OpenRouter Management API key needs to land in Secrets Manager) — does not block this PR.

## Rollback

Revert the PR. The table is new and empty in production (nothing can write to it yet); no existing data or behavior changes.

title: fix(intake): reconcile concurrent auto-issue filers (ENG-2426)
body:
## What / why
`fileAutoIssue` is list-then-create. Two concurrent filers both saw no open canonical and both created: ENG-2416/ENG-2417 (0.3s apart) and ENG-2414/ENG-2415 on the 2026-10-12 09:01Z Meta sweep.

Fix: after creating, re-list open Auto issues with the same matcher (alert class / idempotency key / normalized title). If an older match exists, the lowest issue number wins: the new issue gets a "Duplicate of" comment plus a Linear duplicate relation, the winner gets an occurrence comment, and the call returns the winner with `deduped: true`. "Oldest wins" is deterministic, so every racer lands on the same canonical. Errors are swallowed and the created issue is returned as before.

Closes ENG-2426 (acceptance criteria 1-4 on the issue).

## Evidence
- New `intakeService.autoIssueRace.test.ts`: 4 tests. The race test FAILS without the fix and passes with it (RED->GREEN verified locally).
- `jest src/services/__tests__/intakeService*`: 3 suites, 14/14 pass.
- `tsc --noEmit -p backend`: clean.

## Risk / rollback
- Only the create path runs this. Cost: one extra Linear list call per newly filed Auto issue. No change to the dedupe-hit path or to persistence. No DB/data-plane change.
- Rollback: revert this commit.

## Complexity ledger
+1 post-create block in `fileAutoIssue`. No new modules or exports.

## How to test / post-deploy
After the next Meta sweep (09:00 UTC), check that no new pair of open Auto issues has identical titles.

## Not tested
A live Linear race. The tests mock linearService.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium — reconciliation runs on the production issue-filing path. Failures fall back to the newly created issue, but an incorrect match could mark an issue as a duplicate.

After filing, `fileAutoIssue` re-lists open Auto issues and applies the existing match rules. When another match has a lower issue number, it marks the new issue as a duplicate, comments on the canonical issue, and returns the canonical issue.
