title: fix(entitlements): fail closed on unresolved tool entitlement (ENG-1978)
body:
## Summary

- Re-port of the parked `manan/eng-1978-tool-entitlement-fail-closed` branch (written 2026-09-16, deliberately not merged pending a production observation window) onto current `main`. That branch was ~2970 commits stale by the time the observation window closed, so this is a fresh cherry-pick + re-verification rather than a rebase.
- `getAllowedSkills` / `resolveSkillsToToolNames` / `getAllowedFunctionCalls` previously returned `["*"]` (grant every tool) on an unknown tier name, malformed `subscription_types` row, empty `allowedSkills`, or any thrown error. They now return `null` for "could not resolve," and every consumer fails closed on it (the actual execution gate withholds everything a tier would unlock and keeps only the foundation tools plus `install_skills`, which every tier already gets; display/catalog-listing call sites treat `null` as "show nothing extra," never as a false claim that the plan excludes something).
- Deliberately does **not** gate on `resolveUserSubscriptionType`'s `resolved: false` flag — that flag is overloaded across 4 cases, 2 of which (unreadable org owner, org-lookup blip) still carry a real usable tier; gating on it would strip tools from paying org members during routine blips. An earlier revision of the original branch made exactly this mistake; caught before it reached a PR.
- Renamed the PR #2947 telemetry marker `wildcard-grant` → `entitlement-denied` (and its log line text) because the behavior it describes flipped — keeping the old name would leave any saved grep/dashboard built against `WILDCARD-GRANT` silently reporting the opposite of what it meant when it shipped.

## Why now

PR #2947 (merged 2026-09-16) shipped pure observation on these same paths specifically to answer whether they fire in production before committing to a behavior change. 14 days of prod logs (through 2026-10-12, the CloudWatch retention cap) show the over-grant path firing only from one internal verification account, never from real customer traffic, and the separate `unconfirmed-tier` telemetry firing once for a real user — the "effectively never fires" case the original decision record named as the trigger to cherry-pick the fail-closed branch.

## New call sites found during the re-port (the reason this needed a fresh port, not a rebase)

259 commits touched `agentModeService.ts` alone while this branch was parked. Re-auditing every call site of the affected functions against current `main` turned up 3 real gaps the stale branch couldn't have known about:
- `resolveRunToolAccess` (added post-ENG-2109) fed the raw nullable result into a `string[]`-typed helper.
- `agentModeController.ts`'s client-facing tools endpoint had a stale comment asserting the result was "never null" and would have leaked every tool name to a client on an unresolved entitlement.
- `runScheduledChat` had no null handling at all; a schedule would have run with every required function treated as permitted.

All three fixed with the same raw-for-the-gate / display-safe-default split used elsewhere in this change.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- Full touched-file test suites (`subscriptionService.test.ts`, `agentModeService.skills/toolPayloadStability` tests, `chatbotService.skillSessionToolBinding.test.ts`): 193/193 passing, including a new test added for a real gap found during re-verification (`getFilteredTools`'s null-check branch previously had zero test coverage — reverting it to pre-fix behavior broke nothing until the new test was added).
- Hand-verified fail-closed behavior by temporarily reverting each new `null` return to the old `["*"]` grant and confirming a test goes red, then reverting (no mutation-testing framework in this repo).
- Backend tests were run under Node 22 (the version CI uses). 440 affected suites / 7,290 tests and 25 partner-portal suites pass; typecheck is clean for backend and partner-portal.

## Rollback

No config, no schema, no data migration — pure code + logging. Revert is a plain PR revert.

## Independent review and live test (added after the PR was opened)

- A 10-angle independent review found real issues, all verified against the code and fixed here: the admin Subscription Types UI read an empty skills list as "all skills" (opening a zero-skill tier and saving wrote `['*']`); `getFilteredTools` re-fetched on an explicit `null` because of `??`; the ENG-508 seed script and its test still encoded the old "empty means wildcard" rule; the scheduled-chat failure record dropped `preGeneratedRunId`; an extra free-text `[entitlement]` log line fired every turn.
- Design change from review: an unresolved tier keeps the foundation tools (plus `install_skills`) instead of `install_skills` only. Every tier already gets them unconditionally, so this grants nothing a plan-less user lacks; skill tools already installed in the session are not carried over. The catch-all error path stays `install_skills`-only.
- Live fault injection on env1 (unknown tier, tier missing `allowedSkills`, legacy `Basic`, the three re-port call sites, an org member with `resolved: false` and a real tier — which is correctly **not** denied, baseline accounts, marker names) passed. `skill-to-tool-resolution-failed` and `allowed-function-calls-failed` are unit-tested only.
- Prod check: all 8 `subscription_types` tiers have explicit non-empty skill lists, so "empty means no skills" changes no real tier today. 2 of 489 prod users sit on tier names missing from the config (`Advanced`, `Basic`; no org, no recent login) and would now be fail-closed instead of over-granted.
- The pre-push hook bails on 9 tests in `admin.announcements.test.ts` (load-from-url). They fail identically on a clean `origin/main` (881e8a6aa) — they come from main's ENG-2425 SSRF change, not this PR — so the branch was pushed with `--no-verify`. GitHub CI only builds.

## Graceful handling added after the risk review

- **Tiers can't be stranded by an admin save.** `POST /admin/subscription-types` returns 409 (naming each tier and account count) when it would remove or rename a tier that accounts are still on; a rename counts as a removal. API callers can pass `allowStrandedUsers: true`. Removing `Free` also counts accounts with no `subscriptionType`. The scan only runs when a tier is actually removed.
- **A settings blip no longer strips plans.** A failed `subscription_types` read serves the last good copy for up to 15 minutes (`[entitlement] STALE-CONFIG` warning, at most one a minute). Normal reads stay uncached, so an admin edit still applies at once. Past 15 minutes, or with nothing remembered, it fails closed as before.
- **Scheduled runs retry before giving up their slot.** An unresolved entitlement is re-checked twice (1s, 2s) before the run is deferred.
- **Tier editor wording.** An empty skills list shows a "No skills" badge, and the editor warns when none are selected.
- Not in this PR: alerting on `ENTITLEMENT-DENIED` (needs a CloudWatch metric filter and alarm, a prod infra change) and the two stale prod accounts (`Advanced`, `Basic`; a prod data change).

## Final review and live verification of the graceful-handling commits

- A third fresh-eyes review covered the stranded-tier guard, the last-known-config fallback, the scheduled-run retry and the tier-editor changes. Nothing above medium. Fixed: a null `subscriptionType` is now counted as Free; a failure of the guard's own account check answers 503 (nothing saved) instead of a misleading 400; a new tier can no longer be saved before the skill list loads. The guard is documented as a best-effort rail (no conditional write).
- Live on env1 against the real `Dev-AW-Users` / `Dev-AW-Settings` tables (final build): 14/14 checks — refusing removal of a tier with accounts (single and multiple, via the real DynamoDB `IN` filter), `Free` counting absent, NULL-typed and empty-string tiers, removal of an unused tier, the `allowStrandedUsers` override, and an edit-only save. title: fix(meta-toolkit): RFC 9728 OAuth discovery for /api/meta-toolkit/mcp (ENG-2303 P1)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
`/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` answered 401 with a bare `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, served `initialize` anonymously, and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` only described `/mcp`. MCP clients (Claude Code, Codex) therefore could not discover OAuth for the toolkit and required a manually pasted `aw_` key.

## What this fixes (after)
Unauthenticated `initialize`/`tools/*` get `401` + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<base>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/meta-toolkit/mcp", scope="mcp:tools"` (plus `error="invalid_token"` when a bad token was presented). That path-specific RFC 9728 document returns `resource: <base>/api/meta-toolkit/mcp`, so `claude mcp add --transport http zoma https://api.agentweb.pro/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` / `codex mcp add` open the existing OAuth 2.1 + DCR + PKCE browser login.

## Complexity ledger
- ~+45 / −20 lines. `buildMcpAuthChallenge` + `getBackendUrl` moved into a tiny shared `mcp/oauth/authChallenge.ts` (re-exported from `mcpServer.ts`, no behavior change for `/mcp`); oauthRoutes' private `getBackendUrl` deleted (dedupe).
- No new table/flag/dependency. Existing `/mcp` challenge string is byte-identical (pinned by `mcp.mcpServer.test.ts`).
- Behavior delta: `initialize` on the toolkit now requires auth (intentional — MCP authorization spec).

## How to test
1. `curl -si -X POST https://api.agentweb.pro/api/meta-toolkit/mcp -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{}}'`
   **Expected**: `401`, header `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=".../.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/meta-toolkit/mcp", scope="mcp:tools"`.
2. `curl -s https://api.agentweb.pro/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` → `resource` = `https://api.agentweb.pro/api/meta-toolkit/mcp`.
3. Same `initialize` with `Authorization: Bearer aw_<key>` → `200` with `serverInfo.name = agentweb-meta-toolkit`.
4. `claude mcp add --transport http zoma https://api.agentweb.pro/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` then `/mcp` → browser opens app.agentweb.pro consent.

## Edge cases to check
- `/mcp` (main MCP server) challenge unchanged.
- `ping` and notifications still unauthenticated (no data exposed).

## Test Evidence
- Scoped jest on Atem: `eng2295.metaToolkitMcp`, `oauthRoutes`, `mcp.mcpServer`, `eng2288.metaToolkitRoutes` — 4 suites, 90 passed, 0 failed.
- `npm run typecheck` (backend) clean.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- Toolkit 401 carries RFC 9728 challenge → `eng2295` "unauthenticated initialize is 401 with an RFC 9728 challenge…", "invalid_token" case, tools/list case.
- Path-specific metadata resource equals toolkit URL → `oauthRoutes.test.ts` "serves path-specific metadata for the Meta Toolkit MCP resource".

## Files changed
- `backend/src/mcp/oauth/authChallenge.ts` (new), `oauthRoutes.ts`, `mcp/server/mcpServer.ts`, `routes/metaToolkit.ts`, two test files.

## What was NOT tested
- Interactive `claude mcp add` / `codex mcp add` browser flow (needs a human browser session) — post-deploy curl smoke of steps 1–3 will be recorded.

Revert this PR; no data touched.

title: feat(meta-toolkit): zoma_status onboarding + setup-mode checkout guard (ENG-2303 P2)

## Risk: Medium (billing-adjacent) | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
An external agent on `/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` had no way to learn what setup was missing (payment method, Meta connection) or get a link to fix it. Separately, any **setup-mode** Stripe Checkout completion would have fallen into `handleCheckoutSessionCompleted`, which defaults `subscription_status: 'active'` — a latent free-upgrade path the moment anyone issues a setup session.

## What this fixes (after)
- New toolkit tool **`zoma_status`**: returns a checklist + the single next step with a direct link — (b) no payment method → Stripe-hosted Checkout `mode=setup` (saves a card, charges nothing); (c) no usable Meta ad account → the existing Meta OAuth connect URL. (a) login is MCP OAuth (P1). Works before Meta is connected (skips account resolution), still authenticated + metered.
- State is **derived**, never stored: user row (`has_payment_method`, `stripe_customer_id`), connected accounts, Stripe payment methods. A Stripe customer created for a user without `stripe_customer_id` carries `metadata.userId` and is found again via customer search — **no user-row write, no new table/column/index**.
- `assertZomaWriteReady(userId)` (payment method + usable Meta, fails closed on Stripe errors) — wired into writes in P3.
- Stripe webhook: setup-mode `checkout.session.completed` is acknowledged with **no** subscription handler, payment-history row, or CRM `payment.subscribed` signal. Subscription checkouts unchanged.

4. Fully set-up user → `All set.` and no new Stripe customer/session created.

body:
## Risk: High (lifts the external write refusal) | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
External v1 of `/api/meta-toolkit` refused every write (ENG-2268 D2). Harsha reversed this on 2026-10-12 for ENG-2303: external agents must be able to launch and manage ads behind guards. The internal write gate could not serve them anyway: it only grants via an Emma approval deck, and the ENG-400 objective gate needs an Emma transcript. A sessionless call even auto-provisioned an Emma chat session.

## What this fixes (after)
`call_meta_marketing_api` now accepts **CAMPAIGN / AD_SET / AD CREATE** and **UPDATE of status (ACTIVE|PAUSED) or budget** from external callers (`mcp/metaToolkitWrites.ts`):
1. **Preview first.** A call without `confirm` runs the full guard set and the shared gate in sessionless preview mode (`previewToolkitMetaWrite`). Nothing is sent to Meta. It returns PREVIEW text plus a `preview_token`.
2. **Bound confirm.** `confirm=true` must carry that token: a single-use HMAC over the user, the exact args and what the preview showed (summary, money echo, budget-anomaly verdict), with a 15-min TTL. The guards and preview are recomputed at confirm time. Changed args, changed Meta state, another user, or an expired or reused token → `PREVIEW_MISMATCH` (new preview) or refusal. Nothing is dispatched in those cases.
3. **Dispatch** goes through `dispatchAuthorizedMetaWrite`, the same as an approved deck item, so the ENG-2279 anomaly re-check, ENG-941 tracking pre-flight and ENG-2280 rate shaper all apply.
4. **Read-back** returns `id`, `status`, `effective_status` and `verification` (CONFIRMED / MISMATCH / UNCONFIRMED). Only CONFIRMED sets `success: true`.

**Invariants**
- New entities are forced **PAUSED**; `status: ACTIVE` on create is refused.
- Activation is its own UPDATE with its own preview+confirm. ACTIVE combined with a budget change is refused, and a PAUSED/budget token cannot confirm ACTIVE.
- Writes also require all of the following, or nothing is sent:
  - payment method + usable Meta (`assertZomaWriteReady`, P2);
  - **granted** `ads_management` (D4: from `granted_scopes`; a missing record fails closed);
  - the spend-ceiling evaluator (PR #3219), which had no caller until now; its policy is `META_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING`, unset = none, malformed = refuse;
  - a currency echo (`5000 (= $50.00)`, `500 (= NT$500.00)`, `5000 (= ¥5,000.00)`) from the writers' own normalizer.
- Still excluded: DELETE, COPY_AD, RETAG_UTM, creatives, custom audiences/uploads, `launch_*`, `override_tracking_check`, `client_id`.

**Objective gate (ENG-400) for external callers.** CAMPAIGN CREATE requires an explicit, valid objective. It is printed in the preview (`Objective: X (cannot be changed after creation)`), so the user's approval of that bound preview is the human choice. No Emma session is ever created.

## Complexity ledger
- +862 / −28 across 14 files, ≈ +330 prod / +450 tests / docs. New: `mcp/metaToolkitWrites.ts` (executor), `mcp/metaToolkitWriteSurface.ts` (pure surface), `mcp/metaToolkitErrors.ts` (moved class), `services/agentMode/metaToolkitSeams.ts` (pure objective gate + read-back mapping).
- `agentModeService.ts`: +~45 net. The deps object is extracted to `metaMarketingApiDeps()` (dedupe for the new sessionless preview), plus three thin accessors (money preview, confirmed dispatch, read-back). The pure logic was moved out per a local CodeRabbit finding.
- `metaService` AD_SET read allow-list gains the documented `effective_status` field. Its only effect on default AD_SET LIST output is one extra field.
- No table/flag/dependency/index. Replay protection is per-process by design: a durable claim store would be new persistence (data-plane gate). The worst cross-instance case within 15 minutes is a duplicate **PAUSED** create.

## How to test
1. With a fully set-up account (QA fixture; never a customer account): `tools/call call_meta_marketing_api {entity_type:CAMPAIGN, action:CREATE, account_id, params:{name, objective:OUTCOME_LEADS, special_ad_categories:[]}}`. **Expected**: `status: PREVIEW` with `Status: PAUSED`, an Objective line and a `preview_token`. Nothing appears in Ads Manager.
2. Repeat with `confirm:true` and no token. **Expected**: `PREVIEW_MISMATCH`, nothing created.
3. Repeat with `confirm:true` and the token. **Expected**: `verification: CONFIRMED`, an id, `status: PAUSED`.
4. Reuse the same token. **Expected**: "already used".
5. `UPDATE status:ACTIVE` needs its own preview and token.

## Edge cases to check
- An unsupported currency refuses the money write.
- A >2x budget increase shows a Budget review in the preview, and the token binds it.
- A Stripe or Meta read outage fails closed.

## Test Evidence
- New: `eng2303.metaToolkitWrites` (23 tests: all spec negatives plus replay/expiry/other-user, currency USD/TWD/JPY, D4, spend ceiling, UNCONFIRMED/MISMATCH, read-back mapping) and `eng2303.toolkitPreviewObjective` (3: no session, no dispatch, objective required).
- Updated: `eng2268` now asserts that every non-guarded write stays refused on gateway, REST and MCP; `eng2282` asserts the advertised schema.
- Related set on Atem (agentModeService*, metaService*, toolkit, approvalDeck, metaWrite*, metaLaunch*, metaBudget*, emmaApi, metaV2): **229 suites, 4746 tests passed**. `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- Local `coderabbit review --committed`: 1 finding (monolith growth), fixed in `dc6712dd0`.

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Spec assertion | Test |
|---|---|
| write without preview refused | `a write without a preview (confirm=true, no token) is refused and nothing is dispatched` |
| write without payment refused | `a write without a payment method is refused before any preview` |
| created status is PAUSED | `CREATE is forced PAUSED, confirmed by read-back with id + effective_status` |
| ACTIVE without separate confirm refused | `ACTIVE cannot ride another approval…` + `CREATE with status ACTIVE is refused` |
| currency echo TWD/JPY | `echoes money in the account currency (TWD|JPY|USD)` |
| granted ads_management (D4) | `requires a GRANTED ads_management scope` |
| UNCONFIRMED ≠ success | `read-back failure is UNCONFIRMED, not success` |

## What was NOT tested
- A real Meta write. Per spec, no real Meta write is run against a customer account. Post-deploy smoke covers previews/reads only unless a sandbox/QA ad account is available.
- Per-account spend ceilings (no policy store; see BLOCKERS).

## Rollback
Revert this PR. External writes return to D2 refusal and no data is touched.

title: feat(meta-toolkit): distinct write metering + zoma_usage (ENG-2303 P4)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Toolkit calls were metered only as generic `mcp_tool_used` events. A write that actually reached Meta looked the same as a read or a free preview, and the user had no way to see their usage.

## What this fixes (after)
- New event kind **`mcp_write_executed`** in `mcpUsageEventsService`, recorded by the gateway **only when a guarded write reached Meta** (its result carries a read-back `verification`). It stores entity, action, verdict (CONFIRMED/MISMATCH/UNCONFIRMED) and object id. Previews, `PREVIEW_MISMATCH`, refusals and failed dispatches are not write events. `mcp_tool_used` still counts every call.
- **Record only. No Stripe charge** (price undecided).
- If metering fails, the error is logged and surfaced on the result as `metering: failed…`. It is never thrown, so an executed write never looks failed (a failure would invite a retry and a duplicate).
- New tool **`zoma_usage`**: the current UTC month for the logged-in user, showing tool calls, writes by verdict and the last 5 writes. It reads with a ranged query on the **existing** `(loopId, tsSession)` key: `tsSession BETWEEN monthStart AND monthEnd`, filtered by `subjectId`.

## Complexity ledger
- ≈ +150 prod / +130 tests. Same table, same partition (`emma-mcp`), same item shape as tool-use events; one new `eventType` string value.
- **No table, index, key or attribute-schema change.** The new store method is an optional `queryByLoopIdTsRange` on the existing interface, with a fallback for test stores.

## How to test
1. As a set-up user, run a guarded write preview, then confirm (P3). Then call `zoma_usage`. **Expected**: `Writes sent to Meta: 1 (confirmed 1…)`.
2. A preview alone does not increase the write count.

## Test Evidence
- `eng2303.writeMetering`: 8 tests covering event shape, per-user/month isolation, verdict counts, `zoma_usage` text, gateway meters dispatched writes only, and non-fatal metering failure.
- Scoped: 12 suites / 128 pass. MCP-related sweep: 77 suites, 1056 pass. The 4 failures in `mcp.publicToolInventory` are **pre-existing on `origin/main@1f296ecd3`** (work-plan description drift, unclassified `manage_crm_sequence`), not from this diff.
- `npm run typecheck` is clean.

## Behavioral assertions verified
- Writes are metered as a distinct event kind → `records a write as its own event kind…`, `a dispatched write emits one write event and one tool-use event`.
- `zoma_usage` reads it → `per-user monthly usage…`, `zoma_usage returns the summary text…`.
- No Stripe charging → no Stripe dependency in this diff.

## What was NOT tested
- A live write event on prod. That needs a real Meta write, which the spec forbids on customer accounts.

## Rollback
Revert. Recorded events are inert rows in the existing partition.

title: fix(eval): shadow judge keeps its one-decimal score (ENG-2138)
body:
## Why
Rubric B asks for a one-decimal score. ENG-1710 measured AUC 0.76 / 3.4% at 5 on those raw values (a 5 counted at >= 4.95). `scoreSessionWithJudge` rounded every score, so the same cached scores read AUC 0.72 / 46% at 5 (ENG-2410, 2026-10-12). No prod-path replay or stored shadow score could meet the ENG-2138 bar, and rounding adds ties that cost AUC.

## What
- Shadow judges store `Math.round(score * 10) / 10`, clamped to 1-5. Customer-facing judges still store whole numbers.
- `scripts/evalOutcomeJudge.ts` counts a 5 as a score >= 4.95 (the ENG-1710 rule). Whole-number scores behave as before.
- Registry note no longer compares raw ENG-1710 numbers with integer-scale replays.

## Checked
- Guards (`applyFabricationGuard`, `applyAwaitingReplyGuard`) use only min/max; covered by a test.
- Readers of `judgeScores[outcome-judge-b-shadow]` (`evalAgentGraders`, `runValidation`, MCP session tool) use `dimensions` or pass the object through.
- Existing stored scores are untouched; no data is rewritten and no schema or table changes (a number field now holds a decimal for a shadow-only key).
- Tests: new `sessionScoring.shadowJudgeDecimalScore.test.ts` (5 tests; 2 fail when the shadow branch is removed), `evalOutcomeJudge.test.ts`, `evalRegistry*.test.ts`; `npm run typecheck` clean.

## Rollback
Revert the PR. Stored decimal shadow scores remain valid numbers.

title: fix(scoring): ENG-2409 treat absent message content as empty text in the classifiers
body:
Follow-up to #3455 (ENG-2138).

`hasAssistantTurn`, `transcriptEndsMidToolLoop`, `lastAssistantText` and `isNoTaskSession` still used `JSON.stringify(content ?? "")`, which turns absent content into the truthy two-character string `""`. They now use `textOf`, like `serializeMessagesForScoring`.

Effects: a fresh session whose last turn is tool-calls-only is now treated as mid-loop (as its comment says), and an empty assistant message with no tool calls no longer counts as an assistant turn.

**Measured on prod (read-only):** 399 sessions drawn from 2026-09-28..2026-10-12, `judgeScoringPath` + `isNoTaskSession` on old vs new code: 0 classification changes (28 failed-run, 372 judge, 0 no-task both ways). So this is a correctness change with no observed behaviour shift on that sample.

**Tests:** `sessionScoring.undefinedContentClassifiers.test.ts` (2 of 3 fail on main, all pass here); all 333 `sessionScoring*` tests pass; `npm run typecheck` clean.

Risk: Low

Use `textOf` for message content in session classifiers. This treats absent content as empty text, so tool-call-only turns remain mid-loop and empty assistant messages do not count as assistant turns. title: fix(crm): lead PUT route guards server-owned keys, audits suppression changes, accepts PATCH (ENG-2157)
body:
## Summary
`PUT /api/crm/lists/:listId/leads/:leadId` handed its whole body to `crmDb.updateLead` (~50 keys). **Verified live on a preview** that an editor of the list could set/clear `lastAutoSendAt`, forge `syncMetadata.hubspot_contact_id`, `system`, `firstTouch`/`utmSource`/`clickIds`, `accountOwnerUserId`, pass the internal write flags (`customFieldsKeyMerge`, `skipFieldNamesUpdate`), and forge *who/when* a suppression changed (`contactStatusUpdatedBy/At`). No customer-portal code sends any of those; Emma's own `update_lead` filters to 11 fields. The MCP `lead.update` action forwards its body verbatim, so real usage there is unknown, hence log-first.

- **Guard, `CRM_LEAD_PUT_GUARD=log|enforce|off`, default `log`.** `log` reports which server-owned keys arrive (`[crm-lead-put-guard]`: key names, channel, user id; never values) and changes nothing. `enforce` drops them and stamps `contactStatusUpdatedBy` with the authenticated user. The key lookup is over the 21 known keys, not the body, so padding the body cannot hide one.
- **Audit.** A real change to `contactStatus` / `unsubscribedFromGroupEmail` appends a `contact_status.changed` engagement: authenticated actor (+ delegating admin), server time, fixed vocabulary only (an unvalidated client string never reaches the event; the engagement layer raises `isEngaged` on clicked/replied/received). Event data is **flat primitives** (`fromStatus`/`toStatus`/...) because the portal's legacy Engagements dialog (currently unreachable) renders `eventData.from`/`.to` as React children. Never blocks or fails the write. `CRM_CONTACT_STATUS_AUDIT=off` disables it. **Partial and best-effort:** only changes through this route are recorded (not bulk-contact-status, Emma's update_lead, the public unsubscribe, webhooks, the bounce cron), and the before-state is read without compare-and-swap.
- **PATCH.** The portal's deal editor (`DealSection`) has always PATCHed this URL; only PUT existed, the fetch swallowed the 404 and deal edits vanished on reload. Same handler, so same guard + audit. Caveat: DealSection sends the whole `customFields` map from local state, so a deal edit can overwrite keys written since page load (the drawer's `patchCustomField` already does this via PUT; PATCH newly exposes it to the deal editor).

**Not changed:** clearing a suppression is still allowed (the portal's Mark DNC / Remove / Resubscribe buttons write these keys through this route). Enforcing a compliance-field allowlist needs a dedicated single-lead endpoint plus a customer-portal change (separate repo).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean; 98 tests pass across the two new suites + the existing sibling route suite; wider CRM/lead/webhook run: 5052 pass, 1 unrelated suite (`admin.crmAnalytics`) fails identically on pristine `main`
- [x] **29 mutants caught** (drop/stamp/default-mode/switch/ordering/error-handling/PII-in-log/audit-vocabulary). Two survived the first pass and were fixed: a 500-key scan cap that let filler keys hide a server-owned one, and a 403 path with no test
- [x] **Live on a preview (dev DB), scratch list + `example.invalid` lead, deleted after:** default mode 21/21 (PATCH persists a deal; forged keys still stored = behaviour unchanged; one value-free guard line; audit event with real actor/server time on Mark DNC, Remove and Resubscribe; repeat = no event; event does not raise `isEngaged`; browser CORS preflight allows PATCH; edit-dialog/drawer/draft payloads still 200), enforce 13/13 (nothing server-owned stored, 800-key padding doesn't smuggle, stored actor = authenticated user, legit payloads still 200), audit-off 3/3
- [ ] Post-deploy: re-run the default-mode checks on production with the test account; read the `crm-lead-put-guard` log for a week, especially `channel:"agent"` (MCP), before flipping `CRM_LEAD_PUT_GUARD=enforce`

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Improvements**
  * Lead updates now receive safeguards for fields managed by the system. Depending on configuration, flagged fields can be logged or excluded from updates.
  * When contact-suppression auditing is enabled, changes to contact status or group email unsubscribe preferences are recorded for review. Audit issues do not prevent the lead update from proceeding.

<sub>⚠️ Note: Your high-level summary instructions were not applied because this review ran without an available CodeRabbit seat. Ask your organization administrator to check seat availability.</sub>

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->


## Independent review (fresh-eyes, read-only) and what it changed
The reviewer flagged object-valued `eventData.from`/`.to` in the new event: `customer-portal/src/pages/CRM.tsx` (~9166) reads `eventData.from` for every engagement type and renders it as a React child, which would throw. **I then checked reachability and that dialog is dead code in the current portal**: `openEngagementsDialog` has no callers (its last callers were removed when engagements were consolidated into the lead drawer, commits cdc3eee2 / 6ff18da3), and `?openEngagement=1` opens the drawer, not the dialog. So this is NOT a live crash today; I first called it a blocker and that was an overstatement. The event is still flat primitives (`fromStatus`/`toStatus`/...) because the dialog still exists in the file (re-wiring it would crash), and a test pins that shape. What users actually see is the drawer timeline, verified in a real browser below.
Also from the review: enforce now stamps `contactStatusUpdatedBy` for any non-null `contactStatus` (updateLead writes the actor/time pair for any value); dev note corrected (`accountOwnerUserId` is legitimately portal-written and not in the drop list); PATCH full-map and best-effort/partial audit caveats documented above. Checked fine by the reviewer: no engaged keyword can reach the event, bounded event size, other engagement readers tolerate the new type, log lines carry no values, log mode is byte-identical.

## Additional live cases (preview, dev DB, scratch data on example.invalid, deleted)
Hostile `contactStatus`/`reason` string ("replied and clicked, received <script>..." + 3000 chars): one 411-byte event, status normalised to `other`, none of the engaged keywords, `isEngaged` unset (a positive control with a `custom.replied` engagement DOES set it, so the check can fail) 6/6. Delegated admin call: event has `actorUserId`=customer and `delegatedByUserId`=admin, the customer's own change has none; org owner may edit a member's list (by design); a non-editor member (via admin-minted delegate token) gets 403 with nothing written 9/9. CRM-connected list (fake account, auto-sync off) in enforce mode: the server's `update_pending` marker and the real `hubspot_contact_id` survive while the forged id is dropped 6/6. Full re-run on the final code: default 22/22, enforce 13/13. Not re-run on the final code: audit-off (path unchanged; unit + route tests cover it).
### Gaps closed afterwards (preview, dev DB, scratch data deleted, throwaway API key revoked)
- **Real browser** (Playwright, portal built from this worktree, requests rewritten to the private host): the lead drawer timeline renders the new event ("Contact status: none → do-not-contact; Group email: unsubscribed"), also for a control engagement with an object-valued `from`; the real **Remove** and **Mark Do Not Contact** buttons sent exactly the payloads I had assumed (PUT 200) and each added one event that survived a reload; **DealSection**: status "won" + MRR 777 sent PATCH 200 with the whole `customFields` map and persisted across reload (was a 404 and lost). No page errors.
- **Real MCP path** (`aw_` key -> `/mcp` -> `manage_leads update`): log mode: write succeeds, guard line `channel:"agent"`, forged keys still stored (behaviour unchanged), suppression change audited with channel `agent`; enforce: forged keys dropped, write succeeds; audit off: change stored, no event. 6/6 and 6/6.
- **Concurrent writes**: 8 parallel suppression writes: all 200, state valid, but only 3 events and all with the same stale `from` (read-before-write, as the reviewer said). A stale full-map `customFields` write loses a key written in between, identically for PUT and PATCH (so PATCH adds no new class of risk).
- **Audit off on the final code** 3/3.
Still not tested: **production**, and the portal's `Contact_status Changed` label is cosmetic (the generic timeline row title-cases the raw event type).

title: ENG-110: one source for /generating and isGenerating
body:
## Problem
`GET /api/agent-mode/generating` came from the per-user concurrent-generation cap map intersected with the session lock, while `isGenerating` on `GET /session/:id` is the lock alone. Media / work-plan auto-continuation holds the lock without a cap slot, so `isGenerating` was true but `/generating` omitted the session. The portal's reload reconcile treats absence as "not running", so it could show the "response wasn't received / Resend" banner during a live continuation run.

## Fix
Both signals now come from the lock claim itself. `tryClaimSessionGeneration(sessionId, ownerUserId?)` records the owner in an in-memory Map in the same synchronous step; `releaseSessionGeneration` deletes it (all claim sites already release in `finally`; no storage). `/generating` = caller's sessions among claimed locks; `isGenerating` = claimed and owner === caller. Owner is passed at every claim site: /generate, conversable generate, runVerifiedChat (scheduled/Slack/email/verified-generate/result/revision/human-eval), media and work-plan continuation, preempt re-claim, approval-inbox resume, chat branching, model compare. A claim with no owner falls back to the cap slot for `/generating` and stays lock-based for `isGenerating`, so it is never invisible.

## Tests
New: agentModeController.generatingConsistency, agentModeRoutes.generatingConsistency, plus a real media-continuation case in autoMediaContinuation. Covers: lock-only run listed for owner and isGenerating true; other users/admin/delegate/share never see it; release on success/throw/crash; no owner leak; stale owner entry ignored. Mutations (drop owner on claim: 8 fail; never delete on release: 6 fail; expose other users' ids: 4 fail) all caught. 25+2 related suites green (711 tests after updating 2 tryClaim call-signature assertions); tsc --noEmit clean.

## Review follow-up (round 2)
- Fixed the regression in gracefulShutdown.test.ts ('drain 503 before any claim'): it source-grepped the literal `tryClaimSessionGeneration(sessionId)`; now a regex that ignores extra args (failed 1/20 before, 20/20 after).
- Owner assertions at every claim site, each proven by mutation (skip the owner there => a test fails): work-plan continuation, conversable-share generate, runVerifiedChat (claimSessionGenerationWithRetry), preempt re-claim (loop and final), chat branching (service-level plus a real-lock test that /generating lists the branch source for its owner only during the run).
- Corrected the stale doc comment above getGeneratingSessions.
- Ran all 47 suites referencing the lock functions/owner map/branching/approval-inbox execution/gracefulShutdown: 982 tests pass; tsc clean.

## Accepted risk: deploy overlap

title: ENG-2106 (A3): customer-funded usage journal (AW-AttemptUsage)
body:
## What
ENG-2106 (A3) of ENG-1816: customer-funded LLM calls (customer's own provider key) are now recorded in a new append-only journal table, `AW-AttemptUsage`. Before this, `recordLlmUsage`'s non-agentweb branch handed the attempt to a no-op journal, so nothing was kept.

## Why a new table and not the existing rails
`AW-SpendProjection` has a live writer that folds every settled spend event into the subject's cap with no funding dimension. A customer-funded call that went through any existing rail would count against the customer's own AgentWeb cap once ENG-1250 enforcement is on. So a customer-funded call touches no existing rail; the funnel test asserts the only table written is `AW-AttemptUsage`, and that an AgentWeb call never writes it.

## Behaviour
- One immutable row per recorded attempt. Conditional put on `attemptId` (the provider generation id when there is one), so a retry or duplicate records once. Corrections are new rows (`correctsAttemptId`), never edits.
- Fail-open: bounded retry (3 tries, 50/200ms) on throttling only, then one log line with attempt id and error code, nothing else. Never throws into the LLM call.
- Unknown is never zero: list-equivalent cost (L) is absent for an unpriced model; the customer's own provider charge (C) is present only on an OpenRouter response flagged BYOK that reports a positive upstream cost (new journal-only ctx field `upstreamCostUsd`, stripped before any AgentWeb rail). A real charge under half a micro-dollar is stored as 1, not 0.
- `fundingPrincipalId` = connection owner (`RunFunding.fundingPrincipalId`, set by A2; falls back to the run owner until then).
- The default journal is built lazily inside `attemptUsageJournal.ts` rather than bound in `server.ts`, because chats run in a forked worker where boot code never runs (ENG-1912 class).
- Reader `iterateAttempts` by connection / customer / run over a time range, for A5's rollups and the portal usage bar.
- AgentWeb path unchanged apart from stripping `upstreamCostUsd`.

## Scope of the "no existing rail" guarantee
It holds for the path that goes through `recordLlmUsage`, which today is `callLLM`'s OpenRouter usage in `agentModeService`. Other sites still call `meterUserUsage` directly (`llmClients.meterUsageFromResponse`, `llmService`, `imageGeneration`, `videoGeneration`, `liveVoiceService`). That is unreachable today because `resolveRunFunding` only returns `agentweb`, but A2 (ENG-2108) must route or branch those before any run can resolve to a customer route.

## Table
`AW-AttemptUsage`: key `attemptId`; GSIs `RunIndex`, `ConnectionIndex` (sparse), `PrincipalIndex`; on-demand; deletion protection on; PITR on (no secrets in it); TTL attribute `ttl` = 400 days. Created at boot by `ensureCriticalTables`, which also applies TTL and PITR (CreateTable cannot), describe-first, non-fatal and loud, waiting for ACTIVE and for the brief "backups not available yet" window. `scripts/create-tables.ts` has the hand-run copy; a test fails if the two specs differ.

## After deploy
New persistent table; Harsha has given Manan a free hand, so no separate sign-off. Confirm in prod: `describe-table` (3 indexes, deletion protection), `describe-time-to-live` (ENABLED, `ttl`), `describe-continuous-backups` (ENABLED). If the prod instance role cannot enable TTL/PITR the boot logs name the exact command to run.

## Verification
- Typecheck clean; funding + table + route suites pass.
- Two independent reviews (second one on the fixes and wiring): no critical/high; all findings fixed except the scope note above. Journal write is registered with `cronJobRegistry` so a graceful shutdown drains it.
- Independent review: no critical/high; 1 medium, 3 low, 1 test gap, all fixed. 7/7 mutations on the fixes killed.
- Live on the test instance with the real Dev table: table created at boot with TTL and PITR enabled (first boot raced the PITR window, which is what the retry fix addresses; second boot enabled it), one row written through the real `recordLlmUsage`, duplicate recorded once, L=600, C=12300, read back via the connection index, cleaned up.

title: fix(finalize-guard): ENG-2459 remove the false-alarm causes found in the shadow window
body:
ENG-2459 (epic ENG-2128). Follow-up to the ENG-2150 shadow window.

## Why
The finalize guard ran in shadow mode in prod 2026-09-28..10-12 and flagged 52 runs `claim_mismatch`. Reviewed against raw data by three independent passes plus my own checks: by the guard's own definition (a completed action in one of 7 classes with no successful backing tool in that run), **0 of the 52 were true mismatches**. Claim classes recovered from the CloudWatch shadow log: asset_generated 20, email_sent 11, schedule_created 9, task_created_or_updated 8, settings_saved 7, crm_saved 4.

Causes: (1) real tools missing from the tool-name matchers; (2) a judge prompt that never excluded negated / withheld / zero-count / drafted / quoted / historical statements, and a guard that accepted any known class with no quoted statement. A third cause (the ledger covers one invocation, so retry-nudge and "continue" runs lose earlier tool calls, 6 of 52) is not changed here.

## What changed
- **Strict backing** only for tools whose success reliably means the action happened: `notify_session`, `add_gtm_work_items`, `update_gtm_work_item`, `post_on_connected_account`.
- **Loose (ambiguous, never corrected)** for tools that can succeed without doing the thing: `send_gtm_status_report` (silent no-send), `create_html_file` / `update_html_file` / `create_html_from_template` / `create_social_media_posts` (an HTML document, not an image) / `perform_data_analysis`, knowledge-base and work-plan writers. The ledger keeps only a minimised result (`{}` for almost every tool), so `draft` / `duplicate_suppressed` cannot be checked; that is why these are loose.
- **Judge prompt** excludes negated, withheld, zero-count, drafted, quoted and historical statements, keeps this run's own recaps in scope, and requires a quoted statement. Judge `max_completion_tokens` 500 -> 800.
- **Guard**: ignores classes the prefilter did not surface and claims without a statement; tolerates class-name case/whitespace drift; counts dropped claims (`discardedClaims`) and logs them in `agentModeService`.
- `dev/pending` fragment with the findings and known limits.

## Evidence
- Replay of old vs new deterministic stage on 148 real prod runs (52 flagged + 96 control): matcher change alone clears 21 of 58 confidently-unbacked class flags; the new unbacked set is a strict subset of the old one in both sets; no regression; no newly-backed class where the tool result looked like a failure.
- The remaining ~37 class flags in 29 runs look like judge reads of negations or retold history. **The new prompt is not measured against a live judge** (needs an OpenRouter key, Harsha's identity). Before any enforce use: run the live judge-accuracy script on the 52 reply texts and the labelled fixtures with old vs new prompt, then a second shadow window.
- Tests: new `finalizeGuard.precision.test.ts` (30+ cases fail on main code); 134 tests across the guard, accuracy, characterization and ledger-mapping suites pass; wider affected run earlier: 390 suites / 7,085 tests passed (one fixture gained the `statement` the guard now requires); `npm run typecheck` clean. Pre-push hook green (jest budget raised via `AGENTWEB_PREPUSH_JEST_BUDGET_MS` because other sessions loaded the machine; checks not bypassed).
- 360 review: adversarial code review, tool-semantics audit against the real handlers, replay on prod data, and a final independent review (recommendation: merge; its findings on class-name drift, test gaps and an overstated doc line are fixed here).

## Rollout / rollback
`AGENT_FINALIZE_GUARD` and `AGENT_FINALIZE_GUARD_SHADOW` are both unset in prod; with both unset the guard block is skipped, so nothing customer-visible changes. The 800-token cap sits inside the judge call that only runs when the guard is enabled. Rollback is `git revert` of the fix commit (and its tests).

## Known limits
`post_on_connected_account` also succeeds for a LinkedIn `save_as_draft` and the ledger cannot see it; `create_social_media_posts` still strictly backs a "published" claim (pre-existing, follow-up); non-English replies skip the English-only prefilter unless they contain English nouns; real misreports the guard cannot see (a client report built from the caller's own account after every client lookup failed; invented account history) are groundedness failures tracked under ENG-2137.

title: feat(whatsapp): STOP moves the customer to no platform automatically (ENG-273)
body:
Linear: ENG-273

A customer who texts STOP now drops to **no platform** automatically; no admin step. This PR also closes the gaps that came with that.

## What happens on STOP
1. The opt-out is recorded (as before).
2. The account that holds the number is disconnected (number unbound, verification rows cleared). The opt-out row stays, so the number is blocked until START.
3. Approvals still waiting on WhatsApp are **cancelled** (marked rejected by `system:whatsapp-stop`). Nobody can answer them any more; the results they were holding are **not** sent. Older Slack-era approvals are left alone.
4. The owner is **emailed**: WhatsApp was removed, approvals are now off, how to undo it, how many approvals were cancelled.
5. The STOP confirmation is sent. A storage error before this answers 500 so Meta redelivers; every step is idempotent.

## Also in this PR
- **START reconnects when it can.** If the customer typed their connection code while the number was still opted out, START finishes the connection and replies "You're connected". Otherwise they reconnect from Settings.
- **Silence removed:** a tap from a number that is no longer connected gets a reply; an approval that cannot be delivered (502) or a failed delivery receipt for an approval emails the owner (at most once a day).
- **Support can see why:** the account record carries `whatsappDisconnect {reason: stop|customer|admin, at, last4}` (additive, display only, cleared when a number is verified). The admin Users list shows "Not connected (WhatsApp: customer texted STOP, <date>)", and a red note for an account still bound to an opted-out number (one that could not be matched at STOP time).
- A STOP from a number no account can be found for is logged as a warning.
- No change needed: lead alerts email first and ship notifications are additive to email, so an account with no platform still hears by email.

## Consequences to be aware of
- With no platform, **new** approval-required tasks have no channel, so the engine releases their output to subscribers unreviewed (the existing no-channel rule: same as a customer who never connected anything). The owner email says so.
- Cancelled approvals withhold their held results rather than releasing them: releasing would email possibly-unreviewed work because of one message. The customer can request approval again after reconnecting.
- Numbers verified before the phone→user index existed cannot be matched from the number; none exist in production (0 of 489 users have a messaging channel).
- The accidental-STOP risk is real ("Cancel", "End", "Quit" alone count). The owner email is the safety net.

## Customer-facing wording that needs Harsha's review
**STOP confirmation (WhatsApp):** "You're opted out. AgentWeb won't send any more WhatsApp messages to this number, and it is no longer connected to your AgentWeb account. Reply UNSTOP if you change your mind, then reconnect it from Settings in AgentWeb."

**START confirmation (WhatsApp):** "You're opted back in. AgentWeb can message this number again. To receive notifications here, connect it again from Settings in AgentWeb. Reply STOP at any time to opt out."

**Tap from a disconnected number (WhatsApp):** "This number isn't connected to an AgentWeb account any more, so that answer couldn't be recorded. Open Settings in AgentWeb to connect WhatsApp again."

**Email 1, subject "Your WhatsApp connection was removed":** you replied STOP, so WhatsApp was disconnected; the account has no messaging platform, so tasks that require approval deliver their results to subscribers without waiting for review; N cancelled approvals (results not sent, request approval again after reconnecting); how to undo (reply START, then connect again in Settings).

**Email 2, subject "We couldn't reach you on WhatsApp":** an approval request could not be delivered and the results waiting on it are on hold; usually the number can't receive messages from AgentWeb (blocked, number changed); check Settings or connect again.

Portal copy for the opted-out state is in `AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1255`.

## Tests
Affected family: 93 suites / 1,505 tests pass; backend and dashboard typecheck clean. The one failing suite, `admin.announcements`, fails identically on a clean `main` (it needs network). New tests cover: cancel/skip rules and failure isolation, the owner emails (grammar, no phone number, rate limit, never throws), START resume (single-use, expiry, Slack-in-the-meantime refusal), failed-receipt and delivery-failure notices, the unbound-number tap, and ordering/500 behaviour in the webhook. The pre-push hook's typecheck timed out on a loaded machine, so this was pushed with the documented `--no-verify`; CI is the backstop.

title: fix(finalize-guard): saved LinkedIn drafts and default-draft blog publishes no longer back a "published" claim (ENG-2459)
body:
## Why
The ENG-2459 precision change (#3496) lists a known limit: `post_on_connected_account` strictly backs `post_published`, but with `save_as_draft` it also succeeds, so a reply claiming the post was published passes the guard. The ledger result for this tool is minimized to `{}`, so a result check cannot see the draft. The adversarial review of this PR found the same false-backing for `publish_blog_article`, which saves a CMS draft unless `status` is exactly `"published"` (`emma/impl/blog.ts`) while the `publish_` prefix strictly backs `post_published`.

## What
- `FinalizeLedgerEntry` also carries the call's parsed `args`; the monolith's ledger mapping passes `tc.arguments`.
- `claimBackedByLedger` and `claimLooselyMatchedByLedger` skip a `post_published` entry that is a draft: `save_as_draft: true` (or a result flagged `draft`), or a `publish_blog_article` call whose `status` is not exactly `published`. The loose tier must skip it too, otherwise a draft would downgrade the claim to "ambiguous" and it would never be corrected.
- Header and `EXTRA_BACKING_TOOLS` comments updated; the sibling dev fragment no longer lists the fixed known limit.

## Not changed
- `create_social_media_posts` still strictly backs a "published" claim although it only builds an HTML file of drafted posts (pre-existing; listed in #3496's known limits).
- The guard stays off in prod by default (neither `AGENT_FINALIZE_GUARD` nor `AGENT_FINALIZE_GUARD_SHADOW` set); shadow/enforce behaviour is untouched.

## Checked
- Draft semantics read in `emma/tools.ts`, `emma/impl/linkedin.ts` and `emma/impl/blog.ts`; `extractMinimalToolResult` keeps `{}` for `post_on_connected_account`, which is why arguments are needed.
- Adversarial review (code only): no bug in the change. Checked that `tc.arguments` is the parsed object on every path that can hold a successful call, that `save_as_draft` is honoured only as a strict boolean (so the guard matches the tool), that non-LinkedIn drafts return `success:false`, that a real post next to a draft still backs the claim, and that `args` adds no new exposure (the same arguments are already persisted in `metadata.toolCalls`). Its one finding (the blog default) is fixed here. Code-quality review: stale comments and a loop-test mock that still carried `draft` in the result are fixed.
- Tests: 138 pass across the guard, precision, ledger-mapping and judge-accuracy suites on this head (earlier run: 815 across the related suites, including the groundedness grader tests). New tests cover a draft by argument and by result flag, a normal post, a published call next to a draft call, a blog call with no status / status draft / status published, and the argument hand-off through the real loop. Removing the `args` hand-off fails only the loop test (the untrue "published" text is delivered unchanged); removing the blog rule fails exactly the two default-draft tests.
- `npm run typecheck` clean; pre-push hook green on every push (jest budget raised through `AGENTWEB_PREPUSH_JEST_BUDGET_MS` on the loaded machine, checks not bypassed).

No flag change. Revert the PR to roll back.

title: ENG-112: heal legacy branches when their owner opens them
body:
## ENG-112: heal legacy branches when their owner opens them

Branches created before #3463 (2026-10-09..10-13) have the row-0 `branchOrigin` marker but no `branchedFrom`, so they are ungrouped, missing from `GET /session/:id/branches`, and a branch of one starts a new family root.

**Fix (self-healing, no backfill).** On `GET /api/agent-mode/session/:id`, genuine owner view only (not admin/delegated/share/MCP), only when `chat_branching_enabled` is "true", only if the loaded session lacks `branchedFrom` and its row 0 has a well-formed `branchOrigin`: derive the same `branchedFrom` #3463 would have written and persist it with one conditional update (`attribute_exists(sessionId) AND userId = :owner AND attribute_not_exists(branchedFrom)`). Returned in the same response. `updatedAt` untouched.
- Root = source's `branchedFrom.rootSessionId`, else the source itself; inline-message records are followed up to 10 record reads, cycle-safe. Record reads only, never message rows.
- Source must exist and belong to the same owner (archived ok), else skipped silently.
- Best effort: any failure is logged and swallowed; sessions that already have `branchedFrom` or are not branches cost nothing.
- Known limitation (accepted, pre-#3463 data only): with two legacy hops A <- B <- C, healing B first and then C gives one family; healing C first (root B) and B later splits them.
- A session whose source is missing/foreign/cyclic is remembered in a per-process set (max 500, cleared on restart, nothing written) so repeated opens do not repeat the flag + source reads.
- Additive attribute already owner-approved with #3463; no backfill; rollback = revert (stored values harmless).

title: ENG-2108 (A2): per-call funding and strict customer-key transport (dark)
body:
## What
ENG-2108 (A2), PR 1 of 2, the half that needs no OpenRouter Management key. `callLLM` now resolves the funding for each call and passes it to both the transport and the usage record. Dark in production: nothing changes until BYOK is on for an account AND a `CustomerRouteProvisioner` is registered (that is the key-dependent half, ENG-2383, not in this PR).

## Why
`callLLM` recorded and routed with the run's ambient funding. The approved model is per call (decision-per-call-provider-matched-byok-routing): a run can be customer-funded for a call whose model has a matching key and AgentWeb-funded for the next. Recording the ambient funding would mark an AgentWeb-paid call as customer-funded (or the reverse).

## Behaviour
- `resolveCallFunding` (`services/funding/callFunding.ts`): a call moves to a customer key only when ALL hold: the call opted in (`customerRoutable`, set only by the agent's own working loop, so helpers, scoring and judge calls stay AgentWeb-paid in v1), BYOK is enabled and the kill switch is off, a provisioner is registered, and the user has an active API-key connection for the model's lab (anthropic/openai/google; keys in the order added, then org-shared). The funding carries the connection, the owner as `fundingPrincipalId`, and the ordered same-provider list for A4.
- Fails closed: for a run with `fallback: 'stop'`, a connection-lookup failure or a lookup over 3s fails the call instead of quietly billing AgentWeb. Runs that allow AgentWeb fallback stay on AgentWeb.
- `ApiKeyTransport`: pins `provider.only` to the customer's provider with `allow_fallbacks: false`, drops AgentWeb's `ignore`/`order` preferences, never touches the platform client, and surfaces every failure as an error. `pickTransport` now refuses any route other than agentweb/api_key rather than sending it out on AgentWeb's key.
- On a customer key, fallback models from another lab are dropped (unknown ids are kept so they are rejected as on an AgentWeb call).
- `meteringCallerGuard.test.ts`: every direct caller of the AgentWeb metering rails is on a classified allowlist, so a new one fails the build until classified; plus a structural check that only the agent loop opts in.

## Not in this PR
OpenRouter key provisioning and BYOK teardown on revoke (needs ENG-2383); bypass paths (describe_video, image generation, coding agent) are PR 2; A4's fallback policy. Open before enabling a route: the `provider.only` slugs are unverified against live OpenRouter, and whether the `openrouter:web_search` server tool bills the customer's account or AgentWeb's.

## Verification
- Typecheck clean; funding, agent-mode and guard suites pass (5,000+ tests).
- Independent review: no way found for a customer call to bill AgentWeb today; 7 findings, all fixed except the web-search billing question (recorded above). Mutation tests on every routing guard, all caught.
- Live on the test instance (branch synced): normal Emma chat as test@example.com replied, the agent-task usage row incremented on the existing rails, the attempt journal stayed at 0, no resolver errors in the backend logs. A real customer-routed call cannot be live tested until a provisioner exists.

title: fix(eval): ENG-2226 creative-gates adapter reads structural checks only; harness grades only labelled cases
body:
ENG-2226 (epic ENG-2128). Two defects found while verifying the golden-set / validation tickets against prod.

## 1. `creativeGatesPrediction` used the wrong field
It mapped `gates.passed` onto `format_readiness`. Since ENG-2193, `appendCreativeGateChecks` recomputes `passed` over every check, including the advisory content checks (OCR text ratio / legibility, spelling, brand colour, logo, policy keywords). So a launch-ready image with a failing brand-colour check was predicted `format_readiness = fail`. Read-only check of prod `AW-HumanEvalQueue`: 71 gated candidates, 36 with `passed: false`, none of those 36 failing a structural check. Any validation of this grader would have been corrupted.

Now: fail when a structural check (`decode`, `blank_render`, `aspect_ratio`, `dimensions`, `file_size`, `aspect_fallback`) failed; pass when at least one ran and none failed; abstain when the gates were recorded as not checked, when every structural check was skipped (a skipped check measured nothing), or when there are no checks.

## 2. The harness graded every test-split case
`runValidation` called `grader.grade()` on all test-split cases, labelled or not. A prediction is only ever compared with a human pass/fail label, so cases without one cannot change the result, but the account-health adapter calls Meta with the customer's token for each case it grades. It now grades only cases with a binary human label on one of the grader's criteria, and reports `graded`.

## Tests
- 2 of the new adapter tests fail on main code (content checks ignored; skipped/notChecked abstain), the rest pin the structural-fail and mixed cases.
- New harness tests: unlabelled and `na` cases are never graded; any binary label on any of the grader's criteria counts.
- `runValidation.test.ts`: 26 passed; `npm run typecheck`: 0 errors. Pre-push hook passed (tsc/jest budgets raised via the hook's documented env settings because other sessions loaded the machine).

## Rollout / rollback
Offline harness and adapter only; no flag, no runtime path, no customer-visible change. Revert the commit to roll back.

## Not in this PR
The 50 `creative_image` golden cases predate the gates (earliest gated candidate 2026-09-25), so the adapter will abstain on all of them until the seed is refreshed; that needs a table write and is an OPS step.

`format_readiness` now uses structural gate results and abstains when none ran. `runValidation` grades only test-split cases with a binary human label on a grader criterion and reports `graded`. The author reports 26 tests passed and typecheck completed with 0 errors.

title: fix(hubspot): batched push updates by stored contact id instead of orphaning it (ENG-2171)
body:
## Summary
Fixes ENG-2171. `pushLeadsBatched` split leads on email alone, upserted by email and overwrote the stored `hubspot_contact_id` at Stage 3, so a phone-only lead that later gained an email produced a second HubSpot contact and orphaned the first. `batchEnabled()` defaults true, so this was the production path (and `autoSyncLead` takes it too). #3026 fixed only the per-lead path.

Email leads with a stored id (`syncMetadata` or `customFields.hubspot_contact_id`, as the per-lead path reads) are now updated by id through `batchUpdateContacts` (new Stage 1.5), with the email in the properties. **This changes the normal re-push path for every previously synced email lead**, not only phone-only ones.

## Failure rules (HubSpot documents none of these for contact batch update, so unknowns fail closed)
- **Gone** = 404/410, or a 207 whose every error category matches `NOT_FOUND` -> falls back to upsert-by-email; the new id replaces the stale one.
- **Anything else** (409 collision, 400, other 207, merged id) -> lead `sync_failed`, stored id kept, nothing created.
- **429 / 423 / 502 / 503 / 504 / no response** -> the chunk fails once; not bisected. A bare 500 is bisected, so one poison record fails alone.
- Duplicate stored ids with the same email collapse to one input; a lead sharing a stored id with a *different* email upserts by its own email (found in review: it was being reported synced on another lead's data). A no-id lead sharing an email with an updated stored-id lead adopts that contact (no read-after-write on an email just written).
- Kill switch: `HUBSPOT_PUSH_BY_STORED_ID=off` restores upsert-by-email (EB env var, needs a restart). `HUBSPOT_BATCH_PUSH_ENABLED` is left alone.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` clean; hubspotAdapter + hubspotService suites: 402 passed (23 new in `hubspotAdapter.pushLeads.storedId.test.ts`).
- One existing assertion pinned the bug (`c1` -> `c_a@b.com`); it now expects `c1`.
- 15 mutants of the change: all caught (one initially survived because the test mapping already included email; a disabled-email-mapping test now catches it). 407 tests pass across the hubspot suites; 28 are new.
- An independent fresh-eyes reviewer found no blocker; its should-fix items (shared stored id, bare-500 isolation, kill-switch casing, logging unclassified failures, documenting the stuck state) are fixed in the last three commits.

## Known stuck state
If a lead's new email already belongs to a *different* HubSpot contact, updating contact A with it is expected to be refused (undocumented, probably 409). The lead is `sync_failed` on every push, stored id kept, until the two contacts are merged in HubSpot or the id is cleared. Before this PR it upserted the other contact and orphaned A. Failing closed is deliberate; the kill switch is global, not per lead.

## NOT live-verified
No HubSpot was available: the only connected credential was dead and the production log has no `[HubspotAdapter]` line in 7 days (so prod exposure today is ~zero; it starts when a customer reconnects). HubSpot's docs are silent on the missing-id and archived-id response, batch-update atomicity, duplicate ids, email-collision status, merged-away ids and read-after-write; `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` is not in the docs at all (the existing deal handler matches it too). If the "gone" classifier is wrong, a deleted-contact lead shows `sync_failed` and stays stuck; it does not duplicate. Follow-ups: ENG-2464 (live-verify before a reconnect), ENG-2465 (`contact.merge` webhook, which neither webhook handler processes).

Merge gate: author is `mananv-argusoft`, so the owner merges (FOREIGN_OWNER).

title: ENG-2378: per-step model in Work Plans (work_plan_step_models_enabled)
body:
## ENG-2378: per-step model in Work Plans

Owner principle: every user and admin picks the model; the selected model is the only one ever used. No silent swaps, fail loud.

### Design
- Optional `model?: string` (canonical registry id) on `WorkPlanStep`: an **additive optional key inside the existing JSON `steps` array** of AW-WorkPlans. No migration, table, index or attribute. Owner-approved additive-key pattern. Absent = plan `defaultModel` pin, then account default (today).
- Switch: AW-Settings `work_plan_step_models_enabled`, exact `true` enables; default **off** = today's behaviour (writes drop the field with a `warnings` entry, launches do not copy it, the engine ignores it). 60s cache, last-known value on failed refresh, cold start off (same pattern as `compare_save_alternatives`).
- Whitelists: `WORK_PLAN_STEP_FIELDS`, `STEP_CONTENT_FIELDS`, admin merge builder, `createSessionWithPlan`, `applyPredefinedWorkPlan`, session step types, MCP schema; a source-scan test fails if a `WorkPlanStep` field is missing from the whitelist. Emma's LLM `create_work_plan`/`modify_work_plan` deliberately do not set it (model choice belongs to a human; modify preserves a stored one).
- Write (admin + user, create/update): `checkPlanDefaultModelWrite` semantics per step; unchanged stored value tolerated; new/changed must be served + selectable, else 422 `model_unavailable` + `stepCount`. Replace omitting a stored model is refused as content loss; blank `model` in merge clears.
- Launch (launchWorkPlan/accept/applyPredefinedWorkPlan incl. unattended schedules, createSessionWithPlan): ALL steps validated up front, 422 + `stepCount`, nothing written; unattended launch pages oncall.
- Engine (`generateSessionResponse`, `scheduleAutoWorkPlanContinuation`): current pending step's model beats request `llmModel` and session model (session model updated); retired mid-plan => plan PAUSES with a visible message ("Step N uses <model>, which is no longer available. Pick another model for this step to continue.") + oncall alert, no LLM call, never a swap.
- Concurrency cap, retries, autocomplete rounds, compare/branching untouched.

### Review hardening (second round)
- A write never erases a stored step model: switch off/unknown ignores a submitted `model` but carries the stored one (title, then stepCount for a renamed step) on admin, user, MCP replace/merge writes; `modify_work_plan` follows the step by title (not the stepCount slot); `save_work_plan` carries it; `/public/plans` no longer exposes step models.
- Switch state UNKNOWN (settings outage, nothing read yet) is not "off": stored step models are still honoured at launch and in the engine; only a definite off ignores them.
- Paused step is recoverable: an explicit `llmModel` on `/generate` (differing from the stored session stamp) overrides an UNAVAILABLE pending step model, runs that turn and updates the step; an available step model still wins over the picker. Without a pick the plan stays paused ("Choose another model in the model picker and send again").
- A step with no model runs on `workPlan.planDefaultModel`, then `workPlan.launchModel` (recorded at launch only for plans whose steps carry a model; additive session JSON), in interactive and continuation turns; the stamp is exactly what runs. At plan end the pre-plan model returns unless the user picked one (`engineModel` marker). Plan cancel has no mechanism in this codebase, so only completion restores.

### Round-2 hardening
- Carry-over matching is conservative ("a wrong model is worse than none"): unique title; duplicated titles match only the same-numbered stored step; a rename binds only when exactly one step on each side is left unmatched at the same number with unchanged content. Delete+rename, insert and ambiguous cases get no model.
- A pick on a model-less step stands across turns (the `engineModel` marker keeps naming the engine's own choice); a failed end-of-plan restore clears the marker once and logs.
- Share, conversable and anonymous-launch responses never carry step models or `launchModel` / `planDefaultModel` / `engineModel` (the launching owner's own client keeps step models).
- Known consequences (documented, accepted): with the switch off an admin cannot clear a stored step model; a client that always sends `llmModel` never sees the pause and permanently rewrites a retired step model to its pick; authenticated `GET /api/user-work-plans` shows step models of public plans to signed-in users (consistent with `defaultModel` today); a scheduled run paused mid-plan retries up to 20 verified-chat attempts, then the run fails and the next scheduled run re-validates every step model at launch.

### Round-3 hardening
- The picker PATCHes the session model before `/generate`, so the request model equals the stamp. A stamp that differs from the engine's last stamp (`engineModel`; before the first stamp the plan default / launch model) is the user's pick: it resumes a plan paused on a retired step model (the step adopts it, the marker follows), stands on model-less steps and in auto-continuation, and never overrides an available step model. Covered with the real `updateSessionLlmModel` + `generateResponse` handlers.
- Duplicate-titled steps inherit a model only from the same-numbered stored step with the same content; a new/empty step never inherits a rename match. Fuzz (200,000 cases): 0 erased unchanged steps; the 8 remaining wrong-model cases all involve two steps with identical (title, content) after a swap+retitle, which no observable can tell apart (documented).

### Round-4
- An interactive-share viewer's pick can run for the turn on a model-less step but never rewrites the owner's stored step model or the engine marker; on a retired step model the viewer gets the pause and the owner resumes. The first-step baseline (`planDefaultModel || launchModel`) is covered for Emma's pinned launches.
- Documented limits: (a) a stale picker echo (a `/generate` with a model different from the stamp, no PATCH) is indistinguishable from a pick (relies on the portal companion syncing the picker to the stamp); (b) a plan with later steps pending but no engine marker (hand-edited/legacy only, never created by the engine) has no baseline; (c) in the unique-title carry path the TITLE is the identity (a step retitled into a deleted step's title keeps that model, by design) and duplicates with identical title+content cannot be told apart.

### CodeRabbit follow-ups
- Submit-for-review and approve revalidate stored step models as a NON-admin launcher before the plan becomes available (422 `model_unavailable` + `stepCount`, state unchanged; only while step models are honoured).
- On a write, a stored step is the "unchanged" counterpart of at most one submitted step (a retired model copied onto a second step is validated as new).
- `workPlan.pickedModel` records a user's explicit pick during the plan (model-less step or an adopting retired step); the end-of-plan restore never replaces it.
- Switch states are documented: ON, OFF (a successful read of anything but `true`), UNKNOWN (settings failing with no last-known value: stored models are honoured; writes ignore submitted models and carry stored ones).

- `/generate` reports the model that RAN: `generateSessionResponse` returns the step/restore decision and `/generate` serializes it (requestedModel, effectiveModel, modelSelection, usage fields) instead of the request-level decision. The worker (and so the stored message `llm`) already received the overriding model. A paused turn ran no model and keeps the request-level fields.

### Portal contract
- `GET /api/agent-mode/model-options` adds `workPlanStepModelsEnabled: boolean` (next to `chatBranchingEnabled` / `compareSaveAlternatives`).
- Explicit `llmModel` on `/generate` overrides an UNAVAILABLE pending step model and updates it; the portal should show the normal picker when the step model is unavailable.
- Write/launch refusal: HTTP 422 `{error, code:'model_unavailable', requestedModel, reason, stepCount}`.
- Partner-portal admin work-plan editor gets a per-step model select behind the hint.

### Rollout / rollback
Deploy with switch absent (no behaviour change); set `work_plan_step_models_enabled=true` to enable. Rollback: set anything but `true` (nothing to migrate; stored values are ignored).

### Evidence
- Backend: 85 suites / 1811 tests pass (all touched suites plus the requested families); new: 3 backend suites + 1 portal helper suite. `tsc --noEmit` clean on the rebased tree; portal `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` clean.
- Mutation proof (each fails tests, tree restored clean): merge builder drops model, normalizer drops model, `model` removed from `WORK_PLAN_STEP_FIELDS`, swap instead of pause, step model not beating request, skip launch validation (createSessionWithPlan and applyPredefinedWorkPlan), skip continuation pre-check; second round: carry-over removed, explicit pick ignored, fallback chain removed, modify bound to slot, restore disabled, unknown treated as off, public plans expose models.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Adds optional per-step model selection to Work Plans behind `work_plan_step_models_enabled`. Validates models on writes and launch, pauses plans when a selected model is unavailable, and adds a model selector to the partner portal. Preserves stored models when the setting is off or unknown.
