title: fix(leads): a phone-matched merge only fills blanks, never overwrites (ENG-2123)
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #3569 (ENG-2123, phone-only lead dedupe, merged and live with the mode **off**). A live test on the real dev `PhoneKeyIndex` showed that in `on` mode a phone-matched merge reused the email merge and **overwrote stored data**: a blank-name capture replaced a lead's notes ("CURATED NOTES" -> "FORM MESSAGE"), and a capture merged into a hand-entered (backfilled) row overwrote its company and notes. This PR makes a phone-matched merge **fill blanks only**.

- `mergeIntoExistingLead` takes `fillBlanksOnly`. It is true only for the `on` lookup match and the `duplicatePhone` race-loser adopt. Every email path is unchanged (still overwrites with the newer non-empty value).
- Standard fields (firstName, lastName, phone, company, title, notes, linkedin) are set only when the stored value is blank. Custom fields use the new `fillBlankCustomFields`: an existing non-blank value always wins; blank and absent keys are filled. The attribution refresh (`lastTouch`) is unchanged.
- No behaviour change with the mode `off` (production today) or `shadow`. In `create`, the race-loser adopt now also fills blanks only.

## Cost / limits (also in the dev note)
- A repeat visit's new value for an already-filled field is dropped, including re-answered custom keys such as a step `stage`.
- Anyone who knows a number can fill blank fields on that lead; two merges racing over one blank field are last-writer-wins.
- A phone-matched repeat carrying attribution still reports `lead.updated` via the `lastTouch` refresh, as the email path does.
- `on` should still only be enabled after reading the `shadow` name-conflict and shared-line counts.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck`; 18 related suites / 345 tests green on the branch merged with current `main`
- [x] 6 route tests + 3 helper tests + an email-repeat guard + a `duplicateEmail` race guard; 7 mutants, all caught (including one that makes the email path fill-only)
- [x] Live on a dev preview against the real index (mode `on`/`create`): blank-name capture keeps curated notes; hand-entered row keeps company/notes and gets a blank title filled; stored custom field kept and a new key added; name-only row gets company+title filled by step 2; 6 concurrent repeats leave company/notes unchanged; email repeat still overwrites; create-mode race of 8 callers gives 1 row. Scratch data cleaned up.
- [x] Fresh-context review: nothing broken; observations documented
- [ ] After deploy: production check with the mode off (email, phone-only, bypass cases)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Phone-matched lead updates now fill only blank or missing standard and custom fields, preserving values already present on the lead. The same rule applies when a duplicate lead is found during a concurrent creation.
  * Email-matched lead updates continue to replace existing standard fields when incoming values are nonempty.

<sub>⚠️ Note: Your high-level summary instructions were not applied because this review ran without an available CodeRabbit seat. Ask your organization administrator to check seat availability.</sub>

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Opslane P1 on e0dc28d: not this change (smoke-test numbers use a different, pre-existing path)
Opslane's repro used `415-555-0192` and `415-555-0193`. Those match the synthetic smoke-test pattern `415-555-01xx` (`isSmokeTestPhone`). For those numbers the route (a) forces the phone-dedupe mode to `off` regardless of the setting (`webhooks.ts:779`, so "create mode" is irrelevant), and (b) gives the lead the fixed id `lead_ph_<hash>` via `phoneLeadId`; a repeat then takes the `leadAlreadyExists` adopt branch, which has always overwritten non-empty values with the latest submission. That branch is on `main` and is **not touched** by this PR or its follow-up (#3631).
- Real customers cannot hit it: `555-01xx` is the range reserved for fiction and the smoke test uses it on purpose.
- Changing that branch would alter the landing-page smoke test's read-back contract, so it is left as is and listed under "accepted" in the dev note.
- The fill-blanks behaviour this PR adds applies to real numbers (the `on` lookup match and the `duplicatePhone` race loser) and was verified live on those: a blank-name capture and 6 concurrent repeats left company and notes unchanged.

title: ENG-2271 WP7: destination verification and number provisioning tools
body:
ENG-2271 · WP7 of the hot-lead auto-call feature (destination verification + Twilio number provisioning, via Emma tools). Targets the feature branch, not main. These tools do not depend on the kill switch (setup can be done dark).

## What
Four tools (all require `org:configure`, org from the caller only, blocked in shared sessions, refuse unattended runs):
- `provision_hot_lead_call_number` — buys a US local number, persists `twilioNumber`/`twilioNumberSid`; one number per org; purchases capped at 2 per rolling 24h by a conditional reservation written BEFORE the purchase; first-month rent metered (`number_monthly_rent`); a lost race releases its purchase; ambiguous purchase failures are never retried and logged as possible orphans (sid only).
- `release_hot_lead_call_number` — turns calling off first, releases at Twilio, then clears (only a 404 clears locally); capped at 6 per day.
- `start_hot_lead_call_verification` / `confirm_hot_lead_call_verification` — a call to the STORED destination phone reads a random 6-digit code (inline TwiML, no webhook); only an HMAC bound to org+phone (domain-labelled, keyed with JWT_SECRET) is stored; attempts counted before compare; 10-min expiry; 2-min gap, 5 starts/day, 5 attempts; history survives confirm and phone changes; the verification call is metered (`verify` leg, 60s estimate). On success writes `destinationVerifiedAt` only if the phone is unchanged.
- `VoiceProvider.placeCall` also accepts inline `twiml`; `orgDb.getOrgById` has an optional consistent-read flag (additive).

## Persistent data (data-plane note for Harsha)
Two new system-managed org attributes, no new tables or indexes: `hotLeadCallVerification` {phone, codeHash, expiresAt, attempts, callSid?, startedAt[]} and `hotLeadCallProvisioning` {purchases[], releases[]} (+ existing `hotLeadCall` system fields).

## Cost bound and open gate
Worst case per org per day through these tools is about $2.37 (2 purchases $2.30 + 5 verification minutes $0.07). `confirm: true` is advisory only. **A2 — a human approval gate (deck-of-one, as in `crmSequenceActivationGate.ts`) for provision/release is a precondition for general availability**; it does not block an internal/allowlisted rollout because the caps bound the loss and the switch is off by default. Recurring monthly rent metering is NOT built (follow-up).

## Verification
- 814 tests passed in the last run (setup tools 100+, voice, toolDispatch, shareSessionRefusalSim, foundationToolOverride, metering guard); `npm run typecheck` exit 0; real `updateOrg` expressions verified on DynamoDB Local by the reviewer.

title: ENG-2110: Claude adapter for the login host (PR 1b-i, dark, no user impact)
body:
## What
PR 1b-i of the ENG-1816 subscription runtime (ENG-2110): the **Claude adapter for the login host**, built against a scripted `claude` so it needs no root. Design: brain `pr1b-claude-adapter-and-real-ports-design-v1.md` + `-v2-` + `-v3-amendments.md` (two independent design reviews). It follows the merged login host core (#3571).

1. **Core amendments** (`backend/src/loginHost/`): single-use sessions (one process per turn, because the bridge token and model are fixed when the CLI starts; a session counts against the caps until its process is really gone), any reported hazard blocks the connect (previously three named kinds; an unrecognised `other` got through), a turn that ends `auth_dead` parks the connection, a hung turn only kills its uid when no sibling session shares it.
2. **Runner hosting seams** (`services/funding/claudeCliRunner.ts`): injectable process / scratch / binary / env ports and `mcpDelivery: stdin`, all default-preserving. The bridge token reaches the CLI as the first stdin line through a host-owned wrapper (`deploy/claude-turn.sh`): never argv, env or a persistent file.
3. **Claude adapter** (`loginHost/adapters/claudeAdapter.ts`, `claudeParse.ts`, `services/funding/claudeLoginParse.ts`): paste-code sign-in (the code goes to the CLI's stdin only; success is confirmed with `claude auth status`, never by reading a credential file), status, hazards (`claude doctor`, fail closed on anything but the verified Pro/Max wording), logout, one-process-per-turn sessions, stream-json normalisation, auth failures confirmed with `auth status` before `auth_dead`, bounded event queue and line buffer.

## Impact on users: none
- Nothing outside `backend/src/loginHost/` imports the host. The only production files touched are `claudeCliRunner.ts`, `claudeLoginRunner.ts` and a new `claudeLoginParse.ts`; their only importers are the B3 sign-in service (the `claudeSubscription` flag is off for everyone: the prod `AW-Settings` flag row does not exist, the route answers 403) and the host itself. Runner defaults are unchanged (existing runner/login tests: 93 pass unchanged; all of `services/funding`: green).
- No package, lockfile, config or deploy change.

## Live testing: what was and was not done
**Done (real pinned `claude` 2.1.294, UNAUTHENTICATED, no credentials ever used; `CLAUDE_LIVE=1 npx jest src/loginHost/__tests__/claudeAdapter.live.test.ts`, 5/5):** logged-out `auth status` JSON + exit 1 parses; `doctor` works without a TTY (no hang) and its logged-out wording is refused (fail closed); `auth login` prints the real authorize URL and cancel leaves no process; a real turn through the stdin-config wrapper reads the MCP config (a stub bridge sees `initialize` + `tools/list`), prints "Not logged in", and ends as ONE failed result of kind `auth_dead` after the real `auth status` confirms; with an unreachable bridge it ends `transient`.
**Ready to run with a real sign-in (owner's terminal, hidden code entry; I never see a code or token):** `backend/src/loginHost/__tests__/live/claudeAdapterLiveAuth.ts` (brain: `evidence/scripts/1b-adapter-live-auth.sh`). It does the REAL paste-code sign-in through the adapter, then status/hazards (Pro/Max wording), a real turn (usage, rate-limit events, bridge bearer token delivered through the stdin wrapper), 3 concurrent turns on one home, interrupt, close, and logout through the adapter, with redacted output and cleanup always. **Not yet run: it needs the owner's login.**
**NOT done (needs the hardened unit: slices 1b-ii/1b-iii):** anything after a successful login (a successful turn, the Pro/Max `doctor` wording on the real binary, credential refresh under the quota, the real `rate_limit_event`/usage shapes), and everything about systemd/uids. The rest of this PR is tested against `fakeClaude.js` as a REAL local process through the real wrapper (pipes, stdin protocol, lifecycle exercised).

## Verification
- loginHost + funding suites green (incl. 40+ adapter tests with the shared conformance suite, 25 parsing tests, wrapper tests, a 150-seed randomized lifecycle test of interrupt/close/exit races, the 400-seed host invariant test now run half in single-use mode with a session-cap invariant). Typecheck clean; lint clean on touched files (3 pre-existing lint errors at the bottom of `claudeCliRunner.ts` exist on main).
- Mutation checks on every new guard; survivors documented in code (defense-in-depth windows a synchronous `spawnAs` cannot open; the epoch fence on an `auth_dead` result sits behind an earlier abort).
- Independent code review (credentials/concurrency brief): no credential leak found; 2 majors (hung turn with a live sibling freed its cap slot at once and was never killed; `onError`/`kill` semantics could report "gone" too early or leave an unhandled rejection) and several minors, all fixed with tests. A second, narrow DELTA review of those fixes found two bugs the fixes introduced (a kill could hit a turn admitted while it ran; the auth confirmation freed the cap slot early) and a weak wrapper claim (noclobber does not stop a write through a planted FIFO): all fixed with tests and mutants (admission is refused while a kill runs; the session's `closed` waits for the confirmation; the wrapper writes only into a directory it just created exclusively).

## Known limits (tracked for 1b-ii/iii)
Per-turn cold start (measure live); `abandonHung`'s kill is per-uid until the real per-unit kill lands (a hung process beside a never-idle sibling is only killed when the connection next has no live session, or on revoke/disable/reconnect/sweep); the fake CLI emits `init` only after the first stdin line and never produces `error_during_execution`; abstract unix sockets leak between customers on a shared netns and egress is open except IMDS (internal accounts only until PR 2: documented in the design).

title: fix(leads): phone repeat that fills nothing is not an update; same-named racers share one row (ENG-2123)
body:
## Stacked on #3623. Read this first about the file list.
The base is #3623's branch, but this branch also contains 12 newer `main` commits (drip suppression, secrets manager, other dev notes) that #3623's branch does not have yet, so GitHub shows ~21 files here. **Those are not part of this change.** Against `main` the diff is 8 files, all ENG-2123: `webhooks.ts`, `db.ts`, `phoneLeadDedupe.ts`, three test files, and two dev notes (one belongs to #3623). The change itself is these commits only: `b4181e14a`, `5ca037e59`, `1baf97410`, `ad106c93a`, `9fdf01783`. **Merge #3623 first, then retarget this PR to `main`**; the list then shrinks to the real diff.

## Summary
Closes two gaps left by the fill-blanks change (ENG-2123, phone-only lead dedupe; production mode is still **off**, and the production `PhoneKeyIndex` is empty, i.e. there is essentially no real phone-only form traffic today).

1. **A phone-matched repeat that fills nothing is no longer an update.** `isUpdated` for a phone-matched merge now reflects only what the submission itself changed, captured before the attribution refresh. The `lastTouch` is still saved, but the drip enrolment, CRM push and owner alert do not re-run; the response is `lead.unchanged`. The email path is unchanged (guard test: an email repeat with only a new touch is still `lead.updated`).
2. **Same-named submissions that conflict with the number's first row share one separate row.** Previously 4 Ana racing a Bob winner wrote 4 Ana rows (Opslane's P1 on #3569). The conflicting loser now takes the same exactly-once create with an id seeded by the normalized, delimiter-escaped first+last name (`phoneUniqueIdSeed`); a loser of that second race adopts the same-name row with fill-only after a consistent re-read, and falls back to an ordinary-id row if the winner is stale. Different names never share a row.
3. Review fixes: the name-seed delimiter is escaped (a literal `|` could collide), and a phone merge no longer stamps the defaulted `source: 'api'` onto a row that had none (which also caused a spurious `lead.updated`).

## Accepted, unchanged
A filled field's newer value is dropped; anyone who knows a number can fill blank fields; the smoke-number adopt branch still overwrites (synthetic numbers only). See `dev/pending/eng-2123-phone-dedupe-gaps.md`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck`; 18 related suites / 357 tests green on the branch merged with current `main`
- [x] 10 mutants, all caught (one survivor found and fixed with db-level seed tests; two more from the review)
- [x] Live on a dev preview with the real `PhoneKeyIndex`: Opslane's burst of 4 Ana + 4 Bob gives **2 rows** (was 5); Ana x3 / Bob x3 / Cara x2 gives 3; Ana Lee x3 + Ana Kim x3 gives 2; each row holds only its own data. In `on`: a repeat with nothing to fill + a new touch is `lead.unchanged` with curated values kept; a repeat that fills a title is `lead.updated`; an email repeat with only a touch is still `lead.updated`; the off-mode control still gives 8 rows. Scratch data cleaned up.
- [x] Fresh-context review: nothing broken; its two minor findings fixed and tested
- [ ] After #3623 merges: retarget to `main`; after this merges and deploys, production check with the mode off

title: fix: Zoma ad-account picker 403 (Origin: null rejected by CORS) (ENG-2559)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
In Zoma setup, anyone with 2+ Meta ad accounts gets the account picker. Pressing Continue landed on `POST /api/zoma/meta/select` → `{"error":"Forbidden"}`, so the ad account was never saved and setup could not finish. Zoma pages sent `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; under that policy browsers send `Origin: null` on a form POST, and the global CORS check in `app.ts` rejects `"null"` (403 from the global error handler, before the Zoma router runs).

Reproduced in prod: `curl -X POST https://api.agentweb.pro/api/zoma/meta/select -H 'Origin: null'` → `403 {"error":"Forbidden"}`; the same request with `Origin: https://api.agentweb.pro` reaches the Zoma handler.

## What this fixes (after)
Zoma pages are served with `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`. The picker POST now carries `Origin: https://api.agentweb.pro` (already allowed by the `*.agentweb.pro` CORS rule), and no referrer ever leaves our origin, so the Meta/Stripe hops still get none.

## Complexity ledger
+3 / −1 lines in `routes/zoma.ts` (one header value + comment), +15 test lines. No new moving parts: no CORS exemption and no new route. Behavior-preserving apart from the bug.

## How to test
1. Post-deploy: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST https://api.agentweb.pro/api/zoma/meta/select -H 'Origin: https://api.agentweb.pro' --data 't=x&account_id=1'` → **Expected**: 400 (Zoma "expired" page), not 403.
2. Run "get set up with Zoma" with a Meta user that has 2+ ad accounts → pick one → Continue → **Expected**: goes on to Stripe Checkout (or "You're set"), no `{"error":"Forbidden"}`.
3. `curl -sI` on any Zoma page → **Expected**: `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`.

## Edge cases to check
- Single-ad-account users never saw the picker and are unaffected.
- The redirect from the picker POST onward to `checkout.stripe.com` sends no `Referer` (same-origin policy strips it cross-origin).

## Test Evidence
- New regression test fails on `origin/main` (`Expected "same-origin", Received "no-referrer"`) and passes with the fix.
- `eng2496.zomaDeviceFlow` + `eng2303.zomaOnboarding`: 26 passed, 0 failed (on Atem, Node 24).
- `npm run typecheck`: clean (on Atem).

## Behavioral assertions verified
1. Picker submit is not 403 → root cause reproduced in prod with `Origin: null`; the fix makes the browser send the API origin, which the same prod request shows reaches the handler. Live re-run is post-deploy step 2.
2. No referrer sent to third parties → `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` is asserted in the new test.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/routes/zoma.ts`
- `backend/src/__tests__/eng2496.zomaDeviceFlow.test.ts`

## What was NOT tested
- A real browser submit against prod. Browsers setting `Origin: null` under `no-referrer` for a non-GET request is Fetch-spec behavior, verified here via curl rather than a browser. Covered by post-deploy step 2.

## Rollback
Revert this PR. The only behavior change is the one response header.

## Linear issue
ENG-2559

```text
Accountable-Owner: Harsha Vankayalapati
Accountable-Linear-ID: 142fef82-4d45-4070-99be-c5debe565ac6
Accountable-GitHub: harshmoney123
Execution-Actor: claude-code
Linear-Issue: ENG-2559
Automation-Run: interactive-session-2026-10-19-zoma
```

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(zoma): card on file + Manage Billing for non-subscribers; Stripe setup copy (ENG-2571)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
A card saved through Zoma's setup Checkout lives only in Stripe, so the portal showed Zoma users as **Free with no card** and Manage Billing returned **404**. The Stripe setup page explained nothing, a deleted Zoma customer blocked minting a new card link for 24h (idempotency replay), and Zoma readiness trusted a `has_payment_method` row flag that nothing clears.

## What this fixes (after)
- **One live resolver.** `stripeService.resolveUserPaymentMethod` answers three questions: is there a card on file, on which customer, and was it saved through Zoma. It feeds Zoma readiness and a new `GET /api/stripe/billing-summary`, which the portal uses. The response never includes a customer id.
- **Manage Billing for non-subscribers.** `create-customer-portal-session` opens the customer that holds the card. With no card anywhere it still opens the user's own customer, so a churned user keeps invoice history.
- **Stripe page copy.** The setup Checkout shows the approved line.
- **Deleted customers.** A deleted Zoma customer no longer blocks re-adding a card.
- **No data changes.** The user row is never written, and `subscriptionType` stays `Free`. "Pay as you go" is display-only and lives in the portal PR.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** +200/−47 in source (stripeService +90, routes/stripe +65, zomaOnboarding −20). The tests add +280.
- **Moving parts:**
  - Added: 1 read-only endpoint and 1 shared resolver.
  - Removed: `customerHasPaymentMethod` and the duplicate candidate loop in `zomaOnboarding`.
  - No new table, field, flag or dependency.
- **Behavior:** subscribed users are unchanged (tested). Chat is not touched.

## How to test
1. As a Zoma test user (card saved through the Zoma setup Checkout, no subscription), call `GET https://api.agentweb.pro/api/stripe/billing-summary` with the user's JWT.
   **Expected:** `{"hasPaymentMethod":true,"isZoma":true,"card":{"brand":"visa","last4":"…"}}` with no customer id.
2. `POST /api/stripe/create-customer-portal-session` as the same user.
   **Expected:** 200 with a `billing.stripe.com` URL. Opening it shows the card and an option to update it.
3. Run `zoma_status`.
   **Expected:** `[x] Payment method on file`.

## Edge cases to check
- Stripe outage → `billing-summary` returns 503 and the portal shows an error, never "Free".
- A non-subscriber with a row customer → if the card lookup fails, the portal still opens the row customer.
- A stale or unknown `stripe_customer_id` (`resource_missing`) is skipped, not fatal.

## Test Evidence
Run on Atem (swarm box):
- `eng2571.zomaPaygBilling` (20 tests), the `eng2303.*` Zoma suites, `eng2496.zomaDeviceFlow`, and all `stripe*` suites: **19 suites, 210 passed, 0 failed** (1 skipped is pre-existing). After the review fixes, the touched suites pass 96/96.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Each new contract test was confirmed to fail before its implementation. The portal-session fallback test fails when the fallback is reverted.

## Behavioral assertions verified (ENG-2571 contract)
| # | Assertion | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Zoma card reported with brand/last4 + isZoma | `1: Zoma card on a searched customer…` |
| 2 | Manage Billing opens the card holder | `2: unsubscribed user with no stripe_customer_id…`, `2: …different, card-less customer` |
| 3 | No user row write; Free entitlements untouched | `expect(mockUpdateUser).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` in 1/2; `subscriptionType` is never touched |
| 4 | Non-Zoma card → isZoma false | `4: card without a Zoma SetupIntent…` |
| 5 | No card / subscribed unchanged | `5: no card anywhere`, `5: subscribed user -> unchanged` |
| 6 | Stripe error → 503, never silent false | `6: Stripe error -> 503`, `6: any other customer-retrieve error…` |
| 7 | No customer id in the response | asserted in test 1 |
| 8 | Approved Checkout submit message | `8: the setup Checkout shows the approved submit message` |
| 9 | Deleted customer never blocks a new link | three `9:` tests (replayed key, lagging search index, stale row id) plus a concurrency dedupe test |
| 10 | Readiness live, row flag alone ≠ ready | `eng2303.zomaOnboarding` stale-`has_payment_method` test |

## Files changed
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts`: resolver, live-customer helpers, Checkout `custom_text`, idempotency chaining
- `backend/src/routes/stripe.ts`: `billing-summary` endpoint, portal-session fallback
- `backend/src/mcp/zomaOnboarding.ts`: uses the resolver; the row-flag shortcut is removed
- `backend/src/__tests__/eng2571.zomaPaygBilling.test.ts` (new), `eng2303.zomaOnboarding.test.ts`
- `dev/pending/eng-2571-zoma-payg-billing.md`

## Stripe search lag (Opslane run 925)
Stripe customer search lags new customers by up to about a minute. Candidate customers are therefore, in order: the row `stripe_customer_id`, then the user's customers **listed by email** (consistent; only those tagged with this `metadata.userId` count), then search. Zoma's setup Checkout always creates its customer with the user's email (`createCustomerForUser(userId, user.email)`), so a just-saved Zoma card is found immediately. Tests: `a card saved moments ago is found by email while search still lags`, plus `an email match that belongs to another user id is ignored`.

One case still waits on search: a customer created **without an email** and tagged only with `metadata.userId`. No Zoma path creates one. If it happens, the card appears within about a minute, once search catches up. The user row is deliberately never written (ENG-2303 / ENG-2571 decision), so there is no non-search id to fall back on.

## Rollback
Revert the PR. No data was written, so there is nothing to undo.

## What was NOT tested
- A live Stripe outage, and Stripe's eventually consistent search, against real Stripe. Both are covered with mocks only.
- Steps 1–3 above run in production after deploy.

## Copy
"Saving a card lets Zoma make changes to your ads. Nothing is charged today." was approved by Harsha in session on 2026-10-19 (the "Minimal" option).

- AC2 302 → 169.254.169.254 refused; 301 → host resolving 10.x refused; redirect onto :8443 refused; legit public redirect followed. Each hop runs scheme/port check + `resolvePinnedPublicAddress` (DNS-pinned connection).
- AC3 file/gopher/ftp/data and :22 refused before DNS; 2MB body cap passed to transport and enforced; 10s whole-fetch timeout.
- AC4 per-IP limit (default 5/h) refused with Connect message, no fetch, no partial result. AC5 global daily ceiling (default 200) refuses everyone, resets next UTC day.
- AC6 module import allowlist test (no db/mcpFetch/CRM/KB); handler context Proxy proves only `clientIp` is read.

title: AgentRun Inspector: step-by-step run trace for labelling and debugging (ENG-2587)
body:
## Why

The AgentRun Inspector is where a labeller checks whether a run did the task; the eval labelling page links to it (ENG-665). On a work-plan run it showed:
- no work-plan steps
- no tool arguments or results
- the final reply as escaped HTML, cut at 360 characters

These were buried in about 10 screens of boilerplate: 21 decision cards that each said "Chose X based on the requested action…", 5 identical flag cards, and two timeline rows per call with "Succeeded" listed above "Invoked".

## What

**Backend**: `GET /api/admin/agent-runs/trace?sessionId=&startedAt=&completedAt=` (`services/agentRunTrace.ts`)
- Returns one run's ask, its work-plan steps with the agent's notes, and the calls that served each step. A `set_work_plan_status` call that closes steps ends a segment; plan-management calls before any work count as setup.
- Returns every call's arguments and result. Failures are detected from the "Tool Error" text and linked to a later successful call to the same tool. Also returns the final reply and summed cost and tokens.
- Reads messages newest-first back to the run's start, capped at 1,000, so the latest run of a long session is always in the window.
- Caps and redacts every text field.
  - The explicit passes run on the raw text first: URL user:password, Slack/Discord webhook paths, auth schemes, and secret key/value pairs (including header style).
  - After that, URL paths, UUIDs and word-like names are shielded from the opaque-token pass, which only masks strings that contain a digit.
  - Reasoning and memory telemetry are never returned.
- `x-aw-agent-runs-secret` now gets a 403 on any sub-route, so the trace needs an admin session.
- The list endpoint is unchanged, because an external fetcher reads it.

**Portal**: `AgentRunsInspector.tsx` plus `components/agentRuns/`
- **Header:** states the status in words, telling "Completed · 3 failures, all recovered" apart from "Completed · 2 failed calls". Also shows steps done, calls, cost and tokens, and model, plus copyable IDs, grouped flag chips and a "Final reply" jump.
- **Ask:** shown once.
- **Steps:** collapsed by default, with their notes visible. Links inside them are clickable.
- **Calls:** one row per call that expands to arguments and result. Unrecovered failures start open, and there is a Failed filter and a "First failure" jump that moves focus.
- **Final reply:** sanitised through one module-level DOMPurify instance. Scripts, handlers and `javascript:` links are dropped, and images become links. The reply's links are listed above it.
- **Diagnostics:** gateway policy, argument repairs and raw events, collapsed.
- **Behaviour:**
  - `?run=` selects a run without re-running the search, and Enter submits the search.
  - Status icons have accessible names.
  - Brand red, green and orange appear only on icons and borders, never as body text.
  - The layout works at 390px.
- **Labelling page:** its link now opens the trace in a new tab.

## Review

Three design reviewers (information architecture, visual, usability and accessibility) reviewed the live page before the build and the built page afterwards. All second-round findings are fixed. Two of them were redaction gaps, found by running real secret formats through the code: `X-Api-Key: <uuid>` and `Bearer pat-<uuid>`. Both are now test fixtures.

## Verification

- Backend: `agentRunTrace.test.ts`, `agentRuns.routes.test.ts` and `agentRunsAuth.test.ts` pass (41).
- Portal: `AgentRunsInspector.test.tsx` and `EvalLabelling.test.tsx` pass (47). `tsc -b` is clean, and eslint is clean on the changed files.
- I ran the trace builder read-only on a real 21-call work-plan session. It put 6 setup calls first, then 4, 7 and 1 calls under steps 1–3, with 3 failures each linked to its recovery. The payload is 82 KB, with no over-redaction.
- I rendered the page locally against that data at 1366px and at 390px.

Also: `agentToolGatewayService.gaqlAdRelevance.test.ts` (from ENG-2581) failed backend `tsc --noEmit` on main (TS18046, args typed `unknown`), which blocks every push through the pre-push hook. A separate commit types its helper; no behaviour change.

Linear: ENG-2587

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
Risk: Medium

Adds a bounded, redacted AgentRun trace API and responsive Inspector UI. The trace exposes plans, tool calls, results, recoveries, usage, and final replies while excluding telemetry and restricting secret access. The portal adds filtering, diagnostics, URL selection, sanitised replies, accessibility support, and a new-tab labelling link.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: fix(v0): honour Retry-After on 429 and surface rate-limit exhaustion (ENG-949)
body:
Refs ENG-949 (partial: backoff + terminal visibility).

- 429 from v0 previously retried on the generic 2s/4s backoff, exhausting 3 attempts in ~6s against minute-scale windows. Now waits Retry-After (header seconds/HTTP-date or SDK body field), else a 20s floor; capped at 120s.
- Exhausted 429 -> err.code=V0_RATE_LIMITED + recoverable message.
- Non-429 behaviour unchanged. Same thunk retried, no new chats (no duplicate work).

Tests: v0Service.rateLimit.eng949.test.ts + services.v0Service + v0Metering.idempotency: 389/389 pass locally.
Open AC: provider quota telemetry / multi-page fixture within quota needs real-quota numbers (recorded on Linear).
Rollback: revert commit.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

Risk: Medium

Adds bounded HTTP 429 backoff using `Retry-After` seconds, HTTP dates, or SDK details. Delays range from 20 to 120 seconds. Exhausted retries return `V0_RATE_LIMITED` with a recoverable message. Non-429 retries remain unchanged.

title: feat(billing): month-end pay-as-you-go settlement via Stripe, dark (ENG-668 PR-2)
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Data-plane change: needs Harsha's approval before merge.** This stays a draft until that approval lands. Once the switch is on, it adds:
> - **New off-session charges.** A daily sweep makes at most one Stripe invoice per billing owner per month. It always searches Stripe by metadata before creating one, then creates it, fills it and finalizes it (`collection_method: charge_automatically`, `auto_advance` turned on at finalize). It charges the ENG-2571 resolved customer and payment method.
> - **New Stripe write: deleting a draft.** A draft is deleted *before* finalizing if its total differs from the recorded amount, or if it is an empty draft over an hour old (an orphan from a run that died). Nothing is collected either way.
> - **More than one live invoice for a month** means the month is held for a person; settlement never picks one.
> - **Void or missing recorded invoices.** If the invoice a record names turns out void, deleted or missing, the month is held for a person and never invoiced over automatically.
> - **New webhook branches.**
>   - `invoice.paid` / `invoice.payment_succeeded` / `invoice.payment_failed` with `metadata.purchaseType === 'payg_overage'` go to settlement. They never write `subscription_status`, `subscription_amount`, period or offer fields.
>   - A dispute on an overage charge suspends PAYG. Disputes are tracked by id, and the hold lifts once every dispute is closed and none was lost. A refund on an overage charge is recorded only: one history row per Stripe refund.
>   - Recognising an overage *charge*: for refunds this runs only while the switch is on; for disputes it runs always (rv5 MINOR 7: the switch gates new charges, not the handling of existing ones). A failed dispute lookup returns 500.
>   - `invoice.payment_failed` reads the invoice's default PaymentIntent. If it is `requires_action` (3-D Secure), that is not a failure.
>   - New subscribed event: `setup_intent.succeeded` re-points an open overage invoice that is pinned to an old card. It makes no Stripe call for an account with no open overage invoice.
> - **New AW-Users attributes (all additive and optional, no table or index):**
>   - `paygSettlements` (by month, last 12 months; includes `uncollectedInvoice`, the month's frozen `inputs`, `disputes.<id>` and `alertPending`)
>   - `llmUsageCreditsClosed` (only on accounts with a `paygOverage` record)
>   - `paygOverage.poolHighWaterClosed` and `paygOverage.optInClosed`
>   - `paygOverage.admittedMonths` = `[{ month, capHighWaterMicroUsd, tierPoolHighWaterMicroUsd, markupBps, spendBasis }]`
>   - payment history: two new event types, `payg_overage_payment_succeeded` and `payg_overage_payment_failed`. The webhook controller no longer writes `payment_succeeded` / `payment_failed` or the CRM mirror for overage invoices.
>   - `paygOverage.suspended`, now written by settlement (for a dispute hold it also carries `disputeId`, `lost` and `paymentFailedAt`)
> - **Credit-ledger rollover change.** For PAYG accounts only, the first write of a new month (`grantMonthlyLlmUsageCredit`, including the admin transaction, and `recordLlmUsageDebit`) also keeps the closing month as `llmUsageCreditsClosed`, in the same conditional write. Every other account's rollover is unchanged.
> - **Suspension writes.** A payment-failure event may set `paygOverage.suspended` only while the month's record says *that* invoice failed (`status = failed` and the same `invoiceId`, checked in the same write). Only the event that newly fails a month re-stamps it, and it never overwrites a dispute.
> - **Hand recovery of a held month.** On-call sets `paygSettlements.<month>.status = "retry"`; the next daily run re-measures that month from the inputs frozen on its record. `admittedMonths` keeps 13 months.
> - **Gate writes, from turn gates only.** Only `checkTokenUsage(userId, TURN_ADMISSION)` — a check that admits a turn about to run — writes PAYG state. Every read of usage (model resolution, the settings view, runway, drivers, `GET /usage`, the admin view) writes nothing. On the first mark of a month, the gate also writes `poolHighWaterClosed`. When a PAYG admission raises the month's cap or plan pool, lowers its markup, or is the month's first, it makes one conditional write to `admittedMonths`.
> - **PR-1 fix (dark).** An off→on re-measures the opt-in baseline only if PAYG has not already admitted anything that month.
>
> **Copy review also needed:**
> - The two owner emails and the Stripe invoice description are all in `backend/src/utils/paygSettlementCopy.ts`.
> - **New in rv5:** one paid-variant sentence in the invoice email ("Stripe has issued an invoice for that usage, and it has already been paid. The invoice shows the amount."). The 429 / portal `payg_suspended` copy is now worded per reason (`usageBlockCopy.ts`). Payment failure: "…because a recent payment didn't go through. Pay the open invoice to resume pay-as-you-go." Dispute: "…while a recent payment is under review with your bank. Please contact us to resume pay-as-you-go." No other approved copy changed.
> - **The cap is a monthly total** (product decision). Raising the limit during a month applies to the whole month, including overrun already admitted earlier in it, and no change after the month reaches back. The PAYG consent copy (in the customer portal, at the cap picker) must say so, e.g. *"Your limit applies to the whole month."*

## What this does

PR-1 (#3608) shipped the gate, the settings and the switch. This PR bills the overage once the month closes. It ships **dark** behind a separate AW-Settings switch, `payg_settlement_enabled`. Only the exact value `true` turns it on, and it ships off. While it is off, the sweep returns before reading anything, and the refund and dispute webhooks behave exactly as they do on main.

**Schedule.** `cron/paygSettlementCron.ts` runs daily at 12:00 UTC, after the 10:00 seat-credit sweep. It does nothing on day 1 of a month. From day 2, for each owner with a `paygOverage` record, it works the last 12 months:
- any month PAYG admitted in that has no settlement record yet (normally just the month that closed);
- any month still `pending`;
- any month set to `retry` by hand.

One owner-month's failure is counted (with the owner and month) and never stops the rest of the sweep.

**Rollout:** turn `payg_settlement_enabled` on no later than the gate's switch. An admitted month older than the one that just closed has lost its credits, pool mark and opt-in from the row. Such a backlog is held as `inputs_unavailable`, with one alert per owner-month and nothing billed, rather than billed blind.

**Amount: only what was in force *during* the month** (`services/paygSettlement.ts`, pure). Nothing written after month M ends can change M's bill.
- On PAYG admissions, the gate records M's highest cap (`capPercentOfPool` × that moment's pool), highest plan pool and lowest markup. The write is conditional and happens only when an admission changes the record.
- Settlement bills from that record, never from the cap setting or tier as they stand at settlement time.
- The overage uses `paygNetOverageMicroUsd`, the function the gate's `measurePaygOverage` now calls. It runs on M's own plan pool, credits, high-water mark and opt-in.
- Spend is the settled AW-SpendEvents total. It is reconciled against the persisted projection the gate read (`reconcileProjection`, 1 µ$). If they drift, the month is marked `held`, on-call gets one alert and nothing is charged.
- Billable = min(net overage, M's highest cap) × markup, rounded down to cents.
- 0¢ or under Stripe's 50¢ minimum → `nothing_to_bill`.

**Idempotency.**
- `paygSettlements[M]` (`pending`, amount fixed) is written with `attribute_not_exists` **before** any Stripe call. Only `pending` is ever resumed, and always with the stored amount.
- With no invoice id on the record, Stripe is **always** searched by metadata (purchaseType + billingUserId + month) before anything is created.
- Stripe keys are `payg:{id}:{M}:{record createdAt}` plus `:invoice`, `:item` or `:finalize`. They cover the search index's lag, and a record re-created after a cleared hold starts with fresh keys.
- The draft's total is checked **before** finalizing.
- A recorded invoice that Stripe reports void, deleted or missing (404) means the month is held. The record gets `uncollectedInvoice`, on-call gets one alert, there is no "invoiced" email and no replacement invoice. Any other Stripe error is retried by the next run.
- One owner-month's failure is counted and logged, and never stops the rest of the sweep.

**Webhooks.**
- Paid → `paid`.
- Failed → `failed`, sets `suspended = payment_failed` (PR-1's gate refuses while it is set) and sends one owner email.
- The suspension lasts while **any** month is `failed`.
  - Every failure re-stamps `suspended` (time and invoice id of the latest failure; never over a dispute).
  - A paid webhook lifts the suspension only if its read saw no other failed month, **and** only if `suspended` is still exactly the value it read. So a month that fails after that read, even one created after it, keeps the suspension.
  - A dispute suspension is never lifted automatically.
- A `held` record that carries the invoice's id can move to paid or failed.
- Dispute → `suspended = dispute`. Refund → recorded only; PAYG is not resumed.
- API version `2025-05-28.basil`: a charge no longer has `invoice`. The charge → invoice link goes PaymentIntent → `invoicePayments.list` → invoice metadata.

**Closed-month inputs.** The credit ledger, the pool high-water mark and the opt-in are each replaced on a month's first write. For PAYG accounts, each rollover now keeps the closing month in the same conditional write.

**Owner emails.** One when the invoice is created (the percentage of the cap and the Stripe link, never an amount). One when payment fails.

## Review fixes (bounded review at f64876c8e)

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|-----|-------|
| M1/M2 | The cap is read at billing time from M's admission record (highest cap, plan pool and lowest markup seen in M), not from settings | `paygOverage.ts:150,174`; `llmUsagePoolDecision.ts:159,259`; `paygSettlement.ts:145-184` |
| M3 | An off→on re-measures the baseline only if M has no admissions | `paygOverageService.ts:250` |
| M4 | The suspension stays while any month is `failed`; lifting it is checked in the write's condition | `paygSettlementService.ts:472` |
| M5 | Always search Stripe before creating; check the draft total before finalizing, and delete the draft on a mismatch; keys scoped to the record; the alert never says to remove a record that has an invoice; held → paid/failed | `stripeService.ts:549,595`; `paygSettlementService.ts:308,367,449` |
| M6 | The overage lookup for charges runs only with the switch on, and best-effort | `stripeService.ts:1461` |
| M7 | Closed ledger copy only for accounts with a PAYG record | `llmUsageCreditService.ts:206` |
| Follow-up | Resume any `pending` month of the last 12; per-month race test | `paygSettlementService.ts:92,116` |

## Final review round (at 48b48092)

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|-----|-------|
| R1 | A recorded invoice that is `void` → held as `uncollectedInvoice`; no "invoiced" email | `stripeService.ts:579`; `paygSettlementService.ts:364` |
| R2 | Every failure re-stamps `suspended` (never over a dispute); the lift is conditional on the exact value read; the per-month condition list is dropped | `paygSettlementService.ts:516,526,621` |
| R4 | A recorded invoice Stripe reports deleted or 404 → held + one alert, instead of a record stuck `pending`; per-owner sweep isolation | `stripeService.ts:273,578`; `paygSettlementService.ts:123,141` |
| R3 | The cap is a monthly total, stated where it is recorded and billed, and in the copy-review notes above | `paygOverage.ts:145`; `paygSettlement.ts:186` |
| Nits | Credit-balance wording; a single admission lookup with no casts (`paygAdmittedMarkupBps`); typed webhook and charge inputs; no unused destructures; the `evaluatePaygAdmission` doc comment back on its function | `paygSettlement.ts:56,140`; `stripeService.ts:544,1495`; `paygSettlementService.ts:67`; `llmUsageCreditService.ts:208`; `accountSecretRedaction.ts:89`; `paygOverage.ts:348` |

## Review round 3 (at d837a87e)

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|-----|-------|
| MAJOR 1 | A failure event may set `suspended` only while the month's record says that invoice failed (checked in the same write). Only the event that newly fails a month re-stamps it; a redelivered failure changes nothing. This also closes the race where a failure lands after the payment (P2). Disputes keep their own write. | `paygSettlementService.ts:600,679,705` |
| MINOR 2 | Every webhook ignores (and logs) an invoice the record set aside (`uncollectedInvoice`). | `paygSettlementService.ts:531` |
| MINOR 3 | Recovery is `status: retry`, re-measured from the inputs frozen on the record (`inputs`: credits, pool mark, opt-in, taken at first measurement). It works at any point in the 12-month window. `admittedMonths` keeps 13 months. The sweep also takes admitted months with no record; one older than the closing month is held as `inputs_unavailable` rather than billed blind. | `paygSettlement.ts:44,61,93,141,152`; `paygOverage.ts:163`; `paygSettlementService.ts:156,195,241,307` |
| MINOR 4 | The runbook is worded per case: void = finalized and then voided (check whether a payment was taken); missing; deleted draft; nothing created. It never says to delete a record. | `paygSettlementService.ts:443` |
| Nits | Sweep errors carry the month; the guard against a malformed scan row has a comment explaining why it is kept. | `paygSettlementService.ts:124,146` |

## Fresh investigation round (at cac2c9e1)

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|-----|-------|
| MAJOR 1 | The spend basis (`spend_ledger` / `legacy` / `mixed`) is recorded per month at admission. A month is billed only if it was measured on the ledger throughout; the cutover setting at settlement time plays no part. | `paygOverage.ts` (`PaygAdmittedMonth.spendBasis`, merge); `llmUsagePoolDecision.ts` (records it); `paygSettlementService.ts` (decide) |
| MINOR 1 | Lifting the suspension uses a strongly consistent read taken *after* this month's own `paid` write, then a lift conditional on the exact value read. Of two months paid concurrently, at least one webhook sees both paid. | `paygSettlementService.ts` `liftPaymentFailureSuspension` |
| MINOR 2 | Only a turn gate writes: `checkTokenUsage(userId, TURN_ADMISSION)` at the 11 turn call sites. Gate 2 and every read path get the same decision and make no write (`recordAdmission`). | `tokenUsageService.ts`; `llmUsagePoolDecision.ts`; turn sites in `agentModeController`, `chatbot`, `emmaTokenBudget`, `chatSocketHandler`, `modelCompareController` |
| MINOR 3 | With the switch on, a failed invoice lookup on a **dispute** errors the webhook (500, so Stripe redelivers). On a **refund**, the refund is recorded as before and on-call is alerted. | `stripeService.ts` `findPaygOverageInvoiceIfSettling` |
| MINOR 4 | Overage invoices are excluded from the controller's subscription payment-history row and from the CRM mirror. Settlement records them under their own types (deduped per invoice). This keeps the billing audit trail without the classifier, which models subscription health, seeing an overage failure as a subscription at risk, or an overage success masking a real subscription failure. | `stripeController.ts`; `paymentHistoryDb.ts`; `paygSettlementService.ts` `recordOverageInvoicePayment` |
| Orphan draft | In the search, empty drafts over an hour old are deleted, never adopted. If more than one live invoice remains, the month is held `multiple_invoices` with their ids. | `stripeService.ts` `issuePaygOverageInvoice`; `paygSettlementService.ts` |
| Nits | `createPaygOverageSwitch` is renamed `createExactTrueSwitch`; the 12-month window is computed once (`paygSettlementWindowStart`). | `paygOverage.ts`; `paygSettlement.ts` |

## Review round 5 (rv5, at d48442b56)

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|-----|-------|
| MAJOR 1 | 3-D Secure. Before a `payment_failed` fails the month, the handler reads the invoice's default invoice payment (`invoicePayments.list({invoice, expand: data.payment.payment_intent})`; Basil has no `invoice.payment_intent`, and an unexpanded PaymentIntent is retrieved). `requires_action` means the bank is waiting for the owner: no suspension, no failure email, the month stays `invoiced`, and the owner gets the once-only confirm email (whichever event lands first). `requires_payment_method` (a decline, or an authentication the owner failed) still fails the month. If the lookup fails, the webhook returns 500 and the handler never guesses. | `stripeService.ts:684`; `paygSettlementService.ts:797` |
| MAJOR 2 | Disputes are tracked by id (`paygSettlements.<m>.disputes.<id>`). A dispute already recorded closed is final: a later `created` (reordered, retried or resent) changes nothing, with no hold, no history row and no page. Closing is recorded once (`attribute_not_exists(...closedAt)`). A redelivered `lost` never re-imposes a hold someone removed. | `paygSettlementService.ts:847,900,953,998` |
| MINOR 1 | A won dispute lifts the hold only when no dispute on the account is still open. | `paygSettlementService.ts:1045` |
| MINOR 2 | Opening a dispute records it AND re-stamps the hold in one conditional write. A month failing under a dispute hold stamps `suspended.paymentFailedAt`. The lift's write is conditional on the exact `suspended` it read, so either race fails the write; the lift then reads again (up to 5 times, then 500). If a month is still failed, the hold becomes that month's payment-failure hold. | `paygSettlementService.ts:900,1045,1217` |
| MINOR 3 | A record with no invoice id accepts an event only for an invoice its own search would adopt (this record's key in the metadata, not void). A late `invoice.voided` for an old invoice is ignored and logged. | `paygSettlementService.ts:699` |
| MINOR 4 | Refund history: one row per Stripe refund with that refund's amount (`refunds.list({charge})`; a webhook's charge carries no refunds), deduped by refund id. Rows for $12 + $8 now sum to $20. `refundedCents` is only ever raised. The non-PAYG refund path is also cumulative and has no dedupe key; it is left unchanged and noted as a follow-up. | `stripeService.ts:698`; `paygSettlementService.ts:1166` |
| MINOR 5 | The 429 `payg_suspended` copy is worded per reason (`paygSuspendedReason` on the block). Payment failure: "Pay the open invoice to resume pay-as-you-go." Dispute: "Please contact us to resume pay-as-you-go." It never says "update your payment method". The 429 carries no invoice link on a dispute hold. | `usageBlockCopy.ts:85`; `paygOverage.ts:141,429`; `paygSettlement.ts:192` |
| MINOR 6 | Durable held alerts. `alertPending` is set in the same write as the hold and cleared (conditional on its value) only after the alert went out. The sweep sends pending alerts at its start and its own at its end, so delivery is at least once. | `paygSettlementService.ts:132,176,196,312,573` |
| MINOR 7 | Dispute webhooks (`created` and `closed`) recognise overage charges with the switch off. Only new charges and refund recognition are switched. For a non-PAYG charge the outcome is unchanged, at the cost of one more Stripe call. | `stripeService.ts:1546` |
| MINOR 8 | Successor of the invoice-id guard: the lift removes only a hold that a recorded dispute set (`suspended.disputeId` is one of the account's disputes), so a hand-set dispute hold stays. Tested, and the mutation is killed. | `paygSettlementService.ts:1045` |
| NIT | The invoice email is sent only by the write that recorded the month, and the claim is conditional on the state it describes. A failure or void that landed first means no "will charge your card" email. A month already paid (at adoption, before the run, or a held month paid later) gets the paid wording. | `paygSettlementService.ts:502,516`; `paygSettlementCopy.ts:55` |
| PINNED CARD | Chosen fix: `setup_intent.succeeded` (it covers the ENG-2571 setup Checkout and any other card save, and carries `customer` and `payment_method`). Each OPEN overage invoice of that customer that is pinned to another method gets `default_payment_method` = the new card (Stripe: an invoice's own method overrides the customer's default; it stays editable on an open invoice). Not chosen: "don't pin at settlement", because at settlement time the pinned card IS the newest, and that does nothing for retries after a later card change. The ENG-2571 `checkout.session.completed` branch is untouched. An account with no open overage invoice costs one row read and no Stripe call, and a failed read is acknowledged as before. **Ops:** subscribe the endpoint to `setup_intent.succeeded`. | `stripeService.ts:1618`; `stripeController.ts:158` |

**rv5 tests and checks:** unit `paygSettlementService.test.ts` 126 (30 new test blocks; the existing tests are updated for the new shapes); DynamoDB Local 74 (13 new: the reviewer's failing probes, plus real-DynamoDB races for MINOR 2); stripe-mock 48 (6 new: `invoicePayments.list({invoice, expand})`, `paymentIntents.retrieve`, `refunds.list`, `invoices.update default_payment_method` with its key, a signed `setup_intent.succeeded`). Touched-file suites on the final head `bc962959d`: 170 suites, 2953 passed, 1 failed (the known `agentModeController.conditionalSkip`). Both real-runtime suites on `bc962959d`: 122/122. tsc 0 errors. **Mutations** (unit + DynamoDB Local + stripe-mock):
- MAJOR 1: 3DS check removed → 9 fail; `requires_payment_method` treated as action-needed → 8 fail.
- MAJOR 2: a closed entry treated as open → 2 fail; the closed-ignore removed → 2 fail.
- MINOR 1: lift ignores open disputes → 6 fail.
- MINOR 2: no `paymentFailedAt` stamp → 3 fail; a second dispute does not re-stamp → 3 fail.
- MINOR 3: stale-event guard removed → 3 fail.
- MINOR 8: lift guard removed → 1 fail.
- Other checks: cumulative refund rows → 3 fail; no `alertPending` → 3 fail; re-point for any customer → 1 fail; email claim without its state → 1 fail.
- One equivalent mutant: sending the invoice email even when the run did not record the month survives alone, because the state-conditional claim already blocks it. With both guards removed → 4 fail.

## Review round 6 (rv6, at bc962959d)

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|-----|-------|
| MAJOR 1 | When a won dispute hands the hold to a still-failed month, the write is also conditional on THAT month being `failed` on that invoice. If the month is paid or voided after the lift's read, the write fails and the lift reads again. It then removes the hold, so the account is never held for a month that is settled. | `paygSettlementService.ts:1090` |
| MINOR 1 | Each new invoice's metadata carries its record's `createdAt` (`recordCreatedAt`). A record with no invoice id accepts an event only if the invoice has this record's key AND its `createdAt`, and is not void. The key alone is the same for every record of the month. So a redelivered failure, or a void, for the pre-`retry` invoice never touches the new pending record. An older live invoice that the run's search adopts becomes the record's as soon as the run records its id. I chose the metadata match over comparing `invoice.created`, because it is exact. | `stripeService.ts:301`; `paygSettlementService.ts:472,721` |
| MINOR 2 | The PaymentIntent status read on a reported failure maps to three outcomes, checked against stripe@18 `PaymentIntent.Status`. `requires_action` means action needed. `succeeded`, `processing` or `requires_capture` means the payment went through or is in flight: not a failure, and `invoice.paid` follows. `requires_payment_method`, `canceled`, `requires_confirmation` or no PaymentIntent means declined. | `stripeService.ts:709`; `paygSettlementService.ts:822` |
| MINOR 3 | `setup_intent.succeeded` re-points only to the customer's NEWEST attached card (`paymentMethods.list({customer, type: card})`). An older card's late event never moves the invoice back, and a detached or non-card method is never used. If Stripe refuses one update, it is logged, the loop continues, on-call is alerted once (`payg-settlement-repoint`) and the webhook is acknowledged. | `stripeService.ts:1654,1706` |
| MINOR 4a | There is no table scan any more. AW-Users has no `stripe_customer_id` index, and adding one would be a schema change. A SetupIntent tagged with the user costs one indexed row read. An untagged one costs one Stripe call (`invoices.list({customer, status: open})`), and each overage invoice is confirmed against its owner's record (an indexed read by `metadata.billingUserId`). The dev note's claim is corrected. | `stripeService.ts:1654` |
| MINOR 4b | A lost dispute gets its own wording (`paygSuspendedReason: dispute_lost`): "…following a dispute about a recent payment. Please contact us…". It no longer says "under review". | `paygOverage.ts:143`; `usageBlockCopy.ts:92` |
| MINOR 4c | `GET /payg` hides `openInvoiceUrl` under a dispute hold (open or lost), the same rule as the 429. | `paygOverageService.ts:110`; `paygSettlement.ts:203` |
| MINOR 4d | A pooled member gets "Your organization owner can resolve this." (`paygOwnerResolves`), never "Pay the open invoice" or "contact us". | `paygSettlement.ts:214`; `usageBlockCopy.ts:121` |
| MINOR 5 | A payment never confirmed. The first action-required report stamps `actionRequiredAt` (once). The daily sweep looks for a month still `invoiced` `PAYG_PAYMENT_CONFIRMATION_GRACE_DAYS` (7) days after that stamp. If Stripe still has the payment waiting or declined, the month becomes `failed` and PAYG is held (`payment_failed`, `unconfirmed`). The 429 then says "Open the invoice to confirm the payment…", and the owner gets one email with the invoice link. Paying or confirming the invoice lifts the hold. A payment that went through or is processing is left for its `invoice.paid`. | `paygSettlement.ts:171`; `paygSettlementService.ts:174,1177,1200`; `paygSettlementCopy.ts:103` |
| NIT | `findPaygOverageInvoiceForCharge` looks at up to 10 invoice payments of the PaymentIntent, paid ones first, instead of `limit: 1`. I used that rather than a `status: paid` filter, so a refunded or disputed charge is never missed. | `stripeService.ts:674` |

**New copy for review (rv6):**
- Lost-dispute hold: "…following a dispute about a recent payment. Please contact us to resume pay-as-you-go."
- Unconfirmed-payment hold: "…because a recent payment is still waiting to be confirmed. Open the invoice to confirm the payment and resume pay-as-you-go."
- The unconfirmed-payment email (`paygPaymentUnconfirmedEmailCopy`).
- The member line "Your organization owner can resolve this." was approved by the owner.

**rv6 tests and checks:** unit `paygSettlementService.test.ts` 140 (14 more: PaymentIntent succeeded/processing/canceled/requires_confirmation, the unconfirmed expiry incl. a late confirmation and the grace start, card re-point order, non-card/detached methods, a refused update, untagged SetupIntents, the old invoice's redelivered failure, the charge-lookup NIT); copy/gate tests for lost, unconfirmed and member wording, and GET /payg under a dispute hold. DynamoDB Local 78 (4 more: hand-over raced by a paid and by a voided month, the old-invoice failure on a re-created record, the stamp and expiry writes). stripe-mock 49 (1 more: an untagged `setup_intent.succeeded`'s `GET /v1/invoices` and `GET /v1/payment_methods`). On the final head `957653dac`: real-runtime suites 127/127; touched suites 170, 2979 passed, 1 failed (the known `conditionalSkip`); tsc 0 errors. **Mutations:**
- MAJOR 1 (hand-over ignores the month's state) → 2 fail.
- MINOR 1 (no `recordCreatedAt` check) → 2 fail.
- MINOR 2: in-progress treated as a failure → 2 fail; `succeeded` mapped to declined → 3 fail.
- MINOR 3a (re-point to any card) → 2 fail.
- MINOR 5: no expiry → 2 fail; grace period restarts on each report → 2 fail; expiry ignores a late confirmation → 1 fail.
- The rv5 set re-run on this head: all still killed. Three rv5 mutants no longer apply because rv6 rewrote that code; R2, R3 and R4 cover them.

## Review round 7 (rv7, at 957653dac)

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|-----|-------|
| MINOR | The 7-day unconfirmed-payment check reads the invoice first and acts only on an `open` one. If Stripe already settled the invoice before its webhook arrived (its PaymentIntent is then canceled), the sweep does what that webhook would. `paid` is recorded paid. `void` is written off, like `invoice.voided`. `uncollectible` is handled like `invoice.marked_uncollectible`. A deleted or unknown invoice is left alone and logged. The sweep never holds PAYG or emails "confirm your payment" for an invoice that cannot be paid any more. | `paygSettlementService.ts` `expireUnconfirmedPayment`; `stripeService.ts` `retrievePaygOverageInvoice` |
| NIT | A won dispute that hands the hold to a month which failed as unconfirmed keeps `unconfirmed: true`, so the 429 still says the payment is waiting to be confirmed. No copy changed. | `paygSettlementService.ts` `liftDisputeSuspension` |
| Tests | The reviewer's real-DynamoDB hand-over race is applied as given; it kills the hand-over mutant the fake store misses. The rv7 review's unit cases are kept, with their probes flipped to the fixed behaviour. | `paygOverage.dynamodbLocal.test.ts`; `paygSettlementService.test.ts` |
| NIT | The charge lookup pages through invoice payments while `has_more` (at most 5 pages of 10, paid ones first). | `stripeService.ts` `findPaygOverageInvoiceForCharge` |

**rv7 tests and checks.** On the final head `b24e93dc5`:
- unit settlement suite 176/176
- real-runtime suites 130/130 (DynamoDB Local + stripe-mock)
- touched suites: 170, 3015 passed, 1 failed (the known `conditionalSkip`)
- tsc: 0 errors

Mutations, all killed:
- expiry ignores a void invoice → 2 fail
- expiry ignores a paid invoice → 2 fail
- expiry ignores an uncollectible invoice → 1 fail
- all three together → 5 fail
- hand-over drops `unconfirmed` → 1 fail
- no paging → 1 fail
- hand-over ignores the month's state, re-run → 5 fail, now including the reviewer's DynamoDB race

## Deviations from the brief (all deliberate)

1. **`admittedMonths` is now a per-month record of terms**, as the review decided. It is also how settlement knows which months to bill.
2. **`poolHighWaterClosed` / `optInClosed`.** The brief named only the credit ledger, but both have the same rollover problem.
3. **Stripe keys carry a per-step suffix and the record's `createdAt`**, because Stripe rejects one idempotency key reused across endpoints.
4. **Below 50¢ is not billed.** Stripe would otherwise push the amount onto the subscription invoice.
5. **Extra `held` reasons:**
   - the owner was measured on the legacy counter
   - no price was recorded for the month
   - there is no live Stripe customer
   - Stripe's total differs from the record
6. **`resyncAllSubscriptionAmounts` skips overage invoices**, so an overage total never lands in `subscription_amount`.
7. **`UserPaymentMethod.paymentMethodId` (new, optional)** is used as the invoice's `default_payment_method`.
8. **A mismatched draft is deleted rather than voided**, because Stripe can only void a finalized invoice.

## Rollback

Set `payg_settlement_enabled` to anything but `true`. The sweep stops within ~60s, and the refund webhook goes back to exactly today's handling. Dispute and invoice webhooks for overage charges and invoices already issued keep being handled, so an open dispute's hold still lifts when it is won. A month left `pending` stays pending and nothing new is charged. If the switch comes back, the month resumes with the stored amount and Stripe is searched first, so nothing is charged twice. Invoices already issued are Stripe's to collect, and their paid/failed webhooks keep being recorded.

## Tests

Settlement runs over a fake AW-Users row that **evaluates** each conditional write (`__tests__/helpers/userRowFake.ts`), and a fake Stripe that honours and expires keys, can lose a response, applies a discount and deletes drafts.

- `paygSettlementService.test.ts` (65 tests). The review's cases are adapted into permanent tests:
  - rv3 probes:
    - P1: a redelivered failure between the paid webhook's read and the lift does not strand the suspension
    - P2: a failure that lands after the payment does not suspend
    - P3: failure, paid, dispute or refund events for a set-aside invoice are ignored
    - P4: a retry within the next month issues one fresh invoice
    - P5: a retry months later is re-measured from the frozen inputs
    - P8: the void runbook wording
    - also: a no-record older month is held as `inputs_unavailable`; a retry runs only once
  - a void recorded invoice → held, with no email and no new invoice; a recorded draft gone with a Stripe 404 → held + alert; any other Stripe error is still retried
  - one owner's failure doesn't stop the sweep
  - Sept paid while Oct is created **and** fails after the paid webhook's read → still suspended; a failure never downgrades a dispute
  - cap lowered after usage → bills the admitted 27000¢; cap raised after the month → 3750¢; plan or markup change after the month → unchanged
  - September and October both fail → still suspended until both are paid, including a stale read that only the write's condition stops
  - a discounted draft is deleted without finalizing, and after clearing the hold exactly one invoice results
  - a finalized mismatch found by search is held with its id, and the alert says not to remove the record; the paid webhook then records it
  - a held record with no invoice is never moved by a webhook
  - month-2+ race; resuming an older pending month
  - switch off → refunds and disputes are identical to main; switch on with a failing lookup → the refund is still recorded
  - all earlier cases: amount, holds, idempotency, webhooks
- `paygSettlement.test.ts`: settlement's net overage, pool and cap equal the gate's in 7 scenarios. Settlement is fed the admission record the gate itself wrote. Also: the merge only ever moves in the customer's favour.
- `llmUsageCreditsClosed.test.ts` (8): no PAYG record → no closed copy (grant, debit and admin transaction).
- `subscription.payg.test.ts`: off→on after admission keeps the carried-over baseline, the gate refuses at the cap, and settlement bills ≤ the cap; with no admission, a fresh baseline is still measured.
- `paygOverage.gates.test.ts`: the gate's admission-record writes (first of the month, a higher cap raises it, a lower one never lowers it, a lost race).
- **Mutation checks** (each fix reverted in turn, then restored):
  - M1/M2 → 2 fail
  - M3 → 1 fail
  - M4 (snapshot check and write condition) → fail, and the write condition alone → fail
  - M5 → 2 fail
  - M6 → 2 fail
  - M7 → 1 fail
  - pending resume → 1 fail
  - final round: R1 (void treated as issued) → 1 fail; R2 (no re-stamp) → 4 fail; R2 (lift not conditional on the exact value) → 2 fail; R4 (404 rethrown) → 1 fail
  - rv3:
    - MAJOR 1 (re-stamp on every event) → 1 fail; MAJOR 1 (suspension not conditional on the month's status) → 5 fail
    - MINOR 2 (set-aside invoice not ignored) → 1 fail
    - MINOR 3: retry not swept → 2 fail; retry measured from the row → 1 fail; admitted months kept = 2 → 1 fail; an older no-record month billed from the row → 1 fail
- rv4 tests:
  - spend basis in both directions, and the gate recording legacy → mixed
  - concurrent paid webhooks lifting the suspension
  - gate 2, the settings view, the runway and an unflagged `checkTokenUsage` making no write
  - a dispute lookup failure errors the webhook and the redelivery suspends; a refund lookup failure records the refund and alerts
  - controller exclusion of overage invoices, plus the `payg_overage_payment_*` rows
  - orphan drafts deleted, in-flight drafts kept, two live invoices held
- rv4 mutation checks:
  - MAJOR 1: settlement check removed → 2 fail; gate always records ledger → 1 fail
  - MINOR 1: lift decided on the pre-write read → 4 fail
  - MINOR 2: reads write again → 5 fail
  - MINOR 3: dispute lookup failure swallowed → 1 fail
  - MINOR 4: controller records the overage as a subscription payment → 1 fail
  - multiple invoices adopted → 1 fail
- Touched suites: **21 suites, 436 tests, all pass.**
- Related run on the merged tree (every test file importing a module this PR changes, `db.ts` excepted): **239 suites, 4121 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed.** The one failure is the known pre-existing `agentModeController.conditionalSkip` registry drift guard, which this PR does not touch.
- eslint: no errors on any line this PR adds. The new files are fully clean. The 2 `no-explicit-any` errors in `stripeService.ts` are fixed, and one justified `eslint-disable` remains for the loose test-row type in `helpers/userRowFake.ts`.
- `tsc --noEmit`: **0 errors** on the branch after merging current `origin/main` (main fixed the 6 errors that used to be there).
- Merged `origin/main` (121 commits). The only conflict was an import line in `emailService.ts`; both sides were kept. Main's one new `checkTokenUsage` caller (the shared-session model pre-flight) is a read, so it correctly passes no admission flag.

## Follow-ups (known, not fixed here)

- (rv6 NIT 3) While a re-created (`retry`) record has no invoice id yet, a `payment_failed` for the older invoice is ignored; the run then adopts that invoice as `invoiced` (not `failed`), so it relies on Stripe's next failure event. The window is milliseconds unless a run crashes partway.
- (rv6 NIT 2) The 7-day unconfirmed-payment check is part of the settlement sweep, so it does not run while `payg_settlement_enabled` is off. While the switch is off, a payment that is never confirmed never puts PAYG on hold.

- A closed high-water mark can be stale if one check raises it in the last instant of a month while another rolls it over.
- A higher mark lost to a month-change race is only saved at the next check.
- `paymentMethodId` can be a non-card default.
- `mrrCollectionGapService` counts paid overage invoices as "has ever paid".
- The non-PAYG refund path records the charge's cumulative `amount_refunded` and has no dedupe key. This is pre-existing and unchanged.
- An overage invoice the owner never authenticates (3-D Secure) stays open, and PAYG stays on, until Stripe marks it uncollectible. Set Billing → "Manage failed payments" to mark invoices uncollectible after the last retry.
- A refund of a closed month's top-up after the month ends is not reflected in `llmUsageCreditsClosed`. This errs toward billing less, never more.
- The existing subscription invoice handlers still read `invoice.subscription`, which Basil moved under `parent.subscription_details`. This is pre-existing.
- `capHighWaterMicroUsd` includes revocable top-up credit in the pool it is a percentage of, while the pool high-water mark excludes it. This is inconsistent, but stays within the consent the owner gave at the time.
- The gate records the admission month with `getCurrentUsageMonth()`, while its caller's billing month comes from `getCurrentMonth()`. They are identical on the UTC fleet, so this only matters at a UTC boundary; it is pre-existing.

title: fix(leads): a blank optional custom field no longer makes a phone repeat an update (ENG-2123)
body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #3631 (ENG-2123, phone-only lead dedupe; production mode is still **off**). Opslane's re-run on that PR (run 863, P2) found that a phone-matched repeat which only adds **blank optional custom fields** was reported as `lead.updated`, so it still re-ran drip enrolment, the CRM push and the `api.lead_updated` alert. That is exactly what "a repeat that fills nothing is not an update" was supposed to prevent.

- **Cause:** `fillBlankCustomFields` added a key that was absent from the stored lead even when the incoming value was blank, which changed the merged map and flipped `fieldsChanged`.
- **Fix:** one line. A blank incoming value (empty, whitespace, null, undefined) never adds a key. `0` and `false` are real values and still fill an absent key. The attribution refresh is still saved.
- **Scope:** the phone-matched merge only. The email path does not use this helper and is unchanged (live guard below).

## Not changed, on purpose (the other P2 from the same run)
The org-level "New lead" Slack/email message is sent for **every accepted repeat form submission**, even when it merges into an unchanged row. `webhooks.ts` says so in a comment, it applies to email repeats as well, and it is separate from the update flag, which gates drip enrolment, the external CRM push and the `api.lead_updated` owner alert. Changing it is a product call for the owner; it is written up in the dev note.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run typecheck`; 18 related suites / 363 tests green
- [x] 2 new tests failed on the old code and pass now (helper + route); the mutant that restores the removed branch fails exactly those 2; file restore verified
- [x] Live on a dev preview with the real `PhoneKeyIndex` (mode `on`): repeat with only blank optional fields => `lead.unchanged`, no new keys, `lastTouch` saved; a repeat that fills a field => `lead.updated`; a repeat trying to overwrite filled values => `lead.unchanged`, values kept; an email repeat with a blank optional field still adds it and is `lead.updated` (unchanged). Scratch data cleaned up.
- [ ] After deploy: production check with the mode off (email, phone-only, bypass cases)

title: ENG-2110: real ports + host main for the login host (PR 1b-ii, dark, no user impact)
body:
## ENG-2110 PR 1b-ii: real filesystem/process ports + host main (DARK, no user impact)

Adds the real operating-system side of the login host. **Nothing imports it from the backend; no flag, route, or deploy step changes. Zero user impact.**

### What it adds (all under `backend/src/loginHost/`)
- `ports/`: `SystemdUserFs` (the core's `UserFsPort`). Each customer process is a hardened transient systemd unit: root unit + `setpriv` drop to the customer's numeric uid, private `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, shared parent masked, namespaces/address families/syscalls restricted, IMDS blocked, memory/task/runtime limits. Per-uid kill (slice stop, per-unit kill, stray sweep, wait for queued start jobs), wipe (refused while any unit/client exists), residue scan, per-uid quota, atomic promote by a single `rename`.
- `host/`: closed config schema, per-env uid-range registry (+ `/etc/subuid` check), pinned-binary verification (root-owned path, sha256), startup checks (homes on its own `nosuid,nodev,usrquota` mount, root only), `main` (stop env units -> state lock -> recover -> listen).
- `deploy/`: unit template, slice/config examples, install checklist, `aw-write-file.sh`.

### How it was checked
- 655 loginHost tests (incl. a 300-seed sequence/invariant test over an in-memory OS, real shell tests of the write helper, and an end-to-end test over a real unix socket: real core + real port).
- Two independent security reviews of the ports; a working-directory symlink escape (found by replaying on a real instance) and a "kill the client" race were fixed with tests and mutants.

### Honest limits
- Sandbox properties were verified by probes on the test instance, but this code path was **not** run on real systemd until the test-instance live run (comment below).
- Egress is open except IMDS, and abstract unix sockets leak across customers on a shared netns: **internal accounts only until the network-isolation PR**.
- The Claude-side terms question is a separate gate (see Harsha call 2026-10-19).

title: [ENG-2591] agent-task-success grader: stop trusting step checkmarks (kappa 0.20 in trial)
body:
Linear: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2591/agent-task-success-grader-stop-trusting-step-checkmarks-kappa-020-in

## Problem

`gradeTaskSuccess` (`backend/src/loops/eval/agentGraders.ts`) returns success when every step is completed (one trailing pending step allowed) and each step's `requiredFunctionCalls` succeeded. It trusts the agent's own step checkmarks and never looks at failed deliverable calls, the user's last request, explicit constraints, or steps closed with no work. An AI trial run (2026-10-20) on the 40 test-split work-plan cases showed 62% agreement with AI judges, kappa 0.20 (bar: 0.6).

## What to change (deterministic first)

- Fail when a call that produces or delivers something (send/publish/create/generate/export tools, from the tool registry's effect metadata) failed and no later call to the same tool succeeded.
- Fail when a completed step's segment holds only status updates, or only failed calls. The trace builder (`services/agentRunTrace.ts`) already does this step attribution and could be shared.
- Do not fail on pending steps that come after a follow-up which changed the request. This needs the follow-up asks in the input; consider an LLM-judge criterion for "last request met", rather than rules.

## Acceptance criteria

- The same trial, re-run in about 10 minutes from the scratch scripts (blind AI judges, then a comparison), shows kappa ≥ 0.6 on the 40 cases.
- Only then do we ask a person to label 30 cases for the real validation (ENG-665's goal).

---
Note: Linear (ENG-2591) is the source of truth. Please do not open a PR against the private repo from this mirror; external contributors should comment here for guidance on how to contribute.

title: fix: one approval for verified paused Meta ad bundles
body:
## Acceptance criteria
- One explicit review card covers an exact paused campaign, ad set, objective, budget, audience, and all requested creatives; approval executes that bundle without per-object approvals.
- A user request for three ads cannot silently become a two-ad build. Creative IDs must be accessible in the selected account and preflight their readable copy; placeholder text or changed creative content stops creation.
- Created objects are read back; count, budget, audience and other material drift cannot be called complete. Partial builds report IDs and verified count without blind retry.
- PAUSED creation never authorizes activation or spend; ACTIVE updates retain their separate approval.

## Implementation
New CREATE_PAUSED_BUNDLE action uses the existing durable write manifest and approval-deck workflow. Exact brief, count and creative snapshots bind the dispatch; workflow checkpoint returns created IDs and verification result.

- Pre-push Jest: 192 suites / 4,110 tests pass.

## Not tested

- Revert this PR to remove the new action; existing Meta CRUD remains unchanged.

## What
