title: feat(models): tell owners when a schedule or plan step's model is outside their plan (ENG-669 PR-D)
feat(models): AgentWeb Model router behind a switch (ENG-669 PR-C)
body:
## What

ENG-669 PR-C (backend only): **AgentWeb Model**, a selectable model id (`agentweb-model`) that AgentWeb routes to a concrete model per task. Dark behind AW-Settings `agentweb_model_router_enabled` (exact `'true'`); off = byte-identical to main. Builds on PR-A (#3607, tier allowlist, which already reserves the id) and ENG-2378 (per-step models).

Decided design (Linear): picking it is picking the router, so routing is not a swap; v0 = deterministic table, task type -> model; the concrete model and reason are logged and stored per run; a routed-model failure is a visible error, no retry on another model; not the default for anyone in this PR.

## How

- `services/agentMode/agentWebModelRouter.ts` (pure) + `agentWebModelRouterInstance.ts` (wiring)
  - Table `agentweb_model_routing_table` (JSON: `version`, `default`, `routes` per task type, `tiers` overrides), validated on every load **per tier** so one bad entry cannot take the router from every customer:
    - unparseable / missing / unreadable table: unavailable for everyone (`agentweb_model_router:unavailable` alert);
    - an unusable target (unregistered, admin-only / internal-only / live, unpriced, not tool-capable): only the routes resolving to it are unavailable (never falls through to another rule), alert per model;
    - a tier that may select the router but whose PR-A allowlist misses its resolved routes: unavailable for **that tier only**, alert per tier naming the models; other tiers keep routing;
    - an override key naming no configured tier: reported, nothing taken down.
    Unavailable = 422 `model_unavailable`/`not_served` on selection, alerts deduped 1h. 60s cache, last good table kept on a failed read.
  - Task type v0 = the session kind PR-A's system-default exemption already distinguishes (`taskTypeForSession`): `chat`, `scheduled`, `report`, `image`, `video`, `support`. No classifier.
- `resolveEffectiveModelForUser`: the SELECTION is tier-checked (PR-A gate on `agentweb-model`); the routed model is resolved with `modelSource: 'system'` (exempt as a pick), no backup, no silent swap. Paused accounts keep the plain `blocked` decision.
- Stored = the selection, never the routed model, at every write site: createSession, /generate, verified-generate, interactive share, conversable, scheduled runs, branch, step-engine stamps + `engineModel`/`pickedModel` markers + adopted step model.
- Stored decision adds `routedVia`, `routingReason`, `tableVersion`; /generate + createSession responses echo them. Assistant messages add `llmSelected`, `llmRoutingReason`, `llmRoutingTableVersion` beside the concrete `llm` (passed to the worker as plain `modelRouting` data).
- `generateSessionResponse` routes a stored selection for side channels (Slack/transports, email, approval resumes, GTM, continuations) before anything is persisted; refused (422-class) when the switch is off.
- `validateModelPin` (schedules, plan default, step pins, launches), session PATCH and shared PATCH accept it when the router is available and the owner's plan includes it. `/model-options` and `/public/llm-models` offer it only to tiers it is currently valid for.
- A failed tier read while routing (the router reads the tier even with the allowlist off) alerts as "AgentWeb Model router could not read a subscription tier"; the allowlist wording is kept only when the allowlist is on.
- Compare refuses it as a column: 400 `agentweb_model_not_comparable`.
- No `fallbackModels` anywhere on the chat path (verified: only deepResearchService passes them).
- Dev note: `dev/pending/eng-669-agentweb-model-router.md` (switch, table shape + example, seeding, rollback).

## Deviations from the brief (deliberate)

1. **Picker position is index 1, not first.** The customer portal pre-selects `supportedLlmModels[0]` (`useAgentModeSettings.ts:127/134/141`, `ChatInputBar.tsx:930`), so a first entry would make the router everyone's default, which the decision defers (AC3). It goes right after the configured default.
2. **Switch-off PATCH stays 400** ("Unsupported model"), because that is what an unknown id gets on main; turns/schedules get the standard 422 `not_served`.
3. PR-A's dev-note example of narrowing Free to `["agentweb-model"]` alone makes the router unavailable for Free (its routes are outside its plan): Free must also list the routed models. Called out in the dev note.

## Tests

- `agentWebModelRouter.test.ts` (36): every validation constraint, precedence, per-tier checks, switch/table caching, unparseable => everyone unavailable + one alert, unusable target => only its routes, narrowed tier => only that tier, last-known table, route outside live allowlist, helpers, real-registry catalog.
- `agentModeController.agentWebModelRouter.test.ts` (29): narrowing one tier refuses only that tier while Pro/Team route; an unusable target on one route refuses only that route; unparseable table refuses every tier; pickers offer only to valid tiers; tier-read alert wording with the allowlist off; switch off identical to main (same 422 body as an unknown id, PATCH 400, not offered, no table read, no router read for other models); selection stored at every write site; tier check on the selection; routed model exempt; invalid table => 422 + one alert even for stored-only turns; side channels; stale decision stamps nothing; PATCH; pickers; step models: step pinned to the router (write/launch/off), concrete session running a router step (no false pick on echo), router session running concrete step pins (pin, route again, restore), user pick of the router on a model-less step.
- `agentModeService.agentWebModelStamp.test.ts` (3): message carries `llm` + `llmSelected` + reason; only the routed model is called, no `fallbackModels`.
- Additions to `modelComparison.test.ts`, `chatBranching.routes.test.ts`, `agentModeController.scheduledModelUnavailable.test.ts` (Compare exclusion, branch keeps selection, scheduled run).
- Mutation checks (each caught, then restored): /generate storing the routed model; selection not tier-checked; engine marker recording the routed model; tier check not applied at load; per-tier isolation (a tier's unavailability applied globally; an unusable target applied globally; the picker ignoring the tier).

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: clean on the current head (backend; also partner-portal `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json`).
- Review round: touched suites 28/28, 982/982 passed; 5 mutation checks on MAJOR 1–4 all caught (tier name in the reason; viewers keep the routing fields; stored selection corrected when off; per-schedule page; malformed tier made global).
- Related run after the review round: 808 suites, 14,332 tests, 3 failures. `conditionalSkip` and `mcp.scheduledChatTools` are known pre-existing failures. `sdkConstructionGuard` fails on a stale allowlist entry for `services/videoGeneration.ts`, which this PR doesn't touch.
- Related run (744 test files importing a changed module, 3 chunks): 13,128 tests, 5 failures in 4 suites. Known pre-existing failures: `agentModeController.conditionalSkip` and `mcp.scheduledChatTools`. Also failing: `sdkConstructionGuard`, whose stale allowlist entry is `services/videoGeneration.ts`, a file this PR does not touch. Caused by this PR and fixed: `generateMarketingResponseWorker.argOrder`, which now expects `modelRouting` as the new last argument.
- After the rebase: 13 targeted suites, 546/546 passed (including PR-D's notice suites).
- Pushed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` because the pre-push hook bails on the known `conditionalSkip` failure.

## Review round (rv-3677) — fixed

- **Tier names never reach share viewers.** Routing reasons name the task and the kind of rule only (`chat task: plan route`). Share and conversable reads strip `llmSelected`, `llmRoutingReason` and `llmRoutingTableVersion` (`filterMessagesForClient`, non-owner flag). Admin reads keep them.
- **Visible refusals, never silent swaps.** A stored `agentweb-model` that the router can't serve (switch off, or the router unavailable for the owner's tier) gets the 422 "AgentWeb Model isn't available right now. Choose another model to continue." on every path: /generate with or without a body model, verified-generate, interactive share, conversable, branch and side channels. It is never "corrected" to the default, and the stored selection is never rewritten.
- **No alert storm.** Schedules, and plan steps in unattended runs, on an unavailable router no longer page per schedule or per session; the router's own deduped alert covers a broken table. The run text, pause message and owner emails name the AgentWeb Model and say it is "unavailable right now".
- **Per-tier containment.** A malformed tier override (unknown key or task type, empty or non-string target, not an object) takes down only that tier, with one alert naming it. An unusable target takes down only the routes that resolve to it. Only top-level structure errors, or a missing or unreadable table, disable the router for everyone.
- **Refused where it can never run** (visible 400/422):
  - schedule backup models;
  - benchmarks (server-side; the partner-portal benchmark picker drops it);
  - any AW-Settings value (e.g. the default-model setting; the partner-portal default-model pickers drop it);
  - `/api/emma` single-call routes;
  - the sidebar chatbot.

  The plan step-model picker keeps it.
- **Admin-plan launch:** an admin-authored plan's router pin must route for the launcher's tier at launch, or the launch is refused with a visible 422.
- **Stale-model migration:** `migrateStaleModelReferences.ts` treats `agentweb-model` as valid.
- **Customer copy never shows the raw id.**
- **Replies are labelled only when this turn's own caller routed them:** the caller passes its decision explicitly, and the stored decision is never read back.
- **Nits:** `checkTiers` comment fixed; `EmmaLoopBackend` forwards `modelRouting`; routine logs go to `console.log`; pick checks no longer log "routed"; `storedModelFor` replaces the `selectionOf(...) as string` casts; fault logs only when something changes. The dev note now states that the pickers read the cached switch even while it is off.

**Accepted as-is:** with the allowlist on, a tier-read failure while routing fails open (the owner's last-known access, else the table's own routes) and raises the deduped `model_tier_allowlist:tier_unreadable` alert, the same as PR-A. With the allowlist off, that alert is now worded for the router.

**Deviation:** with the switch off, an explicit selection of the id still gets the same 422 code, reason and `requestedModel` as an unknown model, but the sentence now names "AgentWeb Model" instead of the raw id (customer copy rule).

## Final review round (rv2-3677)

- **Auto continuations carry the SELECTION.** /generate hands its media and work-plan continuations `agentweb-model`, not the routed model. Each continuation is a turn of its own and is routed again; the table is deterministic, so it lands on the same model. Two other approaches were rejected:
  - Carrying the routed model plus its decision would keep running a model the router may no longer allow, and would only re-check the switch.
  - Re-routing per turn re-checks the switch, the table's availability and the owner's tier, and stamps the replies, exactly like any other turn.

  A refused continuation (for example after a rollback mid-chain) ends its chain with the refusal saved to the chat and pushed live. The interactive-share timeout and getSession-backstop continuations already passed the stored selection.
- **Approval-inbox resume.** When the router is off or unavailable, the resume saves the visible refusal reply, as it does for `not_in_plan`. Other models keep the passive note only, as on main.
- **Plan launch.** An unattended plan launch refused because the router is unavailable no longer pages; the router's own alert covers it.
- **Settings.** `POST /api/settings` refuses `agentweb-model` the same way the PUT path does.
- **Nits:** the id and display name live in a leaf module (`agentWebModelIds.ts`), so they are shared without an import cycle; the step-pause label uses `modelDisplayLabel`; the code comment and dev note now list the real callers that hand over the selection (Emma email, GTM and result endpoints run the configured default).
- **Tests and checks:** touched suites 50/50, 1,344/1,344 passed; tsc clean; mutation checks caught all three: continuation handed the routed model, refused continuation ends silently, approval resume saves only the passive note.

## Rollout / rollback

Seed the table, then flip the switch; keep it off until the portal display PR ("AgentWeb Model · via X", picker entry) ships. Rollback: switch to anything but `true` (~60s, no deploy).

title: ENG-2110: login host client and turn runner (PR 1c-i, dark)
body:
## ENG-2110 PR 1c-i: login host client and turn runner (dark)

First backend piece that talks to the login host. Two new files plus tests, imported by nothing, so zero runtime change (flag off, no route, no schema, no record change).

- `loginHostClient.ts`: typed client for the host's closed protocol over an injectable `HostTransport` (unix socket now; the prod backend->worker transport is NOT decided, see the design). Our own zod schema runs before any request; replies are shape-checked (wrong shape = `BAD_RESPONSE`); no body, code, prompt or token is ever logged or echoed.
- `loginHostTurn.ts`: `runHostTurn`. Retries `EBUSY` (jittered backoff, bounded). Renews the turn lease every min(10 s, leaseMs/3); two unreachable renews end the turn; `ENOTFOUND`/`ESTALE` on renew just stop the timer. Abort = interrupt, then drop the stream after a grace. Never runs a turn twice: a known idempotency key, or a lost reply probed once with the SAME key, is reported `unknown_outcome` (the host cannot replay events); a stream ending with no `result` is also `unknown_outcome`.

### Safety answer (pre-merge)
Safe to ship: new files only, nothing imports them, no config/env/schema change. Cannot regress or affect users.

### Tests
18 tests against the REAL host server over a real unix socket (fake provider). 8 mutants checked and killed: no renew, EBUSY not retried, no probe, duplicate treated as a run, renew-ENOTFOUND still interrupts, one renew failure ends turn, no interrupt on abort, missing result reported completed. Full `src/loginHost` suite (684) still passes; typecheck and lint clean.

### Not covered here
Prod transport, HostedSubscriptionService, routes, record changes (1c-ii, needs the data-plane decision), revoke/sweeper (1d), turn-scoped bridge token (needs the B4 turn path).

title: ENG-2110: hosted subscription logins, backend side (PR 1c-ii + 1d, dark)
body:
## ENG-2110 PR 1c-ii + 1d: hosted subscription logins, backend side (dark)

The backend half of the hosted login: sign-in, reconnect and disconnect of a subscription login that lives in a per-customer home on the login host. Nothing is enabled: the per-user funding flag is off for everyone and no login host is configured in production (`AW_LOGIN_HOST_SOCKET` unset), so every call answers `host_unavailable`/`disabled`.

### What it does
- **Record (reference only, no secret):** new `sub*` attributes on `claude_subscription` rows (`subHosted`, `subHostEpoch`, `subAccountFingerprint`, `subRevoke*`); `status` gains `revoking` and `disabled`. Hosted rows never carry `sealed`, `subVersion` or lease fields. Old sealed (B3) rows are untouched and ignored.
- **Service (`hostedSubscriptionService.ts`):** two-phase sign-in (host `complete` -> conditional create at epoch 1 -> host `promote`; a failed create cancels the host attempt, a failed promote rolls the record back through the disconnect path); reconnect (record moves to epoch+1 FIRST, then host promote); disconnect (record `revoking` + fenced at epoch+1 + slot released, then the host wipes; `revoked` only after the host confirms).
- **Routes:** `/api/llm-connections/subscriptions/:provider/{start,complete,login/:id}`. Generic `DELETE /api/llm-connections/:id` routes hosted rows through the host and answers **202 `{status:"revoking"}`** until the wipe is confirmed (204 once it is). The plain DynamoDB revoke write now REFUSES hosted rows, so a bug cannot orphan a home.
- **Sweeper (1d):** every 5 min, NOT flag-gated (a disconnect must finish even if the feature is switched off): finishes `revoking` rows (alarm log after 10 failed passes), makes `active` records follow the host (lost home, epoch drift), judges only settled rows (2 min grace) and only the row it read.
- Includes the five fixes for Greptile's findings on #3678 (client/turn runner).

### Data-plane note
Persistent model change on `AW-LlmConnections` (new attributes, two new status values). Flag off, no migration, no backfill, existing rows untouched, readers already require `status === "active"` so the new values fail closed. Made under Manan's free hand from Harsha for this work.

### Pre-merge safety answer
Safe to ship dark: no user can reach any new path (flag off for all, no host in prod), no existing row is rewritten, the only behaviour change for existing flows is that the generic revoke refuses *hosted* rows (none exist) and answers 202 only for them. Rollback = revert; nothing to migrate back.

### Verification
- Tests: service tests against the REAL login-host server over a real socket (fake provider), DB-condition tests, route and cron tests; 49 + 12 new tests; related suites 1787 pass; typecheck and lint clean for new code.
- Dozens of deliberate mutants (wrong epoch, slot released twice, revoked before the host confirms, plain revoke allowed, no grace, unconditional sweeper write, ...) all killed.
- Real DynamoDB: 20/20 write checks against `Dev-AW-LlmConnections` (in-memory double cannot catch expression errors); throwaway rows deleted.
- Independent opus review: 2 MAJOR races (disconnect racing a reconnect; sweeper marking a brand-new connection) + minors, all fixed with tests; rule deviations resolved (202 on pending wipe). Delegated admin may disconnect (existing generic behaviour, recorded) but not start/complete.
- Integration test found a real bug: a failed reconnect promote left a ready attempt that blocked the owner's next sign-in; now discarded.

### Not covered / known limits
- No live run through these routes on the test instance yet (needs the socket wired into the test backend and Manan's login).
- The pending sign-in map is per backend instance: with >1 instance and no sticky routing a complete can land on the wrong instance (`login_not_found`, start again). Not a blocker while dark; blocks multi-instance rollout.
- Production transport between Elastic Beanstalk and the worker EC2 is undecided (unix socket only works on the test box); with Yugo.
- `git push` pre-push hook was bypassed: it failed on files this branch does not touch (`agentModeController.conditionalSkip` drift guard now sees `scan_website_links` as readOnly on main; others are load flakes that pass alone).

title: fix(billing): read Basil invoice subscription and price fields (ENG-2599)
body:
## What

ENG-2599.

**Scope note:** while fixing this, we found a second pre-Basil read, the subscription `discount` field that feeds `activeOffer`. This PR fixes that as well (see the [Basil `discounts` move](#also-the-basil-discounts-move-found-while-fixing-eng-2599) section below).
 Our pinned Stripe API version is `2025-05-28.basil` (`backend/src/services/stripeClientFactory.ts:7`), and it moved two invoice fields our webhook handlers read:

| Removed (pre-Basil) | Basil location | Evidence (installed `stripe@18.2.1`, `ApiVersion = '2025-05-28.basil'`) |
|---|---|---|
| `invoice.subscription` | `invoice.parent.subscription_details.subscription` (`string \| Stripe.Subscription`) | `types/Invoices.d.ts:331` (`parent`), `:1025`, `:1051`; no top-level `subscription` on `Invoice` |
| `invoice_line_item.price` | `line.pricing.price_details.price` (price id) | `types/InvoiceLineItems.d.ts:81` (`pricing`), `:267`, `:285`; no `price` on `InvoiceLineItem` |

stripe-mock v0.195.0 (Basil spec) agrees. Its invoice fixture has no `subscription`, and it has `parent.subscription_details.subscription`, which can be expanded to a subscription object. Its line item has no `price`, and it has `pricing` (`type: price_details`).

Because of this, every invoice webhook read `undefined` for both fields:
- `controllers/stripeController.ts` `handleInvoicePayment`: payment history rows had no `stripeSubscriptionId` or `priceId`. In prod, 53/53 `payment_succeeded` rows are missing both.
- `services/stripeService.ts` `handleInvoicePaymentSucceeded`: `subscriptionId` was always null, so the `stripe_subscription_id` backfill never ran, and the period-end/offer sync worked only when the user row already had an id.
- `services/stripeService.ts` `handleInvoicePaymentFailed`: the `payment_failed` history row had no subscription id.
- `controllers/stripeController.ts` `sendStripeEventToCrm` (the CRM mirror): `invoice.*` events lost `stripeSubscriptionId`.

## Fix

New `backend/src/utils/stripeInvoiceFields.ts`:
- `invoiceSubscriptionId(invoice)` reads `parent.subscription_details.subscription` first and falls back to the legacy `invoice.subscription`.
- `invoiceLinePriceId(line)` reads `pricing.price_details.price` first and falls back to the legacy `line.price.id`.
- Both accept a string id or an expanded `{ id }` object and return `string | null`. An empty string counts as no id.
- Both are typed against the SDK's Basil types plus the legacy field, so a real `Stripe.Invoice` / `Stripe.InvoiceLineItem` and an untyped webhook object are both accepted without `any`.
- The fallback is needed because webhook payloads follow the webhook endpoint's API version, which can differ from the SDK pin.

Every site that was fixed:
- `backend/src/controllers/stripeController.ts:306-307`: `handleInvoicePayment` now writes `stripeSubscriptionId` and `priceId`.
- `backend/src/controllers/stripeController.ts:326-331`: `sendStripeEventToCrm` uses the helper for `invoice` objects. Other objects (subscription, checkout session) are unchanged.
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts:1133`: `handleInvoicePaymentSucceeded` `subscriptionId`.
- `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts:1365`: `handleInvoicePaymentFailed` `subscriptionId`.

**Which subscription a paid invoice syncs, backfills and reactivates** (`handleInvoicePaymentSucceeded`, `stripeService.ts:1117-1200`). This governs `current_period_end` and `activeOffer` (sync), `stripe_subscription_id` (backfill) and `subscription_status: 'active'` (reactivate).
- **Live** means `active`, `trialing` or `past_due` (`LIVE_SUBSCRIPTION_STATUSES`, `:1085`, the same set as `mrrCollectionGapService`).
- **A live stored subscription stays authoritative.** An older, replaced subscription's final invoice, or a second live subscription on the same customer (for example a custom subscription link), cannot overwrite it. One retrieve, as today.
- **Non-subscription invoices** (`parent: null`: one-off, quote, pay-as-you-go) behave as today. They sync the stored subscription and set `active`.
- **Otherwise** we prefer the invoice's own subscription when it is live. This covers the resubscribe race: a canceled stored `sub_old`, with `invoice.paid` for `sub_new` arriving before `checkout.session.completed` / `customer.subscription.created`.
- **If the invoice's own subscription isn't live either**, we use the customer's live subscription: `subscriptions.list({ customer, status: 'all', limit: 10, expand: ['data.discounts'] })`.
  - The pick is the same as `reconcileStripeUser` / `syncSubscriptionFromStripe`: active > trialing > past_due, newest first (`findLiveCustomerSubscription`, `:1100`).
- **`stripe_subscription_id` is only ever backfilled from a live subscription**, and only when the row has none.
- **With no live subscription anywhere:**
  - Nothing is backfilled. The stored subscription, if any, is synced as before.
  - If the invoice's own subscription has **ended** (`canceled`, `incomplete_expired`; `:1092`), the user is **not** flipped to `active`. This is logged, and the lead-list sync is skipped.
  - `incomplete` / `unpaid` subscriptions still flip to `active`, because paying their invoice is what activates them, and a new subscriber must not be held back in that window.
- **Failures:** a failed retrieve or list fetch never backfills, and leaves the status flip as it was before (`active`).
- **Extra calls:** a second retrieve and/or one list call happen only when the primary subscription is not live.

**Opslane P1 (fixed).** With no stored id, a redelivered final `invoice.paid` of a **canceled** subscription used to backfill that dead subscription, sync its period end and set the user `active`, even though the customer had a different live subscription. Seat billing would then act on the dead subscription. This was dormant on `main` only because the backfill never ran.
- Now the customer's live subscription is backfilled and synced instead.
- With no live subscription, nothing is backfilled and the status is not flipped to `active`.
- This is reproduced by Opslane's exact scenario in `invoicePaymentSucceeded.subscriptionChoice.test.ts`, which failed before the fix.

**Swept and unchanged** (nothing read from a moved field):
- `recordSubscriptionEvent`: checkout session `subscription`/`invoice` and subscription-item `price` still exist in Basil (`Checkout/Sessions`, `SubscriptionItems.d.ts:95`, `LineItems.d.ts:57`).
- `stripeService.ts` subscription `items.data[].price` reads.
- `handleCheckoutSessionCompleted`.
- `handleChargeRefunded` and the dispute handlers (they read `metadata` and `dispute.charge`, not `charge.invoice`).
- `resyncAllSubscriptionAmounts` and `mrrCollectionGapService` (they read only `amount_paid` / `invoices.list` length).
- `customSubscriptionLinkWebhook` (checkout `subscription` / subscription `id`). Its local `idOf` was identical to the helper's, so it now reuses the shared `stripeIdOf` from `utils/stripeInvoiceFields`. There is no import cycle, because the util imports only Stripe types.
- `routes/stripe.ts`, `routes/crm.ts` and `routes/stripeConnect.ts`.

## Also: the Basil `discounts` move (found while fixing ENG-2599)

Basil removed `subscription.discount`.
- A subscription now has `discounts: Array<string | Stripe.Discount>`, which are ids unless expanded (`types/Subscriptions.d.ts:120`: "Use `expand[]=discounts`").
- In this API version, a Discount embeds `coupon: Stripe.Coupon` directly. There is no `source` wrapper, and the coupon is not expandable (`types/Discounts.d.ts:99`, `end` at `:114`). stripe-mock's Discount fixture agrees: it has `coupon` and no `source`.

`extractActiveOffer` read `subscription.discount`, and four calls expanded `discount.coupon`. As a result every `activeOffer` was stored as null. In prod there are 30 subscribers and 6 rows with `activeOffer`, all null, even though checkout allows promotion codes.

Nothing displays `activeOffer` yet, so there is no customer impact today.

The old `expand: ['discount.coupon']` did **not** fail in prod. A read-only check of the last 30 days shows 7 paid invoices and 0 `for period_end sync` / `Could not fetch subscription` warnings. The period-end sync therefore ran; only the offer came back null.

What changed in `backend/src/services/stripeService.ts`:
- `pickSubscriptionDiscount` (`:1704`) and `extractActiveOffer` (`:1719`). The rule when several discounts apply is that the **first listed entry of `discounts` wins**, so the pick is deterministic. Stripe does not document list order as the order discounts are applied. Subscription-item discounts are not considered, the same as the old single `discount`.
  - An expanded Basil discount is preferred over the legacy `discount`.
  - The legacy `discount` is the fallback for pre-Basil webhook payloads.
  - The `activeOffer` output shape is unchanged: `couponId`, `couponName`, `percentOff`, `amountOff`, `duration`, `durationInMonths`, `endsAt`.
- Expand paths:
  - `expand: ['discounts']` on the retrieves (`:842` checkout; the paid-invoice retrieves).
  - `expand: ['data.discounts']` on the lists (`:678` login sync, `:1105` paid-invoice live lookup, `:1850` reconcile). This is the same path that `revenueService` and `mrrCollectionGapService` already use.
- **Id-only discounts** (`:1030-1046`, `handleSubscriptionUpdated`). `customer.subscription.*` webhook payloads carry discount ids, not objects.
  - Storing null in that case would wipe a real offer on every subscription update. It would flip back and forth with the paid-invoice sync, which does expand.
  - So the handler fetches the subscription once with `expand: ['discounts']`. This only happens when the chosen discount is an id; subscriptions with no discount never trigger it.
  - If that fetch fails, `activeOffer` is left unchanged (not cleared). A warning is logged and the webhook still succeeds. The next invoice or reconcile sync corrects it.
  - The three paths that already fetch request the expansion. If an id still came back there, the result would be null and nothing throws.

The `User.activeOffer` doc comment in `services/db.ts` now names the Basil `discounts` source.

## Not in this PR (optional follow-ups)

- **No backfill of existing rows.** The 53 `payment_succeeded` rows (and any `payment_failed` rows) missing `stripeSubscriptionId`/`priceId` could be repaired from Stripe by invoice id. That is a production data repair, so it needs approval.
- **No backfill of `activeOffer`.** The existing null `activeOffer` rows correct themselves on each user's next invoice, subscription webhook or reconcile/resync. Running "Resync Payments" would correct them right away, but that is a production write, so it is left to the owner.

## Tests

- `stripeInvoiceFields.test.ts` (15): Basil and legacy shapes, string ids and expanded objects, Basil-over-legacy precedence, empty ids, null parent, quote parent, missing input. The Basil cases are typed as `Pick<Stripe.Invoice,'parent'>` / `Pick<Stripe.InvoiceLineItem,'pricing'>`, so tsc proves the SDK shape is accepted.
- `stripeInvoiceBasilWebhook.test.ts` (8): runs through the real `handleWebhook` and the real stripeService handlers, mocking only the SDK, DynamoDB, payment history and the CRM hook.
  - A paid Basil invoice for a user without `stripe_subscription_id` backfills it and syncs the period end.
  - The history row carries `stripeSubscriptionId` and `priceId`.
  - The CRM mirror carries the subscription id.
  - The current subscription stays authoritative.
  - Both failed-invoice rows carry the id.
  - A null-parent invoice backfills nothing.
  - Legacy-shaped paid and failed payloads still work.
  - On pre-fix code, 4 of these 8 fail.
- `stripeInvoiceFields.stripeMock.test.ts` (4, opt-in): runs on `stripe/stripe-mock:v0.195.0` through `createStripeClient` / `STRIPE_API_BASE`. It skips when `STRIPE_API_BASE` is unset.
  - It checks Stripe's own Basil invoice fixture: `subscription` and line `price` are absent, `parent.subscription_details.subscription` exists as an id and as an expanded object, and line `pricing` exists.
  - It also passes the raw fixture invoice to the real `handleInvoicePaymentSucceeded`, which backfills the subscription and syncs the period end from stripe-mock's subscription fixture. This case fails on pre-fix code.
  - Limit: stripe-mock's line fixture leaves out the optional `pricing.price_details`, so `price_details.price` is proven by the SDK type, not by the fixture.
- `stripeOfferSync.basilDiscounts.test.ts` (13):
  - An expanded discount gives the exact same offer shape, with no extra fetch.
  - An id-only discount is fetched with `expand: ['discounts']`, and a failed fetch leaves `activeOffer` unchanged while the webhook still succeeds.
  - With several discounts, the first one wins.
  - Basil wins over legacy when both are present, and legacy-only payloads (with and without a `discounts` field) still work.
  - No discount gives null.
  - A fetched subscription whose discounts come back unexpanded gives null and no throw.
  - The new expand paths are asserted on the checkout, paid-invoice, `reconcileStripeUser` and `syncSubscriptionFromStripe` paths.
  - On pre-fix code, 8 of these 13 fail.
  - The legacy-shaped `stripeOfferSync.test.ts` (10) is unchanged and still passes.
- The stripe-mock suite has +2 cases, 6 in total, all passing:
  - A subscription retrieved with `discounts` and listed with `data.discounts` has a `discounts` array and no `discount`.
  - The Discount fixture embeds `coupon` with no `source`, and the real `handleSubscriptionUpdated` turns it into the expected `activeOffer`. This case fails on pre-fix code.
  - Limit: stripe-mock's subscription fixture has `discounts: []`, and stripe-mock accepts *any* `expand` path on reads, so none of these tests validate an expansion. The fixture discount is placed on the fixture subscription, and the `discounts` / `data.discounts` paths rest on the SDK docs (`Subscriptions.d.ts:118`) and the existing `revenueService` / `mrrCollectionGapService` usage.
- **Mutation check:** 10/10 invoice-field mutants were caught by at least one test:
  - each of the 4 fallbacks dropped;
  - both precedences swapped;
  - expanded-object ids ignored;
  - empty string treated as an id;
  - the `subIdToFetch` order reverted;
  - the CRM `invoice` branch disabled.
- `invoicePaymentSucceeded.subscriptionChoice.test.ts` (24; adapted from the review, plus the Opslane P1 cases):
  - Resubscribe race, including `trialing` and `past_due`.
  - Old replaced subscription; two live subscriptions; neither live; equal ids give one retrieve.
  - Retrieve failures.
  - **Opslane's scenario:** the live subscription is backfilled and synced.
  - The live-subscription pick order.
  - No live subscription: nothing backfilled, status not flipped.
  - A stored canceled subscription's own final invoice, with and without a live subscription.
  - An `incomplete` subscription.
  - Unchanged cases: live invoice subscription, live stored subscription, one-off invoices with and without a stored id.
  - Live-lookup failure.
  - On pre-fix code, 8 of these fail, including Opslane's scenario.
  - `invoicePaymentSucceeded.test.ts` and `stripeInvoiceBasilWebhook.test.ts` mocks now return the requested live subscription, since backfill requires one.
- **Subscription-choice mutation check:** 14/15 mutants were caught by at least one test:
  - backfill from the invoice id;
  - status never withheld, or withheld for any non-live subscription;
  - live lookup skipped;
  - stored fallback dropped;
  - one-off invoices not special-cased;
  - live-pick sort or filter removed;
  - invoice-subscription preference skipped;
  - lead list always synced;
  - lookup failure rethrown;
  - stored liveness ignored;
  - equal id re-fetched;
  - `past_due` dropped.
  - The one survivor, removing the explicit live check on the backfill, is an *equivalent* mutant. With no stored id, the synced subscription is only ever live, so the check is a defensive restatement of the invariant.
- **Discount mutation check:** 10/10 mutants were caught by at least one test:
  - each expand path reverted to `discount.coupon`;
  - the Basil branch dropped;
  - the legacy fallback dropped;
  - the last discount picked instead of the first;
  - legacy preferred over Basil;
  - id-only discounts returned as null;
  - the id-only fetch skipped;
  - a failed fetch clearing the offer;
  - `extractActiveOffer` given an id.
- **Related run:** the suites for the touched files plus the `stripe*`, `paymentHistory*`, `subscription*`, `crm*`, `invoice*`, `revenueService`, `mrrCollectionGap` and `customSubscriptionLink*` suites and the new tests, with stripe-mock on. Result: **110/110 suites passed, 2385 tests passed, 1 skipped** (an existing `it.skip` in `stripeUpgrade.test.ts`).
- **Pushed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`.** After merging `main` (219 commits, including a `twilio` dependency, re-installed with `npm ci`), pre-push ran 450 suites and its tsc passed. Its only failure was `admin.announcements.test.ts` (9 tests), which fails identically on a clean `origin/main` worktree and is unrelated to this PR.
- The invoice-field helper mutants were re-run after the `stripeIdOf` refactor: still 8/8 caught. `tsc --noEmit` is clean and eslint is clean on the new files.

title: ENG-669 PR-C: router switch-on fixes (model-options agentWebModel, runHealth.lastRunBlockedModel, no skill-default swap)
body:
Follow-up to the merged router PR #3677 (ENG-669 PR-C). Portal half: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1272 (follows portal #1271).

## What was wrong (verified on main)
1. **False "Unavailable" for a plan's router pin.** `offersAgentWebModel()` (`services/agentMode/agentWebModelRouterInstance.ts`) is false when the owner's tier allowlist does not list `agentweb-model`, so neither `/model-options` `allModels` nor `/public/llm-models` carried it. An admin-authored Work Plan pin of it is stored with source `system` and **runs** (`routeAgentWebModelSelection` skips the tier check for `'system'`), but the portal could not tell "not offered to this tier" from "switch off".
2. **`runHealth` had no run model.** `computeRecordedRunHealth` exposed `lastRunBlockedBy` / `lastRunBlockedReason` but not the run's stored `blockedModel` (`utils/unattendedModelNotices.ts scheduleModelBlockFields`).
3. **Silent swap of a stored router selection.** `runVerifiedChatInner`: with no model on the request (Slack threads, revisions, human-eval image actions), the required functions `update_html_file` / `read_file_content` / `create_blog_article` / `generate_image` / `generate_video` caused the session model to be overwritten with the task-type default (source `system`). For a stored `agentweb-model` that replaced the customer's choice with the switch on, and lost it for good after a rollback. I reproduced this with a test that failed on main in both switch states.

## Contract
`GET /api/agent-mode/model-options` adds, **only while `agentweb_model_router_enabled` is on**:
```
agentWebModel: {
  enabled: true,
  offered: boolean,                                   // === offersAgentWebModel(owner); true iff allModels lists it
  reason?: 'not_in_plan' | 'unavailable_for_tier',    // only when offered is false
  name: 'AgentWeb Model',
  description: 'AgentWeb picks the model for each task; every reply shows which model ran.'
}
```
- `not_in_plan`: the router serves this tier and **every route is inside the owner's allowlist**, but the allowlist does not list `agentweb-model`. An admin-plan pin (source `system`) runs. A user pick gets 422 `not_in_plan`.
- `unavailable_for_tier`: the router cannot serve this tier right now (table unusable, tier unavailable, a route with an unusable target, or a route outside the allowlist). Nothing on it runs. If both apply, this one is sent.
- Switch off: the field is **omitted**, nothing is read beyond the cached switch, and the response has exactly main's keys. `switch_off` is never sent because absence means off.
- No tier names. `name` / `description` come from the same entry `/public/llm-models` uses.

`ScheduleRunHealth.lastRunBlockedModel?: string` is the last run's `blockedModel`. It is present only when that run is blocked and names a model.

`router.isAvailableFor(tier, allowedModels?)` takes an optional allowlist. The default is every model, so existing callers are unchanged. It is needed because the load-time `checkTiers` skips tiers that do not list the router, and those are exactly the tiers where only a system pin can run.

`generateSessionResponse(..., turnModelDecision?, routerTaskType?)`: `runVerifiedChatInner` no longer overwrites a stored `agentweb-model` selection. It keeps it and routes it on the task's route (`report` / `image` / `video`). With the switch off, or the router unavailable, the run is refused visibly (`model_unavailable` / `not_served`) and nothing runs on another model. A stored concrete model is still replaced by the task default, as before.

## Tests (all on this head)
- `agentModeController.agentWebModelRouter.test.ts` (+15):
  - switch-off parity: exact main key set, with the allowlist off and on, no table reads, `describeAgentWebModelAvailability` returns null
  - offered / not_in_plan / unavailable_for_tier (3 shapes, including precedence)
  - "the reason says what runs": a system pin runs or is refused, and a pick is refused (real `/generate` turns)
  - `offered` equals `offersAgentWebModel` and list membership across 4 configurations
  - no tier names
  - runVerifiedChat: the selection is kept and routed on the `report` and `image` routes and stamped; rollback refuses visibly with nothing run; non-router parity
- `agentModeController.runHealth.test.ts` (+3), `agentModeController.scheduledModelNotice.test.ts` (asserts `lastRunBlockedModel` end to end), `agentWebModelRouter.test.ts` (+1 `isAvailableFor` with an allowlist).
- Ran: those 4 suites (138 tests) plus 11 runVerifiedChat-related suites (189 tests) plus 8 controller/model-access suites (394 tests, 1 failure: the known `mcp.scheduledChatTools`). Backend `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- Mutations, each killed: emit the field with the switch off (2 failures); skip the routes-inside-allowlist check (2); swap the reason precedence (2); drop `lastRunBlockedModel` (3); drop `routerTaskType` routing (2); the original swap (3 failures on main).

Pushed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`. The pre-push hook's tsc passed, and its jest stopped on the known pre-existing `agentModeController.conditionalSkip` drift-guard failure.

## Review round (rv-3681)
- **MAJOR, fixed:** the headless callers mishandled the new refusal of a stored `agentweb-model` (switch off, router unavailable for the tier, or a pick outside the plan). `runVerifiedChatInner` now saves a `ModelUnavailableError` to the chat with `recordModelRefusal` (once per error, never retried) before rethrowing it. Slack "Request changes" (both the direct-asset and task-based branches), `revisionService.triggerAutoRevision` (including batch) and the human-eval image revision now post the refusal sentence plus "To fix it, choose another model for this chat in AgentWeb, then retry the feedback." (`utils/modelRefusalReviewerNotice.ts`) and do **not** page on-call. Non-model errors are handled exactly as before.
- **Nits:**
  - `describeAgentWebModelAvailability` now reuses `offersAgentWebModel`, with no duplicated offered logic and no redundant `inPlan ||`.
  - The tool-calling comment no longer claims the required functions always stay callable (maxTools truncation applies on any model).
  - New tests pin the `blockedBy &&` guard on `lastRunBlockedModel`.
- **Tests:**
  - Controller: 4 refusal cases (rollback with `update_html_file` and with `generate_image` (the `rvc:off:generate_image` probe), router unavailable for the tier, a pick not in the plan), each asserting one chat refusal, the selection kept and nothing run; plus one case showing a non-model failure is not saved as a refusal.
  - `revisionService.sessionBusy` (+3), `humanEvalActionService` (+2), `slack.sessionBusy` (+2, both branches), `runHealth` guard.
  - 34 suites, 513 tests pass; tsc is clean.
- **Mutations, each killed:** no `recordModelRefusal` (4 failures); each caller's model branch removed (revision 3, human-eval 2, Slack direct 2, Slack task 1); `blockedBy &&` guard removed (1).

title: Add hot-lead auto-call: ring the team, bridge the lead (ENG-2271)
body:
## Summary

ENG-2271: when a hot lead submits a landing-page form, AgentWeb phones a person on the client's team, asks if they can take the call (press 1), then phones the lead, who must also press 1, and connects the two. The feature ships **dark**: it is off until the Twilio account/number exist, the `hot_lead_call_mode` kill switch is on, the org has the opt-in `hot_lead_call` plan feature, and the org has enabled it.

**How it works**
- A team of up to 10 people per business, each with a phone number, weekly availability windows and a priority order (set in the customer portal, or by Emma). Calls only happen inside the business's calling hours in its timezone.
- The first available, verified person is called and presses 1 to accept. If they do not answer or decline, the next available person is tried, up to `maxAttemptsPerLead` (default 3). The lead is only called once someone accepted and must press 1 as well before the two are bridged.
- Example: A 9-12, B 12:15-3, C 3-6, D 2-7. A lead at 11:00 goes to A. At 16:00 C is tried first, then D. At 12:05 or after 18:00 nobody is called and the Slack alert still fires.
- Twilio Programmable Voice REST + signed TwiML webhooks behind a `VoiceProvider` seam. LiveKit was evaluated and rejected (needs an external SIP trunk, no TwiML-like flow, 3x the build, no call records); see `backend/docs/integrations/hot-lead-call.md`.
- Spend is metered per call leg (`twilio:voice:<sid>:<leg>`) with provisional Twilio list prices; rates are editable in the partner portal Vendor Rates tab until the real rate card arrives (tracked separately).
- REST API `/api/orgs/me/hot-lead-call` (revision-checked), per-member phone verification by spoken code, Emma tools, kill switch, per-lead/per-member limits, plan entitlement (opt-in only; fails closed).

**Safety properties (each covered by tests)**: one call record per lead (create-first lock), a member is never rung twice and never more than one at a time, the lead is only dialled for a verified member and an unchanged lead phone, every dialled leg is metered once, no phone numbers or codes in logs/URLs/events, signature validation on all six voice endpoints, crash safety at every database write (a write that commits and then errors is recovered by a per-attempt claim token; failure-injection sweeps of about 4,000 scenarios found no double calls).

## Data plane (approved by Anurag Seth for this PR)

No new table, index or migration. New persistent keys on existing tables:
- Org attributes `hotLeadCall`, `hotLeadCallVerification`, `hotLeadCallProvisioning`.
- `lead.system.hot_lead_call` (call record: state, attempt, member id, call SIDs, outcome, `leadPhoneMac`, `claimToken`).
- AW-Settings keys `hot_lead_call_mode` (kill switch) and `vendor_rate_overrides`.
- `hlc#...` keys in the existing `AW-MCPSessions` table (limits/cooldowns; TTL-based).
Table provisioning/TTL/IAM verification and any data migration are requested from Harsha's agent in separate tickets (see the Linear issue).

## Dependencies
`twilio@6.2.0` added; `overrides` pin `axios ^1.13.5` and `jsonwebtoken ^9.0.3` under twilio (lockfile moves axios 1.9.0 to 1.13.5, jsonwebtoken 9.0.2 to 9.0.3, jws 3 to 4). Post-deploy smoke needed for axios consumers.

## Rollout / rollback
- Deploy order: **backend first, then the customer portal PR**.
- Off by default. Kill switch: AW-Settings `hot_lead_call_mode` (read with a 30 s cache, fails off). Per-org: turn off in settings; plan feature `hot_lead_call` is opt-in only.
- Rolling back the code is safe: nothing else reads the new keys.
- Stuck-record playbook and exact ops steps are in `backend/docs/integrations/hot-lead-call.md`.

## Testing
- New unit/e2e/DynamoDB Local suites for routing, limits, store, webhooks, TwiML, REST, tools, verification, attempts and a store-failure matrix. Typecheck clean after merging the latest `main`.
- Full backend run (before the last `main` merge): 2428 suites passed; 10 failed. 8 of those fail identically on a clean `origin/main` (`sdkConstructionGuard`, `agentModeController.conditionalSkip`, `createTablesDrift`, `icpPersonaIdentity`, `mcp.scheduledChatTools`, `onboardingBrandReview`, `v0Service.withRetry`, `admin.announcements`); the other two were fixed (`orgMemberRemoval` regression from this branch, `services.v0Service` flaky under load, passes alone).
- The pre-push hook stopped on `admin.announcements` (pre-existing on main, verified on a clean checkout), so this branch was pushed with the documented `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` bypass; CI is the backstop.

## Not verified (go-live checks)
Nothing has run against real Twilio. Needs a staging call with a real number and two phones: what the team member hears while the lead is being screened, screening-leg billing, `DialBridged` on a screened-out leg. Conference is the documented fallback if screening sounds wrong. Twilio account/secret/number and the real rate card are requested in separate urgent tickets.

## Merge notes
Squash-merge recommended (the branch history is long and contains intermediate commits that do not typecheck by design). Suggested squash subject: `Add hot-lead auto-call: ring the team, bridge the lead (ENG-2271)`.

Real Twilio behavior remains unverified. Staging validation and backend-first deployment are required before enabling the feature.

title: feat(eval): LLM task-success judge, advisory (ENG-2591)
body:
## ENG-2591: LLM task-success judge

The deterministic `agent-task-success` grader trusts the work plan's own step checkmarks, and scored **kappa 0.20** against blind labels on the 40 test work-plan cases. A rule-based v2 reached 0.28 on test and was dropped, because the misses are semantic:
- a deliverable that failed while the reply claimed success
- the wrong account's data
- an ignored constraint
- made-up intake answers

This PR adds an LLM judge for golden criterion `task_success`. It is **offline and advisory only**: it can't gate (`mayGate` stays false).

### What
- **`services/taskSuccessJudge.ts`**: the `agent-task-success-judge` grader on Claude Sonnet 5.
  - It reads the session as an ordered timeline and applies the human labelling rubric, with a deliverable / requirement / fabrication checklist before the verdict.
  - It refuses non-Claude judges, because the agent runs on Gemini.
  - The verdict parser does a bounded forward brace match.
  - Errors carry no verdict.
- **`services/agentRunTrace.ts`**: an ordered `timeline` of user, agent and call entries, capped at 400 entries (head and tail kept).
- **`loops/eval/runValidation.ts`**: `loadTraceForGrading` and `taskSuccessJudgeGrader`. `defaultGoldenCaseGraders` includes the paid judge only when `llmJudges` is set; `runGraderValidation.ts` sets it for `llm_judge` graders.
- **`scripts/runTaskSuccessJudgeTrial.ts`**: a read-only trial.
  - It calls OpenRouter directly, so no spend rows are written.
  - A `--max-usd` cap counts the upstream cost on our own key (BYOK).
  - It rewrites `--out` after every case and exits on its own when done.
  - `--labeller` runs a blind GPT-5.4 labeller using only the rubric, as a cross-family check.
- **Registry and `EVAL_REGISTRY.md`**: the trial result is recorded as advisory. No `validation` is recorded, because the labels are AI labels, not human ones.

### Trial (production data, read-only; test split)
| Labels | n | Kappa |
|---|---|---|
| Blind Claude labels | 38 | 0.77 |
| Blind GPT-5.4 labels | 39 | 0.88 |
| Cases where GPT and Claude agree | 34 | 0.93 |

- **Label reliability:** the two label sets agree at kappa 0.73.
- **Old grader:** 0.20 on the same cases.
- **Cost:** $2.24 in total.
- **Empty golden cases:** 20 of the 80 work-plan golden cases are empty sessions, with 0 messages.

Full results: [ENG-2591](https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2591/agent-task-success-grader-stop-trusting-step-checkmarks-kappa-020-in#comment-ea8be576).

### Also fixed (main was red)
- `agentModeController.conditionalSkip.test.ts`: pins `scan_website_links` (ENG-1098) in the read-only tool audit.
- `v0Service.withRetry.test.ts`: the 429 case shrinks the ENG-949 20 s backoff floor, which exceeded the 15 s test timeout.

### Tests
- Added: `taskSuccessJudge.test.ts` (rendering, long sessions, parser regressions including the cut-off-reply hang, model guards, labeller, BYOK cost, trial args), plus additions to `agentRunTrace.test.ts` and `evalRegistry.version.test.ts`.
- Pre-push: `tsc` passes, and all 433 related suites pass (8282 tests).

Adds an advisory, offline `agent-task-success-judge` with bounded redacted traces, rubric checks, optional paid-judge execution, and a capped OpenRouter trial with blind cross-family labelling. It also improves BYOK cost detection and fixes related tests. `mayGate` remains false, so this does not sit on a production outage path.

title: ENG-2110: network isolation for customer sandboxes (PR 2, dark)
body:
## ENG-2110 PR 2: network isolation for customer sandboxes (dark; the external-customer blocker)

Until now every customer process shared the host's network namespace: open egress (only IMDS denied), a shared loopback, shared abstract unix sockets. This gives each sandbox its own network namespace and a single, allowlisted way out.

### What it does
- Every customer unit runs with `PrivateNetwork=yes` (own netns: loopback only, own abstract sockets, no route anywhere), an empty read-only `/run`, and only the egress proxy's socket directory bound in (`BindReadOnlyPaths`).
- `deploy/aw-net.sh` (the launcher, runs as the customer uid inside the unit) starts `socat` (127.0.0.1:3128 -> the proxy socket) and exports the proxy environment (telemetry/error-reporting off) before exec'ing the program.
- `egress/egressProxy.ts` (inside the host process, started before the API socket and stopped with it): CONNECT-only to an exact `host:port` allowlist from the host config, plus the Emma tool bridge (plain http rewritten to origin-form for the bridge only). Literal IPs refused; the name is resolved HERE and every address must be public (private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/metadata/6to4/Teredo refused: DNS-rebinding/SSRF defence), and the connection goes to the vetted address. Bounded: header size, handshake, idle, lifetime, connection cap. Logs `host:port` + reason only.
- Config: `egress.allow` is REQUIRED (closed schema): a host with no policy does not start. `launcherPath`/`socat` are root-owned-path checked at start-up.

### Pre-merge safety answer
Safe to ship dark: only the login host reads this, it is not deployed in production and no flag enables it. It does change what a host config must contain (`egress`) and the unit shape, but the only host in existence is the test instance, which I updated. Rollback = revert.

### Security review (independent, opus) and what it changed
Found 3 MAJOR + 3 MINOR; all fixed in this PR: over-cap connections never closed/tracked + no permanent server error listener (host-crash and shutdown-hang risk); bytes after the request head dropped during connect (bridge POST bodies); one customer able to starve every other customer of egress (now ONE proxy socket PER CUSTOMER uid, directory 0700 + socket 0600 owned by the uid, per-customer cap on top of the global one, listener created synchronously before every unit start, fail closed if the proxy is not up); the allowlist pinned host:port but not the destination inside the tunnel (now TLS SNI of the first ClientHello must equal the CONNECT host); only the first resolved address tried; link-local allowed for the bridge; IPv6 bridge URLs unusable (now refused at config); DNS cache for allowlisted names.

### Verification
- Unit/integration: 95 proxy tests (real sockets, fake upstreams; also run under umask 077), config/unit-args/host-lifecycle tests; `src/loginHost` + `services/funding` 1385 pass; typecheck (apart from the sandbox's missing `twilio` module, unrelated) and lint clean. ~40 deliberate breakages of the proxy logic caught.
- LIVE on the test instance, inside real hardened units as a customer uid (no login): 16/16. Only `lo`; direct internet impossible; host loopback service and host abstract socket unreachable; two customers share no abstract socket; through the proxy api.anthropic.com is reachable while example.com, the metadata service and host loopback are refused; per-customer socket 0600 + directory 0700 owned by the uid; another uid gets "Permission denied"; customer A holding its cap does not stop customer B.
- LIVE with a REAL Claude Max sign-in through the full isolation (Manan, final head): sign-in, promote, turn, tool-bridge handshake with token, 3 concurrent turns, revoke, wipe: 14/14. Zero `egress_denied` events during that run, so the 4-host allowlist and the SNI pinning are sufficient for the real CLI.
- A bug found only by the real-login run (and fixed): the host service's umask 0077 made the per-customer directory unusable (0700 root); modes are now set explicitly and tested under umask 077.

### Not covered / known limits
- The allowlist is what sign-in + turn needed today; a new CLI version may need more hosts (refusals are logged as `egress_denied`; SNI refusals as `sni_mismatch`/`no_sni`).
- Per-customer listeners are not removed when a uid is freed (they are cleared at host start); bounded by the number of uids ever used.
- Production transport between the backend and the worker, and the multi-instance pending-login map, are unchanged and tracked separately.
- The pre-push hook was bypassed (failures in files this branch does not touch).

title: fix(hubspot): teammates can use an org-shared HubSpot account; cache the webhook portal lookup (ENG-2605)
body:
## Summary
**1. Org sharing (ENG-2605).** An org owner/admin can mark a connected HubSpot account "shared with org" (the share toggle works and Sources lists it as Organization), but `HubSpotService` resolved the account from the caller's own accounts only, so a teammate still got "No HubSpot account connected" in Emma. Google Ads, LinkedIn and Twitter already use the org-aware lookup; HubSpot now does too.
- Order: the caller's own account first (unchanged errors); only when they have none, accounts that org members shared (`sharedWithOrg === true`): exactly one is used, several give the existing "Multiple HubSpot accounts... Specify account_id" error. An explicit `account_id` is the caller's own first, then a shared one.
- The service is built with the **owner's** user id, so token refresh, its write-back, the refresh lock and `needs_reconnect` all hit the owner's record, never the caller's.
- Emma's `call_hubspot_api` order is: own OAuth account, then a private-app token pasted on the caller's own lead list, then a shared account. A shared account never pre-empts something the caller connected, and an own account that exists but fails (revoked grant) keeps its error instead of quietly switching to a teammate's portal. `HubSpotService.create(userId, accountId?, source = 'any' | 'own' | 'shared')` carries that split; every other caller keeps the default.

**2. Webhook portal lookup.** `getUserIdByHubSpotPortalId` read every user (about 4 MB of AW-Users) once per changed contact in a HubSpot webhook delivery. It now reads one per-instance snapshot of portal -> owner. A snapshot older than 5 minutes is rebuilt; a lookup that MISSES on a snapshot older than 30 seconds also rebuilds once (so an unknown portal costs at most one full read per 30 s, not one per event); concurrent callers share one rebuild.

## Cache behaviour and limits (read this part)
- Only the HubSpot webhook handler uses the lookup. A **cached hit is verified**: one by-id read of the cached owner confirms the user still holds that portal (matching portal id). A portal that moved to another user or was disconnected therefore resolves correctly at once, not after the TTL. If that read fails the snapshot is trusted, and a stale owner is never served from the old snapshot. A stale owner invalidates the snapshot **once** however many callers notice (the rest join one rebuild, no scan storm), the old snapshot stays as the fallback so a throttled rebuild does not take other portals down, and a rebuild that started before the change cannot publish over the fresh snapshot. When a rebuild FAILS, the previous snapshot's owner is verified like any other hit before it is returned (a stale owner is dropped; if that read also fails the snapshot is trusted). The rebuild uses the light `scanWithFilter('attribute_exists(connected_accounts)')` scan, not `getAllUsers()`, which also ran three per-user count scans and let an unrelated table's throttling fail the rebuild. Costs: the owner check reads `UserIdIndex` (eventually consistent, so about a second of lag after a disconnect, or an extra scan right after a connect) and adds one by-id read per contact.
- A miss on a snapshot older than 30 s rebuilds once (shared), so a portal connected on another instance is found within seconds; connecting a HubSpot account clears the snapshot on that instance at once, and a rebuild already reading users when that happens (or when a stale owner is detected) cannot publish or be joined with its pre-change view. A failed rebuild still answers from the previous snapshot.
- **Residual window (accepted):** a brand-new portal can be missed for up to 30 s on an instance that built its snapshot just before the connection; the handler returns 200 first, so HubSpot does not retry those events. Production currently receives no HubSpot webhooks at all (the app's target URL points at staging, ENG-2606), so none of this is exercised in production today.

- Reads: each verified hit adds one by-id read per contact (a delivery of N contacts: N reads, alongside `HubSpotService.create`'s own); not memoised per delivery. A delivery is applied to the lists of the connected account's OWNER only, so a teammate with a list on a shared portal gets no inbound webhook sync.
- Not in this PR: `externalCrmSyncService.isAccountConnected` is not share-aware (a list pointing at a teammate's shared portal can show "reconnect" while the sync works); the first member wins if two share the same portal id; the 403 scope hint in `adsCrmApis.ts` still looks at the caller's own accounts; connecting does not auto-share.

title: feat(eval): exclude empty golden cases; seed only used work-plan sessions (ENG-2608)
body:
## ENG-2608: exclude the empty golden cases

20 of the 80 `work_plan_session` golden cases point at **predefined work plans that were opened and never used**. Production, read-only:
- **Signs:** 0 messages, `updatedAt == createdAt`, and every step still pending; 11 still wait on the plan's input form.
- **Effect:** they can't be labelled or graded. The ENG-2591 judge errored on all 20, and they show up blank in Eval labelling.
- **Cause:** the seeder took any session that has a work plan.

### What
- **`GoldenCase.excluded`** (`{ reason, by, at }`) takes a case out of the set without deleting it, so it can be undone and keeps a record.
  - `listCases` skips excluded cases unless `includeExcluded` is set.
  - `setExclusion` leaves labels and `version` untouched, like `saveDraft`.
- **Admin API:**
  - `PUT /api/admin/eval/golden-cases/:caseId/exclusion` with `{ reason }` excludes a case; `DELETE` on the same path restores it.
  - `GET /` takes `includeExcluded=true`.
- **Seeder:**
  - The work-plan source requires `updatedAt > createdAt`. Against the 80 stored cases, this separates the 60 sessions with messages from the 20 empty ones exactly.
  - Excluded cases are never re-seeded and don't count toward the target, so a re-run can add replacements.

### After deploy
`PUT …/exclusion` with reason `empty_session` on each of the 20 cases, then read each one back.

### Tests
- Parse, store (exclude, restore, list, not found), routes (validation, 404, admin only, `includeExcluded`), and seeder (unused sessions, excluded cases not re-seeded).
- 185 tests across 11 related suites pass. `tsc` is clean, with 0 lint findings on added lines.

title: ENG-2110: backend <-> production worker over mutual TLS, plus the worker installer (PR 3, dark)
body:
## ENG-2110 PR 3: the backend <-> production worker link (mutual TLS) and the worker installer (dark)

Prepares the production login worker (ENG-2114). The production backend is on Elastic Beanstalk and the worker is a separate EC2 (provisioned by Yugo with Harsha's approval, 2026-10-21): the unix socket cannot connect them, so this adds an authenticated network path and the deploy tooling. Everything is dark: no flag, no `AW-Settings` row, no deploy is made by this PR.

### What it adds
- **Host: mutual-TLS listener** (`server.ts`, optional `tls` config): TLS 1.3 only, a client certificate signed by the CA is REQUIRED and its subject CN must be on a pinned list (the CA signing it is necessary, not sufficient), 10 s handshake timeout, own connection cap, same closed API and handler as the socket. Config block validated (private IPv4 only, not 0.0.0.0/loopback, port >= 1024); the key file must be 0600 and every file root-owned; read once at start-up.
- **Backend: `MutualTlsTransport`** (`loginHostClient.ts`): TLS 1.3 floor, the worker's certificate must chain to the CA AND name the address dialled; `UnixSocketTransport` unchanged (shared request code).
- **Backend: `LoginHostProvider`**: worker address from a strict `eng1816_login_host` AW-Settings row (RFC1918 IPv4 only; keep-last-good; fail closed when never loaded) and the client certificate from Secrets Manager (`prod/AgentWeb/LoginHost/client`), fetched with the EC2 instance role EXPLICITLY (the secret's policy names only that role; the SDK default chain may pick static keys), kept only in memory, never logged. Production wiring only happens when the row exists.
- **Worker installer + tarball** (`deploy/prod/install.sh`, `scripts/build-login-host.sh`): idempotent root installer for the SSM document `AW-LoginHost-Deploy-Prod`: refuses to format any disk that holds anything, ext4 + `nosuid,nodev,usrquota` at `/var/lib/aw-login-host/prod/u`, pinned Node and `claude` 2.1.294 (npm package integrity + sha256, fail closed), TLS material from Secrets Manager with SAN/key/CA checks, config validated by the host's own parser, service left stopped until the bridge URL is set (B4). Deterministic tarball + sha256.

### Pre-merge safety answer
Safe to ship dark. The new listener is optional and absent from every existing config; the provider returns "unavailable" unless the settings row exists (it does not); the installer is not run by CI or by any deploy. Existing behaviour (unix socket, test environment) is unchanged. Rollback = revert.

### Review round (four independent angles, all findings triaged; details in the brain)
- **Security:** BLOCKER found and fixed - the pinned client identity was enforced AFTER the request had already run (a CA-signed client with the wrong CN got its request executed 300/300 times); now `prependListener` + a per-request check, with a test that asserts the manager is NEVER called (the old test only checked the client saw an error). Also fixed: leading-zero IPv4 in the TLS bind address; installer mode repair, quota failures, fstab, concurrent runs.
- **Reliability/ops:** BLOCKER - the installer could not run a second time (its own mounted disk was classified "other"); a failed redeploy stopped the healthy host. Now: staged releases + atomic switch + `--rollback`, TLS set validated as a whole, flock, quota failures fatal, mount flags re-asserted before start (reboot), `network-online` ordering, start-limit + `host_start_failed` alert, 3 GB memory slice, 5 s connect timeout and prompt stream close, TLS failure causes in error detail + a rate-limited `tls_client_rejected` log, certificate-expiry visibility on both sides.
- **Maintainability/tests:** an unknown route used to answer ENOTFOUND (destructive meaning in revoke/sweeper) -> `EINVALID/route`; `PROTOCOL_VERSION` + `host.info` with a non-fatal mismatch check and the deploy-order rule; exactly one worker in the settings row (a second needs `subHostWorkerId`, a DynamoDB model change, tracked); versioned tolerant settings schema; one strict IPv4 validator; shared request handler; machine-independent artifact (worker IP read at install time); build gated on tests + clean tree; executable installer tests with fake tools and real openssl on fixtures; stale docs replaced by a runbook.
- **Product/scale/cost (whole system):** not fixable in this PR, recorded as the hardening roadmap: fair admission queue + per-owner cap + scheduled jitter, sign-in surviving deploys / multiple instances, drain mode, expiry warnings and schedule pause, error-code copy, retention wipe, worker id on the record, B4 turn path + portal UI + usage accounting (readiness checklist for first internal vs external customer is in the brain: `nodes/review-2026-10-21-pr3-all-angles.md`).

### Verification
- 1675 tests across `src/loginHost` + `src/services/funding` (53 suites) pass; typecheck (apart from the sandbox's unrelated missing `twilio`) and lint clean; shell syntax checked. About 100 deliberate breakages across the TLS, client, provider and installer code were caught by the tests.
- TLS: rejects no certificate, a client from another CA, a CA-signed client with the wrong identity (and never runs its request), a worker with the wrong address, a worker from another CA, anything below TLS 1.3 in both directions.
- LIVE on the test instance with the final build: host no-login checks 9/9, network-isolation proof 16/16; installer on scratch loop devices: blank disk formatted and mounted with all flags, second run with the disk mounted a no-op, after "reboot" (unmounted) remounted, a foreign disk refused byte-identical; the unit's remount command restores `nosuid,nodev,usrquota` on the real test mount. It found real bugs (`quotaon -pu` exits 1 when quotas are ON; an expired cert reported as "does not chain"), now fixed.

### Not verified (needs the real worker)
The real SSM/S3 deploy path and the SSM document itself (not in the repo; its extraction must be a fresh root-owned 0700 mktemp -d AFTER the sha256 check), the Secrets Manager reads with the instance role, formatting a real NVMe disk, a full non-dry install on AL2023 (dnf, Node/Claude downloads, systemctl, IMDS), and a real restart under the new unit.

### Notes
- `install.sh` exits 3 and leaves the service stopped until `/etc/aw-login-host/bridge-url` holds an https URL (decided with the B4 turn path). `system-prompt.txt` is a placeholder (B4 sets the real one).
- Certificates issued by Yugo expire ~2027-11-22; both sides now log when under 30 days remain. CA rotation procedure (zero-downtime overlap) is in the runbook.
- The egress allowlist still includes `console.anthropic.com` and `claude.ai` (prune after the proxy's allow-log shows them unused).

title: [ENG-2598] Real-DynamoDB test suites fail: the aws-sdk keep-alive agent rejects http:// DynamoDB Local endpoints
body:
Mirrored from Linear: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-2598/real-dynamodb-test-suites-fail-the-aws-sdk-keep-alive-agent-rejects

**Problem**

* **What breaks:** `backend/src/utils/awsHttpOptions.ts` sets an `https.Agent({ keepAlive: true })` as the global aws-sdk v2 HTTP agent (via `buildAwsHttpOptions()` in `services/db.ts`, ENG-749). DynamoDB Local runs on `http://`, and Node refuses to send an http request through an https agent, so every opt-in real-DynamoDB suite fails with `TypeError [NetworkingError]: Protocol \"http:\" not supported. Expected \"https:\"`.
* **Production isn't affected:** real DynamoDB is always https. This breaks test tooling only, but it silently disables the repo's real-DynamoDB safety net.

**Reproduced**

```
docker run -d --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8125:8000 amazon/dynamodb-local -jar DynamoDBLocal.jar -inMemory
cd backend && DYNAMODB_LOCAL_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8125 npx jest src/__tests__/sessionTrackingService.dynamodbLocal.test.ts
→ Tests: 6 failed, 6 total (Protocol \"http:\" not supported)
```

* **Who's affected:** every `*.dynamodbLocal.test.ts` suite.
* **Workaround in use:** the ENG-668 suite (`paygOverage.dynamodbLocal.test.ts`) mocks `utils/awsHttpOptions` to get around it.

**Fix**

* Attach the keep-alive https agent only when the endpoint is https. For example, `buildAwsHttpOptions()` returns no agent, or an `http.Agent`, when `DYNAMODB_LOCAL_ENDPOINT` or another custom `http://` endpoint is configured.
* Or have the opt-in suites set their own agent on their client.
* Then remove the mock workaround from `paygOverage.dynamodbLocal.test.ts`.

**Acceptance criteria**

* `sessionTrackingService.dynamodbLocal.test.ts` passes against DynamoDB Local with no mocking of `awsHttpOptions`.
* Production still uses the keep-alive https agent.

---
Note: Linear is the source of truth for this issue. Status, priority, and discussion live on the Linear ticket linked above.

title: Meter the monthly rent of a hot-lead call number every month (ENG-2614)
body:
## Summary

ENG-2614: meter the monthly rent of a hot-lead-call Twilio number every month, not only the first. Until now only the purchase-time event existed, so a number held for months was under-metered.

- A daily sweep (11:00 UTC, same wiring as the seat-credit cron) reads every org that holds `hotLeadCall.twilioNumberSid` and records the current UTC month's rent with the **same idempotency key as the purchase-time event**, `twilio:number:<sid>:<YYYY-MM>`, built by one shared helper (`services/voice/numberRent.ts`). In the purchase month the sweep's write is a duplicate no-op; the next month gets its own event.
- **Rent is always billed to the org owner** (matches the seat-credit precedent). The purchase-time event now bills `org.ownerUserId` too (acting user only as a logged fallback when an org has no owner): the first review round found that billing the buyer at purchase and the owner in the sweep double-charged a self-paying admin buyer in the purchase month.
- Skipped orgs (no owner, invalid sid, missing rate unit) are missed charges, so they are logged one line per org at error level; the cron summary is error-level when anything was skipped or failed.
- Kill switch: env `HOT_LEAD_CALL_RENT_METERING` (`0`/`false`/`off` disables; default on; any other value leaves it on).
- Released numbers and deleted orgs are naturally not charged; no backfill (nothing to migrate: the runbook go-live checklist has a read-only scan to confirm before enabling).

## Data plane
No new table or key. New environment configuration item `HOT_LEAD_CALL_RENT_METERING` (kill switch). New spend events use the existing event shape. Approved by Anurag Seth.

## Testing
- 28 tests in `numberRent.test.ts`: UTC month key (incl. Jan 31 23:59:59 / Feb 1 00:00:00 and non-UTC offsets), kill-switch values, event fields, per-org error isolation, skip logging (no phone numbers), cron summary level, and tests over the REAL `recordVendorUsage` and the real `provisionNumber` with a fake spend store keyed `(billingUserId, eventId)`: two sweeps in a month give one event, a purchase then a sweep gives one event (also for a self-paying admin buyer and a pooled admin), a later month gives a second event. Also run under `TZ=Asia/Kolkata` and `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`.
- Mutation-checked (purchase billed to buyer, no owner fallback, silenced skip logging, cron level reverted, day-granularity key, kill switch ignored, ...): each caught by a failing test.
- Two review gates (a 360-degree review and a code-quality review), each run twice; last results: no open P0-P2, quality 90 with the remaining items fixed.

## Known limits (documented in the runbook)
Calendar-month billing means a number bought at month end is charged for the purchase month and again within days (at most one extra $1.15 once); owner succession mid-month can create a second charge under the new owner; the recorder's legacy fallback can add the usage aggregate twice after a partial outage; recorder write failures are invisible to the sweep (the daily re-run is the retry).

## Rollout / rollback
Merging is safe: there are no numbers yet. Rollback: set the env var to `off` or revert.

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Medium

Adds a daily 11:00 UTC sweep that meters the current month’s Twilio number rent for organizations with a valid assigned number. Purchase and sweep share a month-scoped idempotency key and bill the organization owner. Set `HOT_LEAD_CALL_RENT_METERING` to `0`, `false`, or `off` to disable metering.

Risk is medium because this adds recurring production billing. The kill switch supports rollback; no production-outage path is evident in the supplied changes.
