title: ENG-2641: refused sends say whether the user message was stored (userMessageSaved)
body:
## Problem

When a send is refused (422 `model_unavailable`, 409 `SESSION_BUSY`, 429 `TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_RUNS`, 429 usage paused / PAYG block), the client cannot tell from the response whether the user's message was already stored. The portal assumes "not stored" (it gives the draft back and drops the bubble), so when the message *was* stored, a resend stores it a second time. For the one case it knew about, the portal works around this with an extra `GET /session/:id` read, but only for `not_in_plan` and only within an 8 s timeout. If that read fails, the draft still comes back.

## Is the message stored before the refusal? (checked against `origin/main` 731a8d18; line numbers are this branch's)

| Path | Refusal | Message stored? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/generate` | 422 pre-flight (explicit model not served / not selectable / not in plan / AgentWeb Model off) | no | `agentModeController.ts:10940` |
| `/generate` | 409 SESSION_BUSY (idempotency claim, in-process lock, cross-instance `activeRun`) | no | `:11122`, `:11146`, `:11166` |
| `/generate` | 429 TOO_MANY_CONCURRENT_RUNS | no | `:11180` |
| `/generate` | 429 usage paused / PAYG block (allowance) | no | `:11262` |
| `/generate` | 422 at dispatch resolve | no | `:11330` |
| `/generate` | 429 usage paused (policy resolved to no model) | no | `:11334` |
| `/generate` | 422 from `generateSessionResponse` final gate (`assertModelInOwnerPlan` `:9694`, router off / route `:9708`) | **no** (thrown before the save at `:9941`) | catch `:11769` |
| `/generate` | 422 from `generateSessionResponse` **Work Plan step-model** refusal (`resolveWorkPlanStepModelForTurn` `:9962`) | **yes** (saved at `:9941`; refusal also recorded for `not_in_plan`) | catch `:11769` |
| `/ishare|share/:id/generate` | 409 SESSION_BUSY / 422 pre-flight / 429 owner allowance / 422 resolve / 429 paused | no | `:12648`, `:12665`, `:12803`, `:12828`, `:12843` |
| `/ishare|share/:id/generate` | 422 from `generateSessionResponse` | final gate: no. Step model: cannot happen for a viewer (`viewerIsOwner: false` turns it into a pause). Marked anyway | catch `:12932` |
| `/verified-generate` | 429 usage paused / 422 pre-flight | no | `:17298`, `:17333` |
| `/verified-generate` | 409 SESSION_BUSY / 429 cap (`runVerifiedChat` `:6234`, `:6241`, before any turn) | no | `:17434`, `:17440` |
| `/verified-generate` | 422 on attempt 1 (final gate) | no (`runVerifiedChatInner` records only the assistant refusal) | `:17423` |
| `/verified-generate` | 422 on a later attempt, or the step-model refusal | **yes** (attempt 1 saved the starting message) | `:6117` mark, `:17423` |
| `/compare/select` (`modelComparison.ts`) | 409 SESSION_BUSY | no, and replay-protected (`findPersistedPair`) | unchanged |
| `generateConversableResponse` | 422s | same as ishare | `:16421`, `:16471`. No route reaches this handler; flagged for one contract |

Out of scope (the message is not stored, the portal's generic path already gives the draft back, no flag): 400 required fields, 403/404, 503 draining, STT 422, 409 `WORK_PLAN_INPUT_INVALID` / `APPROVAL_DECK_INVALID` (card answers), ENG-527 feedback 400/502/503.

The ticket is right, and the case is narrower than its wording suggests: of all the refusals, exactly two are raised after the message is stored. One is the Work Plan step-model refusal. The other is a `/verified-generate` refusal on a later attempt. Every other refusal happens before anything is written.

## Fix

- Every send refusal in the table carries `userMessageSaved: boolean` (via `sendRefusalBody`, or a literal on the inline 409/429 bodies).
- Both post-save refusals are marked where they are raised: `markRaisedAfterUserMessageSaved` adds the error to a `WeakSet`, and the `/generate`, `/ishare` and `/verified-generate` catches answer `wasRaisedAfterUserMessageSaved(error)`. `generateSessionResponse` is now a thin wrapper over the turn (`runSessionTurn`) with a per-turn `{ userMessageSaved }` state, set right after the save; the wrapper marks **every** error the turn raises once the message is in the chat (step-model refusal, worker/transient failure, anything else). `runVerifiedChatInner` sets `startingMessageSaved` as soon as ANY attempt returned or failed with a marked error. Review finding fixed: attempt 1 saves the message, the worker throws a transient error, the retry loop runs attempt 2, which is refused at the final gate before its own save (`:9694`/`:9708`); `startingMessageSaved` used to stay false and the 422 answered `userMessageSaved: false` although the message WAS saved. It now answers `true`. Test: `failLoudSelectedModel` "attempt 1 saves the message then fails transiently; attempt 2 is refused BEFORE its own save: still true".
- Why the step-model refusal was **not** moved before the save: `generateSessionResponse` has more than 10 callers (Slack, transports, approval resume, scheduled runs, continuations). The current order is a deliberate ENG-669 decision ("never an unanswered message": the saved message plus the recorded refusal). Moving it would change behaviour for all of them, which is not this ticket's job. Every other refusal already happens before the save.

## 360 review

- Shared builders `modelUnavailableBody`, `buildTooManyRunsBody` and `buildUsagePausedBody` are **unchanged**; the flag is added only at the send-route call sites. Other users of those builders (sessionResponder, Slack, chatBranchController, PATCH llm-model, schedules, plan launch, templates) are untouched.
- MCP tools (`apiTools.ts`, `workflowTools.ts`) proxy `/generate` over HTTP; the field is additive.
- The old portal ignores unknown fields, so its behaviour does not change. The new portal treats a missing field as "old backend" and keeps the current behaviour, including the chat read (portal PR).
- Delegate sessions: no auth or ownership logic touched; the flag does not depend on `req.user`.
- `/compare/select`: no change needed (above).

## Tests (targeted, Atem-equivalent local run)

- New `ENG-2641` block in `agentModeController.failLoudSelectedModel.test.ts`, 15 tests (incl. the transient-then-refused sequence). `/generate`: pre-flight 422, final-gate 422 and step-model 422 (true, with the exact clientId stored), 409, 429 paused. `/ishare`: pre-flight 422, final-gate 422, 409, 429. `/verified-generate`: pre-flight 422, attempt-1 422 (false), attempt-2 422 (true), 429 paused.
- Mutation check: with both markers removed, exactly the two `true` tests fail.
- Pinned exact-body assertions now include `userMessageSaved: false`: failLoud (3), agentWebModelRouter (3 sites), activeRunGuard, concurrentGenerationCap, verifiedGenerateCap, verifiedGenerateLock. These pin the response contract, which changed; each one was refused before anything was written.
- `npm run typecheck`: pass. 17 related controller suites (504/504 pass: failLoudSelectedModel, agentWebModelRouter, activeRunGuard, concurrentGenerationCap, concurrentRequests, verifiedGenerateCap, verifiedGenerateLock, verifiedGenerateKeepsModel, failLoudOrdering, runSurvival, workPlanStepModel, stepModelOwnerNotice, errorHandling, autoMediaContinuation, ishareUsageGate, modelProvenance, overQuotaFeedbackFiling).

## Opslane run 1202 ([P1] "step model outside the plan returns 500"): seeded plan is malformed and unreachable through real routes

Investigated, no code change for this finding:
- The 500 is DynamoDB rejecting a NaN (`ValidationException`) when `pauseWorkPlanForUnavailableStepModel` writes the pause message; its `metadata.stepCount` is `Number(step.stepCount)`. A step stored **without a numeric `stepCount`** gives `NaN` (and the text "Step NaN uses ..."). Reproduced locally with a throwaway test: step `{ title, status: 'pending', model }` writes `stepCount: NaN`. The same input fails the same way on `main`; this PR does not touch that path.
- Every writer of a session Work Plan enforces a sequential numeric `stepCount` (`!== index + 1` is rejected, so NaN, undefined and strings all fail):
  - `ChatbotService.updateSessionWorkPlan` (`chatbotService.ts:3958`, the only `SET workPlan` in `src`) calls `assertSequentialStepCounts` before any write. `modify_work_plan`, `update_work_plan_steps`, `createWorkPlan` (`workPlans.ts:381`, `stepCount: index + 1`) and `resultEndpointController` (literal 1, 2) all go through it.
  - Predefined-plan launches: `workPlans.ts:712` (Emma launch) and `agentModeController.ts:16861` (`createSessionWithPlan`) call `assertSequentialStepCounts` on the template before copying its `stepCount`.
  - `modifyWorkPlanArgs.ts` types `stepCount` as a number for the tool args, and the admin route normalises it.
  So the seeded scenario (a step with no `stepCount`) cannot be produced by the product.
- With a valid plan, the scenario (no model in the request, the step's own user-sourced model outside the plan, no pick) is not a 422: it is the existing ENG-2378/ENG-669 step-model pause, a 200 with the pause message (`workPlanStepModel.test.ts` "no explicit pick ... still paused"; `stepModelOwnerNotice.test.ts`). `userMessageSaved: true` is answered only when a 422 is raised after the save.
- The `opslane:merge-anyway` label is NOT used. The branch was rebased onto current `main` and pushed, which starts a fresh Opslane run.

## Scope: what `userMessageSaved` covers (Opslane run 1287 on the previous head)

Opslane run 1287 raised two P1s against the earlier head. Both were checked against the code. Neither is a case the ticket covers, and neither is a regression:
- **503 `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` / `SERVER_RESTARTING`, 413 `CONTEXT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, 504 timeout and other failures of a turn that already stored the message** carry no flag. They are generation *failures*, not send *refusals*; the ticket (and this PR) is about refusals (422 `model_unavailable`, 409 busy, 429 cap / usage paused). On `main` they answer the same way, so a resend after one of them also stores the message twice. `generateSessionResponse` now marks every error raised after the save (`markRaisedAfterUserMessageSaved`), so adding `userMessageSaved: wasRaisedAfterUserMessageSaved(error)` to those catch-block bodies is a mechanical follow-up, but it changes what the portal does for ~10 more response codes per route (keep the bubble and re-read instead of giving the draft back), which is a product decision, not part of this refusal contract. Proposed as a separate ticket.
- **409 `SESSION_BUSY` for a duplicate send with the same `clientId` while the first copy is still saving** answers `userMessageSaved: false`. That is accurate for the refused request (it stores nothing itself); the first request owns the row. The stored copy belongs to the other request. A busy refusal naming the in-flight `clientId` is a separate design question, not covered here.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. The field disappears, and the new portal falls back to its pre-ENG-2641 behaviour (absent field = old backend).

## Risks

- A future refusal raised after the save must call `markRaisedAfterUserMessageSaved`, or it answers `false` (today's behaviour). This is documented at the helper and in `dev/pending/eng-2641-refusal-user-message-saved.md`.

title: ENG-2646: house-style registry model names (drop OpenRouter vendor prefixes) + mention matcher version fix
body:
## Problem

Seven entries in `LLM_MODEL_REGISTRY` (`backend/src/services/agentMode/llmModelRegistry.ts:119-125` on `origin/main` 731a8d18) still use OpenRouter's `"<Vendor>: <Model>"` name:

| id | name on `main` | name after this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` | Anthropic: Claude Sonnet 5.5 | Claude Sonnet 5.5 |
| `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813` | DeepSeek: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 | DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 |
| `openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | DeepSeek: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash |
| `openrouter/google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | Google: Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite | Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite |
| `openrouter/openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | OpenAI: GPT-6.1 Sol | GPT-6.1 Sol |
| `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3` | Z.ai: GLM 5.3 | GLM 5.3 |
| `openrouter/z-ai/glm-5.3-flash` | Z.ai: GLM 5.3 Flash | GLM 5.3 Flash |

`getSupportedModelsWithMetadata` returns `name: config.name` (`agentModeService.ts:2388`). Every client shows that name: the portal picker, the Compare dialog (`modelComparison.ts:701`), and saved alternatives (`:1088`). The result is a mixed list, e.g. "Z.ai: GLM 5.3 Flash" next to "GLM 5.2", and "Anthropic: Claude Sonnet 5.5" next to "Claude Sonnet 5". ENG-2646 saw this in production.

## Root cause

The seven names are stale data, not a code bug.
- `cleanModelName` (`modelCatalogRefresh.ts`) already strips the prefix for new additions. It arrived in 1cebe6f49 on 2026-10-08.
- These seven entries came from the 2026-10-07 refresh (aba10efef), one day earlier.
- `refreshModelCatalog` only adds models and updates scores. It never rewrites an existing name, so the old names stayed.

## Fix

Commits are ordered fix, then tests, then docs.

- Rename the seven entries to house style, matching the hand-curated siblings.
- Update the ENG-1778 characterization fixture (`supportedModelsWithMetadata.eng-1778.json`) for exactly these seven `name` values. It pins `getSupportedModelsWithMetadata()` output byte-for-byte, and its header says to regenerate it "when the roster itself is meant to change". The diff is 7 lines, all of them `name` fields.
- `llmModelRegistry.test.ts` gains two invariants:
  - no registry name is changed by `cleanModelName`;
  - no two models share a name.
- A `dev/pending` fragment records the above.

## Portal side

The portal now resolves every model label from this `name` (AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1300). With this PR, the remaining inconsistency (vendor-prefixed vs plain names in the Compare list and picker) goes away at the source. The portal deliberately doesn't strip prefixes itself: that would be a second copy of `cleanModelName`, applied to every name, including any future name that legitimately contains a colon.

## 360° impact

- **Model ids:** unchanged. Pricing, routing, allowlists, sessions, schedules and pins are keyed by id and are untouched.
- **`modelMentionRequest.ts` (Emma "use model X" detection): bug found and fixed.**
  - A registry-level regression test I added (`llmModelRegistry.test.ts`) showed that renaming Sonnet 5.5 broke one phrasing: "use Anthropic: Claude Sonnet 5.5" resolved to **Sonnet 5**.
  - Cause: "5.5" tokenizes to "5" + "5", and `findModelMention` scans position-first. Sonnet 5's id key (`anthropic claude sonnet 5`) therefore matched at "Anthropic" before the scan reached "Claude Sonnet 5.5".
  - The old vendor-prefixed name had registered a longer `anthropic claude sonnet 5 5` key that hid this. Hand-curated names (e.g. "use Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5") already had the bug on `main`.
  - Fix (`ff77bd00f`): a key match that ends right before `.<digit>` is skipped, because it stopped inside a version. Covered by new cases in `modelMentionRequest.test.ts` plus the registry-level test. The existing mention suites (`modelMentionRequest*.test.ts`, `agentModeService.modelMentionAck`, `agentModeService.sonnet45`) pass.
- **Compare:** new responses carry the new names. Alternatives saved before this keep the old name in stored message metadata (`compareAlternatives[].name`). The portal PR shows the live registry name for any model the registry still lists.
- **All seven are `adminOnly: true`,** so only admins (and admin delegate sessions) see them. Customer lists are unaffected.
- **MCP / Emma tools:** they read the same `name`. No code matches on these strings. I grepped for every old and new string across backend and agent-engine: the only hits are the tests and fixtures updated here, plus a comment in `modelMentionRequest.ts`.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx jest` on `llmModelRegistry`, `modelMentionRequest`, `modelMentionRequest.registrySweep`, `agentModeService.sonnet45`, `agentModeService.modelMentionAck`, `agentModeService.supportedModelsCharacterization`, `modelCatalogRefresh` and `modelCompare.renamedModel`: 8 suites, 390 tests passed.
- Earlier, on the same rename: `openRouterCatalog`, `openRouterRequestParams.registryGuard` and `modelPricingCoverage` also passed.
- Red/green check: the registry mention test failed against the rename alone (resolved to `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5`) and passes with the matcher fix.

## Rollback

Revert the PR. The change is data only, with no migration.

## Risks

Low. These are display names only, all on admin-only entries.

title: ENG-2645: send share-link viewers only the fields their page reads
body:
## Update (review round, rebased onto main after #3722)

- **#3722** (merged at 97be8b722) shipped a first ENG-2645 cut, `redactMessagesForShareViewer`. Compared with this PR, it:
  - dropped every system row, including the upload rows the iShare chat renders, which also shifted AgentMode's row counts;
  - stripped `llm`, so the iShare model footer disappeared;
  - still sent `interactiveShareMetadata.token` to read-only viewers.
- On rebase this PR **replaces it**. The helper is removed (nothing else used it), main's `shareMessageRedaction.test.ts` is removed (its interactive-share `supportNote` expectation no longer holds, and its other expectations are covered by `shareViewerRedaction.test.ts`), and its dev fragment is merged into one note.
- **Review fixes:**
  - `supportNote` is the admin's internal free-text note about the account (`PUT /admin/users/:userId/support-note`), not a company name. It is no longer read or sent on either view. The iShare header already falls back to "You're chatting with Emma in a shared conversation" (`AgentMode.tsx:1680-1684`), so no portal change is needed.
  - `feedback` is narrowed to `{type, comment, timestamp}` (no rater `userId`), both in iShare rows and in the feedback response.
  - The first-attempt telemetry placeholder ("a retry follows") no longer carries `isErrorMessage`. The landing page's `api/status` sets `failed = true` on any row with that flag while no report exists, i.e. while the retry is still running. Real failure rows keep the flag. The prefix is now one exported constant shared with the row's writer.
  - The read-only share leaves out server-written `role:'user'` rows (`metadata.kind` `auto-continuation` / `approval-inbox-resolution`), which `ShareConversation` rendered as customer bubbles containing internal instruction text. The conversable view keeps them, with `kind`; AgentMode draws a divider for auto-continuation.
- The sections below describe the contract and were written before this round. Where they differ, this section wins: `supportNote` is no longer sent on either view, and the test counts and head are newer (see the end of this section).
- **Re-run at the final head:** the 35 suites that exercise these handlers, the message filter, share-link minting, Slack, email and result endpoints, **910 tests, all passing**. `npm run typecheck` is clean.

## Problem

Anyone with a share link could see much more than the share page shows. In production on 2026-10-23, an unauthenticated `GET /api/agent-mode/share/:id` for a throwaway chat returned about 148 KB. I re-checked every item below against `origin/main` at 731a8d183, then rebased onto 7f3ff14bd and re-ran everything there. Line numbers are from 731a8d183.

- **System prompt:** `session.messages[0]` was the stored `role:'system'` prompt (about 100 KB). `filterMessagesForClient` (`backend/src/utils/adminOnlyMessageFilter.ts`) drops only `role:'tool'` rows, intermediate tool-call rows and admin-tainted turns. It never drops `system` rows. The comment at `agentModeController.ts:16955` saying it does was wrong.
- **Provider fields on assistant rows:** `reasoning`, `reasoning_details`, `usage`, `refusal`, `tool_calls` and `llm` all came through, because the filter keeps every top-level key.
- **Owner's skills catalog:** `skills` came from `getSkillsForDisplay(session.associatedSkills, session.userId)` (`agentModeController.ts:12477`, added in e261036192). That is everything the owner's plan allows, plus their private and org skills, "Other Skills", and "Admin Tools" with `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES` when the owner is an admin. `ShareConversation.tsx` never reads `skills`.
- **Other owner data:** `supportNote` (read from the owner's user record), `slackThread`, `shareMetadata`, `pendingWorkPlanInput`, `llmModel` and `hasActiveProgress` were all sent. The read-only page uses none of them.
- **Not in the ticket, and the most serious: `interactiveShareMetadata` (including its `token`) was sent to the read-only viewer.** That token is the conversable credential. Whenever an interactive share was active, a read-only viewer could call `/ishare/:id/generate?conversable=<token>` and drive Emma on the owner's account. The existing `sharingIntegration.test.ts` even asserted that the token was present in the read-only response.
- **The ishare endpoints:**
  - `GET /ishare/:id` is the **same handler**: `routes/agentMode.ts:45` maps it to `getSharedConversation`. The ticket's `getConversableSession` (~16320) is **not routed anywhere**.
  - So conversable viewers got everything above.
  - `POST /ishare/:id/generate` returned the same full catalog as `skills` (`generateSessionResponse` → `getSkillsForDisplay`).
  - `PUT /ishare/:id/message/:i/feedback` returned the raw stored row (`message: updatedMessage`), including reasoning and usage. It also takes a raw row index, so it could return a row that the viewer's chat hides.

## Root cause

Both share views built their response by copying the stored session and its rows, and then removing a few fields known to be bad. Every new field written to a session or message was therefore public by default.

## Fix

Both views now use explicit allowlists, in the new pure module `backend/src/utils/shareViewerSerializers.ts`. Each list contains only what the viewer's page reads. Fields were checked one by one in the portal and the landing page (see 360 below).

**Read-only view (`/share/:id`, `ShareConversation.tsx`)**
- Session fields: `{ sessionId, title, messages, workPlan, pendingApprovalDeck }`.
- Messages: only user and assistant rows, each as `{ role, content, metadata: { timestamp, toolCalls, citations, attachments, pendingApprovalDeckId } }`.
- The page renders nothing for system rows, so they are dropped.
- The catalog and the owner's user record are no longer read for this view at all.

**Conversable view (`/ishare/:id?conversable=…` and `/plan/*`, which render `AgentMode.tsx`)**
- Session fields: `{ sessionId, title, messages, createdAt, updatedAt, workPlan, llmModel, hasActiveProgress, slackThread, skills, pendingWorkPlanInput, pendingApprovalDeck }`.
- `slackThread` stays on this view because the ishare header renders a "View in Slack" link (`AgentMode.tsx:1685-1689`). `supportNote` is not sent (see the update above).
- No longer sent: `shareMetadata`, `interactiveShareMetadata` and `isConversable`. They are read only by the owner's Share dialog, which cannot be opened on these routes because `Layout` hides `PageHeader` on `/ishare` and the mobile header menu is disabled in conversable mode.
- Message fields kept: `role`, `content`, `llm`, `modelCorrection`, `messageIndex`, `clientId`, plus the metadata keys the chat reads: `timestamp`, `toolCalls`, `attachments`, `citations`, `kind`, `suggestedReplies`, `feedback`, `pendingApprovalDeckId`, `approvalDeckItems`, `approvalDeckAnswer`, `approvalDeckCancelled`, `awaitingUserConfirmation`, `isErrorMessage`, `isRunFailureNotice`, `stepCount`, `model`.
- Message fields dropped: `reasoning`, `reasoning_details`, `usage`, `refusal`, `tool_calls`, `name`, the top-level `timestamp`, and the metadata keys `ishareSender` (other anonymous visitors' IP address and user agent), `crmEvidence`, RAG chunk details, `systemPromptVersion`, `currentUrl` and similar.
- **System rows are blanked, not dropped**, as `{ role:'system', content:'', messageIndex, metadata:{ timestamp, kind, isErrorMessage } }`:
  - AgentMode counts rows (`messages.length > 1` for the orphaned-message banner, `messages.length === 0` for the empty state, `lastVisibleMessage`) and keys rows by `messageIndex`. Dropping rows would change what the page shows.
  - The landing page's `/api/status` poll reads `metadata.isErrorMessage` on any row, so that flag stays.
  - Successful `upload_image` / `upload_video` system rows are rendered by `ChatMessageItem` (`hasUploadedImage` / `hasUploadedVideo`), so they are kept whole.
- **Skills:** only this session's installed skills, as `{ skillId, name, description, installed, toolNames }`. The `__admin_tools__` bundle is never included; an ishare turn cannot run admin tools anyway. The generate response's `skills` is narrowed the same way.

**Other endpoints**
- Ishare feedback now returns `{ success, message: { metadata: { feedback } } }`. That is everything `MessageFeedbackButtons` reads.
- `getConversableSession` (not routed) now shapes its rows the same way.
- `ADMIN_SKILL_VIRTUAL_ID` is now exported from `agentModeService`.

**Unchanged:** the stored session. Generation still reads the system prompt from the database, so a conversable chat still generates, which the generate tests exercise. The owner's own `GET /session/:id` is also unchanged. The existing redactions still apply because both views start from `filterMessagesForClient(…, { omitBranchOrigin: true })`: ENG-112 `branchOrigin`, ENG-113 `compareAlternatives`, ENG-669 routing fields, ENG-2163 admin turns, and ENG-2378 step models via `redactWorkPlanForViewer`.

**One visible change, on the conversable view only:** the Skills popover lists the session's installed skills and no longer shows the owner's other "Available" skills, which were greyed out. The task brief asked for this narrowing. The read-only page looks exactly as before. Also, the conversable popover was already empty on first load (`loadConversableSession` never copied `skills`) and filled only after a refresh or a reply.

## 360: every consumer checked

| Consumer | What it reads | Status |
|---|---|---|
| portal `pages/ShareConversation.tsx` (only caller of `/share/:id`) | `session.title/messages/workPlan/pendingApprovalDeck`; per message `role`, `content`, `metadata.timestamp/toolCalls/citations/attachments/pendingApprovalDeckId` (`ToolCallGroup` uses `toolCalls[].name/arguments/result`, passed through) | all kept |
| portal `server.js` OG prerender | `/share/:id/og` → `{title, description}` | unchanged endpoint |
| portal `useAgentModeSessions` `loadConversableSession` / `refreshSessionOutcome` | `sessionId`, `title`, `messages`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `workPlan`, `llmModel`, `hasActiveProgress`, `supportNote`, `slackThread`, `skills`, `pendingWorkPlanInput`, `pendingApprovalDeck`. `shareMetadata` and `interactiveShareMetadata` are mapped but read only by `useAgentModeSharing`, `ChatSidebar` and `useSidebarChatHistory`, none of which are reachable in conversable mode. `favorites`, `feedbacks`, `delegateInfo` and `pendingUserQuestion` were never sent. | kept / unused |
| portal `ChatMessageItem`, `AgentMode.tsx`, `agentModeRenderHelpers`, `lib/workPlanStepModel`, `lib/modelUnavailable.sessionHoldsMessage` | message fields and metadata keys listed under Fix (found with `git grep` over every `metadata?.x`, `as any` and destructuring pattern) | kept |
| portal `useAgentModeChat` (generate response, `isMessageSavedByServer`) | `data.skills` (narrowed); `clientId` on rows | kept |
| portal `MessageFeedbackButtons` | `response.data.success`, `response.data.message.metadata.feedback` | kept |
| portal `LeadMagnetPage` ishare poll | `messages[].role/content`, `workPlan.steps[].status/title` | kept |
| `agentweb-landing-page` `api/status/route.ts` (ishare GET) | `messages[].role/content/metadata.isErrorMessage` on any row, `createdAt`, `hasActiveProgress`, `workPlan` | kept (placeholders keep `isErrorMessage`) |
| `agentweb-landing-page` `api/reply/route.ts` (ishare generate) | proxies the body; the client (`linkedin/page.tsx`) ignores it | fine |
| `partner-portal` AdminDashboard | only builds `/share` and `/ishare` links | n/a |
| MCP (`backend/src/mcp`), Emma tools | do not call these handlers | n/a |
| Delegate ("access account") sessions | use the owner's `GET /session/:id`, which is untouched | n/a |
| ai-eval loop telemetry inside `getSharedConversation` | reads raw `session.messages` server-side, after the response | unchanged |

**Other anonymous or token-based serializers (scope item 3).** I swept routes, sockets and MCP. No other endpoint reachable without the owner's login sends `session.messages`, the system prompt, reasoning, usage or the catalog:

- `GET /api/tasks/:id/executions/:eid/public` (`controllers/tasks.ts:802`) returns execution fields only.
- `createSessionWithPlan` returns `{sessionId, redirectUrl, workPlan, conversableToken, userId}`.
- The scheduled-chat-variables public routes return no session data.
- Conversable sockets (`server.ts:168`) join no rooms. Live voice locks to its own session and skips system rows.
- Unauthenticated MCP exposes only `emma_review_site`.
- The owner and admin views (`agentModeController.ts:10733` getSession, `chatBranching.ts:259`, `controllers/chatbot.ts:15`) are authenticated and out of scope.

Separate token-exposure issues found during that sweep are **not fixed here** and need their own tickets:

- `GET /review/:sessionId` (`routes/resultEndpoints.ts:84`, no auth) mints and returns an ishare URL with its token for any result-endpoint session.
- `POST /api/human-eval/candidates` (`humanEvalService.ts:1012`) mints an ishare token for any `sessionId` without an ownership check.
- Emma inbound email continues the session named by `[ref:<id>]` in the subject without checking that the sender owns it (`emmaEmailService.ts:213-216`), then emails back the reply and the ishare link.
- `PUT /session/:id/transfer` lets any logged-in user claim any `anon_` session (`agentModeController.ts` transferSession).

## Tests

- **New:** `backend/src/__tests__/agentModeController.shareViewerRedaction.test.ts` (8 tests) covers:
  - Read-only view: exact key set; no system prompt or telemetry text; no `reasoning`, `reasoning_details`, `usage`, `refusal` or `tool_calls`; no skills, catalog or admin tools; no `supportNote`, `slackThread`, share metadata or token; catalog and owner record not read; and every rendered field present, asserted exactly.
  - Conversable view: exact key set and the same absences; system rows kept as placeholders in place (count, order, `messageIndex`, `isErrorMessage`); upload row kept whole; every rendered row field asserted exactly; skills limited to installed ones without admin.
  - The stored session is unchanged after both reads.
  - A wrong token is refused before any shaping.
  - The generate response's `skills` is narrowed.
  - **6 of the 8 fail on the old controller** (checked by swapping in `origin/main`'s controller). The other 2 are guards that passed before and still pass.
- **Updated, because they asserted the leaky contract:**
  - `sharingIntegration.test.ts`: share metadata and token are now asserted absent. The "Metadata Separation" test is **removed**; its only invariant was that the read-only response exposes both metadata objects and the token.
  - `controllers/__tests__/agentModeSharing.test.ts`: asserts the new shapes.
  - `agentMode.ishareFeedback.test.ts`: only the feedback is returned, with no reasoning or usage.
  - `agentModeController.agentWebModelRouter.test.ts`: read-only rows carry no model fields. `llm`, with routing fields stripped, is asserted on the conversable view, which renders it.
- **Ran** at the final head (jest's configured `maxWorkers`): every suite that exercises these handlers. **23 suites, 624 tests, all passing.** That covers sharing, the ishare variants (model, deck answer, anonymous sender, usage gate, feedback), the sandbox, evaluation access, the message filters, share expiration, model provenance, the AgentWeb model router, fail-loud, error handling, active-run guard, auto-media continuation, generating and token usage.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean after the rebase. `eslint` on the new files: clean.
- I pushed with `--no-verify`. The pre-push hook runs jest across all 305 suites and ran past its 360 s budget on this shared machine; the hook itself suggests `--no-verify` in that case and treats CI as the backstop.
- **No portal PR.** No field the portal reads was removed, and the portal's own ShareConversation tests already render from minimal payloads without the dropped fields.

## Rollback

Revert the three commits. There is no data or schema change and nothing is persisted differently; this only changes how responses are shaped.

## Risks / not verified

- **Not exercised in a real browser.** Local runs against production are not allowed, and no test environment was launched. Rendering parity rests on the consumer read-inventory above and the existing portal tests.
- A portal or landing-page feature that later starts reading a new session or message field on these routes will not get it until the field is added to the allowlist. That is the intended fail-closed behavior, and the module and the dev note say where to add it.

title: ENG-2651: human-eval candidates and landing generation only attach the caller's own session
body:
## Problem

`POST /api/human-eval/candidates` (`backend/src/routes/humanEval.ts:19-75` on main, open to any signed-in user) passed the caller-supplied `sessionId` straight to `humanEvalService.createCandidate`. `createCandidate` → `resolveChatUrl` (`backend/src/services/humanEvalService.ts:1007-1017`) calls `chatbotDb.createOrReuseInteractiveShare(sessionId)` and the route returns the candidate, including `chatUrl`: an `/ishare/<id>?conversable=<token>` link that opens **and chats in** that session. Verified on `origin/main` 7f3ff14bd: there is no ownership check anywhere on this path. The same candidate's `sessionId` later receives the reviewer's Slack feedback as a system message (`addFeedbackToSession`, `humanEvalService.ts:794-820`). So anyone signed in who knew another account's chat id could get a working link into that chat and act as its owner. A no-expiry mint also strips the expiry from an existing timed token (`chatbotService.ts:4527+`).

## Fix

1. **`routes/humanEval.ts`**: if `sessionId` is present, it must be a string (else 400) and name a session the caller **owns, or the caller is an admin**. A missing or foreign session gets the same `404 Session not found`, so the response never confirms another account's id exists. The check runs **before** the artifact dedup claim, so a refused request leaves no claim, no candidate and no link. It does a record-only, strongly consistent read (`getChatSessionRecord(id, true)`).
2. **Same class, fixed here too: `routes/landingPageGeneration.ts` `POST /api/landing-pages/v0/generate`**. It stored `originating_session_id` unchecked as the page's `originatingSessionId`. That id decides which chat `durableLandingService.postToSession` writes the completion/failure message into (a cross-account write), and which session `v0Service.enqueueLandingPageHumanEval` passes to `createCandidate`, which mints the iShare link (posted to internal Slack). A session the caller may not open is now **dropped rather than refused**, because the MCP `generate_landing_page` tool (`mcp/server/apiTools.ts:2099`) sends `context.sessionId`. For an external MCP client that is the MCP transport session id, not a chat (`mcpServer.ts:265-270`), and generating without a chat to report back to is already today's behaviour for that case.

### Why the check is written inline instead of using #3729's `sessionAccess.ts`
#3729 (ENG-2644, not merged) adds `services/agentMode/sessionAccess.ts` (`getAccessibleSessionRecord`). I based this PR on main. Stacking it on #3729 would put that PR's diff into this one. Adding the same module here would cause an add/add conflict. So both checks use the exact predicate already on main in `routes/emmaApi.ts sessionAccessAllowed` (#3702): a `getChatSessionRecord(id, true)` read, then owner-or-`isAdmin`. They add a guard that a caller without a `userId` never matches a session that has no `userId`. Once #3729 merges, both call sites reduce to `getAccessibleSessionRecord(id, req.user)` with no behaviour change. That is a mechanical follow-up.

## Audit: every other `createOrReuseInteractiveShare` / `createCandidate` caller

None of these can be reached with a foreign session id **in a way that hands the link to the caller**:

| Caller | Session id source | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `agentModeController.createConversableShare` | body | owner check already present |
| `routes/admin.ts ensureIshareLinkForReview` | admin listing | router is `isAdmin` |
| `emma/tools.ts enqueue_human_eval`, `enqueueLeadEnrichmentEval`; `emma/impl/mediaVideo.ts` auto-eval; `humanEvalActionService` rerun | running agent's `context.sessionId` / stored candidate | the routes that start a run gate the session (`getSession`/`generateResponse`; emmaApi `generate-image`/`generate-video` via `sessionAccessAllowed`) |
| `emailService` scheduled-result / digest / test-send / session-notification | schedule run results (owner-checked `sendScheduledChatTestEmail`) or agent context | not caller-supplied |
| `conversation/sessionResponder.ts`, `routes/slack.ts` (x2), `revisionService.ts`, `utils/agentModeAlerts.ts` | server-created / thread-bound sessions | link goes to the requester's own Slack thread or internal on-call only |
| `resultEndpointController` `POST /r/:name/trigger` | session it just created | fine |
| `routes/resultEndpoints.ts` `GET /review/:sessionId` (unauthenticated) | path | returns the iShare URL of any **result-endpoint** session to whoever holds its id. A different class: the session id is a capability, by design for reviewer links. **Not changed; listed for follow-up.** It also matters for ENG-2653 (that PR does not let result-endpoint sessions be transferred). |
| `emmaEmailService.processInboundEmail` | `[ref:<id>]` in the subject | **foreign id reachable**: fixed separately in ENG-2652 |
| `landingPageGeneration /generate` → `enqueueLandingPageHumanEval` | body `originating_session_id` | **foreign id reachable** (mint goes to Slack, plus a write into the victim's chat): fixed here |

## 360 impact

- **`POST /api/human-eval/candidates` consumers**: no caller in the customer portal, partner portal, agent-engine or MCP (grep for `human-eval` across all of them). The Emma tool calls `createCandidate` directly, not this route. Behaviour for callers without a `sessionId` is unchanged. A non-string `sessionId` used to be dropped silently and is now a 400, matching emmaApi.
- **Delegate ("access account") tokens**: `middleware/auth.ts` resolves `req.user` to the target account, so a delegate passes on exactly the target's sessions. Admins pass on any session.
- **Landing generation**: the in-process Emma self-call (`mcpFetch` with the session owner's identity) keeps its session, which is the same identity flow #3702's emmaApi gate already relies on. External MCP clients lose a transport id that never named a chat. `findInFlightJobForSession` (controller retry-reconnect) is keyed on chat session ids and is unaffected. `codingAgentSubpageService` takes the same opts and so inherits the filtered value.
- `createCandidate` / `resolveChatUrl` are unchanged, so internal auto-eval paths behave exactly as before.

## Tests
- `src/__tests__/humanEval.routes.test.ts`: +8 (foreign→404 with no claim and no candidate, missing→same 404, caller without a userId refused, oversized id→404 with no read, non-string→400 with no read, owner OK, admin OK, empty→no read).
- `src/__tests__/routes.landingPageGeneration.test.ts`: +6 (foreign dropped with generation still 201, non-chat id dropped, oversized id dropped with no read, failed session read drops the id rather than the generation, owner kept, admin kept). The auth mock now reads an `x-admin` header; the default is unchanged.
- Run: `npx jest src/__tests__/humanEval.routes.test.ts src/__tests__/routes.landingPageGeneration.test.ts`: **204/204 pass**. With the two route changes reverted, **7 of the new tests fail** (the refusal and drop cases), which shows they pin the fix.
- `npm run typecheck`: pass.

### Opslane finding (P2), fixed in the follow-up commits
Opslane found that a ~4000-character `originating_session_id` made `getChatSessionRecord` throw a DynamoDB `ValidationException` (key over 2048 bytes), which failed the whole generation with a 500. Now:
- ids over 200 characters are treated as "not a session" (real ids are 36-character uuids): landing generation drops them, human-eval answers 404, and neither reads the database
- a failed originating-session read drops the id instead of failing the generation
- the pre-push hook ran the 2 suites: 204/204 pass

## Opslane run 1289 ([P1] "landing page from your own chat is saved without a link back"): pre-existing, not caused by this PR

Verified against the code, not assumed:
- `resolveOriginatingSessionId` does keep the caller's own session id (the control with a foreign id logged the "ignoring" warning, the own id did not) and hands it to `generateLandingPage` as `opts.originatingSessionId`.
- The id is then dropped inside `v0Service.generateLandingPage`'s legacy branch (`DURABLE_LANDING_GENERATION` not `"true"`): `addPageToExistingRepo(siteRecord, ..., templateHtml, undefined, ...)` and `generateFirstPage(..., recyclable?.id, undefined, ...)` pass a literal `undefined` where the originating session belongs (`v0Service.ts` legacy block, after `// ── Legacy single-site behavior`). Only the multi-site branch forwards it.
- `v0Service.ts` is not in this PR's diff. On `origin/main` the same call stores no `originatingSessionId` either, so the record had no link back before this PR as well. This PR only decides whether a caller-supplied id may be used (own: kept, as before; foreign: dropped), and never changes what happens downstream of that.
- Not fixed here: forwarding the id in the legacy branch turns on completion/failure messages and review-candidate creation in chats for every flag-off generation. That is a separate behaviour change in code this ticket does not touch, so it deserves its own ticket and tests.

## Rollback
Revert the PR. There is no data or schema change, and no stored records are touched.

## Risks
- A caller relying on attaching a session it doesn't own (none found) now gets a 404.
- An admin-run Emma turn in a customer's chat still keeps the session, as with the #3702 emmaApi gate.

title: ENG-2652: Emma email continues only the sender's own [ref:] session and only for authenticated senders
body:
## Problem

Verified on `origin/main` 7f3ff14bd, `backend/src/services/emmaEmailService.ts` `processInboundEmail` (:188-325):

1. **`[ref:<id>]` was not owner-checked.** `existingSessionId = extractSessionId(subject)`. If `chatbotDb.getChatSession(existingSessionId)` returned anything, that session was continued (:209-213) with no `existingSession.userId === userId` check. The code then wrote the sender's email metadata onto it (:247), ran `generateSessionResponse(sessionId, …, userId)` in it (:290), minted `createOrReuseInteractiveShare(sessionId)` (:301), and emailed the reply plus `Continue in browser: <iShare URL with conversable token>` to the sender. A registered user who put another account's chat id in the subject could run a turn in that chat (its context, memory and tools) and get a working conversable link to it.
2. **The From header was trusted as identity.** `resolveUserId(event.from)` (:99-102) maps the message's From address to the account Emma acts for. The webhook is svix-verified (`routes/webhooks.ts:197`), but that only proves *Resend* sent the event, not that the From address is genuine. A forged `From: victim@…` therefore acted as the victim, and combined with (1) it could reach any of the victim's chats.
3. Side defect: the reply subject kept the inbound `[ref:]` even when a different session answered (`buildResponseSubject`). So after the not-found fallback, the thread kept pointing at the wrong session and every reply started yet another new one.

## Fix

- **Ownership:** a referenced session is continued only when `session.userId === resolved sender`. Otherwise (missing **or** foreign) a new session is started exactly like the not-found path. The metadata write, the agent turn, the iShare link and the reply are therefore always on the sender's own session. The lookup is record-only and strongly consistent (`getChatSessionRecord(id, true)`), so a refused id never loads the other account's transcript. A new session now also gets the subject prepended to the first message, as a fresh conversation always did.
- **Admins: owner-only too.** Decision and reasoning: email carries no delegate ("access account") context, and its sender proof (DKIM/DMARC on a From address) is weaker than a portal JWT. Letting admin email unlock any chat would make "forge or compromise an admin's mailbox" a key to every account. Admins keep portal access (`getSession` owner-or-admin).
- **Sender authentication:** Resend's `GET /emails/receiving/{id}` returns `authentication: { spf, dkim, dmarc }`, each `pass | fail | gray | processing_failed | unknown`. Per [Resend's docs](https://resend.com/docs/api-reference/emails/retrieve-received-email) these are computed by its receiving server, not read from headers. DKIM `gray` = "not signed, or the signing domain does not match the From domain". `getReceivedEmailContent` now passes the object through (an additive field). Emma acts only when **`dmarc === 'pass' || dkim === 'pass'`**, i.e. there is From-aligned proof. **SPF pass alone is rejected**, because it authenticates the envelope sender, which need not be the From domain. A missing or `null` verdict fails closed. Refused mail is logged (`[EmmaEmail] Ignoring inbound email <id>: sender not authenticated (authentication=…)`) and gets **no reply**, since a reply would go to the possibly forged address. This also stops the free-trial invite from going back to forged addresses.
- `buildResponseSubject` now replaces an inbound `[ref:]` with the session that answered.

## 360 impact
- `processInboundEmail`'s only caller is `routes/webhooks.ts` `email.received` (fire-and-forget). The temp-inbox path (`test+…@`) and `db.ts:9633` also call `getReceivedEmailContent`. They only gain an unused field.
- The other webhook tests (`webhooks.resend.complained`, `webhooks.hubspot`, `webhooks.attio`) mock `emmaEmailService` and are unaffected.
- `buildResponseSubject` is used only here.
- Email sessions were never delegated, so no delegate flow changes.

## Tests
`src/__tests__/emmaEmailService.test.ts` now has 56 tests (all pass):
- New ENG-2652 block:
  - a foreign `[ref:]` → new session for the sender, and the victim id never reaches `generateSessionResponse`, `createOrReuseInteractiveShare` or `updateSessionEmailMetadata`, nor the reply's subject, html or text
  - an admin sender is also owner-only
  - the sender's own session still continues
  - 5 unauthenticated verdicts (none, null, SPF-only, DKIM/DMARC fail, unknown/processing_failed) → no user lookup, no session, no turn, no link, no email
  - DKIM-only pass and DMARC-only pass are accepted
- Existing fixtures for genuine mail now carry `authentication: pass` (the new precondition), and the session mock is `getChatSessionRecord`.
- **Changed test, with reason:** `buildResponseSubject › preserves existing ref tag` asserted that the reply kept a `[ref:]` naming a *different* session than the one that answered. That is defect 3, so it is replaced by "replaces a ref naming a different session" and "keeps a ref that already names the answering session" (the single-tag assertion is kept).
- With the service changes reverted, 11 tests fail, including every new security case.
- `npm run typecheck`: pass.

## Rollback
Revert the PR. There is no data or schema change.

## Risks / not verified
- **The production payload was not verified.** I had no access to real Resend inbound data. If production responses lacked `authentication`, every inbound Emma email would be ignored, and the log line above would show `authentication=null`. Resend documents the field as `null` only for emails received before it was introduced. If this happens, revert, or relax the check to log-only while it is confirmed.
- Genuine users whose domain neither DKIM-signs aligned mail nor publishes DMARC (rare; Gmail, Workspace and M365 sign by default) will no longer reach Emma by email and get no notice. A notice email would be new customer-facing copy needing Harsha's review, so it is left as a follow-up.

title: ENG-2650: require reviewer token or admin on /review routes; harden /send
body:
## Problem

Nothing authenticated the result-endpoint review routes on `origin/main` (`7f3ff14bd`). `backend/src/routes/resultEndpoints.ts` is mounted with `app.use("/review", reviewRouter)` (`app.ts:624`), and no auth runs in front of it.

- `GET /review/:sessionId` (`resultEndpoints.ts:84`) returned `leadEmail` (`:183`), `contentHtml`, every generated asset URL, and the send history for any session with `resultEndpointMetadata`. It also called `chatbotDb.createOrReuseInteractiveShare` (`:178`) and returned the **conversable iShare URL**.
- `POST /review/:sessionId/send` (`:197`) sent AgentWeb-branded email through Resend to **any** `recipientEmail` (`:289`). It linked or embedded **any** caller-supplied `assetUrl` (`:223/227/235`), and it interpolated `assetUrl`, `resultTitle` and the reply-to address into the HTML unescaped (`:223`, `:272`).

The only thing protecting these routes was the session id, and that id is not secret. `/r/:name/trigger` returns it to the anonymous caller (`resultEndpointController.ts:202`), and it appears in the lead's `/r/:name/:sessionId` status-page URL and in the review link.

While tracing the review-link producer (`emma/impl/workPlans.ts` `sendForReview`), I also found that the reviewer email interpolated the public trigger `args`, the lead email, and the model-supplied `subject`/`content_url` without escaping (`workPlans.ts:1709`, `:1722`). The skipReview auto-send repeated the unescaped `/send` template.

## Intended design (verified)

- A result endpoint is an admin-configured setting (`/api/admin/result-endpoints`, partner-portal `ResultEndpointsTab`). Its session is owned by `anon_<uuid>`, so there is no customer owner.
- The `send_for_review` tool is the only producer of review links. It emails `${CUSTOMER_FRONTEND_URL}/review/${sessionId}` to the configured `reviewerEmail` (or auto-sends to the lead when `skipReview` is set).
- The customer-portal page `src/pages/ResultEndpoint.tsx` `ResultEndpointReview` (route `/review/:sessionId`) is the only consumer of these routes. I found no Slack message or other caller in this repo, the customer portal, the partner portal, or a GitHub code search of the AgentWebPro org.

So the people who should be able to open a review are the configured reviewer and real admins.

## Fix

1. **`requireReviewAccess`** is now the first handler on every `reviewRouter` route. It accepts either
   - the per-session **reviewer capability token**: `base64url(HMAC-SHA256(HMAC(JWT_SECRET, "agentweb:result-endpoint-review-link:v1"), sessionId))`, sent in `X-Review-Token` and compared with `timingSafeEqual`; or
   - a real admin JWT, using the `isRealAdmin` rule (a delegate token acts as the target account and is rejected).

   The check runs **before any session read**, so a caller without access can't learn which sessions exist and can't mint an iShare link. As a result, the iShare URL and the lead email go only to the reviewer or an admin. The token is derived, not stored, which means no persisted model or schema change, and every review email for a session carries the same valid token. New file: `backend/src/services/resultEndpointReview.ts`.
2. `send_for_review` builds the link with `buildReviewUrl`: `/review/<id>#token=<t>`. The token is in the **fragment**, so it is never sent to the portal host or CDN. CORS now allows `X-Review-Token` (`app.ts`).
3. `/send` hardening:
   - `assetUrl` must be one of the session's collected assets and http(s), or `__inline_html__` when `contentHtml` exists. Asset collection is now `collectReviewAssets`, shared by GET and send. The scan is unchanged.
   - `recipientEmail` must be exactly one address, using the WHATWG `input[type=email]` grammar: no lists, display names or CRLF, at most 254 characters.
   - `customMessage` must be a string of at most 5000 characters.
   - The subject has CR/LF stripped.
   - **10 successful sends per session per hour** (`express-rate-limit`, keyed by session and applied after authorization, so a caller without access can't spend a session's budget). The limiter is in memory, so the limit applies to each instance separately.
4. A single `buildResultDeliveryEmailHtml` helper escapes every interpolated value (`escapeHtml` escapes all 5 characters). `/send` and the skipReview auto-send both use it. The markup and text are unchanged.
5. The reviewer email escapes trigger args, the lead email, the title, the subject and the content URL. The generated `contentHtml` under review is still shown as-is.

## Review follow-ups (second round)

- `leadEmail` is validated at trigger time (`isValidRecipientEmail`; 400 on a list, display name, CRLF or malformed value). `send_for_review` also refuses to auto-send to a malformed stored address and falls back to the review email.
- Reviewer and lead subjects have CR/LF stripped, as `/send` does.
- **Limits, stated plainly:** the send rate limit is per backend instance (in memory), and the reviewer token never expires. To revoke every outstanding review link, rotate `JWT_SECRET`.

## Breaking change / migration

Review links emailed before this deploy contain no token, and they now get **401** (the portal page shows "Access Denied"). There is no safe way to keep them working: the bare session id is exactly the credential that leaked. Migration:
- An **admin signed in to the portal** can open any old link, because the page sends their login when the URL has no token.
- The next `send_for_review` for a result issues a new link that carries the token.

Rotating `JWT_SECRET` also invalidates outstanding review links.

## Companion PR

The customer portal must ship with this PR: AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1303. It sends the token or the admin login, adds an Access Denied state, and stops third-party analytics from loading on `/review/*`. If this backend PR deploys first, review pages fail with 401 until the portal deploys. Links stay valid, so nothing is lost. Ideally merge the portal PR first, or both together. The portal change is harmless on the current backend, which ignores the extra header.

## 360 impact analysis

| Consumer | Status |
|---|---|
| Portal `ResultEndpointReview` (GET + send) | Updated in the companion PR; covered by vitest |
| `send_for_review`: Emma tool (`emma/tools.ts:6541`), `POST /api/emma/send-for-review` (`emmaApi.ts:856`), `agentModeService.sendForReview` wrapper | Same signature and return value; only the link and escaping change |
| skipReview auto-send | Same template through the shared helper; tested |
| `/r/:name/trigger`, `/r/:name/info`, `/r/:name/status/:id` | Not touched |
| Admin result-endpoint CRUD, partner-portal tab | Not touched; existing tests pass |
| CORS (all other routes) | One header added to the allow-list; `cors.test.ts` passes |
| Delegate ("access account") sessions | Can't use the admin path (tested); the link token still works in a delegate tab |
| MCP tools (`backend/src/mcp`) | No reference to `/review` or `reviewRouter` |

## Tests (run on the final head, under the shared lock)

- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0.
- New `resultEndpointReview.eng2650.test.ts` (17) and `sendForReview.eng2650.test.ts` (3), plus the updated `resultEndpoints.test.ts`: 52/52 pass.
- **Red check:** with `routes/resultEndpoints.ts` and `emma/impl/workPlans.ts` reverted to `origin/main`, 12 of the 20 new tests fail. These are every access, send-restriction, escaping, rate-limit and link-token invariant. The 8 that still pass are module unit tests and positive-path checks.
- Related suites: `cors`, `emmaTools.workPlans`, `emmaApi.sessionAccess`, `hardeningGaps`, `sendPressCircuitBreaker`, and every suite that imports `emma/impl/workPlans` (`emma.workPlanTemplateTools`, `workPlanStepModels{,.carryOver}`, `workPlanModelFailLoud`, `modifyWorkPlan.preservation`, `eng1858.usageAttribution`): 11 suites, 386/386 pass.
- Changes to `resultEndpoints.test.ts`: the review cases now present the token (the new contract), and the send case mocks the session asset it sends. No assertion was weakened.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. It is stateless: nothing was persisted. Links issued with `#token=` would still open, because the old routes ignore the header and the fragment.

## Risks / not covered

- The rate limit is per instance, not global. A reviewer token never expires (same lifetime as before); a leaked link stays usable until `JWT_SECRET` rotates.
- `GET /r/:name/status/:sessionId` (lead waiting page) still returns `leadEmail`/`contentHtml` to anyone with the session id, and it doesn't check that the session belongs to `:name`. That page is meant for the lead, so I left it out of scope. Flagged as a follow-up.
- Not live-tested against staging or production (rules forbid running the app against prod). The proof is the supertest route tests, the red check, and the portal vitest.

title: ENG-2653: anonymous session transfer requires the visitor's conversable token
body:
## Problem

Verified on `origin/main` 7f3ff14bd: `routes/agentMode.ts:164` `PUT /api/agent-mode/session/:sessionId/transfer` → `agentModeController.transferSession` (:17194-17222). If the session's `userId` starts with `anon_`, it calls `chatbotDb.updateSessionUserId(sessionId, req.user.userId)` with no proof that the caller is that anonymous visitor. Any signed-in user who learns an anonymous chat id (public plan / lead-magnet links, logs, referrers, shared URLs) can take the chat over, including everything the visitor typed.

## Where anonymous sessions come from, and what the anonymous browser holds
- `createSessionWithPlan` (`POST /public/plan/:planTitle/session`, public plan pages and lead magnets): owner `anon_<uuid>`, `sessionType: 'predefined-work-plan'`. It mints an interactive-share **conversable token** and returns it as `conversableToken` and in `redirectUrl` (`/plan/:title/:id?conversable=…`). The portal's `PlanPage.setPlanSession` stores `{ sessionId, conversableToken, userId }` in localStorage `agentweb_plan_sessions`. That token is the only secret the anonymous browser holds; there is no anon cookie or JWT.
- `resultEndpointController` (`POST /r/:name/trigger`): owner `anon_<uuid>`, `sessionType: 'result-endpoint'`. Its iShare token is also served by the **unauthenticated** `GET /review/:sessionId` to anyone holding the session id, so for these sessions the token proves nothing. The portal never stores them for transfer.

## Fix
- The body must contain `conversableToken` (a non-empty string), else **400** before any read.
- It is compared in constant time (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`, length-checked) against the session's **active, unexpired** `interactiveShareMetadata.token`, using the same expiry rule `getInteractiveShareExpiresAt` applies to iShare access. Anything else gets **404 `Session not found`**, identical to a missing session, so the endpoint confirms nothing about probed ids. That includes not revealing "not anonymous" to a caller without the token. The read is record-only and strongly consistent.
- With valid proof: if the owner isn't `anon_` → 400 `Session is not anonymous` (unchanged contract). If it isn't `predefined-work-plan` → 400 `Session cannot be transferred`.
- `chatbotDb.updateSessionUserId` gains an optional `expectedUserId`, which adds `ConditionExpression userId = :expected` and returns `null` when the condition fails. The transfer passes the anonymous owner it just checked, so a concurrent transfer cannot overwrite the winner (→ 400). This is its only caller; the parameter is optional and additive.

**Companion portal PR (send the proof):** AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1304. Both portal callers (`AgentMode.tsx` home-page sweep and `useAgentModeSessions.transferPlanSessionIfNeeded`) now send the stored `conversableToken`.
**Deploy order: merge and deploy #1304 first, or together with this.** The old backend ignores the body. An old portal against the new backend gets 400 and clears its list, so a new sign-up's anonymous chat would stay anonymous rather than move into the account. Nothing is lost or exposed either way.

## 360 impact
- Callers of `/transfer`: only the two portal call sites above (grep across the portal, the backend, partner-portal and mintlify-docs). `middleware/evaluation.ts` blocks the route for sandbox accounts; that is unchanged, and `evaluationAccess.test.ts` passes.
- Delegate tokens: `req.user` is the target account, so a delegate holding the token transfers into the target account. No other change.
- `updateSessionUserId` has no other callers.
- Not changed: after a transfer the conversable token stays active on the now-owned session, as before. Revoking or rotating it is a possible follow-up.

## Tests
- `src/__tests__/agentModeController.transferSession.test.ts` was **rewritten**. The old suite asserted that a transfer with no proof succeeds, which is exactly the defect. 17 tests now cover:
  - valid token → transfer, with the conditional owner passed
  - valid token on a non-anon session → 400; on a result-endpoint session → 400
  - race → 400
  - missing, empty or non-string token → 400 with no read
  - wrong token and missing session give the same 404; a shorter token → 404; an oversized session id → 404 without a read (DynamoDB would reject the key with a 500)
  - revoked, expired or absent share → 404 even with a matching token
  - no "not anonymous" oracle without the token
  - read and update errors → 500
- `src/__tests__/evaluationAccess.test.ts` still passes. Combined: **89/89 pass** at the first head; the transfer suite is 17/17 at the current head. The pre-push hook ran tsc plus 113–145 related suites (1909–2192 tests) green on each push.
- With the fix reverted, 14 of the (then) 16 fail.
- `npm run typecheck`: pass.
- Portal: see #1304 (vitest 6/6, tsc, eslint with no new findings).

## Rollback
Revert this PR. The portal change is harmless on the old backend. No data or schema change; the conditional write uses the existing key.

## Risks
- Anonymous plan sessions created before a share token existed, or whose share was revoked, can no longer be transferred (404 → the portal clears its list). Neither case has a token the visitor could present.

title: test(billing): pin the clock in the PAYG settlement suite (ENG-668)
body:
## What
`paygSettlementService.test.ts` failed on the last ~9 days of every month (1 test on 23 Oct, 8 on 24 Oct, 1-2 through the 31st). Test-only fix; no change to the billing code.

## Why it failed
The fixtures settle a fixed September invoice and add fixed day offsets (`since + 8 * DAY`, `+ 9 * DAY`) to the real clock: `since` comes from the service's own `new Date()`. But the sweep does nothing on day 1 of a month (`before_day_2`) and settles the PREVIOUS month. So whenever "today + 8/9 days" crossed into the next month, the sweep skipped or settled the wrong month, and assertions like `expect(s2.outcomes).toMatchObject({ payment_unconfirmed: 1 })` saw `{}`.

## Fix
Pin `Date` to the fixtures' day (3 Oct 2026 12:00Z) in the shared `beforeEach`, faking only `Date` (timers, ticks and promises stay real), and restore in `afterEach`. The file already pins that same instant in two tests.

## Verified
176/176 on the real date, and with the system clock set to 24, 25 and 31 Oct, 1 Nov, 31 Dec and 1 Jan (before the fix: failures from 23 Oct on). The repo's pre-push hook ran all 468 affected suites green on Node 22, no bypass.

Risk: test-only. Rollback: revert.

title: ENG-2113 PR A: plan-route decision (dark, no callers) + caller enumeration test
body:
## What
A pure, injectable module (`services/funding/subscriptionRoute.ts`) that decides whether ONE interactive chat turn runs on the user's own Claude subscription, plus a test that classifies every way a turn can start. **Nothing calls it yet** (the backend that consumes a `claude_subscription` route comes in a later PR), so this PR changes no behavior.

## Why
Part of ENG-1816 / ENG-2113 (B4), design v3. The safety rules are written and tested once, before anything uses them:
- The funding choice is the user's **explicit pick**; no pick means AgentWeb, exactly as today, with no I/O.
- **Allow-list, default deny**: only the authenticated session OWNER in the plain interactive chat. A plain admin acting in another user's session, delegated sessions (`isDelegated` must be a real `false`), shares, conversable visitors, Slack/email/Teams and every background caller are denied before any lookup. (An equality check on user ids cannot catch delegation: in a delegated request `req.user` is the TARGET.)
- A pick that cannot be honoured (flag off, connection invalid/expired/revoked, model without a plan alias, lookup failed) is a **typed stop**, never an AgentWeb-paid run. Unusable data (non-list lookup result, NaN/string expiry, records owned by someone else) fails closed.
- Registry id to CLI alias table is exact-by-id and verified against the pinned CLI (2.1.294 `init` event): older versions (e.g. Opus 4.8) have no plan route; the table is pinned against the real registry (haiku/sonnet-5.5 are admin-only there today, a picker/L5 decision).
- `RunFunding` gains optional `hostEpoch` / `planModel` (type-only); `toRunFunding` takes the controller's resolved billing subject.
- Module header documents the caller contract (`sessionOwnerUserId = session.userId`, both delegate sources, canonical explicit-pick model id).
- `subscriptionRouteCallers.test.ts` scans whole files and fails when a `generateSessionResponse` call site is added, removed or moved to another function, or when the function is bound/renamed/assigned/passed as a value.

## Review
Two independent reviewers (security/logic, spec fidelity) found 0 blockers and several majors, all addressed in a978f93a6: strict booleans, owner trust, billing subject, alias/registry pinning, caller-test strength, and removal of `admissionPlanFor` (its flat shape does not match the real gates; to be designed with the wiring PR).

## Tests
- 70 tests (table-driven deny paths, strict inputs, connection states, boundaries, tie-breaks, fake-timer cleanup, registry pin, caller enumeration).
- Hand mutation testing: 27 mutants across two rounds; every one killed except 3 equivalent ones (prototype-key guard, funding owner taken from record when the owner filter already guarantees it, explicit non-list check when the filter would throw anyway). Caller test verified with 3 fake callers and a moved owner site.
- **Live check** (manual, test instance, real Dev funding-flags row read-only + real `Dev-AW-LlmConnections` through the real owner index, throwaway rows): 29/29, 0 rows left. Dev flags row is currently disabled/empty so the real "enabled" path was covered by unit tests only.
- `src/services/funding`: 744 pass; 3 existing tests fail identically on plain `main` (toolBridgeMcp, runBackend.integration, emmaToolBridgeExecutor.integration).
- Typecheck: only the existing local `twilio` errors. ESLint clean on the new files.


## Existing failing funding tests: root cause is the local environment, not the repo
`toolBridgeMcp`, `runBackend.integration` and `emmaToolBridgeExecutor.integration` failed on a machine running Node 18 (CI and the deploy workflows use Node 22; `twilio@6` also requires Node >= 20). Node 18 has no global `crypto`, so `pkce-challenge` (an MCP SDK dependency) falls back to a dynamic `import("node:crypto")` that Jest cannot run. A guarded test-setup polyfill fixed it (669014d44) but was reverted (8d6f3798b) once the right fix was clear: run Node 22 with a fresh `npm ci` (the stale local `node_modules` also lacked `twilio`).

Full backend suite on Node 22 with a clean `npm ci`, no polyfill: 2476 of 2484 suites pass. The 8 failures are pre-existing and unrelated to this PR: 7 fail identically on current `main` (tablePrefix, admin.announcements, agentModeController.agentWebModelRouter, createTablesDrift, icpPersonaIdentity, onboardingBrandReview, sdkConstructionGuard), and `paygSettlementService` was fixed on `main` by a30d72fd4, which this branch now includes. `src/services/funding` + `paygSettlementService` pass 923/923 after merging main; typecheck and eslint are clean.

## Safety / rollback
Pure addition with no callers; deleting the files restores the previous state. No data-plane, schema, infra or flag changes.

## Not in this PR
Wiring into the controller, the backend that runs the turn, funding-aware admission wiring, the bridge/relay, the picker UI. Those follow design v3 (`eng-1816-brain`).

title: ENG-2113 PR B: tool bridge ledger, durable halts, stop, repeat guard, JSON-mode adapter (dark)
body:
## ENG-2113 PR B: tool bridge hardening for Claude subscription runs (dark)

No production caller: nothing opens a bridge run yet (PR C wires it), the funding flag stays off. Every new interface field is optional; the 37 existing bridge tests are unchanged except one assertion for the new `execute` signature.

### What it does
- **Ledger**: every bridge call leaves a backend-only record (minimal result, model text, group, flags) for PR C to persist.
- **Durable halts**: a confirmation-requiring result is handed to `persistHalt` with the write slot held, before the call is answered; same-message siblings announced by the stream (name + args must match) are admitted, everything else is refused. State is session-level, keyed (userId, sessionId), with an epoch bumped by `beginTurn`.
- **Stop**: `cancelSession` refuses unstarted/new calls and closes the session's runs; never touches a pending halt.
- **A write never runs twice by accident**: an identical call arriving while the first is still executing joins it (the 60 s CLI cut + model retry, reproduced live); strict-effect repeats return the original outcome.
- **Liveness**: `isLive` is the last await before the executor; writes use a fresh funding-flags read (never cached, never last-good); definite revoke closes the run, a failed read refuses that call only.
- **Adapter**: `enableJsonResponse: true` (the SDK's default SSE mode breaks the CLI handshake: every turn died in <1 s), abort signal to the ledger, drain/cancel/revoke pass-throughs.

### Evidence
- Funding suite 840 pass; typecheck clean.
- Live (real adapter + real pinned `claude` 2.1.294 + real host, haiku): handshake, 3 batched previews each persisted before return, the cut-and-retry write executed exactly once, unicode byte-identical and equal to the stream input, revoke mid-turn refuses the next write, stop mid-write: **13/13**.
- Independent security + correctness reviews of the diff: 6 + 12 findings, all fixed with a regression test each (`toolBridge.reviewFixes.test.ts`).

### `call_*` classification (for review; tripwire test fails on an unlisted tool)
| tool | repeat rule |
|---|---|
| call_meta_marketing_api, call_google_ads_api, call_linkedin_marketing_api, call_ads | strict (action not in args) |
| call_hubspot_api, call_attio_api | by real args (Emma policy) |
| call_meta_ads_insights_api, call_google_ads_reporting_api, call_linkedin_ads_insights_api | read |
| any unlisted call_* | strict (fail toward not repeating) |

### Findings that shape later PRs (see dev/pending note)
Killing the CLI with SIGKILL while it refreshes an expired token destroys the login; SIGTERM + grace kept it 5/5. The host/PR C/PR K stop paths must send SIGTERM first. Not in this PR: relay (PK), wiring (PC), messageId host->backend (boundary rule is the fallback).

title: ENG-2113 PR H: graceful stop of customer units (SIGTERM first) so a login mid-refresh survives
body:
## ENG-2113 PR H: customer units stop gracefully (SIGTERM first); a login mid-refresh survives

### Why
Every host-initiated stop of the `claude` CLI was a SIGKILL, including the normal end of a turn. The CLI refreshes an expired access token in its first seconds: the server rotates BOTH tokens and the new pair is written afterwards, so a SIGKILL in that window destroys the customer's login (they must sign in again). Reproduced live on the test host: a host abort at 700 ms lost the login; this also explains the earlier "kept login died within 20 h". SIGTERM with a grace period kept it every time.

### What
- Unit properties: `KillMode=mixed` (SIGTERM to the CLI only; the egress helper keeps the network up while the CLI finishes writing, then systemd SIGKILLs the rest as soon as the CLI exits), `KillSignal=SIGTERM`, `TimeoutStopSec=<limits.stopGraceSec>s` (default 10, allowed 2..12), `SendSIGKILL=yes`.
- `UnitChild.kill` / `killUnit` = `systemctl stop <unit>`; SIGKILL only if that stop fails or times out (exit 5 "not loaded" counts as done).
- Revoke and the hazard alarm still kill HARD (`killAll({hard})`): the home is wiped right after and nothing may run on a grace period. Disable and reconnect stay graceful (their login must survive).
- Timers derived from the grace: adapter `killWaitMs`, manager `abortGraceMs`, port `killTimeoutMs`. The `auth status` check after a failed turn no longer runs beside a process still inside its grace (reports transient).
- Host shutdown stops the units BEFORE closing the egress proxy.
- Config: `limits.stopGraceSec` (closed schema: add the key only AFTER the new host binary is deployed; the default needs no config change).

### Evidence
- Host suite 1,194 tests pass; typecheck clean; hand mutation testing (25 + 6 follow-up mutants, all killed).
- Two independent reviews (security/blast radius; correctness + mutation) - all findings fixed, regression test per finding.
- LIVE on the test host, real systemd, real forced-expiry refresh, aborts through the host's own interrupt path at 300/500/700/900/1200 ms and again at 300/700/1200 ms on the final build: login survived 8/8. Normal and aborted turns end with the CLI exiting 143 (SIGTERM).

### Pre-merge
Worker-only change, dark: the prod worker has no customers and deploys through the signed, drain-gated pipeline with automatic rollback. Revert = revert the merge.

title: fix(linkedin): retry fresh-token 401 for createComment (ENG-2663)
body:
## Summary
LinkedIn can answer 401 "revoked by the user" for an access token used under a second after it was minted by a refresh, then accept the same token moments later (prod 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-25; both recovered with no reconnect). #3760 added a one-time 5s retry for `createPost` and `createReaction`. `createComment` is also a write path (scheduled engagement executor and Emma) and was not covered, so a fresh-token 401 there would still tell the user to reconnect.

## Change
- `createComment`, `createRepost` and the post image upload now use the same fresh-token retry as `createPost`/`createReaction` (#3760).
- The helper is renamed `retryIfFreshToken401`. It retries once after 10s (short, so an interactive user is never blocked long) and only for a 401 on a token refreshed in the same call. A 401 creates nothing, so there is no duplicate-write risk.
- If LinkedIn still rejects the fresh token, the adapter throws `FreshTokenRejectedError` instead of the "reconnect" error. It declares class `rate_limit`, so the model gets `Retryable: yes` guidance (call wait_seconds 60, then try once more) and is told not to ask the user to reconnect. The four LinkedIn tool handlers (post, repost, comment, react) pass the declared class through; the engagement executor reschedules such an action 30 minutes later, like a rate limit.
- "Fresh" means minted under 5 minutes ago, derived from the stored `token_expires_at` (60-day lifetime), not "this call refreshed". Otherwise the agent's retry a minute later would read the saved token as a stored one and get the false reconnect error. A 401 on an older token is unchanged and still says reconnect, so a genuine revocation reaches the user, and the executor's 30-minute reschedule cannot loop.
- A fresh-token rejection during a per-image upload is rethrown rather than posting without the image. `createComment`/`createRepost` re-check publish consent (ENG-827) before the retried write.
- The earlier introspection approach in this PR was dropped: introspecting right after a refresh hits the same rejection window and could mark healthy accounts inactive, and the logs show no genuine revocations to detect.

## Verification
- Two new adapter tests: a refreshed token that gets a 401 retries and succeeds; a stored token that gets a 401 is not retried. The first fails without the change.
- New tests: adapter comment/repost/image-upload retries, exhaustion error, end-to-end classification (`Retryable: yes`, not auth), executor reschedule vs. genuine-401 mark-done. Affected suites pass (280 tests, including the real handlers throwing the real error); backend typecheck clean.
- Not verified against live LinkedIn, and the 10s delay is unmeasured. Verify on prod after deploy by watching logs for `ENG-2663: 401 on a just-refreshed token; retry`.

## Not in this PR
Stale "Nothing Posted" session title; the agent filing ENG-2663 on a retryable error. Refreshing tokens ahead of expiry was considered and judged over-engineering for 2 incidents in 14 days.

title: feat: LP consent banner + Consent Mode v2 gating (ENG-2667)
body:
## What
ENG-2667 (ENG-2665 slice 2). New pure util `backend/src/utils/consentInjection.ts` (`applyConsentModeToLayout` / `applyConsentModeToLayoutFiles`). It runs after the GTM/Pixel/Ads injectors. In `consent` mode it:
1. Puts `gtag('consent','default', denied ×4)` first in `<head>`, ahead of any Google tag. A returning visitor with `aw_consent=granted` is updated to granted immediately.
2. Wraps our Meta Pixel block in `window.__awPixelInit`, so fbevents.js is not loaded and `fbq('init')` (which sets _fbp/_fbc) does not run until consent is granted. It also drops the `<noscript>` beacon, which can't be gated.
3. Adds a neutral, script-rendered Accept/Reject banner that writes the first-party `aw_consent` cookie. That is the cookie the ENG-2666 middleware (#3759) already reads to gate the attribution cookies.

- The banner copy is neutral placeholder text. Harsha must review the final client-facing copy before Flatfee rollout (AC5).

## Tests
`src/utils/__tests__/consentInjection.test.ts` has 9 tests, all green. They run the emitted scripts in a vm fake DOM and cover:
- default=denied is emitted first
- before consent: no pixel load, no cookies, banner shown
- Accept: granted cookie, consent update, pixel init
- Reject: only `aw_consent=denied` is set
- returning visitors
- the form is untouched, and the transform is idempotent
