title: ENG-2720: book the web-search fee, re-ground the admission estimate, customer-safe quotes (Apollo stays at 9 credits)
body:
## Summary

ENG-2720 follow-up to #3846 (Luna enrichment default). **This PR no longer changes what Apollo is booked at**: on the 2026-11-02 sync call the owner of the margin rule (Harsha) decided to keep the Apollo email-waterfall booking at 9 credits ($0.445) and revisit when phone fetching ships. What it does change: books the OpenRouter web-search fee, re-grounds the admission estimate, makes the pre-run quote customer-safe and accurate, and closes a token leak.

### What changes
- **Web-search fee is now in the ledger** (`funding/recordLlmUsage.ts` `openRouterByokCostUsd`, used by `agentModeService.callLLM`): on a BYOK OpenRouter response `usage.cost` is OpenRouter's own charge (search fee: $0.007 per search on the default Exa engine, $0.005 on Parallel) and `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` is the provider's token bill; only the latter was recorded (~$1.1 of fees against ~$0.2 of tokens on the real Opiner list). Now booked = upstream + router charge (a fee with no upstream bill is booked on top of price-book tokens). Non-BYOK calls are unchanged (`usage.cost` is already the total). BYOK is decided per call from `is_byok`: prod has four BYOK slots (bedrock, vertex, azure, groq) and a slot error silently falls back to OpenRouter's key (`is_byok: false`). `openrouter:web_search` has exactly one caller (`callLLM`).
- **Admission estimate re-grounded** (`enrichmentBatchBudget.ts`): `?mode=estimate` returned $27.25 for 5 leads while the customer estimate said ~$0.55 (~50x). It reserved an unused `enrich.so phone_finder` ($0.25/lead), Enigma on every field, You.com x4 per field and a gpt-5.5-sized $0.10 per-field band, and omitted `person_match`. Now: each identity vendor once per lead (Apollo waterfall at the booked $0.445), a model-aware per-field reserve (10x the measured booked cost ~$0.0018 on Luna, scaled by the enrichment model's price, floor $0.02), and one worst-case Enigma fetch ($0.52, the documented 52-credit ceiling) only for an Enigma-allowlisted user with a card-revenue field. For 5 leads / 20 plain fields on Luna: about $5.1 (it would be about $40 under the old formula at this Apollo rate).
- **Customer-safe, config- and lead-aware quote** (a list with no saved config is quoted on the reference config as before; a saved config that cannot be read fails the quote with a generic 500 and issues no token, since the run itself would fail on it; `services/enrichmentQuote.ts`, wired in `routes/crm.ts`; `enrichmentCostEstimate.ts`; `enrichmentBatchBudget.ts` `projectAllowance`): `POST .../enrich-v3/estimate`, `POST .../enrich-v3?mode=estimate` and the stale-token 409 now return only `{ leadCount, estimatedPercentOfAllowance, withinAllowance, confirmationToken }`. They used to return dollar totals and a per-vendor breakdown (our allocated rates), contrary to ENG-1212; no portal consumed them yet, so the shape could change now. `estimatedPercentOfAllowance` is the expected cost over the allowance in force (credits and pooling applied; one usage read for the allowance, so a racing or failed-open ledger read cannot skew it; 2 decimals under 1%, otherwise 1; `null` for a plan with no dollar allowance); `withinAllowance` is the conservative admission reserve for that config, so it predicts admission. Expected cost: Apollo line (rate card, $0.445) only on leads with no usable email (blank or placeholder-domain emails count as none, as in the resolver; a selected subset is counted only for ids that really belong to the list, with their real email state, so fake ids cannot amplify the quote: 100,000 fake ids used to read as 28,315%), LLM line scaling with the saved config's fields and the enrichment model's price (floor $0.002 per field per lead, measured ~$0.0018 on Luna), plus one Enigma fetch ($0.28) per lead when an allowlisted user configured a card-revenue field. The 112-lead Opiner reference run at the reference config estimates **$25.37** (was $31.60; only the LLM line changed).
- **Confirmation token is now an HMAC** under a subkey derived from the server secret, bound to the user, over a JSON-encoded tuple (no delimiter collisions), compared in constant time. The old unkeyed `sha256(list:count:total)` could be brute-forced back into the dollar total in milliseconds, leaking our rates through the quote that hides them. Tokens issued before the deploy go stale and the client re-fetches.
- **Rate card, no amount change:** `apollo:full_enrichment` ($0.445) becomes `apollo:waterfall_email` (same $0.445), plus an unused `waterfall_phone` (8 credits, $0.396) so phone numbers can slot in later; nothing books `waterfall_phone` today and the code comment says what to change when phone ships (set `waterfall_email` to 1 credit, or the phone credits are counted twice). The ledger operation label changes with the key; historical rows keep their stored cost. Version `2026-11-02`.
- **Web-search parameters** (`CRM_ENRICH_V3_WEB_SEARCH_PARAMS`, JSON, default unchanged): lets operators pass e.g. `{"engine":"parallel"}` to OpenRouter's `openrouter:web_search` tool for enrichment. Unknown keys and bad values dropped; `max_results` capped at 25; `max_uses` is only honoured by Anthropic's native search.

### Apollo: the decision, and what it costs (for the record)
No request in the backend asks for a phone (no `reveal_phone_number` / `run_waterfall_phone` anywhere) and the Apollo account shows 0 phone credits used, so the 9-credit amount (1 email + 8 phone) is about 10-40x Apollo's real cost (observed 1-2 credits per contact; real $0.01975 per credit). Harsha's call keeps it: wallets are ~40% of price (Starter $80 of $199, Pro $200 of $499), so the margin is already built in. Accepted consequence: included allowances drain faster than the work warrants, and on accounts with pay-as-you-go overage on (prod: one, Opiner, since 2026-10; settlement is enabled) the overage is billed from booked cost at the tier markup (1.5x). Raised with the owner as a question, not a reversal.

### Effect (prod ledger, all-time `enrichment` + `crm_enrichment` rows, Opiner + Nuerraa)
Booked $165.73 today -> ~$113 (-32%) from #3846's Luna switch alone (~$53 real LLM savings); this PR adds the search fee on top (~$0.015 per lead on the Opiner list) and does not touch the Apollo line.

### Why the BYOK fee is `upstream + router charge` (not double counting)
On a BYOK OpenRouter response the two usage figures are separate bills, not overlapping ones. Real calls through the app's own `callLLM` on test env 1 (Bedrock-hosted `gpt-5.6-luna`, `is_byok: true`):

| web-search engine | `usage.cost` (OpenRouter's charge) | `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` (provider tokens) | booked by the ledger |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (Exa) | 0.007 | 0.00050 | 0.00750 |
| `parallel` | 0.005 | 0.00070 | 0.00570 |

`usage.cost` equals exactly the documented per-search fee ($0.007 Exa, $0.005 Parallel) and never contained the token bill (a call whose search ran natively inside the provider showed `usage.cost: 0` with the search fee inside the upstream figure). The ledger rows reproduced the sum to the cent in every run, and the repo already applies the same rule elsewhere (`openRouterCallCostUsd` in `scripts/runTaskSuccessJudgeTrial.ts`, tested in `taskSuccessJudge.test.ts`). An Opslane stand-in that reports `usage.cost` equal to the upstream bill (0.0068 and 0.0068) is a synthetic shape we have not seen from OpenRouter; if OpenRouter ever started folding the token bill into `usage.cost` on BYOK the symptom would be exactly that, and `openRouterByokCostUsd` is the single place to change (its unit tests pin the rule). Calls with no search report `usage.cost: 0`, so for them nothing changes (a plain BYOK call measured `usage.cost: 0` against an upstream bill of $0.00004).

**Why there is deliberately no "ignore a charge as large as the upstream bill" rule (tried, reviewed, reverted):** Opslane's replay uses a stand-in response in which `usage.cost` equals `upstream_inference_cost` and reads that as double counting. Real responses never look like that (see the probes above), and the fee is routinely several times the token bill on the Luna default (fee $0.007 vs tokens ~$0.0005), so any rule keyed on "router charge >= upstream" silently drops the real search fee whenever a response lacks the tool-use field. A guard of that kind was added in `59c35a400`, an independent review proved it drops 93% of a real fee in that case, and it was removed. What remains is a tripwire only: both bills are always booked, and a warning that names the response's keys is logged (at most once a minute) when the router charge is at least the whole upstream bill and no server-tool use is reported, so a change in OpenRouter's reporting shows up in the logs. Opslane's stand-in finding is therefore expected to remain on this PR.

## Test plan (all done)
Changes after Opslane's run on `17cafd0`: an unreadable saved config now fails the quote (read first, before the list scan) instead of silently quoting the reference config; the BYOK double-count guard above; and the token's JSON-encoded tuple.
- **Pre-push hook:** the last three pushes ran the real hook (typecheck + related suites green), not `--no-verify`. (Earlier pushes of this PR bypassed it after a manual typecheck; disclosed to the owner.)
- **Jest under Node 22:** rate card (9-credit amount, phone-split invariant, margin floor), Apollo ledger metering (404/422 on a waterfall request, every emitted key priced, no phone parameter), BYOK cost (helper unit tests, fee + upstream, non-BYOK double-count guard, fee-only case), admission estimate (measured-booking floor, model-aware reserve, name-only Enigma fields, allowlist gating wired into both the budget check and the admission estimate), customer estimate (field/email/model scaling, reference run pinned, token not invertible, bound to user and secret, constant-time compare, de-duplicated lead selection), the quote service (`enrichmentQuote.test.ts`, incl. early exit and the admission-reserve wiring), **route-level tests for all three quote surfaces** (`crm.enrichQuoteRoutes.test.ts`: authorization order, no dollar or vendor leakage, token flow, placeholder/blank emails, fake and duplicate ids reaching the run once, no-saved-config reference quote, unreadable saved config fails with no token, JWT-secret fail-closed) and **the same surfaces against the real access-control code** (`crm.enrichQuoteAccess.test.ts`: owner, org owner, org admin and listed CRM editor allowed; plain same-org member, other org and no org get 403), web-search params. Mutation-checked: removing or downgrading any authorization check, the allowlist gating, the subset clamp or early exit, the de-duplication, the email predicates, the keyed token, the admission reserve in the quote, the config fallback or the customer-safe view fails a test.
- **Live on test env 1, on `17cafd0b5`** (`Dev-AW-UsageRecords`; 25 of 25 checks plus the variants): a 5-lead broker run books 5 `apollo:waterfall_email` rows at exactly $0.445 each (one Apollo request per lead; $2.225 booked in the dev ledger, not spend), `person_match` $0.0495 each, no `waterfall_phone`/`full_enrichment`; no Email field or leads that already have an email book no broker call (also under `always_overwrite` and `refreshFields`); the three quote surfaces return exactly the four customer fields with no dollar or vendor words, share one 32-hex HMAC token; a valid token passes the gate, goes stale when the lead count changes, and does not confirm another user's run; a user from a separate org gets 403 on every surface; 100,000 fake `leadIds` count as zero, duplicate ids count once and a run with duplicate ids processes each lead once. Web tier on Luna (default, valid/invalid/out-of-range search params) and the gpt-5.5 rollback: HTTP 200, 0 failures, quote is model-aware (0.65% vs 1%), rollback booked ~$0.37-0.50 per 4-lead run vs ~$0.005-0.015 on Luna. Search-fee probe: two calls through the app's own `callLLM` booked $0.01320 = the exact sum of both bills. Not tested live: Apollo's async webhook delivery (env1's ngrok domain is held by another endpoint); untouched here, to be verified on prod right after the deploy.
- **CI on the head:** backend build, dev-note guard, CodeRabbit and Opslane (nothing at P1 or above) are green; branch current with main; the dev-log consolidation script was run on a copy and folds the pending fragment.
- **Independent reviews** (fresh-context subagents, read-only, security first, exploit and mutation checks; the sixth read `5a9624939` and found no blocker, the seventh, on `4e7a4e3b7`, found no authorization, leak or token issue; its one recommendation, to drop the double-count guard, is applied). Fixed during the reviews: untested 404/422 path, `max_results` bound, unwired env var, Enigma reserve that never fired for real configs, a model-unaware guard, a fee dropped when a response has no upstream bill, a confirmation token that leaked the dollar total, a percent computed from the difference of two ledger reads, Enigma reserved for users who cannot buy it, fake-id amplification of the quote, untested route glue and Enigma allowlist wiring, a double list scan on the 409 path, a non-constant-time token compare, duplicate ids reaching DynamoDB's batch read, whole-list scans for small subsets, and a dev-note heading that would have aborted the post-merge dev-log consolidation.

## Open items / not in this PR
1. Raised with Harsha: Opiner's pay-as-you-go overage is computed from booked cost, which includes the 9-credit Apollo line (estimated ~$20 of their October overage). His call whether that is acceptable.
2. The customer estimate's per-field LLM figure uses the enrichment model's price but the 34/112 Apollo broker share is an Opiner-wide calibration applied to the leads that lack an email.
3. Webhook delivery to be verified on prod after deploy. Whether Luna lands on a BYOK host in prod is visible in the first run's `is_byok` log line.

**Known low-severity items from the final reviews, deliberately not changed** (each cheap to do in a follow-up):
- The group-level Apollo tier (`enrichmentGroupWaterfall.ts` 3.5a) never looks at `lead.email`, so a unit test that lists `email` as a requested field for a lead that already has one fires the broker. Not reproducible through the real pipeline: live runs with leads that already had an email booked no broker call under fill-if-empty, always-overwrite and refresh-fields. If it ever happens the quote would understate by the Apollo line; admission always reserves one waterfall per lead.
- `estimatedPercentOfAllowance` is uncapped and fine-grained. With the real route code and a known $80 allowance a reviewer recovered the quote formula's blended coefficients (for example the blended Apollo line per lead) from large lists; no single vendor rate is recoverable. ENG-1212 accepts percentages; a "100+" cap or coarser steps would harden it.
- A quote pages the list (200 per page), also for ids that do not exist (about 500 sequential reads on a 100k-lead list); there is no rate limiter on `/api/crm` (pre-existing).
- The BYOK fee booking covers `agentModeService.callLLM`; `codingAgentService` and the Python agent-engine reporter still book upstream cost only on BYOK. The fee-only fallback prices an unpriced model at Sonnet rates.
- If OpenRouter ever changed `usage.cost` to include the upstream bill, a BYOK call would be over-booked by the token bill (about 7% on a Luna search call, up to 2x on a call with no search). The tripwire warning above is the signal; the alternative (a rule that ignores a large router charge) was rejected because it under-books by up to 93% of the real fee.
- `leadIds` is not size-capped (a 50 MB body of ~4M ids costs a few extra seconds and ~340 MB of heap for an authenticated list editor); capping only the quote would make large legitimate selections fail the quote while the run still works, so it is left as is.
- A model id such as `constructor` would make the per-field reserve NaN; reachable only through an operator env value, and it fails closed (usage check throws).

Context: Linear ENG-2720 and the Apollo thread in #harsha-manan-anurag-agent.

title: feat(smartlead): count replied, bounced and unsubscribed contacts per push run (ENG-673)
body:
## What

Counts how many contacts of a Smartlead push replied, bounced or unsubscribed since it was sent, so the push dialog can show it (portal PR in AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal, same branch name).

- The Smartlead event handler adds one to an `events` map (`replied`, `bounced`, `unsubscribed`) on the existing push run item. One count per contact and kind; hard bounces only; a bounce or unsubscribe counts only when that call wrote the block, so our own withdrawal sweep echoed back by Smartlead and admin blocks are not counted, and a retry after a failed block write still counts once.
- Counters are written after every matched contact's reply, alert and block are done, through a try/catch and a 2 s cap on the wait. A failing, slow or missing counter changes nothing for the contact and does not hold up another contact's opt-out.
- `history()` adds each run's counters from the base table (`GetItem`, at most 25). The history indexes project a fixed attribute list that cannot be changed on an existing table, and `BatchGetItem` is not in the app role's grant.
- Additive attribute only. No table, index, key or projection change; runs made before this simply have none.

## Checks

- Unit tests: counter semantics (once per contact, replay, second reply, soft bounce, echo, retry, slow/failing counter, two lists), the run item reader, `countContactEvent`, `getRunEvents`, history.
- Two blind reviews; the second reviewed the final code.
- env1: real DynamoDB, real Smartlead throwaway campaign, simulated events through the public webhook route with the token Smartlead holds.
- Production test after deploy (below).

title: fix(agent): detect paging spirals that evade loop guards (ENG-2778)

- New characterization test (`stepBudgetTruncationFlag.test.ts`): model pages with empty text every step → exactly one synthesis call, it is call 40, content is the model's recap (not the canned apology), the tool call made during synthesis is never executed.

## Not tested
Live LLM behaviour on the forced-synthesis turn (needs staging replay of a session like 3d6be53d). Fixes #1, #2-tool, #5 from the issue remain out of scope.

## Rollback

body:
## What
Retires the Google Custom Search JSON API (closed to new customers, sunsets Jan 2027). ENG-1281.

## Call-site audit (AC1)
Only one module ever called the CSE endpoint: `backend/src/search/googleSearchProvider.ts` (deleted). Its sole consumer was `performGoogleSearch` in `backend/src/emma/impl/searchResearch.ts`, reached by `googleSearchWeb` from:

- `POST /api/emma/google-search-web` (`routes/emmaApi.ts`) and MCP tool `google_search_web` (`mcp/server/apiTools.ts`)

title: ENG-2271: inbound callbacks for the hot-lead org number
body:
## ENG-2271 follow-up: inbound callbacks for the hot-lead org number

When a lead calls the org's Twilio number back, ring the org's team members and connect the caller only when a member confirms. Before this change nothing answered inbound calls on that number.

### Behaviour
1. `POST /api/webhooks/twilio-voice/inbound` is the number's voice URL. The org is found from the signed `To` (`Called` if `To` is empty).
2. Gates, in order: kill switch, valid enabled config whose number equals the dialled one, an org owner, plan entitlement. Anything else says "unable to take your call" and hangs up. It never connects.
3. The first member from `selectHotLeadCallCandidates` (verified, window open, inside calling hours) is dialled from the org number with `answerOnBridge`.
4. The member hears "<business>: a lead is calling back. Are you available to take the call? Press 1." Only digit 1, and only if the member is still on the team and verified, bridges the call.
5. No answer, busy, failed or an unconfirmed screen moves to the next member, up to `maxAttemptsPerLead`. When nobody is left the caller is told nobody can take the call and is hung up. No voicemail, no recording.
6. Stateless: the tried members and the org id travel in the signed step URLs, so each step adds at most one member and a replay repeats the same decision. No lead call record and no timeline event.
7. Metering: only the member leg, at `voice_minute_outbound`, key `twilio:voice:<childSid>:member`, billed to the org owner. The caller's inbound leg is not metered because the rate card has no inbound rate (documented).
8. Newly provisioned numbers get this URL as their voice URL (`BuyNumberParams.voiceUrl`). The existing number `+1 567 221 9671` needs its voice URL set in the Twilio console by a person.

### Org lookup
There is no index on the number, so the org is found by a filtered scan of `AW-Organizations` kept as a 60-second in-process snapshot (`inboundNumberIndex.ts`, `orgDb.listHotLeadCallNumbers()`). The snapshot only locates the org: the org is then re-read consistently and its live config decides, so a stale entry can only end in a refusal. A number stored on two orgs is served to neither. Code only: no index, table or data change.

### Not verified against real Twilio
Listed in the doc's "Not verified" section: `To` is the E.164 dialled number; a hang-up inside a `<Number url>` screen ends the Dial as `completed` with `DialBridged=false`; the child leg's `completed` callback carries `ParentCallSid` and `CallDuration`; a `callerId` equal to the org number is accepted on a `<Dial>` answering an inbound call.

### Known limits
- No abuse limits on inbound (no per-caller limit or blocklist); Twilio's spend limits are the only ceiling. Documented as a go-live item.
- A caller can wait through up to 5 ring attempts.
- A number bought or released within the last 60 seconds is not seen yet.

### Tests
`npm run typecheck` clean. Targeted jest: 31 suites / 1753 tests passed (twilioVoiceWebhook, hotLeadCall, emma.hotLeadCall, orgHotLeadCall, services/voice), plus numberRent, sdkConstructionGuard and vendorMeter. New: `hotLeadCall.e2e.inbound.test.ts`, `inboundCallback.test.ts`, `inboundNumberIndex.test.ts`.

Part of ENG-2783 (full E2E plan). Not live until the number's voice URL is set and the kill switch is on.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Medium — inbound handler failures can block callback routing. The feature is gated by the kill switch and number URL configuration.

Adds stateless callbacks for organization Twilio numbers. Eligible calls ring team members, and a member must press 1 to connect. New numbers receive the inbound URL during provisioning; existing numbers require manual setup. Real-Twilio behavior remains unverified.

title: feat(smartlead): plain-language reply alert email with the contact's reply text (ENG-673)
body:
## What

When a contact replies to a Smartlead campaign, the list owner now gets a plain-language alert email that shows who replied, from which campaign and list, when, and **what they wrote**, with one button into the CRM. Before this, the owner got the shared generic "Lead list alert: email.received" email with raw field names.

ENG-673 (Smartlead connector, slice 3). Copy approved by the owner on 2026-11-03.

## Scope and safety for existing users

- The new email is used only for `email.received` whose event data has `source: "smartlead"`. That source is set only by the Smartlead event handler, so no existing alert (Gmail/Outlook replies, other event types) changes. The generic path in `leadListAlertService.sendAlertEmail` is untouched; the new branch is an early return (+21 lines).
- The reply text is carried only on the in-memory event to the alert. It is not stored on the engagement, not sent to Slack/WhatsApp, and absent for polled replies (the email then says Smartlead keeps the full reply).
- No table, index, IAM or environment change.

## Handling words an outsider wrote

The contact controls their name, the subject and the reply, so:

- everything is HTML-escaped; zero-width, bidi-override, control characters and U+2028/2029 are stripped (`smartleadSafeText.ts`)
- the inbox preview line is fixed wording, the quote bar is grey (not the button blue), and a caption says AgentWeb has not checked the text or links
- the button only takes http(s) URLs
- the excerpt cutter is linear-time and reads at most the first 10,000 characters (a blind review found an earlier version quadratic: 14 s on 100k spaces; fixed and tested)

## Checks

- Jest: `smartleadReplyAlertEmail`, `smartleadEvents`, `smartleadEventService`, `smartleadEventPoll` suites, 143 tests pass (includes hostile input, quote-marker false positives, emoji cuts, "reply text never stored", "other alerts unchanged")
- `npm run typecheck` clean on the final commit
- Final sample sent to the owner's own Gmail from the test environment (Subject `A new lead "Manan Test" replied to your campaign`); owner approved the look
- Blind reviews: three so far; the last found the blocker and spoofing items above, all fixed. A fresh review of the final code runs before merge.
- Still to do after deploy: production test with one real reply from the owner's own address.

## Known gaps, left on purpose

- Slack and WhatsApp alerts for a Smartlead reply still show the raw event name; the list settings screen still lists raw event names.
- Quote trimming is heuristic: a reply that itself uses `>` lines is cut early and shows less (fails safe); the cut is silent.

title: fix: deliver non-admin Meta Ads scheduled reports (ENG-2785)
body:
## What
Customer scheduled reports that use the ENG-1801 Meta Ads tools (`list_meta_ads_campaigns`, `call_meta_ads_insights_api`, `get_meta_ads_metrics`) were classified cross-account-sensitive unconditionally, so they were withheld from every non-admin recipient AND the non-admin owner (FlatFee schedule c1951eeb…, `no_authorized_recipients`). Customer-visible: those reports now email again.

## Why it is safe
getMetaCredentials only honours `client_id` for platform admins, so a non-admin owner's Meta calls can only read their own account. Classification now takes the owner's admin status:
- owner verified non-admin (`isAdmin === false`) → Meta tools don't count
- owner admin, or unknown/lookup failed → unchanged (sensitive, fail-closed)
- admin-only tools (list_all_clients, get_chat_history, …) → sensitive for everyone (unchanged)

Changed: `scheduledReportAccess.ts` (opts on reportContainsCrossAccountData / messagesReferenceCrossAccountTool / scheduleLikelySensitive / checkScheduleActivationRecipients), `emailService.classifyAndResolveScheduledReportRecipients` (resolves owner before classifying), `agentModeController` (preflight, lastKnownSensitive breadcrumb, create/update/toggle activation gates pass owner admin status).

Risk note (Security label): residual edge — an admin who ran a client_id-scoped Meta report and lost admin between run and send would be treated as non-admin. Window is seconds; accepted. Negative tests cover admin owner + Meta and non-admin owner + admin-only tools.

Not changed: existing `lastKnownSensitive=true` breadcrumbs are still honoured by the preflight (conservative). They self-heal on the next run since the breadcrumb is rewritten with the new classification; if SCHEDULED_REPORT_DELIVERY_ENFORCEMENT=true in prod, preflight could skip that next run — no data repair done here (data-plane gate).

## Tests
`npx jest` scheduledReportAccess, emailService.scheduledChat, emailService.dailyDigest, eng778.adminScheduledChats.route, mcp.tools.adminLookup, scheduledReportWithheldAlertDedup, agentModeController.scheduledChat: 7 suites / 295 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Rollback
Revert this PR; behaviour returns to unconditional sensitivity.

## Post-deploy verification
Next FlatFee run of schedule c1951eeb… shows deliveryLog `delivered` to sary@flatfeecorp.com.

Complexity ledger: +~60 LOC prod, no new modules, no schema change.

title: ENG-2271: approval click before Emma turns hot-lead calling on
body:
## ENG-2271 follow-up: a person's approval click before Emma turns hot-lead calling on

Until now `update_hot_lead_call_settings({enabled: true})` was the one money-and-calls action Emma could take on the model's say-so; buying and releasing a number already needed an approval card (ENG-2613). This closes the "known gap accepted at launch" in the go-live checklist.

### Behaviour
- When Emma changes `enabled` from off to on, the first call halts with the same one-question approval card as provision/release. Only after a person clicks approve does the next identical call enable calling.
- The card says what enabling does: AgentWeb will phone the listed verified team member(s) (masked) from the org's number (masked), and then the lead; calls are billed to the org owner per minute at the live rate; it can be turned off at any time. "Decline" is listed first and is the recommended option.
- Same binding as the existing gate: a digest of action, org, user, chat session, the canonical patch Emma sent, the price text and the settings revision; 15-minute validity; single use via `claimMetaWriteManifestDigest`; `ask_user_question` already rejects model-authored `hot_lead_call_approval:` kinds. A different patch or a settings change after the card needs a new card.
- Order: the existing refusals run first (unattended, bad arguments, plan not included, cannot enable: no verified member, number or hours), so a refused caller never sees a card.
- Not gated: turning calling off, lowering limits, other edits, `enabled: true` while already on, and the REST route / portal (a person already clicks there; the handler passes no hook).

### Implementation
- `applyHotLeadCallSettings` takes an optional fourth argument `beforeTurningOn(next)`; it runs after every existing check, just before the write, and only for off to on. Only the Emma tool passes it.
- `requireApproval` moved out of `hotLeadCallSetupTools.ts` into `emma/hotLeadCallApproval.ts` so both tool files share it. The gate gets a third action, `enable`.
- Renamed the digest/card field `rentText` to `priceText` (it holds the per-minute rate for `enable`). Digest bytes change, so an approval card pending at deploy time stops matching; the user simply gets a new card.
- Docs updated: go-live item 14 and "Known follow-ups" no longer list this gap; the approval section covers provision, release and turning calling on.

### Tests
New suite "human approval for turning calling on" (card text and masking, no enable before approval, claim and lost claim, decline/expired/other session/other revision/other patch/another action's approval, unattended and no-session refusals, refusals before any card, not-gated cases), service hook tests, gate tests, and the REST route asserting no chat session is read. Two existing tests that enabled without a card were updated. `npm run typecheck` clean; targeted jest 23 suites / 1328 tests passed.

### Not verified
Not tried in a real chat UI (the deck seam is faked, as in the provision/release tests). The `$0.014/min` shown is the provisional rate-card value.

Part of ENG-2783. No data-plane change.

### Review fixes (two independent reviews + CodeRabbit + Opslane)
- The enable card now also shows that each call bills both the member's call and the lead's call (each rounded up to a whole minute), the caps (`maxCallsPerHour`, `maxCallsPerDay`, `maxAttemptsPerLead`) and the calling hours with timezone; `members` is required for the enable card; dev.md fragments added for this change and for the already-merged inbound callbacks (agentweb#3874).
- **Opslane P1 (two identical enable calls in one reply produced two identical cards and a 409 on a single approval): fixed.** The first card is not persisted until the turn ends, so the second identical call minted its own card with a new random id. `buildQuestionApprovalDeckFromHalts` now keeps one card per card identity (`approvalCardIdentity(kind)` = the kind without its random id: action, org, user, session, patch, price, revision). Provision and release had the same duplication and get the fix through the shared builder. A different patch, session or revision still gets its own card; non-approval questions are never merged. A second identical call after the first was approved re-saves the same config (redundant, harmless).
- Not driven end to end: whether the tool calls of one reply run in parallel on the next turn; if two identical approved calls ran concurrently, one could still see "approval already used" at the claim.

### Pre-push bypass
Pushed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`: the hook runs `agentModeService.prepareTurnContext.golden.test.ts`, which already fails on a clean `origin/main` (f838f42ce): `__golden__/prepareTurnContext.golden.json` has no entry for the registered tool `inspect_client_usage`. Not caused by this PR; CI is the backstop. All other pre-push suites passed (2805 tests).

title: ENG-2271: daily stuck-record sweep for hot-lead call records (report-only)
body:
## ENG-2271 follow-up: stuck-record sweep for hot-lead call records

Until now a call record left in a non-terminal state (a crash between steps, a callback that never arrived) had to be found and closed by hand from the runbook. This adds the daily sweep that finds and handles them. It ships REPORT-ONLY.

### Behaviour
- Runs daily at 12:00 UTC (armed in `server.ts` like the rent sweep). `HOT_LEAD_CALL_STUCK_SWEEP`: unset/other = report only (logs, no writes); `close` = writes; `off`/`0`/`false` = disabled. Read on every run.
- A record is "stuck" when its last write is older than the longest healthy dwell of its state plus 10 minutes: `member_ringing` 10m25s, `member_answered` 10m08s, `bridging`/`connected` 40m41s, `dialing` 10m, `between_attempts` 70m.
- `member_ringing`/`member_answered`: fetch the member call from Twilio (read-only); if ended, meter it through the webhook's own `meterLeg`, then finish. `bridging`/`connected`: fetch both legs; only if BOTH ended, meter and finish (`completed`, or `bridge_unconfirmed` while still `bridging`); a live leg means nothing is written, and every leg is read before any write. `between_attempts`: closed as `failed`/`next_attempt_failed` with a `call.failed` event, guarded by the attempt number (a job that took the record first makes the write lose).
- A record with no call sid to ask Twilio about (`dialing` without a `memberCallSid`, `member_ringing`/`member_answered` without one, `bridging`/`connected` without a lead call sid) is never closed automatically (a billed call may exist; the runbook says it needs Harsha's approval): logged as `needsHuman` every run. A `dialing` record WITH a member call sid is reconciled like `member_ringing`.
- Never dials, never requests a next member, never hangs up a call; at-most-once rule intact; billing exactly once (a late real callback after the sweep bills nothing again). A `completed` leg with no duration is reported for a human, never defaulted to 0. Works with the global kill switch off.

### Finding candidates (no new table, index, GSI, migration or IAM)
`orgDb.listHotLeadCallOrgIds` (a projected scan of AW-Organizations for any org with a `hotLeadCall` config, so orgs that released their number are swept too; a second org scan next to the inbound index's `listHotLeadCallNumbers`, once a day) -> `getOrgMembers` -> `getLeadListsByUserId` per member -> new `crmDb.findLeadsBySystemRecord` per list (a query on the list's partition, filter on state and `updatedAt`, ids only). Caps per run: 500 leads per list, 10,000 leads per run, 50 records settled per run (summary shows `truncated`). Not covered: lists of departed members, and a stuck record older than the newest 500 leads of its list (invisible on every run; a sparse GSI or a persisted cursor needs a data-plane change approved by Harsha: follow-up). Read cost: DynamoDB bills every examined item, up to 10,000 leads per run, per backend instance; prod runs one instance today (EB min=max=1).

### Logs
One line per run: `[hotLeadCall] stuck call sweep completed` (info), `... completed with failures` (error), `... skipped: HOT_LEAD_CALL_STUCK_SWEEP is off`; one warn line per record with org/list/lead ids, never phone numbers.

### Review process
Two independent reviewers plus CodeRabbit/Opslane; findings fixed in follow-up commits (source, tests, docs). Known and accepted: `fetchCall` lands in the `VoiceProvider` interface one commit before the fake gets it (typecheck fails at that intermediate commit; history is not rewritten); the PR merges as a merge commit.

### Tests
Unit decision table with a fake clock, e2e with the existing fakes (each stuck state, live records untouched, report-only writes nothing, idempotent second run, Twilio failure changes nothing, billing once, never dials, kill switch off), and the new query against DynamoDB Local (17 passed). Typecheck clean; 25 targeted suites / 1451 tests passed.

### Not verified
That the REST Call `duration` equals the callback's `CallDuration` and that prod Twilio credentials allow `calls(sid).fetch()` (go-live item 16: check report mode for `Twilio fetchCall` errors before switching to `close`). Read cost is from the code, not measured.

Part of ENG-2783. No data-plane change; closing stays off until the env var is set.

### Pre-push bypass
The merge of `main` (after #3887) was pushed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`: the hook's only failing suite is `agentModeService.prepareTurnContext.golden.test.ts` (2 failed), which also fails on a clean `origin/main` (87f5e4fd8): the golden file has no entry for the registered tool `inspect_client_usage` (ENG-2802). 51 other pre-push suites passed (2865 tests); CI is the backstop. The merge conflict was one block in `hot-lead-call.md` ("Known follow-ups": both sides had removed a different, now-done bullet; both are removed).

### Opslane P1 ("sweep not confirmed armed at startup"): decision
The arming line `[stuckCallSweepCron] Initialized — first run at 12:00 UTC (in N min)` is printed by `server.ts` immediately after the timer is set, in the same startup callback and the same way as the rent sweep's `[numberRentCron] Initialized` line; it is the LAST block of a long sequence of awaited dynamic imports, so a startup-log check made too early can miss it. A failure to arm would print `[stuckCallSweepCron] Failed to initialize`, which Opslane did not see either. Not reproduced locally. Anurag decided (2026-11-04) to merge with the `opslane:merge-anyway` label and verify in prod after the deploy by finding the Initialized line in the live log. The sweep ships report-only (`HOT_LEAD_CALL_STUCK_SWEEP` unset), so a missed arming only means the manual runbook stays in use.

title: ENG-2801: use Apollo's exact request_id_str so waterfall callbacks match their placeholder
body:
## Safety answer (first, per the draft/merge rules)
- **Safe for prod?** Yes by design: the repair writes the placeholder Apollo's callback needs and, by default, changes no run time (the wait is opt-in), no vendor call and no booking.
- **Could it regress or anger users?** (1) One awaited DynamoDB put per emailless Tier-3 request (bounded by Apollo's 500 per user per day); if it throws, that lead's Apollo result is lost, exactly as today. (2) A run can say "not found" for a lead whose email arrives moments later. (3) A late callback can write an email onto a customer lead that had none (new in practice). (4) Org owners / `crm.editor` members who enrich a list they do not own still lose the result (unchanged, fails closed).
- **Rollback:** revert the merge commit and redeploy. Placeholder rows already written stay (no TTL on the table) and the previous handler still honours pending ones; emails already written onto leads stay.
- **Data-plane / persistent changes (owner's OK required before leaving draft):** see "Persisted data" below.

## Summary
Fixes ENG-2801: Apollo waterfall callbacks never matched a placeholder, so emails found asynchronously by Apollo's brokers were never attributed to the lead (pre-existing; found while verifying ENG-2720 / #3867 on prod).

**Cause.** Apollo's immediate `/people/match` response to `run_waterfall_email` returns `request_id` as an unquoted 19-digit JSON integer (`8327452971617011608`) *and* an exact string `request_id_str`. axios's `JSON.parse` rounds the integer (`8327452971617012000`); `ApolloService.findEmail` (Tier 3) only accepted a string `request_id`, so `asyncRequestId` was undefined and the placeholder write (`f.asyncPending && f.asyncRequestId`) never ran. The webhook sends `request_id` as a JSON string, so it had nothing to match.

**Change (7 files).**
1. `extractApolloAsyncRequestId` (`apolloService.ts`): `request_id_str`, then a string `request_id`, a number only if `Number.isSafeInteger`; a rounded number is never used. Negative ids pass through.
2. `brokerWaitMs` (`enrichmentV3RealDeps.ts`): the callback wait in `apolloBrokerChain` is **opt-in** (`APOLLO_BROKER_WAIT_MS`, unset = 0, cap 120 s). A first version waited a hard-coded 30 s; review showed it also gates bulk find-email (concurrency 8, ~1 h per 1,000 emailless leads) and Apollo's documented example takes ~5 min. The placeholder write is unconditional and precedes any wait.
3. `apolloWebhook.ts` (the matched path had never run in prod): the callback email must be a string of at most 254 chars and one plausible address (RFC 5322 atext local part, ASCII domain, 2-63 letter TLD) or it is treated as `no_email` and logged by count and request id only; `status` is reduced to `[a-z0-9 _.-]` and 40 chars (a 390 KB status was written verbatim onto a lead in a review exploit run); a transient `getLeadListById` error now answers 500 so Apollo retries; a verifier vendor counts as `validated` only when its status is a string (a forged object status used to throw and 500); the callback `request_id` is trimmed once so the lookup, the idempotency check, the stored `apolloRequestId` and the logs agree.
4. Tests for each, a dev note.

## Evidence
- Prod CloudWatch: `no placeholder for request_id` for 60 of 60 callbacks on 2026-11-03 (before the ENG-2720 deploy) and 3 of 3 in a 2026-11-04 prod test; consistent GetItem on prod `AW-EnrichmentRawCache` found no placeholder row for the three ids.
- A raw `POST /people/match` with `run_waterfall_email` (2026-11-04) returned the unquoted 19-digit integer and `request_id_str`; the unit tests are built from that shape. Apollo's docs: ids are signed 64-bit integers, may be negative, "pass through unchanged"; the webhook's `request_id` is a JSON string and its `people[].waterfall.emails[].vendors[].emails` shape matches `extractApolloEmail`.
- Independent reviews (fresh context, read-only, security first, exploit and mutation checks): four satisfactory verdicts on earlier heads with their findings applied (wait made opt-in; ordering test; email gate; status cap, rejection log, retryable list errors, atext local part); the final fresh FULL review of `c817d5c4f` (security first; it also ran the real code end to end on DynamoDB Local: placeholder keyed by the exact id, callback wrote the email onto a lead, replay returned `alreadyProcessed`, a cross-tenant attempt got 202 with no write, five concurrent callbacks produced one write) found no security or correctness blocker; its one must-fix was this data-plane statement, applied in `eb9440cce` (dev-note only). A further fresh full review of `eb9440cce` (security, correctness, maintainability/extensibility, scalability; 82 tests, tsc, about 60 adversarial inputs, 20 mutants) found no blocker and three cheap hardening items, applied in `42475e974` (verifier status type guard, one-time `request_id` trim, doc comment back above `extractApolloEmail`; each fix proven by reverting it). The final fresh full review of `42475e974` (85 tests, tsc clean, about 60 adversarial inputs, 20 mutants, 19 killed and the survivor equivalent) found no blocker.

## Persisted data (verified against the code and on DynamoDB Local by the reviewer)
- One placeholder row (~550 bytes + its `entityKey-fieldGroup-index` entry) per emailless Tier-3 request in the existing `AW-EnrichmentRawCache`, bounded by Apollo's `find` quota (500 per user per day); a callback rewrites it once. DynamoDB TTL is **disabled** on that table (checked on prod), so rows persist; they hold first/last name, domain, user/list/lead ids and, after a callback, the found email.
- A late write sets `email` (lower-cased), `enrichmentMetadata.email` (`source: web_search`, `provider: apollo`, `confidence`, `enrichedAt`, `sourceQuote`, `apolloRequestId`) and `updatedAt` on a lead that has no email; it does not set `domain`. That populates the lead's `email-index` and `EmailLookupIndex` entries, and `updatedAt` rewrites its entries in the other GSIs it belongs to (`LinkedinLookupIndex`, `NameCompanyLookupIndex`, `listId-status-index`, ...).
- No schema, key, index, IAM, Apollo dashboard or provider-side change. One optional env var, `APOLLO_BROKER_WAIT_MS`, default off (prod EB environment unchanged).

## Known limits (not changed here; follow-up candidates)
- Late write does not derive `domain` (a similar update once threw `ValidationException` on a real table, so it needs a `#name` placeholder and a real-DynamoDB check) and skips `validateLeadEmailInBackground`.
- Callback refused unless the list owner is the user who started the run (org owners / editors lose the result, fail-closed).
- Placeholder `expiresAt`/status are not enforced; the webhook secret falls back to a value committed in the repo unless `APOLLO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set (not set on prod EB); a forger also needs an existing request id. Rotating the secret is an infra change and drops in-flight callbacks.
- IDN email domains are rejected unless punycode. The callback email gate is looser than the repo's strict address check in `utils/sendEligibility.ts` (accepts `a..b@x.com`, rejects punycode TLDs) and a local part may start with `=`/`+`/`-`; the email array is mapped in full (an authenticated 48 MB body costs about 2 s of event loop); if Apollo ever sent only a rounded `request_id` without `request_id_str` the id is silently undefined (add a warn); the 50 MB body parser runs before the secret check (app-wide); no in-flight dedupe (a re-run before the callback lands pays the 9-credit waterfall again); CSV export has no formula escaping (pre-existing, but a callback email may begin with `=`/`+`/`-`). Tracked in the follow-up ticket.

## Test plan
- [x] `apolloService.test.ts`, `apolloWebhook.test.ts` and the broker tests: 85 pass; 38 related suites / 888 tests pass; mutation-checked (every weakening of the extraction, the wait default, the email gate, the status cap, the rejection log and the retryable error fails a test).
- [x] Real pre-push hook (tsc + related jest) on the pushed commits.
- [x] Independent fresh full review of the exact final head `42475e974` (security first, exploit + mutation checks, maintainability and scalability): no blocker. Earlier DynamoDB Local end-to-end run on `c817d5c4f`.
- [ ] **Prod live test after deploy** (env1's ngrok callback URL cannot receive Apollo, so prod is the only place to verify): a real waterfall writes a placeholder, the callback matches it (confirms the webhook's string `request_id` equals the response's `request_id_str`), the email lands on the lead, run time is unchanged, and what the late-written lead looks like (e.g. `domain`).

title: ENG-2113: plan chat gets its tools through the worker relay (backend half, relay PR 2)
body:
## What
Backend half of the tool relay (relay PR 2). A Claude plan turn on a worker that speaks protocol 4 gets its tools through the worker's stdio shim and a per-turn unix socket instead of the HTTP bridge URL + token: `turn.run` carries a `tools` manifest INSTEAD of `bridgeToken`, each `tool-call` event is executed in process through the same `ToolBridge.callTool` as before (liveness check, the run's tool list, halts, ledger, write confirmation), and the result goes back as `turn.toolResult`. Tools come and go like Emma's: a fresh chat opens with the foundation tools only; a skill's tools arrive in the answer to the install call.

Wire shapes, limits, stops, log lines and residual risks: `dev/pending/eng-2113-relay-backend.md` and `docs/plan-route-tool-limits.md`.

Nothing changes for customers: the plan route stays allow-listed to one user (approval cards come first), and AgentWeb-funded turns do not touch this code.

## Order of the relay PRs
0. #3808 (merged): backend accepts a protocol-4 worker.
1. #3813 (merged 2026-11-04, worker deployed and checked: protocol 4, plain plan turns on Haiku and Sonnet pass with the old backend).
2. This PR.
3. Cleanup (remove bridge URL/token/egress exemption/stub/hold).

## Deploy: read before merging
- This PR touches **no file that triggers the signed worker deploy** (checked against the path filter of `login-host-deploy.yml`: nothing under `backend/src/loginHost/`, no build/sign script, no lockfile). The worker does not restart.
- Merging deploys the backend (Immutable, about 30 minutes of old and new instances overlapping). During the overlap a plan turn may hit either; do tool checks only after one build is left.
- Transport choice fails closed: relay only when the worker reports protocol 4 and the bridge is in process; the first plan turn after a backend start can be refused once with the retryable `host_unavailable` until the protocol status is known.
- Rollback: set the funding flag `killSwitch` (plan route stops, AgentWeb models unaffected) or revert this PR and redeploy. Roll the BACKEND back before ever rolling the worker back to protocol 3 (a protocol-3 worker is refused by this backend).
- CI change: **Backend build** now also runs `relayManifest.registry.test.ts` (mock-only: no secrets, no database). Every tool in the built-in registry must fit the plan route's limits (name, description and schema size); a registry tool that does not fit fails CI instead of failing a customer.

## Evidence
- **Independent reviews (fresh, full, not deltas):** backend security and backend parity on `4d3ba42f6`, plus the two host reviews of the worker half. All four: safe to merge for the single allow-listed user, not yet for arbitrary customers. No cross-customer read, forged identity, credential leak or unconfirmed write found; no data-plane change. Mutation checks per review (39 / 36 / 36 / 43 mutants, in the order host security, host correctness, backend security, backend parity); survivors were redundant checks or test gaps that now have tests.
- **Live on a test worker** (real pinned Claude CLI, the kept test login, Haiku AND Sonnet, results per model): functional group, hostile-input group 38/38, resilience group (host killed and restarted twice) 16/16, legacy HTTP-bridge path, revoke during a running tool call 27/27.
- **Production, worker side:** worker deployed 2026-11-04 (protocol 4); with the OLD backend, plain plan turns on Haiku and Sonnet (two turns each), both refusals (400 `invalid_funding_choice`, 422 `model_not_on_plan`) and Stop mid-turn followed by a working turn pass on the maintainer's own account.
- **Since the reviewed runtime:** only tests, docs, comments and the gate list changed. The six relay bundles built from this branch are byte-identical (code-only esbuild sha256) to the frozen, live-tested ones; the files changed by `main` since the branch point do not overlap the relay files except `backend/src/emma/tools.ts`, which merges cleanly.

## Not in this PR / known and deliberate
Approval cards (the gate for any second user), Codex, the cleanup PR. Findings that only matter before the allow-list is widened are tracked and will be closed first (strikes/cooldown for a login that keeps tripping host guards, a stricter sustained event rate, same-user sibling-turn socket reach, sizing for 8 concurrent relay turns, stripping bidirectional/zero-width characters from tool names in logs).

title: Smartlead: campaign stats tool for Emma, plain wording for replies on Slack and WhatsApp (ENG-2737)
body:
## What (ENG-2737, part of ENG-673)

Two things for Smartlead customers, in one backend PR. Pairs with portal PR #1329 (Luma share controls) as one lot.

**1. `get_smartlead_campaign_stats`, a read-only Emma tool.** Input: a campaign id (from `list_smartlead_campaigns`), optional `accountId`. Output: contacts emailed, emails sent (follow-ups included), replies, bounces, unsubscribes and the lead total, from Smartlead's `GET /campaigns/{id}/analytics`, plus "Smartlead's counts can lag a few minutes behind a recent push or send."
- Same connection rules as the list tool (the caller's own or an org-shared key), same off switch (`SMARTLEAD_PUSH_ENABLED`), offered in chats, blocked for share-link visitors. Writes nothing to Smartlead or the CRM.
- Opens and clicks are left out on purpose: connector campaigns do not turn tracking on, so they would read zero.
- Smartlead sends every counter as a string; parsing is strict, and a missing or garbled counter is an error, never a silent zero. Verified live: an unknown campaign id (or one that is not the key's) comes back as HTTP 200 with `{}`, which now means "not found".

**2. A Smartlead reply reads as a sentence on Slack and WhatsApp** (it showed the raw event name `email.received`). Only when `isSmartleadReplyAlert` is true (the test the email uses).
- Slack: header and fallback `A new lead "Name" replied to your campaign` (`... List: <list>`); the fields, "Received at" line and Open CRM button stay. The name, address fallback and 40-character cap come from one helper shared with the email subject. The fallback text and the Name/Email/Company/Phone/List values are escaped for Slack.
- WhatsApp: template variables `[name, "replied to your campaign on <list>. <CRM link>"]`; the template is unchanged. The name is one safe line.
- Every other event, and an `email.received` that did not come through Smartlead, sends byte for byte what it sent before (pinned by tests, and run on the test environment).
- Email caption under the contact's reply is now `The contact's own words. Check any link before you click it.`

## Copy (owner approves customer copy; do not merge before that)
The caption, the Slack text and the WhatsApp text above.

## Verification
- Typecheck clean. Targeted suites pass (smartleadService, push service, Emma tools, foundation access, Slack payload, reply alert email, alert channels, prompt golden re-recorded for the one new tool name only).
- Mutation checks (break the code on purpose, confirm a test fails): swapped counters, unescaped Slack values, wording not gated on Smartlead, WhatsApp branch always on, an extra field in the tool output: all five caught.
- Live on the test environment with real Smartlead (read-only): real campaigns return the same numbers Smartlead shows (ICP2-Final: 13 contacts, 38 emails, 0 replies, 1 bounce, 0 unsubscribes); string id works; missing campaign says not found; a teammate with no connection is refused; bad or extra arguments refused. The alert code ran for real with only the outbound Slack/WhatsApp/email calls intercepted: new wording on a Smartlead reply, old output unchanged for the other cases, hostile names made safe.
- Independent blind review: no blockers; its should-fix items are fixed (Slack values escaped, strict counters, caption true in every language, test gaps).

## Also in this PR
- **Luma tools refused in share-link sessions** (`luma_list_events`, `luma_get_guests` added to `SHARED_SESSION_BLOCKED_ORG_SETTINGS_TOOLS`, like the Smartlead tools). A share-link visitor runs as the link owner; with the portal PR able to share a Luma key with the whole org, the Luma tools would otherwise reach every org-shared key, guests' phone numbers included. Changes what existing share links can do (before: a visitor could use the link owner's own Luma key). Owner decision 2026-11-04.

- **The caller's own Luma calendar wins when a teammate's shared one is also visible** (`resolveLuma`), as the Smartlead resolver does. Without it, once a calendar is shared, every Luma call of a teammate who already has their own calendar would fail with "pass calendar_id", scheduled runs included. An explicit `calendar_id` still reaches the shared one; other ambiguity still asks.
- **One contact name for a Smartlead reply on every channel** (never a phone number or the lead's database id).

## Not in this PR / open
- **Share-link block caveat (pre-existing, needs its own ticket):** the block list is enforced only in the text-chat dispatch. A share-link visitor on a live voice call runs as the link's owner with the owner's full tool set and no share check, and `manage_scheduled_chat` is not blocked, so every tool in that list (org-settings writes, the Smartlead push tools, now the Luma tools) is still reachable that way. Not changed here.
- The approved Meta body of `agentweb_lead_alert` is not in the repo, so the final WhatsApp text around our variables is unchecked.
- No table, index, IAM or environment change. Note: `dev/pending/eng-2737-smartlead-stats-and-reply-wording.md`.

title: ENG-2747: MCP tool annotations for the Zoma (Meta Toolkit) tools
body:
## What

Every tool the Zoma toolkit advertises (Meta tools, Zoma onboarding tools and Google Ads tools) now carries MCP annotations: `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint`. They appear in both `tools/list` (`POST /api/meta-toolkit/mcp`) and `GET /api/meta-toolkit/tools`. Marketplaces and gateways (Databricks Unity Gateway, ChatGPT apps, the Claude directory) use these hints to decide which calls need approval. Part of ENG-2747 (Databricks Marketplace listing).

**Rebuilt on 2026-11-12.** The first version used a per-tool map that threw for an unlabelled tool. Main has since grown from 7 to about 59 advertised tools (audiences, catalogs, feeds, signals, pages, Google Ads). That made the throw a risk: any tool added without a label would have broken every Zoma call. This version is deny-by-default and never throws.

## How it decides

- **Read-only** only for names in `READ_ONLY_TOOLKIT_TOOLS` (`backend/src/mcp/toolkitToolAnnotations.ts`). Each was checked on main 5436fc962: the handler only issues reads.
- **Everything else is labelled a destructive write.** That includes any tool added later that nobody has classified. Forgetting to classify a new tool makes clients prompt more, never less.
- **Narrower explicit labels for four tools:**
  - `zoma_status` and `zoma_prepare_upload`: not read-only, not destructive. One mints a Stripe setup link, the other a presigned upload URL.
  - `ads_get_errors` and `zoma_usage`: read-only, with no outside call.
- **Mixed read/write tools stay destructive:** `call_meta_marketing_api`, `zoma_custom_audiences` and `call_google_ads_api`. A client that honours the hint will gate their reads too.
- **Inline `annotations` on a tool definition are ignored.** The table is the one place that decides, so a tool cannot label itself read-only by accident.
- **To mark a new read tool read-only,** add its name to `READ_ONLY_TOOLKIT_TOOLS` after checking its handler.

The labels are applied once, in `toolkitManifest()` in `routes/metaToolkit.ts`, which builds both responses. `metaToolkitManifest.ts` and `zomaToolDefinitions.ts` are untouched (identical to main), so this stays out of the files the swarm edits most.

## Judgment calls to check

- `call_meta_ads_insights_api` is read-only. It creates Meta's transient async report run to fetch rows, but changes no ad, budget or status.
- `call_google_ads_reporting_api` is read-only, as documented in `googleToolkitManifest.ts` ("all modes (read-only tool)").

## Not in this PR

- Blocking writes for Databricks-origin tokens (Option B on ENG-2781). The scope decision is pending with Harsha.
- Tool `title` fields (the Claude directory wants them).
- `META_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING` in prod (config, not code).

## Rollback

Pure revert of this PR. The change is additive metadata on two discovery responses: no schema, table or stored-data change, no tool behaviour change, no new config. Nothing in it can throw.

## Verification

- **Jest, Node 24, on this branch after merging origin/main 5436fc962, 12 suites / 231 tests pass.**
  - The rewritten `eng2747.metaToolkitAnnotations` suite: every advertised tool has four boolean hints; the read-only set is exact and contains no stale names; mixed and unclassified tools are destructive; unknown and inherited names (`toString`, `__proto__`) fall back to the default; inline annotations are ignored; and route wiring is checked for `GET /tools` and `tools/list`, with Google off and on.
  - The other 11 suites: eng2288, eng2295, eng2268, eng2282, eng2283, eng2917.signalsHttpRecorder, eng2823 (googleToolkit, googleToolkitHardening, googleToolkitMcp), eng2928 (googleToolkitWrites, googleToolkitMcp).
  - eng2288 and eng2295 each had one expectation updated: the route response now includes `annotations`.
- **`tsc --noEmit`:** clean.
- **ESLint:** the new files are clean. The touched route and tests have the same error counts as on main.
- **Mutation checks (`.mutcheck/mutcheck.py`), all BIND:**
  - The route stops annotating.
  - The default stops being destructive.
  - `meta_delete_product` is added to the read-only set.
  - Inline annotations are honoured.

Opslane run 1885 (P1, "hints for the Zoma status and usage tools couldn't be confirmed"): its captured `GET /api/meta-toolkit/tools` response was truncated inside the first tool's description, so it never reached those entries. The full response includes them. The route test now asserts the exact labels for both over HTTP: `zoma_status` = `{readOnlyHint:false, destructiveHint:false, idempotentHint:false, openWorldHint:true}`, `zoma_usage` = `{readOnlyHint:true, destructiveHint:false, idempotentHint:true, openWorldHint:false}`. This is intended behaviour.

Not verified: this rebuild has not been run on env1 or prod. The first version was verified on env1 over HTTP on 2026-11-04. Whether Databricks Unity Gateway honours these hints is a Databricks smoke-test item.

title: ENG-2720: enrichment helper LLM calls on the enrichment role; alias prompt context; agreed classifications
body:
## Safety answer (first, per the draft/merge rules)
- **Safe for prod?** Yes by design; no schema, key, index, IAM, ledger-label or rate-card change and no new setting. Three small LLM calls around an enrichment run move off the retired `gpt-5-chat-2` (which `callLLM` rewrites to `gpt-5.5`) to the same "enrichment" role every other enrichment call uses (today `gpt-5.6-luna`), the alias prompt gets the context it was missing, and the saved smart-field classification now needs two agreeing samples.
- **Could it regress or anger users?** (1) Alias inference / classification (at config save) and the sibling mapping (at run start) now answer with Luna instead of gpt-5.5. Measured on a 36-field labelled set the alias answers are better, not worse (below); classification is about 2% wrong after agreement (4% for a single sample), and about 6% of fields stay undecided and are asked again at the next save. A residual case: an instruction that names a label but not its alternatives ("high if hiring and funded") is typed boolean by Luna (string by gpt-6-sol, enum by Claude), which the smart evaluator reads as true/false. (2) Every failure path degrades as before (no alias / nothing classified / field-to-itself mapping); a save never fails because of these calls. (3) Classification costs two calls per save instead of one, and a field the samples keep disagreeing on is asked again (2 calls) at every save, bounded at 1 alias + 2 classification calls per save however many fields (a fraction of a cent on Luna; the config PUT route has no rate limiter of its own, unchanged). A field the samples keep disagreeing on runs as an ordinary web-fetched field until a later save agrees (about 6% of fields on Luna); only a server warning reports it. (4) An org that set its own enrichment model now also gets it on these three calls.
- **Rollback:** `CRM_ENRICH_V3_DEFAULT_MODEL=gpt-5.5` (no deploy; also moves extraction back) or the per-call env overrides `CRM_ENRICH_V3_ALIAS_MODEL` / `_CLASSIFY_MODEL` / `_EXTRACT_MODEL`, or revert the merge. Neither undoes configs already saved with a model's answers; those are redone when the field's instruction changes. Prod has no `CRM_ENRICH_*` env var set (checked names on the EB environment), so nothing pins these calls today.
- **Data-plane / persistent changes:** none.

## Summary
ENG-2720 follow-up. Two findings from reading and testing the enrichment config-save path:
1. `enrichmentConfigDeps.ts` (alias inference, smart-field classification) and `enrichmentSiblingConfigFields.ts` (sibling field mapping) defaulted to `gpt-5-chat-2`, removed from the registry on 2026-08-19 and rewritten to gpt-5.5, so they ran on gpt-5.5 while extraction ran on the cheap default.
2. The alias prompt was a bare list of canonical names. It never said what a lead is or whose details each group holds, so models (Luna and gpt-6-sol alike) mapped "email of the CEO" onto the lead's own `email`, "CTO phone" onto `phone` and "founder LinkedIn" onto `linkedin_url`. At run time an alias to `email` fills the custom column with the lead's own email and can trigger the paid Apollo email waterfall.

**Change.**
1. `services/enrichmentMappingLlm.ts`: `createEnrichmentHelperLLM(userId, envModel?)` = env override, else `resolveModelForUser(userId, 'enrichment')`; `requireContent: true`; the cheap default falls back to gpt-5.5 on a provider error. The three call sites use it and pass the user id.
2. `buildAliasInferenceSystemPrompt` (`services/enrichmentPrompts.ts`): lead = one person at one company; `person_*` groups are the lead's own details, the others the employer's; synonyms by meaning ("contact number", "mobile", "cell" = phone); decide who the field is about first, return null for a specific other person or organisation (employer-level lists such as investors, customers and leadership changes still map; `email`/`phone` are the lead's work details, so a personal, home or alternate email or a home phone is null while mobile/cell is still `phone`).
3. `llmClassifySmartFields` asks twice in parallel; `agreeingClassifications` keeps a field only when both samples agree on the smart flag, the type and (enum) the options; a smart field keeps the union of both samples' dependencies (none is fine: the evaluator also gets the lead's own columns). A disagreement, or one failed call, leaves the field unclassified (nothing cached, asked again at the next save). `processEnrichmentConfig` first clears the stored smart tags of every classification candidate and of every field whose instruction was emptied (they were made for the previous instruction), so an edited field with no new answer can no longer keep computing its old condition on every run (the failed-call case had the same hole before this PR). The classification prompt is unchanged.
4. Comment fix in `enrichmentBatchBudget.ts`, `.env.example` examples corrected, a dev note, tests.

## Not in this PR (decided, with evidence)
- **V1 `crmEnrichmentService.ts`** (`DEFAULT_ENRICH_MODEL` / `DEFAULT_SUGGEST_MODEL`, admin `crm-enrichment-config`): live code (the customer portal calls `enrich-web` and the field refresh), and prod has a stored `crm-enrichment-config` row pinning both models to `gpt-5-chat-2`, so changing code defaults would do nothing on prod. Left alone on purpose: across the whole prod `AW-UsageRecords` table its features hold 6 calls and $0.21 in total, one user, last on 2026-09-24; and V1 extraction was never benchmarked on Luna.
- Wrong aliases already saved on existing configs (`f.aliasFor ?? infer`) are not touched; an audit of stored configs is a separate, read-only job if wanted.
- A sharper classification prompt: one run suggested it fixed one field class, but the same current prompt scored 4.0% wrong in one run and 0.7% in another, so the effect is within noise; a "<label> if <condition> is an enum" rule made gpt-6-sol misclassify "good fit if ..." (14 of 16). Not adopted.
- Exhausted `requireContent` retries still do not count in the run-level failure counters.

## Known lows from the final review (left as is after SAFE, per the review-cycle rule)
- **Dependency union can add a paid field** (`enrichmentConfigDeps.ts` ~L104): when both samples agree a field is smart, the union of their dependencies is kept; if one sample adds `email`/`phone`, it becomes a hidden fetched field for every lead, which for emailless leads can reach the paid Apollo email waterfall. A single sample could already do this before the PR; the union about doubles the chance. Follow-up: intersect for paid fields (email/phone), union for the rest.
- A field the samples keep disagreeing on runs as an ordinary web-searched field (and is re-asked, 2 calls, at every save and every Emma call); the user is not told (server log only). Documented design.
- Sibling mapping moved to Luna without its own gold-set run; its prompt has no "who is this about" rule. `findSiblingLeads` has no tenant filter (pre-existing on main).
- Pre-existing on main: `classifications[f.name]` reads prototype keys (a field named `constructor` is marked not-smart without an answer; use `Object.hasOwn`); the alias user prompt inserts the instruction unescaped (bounded: the PUT route already accepts a client `aliasFor`).

## Evidence
- **Prod data (read-only):** since 2026-10-30 the only gpt-5.x enrichment rows are the helper features this PR moves: `crm_enrichment_config` $0.1477 / 31 calls and `crm_enrichment_field_mapping` $0.0139 / 5 calls, 3 users. The saving is small (about $0.16 a week); the point is consistency and correct aliases.
- **Alias prompt, env1, run inside the backend container with its own role (no key left it), 36 gold-labelled fields, 3 repeats, 108 checks per cell:** old prompt Luna 101/108 (94%), gpt-6-sol 103/108 (95%), every miss a third-party field aliased to the lead (`ceo_email`, `cto_phone`, `founder_linkedin`, once `open_roles` null); new prompt Luna 108/108, gpt-6-sol 107/108 (the miss is a conservative null). Synonyms (`contact_number`, `mobile`, `cell`, `work_mail`, `position`...) were already right with the old prompt and still are. The shipped code path (`buildConfigServiceDeps().llmInferAliases`) on Luna: 107-108 of 108.

title: ENG-2816: a logged-in owner on their own share link is the owner, not a visitor
body:
## What

First of several PRs for ENG-2816 (share-link visitors can bypass the shared-session tool block through voice and scheduled chats; design and the two reviews are on the ticket). This one only teaches the text share route who the **owner** is, so the later PRs can restrict visitor-made work without ever restricting the owner.

A share link (`/ishare/<sessionId>?conversable=<token>`) runs the turn under the owner's userId with `isInteractiveShare=true`. The portal never sent the viewer's login on that call, so an owner opening their own link (for example from a scheduled-run email) counted as a visitor.

`generateSharedResponse` now reads an optional `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header, decided last (after the link, lock, usage and model checks, just before the turn). `services/shareViewerIdentity.ts` `isSessionOwnerRequest` (it takes the request itself, so the verifier sees what it sees on every other route) is true only for a normal user login that `getUserFromToken` verifies (signature, expiry, session version) and whose user is the session's owner, and that is not a delegate token (an admin acting as the owner) or a service self-call token. True means the turn runs with `isInteractiveShare=false`: the same tools as the owner's normal view (admin tools too for an admin owner), no anonymous-sender stamp, owner step-model handling, `regular` session type. Delegated (admin-support) access is NOT granted by this (tested). An owner turn logs one line (no token) because telemetry then reads `regular` instead of `interactive_share`.

## What does not change

- No header, no change: the portal does not send it yet (companion portal PR), so this is inert until that lands.
- Any failure (missing, malformed, expired, revoked, someone else's login, a thrown verifier) is the visitor turn it always was. It never errors and never loosens anything.
- The link token, expiry, `isActive`, usage gate, session lock and model policy all run before and independently of this; a login never replaces the link check (a wrong share token is still a 401).
- No table, index, IAM or environment change. CORS already allows `Authorization`. No persisted data.

## Order and safety

Safe to merge on its own. Do **not** ship the later voice guard or the schedule marking before this and the portal PR are live, or an owner on their own link would be restricted.

## Tests

- `shareViewerIdentity.test.ts` (13), `shareViewerIdentity.realJwt.test.ts` (11; real signed tokens through the real `getUserFromToken`, only the user table faked: wrong secret, alg none, expired, revoked session version, missing user, `deleted_` user, colleague, delegate, service, garbage) and `agentModeController.ishareOwnerRecognition.test.ts` (8, through the real handler). The neighbouring share suites still pass (8 suites, 79 tests together).
- Mutation checks, each fails a test: owner never recognised; everyone recognised; any signed-in user is the owner; delegate or service check removed; owner fed into delegated access; trace removed; verifier handed a copy of the request.
- Live on a test environment through the real stack: anonymous visitor, colleague and garbage login refused (`save_memory`); the owner's login ran it with no anonymous stamp; the owner's login with a wrong share token is still a 401.
- `npm run typecheck` clean (exit 0).

## Rollback

Revert; every share-link turn is a visitor turn again.
