title: ENG-2113: approval cards on the Claude plan route (draft)
body:
## PARKED: DO NOT MERGE (2026-11-16)

ENG-1816 and its child cards, including ENG-2113, were parked on 2026-11-13 after the 2026-11-12 call (the card moved to Backlog at medium-low priority; Emma stops being the agent). **Do not merge this PR until Manan says so.**

Why it should not merge now (measured 2026-11-13, so the numbers have only grown since):
- It conflicts with main (`mergeable: CONFLICTING`; main was 646 commits past the merge base). It touches `agentModeService.ts` and `agentModeController.ts`, which the Emma-to-MCP extraction (ENG-2840) will change.
- The live tests (31/31: Haiku 17, Sonnet 14) ran on an older head (b674899dc). The kept test login expired on 2026-11-07, so a re-run needs a new sign-in.
- Merging triggers a production login-worker deploy (the usage-on-interrupt fix is in the worker).
- Only the allow-listed Claude plan route, which has one user, would use it.

What is worth keeping is the design: a human approval bound to the exact change. It is recorded in the ENG-1816 brain. Revisit when the plan route resumes or when Hermes needs the same deck pattern. The local branch also has an unpushed merge with main, because the pre-push test hook fails on known red suites on main.

---

## ENG-2113: approval cards on the Claude plan route (DRAFT, not for merge without Manan's explicit go)

A tool that needs the user's confirmation on the plan route now ends the turn with the **same approval deck AgentWeb chat builds**, and the user's click on the card is the only thing that lets a deck-gated write run. Owner's rule: the plan route behaves exactly like AgentWeb chat.

### What changes
- **Deck at the halt, N items:** the halts of one model message become ONE deck through the chat loop's own builders and conditional write (`AgentModeService.stageApprovalDeckForPlanTurn`; the retry-backstop note was moved verbatim into `annotateMetaWriteRetryBackstop`). Post-halt siblings of the same message are admitted (`relayAdmitPostHaltSiblings: true`), items follow the model's call order.
- **Turn ends at the halt, like the loop:** the dispatcher fires `onHaltSettled` when the halted message is complete (announced siblings waited for up to 15 s, capped by the soft deadline, wait restarts when one arrives); the backend interrupts the turn (the interrupt a Stop uses) and builds the deck whatever the interrupted CLI reports. A real Stop still wins.
- **Plan-connection preflight on deck ANSWERS** (`assertCanStartTurn`): a down connection refuses the answer with the deck still waiting. A deck CANCEL always goes through (as on AgentWeb).
- **Outcome kept for "continue":** `metadata.deckOutcomeDirective` (plan route only, bounded to 20,000 chars) so a continue after a failed turn tells the model what the answer did.
- **WORKER change (usage after an interrupt):** the CLI reports tokens only in its final result, which an interrupted turn never reaches. The adapter sums the stream's per-message counts and emits them when the turn ends without a result; the connection manager drains an aborted stream and forwards exactly ONE usage event rebuilt from four validated numbers (everything else, alarms included, is still dropped after an abort). No protocol change (`PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 4).
- Docs: `docs/plan-route-tool-limits.md` R1 paragraph narrowed; `dev/pending` fragment.

### Deploy consequence (read before merging)
Merge touches `backend/src/loginHost/**`, so it **triggers the signed worker deploy** (idle-gated, auto-rollback) and the bridge-URL stub re-apply with Yugo. Old worker + new backend and new worker + old backend both work (usage is simply absent on the old worker).

### Safety answer (written for review, to be re-stated right before any merge)
- No path found for a compromised worker to make a deck-gated write run without a human-attributed deck answer. The deck is built only from the executor's own results (bridge halts); execution needs an answered deck item for the recomputed digest, claimed once. 
- Normal AgentWeb chat: only the verbatim extraction above; everything else is gated on `planRoute`.
- Plan route stays allow-listed to one internal user until the widening gates below close.

### Verification
- Unit/integration: funding + loginHost + plan route + parity suites 3,399 passed; **parity tests run the real chat loop and the plan seam on the same halts and compare the decks**. Full backend suite on this head: 50,947 passed; 12 failed in 7 suites that fail identically on clean `main` (pre-existing: conditionalSkip, books, mcp.publicToolInventory, eng2398.mutationReadBack, linkedInOutreachAuth.saveAccount, onboardingInterests, tablePrefix) plus one timing-sensitive worker test (cpuBudget) that fails only under full-suite load and passes alone (34/34).
- Mutation checks: every new guard has a test that fails when the guard is removed.
- **Live, test box, real pinned Claude CLI, kept login, Haiku AND Sonnet: 31/31** (3 sibling previews -> one 3-item deck in call order; read + previews; later-message preview never runs; question deck answered with the non-recommended option reaches the next turn; second halt with a deck waiting adds no deck; usage recorded on the halted turn; decks of 12 and 64 items persist whole in Dev).
- **Four independent adversarial reviews** (fresh, one of the whole branch): no approval bypass; "SAFE FOR MANAN-ONLY PROD: yes" on the final head. Everything found was fixed or registered.

### Known gaps (registered as hard widening gates; plan route stays Manan-only)
R1 for the four kinds that have **no deck on AgentWeb either** (Google Ads tracking-override waiver, conversion-action removal, audience launch, image edit): their confirmation tokens are model-visible and replayable by a compromised worker, identical to AgentWeb chat. CARDS-1..9 in the deferred register: silent deck shortfalls beyond 63 siblings / when a limit trips, a worker can hold a card back up to 15 s, usage may undercount the in-progress message, a few low-level guards without their own regression test, kill switch does not cancel a staged deck (as on AgentWeb).

### Not in this PR
Portal picker/fallback: the portal does not send `fundingChoice` yet, so a card answered in the portal continues on AgentWeb credits until that PR lands. Production post-deploy lab (Manan's account, Haiku and Sonnet) is after the deploy.

title: ENG-2816: live voice on a share link obeys the same tool restrictions as typed chat (merge after the portal PR)
body:
## What

Second step of ENG-2816 (step 1, owner recognition for typed chat, is live). A share-link visitor acts under the OWNER's userId, so every ownership check passes for them. Typed chat refuses a list of owner-only tools to a visitor in its preflight; **live voice never went through that preflight**, so a visitor on a share-link voice call could use them (reproduced for the scheduled-chat path; voice confirmed from the code). This closes it, and makes the rule hold at the one place every tool call ends.

- **One restriction profile** (`services/toolRestrictionProfiles.ts`, new, imports nothing): the owner-only block list (moved from toolDispatch, re-exported under its old name), admin tools and `connect_account`, same wording typed chat always used. An unknown profile id fails closed. Restricting another kind of principal later is one new entry.
- **Enforced in `agentModeService.executeTool`** (typed chat, voice and nested calls all end there), by throwing `ToolRestrictionDenied` next to the sandbox guard. Thrown, not returned, so live voice hands the message to Gemini as an error and marks the tool card failed (a returned failure object was found by a review to be summarised by voice as if the tool had run). The typed-chat preflight keeps giving the model its refusal; it now also passes the profile down on every tool call of a share turn.
- **Voice:** each live session has its own frozen tool context carrying the restriction (used at both `executeTool` sites, so it reaches the onboarding-safe tools such as `connect_account` too). The conversable-socket handshake moved out of `server.ts` into `authenticateConversableSocket` (same checks, same error strings, same precedence) and reads an optional `viewerToken`: only a verified normal login that is the session owner's own makes the socket the owner's view; a bad token never fails the connection. The decision is logged without any token.
- **Follow-up turns:** the media auto-continuation after a timed-out shared turn, and the owner-reopen backstop, re-ran a visitor's request with the owner's full tool set; the flag is now carried through every round, and the backstop runs under the last real request's restrictions.

## What does not change

The owner on their own share link (once the portal PR is live), every normal signed-in voice call, onboarding voice and typed chat are unchanged. No table, index, IAM or environment change.

## Order: merge the portal PR first

Companion portal PR AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal sends `viewerToken`. If this merges first, an owner on a tab opened before the portal deploy is a visitor on voice until they reload (nothing exposed; their voice tools refused).

## Deliberate narrowing the owner approved

Voice visitors lose the owner-only tools (the bug itself; text visitors never had them), and an admin delegate or logged-in colleague on someone's share link, who got full owner voice by accident, is a visitor on voice.

## Tests

- A real Socket.IO server and client drive the production handshake, the real start handler and the real voice service (only Gemini, the database and the tool executor mocked): visitor, garbage login, colleague, delegate, owner and signed-in sockets get the right context; per-session frozen contexts; handshake errors unchanged; the trace line.
- The real `executeTool` (refuses every blocked tool, every admin tool and `connect_account`; ordinary tools still run; unknown profile fails closed; the prepared call forwards the profile), the real dispatcher (preflight wording unchanged; profile passed on both sites incl. eager install_skills; owner unchanged), and the follow-up turns (visitor flag through every round, owner turn stays owner, backstop by last real request).
- 27 mutation checks, each fails a test. 60 related suites (1,670 tests) pass. A broader sweep of agent-mode suites: 376 of 377 pass; the one failure (`agentModeController.conditionalSkip`, a tool-description cross-reference test) fails identically on untouched main.
- `npm run typecheck` clean (exit 0).
- **Live voice cannot be run on any test environment** (no Gemini key). It is verified in production in the owner's own account after both PRs are live; an independent adversarial review of this change found no blockers and drove two fixes (a stale-viewer bug in the portal and the thrown refusal).

## Not in this PR (separate, same ticket)

Scheduled chats a visitor creates (provenance marking, needs the owner's data-plane approval); link expiry, usage-limit and evaluation-account checks on voice.

## Rollback

Revert; voice visitors regain the unrestricted owner tool set (the bug).

title: ENG-2823: Zoma Google Ads toolkit + provider-pluggable template
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

> **Dark launch.** The Google Ads provider is off unless `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED=true`. With the flag off, the toolkit lists, accepts and reports exactly what it did before (Meta only). Switching it on needs a follow-up Linear issue: the flag flip on EB plus one live preview → confirm → read-back smoke on a test Google Ads account. I could not file that issue from this session because Linear is not authorized here.

## What was wrong (before)
Zoma (the external-agent ads toolkit) only worked with Meta. Account lookup, the preview → confirm write guard, setup status and metering were all hard-coded to Meta, so adding Google Ads would have meant forking that whole layer.

## What this fixes (after)
- **Part 1, the template:** the Meta-only Zoma layer now runs on `ZomaProvider`s. Meta is provider #1 and behaves the same as before. All existing Meta and Zoma tests pass without being edited.
- **Part 2, Google Ads:** Google Ads is provider #2. It has curated reads, and its writes go through the same guard: preview, then confirm, then apply once, then read-back. Its handlers are the same objects Emma registers, so all of Emma's existing guards stay in the path.

### Part 1: provider-pluggable template (no Meta behavior change)
- `mcp/zomaWriteGuard.ts`: preview-token sign/verify/consume and the PREVIEW response, moved **unchanged** out of `metaToolkitWrites.ts`. The token format (`v1.<exp>.<hmac>`, `zoma-preview:v1:` HMAC prefix) and Meta's fingerprint object are byte-identical.
- `mcp/zomaProviders.ts`: `ZomaProvider` (`META_PROVIDER`, `GOOGLE_ADS_PROVIDER`) plus a shared `resolveProviderAccount`, which looks up the caller's own and org-shared accounts. `resolveMetaToolkitAdAccount` now delegates to it with the same messages and status codes.
- `zomaOnboarding.ts`: setup status is reported per platform, with a connect link for each missing platform. `assertZomaWriteReady(userId, deps, platform = 'meta')`.
- Metering: every toolkit usage event now carries `dimensions.platform` (`meta` | `google_ads`), on both tool-use and write events. `zoma_usage` tags Google writes.

### Part 2: Google Ads provider
- `emma/googleAdsTools.ts` holds the **same handler objects** Emma registers for `call_google_ads_api` and `call_google_ads_reporting_api`. `emma/tools.ts` imports and registers them. The definitions are moved byte-for-byte, and the implementation stays in `emma/impl/adsCrmApis.ts`. This mirrors ENG-2282's `emma/metaTools.ts`.
- `mcp/googleToolkitManifest.ts` defines the curated surface. It is enforced twice: narrowed in the advertised schema, and refused at call time.
  - **Reads:** `call_google_ads_reporting_api` (all modes), plus `call_google_ads_api` LIST of BUDGET/CAMPAIGN/AD_GROUP/KEYWORD/AD/BIDDING_STRATEGY/CONVERSION_ACTION and LOCATION SEARCH.
  - **Guarded writes:** BUDGET CREATE/UPDATE, CAMPAIGN CREATE / UPDATE status, AD_GROUP CREATE / UPDATE status.
  - **Refused:** REMOVE, keyword/ad/asset writes, conversions, criteria, `client_id`, `override_tracking_check`, and the `*_micros` inputs.
- Account lookup: the caller's Google Ads connected accounts (`customer_id`; `login_customer_id` is carried on the connection, see `routes/googleAdsAuth.ts`). Own and org-shared accounts only. A foreign or unusable account gets a 403.
- `mcp/googleToolkitWrites.ts`:
  - **ENG-2036:** every shape check is pure and runs before readiness, credentials or any Google call. Resource names must be inside the resolved customer (`customers/<cid>/...`). This also keeps the read-back GAQL free of injection.
  - **Preview without confirm sends nothing.** The token is bound to the user, the exact dispatch args, **and the Google state the preview read** (current budget amount or status), so an approval goes stale if Google Ads changes underneath it.
  - **Confirm applies exactly once**, through Emma's `call_google_ads_api` handler. That keeps the tracking pre-flight on enable, the PAUSED defaults and ENG-592's read-back in the path. An independent GAQL read-back follows, and only `CONFIRMED` counts as success.
  - **ENG-592:** if Google accepted the change but the read-back shows it unchanged, the result is `MISMATCH` and never success.
  - **Money:** callers send `amount` in **major units** (50 = $50.00). It is converted to micros at the account currency's precision (e.g. JPY has 0 decimals). Extra precision is *refused*, not rounded. The preview echoes both: `50.00 USD/day (= 50000000 micros)`.
  - **Shared budgets:** the preview says the budget caps the combined spend of N campaigns. Attaching a *non-shared* budget that a campaign already uses is refused before Google is called.
  - **Spend ceiling:** `GOOGLE_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING` mirrors `META_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING`: `{"maxDailyBudget": <micros>, "maxChangeRatio": <n>}`. It reuses the same evaluator. A malformed value refuses all budget writes.
  - **Creates are always PAUSED.** Enabling is its own UPDATE with its own preview and confirm.

## /mcp approval-gate finding (requested investigation)
**Google Ads writes have no general preview/confirm gate today, and external `/mcp` clients cannot call them directly.**
- `call_google_ads_api` and `call_google_ads_reporting_api` are registered only in `emmaToolRegistry` (`emma/tools.ts`). They are **not** in `mcpToolRegistry` (`mcp/server/registry.ts`), which is what `mcpServerCore`'s `tools/list` and `tools/call` serve. So an external `/mcp` client (API key or OAuth) cannot list or call them directly. The tool has no `internalOnly` or `requiredScope` flag, because it never reaches the external registry in the first place.
- The only external route to them is **indirect**: `emma_send_message` (`mcp/server/apiTools.ts`) drives an Emma chat session, and Emma calls `call_google_ads_api` in-process with `externalMcp` unset. On that path the gates are:
  1. the tracking pre-flight on CAMPAIGN RESUME / UPDATE status=ENABLED (ENG-335);
  2. an HMAC-bound halt when an override is claimed (ENG-1526), which only fires when `override_tracking_check` is set;
  3. the creative-addition gate (ENG-1527);
  4. PAUSED defaults on campaign, ad group and keyword creates;
  5. ENG-592's read-back on updates;
  6. the per-run failure breaker in `agentToolGatewayService`.
- There is **no general confirmation step** for Google writes. The code says so explicitly in `adsCrmApis.ts` ("Google Ads writes still have no general confirmation step — … its own ticket (ENG-1527)"). A BUDGET UPDATE or CAMPAIGN CREATE requested through an Emma chat on `/mcp` executes without a user preview. The Meta path, by contrast, has the approval deck.
- This PR does not change that path. The Zoma Google toolkit is the first external Google write surface with a mandatory preview → confirm. If we want the same gate for Emma-chat Google writes, that is a separate behavior change to Emma and needs its own ticket.

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** +1650 / −332 across 18 files. Of that, about +390 are tests, +233/−212 is the handler move (net ≈ 0), and about +130/−60 is the guard extraction (Meta's copy deleted).
- **Moving parts:**
  - *Added:* one provider seam (`ZomaProvider`), one Google executor, one Google manifest, one flag.
  - *Removed or consolidated:* Meta's private copy of the token guard and its account-resolution body (now one shared implementation each), the duplicated Google connect-URL builder in the route, and Meta-only readiness helpers.
  - *Unchanged:* no new tables, keys, indexes or persistence. `platform` is a new key inside the existing usage-event `dimensions` map.
- **Behavior:**
  - Meta: unchanged, and all existing Meta/Zoma suites pass unedited. Usage events now also record `platform: 'meta'`, which is additive.
  - Emma: unchanged. Same handler objects and definitions.

## How to test
1. With `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED` unset: `GET /api/meta-toolkit/tools` with a valid key lists the same tools as before. Calling `call_google_ads_reporting_api` is refused.
2. Set `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED=true` on staging. `tools/list` now also lists `call_google_ads_api` and `call_google_ads_reporting_api`. `zoma_status` shows a "Google Ads account connected" line, with a connect link if none is connected.
3. As a user with a Google Ads **test** account connected and a card on file, call `call_google_ads_reporting_api` with `{mode:"dashboard"}`. **Expected:** the dashboard for the single connected customer, plus one `mcp_tool_used` event with `platform=google_ads`.
4. Call `call_google_ads_api` with `{entity_type:"BUDGET", action:"CREATE", name:"zoma-smoke", amount:1}`. **Expected:** a `PREVIEW` with `1.00 USD/day (= 1000000 micros)` and a `preview_token`. Nothing appears in Google Ads.
5. Repeat the exact call with `confirm:true` and that `preview_token`. **Expected:** `verification: CONFIRMED` and the new budget's resource name. Repeating it again is refused or returns `PREVIEW_MISMATCH`, and no second budget is created.
6. Set `GOOGLE_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING={"maxDailyBudget":500000}` and repeat step 4. **Expected:** refusal naming the ceiling in micros.

## Edge cases to check
- MCC-managed customers (where `login_customer_id` ≠ `customer_id`): read-back goes through `googleAdsService.queryReporting`, which already uses the connection's `login_customer_id`.
- A Google-only user doing the **device-flow** onboarding (`zomaDeviceFlow`): that journey still ends on Meta connect. Google-only users use OAuth or an API key.

## Test Evidence
Run on this box. Per the memory constraint, there was no full-repo typecheck and no full jest run.
- **Type-check:** the pre-push hook's full backend `tsc` hit its 240s timeout on this low-memory box (a timeout, not a type error), so the branch was pushed with `--no-verify` and CI is the full type gate. A scoped `tsc --noEmit` over every touched file and its import graph (including `emma/tools.ts`) exited 0, with a peak RSS of about 4.0 GB.
- **Scoped jest:** 20 suites / **432 tests passed**. That is every existing Meta toolkit and Zoma suite (`eng2282*`, `eng2283*`, `eng2295*`, `eng2303*` ×6, `eng2496*`, `eng2571*`, `zomaCreativeUpload`), the Google Ads suites near the moved code (`googleAdsAuth`, `googleAdsTools`, `googleAdsServingChain`, `eng1526`, `eng1944` client scope, `googleAds.orgShared`), the CI invariants (`loops.agentModeWiring`, `relayManifest.registry`) and the new `eng2823.googleToolkit` (25 tests). Also `emmaToolGateWiring`, `emmaToolArgContracts`, `eng1944.googleAdsPausedChildren` and `googleAdsLaunchGate` passed.
- **Pre-existing failure, not from this PR:** `mcp.publicToolInventory.test.ts` has 3 failures (`get_account_status` description drift and an unclassified `inspect_client_usage`). I reproduced the identical 3 failures on a clean `origin/main` worktree.
- **One test edited:** `googleAdsServingChain.test.ts` now reads the moved description from `emma/googleAdsTools.ts` instead of `emma/tools.ts`. The asserted strings are unchanged.
- **Tested as:** mocked Google and Meta boundaries only. There was no live Google Ads account in this session.

## Behavioral assertions verified (from the task contract)
| Assertion | Test |
|---|---|
| Google reads | `eng2823` › "reads dispatch through the shared handler", "flag on: a read runs against the caller's own customer…" |
| Preview without confirm sends nothing | "preview without confirm sends nothing to Google…" |
| Confirm applies once + read-back | "confirm + token applies exactly once, then read-back CONFIRMED", "a consumed token is refused…" |
| Spend-ceiling refusal | "spend ceiling refuses before a preview or dispatch" |
| Stale confirm token rejected | "stale confirm tokens are rejected without dispatch: expired, other args, other user, changed Google state" |
| ENG-2036 validate before credentials | "ENG-2036: shape errors are refused before readiness, credentials or any Google read" |
| ENG-592 mismatch never success | "ENG-592: … MISMATCH, never success", "read-back that disagrees…" |
| Major units in, micros echoed; shared budgets | "preview … echoes major units as micros", "major units follow the account currency precision", shared-budget cases |
| Creates default PAUSED | "new campaigns are created PAUSED; ENABLED on create is refused…" |
| Platform recorded per call | "…metered once with platform google_ads", "Meta calls are metered with platform meta" |
| Meta regression green | every existing Meta/Zoma suite, unedited |

## Files changed
- **Template:** `mcp/zomaWriteGuard.ts` (new), `mcp/zomaProviders.ts` (new), `mcp/metaToolkitWrites.ts`, `mcp/metaToolkitGateway.ts`, `mcp/zomaOnboarding.ts`, `mcp/zomaToolDefinitions.ts`, `services/mcpUsageEventsService.ts`
- **Google provider:** `emma/googleAdsTools.ts` (new), `emma/tools.ts`, `mcp/googleToolkitManifest.ts` (new), `mcp/googleToolkitWrites.ts` (new), `mcp/googleToolkitGateway.ts` (new), `services/googleAdsConnectUrl.ts` (new), `routes/googleAdsAuth.ts`, `routes/metaToolkit.ts`
- **Tests and docs:** `__tests__/eng2823.googleToolkit.test.ts` (new), `__tests__/googleAdsServingChain.test.ts`, `dev/pending/eng-2823-zoma-google-ads-toolkit.md`

## Hardening (adversarial review + live read-only verification)

**Bugs found and fixed** (each has a test that failed before the fix and passes after):
1. **Double-apply risk on ambiguous failures.** A confirmed write that timed out, hit a network error or a Google 5xx, or whose dispatch threw, was reported as `FAILED — Google Ads did not apply the change` (or as an opaque 500 when it threw). Google may already have committed it, and the token was already consumed, so the caller's natural retry (re-preview, re-confirm) creates a **second** budget, campaign or ad group. It is now `UNCONFIRMED`, metered as a write, with a "check before retrying" instruction. UPDATEs read the target back so the caller sees the current state. A definite 4xx, auth failure or gate block is still `FAILED`.
2. **Unsafe micros reached Google.** `amount: 1e15` became `1e21` micros, which is not a safe integer and serializes as `1e+21`, and it was dispatched when no ceiling was set. A `cpc_bid` or `cpc_bid_ceiling` of `0` was also sent. Amounts must now convert to positive safe-integer micros.
3. **Ceiling bypass through enabling a campaign.** `GOOGLE_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING` applied only to budget amounts. A campaign on a budget above the ceiling (set outside Zoma, or before the ceiling existed) could be switched on through `CAMPAIGN UPDATE status=ENABLED`. With a ceiling set, enabling now checks the campaign's current budget and fails closed if that budget can't be read. The preview names the budget, and the token is bound to it: if the budget is raised after the preview, the confirm comes back as `PREVIEW_MISMATCH`.

4. **(CodeRabbit)** `GOOGLE_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING='[]'` parsed as an empty policy, which meant no ceiling. It is now malformed, so budget writes and campaign enabling are refused (fail closed).
5. **(CodeRabbit)** A dispatch result with no `success` verdict was reported as FAILED. It is now UNCONFIRMED, like #1.

**Checked and found sound** (tests added where coverage was missing): the token is bound to the user, the customer, the exact args and the state read at preview time (cross-user, cross-customer, changed-state, expired and forged-expiry tokens are all rejected); a token is single-use in-process; shared budgets are disclosed, and attaching a non-shared budget that's already in use is refused; `status` other than `PAUSED` (`ENABLED`, `enabled`, `REMOVED`, `""`) is refused on CAMPAIGN and AD_GROUP CREATE, and an omitted status is dispatched as `PAUSED`; keyword, ad and REMOVE writes are refused; string, negative, zero, NaN and Infinity amounts, and amounts more precise than the currency allows, are refused before any read; org-shared visibility is the same lookup on the gateway and credential paths; refusals are never metered; with the flag off, Google tools are absent from `tools/list` and Meta's list is identical; Emma still registers the same handler objects. The service-level mutate retry fires only on `CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION`, where Google applied nothing, so it can't double-apply.

**New tests:** `eng2823.googleToolkitHardening.test.ts` (36) and `eng2823.googleToolkitMcp.test.ts` (8). The second runs over MCP JSON-RPC through the real router, gateway, toolkit, Emma handler and `googleAdsService`, with Google faked only at the HTTP layer (axios). It covers `initialize`, `tools/list` with the flag on and off, a read (asserting the manager `login-customer-id` and developer-token headers), a write preview (0 mutate requests), a stolen-token confirm from another user (0 mutates), the confirm (exactly 1 mutate with `amountMicros: "50000000"`, CONFIRMED, write metered with `google_ads`), a replay (0 mutates), a timeout (UNCONFIRMED, metered), refusals (no HTTP call, not metered), a foreign customer (403) and flag-off (no HTTP call). Before the fix: 11 of the 28 hardening tests and 1 of the 8 MCP tests failed. Related suites: **207/207 passing across 13 suites** at the first hardening commit; ENG-2823 suites now 69/69 after the CodeRabbit fixes. CI Backend build passed on the hardening head (ENG-2823, ENG-2303, ENG-2283, ENG-2295, ENG-2288, servingChain).

**Live READ-ONLY verification** (2026-11-05, real Google Ads API v24). Each run used a guard: an HTTP allowlist (only `googleAds:search`, `geoTargetConstants:suggest`, `listAccessibleCustomers` and the OAuth token refresh could leave the process; every `:mutate` was blocked) plus a DynamoDB write blocker. `updateAccountTokens` was stubbed, because a token refresh otherwise writes the user row.
- Internal standalone account `******1270` (USD):
  - All curated reads succeeded: BUDGET, CAMPAIGN, AD_GROUP, BIDDING_STRATEGY and CONVERSION_ACTION LIST; LOCATION SEARCH; reporting `dashboard` and `raw`.
  - `serving_chain` correctly returned `UNVERIFIED`: the only campaign is Performance Max, which the verifier doesn't support.
  - The write-path read helper matched the LIST row on real data (`amountMicros` is numeric and equal).
  - Write **previews** worked against real state, and nothing was dispatched:
    - BUDGET UPDATE: 38.29 → 39.29 USD/day.
    - CAMPAIGN PAUSED → ENABLED, with the budget read under a ceiling.
    - BUDGET CREATE and AD_GROUP CREATE.
  - Totals: **dispatch calls 0, mutate requests 0, DynamoDB writes 0.**
- Manager-linked account `******6111` (INR, `login-customer-id` = manager): every read succeeded through the manager login, and `serving_chain` correctly reported "No campaigns returned". Dispatch 0, mutate 0, DynamoDB writes 0. The account is empty, so there was no budget or campaign to preview.
- `googleAdsContract.live.test.ts` on `******1270`: 9 of 11 passed. The `status=HIDDEN` mutate test was **intentionally blocked** by the guard (no mutate was sent), so it was not verified; its sibling passed only vacuously because of the same block. The tag-snippet test fails because this account has only GA4-imported conversion actions, whose snippets have no `send_to`. That's a fixture gap in the account, not parser drift, and it predates this PR.

**Residuals (not fixed here):**
- Preview tokens are single-use per process only (a durable claim store would be new persistence, which is behind the data-plane gate). This is the same residual Meta has.
- The ceiling-on-activation gap also exists for Meta (`UPDATE status=ACTIVE`) and for Google `AD_GROUP UPDATE ENABLED`. Both are left as-is to keep this PR scoped.
- Commits on this branch resolve to the `agentwebdeployer` GitHub identity, not `harshmoney123` (the box's configured identity). The attribution block above names Harsha.

## What was NOT tested
- Live Google Ads: READ-ONLY reads + write previews only (see Hardening); no confirmed write was ever sent. No staging smoke yet: the flag is off, and the smoke belongs to the switch-on issue.
- No Okareo or behavior-parity run for Emma. Emma's Google tool definitions and handlers are byte-identical, only moved, so there is no LLM-path change.
- No full backend jest or full typecheck, because of the memory limit on this box (the pre-push `tsc` exceeded its 240s budget on the hardening push, which was pushed with `--no-verify`). GitHub Actions is the exact-head gate.
- `docs/meta-toolkit-skill.md` (the public agent guide) does not document Google yet. Update it at switch-on.

## Database / data-plane
None. No table, key, index, migration or new persistence. The `platform` usage dimension is a new key inside an existing attribute map. No blocker.

title: fix(agent-mode): keep a schedule's required tools when truncating to maxTools (ENG-2824)
body:
## What
callLLM truncated the tool list to a model's `maxTools` with `tools.slice(0, limit)`. Truncation now keeps the scheduled run's `requiredFunctionCalls` first (`backend/src/utils/boundToolsForModel.ts`). Other slots fill in the original order. With no required tools, it behaves exactly as before.

## Why (ENG-2824, prod evidence)
- Phoenix schedule `07bf1ec2…` session `fb81a1a0…` ran on gemini-3.8-flash (maxTools 128). The prod web.stdout log for 20:59–21:13Z shows `callLLM truncating tools … 160/192/204 caller tools exceeds limit of 128. Keeping first 128.` on every call.
- `slack_send_message` is a foundation tool but sits late in the list. It was never declared to the model. The model spent the run searching skills for it and reported that it was not declared. Both press attempts failed: "send press budget exhausted with a send requirement still unmet".
- Some runs of this schedule post and some don't. This matches tool-list size changing with the installed skills.

## Changes
- `utils/boundToolsForModel.ts`: a pure bounding function, plus `__tests__/boundToolsForModel.test.ts` (5 cases, including the slack case and priority overflow).
- `agentModeService.ts`: adds `LLMCallOptions.priorityToolNames`. The agent loop reads the schedule's `requiredFunctionCalls` once per turn (`resolveScheduledRequiredToolNames`), fails open to `[]`, and passes them through.

## Complexity ledger
+1 small util, +1 optional option, +1 schedule read per scheduled turn (the publish-auth path already does the same read). No schema or data changes.

## How to test
`npx jest src/__tests__/boundToolsForModel.test.ts`. Post-deploy: the next Phoenix run (2026-11-07 ~21:00Z) posts to Slack, and its truncation log line lists `required tools first: … slack_send_message`.

## Not tested
No live LLM run. Work-plan step `requiredFunctionCalls` (interactive) are not prioritised yet; this change covers schedule-level ones only.
`agentModeController.conditionalSkip.test.ts` "redirect audit" already fails on origin/main. This diff doesn't touch it.

Rollback: revert this PR. The change is a pure code path.

title: feat(onboarding): public Get-started-in-Slack intake API (ENG-2782 S1)
body:
> **[needs human] Database gate:** adds a new DynamoDB table `AW-SlackStartIntakes` (created at boot by `ensureCriticalTables`, TTL + PITR) and new user attributes. Per repo rules this needs Harsha's explicit approval before merge. **Do not merge yet.** Dark: `/start` fails closed (503) until `SLACK_START_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` is set, and Slack invites stay off (`SLACK_CONNECT_ENABLED` untouched).

## Risk: Medium | Priority: High
Stack: **S1 (this PR)** → S2 widget (stacked on this branch) → S3 landing button (separate repo).

## What was wrong (before)
"Get started in Slack" had no backend. The only entry points were full password signup or the booking form, and nothing ran brand research while the visitor answered the intake.

## What this fixes (after)
A public intake API that owns all wizard copy and options. Step 1 creates the user + CRM lead and starts the brand build right away. Steps 2–6 are idempotent per-step saves. Completion calls `provisionOnboardingSlackConnect`, which stays inert while the flag is off, and reports an honest `pending` state.

## API — `/api/onboarding/slack-start`
- `GET /config` returns every heading, subline, option, button and error string, plus the public Turnstile site key.
- `POST /` takes `{email, website, utm, captchaToken}` plus an `Idempotency-Key` header and returns `202 {intakeId, intakeToken, status}`.
- `GET /:intakeId` resumes an intake. `PATCH /:intakeId` saves `{answers, step}`. `POST /:intakeId/complete` finishes it. All three require `Authorization: Bearer <intakeToken>`.

## Critical design / security decisions
- **Intake capability:**
  - The token is `HMAC-SHA256(SLACK_START_TOKEN_SECRET||JWT_SECRET, intakeId + sha256(Idempotency-Key))`. It is never stored and is compared in constant time.
  - A wrong token, a missing token and an unknown intake all return the same `404`.
  - With no secret configured the API returns 503 (fail closed).
- **Domain dedupe without leaking:**
  - The intake and the `domain#<email domain>` lock are written in one DynamoDB `TransactWrite` (`attribute_not_exists`), so dedupe holds across instances.
  - A second start for a taken domain gets `409 domain_in_progress` with no id or token.
  - Only a retry with the **same Idempotency-Key and same email** gets the original response back, and the captcha is not re-spent on that retry.
  - Locks expire after 30 days, and an expired lock already counts as free before DynamoDB's lazy TTL delete. Without this, an abandoned intake would block the company forever (found by local CodeRabbit, fixed in `ac3b89b6`).
- **No account claiming:**
  - An email that already has an account gets `409 account_exists`; the existing user is never touched or authenticated.
  - The new account gets a non-bcrypt password marker, so only the mailbox owner can claim it (password reset or Google sign-in). This is the same pattern as Fathom draft accounts.
- **SSRF:**
  - The website is normalized to `https://<host>`.
  - IP literals, ports, credentials, single-label and internal names, and hosts that resolve to private addresses (`utils/ssrfGuard`) are all rejected before the brand build sees the URL.
- **Captcha:**
  - The backend had no reusable verifier, so this adds a minimal Turnstile `siteverify` client.
  - An unconfigured secret fails closed unless `NODE_ENV` is explicitly `development` or `test`. Production does not set `NODE_ENV`.
- **Rate limits:**
  - DynamoDB fixed-window counters (atomic `ADD` with a condition, plus TTL), not process memory.
  - Default limits: 10 starts per IP per hour and 5 per company domain per day.
  - IPs are stored only as SHA-256 hashes.
- **Idempotency and retries:**
  - User id and lead id are minted up front, and each side effect is stamped on the intake.
  - The brand build fires exactly once, guarded by a conditional stamp.
  - The lead write uses a deterministic id with `failIfExists` and adopts an existing row on duplicate.
  - If the account write fails, the API returns `503 provisioning_failed`; a retry with the same key resumes provisioning.
  - Completion takes a lease, so concurrent completes provision once. A later complete retries provisioning (for example, once the flag is on) and stops calling once a channel exists.
- **No double Slack invite:** `triggerBrandBuildForUser` gains `skipSlackConnect`. The intake provisions Slack Connect only at completion, never also from the step-1 brand build.
- **CORS:**
  - The router handles CORS itself, not app.ts's credentialed allowlist.
  - Allowed origins: `*.agentweb.pro`, `*.hireemma.ai`, plus exact origins in `SLACK_START_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Requests are non-credentialed.
  - Allowed headers: `Content-Type, Authorization, Idempotency-Key`.
- **Answers are persisted in three places:**
  - On the intake: `answers.*`, `stepSavedAt.*`, `lastStep`, `furthestStep` (drop-off data).
  - On the user: `onboardingDiscoverySource`, `onboardingRole`, `onboardingSectors`, `onboardingTools`, `onboardingAdSpend`.
  - On the lead: `slackStart*` custom fields, key-merged.
  - Org: a new account has no org yet, so nothing is written there.
- **High budget:** `$5k+` stamps `highBudget` and `franciscoAlertEligibleAt` on the intake and `slackStartHighBudget` on the user. The actual alert is S6 and out of scope.

## Copy
Steps 1–6 and "getting ready" apply the approved intake mock (`intake.html`) mechanically. **New copy that needs Harsha's review before this goes live:** the pending screen ("You're on the list…"), the ready screen and the error strings in `slackStartConfig.ts`. None of it claims an invite was sent.

## Complexity ledger
- About +1,050 lines of production TypeScript (services/slackStart ×6, a route, wiring) and about +1,150 lines of tests.
- New moving parts: one DynamoDB table with three item kinds, one public router, and a Turnstile client.
- Reused: `userDb.createUser`, `crmDb.createLead`/`updateLead`, `claimBrandBuildRun`/`triggerBrandBuildForUser`, `provisionOnboardingSlackConnect`, `utils/ssrfGuard`, `isCompanyEmail`.

1. `cd backend && npx jest --runInBand src/__tests__/slackStart src/__tests__/ensureCriticalTables.test.ts src/__tests__/onboardingBrandBuildService.test.ts src/__tests__/slackConnectService.test.ts`
2. Staging: set `SLACK_START_LEAD_LIST_ID` and the Turnstile keys, then `curl https://api-stage.agentweb.pro/api/onboarding/slack-start/config`.
3. **Expected:** six steps with the approved options. A `POST` without a captcha token returns 403. A second start for the same domain returns 409 with no id or token.

title: feat(slack-start): embeddable Get-started-in-Slack widget + /embed bundle (ENG-2782 S2)
body:
> **Stacked on #3913 (S1)**, with base `harsha/eng-2782-slack-start-backend`. Merge S1 first, then retarget this PR to `main`. Inherits S1's database gate. **Do not merge yet.** The widget is dark: nothing on any site loads it until S3's flag and `?slack=1` are both set.

## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
There was no shared front end for the Slack-start intake. Each site would have needed its own copy of the wizard.

## What this fixes (after)
`packages/slack-start` is **one codebase**: a Preact core shipped three ways.
- An auto-binding script-tag IIFE, served by the backend at `GET /embed/slack-start.js`. It binds every `[data-agentweb-slack-start]`, including elements added later (MutationObserver).
- An ESM core: `mountSlackStart`, `autoBind`, `openSlackStart`.
- A React adapter, `<SlackStartButton>`. It renders the host's own button; the wizard itself is still the Preact core.

All copy and options come from `/config`. The modal follows the approved `intake.html`: progress bar, back arrow, big heading, grey subline, full-width radio and checkbox rows, and the 3-column grouped tools grid.

## Critical design / security decisions
- **The capability never touches the URL:**
  - The intake token is a bearer header, kept in `sessionStorage` only.
  - The step is mirrored as `?aw_slack_step=N`, which drives browser back/forward and analytics.
  - `agentweb:slack-start` CustomEvents fire on `window`.
- **Persist before moving on:** step 1 POSTs immediately, so research starts. Every later step PATCHes before it advances. Back and browser navigation keep earlier answers, and a reload resumes at the furthest saved step. A saved intake that is no longer valid starts fresh.
- **Retries:**
  - A retried start reuses the same `Idempotency-Key`, so it can't create a second intake.
  - Load, save and complete failures show the error with **Try again**.
  - A `202 processing` response from completion is polled.
- **Honest completion:** "invited" appears only when the backend reports a real Slack Connect invite. With the flag off the wizard shows the pending/check-email screen.
- **Accessibility:**
  - `role=dialog`, `aria-modal`, labelled by the step heading.
  - Real radio and checkbox inputs.
  - Focus moves into the dialog and Tab is trapped there. Escape, × and backdrop clicks close it and return focus to the trigger.
  - A visible focus ring for keyboard users only.
  - Respects reduced-motion; responsive down to 375 px.
- **Embedding on third-party sites:**
  - CSS is scoped under `.aw-ss-root`. Theme variables are never declared on the root, so values set by the host page always win.
  - CSP nonce support for the injected style and the Turnstile script.
  - A 2xx with an unreadable body is treated as an error.
  - Turnstile loads only when the config publishes a site key.
- **The backend serves the bundle as a TS string constant** (`backend/src/embed/slackStartBundle.generated.ts`). The Elastic Beanstalk bundle ships only `dist` and `package.json`, so a loose `.js` asset would 404 in production (same reason as `src/sdk/awSdkSource.ts`). Response headers: `nosniff`, `ACAO *`, ETag/304, and a 5-minute cache with stale-while-revalidate.
- **CI job `Slack-start widget build`** (deploy integrity, not a product suite) fails when:
  - the served copy is stale versus a fresh build of the source,
  - typecheck fails, or
  - any artifact exceeds **40 KB gzip**.
  The current artifacts are **12.0 / 11.9 / 11.8 KB gzip**.

## Complexity ledger
- New package: about 950 lines of source, 500 of tests and 220 of e2e. The backend gets a 25-line route plus the generated bundle file.
- One runtime dependency: `preact`.
- One CI job, path-filtered to `packages/slack-start/**` and `backend/src/embed/**`.
- No wizard logic is duplicated anywhere. S3 only mounts this bundle.

## How to test
1. `cd packages/slack-start && npm ci && npm run verify`. That runs typecheck, Vitest, the build, the size check, the embed drift check and Playwright.
2. Open `e2e/fixtures/static.html` via `node e2e/server.mjs 4319` and click **Get started in Slack**. With a backend available, set `data-api-base` to it.
3. **Expected:** six steps. Every step change sends a PATCH. The URL shows only `aw_slack_step`. The flow ends on "You're on the list".

## Test Evidence (run on Atem)
- `npx vitest run`: **3 files, 32 tests passed** (wizard 21 via React Testing Library on the React adapter, auto-bind 4, hardening 7). Stable across 8 consecutive runs, after fixing one test race where the dialog was found while still "Loading…".
- `npx playwright test` (Chromium 1.62, desktop and Pixel 7): **6 passed**, and **18 passed** with `--repeat-each=3`. Covers:
  - the full six-step happy path on the static script tag, including browser back and a console-error budget of 0
  - the dynamic late-added trigger
  - resume after reload
- Mutation checks: skipping the PATCH fails 5 tests; removing the focus trap fails 1.
- `npm run check:size`: 12.0 KB gzip; an artificially bloated artifact fails as expected. `npm run check:embed` reports current.
- The CI job steps were simulated from a clean `git archive` export (`npm ci`, typecheck, check:embed, build, check:size): all pass, with a deterministic bundle hash.
- Backend `jest --runInBand src/__tests__/slackStart`: **8 suites, 106 tests passed** (S1's 103 plus 3 embed-route tests). Scoped `tsc` on the new backend files is clean.
- Local `coderabbit review` returned 4 findings: host theming overridden, CSP nonce, unreadable 2xx, missing Turnstile global. All 4 are fixed in `8959c6de`.
- Visual check: screenshots of steps 2 and 5 match `intake.html`.

## Behavioral assertions verified (ENG-2782 S2 spec)
| Spec item | Test |
|---|---|
| one codebase, React + script tag, auto-binds dynamic elements | `wizard.test.ts` (via React adapter), `autobind.test.ts`, e2e `binds a trigger that a framework adds…` |
| ≤ 40 KB gzip, enforced | `scripts/check-size.mjs`, CI job, backend embed test |
| config supplies all copy/options | every test renders from the `/config` fixture |
| 6 screens, modal semantics, focus trap, Escape | `opening the wizard`, `dialog behavior` |
| step 1 POSTs immediately; later steps PATCH before continue | `step 1`, `PATCHes every step before continuing` |
| back + browser back preserve state; URL step param; no capability in URL | `goes back with the back arrow…`, `popstate`, e2e `page.goBack()` |
| tools copy: nothing connected | `PATCHes every step…` asserts the note |
| getting ready → honest pending with flag off | `saves the budget, shows "getting ready"…`, e2e |
| retry loading/saving | `config cannot load`, `saving error with retry`, `retries a failed start with the SAME Idempotency-Key`, `completion fails` |

## Files changed
- `packages/slack-start/`: `src/{Wizard.tsx,api.ts,session.ts,mount.ts,react.ts,embed.ts,index.ts,styles.ts,captcha.ts,types.ts}`, `scripts/{build,check-size}.mjs`, `e2e/*`, `src/__tests__/*`, configs, `README.md`
- `backend/src/routes/slackStartEmbed.ts`, `backend/src/embed/slackStartBundle.generated.ts`, `backend/src/app.ts` (mount `/embed` + CORS bypass), `backend/src/__tests__/slackStart/slackStartEmbed.test.ts`
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml` (new `slack-start-build` job and path filter)

## What was NOT tested
- No run against a real backend or staging. The API was mocked by design, and no live Slack runs are allowed.
- No real Turnstile rendering; the config captcha was null in tests.
- No Safari or Firefox (Chromium only).
- `paths-filter-hygiene`, `dependabot-config` and `pipefail-hygiene` script tests pass locally. The new package is not added to Dependabot's config; this is a follow-up if wanted.

title: ENG-2784: caps on inbound hot-lead callbacks
body:
## ENG-2784: caps on inbound hot-lead callbacks

Until now nothing limited the inbound callback path: anyone who learned an org's number could make the team's phones ring without limit, and the member-leg minutes are billed to the org owner. This adds caps on the existing limit store (new key prefixes only; no table, index or other data-plane change).

### Behaviour
- `POST /api/webhooks/twilio-voice/inbound` takes one slot per call, **after** a member would really be rung (a call nobody can take costs nothing), before the ring TwiML is returned. `/inbound-dial` hand-overs to the next member take no slot.
- Caps: org hourly = 2 x `maxCallsPerHour`, org daily = 2 x `maxCallsPerDay` (own counters, so inbound cannot starve outbound form calls); per caller 3 an hour and 6 a day, keyed by an HMAC of the caller's number (`hot_lead_call.inbound_caller`, per org). A withheld or non-E.164 `From` skips the per-caller counters and is still held by the org caps.
- A capped call hears the existing "nobody is available" message. If the limit store fails, or the request has no usable `CallSid`, the call fails closed with the existing "unable to take your call" message (HTTP 200 TwiML, no retry loop).
- Order: read-only look at the CallSid retry marker, caller counters, org counters, then claim the marker last. A redelivery of an admitted call is admitted and not counted again; two deliveries racing both count and the loser gives its counts back; a refused call never holds the marker, so its redelivery is evaluated afresh; any refusal or throw releases everything taken.
- Log lines for alerting: `[hotLeadCall] inbound capped <reason> <orgId>` and `[hotLeadCall] inbound limits unavailable <ErrorName>`. The raw caller number is never logged or stored.

### Implementation
- `services/voice/inboundLimits.ts` (new): `reserveInboundSlot`, `inboundCallerE164`.
- `hotLeadCallLimits.ts`: the claim/count/undo closures of `reserveCallSlot` moved into a shared `slotTaker` (behaviour identical for the outbound path: same order, TTLs and release order), plus `limitTimeZone`.
- `twilioVoiceWebhook.ts`: `/inbound` passes an `admit` hook to `ringNextOrApologise` (now async).
- Docs and a dev fragment (`dev/pending/eng-2784-inbound-caps.md`, which supersedes the "no cap" sentence in dev.md).

### Accepted limits (documented)
A caller who spoofs another person's caller ID can use that person's per-caller allowance for the hour or day; the caps count calls that would ring someone, not calls answered; new-caller rows are written only after a member would be rung and expire by TTL.

### Tests
33 tests in `hotLeadCall.e2e.inboundCaps.test.ts` (each cap at its boundary, hour/day rollover, release on refusal and on a late store failure, redelivery of admitted/refused calls, the concurrent-delivery race, withheld `From`, missing `CallSid`, marker held by another token, no slot for hand-over or when nobody is available, two orgs sharing a caller, UTC fallback, TTLs, fail-closed copy, no raw number in keys or logs). `npm run typecheck` and eslint on the changed files are clean. Targeted jest: 33 suites / 1849 tests passed, 2 DynamoDB-local suites skipped (not runnable offline).

### Review
Two independent reviews (correctness/regressions/security; quality/tests/docs). Fixed: a same-CallSid concurrent redelivery could bypass a cap (order changed as above); lint errors; unused exports; ten missing test cases; doc gaps. Rejected on purpose: editing `dev.md` (never edited; the fragment is the record) and moving the counter loop into `slotTaker` (scope creep).

### Not verified
Real DynamoDB behaviour of the new write order (only the in-memory fake ran); what Twilio sends in `From` for a withheld caller; a real inbound call against these caps on prod. After merge the plan is one attended call from the robots with the kill switch on.

Part of ENG-2783. No data-plane change.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Medium

Inbound callbacks reserve hourly and daily slots only when a member is about to be rung. Caller caps are 3 per hour and 6 per day; org caps are twice the outbound limits. CallSid markers prevent retry recounting. **Production impact:** limit-store failures or a missing CallSid fail closed, which can interrupt inbound calls.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: ENG-2783: lead-local calling hours; Canada off at launch
body:
## ENG-2783: lead-local calling hours; Canada off at launch

The hot-lead call only checked the ORG's calling hours; the lead's own local time was never considered. This adds a lead-local window and refuses Canadian leads in code until their requirements are built. No persisted field, table, index or key change.

### Behaviour
- **Window: 10:00-18:00 in the lead's local time, every day** (two named constants in `voice/leadLocalHours.ts`; a business decision, stricter than the law's 08:00-21:00).
- **No area-code timezone table (yet).** A US number could be in any contiguous zone and mobile numbers move, so the window must hold in BOTH Eastern and Pacific (Central and Mountain fall between): effectively **13:00-18:00 Eastern**. Hawaii (808) and Alaska (907) get the same rule PLUS their home zone (Hawaii about 16:00-18:00 Eastern in summer, Alaska 14:00-18:00). Non-US, +1 territories, malformed numbers and invalid dates fail closed.
- **Gate:** stateless `outside_lead_hours` in `SKIP_GATES` right after `outside_calling_hours`; runs in the dispatch and the job pass (via `review()`), before any slot, record or placed call. A lead outside the window is skipped (`call.skipped`), the Slack alert still goes out, there is no deferral (the job has `maxAttempts: 1`).
- **/gather re-check:** the member may take a while to answer; right before the lead would be dialled the window is checked again. If closed: `call.failed` reason `lead_outside_hours`, the lead is NOT dialled, the member hears the "could not reach the lead" message.
- **Canada:** `HOT_LEAD_CALL_CA_ENABLED = false` makes `callableLeadPhone` refuse CA leads (`country_not_allowed`) regardless of an org's stored `allowedCountries` (stored config and defaults unchanged; team members' phones unaffected). Re-enabling needs the CRTC identification message (email/postal address + local/toll-free number), a Canada branch in the hours check, and flipping the constant.

### Expected effect (read this)
Most leads now fall outside the window and are skipped, including every lead that arrives in the morning or evening Eastern. This is the intended, conservative behaviour. A proper area-code timezone table would widen it per lead; that is a separate change.

### Tests
New `leadLocalHours.test.ts` (boundaries at the exact minute with real DST offsets, 808/907, fail-closed inputs), gate tests (skip reason, no record, no slot, Slack alert, dispatch and job pass asserted separately, org window narrower than the lead window), an UNMOCKED /gather end-to-end test (window closes between the member answering and pressing 1: no `<Dial>`, member hears the unreachable copy, no further attempt, member-leg usage only), a Canada lead test.
Existing tests changed, each as a consequence of the intended behaviour: CA accepted -> refused; fixed clocks and some org-hour fixtures moved inside the new window; `twilioVoiceWebhook.test.ts` mocks the window check true by default (the unmocked path is covered in the e2e suite). The A-first priority proof in `hotLeadCall.e2e.attempts.test.ts` was kept (A's shift widened) after review.
`npm run typecheck` and eslint on changed files are clean. Targeted jest: 36 suites / 1987 tests passed, 2 DynamoDB-local suites skipped (not runnable offline).

### Review
Two independent reviews. Fixed: Hawaii/Alaska needed the Eastern/Pacific bounds too (mobile numbers move), a lost coverage case, a backwards comment, contradictory Canada wording, docs, plus about ten test additions. Skipped on purpose: refactors to reuse `isWithinCallWindow`, and not ringing the next member once the lead window has closed (the lead is never dialled in that case).

### Not verified
State laws with stricter hours are not modelled; whether Twilio's default voice or bridge behaviour is affected (not touched); a real call on prod (planned in an attended window after merge).

Part of ENG-2783. No data-plane change.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Low — the change affects hot-lead outbound calls, adds no persisted data, and can be reverted without migration.

The change adds a fail-closed lead-local calling-hours gate and rechecks the window before `/gather` dials. It refuses Canadian leads while `HOT_LEAD_CALL_CA_ENABLED` is false. The reviewed changes show no production outage path.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: ENG-2783: monthly cap on hot-lead calls, owner notices, honest settings read-out
body:
## ENG-2783: monthly cap on hot-lead calls per org, owner notices, honest settings read-out

### Approvals (recorded)
- **Data-model change approved by the owner (Anurag):** a new field `maxCallsPerMonth` on `Organization.hotLeadCall` (default 200, 1-2000). Existing configs without it read as 200; no migration.
- New key prefixes in the existing `AW-MCPSessions` limit store (no table/index change): `hlc#cap#m#` (monthly counter) and `hlc#notify#80#` / `hlc#notify#100#` (one notice per org per month).
- The customer notice copy was drafted for and approved by the owner.

### Behaviour

At the cap the lead is skipped (`org_monthly_cap`, `call.skipped` on its timeline), the Slack alert still goes out, earlier slots are given back. Inbound callbacks and next-attempt member rings do not count.

A failed 80% send releases its claim and retries at the next crossing (bounded by the hourly cap); a failed 100% send keeps the claim (no retry storm during a provider outage). title: ENG-2783: lead prompt with callback number, press 3 stop and do-not-call list; exact hours-overlap check

## ENG-2783: lead prompt with the callback number, press 3 to stop calls, org do-not-call list; exact hours-overlap check

### Approvals (recorded)
- **Persistent-state additions approved by the owner (Anurag):** a new key family `hlc#dnc#<keyedDigest(orgId, phone)>` in the existing `AW-MCPSessions` limit store (~10-year TTL, no raw number stored), and a new writer of the existing lead `contactStatus` fields. No table, index or schema change.
- The prompt wording was approved by the owner.

### Behaviour
- **New lead screening prompt (US only; Canada still refused):** "This is an automated call from {business} about the enquiry you sent us. To reach a person at {business}, call {number}. Press 1 to be connected now, or press 3 to stop these calls." The number is the org's own Twilio number, read digit by digit in 3-3-4 groups; calling it rings the team through the inbound callback path. Press 2 ("call me again later") is deliberately not offered yet: it needs the due-retries job that comes in the next PR.
- **Press 3 = stop:** writes an org-level do-not-call marker (retried up to 3 times in-process; an error-level alarm line `[hotLeadCall] do-not-call write failed <orgId>` if it still fails), marks the lead `do-not-contact` (reason opted-out), records outcome `lead_opted_out` (event `call.lead_declined` with reason `opted_out`), plays a goodbye to the lead and tells the member. A replayed 3, or a later 1, changes nothing.
- **New gate `do_not_call`** (dispatch/job pass, after the entitlement check) and a re-check in `/gather` before the lead is dialled (`call.failed` reason `lead_do_not_call`). It blocks on the org marker OR a lead whose `contactStatus` is exactly `do-not-contact`. Email unsubscribes and bounces do NOT block (a person who left a newsletter and then submits a "call me" form is still called). Fails closed if the marker read fails (`limits_unavailable`).
- **`/screen`** aborts safely if the org has no callable number.
- **Exact hours-overlap check (fixes the P1 from the automated QA on #3918):** `callingHoursReachLeadWindow` no longer samples every 15 minutes; it decides overlap exactly at minute resolution (hour-by-hour walk plus minute arithmetic; worst case about 75 ms). A 12:04-12:06 Chicago window is no longer wrongly blocked.

### Compliance note
Rotating `JWT_SECRET` silently empties the do-not-call list (the digest is keyed by it); documented in the Do-not-call section and the rotation runbook. The lead-level contact status survives rotation only for the same lead.

### Tests
Prompt text, escaping, spoken number and edge inputs; press 3 end to end (marker, contact status, outcome, copies, each leg metered once, a new lead with the same number in the same org skipped as `do_not_call`, another org's lead not); marker write retries and total failure; replay and a later 1; the gate and the `/gather` re-check; unsubscribed lead still called; `/screen` abort; fail-closed on a failing marker read (the two existing `limits_unavailable` tests were fixed to fail the reservation, not the new marker read); 13 new overlap tests incl. the 2-minute window, window edges, wrap past midnight, Kolkata/London/Auckland. I also cross-checked the exact overlap function against a brute-force minute-by-minute scan on 120 windows across 5 zones (incl. half-hour offsets) and a DST week: 0 mismatches (scratch test, not committed).
`npm run typecheck` and eslint on changed files clean. Targeted jest: 36 suites / 2152 tests passed, 2 DynamoDB-local suites skipped (not runnable offline).

### Review
Two independent reviews. Fixed: a failed press-3 write was lost (now retried and alarmed), the gate was too broad (narrowed), two existing tests proved the wrong failure, missing end-to-end/branch tests, docs. Rejected: using the org id from the call state (the signed state has no org id; documented).

### Not verified
Whether a key press interrupts the nested text-to-speech, how Twilio's default voice reads the digit groups, and that a goodbye followed by a hangup plays before the leg ends (all listed in the docs); real DynamoDB behaviour of the marker; a real call on prod.

title: ENG-2783: press 2 not-available-now schedules one retry via a due-retries cron
body:
## ENG-2783: press 2 "not available right now" schedules one retry via a due-retries cron

### Approvals (recorded)
- **Persisted-state additions approved by the owner (Anurag):** new schemaless fields on the existing `system.hot_lead_call` sidecar map: `deferral` (`dueAt`, `count`), `retryClaimToken`, `retryClaimedAt`. No new table, index or GSI. The new `hlc#dnc#`/`hlc#cap#m#` key families came with the previous PRs.
- The prompt wording (press 2 option) was approved by the owner.

### Behaviour
- **Prompt:** on the lead's first call, when retries can happen, the lead hears "... Press 1 to be connected now, press 2 if you are not available and we will call you again later, or press 3 to stop these calls." On the retry call, or when retries are off, option 2 is not offered ("Press 1 ... or press 3 ...").
- **Press 2:** lead hears "Okay. {business} will call you again later. Goodbye."; the member hears "The lead is not available right now. We will try again later."; outcome `lead_deferred` (event `call.lead_declined`, reason `not_available_now`). The deferral is written in the same conditional transition as the decision; replays and a later 1 change nothing; a 3 after a 2 stops (do-not-call marker + contact status) and cancels the retry. If retries are off or the kill switch is off, a 2 is an ordinary decline.
- **When:** about 60 minutes later, only when both the lead-local window (10:00-18:00, conservative Eastern/Pacific rule) and the org's calling hours are open; searched for up to 36 hours; none found = plain decline. At most ONE retry per lead ever.
- **Due-retries cron** (`cron/hotLeadCallRetryCron.ts`, `voice/hotLeadCallRetrySweep.ts`): every 5 minutes, armed from `server.ts`; env `HOT_LEAD_CALL_RETRY` (unset = on; off/0/false = disabled); does nothing and reads nothing while the global kill switch is off. Discovery shares code with the stuck sweep; per-list read budget `min(500, max(50, 2000/lists))` with a rotating start list and a warn when lists are skipped; at most 100 due records handled and 20 retries started per run.
- **The retry run** (`processHotLeadCallRetry`): if the lead or org window is closed at run time the retry is RESCHEDULED (not spent); otherwise it claims the retry atomically (conditional write, so two runs/instances cannot both fire it), re-runs every gate except `too_old` and the existing-record short-circuit (measured from the deferral, not the submission), takes a fresh slot against the hourly/daily/monthly caps (the lead's own phone marker is accepted only when held by the same lead; another lead's marker still gives `duplicate_phone`), restarts the finished record (new `jobKey`, so late callbacks of the first call stop matching), and rings the team from the start. More than 6 hours late = `retry_expired`. Every post-claim drop logs `[hotLeadCall] retry dropped after claim <reason> <orgId>`.
- **Stuck sweep:** a waiting deferral is a `finished` record and is never touched; a retry in flight is an ordinary live record.

### Known limits (documented)
- Discovery rescans orgs/lists every 5 minutes and sees only the newest leads per list within the read budget; a sparse index of pending deferrals (a data-plane change) is the real long-term fix and is NOT built.
- A claimed retry that is lost to a crash/deploy right after the claim is not recovered; one retry maximum. (Refusals that are not about the lead are NOT lost: see the update below.)
- Expressions (`whenAbsent`, `has`/`lacks` filters, the restart's SET/REMOVE) are asserted against the generated UpdateItem and the in-memory fake, not run against real DynamoDB; the first real test is the attended window.

### Tests
New `hotLeadCall.e2e.retry.test.ts` (54), `hotLeadCallRetry.test.ts`, `leadCallStore.retryWrites.test.ts` (real generated update expressions), cron unit tests (overlap guard, arming/disarming, env parsing), `reserveCallSlot({retry:true})` unit tests, prompt-variant tests, crm.db additions. Existing decline tests changed from pressing 2 to pressing 4 (2 now defers); the digit table still proves unexpected digits decline. `npm run typecheck` clean; eslint clean on changed files (db.ts/server.ts/crm.db.test.ts carry thousands of pre-existing `no-explicit-any` errors: counts unchanged vs main); targeted jest 2492 passed, 17 skipped, 2 DynamoDB-local suites skipped (not runnable offline).

### Review
Two independent reviews: no blockers. Fixed: option 2 was offered/promised even when a retry could not happen; discovery starved later lists; a retry was spent by cron timing near a window close (now rescheduled); silent post-claim drops; the "too old ignored" test did not prove it; real DynamoDB expressions were only tested through a fake; caps/overlap guard/arming untested; stale docs.

### Not verified
The new DynamoDB expressions against real DynamoDB; a real press-2 call and a real retry on prod (attended window planned); behaviour of Twilio's text-to-speech for the new copy.

Part of ENG-2783. Supersedes two statements in `dev/pending/eng-2783-lead-prompt.md` ("press 2 retry not built", "deferral fields are NOT added").

### Update after the automated QA (valid P1) and CodeRabbit
- **Only PERMANENT refusals spend the retry** (lead missing, org config gone, phone changed, do-not-call, entitlement lost, another lead holds the number, smoke-test/draft/invalid phone, retry expired). Everything else (no team member on duty, member cooldown, hourly/daily/monthly caps, closed windows, limit-store or credential errors, thrown errors) gives the claim back with a token-guarded `releaseRetryClaim` and reschedules (+15 minutes or the next open minute), until `deferral.firstDueAt` + 6 hours, then `retry_expired`. New sidecar field `deferral.firstDueAt` (owner-approved with the others). A lead who heard "we will call you again later" is no longer dropped by a transient problem. Log marker: `[hotLeadCall] retry rescheduled after claim <reason> <orgId>`.
- `retry_expired` is written as its own timeline event (not swallowed by the per-lead skip cap); expiry is checked before any window reschedule.
- The cron also runs once about 30 seconds after arming, not only every 5 minutes.
- The press-2 offer uses the same eligibility check as the press-2 handler (`canDefer` = `deferralDueAt !== null`).
- `Intl.DateTimeFormat` instances are cached per zone in `localParts` (results unchanged across DST days).
- Tests: targeted jest 2518 passed, 17 skipped; transient/permanent table, repeated reschedules stopping at the bound, stale-token release, real generated update for `releaseRetryClaim`.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: High

Adds a one-time press-2 retry for eligible hot-lead calls. A five-minute cron processes due deferrals, rechecks call gates and limits, then claims and restarts the existing call record. Pressing 3 cancels a pending retry. The change affects live call handling and persistent state, so rollback needs care.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
### Second update (automated QA, valid)
The 6-hour limit is measured from the retry's FIRST due time (`deferral.firstDueAt`, written when press 2 creates the deferral; legacy records fall back to `dueAt`), checked before any window reschedule and before the claim. A retry is placed within 6 hours of its first due time or given up with a `retry_expired` timeline note; it is never pushed to another day by a closed window after that first due time. (At press time the first due time itself already moves to the next open window if the window is closed then.)

title: ENG-2783: retry polish: /screen fallback, reschedule from now, give up a stale future-dated deferral
body:
## ENG-2783: retry polish: /screen fallback, reschedule from now, give up a stale future-dated deferral

Follow-up to #3920 (merged with the `opslane:merge-anyway` label). No persisted-field, table, index or key change.

### What changes
- **Real bug fixed:** a press-2 deferral whose `dueAt` is in the future but whose `firstDueAt` is older than 6 hours (an operator-written or older-shape record) was left waiting, because the `not_due` return ran before the give-up check. The give-up check (`now > firstDueAt + 6h`) now runs first: the retry is claimed and given up with a `retry_expired` timeline note, and the cron summary counts it as `expired`. This is most likely the last open finding of the automated QA on #3920 (its other two fixtures already passed).
- **Reschedule from now:** when a due retry finds a window closed at run time, the search for the next open minute starts at `now` (no second 60-minute delay), so an opening shortly after a late cron tick is not skipped (CodeRabbit's example: a 15:40-16:00 opening before a 16:00 give-up). The 60-minute delay stays for the initial deferral at press time; the transient-refusal release keeps its +15-minute floor.
- **`/screen` fallback:** if the retry-eligibility read throws, the lead still hears the two-option prompt (option 2 omitted) instead of a hang-up; one warning, error name only.

### Tests
New `hotLeadCall.e2e.retryExpiry.test.ts` drives the REAL cron entry (`runHotLeadCallRetryCron`) over the real store: the QA's three fixtures plus two controls (a window-closed record inside its 6 hours is still rescheduled; a future-dated record inside its 6 hours is still not due). Plus unit tests for the delay parameter (CodeRabbit's 15:30 example, both DST days, press-time schedule unchanged) and the `/screen` fallback. `npm run typecheck` and eslint on changed files clean; targeted jest 2519 passed, 17 skipped, 2 DynamoDB-local suites skipped.

### Not verified
Real DynamoDB behaviour (fake store only); a real retry on prod (attended window).

Part of ENG-2783.

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Medium — changes affect production retry scheduling and the `/screen` call flow, but remain limited to retry handling and can be reverted.

Retries now expire based on `firstDueAt` before the not-due check, falling back to `dueAt` if needed. When a due retry’s calling window is closed, rescheduling searches from now. If `/screen` eligibility reads fail, the lead hears the prompt without option 2, and the handler logs a warning.

A second test pins stopping when a completion-gate follow-up itself exhausts its steps. This is authorized by ENG-2854's no-auto-retry acceptance criterion.

title: fix(agent-mode): batch-lookups nudge for serial reads; LinkedIn reads not writes (ENG-2863)
body:
Fixes ENG-2863 (scheduled "Daily ICP Lead Finder — Every.io" stopped at the 40-step cap).

Root cause (AC1, from prod session 5bfb9d06 in AW-ChatMessages): 39 steps, each carrying exactly ONE read-only tool call — 7x get_leads (incl. 3 cursor pages for dedup the prompt says is unnecessary), 5x get_lead_details one lead at a time, then 26x linkedin_outreach (search-parameters/search-people, then get-profile + get-company per candidate, serially). Every call was unique, so the exact-signature guards and the ENG-2778 paging detector never fired. The dispatcher already executes multiple tool calls from one response in one step; the model never batched. The run reached profile verification but never got to email enrichment / CRM add.

Second defect: the ENG-2854 iteration-limit report listed "Completed tool write: linkedin_outreach — 26 calls" although every call was a read (name-only write classification), telling the operator writes "must not be repeated blindly".

What changed
- `core/serialReadSpiral.ts` (new): after 6 consecutive single-read steps, one system nudge per turn: batch independent lookups into one response, skip unneeded paging, keep budget for writes/report. Nudge only; never blocks a call. Wired next to the paging-spiral check in `agentModeService.ts`.
- `utils/toolWriteClassification.ts`: `linkedin_outreach` with a discovery action (search-people, get-profile, get-company, search-parameters, list-connections, list-sent/received-invitations, list-post-engagers) is a read. Unknown/missing/unparseable action stays a write (fail-safe); `_`→`-` folding matches dispatch.

Cap change (AC3): not proposed — 40 steps is enough for this job if lookups are batched (5 profiles + 5 companies = 2 steps instead of 10).

Tests: new `serialReadSpiral.test.ts` replays the session's step shape (fires once at step 6; batched/write steps don't count; streak resets) + classification/report cases. 49 related suites / 1920 tests pass (every suite referencing isWriteToolCall/buildIterationLimitReport/linkedin_outreach + loopDetection). Scoped tsc: no errors in touched files (full tsc OOM-prone on swarm box).

Risk: Low. Classification change makes LinkedIn reads count as reads everywhere isWriteToolCall is used (skip-veto, iteration report) — correct direction; sends/accept/cancel/cap remain writes (negative tests).
Rollback: revert the commit.
Complexity ledger: +1 module (~55 LOC), +18 LOC classifier, +9 LOC wiring.

Not tested: live LLM response to the nudge.
No data-plane changes; no customer messaging.

## Opslane finding 3 (founders replace wording) — intended, already shipped
The update_brand_guidelines declaration the model receives is built from backend/src/emma/tools.ts: brandData description (line ~1997) says "founders, if sent, is the complete founder list — omitted founders are removed", and brandData.founders (line ~2035) says "This list replaces the stored founders ... founders left out are removed." Gemini's sanitizeGeminiSchema keeps `description` on every nested property, and the wording is pinned on the exported declaration by backend/src/__tests__/emmaTools.brandMarketStrategy.test.ts (commit 53971f2ed). Opslane's own note says the phrase was missing before AND after the PR, so its probe is reading a surface other than the declaration; no code change.
