title: feat: Zoma waitlist + 60-user free-plan cap (ENG-2881)
body:
## ENG-2881

**DATA-PLANE GATE — needs Harsha pre-merge approval (new counter item/persistence). Do not merge.**

**Dark until enabled:** `ZOMA_WAITLIST_ENABLED=true`; `ZOMA_FREE_USER_CAP` defaults to 60. Applies to new password and Google OAuth registrations across this backend deployment; enable only on the intended Zoma deployment. Existing accounts are grandfathered and never disabled.

### Implementation
- Atomic DynamoDB transaction increments a conditional capacity counter and persists a per-email approval together; duplicate/retry requests cannot consume twice. Missing counter fails closed instead of assuming zero existing users.
- Overflow is a durable waitlist decision; no account or JWT is created. Retrying a waitlisted/rejected email does not auto-activate it.
- Existing authenticated admin pattern protects count and approve/reject endpoints: `GET /api/waitlist/zoma/capacity`, `POST /api/waitlist/zoma/:email/decision` with `{decision:"approve"|"reject"}`. Approvals/rejections store authenticated actor and timestamp; manual approval respects capacity; rejection cannot disable approved users.
- Approval reservations survive failed account creation, deliberately counting approved seats rather than only completed accounts. Legacy deletion cannot erase admission idempotency records.
- No approval notification email or UI changes; approved applicants retry signup.

### Enablement prerequisite
Pause signups; audit existing approved free users and initialize `AW-Waitlist` (Dev- prefix in development) item `email=__zoma_free_capacity__` with audited integer `approvedCount`; enable consistently on all instances before reopening. No automatic bootstrap/backfill or AWS writes performed. Never reset an existing counter. Re-audit accounts created while dark before re-enabling. The fragment documents semantics and operational checks.

### How to test / actual results
From `backend/`:
```
npx jest --runInBand --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/eng2881.zomaAdmission.test.ts src/__tests__/auth.registrationPersistence.test.ts src/__tests__/waitlistRoutes.auth.test.ts --silent
```
**34 passed, 0 failed; 3 suites passed.** Covers under-capacity access, 60th/61st boundary, concurrent distinct and duplicate signups, retries, sticky waitlist, approval audit, manual approve/reject/count, admin authorization, waitlisted HTTP contract, OAuth bypass prevention, and existing-account grandfathering. `git diff --check` passed. Local CodeRabbit completed; missing admin error logs fixed.

### What was not tested / blockers
- Full no-emit TypeScript check did not execute: root `npx tsc` resolved the wrong package; invoking the actual installed backend compiler was blocked by the runtime lifecycle guard because TypeScript exceeds its 1 MiB scanner limit. No successful full compile claimed; exact-head CI backend build is still required.
- No live DynamoDB/IAM/bootstrap or live transaction race; mocks only. No staging/prod deployment, browser/UI, email delivery or full-repo suite. Jest reports forced teardown of an existing open timer. No servers/browsers or real database writes.
- Standard pre-push hook skipped via documented `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` to avoid violating scoped-test/low-RAM execution limits. Scoped tests were executed explicitly.
- CodeRabbit's email-ownership-before-reservation suggestion is deferred: password signup currently provides immediate access with no verification prerequisite. Existing auth rate limit (10 attempts/15 minutes/IP) remains, but multi-address seat exhaustion is a known pre-enable security/product decision; email verification is not implemented here. Do not enable without addressing or explicitly accepting this risk. Reservations have no unauthenticated release path.

### Rollback
Set `ZOMA_WAITLIST_ENABLED=false` on every instance (reopens unrestricted signup), or revert these commits. Preserve counter and approval records; never delete/reset to roll back. Re-audit before re-enable. Post-deploy verify dark config first; after approved enablement verify admin count, with boundary smoke using isolated staging fixtures only.

title: feat: Zoma activation events + progress report (ENG-2880)
body:
## Reviewer-first summary

Adds one typed activation emitter and a read-only admin JSON/CSV progress report. All 12 requested stages have real Meta-toolkit/account lifecycle call sites. First accepted user/stage observations are conditionally persisted across workers; failures never overwrite the first timestamp. Signup, login, setup and PAUSED ad creation **never** count as activation: only provider-confirmed `ad_published` with `effective_status=ACTIVE` does.

**Dark:** event collection is disabled unless `ZOMA_ACTIVATION_EVENTS_ENABLED=true`. No deployment/config change is included. The admin-only report is available read-only; accounts without observations are explicitly unknown.

### DATA-PLANE GATE — Harsha approval required before merge

New optional `zomaActivationEvents` map on existing AW-Users items (bounded to the 12 stage names, userId/timestamp and categorical launch error). No new table, index, key, access policy, migration or backfill. The existing tracker/session sink is last-write-wins and cannot preserve first occurrence; append-only MCP usage events lack this first-stage read model. Reusing AW-Users avoids a new table/key design but **is still a persisted-model change**. Do not merge without Harsha approval, even though writes are dark.

### Where to review

- `services/zomaActivationEvents.ts`: enum, safe emitter, UTC later-day rule, write-result observation, semantic progress/stuck logic, CSV formula/quote handling.
- `services/db.ts`: owner-bound conditional first-write updates and bounded 250-evaluated-item projection scan; signup emission only after successful account persistence.
- Lifecycle wiring: password/Google auth, external toolkit auth, Zoma readiness, Meta account connection, waitlist completion/invitation/resend/status routes.
- `GET /api/admin/zoma/activation-progress?format=json|csv&stuckAfterHours=24[&cursor=...][&userId=...]`: existing authentication/admin/delegation restrictions; no-store; safe projection. JSON `scope: page`, `hasMore`, `nextCursor`; CSV `X-Report-Scope`/`X-Next-Cursor`. Follow every cursor for a whole-account report. `stuckByStage` is explicitly page-scoped, never a misleading fleet total.
- `dev/pending/eng-2880-zoma-activation-events.md`: event definitions, coverage limits, test evidence, rollback/post-deploy smoke. `dev.md` untouched.

### Unwired stages / limitations

- **No entirely unwired stage on the Meta toolkit path.** Google ad-write creation/submission/publication is not instrumented: its resource/status model differs, and ENABLED is not evidence of delivery. Google authentication/readiness/connected-account observations are covered.
- Meta asynchronous review transitions are not polled: an ad PENDING_REVIEW at activation does not count as published just because configured status is ACTIVE. Later publication is only observed on a later confirmed ACTIVE write; there is no new delivery webhook/poller in this PR.
- Internal Emma/other ad paths are not labeled Zoma. Signup/login are shared account lifecycle events; Zoma engagement starts at onboarding_started. Existing uninstrumented accounts are unknown, not backfilled/inferred.
- Sink outages/process termination may leave gaps (best effort, no outbox). Atomic idempotency guarantees first accepted persistence, not exactly-once delivery.

## How tested

**125 tests passed / 11 selected suites; 84 new ENG-2880 tests**, mock-only. Covers emitter, dark mode, first-write conditions, no phantom users, lifecycle/write/onboarding/waitlist wiring, authorization/delegation, pagination, CSV, semantic ordering, stuck grouping, and signup-never-activated.


Scoped strict tsc passed. Local CodeRabbit completed: three minor findings addressed and retested (nonblocking toolkit login signal, duplicate-write fast path, sanitized report failure log). `git diff --check` passed. Selected suites print existing mocked-service negative-path logs and imported-timer forced-worker-exit warning; all assertions pass.

## Not tested

No full-repo typecheck/production build on this low-RAM host (explicit task restriction). Pre-push full-build hook intentionally bypassed with its documented `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`; exact-head GitHub build remains required before merge. No servers, browsers, real AWS/DB writes, production deployment, live OAuth/provider delivery, real DynamoDB concurrency, or historical backfill. PR remains **draft**; do not merge.

## Rollback / post-deploy verification

Disable/unset `ZOMA_ACTIVATION_EVENTS_ENABLED` to stop collection without data mutation, or revert these commits. Existing optional attributes remain inert; no deletes or cleanup job. Report remains authenticated/admin-only and read-only.

Do not create live/paid ads as an unapproved smoke.

title: feat(zoma): multi-variant creatives, carousel/placement, bulk, video from URL (ENG-2915)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Zoma's external creative path could only build one-image / one-video creatives. Agents couldn't send several headlines/bodies/media in one Advantage+ creative, carousel/placement creatives weren't wired through the toolkit's URL guard, a batch meant N separate calls, and a public video URL was handed to Meta unchecked (a TikTok/Instagram post page, an over-1 GB file, or a redirect into a private network got through).

## What this fixes (after)
- **Multi-variant CREATE**: `headlines[]` / `bodies[]` / `descriptions[]` (up to 5 each, 255/2200/255 chars) plus `image_hashes[]` / `video_ids[]` (up to 10 each), `call_to_action_type`, `link_url` → one `asset_feed_spec` creative (`DEGREES_OF_FREEDOM`; `AUTOMATIC_FORMAT` when images and videos are mixed). Counts, lengths, duplicates, singular+plural mixes, image_url/carousel mixing and CTA format are all refused with a clear error before anything reaches Meta. Video thumbnails come from Meta's processed thumbnail unless `video_thumbnails` is given.
- **carousel_cards / placement_assets** work with no top-level image. Card and asset `image_url`s go through the SSRF guard, card videos must be processed, and every card needs a `link_url` (its own or the top-level one).
- **Video from any public HTTPS URL**: same upload path and 1 GB limit, same processing poll. New `ssrfGuard.probePublicMediaUrl` checks the URL with a headers-only GET, re-resolving and pinning every redirect hop and allowing https only. It refuses a private redirect target, an HTML page, the wrong content type, an oversize or empty file, or a non-2xx answer. Meta then gets the validated final URL. Images get the same probe.
- **BULK_CREATE**: up to 10 creatives per call. `params.items` holds the per-item media and overrides; the other params are shared. `video_url` items are uploaded first and awaited on one shared deadline. Every item comes back in `results[]` with its own verdict, so a partial success is shown as partial.
- **Invariants kept**: creatives still need no preview token (they can't spend). Ads are still created only through the guarded `AD CREATE` (PAUSED). Readiness and `ads_management` are checked once per call. The ENG-2865 aw_ key scopes apply (BULK_CREATE is a write). The gateway now meters one write event per bulk item that reached Meta. Read-back returns `CONFIRMED`, `UNCONFIRMED`, or a new `MISMATCH` when Meta stored fewer variants or cards than were sent.

## Complexity ledger
- +991 / −27 lines (≈ +430 production, ≈ +430 tests, rest docs/manifest).
- Moving parts: one new toolkit action (`BULK_CREATE`), one probe helper next to the existing `fetchBufferFollowingRedirects` (it reuses `resolvePinnedPublicAddress`, so there's no second SSRF implementation), and a multi-variant branch in `MetaService.createAdCreative` / `validateCreativeParams` that mirrors the existing `placement_assets` asset_feed_spec path. No new tables, flags, or dependencies.
- CREATE was refactored into `createCreative()` so CREATE and BULK_CREATE share one gate → dispatch → read-back path.
- Behavior: a single-video CREATE with no thumbnail used to fail validation. It now uses Meta's processed thumbnail. Emma's own tool schema is unchanged.

## How to test
1. With a Zoma token, `call_meta_marketing_api` `AD_CREATIVE CREATE` with `{name, page_id, link_url, headlines:["A","B"], bodies:["x"], image_hashes:[<hash>]}` → **Expected**: `verification: CONFIRMED`, and `AD_CREATIVE GET` shows `asset_feed_spec.titles` with 2 entries.
2. `headlines` with 6 entries → **Expected**: refusal "maximum is 5", nothing created.
3. `UPLOAD_VIDEO` with a TikTok post-page URL → **Expected**: "That URL is a web page, not a video file…". With a direct `.mp4` CDN URL → `video_id` + thumbnail.
4. `BULK_CREATE` with 3 items, one using a Page you lack → **Expected**: `status: PARTIAL`, two CONFIRMED results with `creative_id`, one FAILED item naming META_PAGE_ACCESS_MISSING; `zoma_usage` shows 2 writes.
5. `AD CREATE` with one of the creative_ids → normal preview/approval; ad created PAUSED.

## Edge cases to check
- Meta's acceptance of `AUTOMATIC_FORMAT` + `DEGREES_OF_FREEDOM` for mixed image+video on non-dynamic ad sets (built from Meta's asset_feed_spec docs; **not exercised against live Meta**).
- Instagram placements on a multi-variant creative may need `instagram_user_id` (passed through when supplied; not auto-resolved like `placement_assets`).
- CDNs that reject a header-only GET will now be refused up front ("answered HTTP 4xx") instead of failing later inside Meta.

## Test Evidence
Scoped run on Atem (per instructions; no full suite / full typecheck):
```
npx jest src/__tests__/eng2915 src/__tests__/zomaCreativeUpload src/__tests__/eng2303.metaToolkitWrites src/__tests__/eng2865
Test Suites: 5 passed, 5 total
Tests:       107 passed, 107 total
```
Scoped `tsc --noEmit` (temp tsconfig extending the repo's tsconfig, covering the 6 touched source files + 3 test files and their transitive imports): clean.

## Behavioral assertions verified
No human-written acceptance contract was attached in this session (Linear was unreachable from here). The task brief's requirements map to these tests:
- Multi-variant counts/lengths/clear errors → `eng2915.zomaCreatives` "refuses %s…" (12 cases), `eng2915.multiVariantSpec` builder/validator
- Carousel/placement without top-level media → "carousel_cards and placement_assets need no top-level media"
- Video from public URL + 1 GB + SSRF → "video ingest from a public URL", `probePublicMediaUrl` redirect tests
- Bulk ≤10 with per-item/partial results → "BULK_CREATE"
- Scopes + metering → "gateway: surface, scopes, metering"
- CONFIRMED/MISMATCH/UNCONFIRMED → MISMATCH tests + existing UNCONFIRMED test

## Files changed
- `backend/src/mcp/metaToolkitCreatives.ts`, `metaToolkitGateway.ts`, `metaToolkitManifest.ts`, `zomaToolDefinitions.ts`
- `backend/src/services/metaService.ts`, `backend/src/utils/ssrfGuard.ts`
- `backend/docs/meta-toolkit-skill.md`
- tests: `eng2915.zomaCreatives.test.ts`, `eng2915.multiVariantSpec.test.ts`, `zomaCreativeUpload.test.ts` (adds the new `probeUrl` dep to its helper)

## What was NOT tested
- Nothing ran against live Meta or a real UGC CDN. Everything here is mocked.
- Full backend suite and full typecheck (out of scope per instructions).
- DNS rebinding between the image probe and `uploadMetaAdsImage`'s own unpinned `axios.get`. The probe pins every hop it makes, but the later image download re-resolves DNS. That was already true before this PR; the probe narrows the window but doesn't close it.

title: feat(zoma): custom audiences, lookalikes, hashed customer lists, exclude existing customers (ENG-2914)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Zoma (the external MCP toolkit) had no custom audiences. Agents could not build a customer list, a website, engagement or lookalike audience, or keep prospecting ads away from existing customers. The manifest said "custom audiences are not available".

## What this fixes (after)
Adds a new toolkit tool, `zoma_custom_audiences`:
- **Reads:** `LIST`, `GET` and `LIST_AD_SETS` (ad sets that include or exclude a given audience, with active state). Each one checks that the audience or ad set belongs to the resolved ad account.
- **CREATE** uses a pluggable `AudienceSource` registry (`metaToolkitAudienceSources.ts`) with these sources:
  - `customer_list`
  - `website` (pixel rule, up to 180 days, URL or event filter)
  - `engagement` (Facebook Page or Instagram business account, up to 365 days)
  - `lookalike` (source audience must be owned, 2-letter country, `ratio_percent` 1–10)
  - `external_provider` (for Tero AI later): registered, but refused with "not available yet"
- **UPDATE** changes name, description or rule. `rule` is allowed only on rule-based audiences.
- **ADD_USERS / REMOVE_USERS** take raw emails and phones. They are normalized and SHA-256 hashed on the server, already-hashed values pass through, duplicates and invalid entries are counted, and uploads go in batches of 10k (Meta's per-request cap), up to 100k per call. Raw PII never goes to Meta and is never returned, logged or persisted. Results carry counts only.
- **DELETE** is refused while an active ad set uses the audience, unless `confirm_in_use=true`. If the account has too many ad sets to check them all, `confirm_in_use=true` is also required.
- **EXCLUDE_CUSTOMERS** works in one call. It creates a customer list, or reuses one with the same name, or uses a given `audience_id`. Then it adds the audience to `excluded_custom_audiences` on 1–50 ad sets through the **shared AD_SET UPDATE path** (`previewToolkitMetaWrite` → `dispatchToolkitConfirmedMetaWrite`). The preview shows each ad set's `excluded_custom_audiences` before and after. It refuses an ad set that already targets the audience.
- **Custom Audience Terms not accepted** (subcode 1870090, or terms wording) returns `status: TERMS_NOT_ACCEPTED` with `terms_url = https://business.facebook.com/ads/manage/customaudiences/tos/?act=<id>`.

Invariants kept:
- Every write goes through the `zomaWriteGuard` preview → `confirm` + single-use `preview_token`. The token fingerprint covers the Meta state the preview showed, so a changed ad-set targeting gives `PREVIEW_MISMATCH`.
- Every write needs the same write gate: `assertZomaWriteReady` plus a granted `ads_management` scope.
- aw_ key scopes (ENG-2865): reads need `tools:read`; writes and unknown actions need `tools:execute`.
- Executed writes are metered as `recordMcpWriteExecuted` with `entityType: CUSTOM_AUDIENCE`.
- Every write reports CONFIRMED, MISMATCH or UNCONFIRMED from a read-back.
- Nothing here creates or activates an ad. Creatives and ads are unchanged: ads are still created PAUSED through `AD CREATE`.

New seam: `agentModeService.toolkitMetaGraphRequest`, one Graph call with the caller's credentials. It rethrows errors carrying only Meta's error fields, never the axios config (which holds the access token).

## Complexity ledger
- Lines: +1540 / −18 across 10 files. 459 of the added lines are tests and 17 are docs. Production code: two new modules (`metaToolkitAudiences.ts` 701 lines, `metaToolkitAudienceSources.ts` 246 lines), 31 lines in agentModeService, and small edits to the gateway and tool definitions.
- Moving parts: one new toolkit tool and one narrow AMS Graph seam. No new table, flag or dependency. It reuses the existing preview guard, write gate, scope helper, metering, shared AD_SET UPDATE gate and dispatch, and the existing `manageMetaCustomAudiences` UPLOAD_USERS/DELETE_USERS batch paths.
- Behavior: Emma / AgentMode chat behavior is unchanged. The `call_meta_marketing_api` external action enum is unchanged, so CUSTOM_AUDIENCE writes through it are still refused (eng2282 still green).

## Database / data-plane classification
Not a database change. Nothing new is persisted. The change writes Meta audience state and ad-set targeting through the existing guarded Meta write path.

## How to test
1. Zoma MCP with a test ad account: `zoma_custom_audiences {action: "LIST"}` → audiences.
2. `{action:"CREATE", source:{type:"lookalike", origin_audience_id:"<id>", country:"US", ratio_percent:1}, params:{name:"LAL 1%"}}` → **Expected:** PREVIEW and token. Repeat with `confirm:true` and the token → `verification: CONFIRMED`.

title: feat(zoma): archive/delete/copy + Google keywords, RSA, PMax assets (ENG-2922)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

**Scope note:** this PR covers **Part A (Meta) only**. Part B (Google: keyword/negative-keyword writes, RSA create, PMax asset upload + asset group, and the PMax brand_business_name/logo gap) was not built. It is several times the size of Part A and needs its own PR. It still needs a Linear follow-up issue (it could not be filed from this session because Linear is not authorized here).

## What was wrong (before)
External Zoma agents could create, pause, activate and re-budget Meta campaigns, ad sets and ads. They could not archive, delete or duplicate them, so those steps still had to be done in Ads Manager. DELETE was explicitly refused.

## What this fixes (after)
`call_meta_marketing_api` now accepts `ARCHIVE`, `DELETE` and `COPY` for `CAMPAIGN` / `AD_SET` / `AD`. They use the same preview → confirm guard as the other toolkit writes (single-use HMAC `preview_token` bound to the user, the exact args and the Meta state shown in the preview).
- **ARCHIVE / DELETE** are refused when the entity spent in the last 24h, or when its spend can't be read. `confirm_recent_spend=true` overrides this, and that flag is part of the token fingerprint.
- **COPY** calls Meta `/{id}/copies` with `status_option=PAUSED`. `deep_copy` is optional for campaigns and ad sets. You can pass a destination `campaign_id` (ad set copy) or `adset_id` (ad copy); the destination must be in the same ad account. The new copy is read back and must be `PAUSED`.
- **Read-back verdicts:** CONFIRMED / MISMATCH / UNCONFIRMED. A DELETE counts as CONFIRMED when the node reads back `DELETED` or is gone. If a write throws, the read-back decides the result. When Meta answered with an error and the read-back shows nothing changed, the result is `FAILED`, which is not metered.
- Same write gate as before: payment method + usable Meta connection + granted `ads_management`. aw_ keys need `tools:execute` (ENG-2865). Executed writes are metered through `recordMcpWriteExecuted`.

## Complexity ledger
- +701 / −15 lines in total. Code: about 330 lines across two new modules (`mcp/metaToolkitLifecycle.ts` for the guard, `services/agentMode/metaToolkitLifecycleGraph.ts` for Graph I/O) plus about 40 lines of wiring. Tests: about 290 lines. Docs: 9 lines.
- Monolith: +6 lines (`getToolkitMetaGraphCredentials` accessor only). All logic lives outside `agentModeService`.
- Moving parts: one new action family routed through the existing gateway, guard (`zomaWriteGuard`), metering and scope check. No new persistence, flag or dependency. ARCHIVE/DELETE use the existing `metaService` writers, which re-verify ownership inside the write (ENG-1724).
- Behavior: AgentMode chat is unchanged. The external toolkit surface grows by these three actions.

## How to test
1. With a Zoma token, call `call_meta_marketing_api` `{entity_type: CAMPAIGN, action: ARCHIVE, campaign_id: <paused test campaign>}`. **Expected:** a `PREVIEW` with spend for the last 24 hours and a `preview_token`. Nothing has changed in Ads Manager.
2. Repeat with `confirm: true` + the token. **Expected:** `verification: CONFIRMED`, `status: ARCHIVED`.
3. ARCHIVE an ACTIVE campaign that is spending. **Expected:** refused with the spend amount. With `confirm_recent_spend: true` you get a preview that says so.
4. COPY a campaign with `params.deep_copy: true`, then confirm. **Expected:** a new `id` plus `child_ids`, `status: PAUSED`, and the copy shows as paused in Ads Manager.
5. Use an aw_ key with only `tools:read`. **Expected:** 403 on all three actions.

## Edge cases to check
- Deep copies larger than Meta's synchronous limit: Meta refuses them, and we report `FAILED` with Meta's message. Async batch copies are not supported.
- Spend window is yesterday+today in UTC dates (≥24h, may include up to ~48h) — deliberately conservative.

## Test Evidence
- Scoped only, per instructions: `npx jest src/__tests__/eng2922 src/__tests__/eng2303.metaToolkitWrites src/__tests__/eng2865 src/__tests__/eng2823.googleToolkit src/__tests__/eng2282` → **7 suites, 153 passed, 0 failed**
- Also ran: `eng2283.metaToolkitGateway`, `eng2295.metaToolkitMcp`, `zomaCreativeUpload` → 60 passed
- Scoped `tsc --noEmit` over all touched files (which also pulls in `agentModeService` and the gateway through their imports): clean (exit 0). Full typecheck and full suite were not run (memory limit on this machine).

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Contract (from the task) | Test |
|---|---|
| ARCHIVE/DELETE/COPY behind preview+token | `%s preview sends nothing; confirm without a token is refused`, `single use and bound to the user` |
| Refuse with 24h spend unless confirm_recent_spend | `%s is refused when the entity spent…`, `unknown recent spend fails closed`, `token minted without confirm_recent_spend…`, `spend appearing between preview and confirm…` |
| COPY via /copies, deep_copy, status_option=PAUSED, read back PAUSED | `COPY is created PAUSED with deep_copy…`, `copyMetaNode posts /copies…`, `COPY whose copy reads back ACTIVE is MISMATCH…` |
| aw_ key scopes enforced | `a read-only aw_ key is denied 403…` |
| Metering recorded | `an executed lifecycle write is metered…; a preview is not` |
| CONFIRMED/MISMATCH/UNCONFIRMED | ARCHIVE/DELETE/COPY verification tests + FAILED cases |

`eng2282.metaToolkitManifest`: one assertion changed. DELETE is no longer in the excluded-actions list, because ENG-2922 lifts that exclusion. The remaining exclusions (UPLOAD_USERS, COPY_AD, RETAG_UTM) are still asserted, and `executeMetaToolkitCall` still refuses DELETE: it now routes to the guarded path in the gateway, never to the shared registry.

## Files changed
- `backend/src/mcp/metaToolkitLifecycle.ts` (new): the guard
- `backend/src/services/agentMode/metaToolkitLifecycleGraph.ts` (new): Graph read / spend / copy
- `backend/src/mcp/metaToolkitGateway.ts`, `metaToolkitManifest.ts`, `metaToolkitWriteSurface.ts`, `metaToolkitWrites.ts` (header comment)
- `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`: credentials accessor
- `backend/docs/meta-toolkit-skill.md`
- tests: `eng2922.metaToolkitLifecycle.test.ts` (new), `eng2282.metaToolkitManifest.test.ts`

## What was NOT tested
- No live Meta calls. The `/copies` response shape, insights `time_range`, and DELETE read-back behavior (`DELETED` status vs. code 100) come from Meta docs and are mocked.
- Full backend suite and full typecheck.
- Google Part B: not implemented.

title: feat(zoma): Google keywords, negatives, RSA, PMax assets + asset groups (ENG-2928)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
The Zoma external MCP Google Ads toolkit could only create budgets, campaigns and ad groups. It had no keyword, negative keyword, ad, asset or asset-group writes. It also never forwarded `brand_business_name` / `brand_logo_asset_resource_name`, so a Performance Max campaign created through Zoma could not serve. And Google Ads had no way to enable a PMax asset group, which is always created PAUSED, so a PMax launch could not finish through the API.

## What this fixes (after)
External agents can now run a Search build (keywords, negatives, a responsive search ad) and a Performance Max launch end to end through `call_google_ads_api`:
1. ASSET UPLOAD the logo and images
2. BUDGET CREATE
3. PMax CAMPAIGN CREATE with the brand
4. ASSET_GROUP CREATE
5. ASSET_GROUP UPDATE and CAMPAIGN UPDATE to ENABLED

Every write goes through the existing guards.

| Op | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| KEYWORD ADD | preview + token | created PAUSED; read-back from the ad group's keyword list (Google returns no ids); duplicates refused at preview |
| KEYWORD UPDATE status | preview + token | ENABLED is ceiling-checked via ad group → campaign → budget; negatives refused (they have no status) |
| KEYWORD REMOVE | preview + token | CONFIRMED only if read-back shows REMOVED or the keyword is gone; a failed read is UNCONFIRMED |
| KEYWORD ADD_NEGATIVE | preview + token | exactly one of ad group / campaign level; read back from that level's negatives |
| AD CREATE (RSA only) | preview + token | 3–15 headlines ≤30 chars, 2–4 descriptions ≤90 (counted in code points), https final_url, no duplicates; PAUSED; the Emma creative-addition gate stays in the path |
| AD UPDATE status | preview + token | ceiling-checked when enabling |
| ASSET_GROUP CREATE | preview + token | PMax campaigns only; the campaign must have a linked business name and a logo (campaign or asset-group level); 3–15 headlines, 1–5 long headlines, 2–5 descriptions (at least one ≤60), ≥1 square and ≥1 landscape image; PAUSED |
| ASSET_GROUP UPDATE status | preview + token | **new Emma/service path** (`googleAdsService.updateAssetGroup` + `getAssetGroup`); enabling runs `guardCreativeAddition` |
| CAMPAIGN CREATE PERFORMANCE_MAX | preview + token | now requires `brand_business_name` (≤25) + `brand_logo_asset_resource_name` (the logo must read back as an IMAGE asset); the brand is checked on read-back, and a missing brand is MISMATCH |
| ASSET UPLOAD (IMAGE/LOGO/TEXT/VIDEO) | **direct, no token** | cannot spend by itself, same as Meta creatives. Still checked: write gate (payment + connection), aw_ write scope, the Meta creative URL rule (caller's own staged file or a public https address), read-back, metering |

Unchanged invariants: preview tokens are bound to user, args and state, and are single-use. Creates are always PAUSED. A dispatch that fails without a definite answer is UNCONFIRMED and metered. ENG-592 "accepted but unchanged" is MISMATCH. aw_ key scopes: `isGoogleToolkitWrite` (guarded or direct) drives `assertMetaToolkitScope` (ENG-2865) and write metering. `zoma_prepare_upload` now also accepts Google-only accounts while the Google flag is on, so staged images can feed ASSET UPLOAD.

## Complexity ledger
- Lines: +642 / −69 across 11 source/doc files, plus 2 new test files. Most of it is `googleToolkitWrites.ts` (one new branch per operation, shared helpers for text/asset/URL/keyword validation and keyword-list read-back).
- Moving parts: no new tables, flags, dependencies or persistence. One new Emma action (ASSET_GROUP UPDATE) and one new asset type (TEXT) on the existing handler. The enable-ceiling logic is generalized from campaign/ad group to all status-only updates, not duplicated. The URL resolver is reused from `metaToolkitCreatives`, not copied.
- Behavior: Emma chat is unchanged except for the added ASSET_GROUP UPDATE / TEXT capability, which is advertised in Emma's schema. Still behind `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED`.

## How to test
1. With `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED=true`, use an aw_ key that has `tools:execute`. Call `call_google_ads_api` `KEYWORD ADD` without `confirm`.
   **Expected**: PREVIEW + `preview_token`, no mutate. Repeat with `confirm: true` + the token. **Expected**: `verification: CONFIRMED` and `ids`.
2. `ASSET UPLOAD asset_type: LOGO, name, data: <https png>`. **Expected**: CONFIRMED with an asset resource name and no preview.
3. PMax: `CAMPAIGN CREATE type PERFORMANCE_MAX` with the brand → `ASSET_GROUP CREATE` → `ASSET_GROUP UPDATE status ENABLED`. **Expected**: each is CONFIRMED, and the asset group and campaign stay PAUSED until their own enable.
4. With a read-only key: any of the writes above. **Expected**: 403 `tools:execute`.

## Edge cases to check
- Live GAQL: `campaign_asset … asset.text_asset.text` and `campaign_criterion … negative = TRUE` queries against a real account. Only exercised through an HTTP-level fake.
- A brand-guidelines-disabled legacy PMax campaign (business name only at asset-group level) will be refused by ASSET_GROUP CREATE with a clear message. This is deliberate: the toolkit only creates brand-guidelines campaigns.

## Test Evidence
Ran on Atem, scoped as instructed. The full suite and full typecheck were not run.
- `npx jest src/__tests__/eng2928 src/__tests__/eng2303.metaToolkitWrites src/__tests__/eng2865 src/__tests__/eng2823.googleToolkit src/__tests__/eng2905 src/__tests__/zomaCreativeUpload`: **9 suites, 195 passed, 0 failed**
  - `eng2928.googleToolkitWrites.test.ts` (49): executor per op (preview, confirm, PAUSED, read-back verdicts, shape refusals before readiness, ceiling on enable, duplicates), ASSET UPLOAD direct path, PMax brand, surface/schema, read-only key 403s
  - `eng2928.googleToolkitMcp.test.ts` (4): real router → gateway → toolkit → Emma handler → googleAdsService, with Google faked at axios. Covers KEYWORD ADD mutate shape + GAQL read-back + metering, the new ASSET_GROUP UPDATE Emma branch, TEXT asset upload, and refusals that reach no Google endpoint
- Scoped `tsc --noEmit` over all touched files plus their transitive imports (temp tsconfig): **exit 0**
- One existing assertion changed: `eng2823.googleToolkit.test.ts` pinned `KEYWORD ADD` as refused. It now checks the still-refused `CAMPAIGN_ASSET ATTACH`.

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Requirement | Test |
|---|---|
| Every write: preview + token, nothing sent first | `approve()` helper asserts PREVIEW and no dispatch for every guarded op; MCP test checks no mutate on preview |
| Created PAUSED | KEYWORD ADD / RSA / ASSET_GROUP CREATE dispatch args; `status ENABLED` on create refused (it.each) |
| RSA 3–15 headlines ≤30, 2–4 descriptions ≤90 | `CREATE refuses %s` it.each + non-ASCII character test |
| Read-back CONFIRMED / MISMATCH / UNCONFIRMED | keyword ADD/REMOVE, RSA, PMax brand, ASSET TEXT mismatch, timeout tests |
| Creative creation non-spending, no token | `assets (non-spending: no preview token)` describe |
| aw_ key scopes enforced | `a read-only aw_ key cannot run %s` (ASSET UPLOAD, KEYWORD ADD, ASSET_GROUP UPDATE) |
| Metering recorded | MCP tests: `recordMcpWriteExecuted` for KEYWORD ADD and ASSET UPLOAD; not metered on refusals |
| PMax brand gap fixed | `CAMPAIGN CREATE PERFORMANCE_MAX carries the brand…` + MISMATCH-without-brand |

## Files changed
- `backend/src/mcp/googleToolkitWrites.ts`: new ops, reads, verification
- `backend/src/mcp/googleToolkitManifest.ts`: surface, advertised schema, `isGoogleToolkitWrite`
- `backend/src/mcp/googleToolkitGateway.ts`, `metaToolkitGateway.ts`: write detection for scope and metering
- `backend/src/mcp/metaToolkitCreatives.ts`: exported `resolveZomaImageUrl`; Google-only accounts can stage uploads
- `backend/src/mcp/zomaToolDefinitions.ts`: `zoma_prepare_upload` description mentions Google
- `backend/src/services/googleAdsService.ts`, `emma/impl/adsCrmApis.ts`, `emma/googleAdsTools.ts`: ASSET_GROUP UPDATE, TEXT assets
- `backend/docs/meta-toolkit-skill.md`: Google section (agent-facing instructions; flagging for review as external-facing copy)
- `dev/pending/eng-2928-zoma-google-writes.md`

title: feat(crm): mailbox group emails over 50 leads send in the background (ENG-2929)
body:
Fixes ENG-2929 (Nuerra/Sondra need 250-300 recipients from a Gmail sender).

What changed
- Removes the hard 400 `MAILBOX_SENDER_LEAD_CAP_EXCEEDED` for mailbox senders. Up to 50 leads stays synchronous (unchanged). Above 50: claim the list's pending-batch record via CAS, return 202 `{ background: true, total }`, send in the background. Sender dailyLimit/warmup still enforced per send by sendAsSender; hitting it releases the run and leaves the remaining set for resume (existing ENG-265 flow).
- No duplicate sends on resume: each lead is removed from the durable remaining set before its send (at-most-once). Run ownership (`backgroundRunId` + 2-min heartbeat) blocks concurrent send/resume on the same list (409 `GROUP_EMAIL_ALREADY_SENDING`); a superseded run stops.
- Progress: existing GET .../group-email/pending record + socket `group-email-progress` / `group-email-complete`.

Not database/data-plane: no table/schema/index change; reuses the existing AW-Configs pending-batch record with two optional fields.

Follow-up (portal, separate PR): GroupEmailComposer should render the 202 `background` message instead of a 0-sent result; until then the pending banner on CRM shows progress.

Tests: `jest src/__tests__/crm.groupEmail.test.ts` 52/52 (new: 300-lead background send sends each lead exactly once and clears the record; 409 on live run; mark-before-send + abort when superseded). backend `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Rollback: revert (restores the 50 cap).
Post-deploy smoke: POST a 60-lead mailbox group send on a test list -> 202, pending record sentSoFar climbs to 60, record cleared.

title: test(zoma): first-ad journey mocked E2E harness (ENG-2932)
body:
Fixes ENG-2932 (child of ENG-2883).

What: a no-network Jest journey harness for the Zoma first-ad path, through the real guarded write executor (`executeMetaToolkitWrite`) with an in-memory Meta Graph that backs both dispatch and read-back, so what Zoma reports must match what "Meta" holds.

Journey: fresh org write refused until Meta connected ("Reconnect Meta") -> connect -> campaign / ad set / ad CREATE (each preview + approval, PAUSED) -> launch (AD, AD_SET, CAMPAIGN to ACTIVE, each its own approval).

Cases (exact user-facing status/message asserted):
1. Happy path: every step CONFIRMED with distinct created ids; launch messages `UPDATE <ENTITY> confirmed by read-back: id <id>, status ACTIVE (effective ACTIVE).`; budget stored in minor units.
2. Meta rejects ad create: `{status: FAILED, success: false, message: <Meta error>}`, no ad object, nothing activated.
3. Ad created, enable rejected: launch `FAILED` with Meta's message; ad stays PAUSED.
3b. Enable accepted but not applied: `MISMATCH`, success false, "Review AD <id>".

Proof it can fail: neutralising the `!result?.success` branch in metaToolkitWrites.ts turns cases 2 and 3 red (2 failed / 4); reverted.

No product code change; no bugs found on these paths (ENG-2931 / #3975 covers the dispatch-throw sweep, not duplicated). No migrations/tables/persisted models.

Fixes ENG-2939 (Linear).

Problem: coding_agent stops at its 50-iteration limit on multi-file tasks after it has already saved real edits. The parent agent then re-ran the whole task and hit the limit again, which produced the invalid_output cluster (sample: Google Ads tag across several files).

Change:
- The result now says the edits so far are saved on the draft branch and tells the parent to continue with only the remaining work, or to split it into smaller tasks. This guidance is added only when files were edited.
- The result carries `terminationReason: 'iteration_limit'`. It is in-memory only; there is no persistence or schema change.
- The run is still a failure classed invalid_output, so nothing is hidden from telemetry.

Tests: new eng2939.codingAgentIterationLimit.test.ts plus the existing codingAgentFailureClass.test.ts: 12/12 pass. Full backend tsc --noEmit is clean.

Rollback: revert this commit. Post-deploy check: the next failure-cluster window for coding_agent.

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Low

Adds `iterationLimitMessage` in `codingAgentService.ts`. When an iteration-limit stop follows file edits, the result tells the parent that edits are saved on the draft branch and to continue only remaining work. The result also sets `terminationReason: 'iteration_limit'`. No persistence change.

Reasoning: The change alters only a failure-path message and an optional in-memory field. It is not on a production outage path. Rollback is a single revert.

title: feat(ghl): dark Social Planner draft-only client (ENG-2941)
body:
Dark. Nothing calls this module yet. It is not registered as an Emma tool, and `GHL_SOCIAL_PLANNER_ENABLED` defaults to off. Turning it on needs ENG-2872 (GHL OAuth app, credential storage, tool registration).

## What

- Validation: https-only media (max 10), text 1-3000 chars, at least one account id, location id safe for the URL path, ISO scheduleAt.
- Typed errors: 401/403 auth, 400/422 validation, 429 rate_limited (with retry-after), 5xx/transport retryable, otherwise unexpected.

2. No tables, secrets or env values are required. The flag defaults off.
3. dev/pending fragment added.

Against a live GHL account: there are no credentials (ENG-2872). The endpoint shape follows GHL's public v2 docs and needs a live contract check once OAuth exists.

title: fix(crm): Warm/Hot heat score from genuine engagement only (ignore OOO, outbound volume, createdAt)
body:
## Problem
CRM Inbox Warm/Hot (`contactDedupService.computeHeatScore`) = min(#engagements, 5) + recency of the latest engagement of **any** type, falling back to `lead.createdAt`. Outbound sends, `status.changed`, OOO auto-replies and fresh imports all scored Warm. Reported by Nu|Erraa (Lisa Calhoun: zero replies, Warm because a Nov 11 webinar import refreshed `createdAt`).

`isEngaged` had the same flaw: substring `received`/`replied`/`clicked` anywhere in event type or JSON payload.

## Change
- `services/leadEngagementSignals.ts`: classifies events → `reply | meeting | click | auto_reply | negative_reply | none`. Auto-reply/OOO/bounce detection reuses `dripInboundReplyClassifier` (RFC 3834 headers, OOO subject/body, daemon senders). Negative = `sentiment: negative`, not-interested outcomes, decline phrases.
- Score: reply 5 (+1 per extra distinct reply, max +2), meeting 6, clicks +1 each (max 2, never Warm alone), recency +3/+2/+1 (<7/14/30d) **only from genuine replies/meetings**. Re-logged duplicate replies counted once at first timestamp. Thresholds unchanged (Warm ≥5, Hot ≥8).
- `routes/crm.ts` isEngaged lookup uses the same classifier.

## Validation (prod data, read-only, Nu|Erraa: 352 contacts, lead engagements + LinkedIn/EmailEvents logs)
- Before: 59 Warm / 3 Hot. After: 5 Warm / 0 Hot.
- Every reply/meeting-type event in their data audited: only exclusions are 1 OOO ("traveling, slow to respond") and a polite decline re-logged 21× (Ashley Chang Dawson).
- Lisa Calhoun: 4–5 → 0.
- Known judgement call: a genuine reply that is neutral (e.g. "I'm not at that company") still scores Warm.

## Tests
New `leadEngagementSignals.test.ts`; `contactDedupService.test.ts` updated (old tests asserted outbound count scoring). crm.routes/crm.db/admin.crmAnalytics/drip classifier/isEngaged suites pass; tsc clean.

## Rollout
Affects every customer's Inbox heat and isEngaged (recomputed on read; no migration). **Do not merge without engineering review**; coordinate global rollout. Portal legacy fallback `InboxView.computeHeatScore` (used only if `/api/crm/contacts` fails) still has the old formula — follow-up.

title: feat(zoma): accept configured custom conversion events on MCP ad set create (ENG-2942)
body:
## What
Slice A of ENG-2911 (ENG-2942). An MCP-created Meta ad set can optimise for a custom conversion (`custom_conversion_id`) or a custom pixel event (`custom_event_type: OTHER` + `custom_event_str`) that the account has configured. Unknown, archived, wrong-pixel, or unverifiable events are refused before anything reaches Meta.

## Where the "Lead requirement" lives (AC 1)
There is no Lead-only gate on origin/main. The toolkit AD_SET CREATE path (`backend/src/mcp/metaToolkitWrites.ts` `validateWriteShape` ~L131 → `executeMetaToolkitWrite` ~L288) passes `promoted_object` through. `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts` `buildMetaOptimisationEventWarning` (~L12883) only WARNS when the event has no recent fires. `metaTrackingPreflight.ts` checks page pixel presence and ownership only (ENG-941, unchanged). What was missing was the refusal half for custom events, which is what this PR adds.

## Change
- New `backend/src/mcp/metaToolkitConversionGate.ts`: `assertOptimisationEventConfigured` (pure, lookup injected).
- `metaToolkitWrites.ts`: new optional dep `conversionLookup`; runs on AD_SET CREATE when `promoted_object` is present (preview and confirm both re-run it).
- `agentModeService.toolkitMetaConversionLookup`: reads via the existing `executeSignalsRead` (account-bound customconversions + pixel stats `aggregation=event`; the foreign-pixel refusal is inherited).
- Standard events (LEAD, PURCHASE, ...) are not looked up. No behaviour change there.

Customer-visible (for #feature-launches): Zoma/MCP users can create Meta ad sets optimised for their own custom conversions or custom pixel events, not only standard ones. Not dark.

## Database / data-plane classification
None. Nothing is persisted, and there's no schema change. Graph reads only.

## Tests
- `src/__tests__/eng2942.customConversionEvent.test.ts` (9): custom-conversion create+enable succeeds; custom_event_str accepted; unknown, archived, wrong-pixel and never-reported refused with nothing dispatched; lookup failure refuses with a retry message; LEAD path makes no lookups.
- `npx jest --testPathPattern "metaToolkit|eng2913|eng2914"`: 21 suites, 315 tests passed.

## Not tested
- No live Meta calls. The pixel stats `aggregation=event` response shape (`data[].data[].value`) is assumed from Meta docs.
- Full `tsc` timed out locally (box memory). CI build is the typecheck.

## Rollback
Revert the merge commit. The gate is additive.

## Complexity ledger
+1 small module (~90 lines), +1 optional dep, +1 AMS method. No new flags, tables or dependencies.

Pre-push note: hook tsc passed; hook jest bailed on agentModeService.prepareTurnContext.golden.test.ts, which fails identically on main 9af124132 (20/27, priorityToolNames drift). Not touched by this PR.

title: refactor(zoma): shared ConsumedTokenStore for preview tokens (ENG-2945)
body:
## What
Adds `ConsumedTokenStore` (async `consume(token, expiresAt)`) + `InMemoryConsumedTokenStore` + process-wide `defaultConsumedTokenStore` in `backend/src/mcp/zomaWriteGuard.ts`. All six Zoma write toolkits (Google writes, Meta writes/audiences/catalog writes/catalog feeds/event sources) default to the one shared store via `consumeToken()`; none keeps its own Map. Bare-Map injection still accepted so existing tests are unchanged.

## Why
ENG-2945 (prep for gated ENG-2862): the durable cross-instance store becomes a one-file swap. Side effect: cross-toolkit replay inside one process is now rejected.

## Risk / not done
- No table, TTL, IAM or persistence (AC4). Cross-instance replay residual unchanged (ENG-2862).
- In-memory store also refuses already-expired tokens (signature check already refused them upstream).
- Full `tsc` OOMs on the swarm box; relying on CI Backend build.

## Tests
- New `eng2945.consumedTokenStore.test.ts` (6): double consume, cross-toolkit shared store, expiry, fake async store, legacy Map, default store.
- Toolkit suites eng2303/2823/2853/2905/2913/2914/292x/2932/2942: green. eng2931 has 6 failures that are identical on origin/main (`deps.probeUrl is not a function`, pre-existing).

## Complexity ledger
+1 interface, +1 class, +1 helper; 6 call sites swapped 1:1.

Rollback: revert this PR.

title: refactor: PublicRateLimitStore port for lead-magnet execute (ENG-2946)
body:
Reviewer-first: extracts lead-magnet per-email/per-IP daily limits from module Maps into an injectable `PublicRateLimitStore` (`backend/src/services/publicRateLimitStore.ts`) so the durable store for ENG-1755 is a one-line swap. Not customer-visible.

- Interface: `consume` (atomic check+increment), plus `check`/`record` which the route uses to keep today's exact semantics (counts only recorded after task creation succeeds).
- `InMemoryPublicRateLimitStore`: same caps (1/email, 5/IP), same 24h sliding window; email keys are `email:<sha256(lowercased)>` — no raw PII.
- `createLeadMagnetRouter({ rateLimitStore })` factory; default export uses the shared default in-memory store. Global ceiling + kill switch (ENG-2353) untouched. Legacy test exports `dailyEmailTracker`/`dailyIpTracker` alias the default store's `clear()`.
- No table, no DynamoDB calls, no persisted attributes (AC3).

Complexity ledger: +1 service file (~80 LOC), route net ~neutral.

How to test: `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/publicRateLimitStore.test.ts src/__tests__/leadMagnet*.test.ts` → 6 suites / 45 tests pass locally; existing lead-magnet tests unchanged (AC1). New tests cover cap, window expiry, independent keys, hashed email keys, and two routers sharing one store (AC2).

Not tested: durable store (out of scope, parent ENG-1755). Rollback: revert this PR.

Moves lead-magnet per-email and per-IP daily limits behind an injectable PublicRateLimitStore with an in-memory default. Adds createLeadMagnetRouter factory and hashed email keys. Caps stay at 1 per email and 5 per IP. Adds store test suite. Legacy tracker exports now alias the default store.

title: ENG-2783: platform-wide daily ceiling on automatic hot-lead calls, with an operator alert
body:
## ENG-2783: platform-wide daily ceiling on automatic hot-lead calls, with an operator alert

Every limit until now was per organization. This adds one ceiling across all customers so a bug, an abusive org or a spike cannot spend without bound.

### Approvals (recorded)
- **Persisted-state addition approved by the owner (Anurag):** new key families `hlc#cap#g#<UTC date>` (2-day TTL) and `hlc#notify#g80#<date>` / `hlc#notify#g100#<date>` in the existing `AW-MCPSessions` limit store. No table, index or schema change.
- The owner asked for "a daily budget and alert". The default of 300 leads per UTC day is a conservative starting value chosen by the builder, not a measurement; the owner changes it.

### Behaviour
- **Cap:** leads that get a call, per UTC day, across all orgs. Env `HOT_LEAD_CALL_PLATFORM_DAILY_MAX` (positive integer; unset/invalid = 300 with one warn; clamped at 100000; it can be raised but not disabled).
- **Order:** the counter is taken LAST, after the phone marker and the org hourly/daily/monthly counters, so an org's own refusals never inflate the shared count; any refusal releases everything. Retries (press 2) take a slot too and cannot bypass the ceiling; a platform refusal of a retry is transient (released, rescheduled at least 15 minutes out, given up at `firstDueAt` + 6 hours).
- **Refusal:** `platform_daily_cap`, recorded as a `call.skipped` timeline event; nothing is rung. It does not read as the customer's own limit. No customer email.
- **Counts leads attempted**, not calls connected: a slot stays taken once a record is created.
- **Alert:** at 80% (not for caps below 5) and 100% of the cap, once per level per day (claim in the limit store): an ERROR line `[hotLeadCall] PLATFORM daily cap 80%|100%` (the alarm hook) and, if `HOT_LEAD_CALL_ALERT_EMAIL` is set, an email with counts only (no phone, org or lead data). Fire-and-forget; never throws; a failed send keeps the claim so the marker logs once.

### Tests
Unit (key, env parser, order/rollback matrix, retry, alert de-dup under concurrency, email failure, env unset) and e2e through the real dispatch path (the (cap+1)-th lead skipped; day rollover with a fake clock) and through the real retry path (repeated sweeps at a full cap reschedule and keep `firstDueAt`; adding the reason to `PERMANENT_REFUSALS` makes them fail). Nine existing counter-count expectations went from 3 to 4 counters because the platform counter is a fourth counter (intended change). `npm run typecheck` and eslint on changed files clean; targeted jest 2554 passed, 17 skipped, 2 DynamoDB-local suites skipped.

### Review
Two independent reviews, no blockers. Fixed: the 80% alert re-logged on every call during an email outage; wording said "placed" for a count of leads attempted; the cost estimate's assumptions; the retry path had no test; stale key list.

### Not verified
Real DynamoDB behaviour (in-memory store only; `incrementBelow` is the same primitive as the existing caps); the email on prod; the default's cost with a measured per-lead figure (the attended test window will give one).

title: ENG-2747: read-only Zoma for Databricks-origin OAuth clients (ENG-2781 option B)
body:
## What

Implements ENG-2781 decision 4 (Harsha, 2026-11-03, option B): **Zoma is read-only on Databricks.** Writes are disabled for Databricks-origin tokens until server-enforced human approval exists, because an agent in a Databricks workflow can confirm its own previews. Part of ENG-2747.

Stacked on #3893 (tool annotations), and uses its `READ_ONLY_TOOLKIT_TOOLS`. Retarget to `main` once #3893 merges.

## How it works

- **Detection.** Databricks connects over OAuth and registers a client whose redirect URI is on the customer's workspace host (documented: `https://<workspace-hostname>/login/oauth/http.html`). An OAuth client with any redirect URI on `*.databricks.com` or `*.azuredatabricks.net` (dot-boundary match, so `databricks.com.evil.example` doesn't count) is Databricks-origin. The check reads the existing OAuth client record per call. There is no new table, schema or stored data.
- **Allowed for that caller (deny-by-default):**
  - the verified read tools (`READ_ONLY_TOOLKIT_TOOLS`);
  - `zoma_status`, `zoma_usage` and `ads_get_errors`;
  - `call_meta_marketing_api` with a read action (LIST, GET, PREVIEW, SEARCH, GET_MATCH_QUALITY) and no `confirm` or `preview_token`.
- **Everything else is refused.** That includes tools added later, mixed tools (`zoma_custom_audiences`, `call_google_ads_api`) and `zoma_prepare_upload`. The refusal happens before any upstream call or metering, with a message pointing to the direct Zoma setup.
- **`tools/list` and `GET /tools`** show that caller only the allowed tools, with `call_meta_marketing_api` narrowed to read actions.
- **Fail closed.** If the client lookup errors, the OAuth caller is treated as read-only (and logged). A client with no record, such as the Zoma device-flow client, is not Databricks-origin.
- **Unaffected:** `aw_` keys, Zoma device tokens, and every other OAuth client. The Databricks listing must therefore offer OAuth only, not a bearer key.

## Not in this PR

- Server-enforced human approval, which would lift the block (option C).
- Identifying Databricks via `aw_` keys (not possible; the listing uses OAuth).

## Rollback

Pure revert. No schema, table or config change. Reverting makes Databricks-origin callers behave like any other OAuth client.

## Verification

- **Jest, Node 24: 37 toolkit suites / 639 tests pass.**
  - New `eng2747.databricksReadOnly`: host detection for AWS, Azure and GCP; lookalike, http and malformed URIs rejected; allowed and refused calls; the gateway refuses Databricks writes before upstream calls or metering, lets Databricks read, and leaves Claude-client OAuth, unknown clients and `aw_` keys writable; fail-closed on lookup error; the tools/list view and schema narrowing, with the source left unmutated.
  - eng2288: one route test showing a Databricks caller sees only allowed tools.
  - eng2865: the OAuth case now injects a non-Databricks client lookup.
- **`tsc --noEmit`:** clean.
- **ESLint:** new files are clean; touched files have the same error counts as main.
- **Mutation checks, all BIND:**
  - The gateway refusal is removed.
  - Lookalike hosts are accepted.
  - The lookup fails open.
  - `confirm` is allowed on a read action.

Not verified: not run against a real Databricks workspace yet. The smoke test will show the actual redirect URI Databricks registers. If it differs from the documented host pattern, detection needs adjusting before the Zoma listing goes live.

body:
Dark. Nothing changes unless `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW=true` is set. Caps: `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW_MAX_TURNS` (default 40) and `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW_MAX_SPEND_USD` (default 5).

## What / why
ENG-2953 (child of ENG-2812). This wires the merged-but-unused ENG-2820 evaluator into the agent-mode loop in shadow mode only. The goal is evidence for choosing per-tier caps.
- New file: `backend/src/services/sessionBreakerShadow.ts`. It keeps an in-memory per-session accumulator (turn = one agent-loop LLM call; spend = `usage.cost`, falling back to `estimateCost`). It runs `evaluateSessionSpendBreaker`. Each time a new cap multiple is crossed, it logs one `session_breaker_would_pause` JSON line with sessionId, userId, billingUserId, turns, spendUsd, multiple, action, reason and isScheduled.
- `agentModeService.ts`: one call after each LLM response. It returns void and never throws. It never pauses, changes the response, writes to a table or sends a notification. When the flag is off it returns immediately, so cost isn't even computed.
- Fragment: `dev/pending/eng-2812-session-breaker-shadow.md`.

## Tests
`sessionBreakerShadow.test.ts`, 5 tests:
- (a) Flag off: the evaluator and the cost function are never called and nothing is logged.
- (b) Synthetic Opiner `aea6a0ee` replay (549 turns, ~$47, caps 40/$5): the first would-pause comes at turn 40, then one log per multiple (13 total), and every call returns void.
- (c) Scheduled run: logs `pause_and_notify`.
- Errors in logging or in the cost function don't propagate.
- Sessions are isolated, and invalid env values fall back to the default caps.

Results: these tests plus the existing `sessionSpendBreaker` suite pass (12/12). Two integration suites that call `generateMarketingResponse` pass (26/26). Full `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

+1 small module, +1 call site. No new deps, no persistence, no data-plane change.

title: ENG-2957: voice mode works again (client-side voice; GET /public/voice-model)
body:
Fixes ENG-2957: the "Switch to voice mode" button has done nothing for everyone since 2026-10-07.

**Why it broke.** The portal entered voice mode only when the text picker's list contained the live-voice model, then saved that model as the chat's model. On 2026-10-07, #3339 (ENG-903) removed it from `/model-options` and commit `8b0794b64` (#3276) made both model-switch routes refuse live models. So the button did nothing.

**Design: voice mode is client-side** (revised after an independent review). The voice session never reads the chat's stored model, so the portal now switches only the picker and never saves the voice model. Saving it (the old behaviour, and this PR's first version) left chats stored on the live model whenever voice was left without End, and text paths that read the stored model then fail (share-link plan check, Slack and email replies, work plans).

**What this changes (backend):**
- `agentModeService.getVoiceModelFor(isAdmin)`: the served live-voice model, same internal-only and admin-only gates as the picker.
- New `GET /api/agent-mode/public/voice-model` returns `{ voiceModel }`.
- **Unchanged on purpose:** both model-switch routes still refuse the live-voice model (now pinned by a test); `/model-options` and `/public/llm-models` still never list it.

**Known, not in this PR (raised for a decision):** `live:start` has no usage, paused or plan gate (usage is charged to the owner after the fact), and share links and public-plan pages get voice back (lost there since 2026-08-19).

**Tests:** `agentModeController.voiceModel.test.ts` (7 cases); 19 related suites, 832 tests pass; typecheck clean. Live on the test environment with the portal PR: owner voice (live session, typed turn answered, stored model unchanged, zero model saves, exit restores, reload mid-voice returns to text), a new chat started from voice (saved with the pre-voice model), a logged-out share-link visitor (voice live, nothing saved).

**Rollout:** either order is safe (an older backend answers 404 → the portal hides the button). Production check after deploy in the owner's own account.

title: ENG-2803: harden the Apollo waterfall callback path
body:
## Safety answer (first, per the draft/merge rules)
- **Safe for prod?** Yes by design. Backend only; no schema, key, index, IAM, ledger-label or rate-card change and no new setting. The Apollo async callback path gets stricter (more inputs refused, never more accepted except punycode TLDs), and the late email write additionally sets `domain` fill-if-empty.
- **Could it regress or anger users?** (1) If `APOLLO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` were ever unset on prod, Tier 3 would send a basic match instead of the email waterfall (fewer emails found, cheaper) instead of silently using the committed default; prod has it set (verified 2026-11-12, not the default). (2) A vendor email that fails the stricter gate (doubled/leading/trailing dot, hyphen-led domain label, one-letter or numeric TLD, local part starting with `=`, `+` or `-`) is treated as "no email" for that callback; the gate is the one the send path already uses, so such addresses could not be emailed anyway. (3) Callbacks arriving more than 7 days after the run are refused (Apollo's chain lands in seconds to minutes). (4) Late-written leads now get a `domain` like every other email write; an existing domain is never overwritten.
- **Rollback:** revert the merge; no data migration. Leads that got a `domain` keep it (same value any other email write would have set).
- **Data-plane / persistent changes:** one more attribute (`domain`, derived from the email) on leads written by the late callback, fill-if-empty. No new rows, tables or settings.

## Summary
Hardening items parked by the ENG-2801 (#3890) reviews, tracked in ENG-2803:
1. `utils/secretsManager.ts`: `getApolloWebhookSecret()` throws in production when `APOLLO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset (no committed default in prod). `apolloServiceFactory.buildWebhookUrl()` catches it and returns null, so the sender uses the existing "no webhook → basic match" path; `initApolloServiceFromEnv` already logs it once at startup; the route answers 503.
2. `routes/apolloWebhook.ts` `cleanCallbackEmail`: normalize (trim + lower-case) and use the send path's `isValidAddress` (`utils/sendEligibility.ts`, now exported), plus callback-only rules: TLD is 2-63 letters or `xn--` punycode, and no leading `=`, `+`, `-`.
3. `extractApolloEmail` (now exported for tests) stops at the first usable address in a vendor's `emails`.
4. A callback whose placeholder is past `expiresAt` answers 202 `{ matched: false, expired: true }` and writes nothing. `status` is not enforced on purpose (a retry after a failed lead write must still land).
5. `crmDb.setLeadEmailIfMissing` sets `domain = if_not_exists(domain, <email domain>)` through a name placeholder (`domain` is reserved), free-mail domains skipped, on the first try and the bootstrap retry.

## Not in this PR
- Org owner / `crm.editor` callbacks are still refused when the list owner is not the run user: the intended owner rule is a product decision.
- TTL on `AW-EnrichmentRawCache` (infra change).
- `validateLeadEmailInBackground` on a late write (costs an enrich.so call; Apollo already reports verification).

## Known lows from the final review (left as is after SAFE, per the review-cycle rule)
- The expiry check fails open when a placeholder has no / non-numeric / zero `expiresAt` (a legacy or hand-made row could still be replayed by a holder of the secret). Both writers (`enrichmentWaterfall.ts`, `enrichmentV3RealDeps.ts`) always set a numeric +7d and the forced re-stamp keeps it, so no such row is produced today.
- RFC-valid addresses starting with `-` or `+` (e.g. `-info@x.com`) are refused as "no email" — deliberate (CSV formula safety), very rare in B2B.
- `if_not_exists(domain)` treats a stored `domain: null` / `''` as set; the write paths remove empty domains rather than storing them, so this does not occur today.
- `dev.md` (~L416) still says the secret is not set on prod and lists `expiresAt`/`domain`/default secret as open; fold the new pending note in when consolidating. Doc-comment placement nit in `apolloWebhook.ts`.
- Pre-existing: the 503 is answered before the secret check (reveals "not configured"); outside production the committed default still applies (Dev- tables only).

## Evidence
- **Real DynamoDB (DynamoDB Local, throwaway container) running the real `setLeadEmailIfMissing`:** lead without `enrichmentMetadata` → bootstrap + retry, email + `domain` written; existing domain kept; existing email untouched (`written: false`); free-mail sets no domain; deleted lead not recreated.
- **Prod config (names/booleans only):** `NODE_ENV=production`, `APOLLO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` set and not the committed default, `BACKEND_URL` set.
- **Tests:** 83 related suites / 2087 tests pass (apollo, webhook, secretsManager, sendEligibility, crm.db, enrichmentWaterfall, crmFindEmail, enrichSo); tsc clean; eslint: no new errors versus `origin/main` on any changed file (test files counted per file). Mutation checks on the runtime changes: 11 of 11 killed (prod throw, URL catch, CSV rule, TLD rule, normalize, shared validator, early break, expiry removed / inverted, domain overwrite, domain removed); one equivalent (the 254 length cap is also enforced by the shared validator).
- Real pre-push hook (no `--no-verify`).

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests, mutation checks, tsc, eslint vs base, DynamoDB Local check, hook.
- [x] Fresh independent full review of the exact head `98d9f675e`: **SAFE TO MERGE**, no blocker/medium. 22 mutants, 18 killed (survivors: two duplicated length guards, `Number.isFinite` (no behaviour change), and `expiresAt > 0` (untested)). Real DynamoDB Local re-run by the reviewer; eslint per file equal or lower than main; tsc clean; 2087 tests pass.
- [ ] CI green on the exact head; branch current with main.
- [ ] After deploy, prod check in the test account: a 1-lead run on a throwaway list (callback still matches under the real secret), a forged callback with the real secret against my own expired/unexpired placeholder only is NOT planned (needs the secret value); instead verify via logs that callbacks match and no 503s appear.

title: UI Bug: I can access the ClickUp space, but I just found out that everyone at our compan
body:
## ENG-2935 — ClickUp connection not shared with the org (backend)

**Root cause:** `getAccessToken` prefers `org.secrets.clickup_access_token` and falls back to the caller's personal token. XCures' org record had none; the owner's token lived only in his user secrets, so he looked connected and teammates saw nothing. Nothing promoted a personal token to the org, the UI hid Connect (status said "connected" via the fallback), and Disconnect only cleared the already-empty org secret.

**Changes**
- `GET /api/oauth/clickup/status` is read-only: reports `scope` (`solo|org|personal`) and `canShare`; a lookup failure degrades to no scope rather than "disconnected". Failures carry `reason` (`invalid_token` | `unavailable`).
- New `POST /api/oauth/clickup/share-with-org`: explicit, admin/KB-editor only; verifies the token against ClickUp, then writes via new `orgDb.setOrgSecretIfAbsent` (single conditional update, 409 if the org already has one). Sharing is never silent.
- Org-admin Disconnect also clears the caller's personal token; idempotent and retry-safe.
- `orgDb.removeOrgSecret` no longer swallows real failures (only the missing-secrets-map case), so Disconnect can't report success while the org token survives. Foreplay Disconnect shares this helper and now surfaces real failures as 500.
- `migrate-clickup-to-org.ts`: `--org-id`, prefers the org owner's token, conditional write.

**Data repair:** already run for XCures (org `3583d005…`) by Yugo with Harsha's approval; org token verified byte-identical to the owner's personal ciphertext. Duplicate report: ENG-2933.

**Verification:** backend typecheck clean; 111 tests pass across clickupAuth / orgClickupIntegration / orgForeplayIntegration / orgSecrets.db. UI exercised in a preview browser (see portal PR AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1335).

**Data-plane note for reviewers:** adds an org-secret write path (`/share-with-org`), explicit and confirmed in the UI.

## Safety answer (first, per the draft/merge rules)
- **Safe for prod?** Yes. A new read-only daily cron: it reads the usage ledger (`usageRecordDb.scanByDateRange`, ~8 days of compact daily aggregates) and at most sends one oncall email a day. No writes, no schedule change, no new setting, table, index or IAM.
- **Could it regress or anger users?** Customers see nothing. Oncall (the `oncall_emails` setting: Manan + aseth) gets at most one extra email a day when a schedule's daily cost jumps; the backtest (below) shows ~6 alert days in 18. No Linear issue is filed. The scan runs once a day on the cron instance (`isCronEnabled()`), same as the admin cost aggregation.
- **Rollback:** revert the merge (or ignore the email); nothing persistent.
- **Data-plane / persistent changes:** none.

## Summary
ENG-2743 acceptance item "flag schedules whose cost per run jumps". Scheduled runs have no per-run cost cap (that is ENG-2812, Harsha's decision on cap values), and a schedule's cost can double unnoticed. `cron/scheduleCostJumpCron.ts`:
- sums each schedule's agent-loop cost per UTC day from the ledger (`agent_task:scheduled:<scheduleId>`, all models together, so a fallback to an expensive model counts);
- evaluates the last complete UTC day against the median of the schedule's billed days in the previous 7 (needs >= 3; new schedules skipped);
- flags when that day cost >= $3 and >= 2x the median; all flagged schedules go into ONE email to the oncall list via the new `emailService.sendOncallEmailOnly` (production only, HTML-escaped, no Linear filing; returns true only when the send really went out), at most once per evaluated day per process, with schedule id, cost, calls, ratio, billing user and last session id.
Wired in `server.ts` like the skill-review digest, but as a 15-minute tick that acts only during 07:00-07:59 UTC (once per day per process): every deploy starts a new process, and a boot-time daily run would re-send the same flagged day on each deploy (found by the final review). A failed read/send retries on the next tick of the hour; a deploy overlapping that hour (immutable deploys, ~12/day) can still send a flagged day twice — accepted by Manan (2026-11-12) instead of a stored per-day marker.

## Review findings
- **Medium, routing (fixed in the next head):** `sendAgentModeOncallAlert` no longer emails: since the founders' 2026-11-07 change `emailService.sendOncallAlert` files a Linear issue (labels Bug, Needs PM, Oncall; Todo; assigned to Harsha) and emails only if filing fails. With a dated subject and no `Alert Class`, each flagged day would open a NEW issue (~1 every 3 days per the backtest). Not merged until the routing is decided.
- Low: `eval_` sandbox principals are not excluded (no userId passed). Low: untested edges (exactly $3, empty-id / missing-date guards; `base <= 0` unreachable). Info: daily full-table scan of the ledger (~8 MB, same as admin reporting); side calls (`finalize_guard_correction` etc.) and Python-engine spend are not counted; the schedule-id parse keeps text after a second colon (moot: ids are `[a-f0-9-]`).

## Evidence
- **Backtest on the prod ledger** (read-only, real detector, nothing sent), each day Oct 25 - Nov 11: Oct 26 `b2bce0d0` $13.45 (5.2x) + `04b34124` $4.47; Oct 28 `b2bce0d0` $17.36 (5.7x) + `04b34124` $6.35; Oct 29 `b2bce0d0` $15.03 (3.8x) + `75063398` $3.89; Nov 1 `04b34124` $33.60 (7.4x, the Opus day); Nov 3 `64aa9dd7` $5.55 (2.3x); every other day nothing. Known limit: a gradual climb that never doubles within one day (hourly `0052c195`, $5.6 -> $11.6 over five days) is not flagged.
- **Tests:** 21 (thresholds at the boundary, multi-model sum, median vs one old spike, exact 7-day window, zero-cost days, non-scheduled features, malformed rows, ordering, ledger/alert failures, default reader, dedupe key). Mutation checks: 14/14 killed (ratio boundary, $3 floor, min baseline days, mean vs median, window +1, evaluating today, sort, prefix filter, dedupe key, read-failure catch, per-model sum, zero-cost days, even median, alert-failure catch).
- eslint clean on both new files; pre-push hook (tsc + suite) green.

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests, mutation checks, eslint, hook, prod-ledger backtest.
- [x] Fresh independent full review of `2f3862f37`: SAFE apart from one **medium** (routing, below); 18 of 22 mutants killed.
- [x] Routing decided by Manan (2026-11-12): email only to the oncall list, no Linear issue. Applied in this head (`sendOncallEmailOnly` + cron switched to it; 6/6 new mutants killed). Needs its own fresh full review.
- [x] Fresh full review of `a5cf1a70d`: SAFE; its one low (a boot-time daily run re-sends the flagged day on every deploy / per instance) fixed in the next head with the fixed-hour tick (6/6 tick mutants killed, 36 tests).
- [x] Fresh full review of `f5fb6651e`: **SAFE TO MERGE**. Its low (duplicates on deploys overlapping 07 UTC) accepted by Manan; wording corrected in the next head (comments/docs only). Test-quality infos: the 07:59:59 boundary is reached only after the day is finished; TZ not pinned in tests (EB runs UTC).
- [ ] CI green on the exact head.
- [ ] After deploy: the cron logs `[scheduleCostJumpCron] <day>: ...` once at boot on the cron instance (CloudWatch).

title: fix: accurate autopublish instructions + log refused consent (ENG-2975)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
When a scheduled post was blocked for missing standing publish authorization, the instructions the model gave the owner (system prompt + publish-block tool error) said to "confirm the publish tool is selected under Required Actions **and saved**, then use the control". That reads as if saving the schedule grants the authorization, and it did not match the new single portal flow. Separately, `revokeScheduledChatPublishConsent` refused requests (400/404/403/400) without logging anything, so failed grants left no trace. Only the 409 path logged.

## What this fixes (after)
- `agentModeSystemPrompt.ts` (never-granted branch) and the matching `agentModeService.ts` publish-block error now describe one flow: open the schedule → make sure the publish tool (e.g. `post_on_connected_account`) is selected under Required Actions → check **Publish without my review** → click **Update Schedule** and confirm → a **"Standing publish authorization on"** confirmation appears. Both state explicitly that saving alone does NOT grant it.
- The 409 error copy now says "check … again and click Update Schedule" instead of "turn on … again".
- `console.warn` with scheduleId, userId and reason on every refused path: 400 invalid body, 404 (not found / not owner), 403 delegated grant, 400 no publish tool. **Authorization logic is unchanged.** Each log sits directly before its existing `return`.

## Complexity ledger
+31 / −4 lines. No new branches, flags or abstractions. Logging only, plus a prompt/error-string rewrite. Behavior-preserving except for the instruction text the model relays.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/agentModeService.publishApprovalBlockReason.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeSystemPrompt.scheduledTruthfulReporting.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeController.revokePublishConsent.test.ts src/__tests__/grantScheduleAutopublish.realDbWrite.test.ts`
2. **Expected**: all pass. The never-granted assertions now pin `Update Schedule`, `Standing publish authorization on` and "Saving the schedule alone does NOT grant it", and reject the old "selected under Required Actions and saved" wording.

## Test Evidence
- Scoped jest (4 suites above): 67 passed, 0 failed
- `npm run typecheck`: clean

## Behavioral assertions verified
- Instructions describe only the check box → Update Schedule → confirm flow and never imply that saving grants consent: covered by the new assertions in both prompt/service tests.
- Refused paths log and authorization is unchanged: the existing `agentModeController.revokePublishConsent.test.ts` still passes unchanged.

## Files changed
- backend/src/docs/agentModeSystemPrompt.ts
- backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts
- backend/src/controllers/agentModeController.ts
- backend/src/__tests__/agentModeService.publishApprovalBlockReason.test.ts
- backend/src/__tests__/agentModeSystemPrompt.scheduledTruthfulReporting.test.ts

## What was NOT tested
- No test asserts on the new `console.warn` lines.
- No live portal check that the UI labels ("Update Schedule", "Standing publish authorization on") match exactly. They depend on the companion portal change for ENG-2975.

## Linear issue
ENG-2975

title: feat: Zoma toolkit Meta calls honor BUC usage with bounded backoff (ENG-2977)
body:
## Summary
- Extract/reuse the existing metaService BUC parser; select worst usage and regain estimate across account/use-case entries.
- Run toolkit Meta calls in async-local backoff context: read-only calls get at most one retry, injectable sleep, and a hard 30s wait cap at the named 90% threshold or throttle codes 4/17/32/613/80000–80014 (also HTTP 429).
- Observe both axios Graph responses and the shared fetch path. No auto-retries for writes, including HTTP POST/DELETE. Exhausted/read and write limits return a caller-visible rate-limited result with regain estimate. Writes warn to verify state before trying again.
- No database changes; zomaMetaParityMatrix.ts and dev.md untouched.

## Risk
Near-limit reads can incur up to 30s additional latency. A successful response whose usage remains high after retry becomes an explicit rate-limited result. Axios hooks are inert outside the toolkit async-local context; legacy fetch retries remain unchanged outside it. A throttled write may already have executed, so the result explicitly warns against blind replay.

## Rollback
Revert this PR.

## How to test / evidence
- Scoped Jest: metaToolkitBackoff, eng2283.metaToolkitGateway, metaService.capi: 3 suites / 74 tests passed. Gateway mocked-fetch acceptance covers under-threshold, one successful retry, cap exhaustion, and no write retry. Transport tests cover every requested throttle code, minute conversion/cap, parser maxima, and axios reads.
- Scoped semantic TypeScript check (4 leaf files) plus gateway/service syntax checks: 0 diagnostics.
- Repository pre-push hook additionally ran backend tsc --noEmit successfully (56s), then 19 related Jest suites / 410 tests passed. This hook ran automatically; no manual full-repo typecheck was requested. Jest reported a worker teardown warning.
- Post-deploy smoke: connected-account toolkit read should return normal data and one usage event; mocked throttling should show one capped wait and the regain estimate.
