title: fix: treat "<X> not connected" precondition wording as never-connected in the failure-cluster loop (ENG-3037)
body:
## What changed

The agent-mode failure-cluster loop now treats a second wording of the never-connected precondition as `not_connected`, so it no longer files an Auto oncall row for it. One regex added to `isNeverConnectedMessage` in `backend/src/loops/instances/agent-mode/failureRuleSet.ts`, plus tests. No error message a user sees is edited.

ENG-2943 only matched "No <X> account connected". Messages such as "Google Drive not connected. Connect Google Drive in Settings → Connected Accounts." (the google_drive cluster on ENG-2788) stayed `config` and were dispatched with nothing for anyone to fix.

## Which call sites are included

The new matcher is an allow-list of integrations, not a general "not connected" pattern. I read each throw site on `origin/main` `a6f60b684`.

| Site | Included | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `googleDriveAccess.ts:82` Google Drive | yes | thrown only when `getAccountByPlatform(userId, 'google_drive')` returns nothing |
| `hubspotService.ts:405`, `:414` HubSpot | yes | thrown only when the user has no own account and no org-shared account |
| `attioService.ts:88` Attio | yes | thrown only when the user has zero Attio rows |
| `gmailService.ts:84`, `:520` Gmail | yes | thrown only when `getAccountById` finds no row for the requested account id |
| `outlookService.ts:76`, `:162` Outlook | yes | same as Gmail |
| `adsApis.ts:3318` LinkedIn Ads | **no, stays `config`** | the filter also drops a connected row that has no `access_token`, so a connected account in a bad state produces the same message |
| "ClickUp not connected" (`knowledgeBase.ts`, `tools.ts`) | **no, stays `config`** | `clickupService.getAccessToken` returns null when a stored token fails to decrypt |
| "Foreplay not connected" (`knowledgeBase.ts`) | **no, stays `config`** | same swallow-and-fall-through shape in `foreplayService.getAccessToken` |

Gmail and Outlook are "no row for this account id", which also covers a stale or removed id, not only a user who never connected. In both cases there is no account row to repair, so I included them. Say so if a stale id should still file.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Exact Google Drive string is `not_connected` and produces no proposal, alone and mixed with real failures of the same tool: tested (the mixed case files only the 4 `invalid_grant` failures and reports 5 excluded).
2. "<X> account not connected. Please connect ..." for the confirmed sites: tested for HubSpot, Gmail, Outlook, Attio. Sites left as `config` are named in the table above.
3. Genuine auth failures still file: tested for `invalid_grant`, the Drive "authorization has expired or is not connected" message, missing scope, the `adUtmAuditAdapters.ts:139` specific-account message, and the three excluded sites.
4. The ENG-2943 cases are unchanged and pass.

## Risk and rollback

A cluster made up only of the five included messages stops filing. If one of those sites later starts firing for a connected account, that failure would be hidden from this loop; the strings are matched narrowly (full first sentence) to limit that. A new integration using this wording is not excluded until its name is added. Rollback: revert the commit.

Data-plane: none. External copy: none.

## Complexity ledger

+1 regex constant and one `||` in an existing function. 0 new modules, tables, flags or packages.

## How to test

In `backend`:

1. `npx jest src/__tests__/loops.agentFailureRuleSet.test.ts`: 34 tests pass locally (7 of the new ones failed before the change).
2. `npx jest --testPathPattern 'src/__tests__/(loops\.agent|toolFailureType)'`: 7 suites, 174 tests pass locally.
3. `npm run typecheck`: clean locally.

## What was NOT tested

- Not run against real failure events from production; the messages are copied from the source.
- No staging or browser run (nothing user-facing changes).
- Local `coderabbit review` was not run.
- The worktree borrowed `backend/node_modules` from another worktree at the same lockfile.

```text
Accountable-Owner: Harsha Vankayalapati
Accountable-Linear-ID: 142fef82-4d45-4070-99be-c5debe565ac6
```

title: feat: Zoma ads_boost_ig_post guarded write, created PAUSED (ENG-3033)
body:
**Wording gate cleared: Harsha approved the tool description as written (ENG-3045). Copy unchanged.**

~~**[needs human] Held for one answer from Harsha: the wording of the new tool's model-facing description (below).** The tool name `ads_boost_ig_post` is Meta's own and is fixed by ENG-3033. Everything else is ready for review. Draft until the wording is answered.~~

## What changed and why

ENG-3033 (slice 2 of ENG-2920): adds the Zoma toolkit tool `ads_boost_ig_post`, which turns an existing Instagram post into an ad on the selected ad account. It was the last `gap` row in the Pages, Instagram & Ad Library category of the parity matrix.

One call creates one campaign (objective OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT), one ad set and one ad. All three are created PAUSED. Activating them stays a separate `call_meta_marketing_api` UPDATE with its own preview and approval.

## The wording to approve

> Boost an existing Instagram post as an ad on this ad account. Creates one campaign, one ad set and one ad, all PAUSED: nothing spends until they are activated with call_meta_marketing_api, which is a separate preview and approval. Two calls: PREVIEW (everything that would be created) + preview_token, then confirm=true with the token. daily_budget is in MAJOR units of the ad account currency (e.g. 20 = $20.00). Verified by read-back.

Arguments: `ig_account_id`, `ig_media_id`, `page_id`, `daily_budget`, `countries` (required); `age_min`, `age_max`, `duration_days`, `name`, `account_id` (optional); `confirm`, `preview_token`.

## Review focus

1. **Design choices I made that the issue did not specify.** Objective is fixed to OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT with `optimization_goal: POST_ENGAGEMENT`, `billing_event: IMPRESSIONS`, `destination_type: ON_POST`. Targeting is countries plus an age range only. A Facebook Page id is required as the ad identity. I did not read Meta's published description of its own `ads_boost_ig_post`, so the argument set may differ from Meta's.
2. **One path for the money-bearing writes.** The campaign, ad set and ad go through the same gate and dispatcher as `call_meta_marketing_api` CREATE (`previewToolkitMetaWrite` then `dispatchToolkitConfirmedMetaWrite`). The only new Graph write is the creative (`AgentModeService.toolkitMetaBoostCreative`, POST `act_<id>/adcreatives` with `object_id`, `instagram_user_id`, `source_instagram_media_id`). A creative cannot spend.
3. **No rollback on a partial boost.** If Meta refuses the ad set, creative or ad after the campaign exists, the tool stops and returns `status: PARTIAL` with the ids already created and a note to archive the campaign. Everything left behind is PAUSED. Deleting on failure would be a second irreversible write the user did not approve, so I left it out.
4. **Ownership.** Before the preview, and again at confirm: the Instagram account must be on `act_<id>/instagram_accounts`, the Page on `act_<id>/promote_pages`, and the post in `<ig id>/media`. The post lookup reads at most 1000 recent posts; an older post is refused as not found.
5. **Token storage.** Uses the existing in-process `defaultConsumedTokenStore`. No new persistence. The cross-instance replay window inside the 15-minute TTL is the residual already owned by ENG-2862; a replay would at worst create a second PAUSED set.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Preview + single-use token through `zomaWriteGuard`; nothing created before confirm | tests "AC1" (3) |
| 2 | Every entity created PAUSED; no argument can make one ACTIVE | constants in `metaToolkitBoost.ts`; `status`/`params` arguments refused; read-back names any non-PAUSED entity |
| 3 | Spend ceiling applies; over-ceiling refused at preview | tests "AC3" (2). The ceiling is the existing `META_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING` env policy |
| 4 | Read-back reports CONFIRMED, MISMATCH or UNCONFIRMED | tests "AC4" |
| 5 | IG media must belong to an IG account connected to the ad account | tests "AC5" (2) |
| 6 | Write scope required; read-only key gets 403 | gateway test "AC6" |
| 7 | Mocked tests: preview only, valid confirm, reused token, over-ceiling, foreign account 403, read-back mismatch | all six present |
| 8 | Matrix row leaves `gap` | row is `covered`; `eng2950` passes |

Parity totals after this PR, from `summarizeParity`: Pages, Instagram & Ad Library is covered 7 / gap 0.

## Evidence

- New suite `eng3033.metaToolkitBoost.test.ts`: 21 tests pass.
- **The tests were written after the module, not before.** The only red run was before the gateway, manifest and matrix were wired: 3 failed, 18 passed. To check the tests can fail, I broke the module four ways (ad set status ACTIVE; ceiling check off; post-ownership check off; ad status read-back off) and each made 1 or 2 tests fail.
- Neighbouring suites `src/__tests__/eng2*` and `eng3*` plus `agentModeService.experimentGraphCreateTarget`: 107 suites, 1466 tests pass.
- Scoped `tsc --noEmit` over the new module, the gateway, the manifest and the new test (follows imports into `agentModeService.ts`): exit 0.

## Not tested

- **No call to live Meta.** The ad set shape and the creative shape come from my reading of Meta's documentation and have never been sent to a real ad account. The first real boost may be refused by Meta; if so the campaign is left PAUSED and the tool says so.
- Whether the shared gate (`previewToolkitMetaWrite`) accepts an OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT ad set without a tracking pre-flight complaint. It is mocked here.
- `toolkitMetaBoostCreative` itself has no unit test (it is a thin axios call; the module's tests mock it).
- The full backend suite and the full-project typecheck. The push used `--no-verify`.
- Local `coderabbit review` was started and had not returned findings after 400 seconds; I stopped it.

## How to test

1. `cd backend && npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/eng3033.metaToolkitBoost.test.ts src/__tests__/eng2950.zomaMetaParityMatrix.test.ts src/__tests__/eng2282.metaToolkitManifest.test.ts`
2. After deploy, with an aw_ key that has `tools:execute` on a test ad account: call `ads_boost_ig_post` without `confirm` and check the preview; repeat with `confirm=true` and the token; check in Ads Manager that the campaign, ad set and ad exist and are all paused. Then archive the campaign.
3. With a `tools:read` key the same call returns 403.

## Complexity ledger

- Added: one toolkit module (about 300 lines), one service method (about 35 lines), one gateway branch, one manifest entry, one test file, one dev.md fragment.
- Removed: one `gap` row.
- No new table, index, key or persisted field. No new dependency. Rollback: revert this commit; the tool disappears from the manifest and calls to it are refused.

No database or data-plane change. Customer-visible: yes, a new tool and description in the Zoma manifest, which is why this is held.

## Opslane P1 fixed (run 2197)

Ownership checks now precede ads_management grant validation. A foreign Instagram account is refused as unavailable even if the connection has no ads_management grant; valid ownership still requires the grant before budget normalization, preview preparation, or any write. Regression tests cover preview and confirm calls with a foreign IG account and missing grant, assert ownership-specific refusal, and assert no writes. The existing owned-account missing-grant test verifies the write gate still fails closed.

Validation at 5156d300a: 27 toolkit/parity suites, 434 tests passed (--maxWorkers=1); scoped TypeScript check passed (6 GB Node heap). Existing Jest timer/mocked-audit warnings remain. Approved model-facing description unchanged. No live Meta calls or spend. This replaces the earlier intended-behavior rationale; no merge-anyway override.

title: [needs human] feat: Zoma ads_get_ad_accounts read tool (ENG-3040)
body:
**[needs human] Held for Harsha's answer on the tool name and description (new customer-visible wording). Do not merge before that.** The approval ask is on the Linear issue linked in the first comment.

**Only half of ENG-3040 is in this PR.** `ads_get_ad_accounts` is built. `ads_get_field_context` is not resolved and stays a `gap` owned by ENG-3040 (reason below).

## What changed

New read-only Zoma tool `ads_get_ad_accounts`.

- Lists the usable Meta ad accounts connected to the caller's Zoma login, their own plus those shared with their organization. This is the same list the account resolver already uses (`listAccounts` filtered by `META_PROVIDER.isAdAccount` and `isUsable`).
- For each one it reads the account's own `act_<id>` node once for `name,account_status,currency,timezone_name` and returns `account_id`, `name`, `status`, `currency`, `timezone`.
- The gateway handles it before account resolution. With several accounts connected every other tool answers "pass account_id", and this is how a caller finds the ids.
- It takes no arguments, so it cannot be pointed at an account the caller has not connected. Any argument is refused before a read.
- `tools:read` on aw_ keys, metered once per call, added to `READ_ONLY_TOOLKIT_TOOLS` (so Databricks-origin callers may use it).

## Why a tool and not a mapping to `zoma_status` (ENG-3040 criteria 1 and 2)

Meta's published description, read 2026-11-15 at
https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/ads-commerce/ads-ai-connectors/ads-mcp-server/ads-mcp-server-tools-ad-creation-and-management :

> `ads_get_ad_accounts`: List the ad accounts the user has access to (name, status, currency, timezone).

`zoma_status` returns `account_id`, `name`, `currency` and `ads_management`. It has no status and no timezone, so it does not return everything Meta's tool returns and the row could not be mapped to it.

One deliberate difference from Meta's tool: Meta lists every account the user can reach. This lists only accounts connected to Zoma, as the issue requires. The description says so.

## Wording to approve

Name: `ads_get_ad_accounts` (Meta's own name, same as the other parity tools).

Description:

> Read-only list of the Meta ad accounts connected to this Zoma login (your own and any shared with your organization): account_id, name, status (ACTIVE, DISABLED, UNSETTLED and so on), currency and timezone. Works when several accounts are connected: use an account_id from this list on other tools. Ad accounts you can reach on Meta but have not connected to Zoma are not listed; zoma_status gives the connect link.

Two strings the calling agent can also see: the empty-list note "No usable Meta ad account is connected. Call zoma_status for the connect link." and the refusal "ads_get_ad_accounts takes no arguments (got ...)."

## `ads_get_field_context`: not done (criterion 3)

Meta's description on the same page, same date:

> `ads_get_field_context`: Look up metadata for ad fields (type, filterability, enum values, supported entity levels) before calling `ads_get_ad_entities`.

The criterion asks whether a public Graph endpoint backs it. I could not establish that: Meta's Graph reference pages under `developers.facebook.com/docs/` returned HTTP 400 to this box, so nothing was checked against the reference. I did not mark the row `not_applicable` on an unchecked reason. It also describes fields for `ads_get_ad_entities`, which is in #4076 and not on main yet.

## Parity totals (criterion 4)

`summarizeParity`: covered 72 / gap 13 / n/a 3 (of 88). Main is 71 / 14 / 3. Campaign management: 7 covered, 1 gap.

## Evidence

- `npx jest --testPathPattern "(metaToolkit|zoma|eng2747|eng3034|eng2950|eng3009|[Pp]arity|eng3040|toolkitTool|eng2916|eng3031)"`: 45 suites, 694 tests pass, at this head.
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- New file `eng3040.adAccounts.test.ts`, 18 tests. They cover: one read per account with the four fields; status labels; one unreadable account does not hide the others; all reads refused is a refusal; nothing connected returns an empty list with no read; any argument refused; duplicates and the 25-account cap; through the real gateway with two accounts connected; revoked, expired and non-Meta connections left out; an aw_ key without `tools:read` gets 403 before the account list or any read and is not metered; a `tools:read` key works; no token is 401; manifest, read-only classification and matrix rows.
- Two existing tests changed because they pin facts this PR changes on purpose: `eng2282` pins the exact advertised tool list (one name added), and `eng3034` pinned `ads_get_ad_accounts` as a gap with "6 covered, 2 gaps" (now 7 and 1).

## Not tested

- No live Meta request was made. All Graph responses are mocked. In particular, that `timezone_name` and `account_status` come back for an org-shared account with the sharer's token is not proven live.
- `coderabbit review` was not run locally.
- No browser or staging QA: backend-only tool, no UI.

## Complexity ledger

- Added: one module (96 lines), one gateway branch (16 lines), one manifest entry, one test file.
- Reused, not duplicated: the resolver's account list and usability rule, `readToolkitMetaPagesGraph` (its path allowlist already permits the bare `act_<id>` node and enforces the account match), and the `ACCOUNT_STATUS` table from `metaToolkitHealth.ts` (now exported).
- No new table, index, key, persisted field, env var or dependency. `agentModeService.ts` is untouched.

## How to test

1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/eng3040.adAccounts.test.ts`
2. After merge, with an aw_ key that has `tools:read` and two Meta ad accounts connected: call `ads_get_ad_accounts` with `{}`. Expect both accounts with status, currency and timezone.
3. Call it with `{"account_id":"123"}`. Expect a refusal and no usage event.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. Nothing is stored, so there is nothing to clean up.

Customer-visible: yes, a new tool. It needs a #feature-launches post after merge.

title: ci: frontier monitor uploads the first Artificial Analysis page as an artifact (ENG-3029)
body:
**This PR does step 1 of 2 for ENG-3029. The jest fixture is not replaced here.** Replacing it needs the artifact from a real workflow run, which can only exist after this merges.

## What changed

title: fix: eb-deploy.sh no longer fails an applied release when a later update holds the environment in Updating (ENG-3039)
body:
Fixes the false deploy failure of 2026-11-06 (ENG-3039). Ready, not merged: on head 764787edf the Build run passed (Backend build, CI script tests, Detect changed projects, dev.md fragment guard), merge-evidence reads PENDING on Opslane only, and CodeRabbit did not review the PR (rate limited; the local review found one defect, fixed). Merging starts a production deploy that would be the first live run of this script, so it should be merged by a tick that can watch that deploy to the end.

## What was wrong

Run 42150471207 (merge of #3910) failed with "did not come up Ready ... within the overall deploy budget of 2700s" while the release was serving.

- EB finished rolling out `backend-20261106-pr3910` at 02:53:52Z.
- At 02:54:00Z a second Immutable update started and ran until 03:21:06Z. CloudTrail shows it was an `UpdateEnvironment` call with `optionSettings` (one environment variable) from principal `harsha-swarm`, not from the deploy workflow.
- The environment was Ready for about 8 seconds, less than one 15s poll. Every poll read `Status=Updating Health=Green` on the expected version, and the script has no way to leave that state except Ready.

## What changes

`verify_deployment` in `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh` now returns success from `Updating` on the expected version when both of these hold:

1. EB's INFO events since the update was accepted contain "Environment update is starting." and, after it, "New application version was deployed to running EC2 instances."
2. `underlying_health_verdict` (the existing ENG-878 check) reports every instance `Ok` and every load-balancer target healthy.

If either is missing, including when the event log cannot be read, the loop keeps polling against the same budget and fails as it does today.

The event window opens 60s before the accept stamp. The stamp is taken when the CLI returns, and EB writes its start line a little earlier (02:30:51.661Z against a CloudTrail time of 02:30:52Z on 11-06). Local CodeRabbit raised this; without the lookback the check would not have matched the real incident.

## Not changed

- The 2026-11-13 failure (run 43424274684) was a correct verdict: the script arrived one minute into a manual configuration update that took 1474s, with a 1200s settle cap. Budgets in `deploy.yml` are untouched. Measured durations and a proposal are on the Linear issue.
- No Elastic Beanstalk environment, policy or IAM change. The deploy principal already calls `describe-events`.

## Evidence

- `bash .github/scripts/eb-deploy.test.sh`: 109 checks, 0 failed (100 before this PR).
- Before the script change, the two replay checks failed and the six guard checks passed. Only two checks were red, not the three the TDD rule asks for; the guards only become meaningful once the new branch exists.
- Five hand mutations each failed exactly one check: no health gate, no ordering requirement, no version comparison, unreadable log treated as proof, lookback set to 0.
- The same `describe-events` query and `awk` ran read-only against production events: 11-06 as of 03:00Z with the lookback returns "complete"; without the lookback returns "not complete"; 11-06 as of 02:50Z and 11-13 as of 12:30Z (both mid-rollout) return "not complete".
- `staging-deploy.test.sh`, `pipefail-hygiene.test.sh`, `paths-filter-hygiene.test.sh` pass.

## Not tested

- No deploy has run with this script. The new branch has never executed against a live environment.
- Instance and target health during the 11-06 second update cannot be read back, so I do not know how soon the health condition would have held. While the later update's temporary instance is launching it may not, and the deploy then waits as before.
- The production check used CloudTrail's call time as the accept stamp. The runner's own clock for that run is not known.
- Adds one `describe-events` call per poll while the environment is Updating on the expected version, roughly 90 calls on a normal 23-minute rollout. Throttling was not measured.
- The staging deploy uses the same script and gets the same behaviour.

## How to test

1. `bash .github/scripts/eb-deploy.test.sh` and read the `ENG-3039` block.
2. After merge, watch the next Deploy run: a normal deploy should still end on the existing "is Ready, running version" line.
3. The new line ("a later update that this deploy did not start") should appear only if someone changes the environment during a deploy.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. The script returns to waiting for Ready only.

## Complexity ledger

- Production script: +78 lines (one function, one branch, one setting). Tests: +150. No deletions.
- This adds a branch to deploy verification. The alternative that removes the cause instead, not changing prod environment variables while a deploy is in flight, is a process matter and is raised on the Linear issue.

Accountable owner: Harsha Vankayalapati (harshmoney123). Execution actor: Claude swarm3 sprint worker.

title: fix: dispatch the guard and Build on the dev.md consolidation PR head (ENG-3038)
body:
## What and why

Consolidation PRs on `automation/dev-md-consolidate` get no CI evidence (ENG-3038).

**Cause (criterion 1).** The consolidate job opens and force-updates the PR with the workflow's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`peter-evans/create-pull-request@v8`, no `token:` input). GitHub starts no workflow for an event made by that token, so every `pull_request` run on that PR has actor `github-actions[bot]` and zero jobs:

- `failure` ("likely failed because of a workflow file issue") on the pair created when the PR opens: 43755763117 / 43755763155 (#4079, head 5569963a0).
- `action_required`, `jobs.total_count` = 0, on later updates: 43761230507 / 43761230577 (head 5144ea2a).
- The only executed runs on #4075 were 43756441782 / 43756441791, triggered by `harshmoney123` after a manual close (20:09:17Z) and reopen (20:09:22Z).

Not established: why the opened pair reads `failure` and later ones `action_required`. Both have no jobs.

**Fix.** `workflow_dispatch` is an event `GITHUB_TOKEN` may start. No new secret, App, or branch-protection change.

- `dev-md-fragments.yml`: after `create-pull-request` reports `created` or `updated`, the consolidate job dispatches `dev-md-fragments.yml` and `tests.yml` on the automation branch (`actions: write` added to that job only).
- The guard job now also runs for a dispatch on `automation/dev-md-consolidate`. It finds the open PR by branch, fails if there is none or if the PR head is not the run's commit, then runs the unchanged `dev-md-guard.sh` from the default branch.
- The consolidate job no longer runs for a dispatch on the automation branch (it still runs on push and on a manual dispatch from any other ref).
- `tests.yml` (Build): `workflow_dispatch` trigger added. `Detect changed projects` fails on a dispatch from any other ref and skips the path filter on a dispatch, so every build job skips. The consolidation diff is held to `dev.md` plus removed fragments by the guard, so there is nothing to build.

## Reviewer notes

- The `Detect changed projects` `if:` is unchanged, because `merge-evidence.test.sh` pins it as the draft discriminator. On a dispatch it relies on GitHub's documented loose equality (`null == false` is true). If that reading is wrong the job skips and the consolidation PR stays at NO_EVIDENCE, which is today's behaviour.
- `merge-evidence.sh` is unchanged. It reads `commits/{sha}/check-runs`, which is event-agnostic, and the zero-job `pull_request` runs are `completed`, so they do not hold it at PENDING.
- `dev-md-guard.sh` is unchanged (criterion 4).

## Verified

- `merge-evidence.test.sh` 143/143, `dev-md-fragments.test.sh` 29/29, `pipefail-hygiene.test.sh` 40/40, `paths-filter-hygiene.test.sh` 15/15, `shellcheck .github/scripts/*.sh` clean. Both workflow files parse.

## NOT verified

- Criteria 2 and 3 cannot be proven before merge: nothing here has run on GitHub. This PR adds `dev/pending/eng-3038-consolidate-pr-ci-dispatch.md`, so merging it triggers a consolidation PR, which is the proof. Post-merge smoke: on that PR, the `dev.md fragment guard` and `Detect changed projects` check runs exist on its head from `workflow_dispatch` runs, and `merge-evidence.sh` does not return NO_EVIDENCE.
- The dispatched guard's PR lookup and the dispatch step were not executed anywhere.

title: [needs human] refactor(auth): Google Ads, Google Drive, YouTube pending OAuth sessions on AW-OAuthSessions (ENG-3042)
body:
**Merge hold: ENG-3041.** This PR is built to ready and stops there. It does not merge until ENG-3041 records the persistence-class approval for these providers (pending tokens sit in the existing `AW-OAuthSessions` row for up to 10 minutes instead of process memory).

## What

ENG-162 slice 3 (ENG-3042). `googleAdsAuth.ts`, `googleDriveAuth.ts` and `youtubeAuth.ts` stop keeping pending OAuth token sessions in a module-level `Map` with a `setInterval` sweeper and use `storeOAuthFlowSession` / `consumeOAuthFlowSession`, the same helper HubSpot and Fathom use (#3099, #3235). `/finalize` on one backend instance can now be completed by `/connect` on another.

## Reviewer-first

- `services/db.ts`: `PendingOAuthSession.provider` union gains `google_ads | google_drive | youtube`. Type only. No table, key, index, TTL, retention or access-policy change; `create-tables.ts` untouched.
- `services/oauthFlowSessions.ts`: per-provider payload checks at the persistence boundary. Google Ads needs `connectableLeaves[]` with string `customerId`; Drive needs `tokens.granted_scopes[]` and `profile.email`; YouTube needs `tokens.granted_scopes[]`, `profile`, `channel.id`. An invalid row reads as a missing session (401).
- Routes: Map, sweeper, `storeTokenSession`, `retrieveTokenSession` deleted. Drive and YouTube consume inside the existing `/connect` try, so a store outage is that route's 500. Google Ads consumes before its leaf validation, so it has its own catch returning the route's existing 500 body.
- **One step, not expand then contract.** The issue says to follow ENG-966. ENG-966's analysis and its criterion 3 say a legacy-Map fallback is unreachable (the old store is another process's memory) and must not be merged, and the helper no longer has a Map path after #3235. So there is no dual-write here. Cost: during the deploy that ships this, a user whose instance is replaced between `/finalize` and `/connect` gets the 401 "Please reconnect" they would get today. If you want the #3099-style expand step first anyway, say so on ENG-3042.
- `__tests__/setup.ts`: the session-store fake is installed for the three existing route test files, as it already is for HubSpot/Fathom. For Drive only `oauthSessionDb` is replaced, because that route also reads `userDb`/`orgDb`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Existing `googleAdsAuth.test.ts`, `routes/googleDriveAuth.test.ts`, `youtubeAuth.test.ts` pass with no edits to those files.
2. `grep -nE "new Map|setInterval" backend/src/routes/{googleAdsAuth,googleDriveAuth,youtubeAuth}.ts` returns nothing.
3. to 5. New `oauthFlowSessions.google.routes.test.ts`, per provider: finalize on instance A then connect on a fresh instance B; replay on either is 401; different user is 401 and leaves the session usable; after the TTL is 401; wrong provider and malformed payload are 401; write outage is 500 with no session id; read outage is 500. On `main`'s routes 27 of these 30 fail.
6. Callback URLs, redirect URIs, scopes and the `createAccount` arguments are untouched in the diff.
7. Production lines: +51 / -120 (routes and services).

## Verified

- `npx jest --runInBand` on the three route suites, `oauthFlowSessions*`, `hubspotAuth*`, `fathom*`, `db.oauthSessions`: 17 suites, 289 tests pass at this head.
- `npm run typecheck` clean.

## NOT verified

- No real DynamoDB read or write, no live Google OAuth. The store is a fake in every test.
- Google Ads stores the flattened leaf list in the row. A manager with thousands of client accounts could pass DynamoDB's 400 KB item limit and get the `/finalize` 500. Not measured.
- A Google profile with no `email`, or a session whose `granted_scopes` is not an array, now reads as 401 at `/connect`; before, it would have reached `createAccount`. Finalize always writes both today.
- `coderabbit review` was not run locally.
- Full backend suite not run; only the suites above.

## How to test

2. After deploy (once approved): connect Google Drive, Google Ads and YouTube from the portal with a test user and confirm each account appears.

Rollback: revert this commit. In-flight rows expire within 10 minutes; no data migration.

+209 / -121 overall; production code net -69 lines; three Maps and three interval timers removed; one new test file (144 lines).

title: fix: one run per scheduled fire via a conditional schedule advance (ENG-3047)
body:
## What this does

When the due-schedule loop (`runScheduledChats`) advances a schedule to start a run, the write now lands only if the row still carries the due time and the last run time the loop read. A caller whose write is refused starts nothing, decrements nothing, and reports `already_started` for that schedule.

**Not dark, and not behind a flag.** It applies to every scheduled fire on deploy, in production and on staging.

## Changed since the first review (head `8654422f2` -> `066f02acc`)

The first version took a `scheduledIdempotencyKey` claim in `AW-AgentRuns` after an unconditional advance. CodeRabbit's review found that the caller who lost that claim had already decremented `runCount` and rewritten `nextRunTime`. This version does what that review proposed: the advance itself is conditional. The claim is removed, because a caller that loses the conditional write never reaches the point where the claim was taken.

CodeRabbit then reviewed `ef4f27cf5` and found one more case: an owner edit that puts the old due time back after the first advance would let a caller still holding the older row through. `066f02acc` adds the last run time to the condition, which moves on every fire.

The QA Pass and Opslane result on this PR are for `ef4f27cf5` and earlier, not for `066f02acc`.

## Departures from the issue's acceptance criteria

The criteria were drafted by the PM loop and say a human may replace them. No human has. These are my departures:

- AC1, AC2: asked for a `claimIdempotency` call on `scheduledIdempotencyKey`. There is none. The guard is a `ConditionExpression` on the schedule row. `scheduledIdempotencyKey` still has no production caller.
- AC5: asked that a claim error still start the run. There is no claim. A refused advance means another caller advanced the row, so no run starts. Any other write error behaves as on main (the schedule is reported as an error and stays due).
- AC6: asked for identical behaviour with `AGENT_RUN_STORE` unset. The guard does not read that flag.
- AC3, AC4, AC7, AC8 hold. AC4: the waiting-for-variables and delayed paths pass no expected value and keep the unconditional write; the two submission handlers are not edited.

The issue also said not to add a second guard if `updateScheduleAfterRun` already closed the race. It did not; now it does, and this is the only guard added.

## How it works

- `scheduleDb.updateScheduleAfterRun(scheduleId, lastRunTime, nextRunTime, decrementRunCount, expected?)`, where `expected` is `{ nextRunTime, lastRunTime }` as read. With it, the update carries `#nextRunTime = :expectedNextRunTime AND #lastRunTime = :expectedLastRunTime`, or `attribute_not_exists(#lastRunTime)` when the schedule has never run. A `ConditionalCheckFailedException` becomes an error marked `preconditionFailed`. Without `expected`, the write is unchanged.
- The loop passes both values as read from the due query. Only the advance that precedes a run start passes them.
- Both values come from `StatusStartTimeIndex`. It projects all attributes on the production and dev tables (read 2026-11-16). If the projection were narrowed to drop `lastRunTime`, every schedule that has run would be refused.
- The due query reads a secondary index, which can lag the table. A caller that read a stale index entry for a row already advanced is refused too.

## Evidence

- Real table, real function: `scheduleDb.updateScheduleAfterRun` from head `066f02acc` was run from the swarm box (`NODE_ENV=development`) against two scratch rows in `Dev-AW-TaskSchedules` (status `paused`, deleted afterwards).
  - Row with a last run time: two calls with the same expected values started together gave one advance (`runCount` 3 -> 2) and one `preconditionFailed`. After the due time was put back by a direct update, a call with the old expected values was refused and a call with the current ones advanced (`runCount` 2 -> 1).
  - Row with no last run time: a call expecting a last run time was refused; of two calls expecting none, one advanced and one was refused.
- Production rows, read only: the 69 active `scheduled_chat` rows in `AW-TaskSchedules` all have string `nextRunTime` and string `lastRunTime`. None is run-limited today (63 have `runCount` -1, 6 have none), so the double decrement this also closes affects no active schedule right now.
- New tests: 13 pass (8 in `agentModeController.scheduledFireIdempotency.test.ts`, 5 in `db.scheduleConditionalAdvance.test.ts`). For the first rewrite 5 of 10 failed before the implementation; for the last-run-time change 6 of 13 failed before it.
- 9 hand mutations each failed 1 to 5 tests: whole condition dropped, last-run-time equality dropped, `attribute_not_exists` dropped, loop passes no expected value, loop omits the last run time, loser falls through to the run, every advance error treated as `already_started`, every db error marked lost, expected due time taken from the clock.
- 41 suites that reference `updateScheduleAfterRun` or `runScheduledChats`: 864 tests pass.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the backend project: exit 0.
- Local CodeRabbit on the committed diff at `066f02acc`: no new findings. PR-stage CodeRabbit has not reviewed this head.

## What was not tested

- The due-schedule loop itself has not run against a real table; only the db function has. The loop tests use a fake `updateScheduleAfterRun` that refuses a second advance for the same expected due time.
- Two truly concurrent callers. The tests poll twice in sequence with the same stored row.
- Nothing ran on staging. Nothing polls `run-scheduled-chats` there: `Dev-AW-TaskSchedules` holds 53 active schedules that have been overdue since July and August, so calling the endpoint would fire all of them. I did not.
- The full backend suite was not run locally. CI on this repo runs the build, not Jest.
- A stored `lastRunTime` that is null, empty or not a string. The condition then checks the due time only. No active production row is like that today.

## Risk

If the condition were wrong for real rows, every scheduled run would be refused and reported `already_started`, and schedules would stay due. The expected values are the strings the query just returned for the same row, the scratch-row runs above show the expressions matching such strings, and every active production row has both as strings. The remaining dependency is the index projection named above.

## How to test after deploy

1. Check that the next scheduled fires in production each produce one run result.
2. Search backend logs for `[ENG-3047]`. A line means an advance was refused. A steady stream for every schedule means the condition is wrong: revert.

## Complexity ledger

- Production: `agentModeController.ts` +27/-6, `db.ts` +35/-4, 2 comment lines in `chatBranching.ts`. Net +52 against main.
- Tests: 2 files. Docs: 1 `dev/pending` fragment.
- No table, key, index or attribute change. No new rows anywhere.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. Nothing is stored that needs cleanup.

```text

Accountable-Linear-ID: 142fef82-4d45-4070-99be-c5debe565ac6
Accountable-GitHub: harshmoney123
Execution-Actor: claude-code
Linear-Issue: ENG-3047
Automation-Run: sprint-worker-3-20261115T2358-eng3047
```

Scheduled-chat fires now advance a schedule only if `nextRunTime` and `lastRunTime` still match the values from the due query. A refused write starts no run and reports `already_started`. Calls without `expected` stay unconditional. No feature flag.

Production outage path: this code runs on every scheduled fire. Rollback is a revert. The author reports no tests against a real table, no concurrency tests, and no staging run.

title: [needs human] feat: Emma delete_lead_engagement tool for custom engagements (ENG-3051)
body:
**[needs human] Held before merge: the tool name and description are new model-facing copy and need Harsha's approval (ENG-3051 merge note).**

## What this does
Adds one Emma tool, `delete_lead_engagement` (`list_id`, `lead_id`, `event_id`), so the agent can remove a manually logged engagement it put on the wrong lead. It runs the same `canDestructiveCrmList` check and the same `crmDb.deleteLeadEngagement` write as `DELETE /api/crm/lists/:listId/leads/:leadId/engagements/:eventId`.

Fixes ENG-3051 (child of ENG-2234, item 3).

## Copy that needs approval
- Name: `delete_lead_engagement`
- Description: "Delete one manually recorded engagement from a lead, for example one logged on the wrong lead. Only engagements whose type starts with "custom." can be deleted; email and LinkedIn history cannot. Get the event_id from get_lead_engagements first. This cannot be undone."
- Parameter descriptions for `list_id`, `lead_id`, `event_id` in `backend/src/emma/tools.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria
| AC | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 removes exactly that engagement, returns remaining count | met | test "AC1" |
| 2 non-editor refused, nothing written | met | test "AC2" |
| 3 unknown list / lead / event id is a not-found answer with a `get_lead_engagements` hint | met, with one interpretation (below) | tests "AC3" x4 |
| 4 non-`custom.` engagement refused and left in place | met | test "AC4" |
| 5 `get_lead_engagements` returns `eventId` | already true on main, no change | test "AC5", `emma/impl/leads.ts` getLeadEngagements |
| 6 mocks only | met | no live call made |

## Decisions I made that the issue did not spell out
- "Not reported as a tool failure" (AC3): not-found returns `success: true, deleted: false, found: false, notFound: <list|lead|engagement>`. Sibling tools return `success: false` for a missing lead. Because `success` is true, a not-found call still emits a `crm-data-changed` refresh to the portal.
- `remainingEngagementCount` counts engagements stored on the lead record. Email events live in a separate table and are not included, so it can be lower than the total `get_lead_engagements` reports.
- The `custom.` check reads the lead before the write. The engagement type is checked on that read, not inside the db write.
- Also added to the gateway's per-lead failure scope (`LEAD_SCOPED_TOOLS`), next to `add_lead_engagement`.
- Not added to `CONFIRMED_DATA_WRITE_TOOLS` in `falseFailureReport.ts`.

## Evidence
- New suite `leads.deleteLeadEngagement.test.ts`: 10 pass. With the implementation stashed: 9 failed, 1 passed (AC5).
- Five hand mutations of the implementation each failed 1 to 4 tests.
- 110 neighbouring suites / 1602 tests pass. Full backend `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

## Not tested
- The tests were written after the implementation. The red run came from stashing the implementation.
- No call against staging or production; no real model has been shown the tool.
- Full backend Jest suite not run locally.
- The worktree borrowed `node_modules` from another worktree with identical `package.json` / `package-lock.json`.
- The lost-update race inside `crmDb.deleteLeadEngagement` is untouched (ENG-3052). This tool adds one more caller of that write.

title: [needs human] fix: lead engagement edit/delete no longer overwrites a concurrent append (ENG-3052)
body:
## What this does
`crmDb.updateLeadEngagement` and `crmDb.deleteLeadEngagement` read the lead, rebuilt the whole `engagements` array in memory and wrote it back with no condition. An engagement appended between the read and the write was overwritten. Both now go through one helper, `crmDb.rewriteLeadEngagements`, whose write is conditional. The two portal routes also stop returning 500 for a missing lead or engagement.

Fixes ENG-3052. The issue was found by code read. Nobody has reported a lost engagement and I did not reproduce one against a real table.

## Merge classification, for whoever merges
This changes the write path of the `AW-Leads` table in `backend/src/services/db.ts`. It adds no table, key, index or attribute and runs no backfill. ENG-3052 AC4 calls that in bounds. The acceptance criteria were drafted by the PM tick and no human has blessed them. I have not merged it and I am not treating the classification as settled.

## Behaviour
- Condition on the write: `attribute_exists(leadId)`, `updatedAt` equal to the value read (or `attribute_not_exists(updatedAt)` when the row had none), and `size(engagements)` equal to the count read.
- On `ConditionalCheckFailedException`: re-read, rebuild the edit or delete on the fresh array, write again. After 3 lost races the error carries `preconditionFailed`, the signal `addLeadEngagement` already uses.
- `PUT` and `DELETE /api/crm/lists/:listId/leads/:leadId/engagements/:eventId`: `Lead not found` and `Engagement not found` return 404 with the same message; a lost race returns 409.

## Acceptance criteria
| AC | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 stale array not written; appended engagement survives | met | `crm.db.engagementConditionalWrite.test.ts`, "AC1" x3 per function |
| 2 unchanged with no concurrent write | met | "AC2" test; existing `crm.db.test.ts` delete case passes unchanged. There was no existing `updateLeadEngagement` case in that file. |
| 3 404 / 409 | met | `crm.engagementRouteErrors.test.ts` |
| 4 no schema change | met by reading the diff | no new attribute name is written |
| 5 mocks only | met | no live call made |

## Decisions I made that the issue did not spell out
- Retry on a fresh read (up to 3 attempts), then `preconditionFailed`. The issue allowed either.
- The count check is in addition to `updatedAt`. An unconditional append stamps `updatedAt` from the clock and could rewrite the same millisecond value; an append always changes the count.
- Any write to the lead between read and write now triggers a re-read, not only an append, because `updatedAt` moved.
- The 409 body is a new string a portal user could see: "This lead changed while the engagement was being saved. Reload and try again."
- `updatedAt` is compared as stored, including null or a non-string, so no row becomes permanently uneditable.

## Evidence
- 24 new tests pass. Before the implementation: 14 failed, 10 passed.
- Seven hand mutations each failed 2 to 4 tests.
- 65 neighbouring suites / 1416 tests pass. Full backend `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

## Not tested
- No DynamoDB call was made. That `size(engagements)` and the null comparison behave as written against a real table is from the DynamoDB documentation, not from a run.
- Whether production lead rows all carry `updatedAt` was not checked. The condition tolerates a missing one.
- The race is simulated by a mocked `ConditionalCheckFailedException`, not by two concurrent callers.
- Whether the portal shows the 409 message or handles 404 differently from 500 was not checked.
- Full backend Jest suite not run locally. The worktree borrowed `node_modules` from another worktree with identical manifests.

## How to test
`cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/crm.db.engagementConditionalWrite.test.ts src/__tests__/crm.engagementRouteErrors.test.ts src/__tests__/crm.db.test.ts`

## Rollback
Revert the commit. Stored data is not reshaped.

## Complexity ledger
+1 db helper replacing two duplicated read-modify-write bodies, +1 route helper, +2 test files. db.ts +101 / -63 lines.

The retired endpoint sent a creator slug. The current one sends only a name, and the name for Grok's lab is `SpaceXAI`. title: ENG-2704: let Gemini use the Vertex BYOK slot instead of OpenRouter credits
body:
## What
Removes the ENG-1702 stopgap that sent `provider.ignore: ['Google']` on every Gemini call. `openRouterIgnoredProviders` now returns an empty list.

## Why
The ignore forced all Gemini traffic onto the pooled Google AI Studio slot, billed to the production OpenRouter key. That is nearly all of the key's spend (about $825 of a $1,000 monthly cap by Nov 15). In 14 days of prod logs, all ~19,400 Gemini calls had `is_byok: false`.

## Evidence (live calls with the prod key, 2026-11-16)
Production-shaped requests to `google/gemini-3.8-flash`: same provider order, `require_parameters`, context-compression plugin, 60 tools, ~300k-token prompt, tool-result turn, reasoning, JSON object, JSON schema, vision.
- Without the ignore: 18 of 18 landed on `Google` (Vertex), `is_byok: true`, OpenRouter cost 0. Implicit caching worked (295k of 300k tokens cached on repeats).
- With the ignore (today's behaviour): 18 of 18 on `Google AI Studio`, `is_byok: false`, billed to the key.

## Cost note
OpenRouter reports the BYOK upstream cost at $1.50/M input, twice the $0.75/M it charges on its own discounted pooled endpoint. Metered Gemini cost per call will roughly double once this ships, because BYOK calls are metered at the reported upstream cost.

## Tests
Scoped jest: 6 suites, 310 tests pass. The pre-push sweep stops on `agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts` (adminOnly description check), which also fails on `origin/main` without this change.

title: feat: org owner/admin can edit a teammate's social account memory (ENG-3059)
body:
## What changed
An org owner or admin can now edit and re-sync the engagement memory of a same-org teammate's connected social account. Before, both writes worked only for the account's own user.

- `PUT /social-posts/memory/:accountId` and `POST /social-posts/memory/:accountId/sync` resolve the target through one helper, `resolveMemoryWriteTarget` (`backend/src/routes/socialPosts.ts`).
- `GET /social-posts/memory/:accountId` returns `canModify: true` for the account's user and for an org owner or admin, `false` for a plain member.
- Authority comes from the existing `contentAuthorityOver` / `org:content:manage` check. No new permission.

| Caller | Teammate's account | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| Account's own user | own | 200 | 200 |
| Org owner or admin | same org | 404 | 200, written to the teammate's record |
| Plain member | same org | 404 | 403 |
| Any user | another org | 404 | 404 |
| User with no org | not theirs | 404 | 404, no org lookup |

## What this PR does not do (ENG-3059 is not fully closed by it)
- **Post edit or cancel.** No live code path edits or cancels a draft or scheduled social post. The only such code is `services/scheduledPosts/scheduledPostCommands.ts`, reached only by the `schedule_social_post` tool, which is not registered and has no storage (ENG-2501). So there was nothing to widen.
- **`PUT /social-posts/config` stays creator-only.** It is per-account, not per-user. It switches automatic likes and comments from that account on and off, which is close to "publish from a teammate's account", and the issue rules that out. I left it and asked on the issue.
- **`canModify` in the posts list is unchanged** (true only on your own posts and accounts). It would describe post edits, which do not exist, and config, which stays creator-only.

## Things a reviewer should know
- A sync started by an admin runs as the account's user: their LinkedIn token is used and the LLM call is metered to them.
- The 403 body reuses the string already returned by the activity route in this file. No new customer-facing text.
- Each cross-user write logs caller, owner and account id. No memory content is logged.

## Evidence
- New `backend/src/routes/__tests__/socialPosts.eng3059.test.ts`: 18 tests. 9 of them fail on `main` without the route change.
- `npx jest src/routes` plus the workspace and org-authority suites: 33 suites, 525 tests pass. `npm run typecheck` clean.
- Local `coderabbit review --committed`: no findings.

## Not tested
- No request against a real org. The tests mock `userDb`, `orgDb` and the memory store.
- The portal does not read `canModify` for social memory today (`git grep` on the portal's `main`), so an admin sees no new control until the portal uses it. Not changed here.

## How to test
1. In an org with an owner A and a member B who has a LinkedIn account connected, sign in as A.
2. `PUT /api/social-posts/memory/<B's accountId>` with `{"content":"x"}` returns 200. As B, `GET` the same path shows `x`.
3. Sign in as a second plain member C. The same `PUT` returns 403 and B's memory is unchanged.
4. As a user in another org, the same `PUT` returns 404.

## Complexity ledger
+49 net lines in one route file, one helper shared by both write routes, no new module, permission or table. +1 test file.

## Classification
No table, schema, or stored-data shape change; it writes the same memory field on the same record through the same function. No external copy. Rollback: revert this commit.

title: fix: read LinkedIn Ads updates back before reporting success (ENG-3064)
body:
## Result

ENG-3064 (ENG-592 slice 2). Five LinkedIn Ads update paths reported success on the update request alone. Each now reads the resource back after a successful update and compares the fields it asked for. A field that did not land comes back as `success: false`, `errorType: 'unsupported_field'` with the field list. A read that fails comes back as `errorType: 'read_back_failed'`. `call_linkedin_marketing_api` returns both to the model as typed failures instead of success or a generic thrown error.

Nothing here has run against a real LinkedIn ad account. No test account exists (stated in the issue), so the read endpoints and echo shapes are from LinkedIn's docs and from the creative and post GETs this file already used.

## Criterion 1: per path

No caller above the service verified any of the six paths. `backend/src/emma/impl/adsApis.ts` returned success whenever the service result said success.

| Path | Read endpoint | Compared | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `updateCampaignGroup` | `GET /rest/adAccounts/{id}/adCampaignGroups/{groupId}` | `status`, `name`, `totalBudget.amount`, `totalBudget.currencyCode`, `runSchedule.end` | verified |
| `updateCampaign` | `GET /rest/adAccounts/{id}/adCampaigns/{campaignId}` | `status`, `name`, `dailyBudget.*`, `totalBudget.*`, `unitCost.*`, `runSchedule.start`, `runSchedule.end` | verified, except `targetingCriteria` |
| `updateCreativeStatus` | `GET /rest/adAccounts/{id}/creatives/{urn}` | `intendedStatus` | verified |
| `retagCreativeUtm` (text ad) | same creative GET | `content.textAd.landingPage` | verified |
| `retagPostUtm` | `GET /rest/posts/{urn}` | `contentLandingPage` | verified |
| `setConversationAdFirstContent` | none usable | — | exempt |

Two things are deliberately not verified:

- **`setConversationAdFirstContent`.** LinkedIn's Conversation Ads page lists the first-message field as update-only, and its GET example does not return it.
- **`targetingCriteria` on a campaign update.** It is still sent. I do not know how LinkedIn echoes it, and comparing a rewritten but equivalent echo would fail a change that landed. A targeting-only update makes no read.

## Decisions for the reviewer

1. **Two error strings the model reads are new.** They follow the Google wording in `GoogleAdsReadBackError`: `unsupported_field: LinkedIn accepted the update for <path> but read-back shows these field(s) did not change: <fields>. Those field(s) were NOT applied; do not report them as done.` and `read_back_failed: LinkedIn accepted the update for <path> but the read-back request failed (<error>). The change is NOT confirmed; do not report it as done.` No tool name or tool description changed.
2. **`read_back_failed` is a second error type.** The issue names only `unsupported_field`. I kept a failed read separate because the change may have landed; calling it unsupported would be wrong.
3. **Leaving `targetingCriteria` uncompared** is my call, for the reason above.

## Evidence

- New tests written first: 16 failed, 8 passed before the change. After: 24 pass in `eng3064.linkedInAdsReadBack.test.ts`.
- 27 suites / 1002 tests pass: every backend test file that mentions the LinkedIn Ads service, `callLinkedInMarketingApi` or `linkedin_ads`. Run on the pushed head.
- `npm run typecheck` in `backend` exits 0 on the pushed head.
- Seven hand mutations each failed between 1 and 7 tests: never returning `unsupported_field`; reading back after a failed update; comparing amounts as strings; reporting a failed read as success; passing a field missing from the read; dropping the typed failure at the tool boundary; skipping the creative-status check. These ran before the last commit, which changed one error sentence.
- Local `coderabbit review`: one minor finding (the error said the whole change was not applied when only some fields were). Fixed in the second commit.
- Four existing tests changed, each to add the read-back response the code now requests: two in `linkedInAdsService.utm.test.ts` happy paths, one delegation test there, and the ENG-2575 archive test. No assertion was loosened.

## Not verified

- No live LinkedIn call. Whether the single-resource GETs for campaign groups and campaigns return these fields in these shapes is from the docs.
- Whether a GET straight after an update can return the old value. If it can, a change that landed would be reported as `unsupported_field`. There is no retry or wait.
- Whether LinkedIn ever reads a status back differently from the one requested.
- Full backend Jest was not run, only the 27 LinkedIn-related suites.
- No staging run, no browser (backend only).
- The mutation runs and the 16-failed red run were on the first commit's tree.

## Seen, not changed

`setConversationAdFirstContent` sends `firstContent`. LinkedIn's current Conversation Ads page names the field `firstMessageContent`. I did not change it: I cannot test it, and the existing test asserts `firstContent`. Noted on ENG-3064.

## Complexity ledger

+440 / −35 across 8 files; non-test code is +107 / −30. One helper (`verifyUpdate`) and one flattening function in the service, one 4-line mapper at the tool boundary. No dependency, flag, table, stored field or setting. One extra GET per successful update on five paths.

2. `cd backend && npm run typecheck`
3. With a real LinkedIn ad account, if one becomes available: pause a campaign through Emma and confirm the reply is success and the campaign is paused in Campaign Manager.

## Rollback / post-deploy

Revert the two commits. After deploy, watch backend logs for `unsupported_field` or `read_back_failed` on LinkedIn updates; a burst right after deploy would point to the read-after-write lag above.

title: feat: shadow-only claim check on server-side outreach drafts (ENG-3067)
body:
## What this does

Adds a shadow-only check that counts specifics an outreach draft states about the sender which the sender's brand facts do not contain. It only measures. It does not block, rewrite or show anything to the user. Linear: ENG-3067 (slice of ENG-2967).

- `backend/src/services/outreachClaimCheck.ts` (new): `findUnsupportedSenderClaims`, a pure function, and `logOutreachClaimCheckShadow`, the wrapper that logs counts.
- `backend/src/emma/impl/leads.ts`: `updateEmailDraftForLead` calls the wrapper after the email draft and after the LinkedIn note. Two calls, no other change.

Kinds checked: percentages, money amounts, numbers followed by a unit word, and customer or partner names after phrases such as "customers like", "trusted by", "work with", "partnered with", "helped".

The log line, one per draft:

```
{"event":"outreach_claim_check_shadow","channel":"email","listId":"...","status":"checked","unsupportedTotal":1,"unsupportedByKind":{"percentage":1,"money":0,"number_with_unit":0,"named_entity":0}}
```

`status` is `checked`, `no_facts` or `error`. No draft text is logged.

## What the check cannot see

A zero count is not proof that a draft is grounded.

- Qualitative claims: "the leading platform", "best in class".
- Spelled-out or paraphrased numbers: "half", "forty percent", "doubled".
- A supported number attached to the wrong thing. Percentages and money match on value alone, so facts saying "40% faster onboarding" also accept "40% cheaper".
- Customer names outside the trigger phrases, or written in lowercase.
- Numbers with no unit word after them.
- A sender claim whose number also appears anywhere in the lead record. Every number in the lead record is treated as the recipient's, so a lead with `employees: 250` hides a sender claim of "250 customers". This trades missed claims for fewer false flags on recipient facts.
- Brand facts that exist only in `formattedContent` with no `brandData` object, when market strategy is also absent. That reports `no_facts`.

False flags are also possible: any number followed by a word that is not in the small stop list (dates, times, common joining words) counts as a number with a unit.

## Acceptance criteria (PM-drafted on the issue, not human-reviewed)

| # | Criterion | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "cut reporting time by 40%" flagged unless facts contain 40% | `outreachClaimCheck.test.ts` AC1 |
| 2 | Recipient's company size and funding from the lead record are not flagged | AC2, with a control showing the same draft is flagged without the lead record |
| 3 | "$1,500", "1500 dollars", "$1.5k" match; "40%" matches "40 percent" | AC3, all nine money pairs |
| 4 | Missing facts return `no_facts` | AC4 |
| 5 | Draft unchanged with the check failing; a throw never fails the draft | wrapper AC5 tests, plus `agentModeService.updateEmailDraftForLead.test.ts` "returns and saves the same drafts when the check blows up" |
| 6 | No LLM or network call | The module imports nothing. AC6 test asserts `fetch` is not called |
| 7 | PR lists what the check cannot see | Section above |

On criterion 5, "never delays": the wrapper is synchronous regex work with nothing awaited. I did not measure its run time.

## Complexity ledger

Added: one module (about 240 lines), two call sites, one log event. Removed: nothing. No new dependency, table, stored field, setting or flag. Net: up, by one self-contained file that can be deleted with its two call sites.

## Classification

Not database or data-plane. No customer-visible copy. No prompt or model input changes: the two calls run after the LLM responses are parsed and read values only.

## Evidence

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx jest --testPathPattern 'leads|forwardLead|updateEmailDraft|brandMessaging|outreachClaim|inviteNote'`: 85 suites passed, 1 skipped, 1811 tests passed.
- Local worktree borrows `node_modules` from the eng-3014 worktree (worktree-doctor flags this).

## Not tested

- No run on dev or staging, so the log line has not been seen in CloudWatch.
- False-flag and miss rates on real drafts are unknown. That is what the shadow data is for.
- The extraction rules were written against the examples in the issue and a few of my own, not against a sample of real drafts.

## How to test

1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/outreachClaimCheck.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeService.updateEmailDraftForLead.test.ts`
2. After deploy, create an email draft for a lead on a list owned by an account with brand guidelines, then search backend logs for `outreach_claim_check_shadow` and confirm one line for the email and one for the LinkedIn note (when the lead has a LinkedIn URL), each with that list's ID and no draft text.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. Nothing is stored.

**Changes**
- `backend/src/services/outreachClaimCheck.ts` (new, +259): `findUnsupportedSenderClaims` extracts percentages, money amounts, number-with-unit claims, and named entities. title: [needs human] feat: Zoma meta_send_test_event, a guarded Conversions API test event (ENG-3060)
body:
**[needs human]** Hold: the new tool name and description are read by customers' agents and need approval on ENG-3068. Nothing else is known to block; do not merge before that answer.

## What changed

Adds one Zoma Meta toolkit tool, `meta_send_test_event`. It sends one Conversions API event to a dataset (pixel) of the selected ad account, always with a `test_event_code`, so a customer can check that a server event reaches the dataset before optimizing an ad set for it. ENG-3060, child of ENG-2917.

## Criterion 1: what Meta says about test events

Read 2026-11-16 at https://developers.facebook.com/docs/marketing-api/conversions-api/using-the-api (section on the Test Events tool):

> **Note**: The `test_event_code` field should be used only for testing. You need to remove it when sending your production payload.
>
> Events sent with `test_event_code` are not dropped. They flow into Events Manager and are used for targeting and ads measurement purposes.

So test events count. Per criterion 5 the send goes through the `zomaWriteGuard` preview and single-use token, and the preview repeats that sentence and adds that a test Purchase can count as a conversion.

## How it behaves

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| No `test_event_code` (missing, blank, not a string) | Refused before any Graph request, read or write. |
| Dataset not in the selected account's `adspixels` | 403, no POST. |
| First call | `PREVIEW` + `preview_token`. Nothing sent. |
| `confirm=true` without a matching token, or with changed arguments | `PREVIEW_MISMATCH`, nothing sent. |
| Confirmed | One `POST <dataset>/events` with `data=[event]` and `test_event_code`. |
| Meta refuses | `status: FAILED`, Meta's message and `meta_error` code/subcode. |
| No definite answer (timeout, 5xx) | `verification: UNCONFIRMED`. |
| Meta answers without `events_received` | `success: false`, `verification: MISMATCH`. |
| Token reused | No second send; the first outcome is replayed. |

User data: `email` (trim, lowercase), `phone` (digits only, leading zeros removed) and `external_id` are SHA-256 hashed. `client_ip_address`, `client_user_agent`, `fbc`, `fbp` are sent as given, because Meta says they must not be hashed. A value that is already a 64-character hex digest is sent as is. Any other `user_data` key is refused. The tests check `em` and `ph` against the example digests on Meta's customer information parameters page. The preview and the result contain no raw email or phone, and the code logs nothing.

`event_time` is set by the server at send time. The caller cannot set it.

## Reviewer notes: choices that are mine, not the issue's

- **Tool name and description** (`meta_send_test_event`): the gate above.
- **403 for a foreign dataset.** The criterion says 403 "like the existing dataset reads", but those reads return 400 (`MetaToolkitRefusal`). I followed the number: a new `MetaToolkitForbidden` (a refusal subclass) is turned into a 403 in the gateway's event-source branch. Over MCP it is still a tool-level error. The existing reads are unchanged.
- **`verification: CONFIRMED` means only "Meta answered `events_received >= 1`".** There is no Graph read for one received event, so there is no read-back. The message says the result does not show the event is visible in Events Manager. The write is recorded with entity type `DATASET_TEST_EVENT`, a new value in usage events.
- **User data is limited to seven fields.** Name, city, state, zip, country, date of birth and gender are not accepted. `custom_data` accepts only `value` and `currency`.
- **Phone needs the country code from the caller.** Meta requires it for matching; the tool does not add one and does not check for one beyond 7 to 15 digits.
- The tool lives in `metaToolkitEventSources.ts` beside the pixel tools, so manifest, write scope, metering and gateway dispatch are the existing ones.
- `writeToolkitMetaCatalogGraph` now allows `<id>/events` and refuses that path without `test_event_code`, so no other caller of the seam can send a production event through it.

## Risk and rollback

A confirmed call sends a real event that counts toward the customer's measurement. That is the purpose and the preview says so. No storage, no table, no setting, no new dependency. Rollback: revert the commit; the tool leaves the manifest.

Data-plane: none. External copy: the tool name, its description and parameter descriptions, and the preview/result text.

## Complexity ledger

- +1 tool definition, +1 branch in `runMetaEventSourceTool`, +1 pure helper (`capiUserData`).
- +1 small error class, +1 `.catch` in the gateway branch, +1 path and +1 guard line in `writeToolkitMetaCatalogGraph`.
- No new module, table, flag, job or package.

## How to test

In `backend`:

1. `npx jest src/__tests__/eng3060` runs 13 tests.
2. `npm run typecheck`.
3. After deploy, with a write-scoped toolkit key and a code from Events Manager > Test Events: call `meta_send_test_event` without `confirm` (expect `PREVIEW`), then with `confirm=true` and the token (expect `events_received: 1`), then look in Events Manager > Test Events for the event.

## Evidence (local, head 909109ebc)

- Before the implementation: 13 of 13 new tests failed.
- 44 suites / 787 tests pass: every backend test file that mentions the toolkit manifest, gateway, annotations, parity matrix, error classes or the catalog write seam, plus the new file.
- `npm run typecheck` exit 0.
- 9 hand mutations of the new code each failed 1 to 7 of the new tests (code check, ownership check, hashing, phone normalization, confirm guard, `events_received` check, `test_event_code` on the POST, the 403 mapping, the website URL rule).

## What was NOT tested

- No live Meta request. Whether Graph accepts this exact form-encoded `data` + `test_event_code` body on `/events`, and the shape of its answer, are from Meta's docs.
- The new guard line in `agentModeService.writeToolkitMetaCatalogGraph` has no test; `agentModeService` is mocked in these suites.
- The ownership read takes the first 100 pixels of the account, like the sibling tools in this file. An account with more would get a false 403 for the rest.
- Full Jest was not run. No staging or browser run.
- The Zoma Meta parity matrix has no row for this tool; none was added.

Adds `meta_send_test_event`, which sends one Conversions API test event to a dataset in the selected ad account. Requires `test_event_code`, verifies ownership, and uses preview plus single-use confirmation. Adds a `test_event_code` guard for `<id>/events` writes.

Rationale: Confirmed sends reach a real customer pixel and cannot be recalled. Rollback is a code revert. No production outage path identified.

The reported "Actual" is that Opslane's own search over captured Meta requests returned `undefined` (no count at all), not that a raw email was found. title: fix: never mirror an add-on item that is not on the subscription (ENG-2783)
body:
Found by running the real add-on code against a Stripe sandbox. The idempotency key repeats within a minute, so cancelling the add-on and buying it again within the same minute made Stripe replay the first response (an item that was already removed). The add reported success and mirrored an item that does not exist.

The add now writes the mirror only when the created item is really on the subscription; otherwise it refuses with a plain 'could not be confirmed, nothing turned on, try again in a couple of minutes'. Unit test added (23 pass); the sandbox run passes 7 of 7 with the fix, including a same-minute refusal followed by a real re-buy a minute later. Billing stays off in prod.

Adds a user-safe NOT_CONFIRMED refusal when an add-on item is not confirmed on the subscription. Mirrors are written only after confirmation. stripeService.ts excludes add-on items when selecting the base plan item and uses that helper at three tier-derivation sites.

title: [needs human] feat: count Google Ads campaigns in the Zoma first-ad check (ENG-3072)
body:
## [needs human] Do not merge without approval on ENG-3072

Held for two reasons. Harsha, Matt or Fangfang can clear both on the Linear issue.

1. **A stored field can hold a new value.** `zomaFirstAdLive.platform` on the AW-Users row was always `meta`. After this it can be `google_ads`, and for Google the `campaignId` / `approvedEntity.id` are resource names (`customers/<cid>/campaigns/<id>`) and `effectiveStatus` is Google's word (`ENABLED`). No migration, no backfill, no new attribute. The Google gateway also starts filling the existing optional `writeKind` dimension on its `mcp_write_executed` events (Meta already does).
2. **This does not count Google go-lives that already happened, Kraftersland's included.** See "What this does not fix".

## What changed

The Zoma first-ad check (`verifyZomaFirstAds`, admin scoreboard "verify" action) skipped every go-live approval that was not on Meta. It now checks Google Ads approvals under the same rule: campaign created through Zoma, go-live approved through Zoma with a CONFIRMED read-back, at least 1 lifetime impression at the provider, recorded once per user.

- `backend/src/services/zomaScoreboard.ts`: provider reads are picked by the approval event's platform. Top-level reads stay Meta's; `deps.google` (new, `googleFirstAdDeps`) does three GAQL reads through the existing `googleAdsService.queryReporting`. "Created through Zoma" is now matched on the same platform as the approval. The `ad_live` milestone carries the record's platform instead of a hard-coded `meta`.
- `backend/src/mcp/googleToolkitGateway.ts`: records `writeKind` on Google writes. `UPDATE status=ENABLED` on CAMPAIGN / AD_GROUP / AD / ASSET_GROUP is `approve`; status=PAUSED is `pause`; enabling a keyword stays `edit`.
- `backend/src/services/zomaWriteKind.ts`: `zomaWriteKindFor` takes the provider's live status (default `ACTIVE`, so Meta callers are unchanged).

## What this does not fix

Before this PR the Google gateway stored a go-live as a plain `UPDATE` with no status, so in stored events an enable looks the same as a rename, a pause or a bid change. The scoreboard's rule is that a first ad is never inferred, so those old events are not treated as approvals. A Google campaign that went live before this deploys is counted only if it is approved through Zoma again afterwards (for example pause, then enable).

Open question for a human, not decided here: whether to accept a weaker rule for old Google events (Zoma-created campaign + any confirmed Zoma UPDATE on it + at least 1 impression) so existing Google launches count without a re-approval.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-3072)

1. Findings comment posted on the issue before coding.
2. Google first ad recorded, write-once, after the provider check: covered.
3. Not Zoma-created / no confirmed approval / zero impressions not counted; Google read error is `provider_error` with nothing recorded: covered.
4. Meta + Google counted once (earliest approval wins; falls through to Google if the Meta campaign never delivered): covered.
5. Meta unchanged: `eng2902.zomaScoreboard.test.ts` passes with no edits.
6. Mocked tests only: `backend/src/__tests__/eng3072.zomaGoogleFirstAd.test.ts`, 21 tests, no live Google call.

## Tested

- `npx jest` on eng3072, eng2902, eng2823, eng2928 and the Meta toolkit gateway suite: 8 suites, 196 tests pass.
- `npm run typecheck` (backend): clean.

## Not tested

- No live Google Ads call. The impressions query has no date segment and I am relying on Google returning the all-time total in that case; that is from memory of the API, not checked.
- That `campaign.resource_name` can be selected from `ad_group`, `ad_group_ad` and `asset_group` in one GAQL query was not run against Google either. If Google rejects it the check reports `provider_error`; it does not record anything.
- Full backend jest suite was not run locally. No dev or staging run. No browser.
- Tests were written after the implementation, not red-first.
- Whether any Kraftersland Google campaign has a Zoma CREATE event or impressions was not looked up.
- The worktree borrows `node_modules` from the eng-3014 worktree (worktree-doctor flags it).

## How to test

1. On staging, as an admin, with a Zoma test user that has Google Ads connected: create a Search campaign through Zoma (it is created PAUSED), then approve `UPDATE status=ENABLED`.
2. Read the newest `mcp_write_executed` event for that user: `platform` is `google_ads`, `writeKind` is `approve`.
3. Admin scoreboard, "verify first ad" for that user: with zero impressions the outcome is `no_impressions` and the user row has no `zomaFirstAdLive`.
4. Once the campaign has an impression, verify again: outcome `verified`, and `zomaFirstAdLive.platform` is `google_ads`.

## Complexity ledger

+1 exported function for the Google reads (about 35 lines), +1 small interface split, +1 helper in the Google gateway. No new table, tool, flag or env var. Removes the Meta-only special case in the approval filter.
