title: [needs human] fix: read Meta ad updates and deletes back before reporting success (ENG-3065)
body:
**Held for Harsha before merge:** this adds two error sentences the model reads (below), and the acceptance criteria on ENG-3065 are PM-drafted and not yet reviewed by him. No live Meta call was made.

## What changed

Emma's Meta handlers reported "updated successfully" / "deleted successfully" as soon as the SDK call returned. Only budgets, `spend_cap` and creative swaps were read back. Now:

- After a campaign, ad set or ad **update**, the object is read back. A requested `name` or `status` (ad sets also `bid_strategy`, `bid_amount`) that did not change returns `success: false`, `errorType: 'unsupported_field'`, `fields: [...]`.
- After a **delete**, the object is read back. It passes when the status is `DELETED` or `ARCHIVED`, or Meta says the object does not exist. Anything else is a failure.
- A read that keeps failing returns `success: false`, `errorType: 'read_back_failed'`.
- A new test lists every mutation-shaped `MetaService` method as verified or exempt with a reason, and fails when a new one is neither.

The read is retried up to 4 times, 3 s apart (the existing spend-cap policy). The write is never sent again.

## Decisions for the reviewer

1. **Two new model-facing error sentences** (`backend/src/services/agentMode/metaWriteReadBack.ts`), worded after the Google and LinkedIn ones:
   - `unsupported_field: Meta accepted the update to campaign <id>, but these fields did not change after 4 read-back(s): status: requested "PAUSED", Meta has "ACTIVE". Do not report them as updated.`
   - `read_back_failed: Meta accepted the update to campaign <id>, but it could not be read back after 4 attempt(s) (<reason>). The change is not confirmed. Read the campaign before reporting it or sending the update again.`
   - Delete variants say "the delete of" and "Do not report it as deleted."
2. **A failed read is a failure here.** The older spend-cap and budget checks return `success: true` with a warning when the read fails, because a spend cap was once seen to take over six seconds to appear. I chose failure for name/status/delete so Meta matches the Google and LinkedIn slices and criterion 4. The cost: an update that landed but could not be read for about 9 seconds is reported as failed. `read_back_failed` is a second error type that the criteria do not name.
3. **Only four fields are compared.** Targeting, schedule (`start_time`, `end_time`), `promoted_object` and every other update field are not verified. Meta rewrites those on read, so a plain comparison would report false failures.
4. **In the creative-swap path**, an ad-level field (for example `status`) sent together with new creative content is now checked before the new creative is attached. If it did not land, the call stops there: the new creative exists but is not attached.
5. **Custom-audience user upload, delete and replace are listed as not verified.** Meta processes those lists later and offers no immediate read that proves the rows landed.

## Write surface (criterion 1)

| `MetaService` method | Verified | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `updateCampaign` | yes, handler | `checkMetaUpdate` (name, status); `verifyMetaBudget` (budgets); `verifyCampaignSpendCap` |
| `updateAdSet` | yes, handler | `checkMetaUpdate` (name, status, bid_strategy, bid_amount); `verifyMetaBudget` |
| `updateAd` | yes, handler | `checkMetaUpdate` (name, status); `verifyCreativeSwap`; image-swap check |
| `deleteCampaign`, `deleteAdSet`, `deleteAd` | yes, handler | `checkMetaDelete` |
| `createCampaign`, `createAdSet`, `createAdCreative`, `createAd`, `createCustomAudience`, `uploadImage`, `uploadVideo` | exempt | the returned id or hash is the evidence |
| `uploadCustomAudienceUsers`, `deleteCustomAudienceUsers`, `replaceCustomAudienceUsers` | **not verified** | asynchronous list processing |
| `sendCapiLeadEvent`, `setAppCredentials`, `createPlacementCustomizedCreative` | exempt | not a config write / private helper |

The Zoma Meta toolkit does not call these methods. It has its own read-back (`metaToolkitWrites.ts`, `metaToolkitLifecycle.ts`), which this PR does not touch.

## Evidence

- New file `eng3065.metaWriteReadBack.test.ts`: 23 tests. Before the handler wiring, 8 of the then 22 failed. The helper tests and the guard passed in that run because the helper module already existed.
- 27 suites / 758 tests pass on this head: every backend test file that mentions these handlers, the `MetaService` update/delete methods, or the new module.
- Backend `npm run typecheck`: exit 0 on this head.
- 12 hand mutations: 9 failed 1 to 6 tests; 1 showed a redundant line, which I removed; 2 were not caught, so I added one test for each and re-ran those two (now caught).

## Not tested

- No live Meta call. That a deleted object reads back `DELETED`, and that a missing one answers code 100 / subcode 33, comes from Meta's documented behaviour, not from a run.
- The full Jest suite was not run locally, and nothing ran on staging.
- 20 existing tests were edited: 16 gained a read-back response in their mocks, and 4 that asserted "no read-back" on a status-only or ad-level update now assert exactly one read. One test was added to `agentModeService.metaAdsCRUD.test.ts`. All are in the diff of the five `agentModeService.meta*.test.ts` files.
- The mutations ran before the merge of `main` into this branch.

## Opslane verification note (swarm3, head 4355492)

The open Opslane P1 ("could not test whether Emma leaves a pause unconfirmed") is a harness setup failure, not a behaviour of this diff: its run stopped when opening an agent session for a skill named `verify-<marker>-meta-tools`, which returned 404 because that skill is never created in the run, and the same step failed on the base commit. This PR does not touch session or skill routes. To reach the read-back path, open the session with `POST /api/agent-mode/sessions` and body `{"portalType":"agent","pageIdentifier":"agent-mode"}` (no skill), then ask Emma to pause the campaign while the Meta campaign GET answers 500. Expected: the reply says the pause could not be confirmed. The same behaviour is covered at head by `backend/src/__tests__/eng3065.metaWriteReadBack.test.ts` plus the five `agentModeService.meta*` suites: 21 suites, 456 tests pass at 4355492.

## How to test

1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/eng3065.metaWriteReadBack.test.ts`
2. In a session with a Meta test ad account: pause a campaign through Emma and confirm the reply still says it was updated.
3. Delete a test ad through Emma and confirm it reports the delete.

## Complexity ledger

- Added: one 125-line module, one test file, 35 lines in `agentModeService.ts` (six call sites and two small helpers).
- Removed: nothing.
- Net: up. The six write paths now share one check instead of none.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No stored data, table or setting changes.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Medium

Adds Meta read-back checks after campaign, ad set, and ad updates and deletes. Writes are not resent. Reads retry four times, three seconds apart. Mismatches return typed errors. Custom-audience operations stay unverified. Held for human review.

Outage path: none identified. Each write adds up to about 9 seconds of latency. Subcode 33 alone counts as deleted, so missing permissions can produce a false success. Exact-case status and trimmed name comparison can produce false failures.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->


## Opslane run 2371 P1 ("0 results carrying read_back_failed") — harness route, not a defect (swarm3, 2026-11-21)
Step 5 again opened the session via `POST /api/agent-mode/skill/opslane-verify-<marker>-ac1/session`; that skill is never created, so the session/generate calls never reach the Meta tool and no tool result exists to inspect. Code trace at head b163d83: the only Meta campaign-update path is `manageMetaAdsCampaigns('UPDATE')` -> `updateMetaAdsCampaign` (agentModeService.ts:13435) -> `checkMetaUpdate` (metaWriteReadBack.ts:58). `metaService.getCampaign` rethrows via `handleError` on a 500, so every read attempt sets `readError` and the tool result is `{success:false, errorType:'read_back_failed', error:'read_back_failed: Meta accepted the update ... could not be read back ...'}`. `eng3065.metaWriteReadBack.test.ts`: 23/23 pass at b163d83. To test AC1, use `POST /api/agent-mode/sessions` with `{"portalType":"agent","pageIdentifier":"agent-mode"}` (no skill route).

title: feat: admin read of a named client's Meta change history (ENG-3070)
body:
## What this does

An admin can now ask Emma for one named client's Meta ad account change history: who changed what, when, and for budget changes the old and new values. Read-only. Nothing is written to Meta, no table or stored field changes, and nothing a non-admin customer sees changes. Closes the read gap from CS-79 for ENG-3070 (slice of ENG-1171).

## New admin-only tool (name and description, per the issue)

`read_client_meta_activity`, not listed on the public MCP surface (`"listed": false` in `mcp-public-tool-inventory.json`). Arguments: `client_name_or_email` (required), `since`, `until`, `limit` (1-100), `after`.

> Read the Meta ad account change history (who changed what, when) for one named client. Admin-only tool, read-only — nothing is written to Meta.
>
> Resolves the client the same way assess_client_health does, with one difference: a name that matches more than one client is refused, so pass the exact email when a name is ambiguous.
>
> Returns:
> - 'ad_account_id' and 'client': the account that was actually read and whose it is. Check these before quoting the history.
> - 'events': one page of Meta activity events (event_time, event_type, object_id, object_name, object_type, actor_name, extra_data). When Meta supplies old and new values (for example a budget change), they are also given as 'before' and 'after'. Fields Meta did not return are absent.
> - 'paging': cursors; pass paging.cursors.after as 'after' to read the next page.
>
> A result with success:false means nothing was read ('reason' says why: ambiguous_client, client_not_found, no_meta_connection, credential_pair_mismatch, invalid_argument, meta_read_failed). Never report a failed read as "no changes".

I treated this as internal copy (only admins' sessions get the tool) and did not hold the PR for copy review. If the name should be different, it is one rename across six files.

## Where to look

1. `backend/src/services/clientHealthService.ts`
   - `findClientMatches` and `resolveClientMetaAccount` are the client lookup and the account/token pairing, moved out of `assessClientHealth` unchanged. `assessClientHealth` now calls them and still takes the first name match, so `assess_client_health` behaves as before (its 100+ existing tests pass untouched).
   - `readClientMetaActivity` is new. It refuses on more than one match, on no Meta connection, on an expired connection that cannot refresh, and on a connected account that has an id but no token of its own (it will not read that id with the shared token). It only ever calls `getAccountsByUserId` for the matched client.
2. `backend/src/routes/clientHealth.ts`: `GET /api/client-health/:client/meta-activity`, behind the same `authenticateToken, isAdmin` mount as the rest of the router.
3. `backend/src/mcp/server/apiTools.ts`: the tool. The Graph call itself is the existing `executeActivityLogRead` (`ACTIVITY_FIELDS`, same validation, same failure classification via `metaReadErrorClass`).
4. Registration lists: `ADMIN_SKILL_TOOL_NAMES` (both copies), `emma/tools.ts`, `agentExecutionTools.ts`, `toolAnnotationPolicy.ts`, `scheduledReportAccess.ts` (`CROSS_ACCOUNT_USER_DATA_TOOLS`).

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-3070)

| # | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 | Done, commented on the issue: the name fallback takes the first substring match and never detects a second. |
| 2 | Admin read for a since/until window; non-admin refused (test). |
| 3 | Event fields passed through as Meta returned them; `before`/`after` added only when `extra_data` carries `old_value`/`new_value` (test covers an event with none). |
| 4 | `ad_account_id` in every result past resolution; paging cursors passed through, token-bearing `next`/`previous` URLs dropped (test). |
| 5 | Ambiguous name, no connection, pairing mismatch each refuse with a distinct `reason` (tests). |
| 6 | Meta error 190 comes back as `success:false`, `reason: meta_read_failed`, with the existing classification (test). |
| 7 | 13 mocked tests, no live Meta call. |
| 8 | No write, no new table or field. |

## Behaviour change outside the new tool

- The admin skill line in the agent-mode system prompt gains one tool name (27 characters, admin sessions only). `prepareTurnContext.golden.json` was re-recorded for that; the diff is the two admin fixtures only. Customer turns are byte-identical.
- The tool is classified `write` in `toolAnnotationPolicy.ts`, like `assess_client_health`, because the read can refresh and persist the client's Meta token.

## Tested

- `npm run typecheck` clean on head `c09be6a8d`.
- New suite 13/13. Related run before the rebase: 217 suites, 4,697 tests, 2 failed: `agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts` and `agentModeService.supportedModelsCharacterization.test.ts`. Both fail the same way on a clean `origin/main` `d625f4a30` (model-registry assertions; this PR does not touch models). The pre-push hook stops on the first of them, so the push used `--no-verify`.
- After the rebase onto `d625f4a30`: typecheck and 5 suites / 134 tests re-run (new suite, clientHealth, public inventory, golden, eng2921).

## Not tested

- No live Meta call. The shape of `extra_data` for a real budget change was not checked against a real account; `before`/`after` are whatever Meta puts in `old_value`/`new_value`.
- No dev or staging run of the tool through Emma. No route-level test of the query-string parsing (the service is tested directly).
- Full backend jest was not run locally.
- No admin audit-log entry is written for this read. `assess_client_health` does not write one either; I left that as is rather than decide it here.

## How to test (staging, as an admin)

1. Ask Emma: "Show Meta changes for <client email> from 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-15." Expect `read_client_meta_activity` with `ad_account_id` matching that client's account in `assess_client_health`.
2. Ask with a first name shared by two clients. Expect a refusal listing the matches, no events.
3. Ask for a client with no Meta connection. Expect `no_meta_connection`, no events.
4. As a non-admin, the tool is not offered; calling the route directly returns 403 from the `isAdmin` middleware.

## Complexity ledger

Production: +259 / -55 lines across 8 files (one new service function, one route, one tool, two extracted helpers that replace inline code). Tests and fixtures: +218 / -6. One new admin tool; no new dependency, table, setting or flag.

## Rollback

Revert this commit. No data to migrate back.

title: feat: give unattended scheduled runs the compact brand block up front (ENG-3066)
body:
**Held as draft: evidence gate, not a human gate.** ENG-3066 requires before/after evidence from dev on one scheduled outreach run and an Okareo simulation pass against baseline before this merges. Neither exists yet; this tick could not produce them (sprint workers do not start dev). Code and tests are complete.

## What this does

When Emma runs a schedule with nobody present, she now gets a short summary of the account's brand (name, offer, value proposition, key messages, voice) at the start of each turn. Before this she only knew what the sender sells if the model chose to call `read_brand_guidelines`.

## Criterion 1: which outreach tools had brand context without that call

Read from tool definitions on `origin/main` `d625f4a30`. I did not trace each handler.

| Tool | Who writes the text | Brand context before this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `update_email_draft_for_lead` | Server-side prompt | Yes (loads brand guidelines itself; compact block since #4016) |
| `send_email_to_lead` | Sends the saved draft above | Yes, through the draft |
| `send_email_from_sender` (`subject`, `html`/`text`/`body`) | Model | No |
| `email` / MCP `send_email`, action `send` (`subject`, `body`) | Model | No |
| `linkedin_outreach` (message and invite note) | Model | No |
| `twitter_outreach` (DM `text`) | Model | No |
| `manage_crm_sequence` (`steps`) | Model | No |

Not checked: Smartlead push tools (`preview_smartlead_push` and siblings) and whether they carry model-written copy. `prepareTurnContext` had no brand read of any kind before this PR, so no other layer was supplying it.

## Where to look

1. `backend/src/services/agentModeService.ts`, the `sessionType === 'scheduled' && isUnattendedRun === true` branch of `prepareTurnContext`: 5 added lines. The brand message is pushed before the unattended publish directive, so the directive is still the last message (ENG-827).
2. `backend/src/services/brandMessagingContext.ts`: `unattendedBrandContextMessage` wraps the existing `brandMessagingContextFromGuidelines`. No second formatter, no slice of `formattedContent`.

## Acceptance criteria

| # | Status |
|---|---|
| 1 | Table above. Five model-written paths had no brand context, so the change is needed. |
| 2 | Test: the first model call of an unattended scheduled run contains the block, with no assistant or tool message before it. |
| 3 | Uses `brandMessagingContextFromGuidelines`. |
| 4 | Tests: no guidelines, guidelines with no messaging fields, a read that throws, and a failed read result all give no block and no error. |
| 5 | Test: an org member gets the org's brand, not their own leftover record (same `readBrandGuidelines` resolution). |
| 6 | `agentModeService.prepareTurnContext.golden.test.ts` passes with no fixture edit. A scheduled session reopened attended gets no block and no brand read (test). |
| 7 | 264-character lead-in plus at most 1,500 characters of block, per turn. |

## Decisions I made that you may want different

- **Every unattended scheduled turn gets the block, not only outreach runs.** Deciding "is this an outreach run" before the model has acted would need tool-set or intent detection; this is one unconditional message. Cost: up to about 1,764 characters per turn on runs that never write outreach. It sits after the conversation, so it does not move the cached prompt prefix.
- **Only `sessionType === 'scheduled'`.** The issue title says "scheduled or other unattended"; criterion 2 says scheduled. Unattended runs of another session type do not get the block.
- **The lead-in sentence is new model-facing prompt text** (not customer-visible): "SENDER BRAND CONTEXT (saved brand guidelines for this account, summarized). Any email, LinkedIn message or invite, DM or sequence step you write in this run must be consistent with it. It is a summary: call read_brand_guidelines when you need the full guidelines."

## Behavior-preserving proof

This PR is not behavior-preserving for unattended scheduled turns of accounts with brand guidelines: that is its purpose. Everything else is unchanged: the golden prompt suite passes untouched, the publish-directive delivery and position tests pass untouched, and accounts without guidelines get byte-identical messages (test).

## Tested

- New suite 8/8; with the `agentModeService.ts` change stashed, the two positive tests fail (red first confirmed after the fact, the tests were written alongside the code).
- `npm run typecheck` clean on `127965cf8`; head `fa0bc69de` adds only a one-word fix to the dev note.
- 332 suites / 6,489 tests matching agentModeService, agentModeController, brandMessaging, scheduledChat: 2 failed, `agentModeService.sonnet45.test.ts` and `agentModeService.supportedModelsCharacterization.test.ts`. Both fail identically on clean `origin/main` `d625f4a30` and are unrelated (model registry). The pre-push hook stops on them, so the push used `--no-verify`.

## Not tested

- **No dev before/after run and no Okareo pass.** This is the merge gate above.
- Whether the block actually changes what the model writes. The tests prove it is in context, not that outreach quality improves.
- Full backend jest. Local CodeRabbit review not run.
- Added latency of one brand read per unattended turn (one or two DynamoDB gets) was not measured.

## How to test (dev)

1. Pick an account with brand guidelines and a schedule that writes outreach. Run it once on `main`, once on this branch.
2. In the trace for the first model call, confirm a system message starting `SENDER BRAND CONTEXT` sits second to last, with the publish directive last.
3. Compare the outreach text: the branch run should name the product and value proposition without a `read_brand_guidelines` call.
4. Run the Okareo scheduled-run simulation against baseline.

## Complexity ledger

Production: +23 / -0 (5 lines in the monolith plus one import, 17 in `brandMessagingContext.ts`). Tests: +166. One new exported function. No table, setting, flag or dependency. The monolith gains one responsibility-free call site; no seam is removed.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. No stored data.

Risk: Low

Adds a compact brand-context system message to each turn of unattended scheduled runs, placed before the publish directive. The block summarizes saved brand guidelines and points to read_brand_guidelines. No block is added when guidelines are missing or unreadable. Attended and reopened sessions are unchanged.

title: feat: admin read of a managed client's Meta budgets and spend for an exact window (ENG-3069)
body:
## What
ENG-3069 (read-only slice of ENG-1171). An admin can read one managed client's Meta budgets and spend for an exact since/until window.

- `backend/src/services/clientMetaBudgetsService.ts` — `readClientMetaBudgets`. Admin check same as assess_client_health. Exact email first, else a name/email substring that must match exactly one client.
- No second resolver: uses `findClientMatches` and `resolveClientMetaAccount` that ENG-3070 (#4116, merged) extracted from `assessClientHealth`, with the same refusal reasons and the same `credential_source` field as `read_client_meta_activity`. (The first push of this branch did its own extraction; I rebuilt it on main after #4116 merged, force-pushed this swarm3 draft, and clientHealthService.ts is no longer touched.)
- Route `GET /api/client-health/:clientEmail/meta-budgets?since=&until=`.
- MCP tool `read_client_meta_budgets`, added to the admin lists (agentModeService, emma/impl/misc, emma/tools, agentExecutionTools DETERMINISTIC_TOOLS, scheduledReportAccess CROSS_ACCOUNT_USER_DATA_TOOLS), annotation 'write' like its sibling assess_client_health (not readOnly, so a tools:read API key scope does not gain it). Golden MCP inventory and the prepareTurnContext admin-prompt golden re-recorded (the only prompt change is the new tool name in the admin tool list).

## Model-facing copy (needs Harsha's wording approval; held as draft)
Name: `read_client_meta_budgets`
Description: "Read one managed client's Meta ad budgets and spend for an exact date window. Admin-only, read-only; never changes a budget. Resolves the client (exact email, or a name that matches exactly one client) to the same Meta ad account and token assess_client_health reads. Returns the ad account id read, account spend for the window, and per campaign and per ad set: status, current daily or lifetime budget (minor currency units, as Meta returns them), and spend for the window. Refuses instead of guessing, with a reason: ambiguous_client (several clients match; ask with the email), client_not_found, no_meta_connection, credential_pair_mismatch, invalid_window, and meta_read_failed (a Meta read failed; no numbers are reported, which is not the same as zero spend)."
Params: client_name_or_email, since, until (YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive).

## Acceptance criteria
1. Criterion-1 comments on ENG-3069 (multi-match: first contains-match wins; no budgets/ad sets/window spend returned today).
2. Admin + exact client + window; non-admin refused. Tested.
3. ad_account_id, account_spend (+currency), per campaign and per ad set status/effective_status, daily_budget/lifetime_budget, window spend. Tested.
4. ambiguous_client (lists up to 10 matches), no_meta_connection (none or expired), credential_pair_mismatch (connected id without its own token is never paired with the shared token). Tested. As in read_client_meta_activity, a client with only a legacy `adAccount` is read with the shared token and labelled `credential_source: legacy_shared_token`; that is the existing ENG-1767 matched pair, not a mismatch.
5. Graph error body, truncated paging, or thrown fetch -> meta_read_failed with no numbers. Tested.
6. 11 mocked tests in `src/__tests__/clientMetaBudgets.test.ts`; no live Meta call.
7. Three GET reads only; no table/field; non-admin surface unchanged.

## My choices (please review)
- Refusal semantics copied from read_client_meta_activity so the two sibling tools agree (legacy-only clients are read via the shared token and labelled).

title: fix: client health reports whether the Meta optimisation event is arriving (ENG-3079)
body:
## What
`assess_client_health` always reported `meta_connection_health.selected_event: 'unknown'`. It now reports `recent`, `missing` or `unknown` from a live Meta read that reuses the tracking monitor's fetch and verdict. ENG-3079, child of ENG-2274.

- `backend/src/services/clientHealthService.ts`: new `readSelectedEventState(adAccountId, accessToken)`. It starts beside the campaign reads, is cut off at 8 s, and never throws.
- `backend/src/services/metaOptimisationCoverage.ts`: the verdict gains an `arriving` list, and `selectedEventState(verdict)` reduces a verdict to one word.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Source of the answer: the monitor's existing logic with a live read (`fetchOptimisationInputs` + `evaluateAccountOptimisationCoverage`). Nothing stored, no new field. Recorded on the issue.
2. `missing` = the monitor's confirmed case (`verdict.alerting`). `recent` = a pixel reported an optimisation event and nothing is confirmed missing. Window and matching are the monitor's evaluator, not a copy.
3. No conversion ad set, no connected Meta ad account, or a failed read gives `unknown`. A failed read cannot give `missing`.
4. Bounded at 8 s; a slow, failed or throwing read gives `unknown` and the health check still succeeds.
5. `reconnect_required` unchanged.
6. 15 tests with the Meta read mocked.

## My choices, for review
- "Recent" uses the pixel's window, which Meta fixes at about 24 hours. The monitor's 7-day insights streak is used only to confirm `missing`.
- Ad sets the monitor logs but does not alert on (paused, pixel quiet with no streak, no pixel, silent pixel, stopped delivering) give `unknown`, not `missing`.
- If one ad set's event is arriving and another's is confirmed missing, the answer is `missing`.
- The monitor's day-1 detection is not applied: it needs account-level history the health check does not fetch. A brand-new broken ad set reads `unknown` until its 3-day streak completes.
- A client on the legacy ad-account field with no connected account gets no read (there is no `meta_connection_health` object for them today either).
- Cost: each `assess_client_health` call on a connected client now makes the monitor's Graph reads (ad sets, up to 8 pixels, ad-set insights) and can take up to 8 s longer.

## Evidence
- 15 new tests. Before the source change: 11 failed, 4 passed. The source was written first; the red run was made by stashing it, and some of those failures are the missing export rather than behavior.
- 30 suites / 736 tests pass (every test file that mentions clientHealthService, metaOptimisationCoverage, metaTrackingMonitor or assess_client_health).
- Backend `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- 7 hand mutations, each failed 1 to 3 tests.
- No tool name, description or prompt text changed. I did not run the admin-prompt or tool-inventory golden suites.

## Not tested
- No live Meta call, so the real latency and the real answer for any client are unmeasured.
- No staging, full Jest not run, no local CodeRabbit run.
- The existing test that expects `selected_event: 'unknown'` (clientHealth.test.ts) still passes without edits, but only because its mock of `metaApiFetch` makes the new read throw before any network call. It does not prove anything about the new path.

## Complexity ledger
+63/-5 source lines in two files, +186 test lines. One new exported function, one new verdict field, one timeout constant. No new module, flag, table or stored value.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/eng3079 src/__tests__/clientHealth.test.ts`
2. As an admin, run `assess_client_health` for a client with an active conversion campaign: `selected_event` is `recent` if the pixel reported the event in the last day.

Rollback: revert this commit. Post-deploy check: `assess_client_health` for one connected client returns within its usual time plus at most 8 s and carries a `selected_event` value.

title: ENG-2987: read-only check of the enrichment estimate against booked cost
body:
> **Correction 2026-11-16 (after merge, see #4129):** the evidence below says the replay of 2026-11-04 to 2026-11-13 was 97 contacts at ratio 1.13, "inside the 25% band". That sample included an internal `agentweb.pro` account (39 of the 97 contacts, cheap runs). With internal accounts left out it is 58 contacts from 2 customers at ratio 1.50 (insufficient data; the quote looks low for fresh customer lists). The default 14-day window also printed a false "DRIFT", and several review findings were left as limitations; #4129 fixes all of them.

## Safety answer (first, per the draft/merge rules)

- **Safe for prod?** Yes. The PR adds three files and changes no runtime code: `scripts/enrichment-estimate-calibration.py` (a script nobody runs automatically), `docs/enrichment-estimate-calibration-runbook.md` and a `dev/pending` note. Nothing under `backend/` or `partner-portal/` changes, so the path filters in `deploy.yml` do not fire and **no deploy happens**. (One caveat in `deploy.yml`: its fail-safe path deploys everything when it cannot resolve the base commit; that is existing behaviour and applies to any push to main.)
- **Could it regress or anger users?** No. It is not imported or scheduled by anything. The script only reads: `aws logs describe-log-groups`, `aws logs filter-log-events`, `aws dynamodb scan` and `aws dynamodb get-item`. It writes nothing to AWS, and prints only a 6-character user id prefix, counts and dollars (never an email, lead or field value).
- **Rollback:** revert the PR; nothing depends on it.
- **Data plane?** No schema, key, index, IAM, retention or stored-data change.

## What and why

ENG-2987 (follow-up to the estimate recalibration #4038, ENG-2720) asks for a small read-only check that joins prod enrichment run logs to the usage ledger per customer and day and compares booked dollars per processed contact with what the estimate quotes. The script reads the constants from `enrichmentCostEstimate.ts` (parsed with a tree walker that accepts only numbers and `+ - * /`, no `eval`), applies the quote's field-count formula to each list's saved config, leaves out test accounts, platform admins and `--exclude-user-ids`, excludes the paid email search from the ratio (shown in its own column), warns when `--since` reaches past the log group's 14-day retention, and refuses to call a drift below 100 contacts from 3 customers. The runbook says when to run it (at least every 14 days), how to read it, its limits, the paid-email-search measurement and the decision not to build a cache-aware quote.

## Evidence

- **Live, read-only runs on prod** (2026-11-16): `--since 2026-11-13`: 7 contacts, booked $0.48 vs quote $0.49 (ratio 0.97), INSUFFICIENT DATA. `--since 2026-11-04`: 97 contacts from 3 accounts (2 customers and 1 internal `agentweb.pro` user), booked $7.64 vs quote $6.77 (ratio 1.13, inside the 25% band); also INSUFFICIENT DATA by the gate (2 customers).
- **Offline against a fake `aws` with hand-computed numbers**: weighted fields 7.0, ratios 1.09 and 0.96, total 130 contacts at 1.07 from 2 customers, INSUFFICIENT by default, "within 25%" with `--min-customers 2`, DRIFT with `--tolerance 0.05`, the empty-ledger guard, the retention warning, a clean exit for a bad date.
- **Nine hostile estimate-source files** (negative, zero, divide by zero, 400-digit literal, 3,000 nested parentheses, `2**3`, a function call, missing constants): all exit with a message and no traceback.
- The pre-push hook skipped tsc and jest by design: no pushed commit touches `backend/`.

## Reviews

1. **Review 1** (security first): no security problem; mediums on log retention, a field count that differed from the customer quote (it had printed a false +23%), and internal accounts counted as customers; plus runbook claims stronger than the evidence (it also exposed that a real found-email Apollo callback HAS been observed, on 2026-11-05). All verified and fixed.
2. **Review 2** (fresh agent, full review of head `9bbcbd630`): **SAFE TO MERGE**, no blockers, no security finding. Its mediums were verified against code and prod data: the quote counts saved config merged with the list's current columns (wording fixed, about 3% of the ratio per column), the 2026-11-16 sample was an internal account (fixed), and an unpadded `--since` silently drops ledger rows (documented below).
3. **After review 2, wording only** (per the review-cycle rule): the script's docstring and the runbook. The executable code is **identical** to the reviewed head (same syntax tree with the module docstring excluded; `git diff --name-only 9bbcbd630..HEAD` lists only the runbook and the script).

## Known limitations left as they are (lows, documented in the runbook)

Write `--since` zero-padded (the ledger filter is a string compare); staff accounts that are not admins are not excluded automatically (pass `--exclude-user-ids`); a START with no DONE is not reported; the 3-customer gate counts totals, not spread; AWS CLI error text is echoed; a hostile source line of 50,000 `-` could raise `MemoryError` (a traceback, no data leak).

## Not done here

No retune of `ENRICHMENT_COST_RATES_USD`: the data is not enough. The check is re-run when real runs accumulate.

title: fix: eb-deploy.sh does not fail a serving release whose version label has not moved (ENG-3082)
body:
## What
Production deploy run 43832897163 (merge of #4118, 2026-11-16) ended as failed although the release had been serving for about 20 minutes. `eb-deploy.sh` now reports that case as a success. ENG-3082, follow-up to ENG-3039 / #4086.

Why it failed: Elastic Beanstalk moves the environment's version label only when the old instance is gone. That took 17 minutes, and the run had already spent 18 minutes waiting behind an update it did not start. The budget ran out 100 seconds before EB finished, with every poll reading `Updating` on the previous label.

The change, in `.github/scripts/eb-deploy.sh`: when the budget is spent and the environment is `Updating` on the previous label, `verify_deployment` calls the new `release_serving_while_old_instances_terminate` before failing. Success needs all three:

1. EB's INFO events since our update was accepted show "Deployment succeeded. Terminating old instances and temporary Auto Scaling group." after the last "Environment update is starting."
2. At least one instance reports the expected version as `Deployed` with health `Ok`, and no instance on that version reports anything else.
3. Each of those instances is `healthy` in a load-balancer target group.

## Acceptance criteria (PM-drafted, not confirmed by Harsha)
1. Replay of the 11-16 sequence reports success. Done. The status line and events are from the run log and EB events. The per-instance fixture is the shape I read from production at 09:47Z during the same phase of the next deploy (new instance on the new version, old instance still listed on the old one and `draining`), not a recording of 09:26Z.
2. Positive evidence that names the expected version. Leg 2 reads the version from the instance itself. Why the three cannot hold for a release that did not apply: an instance only reports our label as `Deployed` if our bundle was installed on it; EB writes the "Deployment succeeded" line when it keeps the new instance and starts removing the old one; and `healthy` in the target group means it is taking traffic. My understanding that a failed Immutable update removes the new instances and never writes that line comes from EB's documented behaviour. I did not reproduce a failed Immutable update.
3. Instances on a different version, and no success event for this update, each still fail. Done, one test each, plus: success event from the previous update, deployment not finished, instance not Ok, instance not healthy in the target group, unreadable instance read, unreadable event log.
4. The 109 existing checks pass unedited. A real failure prints the same message as before.
5. No new AWS action. The instance read adds the `Deployment` attribute to `describe-instances-health`, which the script already calls. I did not read the deploy role's IAM policy; if it restricts that action by attribute this would be denied, and a denied read leaves the old failure in place.

## My choices, for review
- The check runs only when the budget is spent, in place of the failure. I first considered accepting as soon as the three hold. That would end every deploy about 20 minutes sooner, but the next queued deploy would then wait for the old instance inside its own 1200 s settle cap, and a 27-minute removal (seen at 08:32Z the same day) would fail it. So a deploy still takes as long as it does today.
- An instance on another version is not counted against the release. It is the old instance being removed.
- `Updating` on our own label is left to the ENG-3039 rule. A test pins that.
- The success line names the instance and says EB is still removing the old one.
- The target-group lookup is repeated in the new function instead of refactoring `underlying_health_verdict`, which treats a `draining` target as unhealthy.

## Evidence
- `bash .github/scripts/eb-deploy.test.sh`: 123 checks, 0 failed (109 before, 14 new).
- Before the script change, with the tests in place: 4 of the first 13 new checks failed (the success cases). The 8 negative cases and the budget check passed then too, because the old script fails all of them.
- 6 hand mutations of the new code: 5 failed 1 to 4 checks. The sixth (dropping the status and label guard) passed, so I added a check that fails on it.
- Read-only run of the new function against production at 09:51Z, while prod was in this exact state (`Updating`, label `pr4118`, `pr4121` serving): true for `pr4121`, naming `i-069eb20aff5910b00`. False for a label nothing runs. False for `pr4118`, whose instance was `draining`.
- `bash -n` passes. `shellcheck` is not installed on this box.

## Not tested
- No production deploy has gone through this path. The first real proof is a deploy that runs out of budget in this state.
- Staging and the partner portal call the same script. The "Deployment succeeded" line is specific to Immutable updates; I did not check their deployment policies, so on a rolling environment this path may simply never apply.
- Local CodeRabbit not run.

## Complexity ledger
+142 script lines (one function, one call site), +180 test lines, +8 dev note. No new flag, environment variable, or AWS action.

## How to test
1. `bash .github/scripts/eb-deploy.test.sh` and read the ENG-3082 section.
2. After merge: the next production deploy should finish through the normal `Ready` path with no change in its log.

Rollback: revert this commit. Post-deploy check: the Deploy run for this merge succeeds and its log shows the usual "is Ready, running version" line.

title: fix: client-health routes stop decoding the client name a second time (ENG-3084)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Low

## What was wrong (before)
`GET /api/client-health/:clientEmail` and `GET /api/client-health/:clientEmail/meta-activity` called `decodeURIComponent` on a route param that Express had already decoded. A client name with a literal `%` (for example "Acme 50% Off") threw `URIError` and returned 500, and escape-shaped text was rewritten ("Promo %41 Team" reached the service as "Promo A Team"). These routes back the admin tools `assess_client_health` and `read_client_meta_activity`.

## What this fixes (after)

title: ENG-2987: require --since in the calibration script and fix every review finding
body:
## Safety answer (first, per the draft/merge rules)

- **Safe for prod?** Yes. Follow-up to #4124. It changes one read-only script (`scripts/enrichment-estimate-calibration.py`), its runbook and a `dev/pending` note. Nothing under `backend/` or `partner-portal/` changes, so no deploy happens (one existing caveat in `deploy.yml`: its fail-safe path deploys everything when it cannot resolve the base commit, for any push to main), and nothing imports or schedules the script. It still only reads (`logs describe-log-groups`, `logs filter-log-events`, `dynamodb scan`, `dynamodb get-item`) and prints no email, lead or field value.
- **Could it regress or anger users?** No. The behaviour changes are stricter input (`--since` required, zero-padded, not in the future; `--log-group`, `--region`, `--tolerance`, `--min-*` and `--max-account-share` validated) and a more careful comparison, in a tool nobody runs automatically.
- **Rollback:** revert the PR.
- **Data plane?** No.

## Why

Running the merged script from #4124's merge commit with its default 14-day window printed **"DRIFT: retune"** on 2026-11-16. Two causes, both fixed here: (1) the 2026-11-03 run's 60 paid email searches ($26.70) were booked under the model name the search had until 2026-11-02, `apollo:full_enrichment`, which the script did not exclude, so that run read 3.6 times the quote; it now reads 1.01; (2) internal staff accounts were counted as customers. With internal accounts left out, the customer runs after the fixes (2026-11-04 to 2026-11-13) are **58 contacts from 2 customers at ratio 1.50**, not "97 contacts at 1.13 inside the band" as #4124's description and the ENG-2987 comment first said (corrected on #4124, ENG-2987 and ENG-2801). Still INSUFFICIENT DATA, nothing retuned, but the quote looks low for lists with nothing cached and the runbook says so. A window that includes the 2026-11-03 list (the sample the recalibration was fitted to) is 72% that one list, so the script now refuses a verdict when one account supplies more than half of the contacts.

## What changes (every finding of every review so far, fixed here as asked)

- `--since` required, zero-padded ASCII digits only, not in the future; `--log-group`, `--region`, `--tolerance`, `--min-*`, `--max-account-share` validated; no stdin and a 30-minute limit on every AWS call.
- Retention warning compares dates and fires whenever `--since` is at or before the oldest retained day (that day is only partly covered while the ledger counts whole days), naming the day to start from.
- Internal accounts left out by default, matched **in Python** over the whole user table (no email in any DynamoDB expression), case-insensitively: platform admins, `--exclude-emails`, any account on `--exclude-domains` (default `agentweb.pro,argusoft.com`) or a subdomain, `--exclude-user-ids` (6-character prefixes work). The script prints how many accounts each rule excluded and warns when an id entry matches nothing.
- The paid email search is recognised under both of its ledger names; Enigma spend is excluded from booked like the email search (the customer quote adds it separately).
- Gate: at least 100 contacts, at least 3 accounts that each supplied 10 or more, and no account above 50% of the contacts; the verdict names every shortfall.
- A repeated DONE line counts once; customer runs that never finished, and finished runs whose start is before `--since`, are reported; START and DONE log patterns anchored on `[v3] runEnrichment`.
- AWS error text is reduced to its error code and operation (the free text can carry account names); parser errors truncated to 60 characters; the rate-constant reader is linear (lines over 300 characters are skipped) and the file size-limited; `referenceFieldCount` must be a whole number.
- Run lines must start with the real syslog prefix, then the marker (any other line that mentions a run, bad digits and non-string messages are counted as ignored); a deleted list is reported and its row marked `?` (a list that exists without a saved config is not); the rate-constant reader skips block, doc and `//` comments; decoding errors in AWS output are replaced; `--since` before 2020 is rejected.
- One combined CloudWatch search for the START and DONE lines (about half the run time: 13 days in about 7 minutes); a malformed or empty `--aws` is a clean error; log text copied into the table is validated (only the modes `enrich` and `preview` and plain user ids; other lines are ignored and counted); an empty user-table scan is refused and the number of accounts read is printed; a ledger row missing a field is skipped and counted; shares print with one decimal so a 50.5% share never reads "50% (at most 50%)"; `--log-group` and `--region` may not start with a dash.
- Runbook: callback evidence "consistent with a real callback" (cannot prove who called the webhook); the seven placeholder rows described exactly; claims limited to what the data shows; the cache-aware-quote decision re-based on what the code and data show (the cache key falls back to the company name; no measured need yet); `--since` guidance; corrected history rows including the 2026-11-03 fitted list.

## Evidence

- **Live read-only runs on prod, 2026-11-16 (each recorded as a PR comment for the head it ran on; docs-only commits do not change the script):** `--since 2026-11-03`: 48 accounts excluded (9 platform admins, 1 test email, 46 on internal domains), 12 customer runs, 206 contacts from 3 accounts, booked $16.77 vs quote $14.56 (1.15), the 2026-11-03 list 148 contacts at 1.01 with its 60 searches ($26.70) in their own column, the Nuerraa run 1.68, the ThinkingAI run 1.29; verdict INSUFFICIENT DATA because one account supplies 72% of the contacts. The same code over `--since 2026-11-04` earlier gave 58 contacts, 2 accounts, 1.50.
- **Offline against a fake `aws` with hand-computed numbers:** 13 runs, 5 excluded accounts (admin, `AgentWeb.pro`, `updates.agentweb.pro`, mixed-case `Dev@AgentWeb.pro`, `Test@Account.com`), a look-alike domain kept, a user row without an id skipped, a duplicate DONE counted once, bogus un-anchored log lines ignored, 1 unfinished customer run and 1 orphan run reported, Enigma and both email-search names excluded from booked, 166 contacts from 5 accounts at 1.05, largest account 60%: INSUFFICIENT by default, "within 25%" with `--max-account-share 0.7`, several shortfalls listed together; `--exclude-user-ids custE-` removes one account, a 5-character entry is rejected, a non-matching entry warns.
- Date and input cases (13, 14, 15 days ago; tomorrow; unpadded, fullwidth and impossible dates; `file:///etc/passwd`; `us west`; `--tolerance nan`; `--min-contacts 0`; `--max-account-share 0` and 1.5), AWS error text (known and unrecognised) revealing no ARN, email or name, `--help` printing no email, and hostile source files (50,000 minus signs or parentheses, a 6 MB file, 100,000 blank lines in 0.7 seconds) all behave.
- The pre-push hook skipped tsc and jest by design: no pushed commit touches `backend/`.

## Reviews

#4124: reviews 1 and 2. This PR: review 3 (head `2a94c973e`), review 4 (head `84bc481f2`), review 5 (head `63117d9e9`) and review 6 (head `f1b655374`: SAFE, two mediums and eight lows) review 7 (head `70af3c860`: SAFE, two documentation mediums and lows) and review 8 (head `a6a189610`: SAFE, ten lows) and review 9 (head `4e78fe5bd`: SAFE, no blockers, two mediums and lows). From review 9, the one finding close to the purpose (a run by an account deleted from the user table could not be excluded by `--exclude-user-ids`, a regression) is fixed in head `800f8ebcf` with a 12-line change and the docs caveats; the three findings far from the purpose (a DONE line with a malformed timestamp, a block comment opened mid-line in the source file, a traceback on malformed AWS output) were put to the owner, who said to fix them if tiny: they are fixed in head `698ac93cd` (a few lines each; a bad-timestamp DONE is counted and its run is not called unfinished, comment openers anywhere in a line hide their decoys, malformed AWS output is a clean message). The owner also decided not to run a tenth full review: the final code is proven by the 69-check regression suite and a live read-only run on prod instead.

title: fix: failure-cluster intake posts "Recurred" only when a failure is new (ENG-3088)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
The agent-mode failure-cluster loop reads a rolling 7-day window. A tool whose fix has merged stays over threshold until its old failures age out, and intake posted `Recurred on <date>` on the issue every day from those same failures. PM and the post-merge verifier read "Recurred" as "the fix did not hold".

Checked on ENG-2938 (read-only, loop events table): all three `get_ads_thresholds` failures are 11-11 10:04Z to 10:33Z. #3983 merged 11-11 22:10Z. The two calls after it (11-12, 11-14) succeeded. The 11-12 to 11-15 "Recurred" comments were those three failures.

## What this fixes (after)
`ClusterIntakeTool` compares each cluster's failure times with the newest of: the canonical issue's creation time, and its `Recurred on` / `Reopened` comments.
- No failure newer than that: no comment, and a closed canonical is not reopened. The mutation records `intake.noNewFailures: true`.
- At least one newer failure: it posts as before, with one more line: `New Since Last Comment: N of M failures`.
- No canonical yet: first filing is unchanged.

The baseline is read back from Linear. Nothing new is stored.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-3088, PM-drafted, not confirmed by Harsha)
1. Events read; premise holds for ENG-2938. Recorded on the issue. The ENG-2939 events were not read.
2. Same failures on day 2 as on day 1: no second comment. Tested.
3. A failure newer than the last comment posts and says how many are new. Tested, including counting from the newest Recurred comment and not from the filing.
4. First filing unchanged. The existing ENG-589 intake suite and the intake dedupe suites pass with no edits.
5. No new table, key or stored field. `failureTimes` is a non-enumerable property on the proposal payload, because the proposal is JSON-serialised into the learning store and the fix spec. A test asserts it does not appear in either.

One thing beyond the criteria: the same check also stops a closed canonical being reopened by failures that all predate its last post. Without it, a Done issue would be reopened daily for up to seven days, which is the same defect. Say so on ENG-3088 if that should come out.

## Complexity ledger
- `clusterIntakeTool.ts` +55: one private method, one port (`listComments`), one early return.
- `failureRuleSet.ts` +21: collects failure times per class.
- `linearService.ts` +6/-4: `createdAt` added to two existing issue queries and to `OpenIssue`. No new query.
- New test file, 9 tests. One new moving part (the comparison); no new state.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/loops.agentModeClusterIntake`
2. **Expected**: 2 suites pass (the existing ENG-589 suite and the new recurrence suite).
3. After deploy, the daily 17:30 UTC run: ENG-2938 and ENG-2939 get no new "Recurred" comment unless a failure happened since their last one. ENG-2858 gets one that includes a `New Since Last Comment` line if `playwright_browser_fill_form` failed again.

## Edge cases to check
- Fails open. No timestamps on the payload, no creation time and no marker comments, or a comment read error: it posts as before. Two tests.
- A failure recorded in the seconds between a run's event read and its comment is older than that comment and is never counted as new. It still counts toward the threshold. Not fixed here.
- A wrapper that clones or spreads the payload would drop `failureTimes` and silently return to the old behaviour. The two wrappers in use today (`withLegacyToolCooldown`, the orchestrator cap) pass proposals by reference; I read both.
- A human comment starting with "Recurred on " or "Reopened " would move the baseline.

## Test evidence
- New suite without the fix: 6 failed, 3 passed. With it: 9 passed.
- 11 suites, 251 tests pass: cluster intake, failure rule set, every intakeService suite, linearService, scheduledReportWithheldAlertDedup.
- Backend `npm run typecheck` printed no errors. I did not capture its exit code.

## What was NOT tested
- Nothing ran against live Linear or the production loop. Step 3 above is the first real proof.
- The full backend suite was not run locally. CI runs it on ready.
- The worktree borrowed `node_modules` from the canonical checkout, whose lockfile is one package behind `main` (worktree-doctor: borrowed_stale).
- Local `coderabbit review` not run.
- The pre-push hook did not pass: its backend `tsc` step hit the hook's 240s limit on this machine. Pushed with `--no-verify`, as the hook suggests. The separate typecheck above is the only local type evidence.

Rollback: revert this commit. No data to undo.

title: fix: fill_form defaults a missing field type and names the next step when a field has no ref (ENG-3089)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

**Hold before merge:** this changes tool dispatch. ENG-3089 requires before/after behaviour evidence and an Okareo simulation pass against baseline. Neither exists yet. Draft until they do.

## What was wrong (before)
#3927 (ENG-2858) repaired a missing `fields[].name` on `playwright_browser_fill_form`. The tool kept failing. Read from the loop events (read-only), four failures since that merge, all around 01:50Z:
- 3 of 4: `fields[0].type` invalid. The name is present; the field has no `type`.
- 1 of 4: `selector` in place of `ref`, no name.
- None was a stale ref or page state.

In the three `type` cases a second call a few seconds later succeeded, so the cost was one wasted step and one failure counted toward the alert. Per-failure table is on ENG-3089.

## What this fixes (after)
- The gateway repair sets `type: "textbox"` on a field with a text value and no type. It does not overwrite a type the model sent. It does not guess when the value is `true` or `false`, since that is a checkbox or radio.
- A field with no `ref`, or with a missing or unknown type that was not repaired, is rejected before the call with a next step: take a `playwright_browser_snapshot` and retry with the ref, or the list of valid types. Before, the model got the Playwright MCP zod dump.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-3089, PM-drafted, not confirmed by Harsha)
1. Done, recorded on the issue.
2. Largest group (missing type): regression test fails without the fix, passes with it.
3. Unrepairable field (no ref): unit test on the message. The issue's example was a ref that no longer exists on the page. That case did not occur in the window and is not handled here: it fails inside Playwright, after validation.
4. No failure in the window was page or browser state. Nothing to name.
5. The parent's criterion 2 stays on ENG-2858.

## Behaviour change to review
- Calls with no `type` and a text value now run as a textbox fill. If the element is really a select or a checkbox, Playwright's `fill` throws. That is a visible error, not a wrong write. For an ARIA combobox built on an input, it types the text and does not pick an option.
- Calls with no `ref` are now rejected at the gateway. `@playwright/mcp` 0.0.70 declares `ref` as a required string (`playwright-core/lib/tools/backend/form.js`), so they failed before too, one hop later. If that package is upgraded to a version that accepts `selector` alone, this check must be relaxed.
- An unknown type such as `"text"` is rejected with the list of valid types, not rewritten.

## Complexity ledger
`agentToolGatewayService.ts` +58: one repair block beside the existing name repair, one branch in `validateSemanticToolContract`, one constant, one helper. Tests +66 (4 cases). No new state, no new dependency.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/agentToolGatewayService.test.ts`
2. **Expected**: 223 tests pass.
3. After deploy: the daily run that calls `playwright_browser_fill_form` around 01:50Z records no `fields[0].type` failure.

## Test evidence
- The 4 new cases without the fix: 4 failed. With it: the file's 223 tests pass.
- Backend `npm run typecheck` exit 0.

## What was NOT tested
- No Okareo simulation and no dev before/after run. Required before merge (see top).
- No browser, no Playwright MCP process. The claim that 0.0.70 requires `ref` comes from reading its schema source, not from calling it.
- Whether the recorded `failedArgsJson` is the repaired or the original arguments. I assumed repaired, because `name` appears there after #3927 and not before.
- The full backend suite was not run locally.
- The worktree borrowed `node_modules` from the canonical checkout, one package behind `main`.
- Local `coderabbit review` not run.
- The pre-push hook did not pass: its backend `tsc` step hit the hook's 240s limit on this machine. Pushed with `--no-verify`, as the hook suggests. The separate typecheck above is the only local type evidence.

Rollback: revert this commit.

`staging-env-override.sh` now runs against real backend staging. Before, it exited 2 on `Agentweb-backend-env-1` because that name does not contain the word "staging", so the ENG-2353 kill-switch proof could not run.

- Production (`Agentweb-backend-env-prod-3`) is refused first, with its own message. Every other name is refused too. All refusals exit 2 before any AWS call.
- Both names are `readonly` constants in the script. No variable a caller passes can change them.
- `AWS_REGION` defaults to `us-west-2`. The old default was `us-east-1`, where there are no Elastic Beanstalk environments, so the script would not have found staging even with the name fixed. This second fix is not in the issue; I recorded it there.
- `docs/staging-env-overrides.md` gives the lookup that works: `gh variable get <name> --env staging`. The names are variables on the GitHub `staging` environment, and the same command without `--env` reports "not found".

2. Runs against the staging environment and no other; no substring guess. Done. The name is a constant in the script rather than passed in, so that criterion 3 holds whatever the caller passes. The cost: if staging is renamed, the script and its test need a one-line edit.
3. Production refused by exact name whatever else is passed; tests for staging accepted, production refused, unknown refused, empty refused. 5. `show` run once against real staging. Done. It exited 0 and printed nothing, because no `LEAD_MAGNET_*` override is set there. A direct read of the same environment listed 60 properties, none starting with `LEAD_MAGNET`. `set` and `restore` were not run against any real environment.

3. `EB_ENVIRONMENT_NAME=Agentweb-backend-env-1 EB_APPLICATION_NAME=agentweb-backend bash .github/scripts/staging-env-override.sh show` exits 0.

Not customer-visible. The script is not called by any workflow; only its test runs in CI. Rollback: revert this commit. Post-merge check: the `CI script tests` job passes on main.

title: [needs human] fix: termination guard retries the lifecycle hook answer until the hook opens (ENG-3093)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

**Hold before merge (decision, ENG-3093 criterion 5):** a scheduled run can still be in flight when the hook is answered, in one case: the drain hit its 10-minute ceiling with work still running. Today that run gets up to 3 more minutes by accident; with this change it does not. The issue says to stop and ask in that case. Draft until Harsha answers on ENG-3093.

## What was wrong (before)
On every prod backend update the old instance stayed up 13 to 15 minutes. The termination hook only opens after the load balancer's 600 s connection draining. The guard answered as soon as the app's drain returned, got "No active Lifecycle Action found", retried for 14 seconds and gave up. The hook was then answered only because the process force-exited at drain ceiling + 3 minutes and its replacement answered it. Source: the ENG-3083 diagnosis, which I did not re-measure.

## What this fixes (after)
The guard retries that one reply every 15 seconds for up to 12 minutes (48 waits), so it answers within 15 seconds of the hook opening. Two constants changed in `backend/src/services/asgLifecycleGuard.ts`; the retry loop is unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-3093, PM-drafted, not confirmed by a human)
1. Done. New unit test: the reply is "not active" for 10 simulated minutes, then succeeds; exactly one attempt lands after the hook opens, less than 15 s after it.
2. Done. Limit is 49 attempts / 12 minutes; the existing test for the limit now asserts 49 attempts, 48 waits, 12 minutes in total, and the same "hook will time out" log line.
3. Done, unchanged. Existing test: an AccessDenied error is tried once.
4. Done. The new test fails if the answer is attempted before the drain callback has returned.
5. **Not met for merge: the answer is "yes, it can".** See below.
6. Not done. Needs a prod deploy.

## Criterion 5: can a run be in flight when the hook is answered?
Read from `runDrain` in `backend/src/server.ts` and `DRAIN_CEILING_MS` (10 minutes):
- Normal case, no. The drain returns when all tracked work has settled, and cron is disabled first, so no new run starts. The guard then waits for the hook and answers at about minute 10.
- Ceiling case, yes. If a run is still going after 10 minutes, the drain returns anyway and logs it as stuck. By then the hook is open, so the first answer succeeds and the instance is terminated at about minute 10. Today the same run lives until the force-exit at minute 13.
- What that run can still do in those 3 minutes is limited: `runDrain` has already closed the HTTP listener, the MCP sessions and the parent MCP clients. I did not test whether a run in that state can finish.

Options for Harsha, on the issue:
- A. Accept it: a run past the 10-minute ceiling is cut about 3 minutes sooner.
- B. Answer the hook early only when the drain reported everything settled; when it hit the ceiling, keep today's path. Needs `runDrain` to return its result; small follow-up change.

## Behaviour change to review
- Up to 48 warn lines, one every 15 s, on each terminating instance while it waits for the hook.
- The old 14-second window is gone; the "bounds to fifteen attempts" test was changed to the new limit, because the issue changes that contract.

## Complexity ledger
2 constants and a comment in the guard. Tests +45 lines (1 new case, 1 updated). No new state, branch or dependency.

1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/asgLifecycleGuard.test.ts`
2. **Expected**: 18 tests pass.
3. After deploy: read the Auto Scaling activity history for the next prod update. Expected old-instance termination at about 10 to 11 minutes (an estimate from ENG-3083, not measured).

## Test evidence
- With the old constants: 2 of 18 fail (the new case and the updated limit). With the change: 18 pass.

## What was NOT tested
- No real termination. Nothing here proves when the hook opens on AWS; that is from ENG-3083.

title: fix: no run-wide LinkedIn invite-block notice when a later invite went out on another account (ENG-3092)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

## What was wrong (before)
On 2026-11-11 a scheduled LinkedIn run (session `97d98044`) had 5 invites refused on a disconnected account, then sent 10 on a second account. The session note, the owner email text and the oncall alert all said "No invitations can be sent ... the remaining invitations were not sent" and "fully blocked".

`detectLinkedInInviteSendBlock` took the first failed send-invite that matched a block pattern and returned a run-wide notice. It never looked at later invites.

## What this fixes (after)
A matching failure no longer produces the notice if a later send-invite in the same run succeeded on a different account. One check, applied to all three patterns (disconnected, cooldown, pacing), because each of them belongs to one sending account.

No new owner-facing text. A run in this state now gets no added notice, which is what the owner saw before #3970. That default was set by the PM tick on ENG-3092, not by a human; the wording question is ENG-3097.

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-3092, agent-drafted; PM scoped the executor to 1 to 3)
1. Done. Disconnected failure, later success on another account: `null`, so no session note, no email text, no oncall alert.
2. Done. No later invite (the `5ce91f8f` shape), or only failed later invites: notice unchanged.
3. Done. Regression test replays the 21 send-invite calls of session `97d98044` in stored order: 5 disconnected, 10 sent, 3 daily-ceiling refusals, 3 identity refusals. Error strings are the stored ones with the lead name, company and profile URL replaced. Read from prod `AW-ChatMessages`, read-only.
4. Not in this PR (ENG-3097).

PM's extra question, whether cooldown and pacing can give the same false notice: yes by reading the code, same shape; no real case seen. Fixed here because it is the same check.

## Behaviour change to review
- The 11-11 ledger now yields no notice at all. Its three daily-ceiling refusals ("today's safety ceiling of 10 ... daily safety limit") do not match the existing pacing pattern, so they never produced a pacing notice and still do not. Not changed here.
- Still possible, not changed: a block on an account that sent invites earlier in the same run keeps the notice and the "fully blocked" oncall subject, although some invites went out.
- If one call names an account and the other does not, they count as different accounts. If neither does, they count as the same and the notice stays.

## Complexity ledger
`agentModeController.ts` +11 / -1: one helper, one extra condition in the existing `find`. Tests +95 (9 cases). No new state, text or dependency.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/eng3092.linkedInInviteBlockLaterSuccess.test.ts src/__tests__/eng2900.linkedInDisconnectedBlock.test.ts`
2. **Expected**: 12 tests pass.
3. After deploy: the next scheduled run that is refused on one account and sends on another has no "No invitations can be sent" message at the end of its session.

## Test evidence
- New file without the fix: 4 of 9 fail. With it: 9 pass.
- 5 neighbouring suites that reference this function or its notices: 196 tests pass.
- Backend `npm run typecheck`: exit 0.

## What was NOT tested
- No scheduled run was executed. The session note, email and alert were not exercised; they read the same return value (lines 8134 to 8177).
- The full backend suite was not run locally.
- Whether other runs since 11-11 carried the false notice.

title: fix: termination guard keeps polling after a failed metadata read (ENG-3094)
body:
## What this does

The ASG termination guard (`backend/src/services/asgLifecycleGuard.ts`) used to stop polling for the life of the process after ONE "unavailable" IMDS read: the token fetch failed, or `autoscaling/target-lifecycle-state` returned 404. It logged the same line for both. On 2026-11-16 prod instance `i-083786db744a33a52`, which was in the group, logged "not an ASG instance" at boot; nothing answered its termination hook and it waited out the 900 s heartbeat (26m44s to terminate, against 14-16.5 min for the other five that day).

Now:

- The guard gives up only after `UNAVAILABLE_READS_BEFORE_DISABLE` = 60 consecutive unavailable reads (5 minutes at the 5 s poll). Any read that is not unavailable resets the count; that includes a non-404 error status on the state path, not only a 200.
- A 404 counts toward the same streak as a failed token fetch. AWS documents the item as present only once the instance has transitioned to a target lifecycle state, "otherwise ... you receive an HTTP 404 error", and tells callers to poll and retry ([source](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/retrieving-target-lifecycle-state-through-imds.html)). The page does not give a timing, so this is the cautious reading, not a proven early-404.
- The log names the cause: `IMDS token fetch failed` or `autoscaling/target-lifecycle-state returned 404`.
- A machine outside a group logs two lines in total: one warn on the first failed read, one "termination guard disabled" at give-up.
- An unavailable read also resets the two-read `Terminated` confirmation streak (not asked for; keeps "two consecutive confirming reads" literally true).

## Acceptance criteria (ENG-3094, PM-drafted, not confirmed by a human)

| # | Criterion | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Log names which case occurred | Done, unit test |
| 2 | Token failure does not disable on first occurrence; stated number | Done: 60, reason in the constant's comment and on the issue |
| 3 | Decide the 404 case from AWS docs | Done: treated like a token failure, source above |
| 4 | Off-group machine still ends up off, no per-poll logging | Done, unit test (2 lines total) |
| 5 | Transient failure then normal read still drains and answers the hook | Done, unit tests for both causes |
| 6 | Next three prod instances log no "guard disabled" at boot | NOT done, needs a deploy |

## Tests

`backend/src/__tests__/asgLifecycleGuard.test.ts`: 25 passed locally. Against the old source 8 of the 25 fail (6 new behaviour tests plus the 2 updated return-shape tests). 6 mutations of the new code, all caught. eslint clean on both files.

## How to test

1. `cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/asgLifecycleGuard.test.ts`
2. After deploy: in the prod log group, search the boot window of the next three instances for `termination guard disabled`. Expect none. A `lifecycle state unavailable (...); still polling` warn is acceptable and names the cause.

## Not tested

- Nothing was run on an EC2 instance. Why IMDS failed at boot on 2026-11-16, and which of the two causes it was, is still unknown; the new log line is what will tell.
- Local run used a node_modules link into another worktree with identical manifests; `worktree-doctor` flags that link as unsafe. CI is the clean run.
- A token failure lasting five unbroken minutes on a real ASG instance still disables the guard.

## Complexity ledger

+1 constant, +1 counter, +1 optional field on the read result. No new module, no new dependency, no stored state. Backend-only, no customer-visible change, no database or data-plane change.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. With the guard off the hook still times out to CONTINUE.

Accountable-GitHub: harshmoney123
