Customer-visible: yes (Emma asks before re-posting a live caption). Not dark.

## AC mapping
1. Read-only check against the account's stored posts — `findLiveDuplicateCaption` in `backend/src/emma/impl/linkedin.ts`.
2. Match → no publish, structured result + confirm flag. No prompt changes; only the new arg description and a short tool-result message.
3. Confirm flag set, no match, drafts, other platforms, scheduled publisher, `/api` route: unchanged (guard is only requested by the Emma tool).
4. Jest, mocked DB/adapter: match blocks, confirm proceeds, no match proceeds, other account ignored, DB read failure fails open, draft skips.
5. No table/index/schema change. No live LinkedIn calls.

- `npx jest` over all 69 suites referencing the tool/function: 1929 pass; the only red is `socialAdapters.publishRevalidation.test.ts` (2), which fails identically on clean `origin/main` 65ff68ae (stale `uploadImageFromUrl` mock), untouched here.

- Attribution: author+committer resolve to harshmoney123.

## Not tested
Live LinkedIn; captions only in LinkedIn but not yet synced to the posts cache are not caught (cache is the source by AC 1).

## Rollback
Revert this PR; no data written.

Risk: Low

Adds a duplicate-caption guard to Emma's LinkedIn `post_on_connected_account` tool. A caption that matches a stored post in the newest 50 blocks publishing and returns `duplicate_caption: true`. `confirm_duplicate_caption: true` bypasses the guard. Drafts and other platforms are unchanged.

Review notes:
- Verified: the guard runs only when `platform === 'linkedin'`, `!saveAsDraft`, and `duplicateCaptionGuard === true`. The tool sets that flag whenever `confirm_duplicate_caption` is not true.

title: fix(zoma): require paid invoice before publishing (dark, stacked on #4156)
body:
## Summary
Stacked on #4156, not a duplicate billing implementation. Harsha’s latest Slack decision is $50/month including 5,000 successful calls, then 1 cent/call, entered through the $1 seven-day trial at first publish.

- Require an expanded latest invoice with status paid as well as trialing/active subscription state before publish entitlement.
- Fail closed for absent/unexpanded/unpaid invoice evidence; do not offer a second subscription checkout while payment is pending on an otherwise-live plan.
- Match zoma_status readiness to the same entitlement.
- Document the architecture, exact Slack source timestamps, inherited implementation limitations and live launch gates in docs/zoma-payments-design.md.

## Scope and safety
Dark behind the inherited ZOMA_BILLING_ENABLED flag. No live charges, Stripe writes, price creation, staging/prod deployment, database changes or ad-account actions. Review/merge after #4156, or cherry-pick this change into that implementation. Base branch is explicitly yugo/eng-3130.

## Verification
- TDD: six negative invoice-entitlement cases failed before the rule change; pending-payment presentation tests also failed before implementation.
- Five scoped Jest suites: 128 passed, zero failures (new entitlement, existing billing, onboarding, device flow and payment setup).
- Inherited rate-limiter intervals keep the suite alive; detectOpenHandles identified the two timers. Final scoped run used --forceExit.
- git diff --check passed.
- Scoped TypeScript check rooted at the three touched TS files exhausted its bounded 2.5 GiB heap via transitive imports. No full-repo typecheck was run; typecheck is NOT proven locally. Normal local hooks were bypassed to avoid an unscoped full check on the shared-memory host.

## Remaining blockers / open questions
- Bookface post 128626 redirects to YC login. Browser vault has no YC account, so its contents are unread and not inferred.
- Hosted Checkout payment, test-clock conversion and overage invoice must be verified in Stripe test mode before live enablement. Prior Slack reports of API-created subscriptions do not prove hosted Checkout, and were not rerun here.
- Clarify whether reads/drafts are free only before subscription or permanently: #4156 meters all successful gateway calls after a billing customer exists.
- Inherited duplicate-checkout, fire-and-forget meter delivery, multi-instance reminder and cancellation-on-expiry risks are documented, not resolved by this focused correction.

## Rollback
Keep ZOMA_BILLING_ENABLED unset. Reverting this correction needs no migration, but reintroduces unpaid-trial publishing if billing is enabled.

title: feat: Zoma redesign — agent-first onboarding without Emma, pal classification, zoma_ads_report (ENG-3134)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Zoma's MCP onboarding still leaned on Emma. A user who connected with `claude mcp add` and then followed the Meta link from `zoma_status` landed on the AgentWeb (Emma) portal callback, which needs a portal session and its onboarding. The card link returned to `app.agentweb.pro/settings`, and shared Meta errors said "Settings -> Connected accounts". The first contact was a setup checklist rather than a greeting. A friend ("just a friend") got a long message and showed up as `test` on the scoreboard. Tool results had no next step, and no single tool answered "how are my ads doing".

## What this fixes (after)
From the first MCP connect, Zoma runs without the Emma app:
- MCP `initialize` sends `instructions` that open with **"Hey, welcome to Zoma."**. The first `zoma_status` returns that greeting plus **one** question ("How familiar are you with ads?") and no checklist or links.
- Both "ads" answers (`runs_ads`, `new_to_ads`) lead straight to the **Meta connect link**. Its signed state (`zoma: "mcp"`) is forwarded by the existing `/api/oauth/meta/callback` to Zoma's own pages (`/api/zoma/meta/callback`, picker, no-ad-account guide). Those pages finish server-side for that user and say "Go back to your agent and say: Check my Zoma setup". The device-flow browser path for `new_to_ads` also goes straight to Meta, and the setup guide now appears on the "No ad account found" page.
- When connected, the reply is "All set." plus a **docs link** (`/api/meta-toolkit/skill.md`) and a **concrete first prompt** that runs the new report.
- **Every tool response** gets a `Next step:` block (MCP) or a `next_step` field (REST). The exceptions are `zoma_status`, which already carries its own next step, and the friend path. A 403 about the user's own setup includes the fix. Shared Meta refusals have "Settings -> Connected accounts" rewritten to the Zoma reconnect path.
- **Friend path** is exactly `Thanks for signing up and trying out Zoma.` On the scoreboard (lead list) it is classified **`pal`**, with a `pal` chip in the partner portal and `summary.palUsers`. Activation-queue rows carry `classification: pal|prospect`. Pals stay out of potential-user counts and help alerts.
- New read-only **`zoma_ads_report`**: spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, conversions and ROAS per campaign (or account total) for a `date_preset` or `since`/`until`, with optional `campaign_ids`. It makes one paged Graph insights read with the connected account's token, which is never echoed. It is listed in tools/list with `readOnlyHint`, works on Databricks, is documented in skill.md and is named in the "All set" prompt.
- The card return (only when `ZOMA_REQUIRE_PAYMENT_METHOD=true`) goes to Zoma's `/api/zoma/done?mcp=1`, not Emma settings.

OAuth consent branding (portal consent page) is unchanged, as allowed. Gmail with Zoma intent and the no-Emma-detour behaviour from ENG-3124/25/26/28 are kept.

## Complexity ledger
- Net ≈ +600 / −110 lines. About 330 of the added lines are the new acceptance test (`eng3134.zomaRedesign.test.ts`), about 230 are `zomaAdsReport.ts` and about 60 are `zomaNextStep.ts`.
- Moving parts added: one read-only tool (no storage, no writes) and one pure next-step/voice helper at the transport. Nothing new in persistence: no table, index, flag or dependency. The MCP Meta link reuses the existing registered redirect URI and Zoma pages (one `zoma: "mcp"` state value plus a `uid` claim on the existing signed picker link).
- Removed: the guide-first detour page for `new_to_ads`, and the Emma-portal destinations for MCP Meta connect and card return.
- AgentMode/Emma chat behaviour is unchanged. The shared Meta messages are rewritten only on the Zoma transport.

## How to test
1. `claude mcp add --transport http zoma https://api.agentweb.pro/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` with a fresh account → the agent opens with "Hey, welcome to Zoma." and asks one question.
2. Answer "I already run ads" → the reply is the Meta connect link (facebook.com). Log in → you land on `api.agentweb.pro/api/zoma/meta/callback` → "Meta connected. Go back to your agent…". At no point do you see app.agentweb.pro.
3. Say "check my Zoma setup" → "All set." with the docs link and the first prompt. Ask it → `zoma_ads_report` returns per-campaign spend/impressions/clicks/CTR/CPC/conversions/ROAS.
4. As another user, answer "Not interested, just a friend" → exactly "Thanks for signing up and trying out Zoma." Partner portal → Zoma scoreboard shows that user with a `pal` chip, and they are not counted.

## Edge cases to check
- Multiple Meta ad accounts → Zoma picker → "Meta connected". No ad account → setup guide plus a fresh Reconnect link. Forged or expired state → rejected, nothing connected.
- Page blocker after connect → guided fix page with a fresh MCP Reconnect link (ENG-3125 behaviour on the new path).
- `zoma_ads_report`: bad dates, presets, ids or level are refused before any Meta call. Meta code 190 → "reconnect" message. Paging is capped at 10 pages.

## Test Evidence
- Backend (Atem, serial): 53 Zoma/toolkit suites, **822 tests passed, 0 failed**. This includes the new `eng3134.zomaRedesign.test.ts` (18 tests: real `/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` → gateway → Zoma tools → `/api/oauth/meta/callback` forward → Zoma pages. Only the user row, connected accounts, usage events, Meta OAuth finalize and Graph `fetch` are mocked). Mutation check: removing the Emma-text rewrite or the `title` makes it fail.
- Scoped `tsc --noEmit` over every changed file and test: clean. A full backend tsc OOMs on this 9.7 GB box, so CI's Backend build is the full-compile proof.
- Partner portal: `ZomaScoreboardTab.test.tsx` 3/3, including the new `pal` chip and caption.
- Note: `eng2823.googleToolkit.test.ts` was already failing on `main` (ENG-3128 made the question the first step). Its fixture user now has `zomaAdsExperience: runs_ads`.

## Local CodeRabbit review (CLI, before push)
5 findings. Fixed 4: the report refuses rather than returning partial totals past the 10-page cap; ROAS is always purchase value even when conversions count leads; an unreadable or data-less Graph response is a read failure; the all-set prompt is Google-specific when only Google is connected. Each has a regression test. Not changed: "redirect MCP Meta states to the Zoma callback". `/api/oauth/meta/callback` already forwards any `zoma` state, and the end-to-end test covers that hop.

## Behavioral assertions verified
| Requirement (Harsha, 2026-11-16) | Test |
|---|---|
| First MCP connect → "Hey, welcome to Zoma." + one question | `initialize tells the agent…`, `runs the whole journey…` step 1 |
| Answer → Meta connect directly | `runs the whole journey…` step 2, `new_to_ads also leads with the Meta link`, eng3128 device flow `new_to_ads: … straight to Meta` |
| No Emma redirects in user-facing Zoma flows | `runs the whole journey…` (callback → Zoma page, no app.agentweb.pro), `shared Meta refusals never point at the Emma settings screen`, eng2303 card return URLs |
| Once connected: docs link + concrete next prompt | `runs the whole journey…` step 4, eng3078 `ALL_SET` |
| Every tool response has an actionable next step | `a read, a refusal and a missing-account call each end with "Next step:"`, eng2295/eng2288 |
| Friend path exact text, `pal`, excluded from counts | `friend path` describe, eng3128 scoreboard/queue, partner-portal test |
| Meta ad reporting tool (campaign/date range, spend, impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, conversions, ROAS) | `zoma_ads_report` describe (discoverable, computed metrics + totals, filters, validation, expired token) |

## Files changed
- Zoma flow: `backend/src/mcp/zomaAdsExperience.ts`, `zomaOnboarding.ts`, `zomaDeviceFlow.ts`, `zomaSetupLinks.ts`, `backend/src/routes/zoma.ts`
- Transport + next step: `backend/src/routes/metaToolkit.ts`, `backend/src/mcp/zomaNextStep.ts` (new), `zomaDatabricksReadOnly.ts`
- Reporting: `backend/src/mcp/zomaAdsReport.ts` (new), `metaToolkitManifest.ts`, `metaToolkitGateway.ts`, `toolkitToolAnnotations.ts`, `backend/docs/meta-toolkit-skill.md`
- Lead list: `backend/src/services/zomaScoreboard.ts`, `zomaActivationQueue.ts`, `partner-portal/src/components/admin/ZomaScoreboardTab.tsx`
- Tests: new `eng3134.zomaRedesign.test.ts`, plus updated contract assertions in eng2282/2288/2295/2303/2571/2823/2902/3078/3125/3128 and `ZomaScoreboardTab.test.tsx`

## What was NOT tested
- A live Meta OAuth login against real Facebook. This needs a human Facebook login; after deploy, the production link is checked down to the Meta dialog and the callback forward.
- A live `zoma_ads_report` against a real ad account. It is a read; the post-deploy smoke covers the MCP surface and tools/list.
- Google Ads connect (ENG-3135, Anurag) is not changed here and still uses the portal flow. Google is gated by `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED`.

## Database / copy classification
- No database or data-plane change: no table, index, key or persistence-model change. Existing user-row fields are written exactly as before.
- User-facing copy: the strings are the ones Harsha specified ("Hey, welcome to Zoma.", "Thanks for signing up and trying out Zoma.") plus functional setup instructions.

## Rollback
Revert this PR (backend + partner portal deploy on merge). No data migration to undo.

## Linear issue
ENG-3134. Related: ENG-3124, ENG-3125, ENG-3126, ENG-3128 (kept), ENG-3135, ENG-3136 (Anurag's; the MCP Meta path here gives ENG-3136 a Zoma-owned resume/no-ad-account guide, but its provider-side create-account root cause is not claimed).

title: [needs human] Zoma Google Ads connect returns to the agent, without campaign creation or invented defaults (ENG-3135)
body:
What was wrong: the Google Ads connect link from zoma_status signed only userId+nonce, so Google's callback always redirected into the customer portal (Emma) finalize flow rather than back to Zoma/the agent. When no connect link could be minted, zoma_status fell back to the bare https://ads.google.com, which is Google's campaign-signup funnel (provider-hosted, locale-prefilled country), and the 'no account' guidance did not tell users to avoid a campaign or to pick country/currency/time zone themselves. Nothing in our code sets a country/locale/currency (the OAuth URL carries only standard params + access_type/prompt; a test pins this), so the 'Italy' default is attributed to Google's own signup prefill, though this could not be confirmed without the recording/screenshots.

What changed: (1) connect link state carries zoma:'mcp' for MCP users (same pattern as Meta); /api/oauth/google-ads/callback forwards such states to new GET /api/zoma/google/callback, which finalizes server-side for the signed state's user and renders Zoma pages (auto-connect for one account, signed picker for several, retry pages, 'back to your agent'); POST /api/zoma/google/select connects only offered accounts. title: ENG-3131: Zoma $1 trial paywall — rebase of #4156 plus reminder, entitlement and cancel fixes (dark)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

Dark billing. Nothing changes in production until `ZOMA_BILLING_ENABLED=true` and the Stripe objects exist. Rollback: leave the flag unset.

## What this PR is
ENG-3131 (Zoma paywall at first publish: $1 7-day trial, then $50/mo; day-3 email). It is **#4156 rebased onto current `main`, plus fixes for the gaps found in review**. It contains #4156's commits, so it supersedes #4156 and the stacked draft #4159; whoever owns those can close them once this is accepted. Based on `main` (not `yugo/eng-3130`) because the old branch no longer merges cleanly and a diff against it would carry unrelated main commits.

Read #4156's description for the billing design, env vars and Stripe setup. Only the delta is described here.

## Delta over #4156
1. **Conflicts with main resolved** (`zomaOnboarding.ts`, `metaToolkitGateway.ts`): kept main's `ads_experience` / `blocker` / `docs_url` and the PR's `plan`.
2. **Day-3 email delivery.** `emailService.sendEmail` never throws; it returns `sent | suppressed | failed`. The job ignored that, so a failed send was recorded as sent with no retry. The marker on the subscription is now written only after a non-failed send; a failed send retries on the next hourly pass; `suppressed` (non-prod mail guard) is marked done and not counted.
3. **One send across instances.** `isCronEnabled()` is only a drain flag. Each pass claims `(subscription, hour)` with a conditional write on the existing usage-event table (`trial_reminder_claimed`). No new table.
4. **Ad performance in the email** (ticket: "short summary of how their ads are doing"): the account-level `zoma_ads_report` summary for the trial window (Meta), falling back to the usage summary when there is no usable ad account or no data. Google Ads has no report yet.
5. **Entitlement.** `active` always publishes; `trialing` publishes only when the expanded latest invoice (the $1 fee) is `paid`. An unpaid trial returns "payment pending, do not start a second plan" and mints no new checkout. The invoice of an `active` plan is not consulted (Stripe keeps a renewal invoice in draft for about an hour, which would block paying users under #4159's rule).
6. **Cancel at card entry** (ticket: track cancels). Stripe does not substitute the session id into `cancel_url` (documented only for success/return URLs), so the cancel redirect carries the user id plus an HMAC. Landing on it records `checkout_canceled` once per user per hour. `checkout.session.expired` now records `checkout_expired`.

7. **Review round (two independent reviewers, findings verified before fixing):**
   - Funnel rows with a `dedupeKey` embedded the timestamp in the sort key, so the conditional write could never see a repeat (broke the reminder claim and cancel dedupe). Key no longer contains `ts`.
   - The Zoma plan customer carried the user's email and Emma looks customers up by email alone, so Emma could adopt it. Plan customer is now created without an email, and Emma's two by-email lookups (`routes/stripe.ts`) skip customers tagged `zomaBillingUserId`.
   - Every blocked write / `zoma_status` minted a new open Checkout, so one user could buy two plans. An open Zoma Checkout with at least an hour left is reused.
   - A user who cancelled the trial no longer gets "cancel before you are charged"; `zoma_status` says it will not renew. `paywall_shown` is recorded once per hour per surface. Paywall copy says the card is charged automatically after the trial. Google go-live gate now has a gateway test (the Google path is dark behind `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED`, so the earlier tests never reached it).
   - Rejected: failed in-band calls staying out of `mcp_tool_used` (it feeds `zoma_usage`'s "used", which must equal what Stripe bills; already listed under #4156's "Live on merge"). Not done, product call: a user can cancel and buy another $1 trial.
   - `ZOMA_REQUIRE_PAYMENT_METHOD` is NOT repurposed as the ticket words it: the paywall is a separate gate and the flag still means "card at signup", so it must stay unset (comment added in `zomaOnboarding.ts`).

8. **Failed-call audit row (from #4166, authored by Manan Varma, cherry-picked here):** a call that fails in-band still writes one `mcp_tool_failed` row (tool, platform, client only), never counted as usage and never sent to Stripe. This resolves the earlier "failed calls leave no audit trail" concern without changing what `zoma_usage` or the meter count. Reviewed: the usage readers filter on `MCP_USAGE_EVENT_TYPES` and count only `mcp_tool_used`.
9. **Rebased on current main** (merge commit; the only conflict was `createZomaRouter`, which now takes `(deps, googleDeps, billingDeps)`).
10. **Real Stripe test-mode rehearsal run (31/31 passed):** `backend/src/scripts/zomaBillingRehearsal.ts` against a Stripe sandbox with a test clock and a hosted Checkout paid with the 4242 test card. Proven: $1 charged while `trialing`, 7-day trial, day-3 reminder (clock time injected), day-7 conversion with a draft renewal invoice not blocking publish, overage billed 2 cents for 5 calls on a 3-call tier, all 17 events claimed before the Emma handlers. Not proven: a real Meta write through staging (ENG-2930), the real webhook endpoint config and API version, live mode.

No database or data-plane change: no table, column, index or user-row write; funnel rows reuse the existing event table with new `step` values.

## Verification
- Suites run (jest, 2 workers): 83 Zoma / toolkit / Stripe / usage-event suites, **1,217 passed, 0 failed** (plus `eng2282.metaToolkitManifest`, which cannot load locally). Billing suite: 83 passed (new cases: email outcomes, claim, ad-summary fallback, entitlement matrix, signed cancel redirect, Google gate, checkout reuse, funnel dedupe, cancelled trial).
- Scoped typecheck: no errors in any touched file. The full `npm run typecheck` fails on this machine only for missing modules in untouched files (`twilio`, `tesseract.js`, `botbuilder`, `sanitize-html`), so the pre-push hook was bypassed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`. The GitHub Backend build is the full-build proof.
- `eng2282.metaToolkitManifest` did not load locally for the same missing-`twilio` reason; it is unrelated to this change.

## NOT verified (needs Stripe test mode before the flag goes on)
- Nothing has run against real Stripe: the $1 one-time line charged while the subscription is `trialing`, day-7 conversion to $50, the overage invoice, meter events, and the webhook events.
- Test clock: the code does not attach customers to a clock. For the acceptance run, pre-create a test-clock customer with `metadata.zomaBillingUserId=<userId>`; unknown whether meter-event timestamps behave on a test clock.
- Staging mail is suppressed unless the recipient is in `NONPROD_EMAIL_ALLOWLIST`.
- Still open from #4156: prices are trusted by id (no check against env copy), meter sends are fire-and-forget, repeat checkouts can open duplicate sessions, reads are metered once a plan exists. Product decisions pending with the founders.

## Launch gates
Test-mode run with evidence on ENG-3130/3131, `#feature-launches` post (AGENTS.md), then `ZOMA_BILLING_ENABLED=true` with live price ids.

ENG-3131, ENG-3130

title: Session-breaker shadow on by default in code (ENG-2812)
body:
## What
Turns the ENG-2953 session-breaker **shadow** counter on by default in code. It stays off only when `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW` is `false`, `0` or `off` (trimmed, case-insensitive). Three code lines plus tests and a dev.md fragment.

## Why
Prod Elastic Beanstalk's environment-variable block is at CloudFormation's 4096-character cap (88 properties, about 4,180 characters). On 2026-11-16 17:33Z setting `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW=true` was rejected and EB rolled itself back (no instance launched, version label unchanged, health Warning for about a minute then Green/Ok). So the flag cannot be set on prod. Manan chose to default it on in code (Yugo's option 2); Yugo agreed on the thread and changes nothing in EB.

## What it does when on (unchanged from ENG-2953)
Counts turns and spend per session in memory and logs one `session_breaker_would_pause` JSON line per cap multiple crossed (defaults 40 turns or $5; `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW_MAX_TURNS`, `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW_MAX_SPEND_USD`). It never pauses a session, changes a response, writes a table or notifies anyone. Counts are per instance and reset on restart. Purpose: real would-pause evidence for ENG-2812 per-tier caps.

## Safety answer
- **Safe for prod?** Yes as far as I can tell: the function is wrapped in a try/catch, only reads in-memory state, and the sole output is a log line. The `costUsd` callback is now evaluated on every turn (before, never); it reads `response.usage` or calls `estimateCost`, and any throw is swallowed.
- **Could it regress or anger users?** No visible behaviour change. Extra cost per turn is a Map lookup and a pure evaluator call. Memory is bounded at 5,000 tracked sessions (oldest evicted). Log volume is at most one line per 40 turns (or per $5) of a session.
- **Rollback:** revert this commit and deploy. Setting `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW=false` on prod EB is NOT available while the env block is over the cap (EB rejects any config update, even changing an existing value).

## Tests
- `sessionBreakerShadow.test.ts` (6 tests): explicit-off values (`false`, ` FALSE `, `0`, `off`) never call the evaluator or the cost callback and log nothing; new test: flag unset gives default caps (40, $5) and exactly one would-pause line at turn 40, return value undefined.
- `sessionSpendBreaker` + `loops.agentModeWiring` + all 21 `src/__tests__/agentMode/` suites (133 tests) pass on Node 22; `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint reports the same 3 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` errors in the shadow test as on main, none new.

## Live test (exact head `de47c8fab`, env1 test instance, Dev DB)
Backend rsynced from this branch to env1 and rebuilt; only `SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW_MAX_TURNS=1` set, the flag itself left UNSET. Real turn through `POST /api/agent-mode/generate` as the env1 test account:
- **Flag unset:** HTTP 200, reply "ok" (unchanged), and exactly one log line `session_breaker_would_pause` with `turns:1, spendUsd:0, multiple:1, action:pause_for_confirmation, reason:turn_cap, isScheduled:false, maxTurns:1, maxSpendUsd:5`.
- **`SESSION_BREAKER_SHADOW=false`:** same request, HTTP 200, reply "ok", 0 would-pause lines.
- env1 override removed afterwards. Not live-tested on prod: the flag cannot be set there; the post-deploy check is EB Green/Ok (Yugo) plus would-pause lines appearing in prod logs once a real session passes 40 turns or $5.

## Independent review
A fresh full review of this exact head by an agent that did not write it: **SAFE, no blocker or medium findings.** It checked that no path can throw, hang or change a live turn (every new call is inside the try/catch), memory/CPU bounds (Map capped at 5,000 sessions, about 2 microseconds per repeat turn), log volume (at most turns/40 lines per session) and content (opaque ids only, JSON-encoded), env parsing, shared-state effects on the test suites (155 suites, 2,476 tests pass), test strength (reverting to `!== 'true'` fails the new test) and rollback (single-commit revert). One low item: `dev.md` line 696 still says "DARK"; dev.md cannot be edited directly (fragment guard) and the new fragment supersedes it.

## Deploy note
Prod is currently on `backend-20261117-pr3c2d8b097` (= current main), so this merge's backend deploy ships only this change.

title: fix(zoma): audit failed in-band calls with an unmetered mcp_tool_failed row (ENG-3130, stacked on #4163)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: High

Stacked on #4163 (base is `anurag/eng-3131-zoma-paywall`, not `main`). Merge it into that branch and it rides #4163 to main; do not merge it to main on its own. Billing stays dark behind `ZOMA_BILLING_ENABLED`; this change does not need the flag.

## What was wrong (before)
#4163 stops writing an `mcp_tool_used` row for a call that reports failure in-band (`success:false`, not a PREVIEW and not a write with a read-back verdict). That is right for billing and usage, but it also means a failed Meta or Google write attempt leaves no row at all. On `main` it still left one. The latest independent review of #4163 flags exactly this: no audit trail for failed write attempts.

## What this fixes (after)
- A failed in-band call writes one `mcp_tool_failed` row (`recordMcpToolFailed`, same table and key shape as `mcp_tool_used`).
- The row holds tool name, platform, auth method, client and session only. No arguments and no error text (they can hold ad copy and ids).
- It is not in `MCP_USAGE_EVENT_TYPES`, and `getMcpUserUsage` counts only `mcp_tool_used`. So usage reports, `zoma_usage` "used" and the Stripe meter are unchanged: a failed call is still never counted and never billed.
- An audit-write error is logged and never fails the call (`deps.recordFailure` is injectable, defaults to `recordMcpToolFailed`).
- No database or data-plane change: no table, column or index, one new `eventType` value in the existing event table.

## How to test
1. `cd backend && npx jest --runTestsByPath src/__tests__/eng3130.failedCallAudit.test.ts src/__tests__/eng3130.zomaBilling.test.ts`. **Expected:** 91 passed.
2. In any Zoma call that returns `success:false` (for example a rejected UPDATE), look for one `mcp_tool_failed` row for that user in the MCP usage-event table, and confirm `zoma_usage` "used" did not move.

## Test evidence (run on Manan's machine, Node 24)
- New service test `eng3130.failedCallAudit.test.ts` (3): row shape and no arguments, no row without a user id, a failed call is never counted as a tool call.
- 3 new gateway tests in `eng3130.zomaBilling.test.ts`: a failed write is audited and not metered, a successful or thrown call writes no failure row, an audit error never fails the call.
- Every suite that imports the gateway or the usage service: 41 suites, 918 tests, 0 failed (`eng2282.metaToolkitManifest` cannot load locally, same missing-`twilio` reason as in #4163).
- Scoped TypeScript check of the 4 touched files: 0 diagnostics. A full `tsc -p` runs out of memory on this machine at 4 GB, so the pre-push hook was bypassed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`; the GitHub Backend build is the full-build proof.

## NOT verified
- Not run live: no DynamoDB write was observed, only the injected store in tests. An env1 live test is the next step.
- Failed reads now also write a failure row (same volume as `main`, which wrote a `mcp_tool_used` row for every call). If that volume matters, restrict it to writes.

title: ENG-3131: Zoma paywall review round 2 (reminder marker, failed payments, copy) (dark)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

Follow-up to #4163 (merged as 8889048c4). Billing is still dark behind `ZOMA_BILLING_ENABLED`; nothing here changes behaviour while it is off.

Two fresh independent reviewers (correctness/Stripe, and quality/tests/copy) reviewed the code changed after the first review round. Every finding below was verified against the source before fixing.

## Fixed
1. **Reminder could repeat every hour.** The "sent" marker was written after the send; if that write failed after a delivered email, each hourly pass (new claim key) resent until the trial ended. Now the marker is written BEFORE the send (a failed write sends nothing and retries next hour) and a failed send clears it again (Stripe drops a metadata key set to `''`).
2. **A failed payment could sell a second plan.** `past_due`/`unpaid` got a fresh $1 Checkout while the old subscription kept collecting overage. They now get "update your card on the existing plan" (portal link when `ZOMA_BILLING_PORTAL_URL` is set) and no new Checkout.
3. **Copy:** the pending-payment message pointed at a Checkout that `openZomaCheckout` already answers with 410; the day-3 email and the done page now say the card is charged automatically; a cancelled paying plan shows "active until <date>, cancelled, it will not renew" (`cancels_at_period_end`, was `cancels_at_trial_end` and trial-only).
4. **Tests:** the trial-end grace window had no test that fails when reverted (rows now at +30min and +3601s); added marker-write failure, marker rollback, `past_due`/`unpaid`, cancelled active plan.
5. Comment/dev-note accuracy (failure audit covers reads too; hardening note now records the real-Stripe rehearsal).

## Deliberately not changed
- A user who cancelled can still buy another $1 trial: founders' call.
- Two simultaneous first paywall hits can open two Checkouts; the 410 on a live plan limits the damage (an idempotency key would be the next step).
- The signed cancel redirect never expires: impact is one funnel row per user per hour.
- `createCustomer`'s idempotency key can replay a deleted customer for 24h (only if someone deletes a Zoma customer in Stripe).
- `trial_canceled` can be mislabeled for a cancel within an hour of converting (analytics only).

## Verification
83 Zoma/toolkit/Stripe/usage suites: 1,134 passed, 0 failed (plus `eng2282.metaToolkitManifest`, which cannot load locally because `twilio` is not installed here). Scoped typecheck clean; pre-push hook bypassed with `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1` for the same unrelated missing-module reason.

title: ENG-3131: Zoma launch policy: one $1 trial per user, USD-only Checkout (dark)

Launch-policy decisions for the Zoma plan, still dark behind `ZOMA_BILLING_ENABLED` (no effect while it is off). Zoma is a hard launch to everyone, so no pilot exemption list is added.

## Changes
1. **One $1 trial per user.** If the user ever held a Zoma plan (cancelled or paused counts; `incomplete`/`incomplete_expired` never started, so it does not), Checkout sells the plan itself: plan + metered price, no $1 line, no trial. The refusal and `zoma_status` say "$50/month, charged today". Closes "pay $1, cancel on day 6, repeat".
2. **USD-only Checkout** (`adaptive_pricing.enabled=false`): the earlier sandbox run showed INR with a conversion fee, contradicting "$1 then $50".

Scoped typecheck clean; pre-push hook bypassed for that unrelated reason.

Risk: High

Change: Zoma checkout now sells only the plan and metered overage to returning users, with no $1 fee or trial. It also disables adaptive pricing and updates the paywall, plan-line, and reads copy. The rehearsal asserts USD-only checkout.

Findings:
- The diff has four files, not three. The raw summary omits `backend/src/__tests__/eng3130.zomaBilling.test.ts` (+44 lines).
- Returning-user checkout now calls `deps.listSubscriptions` before creating the session. This adds a Stripe read to the checkout path. The diff does not show how a failure there is handled.

title: feat(zoma): weekly ad-performance email, dark behind ZOMA_WEEKLY_REPORT_ENABLED (ENG-3133)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

**Draft. Dark: nothing happens until `ZOMA_WEEKLY_REPORT_ENABLED=true`. Rollback: leave the flag unset.**

## What this adds (ENG-3133)

A weekly email to Zoma users: how each connected ad platform (Meta and Google Ads) did over the last 7 complete days, set against the 7 days before, plus what Zoma changed for them. It goes to every Zoma user who made at least one successful Zoma call in the last 7 days, otherwise nothing.

Each platform gets: headline numbers with the change vs last week (spend, conversions, cost per conversion, clicks, click rate, cost per click, return on ad spend where Meta reports a value), a daily-spend bar chart with a most-conversions / no-spend line, the top 3 campaigns with their cost per conversion, up to three plain "worth a look" flags, and one factual sentence. Everything is computed from data already read: no benchmarks, no guessed causes. The charts are plain HTML table cells, so they also show with images off. Platforms are never added together (currencies differ). A note says recent conversions can still go up.

Sent Monday from 15:00 UTC (hourly job, claim-before-send so nobody gets two). Opt-out is one signed, opaque link per email (plus one-click `List-Unsubscribe`), stored on the user record.

## Needs the founder before the flag is turned on

1. **New optional attribute `User.zomaWeeklyReportOptOutAt`** (a model change, so the data-plane gate applies). Partial update of one user, no migration, no backfill, no new table or index. Chosen because the users table is per-environment, has point-in-time recovery and the attribute is already on the row the job scans.
2. **The email wording** (customer-facing copy). A marked SAMPLE with made-up numbers was sent to Manan for forwarding.
3. **First send:** everyone eligible at once, or a canary first (`ZOMA_WEEKLY_REPORT_ONLY_USER_IDS` restricts a pass to named users).

## Evidence

- Typecheck: scoped `tsc` clean on the 7 changed source files (at 8485a5e0f).
- Tests: 124 in `eng3133.zomaWeeklyReport.test.ts` plus 12 in the new `eng3133.dailyReadAndUsageStore.test.ts` (the real daily Meta read against a fake Graph, and the real event store's all-users query against a fake DynamoDB client). 206 related suites, 4,407 tests, 0 failures (at 8485a5e0f); the last two commits (campaign row layout) re-ran the weekly suite.
- Live on env1 at the final head (1bc2163e1): 25 pass, 0 fail, 1 info. Real events table (one all-users query), environment-scoped claim row present and the production-shaped key absent, no claim rows left behind, one-click unsubscribe on the real route, opaque link, an account that does not exist is never emailed, a stale scan row's opt-out caught by the fresh read, a real Meta rejection and a real Google 401 both reported as "could not read" at once.
- The HTML was rendered at desktop and phone width and read by eye; that found and fixed three layout bugs.
- Two independent reviews (fresh reviewers, read-only). Everything they found that touched truthfulness or safety is fixed; see "Review findings" below.

## Review findings fixed

- The claim row lives in the loop-events table whose name is the same in every environment while non-production users are clones of production: the claim key is `nonprod#`-prefixed outside production, so a test run can never block production's send.
- Emma's own MCP traffic shares the event type: usage is filtered to the Zoma product, in one all-users query per pass.
- Several ad accounts: every usable account of a platform (up to 5, each stored account read once) is read; same-currency accounts are added, others are listed as "not included"; "no delivery" is only said when every account was read.
- The unsubscribe link no longer shows the internal user id (AES-256-GCM token).
- Real error classification (found live): a dead Google credential is 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, now treated as permanent.
- A "no conversions" flag names the one conversion event Meta counts; ties are never turned into a winner; a "dearest campaign" is never named while another campaign spent without converting; numbers read correctly at the edges (tiny rates, huge jumps, counts under one).
- The Google section only appears while the Google toolkit flag is on; a pass stops after 3 failed sends in a row; the send hour cannot be set before 12:00 UTC; wording says "recorded", not "made".

## Known limits (documented in `dev/pending/eng-3133-zoma-weekly-report.md`)

- A user who deletes the account and signs up again loses the opt-out (a suppression table would fix that; it is a new table, so out of scope).
- The candidate list is the scoreboard's Zoma-user list: a caller whose `products.zoma` flag was never written is not emailed.
- If the mail provider is down for the first three sends of a pass, those three users' week is spent (a missed weekly email was judged cheaper than a duplicate).
- A transient ad-read error retries hourly and re-reads that user's accounts each time, until the 23:00 UTC tick.

## Not verified

- A real Meta ad account's daily insights request (no dev account with a valid token; the request follows the Graph docs and is unit-tested only).
- Charts with real spend, a really delivered email to a customer, the full job over real users.
- Rendering in real mail clients (desktop Outlook, Gmail, iOS dark mode); only a browser at desktop and phone width.
- GitHub's backend build (the PR is a draft, so CI has not run).

## Commits

Granular: services, the report, tests and the dev note are separate commits; the full history is on the branch.

title: fix(security): perform_data_analysis reads S3 only for keys the caller may read
body:
## What was wrong
`perform_data_analysis` read S3 through the SDK, with the backend's own credentials, for three kinds of caller-named reference, without asking whether the caller may read them:
- an `s3://<bucket>/<key>` URI, where the **bucket came from the caller's string** (those credentials can read other buckets as well as the user-file bucket);
- a bare `tool-responses/<session>/...` key;
- tool-response keys written inside `analysis_instruction` (found while building this; not in the original list).

ENG-2988 closed the same class on the REST file routes; the agent-tool paths were not covered.

## Fix
- Only our own bucket is read on a caller's say-so.
- Each key must pass the ENG-2988 rule (`decideStorageAccess`, read) for the caller. A tool carries no admin power, as on the REST self-calls.
- The checked key is the key that is read (a key the policy would rewrite, such as one with a leading `s3:`, is refused).
- A refused key gets the same answer as a missing one ("File not found or you do not have access to it."), with nothing about the target. A failed access lookup answers "try again" (`upstream_5xx`), not "not found".
- The rule is one small module, `emma/impl/toolStorageAccess.ts`, loaded lazily inside the function (as `searchResearch.moduleIsolation.test.ts` requires), so other tools can reuse it instead of growing their own check.

## Not in this PR (so nobody reads it as more than it is)
- Plain HTTP(S) URLs in `file_urls` are unchanged: a plain GET uses no server privilege. Hardening outbound fetches is separate work.
- Other tools that read our bucket through the SDK with a caller-named key: `read_tool_response` and `search_tool_response` (`agentModeService.ts`), and `read_file_content` (older `isS3KeyOwnedByUser` rule). The bucket still allows public reads by raw URL (ENG-2988 notes), so this PR mainly closes reads of other buckets and enforces ownership where the SDK reads; it is not yet a cross-tenant boundary for own-bucket keys on its own.

## Behaviour changes
- Refused: another bucket, another tenant's keys, owner-only kinds, keys the policy cannot place.
- A non-delegated admin no longer reads other users' files through this tool (delegation still works), as for REST self-calls.
- A failed lookup now gives a retryable error.
- Unchanged and tested: own files, teammates' org-shared kinds, own tool responses, plain HTTP(S) URLs.

## Tests
- New `performDataAnalysis.storageAccess.test.ts` (26 cases): real policy, stubbed database lookups. **20 of 26 fail against the unfixed code** (mocks only; nothing real was touched).
- The two existing data-analysis suites treat the policy as a boundary (default allow); no assertion in them changed. Without that mock, the empty-file test in `performDataAnalysisFailureClass` would pass for the wrong reason.
- 38 suites / 620 tests that reference the touched modules pass locally, including `searchResearch.moduleIsolation` (an independent review found my first version broke it; fixed with the lazy import). `npm run typecheck` exit 0.
- CI runs only the backend build; the suites above were run locally.

## Safety and rollback
- It can only make reads fail that should not have worked. No data is touched; no schema or database change (the policy only reads), so no database gate.
- Rollback: revert this PR.
- Not verified: whether any customer legitimately passes an `s3://` URI for another bucket (unlikely); behaviour in production (not deployed).

title: feat(zoma): hide Google advertising behind ZOMA_GOOGLE_ENABLED (default off)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: High

## What was wrong (before)
Zoma advertised Google Ads to customers: production sets `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED=true`, and several surfaces named Google even with the flag off (tool descriptions, ads-experience options, new-advertiser steps, MCP instructions, agent guide, next-step text, `/api/zoma/google/*` pages).

## What this fixes (after)
All customer-facing Zoma Google advertising sits behind **`ZOMA_GOOGLE_ENABLED`**, default **false** (only `"true"` enables). The legacy `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED` is no longer read, so prod becomes Meta-only on deploy with no env change. `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ENABLED=true` restores the preserved Google implementation unchanged.

Gated surfaces (off → Meta only):
- tool list + routing + `zoma_status` Google section (already gated; now on the new flag)
- `zoma_status` / `zoma_prepare_upload` descriptions
- ads-experience option label ("use the Meta MCP") and new-advertiser steps (device page, poll, zoma_status)
- multiple-accounts next step, MCP `initialize` instructions
- `/api/meta-toolkit/skill.md` Google section (between `zoma-google` markers)
- Google writes in `zoma_usage`
- `/api/zoma/google/callback` + `/select` → generic 404 "Zoma setup" page; never calls Google

## Complexity ledger
Net ~+60 src lines / +150 test lines. No new flag system: the existing `googleToolkitEnabled()` switch is renamed and reused; four constants became flag-aware functions. No storage, schema, or dependency changes. Behavior with flag on is unchanged.

## How to test
1. With `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ENABLED` unset: `curl -s https://api.agentweb.pro/api/meta-toolkit/skill.md | grep -ci google` → **0**.
2. MCP `initialize` instructions say "Meta ads"; `tools/list` has no `call_google_ads_*` tools and no zoma_ tool description names Google.
3. `GET /api/zoma/google/callback` → 404 "Zoma setup" page.
4. Set `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ENABLED=true` on an env → Google returns everywhere.

## Test Evidence
- Scoped `tsc --noEmit` over all changed files (+ their import graph): clean.
- `jest --maxWorkers=1 --runTestsByPath` over 17 Zoma suites: **17 passed, 339 tests passed, 0 failed** (incl. new `zomaGoogleFlag.test.ts`, flag false + true + legacy var).

## Behavioral assertions verified
- Flag false (default / legacy var true) → no Google on any listed surface: `zomaGoogleFlag.test.ts` "unset (default): Meta only" block; MCP `tools/list` off: `eng2823.googleToolkitMcp.test.ts`.
- Flag true → Google restored: `zomaGoogleFlag.test.ts` "=true" block + existing Google suites (eng2823/2928/2959/3135/3130) run with the flag on.

## What was NOT tested
- Full backend jest suite (memory-limited box; CI builds). No live Google OAuth (mock-only). No change to the production EB env vars; the old `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ADS_ENABLED=true` remains set but is inert.

Rollback: set `ZOMA_GOOGLE_ENABLED=true` on EB (instant), or revert this PR.

title: ENG-2816 step 3: schedules a share-link visitor wrote run with the visitor limits; a visitor cannot stop the owner's turn
body:
## What was wrong (ENG-2816, steps 1 and 2 already merged; this is step 3 and the stop route)
A share link (`/ishare/<id>?conversable=<token>`) lets a visitor chat with the owner's agent, which acts under the OWNER's account with the `share_visitor` limits. Two holes were left:
- **Schedules.** A visitor could ask the agent to create or edit a scheduled chat. The schedule later ran as the owner with NO visitor limits (reproduced on the test environment on 2026-11-05: a visitor-made schedule ran `save_memory` as the owner). Publishing steps and Slack sends of such a schedule also followed the owner's defaults ("authorized unless opted out").
- **Stop.** Anyone holding the share link could press Stop and cancel the owner's running turn.

## What changed
**Who is asking travels with the call.** The agent's own calls to the schedule routes now carry a signed claim (`_rp` in the service token, trusted only on a verified service token, never on a delegate token); a second signal is an in-process "this turn is a visitor's" marker set where the generation lock is claimed.

**One new optional attribute, `provenance` (String Set) on schedule items.** It lists which of eight content fields a visitor wrote: `startingMessage`, `keywords`, `requiredFunctionCalls`, `functionCallMinCalls`, `variables`, `variableValues`, `emailNotifications`, `selfImprove`. It is written in the SAME write as the content. A visitor write to an existing schedule marks only fields whose final value differs from the stored value (consistent read), so a no-op edit marks nothing. Items without it behave exactly as before. **No table, index or IAM change, no backfill.** Templates get no attribute (see below).

**A marked schedule runs with the visitor limits, checked live.** `executeTool` re-reads the schedule (consistent read) for the tools the `share_visitor` profile refuses, the admin tools, `connect_account` and the schedule-write tools. The refusal wording of `share_visitor` is unchanged (pinned by test). If it cannot be verified, an unattended run is refused; an attended owner is never refused for that reason. Marked runs also: drop refused tools from their required calls (recorded as `skippedRequiredCalls`), retry 3 times not 20, and have publish steps, Slack sends and the full-autonomy waiver WITHHELD (drafts), at every "unattended default = authorized" gate.

**Only the owner can lift it.** Marks come off ONLY through `POST /api/agent-mode/scheduled-chats/:id/adopt-visitor-edits`, a real portal login (not an in-process tool call, not a delegated session, not a visitor), with `expectedContentVersion` (a digest of the content the visitor can write, computed on the list, never stored). The write removes the whole attribute, conditioned on the version just read. Editing a schedule does NOT lift anything. A visitor-created schedule is stored with "require approval before publishing" (and Slack approval when it requires a Slack send), so adopting it does not switch on unattended posting; the same hold is set when a visitor edit adds a publish tool or a Slack send.

**Templates.** A visitor can no longer create, change, delete or submit a schedule template in the owner's account (a visitor could rewrite an approved public template other customers use, or plant one the owner later runs). Using a template as a visitor marks every field.

**Stop route.** A stop on a share route is honoured only for the owner's login or for a turn a visitor started; an ignored stop answers the same 200 and does nothing. A share-route request from a non-owner no longer preempts the owner's own background continuation (an owner on their own link still does). The owner's own Stop from their share link needs the portal change (below).

## Deploy order (important)
**Merge and deploy the portal PR first** (AgentWebPro/agentweb-customer-portal#1341), then this one. The portal sends the viewer's login on Stop, shows the "Visitor-edited" badge and the Adopt button. With the NEW backend and an OLD portal tab, the owner's Stop on their own share link is ignored (visitors' stops too, by design); open tabs need a reload. With the new portal and the old backend nothing breaks (the badge and Adopt button need `provenance` and the adopt route, so they simply never show).

## Rollout hazards
- During the Immutable deploy overlap the old instances write schedules unmarked for a few minutes.
- A rollback ignores existing marks (the attribute stays in the table, harmless).
- Schedules a visitor made BEFORE this ships cannot be told apart (no backfill, by decision). The owner can see them in the portal's schedule list.

## What it does NOT close (documented, not hidden)
Approval-inbox resumes and work-plan continuations of a visitor's session run without the visitor flag; `create_skill` / `save_work_plan` / `install_skills` and owner flows that read visitor text; email to the agent's inbound address; visitor toggle/retime/delete/pause of owner schedules and `llmModel`/timing/name/description (untracked on purpose); a visitor-written template that already existed; schedules created by paths with no claim (work-plan steps, outreach auto-create, admin routes); voice has the claim only, no marker fallback; only the `share_visitor` block list is enforced for marked runs; a Slack send written into a prompt without listing `slack_send_message` is not held after Adopt; visitor variable-link submit is unconditioned; Adopt can give a retryable 409 around run bookkeeping.

## Review and tests
- Five independent code reviews (full-context and blind, four rounds; every finding fixed in this PR, the last rounds found nothing above low). Each guard was mutation-checked (broken on purpose, a test fails).
- Typecheck clean. Unit: new suites for the claim, marking, enforcement, gates, adopt, templates, stop route; neighbouring suites green. The full backend run shows 3 unrelated failures that also fail on current main (four suites: LinkedIn consent re-check, ndjson empty-flood, table prefix, login CPU budget; all four fail identically on main 9c88f0a0d).
- **Live on the test environment (real stack, real LLM, rebased head):** 24/24 checks: a visitor on a share link creates a schedule (marked), its run refuses `save_memory`; an owner-made schedule is unmarked and still saves memory; routine saves and portal edits lift nothing; Adopt: refused without a version, with a stale version, from another account, without login; works with the version on screen and after the timestamp moved; visitor edit of an owner schedule marks, a no-op edit marks nothing, `self_improve` and a newly added Slack send are marked/held; a visitor cannot create a template; the typed visitor chat still refuses `save_memory` with the unchanged wording. Stop: a visitor's stop does not cancel the owner's turn (15k characters still produced), the owner's stop with login does, a visitor's stop of their own turn does. Real browser: badge, disabled Duplicate, Adopt (200, badge gone), Stop on the owner's own share page sends the login and stops.

Plain language for non-engineers: a stranger with a share link can no longer leave behind a schedule that later acts with the owner's full powers, and can no longer cancel the owner's work; the owner reviews and adopts such a schedule with one click when they want it to run with full powers.

Rationale: The webhook path now calls referral code, so this is not unused. Store errors propagate. If the flag is enabled before the tables exist, Zoma billing webhooks could fail. Rollback must account for ledger data once enabled. The default value of `ZOMA_REFERRAL_ENABLED` is not verified here.

title: fix: session-breaker shadow prices BYOK turns by the ledger rule (ENG-2812)
body:
## What

ENG-2812. The session-breaker shadow (log-only, on by default since the last change) counted every turn on our own provider key (BYOK, the default route) as $0, so its $5 cap could never fire. This makes it price a turn by the same rule the ledger books it.

## Why

First prod evidence after the default-on deploy: two `session_breaker_would_pause` lines (2026-11-17 16:10Z scheduled, 18:46Z interactive, 40 turns each), both with `spendUsd: 0`. The old code did `if (typeof usage.cost === 'number') return usage.cost`. On BYOK, OpenRouter reports `usage.cost: 0` for a plain call and puts the real bill in `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost`, so the token-estimate fallback was never reached. Only the turn cap worked; the half of the evidence that picks a dollar cap was blind.

## Change

- `shadowTurnCostUsd(usage, tokenCostUsd)` in `sessionBreakerShadow.ts`: BYOK turns use `openRouterByokCostUsd` (upstream bill plus any OpenRouter fee, the ledger rule from ENG-2720); other turns use `usage.cost` when positive; anything else falls back to the price-book token cost; no usage block is still 0.
- Call site in `agentModeService.ts` passes the price-book cost (cache read/write tokens included, same arguments as the message's `estimated_cost`).
- Still log-only: same one line per cap multiple, never pauses, writes or notifies, errors swallowed by the existing try/catch.
- `dev/pending` fragment (the CI guard rejects edits to `dev.md`).

## Safety answer

- Safe for prod: yes. A pure number in a log line; no table, response, notification or billing path reads it. Per-turn cost is a few arithmetic operations.
- Could it regress or anger users: no user-visible effect. Worst case the shadow logs a wrong dollar figure, as it did before.
- Rollback: revert this commit (a code deploy; the EB env block is at its size cap, so a flag cannot be changed there).
- Lines logged before this deploys keep `spendUsd: 0`; read spend only from lines after it.

## Tests

- `sessionBreakerShadow.test.ts`: 13 pass (7 new: plain BYOK, BYOK with a search fee, BYOK with no cost, fee with no upstream bill, non-BYOK, no usage / NaN, and a BYOK session that now reaches the spend cap). A mutant with the old rule fails 6 of 13.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean. ESLint: the same 3 `any` errors that are already on main in that test file, none new.
- Live on env1 at the exact head: with the spend cap at $0.00001, a real turn logged `spendUsd: 0.1046` and `reason: spend_cap`. The raw response was `{"cost":0,"is_byok":true,"cost_details":{"upstream_inference_cost":0.1045695}}`; the old rule reads that as $0.

- Independent fresh full review of `888b9f716` (security first): no blockers, no mediums. The head `a3f3e9bac` adds one comment-only commit on top (esbuild-minified output of `sessionBreakerShadow.ts` byte-identical before and after; `agentModeService.ts` untouched).
- Review lows, each checked against the code: (1) the doc comment overstated "same as the ledger" for a non-BYOK response reporting cost 0 -> comment fixed; (2) the token fallback prices raw `prompt_tokens` where the ledger normalizes per provider: the normalizer needs the provider label, which is not in scope at this call site, the fallback only runs when the response reports no cost, and it matches the message's own `estimated_cost` -> left as is; (3) the thunk wiring is covered by the live env1 turn, not a unit test; (4) the shadow module now loads the ledger module, which `agentModeService.ts` already loads, so there is no new load in prod.
- Pre-push `tsc` hit the hook's 240 s budget on this machine (full `tsc --noEmit` takes ~9 min here and passed clean on this code), so the push used the hook's documented `AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`; CI runs it again.

body:
## ENG-3132 slices C-D: referral admin endpoints, payout roll-up, reconcile, rehearsal

Follows #4176 (merged). Note: #4176 turned out to contain slices A and B1-B5 (registry, commission arithmetic, ledger store + `AW-ZomaReferralLedger` table definition, accrual, reversal/void, webhook wiring), not only slice A as its description said. All of it is dark behind `ZOMA_REFERRAL_ENABLED` and both tables are still to be created by Yugo.

**This PR adds**
- **Admin (slice C):** admin-only `POST/GET /api/admin/zoma-referrals/codes[/:code]`, `POST .../codes/:code/revoke`, and `GET .../payouts?month=YYYY-MM[&format=csv]` (JSON or formula-safe CSV). Not gated by the flag so codes can be registered first. createdBy comes from the admin's login; store outages are 503 without leaking the error. Roll-up groups by each ledger row's payout month and nets reversals.
- **Reconcile (slice D):** read-only `scripts/zomaReferralReconcile.ts [--month]` compares ledger vs Stripe paid/refunded and flags `refund_not_reversed`, `over_reversed`, `net_mismatch`, missing invoices. Never writes. Run before every payout.
- **Rehearsal:** `zomaBillingRehearsal.ts` dumps invoice lines and exercises accrual, credit-note reversal and the raw-refund reconcile against real Stripe test mode.

**Proven on Stripe test mode (2026-11-18, sandbox):** the $1 invoice is fee + $0 plan/overage lines; overage is billed in arrears on the NEXT invoice beside that period's plan line; credit-note line id equals the invoice line id; credit-note and refund events are retrievable; accrual is exactly 20% of ex-tax less the fee and idempotent on replay; a credit note reverses exactly its commission; a raw refund with no credit note is ignored by the webhook and flagged by reconcile. 51/52 rehearsal checks passed; the one failure is the pre-existing section-5 meter-timestamp check.

**Not proven:** live endpoint event subscriptions, a third commissionable invoice, `credit_note.voided` delivery (Stripe only voids notes on open invoices).

**Verification:** 223 tests (eng3132 suites, eng3130.zomaBilling, createTablesDrift) pass; ESLint clean on new files; typecheck clean for touched files. Pre-push hook bypassed (`AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`); CI is the backstop.

**Rollback:** admin routes only read the ledger and write codes; revert the commits.

title: fix(zoma): weekly email bars keep their width in Gmail's Android app (ENG-3133)
body:
## Risk: Low | Priority: Medium

**Draft. HTML of the weekly Zoma email only. The email is still off (`ZOMA_WEEKLY_REPORT_ENABLED` unset), so no customer sees any change.**

## Bug

Seen by Manan on a real phone (Gmail's Android app, dark mode): the daily-spend bars and the per-campaign bars drew as thin lines. Heights were correct, widths collapsed: that app ignores `width` attributes on these tables. A desktop browser honours them, so the earlier desktop and phone-width renders missed it.

## Fix

Each bar is one table cell that carries its size in CSS (px, plus the attributes for Outlook) and a spacer `div` of the same width that holds the cell open. No bar depends on a width attribute or a percentage. Daily bars are 36px in 40px columns (7 x 40 = 280px), campaign bars are pixel lengths up to 250px.

## Evidence

- A unit test strips every `width` attribute from the generated HTML and asserts all 17 sample bars still define their width in CSS with a spacer; a second test pins the size limits. Weekly suite: 126 tests pass.
- The sample was rendered with every width attribute stripped at 360px: solid bars, daily and per campaign.
- A fresh SAMPLE email (made-up numbers) goes to Manan to check on the same phone.

## Not verified

Real Gmail (Android) rendering of this exact version until Manan checks the sample; desktop Outlook and iOS Mail.

title: fix(security): tools that fetch a caller's URL use one guarded fetch; update_html_file writes only files the caller owns
body:
## What was wrong
Four agent tools fetched a URL **chosen by the caller** with a bare `fetch` / `axios.get` from the backend host:

| Tool | Argument |
|---|---|
| `create_html_template` | `html_source` |
| `update_html_file` | `file_url` |
| `generate_book_content` | `research_url` |
| `perform_data_analysis` | plain http(s) entries of `file_urls` |

A private, loopback or cloud-metadata address (or a public URL that redirects to one) was reachable from the backend host, and the body came back to the caller as tool output, a saved template, or an edited file (`update_html_file` in CSS mode even returns the edited HTML). There was no size cap either: axios defaults to unlimited, and `fetch().text()` reads everything into memory.

`update_html_file` also **writes**. It uploaded the edited copy (next version name, `x.html` -> `x_v2.html`, replacing it if present) with the backend's credentials under the directory taken from the **caller's own URL path**, whoever the caller was, so a user could put a file into another user's folder by naming that path.

Reachable through chat, the REST routes (`/api/emma/update-html-file`, `/api/emma/create-html-template`) and an outside agent through `emma_send_message`.

## Fix
- **One guarded fetch**, `utils/callerUrlFetch.ts`, over the existing helpers in `ssrfGuard.ts` (DNS pinned to a public address, every redirect hop re-checked, size and total time bounded). The four tools use it.
- **One generic answer for any refused URL** (private/loopback/metadata, no DNS, non-http(s) scheme, a redirect to one): "That URL cannot be fetched. Use a public https link." No address, no reason, no `cause`, so it cannot be used to map the internal network. Logged with the caller and the **host only**, never the path or query.
- Caps: HTML sites 20 MB / 30 s; `perform_data_analysis` caps each download at **what is left of its total size budget** (default 50 MB); a non-numeric `DATA_ANALYSIS_FILE_SIZE` no longer switches the cap off (a NaN limit compares false with everything).
- **`update_html_file` writes only files the caller owns.** It asks the same rule as `/api/files/html` (`decideStorageAccess`, write: only the owner) about the **exact key it will write** (the directory as given plus the file name after the upload's own rewriting), **before fetching anything**, on both the part/full path and the CSS path. A teammate is told the file is read-only; anyone else gets the generic "File not found or you do not have access to it."; a failed lookup says to try again.
- Both S3 link styles of a page (virtual-hosted and path-style) name the same object: the directory comes from the bucket-aware key helper the file lookup already uses, and that directory is the one that is checked and written (found by Opslane: the path-style link of the caller's own page was refused; before the write check it wrote the copy into a junk folder named after the bucket).
- An anonymous result-endpoint visitor (`anon_<uuid>`) may still edit the pages in its **own** folder (the rule alone would let only an admin; found in review).

## Not in this PR (so nobody reads it as more than it is)
- Other tools that still fetch a caller URL with a bare client: `publish/repair blog` (`blog.ts`), LinkedIn media upload (`adsApis.ts`), `describe_video`, `remove_c2pa_from_image` / `remove_image_background` (`mediaVideo.ts`), `cssExtractor`, `generate_image` and friends. Next PR.
- `read_tool_response` / `search_tool_response` read any key of the file bucket (same class as the earlier `perform_data_analysis` fix). Separate small PR; the bucket itself is readable by raw URL, so this is hardening.
- **IPv6 literal URLs** (`http://[::1]/`) are refused today, but by accident: `URL.hostname` keeps the brackets, so they fail a DNS lookup before any range check. I left that alone on purpose: judging them by range would expose gaps in `isPrivateIPv6` (site-local `fec0::/10`, `::ffff:0:a.b.c.d`, `64:ff9b:1::/48`, Teredo, `2001:db8::/32`, `100::/64`). The same gaps exist today for a hostname whose AAAA record points there. The comment in `ssrfGuard.ts` now says so. Needs its own change with a complete range list.
- Full URLs are still written to the info log at three call sites (pre-existing).

## Behaviour changes (what could annoy a user)
- Refused now: private/internal/metadata/loopback targets, non-http(s) schemes (including `data:`), IPv6 literal hosts. A host that does not resolve now looks the same as a refused one (one generic message, on purpose).
- Limits: HTML sources over 20 MB; downloads over the remaining budget; **30 s total** per download (was an idle timer for data analysis, none for the other three) and at most 5 redirects (`fetch` allowed 20). A slow host sending a large file can now time out; that is reported as a timeout and a bad argument, not as a config fault.
- `update_html_file`: only the owner writes. A file URL whose path is not one of the caller's own keys is refused (including paths on non-bucket hosts and path-style bucket URLs). A non-delegated real admin no longer edits other users' files through this tool (delegated sessions act as the target user and are unaffected), same as the earlier read-side change.
- A bare file name or local path in `perform_data_analysis`' `file_urls` is answered with a plain "is not a URL" (a bad argument) and is logged under `caller_url_invalid`, not counted as a blocked address (found by Opslane).
- A dead template URL now reports "Request failed with status code 404" instead of the status text.
- Unchanged and tested: public URLs, own files, task files the caller owns, `generate_book_content` still skips an unreachable research URL silently.

## Tests
- New: `callerUrlFetch` (no DNS allowed in the suite; a lookup fails it), `performDataAnalysis.callerUrl` (real wrapper and guard, literal addresses only), `updateHtmlFile.storageAccess` (real policy, stubbed lookups, both edit paths, anonymous visitors, task owners, traversal and encoding cases), and `updateHtmlFile.writtenKey`, which runs the **real upload** against a fake S3 client and proves the key S3 receives equals the key the rule was asked about, across awkward names (unicode, control characters, presigned query, doubled slashes).
- Suites that mocked `fetch` / `axios` for these tools now mock the wrapper, or use a small bridge (`__tests__/helpers/callerUrlFetchAxiosBridge.ts`) that hands the wrapper's request to the suite's own `axios.get` mock, so their download assertions mean what they meant. The `update_html_file` suites treat the write rule as a boundary. One assertion changed on purpose (the 404 text above).
- **Deliberate-breakage runs** (change the code on purpose, expect a failing test): 9 of 9 on the wrapper, 27 of 28 on the sites and the write check (the 28th is an equivalent mutant: no key shape lets a non-owner write, so a blank caller is refused by the rule regardless), 12 of 12 on the review follow-ups.
- Locally: 198 suites / 4,563 tests that reference anything touched pass, including all the `*.moduleIsolation` suites; `npm run typecheck` exit 0.
- **Two independent reviews** (diff and intent only, no conclusions given): the first found a regression (anonymous visitors could no longer edit their own pages), the time-limit semantics, DNS-pinning limits and test gaps, all addressed or stated above. The second reviewed the fixes and caught that my IPv6 "fix" would have exposed the range gaps above, so I reverted it.
- **Live, test environment** (this build, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5): a public URL still analyses (total 10); the backend's own loopback URL and an IPv6 loopback are refused with the one generic message and no content; `create_html_template` refuses a loopback source (no template created) and builds one from a public page (Haiku). The deployed build was also exercised directly inside the test container (real database lookups, real S3, real network): own page edited and written as `_v2` beside the original; another user's page and a foreign-host path refused with nothing written; a metadata or loopback host with a path shaped like the caller's own refused by the fetch; `example.com` fetched for real. The model provider's own filter blocks the metadata address wording, so that one is covered by the unit tests and the in-container call. `update_html_file` could not be driven through chat on that box (its skill is not installed there); it is covered by the in-container call.

## Intended, unchanged behaviour (so reviewers do not read it as a gap)
- `create_html_template`'s `html_source` is raw HTML **or** an http(s) address. Anything that does not start with `http://` / `https://`, a `data:` string included, has always been used as the page text itself, and nothing is fetched for it. So a `data:` string becomes a template made from that text and is reported as created. That is the same as before this PR and not a fetch path.

## One unrelated commit
`test: three array reads in the zoma weekly report suite may be undefined (typecheck)`: three `seven[0]` / `six[0]` reads in `eng3133.zomaWeeklyReport.test.ts` that `main` already has fail `npm run typecheck` (TS2532), which the pre-push hook runs, so the branch could not be pushed without bypassing the hook. It is its own commit and can be dropped if the same fix lands on `main` first. The suite is otherwise untouched (124 tests pass).

## Safety and rollback
- It can only make fetches fail that were allowed (internal targets, oversized or slow bodies, redirects beyond 5) and stop a user writing into a file they do not own. Public URLs and own files behave as before. No data is touched; no schema or database change (the rule only reads), so no database gate.
- Rollback: revert this PR.
- Not verified: behaviour in production (not deployed); hosts that publish an IPv6 address first behave as in the other tools that use the same pinning; whether any customer relied on editing someone else's page, a non-bucket path, or a download slower than 30 s (unlikely).

title: ENG-3149: email the account owner when a share-link visitor first marks one of their schedules
body:
## What this does (plain language)
Follow-up to ENG-2816. When someone using a share link makes the agent create a scheduled chat in an account, or change one that had no visitor mark, that schedule runs with limited access until the account owner adopts it. Until now the owner only saw an amber "Visitor-edited" badge on the Scheduled page, which most owners will not open. This sends the **account owner** (the login address of the account whose share link was used) **one email**:

- Subject: `Someone using your share link set up a scheduled chat`
- Body: "Someone using one of your Emma share links created or changed the scheduled chat "<name>". Until you review it, it runs with limited access: it can't use account-level tools such as saving memory or changing organization settings, and anything it would publish or post to Slack is kept as a draft. If it's yours or you trust it, open Scheduled chats, read what it does and press Adopt. If you don't recognise it, delete it, and consider turning off the share link." Button "Review the schedule" opens the Scheduled page. Footer shows the schedule ID.
- The wording was approved by the owner (Manan) on 2026-11-18.

## When it is sent
- Once, when a schedule gets its **first** visitor mark: a visitor creates a schedule (also from a template), or a visitor edit adds a mark to a schedule that had none (also a visitor writing variable values). It is sent again only if the owner adopts it and a visitor marks it again.
- Never for: the owner's own writes, a visitor edit that changes nothing, a visitor edit of an already-marked schedule, the emailed variables link, delegated/admin sessions, or a marked run's own writes (the root schedule already alerted; this stops a marked schedule that creates schedules from dripping mail).
- The only recipient is the account owner (the schedule's owner; never the visitor, never a notification list).
- At most 5 per account per rolling hour and 15 per rolling day (in process; a restart or a second instance can let a few extra through). Beyond that the badge is all the owner gets.

## Safety of the email and of the visitor's request
- The **schedule name is the only visitor-written text** in the mail (subject is fixed; no prompt text, IP, token or recipients). Because it lands inside a real AgentWeb mail, it is cleaned with a bounded allow-list: only the first 300 characters are read, then Unicode-normalised, invisible/format/bidi characters deleted, and only letters, marks, digits, spaces and a few safe symbols kept (a dot survives only between two digits, so `v2.1` stays). Everything else, including `. : / @`, becomes a space, so no link, address or hidden character can survive; at most 100 characters; empty becomes `Untitled`. Consequences: `evil.example/x` reads `evil example x`, `Sales.Report` reads `Sales Report`, emoji disappear. Phone-number-like digit text stays (accepted, listed).
- It is a notification only: sent after the write succeeded, not awaited, every failure only logged under `[ENG-3149]`; it cannot delay, change or fail the visitor's request. No new table, index or attribute.

## Review and tests
- Two independent code reviews. The first (no blocker) found a phishing-capable name and a drip from marked runs; the second found that the first fix had a quadratic slowdown on very long names (a long name could freeze the server) and several bypasses, so the name cleaning was replaced by the bounded allow-list above. 100% of findings fixed; every guard mutation-checked.
- Tests: new suites for the email (verbatim copy, escaping, 100+ attack names, ordinary names, other scripts, 1M and 5M character inputs under 100 ms, idempotence), the throttle (hourly and daily windows) and the four hooks (alert once, none for owner/no-op/already marked/marked run, send failure never fails the request, recipient always the owner). My own property fuzz: 400,000 hostile names, none leaving anything outside the safe set.
- Live on the test environment (real stack, real LLM): owner-created schedule no alert; a visitor edit of a clean schedule marks it and sends exactly one alert; a second visitor edit, an owner edit and a no-op visitor edit send none. The test environment's mail provider is not real, so the inbox check is done on production in the owner's own account after the merge (one read-only Gmail search, approved by the owner).
- Note: `npm run typecheck` already fails on main in another team's test file (`eng3133.zomaWeeklyReport.test.ts`, three "possibly undefined" errors); CI builds with `npm run build`, which does not compile tests.

## Problem
The scheduled capture-drift sweep (`captureDriftMonitor.ts`) detected drift on 5 landing-page sites, but all 5 oncall filings collapsed into a single issue. The monitor suppresses per site (`${CAPTURE_DRIFT_ALERT_CLASS}:${repoFullName}`), so the collapse appears to happen downstream in the oncall transport, which seems to dedupe on alert class rather than on repo.

## Acceptance criteria

2. The oncall transport's dedupe key for capture-drift alerts includes the repo. Other alert classes keep current behavior.

No production access needed — mock the transport and Linear client in tests.
