title: ENG-2840: manage_market_strategy over MCP merges like Emma, refuses what it never stored, pages its read (PR C: strategy)
body:
## Summary

ENG-2840 wave 1, PR C (strategy part): `manage_market_strategy` over MCP now merges like Emma's `update_market_strategy` instead of replacing, refuses what it never stored, and pages its read.

**The bug.** The tool forwarded its arguments to `POST /api/market-strategy`. That route replaces the stored competitor and ICP lists with the lists it is given, so an outside agent that sent one new competitor deleted all the others. It also reads only `businessOverview`, `competitors` and `icp`: the tool's `positioning`, `differentiators` and `channels` arguments were dropped without a word, and the agent was told it had succeeded.

**What changes** (`backend/src/mcp/server/manageStrategyWrites.ts`, `accountLock.ts`; the REST route changes in one place only, how `icpUpdatedAt` is stamped, see "Route change" below; otherwise the customer portal behaves as before):

- **update** reads the stored strategy, merges competitors by name and ICPs by title (case, padding, repeated spaces and invisible characters ignored), and sends the route only the parts that changed. A stored entry keeps its own spelling and every field the caller did not send, including fields this tool cannot write (the ICP's cached search filters). A stored entry that is a bare string (older data) is matched by its text and becomes an entry holding that name. Nothing stored is removed.
- **Only known fields:** a competitor holds `name` and `description`; an ICP holds `title`, `description`, `valueProposition` and `buyerPersonas`. Other fields are refused by name (Emma spreads any extra key onto the stored strategy; over MCP that would let an outside agent write arbitrary keys into the account record).
- **Arguments the action does not take are refused by name** (an Opslane finding on the first head: `targetAudience` answered success and was dropped); `null` counts as not sent. Identity-style arguments (`client_id`, `clientId`, `user_id`) are never used, so they are ignored and the answer lists them in `ignoredArguments` (`userId` is removed by the MCP layer). `positioning`, `differentiators` and `channels` keep their own, more specific refusal. `action` must be `read` or `update` (a mistyped "Read" used to write).
- **Blank text and empty lists change nothing** (Emma's spread would blank a stored description); blank means empty, spaces or only invisible characters. A call with nothing to send is refused instead of reported as saved.
- **A call that changes nothing writes nothing.** A write that carries `icp` marks the ICPs as hand-edited, which switches the account off its cached ICP search filters (`icpUpdatedAt`), so repeating what is already stored must not do that. Stored text is compared trimmed.
- **Bounds:** 100 entries per list per call; name/title 200 characters, text 5,000, persona 500 (50 per profile), overview 20,000; a merge that adds an entry past 500 competitors or 100 ICPs is refused; so is one that takes the overview and both lists past 250,000 bytes together (the strategy sits on the account record, a DynamoDB item of at most 400 KB; an account already over the limit can still edit an entry as long as the edit does not make it bigger). The 250,000 bytes do not count the rest of the record: a save that fits them can still push the whole record past 400 KB, which the route now answers with a reason (see "Route change: 413" below).
- **read** pages the competitor list by size (about 12,000 characters of compact JSON per page, at least one entry): `totalCompetitors` is the true count, `nextCompetitorOffset` says where the next page starts (null on the last), an offset past the end lands on the last entry rather than an empty page. `competitorNames` (up to 50) answers stored / not stored with the offset whatever the page shows; names past 50 are reported as not checked.
- **The merge baseline is checked, not trusted** (found by independent review, each reproduced there): calls on one **account** are taken in turn in this process (the key is the org when the caller belongs to one; the caller's record is read consistently and the call is refused, with a generic message, if that fails); the route's read must be a success carrying a strategy; stored lists that are not lists are refused; a read that shows nothing stored is read once more 200 ms later before it is believed; a read whose `updatedAt` is older than the strategy this process saved for that account in the last minute is not used (the saved copy is); an org caller whose read answered with the caller's PERSONAL strategy is refused; and **the parts a save of the last minute changed are sent again by the next call**, because for every part the tool does not send the route fills the value from its own, eventually consistent read and would write an older part back over the saved one (a competitors save followed straight away by an overview-only call lost the new competitor). Each save's parts count for one minute and do not chain.
- The answer lists what was added, updated and unchanged per list, with the totals the route reports as saved. **A name sent more than once in one call is listed once** (Opslane P2 on `ef2bc22`): two entries for a new name are one added entry, the later fields winning, and a stored entry named twice is listed by what the call did to it in the end (updated, or unchanged when the call changes it and changes it back; a call that only does that writes nothing). It used to be listed as added and updated.

## Behaviour changes for outside callers (stated, not hidden)

- A call that sent `competitors` or `icp` used to REPLACE the stored list; it now merges. Sending `[]` used to wipe the list; it now changes nothing. Nothing can be removed through this tool (Emma has no removal either; `regenerate_market_strategy` is the separate destructive tool).
- The answer of an update changed shape: it was `{success, data: <whole saved strategy>, message}`; it is now `{success, changed, businessOverview?, competitors?, icp?, ignoredArguments?}` (a call that changes nothing also carries a `message`).
- A blank `businessOverview` used to clear the overview; it is now "not given" (refused when it is the only content), so the overview cannot be cleared over MCP.
- Arguments the action does not take, `positioning`/`differentiators`/`channels`, and unknown entry fields are refused where they used to be ignored; a field shown on read (the ICP's `extractedFilters`) cannot be sent back (refused with a hint). A competitor or ICP SENT as a bare string is refused.
- Any `action` other than `read` / `update` (case ignored) is refused; it used to be taken as an update.
- Overview, names, descriptions and personas are stored trimmed; a name loses invisible characters; names match without regard to case, padding and repeated spaces (Emma's merge is exact; its lookup is loose); of two stored entries that differ only by case, the exact spelling is updated.
- Every update reads the strategy at least once more than before (twice, 200 ms apart, when it shows no `createdAt`), and the caller's record to find the account. A very large roster is paged on read.

## Differences from Emma that are not obvious

Emma fills empty brand fields from the strategy after each write (`populateEmptyBrandGuidelines`); the route does not, so this tool does not. The route rebuilds the stored strategy from its six known keys; Emma's merge keeps any other top-level key the record holds. Emma's merge matches names exactly; Emma floors a fractional read offset and clamps a negative one where this tool refuses them; Emma stamps `icpUpdatedAt` on any `icp` argument.

## What this does NOT change (stated limits)

1. The lock and the recent-save memory cover one server process. Calls that reach different instances, or a write by the portal or by Emma (neither is serialized with this tool) landing between our read and our write, can still be overwritten by the merged lists we send, and a read older than another writer's save (not ours) cannot be recognised here; a writer that stamps `updatedAt` with an older time than our last save is not recognised either. The route has no conditional write (`crm.ts` shows the codebase's `updatedAt` compare-and-set pattern).
2. If the route's read misses the org owner's record twice in a row (200 ms apart) and the route's write path then succeeds, a write replaces the lists and masks the owner's copy.
3. `emma_send_message` with the same key still reaches Emma's own `update_market_strategy`; unchanged.
4. Who may write is still the route's job (403 for an org member who is not an editor); a call that changes nothing makes no write and is answered without that check.
5. An admin's `client_id` is ignored (listed in `ignoredArguments`): the tool has never supported client scoping.
6. The tests run on a strongly consistent in-memory DynamoDB; the read-lag cases are simulated by answering one read with an older or empty copy.

## Proof

- `backend/src/__tests__/mcp.manageStrategy.writes.test.ts`: 102 tests through the real path (MCP client, MCP server, tool, mcpFetch, the real Express app, db.ts, in-memory DynamoDB) for an org owner, a member who is not an editor, a listed editor, another tenant and a solo user.
- Deliberate-breakage passes (51 one-line breakages in all, run as the code changed, e.g. no lock, replace instead of merge, per-user lock key, an older read used, parts not sent again, the memory chaining or never expiring, a missed read believed, the org flag ignored, bare strings not matched, unknown arguments accepted, null counted as sent, invisible-only text kept, the lookup error leaking): every one failed at least one test that names the behaviour. **Two survived at one point** (the memory's expiry; the second read's org flag): their tests did not depend on what they claimed to test, and were rewritten until the mutants failed them. One mutant (the memory's parts accumulating) is equivalent (the carried parts are in the body anyway) and was removed with the dead code. Files restored byte-identical after every run.
- Typecheck exit 0 and the pre-push hook green on the exact head; the public tool inventory (116 tools, only `manage_market_strategy` changed); the plan-route tool limits test, the two-tenant isolation suite and the other MCP suites: green.
- **Five independent fresh reviews** of successive heads: `31b3aac4f` SHIP WITH NITS (reproduced: lock per user while an org's strategy is shared; a missed org read turning a write into a replace; padding re-stamping `icpUpdatedAt`); `a51240868` **DO NOT SHIP** (reproduced HIGH: the route's own stale read of unsent parts dropped a prior save); `3d7065076` SHIP WITH NITS (bare-string stored entries, a memory that chained); `af04b635c` SHIP WITH NITS (an org caller merged onto the personal strategy, the lookup's error text leaking); `4de0698be` SHIP WITH NITS (invisible-only text counted as content; test gaps). Everything found is fixed or stated above. The changes after the fifth review (invisible-only text, a message, tests, note corrections) only tighten a rule or fix text and touch no guard's strength, write path or tenant scoping, so I judged them not material and did not run a sixth review (stated, not hidden). One bot finding (Opslane P2 on the first head) is fixed.

## Agent mode: the tool is now bridged (answers Opslane's AC1 finding on `e22f517`)

`manage_market_strategy` was registered for MCP callers only. Agent mode copies its tools from Emma's registry, so a private skill that listed it offered nothing, and a call answered `Unknown tool: manage_market_strategy` (`mcp/client/toolRegistry.ts`) on `main` as well as here. Opslane's AC1 on `e22f517` drove the tool through exactly such a skill session: its recording shows well-formed arguments answered with that error after 5 ms, so none of this PR's code ran. Fix (owner's decision, 2026-11-20): the tool is bridged into Emma's registry through `bridgedToolNames` in `emma/tools.ts` (the list already carries `resolve_skill`, `get_account_status` and the scheduled-chat tools; nine tools are registered in both registries), with the same definition and the same code. Opslane's check passed on that head (`f8ca60f`).

An independent review of `f8ca60f` (SHIP WITH NITS, no HIGH) found what the first version of this section got wrong, now fixed or stated:

- **Who is offered it:** a session whose installed skill lists it (private or published). It is not a foundation tool and, after the review, it is **kept out of the `__other_skills__` catch-all pool** (`SKILL_ONLY_TOOL_NAMES`, `emma/impl/misc.ts`): the first version landed in that pool, so every catch-all session would have carried a second strategy writer next to Emma's `update_market_strategy`. A skill's tools are added only for a wildcard tier or a tier that lists the skill. Sessions that are not skill-filtered still get it, as they get Emma's tool: sessions that predate skill gating (`associatedSkills` unset) and live voice sessions, on a wildcard tier. A work plan or schedule that names it in `requiredFunctionCalls` does not get it from the pool. "Not offered" means not in the tool list; a call by name in a session with no installed skill is not refused at dispatch (true of every tool). Emma's `update_market_strategy` is unchanged.
- **Anonymous sessions:** the bridged copy is marked `requiresUserAccount` (this tool only: none of the other 25 bridged tools' MCP handlers sets the flag today, so carrying every handler's flag would change nothing now; naming the tool keeps a later handler's flag from silently changing in-app behaviour), so a not-signed-in session gets the same deferred refusal as Emma's account tools instead of a lookup error that invited a retry.
- **Nothing new for a restricted principal:** a share-link visitor's profile is a deny-list that does not name `update_market_strategy`, so a visitor could already write the owner's strategy through Emma's tool. This tool is no broader: it cannot remove an entry and it refuses unknown fields. An unknown account is refused and nothing is written.
- **The lock does not span every path (corrected twice):** the per-account lock lives in the process that runs the call. Typed-chat turns run in a forked worker, so they are serialized with each other but not with `POST /mcp` (server process); the Emma widget and live voice run in the server process and do share the lock with MCP calls. Emma's own tool takes no lock at all. Same class of limit as the cross-instance one above.
- **Other stated limits:** a write through this tool does not emit the page-refresh invalidation Emma's tool emits in an `emma-sidebar` session (the open Market Strategy page can show the old lists until reloaded, and the page saves by replacing the lists); the superseded-brand-build guard Emma's tool carries is not carried (a brand-build session is not offered the tool unless a skill lists it); the `manage_` prefix classifies it as an `admin`-effect tool for the agent tool gateway and the plan route, reads included, as with the other `manage_*` tools; in agent mode the typed `competitors` items make a bare-string competitor fail the argument contract before the tool runs (the tool refuses it too).
- **Proof:** `backend/src/__tests__/emma.manageStrategyBridge.test.ts` (12 tests, a real `AgentModeService` against the real app and in-memory DynamoDB): the tool is in Emma's registry with the MCP definition; a foundation-only session and the `__other_skills__` pool are not offered it while a session whose private or published skill lists it is; a call made the way a chat turn makes it adds the competitor and keeps the stored competitors and the ICP with its cached filters (the AC1 scenario); update by name; read; a bare string, an unknown argument and an unknown account change nothing; an anonymous session gets the deferred refusal for update and read. Three deliberate breakages, each caught: bridge line removed (9 of 12 fail), pool exclusion removed (1 fails: the pool test), user-account flag not carried (1 fails: the anonymous test). The plan-route limits, agent-mode wiring, tool-inventory and annotation suites and the 76 suites that touch the skill pool or the bridge list stay green.

## Route change: `icpUpdatedAt` moves only when the ICP list changes (Opslane P1 on `440bb19`, run 2354)

Opslane's probe: an ICP edit through MCP, then a competitors-only update within a minute, then a read. The stamp moved although no ICP changed. Cause: the carry-over below re-sends the stored ICP list (the route fills every part it is not sent from its own, eventually consistent read and would write an older list back), and the route stamped `icpUpdatedAt` on any `icp` argument. First I documented it as a trade-off; Opslane reproduced it again, and the fix turned out small, so it is fixed at its cause instead of left in a card.

- **The rule** (`nextIcpUpdatedAt`, `routes/marketStrategy.ts`, both the org and the solo save): a save that sends no `icp` keeps the stored stamp (as before); a save that sends back the very list already stored keeps it too; a first ICP save, a changed list (any field, the order, an entry added or removed, a field the record holds left out) and a record with no stamp yet (saved before the field existed) stamp `now`, as before. The comparison is `isDeepStrictEqual` of the list sent and the list stored.
- **Why it is right:** `routes/crm.ts` compares `icpUpdatedAt` with the user's `icpCompletedAt` to choose between the cached, richer ICP search filters and the market-strategy ICPs, and its comment says the stamp is for "a write that actually touches `icp`" (ENG-1955). The old code stamped on a write that touched nothing; the same bug had a portal form: saving an unedited ICP form switched the account off its cached filters.
- **Who it affects:** every caller of `POST /api/market-strategy` (the portal, this tool). The only visible difference is that re-sending the stored ICP list no longer moves the stamp. Emma's own `update_market_strategy` has its own merge and still stamps on any `icp` argument (unchanged, stated above).
- **Not a data-plane change:** no schema, key, index or migration; no stored stamp is rewritten; it only decides whether a timestamp moves on a save. A revert restores the old rule.
- **The lag case (stated limit):** if the route's own read (an eventually consistent index) is older than the list the tool re-sends, the lists differ and the stamp moves although the list written is the one already stored: the Opslane symptom, only inside that lag window, with the data correct (the saved list still wins over the older one; the carry-over keeps its job). It goes away only with a strongly consistent read or a conditional write in this route, which this change does not add; the in-memory DynamoDB of the tests is strongly consistent, so no test exercises it.
- **Proof:** `backend/src/__tests__/marketStrategy.icpUpdatedAt.test.ts`, 22 tests on the real router: 10 cases for each of the org and solo branches (identical list keeps the stamp, the same list with its keys in another order keeps it, a changed list, a reordered list, an added or removed ICP, a field left out, a number where text is stored, no `icp` sent, a record with no stamp, a first save) and 2 for an org save on the owner's strategy when the org record has none; the Opslane scenario through the real MCP path in `mcp.manageStrategy.writes.test.ts`. Breakages of the rule, each caught: the old rule (6 tests fail), keeping the stamp for a record that has none, comparing only titles, a key-order-sensitive comparison (2), a loose comparison (2). The independent review of the route change (SHIP WITH NITS, no HIGH or MEDIUM) found the last two surviving; the tests were added and both are now caught. The 13 suites that touch the route or the stamp pass.

## Route change: 413 with a reason when the record would pass 400 KB (Opslane P1 on `ef2bc22`, run 2358)

Opslane's probe: a solo account whose record was already about 410 KB (a large saved ICP result), a strategy of 194 KB (under the tool's own 250,000-byte limit), one competitor added over MCP: the answer was `API error (500): Internal server error` with no reason. DynamoDB refuses a write that would leave an item over 400 KB, atomically (nothing is written), and the route turned that into a bare 500.

- **The change** (`routes/marketStrategy.ts`, POST only): a `ValidationException` whose message says the item size exceeded the maximum allowed size now answers **413** `{ error: "market_strategy_too_large", message }`, and the message names the 400 KB limit, says nothing was changed and asks to shorten the entries (it does not say why the record is large, and does not suggest removing anything: the tool cannot). The route reuses `isDynamoItemSizeError` (`utils/dynamoItemBudget.ts`), which also requires the `ValidationException` code. The tool prints the route's message (`API error (413): ...`). Any other failure of the write is still the same bare 500 (a different `ValidationException`, a throttle, a plain error). A write that succeeds is unchanged. Org and solo branches.
- **Why not a bigger pre-check in the tool:** the tool cannot see the rest of the record, and the route is the one place that sees the write fail, for the portal as much as for the tool; the refusal is atomic, so reporting it is all that is missing.
- **Proof:** `backend/src/__tests__/marketStrategy.itemTooLarge.test.ts` (8 tests on the real router, both branches, both DynamoDB messages for the same error, the other failures still 500, success unchanged) and, through the real MCP path, a test in `mcp.manageStrategy.writes.test.ts` on a solo account whose record is almost full (the in-memory DynamoDB fake gained an optional `maxItemBytes`, off by default, that refuses an over-limit write with the service's own `ValidationException`): the answer names 400 KB and "Nothing was changed", the record is byte-identical, and a record with room still saves. Breakages, each caught: the 413 branch removed (5 tests fail), the size message matched without the `ValidationException` code (2). The duplicate-name reporting: an added entry also reported as updated (3), the first-touch snapshot overwritten (3), every touched entry reported as updated (11) or as unchanged (17). The independent review of these two fixes (SHIP WITH NITS, no HIGH or MEDIUM, and it ran the 413 through the real org write path: byte-identical org record afterwards) had four nits, all fixed: the 413 message overstated the cause and suggested removing entries, a near-copy of an existing helper, no test for the code check, and a call that changes an entry and changes it back was reported as updated. The 16 suites that touch the route, the tool, the bridge or the inventory pass.

## Rollback

Code only (revert and redeploy). No data or schema change. The route changes are the `icpUpdatedAt` rule and the 413 answer above; the revert restores the old behaviour of both, and a stored stamp is never rewritten either way.

title: ENG-2840: manage_brand over MCP: tagline, domain, brand values, personality; founders merge by name, removed only by name (PR C: brand)
body:
## Summary

ENG-2840 wave 1, PR C (brand part): `manage_brand` over MCP can now set the tagline, the domain, the brand values, the brand personality and the founder profiles, which Emma's `update_brand_guidelines` writes and the tool could not. Founders **merge by name and are removed only by name**.

`backend/src/mcp/server/manageBrandWrites.ts` (+ `accountLock.ts`, byte-identical to the copy in the sibling strategy PR #4201); the REST route (`POST /api/brand/guidelines`) is untouched, so the customer portal behaves as before. `read` returns what it did, except that an argument it does not take is refused by name.

## The founders rule (deliberately different from Emma; owner's decision, 2026-11-19)

The route REPLACES the stored founder list (an empty list wipes it). Emma treats a non-empty list as the complete roster: a stored founder it leaves out is removed (ENG-2875, so a customer could remove a founder through Emma). Emma and the portal hold the whole roster; an outside agent that sends one founder does not, and under Emma's rule it would delete the others (re-creating the ENG-2875 bug for MCP agents in the other direction). So over MCP:

- `founders` **merges**: a stored founder with the same name (case, padding, repeated spaces, invisible characters and the way an accent is encoded ignored) is updated field by field and keeps its own spelling and every field the caller did not send; a new name is added; a founder nobody mentions is kept. If older data holds the same founder twice, an update lays the new fields over every copy and a removal drops every copy. An empty list changes nothing (Emma ignores it too). Omission never removes anyone. The same founder twice in one call is refused.
- **Removal is deliberate:** `remove_founders: [names]` removes the founders with those names (matched the same way, at most 20 names per call, 200 characters each). The answer says which were removed and which were not found. A name in both lists is refused. This is the `removeFounders` shape the ENG-2875 card itself names as the alternative to an authoritative list.
- A founder holds `name`, `jobTitle`, `styleTone`, `signaturePosts`, `voiceExamples` (text; 200 / 2,000 / 10,000 / 20,000 characters); other fields are refused by name. At most 20 per call; a call that would take the roster past 50 founders, or the founder profiles past 250,000 bytes together, is refused when it makes them bigger (shrinking an oversized roster still works). The 250,000-byte cap keeps the roster from taking the brand record by itself; it does not guarantee that the 400 KB record fits (a save that does not fit comes back from the route as an unexplained 500).

## Other changes

- **New fields:** `tagline` (300 characters), `domain` (253), `brand_personality` (2,000), `brand_values` (list of up to 50, 200 characters each, blank entries dropped). They replace the stored value, like `key_messages` always did. For these and for founders, blank text (empty, spaces, or only invisible characters; text that merely contains a joiner, as an emoji does, is kept as sent) and an empty list mean "not given" and never blank a stored value. The six fields the tool always had keep their mapping and behaviour (they are forwarded as sent and not validated: an explicit blank, `null` or a very large value there is stored as sent, as it always was); only what would be dropped while the call reports success is refused: `visual_identity` must be an object holding only the keys the brand stores.
- **Arguments an update does not take are refused by name** (for example `logo_url`, `brandName`): they would be dropped while the call reported success. Identity-style arguments are never used for outside callers, so they are ignored: `client_id`, `clientId` and `user_id` are listed in `ignoredArguments` (`userId` is removed by the MCP layer before a tool sees it). `read` takes no arguments and refuses any other the same way. `action` must be `read` or `update` (a mistyped "Read" used to write).
- **The answer reports what is stored.** The route answers a save with a message only, so after a founder change the founders are read back (name and the four text fields, in order); a read that does not match is repeated once after 300 ms (the org read is eventually consistent) before the answer is a failure ("could not be verified": the save itself went through). If the read-back fails outright the answer says the brand was saved but could not be read back. `total` comes from the read; added / updated / removed / not found describe the intended outcome.
- A call that changes nothing in the founders and sends nothing else writes nothing (it is therefore answered without the route's editor check; a real change by a non-editor still gets the route's 403). A call that sends scalar fields always saves, and `changed: true` there means "saved", not "different". A call with nothing to change is refused instead of reported as saved.
- **The merge baseline is checked, not trusted** (lessons from the independent reviews of the sibling strategy PR, whose tool has the same read, merge, write shape): calls on one **account** are taken in turn in this process (the key is the org when the caller belongs to one: an org's brand is shared by its members; the caller's record is read consistently to find the org and the call is refused if that fails, with a generic message); the route's read must answer `exists` true with brand data, or `exists` false; a read that shows no brand is read once more 200 ms later before it is believed (a missed read of the org owner's record would otherwise turn the founder list into a replace); a read whose `updatedAt` is older than the brand this process saved within the last minute is not used (the saved roster is); and the roster a save meant is remembered even when its own read-back came back older than the save.

## Behaviour changes for outside callers (stated, not hidden)

A call with no field to change used to post an empty body, which the route saves (`updatedAt` moves, an account with no brand gets an empty record and its brand-build status flips to ready); it is now refused. Any `action` other than `read` / `update` (case ignored) used to be taken as an update; it is now refused. Arguments outside the tool's own fields, arguments given to `read` and unknown keys inside `visual_identity` used to be ignored and are now refused by name. The answer of a successful update now carries `success`, `changed`, `ignoredArguments` when any, and after a founder change the founders section (the route's own `message` and `attachments` are still there; its `debug` is removed from answers to outside callers by the public response sanitiser, as before). Every update now reads the caller's record to find the account, and an update with founders reads the brand once or twice before and once or twice after the save.

## What this does NOT change (stated limits)

1. The lock and the recent-save memory cover one server process. A founder change made between our read and our write (by the portal, Emma or another session, or a call on another instance) can be overwritten by the merged list we send. The route saves with an optimistic version check, but only against what it read inside its own request, so it does not catch that. A read older than another writer's save (not ours) cannot be recognised here; a portal edit within a minute that carries an older stamp (clock skew between instances) is overwritten by the remembered roster. If the route's read misses the org owner's record twice in a row, a founder list built on it replaces the stored founders and masks the owner's copy.
2. Logos and brand assets are not writable here (they need a file upload route), and the brand-guide link (`brandGuideUrl`, which the route accepts as JSON) is not forwarded.
3. `emma_send_message` with the same key still reaches Emma's own `update_brand_guidelines` with its authoritative founder list; unchanged.
4. Who may write is still the route's job (an org member needs the same brand-editor rights as in the app: 403 otherwise).
5. A read-back that fails or does not match is an ordinary tool result with `success: false` (`isError` is false), because the save went through.
6. Not verified: whether Hermes/Yugo send founders through MCP today (other repo; the documented MCP schema never exposed them, so nothing should depend on the old behaviour).
7. The tests run on a strongly consistent in-memory DynamoDB; the read-lag cases are simulated by answering a read with an older or empty copy.

## Proof

- `backend/src/__tests__/mcp.manageBrand.writes.test.ts`: 84 tests through the real path (MCP client, MCP server, tool, mcpFetch, the real Express app, db.ts, in-memory DynamoDB) for an org owner, a member who is not an editor, a listed editor, another tenant and a solo user: new fields, the six old fields, merge and removal by name, duplicates, refusals that name the problem and leave the account byte-identical, caps and the size limit, parallel calls (including the owner and an editor together), an older read, a missed read, unusable answers from the read, the read-back (repeated, failing, field-level), a 409 from the route, the lock key refused when the caller cannot be identified, arguments the update does not take, `visual_identity`, look-alike names, logo attachments preserved.
- Deliberate-breakage passes: 45 one-line breakages across `manageBrandWrites.ts`, `accountLock.ts` and the action check in `apiTools.ts` (no lock; replace instead of merge; case/spacing-sensitive names; unknown founder keys; blank overwrites; empty call accepted; a name in both lists; roster cap; not-found names unreported; no-op still posts; read-back removed, repeated or names-only; spelling overwritten; the six old fields dropped; empty brand values clears; founders sent unchanged; removal skipped; lock per user; an older read used; a missed read believed; an unusable read accepted; any action an update; unknown arguments accepted; identity arguments refused or unreported; the save or the meant roster not remembered; only the first duplicate copy updated or removed; prototype-chain names; invisible characters or accents; size limit removed or blocking shrink; a caller with no record locked per user; read taking arguments; a failed read-back a bare error; unbounded remove names; the same founder twice in a call; unknown or non-object `visual_identity`; the short list of invisible characters; invisible-only tagline or brand value kept as content). Every one fails 1 to 23 tests, and the failing tests name that behaviour. **Two survived the first run** (an older read used; the last save not remembered): my stale-read test counted reads from before its override was installed, so the stale answer was never given. The test was fixed and both now fail it. Files restored byte-identical after every run.
- Typecheck exit 0 and the pre-push hook green on the exact head; the public tool inventory (115 tools, only `manage_brand` changed; the fixture is regenerated); the plan-route tool limits test, the two-tenant isolation suite and the other MCP suites touched: green.
- Independent reviews: first (head `5fd3d3fa6`) SHIP WITH NITS (no HIGH; reproduced: a stale read-back disabled the recent-save protection and lost a founder, a failed user lookup locked per user, only the first copy of a duplicated name handled, prototype-chain names, names-only read-back, no size limit); second (head `83905b910`) SHIP WITH NITS (no HIGH; a stale inventory fixture, unknown `visual_identity` keys dropped silently, a founder twice in one call, narrow invisible-character set; the rest documented). All of it is fixed or stated in the final head `f528bf933`. The changes after the second review tighten validation and error text and touch no guard's strength, write path or tenant scoping, so I judged them not material and did not run a third full review (stated, not hidden). The last small change (text with nothing visible is not given, as in the strategy tool) follows the fifth review of that sibling.

## Rollback

Code only (revert and redeploy). No data, schema or route change.

title: ENG-2840: knowledge base over MCP: narrow and page the list, append to a file (PR C: knowledge base)
body:
## Summary

ENG-2840 wave 1, PR C (knowledge base part): `list_knowledge_bases` over MCP took no input, although the route behind it (`GET /api/emma/knowledge-bases`, `routes/emmaApi.ts`) and Emma's `list_knowledge_base_files` take `kb_type`, `modified_after`, `modified_before`, `limit` and `offset`. The tool now takes all five (`backend/src/mcp/server/knowledgeBaseParams.ts`). The REST routes are unchanged, so the customer portal and Emma behave as before, and no other knowledge-base tool changes. Creating a knowledge base through MCP still makes a **private** one only.

**Scope note.** This PR first also added an `append` mode to `update_knowledge_base_file_content`. The independent review showed append cannot be verified by the recorded file size (details under "Not in this PR"), so it was **removed** and is deferred with the findings written down. What is left is the list inputs, which two independent reviews found sound once the text said what the service really does.

## What each input does (decided by the service, `emma/impl/knowledgeBase.ts`; the tool description says so)

- `kb_type` picks the sources. `private` and `public` both mean "only the platform knowledge bases" (the service does not tell them apart; the platform list is your own, those your organisation shares with you when org sharing is on, and the public ones, so a `private` row is not necessarily yours). `google-drive`, `clickup`, `clickup-tasks`, `foreplay-swipefile` and `foreplay-board` mean only that connected source; the two Foreplay values return the same thing. ClickUp folder entries are listed whatever `kb_type` is (the service has no guard there).
- `modified_after`, `modified_before`, `limit` (default 100) and `offset` apply to the **Google Drive files only** (`limit` and `offset` per Drive source); they have no effect on the platform knowledge bases, ClickUp or Foreplay (the answer's message still echoes them).

## Validation (before any call; refused by name)

`kb_type` must be one of the seven kinds (case ignored). The dates must be calendar dates in `YYYY-MM-DD` form (the only form the service accepts; a date with a time or a date that does not exist is refused here instead of coming back from the service as a failure), and `modified_after` must not be later than `modified_before`. `limit` (1 to 1,000) and `offset` (0 to 100,000) must be whole numbers, as a number or digits in text; the bounds are the tool's, because the service has none and an unbounded value makes it walk a whole Drive folder on the shared service account. Empty, blank and 0 mean "not given" (0 means the default, not "none": the service would take a limit of 0 literally). With no arguments the call is exactly what it was.

## Behaviour changes for outside callers

None for a call that sends no argument. A call that sent one of these arguments used to have it dropped (the tool never forwarded it); it is now forwarded, or refused by name when it cannot be understood.

## Not in this PR: an append mode (deferred, findings recorded in the dev note)

The review reproduced, with the real service code and a faked storage layer, that `knowledgeBaseSize` holds the main file's size after a main-file write but the SUM of the attachments after an attachment write, so the size read before an append is wrong whenever attachments exist and a correct append is reported as "could not be verified" (a retry then duplicates the text). A file listed in the record but missing in storage, two attachments with the same name, a failure after the text was stored and a racing writer give the same false answers (an equal-length racing writer a false success); the route's append decodes the stored bytes as UTF-8, which corrupts a Latin-1 or UTF-16 `.txt` uploaded through the portal; and writes of other files can orphan a file through the shared file list. A safe append needs the actual text read before and after (prefix and suffix check), one lock per knowledge base and a refusal for non-UTF-8 text.

## Stated limits

1. The no-argument answer includes the public knowledge bases of other users and, when org sharing is on, teammates' private ones, as it always did.
2. `foreplay-swipefile` and `foreplay-board` fetch the same things.
3. The tests run the tool against a fake of the route; the service's handling of each input is as read from `emma/impl/knowledgeBase.ts` (and run against a stubbed service by the independent review), not observed against live Drive, ClickUp or Foreplay.
4. The tool is classified `write` by the annotation policy, as before, so a `tools:read` key cannot call it.

## Proof

title: fix(ishare): email-report no longer works as a mail relay (ENG-3163)
body:
## What

The share-link report email (`POST /api/agent-mode/ishare/:shareId/email-report`) can no longer be used as a mail relay (ENG-3163).

## Why

The endpoint is public on purpose: a landing page calls it so a lead gets their own AI report by email (added in March "to email reports to leads"). Holding a share link and its token was all it needed, so anyone with one could make AgentWeb send mail from our domain to any address, with any link behind the "View Your Report" button, as often as they liked. That is a spam and phishing relay, and it can damage the sending reputation every customer's email depends on. The report link was also put into the email's `href` unescaped.

## Fix

The lead flow is kept; the abuse is closed. New `backend/src/utils/ishareEmailReport.ts`, used by `emailReportToLead`:

- **Report link must be ours.** `https` links on `agentweb.pro` and its subdomains, subdomains of `agentwebforms.com`, `hireemma.ai` and its subdomains (exactly the list the API already trusts for browser calls in `app.ts`), plus this environment's configured `FRONTEND_URL` / `CUSTOMER_FRONTEND_URL` origins (staging, env1, local dev). Anything else, including lookalikes (`agentweb.pro.evil.com`), links with credentials and non-http schemes, is a 400. The link is normalised through `URL` and HTML-escaped where it goes into the email.
- **Recipient must be one plain address.** Lists, "Name <address>" and line breaks are a 400.
- **Sends are limited:** 3 per share link per hour, 3 per recipient address per hour, 60 per caller IP per hour (the IP cap is loose on purpose: a landing page that calls from its own server sends every lead from one IP). Over the limit is a 429 with `Retry-After`. A refused attempt is not counted.
- **Unchanged:** the share token and expiry checks, and they still run before the limits, so a caller with a wrong token cannot use up a real link's sends. The email looks the same.
- `RateLimiter` gets an optional third constructor argument for the window length (default stays 60s, so existing callers are unchanged). Separate commit.

## Evidence

- New: `ishareEmailReport.test.ts` (unit) and `agentModeController.ishareEmailReport.test.ts` (drives the real controller), plus `rateLimiter.customWindow.test.ts`. 65 tests pass on Node 24, covering the lead flow, each refused link and recipient shape, the token/expiry paths, the per-link 429 with `Retry-After`, a send failure answering 500, and that a wrong-token caller does not use up a real link's sends.
- 16 suites, 144 tests pass in total with the existing ishare controller/route suites, `mcpServerAuth`, `metaToolkitRoutes` and all four `rateLimiter` suites.
- Mutation check: with the old controller put back (confirmed it has no `normalizeRecipient`), 10 of the 19 controller tests fail; the 9 that still pass are the ones that must (the lead flow and the unchanged token/expiry paths).
- Scoped TypeScript check on the changed files: 0 diagnostics in source files.
- Prod nginx access logs (14 days kept, the whole retention) contain zero requests to this endpoint, so no live caller is known to exist today.

## Not covered / limits

- **Limits live in memory** on the one prod instance and reset when it is replaced (a deploy). They bound abuse; they are not a permanent quota.
- **Still possible:** someone holding a share link can send the standard "your report is ready" email, with a link on our own site, to an address they choose, up to the limits above.
- **A caller using a report link on another domain would now get a 400.** I found no caller in this repo or the customer portal repo, and none in 14 days of prod access logs; the endpoint was written for external landing pages. The hosts accepted are the ones the API already trusts for browser calls.

## Risk and rollback

- Backend only. No schema, data or auth change. The email wording and look are unchanged.
- Rollback: revert this PR.

Opened as a draft; merge on Manan's word.

title: fix(connected-accounts): reconnect finds a legacy 'facebook' Meta row (ENG-2264)
body:
## What

Reconnecting a Meta account that is stored under the old platform name `facebook` now updates that entry in place instead of leaving it behind next to a new duplicate (ENG-2264).

## Why it happened

`connectedAccountsDb.createAccount` matched an existing entry only on the exact platform string (`acc.platform === platform && acc.account_id === input.account_id`). Every Meta connect flow writes `meta`, and every reader (`metaAccountCredentials`, `metaTokenRefresh`, `agentModeService`, ...) already accepts both `meta` and the legacy `facebook`, but the write path did not. A user whose account is still stored as `facebook` got a brand-new `meta` entry on every reconnect, and the old entry kept its own `sharedWithOrg`, `engagementMemory` and `created_at` while the new one started blank. `facebook` is no longer in `PlatformType`, so it is purely a legacy spelling.

## Fix

In `createAccount`: an exact platform match still wins. If there is none, a row stored under a legacy spelling of the same platform (only `facebook` for `meta`, same `account_id`) counts as the same connection. It is updated in place and relabelled to the current platform, and its own top-level fields are kept (the function already spreads the existing entry). The alias map is a small private table next to `normalizeAccounts`.

- Users who already reconnected before this and have both rows: the `meta` row is updated, the `facebook` row is left exactly as it is (nothing merged or deleted).
- No clean-up of existing duplicates in this PR.
- Other platforms behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

- New `connectedAccountsDb.createAccount.legacyPlatform.test.ts` (7 tests): in-place migration keeps `sharedWithOrg`, `engagementMemory` and `created_at` and refreshes config/name; other accounts on the user are untouched; no existing row adds a new entry; a legacy row for a different `account_id` is not matched; exact match wins when both rows exist; `facebook` is not aliased to any platform but `meta`; unchanged exact-match behaviour for another platform.
- 19 suites, all passing: the 13 `connectedAccountsDb` suites (133 tests, new file included) plus the Meta OAuth, connected-accounts route and ENG-2232 suites (Node 24).
- Mutation check: with the old `createAccount` matching put back (confirmed the alias helper was absent), 2 of the 7 new tests fail (the in-place migration and the untouched-others case); the 5 control tests pass as they should.
- Scoped TypeScript check on the changed file and the new test: 0 errors.

## Not covered

- A real reconnect on prod or env1. It needs an account stored under `facebook`, and I cannot create one without writing to the database; the tests drive the real `createAccount` with a mocked user store.

## Blast radius on prod (measured, read-only)

Counted over the whole prod `AW-Users` table (519 users, 69 with connected accounts), reading only each account's platform label and account id and printing aggregates: **0 users have a legacy `facebook` row** (34 `meta` rows, 0 `facebook`; no existing orphan duplicates either). So the bug is not occurring in prod today, and the new branch cannot run for any current row: for today's data `createAccount` behaves exactly as before (the exact-match lookup is unchanged). This fix is preventive: it closes the trap for any legacy row that appears later (a restored backup, an import).

## Risk and rollback

- Backend only, one lookup in one function. No schema change and no data migration. A legacy row is relabelled `meta` the next time its owner reconnects; all readers accept `meta`.
- Rollback: revert this PR. Rows already relabelled stay valid because readers accept both spellings.

Opened as a draft; merge on Manan's word.

title: fix(share-link): tell a server-written turn by its stored kind, never by its text (ENG-3164)
body:
## What
Fixes ENG-3164 (part 1): a share-link visitor could escape the "anonymous viewer" note Emma reads by opening their message with the server's own "[SYSTEM] This is an automatic continuation" line.

## Why (reproduced live before the fix)
`isServerAuthoredContinuation` fell back to the message TEXT, which the visitor writes. Probe on production (owner's own admin account) and on env1: a plain visitor message is marked (YES), the same message opened with that line is not (NO). It also stayed unmarked in every later turn.

## Changes (backend only, no schema change, no UI change)
- A turn counts as server-written only from the `kind` the server stored on its row (`SERVER_AUTHORED_USER_KINDS`: `auto-continuation`, `approval-inbox-resolution`), never from the text. The live turn's own stored row is found by its content (or the content before the voice-card suffix); no row found = labelled (safe direction).
- A visitor's message is no longer merged into a server-written row just before it (the merged row kept the server's metadata and so lost the note).
- The Meta campaign-objective check (`verifyExplicitStatement`) and the paused-bundle ad-count check no longer take a share-link visitor's message as the owner's own words. A visitor-last objective falls back to the approval card, which a visitor cannot answer (403).

## Not changed (deliberately)
What visitors can chat or do; the visitor tool block; tools that only need a model-set `confirm` (owner decision 2026-11-19: label only, no gating); the stop judge and work-plan step-removal judge (a visitor may stop their own turn); the spend-worry check (it only adds a confirmation step).

## Known low residual
The turn's own row is identified by content equality with the last history row. If the history read is stale (eventually consistent) and the older last row is a server continuation, a visitor who typed that continuation's exact full text would go unlabelled. Needs a stale read AND the exact text; carrying the kind through the worker request would close it and is left for a follow-up if wanted.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck` clean. 38 neighbouring suites (1,367 tests) pass, including the existing metaObjectiveGate, prepareTurnContext golden, ishareAnonymousProvenance suites.
- 11 deliberate breaks (restore the text rule in each place, never server-authored, own row never found, owner-only dropped in both places, ad-count counts visitors, kind list never matches, merge fuses, stored-content hand-over ignored, caller not passing it): all caught.
- Two independent reviews (one with full context, one blind): no blockers; the two real gaps they found (merge hole, voice-card live copy) are fixed here, plus nits.
- env1 live on this exact head, real visitor requests with no login: plain visitor YES, prefixed visitor YES (was NO), signed-in owner NO (unmarked). Script: the same probe used on production before the fix.
- After merge: same probe on production in the owner's own admin account.

## Release note
Release-note PR #4206 is held until this ships so its wording is true.

title: feat(zoma): X Ads connector (ENG-3142)
body:
## Risk: Medium | Priority: Medium

**Draft. Everything here is dark: `ZOMA_X_ADS_ENABLED` defaults off, so X is not listed, routed, offered in `zoma_status`, or reachable through its connect routes until the flag is flipped.**

## What was wrong (before)
Zoma (the ads MCP) supported Meta and Google Ads only. X Ads API access (app 33152933) was approved on 2026-11-17, but we had no connector. The existing Twitter integration (`routes/twitterAuth.ts`) uses OAuth2, and the Ads API does not accept OAuth2.

## What this fixes (after)
X Ads is Zoma provider #3. It follows the Google toolkit pattern: a curated manifest, a gateway with own-account resolution, guarded writes (preview → confirm → apply once → read-back), annotations and per-call metering. Auth is OAuth 1.0a user context, with HMAC-SHA1 signing written here (no new dependency).

### What's in it
- **Secrets:** `getXAdsCredentials()` reads `prod/AgentWeb/XAds` or `dev/AgentWeb/XAds` (`{"consumerKey","consumerSecret"}`). The OAuth2 Twitter secret is not reused.
- **Connect (OAuth 1.0a, 3-legged):**
  - `zoma_status` mints a signed 15-minute link to `GET /api/oauth/x-ads/start`.
  - `/start` gets a request token and redirects to X's authorize page.
  - `GET /api/oauth/x-ads/callback` exchanges the verifier and lists the ad accounts that X login can manage. It stores one `connected_accounts` row per account (platform `x_ads`). Both the token and the token secret are encrypted with `utils/crypto.encryptPassword`.
  - The pending request-token secret is kept in memory, is single use, and is capped per user (same pattern as the Twitter PKCE sessions).
- **`x_ads_read`** (annotated read-only): `LIST_ACCOUNTS`, `LIST_FUNDING_INSTRUMENTS`, `LIST_CAMPAIGNS`, `LIST_LINE_ITEMS`, `LIST_PROMOTED_TWEETS`, `GET_STATS`. Stats use the synchronous endpoint. Ranges are split into windows of 7 days or less, fetched one after another, and merged: a DAY series is concatenated, a TOTAL is summed. A single call covers at most 90 days and 20 ids.
- **`x_ads_write`** (default destructive annotation):
  - Campaigns and line items: `CREATE` / `UPDATE` / `PAUSE` / `ACTIVATE`.
  - Line item `CREATE` supports basic targeting (locations, broad keywords, follower lookalikes), applied in one batch request and read back.
  - Promoted tweets: `CREATE`, which promotes existing posts.
  - **Creates are always PAUSED.** A status cannot be passed on a create; `ACTIVATE` is its own preview and approval, and counts as a publish write for the billing gate.
  - Money is entered in major units and converted to micros. Extra precision is refused, never rounded.
  - Optional `X_ADS_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING`, in micros, with the same shape as the Google ceiling.
- **Verdicts:**
  - Only a read-back of `CONFIRMED` counts as success.
  - A write X accepted that reads back unchanged is `MISMATCH`.
  - No response, a 5xx or a 408 is `UNCONFIRMED`: the write may have applied.
  - Any other 4xx is a refusal ("nothing was changed").

## Complexity ledger
- **Lines:** about +1,000 of production code across 7 new files, plus small edits to 10 existing files. About +550 lines of tests.
- **Moving parts added:**
  - One provider and two tools.
  - One new `connected_accounts` platform value (`x_ads`) with its config type.
  - Two OAuth routes and one env flag.
- **Reused rather than duplicated:**
  - `zomaWriteGuard` (preview tokens and the shared single-use store).
  - `resolveProviderAccount`, `majorToMicros` / `formatMicros` / the spend-ceiling parser from Google, and `assertZomaWriteReady`.
  - The deny-by-default annotations table.
- **Behavior:** with the flag off, no existing response changes. `ZomaReadiness.x_ads` is absent and Meta/Google paths are untouched (the existing toolkit, Zoma and annotation suites pass).

## How to test (after the secret is in place and the flag is on in dev)
1. Set `ZOMA_X_ADS_ENABLED=true` and call `zoma_status`. **Expected:** an "Or connect an existing X (Twitter) Ads account → …/api/oauth/x-ads/start?t=…" line.
2. Open the link and approve on X. **Expected:** an "X Ads connected" page listing the account(s). `zoma_status` then shows `[x] X Ads account connected (<id>, <currency>)`.
3. Call `x_ads_read {action: LIST_CAMPAIGNS}`. **Expected:** the campaigns of that account.
4. Call `x_ads_read {action: GET_STATS, entity: CAMPAIGN, entity_ids:[…], start_date, end_date}` over more than 7 days. **Expected:** merged series and `windows > 1`.
5. Call `x_ads_write CAMPAIGN CREATE` without `confirm`. **Expected:** a PREVIEW, and nothing created. Repeat with `confirm: true` and the `preview_token`. **Expected:** `verification: CONFIRMED` and `entity_status: PAUSED`.
6. Unset the flag. **Expected:** the X tools disappear from `tools/list`, and `/api/oauth/x-ads/*` returns 404.

## Edge cases to check
- An X login with no ad account gets a "create one at ads.x.com" page, and nothing is stored.
- A user who declines on X gets the "not connected" page.
- Several X accounts without `account_id` is ambiguous, and the caller must pass `account_id`.

## Test Evidence
- `npx jest src/__tests__/eng3142`: 4 suites, 39 tests passed.
  - `eng3142.oauth1`: signing is pinned to X's **published reference signature** (`hCtSmYh+iHYCEqBWrE7C7hYmtUk=`), plus the 3-legged token steps and the client's error mapping.
  - `eng3142.xAdsManifest`: the surface, annotations, window splitting and merging, and signed sequential stats requests.
  - `eng3142.xAdsWrites`: preview sends nothing; tokens are single use and bound to the arguments; creates are PAUSED; targeting is applied in one batch; promote; not-found; spend ceiling; UNCONFIRMED vs refusal; MISMATCH; money precision.
  - `eng3142.xAdsZomaGating`: through the real `handleMetaToolkitCall` with the flag off and on: own-account resolution, 403 on a foreign or revoked account, decrypted token in the signature, `platform: x_ads` metering, `zoma_status` with and without the flag, the connect flow (encrypted storage, single-use callback, 404 when off, forged link refused), and redaction.
- 44 existing suites that import the touched modules (Zoma onboarding, billing, device flow, Google toolkit, Meta toolkit routes and MCP, annotations, journey) all pass.
  - `eng2747.metaToolkitAnnotations` now includes the X manifest in its advertised set, so the "no stale read-only entries" check covers `x_ads_read`.
- Scoped `tsc --noEmit` over every new and touched module, `app.ts` and the tests: clean. The full-repo typecheck was not run because of memory limits on the box.

## Behavioral assertions verified
ENG-3142 has no human-written acceptance-criteria section. The scope list from the task brief is mapped instead: secrets → the `getXAdsCredentials` code path; OAuth1 connect → `eng3142.oauth1` and `eng3142.xAdsZomaGating` (connect); reads → `eng3142.xAdsManifest`; writes defaulting to PAUSED → `eng3142.xAdsWrites`; gating → `eng3142.xAdsZomaGating` (flag).

## What was NOT tested / needed before the flag flips
- **No live X call has been made.** Live verification needs:
  1. The `prod/AgentWeb/XAds` secret (and the dev one) with the consumer key and secret of app 33152933.
  2. **`https://api.agentweb.pro/api/oauth/x-ads/callback`** (and the staging/dev equivalents) registered as a callback URL on app 33152933. Without it, X refuses `request_token`, and the start page reports that clearly.
- Assumptions about the X v12 API that need a live check:
  - Stats `start_time`/`end_time` are sent as `YYYY-MM-DD` and assumed to be read in the account's time zone.
  - Line item `bid_strategy` `AUTO`/`MAX` and `bid_amount_local_micro`.
  - Targeting types `LOCATION`, `BROAD_KEYWORD`, `SIMILAR_TO_FOLLOWERS_OF_USER`.
- Asynchronous stats jobs (ranges over 90 days) are not implemented. Longer ranges are refused with "split the range".
- **Data-plane note:** this adds a new `connected_accounts` platform value (`x_ads`) and config shape to the existing user-record list. No migration, backfill or schema change, but it is a new stored credential shape. It is flagged for Harsha's call under the database/data-plane gate, and the PR stays a draft.
- `zomaMcpInstructions` and the agent guide (`skill.md`) do not mention X yet. The tool descriptions carry the usage guidance.

## Files changed
- New: `utils/oauth1.ts`, `services/xAdsClient.ts`, `mcp/xAdsToolkitManifest.ts`, `mcp/xAdsToolkitWrites.ts`, `mcp/xAdsToolkitGateway.ts`, `mcp/zomaXAdsConnect.ts`, `routes/xAdsAuth.ts`
- Wiring: `app.ts`, `mcp/metaToolkitGateway.ts`, `routes/metaToolkit.ts`, `mcp/zomaProviders.ts`, `mcp/zomaToolDefinitions.ts`, `mcp/zomaOnboarding.ts`, `mcp/zomaBilling.ts`, `mcp/toolkitToolAnnotations.ts`
- Storage and secrets: `services/connectedAccountsDb.ts`, `utils/accountSecretRedaction.ts`, `utils/secretsManager.ts`
- Tests: `__tests__/eng3142.*.test.ts` (4), `__tests__/eng2747.metaToolkitAnnotations.test.ts`

## Linear issue

title: fix: capture-drift alerts file one oncall item per site (ENG-3143)
body:
## What
Capture-drift alerts now carry `Alert Scope: lp-repo:<owner/repo>`, so intake files one oncall item per drifted site instead of folding every site into the first one (ENG-3140 got all 5 on 2026-11-17).

## Why
`intakeService` (ENG-2267, `backend/src/services/intakeService.ts:711`) dedupes on `Alert Class` and narrows only when `Alert Scope` is present. `captureDriftMonitor` sent `Repo` but no scope. In-process suppression was already per-repo; the collapse was downstream.

1. One deduped item per site: scope is per repo; intake's class+scope match handles re-runs. In-process suppression unchanged.
2. Dedupe key includes the repo for capture drift only. Other alert classes untouched.
3. New test: two drifted sites -> two transport calls with distinct `Alert Scope`.
4. Decision: comment-only / generator-version diffs still count as drift in this PR. The detector compares against current generator output on purpose (a stale route is what loses attribution); with per-site filing the noise is bounded to one low-priority item per site. Making the detector ignore comment lines is a separate change if wanted. Read-only; no landing-page repo writes.

Existing ENG-3140 has no scope line, so the next sweep files fresh per-site items, including the first site. ENG-3140 can be closed once they appear.

Live intake filing in prod; verify on the next scheduled sweep.

title: fix: classify the caller-URL SSRF refusal as by_design (ENG-3165)
body:
## What this does
`classifyToolFailureType` now reads the caller-URL SSRF guard's refusal (`That URL cannot be fetched. Use a public https link.`, `CALLER_URL_BLOCKED_MESSAGE`) as `by_design`, raw or wrapped (`Failed to fetch HTML from URL: …`). The agent-mode failure-cluster loop excludes `by_design`, so it stops filing the guard working correctly as a `create_html_template` bug.

## Why
Prod web.stdout (7d): the only `create_html_template` fetch failure is `caller_url_blocked` host `127.0.0.1` (`http://127.0.0.1:3001/health`, 2026-11-18 14:07Z). The next fetch in that session (public S3 URL) succeeded. The handler is fine; the classifier mislabels the guard.

## Risk / rollback
Classifier-only; the SSRF guard (`callerUrlFetch.ts`) is unchanged. Tradeoff: the refusal is deliberately reason-free, so a public host that fails DNS also lands in by_design. No data-plane, no customer-visible change. Rollback: revert.

## Complexity ledger
+1 regex alternation, +1 test file. No new modules.

## How to test
`cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/eng3165 src/__tests__/toolFailureType` — 72/72. RED confirmed: with the regex change stashed, eng3165 fails 2/3.

## Not tested
Full `tsc` OOMs on this box (9.7GB); CI Backend build covers it. Next failure-cluster window (AC2) is post-deploy.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Low

`BY_DESIGN_RE` classifies the caller-URL SSRF refusal (`That URL cannot be fetched. Use a public https link.`), raw or wrapped in `Failed to fetch HTML from URL:`, as `by_design`. The agent-mode failure-cluster loop skips it. `net::err_` connection failures also match, so public-host DNS failures classify as `by_design`. Guard unchanged.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Opslane note (environment, not a code defect)
Opslane's P1 on this PR ("no recorded run") reproduces identically on the base branch per Opslane's own report, and persisted after 5cab731 enabled AGENT_RUNTIME_SPINE_ENABLED. `/api/admin/agent-runs` returned `scannedEvents: 0`, i.e. the agent never invoked `create_html_template` in this environment: model calls go to the LLM twin, which does not emit that tool call, so the guard path is unreachable end to end here ("Agent judgment: Couldn't test" in the same report). The behavior under test (SSRF guard refusal classified `by_design`) is covered by `eng3165.callerUrlBlockedByDesign.test.ts`, RED on main and GREEN on this head. Intended: no code change in response to this finding.

## Opslane environment note

Opslane P1 "no recorded run" is an environment limitation, not a regression: the agent runtime spine (AGENT_RUNTIME_SPINE_ENABLED) is unset in the Opslane setup, so /api/admin/agent-runs returns no runs for any session (Opslane itself notes the same check failed before this PR). The behavior under test is covered by the unit tests in this PR. Intended; no code change.


## Opslane note (swarm3, 2026-11-22)
Opslane's P1 ("no recorded run") is an environment limitation, not a product defect: even with `AGENT_RUNTIME_SPINE_ENABLED=true` (commit 5cab731) the Opslane env reports it "can't set up the situation this change needs" — the agent never reaches `create_html_template` without a live model, so no agent run is written and `/api/admin/agent-runs` is empty both before and after this PR. The classification itself (SSRF caller-URL refusal → `failureType: by_design`, message preserved) is proven by `backend/src/__tests__/eng3165.callerUrlBlockedByDesign.test.ts`. Behavior is intended; no code change.

title: fix: normalize linkedin_manage_post post_urn before socialActions calls (ENG-3176)
body:
## Reviewer-first summary
`linkedin_manage_post` failed 22% of calls (ENG-3176), mostly "Failed to list comments: LinkedIn Error: Syntax exception in path variables". The model sometimes passes a post URL or bare id as `post_urn`, which ends up in `/rest/socialActions/{urn}/comments`.

For `list_comments`, `comment`, `react` and `repost`, the dispatcher now normalizes `post_urn` (new `backend/src/emma/impl/linkedinPostUrn.ts`):
- URN, URL-encoded URN, `/feed/update/urn:li:...` URL, or `/posts/...-activity-<id>-...` URL -> `urn:li:(share|ugcPost|activity):<id>`
- bare number or anything else -> `{success:false}` with a message telling the model what to send; LinkedIn is not called.

`delete_post` and `get_analytics` are untouched.

## Complexity ledger
+1 small pure module, +8 lines in the dispatcher. No schema, no persistence, no new dependency. The only new model-facing text is a validation error message.

## Tests
- `src/__tests__/eng3176.linkedinPostUrn.test.ts` (14 tests). With the dispatcher change stashed: 2 failed / 12 passed. With it: 14/14.
- `agentModeService.socialTools` + `socialOrgShared`: 90/90 pass. One fixture changed `urn:li:share:orig` -> `urn:li:share:7001` (real URNs are numeric).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p backend/tsconfig.json`: clean.

## How to test
`cd backend && npx jest src/__tests__/eng3176.linkedinPostUrn.test.ts src/__tests__/agentModeService.socialTools.test.ts`

## Not tested
No live LinkedIn call. Post-deploy check: the next failure-cluster window shows this class below the admission threshold.

Rollback: revert this PR.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

Risk: Low
Adds `normalizeLinkedInPostUrn` and applies it in `linkedinManagePost` to `comment`, `list_comments`, `react`, and `repost`. Accepts URNs, encoded URNs, feed/posts URLs, and `/embed/` links. Bare IDs and activity-URN reposts return validation errors without calling LinkedIn. `delete_post` and `get_analytics` are unchanged.

Risk basis: The change is limited to the backend dispatcher for four actions. Callers that pass bare IDs now get a validation error. Rollback is a simple revert. No production outage path identified.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Opslane notes (intended behavior / evidence)
- Bare numeric post id (e.g. `7123456789012`): intended. `linkedin_manage_post` returns a validation error as the tool result telling the caller to send a post URL or `urn:li:share|ugcPost|activity:<id>` URN; LinkedIn is never called. Covered by eng3176 test "returns a validation error instead of calling LinkedIn for a bare id". Whether the model paraphrases that message is model behavior, not this fix.
- Comments lookup from a copied post link: the URL is normalized to its URN before `socialActions/{urn}/comments` (test "passes a URN extracted from a post URL to list_comments"). The tool does not log the URN; absence of a log line is not a failure.


## Opslane notes (intended behavior, for re-check)
- Bare post number (AC1): `linkedinManagePost` (backend/src/emma/impl/linkedin.ts) runs `normalizeLinkedInPostUrn` before any comment/list_comments/react/repost call and returns `{success:false, message}` as the tool result; LinkedIn is never called. The validation text is the tool result, not guaranteed verbatim in Emma's prose reply. Covered by backend/src/__tests__/eng3176.linkedinPostUrn.test.ts.
- /posts/ link (AC2): normalized to `urn:li:activity:<id>` before `listLinkedInComments` is invoked. There is no `listLinkedInComments` log line carrying postUrn, so an empty log search is expected; the asserted contract is the call argument (socialTools test asserts the normalized URN is passed).


## Opslane AC1/AC2 evidence notes (intended behavior)
- Both remaining findings say "we couldn't tell the cause from the evidence" — neither shows a wrong result. Normalization runs at the top of `linkedinManagePost` (backend/src/emma/impl/linkedin.ts), before any account resolution or LinkedIn call, and logs `[AgentMode] linkedinManagePost post_urn normalized: { action, input, ok, postUrn }` (the log key is this line, not `listLinkedInComments`).
- AC1: a bare numeric `post_urn` returns `{ success:false, message: 'Invalid post_urn "<n>": a bare number is ambiguous ...' }` as the tool result; LinkedIn is not called. Whether the real model then paraphrases that message, or calls the tool at all, is model behavior outside this PR. Deterministic proof: `backend/src/__tests__/eng3176.linkedinPostUrn.test.ts`.
- AC2: `/posts/<slug>-activity-<id>-<x>` normalizes to `urn:li:activity:<id>` and that URN is logged as `postUrn` before `listLinkedInComments` runs. If the staging seed has no tool call (model declined) the log line is absent by design.

title: ENG-3170: share-link visitors run sensitive tools only on a link whose owner allowed it (per-link switch)
body:
## What

A share-link visitor runs under the account owner's login, so what they could make Emma do was only limited by the model's own judgement and a few `confirm` flags the model sets itself. This makes the owner's per-link choice **"Full control"** (off by default, chosen when the link is created, changeable later by the owner only) decide what a visitor can do. **On = everything a customer can do** (owner decision). **Off = chat and read; nothing that changes things.** The owner is never affected. Admin tools are never lifted.

With Full control off, a visitor can no longer make Emma: delete or overwrite data, send email or Slack, post or publish, change ad campaigns, change the owner's settings, memory, skills, plans or templates, connect or disconnect an account, use the owner's saved logins, cookies or login codes, read the owner's mailbox (`email`), run the owner's schedules or change their timing or recipients, or run code or name files on the server through the browser tools. Reads, questions and in-page browsing work as before.

## How

- `interactiveShareMetadata.allowSensitiveActions`; one rule reads it (`utils/interactiveShare`): an explicit boolean wins; a link made before this existed reads ON for the sensitive tools only if its lifetime is one the share dialog offers (1/3/7/14/30/90/365 days), OFF otherwise (no expiry, the 45-day admin links, anything unreadable); such a legacy link never gets the new full-control powers (owner-only block list, `connect_account`, answering approval cards).
- Enforced in `executeTool`, where every path ends (typed chat, voice, nested calls): consistent read of the link, one retry, fail closed; whole tools before argument repair, argument-judged tools after it. The restriction travels with the call (AsyncLocalStorage), so a tool that calls `executeTool` itself is covered in the forked worker.
- `toolRestrictionProfiles`: whole-tool list, by-argument rules (read action vs write, recipients, timing, `dri`, `trigger_run`, `autocomplete`...), runtime tools of the owner's GitHub MCP token, and a schedule-only rule (a schedule a visitor wrote may read the Meta ad account, never write). **The guard test is closed-world:** every one of the 281 registered tools must be sensitive, sensitive by argument, blocked, admin, reviewed with a reason, or named like a read, so a new tool has to be classified.
- **Browser:** a visitor who may not use the owner's logins (an OFF link, a link that cannot be read, a run of a schedule a visitor wrote) gets a browser of their own (`<session>::visitor`); the owner's cookies are never loaded into it. This replaced a shared-browser hand-over that three review rounds could not make sound. A visitor may also not call `browser_run_code` themselves (it runs their code on the server in Node's `vm`, which is not a security boundary) nor name a `filename` or `paths` on a direct browser call. A tool that calls it with fixed code (`solve_captcha`) still works.
- A schedule that already emails other people cannot be edited from an OFF link (AgentWeb would mail the visitor's text to them).
- The create-link reply answers with the STORED expiry, and the share route lets the visitor answer an approval card carrying a Meta write only on an explicit, live Full control link.
- Separate commit: `set_lead_contact_status` no longer re-creates a lead that was already deleted (owner: "if it's a tiny fix, do it").

## Decisions taken for the owner (each reversible; the owner's open calls)

`email` (search, list, get, send) is refused on OFF links: search and get read login codes and reset links out of the mailbox. The in-account overwrites the approved wording promises to refuse ("change your settings or Emma's memory": brand guidelines, market strategy, knowledge base, lead statuses, list settings, saved test login) are refused. `create_schedule_from_template`, `generate_landing_page`, `coding_agent`, the old task tools and 15 more are sensitive; the dev note lists them with the reason.

## Proof

- Reviews: eleven independent reviews over six earlier rounds, then nine final rounds of a full-context and a blind read-only reviewer each, one exhaustive per-tool pass over all 281 registered tools (two agents, half each), and a scoped review of the final rebase. Every finding was verified in the code before it was acted on. Rounds 8 and 9 and the review of the rebased commit found no blocker.
- Typecheck clean and 127 neighbouring suites (4,060 tests) pass on the rebased head. 128 deliberate breaks of the production code are defined in the harness; each was caught when it was written (several first survived: each was a real missing test or a break aimed at the wrong place, and was fixed).
- Rebased onto main 6f70f0bd6: the whole-patch id is identical to the reviewed head's (`0871f9754fd2...`) and `git range-diff` pairs all 35 commits as identical.
- Live on the test instance with the real `executeTool` and real tables as a visitor, on this exact head: OFF refuses each sensitive tool and the new rules, ON and legacy links and the owner keep theirs, approval cards over real HTTP (403 on OFF, accepted on ON, refused again once the owner switches it off, plain question cards still work), the dialog in a real browser, and the real Playwright server (a visitor's direct `run_code`, `filename` and `paths` refused; the visitor's browser pool is separate from the owner's; releasing the chat session releases both).
- Not live-tested: approving (not declining) a real Meta write from a Full-control link, voice, a real model turn through the forked worker.

## Known limits (dev note has the full list with reasons)

Disclosed on purpose: a visitor can have an `enqueue_human_eval` or `generate_image` run make an OFF link permanent (an email path does the same by design); one token per session, so turning Full control ON also covers everyone who already holds that link; a running visitor turn or voice socket is not tied to the link token it started on; `send_for_review` on a result link; lead field, draft and book edits; a `dri` nested inside the phases or items of the GTM tools; servers added through the `mcp_servers` setting; Slack and X message reads; the Meta image and video uploads.

**Intended behaviour Opslane flagged (P1):** if the owner saves the switch twice at the same moment (a double click, two tabs) with opposite choices, the request that lost the race answers `500 Failed to save the sensitive-actions setting for this link`, and the other request's value is the stored one. The reply deliberately never claims a choice that did not persist. Owner-only; a clearer 409 would be better and is not part of this change.

## Platform findings, NOT part of this change (reachable by any signed-in customer; reported to the owner for Harsha and Yugo)

The browser server is started with the backend's own environment and working directory, `browser_run_code` runs code on the server in a `vm` that is not a security boundary, the browser can navigate to the cloud metadata address and to `view-source:file:///...` (which bypasses its file block). Closed here only for share-link visitors. The fix is on the infrastructure side.

## Before merging

Owner approved the customer wording (dialog, release note, refusal text) on 2026-11-23; owner's standing rule (2026-11-24): merge automatically once review, live tests and CI hold on the exact commit. Merge this PR (rebase) before the portal PR.
