title: ENG-2840: memory readers return every memory up to a bound instead of one page; memory tool bodies move to one module (W2-1)
body:
## Summary

ENG-2840 wave 2, slice W2-1. No new tool, route, schema, index or stored attribute. It repairs what Emma and the Settings memory screens read, and moves the four memory tool bodies into one module so the MCP memory tools of the next slice can share one set of guards.

**The bug.** A memory row carries a 1,536-number embedding, about 17 KB, and one DynamoDB query page holds at most 1 MB, so one page is 56 to 60 rows. `accountMemoryDb.getUserMemories` returned after the first page that held any ordinary row, and `orgMemoryDb.getOrgMemories` was one unpaged query. Memory ids are ULIDs and the query reads oldest first, so an account with more memories than one page showed only its **oldest** ~56, to Emma's prompt and to the Settings memory tabs alike. Measured on prod on 2026-11-23: 14 of 52 accounts with memories (and 1 org) were past one page; the largest stores 277 and one page returned 56. Every memory saved after the first page was invisible.

## What changes

- `services/db.ts`: both readers take a fourth argument `options: { maxRows?, newestFirst?, omitEmbeddings? }`. **A call with a `limit` behaves exactly as before.** A call without one follows the cursor until the rows run out or `maxRows` is reached.
  - The prompt loader (`agentModeService`) is **unchanged** and gets the defaults: the newest 200 rows (`MEMORY_READ_MAX_ROWS_PROMPT`), embeddings included because it ranks by them. A test now pins that the loader passes no options.
  - `GET /api/memory` and `GET /api/org/:orgId/memory` read the **newest** rows up to 1,000 and return them **oldest first** as before (screen order unchanged; if an account ever held more than 1,000, the oldest are left out, never the newest). They **do not fetch the embedding vectors**: the read names every other attribute (a DynamoDB projection, about 40 of every 45 KB of a row on the wire). The exact expressions were checked against the real service on the account table and the category index of both tables (seven attributes back, no vector). A category-filtered list is returned as read (its index sorts by category, not time).
  - The account reader keeps its structured-learning skipping and its jump over that id range (both directions are now tested); the page budget grows with the bound (17 pages for 200 rows, 44 for 1,000, 10 for a `limit` call); it still fails closed on a page that is not a list, on an item that is not a row at all (not an object, no string id), and on any row when the read has a `limit` (`getRecentMemories` and limited callers are exactly as before). **One change, found by Opslane on `f459c4b0c`:** the read without a `limit` (the prompt loader and the list screens) now reaches rows far past the first page, so a row that has an id but no text `content` is skipped and logged (`[memory] account memory read skipped N row(s) without text content, ids ...`) instead of failing the whole list (500) and dropping every memory from the Emma prompt for that account. Checked on prod on 2026-11-23: no such row exists today. The org reader still validates no rows (it never did; one odd row must not take down an org list or every member's prompt). The bound is clamped (not a number, zero or negative: the default; a fraction rounds down, never below 1). A read that stops at its bound logs `there may be more rows stored` (DynamoDB returns a cursor whenever the limit was used up, even when nothing is left).
  - `deleteMemory` (both tables) resolves `true` when a row was deleted and `false` when there was none.
  - `setMemoryEmbedding` (both tables) is now conditional on the row existing: a memory deleted while its embedding was being backfilled used to come back as a row with no content, which makes the account reader refuse the whole list.
- `emma/impl/memory.ts` (new): the four memory tool bodies, moved out of `emma/tools.ts`. `services/db` and `utils/embeddings` stay lazy (module-isolation test). `utils/memoryCategories.ts` is the one category list (the save tools' schema enum uses it).
- Defects fixed on the way, each with a test that fails on the old behaviour:
  - an invalid category was embedded (and the embedding billed to the caller's cap) before the database layer refused it; arguments are now checked first. **Found by Opslane on `f459c4b0c` for the HTTP routes too:** `POST /api/memory` and `POST /api/org/:orgId/memory` embedded, billed, then were refused by `addMemory` for an invalid category, a blank content or a content over 2,000 characters. Both routes now run the same checks (`utils/memorySaveGuard.ts`, same messages, same 400) before the embedding is requested; a test pins that its messages equal `addMemory`'s;
  - whitespace-only content over 2,000 characters split into nothing and answered `success: true` with no row saved;
  - content that was not text threw after the earlier rows were saved, so a retry saved them twice;
  - the 8,000-character limit was enforced only by the agent-mode tool schema; it is now enforced in the module too, so a caller that skips that schema cannot write a larger memory;
  - a delete of an id that does not exist answered "deleted";
  - the `delete_org_memory` description said only owners can delete; owners and admins can (`org:configure`).

## What an end user sees

- **Emma:** for an account past one page, her memory context now includes the newer memories as well (still the top 20 by relevance). Nothing changes for an account with 56 or fewer memories.
- **Settings > Memory and the org memory tab:** an account past one page sees all its memories (up to 1,000) instead of the first ~56. The tabs have no pagination, so it is one longer list. The response is much smaller per row because the vectors are not fetched.
- **Emma's save and delete memory tools:** the same answers, except the edge cases above, which are now an error or "not found" instead of a false success.
- Unchanged on purpose: no cap on how many memories an account may save (the MCP write cap belongs to the next slice); `DELETE /api/memory/:id` and `DELETE /api/org/:orgId/memory/:id` still answer success for a missing id (the portal behaves as today).

## Proof

- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0 on the final head.
- **Final head (`083847a2c`): 110 test files that touch the changed modules (every test referencing the memory db objects, memory tools, content limits, categories or read bounds; all of `emma/impl/__tests__`; the tool-gate wiring and public-inventory tests): 110 suites, 2,258 tests passed.** The pre-push hook on the pushed head: 23 related suites passed.
- New tests: reader paging and bounds (including the prod shape, 277 rows in pages of 56, the page-budget numbers 17 / 44 / 10, both learning-range jump directions, the projection on every query shape, the clamp, the warnings, org row validation, the conditional backfill), the memory module (guards unchanged plus each fix), the four registered tools through the registry, both list routes (order, bound, category), module isolation, and that the prompt loader passes no options.
- Deliberate-breakage passes: 95 mutants in four passes (old stop rule, no per-page `Limit`, default bound removed, order flipped, vectors kept or dropped from the wrong reads, page budget fixed, org reader one page, delete always true, `ReturnValues` dropped, every new check removed, org id from an argument, permission check removed, list options dropped from a route, each tool wired to the wrong body, ascending jump wrong, org `limit` direction, projection attributes, clamp, warnings, row validation, conditional backfill, loader options). The fourth pass covers the skip rule (never skips, skips for limit reads, skips non-rows, no record, no warning on either exit), both routes' check order and the guard's three checks and messages. All 95 killed, each by a test that names the behaviour; every file restored byte-identical. Five mutants survived their first run and each led to a test or a retargeted mutant: a tool wired to the wrong body (no test ran the registered tool), the early return in the ascending jump branch, the org reader warning when its rows ran out, the skipped-row warning on the jump exit, and a mutant of mine that hit an unrelated function.
- Two assertions in `accountMemory.test.ts` pinned the old argument list of `GET /api/memory`; they now pin the new list read. The contract changed on purpose.
- **Opslane on `f459c4b0c` reported two problems; both are fixed on `083847a2c`** (see above): P1 a content-less account row past the first page broke the Settings list and Emma's memory; P2 a refused save was still billed an embedding. It also lists three agent problems that exist on `main` and do not block the merge (a repeated `save_memory` writes twice; a model failure right after a save answers 503); they are not touched here.
- **Two independent reviews, both SHIP WITH NITS, neither with a HIGH.** Review 1 (head `fea1ec85b`) found: the list routes silently kept the oldest 1,000 (now the newest, logged); the ascending learning-range jump and the org `limit` direction were untested (now tested); the vectors were fetched then discarded (now a projection, wire size and parse cost corrected in the dev note); the embedding backfill could resurrect a deleted memory (now conditional); missing content answered the wrong message (restored); the save tools' enum is now the shared list; a test pins that the loader passes no options. Review 2 (head `3f0d6ba92`) found: one data-dependent risk (an org row without `content` would now fail a whole read), which I checked on prod (no row in either table lacks a string `content` or `memoryId`) and removed by dropping the org row validation I had added; a warning that was misleading at exactly the bound; a surviving mutant in the jump branch and an untested early return (tested); the hand-kept projection lists (a test now compares them with what `addMemory` stores); the honest trade-off for the largest account (stated below); and lint nits. The changes since review 2 add no guard, write path or tenant boundary: they revert the org validation to the old behaviour, adjust edge cases and wording, and add tests, so I did not ask for a third review then. The Opslane fixes above change a guard (fail-closed becomes skip-and-log on one read path), so the delta `f459c4b0c..083847a2c` gets its own fresh independent review (result in a comment below).

## Limits, stated

- The prompt loader reads at most the newest 200 rows. An account above that keeps its memories, but Emma ranks among the newest 200 only: for the largest account today (277 rows) facts 1 to 77 stay out of her prompt, where before 221 of 277 did (the old reader returned one page of 56 rows; measured on prod after the merge). It costs about four sequential queries per agent turn for that account, against one before.
- A 200-row read for the prompt is about 3.4 MB stored and about 9 MB of DynamoDB JSON on the wire for an account with an embedding on every row (the largest account today is 277 rows). The parse (about 100 ms) runs in the forked generation worker (the main generation path), not on the API event loop, once per turn. Only 16 of 2,411 rows lacked an embedding on 2026-11-23, so the backfill the loader does for them stays negligible.
- A read through an eventually consistent index can lag a save made a moment earlier.
- A write or embedding failure after some chunks of a split save are written still leaves those rows (a retry would duplicate them); only the non-text case was fixed here.
- Rollback is a revert of the PR (code only; no data, schema or index changed).

## After deploy

Watch the deploy; check the API; run a Haiku and a Sonnet chat on the owner's account that saves a memory, finds it, and deletes it (one row written and removed); compare the number of memories Emma sees for the largest account before and after.

title: ENG-2840 W2-2: memory tools over MCP (save, delete, list; org writes behind memory:org), mint-time rate check, batch counting
body:
## Summary

ENG-2840 wave 2, slice W2-2 (plan v3, section 3.4 to 3.6). Outside agents (the Hermes agents: Yugo, Hue, Remy) can now keep Emma's memory over MCP: **save, delete and list** the user's own memories, and, behind a new opt-in scope, **save and delete the organization's memories**. No table, index, stored attribute, backfill or migration (the plan's data-plane rule: none in this slice).

Builds on W2-1 (#4225, live): the four memory tool bodies already live in `emma/impl/memory.ts`, and both readers return everything up to a bound. This slice puts the same bodies on the MCP server, with what an open MCP path needs.

## What an outside agent gets

| Tool | Scope needed | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `save_memory`, `delete_memory` | default (`tools:execute`) | the user's own memory; OAuth clients may use them |
| `list_memories` (new) | default (`tools:read`) | `scope: "user"` (default) or `"org"`, `category`, `limit` 1 to 50 (default 20), `cursor`; newest first; id, category, content and dates, never embeddings |
| `save_org_memory`, `delete_org_memory` | **`memory:org`** (new opt-in scope) **and an `aw_` key** (`apiKeyOnly`) | org memory goes into EVERY member's Emma prompt; OAuth and anonymous callers are refused; `tools:execute` does not imply the scope; a delegated (admin-as-customer) session cannot mint a key with it |

Reading org memory (`list_memories`, scope `org`) needs no opt-in scope: any member may read what Emma already shows them. Delete on the org needs `org:configure` (owners and admins), as in Emma's own tool; any org member's key holding `memory:org` may save. A key holding `memory:org` is offered `list_memories` in `tools/list` only when it can also call it (`tools:read` or `tools:execute`).

## What changes

- `mcp/server/memoryTools.ts` (new): the five tools, in process on the shared module, so Emma's guards apply unchanged (identity from the key, the org from the user record, memory off, no org, org memory off, the role check on delete, 2,000-character split and 8,000 limit, ads-learning rows never deleted or listed). Added for the MCP path:
  - the MCP path validates nothing against the input schema, so each handler checks its own arguments, and **an argument that is not an input of the tool is refused by name** ("orgId is not an input of save_org_memory"). (The MCP server itself drops `userId`, `sessionId` and `llmModel` before any tool sees them, so those run as the caller; tested.)
  - **a cap of 200 stored memories per account and per org** on writes made here; a split save counts its rows. An account already above 200 keeps everything and is refused new saves until it deletes (prod: two accounts above 200, 277 and 236).
  - **each save runs under a lock** for the account (the org when the caller has one), in arrival order, so the cap and the duplicate check cannot interleave with a write, **including the members of one JSON-RPC batch and a retry sent at the same instant**. Per server process: with several instances the cap is approximate across them.
  - **an exact duplicate** (same category, same text ignoring surrounding whitespace; for a long split text, every part already stored) is not written again and costs no embedding; the answer says `saved: false, duplicate: true` and names the existing id(s).
  - `list_memories` pages by memory id over the bounded newest-1,000 read the Settings screens make, so a cursor can only ever select rows of the caller's own account or org.
- `emma/impl/memory.ts`: `saveAccountMemory` / `saveOrgMemory` take an optional `gate`, called after the shared guards and argument checks and before anything is embedded or written. Emma's own tools pass none, so their behaviour and order of checks are unchanged (tested).
- `services/db.ts`: new `consistentRead` option on `getUserMemories` / `getOrgMemories`: `ConsistentRead: true` on a TABLE read only (an index cannot be read consistently). The MCP tools use it (and filter a category in code); nothing else passes it.
- `publicResponseSanitizer.ts`: the five memory tools are exempt from the public-response sanitizer. It strips internal id fields from JSON-looking text in tool results for outside callers, so a memory whose text is a JSON object with an `apiKeyId` field came back over MCP altered (found by Opslane). A memory is the caller's own text.
- `apiKeyScopes.ts`, `routes/agentApi.ts`, `toolDiscovery.ts`: the `memory:org` scope, grantable at key creation (refused from a delegated session), and listed in `tools/list` for a key that holds it.
- Classification: `toolAnnotationPolicy.ts`, `agentExecutionTools.ts`, the public inventory snapshot (exactly these five tools added).
- Fixes found on the way (small, in the plan or found in review):
  - `POST /api/agent/api-keys` validated nothing about `rateLimitPerMin`, and the limiter trusts it: a key minted with a huge, negative or text rate had no effective limit (and `null` was stored, which blocked the key for good). It must now be a whole number from 1 to 600 (missing or null: the default 60). **No existing key is touched** (prod: 66 keys, 61 at 60 and 5 at 10). A broker that mints with a string, a fraction or a rate outside 1 to 600 now gets a 400.
  - The limiter counted HTTP requests, so a JSON-RPC batch of 100 calls cost one count. The other members are now charged, for aw_ keys and OAuth users, **when the batch is about to be served**: one that does not fit in what is left is refused whole (429) before any member runs, while a batch answered 404 (expired session), 403 or 503 costs only its own request (found by Opslane: charged earlier, a client that reconnected after a 404 was refused for a minute). Clients that send batches larger than their allowance (over 60 for an OAuth user, over 10 for the five prod keys at 10 a minute) will now see a 429. `req.body` is parsed before the limiter in production (`app.post("/mcp", express.json(), validateMcpAccessToken, ...)`).
  - A tool name in a `tools/call` that is not text (an object with a hostile `toString`) made the scope check throw inside an async handler and left the request hanging (any authenticated key could do it). It is now an unknown tool, a write.

## What users see

- **Emma's own memory tools, the Settings screens and the agent-mode path: unchanged.**
- An outside agent with a key can now save, list and delete memory; one that tries to write org memory without `memory:org` gets a 403 naming the scope.
- Minting a key with a rate outside 1 to 600, or a batch over the key's per-minute allowance, now gets a refusal instead of silently working.

## Proof

- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0.
- Tests selected by what they reference (289 suites: every test touching the changed modules, the helpers, the gate suites and the classification lists): **6,212 of 6,213 pass.** The one failure, `emmaToolArgContracts.test.ts` ("call_hubspot_api observed shapes", ENG-2792), **fails identically on a clean checkout of `main` (1a211a8b8)**; it is not touched by this change.
- New and extended tests: `memoryTools.test.ts` (unit: registration and scope gating against the real scope functions, argument checks, cap, duplicate including split saves, the lock and concurrent saves, org guards, paging, audit line), `mcp.twoTenantMemory.test.ts` (both directions through the real MCP server, real tools, real db code and the in-memory table, plus 50 concurrent saves, identical concurrent saves, two members at once, JSON-looking memories read back unchanged), `mcp.memoryScopeGate.test.ts` (the HTTP-layer gate against the real registry, which the inventory snapshot cannot pin because it records neither the scope nor `apiKeyOnly`; hostile tool names over HTTP), `mcp.batchRateLimit.test.ts` (through the real `/mcp` route with sessions: a batch is charged when served, not for a 404, 403 or 503, rehydrated sessions, OAuth, a non-numeric allowance), `apiKeyScopes.test.ts`, `agentApi.routes.test.ts`, discovery and search tests, `memory.test.ts` (the gate and its order), `memoryReaders.test.ts` (`consistentRead` on table reads only), `inMemoryDynamo.deleteReturnValues.test.ts`.
- Shared test helpers changed: the in-memory DynamoDB's `delete` now answers `ReturnValues: 'ALL_OLD'` the way DynamoDB does (it always answered `{}`, so every delete that tests existence looked like "not found"); the two-tenant harness gained the memory tables, seeded memories and an OAuth caller. **All suites that use these helpers still pass**, including the wave-1 isolation matrix and the three wave-1 write suites.
- Deliberate-breakage pass: **about 105 mutants** over the final code (each scope and `apiKeyOnly` flag, argument refusal, id checks, the duplicate comparisons including split saves, every cap boundary, consistent read, ordering, cursor, paging, switched-off checks, leaked fields, the gate wiring, the lock on both save tools, grant and delegated refusal, rate boundaries, both limiter call sites, the moved batch charge and its state, discovery and search, tool-name hardening, the sanitizer exemption), run one at a time. All killed, each by a named test, every file restored byte for byte. Survivors found along the way (a trim of stored text, the org delete's id check, the non-numeric allowance guard) each got a test.
- **Four independent reviews and Opslane, every finding fixed in this PR.**
  - Review 1 (first head `33bd70ae3`): SHIP WITH NITS, no HIGH; it confirmed the org write tools cannot be reached without an `aw_` key holding `memory:org` on any path it tried, and found no cross-tenant path. Two mediums, fixed: the cap and duplicate check were not atomic (a batch of 50 saves took an account from 199 to 249), and `memory:org` was described as a wall around org memory when it controls the two tools (a key that may start an Emma agent run reaches Emma's own org-memory tool in that run, as for `email:read` and the Smartlead scopes).
  - Opslane on the same head: nothing at P1 or above, four P2s, all fixed (concurrent identical saves; a `memory:org`-only key offered a tool it was refused; a stale-session batch using up the allowance; JSON-looking memories altered by the sanitizer).
  - Review 2 (head `2594115e5`): SHIP WITH NITS, no HIGH; it re-ran its own probes against the real route and confirmed every earlier finding closed. Found and fixed: a hung embedding held the org lock (no timeout on the embedding call: now bounded to 15 seconds, then the row is saved without one); a split save that failed part-way and was retried duplicated its first parts (a failed split save now removes the parts it wrote; this is in the shared module, so Emma's own save tools get it too); a JSON-RPC `method` that is not text hung the request (a debug log line interpolated it; present since February); test gaps.
  - Opslane on `2594115e5`: one **P1**: at the 200 cap an org member was told to delete memories, and a plain member cannot delete org memory (`org:configure`). The refusal now says an owner or admin must make room when the caller cannot delete, and shows the tool names when they can. Fixed and tested, including through the real server.
  - Review 3 (head `2a9ad9e45`): SHIP WITH NITS, no HIGH or MEDIUM. Fixed: the 15 second embedding bound was per embedding (a split save of seven parts under a fully hung embedding service could hold the lock about 105 seconds), so it is now ONE deadline per save; a timeout value that is not a positive finite number means no bound instead of silently dropping embeddings; the cap refusal told an org owner to `list_memories`, which defaults to the owner's own memories (it now names `scope "org"`); docs that overstated ("no half of a memory is left", "Emma's own tools unchanged"); a test gap (the cleanup finishing before the error). Opslane on `2a9ad9e45`: a fresh run, nothing at P1 or above ("All looks good").
  - Review 4 (the last small change, head `15c7dc658`) and Opslane on that head: see the comments below.

## Limits, stated

- A key holding `memory:org` can put text in front of every member's Emma. That is why the scope is opt-in and key-only; the cap of 200 bounds how much. The scope controls the two TOOLS, not every route to org memory: an outside agent that may call `emma_send_message`, `emma_run_marketing_task` or `emma_create_session` starts an Emma run that has Emma's own `save_org_memory` with no scope check and no cap. Keeping the agent-run tools (`AGENT_EXECUTION_TOOLS`) out of an outside agent's allowlist is the control, and it lives with whoever mints and brokers the key, not in this repo.
- A signed-in OAuth client (third-party marketplace apps included) can write the user's own memory, which Emma reads into her prompt: the plan's documented decision, and a persistent channel for text. Provenance on a row is only `sourceSessionId` or `sourceUserId`.
- Each save and each `list_memories` reads up to the newest 1,000 rows strongly consistently (about 17 KB each; the largest prod account, 277 rows, about 4.7 MB). Both memory tables are pay-per-request.
- Outside this repo: the key broker must request `memory:org` when it mints for an agent that writes org memory; the customer portal's key form cannot grant it today.
- Memory is never deleted by age (TTL off on both tables) and no source attribute is stored.
- Rollback: revert the PR (code only).

## After deploy

Direct MCP checks on prod with the owner's own key (typed by him, never by me), one reversible marker memory on his own account and refusals that write nothing: list, save, list right after, duplicate, a different category, category filter, paging, delete, a refused org write with a default key, a refused unknown argument. The agent-mode path is unchanged, so no Haiku or Sonnet pass is needed.

title: fix(zoma): style the Zoma browser steps and make the ads question one click

## What

Every Zoma browser step (code entry, the "How familiar are you with ads?" question, the Meta and Google account pickers, result pages, billing return, unsubscribe) shares one page helper in `backend/src/routes/zoma.ts`. Its only form rule, `input{width:10rem}`, was written for the activation-code box. It also hit the radio buttons on the ads question, so the page rendered with a wide gap and wrapped labels, and the whole flow looked unstyled.

## Changes

- One shared stylesheet: centred card, Zoma header, real buttons, aligned checkboxes, mobile layout. Palette matches the Zoma weekly email. Inline styles only, so the CSP is unchanged.
- The code box gets its own `code` class instead of styling every input.
- The ads question answers are submit buttons carrying the same `answer` field. One click answers; no radio plus Continue. The server handler is untouched.

## Not changed

- The flow itself (approve, then the question, then Meta). The step comes from ENG-3128 and is Harsha's product call.
- No env, data, billing or auth change. Rollback is a revert.

## Checks

- `npm run typecheck` in `backend/`: exit 0.
- Targeted suites that exercise the Zoma router (10 suites, 328 tests): all pass.
- One test assertion changed (`eng3128`): the radio markup became the button markup. The criterion it protects, that the question shows and posts the same `answer` field, is unchanged.
- Rendered the real pages and checked them in a browser at desktop and phone width (code entry and the question).

Opened as a draft. Not merged.

title: fix(mcp): ENG-2840 W2-4 GTM plan tools work for outside agents; status reports say what was sent
body:
## Summary

ENG-2840 wave 2, slice W2-4. `manage_gtm_plan` and `manage_gtm_items` (the GTM plan tools that outside agents such as Hermes call over MCP) were mostly broken: most actions failed on every call, and the rest succeeded while dropping what the agent sent. This makes them work, and fixes status reports that said "sent" when nothing went out.

No table, index, key, stored attribute or migration changes: a plan is still one row, and every write has the shape the customer portal already writes.

## What was wrong (each read against the route it calls)

- `add_phase` sent `name`; the route wants `title` and answered 400 on every call.
- `update_phase` called `PUT /api/gtm-plan/:planId/phases/:phaseId`, which the router did not have: 404.
- `add_work_items` sent an array to a route that takes one item: 400.
- `update_work_item` forwarded every argument raw: `name` and `due_date` were ignored, and a call with nothing the route reads still answered success after changing only `updatedAt`.
- Plan create and update declared `goals`, `target_audience`, `timeline`, `budget` and `status`; no route reads them, and a status-only update answered success.
- `send_status_report` sent arguments no route reads. Separately, the report functions returned without sending when no recipient option was chosen, when the chosen contact (plan or phase DRI) was not set, and when every email was refused (the error was caught and logged), and the routes, the portal toast and Emma's `send_gtm_status_report` all answered "sent successfully".

## What changed

- **Tools** move to `mcp/server/gtmTools.ts`. Each action has an exact list of inputs; an argument that is not one of them is refused by name, with "Nothing was changed." They still call the routes the portal uses through `mcpFetch`, not Emma's in-process functions: only a route sees the delegation and the share-link restriction claim that `mcpFetch` signs into the self-call token.
- `title` names a phase or item (`name` stays accepted as the old spelling). Dates are real `YYYY-MM-DD` days (or empty to clear), `dri` is an email address (or empty), a work item status is one of `pending`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `skipped`. Titles at most 300 characters, text 5,000.
- `add_work_items` takes 1 to 20 items, validates all of them first (one bad item builds no request), sends them one after the other, and on a failure says which were added and that the rest were not tried.
- A plan's and a phase's status follow their work items, so setting one is refused with that reason. Goals, audience, timeline and budget are refused with "put them in the description".
- **New route** `PUT /api/gtm-plan/:planId/phases/:phaseId` (title, description, dri, dueDate): same ownership checks and write shape as the other phase routes; a phase's status stays derived.
- **Overlapping writes no longer lose data** (Opslane P1 on this PR). Every route that rewrites a plan read the whole plan, changed one phase or item and wrote every phase back, so two overlapping writes overwrote each other: an item reported as added was missing, or a deleted phase came back with its items. This PR makes that reachable (a batch is one write per item, two agent sessions can overlap), so the eight routes the tools call now read the plan consistently and write it only if it still exists and its `updatedAt` is what they read, and a handler whose write lost the race re-reads and runs again (at most 8 attempts, then 409 "nothing was lost, please try again"). A write the SDK resent after losing the answer, whose first copy had been applied, is recognised as our own (the stored plan holds exactly what it meant to write) rather than rerun, so an add is not stored twice. No new stored attribute. The two delete routes did not set `updatedAt`, so no other writer could see a delete: they do now.
- **Status reports** now return `{recipients, sent, failed}` (and `suppressed` when the non-production email guard held a send back: not delivered, so not "sent"); a small pure module turns that into 400 (nobody could be emailed), 502 (every email refused, or the report could not be built) or success with counts. The portal's route and Emma's `sendGTMStatusReport` use it.
- **The three emails escape what a caller wrote.** Plan, phase and work item titles, descriptions, notes, contacts, statuses, the change text and the optional message went into the email HTML as written (29 lines, 32 values, in `gtmPlanNotificationService.ts`); they now go through the shared `escapeHtml` (`emma/impl/shared/htmlEscaping.ts`). The plain-text part and the subject are unchanged, ordinary text renders the same, and markup someone typed on purpose into a note or a message now shows as text. The portal already shows `err.response.data.error`, so the new error bodies read correctly there. The two admin status report routes are a separate admin surface and are not changed.

## Decision: neither GTM tool emails anyone

Found while building this, and confirmed by the independent review: the status report and update emails put what the caller wrote into the HTML of an email from AgentWeb's system sender without escaping it, to addresses stored on the plan (a DRI can be any address the caller sets). The old tools were not clean either (a plan update forwarded a whole `phases` list, a work item update forwarded title, contact and notes), and this change adds phase writes that used to fail, so an agent could plant a link dressed as "reset your password" in a plan for anyone who then sent a report from the portal (it ticks the plan and phase contacts by default) or Emma to mail from AgentWeb's domain. So this PR escapes the templates (above) and also keeps emailing off MCP: `send_status_report` is not an action here, and `update_work_item` takes no `notify_*`, `notification_message`, `notifications` or `message` (each refused by name with the reason). The old `update_work_item` forwarded a guessed `notifications` object to the route (undeclared, but it worked); that is removed.

Emailing over MCP will come in its own later PRs: first two lanes for the shared system email queue (so agent mail can never delay password resets), then an opt-in `gtm:email` key scope with a recipient cap, an hourly budget and an audit line.

This is about these two tools. A key that may call `emma_send_message`, `emma_create_session` or `emma_run_marketing_task` starts an Emma session, and Emma has `send_gtm_status_report`; whether such a session can call it depends on the account having the `gtm-plan` skill (registered in `emma/tools.ts`; not run here). That route is as open as before, and its emails are escaped now.

## Behaviour changes for existing clients

- Failed before, works now: `add_phase` (with `title`, or the old `name`), `update_phase`, `add_work_items`.
- Worked or appeared to, refused now with a message that says what to send: `status` on a phase or plan; `goals`, `target_audience`, `timeline`, `budget` on a plan; an empty `update_work_item` or plan update; camelCase `dueDate` (send `due_date`) and a `phases` list on a plan update; a free-form work item `status` (must be one of the four); a `dri` that is not an email address; both `target_phase_id` and `new_phase_name` on `add_common_items`; extra keys on a common item (only `title` and `description` are added; `id` and `sortOrder` from `get_common_items` are accepted and left out; at most 50); titles over 300 characters and text over 5,000; a due date that is not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` day; `send_status_report` and every notify argument.
- `null` clears an optional text, date or contact, the same as an empty string (agents send it to clear a field; the old tool passed it through, and an Opslane P2 caught my first version refusing it). A required title still refuses it.
- `due_date` on a work item is no longer ignored. `get_common_items` still accepts the `plan_id` its old schema asked for. Titles are stored trimmed.
- Deleting a phase or item now sets the plan's `updatedAt`; a write that keeps losing to others answers 409 where it used to overwrite silently.
- Two overlapping creates of the same item now both store (neither overwrites the other); before, one often vanished by accident.
- Marking a work item completed still adds a reaction in Slack when the item carries an agent session and the token is set (unchanged, not an email).

## Proof

- `mcp.manageGtm.writes.test.ts` sends every action through the real path (MCP client, MCP server, tool, `mcpFetch`, the real Express app, the in-memory DynamoDB) and reads the stored plan back, with a second tenant that cannot read, change or delete the first tenant's plan, and the refusals for anything that would email. Run against the previous tool code the same file fails 19 of its 28 tests.
- `gtmTools.test.ts` pins the request each action builds, every refusal, the exact limits and the batch failure report. Route, service and outcome tests cover the report results and the new route.
- Mutation pass: about 190 mutants on the new code (tool arguments and refusals, the routes, the outcome function, the counters, each of the 29 escape sites, the overlapping-write guard at each of its eight sites, the lost-answer recovery), all killed except two equivalent ones (a byte order mark is already excluded by the whitespace class; recovering a scalar write too would also be correct, since its rerun is idempotent). Where a mutant survived at first, it got a test.
- Typecheck exit 0. Wide run over every test touching the changed modules: 3,979 of 3,980 pass in 192 suites; the one failure is the HubSpot ENG-2792 test that is red on a clean main.
- The inventory fixture changes for these two tools only.
- `gtmPlan.concurrentWrites.test.ts` (46 tests) makes two requests read the plan before either writes, for every pair the tools can produce in both orders, and also covers a lost answer after an applied write (stored once, answered with the stored plan, notifications once), a competitor that landed the same phases under its own stamp (still a conflict), a failing check of our own write (falls back to a rerun), a plan deleted mid-write (404, no row left behind), consistent reads and the exact 409; 45 of 46 fail on the previous routes (items lost, a deleted phase back). The exact request shapes with the final condition text were also run against the real dev `AW-GTMPlan` table with throwaway rows (accepted; a stale write fails with `ConditionalCheckFailedException`; a write to a missing plan fails and creates no row), and the lost-answer case against a DynamoDB emulator with the real SDK and a proxy that drops the answer after the commit.
- Four independent reviews, each by a reviewer who had not seen the work, each on a `git archive` copy, all SHIP WITH NITS with no HIGH: (1) the tools and routes, whose MEDIUM was that the emails put caller text into HTML unescaped and this change newly lets an agent write phase text (hence the escaping here); (2) everything changed since; (3) the overlapping-write guard, whose two MEDIUMs were that the tests pinned only one of the eight guards and that an SDK resend after a lost answer would store an add twice (both fixed: tests in both orders for every route, and the recovery check); (4) the recovery and hardening, whose findings were test gaps (what a recovered write answers, the stamp comparison), a failing recovery read becoming a 500 (now a rerun), and one residual that is documented. Every finding was fixed in this PR with a test or is stated as a limit in the note.

## Limits

- Not guarded: the attachment and start-session routes, the agent-mode hooks that mark a linked work item at the start and end of a turn, the Slack session writers, Emma's in-process plan functions and the admin routes still write a plan without the check; a `phases` list sent in a plan update (the portal's whole-list rewrite) is guarded but replays the caller's list. `updatedAt` has millisecond resolution and comes from each server's clock.
- The work item update route still ignores a failed notification email on purpose; the tool no longer sends any.
- The customer portal shows a fixed "sent successfully" toast on any 2xx, so a partial send ("sent to 2 of 3") reads as full success there; 400 and 502 show the new message. That is the customer-portal repo.
- Pre-existing and unrelated: `emmaToolArgContracts.test.ts` (HubSpot, ENG-2792) is red on a clean main.

## After deploy

Haiku and Sonnet in agent mode check Emma's own status report now answers honestly (no recipient chosen); the owner runs `w24_live_check.cjs` with his own key against the real MCP endpoint (creates one `ZZ-W24-LIVE-CHECK` plan on his own account, checks every action and refusal, deletes the plan).

title: feat(zoma): LinkedIn Ads toolkit, dark behind ZOMA_LINKEDIN_ADS_ENABLED (read / true)
body:
## What

LinkedIn Ads as the fourth Zoma ad platform (Meta, Google and X exist), reads and writes, **off by default**. Built to the Google and X pattern and reusing Emma's LinkedIn service. Related: ENG-2818 (the LinkedIn Standard tier upgrade). Lands **dark** before the Nov 25 end-of-day feature freeze, at Manan's direction (2026-11-24). Nothing is on in production: see "Merge and rollout".

## One flag, three states

`ZOMA_LINKEDIN_ADS_ENABLED` (strict, case-sensitive):
- unset or anything else: off. Not listed, routed, offered in `zoma_status`, or reachable through its connect routes. Everything else behaves as before (tested; the served agent guide and the flag-off routes are byte-identical to main).
- `read`: `linkedin_ads_read`, the Zoma connect pages, the `zoma_status` block and reporting. `linkedin_ads_write` is not listed and is refused before the scope check and paywall. Consent asks only for read scopes (plus, on a reconnect, scopes the user already granted).
- `true`: full, adds `linkedin_ads_write`.

One variable on purpose: the prod environment has about 18 characters of room left.

## Safety design

- Writes: preview token (15 min, single use) then confirm, applied once, then an independent read-back reported as CONFIRMED, MISMATCH or UNCONFIRMED. Anything unexpected is UNCONFIRMED; a failure carrying an `errorType` (the service's own read-back) is never reported as "nothing changed".
- Every create is DRAFT with explicit values; a request carrying any `status` is refused. Zoma never relies on Emma's service defaults (ACTIVE groups and creatives, 2.00 USD unit cost).
- ACTIVATE is checked against the budget it unlocks, and every budget must be in the account's own currency. Non-string `action` or `entity_type` values are refused before anything coerces them.
- Spend ceiling: `LINKEDIN_ADS_TOOLKIT_SPEND_CEILING` (JSON by currency, micros). **Unset means a built-in default: USD only, 50.00 a day, 2x change ratio, total (lifetime) budget capped at 30x the daily limit (1,500); other currencies are refused.** A stored budget that exists but cannot be read refuses; decreases are never refused. This differs from Google and X, where unset means no limit. **The numbers need Harsha's confirmation.**
- Previews echo every value that will be sent (targeting facet values, landing page, text, image or post URN), with third-party strings flattened to one line and truncated; creative PAUSE and ACTIVATE show the stored content (post text is fetched, or ACTIVATE is refused) and the whole content is bound into the preview token. A text ad's preview shows the final URL with the utm parameters our service adds.
- 403 'not configured to access the advertiser account' becomes a clear customer message. Only adAnalytics reads are confirmed by LinkedIn to work for accounts not listed in the app; other reads are untested for unlisted accounts.
- Tokens are stored exactly like the existing linkedin_ads, Meta and Google accounts (plain config values, redacted from every response). No new encryption layer.

## Connect flow

Zoma pages, no new redirect URI: the portal callback forwards a signed state carrying a `zoma` claim (signature verified, never an unsigned parameter), and the Zoma routes verify signature and expiry again and bind the user. The page never auto-connects: it shows the **full email** of the Zoma account being connected and an explicit Connect button (a masked email can match another account on the same mail domain). A reconnect never replaces a stored row with a narrower grant, unless the stored token is dead. If a usable connection already holds the read scopes, no link is minted.

## Changes outside the new files

- Portal `routes/linkedInAdsAuth.ts`: finalize and connect extracted into `services/linkedInAdsOAuthFinalize.ts`, same behaviour for the portal. Intended differences: the error handlers (and the profile-lookup warning) log only a message (the raw AxiosError carried `client_secret` and `code`); the cleanup timer is unref'd.
- `zomaBilling.ts`: the LinkedIn publish classification. (The X one-line fix this branch used to carry landed on main as #4232.)
- Shared picker step: optional `submitLabel` (Meta and Google do not use it).
- Two pinned tests updated with reasons: `eng2747.metaToolkitAnnotations` and `eng2747.databricksReadOnly` (X's omission from the latter has no recorded reason, so it was left).

## Evidence

All on the exact merged head (main at `6f70f0bd6` merged in; 0 commits behind when checked).

- Full typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`, tests included): exit 0 with a 9 GB heap. **The repo's own 6 GB cap (`npm run typecheck` and the pre-push hook) ran out of memory on this head, which carries main's GTM tools** (not checked on main alone), so the push used the hook's documented bypass (`AGENTWEB_SKIP_PREPUSH=1`). Not a type error, not changed here.
- CI-equivalent build (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit`, 4 GB heap, as in `tests.yml`): exit 0. The env2 Docker image ran the real `npm run build` too.
- 92 targeted suites (Zoma, LinkedIn, Google, X, toolkit, annotations, billing, referral, Emma LinkedIn Ads): 1,888 tests pass, exit 0.
- Every new guard was mutation-checked and binds.
- Two independent adversarial reviews. Round 1 found 7 important issues (paywall skipped by an array `action`, previews hiding values, no spend limit when the ceiling is unset, a missing change-ratio test, a failed account list shown as "no ad account", a reconnect that could narrow Emma's scopes, a bearer connect link). Round 2 found 4 more (masked email too weak, read mode asking for write consent, a kept dead row, creative content not fully bound) plus ceiling and preview nits. All fixed in this branch.
- Real runtime on env2 (this branch built into the Docker image, `NODE_ENV=development`), booted three times with the flag unset, `read` and `true`:
  - unset: `/api/zoma/linkedin/callback` and `/select` fall through (404); `POST /api/zoma/setup` works; `/api/meta-toolkit/mcp` answers 401 without a token.
  - `read` and `true`: both LinkedIn routes are live (400 and the Zoma page for a bogus state).
  - Emma's `GET /api/oauth/linkedin-ads/init` returns the real LinkedIn authorize URL in all three states, same client id, redirect and scope list as the pre-change container; the `/init` handler is byte-identical to main; `POST /finalize` with no code answers 400 "Invalid or missing OAuth code" in all three. No errors in the backend log.
- Data plane: no new table, key, index or stored shape. Tokens go through `createAccount`, `getAccountsByUserId` and `updateAccountTokens`, the same helpers (and the same `linkedin_ads` row) Emma already uses.

## Not verified (read this)

Everything is mocked. There is no LinkedIn test account, so **nothing here has run against a real LinkedIn ad account**: read-back shapes, DRAFT acceptance for groups and creatives, `x-restli-id` shapes, default analytics fields. LinkedIn read-back in Emma (ENG-3064) was also merged on mocked evidence. First live check needs a test ad account on prod with the flag at `read`, then a paused create, read-back and archive before `true`.

Also not run on env2: a signed-in `zoma_status` or `tools/list` call (the Zoma token is only issued through the browser sign-in), the full LinkedIn consent and `/finalize` success path (needs a real LinkedIn login and a redirect URI registered for that host), and the Zoma connect pages in a browser. Those are covered by the mocked suites only.

Known limits: pending OAuth sessions live in memory with a 10 minute TTL (same as Google, ENG-3043); a fixed `retry_after_seconds: 60` on 429 because the shared service does not expose headers; no inline or dynamic creatives, message ads, media upload or schedule edits; a revoked connection that still looks usable gets no reconnect link from `zoma_status`.

## Merge and rollout

- Dark on merge: with `ZOMA_LINKEDIN_ADS_ENABLED` unset, the tools, routes and `zoma_status` block do not exist. This is a feature landing before the Nov 25 freeze, not a launch item for Dec 3.
- Turning it on needs an env change through Yugo (about 31 characters for `read`; the environment has about 18 left, so the `.ebextensions/99-enigma-eng2070.config` cleanup comes first). The ceiling default needs no env.
- Before `read` in production: the Standard-tier case (CAS-12332840-W1P8W8 and the new case), the Databricks marketplace docs (`linkedin_ads_read` joins the read-only view), Harsha's confirmation of the ceiling defaults, and a paused create, read-back and archive on a test ad account before `true`.
- Rollback: the flag is already off. To remove the code, revert the merge commit.

title: fix(zoma): X paywall check classifies the same coerced action as the write validator
body:
## What

`isZomaPublishWrite` decided whether an X Ads write makes ads live with `args.action === 'ACTIVATE'`, while the X write validator coerces `action` with `String()`. A non-string action such as `["ACTIVATE"]` therefore passed validation as an ACTIVATE but skipped `assertZomaPublishAllowed`. The paywall check now classifies `String(args.action)`, the same value the validator uses.

## Impact (honest)

Not an exploit on X today: the apply step compares `action` strictly, so that request ends up **pausing** the campaign, never activating it, so no ad goes live without the paywall. It is a consistency fix so the paywall and the validator agree. The same pattern was a real bypass in the new LinkedIn toolkit (separate branch), which is fixed there.

Checked and unaffected: Google (`status === 'ENABLED'` is validated strictly) and Meta (`String(args.action).toUpperCase()`).

## Changes

- `backend/src/mcp/zomaBilling.ts`: one line plus comment.
- `backend/src/__tests__/eng3130.zomaBilling.test.ts`: X rows in the publish classification table, including `["ACTIVATE"]`. Reverting the fix makes the new row fail (checked).

## Evidence

`npm run typecheck`: exit 0. `eng3130.zomaBilling` and the `eng3142` X suites: 148 tests pass.

## Rollout and rollback

Billing is not live yet, so behaviour for real users is unchanged. A merge deploys the backend (about 25 minutes, immutable swap). Rollback: revert.

title: ENG-2840: two lanes in the shared email queue (a bounded bulk lane for automated mail)
body:
## What this does

All platform email (about 30 call sites in 12 files: support, webhooks, admin, intake, roadmap, hot-lead notices, send-as-sender, Emma, ...) goes through ONE in-memory Resend queue, paced at 500 ms a send, with no priority and no bound. When several senders overlap (several GTM reports at once, or later several outside agents over MCP, each emailing many contacts) a password reset or a support reply could wait behind all of their mail, and an unbounded queue is also unbounded memory. One GTM report sends one email at a time, so a single report holds one slot only: the lanes matter when senders overlap, and they cap how much automated mail can wait at once.

This adds two lanes to that queue:

- `lane?: 'transactional' | 'bulk'` on `sendEmail` / `sendSystemEmail`. **An email that names no lane is transactional, exactly as before**, so none of the ~30 existing callers change.
- The worker serves the transactional lane first. While bulk mail waits, every eleventh send is a bulk one, so bulk mail is never starved.
- The bulk lane holds at most 100 waiting. A full lane rejects at once with `EmailQueueFullError` (`code: 'EMAIL_QUEUE_FULL'`, "Nothing was sent. Try again in a minute."): nothing is queued, so nothing waits and memory stays bounded. The transactional lane is never refused and stays unbounded, as today.
- The three GTM emails (work item update notification, phase status report, plan status report) now use the bulk lane. Nothing else changed lane. The phase and plan report loops already count a refused send as a failed recipient, so a report says so honestly instead of throwing (the work item update notification only logs a failed send, as before).
- The non-production email guard keeps the lane when it drops some recipients and queues the rest; `lane` never reaches Resend; the queue log lines now say `lane=` and show the depth of both lanes.

## What it does not do (said plainly)

- A transactional email can still wait behind the one send already in flight and the 500 ms pacing gap after it, plus one bulk slot per eleven transactional sends while bulk mail waits. "In flight" includes that send's retries (sleeps of 1 s and 2 s plus up to three Resend calls), and a Resend call has no timeout, as before.
- The cost for bulk mail: once a bulk email is first in its lane it waits for at most ten more transactional sends (about 5 s under a sustained transactional stream); the GTM report routes hold the HTTP request open while their emails send, so a report can take that much longer in that case.
- The existing callers all stay in the transactional lane, so heavy existing senders still share a lane with each other. Moving one is a one-word change per call site; not done here because it changes when those emails go out.
- Both lanes send from the same Resend domain, so sender reputation is not separated. A separate sending domain for bulk mail is an infrastructure step and cannot be proven live without it, so no code for it is added.
- The bound and counters are per process. Exact on today's single backend instance (EB MinSize=MaxSize=1); revisit if it ever scales out.

This is PR A of the plan to give MCP agents Emma's emailing. PR B (separate, after this) adds an opt-in `gtm:email` key scope with a recipient cap per call, an hourly budget per key and an audit line.

## Behaviour changes to know

- A GTM report or update email now waits behind transactional mail when the queue is busy (by design), and is refused if 100 other bulk emails are already waiting.
- A refusal by a full bulk lane shows up as failed recipients in the report routes and Emma's report tool. The two admin report routes (`routes/admin.ts`) still ignore the report result and answer "sent successfully" for any failure; that was already so, and it is fixed in its own small PR on this card, not here.
- Log lines changed: `Queued Resend email #N (lane=...)`, `Processing Resend queue item #N (lane=...) ...`. Searched the repo for readers of these strings (see the review).

## Proof

- New `resendService.lanes.test.ts` (21 tests) plus additions to `gtmPlanNotificationService.test.ts`; the existing queue, retry, error-propagation, guard and reply-to tests pass unchanged.
- Mutation pass on the final code: 36 mutants of the lane logic and the three GTM call sites; 34 killed, 2 equivalent. The reviews found behaviours the first tests did not pin (the bound counting bulk mail only, the streak reset, a new bulk arrival resetting the streak so the oldest bulk email starves) and I added a test for each, plus the log depth and the pacing gap. The two that survive cannot change behaviour: a defensive streak reset (the bulk lane only shrinks where the streak is reset anyway) and a restart-on-race branch that was already there and cannot fire (no `await` sits between the loop exit and the check).
- Type-check: `npm run typecheck` exits 0 (see the heap fix below).
- Independent review 1 (an earlier head): SHIP WITH NITS. It found no regression for default-lane callers (a differential run of the old and new service over 8 seeded scenarios gave identical Resend calls, settle order and log lines) and model-checked the scheduling over 20 seeds. Every nit is fixed in this PR: the worker now chooses the next email after the 500 ms pacing gap (it chose before, so a password reset arriving in the gap queued behind a bulk email already chosen), four more tests, and a corrected dev note. Independent review 2 (head `e9e2eb9fd`, whole diff): SHIP WITH NITS, again no code defect: its own differential run (old vs new service, 60 random seeds, same-tick and delayed arrivals, failures, retries) was identical for default-lane callers, and it model-checked the scheduling (each transactional email served within `p + ceil(p/10) + 1` sends, each bulk email within `11p`). Its nits are fixed in the commits after that head, which change comments, docs and tests only (the transpiled output of both service files is identical with comments removed): the benefit is now described as "when several senders overlap" (one report sends one email at a time, so a single report holds one slot), the cost for bulk mail is stated, and one more test closes a starvation bug the lane tests did not catch.
- Related-tests run (`jest --findRelatedTests`, 2,106 suites): 2,095 pass; the 2 that fail (`emmaToolArgContracts`, the HubSpot ENG-2792 test, and `socialAdapters.publishRevalidation`, the LinkedIn consent test) fail identically on a clean checkout of origin/main, so they are not caused by this change.
- Pre-push hook green on this head (type-check plus the directly related suites, 73 tests).

## Also in this PR: the local type-check heap (last commit)

`npm run typecheck` and the pre-push hook gave tsc a 6144 MB heap. A full backend type-check now uses about 6.7 GB, so it crashed with exit 134 on a clean origin/main too (verified in a separate checkout): every push failed in the hook. Raised to 10240 MB in `backend/scripts/ci-prepush.mjs`, `backend/package.json` and the note in `CLAUDE.md` (a heap limit is a ceiling, not a reservation). CI is unaffected: it builds with `tsconfig.build.json` at 4096 MB.

title: [ENG-3054] Refreshed Artificial Analysis scores carry no index version, so the version-mix warning cannot see them
body:
Linear: https://linear.app/emmabyaw/issue/ENG-3054/refreshed-artificial-analysis-scores-carry-no-index-version-so-the

`refreshScores` (`backend/src/services/agentMode/modelCatalogRefresh.ts`) writes refreshed scores with a `qualityScoreSource` string that lacks the Intelligence Index major version (e.g. `Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, API v2, snapshot <date>, <slug> (...)`). The version-mix warning in the same function only reads sources containing `Intelligence Index v<N>`, so refreshed scores are invisible to it. Scores are only comparable within one major version.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A score written by `refreshScores` records the feed's `intelligence_index_version` in `qualityScoreSource` when the feed sends one.
2. The existing version warning fires for a registry mixing a refreshed v5 score with a labelled v4 score (unit test with mocked feed).
3. The variant-matching rule that reads the end of `qualityScoreSource` still matches the same rows as before (existing tests unchanged).
4. No registry entry is rewritten by this change alone.

Fully testable with mocked fixtures; no production data or credentials needed.

title: ENG-2840: admin GTM status report routes answer for what the report did
body:
## What this fixes

The two admin routes `POST /api/admin/gtm-plans/:planId/send-status-report` and `.../phases/:phaseId/send-status-report` called the report functions, ignored the counts they return, and answered `200 "... sent successfully"` whatever happened: a report to nobody, or a report the mail service refused in full. The customer routes (`routes/gtmPlan.ts`) and Emma's tool already answer through `describeStatusReport` since ENG-2840 W2-4; the admin routes were the one place left that still said "sent" for a report that did not go out. Two independent reviews of the email queue work (PR #4236) both pointed at this gap.

Both admin routes now answer through `describeStatusReport`, exactly as the customer routes do:
- `400` when nobody was chosen or the chosen contacts have no address,
- `502` when the mail service refused every email,
- `200` with exact counts otherwise (`sent`, `failed`, `suppressed`), e.g. "sent to 2 of 3 recipients; 1 could not be sent", and an email the non-production guard held back is not called sent.
Failure answers are `{ success: false, error: <message> }`, the same shape as the customer routes. An error while reading the plan is still a `500` in the old shape.

## Behaviour change to know

A request that chooses no recipient used to get `200 "Plan status report sent successfully"` and now gets `400`. The only caller is the admin screen (`partner-portal/src/pages/GTMPlans.tsx`): it closes its dialog only when `success` is true and logs any error to the console, so on a failed report the dialog now stays open instead of closing as if the report went out. It does not show the message; showing it is a front-end change and is not part of this fix. I searched the whole repo for any other reader of the old text ("Phase/Plan status report sent successfully") or of a `200` for a report to nobody: there is none.

## Tests (a reason for each change, per the repo rule)

The status report tests in `admin.gtmPlans.test.ts` now run the REAL route and the REAL report code against a mail service double that says what it did (sent, nobody chosen, every email refused, a partial send, a guard-suppressed send, the custom message in the email, the account-owner option, and the 500). I replaced the old status report tests because they could not fail for the bug: the mail mock had no `sendSystemEmail`, so every send threw and was swallowed while the route still answered "sent successfully" (the reviewer reproduced `sendSystemEmail is not a function` printed for every recipient with all six old tests green), and they stubbed the notification service with `jest.doMock` after the route was imported, which replaced nothing. The old "missing notification options" test asserted the bug itself (`200` for a report to nobody); it is replaced by the `400` case. The three 404 tests and all the update-endpoint tests are kept unchanged.

## Proof

- The 9 cases that pin the honest answers (sent, nobody chosen, every email refused, a partial send, a guard-suppressed send, for both routes) fail on the old route code and pass with the fix (checked by restoring the old file temporarily). The 5 cases added after review (the custom message reaching the email, the account-owner option, the 500 shape) pin behaviour that did not change, so they pass on the old code too; they are regression guards, and the mutants below show each one catches the change it is meant to catch.
- Mutation pass: 18 mutants of the new route logic (ignore a failed outcome, wrong status, wrong counts, fixed message, subject without title, result not read, message dropped, error answered with 200, notifications ignored); 18 killed.
- Independent review: SHIP WITH NITS, no defect in the production change. Its findings were two test gaps (the custom message reaching the email, the 500 shape), the owner option not exercised, and a wrong sentence in the dev note (it said the MCP tool answers with `describeStatusReport`; the MCP tool refuses emailing altogether). All fixed here. Left as is: the admin answers name the plan or phase title where the customer routes do not (Emma's tool matches admin), and the rewritten test file is over its `eslint-suppressions.json` counts for `no-explicit-any` (no lint step runs in CI or the hooks; `admin.ts` is already over its own count on `main`).
- `npm run typecheck` exit 0; pre-push hook green (type-check plus 32 suites, 446 tests).

title: ENG-2840: email a GTM status report over MCP, behind an opt-in gtm:email key scope
body:
## What this does

Outside AI agents (Yugo, Hue, Remy) can now make AgentWeb email a GTM status report, the same capability Emma has. It was held back over MCP until three things were in place: the report emails escape caller text (done in W2-4), one report can no longer crowd out password resets (the GTM emails have their own bounded queue lane, PR #4236), and the agent's key is explicitly allowed to do it. This PR adds the last part and the limits.

- **New tool `send_gtm_status_report`**, behind a new opt-in key scope **`gtm:email`**. It is registered with `requiredScope` + `apiKeyOnly`, the same gate as `save_org_memory`: only an `aw_` key that holds the scope can call it. A default key, a legacy key, a read-only key, an OAuth client and a delegated session are refused; `tools:execute` does not imply it. The scope is on the grantable list, cannot be granted from a delegated (admin-as-customer) session, is not a default, and `tools/list` offers the tool only to a key that holds it. The customer portal's key form does not offer opt-in scopes, so a customer cannot tick it there; Yugo's key broker has to request it for the agents that should email.
- **Nobody is emailed by default.** Inputs mirror Emma's: `plan_id`, `phase_id` (omit for a whole-plan report), `notify_user`, `notify_plan_poc`, `notify_phase_poc` (phase report), `notify_phase_pocs` (plan report), `message` (at most 2,000 characters). At least one choice must be `true`; a choice written as text is refused, not guessed; an argument that is not an input is refused by name.
- **Limits** (`mcp/server/gtmEmailLimits.ts`):
  - **at most 10 people per call**: the report service gets a new `maxRecipients` option and refuses BEFORE sending anything when the de-duplicated recipients exceed it (a 400 "it would go to N people and one call may email at most 10. Nothing was emailed."). With a cap, every chosen contact must also be ONE address: a contact stored as a list (the portal stores contacts unvalidated) is one send to several people, so it is refused before anything is sent (400 "N contacts on the plan hold more than one email address ... Put a single address in each contact."), with ASCII and fullwidth commas, semicolons, spaces, line breaks and invisible separators all recognised. Reports without a cap (the portal, admin routes, Emma) are unchanged.;
  - **about 50 emails an hour per account, all of its keys together**: a call reserves the most it could send, settles to what it attempted, and gives everything back when the route refused before sending, so parallel calls cannot overshoot (at most 50 attempted per account per hour; minting more keys buys no more email);
  - **the same report is not sent twice within 10 minutes** (same account, plan, phase, people and message; the message is hashed, never stored).
- **One audit line per attempt** (`mcp_gtm_email`): user, key, plan, phase, which people were chosen, the outcome and counts. Never the message and never an address.
- The tool calls the portal routes through `mcpFetch`, so the plan owner check and the delegation and restriction claims stay on the route: a key can email only the people on its own user's plans. A POST self-call is never retried, so a network blip cannot send a report twice.

## What the scope means (a decision, written down)

`gtm:email` bounds the VOLUME an agent can email, not the AUDIENCE. The report goes to the addresses on the plan, and a key can write those itself: `manage_gtm_plan update dri` needs only `tools:execute`. So a key that holds `gtm:email` can put any address on a plan it owns and email it, with up to 2,000 characters of its own text (more through work item notes, which the report includes), from AgentWeb's system sender. The portal already lets a signed-in user do the same with no limit; this is about a compromised or prompt-injected agent holding an owner's key. The account owner grants the scope knowing that; the caps and the audit line bound and show what happens; grant it only to agents trusted with it. Restricting recipients to the owner's organization, or a per-address cap shared across accounts, would narrow it, and is not done here because contacts on a plan are often people outside the organization and it would change what the portal does too. (Found by the independent review; written down rather than left implied.)

## What it does not do (said plainly)

- **No emails on `update_work_item`**: `manage_gtm_items` still refuses every email argument, and now says where emailing lives. To tell people about an update, update the item and send a report.
- **The audit line's `apiKeyId` is the key that opened the MCP session.** A second key of the same user that reuses that session id is checked on its own scopes per request (no scope is ever borrowed) but is logged under the opener's id, as every MCP tool's audit line is; `userId` is always right. Binding sessions to keys is a change to the session layer for every tool, so it is not made here.
- **Deliberately not added, with the reason:** a process-wide hourly ceiling and a per-address cap across accounts (the portal route already lets any signed-in user email any contact with no limit at all, so a ceiling on this tool alone would bound the new automation and not the real exposure; the right place is the route); an "on behalf of <owner>" line in the reports (it changes email copy customers' contacts receive, and copy Harsha has not reviewed does not merge); recipient domains in the audit line (the route answers counts, not addresses).
- **The scope controls this tool, not every route to a GTM email.** A key that can start an Emma run (`emma_send_message` and the others in `AGENT_EXECUTION_TOOLS`) reaches Emma's own `send_gtm_status_report` inside that run with no scope and no cap, exactly as for `memory:org`. The control is the outside agent's allowlist.
- **The limits are per process, in memory.** Production runs one backend instance (Elastic Beanstalk MinSize=MaxSize=1, checked 2026-11-24), so they are exact; if the backend scales out each instance counts separately. A restart empties the counters.
- A 5xx or a timeout from the route keeps the reservation and the cooldown (the mail service may have taken some); a 4xx gives them back.
- Same sender domain as all platform mail; separating bulk reputation is an infrastructure step.

## Behaviour changes to know

- Report email subjects collapse line breaks and control characters in a plan or phase title to a space, and a mailbox written in different cases or with stray spaces is one person, for the portal, admin routes and Emma as well as MCP.

- The refusal text of `manage_gtm_items` for email arguments changed (the stem "emailing people is not available over MCP" is kept). The public tool inventory snapshot gains the new tool and that description.
- `StatusReportResult` gains an optional `overCap`; `describeStatusReport` answers 400 for it. The portal, admin and Emma set no cap, so they are unchanged.

## Proof

- Tests: the limiter on a fake clock (cooldown, rolling hour, reservation, release, the memory bound); the tool (request, every refusal, the whole send flow, audit); the HTTP scope gate against the real registry (default, legacy, read-only, OAuth, batch; the scope opens only this tool and no other scope opens it); key creation and discovery; and the REAL routes with two tenants (a report goes to exactly the people chosen, in the bulk lane; the cap sends nothing over 10; tenant B's key can never email tenant A's people, 403/404 send nothing; a key that has used its hour is refused).
- Mutation passes: 104 mutants over the cap, the single-address rule, the outcome, the tool, the limiter, the scope plumbing and the review fixes; 103 killed. The one survivor is equivalent: at exactly 10 minutes the cooldown check is already false, so whether the pruning step drops the entry a tick earlier changes nothing.
- `npm run typecheck` exit 0; the pre-push hook (type-check plus the related suites) is green on every push. All 110 plans and 365 phases on production have ids that fit the strict id pattern the tool now requires (read-only scan).
- Independent review 1 (head `254d9832c`): SHIP WITH NITS. No way for a caller without `gtm:email` to reach the handler (default, legacy, read-only, OAuth, anonymous, batch, session reuse, in-process), no cross-tenant send in either direction. Its findings are fixed in the commits after it: the hour and the cooldown are counted per ACCOUNT (two keys of one user got twice the hour); a refused call no longer holds limiter capacity (1,000 junk keys could make the limiter refuse every other key); `settle()` ignores a number that is not finite (NaN would have switched the budget off, one mutation away); the tool accepts only real ids, so `plan_id: ".."` cannot burn the hour; the tool's refusals all say "Nothing was emailed"; a plan or phase title with a line break reaches the email subject as one line; one mailbox written in different cases is one email and one person against the cap; `skill.md` documented an input (`recipients`) the tool refuses; the dev note states the audience decision above. The two report-service changes (subjects, distinct people) are shared with the portal, admin routes and Emma. Independent review 2 (head `898be24f4`): SHIP WITH NITS. It confirmed the per-account, id, shared-service and subject fixes, again found no way for a caller without `gtm:email` to reach the handler (real HTTP end to end: default, legacy, read-only, OAuth, anonymous, batch, seven parallel calls) and no cross-tenant send. Findings, all handled: **the public tool inventory snapshot was stale at that head** (I changed the tool description after regenerating it; the pre-push hook runs only the directly related suites, so it slipped through): regenerated, and a 140-suite sweep of every MCP, GTM, tool-policy and API-key suite (2,846 tests) is green; **a `dri` written as a comma-separated list counted as one person against the cap** (the first fix counted the addresses inside it; review 3 then showed a list is still one send to several people); a 5xx other than 502 was unpinned: tests for 500, 503, 504; a negative count from the route and an unbounded audit error: tests; limiter refusals said "API key" for what is per account: reworded; the tool header overclaimed that delegation and restriction claims stay on the route: corrected.
- Independent review 3 (head `f86db64a8`, the whole diff): SHIP WITH NITS, nothing blocking. It re-verified who can call it (HTTP gate and registry for a default key, a legacy key, `tools:read`, OAuth, anonymous, a batch, a rehydrated session), whose people (owner check on both routes, ids, no agent-controlled cap), the limits (200 parallel calls from one account reached the route exactly 50 times; 150 across three keys of one user also 50), injection and logging, and judged "volume, not audience" an acceptable place to stop (the portal route already lets any signed-in user email any contact with a free-text message and no cap, so this tool is strictly tighter). Its findings, all handled in the commits after it: a contact stored as a list is one send to several people, so the hourly budget could undercount (only an owner can write such a contact, and how Resend treats a comma-joined `to` is unverified): with a cap, a contact holding more than one address is now refused before anything is sent, with ASCII and fullwidth separators and invisible characters recognised (it showed a fullwidth comma and a zero-width space slipped past a plain split); a stale sentence in the dev note: fixed; no test pinned that another opt-in scope does not list the tool: added.
- **Not independently re-reviewed:** the last commits after review 3 (the single-address rule, about 30 lines in the report service plus its wording) were checked by 17 more mutants (all killed) and by two sweeps of every MCP, GTM, tool-policy and API-key suite (140 suites, 2,856 tests, green). That rule can only make the tool refuse more (it fails closed and adds no capability or surface), and it was the fix review 3 itself proposed, so I judged a fourth full review not worth its cost; say so if you want one.

title: fix(group-email): consistent camelCase/snake_case variable recognition
body:
Reported by Francisco: a lead with First Name populated was flagged missing `{{first_name}}` and skipped.

**Root cause:** `leadHasVariable` did an exact `lead[varName]` lookup, so `first_name` never matched `firstName`. `substituteVariables` had a separate hard-coded alias list (spaced only). Coverage, send eligibility and substitution disagreed.

**Fix (`backend/src/utils/emailVariables.ts`):** one `canonicalVariableName()` resolver (case-insensitive, ignores spaces/underscores/hyphens; `company_name`→`company`) used by `leadHasVariable`, `substituteVariables` and `isSupportedVariable`. That covers the composer's prepare endpoint, the send-time eligibility filter, group-email + sequence sends and drip substitution. Template imports (`templateParser.extractVariables`) keep names as written; they now resolve the same way at send. Unknown tokens are still left as-is; `customFields.*` unchanged.

**Tests:**
- `emailVariables.canonical.test.ts`: coverage/substitution/support for each spelling (32 of these fail on main)
- `crm.groupEmail.test.ts`: prepare reports `{{first_name}}` covered; send emails the lead with `{{first_name}} {{last_name}}` substituted and skips only the lead that is actually missing the name
- emailVariables, crm.groupEmail, sequences and drip suites: all passing (806 tests)
